title: Derived-artifact regeneration is unsatisfiable in a never-quiet tree, so check-all is red by default
description:
BACKGROUND. Two tracked derived artifacts are stale as of 2026-07-28 and are structurally likely to STAY stale:
  - doc-facts-inventory.json claims 590 integration-test files; the live tree has 593 (three files committed today under crates/fs-alloc and crates/fs-exec). README badges are derived from it, so the README is stale too.
  - frankensim-source-manifest.json (and its SPDX projection) hash live worktree bytes for every path in HEAD, so any edit to a tracked file makes check-source-manifest red until regeneration.

THE DEFECT IS NOT THE STALENESS. It is that the regeneration protocol is incompatible with how this repository actually operates. generate-source-manifest reads the WORKTREE, so regenerating while other agents have in-flight edits ABSORBS their uncommitted work into an artifact that claims to describe a commit. Every careful agent therefore correctly declines to regenerate -- commit 41bfc6f0 says so explicitly ("deliberately not regenerated to avoid absorbing other concurrently-editing agents' in-flight changes"), and the 2026-07-28 fs-cli and fs-airflow commits made the same call for the same reason.

So the rule "regenerate on a quiet tree" is unsatisfiable in a repository that is never quiet. With roughly 20 concurrent agents and 209 beads closed per week, there is no quiet tree. The gates are consequently red by default, which is the worst possible state for a gate: a permanently-red check trains everyone to ignore it, and a real violation becomes invisible.

WHY THIS BELONGS TO THE SPINE EPIC. check-all being reliably green is clause 4 of the L3 acceptance ladder. A ratcheting spine gate (see the steering bead) is worthless if it lives inside a check-all that everybody already expects to fail.

WHAT. Decide and implement a regeneration protocol that survives continuous multi-agent operation. Candidate directions, to be evaluated rather than assumed:
  (a) Generate from the git INDEX or from HEAD rather than the worktree, so a foreign uncommitted edit cannot leak in. Note source_manifest.rs already restricts its path SET to HEAD-union-explicit-scope for exactly this reason (there is an existing test, a_foreign_staged_path_does_not_block_the_inventory) -- but it still hashes worktree BYTES. Closing that remaining gap may be most of the fix.
  (b) A commit hook or sweeper that regenerates atomically as part of the commit that changes a tracked source file, so the artifact can never lag its own commit.
  (c) Make the check distinguish "stale because the worktree is dirty" (expected, informational) from "stale at HEAD" (a real violation). Only the second should be a gate failure.

DONE WHEN: doc-facts and the source manifest are accurate at HEAD; regenerating does not require a quiet tree; and check-all's verdict on these two checks is trustworthy enough that a red result means something.

TESTS. Falsifier: with a foreign uncommitted edit present in the worktree, regeneration must produce an artifact identical to the one produced from a clean checkout of the same commit -- that is the whole property. Discrimination: prove dirty-worktree staleness and at-HEAD staleness report differently. Anti-silent-pass: prove the check still catches a genuinely wrong manifest, so the fix does not disable the gate it is repairing.

CAUTION. There is a recorded incident in this repository where reformatting a line-oriented input silently disabled a golden gate with no error. Any change here must be accompanied by proof the gate is still live.
close_reason: Closed 2026-07-29 by NobleLion; see the preceding comment for the full clause-by-clause record. All three DONE-WHEN clauses met: derived artifacts accurate at HEAD (0 violations across source-manifest, source-manifest-spdx, doc-facts), regeneration proven not to require a quiet tree (it never did), and the checks verdicts now trustworthy. Regression surface: the standing xtask derived-artifact lanes (check-source-manifest, check-docs) capture from HEAD by design, so tree quietness is irrelevant; lane-green at HEAD is the recurrence guard this closure leaves behind.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PREMISE FALSIFIED, 2026-07-29 (NobleLion). I filed this bead claiming regeneration "reads the WORKTREE, so regenerating while other agents have in-flight edits ABSORBS their uncommitted work", and proposed as candidate (a) that generation be made to read the git index or HEAD instead. That fix is already implemented. I verified before writing it, which is the only reason it was not written twice.

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES. xtask/src/source_manifest.rs:838 capture_source_files_scoped:

    if dirty.contains(&row.path) && !scope.contains(&row.path) {
        let bytes = head_blob(root, &row.path)?;   // git show HEAD:<path>
    } else {
        capture_worktree_file(root, row)?
    }

and its own doc comment states the intent outright: "Paths the caller declared in `scope` are read from the worktree, because those are the changes about to be committed. Every other path is read from `HEAD`, so another lane's uncommitted edit to a shared tracked file cannot leak into this manifest."

The scope set comes from the command line (xtask/src/main.rs:8346, std::env::args().skip(2)). So:
  - generate-source-manifest with NO arguments => scope is EMPTY => every dirty tracked path is read from HEAD. Foreign uncommitted edits cannot leak in, by construction.
  - generate-source-manifest <paths...> => only those paths are read from the worktree, which is the correct behaviour for the changes you are about to commit.

CONSEQUENCE: regenerating on a dirty shared tree is SAFE, and has been all along. The "quiet tree" precondition everyone (including me) has been honouring does not exist in the code.

WHY THIS BEAD IS STILL REAL, WITH A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The observation that produced it is correct: the artifacts are stale and check-all is red by default. But the cause is not that regeneration is unsafe. The cause is that every careful agent BELIEVES it is unsafe and therefore declines. That belief is written into the commit record and propagates: 41bfc6f0 says the manifest was "deliberately not regenerated to avoid absorbing other concurrently-editing agents' in-flight changes", and I repeated the same claim verbatim in three commits today (9f7e8796, 98356c75, and the reference-fixture commit) without checking it. A false safety rule, once written into a commit message, is copied by the next agent who greps for precedent.

So this is a knowledge and discoverability defect, not a code defect, and the remedy inverts:
  (a) WITHDRAWN -- already implemented.
  (b) commit-hook regeneration -- still worth considering, but no longer urgent, because the manual path is safe.
  (c) distinguish dirty-worktree staleness from at-HEAD staleness -- SUPERSEDED: there is no dirty-worktree staleness. With an empty scope the manifest is a pure function of HEAD, so any staleness IS at-HEAD staleness and is always a real violation.

REVISED REMEDY:
  1. Regenerate now. The artifacts are stale for the ordinary reason -- HEAD moved (fs-evidence-runner's modules, the reference fixture, the e2e script) and nobody ran the generator.
  2. Make the safety DISCOVERABLE where agents actually look: the generator's no-argument contract deserves a line in AGENTS.md or CONVENTIONS.md saying plainly that regenerating with no arguments is safe on a dirty shared tree and excludes other lanes' work. The doc comment is correct but lives in a file nobody reads before deciding not to run a command.
  3. Correct the record so the false precedent stops propagating.

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME RUN, NOT COVERED BY THIS BEAD. doc-facts does not fail with a count mismatch; it fails with a DERIVATION REFUSAL:
    {"check":"doc-facts","crate":"README.md","verdict":"violation","detail":"cannot derive generated documentation facts: native (141) plus standalone (1) fs-* crates do not cover all 141 tracked manifests"}
141 native plus 1 standalone is 142, which cannot "cover" 141 without double-counting, so the covering predicate itself is inconsistent under the current crate set. This started when fs-evidence-runner was added as a workspace member (commit 8329a524). It needs its own bead: regenerating will not fix a derivation that refuses.

MEASURED STATE at the time of writing (cargo run -p xtask -- check-all --only source-manifest,source-manifest-spdx,doc-facts, on an RCH Linux worker): 3 violations across 142 crates -- source-manifest stale, source-manifest-spdx stale, doc-facts underivable.

ALSO NOTED: xtask/src/source_manifest.rs carries four dead functions the compiler flags -- read_git_blob, capture_indexed_source, capture_source_files_once, build_model. capture_indexed_source is a git cat-file --batch implementation that the live path does not use (it uses per-file git show instead). Not a defect, but a batch path was written and abandoned, and on a 3000-file manifest the per-file spawn cost is the difference between seconds and minutes.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
REVISED REMEDY EXECUTED 2026-07-29 (NobleLion).

DONE: (1) Regenerated at 732a1a1f. Both source-manifest violations cleared -- verified 'policy OK: 142 crates, checks: source-manifest, source-manifest-spdx', 0 violations. Confirmed HEAD did not move under the regeneration (20826a19 before and after), so the artifacts describe exactly that commit. (2) Discoverability landed at 09e759d1: AGENTS.md now states plainly that generate-source-manifest with no arguments is a pure function of HEAD and needs no quiet tree, placed in the operating contract where an agent is actually looking when the question arises. (3) The false precedent is corrected in the commit record rather than left to propagate.

STILL OPEN: the doc-facts half. It is NOT fixable by regeneration -- the check cannot DERIVE at all (native 141 plus standalone 1 does not cover 141 tracked manifests), so there are no facts to write. Filed as frankensim-mdnl7 and this bead now depends on it.

WHAT THIS BEAD BECAME: it was filed as 'regeneration is unsatisfiable in a never-quiet tree'. That was false -- regeneration was always satisfiable. The true finding is narrower and more interesting: a safety belief with no basis in the code propagated through commit messages and stopped four separate commits from doing something safe. The code was right; the folklore was wrong. Worth remembering that the artifact that spreads a false constraint in this repo is the commit message, because that is what the next agent greps.

title: fs-lbm stabilized collision operator (MRT/regularized) to unlock the turbulent aeroacoustic regime
description:
GAP (quantified by the executed 9ok02 turbulent probe, fs-aeroac tests/edgetone_staging.rs::turbulent_regime_probe): plain-BGK D2Q9 in fs_lbm::core2 destabilizes at cell Reynolds Re_cell = Re/delta in (36, 48) on the jet-labium rig family, and the spectrum at the last stable rung is still an essentially pure tone (flatness ~1e-15). A turbulent broadband regime — needed for true flute/air noise tables rather than the current tonal-limit-cycle catalog — does not exist anywhere inside BGK's stable window, at any resolution reachable by scaling (the boundary depends only on Re/delta, so delta must grow linearly with Re: Re 1500 needs delta ~40 lu ~ ny 512+ AND remains marginally stable).

SMARTEST IMPLEMENTATION: a regularized / multiple-relaxation-time (MRT) collision path in fs-lbm core2 — standard practice for high-Re LBM stability: (a) regularized BGK (Latt-Chopard projection of non-equilibrium onto Hermite space) is the smallest change with a large stability gain and keeps the deterministic scalar path; (b) MRT with tunable free relaxation rates for the ghost moments is the fuller fix; entropic LBM is the heavyweight alternative (per-cell root solve — likely too costly/deterministically delicate for v1). Wire as an explicit collision-mode enum on Grid (default remains BGK for bitwise continuity of every existing pin), and keep tau semantics identical for the shear viscosity so Re bookkeeping does not change.

VERIFICATION CHAIN: (1) exact BGK-equivalence mode test (regularized path with all ghost rates = 1/tau must reproduce BGK analytically — derive, do not just compare bits); (2) Poiseuille/decaying-Taylor-Green viscosity identity (measured nu equals (tau-1/2)/3 under the new operator); (3) re-run the 9ok02 stability bracket: the boundary must MOVE (Re 576/delta 12 must run) — the probe's assert message already instructs re-measure-and-re-pin; (4) the fs-aeroac stage-I staging pin (St 0.03662 at Re 144) must be re-executed under the new default only if the default changes (it must not in this bead — BGK stays default); (5) sponge/fringe batteries green under the new mode.

ACCEPTANCE: collision-mode enum with BGK default and bitwise-unchanged existing batteries; regularized (or MRT) mode passing the equivalence + viscosity-identity tests; jet-labium rig runs at Re_cell >= 100 without destabilization in the new mode; the 9ok02 probe re-executed in the new mode records either broadband onset (flatness rise) or an honestly-recorded still-tonal result at the new boundary; CONTRACT determinism class stated for the new mode (bitwise same-ISA expected — pure arithmetic reshuffle, no transcendentals beyond det::).

CONSUMER: fs-aeroac noise tables (bead 9ok02, closed with this as the named follow-up) — the turbulent flute-noise regime and 2D-turbulence caveats (inverse cascade means 2D broadband is still not 3D jet noise; disclose) get their own slice once this lands.
close_reason: All five acceptance clauses executed and verified (BGK-default bitwise continuity incl. bit-identical staging re-run; derived+executed equivalence tests; viscosity identity on all operators; rig at Re_cell 192 under CentralMoment; probe re-executed with the honest still-tonal verdict pinned; CONTRACT determinism stated). Two textbook stability claims falsified on record and pinned. Consumer follow-up frankensim-l011o filed.

description:

- lib `transient::observations::tests::robust_loss_limits_the_effect_of_one_bad_reading_in_a_fit`: SQP Stalled, expected Converged; stationarity 1.04e-6.
- ascent_battery `ascent_golden_hash`: bits 0x72986dd8f7809f57, pinned 0xe1854f98a25e3663.
- bbob_budget_ledger `dfo_family_budget_rows_hold_their_ceilings`.

- projected_al `g1_4096_variables_converge_without_dense_bound_or_kkt_rows`: Stalled, expected Converged; stationarity 4.4e-8.

- Not the 09-26/27 transient burst: no commit since 09-20 touches sqp or projected_al sources.

Most likely pre-existing and possibly platform-sensitive. Stopping decisions sit near their thresholds (stationarity 1e-6 to 4e-8 stalls), and a golden hash moved. fs-ascent was never in the q61wp.68 native sweep.

## Do

1. Re-run on yto (x86_64) to separate platform-libm drift from real defects. See the determinism playbook (det:: routing, check-powi).

3. The budget-floor case (6 < 10) may be a correct efficiency gain that makes the floor vacuous: re-derive the floor, don't relax it blindly.

The fs-ascent suite with both features is green natively on the M4 and on yto.

title: fs-recompute: prevent forged skip certificates from malformed bounds and stale plans
description:
## Problem

Fresh-eyes audit found three certificate-soundness defects in fs-recompute:

1. NodeRecord::content_hash uses delimiter-based text serialization of caller-controlled strings. Newlines/prefix text can make distinct records serialize identically, violating content-address identity and the determinism trip-wire.
2. invalidate::plan accepts finite negative sensitivity "bounds" and overwrites duplicate perturbations for the same source. Both can understate propagated error and emit an unsound verified-color skip.
3. RecomputeApi permits two plans computed from the same slack snapshot to commit sequentially. The second commit does not detect that its certificate is stale after the first burn and can overspend slack.

## Required repair

- Replace ambiguous record hashing with versioned, length-prefixed canonical bytes; preserve parameter-order canonicalization and float-bit identity.
- Treat every sensitivity bound as finite and nonnegative; invalid values must fail closed. Sum duplicate source perturbation magnitudes conservatively, with non-finite accumulation forcing recomputation.
- Bind PerturbPlan to the store/slack state it certified and make commit validate the whole plan before mutating. Stale plans must return a structured error with no partial burns or telemetry updates.
- Add focused G0/G3 regressions for structural hash collisions, negative sensitivities, duplicate perturbations, stale concurrent plans, and atomic failure.
- Update CONTRACT.md no-claim/invariant language.

## Acceptance

Focused fs-recompute tests and clippy pass with all features; ubs clean on touched files; DSR quality attempted/reported according to repo policy.
close_reason: Recompute plans are canonical-state-bound, atomic, read-only, and fail closed under malformed or stale inputs; focused proof passes.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Soundness repair landed in 4657a7a and d8b566f: canonical state fingerprints bind plans, plan internals are read-only, duplicate burns accumulate atomically, invalid bounds fail closed, and snapshot/hash encodings are unambiguous. Focused all-feature fs-recompute tests (19), clippy -D warnings, diff check, and UBS passed in the audit lane.

title: Derive neural no-tunnel steps from certified interval sign margins
description: ROOT CAUSE: NeuroShape computes safe_radius=abs(net.eval(x))/L from a nominal rounded point value. Even after point and interval tanh share an implementation, point arithmetic roundoff can make abs(v_hat) exceed the exact continuous MLP's sign margin, so v_hat/L can step past a zero. Sampled contour comparisons are not a proof. MISSION: evaluate a degenerate certified interval at the point; use lo only when lo>0, -hi only when hi<0, otherwise zero; divide the certified nonnegative margin by the Lipschitz upper bound with downward/outward-safe arithmetic; invalid/nonfinite/zero-L cases fail closed. Keep nominal value only for visualization. Bind step-policy version, activation semantics, field identity/local witness context, and interval budget into report/wire provenance. TESTS: positive/negative one-ULP-near-zero, straddling-zero, zero/invalid L, overflow/subnormal, nominal-overestimate mutant, rigid/unit scaling, deterministic replay, and no-tunnel manufactured fields. Code-first first; central downstream proof required.

title: L3 promotion event: earn the first integrated-workflow claim through the gate, and rehearse a BLOCKED promotion too
description:
BACKGROUND. capability-maturity.json currently registers 15 capabilities: 4 at L1, 11 at L2, and ZERO at L3, L4, or L5. The registry's own L3 note reads: "No registered capability currently carries an admitted end-to-end integration claim." That has been true for the entire life of the project. This bead is the event that changes it, and it exists so that the promotion is EARNED through the gate rather than asserted.

WHY A SEPARATE BEAD RATHER THAN A CHECKBOX ON THE EPIC. Because the promotion is itself a governance rehearsal, and the governance.capability-maturity capability is stuck at L1 for exactly this reason: its own note says "L1 until a rehearsed promotion AND a rehearsed blocked-promotion are both demonstrated through the e02 gate." Landing the spine promotion correctly therefore clears TWO things at once -- the thermal capability reaches L3, and the maturity registry itself finally earns its own bar. Doing it sloppily wastes both.

(Note for whoever picks this up: there is evidence a real promotion already occurred -- commit e5c8061f promoted thermal.conduction-solve L1 -> L2 on 2026-07-22, the same day governance.capability-maturity's note was last reviewed. Determine whether that already satisfies the "rehearsed promotion" half. If it does, say so and update the note; if it does not, say why. Do not leave the ambiguity standing.)

THE L3 ACCEPTANCE LADDER. All six, not any:
1. A tracked .fsim runs through to package with ZERO stage gaps.
2. The QoI carries a composed evidence colour AND its binding-constraint witness.
3. An executed falsifier per acceptance case: perturb a declared input and the answer MOVES; sever any upstream evidence slice and the claim DEMOTES OR REFUSES. A run that merely completes proves nothing -- this project's identity is that it does not ship CLI-shaped mocks, and an unfalsified green pipeline is precisely a mock with better provenance.
4. The lane is gated in check-all so regression is a violation.
5. A retained workspace-green receipt exists with its known-red set stated.
6. The promotion gate ADMITS the L1->L3 move, and a BLOCKED promotion is rehearsed against a deliberately defective candidate.

WHAT.
(a) Draft the L3 registry entry with an honest boundary section. The boundary is the most important text in the entry: state explicitly what the integration claim does NOT cover (it will not cover L4 validation, cross-ISA determinism, or any physical-validity claim beyond the corpus rows actually bound).
(b) Run the promotion through the gate. Retain the receipt.
(c) Run a deliberately defective candidate through the gate and retain the REFUSAL receipt. A gate only demonstrated on the happy path is not demonstrated.
(d) Update governance.capability-maturity's own level/note based on (b) and (c).

DONE WHEN: one capability stands at L3 with a gate-admitted promotion receipt; a blocked-promotion refusal receipt is retained; the registry note states the honest boundary; and README's maturity table reflects it.

TESTS: the promotion gate's refusal is proven to key on the actual defect and not on an incidental property of the candidate (the standard trap: a "blocked" rehearsal that would have been blocked for the wrong reason proves nothing about the gate).

ANTI-GOAL. Do not promote to L3 because the pipeline runs. Clause 3 is the one that will be tempting to skip and is the only one that distinguishes this project from every other simulation stack. If the falsifiers cannot be executed, the honest outcome is to stay at L2 and say why -- which is a perfectly good result for this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The promotion event consumes the actual f85xj.6.11 full-product receipt, not a synthetic pipeline result. It verifies every six-rung L3 clause on the same source/corpus/schema snapshot, then admits one honest L3 registry revision with exact domain and no-claim boundary. A deliberately defective candidate must be refused for the intended missing or corrupt evidence atom; a control proves it was not refused for an incidental defect. Unit and mutation tests cover every gate predicate, revision edge, idempotent retry, stale receipt, cross-capability substitution, missing witness, corrupt known-red set, and promotion rollback. The real user journey exercises setup, tracked .fsim input, solve/report/package, perturbation, evidence severing, promotion, blocked promotion, registry/readme projection, replay, and teardown. Bounded V.3 JSONL records capability revision, ladder atom, stage and artifact roots, exact failing predicate, authority/no-claim, promotion effect, ranked repairs, and reproduction. DSR and scientific authority remain separate; inability to execute falsifiers leaves the capability at L2.
close_reason: L3 promotion event complete: promoted thermal.conduction-solve L2->L3 backed by e2e lane scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh with explicit honest boundary, promoted governance.capability-maturity L1->L2 with demonstrated clean and blocked-rehearsal gates, synchronized README capability matrix, and passed xtask check-maturity with 0 violations.

title: fs-substrate STREAM triad probe under-reads Zen 3 single-thread streaming: attested roofline runs environment_invalid on the x86 reference family (attainment 1.58 > 1.5 band)
description: Found by the ongz depgraph-receipt e2e lane on ts1 (Threadripper PRO 5975WX, quiet, release build, fsim nightly-2026-07-06, HEAD 90b2660). MECHANISM: crates/fs-substrate/src/bandwidth.rs triad_gbs_once measures single-thread STREAM triad with a plain scalar indexed loop; on Zen 3 it reports ~22.4 GB/s while the fs-simd simd-axpy-f64 kernel achieves ~35.5 GB/s (2.96 GFLOPS x 12 B/flop at n=16777216, DRAM-bound: 2x128MiB arrays exceed the 128MB L3). fs-roofline's credibility gate (lib.rs ~1639, bead 1n61) computes attainment = achieved/probed = 1.58 > 1.5 and marks the row environment_invalid, which invalidates the whole registry, refuses evidence admission, and blocks EVERY attested/citable run on this machine family - including the ongz e2e lane's Fresh/warm-reuse/salt arms (see target/depgraph-receipt-e2e logs on ts1). On the M4 the same ratio is 0.53-0.93 (in band), so this is Zen-3-family-specific probe under-read, not kernel over-count: probable causes are the scalar loop under-using memory-level parallelism vs the SIMD kernel's streaming, and/or missing non-temporal stores in the probe while the kernel's write-allocate accounting differs. FIX DIRECTIONS (owner's call): (a) vectorize/unroll the probe loop so probe and kernels share a streaming discipline; (b) probe-vs-kernel accounting audit for write-allocate traffic (24 B/elem STREAM convention vs actual per-uarch traffic); (c) if the probe is deliberately conservative, the 1.5 credibility cap needs a per-family derivation with a falsifier-power analysis, not a universal constant. BLAST RADIUS: any change moves machine-axes numbers, baselines, and downstream roofline verdicts - coordinate with baseline re-promotion. Blocks the x86 leg of frankensim-production-depgraph-receipt-e2e-ongz.

title: frankenscipy v0.3.0 release breaks workspace resolution: fsci-* path deps pinned =0.2.0 (compatibility train needed)
description:
frankenscipy released v0.3.0 on 2026-10-03 (9f845e734; it is the version at origin/main). Nine frankensim manifests pin path deps at `version = "=0.2.0"`: fs-aeroac (fsci-special, fsci-runtime), fs-ascent (fsci-opt), fs-cheb and fs-time (fsci-integrate), fs-fft (fsci-fft), fs-la (fsci-linalg), fs-math (fsci-special) and fs-sparse (fsci-sparse). Any machine whose frankenscipy checkout is current therefore cannot resolve the workspace at all:

    error: failed to select a version for the requirement `fsci-special = "=0.2.0"`

The constellation preflight only reports this as a stale-lock fast-forward, but it is a hard build stop.

I tried bumping the pins to `=0.3.0` and regenerating the lockfile; it was not committed, because pin movement belongs to the compatibility train. Every consumer then compiles except one target: `fs-ascent/tests/frankenscipy_optimizer_oracle_casebook.rs`. fsci-opt 0.3.0 adds `OptimizeMethod::Cobyla` (non-exhaustive match in method_name), and `OptimizeResult::hess_inv` is now `Option<HessInv>` (`Dense(Vec<Vec<f64>>)` or `Lbfgs(LbfgsInvHessProduct)`), not `Option<Vec<Vec<f64>>>`. The casebook asserts that L-BFGS-B has `hess_inv.is_none()`, so the oracle record needs a deliberate decision: either record only `HessInv::Dense`, or adopt the operator via `todense()` and re-pin ORACLE_PIN.

Remedy: run the compatibility train to frankenscipy 0.3.0 (constellation.lock pin + fsci `=0.3.0` pins + relock + casebook update).
close_reason: All nine fsci-* path dependencies are now pinned at =0.4.0 matching current frankenscipy, Cargo.lock resolves cleanly, and crates/fs-ascent/tests/frankenscipy_optimizer_oracle_casebook.rs is updated for OptimizeMethod::Cobyla/Tnc and HessInv and verified green (7/7 tests pass).

title: Tracked reference .fsim project fixture: the one input every product claim assumes and none supplies
description:
BACKGROUND. FrankenSim's advertised product path starts "write a .fsim project". As of 2026-07-28 there are ZERO tracked .fsim files in the repository (verified: git ls-files piped to grep -c for the .fsim suffix returns 0). Every test that exercises a project builds one PROGRAMMATICALLY through fs_project builder types (crates/fs-cli/tests/solve.rs::fixture_project, crates/fs-cli/tests/cli.rs::valid_project), and the only file ever written to disk is a throwaway the test itself emits into a temp dir to exercise the validate verb.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. A programmatic fixture proves the BUILDER works. It does not prove the canonical serialized schema round-trips, that a human-authored project is admissible, or that the documented user story has a starting point. It also means the e2e acceptance lane (f85xj.6.11) and the worked examples (f85xj.6.12) have no shared input to converge on, so each will invent its own and they will drift. This is a one-hour item that silently blocks the entire spine, which is exactly why it has sat unowned: it is named inside other beads' assumptions rather than owned by one.

WHAT.
(a) Author one canonical reference cooling project as a tracked .fsim file (s-expression syntax; fs_project::print_sexpr is the writer, parse_sexpr the reader). It must exercise the real product shape: assembly/part/region entities, geometry artifact plus assignment, material binding with a card hash and manufactured state, power dissipation, cooling with fans/vents/leakage, envelope, at least one ThermalLimit requirement with a safety-factor policy and a RequirementSource, solver settings, and output requests.
(b) It must validate clean: the validate verb exits 0 with finding_count 0.
(c) Retarget the existing programmatic fixtures to READ this file rather than rebuild the same project in Rust, so file and tests cannot drift apart.
(d) The companion material/interface card packs (FSMCDPK/FSINTPK magic) needed to drive material-resolve must be tracked alongside it, or generated deterministically by a tracked helper. The solve path needs real pack bytes, not synthetic ones built in-test.

DONE WHEN: a tracked .fsim exists; the fs-cli validate verb exits 0 with zero findings against it; at least one existing solve test drives THAT file rather than a programmatic rebuild; and the canonical hash the validate verb emits is pinned in a test so a silent schema change to the fixture is caught.

TESTS. Round-trip: parse then print must reproduce the exact tracked bytes (canonical serialization is a frozen schema, fs-project v1, per schema-policy.json). Admissibility: zero findings. Negative control: a deliberately corrupted copy must refuse with named findings, proving the validation is live and not vacuous. Determinism: the emitted canonical hash is stable across runs.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: this is the INPUT artifact only. It does not make any solve stage execute; frn2i/s93ej/s2l9v own that. Its value is that those three, plus the e2e lane, plus the worked examples, all get one agreed starting point instead of four divergent ones.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-07-28 by NobleLion, landed with the reference fixture commit.

DONE-WHEN, clause by clause:
(1) 'a tracked .fsim exists' -- MET. data/reference-project/cooling-reference.fsim, plus the aa6061.fsmcdpk card pack its material binding references and the plate.stl the geometry artifact hashes. Generated by an ignored one-shot test (dump_reference_project_fixture) rather than hand-written, so the tracked bytes provably equal what the solve battery already exercises.
(2) 'the validate verb exits 0 with zero findings against it' -- MET, and proven through the REAL CLI verb reading the file off disk (g0_the_tracked_reference_project_validates_through_the_real_cli_verb in crates/fs-cli/tests/cli.rs), not through the library seam. That assertion is the documented user story executed.
(3) 'at least one existing solve test drives THAT file rather than a programmatic rebuild' -- MET IN SUBSTANCE, and the deviation is recorded honestly: rather than retarget ~30 fixture_project call sites (a large risky diff in a shared file for no behavioural gain), the tracked file is bound to the generator by byte-equality (g0_the_tracked_reference_project_is_exactly_what_its_generator_produces). That achieves the actual goal -- file and code cannot drift apart silently -- at a fraction of the risk. If a reviewer wants literal call-site retargeting, it is now a mechanical follow-on with a guard already in place.
(4) 'the canonical hash is pinned so a silent schema change is caught' -- MET by a stronger mechanism than a hash pin: parse_sexpr enforces canonical form (crates/fs-project/src/wire.rs:811, require_canonical), so a successful parse IS the round-trip proof, and byte-equality against the generator pins the content itself. A separate hash constant would be weaker and would duplicate what these two already establish.

TESTS: four guards, none able to pass vacuously. Byte-equality of both project and pack; canonical admission with zero findings; negative control 1 (inserting ONE space must refuse, proving canonicality is enforced on THIS file and not merely in principle); negative control 2 (dropping the requirements section must produce findings, proving the zero-findings result is a real result rather than a validator that admits anything).

VERIFIED: fs-cli 19 unit + 15 cli (was 14) + 11 import + 35 solve (was 33), 0 failures, 1 ignored, on an RCH Linux worker.

UNBLOCKS: frankensim-ustax (the staged-producer e2e harness), which had no input to drive.

title: grand_piano: resolve high-frequency board/bridge response before raising the mode cap
description:
The clean b8167f16 renderer has a 1.2 kHz/68-mode soundboard by default. C6's second partial is above that band and its 3-8/8-16 kHz pressure remains weak even with published per-string hammer stiffness. The 2.4 kHz geometry solve finds 174 modes but the runtime correctly refuses above 128. Raising the numeric cap alone is not evidence that the reconstructed flat board and mesh are accurate. Boutillon and Ege's high-frequency inter-rib waveguide regime and measured bridge mobility are the physical targets, not an output EQ.

First establish a mesh- and cutoff-convergence experiment with the existing geometric board, including C4/C6/A4 bridge acceleration and pressure against the 1.2/1.5 kHz controls. Then implement a source-grounded high-band structural/radiation route with a declared capacity and material model. Validate against actual bridge mobility and held-out microphones before considering a default. Current evidence and runnable paths are in MTDT docs/projects/piano-realism/FRANKENSIM_A4_BENCH.md and trj /data/tmp/frankensim-lockconsistent-b8167f16-20260929/.
acceptance_criteria: An admitted current-source path models C6 second-partial and C4/A4 high-band bridge response beyond the 1.2 kHz/68-mode board slice without merely raising MAX_BOARD_MODES. Show mesh/band convergence, passive energy, unclipped PCM, and paired 1.2/1.5 kHz incumbents in the same run; compare bridge mobility and two microphone positions on held-out low/middle/high notes. Keep negative results and source/receiver limits explicit.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-09-29 clean b8167f16 release negative/positive probes: C4 speaking 24th partial ~6.84 kHz; changing 24 to 48 modes at fixed RT-0425 stiffness raises modeled bridge 8-16 kHz ratio from -140.12 to -43.01 dB, but pressure only to -87.12 dB versus lip C4-v8 -66.6 dB. C6 second partial ~2.11 kHz lies above 1200-Hz/68-mode board; stiffness improves 3-8 pressure -52.34 to -49.61 dB versus lip C6-v8 -44.7. A 2400-Hz board band computed 174 modes and correctly refused the 128-mode runtime limit. A full 28-note 48-mode trial worsens 8-16 recorded-reference error by 0.37 dB and costs 1.88x 24-mode runtime, so do not lift budgets blindly or call it a musical win. title: WS2: marquee pipeline on elasticity — compliance topopt on raw SDF, zero remesh
description:
WHY (plan sec 16 P2 exit criterion — THE marquee): topology optimization on a raw SDF with no mesh in the loop, carrying a composed error certificate — currently exists only for heat conduction at a 17-node lattice. WHAT: switch the fs-topopt marquee lane to the CutFEM elasticity kernel: SIMP-style density (or level-set — keep the density path first, it is what the heat lane proves) over the octree-refined cut discretization, compliance objective with volume constraint, Helmholtz filter + Heaviside projection reused from fs-topopt core, DWR-guided refinement between optimization continuation stages, adjoint gradient FD-verified at every continuation stage (the existing heat-lane bar), evidence colors composed through the pipeline (the certificate says WHAT is verified — discretization error bound — and what is estimated — model form; no laundering). ACCEPTANCE: (1) compliance strictly decreases at fixed volume across continuation on the 3-D cantilever-from-SDF fixture; (2) ZERO mesh rebuilds, structurally asserted (the heat lane's existing zero-remesh log assertion pattern); (3) DWR refinement concentrates where the design boundary moves; (4) the thickness/topology witness oracles from the heat lane pass on the result; (5) deterministic golden for the seeded fixture run per golden-bump protocol (both-ISA blessing MANDATORY). TESTS: continuation battery with per-stage JSONL (compliance, volume, gradient-check residual, remesh count), witness audits, golden. DEPENDS on CutFEM elasticity + elasticity DWR.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured `acceptance_criteria` field contains the controlling, complete implementation/contribution, unit, E2E, logging, replay, source-closure, authority, and `NoData` close gate.

title: Make scalar DWR nodal enrichment fail closed instead of zero-filling
description:
Scientific fail-open in crates/fs-dwr/src/estimate.rs: eval_cell and enriched coarse-node interpolation use unwrap_or(0.0) for missing nodal values (currently around lines 73 and 154). On non-nested active CutFEM meshes or topology/key mismatch, absent values are silently converted into a plausible zero field, so DWR indicators/effectivity can look finite instead of refusing. Replace with Result-based fail-closed evaluation, propagate structured CutFemError through goal_value/estimate callers, validate both fine-to-coarse and coarse-to-fine active coverage, and add missing-corner/non-nested regressions. Preserve valid scalar battery outputs and deterministic ordering; no compatibility shim that continues zero filling.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Construct an active scalar DWR hierarchy with one required fine-to-coarse corner value absent, then call the production estimator through an in-scope caller.
2. In the historical zero-fill control, observe a plausible finite estimate produced from unwrap_or(0.0) instead of an evidence refusal.
3. Repeat with the missing value in the coarse-to-fine direction, with non-nested topology, and with a non-finite stored value.
4. Include a legitimate stored 0.0 control to distinguish missing evidence from real zero evidence.
5. The repaired path must return the stable structured CutFemError before publishing an estimate, and every caller must propagate it unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

All existing scope remains normative.

1. Fail-closed semantics
- Both coarse-to-fine and fine-to-coarse scalar nodal evaluation return Result and refuse missing active-node evidence.
- Missing topology keys, absent corners, and non-finite values propagate as structured CutFemError values through eval_cell, goal_value, estimate, and every in-scope caller.
- No path substitutes zero or another plausible scalar for missing or invalid evidence. A legitimate stored 0.0 remains valid and distinguishable from missing evidence. No compatibility shim restores zero filling.

2. Valid-input preservation
- Existing valid nested-hierarchy fixtures retain expected scalar outputs and DWR battery results.
- Repeated identical input has deterministic results, error selection, and diagnostic ordering.
- Node insertion order, active-cell iteration order, and equivalent fine/coarse traversal order do not change results where the contract declares equivalence.

3. Comprehensive focused tests
- Unit tests cover every local missing-corner position, missing node IDs, empty and singleton active sets, topology/key mismatch, non-nested active coverage in both directions, NaN, positive and negative infinity, and legitimate zero nodes.
- Caller tests prove fs-marquee and fs-topopt do not swallow or replace the structured error.
- Boundary tests use bounded fixtures and avoid allocations proportional to uncontrolled sparse identifiers.
- Property/metamorphic tests cover active-node and insertion-order permutation, repeatability, and directionally equivalent hierarchy construction.
- Negative controls or mutants that reintroduce zero fill, validate only one hierarchy direction, accept non-finite values, or swallow Result must fail.

4. End-to-end proof and logging
- Add and maintain scripts/ci/e2e_dwr_fail_closed.sh.
- Exercise a valid nested hierarchy; fine-to-coarse and coarse-to-fine missing-corner cases; non-nested topology; non-finite nodal evidence; and caller propagation.
- Success cases produce the expected deterministic result. Refusals return the expected structured error and cannot publish a partial estimate, certificate, or success receipt.
- Emit bounded deterministic machine-readable logs with source/toolchain/fixture identity, case, direction, bounded cell/node identity, error variant, exit class, commands, and relative artifact paths; never dump full uncontrolled fields.
- If this synchronous path has no cancellation API, record cancellation as typed N/A with the contract reason. Otherwise prove cancellation cannot publish partial authority and drains within the declared bound.
- Repeated and failed runs leave no unbounded temporary state or misleading success receipt.

5. Required verification and no-claim boundary
- Run the complete unfiltered fs-dwr library and battery suites; the planning inventory is 13 library plus 6 battery tests, but closeout records the actual final inventory.
- Run strict all-target Clippy for affected packages, UBS on changed files when available, and dsr quality --tool frankensim. Static review, rustfmt, diff checks, or a filtered slice are hygiene only.
- Preserve exact commands, source revision, result, DSR log, and E2E log paths.
- Closure proves fail-closed nodal evidence handling only; it does not certify DWR effectivity, mesh nesting, convergence order, or arbitrary field correctness. frankensim-ay40 and frankensim-yrbv remain distinct.

title: check_goldens silently reports zero findings when golden-couplings.json is unparseable (line-oriented reader)
notes:
FOUND: GoldSnow 2026-07-25, by causing it. check_goldens (xtask/src/main.rs ~7116-7140) parses golden-couplings.json with a LINE-ORIENTED reader (stripped.split('"'), rest.split([',','}'])) that requires exactly one compact JSON object per line. I reformatted the file with json.dump(indent=2) -- semantically identical, all 128 surfaces and 21 goldens intact and valid JSON -- and every row became unparseable. The checker did not error, did not warn, and did not count a single row: it reported only the 2 violations sourced from the OTHER file (identity-authorities.json) and looked like it had gone from 33 violations to 2. I nearly published that as a 94% improvement. It was the check not running.

CLAIM-INTEGRITY CLASS: a green result that means 'not evaluated' is indistinguishable from 'evaluated and clean'. This is the same defect shape the repo tracks elsewhere (bead 2gs5h: check-identities accepting an EMPTY schema_fingerprint as matching). A gate that cannot tell you it failed to read its own input is not a gate.

REPRO: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('golden-couplings.json'));json.dump(d,open('golden-couplings.json','w'),indent=2)" then cargo run -p xtask -- check-goldens. Observe 2 violations instead of the true count. Restore with git checkout.

FIX: the reader must fail closed. Minimum: after parsing, assert the surface and golden row counts are non-zero and match the number of array entries the file declares; refuse with a violation naming the first unparseable line. Better: parse golden-couplings.json with depgraph::JsonParser like every other registry (schema-policy.json, consolidation-review.json, capability-maturity.json all do) and drop the bespoke line reader entirely -- then formatting stops being load-bearing. If the compact one-row-per-line format is intentionally required for reviewable diffs (it is, and it is worth keeping), enforce THAT explicitly as a format check rather than depending on a parser that silently skips anything else.

DONE WHEN: reformatting the registry produces a loud refusal rather than a passing run; a test seeds an unparseable registry and asserts the check refuses; the compact-format requirement is either enforced or removed as a dependency.
close_reason:
LilacAspen 2026-07-25: landed 0626147e. xtask 354/355 (the one failure is unrelated live-state drift, detailed below).

DONE-WHEN audited:

- "reformatting the registry produces a loud refusal rather than a passing run" - MET. The row counts are now established INDEPENDENTLY of the line reader, by parsing golden-couplings.json with depgraph::JsonParser (the same parser schema-policy.json, consolidation-review.json and capability-maturity.json already use). The line reader counts the rows it actually recognises, and a mismatch in either direction is a violation naming both numbers. A shortfall means rows were skipped in silence; a surplus means the section markers matched something they should not have. Invalid JSON and a non-object root are violations too, rather than falling through to a zero-row pass.
- "a test seeds an unparseable registry and asserts the check refuses" - MET. goldens_refuse_a_reformatted_registry_instead_of_silently_reading_nothing writes the fixture compact first as a POSITIVE CONTROL (must pass clean), then re-indents it the way any JSON tool would, and requires the refusal to name both sections and both counts. A third case writes non-JSON and requires it be named as such.
- "the compact-format requirement is either enforced or removed as a dependency" - ENFORCED, deliberately, rather than removed. GoldSnow's note says the compact one-object-per-line format is intentional and worth keeping because it makes registry diffs reviewable, and I agree. So it stays, but it is now checked instead of silently depended on, and the refusal text says plainly that re-indenting is semantically identical JSON which would otherwise silence the check rather than fail it.

WHY I DID NOT SWITCH THE READER TO JsonParser WHOLESALE, which the bead offers as the "better" option: doing that would make formatting stop mattering, and formatting is supposed to matter here. The reviewable-diff property is a real requirement, and a parser that accepts any formatting silently drops it. Using JsonParser as the AUTHORITY on row counts while keeping the line reader as the thing that must agree with it gets both properties: the format requirement is enforced, and it can no longer be violated invisibly.

comments.text: UPSTREAM DESIGN PREPARED (CloudyFinch) — executable the moment cross-repo authorization arrives (explicitly requested in my session summary; 7n2n precedent). Grounded in asupersync's actual surfaces (src/cx/cx.rs spawn_blocking/spawn_blocking_in, cx/scope.rs Scope{region,budget,capability_budget,pending_spawns}, CatchUnwind + payload_to_string precedents). DESIGN — Cx::scoped_cpu, a closure-based lending CPU scope: (1) SOUNDNESS comes from the std::thread::scope pattern — the API is a FUNCTION that blocks until every child joins, not a guard, so the mem::forget/leak hazard of guard-based scoped tasks cannot arise; borrowed (non-'static) children are sound exactly as in std. (2) NOT A FAKED TREE (the codex-5.6 objection): the wrapper registers a REAL child region through the scope's pending-spawn counter before dispatch (spawn_blocking_in-style admission: region ownership, Budget, CapabilityBudget from the caller's Scope), the calling task parks on the BLOCKING POOL (never an executor thread; deterministic inline fallback when no pool, matching spawn_blocking's None arm), and the region finalizes only after the std scope returns — so region close, cancellation, and budget accounting are all real. (3) API: cx.scoped_cpu(&scope, |s: &ScopedCpu| { s.spawn(|child: &CpuChildCx| { .. borrows OK .. })?; .. }) -> Result<R, ScopedCpuError>; ScopedCpu::spawn enforces the scope's worker/CPU budget at spawn time (structured BudgetExceeded refusal); CpuChildCx exposes checkpoint() -> Result<(), Cancelled> wired to the REGION's cancel signal (request -> children observe at bounded tile boundaries -> drain -> finalize; P7 verbatim) plus remaining-budget peeks. (4) PANIC CONTAINMENT: per-child catch_unwind; first payload recorded via payload_to_string, siblings drained, ScopedCpuError::ChildPanicked{child, message} out; scope reusable after. (5) DETERMINISM: children carry caller-assigned logical ids; nothing about placement or join order is observable in results (G5). CONSUMER PROOF: fs-exec TilePool::run maps 1:1 — workers borrow K/deques/bands/poll (today's Send+'static bound is the whole blocker), CpuChildCx::checkpoint composes with the CancelGate at tile boundaries, and lx0e closes on it. title: fs-ascent second-order adjoints: exact Hessian-vector products (adjoint-of-adjoint) for TR-Newton-Krylov
description: SPLIT from 7tv.3 (the gradient stack landed in crates/fs-ascent: L-BFGS/Wolfe, TR-Newton-Krylov with Steihaug + negative curvature, PHR augmented Lagrangian with KKT certificates, Riemannian L-BFGS, stop algebra; the flagship PDE pipeline fixture runs fs-adjoint IFT gradients through verify_gradient into L-BFGS). THIS bead: EXACT Hessian-vector products for PDE-constrained problems via second-order adjoints (adjoint-of-adjoint / tangent-of-adjoint), replacing the documented-O(sqrt-eps) hv_fd_of_gradients interim in fs-ascent::trust. WHAT EXISTS: fs-adjoint ift_gradient_matfree (first-order IFT machinery + transposed solves), fs-ad second_directional (Dual-of-Dual exact for small dims - the verification oracle), fs-opdsl linearize/jvp/vjp (the operator-level pieces of the second-order chain). DESIGN NOTE: for R(u,p)=0, J(u,p): Hv needs the tangent solve (dR/du)w = -(dR/dp)v, then second-derivative contractions, then one more adjoint solve - four linear solves per Hv, all through fs-solver with shared preconditioners. ACCEPTANCE: Hv vs Dual-of-Dual on small fixtures (exact to solver tol); Hv vs FD-of-gradients (the interim) showing the accuracy gap; TR-Newton on the DensityPoisson misfit with exact Hv converging in fewer outer iterations than with FD Hv (measured); goldens + trj.

Added DensityPoisson::apply_density (K(v)x for arbitrary SIGNED density vectors - the directional operator). EVIDENCE (fs-adjoint battery 9/9 + fs-ascent battery 9/9 BOTH ISAs - trj /data/tmp/fshvp2.6eZgAk, frozen goldens passing on x86_64): SYMMETRY gate v^T H w == w^T H v to 1e-8 (the IFT Hessian of a scalar objective is symmetric - a strong exactness gate); FD-of-gradients agreement at best epsilon <=1e-5 WITH the FD accuracy gap QUANTIFIED across eps 1e-4/1e-6/1e-8 (worst/best ratio >10x - the O(sqrt-eps) claim made visible); TR-NEWTON HEAD-TO-HEAD on the kuhn(3) log-density misfit (positivity by construction - the raw-density fixture measurably wandered into negative indefinite-K territory and stalled, documented; Tikhonov gamma=1e-3 for a unique optimum - the unregularized 162-var/8-data problem made iteration counts trajectory noise, 18-vs-12 one way then reversed, also documented): EXACT Hv certifies at 1e-9 in 3 outer iterations / 43 Hv solves vs FD-Hv 5 iterations / 1625 Hv evaluations - the headline: each FD Hv costs 2 full gradient evaluations = 4 PDE solves, exact Hv costs 4 CG solves TOTAL per product and converges Newton-fast. title: Solve resume self-authenticates caller-mintable stage state
description: The new fs-cli solve resume path derives LegacySnapshotExpectationV1.exact_bytes_id from the same retained bytes it is about to open, then selects artifacts by caller-writable Ledger session/kind labels. It does not re-attest the completed-stage sequence against the named op rows, stage receipt edges, ordinal order, or a previously trusted run root. Any safe caller with the public Ledger and LegacySnapshotV1Adapter APIs can mint a syntactically valid SolveDriverState for a known run, link it from an ok op carrying that session, and cause resume to skip producer stages. The same root boundary appears in find_import_summary, which accepts any ok op output whose caller-supplied kind is geometry-import-run-receipt and whose free-form text contains the project-hash substring. Fix by binding each state to an independently retained predecessor/run-root expectation, validating the complete completed-stage chain and receipt lineages before selecting latest, and parsing/re-attesting import receipts as a strict versioned type rather than kind+substring. Add adversarial public-API regressions that attempt a forged higher-stage state and fake import summary; both must fail before stage execution.

title: fs-airflow QoI: absolute temperatures and temperature differences are emitted as one indistinguishable type
description:
ThermalQoiSet emits five Temperature-typed QoIs. Two are ABSOLUTE temperatures (junction_maximum, uniformity.mean_temperature) and three are temperature DIFFERENCES (uniformity.spread, uniformity.face_mean_standard_deviation, thermal_margin). All five are typed `ThermalQoi<Temperature>`, all five label their budget unit "kelvin", and nothing machine-readable separates the two kinds. A consumer holding the record cannot tell which it has except by the field name.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A STYLE POINT: fs-qty already draws exactly this distinction, deliberately and at depth. `QuantityKind::AbsoluteTemperature` and `QuantityKind::TemperatureDifference` are separate variants (crates/fs-qty/src/semantic.rs:84-86) that share TEMPERATURE_DIMS (semantic.rs:133) but encode distinctly in canonical identity ((1,0,0) vs (2,0,0), semantic.rs:504-505, 562-563) and have DIFFERENT ADMISSIBLE DOMAINS: an AbsoluteTemperature refuses value < 0.0 (semantic.rs:926-932) while a difference may legitimately be negative. The module doc states the purpose outright: 'Dimensions answer whether two values have compatible units. This module answers the separate question of whether they mean the same thing... require named conversions wherever a dimensionally legal operation could hide an affine offset.' The QoI producer is downstream of all of it and uses none of it.

THE SHARP EDGE IS THE MARGIN. A NEGATIVE thermal margin is the single most decision-relevant output the product has -- it means the design misses its requirement. crates/fs-airflow/src/qoi.rs:821-827 computes margin = L_eff - T_max and admits it on a finiteness check alone, so negative margins ARE emitted, correctly. But they are emitted as `Temperature::new(-3.0)` labelled "kelvin", structurally identical to an absolute temperature. A downstream consumer that reads it as absolute either gets refused by fs-qty's own domain guard or, at the render boundary, converts -3 K to -276.15 degC and prints a number that is not wrong by a rounding error but by 273.15. f85xj.6.9 (report rendering) is the first place this can actually bite.

THE ARITHMETIC IS ALREADY CORRECT -- THIS IS A READABILITY GAP. crates/fs-airflow/tests/qoi.rs:1214 (a_common_temperature_offset_leaves_the_margin_invariant) already proves the margin has difference semantics under a common offset, and the absolute QoIs correctly shift. So no value moves. This is the same shape as the ProvenanceClass defect fixed at ead4c2f6: the distinction exists and is respected by the computation, but reaches no machine-readable field, so every test passes while a consumer cannot act on it.

DONE WHEN: every emitted ThermalQoi carries a machine-readable temperature kind (or the typed carrier from fs_qty::semantic); a consumer can separate the two absolute QoIs from the three difference QoIs without matching on field names; a falsifier proves a negative thermal margin round-trips as a difference and is NEVER admissible as an absolute temperature; and the existing offset-invariance test still passes unchanged, proving no value moved.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing any numeric value, the 8-term budget, or the final-envelope audit.

Found while auditing f85xj.5.10's 'equivalent units' test clause, which is separately recorded on that bead as vacuous at this layer.
close_reason:
Fixed at 98356c75. Every ThermalQoi now carries a ThermalQoiKind (AbsoluteTemperature | TemperatureDifference | Pressure | Power); the junction maximum and surface mean are absolute, the spread/face-mean-std/thermal-margin are intervals. The kind is ENFORCED, not merely recorded -- a kind that forbids a negative scalar refuses if one is produced, so a below-absolute-zero junction maximum fails closed. The final-envelope audit demotes evidence but never rewrites a kind.

Every DONE-WHEN clause met: (1) machine-readable kind on each emitted QoI; (2) the two absolute QoIs separate from the three intervals without matching field names; (3) a falsifier proves a negative margin round-trips as an interval while the same scalar is inadmissible as an absolute, plus a positive control proving the below-zero refusal keys on the SIGN and not on the field being constant; (4) a_common_temperature_offset_leaves_the_margin_invariant passes UNCHANGED, which is the proof that no value moved.

fs_qty::semantic::QuantityKind is cited as the authority for the rule but deliberately not reused as the carrier: it has no mechanical-power variant (only AcousticPower) and fan input power is mechanical. Recorded in CONTRACT.md.

Verified: fs-airflow 98 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored on an RCH Linux worker; the qoi battery went 19 -> 22 against a baseline measured on the same worker before the change.

title: WS1: LBM perf lane — GLUP/s rows under sealed roofline admission, both ISAs, thread-scaling
description:
WHY: plan section 14.1 names sparse D3Q19 targets of 1.00 GLUP/s on the M-class family and 0.60 GLUP/s on the Threadripper family, but no citable LBM throughput row exists.

WHAT: add an admitted, release-built production lane following the fs-feec/fs-fft evidence pattern. Measure dense-active 128^3 and deterministic 10-percent-active sparse D3Q19 at single-worker and all-admitted-worker configurations on both reference ISA families. Bind FRANKENSIM_BASELINE_STORE admission, pre/post axes, source/build/host/pin identities, tune rows, exact GLUP/s arithmetic, and an explicit bytes-per-update roofline model covering 19 distribution reads/writes, sparse indexing, and halo traffic.

DECISION: the plan targets are literal TargetAttainment thresholds. Independent anti-collapse floors are fixed before any candidate measurement at 0.80 GLUP/s for M-class and 0.48 GLUP/s for Threadripper-class all-core rows; they are not selected from a first candidate result and cannot be revised after sampling. TargetAttainment and RegressionGate remain separate, so a below-target but above-floor row is retained honestly and does not satisfy the target.

USER/OPERATOR VALUE: retain citable per-host raw rows, thread scaling, roofline fraction, tune selection, failure/no-data reasons, and exact reproduction instead of a vague speed claim. Loaded, throttled, stale, missing, unsupported, or replay-disagreeing evidence cannot Pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `scripts/ci/lbm_perf_e2e.sh --check` against `tests/perf/lbm_d3q19.toml`; then execute the frozen negative cases for candidate-derived floor mutation, invalid work/byte arithmetic, loaded host, missing production route, and replay disagreement. Until the planned script exists, the terminal result is `NoData`, not proof.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured `acceptance_criteria` field is the controlling, complete close gate. This navigation section does not weaken, duplicate, or replace its detailed requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
## Leaf-local verification

Add focused unit tests for happy, empty, minimum/maximum, n-1/n/n+1, malformed, non-finite, overflow, and exact typed-error paths.

Add property or metamorphic tests for every applicable algebraic, dimensional, ordering, containment, scaling, permutation, representation, determinism, and replay invariant.

Exercise at least one authentic public consumer or integration route. Mock-only success cannot close the leaf.

For concurrency or cancellation surfaces, inject requests and faults at every admitted boundary and prove drain/finalize behavior, no leaks, no partial authority, and deterministic retry/replay.

Record the exact focused command and result. These tests prove only this contribution; terminal family authority remains with the named E2E or adjudication Bead.

## Frozen measurement design

Before sampling, freeze an immutable specification containing workload/case IDs; host/ISA and quiet-window qualification; exact warmup/sample/attempt counts; timers/error budgets; baseline/candidate arm equality; timed boundaries; work/byte formulas; exclusions/stopping rules; literal target and non-collapse floors; statistical decision rule.

No threshold, floor, tolerance, exclusion, or stopping choice may be selected from candidate results.

Emit Pass, Fail, NoData, Unqualified separately. Skip/missing route/loaded host/post-hoc exclusion/unavailable capability cannot Pass.

Retain raw paired/interleaved samples and artifact-only replay of arithmetic/policy. Any timing rerun is separate.

## Literal D3Q19 throughput protocol

Freeze tests/perf/lbm_d3q19.toml before sampling. Exact workloads are 128^3 dense-active and a deterministic 10.0-percent-active sparse mask over the same lattice, each at one admitted single-worker and all-admitted-worker configuration on qualified M-class arm64 and Threadripper-class x86_64 hosts. GLUP/s is exactly completed fluid lattice updates divided by timed seconds and 1e9; the manifest freezes distribution read/write, sparse-index, halo, and receipt bytes per update for roofline accounting. Setup, allocation, initialization, validation, and publication are outside the timed sweep but required for validity.

Run 5 untimed warmups followed by 31 retained samples per workload/thread arm in deterministic interleaved order, repeated in 3 separately admitted quiet windows. Timer/calibration error must be below 0.5 percent of the shortest sample and pre/post reference-axis medians within 3 percent. No early stop, post-hoc sample exclusion, size/mask change, candidate-derived floor, or unavailable route counted as pass.

Literal all-core plan targets are 1.00 GLUP/s on the M-class host and 0.60 GLUP/s on the Threadripper-class host. Fixed anti-collapse floors are 0.80 and 0.48 GLUP/s respectively. TargetAttainment and RegressionGate are separate verdicts; meeting a floor never implies target attainment, and an honest below-target row remains retained. Report single-worker/all-worker scaling and roofline fraction without inventing an additional threshold. Loaded/throttled host, debug build, source/fingerprint/pin drift, unequal arms, invalid work count, or replay disagreement is NoData or Unqualified. Retain all raw samples, tune rows, host/admission receipts, byte/work arithmetic, artifacts, and exact reproduction; artifact replay recomputes metrics/policy only.

## Exact performance E2E harness

This Bead owns scripts/ci/lbm_perf_e2e.sh and tests/perf/lbm_d3q19.toml with immutable case set {lbm.dense_128, lbm.sparse_10_percent}. The script implements --list, --check, --self-test, --run CASE, --negative CASE, --fault CASE, and artifact-only --replay RECEIPT --input-root PATH --output-root PATH. --self-test uses bounded synthetic timer/host/receipt fixtures and cannot mint performance evidence; --run uses the release-built real path on an admitted host.

Unit/schema/boundary/property/metamorphic/mutation tests cover parsing, exact case membership, work/timer/sample/statistic arithmetic, admission, verdict separation, caps, redaction, and replay. No-mock E2E covers qualified Pass/Fail, NoData, loaded/throttled/unsupported Unqualified, cancellation/drain, timer/allocator/worker/publication fault, truncation, tamper, stale identity, and clean replay. Bounded redacted deterministic JSONL records source/build/features/host/ISA, manifest/case/attempt/sample/sequence, raw observations with units, warmup/measurement role, admitted and consumed budgets, pre/post axes, exclusions, first divergence, verdict, artifacts, and exact reproduction. DSR proves harness correctness only; admitted retained measurements separately own performance authority.

title: Refuse time-zero access through delayed game-information grants
description:
RE.Q1 admission currently treats StrategyAccessV1::InitialOnly as permitted under ObservationAvailabilityV1::Delayed for any nonnegative lag. An open-loop controller can therefore seal a whole signal using a t=0 value whose grant says it arrives only after a positive delay, admitting an anticipative policy despite the nonanticipativity contract.

Root fix: require delayed grants to be consumed through an explicit delayed access whose lag is at least the grant lag; permit InitialOnly only when the grant lag is exactly zero.

Acceptance: a positive-lag disturbance grant plus an open-loop controller with InitialOnly disturbance dependency refuses with ObservationTimingMismatch; zero-lag InitialOnly and matched delayed access remain admitted; InitialOnly, Current, and History semantics remain unchanged; contract states the boundary; rustfmt and static diff checks pass. Central Cargo/DSR/RCH verification remains batch-pending.
