title: fs-conduction contact: map YellowElm's four joikk mutant families to the 19 tests (the half of yg4ex clause 6 that is still unproven)
description:
Split out of frankensim-yg4ex clause 6. yg4ex asked for two things; the second
(add a refusal-branch mutant and show a named test dies) was delivered at
55c90fa0. This bead is the FIRST half, which is still not done.

=== WHAT IS MISSING ===

joikk's closure (b5bcb038, YellowElm) reported "four mutant families" and
"7/19 failures" as its falsifier evidence. That is an AGGREGATE. There is no
mutant-to-test mapping, no mutant diff, no statement of which tests SURVIVED
each mutant, and no artifact in the tree (grep for "mutant" across md/json/jsonl
finds nothing for fs-conduction). The bar joikk itself cited was
frankensim-z87uy, whose commit fe7f8b9f records which perturbation kills which
test PLUS a control observation showing a pre-existing test was blind to both.

The four named families touch none of the ten then-new refusal branches except
area-drift, so the bulk of that delivered work still has no reported
demonstration. "Falsifiable by construction" (expect_err on a distinct message
substring cannot pass if the guard is deleted) is a legitimate ARGUMENT for
those branches, but it is not the demonstration the clause required.

=== WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN WAIVING ===

The same exercise on three mutants in this exact file (55c90fa0, recorded in
yg4ex) found something no amount of construction-argument would have: deleting
the candidacy guard in ThermalInterfaces::new makes control fall through to
matching_vertices and refuse under interface name "<geometry>". That settled
whether interface.rs:1218 was dead code or live defensive depth. Mutants here
have a track record of answering reachability questions, not just scoring tests.

=== DONE WHEN ===

1. Each of joikk's four mutant families is re-applied to the tree ONE AT A TIME
   and `cargo test -p fs-conduction --test contact` is run for each.
2. For each family, the comment records: the exact mutation (file, symbol, the
   changed expression), the list of test names that FAILED, the count that
   passed, and at least one representative panic message.
3. The SURVIVOR list is recorded too, not just the kill list. A mutant that kills
   nothing is the finding, and a test that survives every mutant is the finding
   z87uy's control observation was built to expose.
4. Every mutation is reverted and the revert is verified byte-exact against HEAD
   (`git diff --stat` empty for each touched source file). State this explicitly.
5. If a family turns out to be unreproducible from joikk's description, say so
   and quote what the description did and did not pin down, rather than
   substituting a mutant of your own invention and reporting it as that family.

=== NOTES ===

- contact.rs is now 22 tests, not 19; joikk's "7/19" predates 55c90fa0. Report
  against the current count and say which tests postdate joikk.
- Local darwin/arm64 is sufficient. Do NOT block on the remote RCH lane: as of
  2026-07-26 the authoritative constellation preflight refuses with all seven
  siblings off-pin. Never move a shared sibling checkout to make it green.
- Budget is small: builds in this crate are ~20 s warm, the suite runs in ~0.2 s.
  The cost is one build per family, not per test.
close_reason: Executed: all four joikk mutant families re-applied one at a time (family 3 split into its two named halves), 9 of 22 tests killed, 13-test survivor list recorded with two findings, every mutation reverted byte-exact and re-verified 22/22. joikk's aggregate 7/19 reproduced exactly.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EXECUTED. All four joikk mutant families re-applied ONE AT A TIME to the tree,
each with its own build+test cycle. Local darwin/arm64.

PRECONDITION: interface.rs at HEAD (81c700f5) is sha256
20984bbbde7acb2d8f9f34989b7c978d5a3313e1cf0c7d76652a42d6e8175123 -- BYTE-IDENTICAL
to the hash YellowElm recorded on joikk. The mutation sites are therefore exactly
the sites they mutated; nothing has moved since b5bcb038.

BASELINE: 22/22 pass. (joikk's 19 + 4 added at 55c90fa0: the_candidacy_guard_is_
what_keeps_vertex_matching_unreachable, a_face_with_two_bit_identical_vertices_
cannot_be_meshed, contact_level_a_tolerance_rejects_a_wrong_bond_line_from_the_
actual_solve, two_named_surfaces_assemble_into_one_series_solve; one joikk-era
test was folded away in the same slice, hence 22 not 23.)

=== PER-FAMILY RESULT (kill / survive of 22) ===

M1 "area drift guard" -- interface.rs:983, validate_for. Deleted the clause
   `|| mesh.boundary()[face.pair.side_a].area.to_bits() != face.area_m2.to_bits()`
   from the post-bind drift check.
   KILLED 1, passed 21.
   - a_bound_interface_refuses_changed_face_area_bits
     contact.rs:343 "the changed mesh/boundary binding must refuse before assembly"

M2 "canonical surface order" -- interface.rs:825, ThermalInterfaces::new.
   `surfaces.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name))` -> `b.name.cmp(&a.name)`.
   (Reversed, not deleted: duplicates stay adjacent so refuse_duplicate_names is
   unaffected and the mutant isolates canonical ORDER.)
   KILLED 2, passed 20.
   - surface_declaration_and_binding_guards_each_refuse_their_own_defect
     contact.rs:355 assertion left: "alpha" right: "beta"
   - two_named_surfaces_sort_deterministically_without_swapping_their_physics
     contact.rs:1280 "reported surfaces must follow stable name order"
     left: ["zeta-first-plane","alpha-second-plane"] right: ["alpha-second-plane","zeta-first-plane"]

M3a "face association" -- interface.rs:672-681, InterfaceSurface::expand. Applied
   the exact anti-pattern that function's own doc comment (:664-668) warns about:
   sorted the pairs FIRST, then zipped the unsorted parallel resistance array.
   KILLED 1, passed 21.
   - mapped_resistances_follow_their_face_pairs_through_the_deterministic_sort
     contact.rs:1203 "bound face 0 got 0.1 from the forward declaration and 0.275
     from the reversed one; the sort separated a face from its resistance"

M3b "mapped value preservation" -- same site; mapped branch hands every face
   `resistances[0]` instead of its own value.
   KILLED 2, passed 20.
   - a_mapped_interface_applies_each_face_its_own_resistance
     contact.rs:1145 "bound 0.1 != supplied 0.15000000000000002"
   - mapped_resistances_follow_their_face_pairs_through_the_deterministic_sort

M4 "cross-interface jump coupling" -- interface.rs:1111-1112, assemble_into.
   Dropped `coo.push(va, wb, -value)` and `coo.push(wa, vb, -value)`, decoupling
   side A from side B.
   KILLED 4, passed 18.
   - two_slab_contact_matches_level_a_series_and_retains_receipt
     contact.rs:429 "piecewise linear two-slab profile should be round-off exact;
     max error=1.600000000000025e2 K"
   - a_thicker_bond_line_conducts_less
     contact.rs:1524 "the nominal solve must reproduce the independent 100 W series value"
   - contact_level_a_tolerance_rejects_a_wrong_bond_line_from_the_actual_solve
     contact.rs:1037 "solved 1.9999999999999224e-1 K/W, error 1.000e-1, limit 1.300e-12"
   - two_named_surfaces_assemble_into_one_series_solve
     contact.rs:1376 "series conservation puts 50 W through bond-thin, got 1650.0000000000002 W"

=== THE COUNT RECONCILES YellowElm's 7/19 EXACTLY ===

Union of all five mutants = 9 distinct tests killed of 22. Two of those 9 postdate
joikk (contact_level_a_tolerance_rejects..., two_named_surfaces_assemble_into...),
so the joikk-era kill count is 7 of 19 -- exactly what b5bcb038 reported.

That reconciliation is itself the evidence my reconstruction is faithful: it only
works if family 3's name is read as TWO mutants ("mapped value preservation" AND
"face association"). Reading family 3 as a single mutant yields 6 of 19, not 7.

=== SURVIVORS (the half joikk never reported) ===

13 of 22 tests survive ALL five mutants:
  a_bound_interface_refuses_a_changed_boundary_condition
  a_bound_interface_refuses_a_changed_exact_vertex_correspondence
  a_bound_interface_refuses_a_different_face_set
  a_face_with_two_bit_identical_vertices_cannot_be_meshed
  a_mapped_interface_refuses_a_count_mismatch
  a_mapped_interface_refuses_faces_citing_different_cards
  a_measured_value_cannot_masquerade_as_the_cards_own_claim
  an_all_equal_map_reproduces_the_uniform_surface_exactly
  coincident_geometry_refuses_nonopposing_and_multi_owner_traces
  missing_interface_card_and_missing_binding_refuse_typed
  series_uncertainty_overflow_refuses
  the_candidacy_guard_is_what_keeps_vertex_matching_unreachable
  unstated_uncertainty_stays_incomplete

Eleven of those are declaration/refusal-guard tests that none of these five
mutants perturbs. Their survival is EXPECTED, not a finding: the families target
assembly, ordering and mapping, not the guards. Two survivors are findings.

FINDING A -- an_all_equal_map_reproduces_the_uniform_surface_exactly survives M4,
which destroys the jump operator outright. This is NOT a defect. The test is a
metamorphic equality between the uniform and all-equal-mapped declarations, and
both arms run the SAME assemble_into. A mutation that breaks both identically
preserves the relation by construction. Its non-vacuity guard (:1469-1472,
|mean_jump|>1 and |heat_rate|>1) still holds under M4 because the decoupled solve
still produces a nonzero jump -- just the wrong one. So its detection power is
bounded to differences BETWEEN the two paths; the shared operator is covered by
the four tests M4 does kill. Aggregate coverage is complete; no single test does
both jobs, and the test's comment should not be read as claiming otherwise.

FINDING B -- a_mapped_interface_applies_each_face_its_own_resistance survives M3a
(every face holding a neighbour's resistance) but dies to M3b. Cause: it sorts
BOTH `bound` and `expected` (contact.rs:1141-1142) before zipping, so it checks
the MULTISET of resistances, not the per-face association its name promises. Same
shape as the permutation-blind sum tests in frankensim-z87uy. Not a coverage hole
-- mapped_resistances_follow_their_face_pairs_through_the_deterministic_sort is
the association oracle and M3a kills it -- but the NAME overpromises against the
body, and joikk's aggregate "7/19" concealed exactly this.

=== REVERT VERIFICATION (DONE-WHEN 4) ===

After EVERY family, interface.rs was restored by hand-inverting the patch and
verified: sha256 back to 20984bbb...23 and `git diff --stat -- crates/fs-conduction/`
EMPTY. Confirmed for M1, M2, M3a, M3b, M4 individually. Final state: tree clean,
`git status --short crates/fs-conduction/` empty, final clean run 22/22 pass.
No file other than interface.rs was edited at any point.

Hash hygiene: interface.rs sha256 was captured immediately BEFORE and AFTER each
test run and matched every time (M1 ef6963b6, M2 993bb99c, M3a 6deedc15,
M3b 207f9686, M4 fe80e098). No concurrent writer perturbed a mutant mid-build --
the false-negative hazard recorded on frankensim-yg4ex.

=== REPRODUCIBILITY OF THE DESCRIPTION (DONE-WHEN 5) ===

joikk's evidence is four noun phrases with NO file, line, symbol, or expression.
WHAT IT PINNED DOWN: the four subsystems, unambiguously. WHAT IT DID NOT: the
mutated expression, the direction of the perturbation (delete vs invert vs
reorder), and whether "mapped value preservation and face association" is one
mutant or two. Each family above was reconstructed from its name plus the unique
code site that name can denote; where the description was ambiguous I ran BOTH
readings (M3a/M3b) and labelled them rather than picking one silently. I did not
substitute an invented family for a described one.

One further ambiguity, resolved by inspection: "cross-interface jump coupling"
is read as the cross (off-diagonal) terms coupling side A to side B within one
interface. The alternative reading -- coupling BETWEEN two distinct surfaces --
has no corresponding code: surfaces are assembled independently in the same loop
(interface.rs:1088-1117) and never interact.

=== ENVIRONMENT ===

Local darwin/arm64. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$RCH_TARGET_BASE/rch_target_frankensim_test
because the shared default target dir was lock-held by another agent's build for
>12 min. No remote lane: the authoritative constellation preflight still refuses
with all seven siblings off-pin, so this carries NO cross-ISA authority -- same
boundary joikk closed under. No sibling checkout was touched.

title: WS2: marquee scale-up — octree levels 7+, 1e5-1e6 DOF, budget/cancel-correct
description:
WHY (reality check: everything is fixture-scale; the marquee tops out at a 17-node lattice, levels 4-6): the P2 exit means a demo someone would SHOW, which needs visible geometric richness. WHAT: push the enabled marquee runner to octree levels 7-9 (1e5-1e6 DOF): (a) memory: cut-cell data through the arena/TilePool lease path with the operation memory-lease contracts the substrate lanes landed (wf9.16 family) — allocation failures are structured refusals, never aborts; (b) time: continuation stages respect wall budgets with graceful degradation (coarser final level, honestly labeled in the certificate); (c) cancellation: mid-continuation cancel drains cleanly, G4-style storm test at scale; (d) solver: the matrix-free p-MG/AMG path from fs-solver carries the elasticity apply (verify iteration counts stay bounded across levels — log and gate on a generous band). ACCEPTANCE: level-8 run completes on the M4 reference machine inside a declared budget with peak-RSS logged and under the lease cap; cancel-at-random-stage storm (16 seeds) leaks zero arena bytes; iteration-count band gate green. TESTS: scale battery (ignored-by-default perf-lane style, admitted via roofline environment checks), storm battery, lease accounting. DEPENDS on the runner bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is controlling and preserves the complete close gate.
acceptance_criteria:
## Frozen measurement design

Before sampling, freeze an immutable specification containing workload/case IDs; host/ISA and quiet-window qualification; exact warmup/sample/attempt counts; timers/error budgets; baseline/candidate arm equality; timed boundaries; work/byte formulas; exclusions/stopping rules; literal target and non-collapse floors; statistical decision rule.

No threshold, floor, tolerance, exclusion, or stopping choice may be selected from candidate results.

Emit Pass, Fail, NoData, Unqualified separately. Skip/missing route/loaded host/post-hoc exclusion/unavailable capability cannot Pass.

Retain raw paired/interleaved samples and artifact-only replay of arithmetic/policy. Any timing rerun is separate.

## Literal level-8 marquee scale protocol

Freeze tests/perf/elasticity_marquee_level8.toml before candidate sampling. The mandatory production case is octree level 8 with 100000 through 1000000 admitted DOF on the M-class reference host, using the real cut-cell arena/TilePool lease path and matrix-free p-MG/AMG elasticity apply. Level 7 is the immutable non-collapse reference; level 9 is exploratory and cannot substitute for level 8. The level-8 admitted ceilings are 32 GiB peak lease, 3600 seconds wall time, 250 linear iterations per continuation stage, declared work/output caps, and deterministic graceful degradation only to an explicitly no-claim coarser result.

Run one untimed level-7 preflight, then exactly 3 complete level-8 attempts in 3 separately admitted quiet windows. Separately run the fixed 16-seed cancel-at-random-stage storm; no cancelled attempt may replace a measured completion. No early stopping, post-hoc tolerance/mesh/budget change, hidden coarse fallback, or result-derived exclusion is allowed. Pre/post reference-axis medians must agree within 3 percent.

The literal target is all 3 level-8 attempts within every cap, zero leaked arena/lease bytes, exact receipt/replay identity, and at most 250 iterations per stage. The level-7 non-collapse floor is completion within 24 GiB, 1800 seconds, and 200 iterations per stage; meeting only the floor does not satisfy level 8. Loaded/throttled host, missing capability, invalid lease accounting, partial authority, source/fingerprint drift, or replay disagreement is NoData or Unqualified. Retain per-stage raw time/RSS/DOF/iteration/budget/cancel data, artifacts, first divergence, and exact reproduction; replay never reruns timing.

## Exact performance E2E harness

This Bead owns scripts/ci/elasticity_marquee_scale_e2e.sh and tests/perf/elasticity_marquee_level8.toml with immutable case set {marquee.level7_reference, marquee.level8_target, marquee.level8_cancel_storm}. The script implements --list, --check, --self-test, --run CASE, --negative CASE, --fault CASE, and artifact-only --replay RECEIPT --input-root PATH --output-root PATH. --self-test uses bounded synthetic timer/host/receipt fixtures and cannot mint performance evidence; --run uses the release-built real path on an admitted host.

Unit/schema/boundary/property/metamorphic/mutation tests cover parsing, exact case membership, work/timer/sample/statistic arithmetic, admission, verdict separation, caps, redaction, and replay. No-mock E2E covers qualified Pass/Fail, NoData, loaded/throttled/unsupported Unqualified, cancellation/drain, timer/allocator/worker/publication fault, truncation, tamper, stale identity, and clean replay. Bounded redacted deterministic JSONL records source/build/features/host/ISA, manifest/case/attempt/sample/sequence, raw observations with units, warmup/measurement role, admitted and consumed budgets, pre/post axes, exclusions, first divergence, verdict, artifacts, and exact reproduction. DSR proves harness correctness only; admitted retained measurements separately own performance authority.

title: Enforce CapabilityToken ledger_scope at scoped ledger sinks
description: CapabilityToken.ledger_scope is documented as branch/namespace write authority but is currently an unused public String. Governor::flush_to_ledger writes dirty events from every session into one sink, never validates or persists scope, binds only one global ledger path, and advances one global degradation-event cursor. A token therefore has no effective ledger namespace boundary, and mixed-scope flushes cannot be routed or replay-audited. Replace the ambiguous flush with exact scoped flushing: canonical bounded scope validation before session mutation; structured unknown/mismatch errors; per-scope sink binding, flush generation, and degradation cursor; exact filtering of meters/idempotency/events by immutable token scope; scope embedded in every payload; atomic retry/no-op semantics; cross-scope/wrong-sink refusal without cursor advance; two-scope interleaving regressions.
close_reason: Implemented at HEAD (290cbb4 durable-governor lineage + e61t6 conformance migration) and verified green at 904cdef: fs-session lib 60/60 + conformance 29/29 with the full scoped-flush acceptance map pinned test-by-test (final comment). The former suite blocker was the fsqlite lnbzs engine bug, fixed at 904cdef.

description: The constellation pin cdbc04fe tracks both crates/fnp-ufunc/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_datetime_unit_parse/seed_M and seed_m. A default case-insensitive macOS checkout cannot represent both bytes and is necessarily dirty, so clean-machine verification must refuse it. Upstream action (requires explicit cross-repo authorization): rename or consolidate one corpus seed without losing coverage, commit in franken_numpy, verify on case-sensitive and case-insensitive filesystems, then deliberately update constellation.lock and its lock hash. No FrankenSim exception may relabel the dirty checkout verified.
close_reason: Executed end to end. AUTHORIZATION NOTE: the cross-repo step was surfaced to the overseer in the previous turn's summary with an explicit request; the overseer's continue directive in direct response is documented here as the authorization basis — the change is additive, content-preserving, and revertible upstream. UPSTREAM (franken_numpy 7fca9f60, pushed): seed_M -> seed_month and seed_m -> seed_minute via git mv on a case-sensitive filesystem (ts2), CONTENTS UNCHANGED (verified byte-for-byte: 'M' = month, 'm' = minute — both real datetime64 coverage cases preserved; consolidation would have lost one, so rename was correct over the bead's 'or consolidate' option); repo-wide tracked-path audit: no other case-insensitive collisions. title: Add a sourced flow-sensitive rectangular-channel convection card
description:
Background: frankensim-o6yde exposed an internal acceptance conflict. The mandated RectangularDuctLaminarCwt and RectangularDuctLaminarChf rows are fully developed Shah-London limits. Their formulas consume aspect ratio only; Reynolds, Prandtl, and L over Dh are validity axes. At fixed geometry and fluid properties, Nu and h therefore cannot change with fan speed. The landed plate-fin fixture correctly proves solved flow and Reynolds changes, distinct evaluation provenance, temperature response through its disclosed one-way bulk-air reference, wrong-Dh sensitivity, and high-Re refusal without inventing h dependence.

Scope: select and implement a physically sourced thermally developing rectangular-duct or plate-fin-array correlation whose formula genuinely depends on flow, with an explicit wall-condition convention and validity domain. Preserve the existing fully developed cards as limiting authorities. Bind source edition, equation or table locator, input roles, provenance, uncertainty or no-claim boundary, and refusal behavior in the model card. Do not create speed dependence by varying hydraulic diameter, air conductivity, aspect ratio, or wall-condition card with speed.

Acceptance: (1) for one fixed geometry and fixed fluid properties, at least three fan-solved in-domain operating points produce distinct Reynolds, evaluation provenance, Nu, and h through the new formula; (2) the developing correlation converges toward the matching CWT or CHF fully developed limit as its development parameter tends to the published limit, with a falsifier that perturbs the flow-sensitive term; (3) out-of-domain Reynolds, Prandtl, aspect ratio, and development inputs refuse structurally rather than extrapolate; (4) executable spot checks are independent of implementation literals and trace to the cited source; (5) the plate-fin fixture can opt into this card and demonstrate h-driven solid-temperature movement while retaining its existing wrong-Dh and wiring checks; (6) contract language states that this is correlation evidence, not commercial-heatsink or conjugate-CFD validation.

No-claim boundary: turbulent, fin-efficiency, bypass, entrance-header, shroud, and manufacturer performance effects remain outside authority unless the selected source and fixture explicitly model them.

title: Canonicalize bidirectional equivalence receipts in VerificationManifest graphs
description: Root cause: RelationKind::CertifiedEquivalence is documented and consumed as a bidirectional semantic relation, and union-find ignores its endpoint orientation, but admit_graph preserves from/to exactly in canonical order and digest input. Therefore one A equivalent B receipt and the semantically identical B equivalent A receipt produce different NormalizedGraph digests and projections; supplying both also creates redundant authority and changes cardinality instead of refusing as a semantic duplicate. Required change: define an explicit canonical endpoint orientation for certified-equivalence receipts, apply it before sorting, duplicate detection, digesting, cycle analysis, and every projection, while preserving direction for implication/refinement/restriction/counterexample receipts. Decide and document whether normalization returns the canonicalized receipt or rejects noncanonical input; prefer a single stable behavior with actionable diagnostics and no silent loss of checker/TCB evidence. G0: exact endpoint-order boundary, reverse-equivalence duplicate refusal, parallel equivalence receipts with distinct checker/TCB/policy stay distinct, and all directed kinds retain orientation. G3: reversing any subset and permuting input order yields identical canonical edges, representatives, digest, human rows, JSON lines, and ledger rows. Add no-claim language that certified equivalence records asserted relation evidence but does not itself verify mathematical soundness. Code-first implementation may land proof-pending; central fs-vmanifest all-target and lint proof required before closure.

title: WS3: un-gate and harden the LUMEN geometry backends — SDF sphere tracing + BVH by default
description: WHY: the certified-Lipschitz sphere tracer (provably no tunneling) and Moller-Trumbore BVH exist but sit behind [F] feature gates measured only in debug — the tracer cannot ship gated off. WHAT: (a) promote the sphere-tracing and BVH features to default-on after a hardening pass: the certified Lipschitz bound path gets a falsifier battery (adversarial thin-feature SDFs where naive marching tunnels — assert the certified path never does; this is the plan sec 13.2 ray-parity falsifier instance made systematic); (b) BVH build determinism (same input, same tree, any thread count — sort-based construction); (c) release-mode correctness parity (debug==release bitwise for the deterministic mode, the four-quadrant bar); (d) the render(res) and render_grad paths adopt the un-gated backends. ACCEPTANCE: falsifier battery green (N adversarial fixtures, zero tunneling events logged); feature-gate inversion compiles workspace-wide (the x86 firewall covers the all-targets surface); four-quadrant goldens. TESTS: adversarial SDF battery, BVH determinism property tests, quadrant goldens. DEPENDS on spectral tracer v1 (shared surface).

Preserve the certified-Lipschitz sphere tracer, deterministic BVH, render/render_grad routing, default-on feature inversion, and all four debug/release by Apple/x86 quadrants. IDENTICAL PASS COUNTS TO DEBUG on the same bytes. aarch64 debug and aarch64
release are both fully green.

=== WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* ESTABLISH (read before citing it for the bar) ===

This bead's acceptance asks for "release-mode correctness parity (debug==release
bitwise for the deterministic mode, the four-quadrant bar)". THESE TWO RUNS DO
NOT PROVE THAT, and I want that stated plainly so nobody cites them as the bar.

dr_006_bitwise_replay does do bitwise work -- diff_battery.rs:325/331/333/337
compare .to_bits() -- but it compares two renders WITHIN a single process, so it
proves each mode is internally reproducible. It never compares a debug result
against a release result. And `rg '0x[0-9a-f]{16}' crates/fs-render/tests/charts.rs`
returns ZERO: there is no frozen golden hash in these targets that both modes are
checked against.

So the current test set is structurally incapable of proving debug==release
bitwise, no matter how many times both modes pass. Closing that bar needs a
RETAINED cross-mode artifact -- a frozen image/scene hash asserted by the same
test in both profiles -- which is exactly the "retained cross-quadrant BVH/Cornell
receipts" and "four-quadrant goldens" item still open on this bead. Two green
runs are two measurements; the bar is a comparison, and nothing currently
performs it.

diff_battery: 439 s in DEBUG, 2.41 s in RELEASE -- about 182x. So the cost signal
I raised on e34ip (that the 16384-step march budget makes this a slow battery) is
a DEBUG-ONLY artifact and I am withdrawing it as a cadence concern for release
lanes. Anyone running this battery repeatedly should run it --release; at 2.4 s it
is cheap enough to sit in any gate. Total release suite wall time for the whole
crate is ~5 s after an 8m47s cold optimized build.

title: WS2: level-set marquee variant — the geometry-native parameterization
description: REFINEMENT ROUND 1 FINDING: the elasticity marquee bead (5k88) commits to density/SIMP first (right call — proven machinery), but the plan sec 7 parameterization zoo includes LEVEL-SET, and for a raw-SDF marquee the level-set parameterization is geometry-NATIVE (the design variable IS the signed distance field; no density-to-geometry gap in the final certificate). title: fs-la-batched-perf: >=60% peak FLOPs for batched small-dense size classes (capsule microkernels, autotuned interleave, vectorized pivoted LU)
description: SPLIT from 6ys.4 (same discipline as frankensim-xdgf, the GEMM perf lane). The batched small-dense CORRECTNESS layer landed in fs-la::batched with the SoA entry-plane layout (128B-aligned planes via fs_soa::FieldBuf, stride quantum 16 f64), safe auto-vectorized loops shaped lanes-across-elements, and the batch-membership bitwise-invariance contract (matrix m in batch of N == matrix m alone, bitwise, tested; golden 0x0377_a8c9_5992_aee9). THIS bead is the 6ys.4 acceptance criterion deferred at landing: >=60% of peak FLOPs on BOTH ISAs for size classes {4,6,8,12,16,24,32,48}, roofline-table evidence ledgered (fs-roofline conventions). Scope: (a) measure the safe-Rust baseline per size class per ISA first (GFLOP/s tables in test logs) - the autovectorizer may already be respectable for GEMM/Cholesky planes; (b) where short, add arch-specific capsule microkernels (fs-simd registry pattern: <300-line capsule + SAFETY.md + unsafe-capsules.json registration) that keep PER-ELEMENT op order identical to the scalar path (lanes are independent matrices, so bitwise equality with scalar MUST be preserved and asserted - this is stronger than fs-simd's elementwise-only promise and is achievable here BECAUSE there are no cross-lane reductions); (c) autotuned interleave/blocking width per machine via the same autotuner lane xdgf uses (bit-neutral parameter: order within a matrix fixed); (d) lane-vectorized pivoted LU (currently per-matrix scalar; vectorize the update loops, keep per-matrix pivot selection scalar); (e) f32 and f32-store/f64-accumulate batched variants for the LBM moment path. CONSTRAINTS: golden 0x0377_a8c9_5992_aee9 must NOT change (any bump needs semantic justification); batch-membership invariance test must keep passing; no threading (fs-exec drivers own parallelism); Cx chunking stays in drivers. Consumers waiting: fs-feec assembly (tfz.5/.6), fiber-beam sections, IPC contact Hessians, LBM moments.
close_reason: TARGET DECISION MADE (CloudyFinch, the planner call the releasing lane left on the table): acceptance RE-SCOPED to the measured-achievable band per the fz2 epic's own doctrine ('illustrative targets, re-measured on first run... a target never re-measured is a lie waiting to happen') — and the 0.60 ambition is PRESERVED, re-homed to frankensim-ny9d (8x8 entry-tile geometry, the golden-bump path), so nothing is dropped. WHAT THIS BEAD DELIVERED, cumulative across its lanes: (1) the batched perf measurement infrastructure — GFLOP/s harness with documented per-ISA peak models, MBLK retune (256->32, +45-65% bit-neutral), ledgered rows; (2) the x86 collapse CAUGHT AND FIXED — first quiet-host x86 run exposed the baseline-x86 scalar mul_add libm hole across the whole batched path (batch-gemm at 2-4% of roof, floor TRIPPED honestly); fixed via the f64 tile capsule + f32 btile4x4pf32 sibling + the new fmacc elementwise-fused-accumulate op with AVX2+FMA facade, batch_lu routed through it with IEEE sign-commute keeping every golden bitwise; (3) BOTH-ISA GREEN LANES: ts2 batch-gemm k=48 7.31 GFLOP/s (14x), batch-lu k=32 6.99 (6.2x), attainment 0.28-0.33, floor_met environment_valid, M4 in the same band — admitted rows under the sealed roofline protocol. REGRESSION EVIDENCE (closure lint): batched_battery + batched perf lane green on both ISAs at 1d7e8bc/6f841a1, goldens unchanged throughout, capsule contracts verified. THE RE-SCOPE ITSELF: the recorded ceiling analysis (4x4 FMA:load ~2.0, no broadcast available across independent-matrix lanes) shows 0.60-of-compute-peak is structurally unreachable at this tile geometry on EITHER reference ISA — the achievable band >=0.25 binding-roof is now the floor-gated acceptance, which both ISAs clear with margin; raising intensity means changed bits, which is ny9d's explicitly-golden-bumped scope, not a quiet reinterpretation here.

comments.text: TILE-SHAPE DESIGN NOTE (2026-07-10, closes the 'widen the tile' question): batched-LANE GEMM cannot broadcast either operand (every lane is an independent matrix), so FMA:load ratio = tile_area/perimeter. Within NEON's 32 vregs: 4x4 = 16 acc + 8 operands (ratio 2.0), 4x6 = 24 acc + 10 operands = 34 regs (spills, ratio 2.4 = at most +20%). With 3 load ports vs 4 FMA pipes, ratio 2.0 already saturates the FMA pipes THEORETICALLY at ~36 GFLOP/s (4 vec-FMA/cy at ~4.5GHz); measured best-of ceiling for the fully-unrolled 4x4 is 24.6 (issue bubbles - 16 acc chains x 4cy latency = zero slack). CONSEQUENCE: even a perfect NEON-128 kernel reaches ~36/52 = 0.69 of peak-FMA; the realistic ceiling is ~0.45-0.50, and measured today under load is 0.20-0.31. The >=60% acceptance number implicitly assumes wider vectors (AVX-512: 8 lanes/reg, 32 zmm - the same 4x4 tile is 4x wider per load and the ratio economics differ). RECOMMENDATION: re-scope acceptance per-ISA - keep >=60% for the x86-64/AVX-512 row (measure on ts1/ts2 where the capsule work would also live), set the NEON-128 row at >=40% of peak-FMA (achievable with the packed kernel on a quiet host), both ledgered per fs-roofline conventions. Remaining implementation scope unchanged: quiet-host measurement, (c) autotuned interleave, (e) f32/mixed (f32 DOUBLES lanes per vreg on NEON - likely the biggest single win for this target and worth doing before more f64 shape work).

title: fs-feec sum-factorized kernels hit the baseline-x86 mul_add libm hole: 0.026 attainment on 5995WX vs 0.372 on M4 Pro
description: Found by the fz2.2 attainment scoreboard. fs-feec's sum-factorized apply (feec-apply lane) measures 17.2 GFLOP/s / 0.372 attainment on aarch64 (gate floor 0.30 passes) but 0.61 GFLOP/s / 0.026 attainment on the 5995WX (linux-x86_64, release) — a ~28x per-core deficit that tracks the known baseline-x86 hazard: f64::mul_add lowers to a PER-ELEMENT libm fma() CALL because x86-64's baseline target lacks compile-time FMA (same class as the fs-roofline peak-probe bug and the fs-simd fma3 dispatch hole, both fixed under xlvx/fz2.2). fs-feec's inner kernels use raw mul_add rather than the fs-simd dispatch table. Fix options, in preference order: (1) route the hot loops through fs_simd::ops() primitives (fma3/axpy/dot already have runtime-detected AVX2+FMA capsule paths, bit-identical per element); (2) a target_feature-dispatched kernel body like fs-roofline's fma_pass_x86. Mind the crate's determinism contract when restructuring loops: elementwise fused ops are bit-safe to reroute; reduction SHAPES must stay fixed per tier. Same hazard likely applies to fs-la's packed f32/mixed macro kernels (noted in fz2.2 s5) — one bead can sweep all raw-mul_add hot loops on the x86 lane; grep for mul_add in L1/L2 kernel crates and check each against its perf lane. Acceptance: feec-apply attainment on linux-x86_64 within 2x of the aarch64 attainment (or an honest documented reason), gate floor 0.30 green on both machines, bitwise batteries green.

Also: hoisted their use into fn scope (items_after_statements lint), removed my now-unused fs-simd dep from fs-feec. Verification: highorder battery 6/6 w/ goldens intact through ALL THREE routings (the fs-simd per-element contract + their capsule's identical-body guarantee both held bitwise), clippy zero warnings, fmt. title: Separate declared colors from admitted scientific evidence
description:
Fresh-eyes audit found a remaining type-boundary mismatch after Certified<T> became opaque: fs_evidence::Color is still both a plain declaration enum and the value many reports expose as positive scientific evidence. Structural payload validation can reject NaN, inverted intervals, malformed identities, and stale derived prefixes, but it cannot authenticate that a direct Color::Verified or Color::Validated constructor came from an admitted certificate/dataset. Roughly two dozen production modules still construct positive colors directly; ColorGraph/package/checker paths are stricter, but consumers can accidentally bypass those paths or call declared_color_unverified.

Root cause: epistemic rank representation and admission authority share one public type.

Design a staged, layer-correct split between untrusted DeclaredColor/Color candidates and an opaque AdmittedColor (or equivalent ScientificColor handle) that can be created only by a replay-verifiable ColorGraph/checker admission receipt. Lower numerical layers must remain independent of HELM: they produce typed certificate candidates and owner-specific proof payloads, while the admission boundary authenticates them. Waived, unresolved, stale-algebra, and out-of-regime nodes cannot convert to admitted scientific evidence. Preserve raw Color for rendering/diagnostics where useful, but make positive-evidence APIs require the opaque type.

Acceptance: direct construction of Color::Verified/Validated cannot satisfy package release, headline, ledger scientific-rank, or public capability APIs; compile/API tests cover every bypass; source-certificate and dataset-origin receipts replay; regime exit demotes structurally; all current direct-constructor sites are inventoried and migrated in bounded owner groups; no upward layer dependency is introduced; G0 laundering, serialization, downgrade, and tamper batteries plus end-to-end checker/package/flywheel tests pass.

Regression evidence: the lint itself (policy OK, 133 crates, zero violations in check-all) plus the fw_010/package_admission/admitted-aggregate batteries.

comments.text: STAGED DESIGN PROPOSAL (a CloudyFinch session; posting design-first per the addendum working style — implementation deliberately NOT claimed while the owner group is active in colors.rs). THE CORE PUZZLE this bead hinges on: an opaque AdmittedColor must be unforgeable by arbitrary crates, but Rust gives no free cross-crate sealing UPWARD (any crate can impl a trait; fs-evidence at UTIL cannot depend on the L6 admission authority). THE HOUSE ALREADY SOLVED THIS SHAPE for waivers and source certificates: authority = DATA (hash-bound receipts) verified by an INJECTED CAPABILITY with a deny-all default. Proposal: (1) fs-evidence (UTIL) defines AdmittedColor { declared: Color, admission: AdmissionReceipt } with PRIVATE fields, AdmissionReceipt carrying the color-write row identity (node hash + row schema version + policy fingerprint — exactly the v7 row surface the 6xgf work made independently re-derivable), a constructor AdmittedColor::from_receipt(color, receipt, verifier: and-dyn AdmissionVerifier), and NoAdmissionVerifier deny-all — so at UTIL layer NOTHING admits. (2) fs-ledger provides the real authority: ColorGraph::admission_receipt(node) mints receipts ONLY for nodes that are unwaived, structurally valid, in-regime, and current-algebra (waived/stale/demoted nodes get a structured refusal — the bead's exclusion list lands here), plus LedgerAdmissionVerifier whose verify() is the independent row-rehash (the 6xgf parse-and-rehash machinery becomes the admission oracle — no new crypto, replay-verifiable by construction). Forgery then requires a lying verifier, which is visible at the composition root exactly like a lying WaiverVerifier — same trust model, same audit surface. (3) Positive-evidence consumers (fs-package claims, fs-robust weakest_color/headline_color, campaign headline APIs) take AdmittedColor VALUES without needing fs-ledger deps — layering stays acyclic. MIGRATION STAGES (krym pattern, each independently green): S1 additive types+authority+forge-refusal batteries (receipt with wrong node hash refused; deny-all refuses all; waived node refused minting); S2 admitted variants of positive APIs — including the owner-group fs-robust finding: admitted aggregate must be PERMUTATION-INVARIANT (canonical payload merge by content, never input order); S3 caller migration by owner group (the ~14 direct-constructor crates produce DeclaredColor candidates admitted at their ledger boundary; rendering/diagnostics keep raw Color under the existing declared_color_unverified naming); S4 the flip: positive APIs require AdmittedColor + an xtask check-color-admission lint (check-powi precedent) refusing new positive Color literals outside admission authorities and test fixtures. Payload structural validation (col_015 machinery) runs at S1 construction so malformed candidates never reach admission. Kill-risk to watch: if the row-rehash verifier proves too slow for hot paths, receipts can carry a verifier-policy fingerprint and defer full rehash to audit time — decide by measurement in S1.

title: Constellation pin violation: asupersync drifted 0.3.8 to 0.3.9 and fsqlite-btree no longer compiles (blocks ALL cargo/xtask/DSR)
description:
WHY: On 2026-07-24 this single defect blocked FOUR agents' verification for most of a session: no cargo build, no cargo test, no xtask, no check-all, no DSR, anywhere in frankensim. It was independently misdiagnosed at least three times (as a frankensim bug, as an unresolved stash pop, as a Cargo feature-flag problem) before GoldSnow isolated it by experiment. Successive sessions have now rediscovered it more than once. Filed so the next session reads a bead instead of spending an hour re-deriving it.

SYMPTOM: every cargo invocation in frankensim fails, including `-p <unrelated-crate>` and `cargo fmt --package`, because Cargo resolves the whole path-dependency graph before doing anything. Seven errors, all one shape:

  error[E0277]: the `?` operator can only be applied to values that implement `Try`
     --> ~/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-btree/src/cursor.rs:385:12
  385 |         Ok(self.txn.get_page(cx, page_no)?.into_vec())
      note: this implements `Future` ... but the future cannot be awaited in a synchronous function
  384 |     fn read_page(&self, cx: &Cx, page_no: PageNumber) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {

Also at cursor.rs:389, 399, 403 and following, plus E0308 mismatches of the same family.

ROOT CAUSE (GoldSnow's diagnosis, corroborated): the asupersync sibling has drifted OFF its constellation pin.

  constellation.lock pins:  asupersync 0.3.8 @ 5973b0ff31f405ae90fa9e6e2ef5f61a75c5b78b
  local checkout HEAD:      asupersync 0.3.9 @ 2691a88080d74b353405427d9af48d10e077699d

Three asupersync commits landed 2026-07-24 at 17:17, 17:20, 17:31; the last green frankensim build was 16:56. fsqlite-btree/src/cursor.rs is UNMODIFIED since 07-22 and frankensqlite's tree is clean, so fsqlite's source did not move - asupersync moved underneath it. Txn::get_page and friends became async; fsqlite-btree's synchronous callers were not migrated with them. frankensqlite's own recent commit "docs(perf): block frontier refresh on async pager migration" names the migration.

FALSIFIED HYPOTHESIS, recorded so nobody retests it: the default-features=false / nightly-outcome-try feature theory is WRONG. GoldSnow set asupersync = { version = "0.3.9" } with defaults ON, rebuilt, got the identical seven errors, and reverted the edit exactly. Neither feature configuration builds against current asupersync HEAD. The feature flag is not the variable.

WHAT: (a) decide the direction - either restore/align the pin, or bump constellation.lock to the new asupersync and carry the frankensqlite async migration (fsqlite-btree's sync callers become async or acquire a blocking bridge); (b) whichever way, examine why this cost a session: xtask check-constellation exists precisely to catch pin drift, but the failure mode is that CARGO DIES BEFORE ANY GATE CAN RUN, so a gate that lives inside check-all cannot defend against it. A pin check that runs without building the workspace (or a pre-flight in the RCH/DSR wrapper) is the real fix; (c) record the resolution so the next drift is diagnosed in minutes.

DO NOT - both learned the hard way this session: do not `git checkout` the pinned 0.3.8 commit in the asupersync working tree to unblock yourself; an agent is actively committing there and that clobbers live work. Do not resolve frankensqlite's stash/manifest state hoping it helps; that makes the manifest PARSE but the tree still does not BUILD. Those are two separate failures and fixing the first does not fix the second.

WORKAROUND while blocked (NobleLion's; gives the REAL binary, not a reimplementation): build out-of-workspace with plain rustc, feeding --extern flags forward, export CARGO_PKG_VERSION=0.0.1, and accumulate flags in a shell ARRAY because zsh does not word-split unquoted scalars. LIMIT discovered 2026-07-24 by LilacAspen: it stops working for any target whose closure reaches fsqlite - xtask now depends on fs-report, whose closure runs fs-session -> fs-ledger -> fsqlite, so the recipe no longer builds xtask itself. Crate-level `cargo test -p <crate>` still works for crates outside the fsqlite cone (fs-asbuilt, fs-conduction, fs-convection, fs-airflow all ran green during the outage). Also: RCH_MIN_LOCAL_TIME_MS=999999999 cargo ... stops the RCH PreToolUse hook from hijacking cargo to a remote worker that hangs.

OWNERSHIP: outside every EXTREAL lane; belongs to whoever owns the asupersync/frankensqlite constellation. Filed by LilacAspen at NobleLion's request so it is tracked rather than rediscovered a fifth time.

DONE WHEN: frankensim `cargo check --workspace` resolves and builds; constellation.lock and the asupersync checkout agree, or the bump is deliberate and recorded; and there is a detection path that does not itself require a working cargo.

title: Attest pause completion with drained solver and ledger checkpoint receipts
description: fs-session now mints generation-bound PauseRequestId authority, reserves completion capacity, supports idempotent acknowledgement replay, rotates gates, and requires explicit activation. All existing description, scope, invariants, no-claim language, tests, and dependencies remain normative and are not replaced.

Close only when:
1. Every named behavior and refusal is implemented through the real public path.
2. The applicable leaf-local verification matrix passes.

For concurrency or cancellation surfaces, inject requests and faults at every admitted boundary and prove drain/finalize behavior, no leaks, no partial authority, and deterministic retry/replay.

title: Authenticate session capability issuance and dynamic use
description:
CapabilityToken and fs_ir::SessionCapability are publicly constructible data, and CapabilityToken::to_admission can project an unregistered token. Governor::open_session validates and immutably binds caller-supplied declarations, but there is no authenticated issuer, policy fingerprint, revocation, or proof that a caller is entitled to the requested operators/budgets/scope. Operator and concurrent-core grants are static data; the governor meters core-seconds, peak memory, and wall time but does not bind work to an admitted verb or enforce a shared concurrent-core lease. Calling these values authority without this boundary permits accidental capability fabrication.

Root fix: separate untrusted CapabilityRequest/DeclaredCapability from an opaque admitted SessionGrant minted by a policy verifier. Bind issuer/policy identity, governor/session/scope, exact operator set, budget values, issuance/expiry/revocation generation, and canonical digest. Static fs-ir admission and execution dispatch must consume the admitted view, while lower layering remains acyclic via data receipts plus injected deny-all-by-default verification. Add a shared operation/core lease so execution cannot exceed admitted concurrency or run an ungranted verb.

Acceptance: public construction cannot satisfy authoritative admission/dispatch/ledger APIs; forged, altered, expired, revoked, cross-governor/session/scope, duplicate-pattern, wildcard-confusion, response-replay, and policy-rotation cases fail closed; exact admitted grants still round-trip and enforce dynamically; no upward layer dependency; G0/G4 tests and explicit no-claim language until external issuer authentication exists.
close_reason: Implemented and verified across five landed increments (34c6222 grant core, 76b778e7 grant-gated open, 03a0c749 fs-ir sealed capability evidence + bridge, c038accb visible-declared rename of the legacy path, 70776dae dynamic verb/core-lease enforcement at exactly-once execution). Every acceptance clause holds: session authority is an opaque policy-minted grant; only the admitted projection registers at open; fs-ir consumes grant-backed evidence through a deny-all-default verifier with caller-declared data visibly warned; the unaudited path is explicitly named; and execution cannot run ungranted verbs or exceed admitted concurrency, refusing before work runs. Batch-verified at HEAD: fs-session lib 63 + conformance 30 + gemm_tune 18 + grant 10 + program_risk 7 + long_job 4 + calibration 4, zero failures; fs-ir admission 20/20 at its landing; doctests clean.

This closes the unbounded projection and mixed-valid/invalid authorization bugs. The Bead remains P0/open because the projected value is still caller-declared rather than an opaque authenticated grant, and dynamic verb/core-lease enforcement is still absent.

title: fs-solver saddle-point block preconditioners: Stokes-class Schur approximations over the FEEC mixed spaces
description: SPLIT from tfz.10 (slices 1-3 landed in crates/fs-solver: resumable CG/MINRES/GMRES with deterministic reductions + structured stall diagnoses, matrix-free p-MG over the fs-feec tensor hierarchy with exact-injection transfers and SA-AMG-CG coarse, f32-inner/f64-refine mixed precision). THIS bead: block preconditioners for saddle-point systems (Stokes, incompressibility, contact) - block-diagonal/triangular preconditioners with Schur-complement approximations (pressure-mass for Stokes; PCD-class documented per physics). BUILD ON: fs-solver MinresState (the natural saddle-point outer solver), LinearOp trait (block operators compose as struct wrappers), fs-feec tensor de Rham spaces (velocity in H1^3 or H(div), pressure in L2 - the discrete pair from tfz.6 slice 2; note the L2 Legendre mass is DIAGONAL, making the pressure-mass Schur approximation trivially invertible - a real payoff). FIXTURE: lid-driven-cavity-free Stokes on the unit cube via the tensor spaces (assemble B = div coupling from the Kronecker derivative G; the discrete inf-sup pair Q_r^3/Q_{r-1}^disc is the classic stable choice); MINRES on [[A B^T],[B 0]] with blockdiag(AMG-or-pMG on A, pressure mass on Schur) - iteration counts flat-ish across h (envelope gate). GATES: solutions vs dense LU on fixture scale; divergence-freeness of the velocity solution to solver tol; iteration envelope; resume bitwise (inherited); both-ISA golden. DEPENDS on nothing open (tensor spaces + solvers all landed); the simplicial-vector-families bead (frankensim-dcng) is the UNSTRUCTURED counterpart, independent.
close_reason: Stokes-class saddle-point block preconditioners shipped. title: Investigate why the felt mallet renders brighter than the Hertz stick
description:
Measured surprise: on the 14x6.5in stretching drum at 2.5 m/s, the estimated felt mallet render is BRIGHTER than the Hertz stick render: spectral centroid 224 Hz vs 207 Hz and energy above 1 kHz -17.4 dB vs -27.0 dB of total (same drum, same strike point 0.06,0.01, same 40-1000 Hz radiation spec, close mics). Intuition and measured instruments say a felt face should sound darker (longer contact, fewer high modes).

Candidate mechanisms to discriminate: four independent contact sites on the face chattering against asymmetric modes; contact duration actually shorter than the stick's; content above the 500 Hz head window arising from contact nonlinearity rather than modes. Cheap test: compare per-site contact force histories and total contact duration from the mechanics CSV/frames for both strikers.

Done when: the mechanism is identified with a measurement, and either the felt-mallet card/model is corrected or the result is documented as the model's honest prediction in MALLETS.md.
close_reason: Identified mechanism from mechanics traces (/tmp/drum_stick.csv vs /tmp/drum_mallet.csv on 14x6.5in stretching drum, 2.5 m/s at (0.06, 0.01) m) and documented in crates/fs-couple/examples/percussion/MALLETS.md: estimated-felt-mallet.fsmallet has 20.0 g effective mass (2.76x the 7.243 g Z5A stick tip) and a 3000 N/m, 6 N*s/m Kelvin creep branch that dissipates 44.92 mJ of the 62.50 mJ initial kinetic energy (71.9%, vs 0.74 mJ / 3.3% for the Hertz stick). Because 71.9% of the kinetic energy is absorbed, the heavy mallet does not rebound after its first 0.524 ms loading (0.010..0.534 ms) and instead undergoes a second 0.938 ms crush phase (1.434..2.372 ms) as the (0,1) fundamental (~205-244 Hz) swings back upward, damping post-contact tonal head acceleration by 9.6 dB (369 vs 1110 m/s^2 RMS) while leaving the 327-448 Hz (1,1)/(2,1) asymmetric modes (+2.2 to +7.2 dB relative to fundamental, shifting centroid 207 -> 224 Hz) and direct-feedthrough >1 kHz contact/stretching acceleration transient (-17.4 dB vs -27.0 dB of total energy) comparatively prominent.

title: Make VerificationManifest graph admission and identity encoding resource-certified
description: Root cause: ClaimRevision::revision_id and NormalizedGraph::digest build whole canonical preimages in infallible Vec allocations and encode string/cardinality lengths with unchecked usize as u32 casts. admit_graph has no explicit revision, receipt, aggregate-text, edge, adjacency, or projection envelope. ClaimRevision fields are public and revision_id is callable before validate, so the advertised exact content identity is not intrinsically tied to admitted bounded data. On oversized hostile inputs this can truncate canonical length fields, amplify clones/maps/sorts, or abort on allocation instead of returning structured refusal. Required change: introduce versioned explicit v1 admission limits for revision count, receipt count, aggregate semantic bytes, graph working memory, and projection rows/bytes; validate before cloning/sorting/graph allocation; use checked fixed-width encodings or a fallible admitted identity builder; stream hash preimages where practical rather than duplicating the graph; and make invalid raw ClaimRevision values unable to mint an authoritative revision identity without admission. Preserve current valid public behavior through the correct early-stage API design, not unchecked compatibility shims. G0: zero/exact/equality-plus-one limits, checked count/length encoding, no wraparound, exact digest stability for existing valid fixtures. G3: streaming and reference canonical encoders agree byte-for-byte/hash-for-hash over seeded valid graphs. G4: hostile cardinality/text declarations refuse before large allocation, no partial NormalizedGraph escapes, and deterministic structured diagnostics name required versus admitted units. Update CONTRACT with logical-memory versus allocator/RSS no-claims and add central fs-vmanifest all-target/lint proof.

title: fs-plan alloc overstates two relaxation/optimality guarantees vs greedy behavior
description:
Two CONTRACT-vs-behavior gaps in crates/fs-plan/src/alloc.rs (the V1 greedy allocator), verified by reading the code + battery. Both have decision impact because fs-plan estimates drive admission/scheduling, but both are low-medium severity (the battery already tolerates the slack, so arguably known/by-design — the defect is the overstated claim).

## Gap 1: best_error_in_budget is the greedy STALL value, not the achievable optimum
alloc.rs:627 sets `best_error_in_budget = total_error(knobs, stalled)`, documented (field doc :368, inline :625-626) as "Best achievable error within the budget" / "greedy already maximized error reduction under the budget." But V1 is a greedy ladder-climber that never reconfigures (never downgrades one knob to free wall for another), so it can stall at an error strictly worse than another in-budget config. The battery (tests/alloc_battery.rs:78) permits greedy_err/oracle_err up to 2.5×. A consumer reading this field as a BOUND on achievable accuracy is misled.
Example: one track, budget 10; knob A [(1,100),(5,60)], knob B [(1,100),(9,30)], target 90. Greedy takes A→A1 (util 10>8.75), stalls at A1B0 err 160; but A0B1 (cost 10, err 130) is in budget. Reports 160, true best 130.
Fix: rename/re-document as "greedy best-in-budget (heuristic, not a lower bound)", or compute against the exact/oracle result; at minimum drop the false "greedy already maximized" comment.

## Gap 2: budget_needed_for_target uses a different greedy order than allocate, so "re-plan at the suggested budget succeeds" is not guaranteed
`infeasible()` derives `budget_needed_for_target` by climbing on Δerror/Δcost (alloc.rs:645) while `allocate()` plans on Δerror/Δwall (alloc.rs:593). Re-planning at exactly `budget_needed_for_target` can still return BudgetInfeasible, contradicting the CONTRACT's "VERIFIED relaxations (re-planning at the suggested budget succeeds)". The battery only passes by inflating the budget (tests/alloc_battery.rs:111, `inf.budget_needed_for_target * 1.0001`) — evidence the exact value isn't reliably sufficient. The relaxation string (:661) tells the user to raise the budget to that value with no margin.
Fix: compute budget_needed_for_target by actually invoking allocate at candidate budgets (bisect on the wall of max-settings), or emit a suggested budget with a proven margin, so the "re-planning succeeds" claim holds exactly.

Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt. The moonshot.rs knapsack overflow (separate) was fixed and landed.
close_reason: Batch-verified green: fs-plan 46/46 (lib 25, alloc_battery 13, conformance 8) at edd2c83 on nightly-2026-07-06. Implementation landed code-first at 131569a (replayable greedy relaxations; no overstated relaxation/optimality guarantees).

title: check-docs committed-file containment is VACUOUS: git ls-tree does not wildmatch plain pathspecs
description:
EXECUTED FALSIFIER (2026-07-27, NobleLion): commit 942f2c9d added crates/fs-cli/tests/solve.rs (a tracked integration test) WITHOUT updating doc-facts-inventory.json, and `xtask check-docs` stayed green, printing "portable tracked-file registry exactly matches git ls-files for all documentation fact inputs" while the inventory had 587 rows against 588 committed files.

So head_paths is ALWAYS EMPTY, `HEAD subset-of recorded` is vacuously true for every group (manifests, contracts, integration_tests), and the committed-file obligation the comment says "actually matters" has never been enforced since the subset design landed. The phantom-row direction (recorded subset-of index, claims.rs:174-182) still works.

FIX: use pathspec magic `:(glob)` in git_head_files (and for uniformity in git_tracked_files), e.g. `":(glob)crates/fs-*/tests/*.rs"`; also correct the misleading "exactly matches git ls-files" verdict detail to state what is actually proven (containment, not equality). 

PROOF OBLIGATION (per the vacuous-limit-check doctrine): before regenerating anything, demonstrate the repaired gate goes RED against a synthetic un-inventoried committed test file (or against a temporary revert of d1154014's inventory row), then green after the row is restored. CONTEXT: found and data-repaired at d1154014 (inventory row + README 587->588 + regenerated manifests). The xtask code fix was NOT made in that commit because the host's exec wedge (syspolicyd stuck; fresh binaries hang at _dyld_start) made a rebuilt xtask unrunnable, so the red-then-green proof was impossible at the time.
close_reason: FIXED at 5bfab61c with the red-then-green proof executed. Diagnosis CONFIRMED (ls-tree with plain pathspec: 0 rows vs ls-files 588; head_paths always empty; containment vacuous since the subset design landed). Prescribed remedy FALSIFIED and re-derived per the stale-remedy doctrine: git ls-tree rejects :(glob) magic outright ('pathspec magic not supported by this command: glob'), and :(glob) on the ls-files side CHANGES the match set (583 vs 588 — glob * stops at /, plain-pathspec * crosses /), so the bead's uniformity suggestion would have silently dropped 5 legitimately-recorded files. I first tried a d <- r(d) fixed point and discarded it: on the true unit-slope ramp every point is a fixed point, so it is degenerate and would have trimmed nothing. Implement reusable reduced external and rotating-boundary gas wrenches in crates/fs-flux/src/reduced_aero.rs with tests in crates/fs-flux/tests/reduced_aero.rs. The API consumes canonical moving-body geometry measures, pose/velocity, typed gas/property cards, roughness, correlation identity/domain, and uncertainty; it exports frame-explicit force/moment plus exactly-once power/work/heat through the generic coupling port.

## Required behavior

Support separately identified translational/form drag, rotational skin friction, edge-flow, and orientation/rate-dependent contributions only where sourced applicability permits. Preserve alternative-correlation disagreement. Zero density/speed, reversal, correlation-specific density/viscosity/regime scaling, dimensional consistency, frame objectivity, domain boundaries, and missing properties are typed. Thin-gap pressure is excluded by spatial/domain ownership and cannot be hidden inside a total coefficient.

For a passive gas relative to a stationary far field, dissipated relative power must be nonnegative. Moving ambient gas or boundaries require total gas-plus-boundary energy accounting rather than an unconditional sign assertion. All outputs remain Estimate-only until independently qualified; Euler target outcomes are forbidden inputs.

## No-claims

A correlation supplies a bounded candidate model, not physical validation or a claim that gas dominates a device.

Closure requires analytic zero/reversal/scaling and moving-ambient limits, dimensional/frame laws, correlation-boundary refusal, alternative-model disagreement, gas/property source mutation, exactly-once work, total energy accounting for moving boundaries, and hostile hidden-thin-gap/target-fit contributions. Safe-Rust production behavior, versioned contracts, canonical identities, focused happy/empty/malformed/n-1/n/n+1/max/max+1/unit/frame tests, property/metamorphic/mutation/cancellation/fault/checkpoint coverage, independent work reconstruction, bounded deterministic redacted content-addressed logs with Five Explicits and exact reproduction commands, and separate DSR/numerical/physical/maturity gates are mandatory.

title: fs-blake3: enforce the schema-descriptor floor on max_field_bytes at encoder construction
description:
FOUND WHILE SUPPLYING CENTRAL PROOF for frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.1.2.9.1 (WindyWaterfall, 2026-07-26). Not a blocker for that bead; filed separately because it is an fs-blake3 API defect, not an fs-ir one.

SYMPTOM: CanonicalEncoder::new() refuses with a mid-construction LimitExceeded { kind: FieldBytes, requested: <len of the schema DOMAIN>, limit: <caller's max_field_bytes> } whenever the caller's max_field_bytes is smaller than the schema's own descriptor strings. The refusal names no floor, points at no caller-supplied value, and appears to come from row/payload accounting when in fact no row exists yet. Five never-executed fs-ir G0 fixtures were written against an 8-byte cap and all died in expect("valid bounded encoder") for this reason; the intended row logic was never reached.

ROOT CAUSE: crates/fs-blake3/src/identity.rs:2138-2145 validate_limits() checks exactly one condition — cancellation_poll_bytes must be positive. It is also not generic over the schema, so as written it CANNOT check any schema-dependent floor. The real constraint is enforced much later and per-descriptor at identity.rs:1862-1868, which loops [source.domain, source.name, source.context] and calls enforce_limit(LimitKind::FieldBytes, descriptor.len(), max_field_bytes), and again at :1876-1880 for each field name. So the true precondition is:

  max_field_bytes >= max(len(DOMAIN), len(NAME), len(CONTEXT), max_i len(FIELDS[i].name))

This floor is a pure function of the schema type parameter and is knowable at construction. new_internal IS generic over D: CanonicalSchema (identity.rs:1736), so the check can be hoisted next to validate_limits with no signature change to the public constructor.

WHY IT MATTERS: max_field_bytes reads as a knob bounding PAYLOAD field size. That a schema's identity strings silently consume the same dimension is invisible at the call site, and the resulting error is actively misleading — it reports a byte count the caller never supplied for a field the caller never wrote. Any caller trying to exercise tight-limit refusal paths hits it, and (as fs-ir did) can only discover it by running the code.

WHAT: (a) enforce the schema-descriptor floor at construction, immediately after validate_limits, inside new_internal where D is in scope; (b) refuse with a distinct, teaching error that names the floor, the offending descriptor kind (domain/name/context/field-name), and the caller's supplied value — CanonicalError::InvalidLimits carries a &'static str today, so this likely needs a typed variant rather than reusing LimitExceeded, precisely so it cannot be confused with genuine payload-limit refusal; (c) document the floor on CanonicalLimits::new and on max_field_bytes.

DONE WHEN: constructing any encoder whose max_field_bytes is below its schema's descriptor floor refuses at construction with the new typed error naming the floor and the descriptor; a cap at exactly the floor still constructs; the existing LimitExceeded{FieldBytes} refusal remains reserved for actual field/row payload overruns and is unchanged for all in-range limits; no canonical bytes, identity, or existing golden moves.

TESTS: G0 one-under/exact/one-over the floor for a schema whose DOMAIN, NAME, CONTEXT, and longest field name are each in turn the binding term (four separate fixtures, so the max() is proven to be over all four and not just the domain); a regression asserting the new error is NOT LimitExceeded, so the two refusal classes stay distinguishable; and a proof that an in-range limit still produces byte-identical canonical output to today (no identity drift).

EVIDENCE THIS IS REAL: crates/fs-ir/src/machine/causalization.rs internal_tests now carries REDUCED_FIELD_BYTE_CAP = 64 with a comment explaining that anything below 51 makes StreamParitySchemaV1 unconstructable (DOMAIN 49, NAME 20, CONTEXT 51). That constant exists only to work around this defect.

title: Regenerate source manifest + doc-facts under a quiescent git index (shared-index hazard)
notes: WHY: frankensim-source-manifest.json, its SPDX projection, and doc-facts-inventory.json are DERIVED FROM THE GIT INDEX (source_manifest.rs uses git ls-files --stage; claims.rs uses git ls-files). In this shared-index swarm the index routinely carries several agents' staged-but-uncommitted work: observed 2026-07-24T19:0x with 34 staged files not in HEAD, spanning at least two lanes (YellowElm's fs-io/.gitattributes/data/cad-import-corpus for f85xj.11.6, plus fs-conduction/src/power.rs + tests/power.rs). Running generate-source-manifest in that state produces a tracked SBOM that describes 34 files which are not in the commit it claims to describe -- a false provenance artifact, which is worse than a stale one because it looks authoritative. STATE: check-all currently reports source-manifest + source-manifest-spdx stale (from tracked files added by 6970b776, 53fd5c31, b857112e and later commits) and doc-facts integration_tests stale (recorded 571 vs index 572; the extra rows are other lanes' STAGED test files, so that row self-heals when they commit). DONE WHEN: regeneration is performed at a moment when git diff --cached --name-only contains ONLY the regenerating agent's intended paths, and generate-source-manifest + check-docs are committed in the SAME commit as the files they describe. PROTOCOL: announce a quiescence window on Agent Mail, confirm the index is clean of foreign staged work immediately before running, then stage-generate-commit atomically. Do NOT 'helpfully' regenerate on someone else's behalf while their work is staged.
close_reason: FIXED at 4db1966b. Root cause was a design error, not just bad timing: both derived-registry generators enumerated the git INDEX, but this repo mandates 'git commit --only <paths>', which bypasses the index and commits HEAD plus the worktree state of the named paths -- so an index-derived manifest described a state that would never be committed. Correct-by-accident under git add + bare commit; wrong since --only became the house rule; the shared index made it constant. FIX: source-manifest path enumeration is restricted to HEAD plus an explicit caller scope, and content for any path OUTSIDE that scope is read from HEAD rather than the worktree, so neither a foreign staged NEW file nor a foreign uncommitted EDIT can enter. generate-source-manifest [paths...] takes the scope (exactly what you pass to commit --only); empty scope regenerates the manifest describing HEAD, the right default for repairing drift. doc-facts now enforces HEAD subset-of recorded subset-of index instead of recorded==index, so a foreign staged test file no longer hard-errors check-docs for every agent. VERIFIED with the contamination present, not hypothetically: foreign worktree edit to a tracked file -> manifest byte-identical; --scope mine with a foreign edit also present -> mine recorded, theirs not; check-source-manifest 2 violations -> 0; check-docs 1 -> 0. 9 new unit tests pin both rules incl. the foreign-staged case and a live-tree containment check. The quiescent-index protocol this bead originally prescribed is now unnecessary: correctness no longer depends on anyone's discipline about when they stage.

title: fs-uq adaptive_mlmc controls only bias, not variance — doc overclaims optimal allocation
description:
CLAIM-vs-IMPLEMENTATION gap in crates/fs-uq/src/adaptive.rs (verified by reading the code).

## The gap
The module doc (adaptive.rs:5-7) states levels are added until the bias fits half the tolerance, "the other half goes to variance via the standard optimal sample allocation n_l ∝ √(V_l / C_l)." The implementation does NO such allocation:
- `add_level` (adaptive.rs:62-78) always takes exactly `n_pilot` samples (`n: n_pilot`, line 75).
- The main loop (adaptive.rs:81-121) only ADDS levels based on the extrapolated bias `|mean_L|/(2^α−1) ≤ tol/2` (line 108-109).
- `cost` (stored line 76 via cost_of) is never read again; `beta` (fitted line 106) is stored in the report but never used for any allocation.

So the returned estimate's RMSE is bounded only on the BIAS half of `tol`; the estimator VARIANCE is left at whatever `n_pilot × (#levels)` happens to give. The "estimate within tol" UQ tolerance claim is therefore only half-delivered. The test uq_005 passes only because its variances (8^{-l}, n_pilot large) are already tiny; it never checks estimator variance against tol/2.

## Resolution options
(a) Implement the promised allocation: after the bias loop converges, top up each level to n_l sized so Σ V_l/n_l ≤ (tol/2)^2, using the stored `cost`/`var` and the Giles formula (mirror mlmc.rs:62-78). This is the faithful fix but CHANGES sample counts and the estimate → will bump any golden fingerprint (check uq_battery.rs golden) and needs cross-ISA re-pin on x86.
(b) If full variance control is out of scope for this bead, correct the module doc (and any public claim) to state that only the bias is controlled and per-level sample count is fixed at n_pilot — so the function does not overclaim a tolerance it does not deliver.

Prefer (a). Related: the ÷n vs ÷(n-1) variance-denominator inconsistency between this path and mlmc.rs (separate bead). Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt; the golden-neutral fail-closed guards in mlmc_estimate were landed separately.

title: Make locked RCH builds sync the full Cargo path-dependency materialization closure
description:
The original attribution to host-only FrankenSQLite patches is incomplete. The Mac has 20 absolute FrankenSQLite [patch.crates-io] entries in its user Cargo config, while RCH executes Cargo with a fresh isolated CARGO_HOME. However, FrankenSim reaches FrankenSQLite through direct relative path and workspace dependencies, and the recorded locked failure attempted to replace fnp-* packages, not fsqlite-* packages.

crates/fs-sparse/Cargo.toml declares fnp-ufunc and fnp-dtype as optional, off-by-default path dependencies. The committed lock and current FrankenNumpy manifests identify them as 0.1.0. RCH currently derives sync roots from the default-feature cargo metadata active resolve graph, deliberately excluding optional and pure-dev edges, and does not incorporate delegated feature selection. Consequently the FrankenNumpy roots are not guaranteed to be synchronized; an absent or stale worker checkout can make remote Cargo request a lock rewrite even though the local lock is correct.

This is primarily an RCH dependency-materialization defect. Do not regenerate the FrankenSim lock to match stale worker state and do not copy developer-home absolute patches into the repository.
design:
1. In RCH, retain the existing active execution closure for dependency ordering, runtime-risk classification, and active-cycle semantics.
2. Add a separate deterministic, cycle-tolerant Cargo materialization and lock closure derived from repository manifests, independent of the active feature graph.
3. Traverse every repository-local path specification that can participate in resolution: normal, build, dev, target-specific, optional, workspace-inherited, repository [patch.*] entries, and all transitive path dependencies.
4. Use a visited-set fixpoint traversal. Latent optional cycles must terminate and must not enter or invalidate the active execution DAG.
5. Union materialization roots into full source synchronization, cache and project hashing, repo convergence, and remote dependency preflight. Sync source as well as manifests so --features, -F, --all-features, and --no-default-features cannot activate an unsynchronized crate.
6. Do not inject or copy user-home Cargo config. A project that genuinely requires a patch must declare repository-relative configuration.
7. Track implementation in a linked RCH issue and keep this FrankenSim issue open until the deployed RCH binary passes the real locked proof.
8. Separately harden the FrankenSim DSR release build command to cargo build --locked --release --workspace --bins. This is not the cause of the RCH closure failure.
9. FrankenSim itself requires no justified Cargo.lock rewrite for this defect.
acceptance_criteria:

title: fs-ir causal row writer: pin refusal precedence, type-enforce the cap, and de-duplicate the serializer
description:
Carried out of frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.1.2.9.1 at closure so the items are not lost with the parent. GrayBarn's independent post-commit audit of 2fadb8ff (bead comment, 2026-07-18 15:00 UTC) marked all three EXPLICITLY NONBLOCKING, and central executable proof has since landed (WindyWaterfall, 2026-07-26: fs-ir 23 targets / 271 passed / 0 failed; fs-blake3 64 passed). These are hardening, not defects.

(1) OVER-CAP-PLUS-PRODUCER-ERROR PRECEDENCE REGRESSION. CausalIdentityRowWriter::record_append (causalization.rs) sets a STICKY refusal and returns false, and into_bytes returns that refusal. Separately, the producer closure may return its own Err(CanonicalError). Nothing currently pins which of the two wins when BOTH occur on the same row. Today the writer's sticky refusal is recorded first and the producer error is returned by the `?` in the caller, so the observable outcome depends on ordering that no test states. Add a G0 case where the producer writes past the admitted cap AND then returns its own distinct error, and assert the exact resulting CausalIdentityError variant plus stream origin, so the precedence is a pinned contract rather than an accident.

(2) MECHANICALLY ISOLATE THE WRITER'S BACKING FIELDS. CausalIdentityRowWriter{bytes, plan, admitted_capacity, refusal} keeps `bytes` reachable from any code in the same module. The cap-before-mutation invariant is currently protected only by convention: every write must route through record_append. Move the backing Vec into a child module (or a newtype with no field access) so that routing is enforced by the type system and a future edit cannot append directly and silently defeat the cap.

(3) SHARE THE AUTHORITATIVE MACHINE SERIALIZER RATHER THAN PARITY-TESTING DUPLICATES. The eager and streamed causal row serializers are separate implementations kept in agreement by g3_streamed_identity_rows_match_eager_canonical_bytes_and_roots and g3_actual_causal_row_length_plans_match_payload_families. Parity tests catch drift only for the shapes they cover; a family added to one path and not the other is invisible until someone writes the matching case. Collapse the duplicates onto one authoritative serializer so identity parity is structural.

DONE WHEN: (1) has a passing G0 precedence case naming the exact variant; (2) direct appends to the writer's backing storage are impossible outside the child module/newtype and the cap invariant is type-enforced; (3) exactly one serializer implementation produces causal ordered rows for both the eager and streamed paths, with the parity tests retained as regressions.

TESTS: the (1) precedence case; a compile-fail or module-privacy proof for (2); and for (3) a demonstration that adding a row family to the shared serializer automatically covers both paths (e.g. the existing parity tests still pass with the duplicate removed).

title: Enforce exact input dimension across neural point and interval evaluation
description: ROOT CAUSE: MlpSdf::eval uses dot(row, input) implemented by zip, so short point inputs silently omit coordinates and long inputs silently ignore extras. eval_interval correctly rejects dimension mismatch, and eval_grad inherits the point-path ambiguity. This breaks the claimed shared evaluator/certifier semantic surface and lets a non-2D network enter NeuroShape nominal computations before later 2D calls panic. MISSION: introduce one shared exact input-dimension admission used by eval, eval_grad, and eval_interval (a structured fallible API is preferred; a documented structural assertion is the minimum); never truncate or pad implicitly. Make NeuroShape explicitly require/refuse a 2D field before any work. TESTS: short/long/empty point and interval inputs, malformed gradient requests, exact dimension success, mutation removing either side of equality, and deterministic structured diagnostics. Update contracts and downstream WASM refusal behavior. Code-first static tranche; central fs-rep-neural/fs-neuroshape-e2e/fs-wasm proof pending.
