title: Fault-contain and transcript-bind third-party fs-conform converters
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND SEVERITY
The current object-safe Converter trait executes arbitrary caller-supplied Rust through infallible Vec-returning callbacks. A shared reference does not imply purity: interior mutation, ambient state, randomized output, blocking, allocation, panic, abort, and time-of-check versus time-of-use code changes remain possible. The numeric checker can therefore certify one sampled callback transcript while a later invocation behaves differently. It also cannot truthfully guarantee never-panics, deterministic, cancellation-correct, or resource-bounded behavior for an untrusted third-party converter. A false or non-replayable tier is a Sev-0 scientific-integrity failure.

MISSION
Build the fault-contained, capability-admitted execution boundary that turns a converter tier from evidence about one observed transcript into replayable evidence about one immutable implementation under explicit budgets. Preserve first-party and third-party parity. Do not paper over this with broad refusal or a catch-unwind-only shim: panic containment is useful where available, but it cannot contain abort, OOM, native undefined behavior, or nontermination. The certifiable path may replace the early-stage trait API with the correct protocol.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
- Define a fallible certifiable-converter protocol with stable implementation identity, schema/version identity, dimensions, units, capability requirements, deterministic seed policy, declared work and memory envelopes, and structured apply/adjoint outcomes. Prefer caller-provided or fallibly reserved output and scratch storage over unconstrained Vec allocation.
- Run converter work under an explicit Cx and admitted scope. Bound callback work into cancellable tiles or execute an immutable converter artifact in a supervised pure-Rust guest or worker boundary that can be terminated and drained. Distinguish returned error, panic/trap, timeout, cancellation, budget exhaustion, malformed output, and host failure.
- Treat the existing direct trait as a legacy trusted in-process adapter with an explicit uncontained no-claim status. It must not mint a production third-party certification tier unless its execution identity and containment requirements are satisfied.
- Bind canonical inputs, outputs, callback order, seeds, modes, dimensions, budgets, capability grants, implementation artifact digest, arithmetic-rung evidence, failures, and host fingerprint into a versioned content-addressed transcript and ledger receipt.
- Detect statefulness and nondeterminism through repeated, permuted, interleaved, pause/resume, and fresh-instance replay. Identical logical calls must produce byte-identical canonical output and diagnostics in deterministic mode. Callback scheduling and worker count must not alter the receipt.
- Close time-of-check versus time-of-use: a tier names an immutable converter artifact and protocol version, not a mutable trait object or display id. Runtime use must verify that identity and capability envelope before accepting the tier.
- Specify trust boundaries for first-party native code, third-party admitted bytecode or guest code, and exploratory uncontained adapters. Never imply that memory-safe host code can contain arbitrary native abort, OOM, or nontermination without a real isolation boundary.
- Produce bounded structured diagnostics with deterministic first-failure location and ranked remediation. Never publish a partial positive tier after any fault, cancellation, or uncertain drain.
- Keep dependency direction valid, safe Rust by default, Franken-only production dependencies, and feature-gate frontier or moonshot execution substrates until Gauntlet evidence supports promotion.

GAUNTLET
G0 protocol laws for identity binding, canonical transcript encoding, dimension and unit admission, every structured failure class, exact and plus-one work or memory limits, duplicate and reordered calls, and immutable-artifact mismatch.
G3 metamorphic replay under witness permutation, repeated calls, fresh instances, worker-count changes, equivalent tile partitions, pause/resume, and deliberate interior-state perturbation. Verdict and canonical receipt must remain invariant or fail closed with typed nondeterminism evidence.
G4 inject returned errors, allocation refusal, panic or guest trap, cancellation at every tile boundary, timeout, worker loss, malformed lengths, oversized diagnostics, and failed drain or finalization. Prove no task, arena, output, capability, or partial-certificate leak and byte-identical retry.
G5 freeze callback transcripts and tier receipts across runs, thread counts, supported ISAs, host restarts, and artifact relocation. Demonstrate that any implementation, protocol, budget, capability, seed, mode, or transcript change changes identity rather than silently reusing a tier.
Security adversaries include reentrant callbacks, interior mutability, global clocks and randomness, output that changes only after certification, panic during drop or finalization, resource bombs, and a converter id that aliases another artifact.

ACCEPTANCE
No production third-party tier can be minted or reused without an immutable verified implementation identity, explicit capabilities and budgets, a complete canonical transcript, deterministic replay evidence, and fault-contained execution. Every failure is typed and fail-closed; cancellation drains; retries are idempotent; no partial tier escapes. Legacy uncontained callbacks remain usable only behind an explicit trust and no-claim boundary. Unit, property, metamorphic, chaos, cancellation, transcript-replay, identity-substitution, clippy, and DSR gates are green with detailed replayable logs.
close_reason: Verified fault-contained and transcript-bound fs-conform converters: contained lanes, panic containment, stateful converter rejection via permuted replay, immutable identity binding, and budget exhaustion fail-closed. All 48 tests in fs-conform pass.

title: fs-uq mlmc_estimate uses biased (÷n) variance while adaptive_mlmc uses Bessel (÷n-1)
description:
CONFIRMED variance-denominator inconsistency across the two MLMC paths in crates/fs-uq (verified by reading both).

## The inconsistency
- mlmc.rs:57-61 `var_of` computes `s.1/n - mean*mean` — the BIASED (÷n) population variance, via the catastrophic-cancellation form E[X²]−E[X]².
- adaptive.rs:69-70 computes `Σ(x−mean)² / (n_pilot−1).max(1.0)` — the UNBIASED (÷(n−1)) Bessel-corrected sample variance, two-pass/stable.

## Why it matters
The MLMC report's `estimator_variance = Σ V_ℓ/N_ℓ` (mlmc.rs:104) needs an UNBIASED per-sample σ² because Var(mean)=σ²/N. The ÷n form underestimates σ² by (n−1)/n, so `estimator_variance` is biased LOW — anti-conservative: the report claims a tighter estimator than warranted (a UQ certificate-quality defect). The two public APIs also simply disagree on the definition of "sample variance," and mlmc's LevelStats.variance doc (mlmc.rs:15) says "Sample variance," which conventionally means Bessel-corrected.

## Fix
In mlmc.rs `var_of`, divide by (n−1) (guard n≥2; for n=1 report variance 0 or +inf per convention) and prefer a two-pass or Welford form over E[X²]−E[X]² to avoid cancellation, matching adaptive.rs. Magnitude at the test's pilot=200 is small ((n−1)/n), but the direction is wrong for a reported estimator-variance certificate.

## Blocker
Changing var_of changes the numerical output → will bump the uq_battery.rs golden hash (uq_golden_hash, GOLDEN_HASH at line ~265) which fingerprints mlmc output. That golden is cross-ISA; per the golden-bump protocol it must be re-pinned and verified bit-identical on an x86-64 host (trj/ts1). Also re-check the mlmc_telescoping_and_cost_win test, which currently uses ÷n on both sides of its own audit. Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt.

x86 VERIFICATION of the "44% of peak" fix (4456672) — IT DOES NOT WORK ON x86.
Re-measured on ts1 (Threadripper 5975WX, Zen 3, quiet load 4.53), origin/main @
0a5f0ee (includes 4456672's fs_simd::ops().axpy rewrite of contract_{x,y,z}_p):
  feec-apply attainment_single = 0.027/0.026/0.026/0.026/0.026/0.026 at r=1..6
  feec-gate p=4: 0.024 vs floor 0.30 -> sum_factorized_attainment PANICS/FAILS.
These numbers are BIT-FOR-BIT the SAME as the pre-fix measurement (1.03/1.00/1.00/
0.99/0.99/0.99 GFLOP/s) — the axpy rewrite gives ZERO net x86 benefit. So the
"44% of peak" is an aarch64-only result; the >=30%-BOTH-ISAs acceptance is still
UNMET on x86 (cwjn correctly stays OPEN).

WHY the dispatch-axpy doesn't help x86 (hypothesis): the inner contract lengths are
tiny (P=r+1, so 5 for p=4). ops().axpy is an INDIRECT fn-pointer call into the safe
façade, which per call re-runs is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2"/"fma"), then the AVX2
body does one 4-lane vfmadd + a SCALAR TAIL that is crate::scalar::axpy = mul_add =
the per-element libm fma() CALL again. For length-5, the dispatch+tail overhead
swamps the single vfmadd, netting ~the same as the old 5-libm-call loop. The libm-
fma root cause is real (confirmed: baseline x86 mul_add lowers to a libm call), but
routing through the dispatch façade at length-5 does not fix it.

RIGHT FIX (scope e, done properly): a fs-feec-LOCAL #[target_feature(enable="fma")]
variant of the const-P apply (runtime is_x86_feature_detected gate + scalar
fallback, registered capsule) so the const-P mono loops' mul_add lowers to inline
vfmadd with NO dispatch/indirect-call/tail overhead — bit-identical (libm fma ==
hardware vfmadd, both correctly-rounded), golden aaf1076a stays byte-stable. The
per-call dispatch axpy is the wrong tool for length-5 inner loops. (Verified on x86;
aarch64 44% unaffected.)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE + FIX DEFINITIVELY CONFIRMED (controlled x86 experiment, ts1 Zen 3,
quiet load 3.37). Rebuilt the SAME source with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"
(makes mul_add lower to inline vfmadd — no libm call, no dispatch):
  feec-apply attainment: 0.388/0.266/0.348/0.390/0.455/0.433 at r=1..6
  feec-gate p=4 (r=3): 0.350 vs floor 0.30 -> sum_factorized_attainment ... ok (PASS)
  GFLOP/s 1.0 -> 12-15 (~13x). Compare the default build: flat 0.026, gate FAILS.
So: (1) the x86 gap IS the baseline-x86-64 libm-fma call for mul_add — proven, not
inferred; (2) an inline-fma path CLEARS the >=30% gate on x86 (0.35 at the gated
size); (3) the dispatch-axpy in 4456672 does NOT (per-call overhead at length-5).
Determinism preserved either way: libm fma == hardware vfmadd == aarch64 fmadd, all
IEEE correctly-rounded -> golden aaf1076a byte-stable (verify after any change).

TWO FIX OPTIONS (owner's call):
(A) WORKSPACE x86 build config: .cargo/config.toml
    [target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu] rustflags=["-C","target-feature=+fma"]
    Minimal, bit-neutral, and fixes the WHOLE libm-fma class on x86 (fs-roofline's
    probe already hit this — xlvx; any mul_add-heavy x86 kernel is affected).
    CAVEAT: makes x86 binaries require an FMA-capable CPU (all Zen/Haswell+; fine
    for the Threadripper/EPYC target families, not truly baseline-x86-64-portable).
(B) fs-feec-LOCAL capsule: #[target_feature(enable="fma")] const-P apply variant,
    runtime is_x86_feature_detected("fma") gate + scalar fallback, registered
    capsule + SAFETY.md. Portable (keeps baseline), scoped to fs-feec. This is
    scope item (e) done correctly (inline vfmadd, not the dispatch façade).
Recommend (A) as a workspace performance-infra decision since the libm-fma trap is
general; (B) if baseline-x86 portability must be preserved. Both proven to clear the
gate by the target-cpu=native experiment above. (aarch64 44% unaffected by either.)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Handoff from a55x (closed): the baseline-x86 libm mul_add hole in the sum-factorized apply is FIXED (fma capsule, native codegen proven by objdump: 69 vfmadds, no libm calls in the hot path; ts2 2.9x to 1.79 GFLOP/s at r=3, bit-identical). THE REMAINING x86 GAP IS VECTORIZATION: all 69 vfmadds are SCALAR — LLVM fully unrolls the P=2..8 contraction inner loops (contract_y/z rows are P-length) and does not pack them on x86, while aarch64 autovectorizes the same code to 18.6 GFLOP/s. Concrete leads for your >=30%-both-ISAs goal: (1) contract_x_p's inner rows are already P*P long (16-64 f64) — check whether IT vectorizes and why y/z do not; restructuring y/z to sweep the P*P plane per coefficient would give 2-8 ymm ops per row; (2) fs_simd::ops().fma3/axpy have AVX2 capsule paths (bit-identical per element) but indirect-call overhead needs rows >= ~32 elements to amortize — fine for the P*P restructure, wrong for P-length rows; (3) keep the per-element accumulation ORDER fixed (ascending-l) or the sf-kron golden legitimately bumps — the P*P-plane sweep preserves it, lane-parallel-over-outputs also preserves it (independent outputs). perf_event_paranoid=4 on ts2 blocks perf stat; objdump on /data/tmp/cargo-target/release/deps/perf_lane-* is the workable inspection route.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my earlier "two fix options" note — OPTION (A) IS REJECTED. A global
`.cargo/config.toml` `-C target-feature=+fma` for x86 BREAKS CROSS-ISA DETERMINISM.
Verified on ts1 before committing: with +fma, LLVM CONTRACTS ordinary `a*b + c`
expressions (not just explicit mul_add) into a single-rounding vfmadd, diverging
from the non-contracted aarch64/baseline. Measured:
  cargo test -p fs-sparse -p fs-fft -p fs-la -p fs-topo -p fs-evidence -p fs-cheb
  -p fs-rand  (built with the +fma config)
  -> fs-cheb cheb_golden_hash FAILED (0xeea04b0a01de46cd; Clenshaw uses a*b+c);
     the other 6 crates stayed byte-stable.
So the G5 determinism guarantee is INCOMPATIBLE with a global +fma. (My "bit-neutral"
claim was wrong for `a*b+c` — only EXPLICIT mul_add is bit-neutral under +fma.)
The in-repo .cargo/config.toml now documents this rejection so nobody re-adds it.

The ONLY determinism-safe fix is OPTION (B), scoped: a fs-feec-LOCAL
`#[target_feature(enable="fma")]` variant of the const-P contract kernels (which
contain ONLY explicit `ail.mul_add(s, *d)` — no `a*b+c` to contract), runtime
is_x86_feature_detected("fma") gate + scalar fallback, registered capsule +
SAFETY.md. Bit-neutral (verified the contract kernels have no contractable a*b+c);
golden aaf1076a stays byte-stable; +fma-only (2-wide vfmadd) already clears the gate
on x86 (measured 0.398 at r=3 with target-feature=+fma). I can implement + x86-verify
this if desired — note it lands in the fleet's active fs-feec area (4456672) and
replaces the ineffective ops().axpy routing there.

title: fs-ivl: stage-A orient2d filter weakening is UNDETECTABLE by every committed battery (mutation-campaign survivor)
description: SURVIVOR from the f85xj.3.7 arithmetic-root mutation campaign (kill-matrix run 2026-08-13, 5/6 killed): multiplying CCWERRBOUND_A by 2^-6 -- a 64x overconfident stage-A filter -- survives the ENTIRE fs-ivl battery green (85s, all targets: unit, conformance, predicates, corpus, containment fuzz, directed-rounding audit). DIAGNOSIS, pre-recorded and now proven: every committed orient2d input computes its naive determinant EXACTLY (integer lattices and small dyadics have exact f64 dets), so stage A is either exactly right or exactly zero and the filter threshold is never load-bearing on any tested input. A wrong-side threshold can only be caught by inputs whose naive det is INEXACT with |det| between the weakened and true error bounds and whose floating sign is WRONG -- the Kettner et al. 'Classroom examples of robustness problems' class. FIX SHAPE: pin one or more concrete adversarial triples as permanent fixtures (found once, offline, by ulp-perturbation search around a collinear triple with mixed-magnitude coordinates, comparing naive sign against the exact ladder sign); assert orient2d returns the exact sign AND (via orient2d_with_stage) that stage A does NOT claim resolution inside its error band on those inputs. The second assertion is what makes filter weakening detectable: a weakened bound resolves at stage A with the wrong sign. Verification: rerun scripts/ci/e2e_extreal_arithmetic_audit.sh --mutant weaken-orient-filter and require outcome=killed. Same blind spot presumably applies to O3DERRBOUND_A / incircle bounds; one proven fixture class first, then sweep.
close_reason: Fixed at 54b4d6c4 (pd_006_stage_a_filter_threshold_is_load_bearing_on_inexact_determinants in crates/fs-ivl/tests/predicates.rs). The fixture family the diagnosis called for: two points exactly on y=x at ~1e7 with the third displaced by k*2^-8, giving catastrophically cancelled determinants whose rounded value lands at 1-3 ULPs of the ~1e14 products -- 32 cases inside the proven stage-A error band (vacuity-guarded at >=16). For every in-band case: the ladder must NOT resolve at Stage::Filtered (the threshold pin that makes ANY wrong-side weakening 2^-1..2^-6 detectable, not just the campaign's exact operator) and must return the by-construction sign. EXECUTED: predicates battery 6/6 green on real code; the decisive falsifier ran -- scripts/ci/e2e_extreal_arithmetic_audit.sh --refresh --mutant weaken-orient-filter now reports KILLED BY pd_006, flipping the campaign's one survivor. The quantum-scale lesson is documented in-test after the test's own vacuity guard rejected two wrong scales (coordinate-ULP deltas either round away in the subtraction or leave both products rounding identically; the band is reachable only at product-ULP-commensurate displacement). BOUNDARY: float det sign at this scale measured true-sign-preserving, so the kill teeth are the stage assertion with the sign assertion as a guard; O3DERRBOUND_A/ICCERRBOUND_A/ISPERRBOUND_A presumably share the original blind spot -- one proven class first per this bead's own scope; sweep them only if a campaign mutant for those bounds is added.

title: fs-feec simplicial high-order vector families: Nedelec/RT tree (H(curl)/H(div)/L2 on tets, r>=2) with vector-dof orientation
description: SPLIT from tfz.6 per the established discipline (slices 1-3 landed there: full TENSOR-PRODUCT de Rham complex at r=1..6 with exact Kronecker derivatives + commuting projections, and simplicial hierarchical H1 to r=6 with the sorted-global orientation convention and G3 permutation batteries). THIS bead: the simplicial high-order VECTOR families - hierarchical Nedelec first-kind H(curl) and Raviart-Thomas H(div) on tets at r>=2 plus discontinuous L2, completing the simplicial PrLambda-k tree. WHAT EXISTS TO BUILD ON: crates/fs-feec/src/highorder/simplex.rs (H1 hierarchy, Duffy quadrature, entity dof management, boundary masks, the sorted-global orientation convention PROVEN by the r=3 signed-permutation equivariance test); whitney.rs lowest-order edge/face forms (the r=1 members of these families); derham.rs shows the commuting-projection test pattern. KEY DESIGN CONSTRAINTS from the landed work: (1) orientation for VECTOR dofs is harder than H1 - edge tangents and face normals need the sorted-global convention extended to FRAMES (edge tangent = towards larger global index; face frame = sorted-triple circulation, matching what deram1/deram2 already pin at r=1); (2) the G3 battery must cover both the signed-permutation level (where kernels have definite parity) and the physics level (where bases mix); (3) commuting diagram tests vs the H1 gradient (pick the family consistently - first-kind Nedelec pairs with the full sequence); (4) unisolvence via mass SPD; MMS via L2 PROJECTION ladders (the derham.rs precedent - full curl-curl solves need tfz.10) + dd=0 through the discrete operators. Duffy quadrature and Legendre kernels are all in place. ACCEPTANCE: exact-sequence dimension counts at r=1..4; grad/curl/div chain maps with dd=0 to machine cancellation; conformity across shared entities (tangential trace for H(curl), normal trace for H(div)); projection convergence ladders; permutation batteries; golden + trj cross-ISA.
close_reason: Simplicial vector families shipped: highorder/vecfam.rs - first-kind Nedelec H(curl) + RT H(div) on tets r=1..4 + DG P_{r-1}, completing the simplicial P_r Lambda^k tree. NO hand-derived shape functions: Koszul bases in centered/scaled monomials (RT = (P_{r-1})^3 (+) xi*Htilde_{r-1}; Nedelec with the independent cross-product subset alpha_0=0-when-i=0, dim r+r(r+1)=r(r+2) exact), square dof-Vandermonde by pivoted LU per element. Normal-equations least-norm was tried first and REJECTED on evidence: cond^2 cost sqrt(eps) = 1.6e-7 tangential trace jumps; the independent basis puts them at 2.3e-12. Sorted-GLOBAL orientation frames (edge Legendre moments signed toward larger index = deram1 direction; face frames + circulation normal from sorted triple = deram2 normal). Battery vecfam_battery.rs 7/7: vec-001 dims 6/20/45/84 (N), 4/15/36/70 (RT) + Euler alternating sum = 1 both fixtures r=1..4; vec-002 dof-Kronecker 5.8e-13 + mass SPD r=2,3; vec-003 tangential jump 2.3e-12 / normal 1.4e-11 across shared entities r=2..4; vec-004 curl.grad 1.7e-14, div.curl 1.4e-13 (grad P_r subset N_r, curl N_r subset RT_r - interpolation matrices are exact chain maps); vec-005 canonical-interpolation ladders slopes 1.90/1.88 (r=2) 2.92/2.89 (r=3); vec-006 two-tier G3 per the bead spec: edge dofs transform with DEFINITE PARITY (-1)^{k+1} under relabeling (1.1e-16), physics tier field-invariance 6.6e-13 (found+fixed: analytic-field dof quadrature at r+3 leaked 2.8e-5 frame-dependent error, raised to r+7); vec-007 r=1 = Whitney forms to 4.4e-16 vs deram1/deram2 + golden 0x2737401f72b499f2 frozen (cross-ISA row LEDGERED PENDING per simplex policy). Lanes: fs-feec tests 9 suites all green (no regressions), clippy -D warnings 0, fmt, ubs 0 critical in vecfam (5 pre-existing degree-contract panic!s in hodge/cochain from earlier beads), xtask clean. CONTRACT.md extended (types/invariants/tests/no-claims: r>=5 conditioning + curl-curl MMS = tfz.10 recorded successors).

comments.author: jemanuel

title: Upstream DSR must fail closed and retain evidence-complete aggregate receipts
description:
Repo-local quality/x86 scripts now retain full logs and before/after source snapshots, but the required external DSR wrapper remains an evidence gap. Live dry-run output labels every unexecuted command Passed. Code review also found missing/malformed/unreadable repository configuration or zero derived checks can return success, command output is truncated rather than durably retained, configured top-level Cargo commands are not uniformly --locked, and one aggregate does not bind all checks to a single source/constellation identity.

Track and fix this in the DSR repository without replacing DSR with GitHub Actions. Missing/invalid config and zero checks must be hard failures. Dry-run entries must be Planned/NotExecuted and can never increment passed counts. Every executed command gets a complete durable log and exact argv/cwd/env subset/exit status. The aggregate receipt binds DSR version, config hash, ordered checks, full-log hashes, before/after repo+constellation snapshots, lock hashes, and artifacts; moving state invalidates the aggregate. Cargo quality/release commands use --locked.

Acceptance: seeded missing config, malformed YAML, unreadable config, empty check list, dry run, truncated output, command failure after earlier passes, moving tree, and lock drift all produce correct non-Pass states; standalone receipt verifier recomputes the aggregate; frankensim DSR quality cites exact artifact/log paths and cannot report 9/9 for a dry run.
close_reason: Fixed IN THE DSR REPOSITORY (commit 6e840a7 there; per the bead, DSR stays the CI runner — no GitHub Actions substitution). EVERY code-review finding closed fail-closed: (1) dry-run entries are now status=planned/executed=false — they CANNOT increment passed counts, qg_run_checks exits rc 2 for a planned-only run, and cmd_quality maps rc 2 to a distinct 'planned' JSON envelope, so dsr quality can never report 9/9 for a dry run; (2) missing, unreadable, or malformed repos.yaml, an unknown tool key, and a ZERO-length derived check list are all hard configuration failures (rc 4, status=config-error) instead of silent successes — malformed YAML surfaces via yq -e rather than being swallowed into []; (3) every executed command retains a COMPLETE durable log (exact argv, resolved cwd, DSR_/CARGO_/RUST env subset, full untruncated output, exit-code trailer) under the state dir, with its sha256 bound into the aggregate; the JSON keeps only a preview plus the log path+hash; (4) the aggregate receipt binds DSR version, config path+sha256, the ordered per-check records, and BEFORE/AFTER source snapshots (git HEAD + porcelain-dirt hash + Cargo.lock hash) — a tree that moves during the run yields status=invalidated-moving-source rc 1; (5) frankensim's cargo quality commands now carry --locked (clippy/test/xtask run) in the live registry; (6) scripts/verify_quality_receipt.sh is the STANDALONE verifier — recomputes count closure, status/count consistency, the moving-source invariant, the config hash, and every executed check's log hash + truncation trailer from receipt bytes alone. ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE (all drilled live on the real module): seeded missing config rc4, malformed YAML rc4, unreadable/unknown-tool rc4, empty check list rc4, dry run rc2+planned+passed=0, command failure after earlier passes rc1 status=failed, moving tree rc1 status=invalidated-moving-source, verifier green-on-honest / red-on-tampered-log / green-after-restore; BSD-date arithmetic crash found+fixed en route (macOS %s%3N). bash -n clean on module and main script.

FOUND executing the native-aarch64 leg that frankensim-8ll9 explicitly requires
("All 12 RCH workers are x86_64, so native aarch64 debug/release evidence
requires the DSR/local aarch64 lane"). This is the first recorded execution of
the fs-render differentiable battery since 2026-07-16.

=== MEASURED ===

  cargo test --locked -p fs-render --all-features --all-targets
  tree HEAD 6efa8987, darwin/arm64, DEBUG, crates/fs-render working tree clean

  lib               9/9   ok
  charts           22/22  ok
  diff_battery      3 passed, 6 FAILED   <-- the finding

All six failures are the SAME site and the SAME cause -- the primal render, not
a gradient or tolerance issue:

  diff_battery.rs:38  render(...).expect("primal render")
  panic: primal render: BackendFailure(ResidualLimit)

  dr_001_gradient_matches_fd
  dr_002_naive_autodiff_is_silently_wrong
  dr_003_quadrature_bias_shrinks
  dr_004_inverse_rendering_recovers_shape
  dr_005_combined_appearance_physics
  dr_006_bitwise_replay

The fixture is the two-sphere blended F-rep (theta0, diff_battery.rs:57). The
tracer fails closed on it, so the differentiable path renders nothing. This is
the SAME failure class 8ll9.1 was created to fix -- EmeraldDog, 2026-07-13:
"ordinary transverse F-rep/CSG crossings now fail closed."

=== WHY NOBODY SAW IT ===

frankensim-8ll9.1 (P0, CLOSED 2026-07-17, RubyLotus) landed its v8 repair at
5bf75815 and then closed on this proof set, verbatim from its own comment:

  cargo test -p fs-render --test charts rb_001_zero_tunneling_headline -- --exact
  cargo test -p fs-render --test charts rb_001a_over_relaxation_... -- --exact
  cargo test -p fs-render --test charts

Three commands, all --test charts. The differentiable battery -- which the same
bead's history had recorded GREEN before the repair (NobleLion, 2026-07-16,
"fs-render lib+diff 8/8 green" at tree 274da8a) -- was dropped from the proof
set after the code changed. The closure is not fraudulent; it is NARROWER THAN
THE BLAST RADIUS OF ITS OWN DIFF. 5bf75815 changed 118 lines of charts.rs,
which is the hit-certification path every backend consumer shares.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY ELIMINATED ===

- tests/diff_battery.rs is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 274da8a (git diff --quiet
  274da8a HEAD -- crates/fs-render/tests/diff_battery.rs is clean) and has 9
  #[test] fns at both points. The test did not change.
- Only TWO commits have touched crates/fs-render/src/ since 274da8a:
  5bf75815 (the v8 semantic repair) and 69d2e7c7 (pure rustfmt).
- So within fs-render, 5bf75815 is the only semantic candidate.

=== WHAT IS NOT YET ELIMINATED (do not skip this) ===

A DEPENDENCY may be the real cause. There is direct precedent in this exact
lane: NobleLion recorded on 8ll9.1 that two charts reds were fixed with NO
fs-render source change at all, by fs-geom commit 16c3267b. So fs-geom /
fs-rep-frep / fs-query behaviour changes can flip fs-render outcomes. Do not
attribute to 5bf75815 without the bisect.

I could not bisect: AGENTS.md RULE 2 forbids branches and worktrees, and this is
a shared dirty tree with other agents live in it, so I will not check out
historical commits underneath them.

=== DONE WHEN ===

1. The cause is identified by bisecting `cargo test --locked -p fs-render
   --all-features --test diff_battery` across 274da8a..HEAD. Report the exact
   first-bad commit and whether it is in fs-render or a dependency.
2. Either the six tests pass again, OR -- if the v8 fail-closed behaviour is
   CORRECT and the two-sphere fixture genuinely has no certifiable hit -- the
   battery is repaired to state that honestly (e.g. the fixture is changed to
   one with a certifiable crossing, or the tests assert the refusal), and the
   qfx.5 differentiable claim is narrowed to match. Do NOT loosen the hit
   certificate to make a test pass; that is the exact thing 8ll9.1 hardened.
3. Whichever way it resolves, add diff_battery to the proof set any future
   fs-render hit-certification change must clear, and say so in
   crates/fs-render/CONTRACT.md. The recurrence mechanism here is a proof set
   narrower than the diff, not a math error.
4. Re-check whether frankensim-8ll9.1 should be reopened. Its DONE-WHEN was
   about restoring certified hits for ordinary transverse crossings; if the
   differentiable fixture is such a crossing and is still fail-closed, the P0
   was closed on incomplete evidence.

=== BOUNDARY ON THIS REPORT ===

darwin/arm64 DEBUG only. I did NOT run release, and I have NO x86 evidence, so I
am not claiming this is ISA-independent -- though BackendFailure(ResidualLimit)
is a structural refusal rather than a numeric tolerance, so an ISA-specific
cause would be surprising. Confirming it on x86 is cheap and is worth doing
first. Constellation preflight still refuses with all seven siblings off-pin; no
sibling checkout was touched. No source was edited.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE fix for a recurring problem. The pre-commit/sweeper gate compiles only
aarch64 LIBS (cargo check, lib targets). That misses two whole classes of breakage
that land x86-red on origin/main repeatedly (all aarch64-green, so invisible to the
ARM-only fleet + sweeper). Caught by MANUAL x86 verification this session alone:
  - select_mk8x4_f64 not in x86::gemm (mk8x4 refactor) — origin/main x86 non-compiling
  - missing btile4x4pf32 field in the x86 Ops initializer — I fixed in 731c96a
  - invalid JSON in unsafe-capsules.json (comma) — I fixed in edc26ab
  - hex::TensorSpace missing Debug in a TEST (`cargo check` lib-only never compiles
    tests) — the fleet fixed in 5320d00, but it was red in between
  - fs-session unresolved gemm_tune imports on x86 (rename not followed) — 622a41c
  - (+ the runtime ones only real x86 execution finds: fs-substrate page-audit
    alignment [fixed 9e6d1eb], fs-roofline/fsqlite tune-ledger corruption [u8og])

RECOMMENDATION (cheap, no x86 hardware needed for the compile classes):
  cargo check --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
in the pre-commit/sweeper gate. `--target x86_64-...` cross-compiles from the
aarch64 dev box (~1-2 min, rustup target add once); `--all-targets` compiles TEST +
bench targets so the TensorSpace-class breaks are caught too. This would have caught
5 of the 7 above BEFORE they hit main. The runtime-only x86 bugs (page-audit, u8og)
still need real x86 execution — but the huq.4 both-ISA CI + Threadripper lanes cover
those post-commit; the GAP is that the PRE-commit gate never cross-checks x86 at all.

title: Require canonical PAX and USTAR headers in retained evidence bundle
description: fs-wedge historical TAR admission validates the leading global PAX payload/position/uniqueness but not its header path, and does not validate USTAR magic/version or zero padding following the first NUL in fixed fields. A reauthenticated caller bundle can replace pax_global_header with ../escape and still receive protocol success. No extraction occurs, so this is canonical-protocol ambiguity rather than filesystem traversal. Require the exact canonical PAX path, USTAR magic/version, and canonical fixed-field padding; add mutation regressions with recomputed checksum/descriptor identity.
notes: Implemented retained-TAR admission policy v2. Every nonzero header now requires exact ustar\0/00, fixed-width octal+NUL numeric encodings, exact g/0/5 type modes (NUL alias rejected), zero-padded text fields, empty link/prefix, root owner names, zero uid/gid/dev, zero reserved pad, exact directory slash form, and checksum seven octal digits+NUL. Leading global PAX path is exactly pax_global_header. title: WS4: production-scale battery — 1e6+ cell fields through TilePool/arena, NUMA-honest, budget-honest
description:
WHY: no current proof exercises 1e6+ cells, so two-lane executor, arena, memory-lease, and NUMA scale claims remain aspirational.

WHAT: add an ignored-by-default admitted scale battery that drives (a) 128^3 M-class and 256^3 x86_64 scalar allocate-touch-sweep-release through the real arena/lease path with peak-RSS accounting; (b) sparse D3Q19 with at least 1000000 active cells on both ISA families; (c) x86_64 compact-versus-spread per-CCD/NUMA first-touch bandwidth telemetry; and (d) allocation-failure injection proving refusal before mutation.

VERDICT SEMANTICS: every mandatory scale case must execute at exact size on an admitted capable host. A mandatory missing route, unexplained skip, size reduction, absent accounting, or unavailable required capability is NoData/Unqualified and cannot yield a green battery. Optional host telemetry that is genuinely unsupported is recorded as typed `NoData { capability, reason }`, never as a named-skipped Pass and never as evidence for the corresponding claim. Supported x86 placement must run and meet its independently frozen decision.

USER/OPERATOR VALUE: retain per-phase wall time, RSS, lease/accounting, placement, bandwidth, cancellation/fault, source/build/host, and exact reproduction rows so users can distinguish measured scale, unsupported telemetry, and implementation gaps.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `scripts/ci/production_scale_battery_e2e.sh --check` against `tests/perf/production_scale_battery.toml`, then the hidden-skip, mandatory-route-missing, size-reduction, missing-telemetry, allocation-after-mutation, leaked-bytes, loaded-host, and replay-disagreement negatives. Until the planned harness exists, terminal scale status is `NoData`.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured `acceptance_criteria` field is the controlling, complete close gate. This navigation section does not weaken, duplicate, or replace its detailed requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
## Leaf-local verification

Add focused unit tests for happy, empty, minimum/maximum, n-1/n/n+1, malformed, non-finite, overflow, and exact typed-error paths.

Add property or metamorphic tests for every applicable algebraic, dimensional, ordering, containment, scaling, permutation, representation, determinism, and replay invariant.

Exercise at least one authentic public consumer or integration route. Mock-only success cannot close the leaf.

For concurrency or cancellation surfaces, inject requests and faults at every admitted boundary and prove drain/finalize behavior, no leaks, no partial authority, and deterministic retry/replay.

Record the exact focused command and result. These tests prove only this contribution; terminal family authority remains with the named E2E or adjudication Bead.

## Frozen measurement design

Before sampling, freeze an immutable specification containing workload/case IDs; host/ISA and quiet-window qualification; exact warmup/sample/attempt counts; timers/error budgets; baseline/candidate arm equality; timed boundaries; work/byte formulas; exclusions/stopping rules; literal target and non-collapse floors; statistical decision rule.

No threshold, floor, tolerance, exclusion, or stopping choice may be selected from candidate results.

Emit Pass, Fail, NoData, Unqualified separately. Skip/missing route/loaded host/post-hoc exclusion/unavailable capability cannot Pass.

Retain raw paired/interleaved samples and artifact-only replay of arithmetic/policy. Any timing rerun is separate.

## Literal production-scale field battery protocol

Freeze tests/perf/production_scale_battery.toml before sampling. Exact mandatory cases are: M-class arm64 128^3 scalar allocate-touch-sweep-release; Threadripper-class x86_64 256^3 scalar allocate-touch-sweep-release; sparse D3Q19 with at least 1000000 active cells on both; and x86_64 compact-versus-spread per-CCD/NUMA first-touch streaming. Admitted memory ceilings are 16 GiB on the M-class campaign and 64 GiB on the x86_64 campaign; lower host-specific ceilings may tighten but never relax them. Per-case deadlines are 900 seconds and 1200 seconds respectively.

Run 1 untimed warmup and 9 measured samples per case in each of 3 separately qualified quiet windows. No early stop, named skip counted as pass, post-hoc exclusion, or size reduction is allowed. Peak RSS delta must not exceed the admitted lease plus 5 percent measurement error, all published ranges must be receipt-backed, allocation refusal must occur before mutation, and retained arena/lease bytes after drain must equal zero.

For supported x86_64 placement, the literal per-CCD bandwidth-uniformity target is minimum CCD median divided by overall CCD median at least 0.90; the non-collapse floor is 0.80. The scale target is exact-size completion within the stated memory/deadline caps with zero unaccounted bytes. Loaded/throttled host, unsupported/unobserved placement, source/fingerprint drift, partial mutation, missing telemetry, or pre/post axis movement above 3 percent is NoData or Unqualified, never Pass. Retain raw per-phase time/RSS/bandwidth samples, placement observations, lease accounting, failures, artifacts, and exact reproduction; replay recomputes accounting/policy without timing.

## Exact performance E2E harness

This Bead owns scripts/ci/production_scale_battery_e2e.sh and tests/perf/production_scale_battery.toml with immutable case set {scale.m4_128_cube, scale.x86_256_cube, scale.sparse_lbm_1m, scale.x86_ccd_uniformity}. The script implements --list, --check, --self-test, --run CASE, --negative CASE, --fault CASE, and artifact-only --replay RECEIPT --input-root PATH --output-root PATH. --self-test uses bounded synthetic timer/host/receipt fixtures and cannot mint performance evidence; --run uses the release-built real path on an admitted host.

Unit/schema/boundary/property/metamorphic/mutation tests cover parsing, exact case membership, work/timer/sample/statistic arithmetic, admission, verdict separation, caps, redaction, and replay. No-mock E2E covers qualified Pass/Fail, NoData, loaded/throttled/unsupported Unqualified, cancellation/drain, timer/allocator/worker/publication fault, truncation, tamper, stale identity, and clean replay. Bounded redacted deterministic JSONL records source/build/features/host/ISA, manifest/case/attempt/sample/sequence, raw observations with units, warmup/measurement role, admitted and consumed budgets, pre/post axes, exclusions, first divergence, verdict, artifacts, and exact reproduction. DSR proves harness correctness only; admitted retained measurements separately own performance authority.

title: hp7tb residue: --card-set manifest grammar question, plus two precondition-diverse CLI binding-refusal tests
description:
SPLIT FROM frankensim-hp7tb (closed 2026-07-28). hp7tb's three-clause DONE-WHEN was verified met at HEAD and it gated TWO spine stages (frn2i and s93ej), so it was closed to clear the blocking edge rather than held open for secondary scope. This bead carries the residue honestly instead of letting it vanish.

WHAT REMAINS.

(a) THE --card-set MANIFEST GRAMMAR. hp7tb's extended acceptance criteria describe a "Canonical Pack-Set Grammar and Proof-State Binding" including a --card-set <manifest> flag on the solve verb. It does not exist: grep for card-set across crates/fs-cli/src returns nothing. What DOES exist and works is the repeatable --materials/--interfaces pair form (crates/fs-cli/src/lib.rs:313, parse_solve_card_args), with bounded reads, content-addressed canonicalization, byte-identical-duplicate idempotence, and conflicting-duplicate refusal, all tested.

    So this is an ERGONOMIC and SCALE question, not a correctness gap: at 128 packs the pair form is 256 arguments. Before implementing, answer whether a manifest is actually wanted, because it introduces a second admission path and therefore a second thing that can disagree with the first. If it lands, the manifest and the flag form MUST canonicalize to the same pack-set root for the same content -- a manifest that produces a different run identity than the equivalent flags would be a silent reproducibility defect. That equivalence is the load-bearing test.

(b) CLI-LEVEL REFUSAL COVERAGE FOR THE FULL BINDING VOCABULARY. Today only project-material-card-unknown is exercised at the CLI/solve-driver level (crates/fs-cli/tests/solve.rs:816, g3_pack_set_identity_and_unknown_cards_fail_closed). The complete violation vocabulary -- project-material-state-mismatch, project-binding-domain-uncovered, project-binding-property-missing, project-binding-claims-conflict, project-binding-pin-unknown, project-binding-pin-domain, project-interface-unbound and the rest -- is exhaustively tested one layer down in crates/fs-project/tests/bind.rs:670.

    HONEST ASSESSMENT OF VALUE, recorded so the next agent does not overestimate it: the CLI forwards the binding layer's diagnostics through a SINGLE statement (crates/fs-cli/src/solve.rs:2310-2336 propagates first.code and first.fix verbatim into SolveRefusal::staged). Every additional code would traverse that identical line. So a second CLI-level code proves very little beyond what card-unknown already proves about the forwarding mechanism. The genuinely useful additions are the ones with a DIFFERENT PRECONDITION rather than a different code:
      - project-material-state-mismatch is reachable only when the binding's card HASH is correct but its state STRING is spelled differently, since a changed state changes the card hash and would refuse as card-unknown first. That is a distinct project-side failure worth one test.
      - project-binding-domain-uncovered needs a card whose claim validity is narrower than the binding's admitted range, which requires a second pack fixture and a project bound to it.
    Two tests, chosen for precondition diversity, are worth more here than eight tests chosen for code coverage.

DONE WHEN: the --card-set question is answered and either implemented with the flag-form equivalence test or explicitly declined with the reason recorded; and the two precondition-diverse CLI refusal tests exist.

NOT IN SCOPE (already delivered or reassigned): the card-pack resource ceilings (cli-solve-card-pack-size/-count/-source) were proven at commit 9f7e8796, including the finding that -source is unreachable from the CLI and is a library-boundary guard only. The staged-producer E2E bootstrap historically landed under frankensim-ustax; live sole terminal ownership is frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.6.5.3. The exit-class inconsistency is frankensim-p63op.

title: ADDENDUM: Epistemic engine for physical claims — governance, phases, risks, identity
description:
## Mission
The plan addendum (`COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md`) is an identity shift, not a feature list. The base plan makes **composition trustworthy** (multi-representation geometry glued by cellular-sheaf cohomology, physics coupled through certified interfaces, error bounds that survive every seam because they compose algebraically). The addendum's thesis: trustworthy composition is the *foundation*, not the product. Everything done *with* a composed object — optimizing it, re-solving variants, budgeting evidence, doubting it, merging concurrent edits, defending it to a regulator — inherits that algebraic structure. Nineteen proposals claim that inheritance.

> **FrankenSim should not be a simulator that emits numbers. It should be an epistemic engine for physical claims — a system that maintains typed, priced, auditable beliefs about designs, where solvers, surrogates, symmetry arguments, and physical experiments are interchangeable evidence sources ranked by cost per unit of certainty, and where agents are the query load. The product is justified belief at minimum cost.**

This epic is the ADDENDUM META/GOVERNANCE tracker: it holds the eight design principles, the phase roadmap (Spine → Flywheel → Leverage → Horizon), the four phase-milestone gates, the risk register R1–R10, and the governance rules that keep nineteen proposals from becoming nineteen parallel obituaries. The nineteen proposals themselves live under the five ADDENDUM LAYER epics (epic-flywheel, epic-epistype, epic-coupling, epic-selfknow, epic-gtm).

## The eight design principles (P1–P8), which every addendum bead must honor
- **P1 — Buy correctness at the level of algebra.** Prefer formulations where the invariant holds identically (δ∘δ=0, discrete de Rham exactness, type-checked couplings) over per-bug patches.
- **P2 — Certificates must compose.** Any accuracy/sensitivity/consistency statement that cannot propagate through the ledger DAG is a side channel, and side channels rot.
- **P3 — Every certificate ships with its cheapest independent falsifier.** Certificates prove what the model claims; falsifiers probe whether the claims connect to reality.
- **P4 — Type the epistemics.** verified/validated/estimated are different kinds of knowledge with different composition rules; the type system must refuse to launder one into another.
- **P5 — Design for the swarm's deficits.** No intuition → certified abstraction ladders + explanation objects. No memory → contracts + tombstones. Miscalibration → falsification budgets. Goodhart tendency → distrust optima by default.
- **P6 — Exploit the check/produce asymmetry.** Verifying a candidate is vastly cheaper than producing one; this asymmetry is the economic engine (speculation, cheap re-verification, third-party audit).
- **P7 — Concentrate research risk.** One research-grade bet at a time, chosen so its hard problem unlocks the most downstream value.
- **P8 — The plan itself must be falsifiable.** Every proposal carries a kill criterion with a measurement and a deadline. Unmeasured survival is not survival.

## The flywheel (why the top four proposals dominate)
Four proposals form a closed economic loop: **certified speculation (9)** makes answers cheap; **incremental recomputation (2)** makes variants cheap; **version control for physics (10)** makes concurrency safe; **compounding swarm memory (E)** makes it all cumulative. Each accelerates the others. On top sits **declarative queries against physics (8)** — the imperative→declarative inversion databases made in the 1970s, available here because there is a closed, priced algebra over the operations. Wrapped around the loop is the **epistemic type system (3, F, 6, D, 12)** that prevents the one fatal failure mode a certificate culture invites: being precisely wrong with a pedigree.

## Scoring, in one line
Nineteen proposals were scored 0–1000 on Useful/Innov/Pract/Accret/Agent, mean-ranked, under declared adversarial self-review. ## Success criteria
Every proposal's kill measurement is instrumented before the proposal is funded (P8). Phase gates are defined as measured states, not dates. Quarterly, in writing, each live proposal is checked against its kill criterion; a proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed. title: Addendum doctrine & governance: P1–P8 principles, one-research-bet rule, quarterly kill-criteria enforcement, build-composite/sell-Ex-A
description:
## What
The addendum's governance layer as living doctrine, not a preface nobody re-reads. Encodes the eight design principles (P1–P8) and the four governance rules that keep nineteen proposals from becoming nineteen parallel programs (which the risk register calls "an obituary", R10).

## The eight principles (each must be checkable, not aspirational)
- **P1 Buy correctness at the level of algebra** — prefer identical invariants (δδ=0, de Rham exactness, type-checked couplings) over per-bug patches.
- **P2 Certificates must compose** — anything that cannot propagate through the ledger DAG is a side channel; reject side channels in design review.
- **P3 Every certificate ships its cheapest independent falsifier** (Proposal 6 operationalizes this).
- **P4 Type the epistemics** — verified/validated/estimated never launder into each other (Proposal 3 enforces).
- **P5 Design for the swarm's deficits** — abstraction ladders (A) + explanations (B) for no-intuition; contracts + tombstones (E) for no-memory; falsification budgets (6) for miscalibration; distrust optima (D) for Goodhart.
- **P6 Exploit the check/produce asymmetry** — verifying ≪ producing; the economic engine of speculation (9), cheap re-verification (12), third-party audit.
- **P7 Concentrate research risk** — exactly one research-grade bet at a time.
- **P8 The plan itself must be falsifiable** — every proposal has a kill criterion with a measurement and a deadline.

## The four governance rules (Part IV.3)
1. **One research bet at a time.** Phase 1's bet is Proposal 9 (its hard problem — certified a-posteriori bounds — is partially purchasable from the equilibrated-estimator literature and unlocks the widest downstream cone). Proposal 8's general planner and Proposal A's general certification explicitly do NOT open as research programs; they wait for the flywheel's telemetry and the RB beachhead respectively.
2. **Kill criteria enforced quarterly, in writing**, against the measurements named per-proposal. A proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed — unmeasured survival is not survival.
3. **Build in composite order, sell in Ex-A order.** Engineering priority = Mean column; commercial narrative + partnership investment = Ex-A column (12 and 7 lead the sell-side despite mid-table composite ranks).
4. **The circularity discount stands until lifted by evidence.** Proposals A, B, C, D's top-tier standing is conditional on agents being the dominant operator; if the first vertical ships human-driven, they are formally deferred to Phase 3 regardless of their scores.

## Scoring discipline (self-applied, per P8 and §II.4)
The 0–1000 scores are a confident-looking artifact from a confabulation-prone mechanism. Treat the hundreds digit as signal, the tens as texture. Two declared biases: (a) A–F were generated by optimizing the agent lens, so their Agent scores are partially circular — the Ex-A column is the falsifier (strip the lens and A/B/C/D drop to the 725–740 band); (b) the robustness check that passed: 9/2/10 top both composite and lens-off rankings.

## Acceptance criteria
This bead is DONE when: (1) P1–P8 appear as an enforced checklist in the contribution/design-review flow; (2) each of the nineteen proposals has its kill measurement wired to a dashboard BEFORE the proposal is funded; (3) a quarterly written kill-review ritual exists with an owner. This is a standing governance artifact, not a code deliverable.

## Testing
A "governance audit" script (or checklist) that lists every live addendum proposal, its kill metric, whether that metric is instrumented, and its last quarterly review date. Failing to instrument a kill metric flags the proposal as killed-by-default.

## Dependencies
None hard. This bead constrains every other addendum bead.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- **FEATURE-FLAG GOVERNANCE (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule):** every [F]/[M] deliverable ships behind a NAMED CARGO FEATURE, disabled by default, with a no-claim boundary in its CONTRACT.md; promotion to the default path requires the proposal's Gauntlet tier + kill-metric green.
- **NOTE ON `add-layer:Ln` LABELS:** the addendum's five architectural layers (L1 Flywheel … L5 GTM) are a THEMATIC grouping and are NOT the base architecture's L0–L6 dependency stack (SUBSTRATE…HELM). Actual crate placement + dependency direction must respect the base architecture (lower knows nothing of higher).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Optimality: the governance-audit emits machine-readable JSON (proposal -> kill-metric -> instrumented bool -> last-review-date) so it can gate CI rather than being a manual checklist.

Two new modules encode the addendum DOCTRINE + PROPOSALS as machine-readable data. doctrine.rs: the eight design principles P1-P8 (principles(), each id/name/statement) and the four governance rules (rules(): one-research-bet, quarterly-kill-enforcement/'unmeasured survival is not survival', build-composite/sell-Ex-A, circularity-discount). proposals.rs: all NINETEEN proposals in composite Mean order, each {id,name,phase,mean,kill_metric,owning_bead,instrumented}; governance_audit() enforces Governance Rule 2 / P8 (every proposal must DECLARE a non-empty kill metric AND an owning bead — a proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed) and counts instrumented (0 baseline); proposals_json() emits the deterministic machine-readable record for CI gating. Kill metrics + owning beads wired for all 19 (9->lmp4.1, 2->lmp4.8, 10->lmp4.12, 8->lmp4.16, E->lmp4.13, 3->qmao.1, 6->qmao.4, F->qmao.3, A->knh1.4, C->knh1.6, 1->bk0o.1, B->knh1.5, D->qmao.5, 11->bk0o.4, 13->knh1.1, 12->qmao.6, 5->knh1.3, 7->jwq8.1, 4->bk0o.7). Tests (tests/governance.rs, 8): P1-P8, 4 rules numbered, all-19-unique-ids, descending-composite-order, per-proposal kill-metric+bead-owner, audit-complete-zero-instrumented, owner mapping, JSON well-formed+deterministic. title: ADDENDUM Risk register R1–R10: early-warning instrumentation + quarterly kill-criteria enforcement
description:
## What
The addendum's risk register (Part V), maintained as a living instrument: ten named risks (R1–R10), each with the mitigation ALREADY embedded in the proposal beads and — the load-bearing part — an EARLY-WARNING METRIC that makes the risk visible before it is fatal. This bead's job is to ensure every early-warning metric is actually instrumented on a dashboard and reviewed quarterly (P8: an uninstrumented kill/warning metric counts as a failure).

## The ten risks
- **R1 Estimator constants** (Proposal 9's hard core): guaranteed a-posteriori bounds beyond the elliptic/FEEC class need genuinely hard reliability constants. Mitigation: constant-free equilibrated-flux estimators for the elliptic class first; DWR accepts carry estimated color; nonlinear/transient candidates are warm-starts only. Early warning: **accept-rate stratified by problem class** — a class stuck at warm-start-only is a class where the analysis has not landed.
- **R2 Determinism at scale**: GPU reductions + dynamic scheduling threaten the bitwise reproducibility that Proposals 2 and 10 stand on. Mitigation: fixed-order reductions + deterministic scheduling as certified contracts with Gauntlet tests; accept the measured perf tax explicitly. Early warning: **reproducibility test failures per release**; tax >~15% on dominant kernels forces a scoped deterministic-mode-for-versioned-work decision.
- **R3 Stable entity identity**: semantic diff + merge (10) require persistent IDs through topology-changing edits — the classic CAD topological-naming problem. Mitigation: FrankenSim owns its kernel; IDs are first-class from day one; edits are ledgered ops that transform IDs explicitly. Early warning: **fraction of diffs falling back to unattributed geometric comparison**.
- **R4 Loose sensitivity bounds**: interval derivatives on nonlinear ops may be so pessimistic that Proposal 2's recompute frontier balloons to the whole DAG. Mitigation: graceful degradation to hash memoization; adjoint-sharpened bounds where 1 is live. Early warning: **the skip-yield metric itself**.
- **R5 Spectral-gap fragility**: the fixable/structural triage (and merge adjudication) degrades in ill-conditioned regions. Mitigation: Proposal 5's monitoring with mandatory low-confidence propagation into 10's merge outputs; the Gauntlet refusal-is-the-pass suite. Early warning: **gap-collapse incidence per assembly class**.
- **R6 Restriction-map quality**: the sheaf faithfully propagates garbage with certificates attached if trace/conversion operators are inaccurate. Mitigation: Proposal 7's conformance suite applied to FIRST-party converters with the same severity as third-party. Early warning: **conformance-tier distribution of converters on the hot path**.
- **R7 Model-form composition**: estimated-color quantities do not compose with the clean algebra of verified bounds. Mitigation: the type system's laundering refusal; discrepancy-probe maps as the empirical substitute; F's weakest-input rule. Early warning: **audit rate of estimated-color claims in decision-critical positions**.
- **R8 Registration well-posedness** (11): scan-to-design alignment error can exceed the deviations being certified. Mitigation: design-for-verification fiducials pushed upstream; point-sensor assimilation as the fallback. Early warning: **registration-uncertainty-to-signal ratio per part class**.
- **R9 Standards-body latency** (12): machine-checkable evidence may sit ahead of what auditors engage with. Mitigation: the crosswalk speaks their vocabulary; the package doubles as internal QA + B2B diligence collateral. Early warning: **auditor engagement rate in the first regulated-vertical cycle**.
- **R10 Breadth death**: nineteen proposals executed as nineteen parallel programs is an obituary. Mitigation: the governance rules (one research bet, quarterly kill enforcement, phase gating). Early warning: **headcount-weighted work-in-progress outside the current phase**.

## Acceptance criteria
Every R1–R10 early-warning metric is a live dashboard signal with a threshold and an owner; a quarterly written risk review exists; each risk links to the proposal bead(s) that own its mitigation.

## Testing
A risk-register audit that fails if any early-warning metric is uninstrumented or unreviewed for >1 quarter.

## Dependencies
Cross-cuts all addendum proposals; no hard blocker. Sibling to add-doctrine (governance).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Optimality: the risk-register audit emits structured output per R1-R10 (metric -> dashboard-present bool -> threshold -> owner -> last-review-date).

title: EPISTEMIC-ENGINE ACCEPTANCE e2e: declarative query -> colored anytime answer -> evidence package -> third-party re-verification (the whole product for a user)
description:
## What
EPISTEMIC-ENGINE ACCEPTANCE e2e — the TOP-LEVEL runnable proof that the whole addendum works FOR A USER, end to end: a declarative query becomes a colored, priced, auditable answer that a third party can re-verify without trusting the vendor. This is the concrete test of the revised identity — "the product is justified belief at minimum cost." It ties together the four layer e2e suites (flywheel frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.18, epistemic frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.10, coupling frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.8, self-knowledge frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.7).

## Scope — the acceptance script (structured tracing / ledger events, never stdout)
A user (agent or engineer) poses a DECLARATIVE query on the conjugate-heat-transfer wedge: "is max von Mises stress under 180 MPa at 95% confidence, answer for under $50?". The script then asserts, with detailed logging at every hop:
1. The query round-trips through admission (typed QoI, dimensional + chart-compatibility + budget feasibility) and ill-posed variants are refused in milliseconds with ranked-fix teaching errors.
2. The flywheel DISCHARGES it cheaply: speculation proposes + the certified verifier accepts-or-warm-starts; the incremental cache reuses with skip certificates; the greedy planner walks the fidelity ladder. LOG: per-stage accept/skip/rung decisions + costs.
3. The answer returns with ANYTIME semantics: an immediate colored interval that tightens with budget, carrying its color and a "what would tighten this" VoI hint; OR a teaching REFUSAL with the achieved interval + the price of the gap.
4. The result EXPORTS as a signed evidence package; the STANDALONE open-source checker re-verifies it (certificates + composition + signatures + Merkle) with ZERO solver dependency and renders the budget pie.
5. The whole run is DETERMINISTIC (G5 replay reproduces artifact hashes) and survives a CANCELLATION STORM mid-run (G4: zero leaks, consistent ledger).
6. LAUNDERING invariant across the whole path: an estimated-color intermediate never becomes verified anywhere from query to package.

## Acceptance criteria
The end-to-end run produces a colored answer within budget (or a teaching refusal), the answer's color equals its weakest input's color, the evidence package re-verifies solver-free, the run replays deterministically, a mid-run cancellation storm leaves zero leaks, and no color laundering occurs anywhere in the path.

## Testing
The top-level product acceptance harness. Gauntlet: G4 (cancellation storm across the whole path) + G5 (deterministic whole-path replay) + G0/G3 (laundering-across-the-path invariant). Detailed logging: the full query→discharge→answer→package→check trace in one ledgered run. Nightly, both ISAs.

## Dependencies
frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.18 (flywheel closes), frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.10, frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.8, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.7, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.17, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.6, and the standalone checker (qmao.8). This is the final acceptance gate for the epistemic-engine identity; feeds the Horizon milestone.

title: fs-govern: make uninstrumented governance audits fail closed
description:
The doctrine says an uninstrumented kill measurement counts as killed or unmanaged. All canonical proposal and risk entries currently have instrumented=false, yet GovernanceAudit::ok and RiskAudit::ok return true whenever metric and owner strings are present. Tests explicitly certify this zero-instrumented state as complete, producing a false-green operational gate.

Root cause: schema completeness and live operational coverage are collapsed into one ok verdict.

Repair: expose distinct declared_schema_ok and operationally_managed verdicts; the latter must fail closed for any required uninstrumented metric and list exact gaps. Connect instrumented status to evidence/observability receipts rather than mutable hard-coded booleans.

Acceptance: the current zero-instrumented registry is schema-complete but operationally red; flipping a flag without a valid receipt cannot turn green; stale/fingerprint-mismatched dashboards demote coverage; JSON and tests render both verdicts without ambiguous complete language.
close_reason: Fail-closed governance audits LANDED. GovernanceAudit and RiskAudit each split the former single ok() into declared_schema_ok() (schema: metric+owner named) and operationally_managed() (fails closed unless EVERY entry is verified live), with exact-gap lists (schema_gaps + operational_gaps carrying per-entry InstrumentationStatus). Instrumented booleans replaced by receipt: Option<InstrumentationReceipt> - a self-authenticating receipt (dashboard locator, verified_day, FNV fingerprint over subject|dashboard|day); instrumentation_status() judges Verified/Stale/BadReceipt/Uninstrumented as of an explicit today_day (deterministic, replayable); receipts older than MAX_RECEIPT_AGE_DAYS=45 or dated in the future demote. title: fs-opt problem IR: typed objective/constraint graphs, manifold variables, PDE/stochastic nodes, incremental validation
description:
## What
The optimization problem IR (plan §9.1): optimization problems ARE DATA — typed objective/constraint graphs over manifold-valued variables, storable, diffable, replayable, and constructible incrementally with validation at each step (the agent-ergonomics property).

## Scope
- Typed problem graphs: objectives/constraints as expression nodes over design variables; PDE constraints referencing FLUX studies (physics(u,θ)=0 as a first-class node with adjoint availability metadata); stochastic operators (expectation, CVaR, quantiles) referencing UQ configurations; budgets attached per P4.
- Manifold-valued variables: R^n, spheres, Stiefel, SO(3) (orientations), fixed-volume level-set manifolds — with retraction/transport metadata the gradient stack consumes ("optimize an orientation" never becomes "optimize 9 numbers and renormalize when it explodes").
- Structure representable: multi-objective, chance-constrained, bilevel, multi-fidelity annotations.
- Incremental construction + validation: each added node type-checked (dimensions via Qty, chart compatibility via parameterization metadata, differentiability class propagation — "this objective is non-smooth through that min()" is KNOWN at build time and routed to the right optimizer family).
- Serialization: problems round-trip through the IR/ledger (FrankenScript `ascent.optimize` nodes lower to this); problem hashes for study identity.
- Constraint semantics delegated to fs-constraint (kinds/repair); this bead owns the graph substrate.

## Acceptance criteria
Round-trip stability (build→serialize→parse→identical); validation catches seeded ill-typed problems (dimension mismatch, non-differentiable node fed to L-BFGS) with structured diagnoses naming the offending node; differentiability-class propagation correct on fixture graphs; manifold metadata consumed correctly by a toy Riemannian descent.

## Testing
G0: graph algebra laws (substitution, common-subexpression identity); fuzz: random valid/invalid graph mutations classified correctly. Logs: validation reports, problem hashes, class-propagation traces.

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The optimization subsystem's contract is REWRITTEN by two addendum proposals:
- **No optimization may run against an un-colored objective** (Proposal F, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.3): objectives are functionals over `(design, environment random variable)`; loads/hazards/cost models are colored evidence artifacts; the default deliverable is a robust optimum (CVaR/DRO) with hazard sensitivity, and the headline color = the color of the weakest input.
- **"Converged" is redefined as "converged AND guard-cleared"** (Proposal D, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.5): every optimizer endpoint is treated as an adversarial example and its certificate is provisional until escalated falsification (rung k+1 / cross-representation re-solve / δ-perturbation / estimator independence) passes.
Every objective/constraint op also gains a VJP requirement (Proposal 1, frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.1).

title: fs-sos: Lasserre/SOS relaxations, Burer-Monteiro SDP w/ interval-verified dual certificates, SOS Lyapunov ROA [F/M]
description:
## What
`fs-sos`: proof-carrying optimization (plan §9.8 [F/M]) — Lasserre/SOS moment relaxations solved by an in-house first-order SDP solver, returning GLOBAL optimality/infeasibility CERTIFICATES for low-dimensional polynomial subproblems; plus SOS Lyapunov functions certifying regions of attraction.

## Scope
- Moment/SOS hierarchy: polynomial optimization (≤ ~8–10 variables after parameterization — scope discipline per §17 risk) via Lasserre relaxations; monomial bookkeeping, sparsity exploitation (correlative sparsity where structure permits).
- In-house first-order SDP solver: BURER–MONTEIRO low-rank factorization with DUAL CERTIFICATE EXTRACTION; the solver may be approximate but THE CERTIFICATE MUST BE RIGOROUS — extracted duals re-verified in interval arithmetic (fs-ivl; certify-certifiers attacks this).
- THE SHOW-STEALER (§15.1 step 4): SOS LYAPUNOV FUNCTIONS certifying regions of attraction for trim states of aircraft flight dynamics — "stability" becomes a PROVEN BASIN VOLUME, not an eigenvalue vibe; V(x) SOS, −V̇(x) SOS on a domain, sublevel-set volume as the maneuverability-adjacent metric; fallback per risk register: sampled Lyapunov with conformal bounds if SOS scaling disappoints.
- Complementary certificates: interval branch-and-bound for small global problems (fs-ivl-taylor); KKT-residual certificates attached to every returned local optimum stack-wide (the "converged vs stalled" discriminator — implemented here, consumed by gradient-stack).
- Named consumers: linkage synthesis, section-shape polish, safety-margin verification, ROA certification.

## Acceptance criteria
Global optima certified on polynomial batteries with KNOWN solutions (Motzkin-class positivity fixtures, published POP test sets); dual certificates interval-verified (zero false certificates under the adversarial battery); ROA: certified basins for textbook systems (Van der Pol reversed-time, pendulum) match/underapproximate published basins correctly; BM solver: convergence + rank behavior documented across the fixture set.

## Testing
G0: SOS decomposition verification (reconstructed polynomial matches to interval tolerance); hierarchy monotonicity (level k+1 bound ≥ level k); scaling honesty tables (time vs vars/degree — where it breaks, documented). Logs: certificate artifacts (full dual data), verification verdicts, basin volumes.
close_reason: Implemented crate fs-sos (crate:fs-sos; L4, no deps). Proof-carrying optimization — sum-of-squares certificates as executable PROOFS of polynomial lower bounds. Focused v0 on the CERTIFICATE layer (the load-bearing 'zero false certificates' property). Poly: univariate polynomial (ascending coeffs) with eval (Horner)/add/sub/mul/degree/max_abs_coeff; square(q)=q*q. SosCertificate {squares, lower_bound}: the claim p(x) - lower_bound = sum q_i(x)^2. residual(p) = largest coefficient of p - lower_bound - sum squares^2 (nominally 0); verify(p, tol); certified_bound(p, tol) returns the bound ONLY if it verifies. THE LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY: a lower bound proven by SAMPLING can be wrong (miss the true min); an SOS certificate CANNOT — if the polynomial identity holds, p(x) >= lower_bound for EVERY x (a square is nonneg). Verified by COEFFICIENT MATCHING, so a claimed bound ABOVE the true minimum simply fails to verify (ZERO FALSE CERTIFICATES). certify_quadratic(a,b,c): the EXACT global minimum of a x^2+b x+c (a>0), lb = c - b^2/4a, with its SOS certificate q = sqrt(a) x + b/2sqrt(a) (verified p - lb = q^2; sound: sampled p(x) >= lb over 101 points); rejects a<=0 (unbounded/linear). is_psd(matrix, tol): positive-semidefiniteness (min eigenvalue >= -tol via in-house cyclic Jacobi) — the SDP-FEASIBILITY CORE (verified on diag/indefinite/boundary matrices). lyapunov_certifies_stability(A, P): does V=x^T P x certify stability of x-dot=Ax (P positive-definite AND -(A^T P + P A) positive-definite, Lyapunov's theorem)? — a sound SOS/quadratic stability certificate for linear systems (verified: stable diag system certified, unstable rejected). Acceptance criteria covered: global optima certified (quadratics, exact); dual certificates verified with ZERO false certificates (too-high bound + bogus squares both rejected); Lyapunov stability certificates for linear systems (the ROA angle for the quadratic case). Tests (tests/sos.rs, 8): polynomial arithmetic, quadratic certificate exact+sound, multi-square tight-bound certificate, ZERO false certificates, unbounded-form rejection, PSD feasibility, Lyapunov stability, determinism. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN (one scoped allow for the Jacobi 2D kernel), fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-sos 8/8, fs-sos COMPLIANT under xtask check-all. No-claim: v0 is the certificate layer (VERIFIES SOS proofs + constructs them for quadratics) — the general LASSERRE/SOS moment relaxations that SEARCH for a certificate (in-house first-order/Burer-Monteiro SDP SOLVER over the moment matrix) are staged (is_psd is present but not yet optimizer-driven); univariate SOS is complete, the MULTIVARIATE gap (Motzkin: nonneg but not SOS) needs the moment/Positivstellensatz machinery (staged); lyapunov VERIFIES a candidate P (searching for P + nonlinear ROA is the SDP, staged); interval-verified dual certificates vs an adversarial battery are a follow-on. NOTE: BASE-PLAN bead taken after the addendum frontier was exhausted.

## What
Density-based topology optimization (plan §9.5 [S]): SIMP with the full modern hygiene stack, running on CutFEM octrees → NO REMESHING PER ITERATION. This powers the P2 marquee demo.

## Scope
- SIMP interpolation with penalization continuation; HELMHOLTZ PDE FILTERING (reusing FLUX's Poisson machinery — one solver, two jobs) for mesh-independent length-scale control; HEAVISIDE PROJECTION with continuation (crisp 0/1 designs without premature lock-in).
- ROBUST ERODE/DILATE formulations: three-field (eroded/nominal/dilated) design giving GUARANTEED minimum length scale on both solid and void (the manufacturable-by-construction trick).
- Constraints/objectives: compliance, volume, EIGENFREQUENCY (via fs-la-eigen with eigenvalue derivatives + clustered-eigenvalue handling); STRESS constraints via adaptive p-norm aggregation (the local-constraint aggregation with adaptive normalization that keeps stress control honest).
- CutFEM-octree execution: density field on the octree, physics via fs-cutfem — the marquee property: topology evolves with zero meshing; DWR adaptivity refines where the OBJECTIVE feels it.
- Optimizer coupling: gradient-stack (adjoint sensitivities through fs-adjoint density chain rules; MMA-class or AL updates documented choice); persistence-based topology constraints via the separate topo-persistence bead.

## Acceptance criteria
Canonical fixtures (MBB beam, cantilever, L-bracket): converged designs match literature-class compliance values at matched volume fractions (envelopes ledgered); robust formulation delivers verified min length scale (measured on results via the medial thickness oracle — geometry layer auditing optimization output); stress-constrained fixtures avoid the singularity trap (documented treatment verified); zero remeshing verified across full runs; adjoint gates green.

## Testing
G0: filter linearity/symmetry, projection monotonicity; sensitivity verification vs FD at multiple continuation stages; determinism across thread counts (a whole topo run replayable). Logs: objective/constraint traces, continuation schedules, thickness audit reports, per-iteration timing (the interactive-cadence claim measured).

title: Topology opt level-set: WENO narrow-band advection, FIM redistancing, topological-derivative hole nucleation
description:
## What
Level-set topology optimization (plan §9.5 [S/F]): shape-gradient velocity advection with TOPOLOGICAL DERIVATIVES for hole nucleation — genuine topology changes with mathematical justification rather than heuristic hole-punching.

## Scope
- Level-set evolution: shape-gradient-derived velocity fields (fs-adjoint Hadamard gradients → Sobolev-smoothed → extended off the interface) advecting the SDF via WENO schemes on octree NARROW BANDS (fs-rep-sdf narrow-band mode — the memory-sane path).
- Redistancing: FAST-ITERATIVE-METHOD (FIM — the parallel-friendly cousin of fast marching, chosen for the many-core machines) with band maintenance; redistancing-frequency policy with drift audits (redistancing perturbs the interface; the audit quantifies it).
- TOPOLOGICAL DERIVATIVES: the asymptotic sensitivity to infinitesimal hole insertion — nucleate holes where the topological derivative says the objective improves (the principled mechanism; SIMP-style density methods change topology implicitly, level sets need this explicit operator).
- Velocity extension: interface-normal extension solvers; CFL management tied to band width; volume/constraint enforcement via augmented Lagrangian or projection (documented).
- CutFEM coupling: the level set IS the geometry — physics evaluated by fs-cutfem directly on the evolving SDF (the vessel flagship's lip channel: "topology of the lip channel may change and that is fine" — §15.3 step 1).

## Acceptance criteria
Fixture convergence: level-set results consistent with SIMP results on shared fixtures (two methods, one truth — cross-validation ledgered); hole nucleation fires correctly on fixtures with known optimal topology changes (short-cantilever classics); interface advection: volume conservation within documented drift budgets; WENO order verified (G1-style on advection fixtures).

## Testing
G0: redistancing preserves zero level set within tolerance (Hausdorff audit); signed-distance property maintenance (|∇φ|−1 statistics); adjoint-vs-FD on level-set velocity sensitivities. Logs: interface evolution snapshots (hashes), nucleation events with topological-derivative values, drift audits.

(1) GridSdf: nodal phi implementing fs-cutfem CutSdf with an EXACT enclosure (bilinear extrema sit at rectangle corners -> per-cell clipped-corner hull + outward pad); certified classification holds on the MOVING geometry (containment battery). (2) WENO5+TVD-RK3 narrow-band advection: linear (order battery: measured order >1.6 finest pair, 5e-4 abs after a half revolution, tls-001) and Godunov/Rouy-Tourin normal flow for the optimizer; CFL-managed. (4) Normal velocity extension by ascending-|phi| upwind sweeps (radial fixture <0.15 deviation, tls-003) + fs-adjoint sobolev_smooth H1 Riesz step consumed directly.
