title: Conformal hardening: Mondrian buckets (by regime/fidelity/family), drift e-tests, false-coverage budgets, shift-adversarial validation
description:
## What
Conformal/e-process HARDENING (patch Rev M): the anytime-valid layer's assumptions made into explicit operational contracts — conditional calibration, drift detection, and false-coverage budgeting. The system must not advertise distribution-free protection while quietly violating exchangeability by changing design regimes.

## Scope
- MONDRIAN (conditional) calibration: conformal buckets by regime class (fs-regime's groups — the cross-layer payoff), fidelity level, geometry family, objective type, scenario cluster, solver settings — coverage guarantees PER BUCKET, not just marginal (marginal coverage can hide systematic per-regime failure).
- DRIFT DETECTION: ledger training distribution vs current candidate distribution → two-sample e-tests (sequential, anytime-valid — eating our own dogfood); on drift: automatic recalibration or escalation, surrogate validity domains SHRINK in response (Evidence validity_domain updates flow through).
- FALSE-COVERAGE-RATE BUDGETING: when thousands of candidates × objectives × constraints × time points are monitored simultaneously, coverage errors get an explicit ledger budget (analogous to the Error Ledger — e-BH machinery from fs-eproc applied to coverage claims); the budget is part of study admission (P4 extended to statistical error).
- Exchangeability accounting: which conformal claims assume what, declared on model cards; optimization-induced distribution shift (the optimizer MOVES toward regions the surrogate hasn't seen — the fundamental tension) handled by weighting/refresh policies with documented validity.

## Acceptance criteria
Per-bucket coverage verified empirically across regime shifts (certify-certifiers' shift scenarios pass); drift e-tests detect seeded covariate shift within documented sample budgets, and the escalation path fires; FCR budget accounting correct under simultaneous monitoring at flagship scale (simulation battery); optimizer-shift stress test: a deliberately surrogate-exploiting optimizer does NOT achieve silent invalid coverage (the adversarial test that matters most).

## Testing
Simulation batteries per mechanism with structured logs (bucket coverage tables, drift-detection latencies, budget ledgers); integration with fs-surrogate's online recalibration. Logs double as the calibration audit trail regulators-of-the-future would want.

title: L1 BEDROCK: numerical foundations
description:
## Mission
L1 BEDROCK: the in-house numerical foundations — dense LA (GEMM, batched small dense, factorizations, eigensolvers, randomized NLA), sparse formats/preconditioners, FFT, certified arithmetic (intervals/affine/Taylor models/exact predicates), function objects (chebfun-style), automatic differentiation, and RNG/QMC.

## Why in-house (plan §6)
Everything here is written in pure safe Rust with audited SIMD leaves because the entire point is kernels shaped for OUR data layouts (Morton tiles, SoA, arena packing) and OUR two machine families, not a 1979 Fortran calling convention. No BLAS/LAPACK/FFI (P1). FrankenScipy serves as the conformance oracle: where semantics overlap, our kernels must MATCH FrankenScipy in the Gauntlet and BEAT it on the roofline.

## Signature positions
- Batched small dense (6×6…48×48 FEM element matrices) is a first-class citizen with SIMD lanes across the batch — routinely 5–15× over loop-over-LAPACK.
- Mixed precision with iterative refinement is a default policy (factor f32, refine f64, escalate to double-double only where the Error Ledger demands).
- Matrix-free-native eigensolvers (LOBPCG/Lanczos) because modal/buckling/stability problems reduce to operator applications (P6).
- fs-ivl is what the word "Certified" means everywhere else in the system: outward-rounded intervals via next_up/next_down (thread-safe, no rounding-mode fiddling), Taylor models, Shewchuk exact predicates.

## Members
fs-rand-philox, fs-rand-qmc, fs-la-gemm, fs-la-batched, fs-la-factorizations, fs-la-eigen, fs-la-randomized, fs-la-mixed-precision, fs-sparse-core, fs-sparse-precond, fs-fft, fs-ivl-core, fs-ivl-taylor, fs-ivl-predicates, fs-cheb, fs-ad-forward, fs-ad-adjoint-infra, bedrock-conformance.

## Success Criteria
GEMM/SpMV/FFT within target roofline bands on both ISAs (see roofline-harness); G0 law suites green; FrankenScipy cross-checks green; deterministic mode bit-stable through all reductions.

Close only when the exact active closure owners .5.1, .18, .20, .21, .22, .23, .24, .25, .26, and .27 reconcile on one compatible source and constellation snapshot. This layer epic is an exact-child delegated rollup with no terminal E2E of its own and owns no aggregate terminal script. title: fs-rand: counter-based Philox streams keyed by logical identity + deterministic distributions
description:
## What
`fs-rand` core: the in-house counter-based Philox-class generator + distributions (plan §6.7) — the foundation of P2's reproducible parallel randomness.

## Scope
- Philox-class counter-based RNG (in-house, P1): stateless function of (key, counter); streams keyed by LOGICAL work identity (seed, kernel_id, tile_id, iteration) so results are independent of which worker ran which tile. SIMD-friendly bulk generation (4×/8× lanes via fs-simd).
- Stream discipline: hierarchical key derivation (study → kernel → tile → draw) with collision-free composition; splittable substreams for nested parallelism; explicit stream provenance (keys are ledgerable values — Five Explicits' "seeds" pillar).
- Distributions: uniform (open/closed variants with correct rounding), standard normal (ziggurat with deterministic table + exact tail handling), exponential, gamma, beta, Dirichlet, categorical/alias method, von Mises–Fisher (for direction sampling in rendering/GA), truncated variants. All deterministic given (key, counter) — no rejection-loop thread-order sensitivity (rejection counts are part of the counter advance contract).
- Statistical quality gates: PractRand/TestU01-class battery reimplemented as needed in-house or via documented dev-only oracle (isolated per dependency policy), run nightly.

## Why
Counter-based RNG is what makes e-raced tournaments bit-reproducible, renders replayable, and MC/UQ results independent of scheduling — the load-bearing seed story of the whole system.

## Acceptance criteria
Known-answer tests vs published Philox vectors; stream independence (statistical + collision analysis); worker-shuffle invariance test (same logical work, different thread counts → identical draws); distribution correctness (KS/chi-square vs closed forms; moments to tolerance).

## Testing
Property: key-derivation injectivity on sampled subspaces; counter-advance contracts under rejection sampling. G5: cross-thread-count hash equality. Logs: battery results, per-distribution statistics tables, seeds everywhere.

title: fs-sparse preconditioners: Chebyshev smoothers, level-scheduled ILU/IC(0), SA-AMG coarse, capped supernodal
description:
## What
`fs-sparse` preconditioner components (plan §6.2): the many-core-honest smoother/coarse-solver toolkit that solver-stack composes.

## Scope
- Chebyshev polynomial smoothers — THE many-core-friendly choice (no sequential dependencies, pure SpMV chains); eigenvalue-bound estimation (power iteration / Lanczos via fs-la-eigen) with safety factors; deterministic by construction.
- IC(0)/ILU(0) with level scheduling where serial chains are tolerable (documented as the bandwidth-hostile fallback, not the default).
- Smoothed-aggregation AMG built in-house: strength-of-connection, parallel aggregation (deterministic tie-breaking on aggregate assignment — P2 applies to setup, not just solves), tentative prolongator + Jacobi smoothing, Galerkin triple product via SpGEMM; primarily employed as the COARSE SOLVER under p-multigrid (§8.9), not as the workhorse.
- Supernodal Cholesky: deliberately minimized per P6 ("never assemble what we can apply") — exists for small coarse grids and 1D-ish problems; explicitly NOT a load-bearing wall; scope capped.
- All components expose the operator interface (apply, not matrices where avoidable) and are cancellation-clean + resumable-safe (a smoother mid-sweep can be abandoned; setup phases checkpointable).

## Acceptance criteria
Chebyshev: smoothing-factor measurements match theory on model problems; AMG: O(N)-ish setup+solve scaling demonstrated on Poisson/elasticity fixtures to 10⁸ DOF class, grid-independent iteration counts within envelope; deterministic setup across thread counts (G5); FrankenScipy baseline comparisons where overlapping.

## Testing

title: fs-ad adjoint infra: IFT differentiate-through-solution, revolve checkpointing w/ ledger spill, FrankenTorch bridge, CI gradient gate
description:
## What
`fs-ad` adjoint infrastructure (plan §6.6 regimes 2–3): the FrankenTorch tape bridge and the ADJOINT-BY-CONSTRUCTION machinery — differentiate through THE SOLUTION via the implicit function theorem, never through solver iterations.

## Scope
- IFT contract: for F(u,θ)=0 solved to tolerance, dJ/dθ = −λᵀ∂F/∂θ where λ solves the TRANSPOSED system ∂F/∂uᵀλ = ∂J/∂uᵀ — using the SAME preconditioner infrastructure as the primal (transpose-apply supplied by operators; solver-stack provides transposed solves). Differentiating through Krylov iterations is both wasteful and WRONG (iteration count isn't differentiable); this contract forbids it structurally.
- Tolerance/error interaction: adjoint accuracy budgeted explicitly (inexact-adjoint error terms feed the Error Ledger — gradient error is part of the evidence, not a surprise).
- Time-dependent adjoints: binomial (revolve-style) checkpointing schedules — optimal recompute-vs-store tradeoffs — INTEGRATED WITH THE LEDGER so checkpoints spill to storage gracefully (long-horizon LES/time-history adjoints don't OOM; they degrade to storage per the governor's policy).
- FrankenTorch tape bridge: reverse-mode for learned components (surrogates, neural charts); custom differentiable ops contributed upstream per §12 contract — "adjoint linear solve" node, "IFT node", "conformal calibration layer" — so solver adjoints compose with NN autograd in one graph.
- Verification harness (THE MERGE GATE, §8.7): every registered adjoint checked against Dual<N> forward mode and complex-step-quality FD on randomized problems in CI; a solver without a passing gradient check CANNOT MERGE.

## Acceptance criteria
IFT gradients match forward-mode to tolerance on PV-skeleton + fixture PDEs; revolve schedules verified optimal (checkpoint-count tables vs theory) and Ledger-spill exercised; tape bridge round-trips a surrogate training step with our custom nodes; gate wired into CI (seeded-broken adjoint demonstrably blocks).

## Testing
G0 adjoint-consistency laws (⟨Av,w⟩=⟨v,Aᵀw⟩ for every linearized operator); checkpoint-schedule property tests (recomputation counts); end-to-end gradient checks with tolerance model documented. Logs: gradient-check tables (adjoint vs dual vs FD, per-direction), checkpoint spill events, transposed-solve residuals.

Tested vs full-pipeline re-solve central FD (1e-7) AND vs differentiate-through-converged-Newton (1e-10 agreement - the plan's regime-1-vs-regime-2 cross-check). (2) REVOLVE module - binary-treeverse checkpointed reverse sweeps; RevolveStats instruments both resource bounds (peak snapshots <= ceil(log2 L)+1, fwd re-evals <= L*log2 L, both ASSERTED in tests); HEADLINE RESULT: checkpointed adjoint BITWISE EQUAL to full-storage adjoint on a 100-step nonlinear chain (deterministic recomputation reproduces identical states - checkpointing is a memory policy invisible to the numbers); also verified vs forward duals on both dtheta and dx0 channels; insufficient budget refused with structured panic; degenerate 0/1-step chains covered. (3) GRADCHECK module - the CI gradient-gate primitive (plan 8.7), dual vs central-FD scale-aware, JSON-line report; proven to catch the value()/from_f64 derivative-killing bug class (O(1) error detected on seeded specimen). 18/18 tests green on BOTH ISAs (trj /data/tmp/adj_verify.Wls7vD/run.log), clippy -D warnings, fmt, xtask 19 crates 0 violations, CONTRACT.md sections in force. title: Make exact CBC construction budgeted, cancellable, resumable, and certificate-producing
description:
## Background

The exact CBC repair correctly removes floating-point candidate-order ambiguity by comparing arbitrary-precision Bernoulli-B2 numerator sums. That mathematical correction increases work and memory with n, dimension, candidate count, and exact-integer limb growth. The current synchronous Lattice::cbc API accepts u32 n and arbitrary usize dimension, allocates n exact products, performs O(n^2 times dim) visits with growing multi-limb arithmetic, uses panic-style resource failures, has no explicit work/memory budget or Cx, and cannot pause/resume. Large hostile or accidental inputs can monopolize a worker or exhaust memory even though the selected vector is mathematically correct.

## Mission

Retain exact canonical ordering while turning CBC into a budget-first tile program with typed admission, bounded cancellation, resumable state, progress receipts, and an independently checkable minimality certificate. Keep the simple tabled-size convenience API only as a clearly bounded facade over the same authority; do not reintroduce floating comparison as an escape hatch.

## Required architecture

1. Define typed CbcProblem, CbcBudget, CbcState, CbcProgress, CbcCertificate, and CbcError. Admission validates n, dimension, admissible units, checked size/work bounds, limb-growth bounds, memory/capability budgets, and units before allocating or evaluating.
2. Tile work by prefix, candidate block, lattice-point block, and limb block under explicit Cx. Poll cancellation at bounded tile boundaries. Cancellation is request, drain, finalize and returns a replayable prefix with no half-committed generator.
3. Preserve exact lowest-candidate tie ordering independently of worker count, tile size, and reduction order. Candidate-score reductions use fixed logical identities and exact addition; parallel scheduling may change timing but not bytes.
4. Serialize enough exact products, candidate accumulators, prefix index, logical tile cursor, budgets spent, and canonical identities to pause, migrate, resume, and fork deterministically. Validate every limb invariant and digest before resuming.
5. Use a work/memory estimator that includes n products, candidate blocks, maximum numerator bit width, prefix-dependent product limbs, score accumulators, and receipt/certificate size. Reject inadmissible work with ranked fixes such as lower n/dim, larger budget, or a separately named approximate no-certificate mode.
6. Produce a per-prefix certificate binding the chosen candidate, exact winning score, exact runner-up score or equality class, admissible candidate set, tie rule, common-denominator derivation, and reduction root. Provide an independent checker that need not rerun the entire construction when a compact proof is available.
7. Keep korobov_error_sq explicitly diagnostic f64 unless separately certified. Exact construction must never be described as an exact floating error value.

## Theorem ratchets

[F] Develop a certificate that unit-residue permutation proves z0=1 for every admitted n and that exact numerator ordering is equivalent to the declared rational Korobov objective at each prefix.

[F/M] Investigate symmetry-orbit pruning of candidates under the unit group modulo n with a proof that the quotient preserves minima and canonical lowest representatives.

[M] Treat candidate blocks and prefix certificates as a sheaf over the lattice-point/candidate cover. Local exact score sections glue into a global minimality witness only when overlap sums, denominator identities, and canonical tie cocycles agree. Explore proof-carrying branch-and-bound or number-theoretic transforms that asymptotically beat exhaustive O(n^2 dim) enumeration without weakening exactness.

[M] Pursue verified fast convolution/FFT or character-sum formulations with interval or modular reconstruction, Chinese-remainder witnesses, and deterministic escalation to arbitrary precision when bounds do not separate candidates.

## Gauntlet

G0: ExactNat arithmetic laws against independent bounded integers and multi-limb KATs; exact B2 numerator identity; unit-residue permutation theorem instances; canonical ties; overflow-free checked admission; zero budget invokes no work.

G1/G2: published lattice KATs and independent development-only exact oracles across prime and composite n; convergence/error diagnostics remain separated from exact selection claims.

G3: invariant under candidate enumeration permutation, tile partition, worker count, equivalent rational scaling, modular residue relabeling, pause/resume splits, and symmetry-orbit expansion. Seeded mutations to scores, limbs, ties, cursor, and certificate roots fail closed.

G4: cancellation at every tile class; budgets at 0, 1, prefix boundary, candidate boundary, and limb-carry boundary; allocation denial; injected faults; no leaks; no partial chosen component.

G5: bit-stable same-ISA vectors, states, and certificates across thread counts; one-shot equals pause/resume/fork; frozen reference identities for multiple prime/composite cases.

## Completion

Production code, contracts, generated catalog/admission, unit/property/conformance/replay tests, independent certificate checker, structured logs, and central DSR/RCH proof are green. Performance evidence records machine fingerprint and exact problem/work sizes. No approximate fallback may inherit the exact-canonical capability name.
acceptance_criteria:
Hierarchy-only CBC exactness rollup. Preserve the exact dependency sequence from schedule/layout through fallible storage, limb cursor, transactional execution, canonical state, budgeted construction, certificate/checker, and .20.10. Close only when each exact child publishes its compatible immutable focused contribution and .20.10 passes the release-built no-mock E2E, bounded redacted replay logs, independent checking, and DSR. No aggregate count, static review, or narrow test substitutes for exact receipts.

title: CBC executor atomic cancellation, budget, and limb-resume semantics
description:
ROOT CAUSE: the code-first CBC executor preserves exact arithmetic bytes but its control transaction is not cancellation-correct or budget-atomic. run() can return AllowanceExhausted before polling, so repeated allowance=1 calls can starve an already-requested cancellation forever and entry is never polled. Candidate/point tiling does not bound multi-limb ExactNat add/multiply work; there is no limb cursor, so latency and allowance overshoot grow with dimension/limb width. Product/score/z mutations occur before debit validation and debit stores an over-limit total before ScheduleOverrun, so an error can leave duplicate-on-resume state. A resumed candidate can also finish and start another full point block in one tile, exceeding the documented bound.

MISSION: make each admitted execution transition a fail-closed transaction with explicit simultaneous cancellation/allowance precedence, poll at entry and after every drained atomic tile, prepay checked work before mutation, and commit accounting only with the mutation. Add a limb-block tile dimension and resumable exact-operation cursor carrying source/factor/carry/normalization progress so request -> drain -> finalize latency is bounded by declared work. Either retain unchanged replayable state on schedule refusal or enter a typed terminal poisoned state that cannot resume or emit a lattice. Make nonzero allowance a strict cap over prepaid atomic units; if a soft quantum remains, name it honestly and retain an exact overshoot theorem. Maintain cross-call candidate/point/limb counters so tile limits include resumed work.

title: CBC fallible exact storage and allocation-atomic arithmetic
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The CBC executor currently builds and grows Vec-backed ExactNat values, product tables, generator/certificate vectors, and replacement products through infallible allocation. CbcExecutor::new, reserve_exact, Vec::with_capacity, resize, clone, to_vec, and push can panic or abort rather than return a structured budget/capability refusal. Product and certificate transitions can remove or mutate authoritative state before later allocations complete. An admitted byte count is not useful if the implementation cannot fail closed when the allocator refuses it.

MISSION
Create one fallible storage authority for base exact-CBC execution. Introduce try_new and checked try-reserve/try-allocate paths; define whether the receipt governs requested payload, observed Vec capacity, allocator usable size, or a conservative arena/slab envelope. Prefer fixed-capacity/slab or capacity-preserving buffers so admitted operations do not reallocate. Make ExactNat add/multiply/normalize transitions transactional: preflight required limbs and allocation, compute into admitted scratch, then atomically commit, leaving source and executor bytes unchanged on any failure. Never use allocation panic as resource admission.

DELIVERABLES
- Typed allocation/storage refusal carrying storage class, requested/admitted/observed counts, phase/cursor, target layout identity, and ranked remediation.
- Fallible construction for product owners/payloads, scores, generator, scratch, and progress metadata.
- Capacity-preserving exact arithmetic or an explicitly charged old/new overlap protocol.
- A storage receipt whose schema/version/target assumptions are bound to the shared CbcExecutionSchedule authority from .20.4.
- A no-allocation hot transition once admission succeeds, or precisely metered separately admitted allocation points.
- No partial prefix, candidate, score, product, certificate, work counter, or progress mutation on refusal.

GAUNTLET
G0 exact required-capacity and one-under KATs for zero/one/maximum limb widths, n=3 d=1 overlap, composite/prime moduli, and every storage class. G3 one-shot versus arbitrary successful allocation schedule equality. G4 deterministic injected denial at every allocation point, byte-for-byte pre/post executor state, no leak/double drop/panic, and retry equivalence after capacity remediation. Include checked usize/address-space boundaries and allocator rounding observations under the declared semantics. Structured JSONL diagnostics must log phase, cursor, requested/admitted counts, schedule identity, and verdict without unescaped fields.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
No claim of allocation-failure recovery, exact actual allocator capacity, no-reallocation execution, or mutation-free storage refusal. This task does not by itself establish cancellation latency, strict run allowance, cross-process state, or certified-mode storage.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Admit empty, minimum, boundary, and maximum CBC storage layouts and retain exact executor, capacity, lease, and charge state.
2. Inject deterministic allocation denial at each construction, reserve, resize, clone, push, arithmetic-scratch, replacement-product, generator, progress, and certificate allocation point.
3. Exercise ExactNat add/multiply/normalize and executor transitions at exact capacity and one limb/byte beyond it, then retry after an explicitly admitted capacity increase.
4. Compare pre/post bytes, live charges, drops, progress, result, and bounded diagnostic fields.
5. The defect is reproduced if any path panics/aborts, leaks or double-drops, mutates an authoritative prefix before refusal, exceeds the admitted storage semantics, or cannot retry deterministically.

title: CBC limb microcursor and bounded exact-arithmetic polling
description:
ROOT CAUSE
Candidate_block and point_block bound outer loops but each ExactNat add-multiply, carry propagation, zero fill, comparison, normalization, and product replacement remains monolithic in limb width. Thus cancellation latency and allowance overshoot grow with dimension/product width even when point_block=1. Local candidate counters also reset across calls, so an already-running candidate plus new work can cross the intended observation envelope.

MISSION
Express every exact arithmetic primitive as a deterministic resumable microprogram with a persistent limb cursor. Extend the tile contract with limb_block and explicit operation classes. Each microstep must have a checked, prepaid schedule charge, bounded memory access, deterministic source/destination/carry state, and a well-defined commit boundary. Poll spacing must be bounded by admitted microsteps rather than by an unbounded big-integer operation. Persist candidate, point, source-limb, factor-limb, destination-limb, carry, zero-fill, comparison, and normalization progress as needed without changing final arithmetic bytes or lowest-candidate ties.

DELIVERABLES
- Versioned LimbCursor/ExactOpState enum with invariants for add-multiply, carry, compare, normalize, and product update.
- CbcTileShape limb_block or a typed nested tile budget with nonzero checked admission.
- Mechanical mapping from each microstep to the .20.4 schedule identity and exact charge class.
- Persistent per-call candidate/point/limb counters so resumed work consumes the same tile envelope as fresh work.
- Drain/finalize boundary semantics for a partially advanced exact operation; public prefixes remain whole-component only.
- Progress receipt fields exposing logical operation/cursors without leaking mutable internal buffers.

GAUNTLET
G0 state-machine transition laws, carry chains spanning every limb, all-zero/high-limb normalization, equal/less/greater comparisons, and zero/one/exact/one-under limb blocks. G3 final lattice, work totals, certificates where enabled, and progress roots equal across one-shot and adversarial partitions of candidate/point/limb tile shapes. G4 cancel at entry and every microstep class, maximum observed operations between polls <= declared bound, huge-width/adversarial-dimension fixtures, no half-committed arithmetic, and deterministic retry. G5 same-target bytes across thread counts and split schedules.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
No bounded cancellation latency or limb-bounded allowance theorem exists until this task and the strict runner task are both green. This task alone does not define allocator failure, sealed cross-process state, or certificate publication.

title: CBC strict transactional runner, cancellation precedence, and progress receipts
description:
ROOT CAUSE
run currently executes before its first poll, checks exhausted allowance before cancellation at a shared boundary, uses saturating subtraction so an atomic tile can overspend an arbitrarily small allowance, and debits after arithmetic/prefix mutation. debit stores an over-limit work_spent before returning ScheduleOverrun. These choices can starve a pre-requested cancellation, make nonzero allowance a soft threshold, and leave state changed after a refusal.

MISSION
Define and implement a fail-closed run transaction over the shared schedule and limb microcursor. Poll at entry. State an explicit simultaneous-event precedence, with cancellation observable even at an exhausted-allowance boundary. Preflight and prepay every atomic microstep before mutation; commit the work counter and state transition together. A strict allowance must never be exceeded. If a requested allowance is smaller than the next indivisible admitted step, return a typed NeedAllowance carrying the exact minimum without executing it. Schedule identity mismatch/overrun must leave replayable bytes unchanged or enter an explicit terminal poison state that cannot resume or publish results.

DELIVERABLES
- Versioned run protocol and precedence table for AlreadyComplete, invalid tile, pre-cancel, zero allowance, NeedAllowance, cancellation, completion, storage refusal, schedule mismatch, and panic/fault containment.
- Per-run progress receipt binding before/after state roots, schedule identity, allowance requested/used/remaining, exact transition counts, last boundary, poll count/maximum spacing, and finalization status.
- request -> drain -> finalize semantics; no silent drop and no result publication before final receipt.
- Exact per-call candidate/point/limb limits including carried work from prior calls.
- Mutation-free failure or irreversible typed poison with a checker-enforced publication ban.

GAUNTLET
G0 zero, one, exact, and one-under allowances for every charge class; pre-cancelled positive and zero allowance; cancellation-versus-allowance same-boundary precedence; Completed lattice validation; monotone exact counters. G3 one-shot equals repeated minimum-allowance calls and arbitrary pause/resume in result/state/progress roots. G4 ScheduleOverrun/storage/panic injection before every commit, byte-identical pre/post refusal, cancellation at every boundary, bounded poll spacing, drain completion, no leaks, and no duplicate-on-retry mutation. Logs must show structured before/after roots and exact charge evidence. G5 same-target receipt and result stability.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Current AllowanceExhausted is a soft quantum, not a strict cap. Do not claim entry cancellation, cancellation precedence, mutation-free ScheduleOverrun, exact per-run work, or progress-receipt completeness before this task closes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Admit a scheduled CBC run and retain the exact before-state root, schedule identity, allowance, counters, and expected next microstep charge.
2. Exercise AlreadyComplete, invalid tile, pre-cancel, zero, one-under, exact, and one-over allowances plus simultaneous cancellation/allowance exhaustion.
3. Inject schedule mismatch, storage refusal, panic, and worker fault immediately before every candidate/point/limb and publication commit; retry from the returned state or typed poison.
4. Compare the progress receipt, poll spacing, debit, committed prefix, finalization, after-state root, and one-shot versus repeated-minimum-allowance replay.
5. The defect is reproduced if work occurs before entry polling, allowance is exceeded, cancellation loses the declared precedence, refusal mutates replayable bytes, retry duplicates debit/work, poison can publish, or final results/receipts vary by schedule.

## Acceptance Criteria

Own planned crates/fs-rand/tests/cbc_transactional_runner.rs. Prove atomic candidate/generator publication, exact committed-prefix semantics, request-drain-finalize cancellation, callback and worker faults, one-before/exact/one-after budgets, panic containment, idempotent retry, no duplicate debit, no half-state, leak freedom, deterministic schedules, and mutation/tamper refusal. Publish an immutable transactional-runner contribution for .20.10; no standalone final or E2E authority is claimed.

title: CBC canonical state serialization, resume, fork, and budget anti-reissuance
description:
MISSION
Make an in-flight exact-CBC construction a portable, authenticated, invariant-checked artifact that can pause, migrate, resume, and fork deterministically without reissuing consumed work/memory authority. The current executor value is process-local and explicitly makes no cross-process claim.

STATE CONTRACT
Canonical bytes must bind problem, admitted budgets, target/layout compatibility class, admission/execution/certificate schema identities, schedule digest, committed prefix, product/score exact limbs, phase, candidate/point/limb microcursors, carry/scratch state, work spent, allowance ledger, progress-chain root, certificate mode/storage authority, determinism mode, and implementation/theorem versions. Decode must be bounded and iterative; every length/count/product is checked before allocation. Normalize or reject noncanonical exact integers, signed zero/NaN where applicable, duplicate encodings, impossible cursor combinations, stale schedules, truncated/trailing bytes, and unsupported versions.

BUDGET / FORK SEMANTICS
A resume must not mint fresh admitted work or forget prior debits. Define non-reissuable budget authority and idempotent continuation keys. Forks share immutable source/admission identity but receive explicitly partitioned or newly authorized remaining budgets; a byte copy cannot double-spend authority. State roots and parent/fork lineage enter the ledger/progress receipt.

DELIVERABLES
- Versioned CbcState canonical encoder/decoder and collision-resistant domain-separated identity using project identity authority.
- Independent state checker that validates structural/arithmetic/cursor invariants without advancing the solver.
- pause/resume/migrate/fork APIs with explicit capability and target-compatibility refusals.
- Idempotent continuation/publication protocol and lineage receipts.
- Structured explain diagnostics and ranked fixes for stale version, incompatible target, insufficient budget, corrupt state, or ambiguous authority.

GAUNTLET
G0 canonical round trip for every phase/microcursor and empty/boundary state; exact byte goldens; malformed/noncanonical corpus; identity-field mutation matrix. G3 one-shot equals serialize/deserialize after every transition class, repeated migrations, and legal forks in final lattice/certificates/progress roots. G4 truncation/resource bombs, allocation denial, corruption, stale schedule/source, panic containment, duplicate continuation, fork double-spend attempts, cancellation during encode/finalize, and no partial publication. G5 bit-stable same-ISA bytes across thread counts; explicit cross-ISA compatibility/refusal evidence.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
No cross-process replay, authenticated resume, fork determinism, budget anti-reissuance, or durable progress identity. A raw Debug/serde-like snapshot is insufficient.

## Acceptance Criteria

Own planned crates/fs-rand/tests/cbc_state_replay.rs. Cover canonical state schema and versioning, every cursor boundary, pause/migrate/resume/fork, exact RNG and budget continuation, stale/mixed identities, malformed lengths, counter regression or reuse, tamper/truncation/reordering, cancellation/fault during encode/decode/publication, atomic replacement, and same-ISA deterministic replay. Publish an immutable state contribution for .20.10 with explicit cross-ISA and no-claim policy.

Cover canonical state schema and versioning, every cursor boundary, pause/migrate/resume/fork, exact RNG and budget continuation, stale/mixed identities, malformed lengths, counter regression or reuse, tamper/truncation/reordering, cancellation/fault during encode/decode/publication, atomic replacement, and same-ISA deterministic replay. title: CBC separately admitted certificate execution and atomic publication
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The landed cbc_cert checker is a useful independent leaf, but CbcExecutor::enable_certificates currently exposes certificate production on the base executor while explicitly placing runner-up retention, tie-class growth, prefix clones, score to_vec, certificate Vec growth, and publication outside admission. Those allocations and copies occur after best.take in places, are not cancellation/limb bounded, are absent from state serialization, and can panic or leave a nonresumable transaction. Schema-v4 naming is already being consumed by base schedule/layout work, so certified mode needs an explicit distinct authority/version.

MISSION
Create a separately admitted certified-execution mode that accounts for every extra operation and byte, uses the same strict transactional runner/microcursor/storage/state authorities, and publishes each certificate atomically only after an independently checkable receipt is complete. Preserve the full minimality-by-exhaustion checker and its honest distinction from compact consistency; pursue compact subquadratic/sheaf-glued minimality proofs as a gated theorem ratchet, not as an excuse to weaken exhaustive checking.

DELIVERABLES
- Typed CbcCertificateBudget/admission receipt with separate schema identity and exact worst-case/prefix-specific tie, runner-up, prefix, limb, receipt, and output storage/work bounds.
- Fallible preallocated certificate construction; no clone/push/to_vec outside authority.
- Cancellation/resume/fork-aware certificate cursor and atomic publish transaction bound to base state/progress roots.
- Certificate identity binding n, exact reduction root/prefix, chosen/tie/runner-up scores, admissible/tie rules, denominator derivation, checker/schema/theorem versions, and execution schedule identity.
- Chain validation: a later prefix certificate is conditional on its declared root unless earlier selections are independently linked; no accidental claim that an arbitrary prefix is the canonical CBC history.
- Keep verify_consistency and audit_minimality names/no-claims precise; independently validate the first-component theorem or emit its explicit no-claim.

GAUNTLET
G0 exact certified-mode admission KATs including maximal tie classes and score widths; malformed/noncanonical limbs; first-prefix/root rules. G3 certified vs uncertified lattice equality and certificate equality across tile/allowance/resume/fork shapes. G4 injected denial at every certificate allocation/publication step, cancellation through tie/runner-up/copy/check phases, byte-identical retry, no partial certificate, no lost best, and strict work caps. Mutation batteries cover prefix/root/history, n, score limbs, tie completeness/order, runner-up minimality, rules, denominator, schema/checker identity, schedule identity, and retained content roots. G5 durable state/certificate bytes under admitted determinism.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Base enable_certificates is not budget-covered or allocation-failure-safe. Consistency mode does not prove global minimality; an isolated later certificate proves selection only relative to its declared prefix unless history is linked. No compact subquadratic proof claim without its own checker and evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

Own planned crates/fs-rand/tests/cbc_certificate_execution.rs. Independently reconstruct schedule, debits, generator bytes, full minimality obligations, state invariants, and authority without reusing producer decision logic. Unit/property/falsifier/mutation/tamper tests must reject every missing, stale, reordered, forged, budget-inconsistent, or checker-disagreeing field and preserve typed Unknown/no-claim on exhaustion. Publish the immutable certificate/checker contribution for .20.10; only the terminal E2E may promote joined authority.

## Contribution-only terminal routing clarification

This leaf owns the independent CBC certificate/checker implementation test contribution, not a terminal shell route. It contributes immutable rows to `frankensim-epic-bedrock-6ys.20.10`, which already solely owns `scripts/ci/e2e_cbc_exact.sh` and its check/self-test/smoke/full/negative/replay modes. The downstream owner exact-joins this contribution and independently executes it; this Bead cannot claim that downstream E2E ran or promote joined authority. Unit/property/mutation/fault/logging/replay/source-closure contribution proof remains mandatory and separate from terminal proof.

title: fs-sparse production cancellation migration: Cx protocol, kernels, assembly, downstream consumers, and acceptance
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Current reality and defect

`fs-sparse` has real CSR/BSR/SELL correctness and performance code and is registered at L1 BEDROCK, but its production numeric kernels do not accept an explicit `Cx`; once admitted, long SpMV/SpMM/assembly/preconditioner work is uninterruptible. That violates the repository-wide tile-program and request-drain-finalize contract and leaves a P0 cancellation hole even if the generic executor storm suite passes.

## End state

Every production sparse hot path used by the P0 performance lane and downstream solvers executes through an explicit cancellation-aware API with checked work and memory admission, bounded polling at deterministic row/block/tile boundaries, transactional publication, and structured consumption/finalization evidence. Existing fixture helpers may remain only if their non-production/no-cancellation status is explicit and production callers cannot reach them accidentally.

## Scope

- Inventory public CSR, BSR, SELL-C-sigma, SpMV, SpMM, deterministic assembly, conversion, smoother/preconditioner, and performance entry points; classify fixture-only versus production.
- Introduce layer-correct `Cx`/scope integration without making BEDROCK depend on HELM. Derive a deterministic poll plan from logical work identity, not worker timing.
- Admit checked dimensions, nnz, block sizes, row widths, output extents, pair/multiply-add work, scratch bytes, and finalization reserve before allocation or mutation.
- Poll at bounded row/block/tile boundaries and inside pathologically wide rows. Avoid a cancellation bound proportional to an attacker-controlled row length.
- Use fallible allocation and output staging so cancel, panic, budget exhaustion, non-finite policy failure, or worker error publishes no mixed old/new vector or half-built matrix.
- Preserve deterministic reduction/order guarantees and documented fast-mode differences across thread counts.
- Integrate the actual P0 SpMV measurement route; a cancellable wrapper around an uncancellable timed kernel is insufficient.

## Failure semantics and no-claim

Return typed distinctions for invalid shape/index, work-budget refusal, memory refusal, cancellation requested, cancellation finalized, numeric-policy failure, and internal fault. Retain completed-work and poll-count evidence without claiming wall-clock latency from a logical checkpoint bound. The <=200 microsecond hardware claim belongs to the G4/host evidence lane and remains unproven until measured.

## Tests and detailed logging

G0 covers empty, one-row, maximum legal extents, duplicate assembly, unsorted indices, invalid offsets/columns, overflow, NaN/Inf policy, CSR/BSR/SELL agreement, and deterministic ties. Property tests compare every production format to an independent scalar oracle. G3 covers row/column permutations and equivalent format conversions. G4 injects cancellation before admission, allocation, first tile, inside an ultra-wide row, between blocks, during reduction, and before publication; also inject allocation failure and worker panic. Assert bounded checkpoint work, full drain, exact-once lease return, unchanged destination on failure, no task/arena leaks, and deterministic structured logs. G5 compares output bits, poll plan, consumed work, and final receipt across required thread counts and repeated runs. Add a no-mock downstream solver/roofline integration test proving the measured production path consumes the new API.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect the public production entry points in `crates/fs-sparse/src` and the cancellation/no-claim section of `crates/fs-sparse/CONTRACT.md`; the hot CSR/BSR/SELL assembly, SpMV, and SpMM kernels accept dimensions/data but no explicit `Cx` or cancellation token. 2. Construct a legal matrix with one pathologically wide row or a large repeated production SpMV workload under an already-cancelled parent scope. 3. Invoke the current production API: no call can propagate the scope into the numeric loop, so work runs to its ordinary return instead of bounded request-drain-finalize. 4. Confirm downstream P0 roofline callers time the same uncancellable path. Preserve this as a failing behavioral/compile-time fixture until the new API lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

All production CSR/BSR/SELL assembly, SpMV, SpMM, and P0-timed paths use explicit Cx-aware, checked-work/memory APIs; polling is bounded even for a maximum legal wide row; cancel/fault/allocation refusal drains and preserves transactional outputs; deterministic results and poll receipts reproduce across required thread counts; focused and downstream no-mock G0/G3/G4/G5 suites plus DSR pass with retained logs.

## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set: `crates/fs-sparse/src`, `crates/fs-sparse/tests`, `crates/fs-sparse/CONTRACT.md`, and only the minimal lower-layer `fs-exec`/roofline consumers required to expose the real production path. Do not edit HELM to smuggle cancellation downward. Prove package tests plus downstream solver and roofline integration with the shared RCH target-dir convention, then run constellation preflight and DSR. Hand the final cancellation/performance receipt to `huq.21`.

## Success Criteria

All four child migrations close; the production callsite inventory contains no uncancellable sparse bypass; scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh exercises real solver and roofline consumers with no mocks; bounded wide-row polling, checked admission, request-drain-finalize semantics, exact-once resource return, transactional publication, cross-format correctness, G5 identity, and every injected-failure twin pass with canonical replay logs; focused crates and the required DSR lane are green.

## Phase 9.5 roll-up structure

Children 21.1 through 21.4 separately own the Cx protocol, production kernels, assembly/conversion, and downstream consumers. Cancellation request is never a premature terminal return: the API returns only after drain/finalization with a typed final receipt and completed-work accounting. The global G4 harness consumes this completed migration. The umbrella closes only after every child and `scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh` prove real solver and roofline paths with no bypass.
design:
Canonical sparse migration design after authority-lifetime reality check

21.1 owns the reusable authority protocol; 21.2 and 21.3 consume it in parallel for numeric kernels and construction/conversion; 21.4 composes both through real preconditioner, solver, checkpoint, and roofline users. No child may recreate Cx, worker completion, memory admission, publication, receipt, or inventory authority locally. The callsite ratchet maps every production route to exactly one migration owner and fails on an unowned or downgraded route.

Publication policies are explicit and non-interchangeable. Default numeric results, matrices, maps, final solver results, and benchmark-visible outputs are InvocationAtomic. Independently durable checkpoints or caches may use preselected ChildLocal only through a separately named result carrying a partial/no-final-result claim; they cannot convert into root success. Committed-prefix output is unavailable until a later separately typed contract. Root failure exposes no raw scientific output: retryable private state is only opaque Unpublished bound to the same root, while a resume starts a new admitted invocation from a verified checkpoint input.

Successful artifacts remain coupled to authority. PublishedAllocation privately owns the registered value/storage inventory and PublishedTransfer; PublishedInvocation adds the finalized receipt. PublicationSlot is Vacant or Installed, uses checked bounded adoption or checked cross-root reparent before work, returns no displacement on first install, and returns guarded DisplacedPublication on replacement. Read and consuming handoff preserve authority; extraction, raw parts, mutable growth, or detached serialization do not. Matrix bundles publish matrix storage plus every required permutation/map/metadata artifact as one registered bundle. Solver/preconditioner caches that should survive a later solve failure are built as their own root or explicit ChildLocal artifact, never as an accidental leak from the default final-result transaction.

Kernel in-place alpha/beta workflows retain their semantics through typed slots. Owned-return is the ergonomic default. Legacy raw mutable-buffer helpers may remain temporarily only as inventory-classified compatibility routes with explicit weaker/no-root-evidence diagnostics and one later migration owner; they cannot serve P0 timing, solver, or proof paths. Slot readers see one coherent generation, rollback restores the previous occupant before unlock, and no user destructor runs while a slot lock is held.

The one E2E runner, `scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh`, freezes the exact catalog `api-inventory|runtime-canary|kernels-p0|assembly-conversion|consumer-solver|all` and canonical commands: `--list`; `--check`; `--self-test`; `--run smoke|full --family-mode MODE --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`; `--negative CASE` with the same output pair; and `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT` with a disjoint output pair. The former quick corpus migrates explicitly and byte/semantically to smoke; `quick`, `--mode`, and `--profile` are not aliases. 21.1.4 owns api-inventory/runtime-canary, 21.2 kernels-p0, 21.3 assembly-conversion, and terminal 21.4 consumer-solver plus the sole registered `--family-mode all`; registered modes refuse until their owner closes. Only successfully preflighted commands emit capped canonical lifecycle records; invalid argv/aliases exit Usage with empty lifecycle stdout and one bounded stderr diagnostic. Declared benchmark durations/counters are typed evidence or capped artifacts; wall-clock timestamps and undeclared host timing are nonsemantic.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical sparse migration acceptance criteria

1. 21.1-.4 close under their own current canonical fields and current-snapshot proof. Historical Phase 9.5 PASS/FINAL comments are superseded and are not evidence.
2. The complete source-verified inventory has zero unclassified production paths, fixture escape, unknown helper, ownerless migration, expired exemption, Cx bypass, publication downgrade, or benchmark-only route. Stable anchors survive line movement. Set evolution is change-controlled: unreviewed/ownerless/downgraded growth fails; reviewed additions carry owner, rationale, features, review/expiry or migration target and preserve prior evidence; removals cannot erase evidence or functionality.
3. Every CSR/BSR/SELL SpMV/SpMM, assembly/conversion, smoother/preconditioner/AMG, solver, checkpoint/resume, fs-wasm, and P0 roofline path consumes checked plan, explicit Cx, exact run/child/memory/publication authorities, and verified receipts rather than recreating them.
4. Default outputs are InvocationAtomic and authority-bearing. ChildLocal is explicit/preselected/nonconvertible; committed-prefix remains unavailable. Retryable root failure exposes only opaque same-root Unpublished recovery, never raw or retroactively relabeled output.
5. PublishedAllocation/PublishedInvocation/PublicationSlot/DisplacedPublication preserve value-transfer-receipt coupling through Vacant first install, checked adoption/reparent, repeated replacement, coherent read, consuming handoff, later drop, and panic/forget fail-closed. Unregistered transitive storage and external post-return copies/mutations are no-claims.
6. Checked plan arithmetic covers every logical/physical work, padded traffic, shape/index, sort/conversion candidate, worker/run/poll/finalizer, scratch/staging/output, allocation-layout, overlap, and publication-envelope term. Zero/max/exact/minus-one/plus-one cases do not require huge allocations and refuse before work/mutation on failure.
7. Bounded polling includes attacker-controlled wide rows, block/slice loops, sort/reduction phases, coarsening/setup, iterative applies, convergence checks, checkpointing, and publication. Request is distinct from drain/finalize; all registered work joins and resources quiesce before terminal return.
8. Successful assembly publishes one canonical matrix bundle including required maps/permutations/metadata; failures leave prior artifacts unchanged and leak no orphan. Final solve output is root atomic; independently durable checkpoints/caches are separately admitted typed artifacts with honest no-final-convergence claim.
9. Unit/property/metamorphic/model/compile-fail/mutation/concurrency/fault suites cover all formats, shape/index/numeric policies, alpha/beta/overwrite, signed zero, duplicates/order, padding/tails, thread counts, exact authorities/partitions, adoption/reparent/handoff/drop, cancellation/deadline/fault/unwind, rollback/late request, retry/resume, bypasses, and receipt forgery.
10. Real no-mock E2E traverses admitted assembly -> format conversion -> preconditioner/AMG setup -> repeated production SpMV/SpMM -> convergence or typed refusal -> checkpoint/resume -> final publication, then the identical kernel route through P0 roofline. It includes active, pre/mid/terminal cancellation and every injected allocation/worker/numeric/transfer/publication/checkpoint fault.
11. E2E covers canonical list/check/self-test; smoke/full `--run` for api-inventory/runtime-canary/kernels-p0/assembly-conversion/consumer-solver/all; frozen negative cases; artifact-only replay with separate input/output roots; and explicit quick-to-smoke migration. Successfully preflighted commands have exact exits/barriers/record counts/caps/inventory/manifest/seal and parser/forgery mutants. Invalid argv, `quick`, `--mode`, and `--profile` exit Usage with empty lifecycle stdout and one bounded stderr diagnostic. Every semantic u64/u128 uses {value,unit,width}; source/constellation/build/toolchain/target/features and all authority/artifact roots are bound; sensitive host data is excluded while declared benchmark quantities remain typed evidence.
12. Performance samples use the same admitted production route, exclude setup only where the frozen protocol says so, retain raw samples and host/load/freshness receipts outside semantic identity, and never substitute an uncancellable or benchmark-only loop.
13. Focused strict-remote Cargo proof is reported separately from scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --verify-only and dsr quality --tool frankensim. Exact commands, terminal result, run-log/artifact path, source HEAD before/after, sibling-pin drift, and any not-run gate are recorded; no shared sibling checkout is repinned to manufacture a pass.
14. No child closes on formatting, static scanning, a synthetic fixture, a stale receipt, a precursor snapshot, or historical comments alone. Parent closes only when all modes and the no-bypass union pass on one stable declared revision.
15. The union runner inherits huq.24 ProofExitV2, case/run-terminal separation, literal caps and stricter family caps, artifact-dir safety, strict parser/tamper matrix, and one-below/exact/one-above tests; each scientific invocation seal remains case evidence rather than the final run terminal.
notes:
2026-07-28 live metadata correction: fs-sparse is L1 BEDROCK, not L2. Protocol implementation is now gated by 21.1.1-.4 so finalizer, real TilePool completion, and memory authority claims are provided by fs-exec/fs-alloc rather than fabricated in sparse.

Canonical 2026-07-28 plan-space correction: the design and acceptance fields above supersede comments 2876, 2922, and 2968 as proof claims. They preserve every format, alpha/beta behavior, assembly/conversion, preconditioner/AMG, checkpoint/resume, solver, fs-wasm, and P0 performance route while replacing ambiguous raw transactional output with explicit authority-bearing root-atomic and preselected partial policies.

Distinct 60-minute estimate covers final cross-child root join, runner-mode completeness check, and closeout review; implementation remains counted on descendants.
The parent inventory policy now permits reviewed feature growth, and runner sealing is explicit at both case and run levels.

Canonical artifact placement inheritance: every artifact-dir or --artifact-dir shorthand in this Bead expands to huq.24.1's required pair --artifact-root ROOT --artifact-dir REL. ROOT is an admitted/canonicalized existing caller-owned workspace, external-volume, or temp directory; REL is a relative-safe new or empty destination. Bundle manifests retain only relative paths, host-specific absolute ROOT is non-semantic/redacted, and omission, escape, link/reparse race, nonempty overwrite, or root mismatch refuses with ranked repair. Candidate runner evidence consumes huq.24.4; authority-bearing final gates additionally consume huq.24.5.

title: Sparse Cx protocol foundation: finalizer/drain/memory authorities, checked plans, callsite inventory, and receipts
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Current reality

The sparse cancellation protocol cannot be implemented honestly as a thin wrapper over the current tree. `fs-exec` already supplies strong `Cx`, invocation accounting, leases, scoped worker joins, and generic receipts, but four composition boundaries must be proven together:

1. reserved finalizer authority that remains spendable only for bounded cleanup after cancellation/refusal;
2. executor-minted completion evidence from the actual TilePool lifecycle plus affine per-run occurrence permits;
3. one serialized memory hierarchy that delegates a single admitted envelope to real allocations without double charging and separates returned from published bytes;
4. invocation-root atomic artifact publication with checked plan/occurrence, complete ordered run and child partitions, bounded prospective evidence, rollback, and a finalized receipt.

Without these, sparse code could appear Cx-aware while returning before finalization, replaying equivalent runs as distinct occurrences, fabricating drain booleans, leaking failed output through recovery, retaining a changed destination under root failure, or lying about memory admission/conservation.

## End state

Every sparse migration child consumes one layer-correct protocol: explicit `Cx`; affine work/finalizer/run/memory/publication authorities; deterministic checked plans and poll bounds; real ordered worker-completion evidence; default `InvocationAtomic` staged or owned artifact results; explicitly preselected weaker `ChildLocal` partial publication; returned-plus-published memory conservation; sparse evidence joined to verified generic receipts; and a canonical publication-aware callsite ratchet. No second scheduler, cancellation gate, resource ledger, or HELM dependency is introduced.

This epic is prerequisite foundation, not the final kernel migration claim. CSR/BSR/SELL kernels remain 21.2; assembly/conversion/densification/optional interop remain 21.3; preconditioners/AMG/solvers/LinearOp/nested fs-wasm/benchmarks/zero-bypass closure remain 21.4. The umbrella 21 retains the complete migrated end-to-end gate.

## Child structure and ownership

### 21.1.2 — TilePool completion foundation

Instrument actual std/asupersync/parked launch/join paths and return verified `WitnessedRun` bundles. Standalone runs preserve an explicit cross-issuer uniqueness no-claim; invocation-bound runs consume one affine permit per declared ordinal. This leaf owns its focused producer/parser and may close independently.

### 21.1.3 — allocator delegation and PublishedTransfer foundation

Provide one serialized affine hierarchy, real allocation charges, close/seal verifiers, u128 cumulative accounting, and exact `granted = returned + published` terminal partition. No TilePool dependency exists. This leaf owns its focused producer/parser and may close independently.

### 21.1.1 — invocation/finalizer join

Reserve cleanup authority; bind plan and occurrence; mint ordered run permits; verify complete run and child partitions with one designated publisher; join worker and allocator receipts; distinguish ChildLocal from InvocationAtomic; implement opaque retry-only `Unpublished<T>`; and return typed in-place or owned results plus finalized receipt. This leaf owns the combined fs-exec protocol runner and depends on 21.1.2/21.1.3.

### 21.1.4 — sparse checked protocol, inventory, and current runtime canary

Define sparse plan/error/evidence/result types; consume the joined authority; inventory every API/callsite with route plus publication scope; preserve read-only CSR validation; add real sentinel destination and owned-return journeys; and wire current API/inventory runtime proof into a focused strict-remote/DSR lane now. Later migrated kernel/assembly/solver modes remain reserved and fail clearly.

## Shared publication and recovery invariants

Cancellation request is an event, not completion. Terminal success requires declared run witnesses, completed output-free siblings, executor joins, transient resource quiescence, prepared transfer, finalizer seal, artifact publication, and receipt verification.

In-place publication privately swaps through an exclusive slot and performs the named post-swap atomic terminal observation; a terminal value at that load wins and rolls back, while a later request loses. Owned-return keeps the object private, observes terminal state, commits transfer, then moves it to the caller. No fallible work, callback, lock, hashing, allocation, formatting, or user destructor occurs after successful observation before cache/visibility.

Retryable failure may return only opaque, private-field, must-use `Unpublished<T>` bound to the same root. It has diagnostic metadata but no extraction, borrowing, dereference, destructuring, serialization, erasure, or conversion to T, ChildLocal, or published output. It can only retry through the same protocol or be discarded. ChildLocal is selected explicitly before execution and cannot be retrofitted after root failure.

Completed nonpublishing siblings are allowed only when verified Completed/output-free. Failed/cancelled/refused/missing/duplicate/additional publishers block root success. Plans bind bounded ordered 0/1/many runs; missing/duplicate/reordered/replayed/extra permits or witnesses refuse.

Memory seal requires no live transient delegation and an exact live-published partition. Destination output may remain alive after invocation seal; later drop closes its own authority without rewriting terminal evidence. RSS, allocator metadata, external threads/work, arbitrary I/O/global side effects, deliberate forget, and process termination remain explicit no-authority/no-liveness boundaries unless separately registered and charged.

## Tests and evidence

Every child includes comprehensive zero/exact/one-over/max-representable boundaries, property tests, short lifecycle models, compile-fail/API authority checks, cancellation/fault/unwind/retry/reuse, forgery/root verification, seeded mutants, deterministic barriers, and capped canonical logs. Coverage includes 0-2 children/workers/runs, all plan arithmetic, dedicated nested-output policy errors, complete partitions, no early evidence, allocation/transfer faults, rollback/late request, panic-on-drop sentinels, opaque retry/discard, exact memory conservation, live output/later drop, post-seal refusal, and bounded deep/wide verification.

Every semantic u64/u128 JSON value uses `{value:"...",unit:"...",width:"u64|u128"}` with exact 2^53/u64/u128 boundary and malformed-parser tests. Logs retain stable source/build/toolchain/case/identity/lifecycle/result/no-claim fields, exact order/count, one proof seal, and capped stdout/stderr/artifacts; host noise and secrets are excluded.

The current sparse API/inventory runtime canary and static inventory ratchet are required focused strict-remote/DSR proof before 21.1.4 closes. Only the later migrated kernel/assembly/solver runtime modes wait for 21.2-21.4. Zero legacy production bypass remains the later 21.4/parent-21 acceptance, so this foundation does not pre-claim migrations.

## Acceptance Criteria

All four children close under their canonical design/acceptance fields and strict current-snapshot proof. The publication-aware inventory has no unclassified, duplicate, stale, fixture-misclassified, ownerless, newly uncancellable, or default-to-child-local downgrade; migration-pending rows have one later owner and only shrink. Combined unit/property/model/compile-fail/mutation/scanner/runtime/receipt/logging gates pass, including the current staged and owned API/inventory DSR canary. Historical Phase 9.5 FINAL/PASS comments are superseded.
design:
Canonical umbrella design after reality check

The foundation is a four-layer authority composition, not a generic Cx wrapper. 21.1.3 supplies one serialized affine allocator hierarchy, close/seal receipts, and returned-plus-published transfer partition. 21.1.2 supplies real TilePool `WitnessedRun` evidence and one-shot per-run permits with standalone no-claim compatibility. 21.1.1 binds plan/occurrence, joins bounded ordered run and complete child partitions, preserves explicit ChildLocal, and supplies default affine InvocationAtomic results. 21.1.4 consumes them in sparse plans, publication-aware inventory, and staged/owned artifact E2E.

One abstract terminal decision has two realizations. In-place privately swaps through an exclusive slot and uses post-swap atomic terminal observation with rollback. Owned-return keeps the object private, observes terminal state, commits transfer, then moves it to caller. No fallible work or user destructor occurs after successful observation before cache/visibility.

Plans declare bounded ordered 0/1/many runs and receipts bind every run/child once plus designated publisher. Completed nonpublishing siblings must be Completed/output-free; failed/cancelled/refused/missing/duplicate/additional publishers block success. Dropped tokens restore admission-closed retry with new generation; forget/process/external side effects are no-liveness/no-authority boundaries.

Failed root-atomic output is held only by opaque `Unpublished<T>` with private storage and diagnostic metadata. It cannot be extracted, borrowed, dereferenced, destructured, serialized, erased, converted to T/ChildLocal/published output, or retroactively reclassified. It may only retry through the same bound root-atomic protocol or be discarded. ChildLocal is selected before execution.

Memory quiescence means no live transient authority. PublishedTransfer moves exact charged bytes to artifact authority; seal proves granted equals returned plus published; later artifact drop closes separately. RSS/allocator metadata are no-claims unless charged.

Execution APIs consume authorities and return typed in-place/published/unpublished results; verifier/join/consumer APIs accept receipts. All guards/results are must-use; diagnostics carry identities, phase, retryability, live counts, remediation. Nested transactional output has a dedicated policy refusal.

Inventory has orthogonal route/publication dimensions: defaults root-atomic, explicit partial child-local, committed-prefix later. Cx-aware downgrade fails. Read-only CSR stays additive; sentinel destination and owned return prove publication/rollback now.

Published-artifact authority and slot bootstrap (canonical; supersedes every older raw-value/raw-transfer shape)

Successful artifacts are authority-bearing, never independently returned raw values. `PublishedTransferEnvelope` uses three disjoint u64 components—logical payload bytes, alignment/layout padding bytes beyond the payload, and separately charged metadata/control overhead—and its checked u128 sum must equal the live allocation charge exactly. `PublishedAllocation<T>` (or a versioned equivalent) privately co-owns `T`, the exact registered storage-layout identity, and its live `PublishedTransfer`; it attests no transitive/internal allocation that was not separately inventoried and charged. `PublishedInvocation<T>` privately co-owns that guard plus the finalized receipt. A bare prepared or published transfer may be installed into one of these opaque guards before visibility, explicitly rolled back, or explicitly closed; it is never returned beside a raw `T`.

`PublicationSlot<T>` has explicit `Vacant` and `Installed(PublishedAllocation<T>)` states. A raw preexisting value may enter the bounded protocol only through fallible checked pre-admission adoption that binds its exact registered layout, slot identity/generation, ambient memory root, and adoption policy and returns it unchanged on refusal. An explicitly unbounded legacy constructor remains available only with stable no-bounded-memory and no-root-atomic-evidence diagnostics. A tracked value from another root may enter only through a checked pre-admission reparent/adoption transaction that accounts for exact old-plus-new live overlap and preserves the old authority until the new one commits; otherwise it refuses unchanged. First install returns no displaced artifact. Replacement returns `DisplacedPublication<T>`, which privately carries the prior value, transfer, and receipt. Shared reads and consuming authority-preserving handoff are allowed; raw extraction/destructuring, `into_inner`/`into_parts`, `DerefMut`/`AsMut`/`BorrowMut`, mutable growth, or conversion/serialization that detaches value from authority are forbidden. Mutation, resize, replacement, or a new output root requires new admission.

The slot is one serialized state machine. Private swap/rollback occurs while readers cannot observe the occupant; successful installation publishes the new generation with release semantics and readers acquire a guard for one coherent old-or-new generation. A rollback restores the prior occupant before unlocking. No slot lock is held while invoking user `Drop`. Drop order is value, transfer close, then receipt; a panicking destructor is fail-closed and mints no close evidence. Deliberate forget, process termination, external copies, and unadmitted mutation remain explicit no-liveness/no-authority boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical umbrella acceptance criteria

1. All four children satisfy canonical fields and strict current-snapshot focused proof; precursor/static/historical FINAL claims do not count.
2. Default execution consumes authority and returns typed root-atomic result plus finalized receipt binding plan, occurrence, ordered runs, full child partition/publisher, worker evidence, memory seal/transfer, finalization, artifact roots, and invocation root. Only verification accepts receipts.
3. ChildLocal remains preselected distinct partial result/no-claim with no root conversion; committed-prefix remains later typed policy.
4. Opaque Unpublished recovery exposes diagnostics only and permits same-bound retry or discard. No extraction/borrow/deref/destructure/serialization/erasure/conversion/relabel route exists; compile-fail and runtime retry/drop tests prove this.
5. Quiescence, prospective fallible construction, generation/token rules, sibling/run partitions, both terminal realizations, rollback/late request, post-seal refusal, destructor boundary, diagnostics, and bounded verification are fully tested.
6. Memory proof covers single charge, delegation, u128 reuse, transient-zero/live-published counts, returned-plus-published conservation, live output/later drop, overlap/rollback/wrong-root/duplicate-failed transfer, forget/process no-liveness, fault/unwind/retry/replay.
7. Worker proof covers all std/asupersync/parked paths, identity/ordinal/permit, joins/quiescence/bundle/reuse, standalone no-claim, completion-disabled legacy semantics, ordered non-reusable permits.
8. Inventory covers every route with stable anchors/owner/static checks/publication scope; all malformed/stale/unowned/fixture/downgraded states fail; the baseline changes only through reviewed additions or removals carrying owner, rationale, feature reachability, review/expiry or migration target, and evidence-preserving history.
9. Combined runners have nonoverlapping ownership, complete modes/barriers/exits and exact capped ordered JSONL with one case_terminal per fixed case, followed by one run_summary and one final run_terminal, typed `{value,unit,width}` counters and boundary/parser mutants.
10. Real sparse journey retains read-only CSR plus staged/owned/opaque-retry cases, full partitions, child-local controls, all cancellation/fault/transfer/rollback/late-request/drop paths and no migrated-kernel claim.
11. Hygiene, strict-remote focused Cargo, required current runtime API/inventory DSR lane, static xtask/DSR ratchet, constellation preflight, and exact proof reporting pass. Only later migrated modes/zero-bypass defer.

12. Published owned, slot, and displaced artifacts preserve value-transfer-receipt coupling across vacant first install, checked bounded adoption, cross-root reparent/refusal, consuming authority-preserving handoff, repeated replacement, later drop, and panic. Compile-fail/API tests reject field separation, raw extraction, transfer-only drop, mutable access/growth, detached serialization, and cross-root slot use.
13. Property/state-model/mutation tests prove `Vacant -> Installed -> Displaced or Handoff -> ValueDropped -> TransferClosed` ordering; wrong-root/refused adoption leaves the slot and value unchanged; first install has no displaced artifact; old-plus-new overlap is exact; unregistered transitive storage is not attested; drop-order inversion, early/double transfer close, omitted prior authority, panic, and forget fail closed; and every live-published count/root remains exact.
14. Concurrency tests (including deterministic interleavings or loom-equivalent models where applicable) prove readers observe one coherent generation, private swap is unobservable, rollback precedes unlock, release/acquire publication is sufficient, no lock spans user destruction, and concurrent install/replace/read/adopt attempts return deterministic structured conflicts without deadlock or poisoning.
15. Canonical JSONL records envelope components, slot/guard identity and generation, prior/new artifact and transfer roots, adoption/reparent/handoff/displacement/drop sequence, value-drop-before-transfer-close, live-published counts before/after, synchronization outcome, panic/fail-closed/no-claim outcome, exact record counts, one case_terminal per fixed case, one run_summary, and one final run_terminal; the scientific invocation seal is referenced by its case_terminal and is never the run_terminal.
notes:
Canonical fields supersede stale generic transactional/exact-return/read-only, historical comments 2877/2923/2969, universal post-swap owned wording, single-run/terminal-child, caller-receipt, and recoverable-value escape assumptions. No original feature is removed.

The authority-lifetime and slot-bootstrap clauses in canonical design and acceptance supersede any older raw T, separate PublishedTransfer, raw displaced-value, or implicitly preinitialized-slot wording. They preserve first-install, legacy migration, replacement, shared read, retry, and handoff functionality through typed paths rather than removing it.

Distinct 60-minute estimate covers final foundation-root join and closeout review; implementation remains counted on descendants.
