title: fs-exec root-atomic invocation finalization: reserved cleanup, exact run/child/memory joins, and authority-preserving publication
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Defect and user impact

`InvocationBudget` correctly latches the first cancellation/refusal, but that also makes every later charge, poll, child split, and normal budget action fail. A caller can reserve nominal finalization work before launch yet cannot spend or evidence that reserve after cancellation. Sparse and other production operations therefore cannot honestly prove request -> drain -> finalize with accounted cleanup; they can only stop accounting at request time or fabricate a post-hoc flag.

## Outcome

Extend `fs-exec` with a one-use affine finalizer authority reserved at admission and isolated from scientific work. It remains valid after cancellation or a worker/domain fault solely for bounded drain, resource release, transactional publication refusal/rollback, and terminal receipt sealing. It cannot restart compute, publish success after a failed run, mint child authority, or overwrite the first terminal cause. Bind finalizer evidence to the exact invocation/child identity and expose a verifier-supported way to join sparse-domain evidence to the matching immutable `ChildReceipt` without allowing callers to hand-author success.

## Design requirements

- Separate normal scientific resources from a typed cleanup/finalization reserve at plan admission; reserve arithmetic is checked before work starts.
- Finalizer authority is non-Clone, non-Copy, one-use, and valid only after the work authority is closed or terminally latched.
- Its state machine distinguishes not-started, active work, terminal requested/refused, draining, resources released, publication aborted or committed, finalized, and replayed-finalize.
- Cancellation and the first fault remain monotone even when cleanup succeeds.
- Cleanup may charge only declared finalization work/polls and release/verify already admitted resources; it cannot allocate new scientific scratch, split new compute children, or publish a success output after cancellation/refusal.
- Successful execution also closes through the same finalizer and must perform a final pre-publication poll before a one-time commit.
- Final receipt creation refuses live children, tasks, workers, reservations, arenas, leases, unsealed publication, incomplete mandatory finalizer steps, or mismatched child/plan identity.
- Exact replay of an already sealed finalization returns the same immutable evidence; no authority or resource is returned twice.
- Preserve existing invocation APIs where their semantics remain sound; provide an explicit migration path and no false strengthening of legacy receipts.

## Unit, property, model, and mutation tests

Cover zero and maximum representable cleanup reserves; one-below/exact/one-above work, poll, memory, output, and finalizer capacities; every checked-add/multiply/conversion overflow; cancellation before begin, after admission, before first work, at last work unit, during drain, and immediately before publication; deadline, explicit refusal, allocation refusal, worker failure, panic/unwind, and duplicate cancellation. Assert first-cause stability, finalizer availability after failure, prohibition on new scientific work, exact-once resource return, no receipt before closure, final pre-publication poll, unchanged output on every non-success terminal, and semantic receipt verification.

Exhaustively enumerate short pure-model traces for zero to two children/workers over admit/start/work/request/fail/drain/release/prepare/commit/finalize/retry-finalize. Illegal transitions must refuse without mutation. Add compile-fail/API tests for cloning/reissuing finalizer authority, finalizing twice through live authority, spending cleanup as compute, fabricating child receipt linkage, and committing after cancellation.

Seeded negative/mutation tests independently remove one cleanup charge, final poll, child close, lease return, publication seal, first-failure field, plan/child binding, or receipt-root field; each mutant must be killed by a named invariant test.

## E2E and logging

Add a focused real `fs-exec` lifecycle E2E mode using an asupersync scope, real Cx, real invocation admission, successful and mid-run-cancelled work, and retained receipt verification. Stdout is canonical JSONL only. Log schema/case/sequence, source and build identity, invocation/child/plan roots, admitted normal and finalizer resources, consumed work/polls, request/drain/release/finalize order, live authority/resource counts before and after, publication state, terminal cause, receipt root, and explicit no-claim. Exclude PID, wall time, absolute paths, tokens, and host noise from semantic identity; bound stderr and retained artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

A reserved affine finalizer authority can always perform only its admitted cleanup after cancellation/refusal, while preserving the first terminal cause and prohibiting new scientific work or success publication. Invocation and child receipts verifiably bind exact-once drain/release/publication/finalization evidence; all boundary, lifecycle, compile-fail, interleaving, unwind, forgery, and mutation tests pass; the real active/cancelled E2E retains deterministic canonical logs. No wall-clock cancellation-latency or unregistered-worker discovery claim is made.
design:
Canonical design after reality check

Publication has three non-interchangeable contracts. `ChildLocal` preserves independently durable child output and explicitly permits a later failed root. `InvocationAtomic` is the default strong protocol: a bound root admits one operation plan and one invocation occurrence, mints a bounded ordered run-permit partition, joins every verified `WitnessedRun`, joins one root-bound terminal delegated-memory receipt plus any exact `PublishedTransfer`, prospectively builds and verifies the complete child partition and all final receipts, and makes one registered artifact visible at one terminal decision. A later committed-prefix policy remains a third separately typed future contract.

Root state is one serialized machine: Open; RootCommitPrepared with designated publishing child and monotone generation; Sealed with the complete child and run partitions. Preparation closes child/work/memory/run admission except for the staged/private artifact, its prepared publication transfer, and pre-admitted evidence storage owned by the affine token. Dropping a prepared token restores an admission-closed retryable pending state, advances generation, and requires another final poll. Stale, wrong-child, wrong-run, cross-invocation, and reused authorities refuse before mutation. Deliberate forget and process termination are fail-closed no-liveness boundaries.

One abstract terminal decision has two concrete realizations. In-place commit privately swaps through an exclusive `PublicationSlot<T>`, then performs the named atomic Cx deadline/cancellation observation; a terminal value at that load rolls back and returns an opaque unpublished recovery authority, while a later request loses. Owned-return commit keeps `T` private, performs the terminal observation first, commits the prepared transfer, then moves `T` into caller-owned `PublishedInvocation<T>`. Failure exposes no published object or transfer. No callback, allocation, formatting, hashing, lock acquisition, fallible verification, or user destructor occurs between either successful terminal observation and cached receipt installation/public visibility.

`InvocationAdmitter::admit_bound` binds schema root, schema version, plan root, expected ordered run partition, and child/publication policy. InvocationBudget derives one affine permit root per declared run ordinal; zero-run operations are valid, and each 0/1/2+ witness partition is exact, ordered, bounded, complete, and non-reusable. The complete child partition is also exact: already-completed nonpublishing siblings are allowed only when verified Completed with zero publication/output; any cancelled/refused/faulted, missing, duplicate, or additional publishing sibling prevents root success.

User-facing shapes are opaque and `#[must_use]`: `PreparedInvocationCommit`; `InPlaceInvocationCommit<T>` privately owning `Option<DisplacedPublication<T>>` plus the finalized receipt; `PublishedInvocation<T>` privately owning `PublishedAllocation<T>` plus the finalized receipt; opaque `Unpublished<T>`; and structured prepare/commit errors that retain recovery authority. These types expose no public fields or raw-parts API. `Unpublished<T>` has a private field and diagnostic metadata only: no `into_inner`, `Deref`, `AsRef`, `Borrow`, destructuring, serialization, erasure, or conversion to `T`, `ChildLocal`, or another publication scope. It may only be consumed by retry through the same bound root-atomic protocol or explicitly discarded/dropped. ChildLocal must be selected before execution, never retrofitted after root failure. Execution APIs consume authorities and return results; only verifier/join/consumer APIs accept receipts. Diagnostics include phase, retryability, remediation, expected/actual plan, occurrence, scope, generation, child/run partition, transfer identity, and live resource counts. Forbidden nested transactional output has a dedicated policy error distinct from capacity exhaustion.

The strong receipt attests only registered typed artifacts and registered executor/delegated-memory authorities. It does not attest arbitrary I/O, global side effects, external threads, process abort/kill, deliberately forgotten tokens, panicking user destructors, RSS, or allocator metadata unless explicitly charged. This bead owns InvocationBudget adoption and `scripts/ci/fs_exec_invocation_protocol_e2e.sh` modes `finalizer`, `completion`, `memory`, `joined`, and `all`; prerequisite leaves own only their focused producers/parsers.

Slot bootstrap and visibility are part of the strong protocol, not caller convention. `PublicationSlot<T>` is explicitly `Vacant` or `Installed(PublishedAllocation<T>)`. Checked bounded adoption binds the registered layout, slot/generation, ambient root, and exact charge and returns the original value/authority unchanged on refusal; cross-root reparenting is a separate pre-admitted transaction with exact old-plus-new overlap. An unbounded legacy slot carries explicit no-bounded-memory/no-root-atomic-evidence diagnostics. First install returns no displacement; replacement returns only a guarded `DisplacedPublication<T>`. The private swap is invisible to readers, success publishes one generation with release/acquire ordering, rollback restores the prior occupant before unlock, and user destruction never runs under the slot lock. `PublishedTransferEnvelope` components are disjoint and their checked sum equals the registered live charge; unregistered transitive storage is outside authority.

Mandatory convergence supplement — identity, verified joins, finalizer phases, and evidence grammar

Identity is a typed algebra. `OperationPlanRoot` is reusable operation content. `InvocationOccurrenceRoot` is minted once by the bound admitter and binds OperationPlanRoot, schema/version, issuer scope, idempotency/occurrence subject, declared child count, publication policy, capability root, and an ordered run declaration table of `{ordinal, expected TilePoolPlanRoot, expected RunId/scope policy}`. Its uniqueness claim is issuer-scoped; no global cross-process uniqueness is claimed unless a governed session/ledger issuer is bound.

For ordinal i in the declared table, `TilePoolInvocationPermit::permit_root` is the domain-separated fixed-width derivation of InvocationOccurrenceRoot, declared run count, and i. It is not the bare occurrence root and cannot depend on a future witness. The executor's `CallReplayRoot` later binds the actual TilePoolPlanRoot, scope, RunId, ordinal, and permit; the invocation run-partition root binds declared count plus the ordered verified witness roots. Zero-run has one canonical empty-partition root. The join verifies each actual call against its matching declaration; wrong operation plan, wrong run plan at the correct ordinal, swapped run plans, wrong RunId/scope policy, or permit/witness substitution refuses.

The root join binds an explicit incidence table, not merely independently complete partitions. Every run ordinal is assigned exactly once to one declared child or an explicitly declared root subject; every child binds its exact ordered run subset; every child/finalizer binds its delegated-memory subject; and the designated publisher binds the exact prepared transfer/PublishedAllocation. Duplicate, missing, individually valid but unrelated, cross-child, cross-run, cross-memory, or cross-occurrence evidence refuses. Under the current designated-child policy, zero nonpublishing siblings means a one-child partition containing the publisher; zero total children cannot publish.

Raw JSON, bytes, loose witness/receipt structs, and caller-provided roots are untrusted transport or diagnostics. Parsing yields Unverified values. Only bounded semantic verification may mint `VerifiedWitnessedRunReceipt`, `VerifiedChildReceipt`, and `VerifiedMemoryReceipt`, and the root join consumes those typed values. JSONL never mints authority. Diagnostic access cannot provide joinable into-parts without consuming and verifying the exact bundle association.

The serialized root machine is explicit: OpenWork; TerminalLatched; Draining; ResourcesReleased; CommitEligible; CommitPrepared{generation,publisher}; RetryablePending{generation,reason}; and Sealed{terminal,receipt}. Replay observes Sealed; it is not a second mutable phase. The affine finalizer authorizes one state-changing close. `finish(&mut self)` retries only failures proved non-mutating and replays cached byte-identical evidence after Sealed without reminting budget, permits, transfers, children, or cleanup authority. Structural preflight rejection returns still-live authority unchanged. Once attempt admission linearizes, the permit is consumed; Busy/refusal/fault/panic is a witnessed admitted attempt. A consumed run retries only under another declared ordinal or a new occurrence.

The finalizer reserve is partitioned from scientific work at admission and includes a mandatory-step manifest plus bounded evidence/parser/verifier storage. It cannot be borrowed by work and returns unused reserve once at seal. Exhaustion, unavailable evidence storage, invariant failure, or verifier-work exhaustion are stable non-success terminals preserving the first cause. The guarantee covers pre-admitted executor-managed resources under ordinary return/caught unwind, not process abort, hardware failure, or deliberately forgotten authority.

Explicit ChildLocal output is `PublishedChildLocal<T>` (or versioned equivalent), privately co-owning PublishedAllocation and child receipt with a partial-publication no-root claim. It cannot yield root-final evidence. All published wrappers attest only registered allocation regions and publication-time content root. Interior mutation, external copies, and unregistered deep allocations are outside current receipt authority until a new transaction rebinds them. `Unpublished::discard` returns discard evidence only if destruction completes normally; ordinary drop, panic, or forget remains fail-closed and mints no close receipt.

Both publication realizations consume one versioned `TerminalDecisionSnapshot` from the root latch. Any fallible deadline evaluation is latched before the critical window; no clock read, callback, allocation, lock acquisition, formatting, hashing, verification, or user Drop occurs after the successful decision and before visibility/cache installation. A later request is retained as late/sealed evidence and cannot rewrite Completed.

The combined runner performs typed in-process joins and parses leaf JSONL only for diagnostic conformance. It consumes huq.24 CanonicalEvidenceRunnerV2. Grammar is exactly run_start; for each fixed-manifest case, case_start, a bounded canonically ordered lifecycle set, and exactly one case_terminal referencing exactly one invocation scientific seal or terminal refusal; then run_summary; exactly one run_terminal; nothing after. A scientific invocation seal is case evidence, never the multi-case run terminal. ProofExitV2 states remain distinct. Shared limits apply, with a stricter 8 MiB per-artifact family cap; every limit is tested at minus-one/exact/plus-one. Strict JSON rejects invalid UTF-8/newlines, duplicate keys, unsupported schema/version/fields, excess nesting/records/bytes, unsafe paths, and noncanonical roots/numbers. SourceIdentity and BuildIdentity remain exact; DSR/RCH run IDs and relative artifacts are proof-envelope fields outside semantic identity.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. Reserved cleanup work/polls remain usable after cancellation/refusal only for bounded drain, release, rollback/abort, verification, and sealing; scientific work, child/run minting, and new memory admission refuse.
2. `ChildLocal` and `InvocationAtomic` have distinct marker/result/receipt types and explicit opt-in API names. Child-local functionality is preserved unconditionally, carries its weaker no-claim, may coexist with root failure, and has no `From`, erasure, or verifier path into a finalized invocation receipt.
3. Strong preparation requires a bound plan/occurrence, exact declared ordered run-witness partition, complete child partition, one designated publishing child, no prior output, all registered work joined/quiescent, all transient delegated allocations closed, verified memory terminal plan, exact prepared published transfer, exact staged/private artifact capacity, and clean root. Only the artifact/evidence/transfer authority held by the token is exempt.
4. Zero-run, one-run, two-run, and bounded-many-run plans mint exact ordinal permits and join matching verified witnesses in order. Missing, duplicate, reordered, replayed, wrong-plan, wrong-occurrence, or extra runs refuse. Permit derivation binds only InvocationOccurrenceRoot, declared run count, and ordinal. The later call and partition joins bind the declared TilePoolPlanRoot, RunId and scope policy, permit, and ordered verified WitnessRoot values; no permit derivation depends on a future witness.
5. Zero, one, and two completed nonpublishing siblings are allowed only when each is verified Completed with zero publication/output. A cancelled, refused, faulted, publishing, missing, duplicated, or unaccounted sibling blocks root Completed and leaves the artifact private/unchanged. The final receipt binds every child exactly once plus the designated publisher.
6. In-place success returns opaque `InPlaceInvocationCommit<T>` privately owning `Option<DisplacedPublication<T>>` plus finalized receipt; the option is None for a vacant first install and Some only for a guarded prior published occupant. Owned success returns opaque `PublishedInvocation<T>` privately owning `PublishedAllocation<T>` plus finalized receipt. No success type exposes public fields, raw parts, or a transfer beside raw T. Refusal exposes no published object/transfer and returns only opaque `Unpublished<T>` recovery authority plus structured diagnostics when retryable. Explicit child-local APIs return only partial-publication results selected before execution.
7. `Unpublished<T>` has private, non-destructurable storage and metadata/diagnostic access only. It exposes no value borrow or extraction, `Deref`, `AsRef`, `Borrow`, serialization, erasure, or conversion into `T`, ChildLocal, or any published result. Its only consuming operations are retry through the exact bound root-atomic authority or explicit discard/drop. Runtime tests prove retry and discard; compile-fail/API tests prove extraction, borrowing, destructuring, conversion, and retroactive ChildLocal relabeling impossible.
8. Every affine guard, permit, prepared token/transfer, unpublished recovery, published result/transfer, and terminal evidence wrapper is `#[must_use]`. Rustdoc compile examples cover default root-atomic in-place, owned return, explicit preselected child-local opt-in, pre/mid/terminal cancellation, retry after non-mutating refusal, unbound-legacy migration, and compile-fail misuse.
9. Prepare/commit diagnostics are stable structured variants with phase, retryability, expected/actual plan/occurrence/scope/generation/child/run/transfer identities, live resource counts, and ranked remediation. `TransactionalOutputScopeViolation` or its versioned replacement remains a dedicated policy error and is never reported as `ResourceExceeded`.
10. In-place linearization is the post-private-swap atomic terminal observation: a terminal state at that load wins and rolls back; a request after it loses. Owned-return linearization observes terminal state while private, then commits transfer and moves the value to the caller. Deterministic barriers test immediately before/after both observations. No user Drop occurs in the critical window; displaced values are returned.
11. Success moves exact charged output once into destination authority; sealed conservation is granted equals returned plus published. Later destination drop closes separately. Wrong ambient root, duplicate/failed transfer, replacement overlap, and transfer mutation refuse before visibility. Post-seal split/work/memory/recovery/permit/second-commit refuse while exact replay remains.
12. `finish(&mut self)` retries after non-mutating preparation/seal/allocation/transfer refusal and idempotently replays cached evidence. Tests prohibit aliasing, second live/concurrent token, clone/reissue, stale generation, wrong child/run/root, and cross-invocation use, without prohibiting legitimate mutable retry/replay.
13. All receipt construction/reservation/hashing/worker-memory-transfer verification occurs before visibility and is test-fallible. After the successful terminal observation only infallible moves/scalar installation occur. The semantic verifier enforces an explicit child/run/work budget, one validated index, bottom-up aggregates, complete partitions, no descendant output grants, correct failure origins, exact returned/published conservation, and bounded deep/wide behavior.
14. Unit/property/model/mutation coverage includes zero/exact/one-over/max arithmetic, u64-max-plus-one cumulative reuse, all request/deadline/fault/unwind points, live siblings/descendants/workers/arenas/leases, allocation/transfer failure, dropped/retried/stale tokens, both linearizations/rollback/late request, postcommit refusal, output alive after seal/later drop, complete run/child partitions, opaque unpublished retry/discard, panic-on-drop sentinel, and exact replay. Models enumerate 0-2 children/workers/runs across every transition; compile-fail tests cover all affine/type boundaries; seeded mutants cover every bound field and skipped step.
15. The combined real-asupersync runner emits huq.24-conformant capped canonical JSONL with exact ordered records, one scientific seal inside each successful case_terminal, and one final run_terminal. Every u64/u128 semantic value is a typed object `{value:"...",unit:"...",width:"u64|u128"}`. Parser/roundtrip mutants cover 2^53-1/2^53/2^53+1, u64::MAX, u64::MAX+1, u128::MAX, leading zeros/sign/overflow/wrong unit/width/truncation/oversize. Records bind source/build/target/features, case/sequence, plan/occurrence/child/run/worker/memory/transfer/publication/artifact/receipt roots, lifecycle order, retry, and no-claims; stdout/stderr/artifacts are capped and host noise is excluded.
16. Formatting, diff hygiene, scanners, rustdoc compile-fail, strict current-snapshot remote focused fs-exec tests and every combined runner mode, constellation preflight, and applicable focused DSR gate pass. The bead remains open on any missing typed partition/join/transfer, ergonomic result/diagnostic, opaque recovery guarantee, test/log requirement, or current-snapshot proof.

17. Slot acceptance covers Vacant and Installed states, fallible same-root adoption, cross-root reparent/refusal, first install, repeated replacement, guarded displacement, consuming authority-preserving handoff, and an explicitly unbounded legacy no-claim path. Wrong root/layout/generation/charge or failed overlap admission leaves the caller value and slot bit-for-bit unchanged.
18. Compile-fail/API tests prohibit raw field separation/extraction, into-parts, transfer-only drop, mutable access/growth, detached serialization, and cross-root slot substitution. Property/model/mutation tests prove `Vacant -> Installed -> Displaced or Handoff -> ValueDropped -> TransferClosed`, exact envelope/overlap/live-count conservation, rollback-before-unlock, value-before-transfer close, no lock across Drop, drop-order/early-close/double-close/omitted-authority mutants, and panic/forget fail-closed behavior.
19. Deterministic concurrency tests prove readers see one coherent slot generation, the private swap is unobservable, release/acquire publication is sufficient, and concurrent install/replace/read/adopt operations produce structured conflicts without deadlock or poisoning. Canonical JSONL includes envelope, slot/guard/generation, prior/new roots, adoption/reparent/handoff/displacement/drop order, live-published counts, synchronization result, and panic/no-claim fields.

20. Identity tests prove same OperationPlanRoot/different occurrence changes permits/calls/witnesses; same occurrence/different ordinal changes permit/call/witness roots; permit roots derive only from occurrence, declared count, and ordinal; zero-run uses the canonical empty partition; each actual TilePoolPlanRoot/RunId/scope matches its declaration; and wrong-operation-plan, wrong-run-plan-at-correct-ordinal, swapped-plan, permit, call, witness, and partition mutants are independently rehashed and rejected.
21. Root join consumes only verified typed receipts and validates the complete child-run-memory-publication incidence table. It rejects unrelated-but-valid partitions, duplicate/missing run assignment, undeclared root work, reused memory across siblings, publisher/transfer mismatch, cross-occurrence evidence, and loose or JSON-decoded values supplied as authority.
22. Runtime and compile-fail tests distinguish non-mutating preflight authority return from admitted-attempt consumption; distinguish one state-changing finish from cached replay; retain recovery authority and original outcome/report on retryable refusal; and reject clone/reissue, authority loss through generic error conversion, or join from unverified transport.
23. A complete transition/error matrix names retryable classes and proves no mutation for each. It covers cleanup/evidence/parser/verifier reserve exact-minus-one/exact/plus-one, cleanup exhaustion after cancellation, first-cause races, late request, unknown schema, verifier work exhaustion, dropped prepare, stale generation, explicit ChildLocal, discard success/panic, and byte-identical sealed replay.
24. ChildLocal and InvocationAtomic publication both preserve registered allocation authority. Compile-fail tests cover raw/deep-value extraction, field separation, provided mutable/interior escape, detached serialization, and ChildLocal-to-root conversion. Runtime tests cover discard, drop panic/forget, repeated replacement, publication-time content root, unregistered deep-allocation no-claim, and no current-content claim after external/interior mutation.
25. Runner tests enforce canonical `--list`, `--check`, `--self-test`, smoke/full `--run --family-mode finalizer|completion|memory|joined|all` with output roots, frozen negative cases, and artifact-only replay with separate input/output roots. The former quick corpus migrates explicitly to smoke and is not an alias. Successfully preflighted commands enforce exact per-case and final-terminal cardinality, manifest ordering, caps, and duplicate/unknown/truncated/oversized refusal; invalid argv/`quick`/`--mode`/`--profile` exit Usage with empty lifecycle stdout and one bounded stderr diagnostic. Property/model failures retain bounded reproducible seeds and minimized traces.
26. Closure evidence is a stable-snapshot matrix: exact focused fs-exec lib/integration/doc/compile-fail commands, every combined runner/parser mode, formatting/diff/scanner status, constellation verify-only, applicable DSR command/run/artifact, and before/after HEAD. Focused remote, combined runner, constellation, and DSR-wide states are reported separately; static or precursor proof cannot close.
27. Runner conformance tests explicitly reject a case seal used as run_terminal, missing/double run_terminal, hidden failed case under a Pass run, any record after run_terminal, exit/state alias, unsafe/nonempty artifact target, and every shared or stricter cap boundary.
notes:
Canonical fields supersede stale sequencing comments, child-local-as-transactional wording, the single-WitnessedRun assumption, post-swap wording for owned return, all-returned memory conservation, and the incorrect compile-fail prohibition on legitimate retry. Failed root-atomic output cannot escape through Unpublished recovery or retroactive ChildLocal relabeling.

Mandatory authority-lifetime supplement and close gate: published values are inseparable from their live transfer. `PublishedInvocation<T>` has private fields and co-owns an opaque allocator `PublishedAllocation<T>` plus finalized receipt; it permits shared read access and authority-preserving handoff only. It exposes no raw field destructure, into_inner/into_parts, DerefMut, AsMut, BorrowMut, mutable growth, serialization erasure, or conversion that separates T from its transfer/receipt. Any mutation, resize, replacement, or new output root requires a newly admitted transaction.

`PublicationSlot<T>` privately co-owns the installed `PublishedAllocation<T>`. In-place replacement returns `DisplacedPublication<T>` carrying the displaced value and its prior transfer/receipt, never raw T separated from a charge. An alternative implementation may drop the old value after the critical window and only then close its transfer, but cannot return raw displaced ownership. Drop order is explicit: value first, transfer close second, receipt last; a panicking value destructor leaves authority fail-closed and cannot fabricate a close.

Compile-fail/API tests prohibit result/slot field separation, raw extraction, into_parts, DerefMut/AsMut/BorrowMut, transfer-only drop while value survives, and mutable-growth escape. Runtime tests cover value-before-transfer drop order, repeated replacement, authority-preserving handoff, live-published counts, panic-on-drop, later close, and wrong prior slot authority. Post-return caller copies or external mutations are outside receipt authority unless separately admitted and bound. These requirements are part of acceptance, not optional notes. No original feature is removed.

Canonical slot bootstrap: `PublicationSlot<T>` is Vacant or Installed. Bounded adoption and cross-root reparent are checked pre-admission transactions; first install has no displaced artifact; repeated replacement returns guarded prior authority. This requirement closes the sentinel/bootstrap gap and is mandatory.

Canonical identity naming uses OperationPlanRoot for the reusable operation and TilePoolPlanRoot for each reusable executor run plan. The occurrence commits prospectively to the ordered run-declaration table. Canonical acceptance items 20-26 promote incidence, verified type-state, finalizer phases, ChildLocal authority, runner grammar, and proof matrix into the close gate.
Per-case scientific seals and the final runner terminal are distinct and machine-checked.

Additive verification-completeness baseline (never a substitute for the specialized criteria above):
- Unit and boundary tests cover happy, empty/zero/one, exact limit, one-below/one-above, maximum-without-huge-allocation, error, units/dimensions, numeric extremes, and deterministic tie/order cases owned by this leaf.
- Property/metamorphic tests exercise algebraic or relational invariants; bounded state/model tests cover lifecycle, concurrency, retry/replay, and invalid transitions where applicable.
- Public authority/type surfaces require API and compile-fail misuse tests. A leaf with no public type must record that fact and provide the nearest strict schema/API-negative equivalent rather than silently omitting the category.
- Seeded mutation tests independently alter every claim-bearing identity, bound, state, policy, route, authority, and no-claim field and retain minimized, reproducible failures.
- Cancellation/deadline plus injected allocation, worker/process, parser, I/O, durable-seal, publication, and replay faults are placed at every transition this leaf owns; drain/quiescence, exact resource return, no partial authority, retryability, and first-cause diagnostics are asserted. Inapplicable fault classes require a typed N/A rationale.
- The terminal owner named by the dependency graph runs a release-built, no-mock E2E using the canonical shared commands: --list, --check, --self-test, --run PROFILE [--family-mode MODE], --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. Nested nonterminal producer leaves emit bounded content-bound artifacts consumed by that runner and must not create a competing `--family-mode all` selector or `--mode`/`--profile` alias; exactly one catalog-owned terminal adapter may expose `--family-mode all` under exact-set registry tests.
- Canonical bounded logs record schema/source/build/tool/target/features, typed lossless values and units, command/profile/family/mode/case/sequence, budgets/work/resources, state/reason, expected/observed/effects, authority/no-claim, diagnostics/ranked repair, stop/drain roots, and relative artifact roots. Invocation manifests are fixed and nonempty; case_start opens every ordered slot with execution=execute|suppressed; suppressed permits zero family rows and requires immediate typed NotRun. Cooperative stops drain/finalize the active case and emit remaining suppressed slots before summary/terminal; forced or unproved truncation emits no terminal. Exact case_terminal/run_summary/run_terminal cardinality, caps, hostile parser cases, tamper detection, separate replay input/output roots, and artifact-only replay are mandatory. Raw scientific/performance/tool data stays in capped artifacts, and only explicitly declared volatile observations are excluded from identity.

title: fs-exec executor-minted WitnessedRun: real TilePool quiescence, affine attempt identity, and focused deterministic evidence
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Defect and user impact

`TilePool` structurally joins scoped worker threads before returning, but the public run result does not mint a typed witness that binds the actual admitted run, all launched workers/tasks, cancellation request, join/drain completion, arena quiescence, lease state, and terminal outcome. `DrainTracker` is strong only for workers that callers explicitly register; attaching synthetic guards around a pool run would not prove that the real pool workers drained. Higher layers can therefore either trust unstructured control flow or overclaim a fake drain report.

## Outcome

Make the executor itself mint a versioned immutable completion witness from the real TilePool lifecycle. It must cover active success, cancellation, worker/domain fault, panic containment, and allocation refusal; bind the exact run/plan/scope and actual worker/task accounting; and be available only after every launched worker joined and executor-owned arenas/leases reached their required terminal state. The witness complements, not replaces, scientific output and invocation receipts.

## Design requirements

- Instrument the actual pool launch/join path, not a wrapper or caller-authored boolean.
- Bind run ID, parent scope/cancellation gate identity where representable, execution mode, tile plan/root, admitted/launched/completed/cancelled/failed tile counts, actual worker count, steal/scheduling no-claim, request observation, join/drain outcome, arena/lease before-after facts, first failure, and terminal disposition.
- Mint no witness while any worker/task guard is live or a worker can still write shared/staging state.
- Cancellation request remains distinct from final cancellation completion. Successful and refused runs also carry quiescence evidence.
- Duplicate inspection/replay returns byte-identical immutable evidence; worker admission is closed after sealing.
- Do not claim discovery of external/unregistered threads, wall-clock latency, scheduler trace replay, or atomic application-state publication.
- Preserve deterministic numerical reduction and existing `RunError`/`RunReport` semantics; provide an additive migration path or a carefully versioned replacement.
- Expose a verifier that recomputes the witness root and rejects count conservation, run/plan mismatch, early finalization, first-failure drift, or missing quiescence fields.

## Tests

Unit/property tests cover zero/one/many tiles and workers, empty plans, worker-cap boundaries, all checked count overflows, success, pre-requested cancellation, mid-tile cancellation, lowest-tile refusal selection, injected allocation failure, injected worker fault, panic containment, steal races, and pool reuse after every terminal path. Assert no witness before joins, admitted/launched/completed/failed/cancelled conservation, no double drain, no stale worker admission, arena and lease quiescence, unchanged first failure, and identical witness roots across repeated deterministic schedules where the contract promises identity.

Model tests enumerate launch/request/complete/fail/panic/join/release/finalize orderings for zero to two workers and refuse every trace that seals early. Compile-fail/API tests prevent callers from constructing or mutating witnesses. Mutation tests omit one join, worker decrement, arena reset, lease release, request field, run/plan root, terminal count, or final seal and must fail independently.

## E2E and logging

Run the real `TilePool` through active, pre-cancelled, mid-run-cancelled, allocation-refused, worker-failed, and panicking kernels under asupersync scopes, then immediately reuse the pool. Retain deterministic canonical JSONL containing schema/case/sequence, source/build identity, run/scope/tile-plan roots, admitted/launched/completed/failed/cancelled counts, worker/task/arena/lease before-after state, request/join/finalize sequence, terminal error/disposition, witness root, reuse verdict, and explicit no-claim. Child stdout/stderr is bounded and kept outside semantic identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every TilePool terminal return used by production cancellation protocols can carry executor-minted evidence that the real launched workers/tasks joined and required executor-owned resources quiesced; no witness can be fabricated or sealed early. Success/cancel/fault/panic/allocation and reuse tests, exhaustive short-trace models, API/forgery checks, and seeded mutants pass with deterministic canonical logs. The witness explicitly does not attest external threads, application publication, or wall-clock latency.
design:
Canonical design after reality check

The real executor launch/join path returns a non-forgeable `WitnessedRun<Out>` containing the existing outcome/report plus a versioned `TilePoolCompletionWitness`; `verify_bundle` checks their exact agreement. `CompletionKernelRunner` provides the additive migration seam while legacy hot APIs retain their existing behavior through a completion-disabled lane that performs no witness hashing, completion-counter updates, or evidence allocation. This is a narrow semantic-work claim, not an unmeasured wall-time speed claim.

Execution identity is structured and versioned. TilePoolPlanRoot binds normalized placement schema/version, pool seed, stable fixed-width KernelIdentity, execution mode, tile plan, and declared bounds; human kernel names are diagnostic only. CallReplayRoot additionally binds the declared RunId, exact scope/cancellation association, declared run count and ordinal, and optional affine invocation permit root. Standalone witnessed runs explicitly have no cross-issuer uniqueness claim. Invocation-bound runs consume a non-Clone permit minted exactly once for one invocation/run ordinal; a second attempt refuses before pool admission, and the witness binds that permit. Multiple-run composition is performed downstream as a bounded ordered partition of these individually verified runs.

Witness sealing occurs only after every launched worker and parked-run callback exits, joins complete, staging is inaccessible, root charge is released, arenas and delegated leases satisfy their terminal predicates, and `verify_bundle` succeeds. Semantic hashing uses static tagged fixed-width fields, never Display, formatting, or diagnostic prose. Parked pool admission is a safe serialized Busy/affine protocol, including recursive and concurrent calls; no panic occurs while its crew mutex is held. Parked OS-thread lifetime is explicitly outside a run-local witness.

Focused evidence remains in `crates/fs-exec/tests/tile_pool_completion.rs` and supplies the `completion` records consumed by the combined runner owned by 21.1.1; no separate competing JSONL schema or shell runner is created.

Mandatory convergence supplement — TilePoolPlanRoot, witnessed type-state, and focused proof boundary

Identity has three roots. `TilePoolPlanRoot` is reusable content and binds placement schema/version and normalized requested placement, pool seed/stream, stable fixed-width KernelIdentity, execution-mode tag/version, tile-plan topology/counts, and declared bounds. Human kernel names are diagnostic only. RunId, scope/cancellation association, invocation occurrence, ordinal, permit, and terminal observations do not belong in TilePoolPlanRoot. `CallReplayRoot` binds TilePoolPlanRoot, declared RunId, typed ScopeBinding where present, declared run count, ordinal, and optional permit root. `WitnessRoot` binds CallReplayRoot plus the complete terminal lifecycle. Same plan with different RunId/scope keeps TilePoolPlanRoot but changes call/witness; changed seed/placement/kernel/mode/tile plan changes TilePoolPlanRoot.

RunId is a caller-visible subject, not uniqueness authority. Standalone witnessed calls have no permit and no cross-call/cross-issuer uniqueness claim. Invocation-bound calls consume a crate-minted affine permit whose root was prospectively derived by the root protocol from InvocationOccurrenceRoot, declared count, and ordinal. The constructor/accessor are named from_permit_root/permit_root; no field calls these bytes invocation_root. The later ordered partition root is owned by 21.1.1 and binds witness roots.

Public naming is uniform: existing run_* methods are completion-disabled legacy; run_*_witnessed methods are standalone/replayable with the uniqueness no-claim; run_*_witnessed_once methods consume a permit. Permit type is crate-constructible only, non-Clone/non-Copy/must-use. Structural preflight mismatch returns the live permit unchanged. Once attempt admission linearizes, it is consumed; success, cancellation, Busy, allocation/spawn refusal, worker fault, tile/reduction panic, and every terminal produce at most one witnessed attempt. Retry needs another declared ordinal or new occurrence.

`WitnessedRun<Out>` has private fields and borrowed diagnostics. Verification consumes it and returns `VerifiedWitnessedRun<Out>`; failure returns a must-use error retaining outcome/report/recovery. Only the verified type yields a joinable receipt. Raw witness structs, JSON, roots, and caller reports never satisfy a join. Out content/scientific correctness is not attested.

If terminal work completes but sealing refuses, `CompletionSealRefusal` retains the legacy outcome/report and recovery material, exposes no witness/receipt, and never drops a successful value in the critical path. Minting and verification are unconditional. Unknown schema/version, verifier-bound exhaustion, or semantic mismatch refuses without authority.

Request phase is a versioned enum: NotRequested, BeforeEntry, BeforeTerminalDecision, AfterTerminalDecision. Entry, terminal decision, resource release, and seal use separate monotone sequence fields. AfterTerminalDecision cannot rewrite Completed; requests after seal are outside the immutable witness. Request-observing-worker count is evidence, not terminal cause.

Accounting separates planned slots, spawn attempts, launched workers/tasks, loop entries/exits, joins, tile guards opened/closed, and every parked-crew callback entry/exit. A versioned conservation table covers every terminal, including prelaunch and partial spawn. Busy is a witnessed zero-admission/zero-callback/zero-root-charge refusal after attempt admission; winner selection/fairness/latency are no-claims, while each logical record shape/root is deterministic.

This leaf owns executor-local arena, root-charge, task-guard, and optional generic memory-observer facts only. title: fs-alloc memory authority composition: affine subleases and inseparable published allocations without double admission
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Defect and user impact

`InvocationAdmission::begin` reserves the declared memory envelope while TilePool, LeasedVec, staging, scratch, and output allocations may reserve the same bytes again. Double charging rejects valid work; bypassing either authority makes memory receipts or caps untrue. Successful output adds a second trap: destination-owned bytes remain live after invocation return and therefore cannot be falsely counted as returned merely to seal the root.

## Outcome

Build one serialized, root-bound, affine memory authority. A bounded pristine `OperationMemoryLease` enables a versioned delegation hierarchy; non-Clone child authorities feed real allocations without a second charge; transient bytes return exactly once; successful output may move exactly once into a typed `PublishedTransfer`; terminal conservation is `granted = returned + published`. Root seal requires no live transient authority and an exact verified set of published-transfer receipts. Later destination drop closes its own authority without rewriting the immutable root receipt.

This leaf is the independent fs-alloc foundation. It does not depend on TilePool. InvocationBudget adoption and worker-plus-memory joining belong to 21.1.1; the real sparse staged/owned artifact journey belongs to 21.1.4. Those downstream E2E obligations are preserved and blocked on this leaf rather than duplicated here.

## Design requirements

- One linearizable serialized state owns configure, delegate, reserve, release, close, prepare-transfer, publish/rollback, destination close, and root seal.
- Root/parent/child `LeaseIdentity` values are versioned, fixed-width, deterministic, allocation-free, and bind dynamic invocation/owner subjects plus a bounded path and static diagnostic label.
- Delegated authorities, charges, prepared transfers, and published transfers are affine, non-Clone/non-Copy, must-use, and cannot outlive or recreate parent capacity.
- Metadata reservation is bounded and fallible, including zero-capacity transfers and duplicate-path tracking.
- Real LeasedVec, scratch, staging, replacement-growth overlap, output, and finalizer allocations consume delegated authority rather than a second root charge.
- Live/used/peak/limit values are u64; cumulative requested/refused/released/violation values are exact u128.
- Refusals retain requested/used/available/root/parent/child/site/sequence facts without addresses or host data. Refused bytes count only byte-bearing requests; control refusals still increment refusal count and bind auxiliary facts.
- Close receipts verify exact identity and direct/delegated/returned/published conservation. Root seal freezes admission, remains drainable after a live-resource refusal, and replays one immutable receipt after success.
- `active_transient_delegations == 0` at seal. `live_published_transfers` exactly equals the verified terminal transfer-receipt partition; published output is not required to drop before invocation completion.
- `PublishedTransferBinding` binds plan, occurrence, output, and destination identities. Wrong root/binding, duplicate transfer, transfer failure, and fabricated destination ownership refuse before visibility.
- Safe Drop, explicit rollback/close, cancellation, fault, partial initialization, caught unwind, and retry return authority exactly once. Deliberate forget and process termination are fail-closed no-liveness boundaries and mint no recovery evidence.
- Lease-less/unbounded compatibility remains explicit non-authoritative for bounded-memory claims.

## Tests

Unit/property tests cover zero, one-under/exact/one-over, max-representable values without huge allocation, split/return trees, siblings/nesting, duplicate identity/path, concurrent reserve/delegate/transfer/seal races, replacement old-plus-new overlap, empty allocations, layout arithmetic, try-reserve/allocation/transfer fault, cancellation, panic/unwind, dropped child, duplicate return/close/transfer, wrong ambient root, seal with live transient authority, success with output alive after root seal, later destination drop, rollback, and immediate retry.

A tiny live cap reused cumulatively beyond u64::MAX proves exact u128 accounting. Compile-fail/API tests prohibit clone/reissue, use after close/transfer, parent-lifetime escape, wrong authority conversions, and bounded evidence from unbounded contexts. Pure models enumerate zero to two children over configure/delegate/reserve/release/prepare-transfer/publish/rollback/close/seal/refuse/drain/retry/destination-drop/replay. Seeded mutants alter every identity, sequence, grant/return/published partition, live-count, peak, refusal, overflow, and root field.

## Focused E2E and deterministic logging

`crates/fs-alloc/tests/lease_delegation.rs` owns the focused allocator journey and `memory` record producer/parser. It covers exact capacity, one byte below, cancellation/fault/unwind, transfer success/rollback/failure, live output after seal, later drop, and immediate retry. Canonical capped JSONL records schema/case/sequence, source/build/target/features, typed identities, capacity/lifecycle counters, returned/published partition, refusal, receipt roots, retry, and no-claims.

Every u64/u128 semantic value is a typed object `{value:"...",unit:"...",width:"u64|u128"}`. Parser/roundtrip mutants cover 2^53-1/2^53/2^53+1, u64::MAX, u64::MAX+1, u128::MAX, leading zeros, signs, overflow, wrong unit/width, truncation, and oversize. Addresses, absolute paths, wall time, PID, allocator secrets, RSS, and uncharged metadata are excluded.

The combined real invocation plus TilePool plus scratch/staging/output journey remains mandatory downstream: 21.1.1 owns the typed join and combined runner; 21.1.4 owns the user-facing sparse artifact cases. Neither may substitute arbitrary receipt roots or double charging.

## Acceptance Criteria

The serialized allocator authority, delegation/charge/close/seal APIs, PublishedTransfer partition, exports/contracts, comprehensive unit/property/model/compile-fail/mutation tests, focused canonical journey, formatting/hygiene, doctests, strict current-snapshot remote full fs-alloc tests, and documented Clippy proof pass. This leaf may then close independently; downstream invocation/TilePool/sparse integration remains open in 21.1.1/21.1.4.
design:
Canonical design after reality check

A bounded `OperationMemoryLease` may enable one versioned delegation hierarchy only while pristine. The hierarchy uses one serialized linearizable state, not loosely coordinated atomics. `LeaseIdentity` binds a fixed domain, root invocation subject, immediate parent subject, child owner subject, and bounded deterministic path. Delegated authorities are non-Clone affine owners; real `reserve` charges share the single root cap; nested children close inside-out; close and sealed-root receipts bind exact identity, sequence, conservation, refusal, peak, and root commitments.

Live, used, peak, and limit values remain u64 because they describe simultaneously representable capacity. Cumulative requested, refused bytes/requests, returns, and release-invariant observations are exact u128 so long reuse cannot wrap. Dynamic identities are passed as typed fixed bytes and static diagnostic labels; no formatting or allocation participates in semantic identity. Metadata is explicitly bounded and fallibly reserved, including zero-capacity children and duplicate-path refusal.

Terminal output ownership is explicit. Transient staging and scratch are returned on rollback. Successful publication may consume one affine `PreparedPublishedTransfer` that moves an exact charged payload/layout envelope into a caller/destination-owned `PublishedTransfer` without a return gap or a second charge. Its receipt binds root/parent/child identity, plan and invocation occurrence subjects, output identity/root, bytes, sequence, and destination authority. Root sealing requires `active_transient_delegations == 0` and permits only the exact `live_published_transfers` already committed into terminal receipts: granted equals returned plus published. Later destination drop closes the published authority through its own exact-once receipt but cannot rewrite the immutable invocation seal.

Deliberately forgotten delegated/prepared/published authorities and process termination are fail-closed no-liveness boundaries: capacity is not magically recovered and no terminal receipt may be claimed. Safe Drop, explicit rollback/close, unwind, and ordinary cancellation are proven; leak recovery is not fabricated.

This epic is the independent fs-alloc authority roll-up and has no TilePool implementation dependency. Children 21.1.3.1 and 21.1.3.2 own the affine ledger and published-allocation guard; terminal child 21.1.3.3 owns their integrated no-mock evidence, canonical parser, DSR proof, and replay. InvocationBudget adoption and the typed pool-plus-memory join are owned by 21.1.1; the actual sparse destination E2E is owned by 21.1.4. Those downstream beads consume this authority rather than double-charge or substitute arbitrary roots.

Published artifact coupling (canonical)

`PublishedTransferEnvelope` carries disjoint payload, alignment/layout-padding, and separately charged metadata/control-overhead u64 components; checked addition is performed in u128 and must equal the exact live charge. The sealed constructor for `PublishedAllocation<T>` accepts only allocator-origin evidence binding that envelope to the registered storage identity. It privately co-owns `T` and its live transfer, offers shared reads and consuming authority-preserving handoff, and makes no claim over transitive/internal allocations not separately inventoried and charged. A bare prepared/published transfer can only be installed into an opaque allocation/slot before visibility, rolled back, or explicitly closed; it is never returned beside raw `T`.

A bounded slot may begin Vacant, adopt an external value through checked pre-admission that returns it unchanged on refusal, or reparent a tracked cross-root value through a distinct checked old-plus-new-overlap transaction. First installation has no displaced artifact; replacement preserves the prior value/transfer/receipt in `DisplacedPublication<T>`. Raw extraction/parts, mutable dereference/growth, detached serialization, and transfer-only close are forbidden. Drop order is value then transfer close; a panicking destructor or deliberate forget is fail-closed and cannot mint close/seal evidence.

Final convergence supplement — allocator ownership, content boundary, terminal partition, and retry generation

Canonical ownership is allocator-only: this bead owns the affine delegated lease ledger, allocator-originated allocation/publication guard, conservation verifier, and allocator evidence schema. It does not own InvocationBudget, run/worker joins, root invocation commit, sparse operation plans, sparse publication policy, or sparse callsite inventory.

Publication is two-phase and metadata-bounded. `PreparedPublishedTransfer` reserves one publication record and binds root/parent/child lease identities, OperationPlanRoot, InvocationOccurrenceRoot, output key, destination, attempt generation, registered allocation-region descriptor, disjoint envelope components, and exact charged total. Rollback consumes preparation and returns its reserved capacity without publication. Commit consumes the matching allocator-originated `LeasedAllocation<T>` plus preparation and produces one opaque `PublishedAllocation<T>`; no arbitrary T injection or bare committed transfer escape is possible.

Allocator authority proves registered regions, layout, capacity, charge, and lifetime only. It does not prove immutable scientific content, arbitrary nested allocations, or absence of interior mutation. Authority-bearing export transports the representation, allocation descriptor, transfer/close state, and receipt together. Higher layers add content authority only for a sealed representation whose complete registered-region inventory and content root are reverified.

Successful destination close is recorded only after value destruction returns normally. Dropping a transfer token never records success. Panic during value destruction leaves the publication fail-closed or records Abandoned using pre-admitted metadata; it cannot mint a close receipt. The design is implementable in safe Rust and does not rely on struct field-drop order.

At root seal:
`granted_bytes = returned_without_publication_bytes + published_total_bytes`
and
`published_total_bytes = published_live_at_seal_bytes + published_closed_before_seal_bytes`.
The same partition applies to counts, including zero-byte publications. Rollback before visibility is returned, never published. A published charge is not recycled into the invocation after destination close, so the terminal partition stays affine. Close after root seal appends separate close evidence without rewriting the immutable root receipt.

Forgetting delegated or prepared authority leaves transient state and blocks root seal. Forgetting an already committed PublishedAllocation does not invalidate a legitimate seal that records it live; it permanently withholds close evidence and is a no-liveness boundary. Forgetting the root yields no root receipt.

Attempt generation is monotone. Failed/rolled-back preparation may retry the same logical binding at a new generation. After one generation commits, later commit for that logical binding refuses before mutation. Diagnostic labels are display-only and excluded from semantic identity/equality/conservation. Admission independently preallocates bounded child, allocation, preparation, publication, close/abandon, and refusal records. Every post-admission transition is allocation-free; overflow or record exhaustion refuses atomically.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. Enabling delegation on a bounded pristine root is one-shot and versioned; unbounded, used, previously configured, already sealing/sealed, or metadata-unreservable roots refuse without partial mutation. One serialized state linearizes configure, delegate, reserve, release, close, publish-transfer, and seal.
2. Root/parent/child identities are typed, canonical, allocation-free, path-bounded, and bind dynamic invocation/child subjects plus deterministic components. Duplicate sibling paths, wrong parent/root/owner/path/version, and identity mutation refuse independently.
3. Delegated authority is non-Clone/non-Copy and capacity affine. Sibling and nested transfers cannot recreate bytes. Real allocations charge only the delegated lease and never also charge the ambient root. Zero-byte transfers still count as live transient authority and block premature seal.
4. Every reservation/drop, child close, panic/unwind, cancellation path, partial initialization, failed try-reserve, and replacement old-plus-new overlap returns capacity exactly once. Parent close refuses live transient descendants/charges; root seal freezes admission, remains drainable after refusal, and replays one immutable verified receipt after success.
5. Successful output publication uses a non-Clone prepared transfer and one linearization point to move exact charged payload/layout bytes from invocation staging into destination authority. Failure returns staging and leaves no published amount. Success seals conservation as granted equals returned plus published, with no gap/double charge; later destination drop closes the published authority separately without relabeling the root receipt.
6.
