title: fs-sparse protocol adoption: checked operation plans, authority joins, classified inventory ratchet, and API/inventory E2E
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Outcome

Build the L1 sparse-domain protocol over the three proven lower-layer authorities: explicit `Cx`; affine child/finalizer/run/memory/publication authority; checked sparse plans; deterministic poll/tile identities; bounded ordered real TilePool witness partitions; full invocation child partitions; default root-atomic staged and owned publication; explicit preselected ChildLocal partial publication; sparse evidence joined to finalized invocation receipts; and a complete classified current-callsite ratchet.

This child creates the stable API/inventory mode of `scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh` and runs its current runtime canary in a required focused strict-remote/DSR lane now. It does not pre-claim the actual CSR/BSR/SELL kernels, assembly/conversion, or downstream solver migrations owned by 21.2-21.4.

## Checked plan and evidence contract

- Plan types bind operation/format, rows/columns/nnz/max-row, block/SELL geometry, rhs/batch/iteration counts, logical/physical pair/FMA work, validation/sort/conversion work, scratch/staging/output bytes, bounded ordered run plan, worker/tile plan, poll-plan version/stride/count/max gap, finalization reserve, publication policy, numeric policy, capability identity, and canonical plan root.
- Checked arithmetic covers row-pointer extents, dense cells, block rounding/tails, SELL padding/permutations, `nnz * rhs * iterations`, SpGEMM candidate pairs, sort bounds, byte layouts/alignment, output/staging overlap, poll-count conversion/products, run/worker/task counts, and finalization totals before allocation or mutation.
- Zero and max-representable plans validate without huge allocation. Exact required capacity succeeds; required-minus-one refuses without work/mutation; required-plus-one succeeds with exactly one unused unit.
- Stable protocol codes distinguish invalid shape/index/geometry, arithmetic overflow, work/poll/memory/output refusal, unsupported capability/format/policy, cancellation requested/finalized, numeric-policy failure, allocation/transfer fault, worker failure, publication conflict, nested transactional-output policy violation, partition mismatch, stale authority, and invariant breach. Nested transactional policy error is distinct from capacity exhaustion.
- Sparse evidence binds plan and occurrence, Cx mode/stream, exact ordered permit/witness partition, complete child partition plus one designated publisher, sealed allocator and PublishedTransfer receipts, logical units, poll observations/max gap, terminal cause, publication scope/generation, artifact before/after roots, and final receipt root.
- Default execution consumes authorities and returns either `InPlaceInvocationCommit<T>` or `PublishedInvocation<T>` plus finalized receipt. Verifier/join/consumer APIs accept transported receipts; execution never asks callers to provide success evidence.
- Retryable failure may return only opaque must-use `Unpublished<T>` with private storage and diagnostic metadata. It cannot expose/borrow/deref/destructure/serialize/erase/convert the value or retrofit ChildLocal. It can only re-enter the same bound retry or be discarded.
- Default in-place APIs use full delegated staging and unchanged destination on every non-success. Owned construction/conversion keeps the object private until terminal observation and transfer, then returns a fully sealed published wrapper. ChildLocal is explicit opt-in before execution. Committed-prefix remains unavailable until a later separately typed contract.
- No sparse runtime, scheduler, cancellation gate, resource ledger, or ledger-layer dependency is introduced.

## Publication and partition state

One operation may declare zero/one/many bounded runs. InvocationBudget mints one affine permit per ordinal; missing, duplicate, reordered, replayed, wrong-plan/occurrence, or extra witnesses refuse. Zero/one/two successful nonpublishing siblings are allowed only when each is verified Completed and output-free. Failed/cancelled/refused, missing, duplicated, or publishing siblings block root success.

Preparation requires registered quiescence: no live unfinished sibling/descendant, worker, arena, or transient allocation; no prior output; exact artifact capacity; complete partitions; clean bound root; and one prepared transfer. Only artifact/evidence/transfer authority held by the token is exempt. Drop restores admission-closed retry and advances generation; stale/wrong/cross-invocation/duplicate authority refuses before mutation.

In-place publication privately swaps through an exclusive slot, then performs the named atomic terminal observation; a terminal state at that load wins and rolls back, while a request after it loses. Owned-return observes while private, commits transfer, then moves the value to the caller. No fallible work or user destructor occurs after successful observation before cache/visibility. Published bytes remain destination-owned after root seal under `granted = returned + published`; later artifact drop closes separately.

## Canonical inventory and phased enforcement

Inventory every public/internal sparse API and all workspace production, performance, optional-feature, test, fixture, and nested fs-wasm callsites. Stable IDs use package, repo-relative source, owning item, and API/signature anchors rather than line numbers. Each row carries two orthogonal dimensions:

- route class: `production-cx`, `migration-pending`, `bounded-accessor`, `fixture-only`, or versioned `explicit-exemption`;
- publication scope: `production-root-atomic`, explicit `production-child-local-partial`, later committed-prefix owner, or not-applicable for proven bounded metadata access.

Default numeric/construction routes must be root-atomic. A route that remains Cx-aware but downgrades publication scope fails. ChildLocal rows require explicit API name, owner, no-claim, and proof they cannot convert to root evidence.

The ratchet fails on empty discovery; duplicate IDs/owners; stale/missing/escaping anchors; unknown APIs; malformed/truncated/unsorted/oversized inventory; test/fixture misclassification; production reachability to fixture helpers; pending rows without exactly one valid 21.2-21.4 owner; expired exemptions; new uncancellable paths; publication downgrade; or unreviewed baseline growth. It combines locked Cargo metadata/module discovery, token-aware source analysis, visibility/Cx-bearing API checks, compile-fail tests, and later runtime proof; it does not call a lexical scanner a complete Rust call graph.

Explicitly classify dimensions/nnz/format geometry and review row/get bounds. Assign to_dense and optional FrankenNetworkx/FrankenNumpy interop to 21.3 unless deliberately bounded. Inventory fs-solver LinearOp and nested fs-wasm under 21.4. Current roofline route remains migration-pending under 21.2 rather than falsely described as a separate production binary.

## Tests

Unit/property tests cover zero/max plans, exact/minus-one/plus-one capacities, every arithmetic boundary, deterministic run/poll plans across worker counts, wide-row polling, finalization reserve, every shared error/diagnostic, plan/evidence roots, wrong child/plan/occurrence/ordinal/witness/receipt joins, complete partitions, forged/incomplete receipts, unchanged destination, private owned failure, opaque retry/discard, pre/mid/post-work cancellation, immediately-before/after both terminal observations, allocation/transfer/worker/numeric faults, duplicate request/finalize, exact return/published transfer, later drop, retry, and post-seal refusal.

Compile-fail/API tests prove Cx plus affine authorities are required; guards/results are must-use; plan/evidence/receipt success is nonconstructible; permit/token/transfer cannot clone/reissue; opaque Unpublished cannot extract/borrow/deref/destructure/convert/relabel; ChildLocal cannot satisfy root APIs; nested transactional output grants refuse; and fixture helpers cannot implement the sealed surface. Rustdoc examples cover root-atomic in-place/owned, preselected ChildLocal, cancellation, retry, and unbound migration.

Pure models cover zero to two children/workers/runs over admit/start/open/work/request/fault/drain/release/prepare-transfer/prepare-commit/drop/retry/swap/rollback/publish/seal/artifact-drop/replay/late request. Seeded mutants alter/omit polls, wide-row polls, plan/occurrence/ordinal/permit/witness, partitions/publisher, resource return, transfer, scope/generation, finalizer, pre/post observation, rollback, postcommit refusal, artifact root, report/root receipt, or evidence fields; each dies independently.

Scanner self-tests retain comments/strings/raw strings, aliases/reexports/qualified/trait/macro ambiguity, unclassified/stale/duplicate/missing-owner/fixture-reachable/missing-Cx/expired/malformed/empty/unsorted/oversized/prefix-tampered/source-movement/publication-downgrade cases. Synthetic fixtures remain non-authoritative.

## E2E and deterministic logging

`scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh` exposes stable `--check`, plain `--list` for the complete catalog, `--self-test`, `--run smoke|full --family-mode api-inventory|runtime-canary|kernels-p0|assembly-conversion|consumer-solver|all --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`, frozen `--negative CASE --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`, and artifact-only `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`. This Bead executes api-inventory/runtime-canary only; kernels-p0, assembly-conversion, consumer-solver, and all are registered-but-reserved until 21.2, 21.3, and terminal 21.4 close. The historical quick manifest migrates explicitly to canonical smoke; no active quick, `--mode`, or `--profile` alias remains.

The current API/inventory mode verifies the real workspace inventory and runs: the read-only canonical-CSR validation/walk canary; a real staged sentinel destination; an owned returned object; full run/child partitions; explicit ChildLocal negative controls; opaque retry/discard; active, pre/mid/post-work cancel; immediately-before/after terminal observations; allocation/worker/numeric/transfer faults; rollback; late request; success; and later destination drop. It uses real asupersync, permit-bearing WitnessedRun, InvocationBudget finalizer/root commit, delegated memory/PublishedTransfer, and receipt verification. It makes no migrated-kernel claim.

Stdout is capped canonical JSONL in exact order/count with exactly one terminal seal; stderr/artifacts are capped. Semantic rows retain schema/domain/version/mode/sequence/case, source/constellation/build/Rust/Cargo/target/features, inventory classifications/owners/publication scope, sparse geometry, plan/occurrence/partitions, resources/polls, lifecycle order, worker/task/arena/lease/transfer facts, artifact roots, receipt/refusal/retry/no-claim, and artifact root. Every u64/u128 semantic value is `{value:"...",unit:"...",width:"u64|u128"}` with 2^53/u64/u128 boundary and malformed parser tests. PID, wall time, absolute paths, environment secrets, tokens, and host noise are excluded.

The static ratchet is wired into xtask check-all/DSR. The current runtime API/inventory canary itself also runs in a required focused strict-remote/DSR configured lane before this bead closes. Only later migrated kernel/assembly/solver modes defer.

## Acceptance Criteria

Checked sparse APIs consume rather than recreate all proven authorities and return typed root-atomic results by default. ChildLocal remains explicit/nonconvertible. The inventory is deterministic, complete, source-verified, publication-aware, and shrinking. All boundary/lifecycle/partition/opaque-recovery/compile-fail/model/mutation/scanner/root/forgery/publication/memory/log tests pass. The read-only plus real staged/owned runtime canary retains bounded canonical evidence and one seal under strict current-snapshot focused DSR proof. Zero legacy production bypasses remains the later 21.4 and parent-21 gate.
design:
Canonical design after reality check

The sparse protocol consumes the three proven lower-layer authorities and exposes publication strength explicitly. Default in-place and owned-construction/conversion execution APIs consume checked plan, occurrence, affine run/finalizer/memory/publication authorities and return the typed 21.1.1 root-atomic result plus finalized receipt. They never ask callers to supply a success receipt. Verifier/join/consumer APIs alone accept transported receipts. `ChildLocal` remains explicit opt-in partial publication selected before execution and cannot convert to the default after failure. Committed-prefix remains a third later policy.

A retryable failure may return only opaque `Unpublished<T>` bound to the same plan/occurrence/root. It exposes diagnostics but no extraction, borrow, dereference, destructuring, serialization, erasure, or conversion to `T`, ChildLocal, or published output. It can only re-enter the same root-atomic retry path or be discarded/dropped, so failed scientific output cannot escape through recovery ergonomics.

One operation may declare a bounded ordered zero/one/many run plan. InvocationBudget mints one permit per ordinal; sparse evidence binds the complete verified witness partition and full child partition with one designated publishing child. Completed nonpublishing siblings must be verified successful and output-free; any failed/cancelled/refused, missing, duplicate, or additional publisher blocks root success.

Plan/evidence types retain every geometry, work, memory, poll, numeric, capability, worker, staging, and output field in the base description. Inventory classification is two-dimensional: migration/reachability class plus publication scope. Defaults are `production-root-atomic`; explicit partial routes are `production-child-local-partial` with owner/no-claim. A Cx-aware downgrade fails the ratchet.

The API/inventory journey keeps read-only CSR validation/walk and adds a real bounded staged destination plus owned returned-object case. In-place uses private-swap/post-swap observation/rollback; owned-return keeps object private, observes terminal state, commits transfer, then returns it. Failure proves unchanged/no returned published object; success proves one exact install/return with live destination authority; child-local controls prove weaker evidence rejection. `scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh` remains the single runner/schema. Its runtime API/inventory canary is a required focused strict-remote and DSR lane now; only migrated kernel/assembly/conversion/solver modes defer.

Sparse artifact lifetime and slot bootstrap (canonical)

Sparse owned output is `PublishedInvocation<T>` privately containing `PublishedAllocation<T>` plus the finalized invocation receipt. In-place output targets an explicit Vacant or Installed `PublicationSlot<T>`; checked sentinel adoption binds exact registered storage, slot/generation, ambient root, and `PublishedTransferEnvelope` before execution and returns the sentinel unchanged on refusal. A tracked cross-root occupant requires checked reparent admission with exact old-plus-new overlap or refuses unchanged. First install returns no displacement; replacement returns only guarded `DisplacedPublication<T>`. Shared reads and consuming authority-preserving handoff are supported. Raw extraction/parts, mutable dereference/growth, and detached serialization are forbidden; modification or replacement is a new invocation.

Slot publication is a serialized generation transition. Private swap is unobservable, rollback restores the old generation before unlock, successful install publishes with release/acquire ordering, and no user destructor runs under the slot lock. Drop ordering is value then transfer close then receipt; panic/forget is fail-closed. The sparse receipt attests only the registered artifact storage inventory, never uncharged transitive allocations or later external copies/mutations.

Final convergence supplement — sparse ownership, transition semantics, inventory axes, and runner grammar

This epic consumes without reimplementing generic finalizer/invocation transaction types from 21.1.1, verified worker evidence from 21.1.2, and allocator publication/conservation from 21.1.3. It owns sparse checked-plan types, sparse admission/error mapping, sparse authority-preserving adapters, the classified workspace inventory/ratchet, and shared-runner api-inventory/runtime-canary modes. Generic prepared commit, slot, displacement, unpublished/published wrappers, terminal transition, retry generation, and drop semantics remain lower-layer implementation ownership and are integration-tested here.

A sparse plan binds schema/version, OperationPlanRoot, occurrence, operation and formats, shapes/index width/nnz/block/padding, maximum inner-loop work per poll, declared TilePoolPlanRoots/run/worker partition, all work/poll/memory/output/finalizer budgets, scratch/staging capacity, destination-before root/capacity/generation, peak replacement overlap, numeric/deterministic/publication policies, dispatch/tuning, and feature/capability roots. Every arithmetic product/sum/conversion/range/capacity comparison is checked before allocation/work.

Root publication consumes one named versioned atomic compare-and-transition or TerminalDecisionSnapshot, not an unstructured load. If cancellation/deadline/failure wins, the private swap rolls back and only opaque recovery remains. If commit wins, later request cannot revoke visibility. An occupied slot is the bound before-state, not prior publication for this occurrence. The new occurrence charges only new regions; peak admission includes the already-authorized old allocation plus staged replacement without recharging old bytes. Displaced authority remains under its prior root/close ledger.

Sparse content authority requires a sealed representation with complete registered-region inventory and reverified content root. Authority-bearing export keeps representation, content/allocation/transfer/final receipt together. Generic shared allocator access is not immutability proof; bare value serialization is a no-claim.

ChildLocal is preselected, separately typed, and weak. It may coexist with later root failure but cannot enter the root-final receipt or default return. Opaque Unpublished retry/discard produces evidence only when destruction completes normally; panic/forget is fail-closed.

Inventory uses three orthogonal axes: reachability (production, benchmark-production, test-only, fixture-only, metadata-only, explicit-exemption); protocol state (compliant, migration-pending, not-applicable); and publication scope (InvocationAtomic, ChildLocal, none). Every entry binds stable symbol/source anchors. Exemptions bind owner, rationale, feature reachability, review/expiry condition, and no-claim. Unreviewed migration/exemption growth fails; a legitimate new route updates baseline only through explicit reviewed classification/owner/target/rationale. Count reduction cannot delete supporting evidence.

Runner grammar is:
`--list`;
`--check`;
`--self-test`;
`--run smoke|full --family-mode api-inventory|runtime-canary|kernels-p0|assembly-conversion|consumer-solver|all --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`;
`--negative CASE --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`;
`--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`.
`--family-mode` is valid only with `--run`; `--mode`, `--profile`, a direct legacy `quick` selector, and conflicting selectors are Usage with bounded diagnostics. A retained legacy `quick` manifest can migrate explicitly to `smoke`; there is no implicit alias. The stream is exactly run_start; for each fixed case, case_start, bounded ordered rows, and exactly one case_terminal that references the scientific seal or typed refusal; then one run_summary and exactly one final run_terminal; nothing follows the run_terminal. Replay is byte-exact only when schema/source/build/target/features match; otherwise it refuses with mismatched fields. Runtime canaries use typed in-process authorities and deterministic barriers; leaf JSON is parsed only for schema testing.

Reality-check acceptance addendum: invocation-root atomicity and real publication E2E

This addendum strengthens and disambiguates the existing transactional-publication language without removing any feature.

1. The default sparse in-place success path accepts only a distinct invocation-root-final receipt produced by a non-Clone prepared-root-commit authority. That receipt must bind the checked sparse plan, the unique invocation occurrence/permit, exact child, executor-minted witnessed run, root-bound sealed delegated-memory receipt, finalization report, output declaration, before/after destination roots, and terminal invocation receipt. A child-local report, loose hash, caller boolean, standalone replay root, or independently recomputed equivalent execution cannot satisfy this type.
2. Preserve independently durable child output as an explicitly named weaker ChildLocal or PartialPublication API/evidence scope. It may coexist with a later cancelled/refused root, carries a precise no-claim, and has no conversion into the strong sparse receipt. Preserve committed-prefix behavior as a third, separately typed future policy; it is neither the default nor interchangeable with child-local or invocation-atomic publication.
3. Replace the read-only-only runtime proof with a real bounded small staged destination in addition to the CSR validation/walk. Each case records a sentinel before root and observed after root. Every pre-admission, pre-work, mid-work, drain, allocation, worker, numeric, prepare, and post-swap refusal must retain the sentinel; success must install the staged root exactly once. Keep read-only validation as an additive canary, not as publication proof.
4. Add explicit negative-control E2E cases showing child-local output can remain changed when the root later fails and is therefore rejected by the strong sparse join. This proves both preservation of the weaker functionality and non-confusion at the user boundary.
5. Unit/property/model/mutation/E2E coverage must include a live sibling, live descendant, live worker, live delegated allocation, prior output from another child, dropped prepare token, retry after drop, stale generation, wrong child, cross-invocation token, wrong plan, wrong occurrence permit, duplicate permit consumption, pre-swap cancellation/deadline, post-swap cancellation/deadline with rollback, cancellation immediately after the successful linearization point remaining Completed, post-commit split/work/recovery refusal, double commit, report/root/witness/memory mutations, and compile-fail rejection of child-local evidence where invocation-final evidence is required.
6. Prospective report/receipt construction, capacity reservation, hashing, and semantic verification happen before destination mutation. After the successful post-swap terminal check, only infallible moves and scalar state installation are permitted. Allocation/construction refusal is structured, destination-preserving, and retryable.
7. The protocol E2E owns the typed integration of the three prerequisite leaves. The fs-alloc leaf proves delegation independently; the TilePool leaf proves executor completion independently; the invocation-finalizer leaf joins their non-forgeable authorities; this sparse leaf proves the actual user-facing default and logging. No prerequisite leaf may silently replace a missing typed join with hashes or prose.

The earlier read-only canary, inventory ratchet, all checked-plan fields, all scanner cases, all logging fields, all migration modes, and every no-claim boundary remain required.

title: Sparse production kernels: migrate CSR/BSR/SELL SpMV/SpMM with bounded wide-row polling and transactional outputs
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Outcome

Migrate the real CSR, BSR, and SELL-C-sigma SpMV/SpMM kernels—including the exact route timed by P0—to the Cx protocol. Polling must be bounded inside attacker-controlled wide rows and padded slices, outputs must be transactional, and deterministic numeric/order semantics must remain explicit across formats, tiers, and thread counts.

## Implementation contract

- Partition logical work by deterministic row/block/slice/tile identity; worker timing never changes the poll plan or reduction order.
- Poll inside maximum-width rows and long block/slice loops so the checkpoint bound is not proportional to a user-controlled row.
- Include physical padded work, conversion/residency, tails, signed-zero behavior, worker caps, scratch, and publication staging in admission and receipts.
- Preserve scalar/reference routes and public alpha/beta/overwrite semantics. On cancel, fault, allocation refusal, or numeric-policy failure, publish no mixed old/new vector or matrix.
- The P0 SELL route must directly call these kernels; a cancellable wrapper around an uncancellable timed loop is forbidden.

## Unit, property, and failure tests

Cross product CSR/BSR/SELL, SpMV/SpMM, empty/singleton/max legal shapes, zero nnz, skewed and ultra-wide rows, duplicates, unsorted indices, invalid offsets/columns, block tails, padding, signed zero, alpha/beta, NaN/Inf policy, alignment, dispatch tier, batch tail, and required thread counts. Compare to an independent scalar oracle and cross-format conversions; test row/column permutation and chunking metamorphics. Inject cancellation before first tile, inside a wide row, between blocks/slices, during reduction, and before publication; also inject allocation and worker faults. Assert bounded max work between polls, full drain, exact-once resource return, unchanged output, deterministic bits/receipts, and no leak.

Seeded mutants include skipped padded traffic, signed-zero loss, wrong worker cap, unbounded wide-row loop, scalar fallback, benchmark-only path, wrong dispatch/tune identity, early cancellation return, partial output publication, wrong work/byte accounting, and one format silently omitted.

## No-mock E2E and logging

Contribute the kernel/P0 mode of `scripts/ci/fs_sparse_cancellation_e2e.sh`. Run the production public API and the real roofline callsite on representative CSR/BSR/SELL fixtures, including the frozen P0 SELL fixture, under live scopes; no fake scheduler or prebuilt receipt. Capture deterministic JSONL fields from the parent protocol plus format, alpha/beta, physical/logical work and bytes, padding, row-width distribution, worker/tile plan, dispatch/tune, scalar comparison root, output before/after root, cancellation/fault boundary, and artifact/receipt roots. Capture command/stdout/stderr/exit hashes and retain raw samples outside timed regions.

## Acceptance Criteria

All production CSR/BSR/SELL SpMV/SpMM and P0-timed paths use the Cx protocol; wide-row and padded work have a bounded deterministic poll plan; cross-format correctness, alpha/beta, signed-zero, worker-cap, G4/G5, fault/allocation, transactional-output, and mutation tests pass; the real solver/roofline E2E contains no uncancellable or benchmark-only bypass and retains canonical logs.
design:
Canonical kernel migration design

All production CSR/BSR/SELL-C-sigma SpMV and SpMM routes consume the checked sparse protocol from 21.1. Logical row/block/slice identities determine work partition, permit ordinal, poll locations, reduction tree, and ties; worker timing cannot change them. Plans separately account logical pair/FMA work, physical padded/duplicate/tail work, input reads, output reads/writes, staging/backup, alignment/layout overhead, worker/tile counts, finalization reserve, and exact PublishedTransferEnvelope.

Owned-return is the ergonomic default and returns PublishedInvocation<VectorOrDenseBatch>. In-place alpha/beta/overwrite uses a Vacant/Installed PublicationSlot with checked adoption/reparent and a full staged/backup transaction; on any refusal, cancellation, deadline, fault, or numeric-policy failure the old generation is restored before unlock. First install has no displacement; replacement returns guarded DisplacedPublication. Raw mutable-slice compatibility remains only as an explicitly inventory-classified weaker legacy route with no root-atomic or bounded-memory receipt and cannot be used by production solver, fs-wasm, P0, or evidence paths.

Poll plans bound work inside a single ultra-wide row, BSR inner block, SELL padded slice, SpMM rhs/batch tail, and reduction segment. Inputs/outputs are checked for aliasing and overlapping layouts before admission. Scalar, NEON/x86 tier, worker-cap, alpha/beta, signed-zero, NaN/Inf, duplicate, unsorted, padding, and tail behavior are frozen by plan/version; unsupported combinations refuse rather than silently changing route or semantics.

The kernels-p0 mode of the shared runner exercises public production APIs and the exact roofline adapter. It proves route identity, scalar/cross-format agreement, root-atomic rollback/publication, authority lifetime, and bounded polling; it does not pre-claim the final bandwidth target owned by fz2.10.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. Every production CSR/BSR/SELL SpMV/SpMM and P0-timed callsite consumes 21.1 checked plan, Cx, exact run/child/memory/publication authorities, and a verified terminal receipt; no wrapper surrounds an uncancellable inner loop.
2. Plans and checked arithmetic cover all shapes/strides/index widths, nnz/row/block/slice/rhs/batch extents, logical and physical work/bytes, padding/tails, alpha/beta output reads, staging/backup, overlap, alignment, workers/tiles/polls/finalizer, and publication envelope. Zero/max/exact/minus-one/plus-one refuse before allocation/work/mutation as appropriate.
3. Deterministic poll gaps are bounded inside ultra-wide rows, block products, padded slices, rhs/batch tails, and reductions. Deadline/cancel requests before and after every named boundary have deterministic request-drain-finalize outcomes.
4. Owned-return and typed-slot in-place routes are InvocationAtomic. Vacant first install, checked baseline adoption, same-root replacement, cross-root reparent/refusal, guarded displacement, shared read, consuming handoff, rollback, later drop, and panic/forget fail-closed are covered. ChildLocal/legacy routes are explicit weaker no-claims and cannot enter proof paths.

> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Gap

The original BEDROCK vision and closed `frankensim-epic-bedrock-6ys.4`/`frankensim-9ekv` headline require >=0.60 of peak for 6x6-48x48 batched dense kernels. Current retained contract evidence is roughly 0.10-0.29, and the later `frankensim-ny9d` closeout intentionally used a lower anti-collapse floor. That floor is useful regression protection but does not satisfy or supersede the original performance goal. No active Bead owns the remaining delta.

## End state

Deliver production-safe, deterministic SIMD-across-batch kernels and autotuned layouts whose declared representative size classes attain >=0.60 of an admitted measured compute peak on Apple aarch64 and x86-64, while preserving pivot/factorization semantics, memory budgets, cancellation checkpoints, fallible allocation, and scalar/tier equivalence.

## Scope

Freeze the size-class portfolio, batch cardinalities, operation-count conventions, data layouts, pivot/no-pivot families, transposition, scalar types, cache/tile policy, and weighting used to determine the aggregate gate. Profile register pressure, load/store intensity, interleave geometry, AoS/SoA transforms, tail handling, packing, dispatch, and batch scheduling. Implement only production-path optimizations with scalar twins and justified golden changes. Integrate autotune decisions and source/build/tune identities into citable roofline receipts. Keep per-class results visible so an aggregate cannot hide a catastrophic class.

## Tests and evidence

G0/property tests compare every size/tier/tail/pivot family to an independent scalar reference with condition-aware tolerances or bitwise contracts as declared. G3 varies batch order and equivalent layouts. G4 cancels during packing, panels, pivots, and publication and verifies drain/no leaks/unchanged destination. G5 covers required thread counts and repeats. Performance tests seed wrong FLOP counts, omitted layout conversion, scalar fallback, class-weight manipulation, stale peaks, one-ISA evidence, and benchmark-only dispatch. Retain raw per-class samples, phase timings, tune choices, machine/build/lock fingerprints, before/after attribution, DSR/RCH logs, and artifact roots.

## No-claim boundary

A lower anti-collapse floor, one favorable size, microkernel-only timing, single ISA, or exploratory/dirty/off-pin evidence is not the >=0.60 production claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

The frozen representative 6x6-48x48 portfolio reaches >=0.60 of admitted peak on both reference ISA families through production APIs; every class remains above its declared non-collapse floor; scalar/tier correctness, pivot semantics, deterministic replay, cancellation, memory admission, and negative-twin tests pass; raw samples and stable-snapshot DSR/RCH receipts are retained.


## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set: `crates/fs-la` batched kernels/dispatch/tuning/CONTRACT/tests, the minimal `fs-simd` safe-facade capsules and SAFETY registry entries if new architecture leaves are required, and `fs-roofline` per-class evidence. Coordinate golden bumps and do not weaken anti-collapse sentinels. Run scalar/tier/property/G4/G5 tests and per-class remote perf first, then stable DSR and two-host adjudication through `6ys.26`.

## Success Criteria

The frozen complete claim matrix and numeric-semantics decision, production route implementation, and real-consumer proof children all pass; no historical operation/dtype/size is lost; every required performance row meets its frozen >=0.60 or non-collapse rule under the >=30-sample conservative protocol on both ISAs; correctness/cancellation/memory/route/denominator/mutation tests and scripts/ci/e2e_batched_dense.sh replay independently.

## Phase 9.5 governing claim rule

Before implementation, freeze a versioned operation x scalar x size x batch x layout x ISA matrix. Reconcile plan 8x8-32x32 performance rows with historical support for 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, and 48 while preserving every operation and dtype. State which rows require >=0.60 and which carry a frozen binding-roof floor; thresholds, weights, exclusions, and denominators cannot change after measurement. New packed/grouped routes may change operation order only under a new numeric-semantics identity, justified golden transition, condition-aware error contract, same-route determinism, and explicit cross-route comparison. Children 22.1 through 22.3 own decision, implementation, and consumer proof.
design:
Canonical source, E2E, and lifecycle contract

Evidence binds a clean content source closure: repository tree/root HEAD, canonical constellation.lock and every transitive sibling head/cleanliness, Cargo.lock, toolchain/target/profile/features, generated contracts/registries, workload/data/oracle/policy/checker identities, and producer version. Capture before dispatch and immediately before seal; movement, undeclared relevant files, dirty inputs, or mismatched roots yields InvalidEvidence. Focused strict-remote and workspace DSR are separate proof states; close records exact commands/exits/run/log/artifact/worker-target identities and retained source bundle.

Every shared script consumes huq.24 CanonicalEvidenceRunnerV2. Family grammar is exactly --list; --check; --self-test; --run smoke|full [--family-mode MODE] --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL; --negative CASE --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL; and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL. Family extensions declare immutable MODE values; negative/replay bind mode and profile through their manifests; --mode/--profile aliases and invalid combinations are Usage before work. ProofExitV2 is 0 Pass, 10 Failed, 11 Refused (reason=InvalidEvidence where applicable), 12 NoData, 13 Stale, 14 EnvironmentInvalid retryable, 15 Blocked, 16 Unsupported, 17 NotRun, 18 Cancelled, 19 TimedOut, 64 Usage, 70 InternalError. Stdout is run_start; per fixed case case_start, bounded ordered rows, exactly one case_terminal; run_summary; exactly one run_terminal; nothing after. Shared literal caps, parser/tamper corpus, typed lossless numbers, bounded stderr/artifacts, and actionable non-Pass diagnostics apply.

Lifecycle phases are Draft -> Frozen -> PreflightValid -> Running or Sampling -> Draining -> Finalized -> Sealed -> Fresh -> Admitted, where Admitted requires an executed Pass case result. Every executed family terminal maps exactly to ProofExitV2 as Pass, Failed, Refused { reason }, NoData, Stale, EnvironmentInvalid, Blocked, Unsupported, Cancelled, or TimedOut; it can never be NotRun. Runner suppression is a separate lifecycle path: after a prior Cancelled, TimedOut, or controlled InternalError, each remaining manifest slot emits case_start execution=suppressed, zero family rows, and immediate NotRun with the matching typed causal root; NotRun is never a scientific verdict or run terminal. Usage is pre-run diagnostic-only and InternalError remains runner-owned. InvalidEvidence is only `Refused(reason=InvalidEvidence)`. Models/mutants reject top-level InvalidEvidence, executed-to-NotRun conversion, every state alias, early/double seal, publication before drain, missing/duplicate/extra rows, stale/future receipt, policy/source/host substitution, partial artifacts, post-result edits, numeric truncation, and output after terminal. Historical Phase 9.5 FINAL/PASS comments are planning review only.

Batched-dense family authority

The target is a deterministic admitted route portfolio retaining lanes-across-batch and allowing a versioned within-matrix or grouped production route where the frozen matrix requires it. No single algorithm is privileged after the structural-ceiling audit. Every normative target row independently attains at least 0.60 conservatively. Weighted aggregates are diagnostic only. Each governed floor/non-collapse row may veto family closure when below its own frozen threshold, preserving user-visible regression protection; it can never satisfy, average into, replace, or inflate a normative target row.

22.1 emits BatchedDenseClaimMatrixV1; 22.2 emits CandidateKernelReceiptV1; 22.3 emits CandidateConsumerEvidenceV1; only independent 26.1 emits AdjudicatedBatchedDensePassV1. All bind the same source/matrix/workload/statistics/denominator/host/checker roots. Refused, NoData, Stale, or EnvironmentInvalid keeps the family open.

Preserve the literal functional inventory: batched GEMM and the declared small dense solve/factorization/eigen/consumer families, scalar twins, deterministic/Cx/cancellation behavior, safe SIMD tiers, explicit numeric semantics, and real public consumer reachability.

Family-wide runner modes are frozen as policy|kernel|tuning|kernel-suite|consumer|capture|candidate|all. 22.1 owns policy; 22.2.5 owns kernel/tuning/kernel-suite; terminal 22.3.4 owns consumer/capture/candidate and is the sole owner of the registered `--family-mode all` selector. Raw durations, counters, pair identities/order, exclusions, and phase reconciliation are performance-root identity; only wall-clock timestamps and other declared volatile annotations are non-semantic.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. Every source-anchored functional row promised by the governing plan is present in BatchedDenseClaimMatrixV1 as functional_support and, where applicable, additionally classified normative_target, floor_only, or diagnostic under the exact 22.1 schema. No promised row may be reclassified unsupported, hidden by representative or applicable wildcards, or replaced by another operation or consumer. Unsupported with no-claim is reserved only for explicitly source-anchored combinations outside the promised inventory and cannot satisfy or veto a promised row; deletion or downgrade of any historical functional row is a mandatory failing mutant.
2. Every normative row independently has conservative attainment >=0.60 on both applicable reference ISA/tier scopes under its frozen workload, PerformanceDecisionSpec, denominator, host policy, and exact execution placement. Aggregates cannot satisfy closure. Each governed floor row must meet its own frozen threshold and may veto closure, but cannot satisfy, average into, replace, or inflate a normative row.
3. 22.1, 22.2, 22.3, and 26.1 receipts bind identical source/matrix/workload/statistics/denominator/host/checker roots. Only a Pass from independent 26.1 can close the family.
4. All declared functional operations are correct, deterministic within scope, checked/admitted, Cx-aware, and cancellation/fault safe. Exact real-public reachability applies to RequiredProductionJourney ConsumerRouteKey rows only; KernelOnlyNoConsumer rows retain full kernel functionality plus explicit no-integration claim and future owner, cannot satisfy consumer evidence, and never justify fabricated fs-contact/fs-lbm/test/bench routes.
5. Unit/property/metamorphic/model/compile-fail/mutation/fault tests and smoke/full/negative/replay E2E cover every row, consumer, route, numeric policy, layout/tail, thread/tier, authority, publication policy, and evidence field.
6. Canonical logging/exits/caps, stable source closure, fresh dual-ISA performance proof, exact commands/artifacts, constellation verify-only, DSR, and independent artifact-only replay pass. Historical comments or candidate evidence cannot close.
7. ProofExitV2 and huq.24 case/run grammar, literal caps, artifact safety, parser/tamper matrix, and every one-below/exact/one-above boundary are exact across 22.1-.3 and 26.1. A dedicated schema/compile-fail mutant proves that top-level `InvalidEvidence` cannot be constructed or parsed; only `Refused(reason=InvalidEvidence)` is admitted. 8. The literal family inventory includes determinant/inverse k=1..4, closed-form batch_eigh3_values, general-small-k batch_eigh with governed 6x6, and every existing GEMM/factor/solve/fallback/numeric/layout/member/publication behavior. 9. Runner ownership and performance identity are exact: only 22.3.4 owns all; raw samples/counters/pairs/exclusions/phases are bound while volatile wall timestamps remain outside semantic identity. Any newly discovered RequiredProductionJourney gap becomes a separately estimated integration Bead with a named domain owner, dependency, public behavior, tests, and E2E; it cannot be hidden inside the 22.3.1 evidence estimate.
10. Public adoption is a family close gate owned by 22.2.1: every pre-existing batched public API, reexport, example, and first-party caller has a source-anchored Retained, IntentionallyBreaking, or Deprecated disposition, with no automatic shim; retained surfaces pass behavior-parity and compile/API examples, deliberate deltas have an exact old-to-new map, migration guide, authority/semantic impact, and actionable compile diagnostics, and all first-party consumers migrate atomically. No candidate or adjudicated family Pass may strand an existing caller or any promised operation, numeric, fallback, member-outcome, cancellation, or publication capability.
notes:
Canonical row-wise authority and independent-adjudication algebra supersede any weighted-aggregate or deterministic-SIMD-across-batch-only reading.

Distinct 60-minute estimate covers claim/implementation/consumer/adjudicator root join and closeout review. Child implementation/evidence estimates total 22,560 minutes and remain separately countable.
Runner mechanics consume huq.24; family-specific rows, consumer paths, evidence, and tests remain owned here.
Runner state/exit semantics inherit exact huq.24.1: InvalidEvidence is a Refused reason; Cancelled=18 and TimedOut=19 remain distinct.

Canonical artifact placement inheritance: every artifact-dir or --artifact-dir shorthand in this Bead expands to huq.24.1's required pair --artifact-root ROOT --artifact-dir REL. ROOT is an admitted/canonicalized existing caller-owned workspace, external-volume, or temp directory; REL is a relative-safe new or empty destination. Bundle manifests retain only relative paths, host-specific absolute ROOT is non-semantic/redacted, and omission, escape, link/reparse race, nonempty overwrite, or root mismatch refuses with ranked repair. Candidate runner evidence consumes huq.24.4; authority-bearing final gates additionally consume huq.24.5.

title: Batched-dense claim matrix and algorithm/numeric-semantics decision
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Outcome

Before implementation or measurement, freeze a versioned operation x scalar-type x size x batch-cardinality x layout x ISA claim matrix and decide which production algorithms and numeric-semantics identities may satisfy each row. Reconcile plan section 14.1's 8x8-32x32 performance target with historical functional support for sizes 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, and 48. No feature, operation, dtype, or size is removed.

## Mandatory functional inventory

Retain GEMM overwrite and beta-accumulate; Cholesky; lower/upper triangular solve and Cholesky solve; partial-pivot LU and LU solve; determinant/inverse for 2x2, 3x3, and 4x4; existing symmetric eigensolver 3x3 and 6x6 routes; f64, f32, and f32-storage/f64-accumulate semantics; generic fallback; alignment and batch tails; poisoned-member isolation; membership invariance; deterministic pivot ties; and documented cancellation/publication behavior.

## Claim and route decision

For every row, freeze required correctness contract, production route, operation/byte model, denominator, threshold, weighting, exclusion, non-collapse floor, batch/shape portfolio, and no-claim boundary before seeing results. State exactly which rows must attain >=0.60 of admitted compute peak and which carry a predeclared binding-roof non-collapse floor. An aggregate may not hide a required class.

`frankensim-ny9d` found the existing lane-independent register-tile family structurally capped near 0.37. Reaching >=0.60 may therefore use packed within-matrix or grouped-matrix execution. Keep lanes-across-matrices for small batches and bit-preserving cases. Any route that changes operation order receives a new numeric-semantics identity, justified golden transition, condition-aware error/residual contract, deterministic same-route replay, and explicit cross-route comparison; it cannot claim scalar bit identity falsely.

Pure microkernels remain leaves. A Cx-bearing production driver owns checked admission, scratch, tiling, request-drain-finalize, polling, and publication. Freeze unchanged-destination versus typed committed-prefix semantics and the staging/double-buffer cost.

## Unit and policy tests

Validate claim-matrix schema/version/canonicalization, complete historical inventory, unique row/route ownership, exact decimal thresholds, denominator authority, plan/historical range reconciliation, no post-measurement edits, and migration/refusal of old identities. Mutation tests delete an operation/size/dtype, change weights/threshold after results, relabel a route, hide a class, claim bit equality after order change, select a stale denominator, omit staging cost, or bypass Cx. Every mutant fails with stable code and repair.

## Planning E2E and logs

Add the decision mode of `scripts/ci/e2e_batched_dense.sh`: load the real registry/contracts/consumer inventory, emit the frozen matrix, verify every consumer maps to a route and claim, and reject ambiguous/missing/historical-feature loss. JSONL records schema, row/case ID, operation/dtype/size/batch/layout/ISA, consumer, route and numeric-semantics identities, correctness and performance contracts, work/byte model, denominator/threshold/floor/weight, Cx/publication policy, source/constellation roots, verdict, refusal, and repair. No performance result is accepted during this phase.

## Acceptance Criteria

A versioned canonical claim matrix preserves every historical operation/dtype/size and reconciles the plan core; every row has an explicit production route, numeric semantics, correctness contract, denominator, threshold or floor, Cx/publication policy, and consumer owner frozen before measurement; all deletion/route-spoof/post-result-threshold mutants fail; the real inventory E2E and deterministic logs pass.

Claim matrix and frozen decision policy

ConsumerRouteKey binds crate, repo-relative file/module, exact public symbol and signature, production caller/call-chain anchor, feature/profile reachability, fixture, owner, and migration disposition.

PerformanceDecisionSpecV1 freezes host selection and numeric HostValidityPolicy limits, samples/attempt cap, valid/excluded rules, exact one-sided confidence method/level/interpolation/rounding, numerator/denominator uncertainty and freshness pairing, and stopping. Solve/factor/eigen families do not inherit GEMM denominators. Consumer inventory is exact set equality. Diagnostics expose requested/selected/rejected routes, reason, budgets, numerical-identity change, and retry. This mode emits policy only, never a performance pass.

No-feature-loss inventory is literal. Alignment, SoA planes, tails, layouts/strides/transposes, pivot/eigen ties, member isolation/failure flags, cancellation, and publication policies remain rows or row fields.

Consumer disposition is exactly `RequiredProductionJourney` or `KernelOnlyNoConsumer { no_integration_claim, future_owner }`. Current production routes are fs_feec::whitney::element_geometry (determinant/inverse k=3) and fs_solid::fiber::update_sections_batched (Cholesky/solve k=2). No fs-contact/fs-lbm route exists today. Every RequiredProductionJourney must have one unique inventory row and a genuine public caller; KernelOnlyNoConsumer preserves functional/API tests but cannot satisfy consumer/performance claims. Execution multiplicity is separately frozen per case and may include warmups and >=30 samples.

Canonical acceptance criteria

1. BatchedDenseClaimMatrixV1 contains exact set equality independently within functional, target, floor, diagnostic, and ConsumerRouteKey inventories, plus declared foreign-key/coverage joins with every literal row field; missing/duplicate/extra/ambiguous/stale rows or consumers refuse.
2. Matrix/workload/numeric/host/statistics/denominator policies freeze immutably before samples. Draft/Frozen model and API tests prevent AdmittedTune, PublishedOutput, unchecked route, or Cx-less production construction.
3. Numeric semantics are explicit per route and operation family; migration/opt-in and cross-route error bounds are versioned. User diagnostics make selection and semantic changes actionable.
4. Unit/property/canonical roundtrip/permutation tests cover every matrix field and consumer; malformed/unknown-version/overflow/truncation/lossy-number cases fail closed.
5. Compile-fail and seeded mutants cover row classification/applicability, consumer substitution, scope/tier/route swap, denominator inheritance, host/statistics policy drift, duplicate/extra entries, and direct authority fabrication.
6. Shared E2E policy mode supports canonical interfaces/logs/exits/caps and emits zero performance verdicts. Current-snapshot focused/DSR proof and independent replay pass.
7. Consumer discovery/review rejects moved/renamed/signature-changed, macro/reexport/trait ambiguity, hidden-feature, benchmark/demo/test-only, duplicate shim, ownerless, or stale caller anchors before implementation. 8. Shared ProofExitV2/grammar/caps/parser/tamper boundaries pass in policy mode. A dedicated schema/compile-fail mutant proves that top-level `InvalidEvidence` cannot be constructed or parsed; only `Refused(reason=InvalidEvidence)` is admitted. 9. title: Taylor derivative authority: remainder jets, differentiation/integration, degenerate-axis semantics, and capability refusal
description:
Implement derivative-aware Taylor authority: outward remainder jets by derivative multi-index, differentiation/integration, units, declared order caps, degenerate-axis semantics, and honest capability refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

The dedicated Acceptance Criteria field is the canonical, complete close gate. This navigation heading exists for Beads template tooling and readers; it does not duplicate, weaken, or override that field.
design:
A differentiable model carries versioned outward remainder jets through a declared derivative-order cap, with units, original domain, active-axis map, and propagation policy. Deliver production SIMD bulk Philox/distribution fills with measured speedup and bitwise scalar equivalence, adjudicate ziggurat strict-mode eligibility on both reference ISA families, and run an isolated development-only full statistical battery with reproducible shard/campaign identities and issue-on-failure discipline. - Define campaign sizes, streams, batteries, p-value interpretation, multiple-testing policy, escalation/retest rules, and false-alarm/issue discipline before running.

title: NEON, AVX2, and AVX-512 Philox fill adjudication: exact streams, transactional cancellation, and measured per-tier admission
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Outcome

Implement and adjudicate safe-facade NEON, AVX2, and AVX-512 production bulk Philox and distribution fills with exact scalar stream equivalence, checked admission, Cx-aware transactional cancellation, and a predeclared statistically defensible per-tier speed decision. NEON is executed on an enrolled capable Apple host; AVX2 and AVX-512 are each executed on enrolled capable x86 hosts. No tier substitutes for another.

## Frozen claim matrix

Before measurement, freeze required functions including existing `fill_u64` and `fill_f64`, length/alignment/tail/consumer portfolio, scalar baseline, forced-dispatch policy, StreamKey/counter/lane/draw semantics, machine/host validity, warmup, >=30 accepted samples, one-sided confidence rule, meaningful portfolio speedup target, and small-size regression bound. No best-of timing, post-hoc trimming, or benchmark-only route.

## Semantics and implementation

Preserve complete logical StreamKey domain, counter/block/lane mapping, exact draw/rejection consumption, odd tails, chunk/batch/thread independence, and scalar bit identity. Production drivers admit work/output/scratch and poll deterministically; atomic cancellation leaves destination unchanged; a separately predeclared prefix returns PublishedChildLocal plus an exact continuation receipt and explicit no-root-success claim. SIMD leaves sit behind audited safe facades with scalar twins and registered invariants.

## Tests

KAT/property cross product zero/max legal length, every alignment/misalignment/tail, forced scalar/NEON/AVX2, chunk/order/thread count, counter boundary/overflow, stream separation, rejection-consuming transforms, allocation refusal, cancel at every tile/publication boundary, and fault/panic. Compare every output bit and final counter/draw receipt to scalar. Mutants permute lanes, overlap counters, skip tails, change draws, silently fall back, spoof dispatch, omit transform work, publish partial output, ignore cancellation, or change the sample rule.

## E2E/logging

Contribute the immutable simd family mode to `scripts/ci/e2e_rng_production.sh --run smoke|full --family-mode simd --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`, with negative and replay journeys using the canonical manifest-bound selectors; --mode/--profile aliases are Usage. Exercise actual downstream consumer adapters without upward runtime dependencies. JSONL records generator/table/stream identities, all StreamKey fields, initial/final counters and draws/rejections, operation/size/alignment/tail, route/tier, scalar root, work/scratch, cancellation/publication, raw throughput samples/confidence/target, machine/load/build/tune identities, receipt/artifact roots, verdict/refusal/repair. Volatile timing metadata is non-identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every frozen production fill is bitwise scalar-equivalent across NEON/AVX2, chunking, tails, and thread counts; admission/cancellation/fault cases are transactional and leak-free; each required large-fill workload has >=30 valid samples whose lower speedup bound exceeds 1.0, the frozen portfolio target is met, and no required small size breaches its bound; every path/stream/sample mutant refuses and artifacts replay independently.
design:
Canonical random identity is the complete typed tuple of generator and algorithm version, distribution version, table version when applicable, seed root, study or run identity, consumer, operation, logical shard or tile, sample ordinal, component ordinal, and raw attempt ordinal for rejection. A derived key does not replace the tuple or claim collision freedom. Tier, worker, thread, host, timing, and schedule live in separate execution or performance receipts.

Freeze the API matrix before optimization. Fixed-consumption raw-word and uniform fills preserve exact scalar raw-word order. Rejection-consuming distributions are separate cells: each either implements scalar-order-preserving lane compaction with exact accepted-sample, raw-attempt, and rejection receipts, or remains scalar. Per-sample substreams require a new distribution identity and cannot claim legacy scalar-stream equivalence.

NEON, AVX2, and AVX-512 are separate execution tiers. AVX2 cannot satisfy AVX-512 evidence. Forced unsupported or disabled tiers refuse before execution. Auto dispatch selects only admitted cells and records tier or fallback; performance tests forbid fallback. Every required tier and workload cell ends Admitted or DisabledByEvidence only after real execution on a capable host. Admission requires exact stream equivalence and a practical speed floor above measurement noise. DisabledByEvidence requires retained capable-host correctness, route, and performance evidence plus safe scalar fallback; absent AVX-512 execution remains Blocked.

Pure indexed access may repeat intentionally. Parallel work uses affine nonoverlapping range permits and non-Clone cursors. Atomic mode consumes 21.1.1 InvocationAtomic authority. A preselected typed-prefix mode consumes PublishedChildLocal and adds an exact RNG continuation receipt with an explicit no-root-success claim; it is not committed-prefix root completion. No path silently advances, reuses raw draws, or exposes an unreceipted partial buffer. Performance uses paired interleaved blocks, valid idle hosts, frozen workloads, warmup, confidence, effect floor, regression caps, and held-out dispatch thresholds. A declared capable host that fails load, thermal, frequency, or other validity preflight is EnvironmentInvalid. NoData is reserved for absent or incomplete evidence. Lack of any enrolled AVX-512-capable host is Blocked and cannot be converted into DisabledByEvidence or closure.

Its simd family mode consumes huq.24 CanonicalEvidenceRunnerV2: ProofExitV2 states, per-case case_terminal plus final run_terminal, new-or-empty artifact-dir, literal caps, parser/tamper fixtures, and artifact replay. Performance admission certifies the speedup/attainment ratio itself with paired interleaved >=95% ratio-level coverage or simultaneous jointly calibrated bounds; marginal interval division is forbidden. Host-policy/load/thermal/frequency/placement breach is EnvironmentInvalid with retry repair; absent/incomplete measurement is NoData; no enrolled required capable host is Blocked; only actual unprofitable capable-host execution can produce DisabledByEvidence.

1. Scalar, NEON, AVX2, and AVX-512 capability and dispatch behavior is explicit. 11. - Unit and boundary tests cover happy, empty/zero/one, exact limit, one-below/one-above, maximum-without-huge-allocation, error, units/dimensions, numeric extremes, and deterministic tie/order cases owned by this leaf.
- Property/metamorphic tests exercise algebraic or relational invariants; bounded state/model tests cover lifecycle, concurrency, retry/replay, and invalid transitions where applicable.

- Seeded mutation tests independently alter every claim-bearing identity, bound, state, policy, route, authority, and no-claim field and retain minimized, reproducible failures.
- Cancellation/deadline plus injected allocation, worker/process, parser, I/O, durable-seal, publication, and replay faults are placed at every transition this leaf owns; drain/quiescence, exact resource return, no partial authority, retryability, and first-cause diagnostics are asserted. - The terminal owner named by the dependency graph runs a release-built, no-mock E2E using the canonical shared commands: --list, --check, --self-test, --run PROFILE [--family-mode MODE], --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. It never enters the production dependency graph and finite campaigns never become a theorem of randomness.

## Frozen profiles and policy

Before results, freeze tool source/build/version digests, named batteries, byte/sample budgets, generator/stream/domain selection, shard schedule, PR-smoke/nightly/release-full profiles, time/memory limits, p-value suspicion/failure bands, multiple-testing correction, rerun/escalation limits, false-alarm policy, and issue filing/ownership. Configuration and manifest roots are immutable after first result. Missing/partial/timed-out shards remain NoData/Refused, not pass.

## Runner/recovery semantics

Each shard is content-addressed, idempotent, resumable, bounded, and tied to exact generator semantics. Coordinator verifies tool/config/output identity, complete shard set, non-overlap, raw output digest, and adjusted decision. Crash/timeout/malformed output/wrong version/duplicate shard/post-result config change fail closed. Recovery resumes only missing exact shards and cannot double-count.

## Tests

Parser/coordinator unit tests cover valid/borderline/failure output, locale/format variation under pinned versions, truncation, malformed numbers, timeout, process crash, missing/duplicate/overlap/out-of-order shards, wrong tool/config, stale artifact, and policy boundaries. Seed bad generators: bias, repetition, correlation, stuck bit, lane permutation, counter overlap, short period, and duplicated shard; each declared detection class must be caught at its frozen profile. Healthy-generator false-alarm fixtures exercise multiple-testing and bounded retest rules without post-hoc forgiveness.

## E2E/logging

Contribute the immutable campaign family mode to `scripts/ci/e2e_rng_production.sh --run smoke|full --family-mode campaign --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`, with negative and replay journeys using the canonical manifest-bound selectors and --mode/--profile aliases classified as Usage. No runtime fetch or production link.

Pinned isolated smoke/nightly/full campaign manifests and a fail-closed resumable runner land outside the production graph; parser/coordinator/crash/timeout/shard/version/config tests pass; every declared bad-generator class is caught at its frozen profile; multiple-testing and bounded retest rules are applied without post-result edits; raw outputs, issues, canonical JSONL, and independent decision replay are retained, with finite-test no-claim explicit.

title: BEDROCK independent deferred-scope adjudication: drift-aware typed family receipts and current-revision smoke
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Purpose

This is the companion proof Bead for four scopes that closed historical Beads explicitly deferred: the original batched-dense performance target, multivariate Taylor/quad-double certifier machinery, the full governed Sobol table, and production RNG SIMD/strict-ziggurat/full statistical campaigns. It prevents each implementation owner from self-adjudicating a broad completion claim from focused local tests.

## Independent adjudication protocol

- Adjudicate each family at its own frozen clean admitted revision. A heavy family receipt may be reused only when its declared source/config/data/tool touch-set digests and semantic identities exactly match the current roll-up revision; relevant drift yields Stale and requires rerun.
- Assign an independent reviewer/reproducer for each family. Re-run from retained source/config/data rather than accepting owner screenshots or prose.
- Verify production reachability: downstream callers and public APIs must use the claimed path; benchmark/test-only code does not count.
- Check every contract and no-claim section against code and receipts. Preserve partial success as a narrower capability claim.
- Produce one deterministic matrix with required claim, exact evidence, authority, pass/refuse, residual gap, and blocking Bead.

## Family-specific gates

1. Batched dense: per-class correctness and >=0.60 admitted attainment on both ISAs with no aggregate masking.
2. Interval precision: independent high-precision/exact containment, multivariate operations, four-component qd invariants, escalation/refusal, and certifier mutants.
3. Sobol: table provenance/digest, high-dimension known-answer vectors, index/skip/scramble/stream identity, and cross-ISA replay.
4. RNG: scalar/SIMD equality and measured speed, honest strict-ziggurat decision on both ISAs, pinned full statistical campaigns, and seeded weak-generator detection.

## Cross-cutting adversarial tests

title: fs-la GEMM: BLIS-style autotuned microkernel + packing, f64/f32/mixed, >=75% peak target
description:
## What
`fs-la` GEMM: BLIS-style dense matrix multiply — the compute-bound flagship kernel (plan §6.1, targets §14.1).

## Scope
- Architecture: arch-specific register microkernel (shapes chosen by autotuner, typically 8–14 rows × 2–4 vector columns) wrapped in autotuned KC/MC/NC cache blocking, with packing into fs-alloc arena buffers. Microkernels are fs-simd unsafe capsules with scalar twins.
- Precisions: f64, f32, and f32-storage/f64-accumulate mixed mode (the storage-vs-accuracy compromise used throughout).
- Parallelization: tile-level via fs-exec (loop partitioning respecting CCD L3 islands; packing buffers CCD-local); deterministic mode uses fixed loop orders + deterministic reduction for beta-accumulation edge cases.
- Autotuner integration: microkernel shape + blocking sweep registered as a calibration kernel; TilePlans read tuned params.
- Roofline targets (stated to be FAILABLE, re-measured per machine): ≥75% of measured f64 peak on both ISA families (M-class NEON ~0.5 TF order; TR ~6–7 TF all-core). SME2 upside handled by the separate exploratory bead.
- Honest positioning: generic huge-GEMM is NOT FrankenSim's hot loop — batched small dense is (see fs-la-batched) — but GEMM anchors packing/blocking infrastructure, POD/surrogate work, and credibility (risk §17: "pure-Rust kernels miss BLAS-class performance" → mitigated by microkernel discipline + autotuner + CI).

## Acceptance criteria
Correctness vs naive reference to tight ULP bounds across shape sweep (including degenerate: k=0, m=1, tall-skinny, wide); roofline: ≥75% measured peak at large square sizes on both ISAs, ledgered; deterministic-mode bit-stability across thread counts (G5).

## Testing

## What

## Scope

title: Canonical rank-deficient TSQR theorem and gauge-stable Q/R certificates
description:
MISSION
Turn the currently over-broad statement that a nonnegative diagonal makes every QR factor unique into a substantially stronger and actually specified frontier theorem/program: define and implement a canonical, deterministic gauge for rank-deficient tall-skinny QR whose observable R, rank profile, null-space frame, and replay certificate are invariant under the admitted TSQR reduction schedule. This is an ambition ratchet, not a retreat. The goal is a reusable canonicalization primitive for Krylov bases, POD, inverse problems, certificate rank decisions, and distributed replay.

BACKGROUND AND ROOT ISSUE
For full-column-rank real A, positive diagonal conventions can select a unique thin QR under standard hypotheses. When A is rank deficient, rotations inside deficient subspaces and zero-diagonal columns leave gauge freedom; merely forcing a nonnegative diagonal does not prove uniqueness. Current fs-la documentation must therefore use a no-claim boundary until a stronger construction is defined and proven. The project should pursue that stronger construction rather than discard the capability.

MATHEMATICAL TARGETS
1. Specify the admitted equivalence relation over inputs, leaf partitionings, legal deterministic reduction schedules, floating-point execution modes, and signed-zero/NaN policy.
2. Define a canonical numerical rank profile using scale-aware thresholds carried with units/error budgets; never hide a tolerance as a dimensionful literal.
3. Define a deterministic gauge for dependent columns and null-space directions. Candidate ingredients include lexicographically pivoted rank profiles, orientation by first certified nonzero coordinate, exterior-power/Pluecker signatures, polar factors on rank strata, and interval-separated tie resolution. Explore and prove the strongest viable synthesis rather than prematurely fixing one method.
4. State theorem tiers separately: exact-arithmetic canonicality; correctly rounded or interval-certified canonicality when separation hypotheses hold; deterministic same-ISA bit stability; and explicit no-claim behavior in numerically undecidable near-rank transitions.
5. Produce proof obligations for idempotence of canonicalization, invariance under admissible TSQR tree regrouping, compatibility with full-rank positive-diagonal QR, stable behavior inside a fixed rank stratum, and structured escalation at rank-boundary ambiguity.
6. Investigate a sheaf-style interpretation: local leaf frames and transition gauges form local sections; successful global canonicalization is a glued section, while a nonzero obstruction/cocycle becomes an executable certificate that uniqueness is not currently justified. This moonshot route stays feature-gated until evidence supports it.

ENGINEERING DELIVERABLES
- A typed CanonicalQrPolicy carrying rank/error budgets, determinism class, tie policy, feature/capability gates, and versioned theorem identity.
- A result object separating canonical R, optional implicit Q action, certified rank profile, null-space/gauge metadata, residual/error bounds, and honest claim status.
- A compact independently checkable certificate or structured no-claim record; checker logic must not merely call the producer again.
- Deterministic replay identity over input artifact, policy, tree identity, arithmetic mode, implementation/theorem version, result, and certificate.
- Cancellation-correct tiled canonicalization with request -> drain -> finalize behavior and resumable state if the operation exceeds a single bounded tile.
- No unchecked shape products or infallible giant allocations in admitted paths.
- Contract and API language that distinguishes exact theorem, conditional certified theorem, deterministic implementation fact, numerical stability evidence, and open conjecture.

GAUNTLET AND TEST MATRIX
G0: full-rank compatibility; reconstruction and orthogonality; canonicalization idempotence; permutation/rank-profile validity; zero-row, zero-column, one-column, repeated-column, exact-zero, signed-zero, and maximally representable shape admission; checked-overflow and allocation-failure diagnostics.
G1: manufactured matrices with known rank, singular gaps, null spaces, and controlled perturbations; verify residual/error-bound scaling and convergence under precision/refinement escalation.
G2: Kahan, Hilbert/Vandermonde families, duplicated/nearly duplicated columns, graded singular spectra, and adversarial cancellation cases with detailed rank/gauge evidence.
G3: row-block repartitioning, admissible tree reassociation, column/unit rescaling, orthogonal left transforms, equivalent representation rewrites, pause/resume/fork equivalence, and certificate mutation rejection. Metamorphic properties must state which quantities are invariant versus covariant.
G4: cancellation at entry and every tile boundary, schedule exhaustion one-before/exact/one-after, panic/allocation fault containment, loser drain, leak checks, and mutation-free failed admission.
G5: bit-stable reruns across thread counts on the same ISA; explicit cross-ISA policy; golden replay identities tied to theorem and arithmetic versions.

ACCEPTANCE AND NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY
Do not restore an unconditional uniqueness claim merely because tests pass. Closure requires a written theorem statement with hypotheses, an implementation that matches those hypotheses, independent certificate checks, adversarial Gauntlet evidence, and explicit behavior when rank is ambiguous. If the sheaf obstruction or interval separation cannot certify one gauge, return a typed ambiguity/no-claim result and ranked escalation options such as more precision, stronger interval bounds, a changed budget, or an alternative policy. The default path remains the honest deterministic TSQR already established; frontier/moonshot canonicality stays gated until promoted by evidence.

## Success Criteria

Preserve the complete existing mission and all theorem tiers. Close only when the six exact children reconcile on one compatible snapshot, including a valid restricted/no-claim outcome for the moonshot if the stronger theorem fails. Exact focused tests, independent checking, release no-mock E2E, detailed bounded logs, replay, DSR, and theorem/no-claim authority are non-substitutable. No unconditional rank-deficient uniqueness claim may be restored from test success alone.

title: fs-la eigensolvers: LOBPCG + Lanczos (selective reorth), matrix-free, resumable, adjoint hooks
description:
## What
`fs-la` eigensolvers: LOBPCG and Lanczos with selective reorthogonalization — chosen precisely because they are MATRIX-FREE-NATIVE (plan §6.1): modal analysis, buckling, and stability eigenproblems all reduce to operator applications (P6).

## Scope
- LOBPCG: blocked, preconditioned (accepts any fs-sparse/solver-stack preconditioner as an operator), with basis-degeneracy detection + recovery (soft-locking, orthogonalization via TSQR), constraint deflation (known nullspaces — rigid-body modes in free-free elasticity), and generalized problems (K,M pencils; M-inner products).
- Lanczos with selective reorthogonalization: for extremal + interior (shift-invert via solver-stack solves) spectra; Ritz convergence monitoring with residual-based stopping tied to caller's budget (P4).
- Both: resumable SolverState (pause/checkpoint/fork per fs-exec-speculation), cancellation-clean, deterministic mode (fixed orthogonalization order), adjoint hooks (eigenvalue derivatives via Ritz vectors — needed for eigenfrequency objectives in topo-simp).
- Consumers wired by design: buckling (fs-solid-stability geometric-stiffness pencils), manifold harmonics (Laplace–Beltrami basis), KL expansions (fs-uq), Orr–Sommerfeld validation cross-checks (fs-cheb).

## Acceptance criteria
Standard batteries (diagonal, Laplacian stencils, generalized pencils with known spectra) converge to requested tolerances; selective reorthogonalization keeps loss-of-orthogonality bounded (monitored, asserted); matrix-free contract honored (operator-apply count is THE cost metric, logged); FrankenScipy cross-check on shared problems.

## What
`fs-la` randomized NLA (plan §6.1 [F]): randomized range finders, randomized SVD/Nyström, sketch-and-precondition least squares, and Hutchinson/Hutch++ stochastic trace estimation.

## Scope
- Randomized range finder with adaptive rank determination (posterior error estimates, block power iterations for spectral-decay-poor cases); randomized SVD on top; Nyström for PSD kernels (GP approximations in bayesopt).
- Sketch-and-precondition least squares: sketch (subsampled randomized trig transform via fs-fft or sparse sign sketches), QR the sketch, precondition LSQR-style iterations — the modern fast path for tall dense LS.
- Hutchinson + Hutch++ trace estimators: log-det and tr(f(A)) machinery; the named consumer is SENSITIVITY AGGREGATION IN TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZATION and log-det terms in GP likelihoods. Variance-reduced (Hutch++) split with deterministic Philox probe streams — stochastic estimates are still replayable (P2) and e-process-monitorable (stopping when confidence sequence is tight enough, wired later via fs-eproc).
- All randomness through fs-rand keyed streams; all results carry probe counts + variance estimates as evidence metadata (Evidence<T> integration point).

## Acceptance criteria
Rank-r approximation errors within theoretical bounds (oversampling p → expected ‖A−QQᵀA‖ bounds) on synthetic spectra (fast/slow decay, gaps); Hutch++ variance beats Hutchinson at matched probe counts (demonstrated, ledgered); sketch-LS matches direct QR solutions to tolerance with the expected speed crossover documented.

## Testing
