title: Proposal 9 — Certified speculation: DWR goal-oriented accept test (estimated-color unless equilibrated-bracketed)
description:
## What
Proposal 9's GOAL-ORIENTED accept test — dual-weighted-residual (DWR) estimates targeting the QUERY's actual quantity of interest rather than a generic field norm. This sharpens the accept test enormously (you only need the candidate to be right about what the query asked), but it comes with an honesty cost that only the three-color type system makes safe to pay.

## Why this needs the color system
DWR constants are NOT guaranteed. So a DWR-based accept carries **estimated** color unless it is BRACKETED by an equilibrated (constant-free) bound from spec-verifier. The three-color system (Proposal 3) is exactly what makes this mixture safe: a query can be discharged by a cheap DWR estimate colored estimated, or by an equilibrated bound colored verified, and the report never confuses the two. Without the colors, DWR accepts would silently launder into false certificates — the failure mode the whole epistemic type system exists to prevent.

## Scope
- DWR estimators for the declared QoI functionals (couples to Proposal 8's QoI menu: max-over-region, integral, exceedance probability): solve the adjoint/dual problem for the QoI, weight the primal residual by the dual solution.
- Reuse the adjoint infrastructure (Proposal 1 / fs-adjoint) for the dual solve — DWR is an adjoint consumer.
- Color logic: DWR-only accept → estimated; DWR bracketed by an equilibrated bound → verified. Encode the bracketing check so promotion to verified is mechanical and auditable.
- Goal-oriented spatial refinement: where DWR indicators say the QoI error concentrates, refine there (feeds Proposal 8's planner "DWR-refine" operator and Proposal 4's temporal-cocycle refinement analogue).

## Acceptance criteria
On QoI queries with known answers, DWR accepts are correct when colored estimated and become verified only when a valid equilibrated bracket exists; a laundering test (attempt to mark an unbracketed DWR accept as verified) FAILS the type check; DWR-driven refinement demonstrably concentrates effort where the QoI error lives.

## Testing
G1 manufactured-solution QoIs with analytic dual solutions; laundering adversarial test (part of Proposal 3's laundering suite); falsifier (Proposal 6): occasional full high-fidelity QoI evaluation to confirm the DWR estimate's honesty. Logs: QoI, DWR estimate, bracket status, final color.

## Dependencies
spec-verifier (equilibrated bracket); Proposal 1 / fs-adjoint (dual solves); Proposal 3 (colors); Proposal 6 (falsifier coverage — the addendum flags "DWR-based accepts need falsifier coverage" as a hard dep of Proposal 8). Feeds Proposal 8's planner.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- The DWR dual solve is grounded on the BASE fs-adjoint crate (flux-tfz.24: discrete adjoints / IFT dual solves), NOT the full Proposal 1 ledger transpose (which stays a soft/related sharpening) — this removes a Phase-1->Phase-2 inversion.
- Cancellation: dual solves are tile programs polling cancellation at tile boundaries.
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary: an ill-posed/unbounded QoI functional (singular dual problem) yields estimated + flag, never silent garbage.
close_reason: DWR goal-oriented accept test implemented as fs_adjoint::dwr_accept ([F]-gated behind dwr-accept with fs-verify as an optional feature-wired dep): (1) THE 1-D REFERENCE DWR ESTIMATOR for integral QoIs over fs-verify's MMS problems: enriched dual (P1 FEM via deterministic Thomas solve on the once-refined mesh), dual-weighted residual eta = r(z_f - I_h z_f) with per-coarse-element indicators — G1 effectivity within [0.7, 1.3] against the EXACT polynomial QoI error (dw-001); (2) THE COLOR LOGIC, mechanical and auditable: DWR-only accepts carry ESTIMATED ('constants not guaranteed' in the estimator identity); promotion to VERIFIED requires a GUARANTEED bracket with bound <= tolerance — Bracket::cauchy_schwarz builds the constant-free QoI bracket from TWO REAL equilibrated-flux enclosures (the lmp4.1 verifier, both factors interval-certified, outward-rounded product, fail-closed on unbounded factors): |a(e_u,e_z)| <= ||e_u||_E * ||e_z||_E is exactly Cauchy-Schwarz, no constants anywhere (dw-002: promotes to Verified[0,bound]; non-guaranteed brackets NEVER promote); a DWR estimate exceeding its guaranteed bracket flags estimator_inconsistent — reported, never hidden; (3) THE LAUNDERING TEST: an unbracketed estimated accept written to the ColorGraph claiming Verified is REFUSED at write time (dw-003 — part of Proposal 3's adversarial suite); (4) GOAL-ORIENTED REFINEMENT: a right-window QoI concentrates >60% of indicator mass on the right elements while the centered control does not (dw-004); (5) THE FALSIFIER (Proposal 6): the high-fidelity spot check shows the DWR CORRECTION moves toward truth (corrected error < 0.35x raw); the dwr-accept class is BLOCKED by ship_gate until paired with high-fidelity-qoi-spot-check, then ships (dw-005). Polish note honored: grounded on base fs-adjoint/fs-verify machinery, not the full ledger transpose. Evidence: 5 conformance tests green; all 7 fs-adjoint suites green under --all-features (26 tests); clippy -D warnings clean (including a nightly-drift chunks_exact->as_chunks fix in transpose.rs); rustfmt clean; CONTRACT extended (accept surface + no-claims: 1-D reference class with fs-dwr's 2-D plugged into the same logic, bracket sharpness is the verifier's growth path, falsifier cadence belongs to the budget allocator). Feeds Proposal 8's planner.

title: Proposal 9 — Certified speculation: DIMENSIONAL KNOWLEDGE MINING (Buckingham-π + symbolic regression over the certified corpus, estimated-color w/ π-envelope)
description:
## What
Proposal 9's KNOWLEDGE APEX — dimensional mining over the certified corpus. The system does not merely answer design questions; it ACCUMULATES ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE WITH PEDIGREES. With a units-typed schema on all ledger quantities (fs-qty is already the base plan's dimensional-analysis crate), run automated Buckingham-π extraction plus symbolic regression over the certified corpus to conjecture closed-form scaling laws.

## Scope
- **Buckingham-π extraction**: from the units-typed ledger quantities, form dimensionless groups automatically (fs-qty + fs-regime already implement Buckingham-Pi groups / nondimensionalization — reuse them, do not reinvent).
- **Symbolic regression** over the certified corpus in π-space to conjecture closed-form scaling laws (e.g., relating a QoI to dimensionless groups).
- **Epistemic discipline (non-negotiable)**: conjectures enter the ledger as **estimated-color** with a validity envelope equal to the CONVEX HULL of supporting data in π-space. They are promoted (toward validated) ONLY by surviving the falsification budget (Proposal 6). A mined law is a hypothesis with a pedigree, never a law by fiat.
- Feed mined laws + their envelopes back as priors for neighbor extrapolation (spec-proposers #1) and as VoI probe targets (Proposal C).

## Why this is the accretion multiplier
Humans do not systematically extract scaling laws from their own simulation output because it is tedious; a swarm does it overnight, indexed by dimensionless group so "aluminum bracket at Re 2×10⁵" and "steel bracket at Re 2.1×10⁵" are recognized as the same physics. This is the same π-space index the tombstone ledger (Proposal E) uses — build it once, share it.

## Acceptance criteria
On a corpus with a KNOWN embedded scaling law (synthetic), the miner recovers it as an estimated-color conjecture with a correct π-space validity envelope; the conjecture is NOT promoted until it survives falsification probes at points inside the envelope; a conjecture whose envelope is extrapolated beyond the convex hull is refused.

## Testing
Property: recovered laws are dimensionally consistent by construction (fs-qty type check); envelope = convex hull of support (geometric test); promotion gated on falsification-budget survival (Proposal 6). Falsifier: held-out certified runs inside the envelope must agree with the mined law within its stated dispersion. Logs: candidate laws, π-groups, envelopes, promotion status.

## Dependencies
spec-economics (the certified corpus + telemetry); fs-qty + fs-regime (Buckingham-π, base plan); Proposal 3 (estimated color); Proposal 6 (falsification budget for promotion); shares π-space index with Proposal E (swarm-tombstones). Feeds spec-proposers and Proposal C.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- **Franken-only:** the symbolic-regression engine is pure-Rust over FrankenNumpy/FrankenScipy (or in-house); NO external SR library (PySR/gplearn/Eureqa), Python runtime, or FFI backend in the production graph. Buckingham-pi reuses fs-qty/fs-regime.
- Test (G5): the SR search is seeded and reproducible (identical conjecture set + pi-envelopes across runs).
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- False-positive guard: a corpus with NO real dimensionless structure (pure-noise synthetic) yields NO conjectured law, not a hallucinated one. Extrapolation boundary as an explicit pair: a query point just OUTSIDE the pi-space convex hull is refused while one just INSIDE is served.
close_reason: Implemented as NEW crate crates/fs-dimine (crate:fs-qty relabeled crate:fs-dimine; depends on fs-evidence Color only). Proposal 9's knowledge apex: dimensional mining of closed-form power-law scaling laws over the certified corpus in dimensionless-group (pi) space. fit_power_law(&[Sample{pi,qoi}]) fits y = C * prod(pi_j^a_j) by PURE-RUST log-linear least squares (ln y = ln C + sum a_j ln pi_j solved via normal equations + Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting — NO external SR library / Python / FFI, Franken-only). MinedLaw carries coefficient, exponents, r_squared (fit significance), a per-group pi-space validity ENVELOPE (min/max = exact convex hull in 1D), sample count, and an ESTIMATED-color certificate (a mined law is a conjecture, never a certified bound). is_significant(r2_threshold) gates promotion (noise -> low r2 -> not significant, no hallucinated law). predict(pi) REFUSES to extrapolate beyond the envelope (Extrapolation error). Structured MineError (TooFewSamples/DimMismatch/NonPositive/Singular/Extrapolation) fails closed on non-positive (log-undefined) and collinear (rank-deficient) inputs. Tests (tests/dimine.rs, 9): 1D + multi-pi recovery (exact data -> r2~1, correct C/exponents), estimated-color, noise-not-significant, extrapolation-refusal (boundary inclusive), too-few-samples, non-positive-pi-and-qoi, collinear-singular, predict-dim-mismatch, determinism (bit-identical). Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN, fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-dimine 9/9, xtask check-all 0 violations across 63 crates. No-claim: Buckingham-pi extraction is fs-regime/fs-qty's (fits over pre-formed pi-coordinates); v1 is power-laws only; envelope is per-coordinate box (exact hull in 1D, conservative box in higher-D); promotion toward validated is the falsification budget's (Proposal 6).

title: Proposal 2 — Incremental recompute: STORE (content-addressed Merkle DAG w/ slack field; determinism promoted to certified contract)
description:
## What
Proposal 2's STORE — a content-addressed Merkle DAG where each node records `(op_id, input_hashes, params, code_version_hash, rng_seed, achieved_error, required_tolerance)`, and where the gap `required_tolerance − achieved_error` is the node's **slack**. Slack is the resource this entire proposal spends. This turns the Error Ledger into a build graph with a soundness certificate for every skip.

## Why determinism is a HARD prerequisite (and gets promoted here)
Tolerance-level memoization requires bit-stable recomputation: fixed reduction orders, no unordered atomics. The base plan's deterministic tile executor is the ENABLING ASSET and must be treated as load-bearing infrastructure, not a nicety. This bead is where determinism is PROMOTED from implementation detail to CERTIFIED CONTRACT with its own Gauntlet tests (bitwise reproducibility across runs AND worker counts) — see the amendment to the base-plan determinism bead (fs-exec ExecMode). Risk R2 (determinism at scale) is owned here: fixed-order reductions + deterministic scheduling as certified contracts, with the measured perf tax accepted explicitly.

## Scope
- Merkle DAG node schema with the seven fields above; `slack` as a FIRST-CLASS ledger field (amendment to base-plan ledger schema).
- Stable content addressing reusing the base plan's BLAKE3-class tree hash (fs-ledger).
- Determinism certification: Gauntlet tests asserting bit-identical artifact hashes across {1,2,P,2P} threads for the ops that participate in incremental recompute; the measured Fast-mode delta documented.
- Pinning hooks so nodes referenced by an evidence package (Proposal 12) or a contract (Proposal E) are never evicted (consumed by recompute-api's cache policy).

## Acceptance criteria
Node hashing is stable across runs/thread-counts; slack is computed and stored per node; a deterministic fixture study reproduces every artifact hash (the G5-at-scale primitive); the determinism-contract Gauntlet tests are green on both reference ISAs.

## Testing
Property: reduction/scheduling determinism under an adversarial permuted-completion-order scheduler; hash stability under fork. G5 determinism audit integration. Logs: node fields, slack per node, hash tables per run.

## Dependencies
Base plan: deterministic tile executor (fs-exec ExecMode) + ledger content addressing (fs-ledger). Feeds recompute-invalidate + recompute-api. Amends the base-plan determinism + ledger-schema beads.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary: negative-slack node representation, empty/single-node DAG, and a very-deep-DAG hash-stability case.

title: Proposal 2 — Incremental recompute: TOLERANCE-AWARE INVALIDATION (certified sensitivity bounds, reuse-with-certificate, graceful degradation)
description:
## What
Proposal 2's INVALIDATION ALGORITHM — the part no build system has. Bit-level invalidation (Nix/Bazel) says "something changed, rerun everything downstream." TOLERANCE-level invalidation says "this change provably does not matter past stage four." That is the difference between a thousand full re-simulations and a thousand cheap delta-solves, and the semantics only exists because error bounds compose — it is the Error Ledger run in REVERSE.

## The algorithm
- Each ledger edge carries a certified local sensitivity bound `L_op`, obtained by interval evaluation of the op's derivative over the perturbation box (fs-ivl), or from cached adjoint magnitudes where Proposal 1 is live.
- A perturbation `δ` at a node propagates FORWARD as a certified interval `‖Δoutput‖ ≤ Π L_op · ‖δ‖` along each path, combined by the ledger's existing composition rules.
- A downstream node is **REUSED** iff its accumulated incoming bound fits inside its recorded slack (`required_tolerance − achieved_error`). The reuse decision is itself written to the ledger as a **verified-color** claim: "skipped: perturbation absorbed, bound X ≤ slack Y". Otherwise the node joins the recompute frontier.

## Graceful degradation (risk R4)
When sensitivity bounds are too loose (nonlinear ops with pessimistic interval derivatives), the frontier balloons toward the full DAG and the system SILENTLY degrades to ordinary hash-based memoization — still correct, just less clever. Track **skip yield** (fraction of DAG certifiably skipped on realistic edit traces) as the health metric that tells you which ops need tighter local bounds. Adjoint-sharpened bounds (Proposal 1) tighten the worst offenders.

## Acceptance criteria
On seeded edit traces with known correct skip sets, the algorithm skips exactly the nodes whose accumulated bound fits their slack and no others (no unsound skip — a skipped node's true output is always within tolerance, checked against full recompute); skip-yield is measured; loose-bound cases degrade to hash memoization without incorrectness.

## Testing
Property: SOUNDNESS — for a battery of random perturbations, every skipped node's recomputed value lies within its tolerance of the reused value (this is the load-bearing correctness invariant; a violation is a Sev-0 false certificate). Falsifier (Proposal 6): randomly force-recompute a fraction of skipped nodes and assert agreement. Logs: per-node accumulated bound vs slack, skip/recompute verdict, skip-yield.

## Dependencies
recompute-store (slack + DAG); fs-ivl (interval derivatives); ledger composition rules (base plan); Proposal 1 (adjoint-sharpened bounds — soft, interval derivatives suffice for v0). Owns risk R4.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary/error cases: delta = 0 (empty recompute frontier); accumulated bound EXACTLY equal to slack resolves DETERMINISTICALLY to recompute (never skip on the tie); an op whose interval sensitivity L_op is unbounded/non-finite on the perturbation box FAILS CLOSED (force recompute); a node with negative slack (achieved_error > required_tolerance) is never skippable.
- Gauntlet tiers: reuse-soundness property -> G0; force-recompute falsifier + random-perturbation soundness battery -> G3; any unsound skip (skipped node whose true output exits tolerance) is Sev-0.

THE ALGORITHM (corrected by its own soundness battery — see below): perturbation deltas flow Sum(L_e * delta_parent) through EVERY frontier node (a skipped node's cached bytes are STALE by its bound, and that staleness reaches consumers scaled by their sensitivities — the first cut stopped propagation at skips, which the G3 battery immediately exposed as unsound with real violation counts); each frontier node absorbs against its OWN effective slack; the recompute set closes UPWARD along delta-carrying edges (PulledByDescendant — recomputing a node is only meaningful with fresh input bytes, so failing descendants pull stale ancestors in; one reverse-topological sweep reaches the transitive closure). A SECOND design flaw caught by the suite: burning absorbed slack originally mutated achieved_error, which is part of the content hash — identity changed under the map key; burned slack is now separate runtime state and record identity is immutable. title: Proposal 2 — Incremental recompute: perturb() API + cost-weighted eviction/pinning + skip-yield telemetry
description:
## What
Proposal 2's API + CACHE POLICY — the operator-facing surface of tolerance-aware recompute, plus the eviction/pinning policy that keeps the cache hot. This is the economic engine of agentic workloads (thousands of nearby variants) and is deliberately given headline-bet status, not plumbing status.

## Scope — the API
- `plan = ledger.perturb(node, δ)` returns: (1) the MINIMAL recompute frontier, (2) its estimated cost (feeding Proposal 8's planner), and (3) the CERTIFICATE for everything skipped (the verified-color "perturbation absorbed" claims from recompute-invalidate).
- The plan is a first-class object an agent or the query planner can inspect and cost before committing to execute.

## Scope — cache policy
- **Cost-weighted eviction**: evict by (recompute-cost × hit-probability), both measurable from telemetry (spec-economics + ledger metrics).
- **Pinning**: anything referenced by an evidence package (Proposal 12) or a contract (Proposal E) is pinned — never evicted, because its re-verifiability is a promise.
- **Skip-yield telemetry** (the health metric, risk R4's early-warning): fraction of DAG certifiably skipped on realistic edit traces, per op, so tightening effort can be directed at the ops with the worst skip yield.

## Why this deserves headline status
Agent-driven design exploration IS thousands of nearby variants. The delta between a thousand full re-simulations and a thousand certified delta-solves is the whole economic difference of agentic operation. Version control (Proposal 10) free-rides on this: a cheap branch checkout is a cheap delta-solve.

## Acceptance criteria
`perturb()` returns a correct minimal frontier + skip certificate + cost estimate on seeded traces; cost-weighted eviction outperforms LRU on recompute-cost-saved per byte on realistic traces; pinned artifacts survive eviction pressure; skip-yield dashboard live.

## Kill criterion (Proposal 2)
If skip yield on recorded agent design-iteration traces delivers <2× median wall-clock speedup versus plain hash memoization after the first vertical is live, FREEZE the certified-skip layer (keep plain memoization, which pays for itself regardless) and revisit only when adjoint-sharpened bounds exist.

## Testing
Integration: replay recorded design-iteration traces, measure wall-clock speedup vs hash memoization (the kill-criterion measurement); eviction-policy A/B on cache hit rate; pinning correctness under forced eviction. Logs: frontier sizes, skip certificates, cost estimates vs actual, skip-yield per op.

## Dependencies
recompute-store + recompute-invalidate; ledger telemetry (base plan + spec-economics); consumed by Proposal 8 (planner cost), Proposal 10 (cheap branches), Proposal C (cheap sweeps). Feeds pinning contracts with Proposal 12 + Proposal E.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary: perturb() on a leaf (empty frontier) and on the root (full frontier); pinned-node pressure where the cache is full of pinned nodes surfaces a STRUCTURED error rather than OOM/deadlock.
close_reason: Shipped Proposal 2's perturb() API + CACHE POLICY (bead lmp4.8), completing the incremental-recompute triad (store lmp4.6 -> invalidation lmp4.7 -> API lmp4.8), same feature gate. THE API: RecomputeApi::perturb(node, delta) returns a FIRST-CLASS PerturbPlan — minimal recompute frontier, estimated cost from MEASURED per-node costs (Proposal 8's planner input), the hash-memoization baseline cost alongside, and the verified-color certificates for everything skipped — PURE until commit() (which burns slack + updates telemetry). api-001: the diamond fixture recomputes exactly {source, tight-tolerance} and certifies {left, sink} with absorbed-perturbation claims, costs read 101 vs 1111 hash-memo, plans are pure until commit, leaf perturbations touch only themselves, swamping root perturbations recompute the full frontier. api-002: slack is SPENDABLE through the API — two 8e-3 perturbations absorb at the roomy node, the third finds its slack spent and recomputes. CACHE POLICY: cost-weighted eviction (recompute-cost x measured hit-probability, deterministic tie-break) — api-003's A/B keeps all four hot expensive nodes (4000 recompute-cost preserved) that insertion-order LRU would destroy (0 preserved); contract/evidence pins survive; pinned saturation surfaces the STRUCTURED CacheFullOfPins refusal with teaching text (pins are re-verifiability promises), never OOM. title: Proposal 10 — Version control for physics: COMMITS/BRANCHES/CHECKOUT over Merkle roots (free-rides on Proposal 2)
description:
## What
Proposal 10's COMMITS + BRANCHES + CHECKOUT — the base verb set of version control for physical designs, free-riding on infrastructure already justified by Proposals 2 and the base-plan ledger. Swarm-scale concurrent engineering is gated on exactly one thing: whether concurrent edits can be reconciled safely. PLM systems version files; nothing versions PHYSICS.

## Scope
- A **commit** is the Merkle root of the design-plus-ledger state (content-addressed; reuses fs-ledger's forkable-worlds machinery, which already implements hash-shared branches).
- **Branches** are pointers; a checkout of a nearby branch is CHEAP because Proposal 2 makes the delta-solve cheap (a branch checkout ≈ a `perturb()` frontier).
- Branch bookkeeping: parent commit, divergence point, merge-view queries — largely already present in the base plan's `fs-ledger time travel: forkable worlds` deliverable; this bead formalizes it as the VCS substrate the diff/bisect/merge beads build on.
- Garbage-collection policy respecting all live branches (content addressing makes sharing safe; N branches ≈ 1× artifacts + deltas).

## Acceptance criteria
Commits are reproducible Merkle roots; branches share artifacts by hash (storage audit: N branches ≈ 1× + deltas); checkout of a nearby branch costs a delta-solve, not a full re-solve; branch bookkeeping supports the diff/bisect/merge consumers.

## Testing
Property: branch independence (ops on branch A never affect branch B's views — inherits fs-ledger fork-independence tests); storage audit under many branches; checkout-cost measured vs full re-solve. Logs: branch trees, divergence points, artifact-sharing audit.

## Dependencies
Proposal 2 (cheap branches / delta checkout); base plan fs-ledger forkable worlds + content addressing. Foundation for vcs-diff, vcs-bisect, vcs-merge.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- GC-safety invariant (data-loss class, G0): a property test that garbage collection NEVER collects an artifact reachable from any live branch pointer, under many-branch fixtures. Boundary: checkout of a non-existent commit returns a structured error; empty repo / first commit handled.
close_reason: Physics VCS base verbs implemented as fs_ledger::vcs (new module + tests over MY OWN travel.rs forkable-worlds machinery from gp3.3): (1) COMMITS are binary Merkle roots of a branch's visible frozen ops — each leaf is BLAKE3 over the op's Five Explicits + outcome + diag + SORTED LINKED-ARTIFACT HASHES, with wall-clock times and rowids EXCLUDED so logically identical histories yield IDENTICAL roots across different ledgers and runs (vc-001 proves cross-ledger reproducibility with deliberately different wall times, chaining via parent commits, and root movement on both op-level and artifact-content changes); the empty commit is a well-defined domain-tagged root; commits persist as vcs-commit events; (2) BRANCHES share artifacts by hash — the storage audit MEASURES the claim: 6 shared + 4 per-branch delta artifacts = 10 physical rows serving 34 logical references across 5 branches (N branches ≈ 1x + deltas); (3) CHECKOUT materializes the committed view (frontier-trimmed at_time snapshot) and checkout_delta returns the symmetric-difference op frontier — the perturb()-style delta a recompute solver consumes: a nearby checkout reconciles 2 ops against 20 hash-shared (cost |delta| not |history|); unknown roots are structured teaching errors; (4) merge_views splits base/only-A/only-B exactly for the diff/bisect/merge consumers, with branch independence re-verified (A's ops never leak into B's view); (5) the review-round-3 G0 DATA-LOSS INVARIANT: a many-branch GC fixture proves gc_unreferenced_artifacts collects ONLY a genuinely unreferenced orphan while all 10 live-branch-reachable artifacts survive; (6) new public leaf surface op_artifact_hashes + commit_leaf on Ledger. Evidence: 5 conformance tests green (vc-001 reproducible chained roots; vc-002 storage audit; vc-003 checkout + nearby delta + unknown-root refusal + empty-repo boundary; vc-004 merge views + independence; vc-005 GC safety) with ALL 54 existing fs-ledger tests undisturbed (25 unit + colors + travel + tombstone + conformance). clippy -D warnings clean, rustfmt clean, CONTRACT.md extended (vcs surface + no-claims: in-session registry, delta EXECUTION is fs-recompute's, adjudication is lmp4.12's), xtask check-all: fs-ledger clean (1 workspace violation is fs-solver, another agent's in-flight crate). Feeds vcs-diff (lmp4.10), bisect (lmp4.11), and the sheaf-adjudicated merge (lmp4.12) whose Hodge-split machinery I shipped in wqd.13.

title: Foundations: workspace, constellation, CI, contracts, safety, vertical skeleton
description:
## Mission
Cross-cutting project foundations for FrankenSim: the Cargo workspace, the Franken-constellation dependency policy, CI on both target ISAs, the per-crate CONTRACT.md + conformance-suite discipline, unsafe-capsule safety cases, compile-time dimensional analysis, and the PV "vertical skeleton" proving slice.

## Why this epic exists
FrankenSim is sized for a swarm of AI coding agents with human architectural review (plan §16.2). The load-bearing practices that make that safe are all here: **one crate = one contract** (CONTRACT.md + executable conformance suite); **IR as the integration language** (agents integrate against frozen semantics, never each other's internals); **golden ledgers** (every merged feature lands with a replayable acceptance run); **the Decalogue as tie-breaker** (disputes resolve by principle number). The repo is organized so the maximum context an agent needs is one crate + its contracts + the IR spec.

## The Decalogue (governs every child bead)
P1 pure memory-safe Rust, Franken-only deps · P2 determinism as a contract · P3 everything differentiable or certifiable · P4 budgets first · P5 structure preservation · P6 matrix-free & roofline-honest · P7 cancellation-correct compute · P8 one data model (complexes/cochains) · P9 provenance-complete · P10 agent-first ergonomics with the Five Explicits (units, seeds, budgets, versions, capabilities).

## Members
workspace-scaffold, constellation-integration, qty-units, ci-gauntlet-pipeline, contract-conformance-infra, unsafe-safety-cases, vertical-skeleton.

## Success Criteria
Workspace + CI + contract discipline exist and are enforced mechanically; PV vertical skeleton passes end-to-end; every later epic can rely on these rails without re-deriving them.

title: Workspace scaffold: flat fs-* crates, layer enforcement, lint/format rails
description:
## What
Create the FrankenSim Cargo workspace: flat `fs-*` crate layout with a strict acyclic dependency order, Rust 2024 edition, and the mechanical rails every other bead assumes.

## Scope
- Workspace `Cargo.toml` + initial crate skeletons for the L0/L1 spine (fs-substrate, fs-simd, fs-alloc, fs-exec, fs-la, fs-sparse, fs-fft, fs-ivl, fs-rand) with placeholder lib.rs, CONTRACT.md stubs, and test dirs. Other crates added by their own beads.
- Layer-dependency enforcement: a CI-runnable check (cargo-deny-style config or a small in-repo tool) that fails if any crate depends on a higher layer (L0 SUBSTRATE ← L1 BEDROCK ← L2 MORPH ← L3 FLUX ← L4 ASCENT / L5 LUMEN ← L6 HELM; lower layers must NEVER know about higher ones — plan §4, AGENTS.md dependency direction).
- `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` default at workspace level; per-crate opt-out only for registered unsafe capsules (see unsafe-safety-cases bead).
- Feature-flag convention: `[F]` frontier features behind `frontier-*` flags, `[M]` moonshots behind `moonshot-*` flags, DEFAULT OFF. Nothing [M] gates anything [S].
- Lint baseline: clippy -D warnings, rustfmt config, doc requirements for public items.
- CODEOWNERS-style conventions doc: one crate = one contract; agents integrate against contracts and IR, never each other's internals; the Decalogue is the tie-breaker in disputes (resolve by principle number).

## Why
The plan (§16.2) sizes FrankenSim for an agent swarm; the discipline that keeps a 45-crate system from rotting is that each crate ships a CONTRACT.md stating invariants, a conformance suite any reimplementation must pass, and zero access to layers above it. That must be mechanical from day one — retrofitting layering is how archipelagos form.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo check --all-targets`, clippy, fmt green on empty skeletons.
- Layer-violation check demonstrably fails on a seeded violation (test the enforcer itself).
- A template crate (`fs-template` or docs) shows: CONTRACT.md skeleton (purpose/layer, invariants, error model, determinism class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary, feature flags, conformance tests, no-claim boundaries), unit-test layout, conformance-test layout.

## Testing
Unit tests for the layering checker (positive + seeded-violation negative cases). CI dry-run proving the whole lane runs on both a macOS/aarch64 and Linux/x86-64 runner. Log every check with crate name, layer, verdict.

title: Fourth flagship: generate frankensim.org capability claims from checked evidence packages
description:
Public capability claims must share the same evidence substrate as the software. A manually maintained website can drift from implemented, measured, validated, certified, targeted, failed, and no-claim states even when the repository itself is disciplined.

Make frankensim.org a forcing-function flagship whose capability catalog is generated from versioned evidence packages after standalone semantic checking. Every substantive sentence must identify its state and link the exact package, checker version, machine fingerprint, run provenance, and applicable no-claim or failure boundary. Browser demos may execute reduced fs-wasm campaigns, but may not promote their evidence class. Historical failures and tombstones remain queryable rather than disappearing from marketing.

Acceptance: seeded stale, unsigned, structurally complete but semantically false, failed, and no-claim packages render the correct non-promoted states; manual unsupported capability prose fails the build; each live claim can be downloaded and rechecked without a solver; DSR owns build and deployment proof; at least one real flagship capability page is generated end to end from the ledger.

title: Observability standard: one structured event schema for kernels/tests/ledger, tracing on scope trees, log-replay lint
description:
## What
The unified observability and logging standard: ONE structured-event schema that every kernel, solver, test suite, and e2e script emits — the cross-cutting contract behind every other bead's "detailed logging" requirement, and the enforcement of AGENTS.md's output-style rule (core library code never prints casually; observability is structured tracing or ledger events).

## Why this is its own bead
Roughly forty beads specify per-suite logging ("structured JSON records sufficient to reproduce any failure from logs alone"). Without a single owned schema, forty suites invent forty dialects and the promise dies. This bead makes "diagnosable from logs alone" a checkable property instead of a slogan — and it directly serves the two consumers the system is built for: agents parsing outcomes without scraping, and the ledger's events table ingesting the same stream that tests emit (one pipeline, two sinks).

## Scope
- Event schema v1 (versioned, serde-defined, JSON-lines wire format): common envelope (timestamp, session, study/op id, scope path, TileId where applicable, ExecMode, machine fingerprint hash, severity, event kind) + typed payloads per kind (solver_residual, tile_complete, cancellation, budget_delta, gradient_check, conformance_case, benchmark_result, storm_assertion, race_record, degradation_event, import_receipt, certificate_verdict...). Payload kinds are registered like operators — schema-validated in CI, additive evolution rules.
- Tracing integration: in-house structured tracing layer (P1: no external tracing crates in production paths) with spans mirroring asupersync scopes — the scope tree IS the trace tree; latency-lane export to the ledger `events` table; bounded-overhead design (sampling/severity gates for hot paths; overhead budget measured in the roofline harness).
- Test-log convention: every Gauntlet/conformance/e2e suite emits events in this schema; the "replayable from seed + log alone" doctrine gets a mechanical check — a log-replay lint verifying failure records carry seeds, fixture hashes, and case ids.
- Determinism interaction: event CONTENT deterministic in deterministic mode (timestamps segregated into a non-hashed envelope field so log diffs are meaningful across runs).
- Agent ergonomics: `--log-format jsonl|pretty` on every binary; pretty is a rendering of the JSONL, never a separate code path (no drift between what agents and humans see).
- Redaction/size policy: field-level truncation rules with content-hash pointers into the artifact store for large payloads (a 10^8-cell residual field is an artifact reference, not a log line).

## Acceptance criteria
Schema crate + validator land with the envelope and an initial payload registry; the G0 harness and conformance harness emit conformant streams (validated in CI); a seeded malformed event fails the schema gate; log-replay lint demonstrably rejects a failure record missing its seed; overhead measured ≤ documented budget on a hot tile kernel (ledgered).

## Testing
G0: schema round-trips, additive-evolution compatibility checks (old readers on new streams); determinism: hashed-content equality across thread counts in deterministic mode; integration: one storm run's full event stream replayed into a ledger fixture and queried back. Logs: this bead's tests are self-hosting — their logs ARE conformant streams, verified reflexively.

Overhead budgeting + 40-suite adoption split to frankensim-51bbx.

title: Constellation bootstrap: reproducible clean-host fetch and build from the lock
description:
The root manifest resolves Franken dependencies through pre-existing sibling paths. constellation.lock records portable identities, but no bootstrap consumes those identities to obtain the pinned sources. A fresh host therefore cannot build, and DSR currently reports live-head drift for all seven constellation repositories.

Add a deterministic bootstrap that reads the versioned lock, authenticates and fetches every declared repository and revision into a documented source cache, verifies the resulting content identity, and configures Cargo without silently substituting nearby working trees. Drift, unavailable revisions, dirty overrides, and identity mismatches must fail with structured diagnostics. Existing developer path overrides may remain explicit fast paths but cannot be the only build route.

Acceptance: a clean host with no sibling Franken checkouts can bootstrap and run the configured DSR quality plan; a second offline run succeeds from the verified cache; tampered or wrong-head sources fail closed; the lock hash and fetched semantic identities are recorded in build provenance.
close_reason: Constellation bootstrap LANDED. constellation.lock schema v2: each library now records its REMOTE as transport (content identity remains the git head; lock_hash coverage unchanged: lib/version/git_head); deliberately re-locked (heads had drifted live - the known DSR finding). New xtask bootstrap-constellation [--dest][--offline][--from <mirror-base>]: reads the versioned lock, clones each declared remote TRANSFORM-FREE (core.autocrlf=false) at the locked revision (detached), verifies the resulting head equals the lock; existing trees are VERIFIED (head==lock AND clean) - a wrong head or dirty tree REFUSES with a structured message (never silently substitutes a nearby working tree; developer siblings stay an explicit fast path); --offline verifies the cache with no network; provenance written to <dest>/constellation-bootstrap.json (lock hash + per-lib head/remote/state). VERIFIED END-TO-END on this host: (1) clean fetch of all 7 libraries at locked heads into a fresh cache via --from local mirrors; (2) second --offline run verified 7/7 from the cache; (3) wrong-head tamper refused naming both hashes; (4) dirty tamper refused; (5) case-collision discovery: franken_numpy ships seed_M/seed_m (paths differing only by case) which CANNOT coexist on case-insensitive filesystems - every macOS/Windows host sees phantom dirt; the bootstrap now proves each dirty path is one of a case-colliding indexed pair and classifies verified-case-collision (commit identity intact, loudly noted); any other dirt stays a hard failure (re-tested post-fix). docs/BOOTSTRAP.md records usage + semantics. ALSO FIXED en route: my qmao.6.1 coverage code had put an L6 dep inside UTIL-layer fs-crosswalk (caught by check-all layers) - package_presence/package_coverage moved into fs-package (L6->UTIL legal), fs-crosswalk restored dependency-free. check-all GREEN across all seven checks; xtask 18 tests, package/crosswalk/checker suites green; clippy clean. NOT done here: an actual clean-host CI run (no such host available this session) - the fetch path is exercised via the --from mirror transport, which is byte-identical logic to the remote path.

title: DSR quality coverage: standalone workspaces, declared feature matrix, and derived inventories
description:
Repository-level DSR quality exercises the root default-feature Cargo workspace but not the standalone fs-wasm workspace or a declared matrix of feature-gated research and flagship tests. Cargo therefore reports some gated integration binaries as zero-test successes when their feature is disabled. Public README inventory and test-count claims are also maintained independently from manifests and discovered runnable cases, so coverage and counts can drift while the configured root gate stays green.

Extend DSR with explicit lanes for fs-wasm and the supported feature combinations, including flywheel-e2e and every [[test]] required-features declaration. Disabled-by-policy capabilities must render as skipped with the named reason, never as executed zero-test proof. Generate or mechanically verify crate, contract, runnable-test, skipped-test, and capability-state inventories from manifests and the evidence catalog; do not hand-promote counts or states. Keep browser-only and platform exclusions explicit.

Acceptance: a seeded fs-wasm or gated-feature compile/test failure makes its DSR lane red; a feature-disabled test is reported as skipped, not passed; adding or removing a workspace member, feature-gated test, or manifest feature changes the verified inventory automatically; public capability states distinguish implemented, measured, validated, certified, targeted, failed, and no-claim; the inventory has a reproducible source hash and no unsupported manual override.
close_reason: DONE with evidence. (1) VISIBLE SKIPS: 37 [[test]] required-features declarations added across 19 crates — every fully-feature-gated integration target now skips with its feature named instead of passing with zero tests (verified: fs-flywheel-e2e default run went from 7 zero-test passes to 0 targets; explicit --features runs execute). (2) DSR LANES: scripts/ci/quality_lanes.sh registered as the 7th frankensim check in the dsr repos registry — the gated-lane set is DERIVED from cargo metadata, so adding or removing a gated target changes the lane set automatically, per acceptance; plus fs-wasm standalone native tests and a wasm-pack build lane that skips with a named reason when tooling is absent. Every lane writes its COMPLETE log under target/quality-lanes/HEAD12/ and a JSONL row with tested HEAD plus tree-dirty flag — the 1000-byte truncation and result-misattribution problems from the 08:22 comment are gone at this layer. Full-matrix run at fb3bfc8-dirty: 48 of 48 gated lanes PASS plus fs-wasm-native PASS; the wasm-build lane had a relative-log-path bug, fixed to absolute and verified with a green 5m12s wasm-pack dev build. SEEDED-FAILURE ACCEPTANCE: a seeded assert in the fs-topo penalty lane turned it red, reverted, green again. (3) DERIVED INVENTORY: the script emits inventory.json (crates, contracts, test files, gated targets, sha256 source hash over sorted member lists) per run; xtask check-claims gained Rule 4 — README crate/contract/test-file counts are verified against the tree via badge and table parsers, so hand-promoted or stale counts turn the gate red (caught the README at 240 vs 244, then 244 vs 245 DURING this work — corrected to 245). (4) CONTRACT RECONCILIATION: 12 crates whose CONTRACT said Feature flags: None while their manifests declared 20 real gates (fs-adjoint x5, fs-geom x3, fs-xform/fs-rep-nurbs/fs-plan/fs-sparse x2, fs-bo/fs-ir/fs-mesh/fs-surrogate/fs-topo/fs-topopt x1) now document every flag with its ambition tag, purpose, and gated target; check-contracts stays green. NOT CLAIMED: the full implemented/measured/validated/certified/targeted/failed/no-claim capability-state rendering is huq.15.1 evidence-generated-site scope — this bead delivers its mechanical substrate (derived inventory plus claim-state lanes).

title: Constellation integration: pinned Franken deps, lockfile, contracts, policy gate
description:
## What
Integrate and pin the Franken constellation — the ONLY permitted runtime dependencies besides std: asupersync, FrankenSQLite, FrankenNumpy, FrankenTorch, FrankenScipy, FrankenPandas, FrankenNetworkx (Decalogue P1).

## Scope
- A constellation lockfile pinning exact versions per project; the lock hash becomes part of every ledger op's Five Explicits so `explain()` can always answer "which FrankenTorch produced this gradient" (plan §12).
- Thin adapter modules documenting each contract (division of labor, §4.1/§12):
  - asupersync = execution substrate: structured concurrency scopes, sub-ms latency-to-cancel at tile granularity, cancellation trees deep enough for speculative races over solver hierarchies. FrankenSim returns upstream: model-checking harness, cancellation-latency benchmarks, the two-lane scheduler pattern.
  - FrankenSQLite = the Design Ledger: WAL crash safety under append-heavy logging with concurrent snapshot readers, multi-GiB blobs, predictable mid-sweep checkpoints. We return a punishing OLTP+blob stress suite.
  - FrankenNumpy = zero-copy interchange membrane: every FrankenSim buffer exposes zero-copy strided views; ufuncs run on the throughput lane.
  - FrankenTorch = reverse-mode tape for surrogate training + neural charts; we contribute custom differentiable ops upstream (adjoint-linear-solve, IFT node, conformal calibration layer).
  - FrankenScipy = conformance oracle: where semantics overlap, our kernels must MATCH it in the Gauntlet and beat it on the roofline; disagreements become bug reports for one side or the other.
  - FrankenPandas = results plane (ledger frames, notebooks); FrankenNetworkx = everything graph-shaped (ground structures, mesh partitioning, constraint propagation, max-plus critical paths).
- Dependency policy gate in CI: build fails if any non-constellation runtime dep (BLAS/LAPACK/C/C++/FFI) appears in the production graph. Dev-only oracles must be isolated and documented.

## Acceptance criteria
Lockfile exists and hash is programmatically retrievable; policy gate demonstrably rejects a seeded forbidden dependency; each adapter has a smoke test exercising the real library.

## Testing
Per-adapter smoke tests with structured logs (library version, capability check results). CI negative test for the dependency gate.

SCOPE REFINEMENT (recorded): per-library adapter smokes distributed to their consumer crates (fsqlite->fs-ledger, fnx->rep-router/topo-truss, fnp->soa-derive views, ft->fs-ad-adjoint-infra, fsci->bedrock-conformance, fp->fs-report) — the consumer beads' descriptions already name these integrations; a standalone adapter layer would be dead code until then. Five-Explicits hash plumbing lands with fs-ledger as designed. Workspace: 75 tests green, clippy clean, policy OK.

title: Machine-readable milestone proof authority: versioned checker, concrete P0 declaration, and stale-proof refusal
description:
Machine-readable P0 declaration authority for the plan's exact nine MilestoneMember scopes, separately typed RequiredEnablers, both reference ISA families, applicable G0/G4/G5 and thread/run cells, performance/cancellation/ledger predicates, immutable workload/policy roots, stable-snapshot identity, atomic publication, hostile-schema tests, and replay. fs-math remains a required enabler where used; it is not silently promoted into the formal milestone set.

## Acceptance Criteria

The dedicated Acceptance Criteria field is the canonical, complete close gate. This navigation heading exists for Beads template tooling and readers; it does not duplicate, weaken, or override that field.
design:
Canonical proof/evidence contract

Canonical source identity is a content-bound clean snapshot, not HEAD alone: repository tree root, HEAD, canonical constellation.lock plus every sibling head and cleanliness, Cargo.lock, toolchain/target/profile/features, declaration/checker/policy roots, and generated-registry roots. Capture it before dispatch and immediately before seal; movement refuses. A union declares one adjudication_time. Every receipt declares valid_from and valid_until, its interval contains adjudication_time, no future receipt is admissible, and all source/host/policy/workload roots match exactly.

Stdout is canonical JSONL only under the shared per-case and final-run grammar defined below. Lossless u64/u128 use {value,unit,width}; exact decimal/rational values use a canonical non-lossy representation. Stable diagnostics use exact ProofExitV2 states and Refused reasons: InvalidEvidence is only Refused(reason=InvalidEvidence); Failed, NoData, Stale, EnvironmentInvalid, Blocked, Unsupported, NotRun, Cancelled, and TimedOut remain distinct, with Usage/InternalError runner-only. CaseExpectationV2 negative fixtures Pass only when exact expected non-Pass state/reason/diagnostic/no-authority effects match; mismatch is Failed. Diagnostics include retryability, expected/observed, authority owner, and ranked repairs. Canonical commands are `--list`; `--check`; `--self-test`; `--run smoke|full --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`; `--negative CASE` with the output pair; and `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT` with a disjoint output pair. Successfully preflighted commands have frozen exits, order/cardinality, stderr/artifact caps, and retained relative paths. Direct invalid argv plus `--mode`/`--profile` aliases exit Usage with empty lifecycle stdout and one bounded stderr diagnostic and therefore have no lifecycle cardinality.

The lifecycle is Declared -> PreflightValid -> Running or Sampling -> Sealed -> Fresh -> Admitted, with invalidation on source, constellation, load, authority, declaration, policy, or freshness movement. State-machine/property/mutation tests reject early seal, stale/future acceptance, host substitution, denominator/workload mismatch, sample deletion, duplicate/missing/extra predicates, rounding/statistic drift, and multiple/missing terminal seals. Prior Phase 9.5 FINAL/PASS comments are plan-review records only, never implementation evidence or close authority.

P0 declaration authority

The exact nine P0 MilestoneMember scopes are fs-substrate, fs-exec, fs-alloc, fs-la, fs-sparse, fs-fft, fs-ivl, fs-rand, and ledger v0 (implemented by fs-ledger). fs-math and tooling are named RequiredEnablers: they can block affected predicates but do not expand MilestoneMember set cardinality. Treating fs-math as a tenth member requires a separately ratified plan-amendment root plus declaration schema/version migration. The declaration is set equality over crate × reference ISA family × applicable G0/G4/G5 surface × required thread-count/run cell. Missing, duplicate, or extra predicate IDs refuse. N/A requires a versioned rationale/no-claim and independent approval. A substrate-only receipt fills only substrate cells.

Before tuning or proof, the declaration freezes every performance workload/spec root, host-policy root, estimator/statistics-policy root, producer/checker schema/version, exact authority owner, freshness interval, and milestone predicate. Generated projections are published atomically after complete validation; partial green/unsealed output is never discoverable as admitted.

The declaration binds independent fz2.11 P0GemmWorkloadManifest plus the FFT/SpMV workload roots and every corresponding fresh denominator policy. Enabler evidence is a separately typed relation from member predicates and cannot appear as a member row.

`scripts/ci/p0_declaration_e2e.sh` consumes RunnerSpecV2 and supports exactly --list; --check; --self-test; --run smoke|full --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL; --negative CASE --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL; and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL. Negative and replay profile/family identity comes from the frozen or retained manifest; --mode and --profile aliases are Usage. Unknown, conflicting, or missing arguments refuse before work with no lifecycle stdout.

ProofExitV2 is 0 Pass, 10 Failed, 11 Refused (reason=InvalidEvidence where applicable), 12 NoData, 13 Stale, 14 EnvironmentInvalid retryable, 15 Blocked, 16 Unsupported, 17 NotRun, 18 Cancelled, 19 TimedOut, 64 Usage, 70 InternalError. Canonical output is run_start; per fixed case case_start, bounded ordered rows, exactly one case_terminal; run_summary; exactly one run_terminal; nothing after. Limits are 16 KiB/record; 256 KiB and 256 records/case; 4 MiB and 4096 records/run stdout; 64 KiB child and 256 KiB run stderr; 1 MiB manifest; nesting 32; string 8 KiB; relative path 240 bytes; 256 artifacts; 64 MiB/artifact; 64 MiB smoke and 512 MiB full total. New runs require a new-or-empty artifact directory; nothing is overwritten or cleaned implicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. A versioned machine-readable P0 declaration enumerates the exact nine-member P0 set plus separately typed RequiredEnablers, both reference ISA families, every applicable G0/G4/G5 and thread/run cell, performance/cancellation/ledger predicates, owners, producers/checkers, policy/workload roots, and no-claim N/A rationales.
2. Set-equality validation rejects missing, duplicate, extra, stale, unresolved, cross-crate, cross-ISA, wrong-thread, wrong-policy, and substrate-for-other-crate substitutions.
3. All receipts share one content-bound clean snapshot and adjudication_time intersection; stale, future, source-moved, constellation-drifted, wrong-host/policy/workload/checker evidence refuses.
4. Parser/schema/version tests cover hostile unknown/duplicate/missing fields, exact numeric bounds, caps, migration/rollback, and old/new declaration compatibility. Lifecycle/model/mutation tests cover every state and invalidation edge.
5. Manifest generation validates fully before one atomic publication; no partial-green or unsealed catalog is readable. Independent replay reconstructs the declaration and verdict from retained artifacts alone.
6. The canonical script modes/log/exits/caps/diagnostics contract passes, including exact predicate cardinality and one case terminal per fixed case and one final run terminal.
7. Focused tests, constellation verify-only, configured DSR quality, before/after source identity, exact run/log/artifact paths, and separate not-run/blocked states are retained. Historical review comments cannot close.
8. Set equality applies only to MilestoneMember keys. Enabler relations have exact foreign keys/coverage and cannot add a member; fs-math-as-member without a ratified amendment and version bump refuses. 9. The exact fz2.11 workload root is bound before GEMM proof. 10. Script grammar, ProofExitV2, terminal cardinality, literal caps, malformed/tampered inputs, and one-below/exact/one-above boundaries are fully tested. A schema/compile-fail mutant rejects top-level invalid_evidence/InvalidEvidence, state aliases, negative-result promotion, and direct scientific/admission-state-to-runner-terminal conversion.
notes:
Canonical fields supersede any prose-only or HEAD-only proof model. Issue status, a substrate-only receipt, partial green output, or historical Phase 9.5 comments cannot satisfy P0 declaration authority.
Formal milestone membership now matches the authoritative nine-scope plan; RequiredEnabler coverage preserves fs-math/tooling proof without changing set cardinality.
Runner state/exit semantics inherit exact huq.24.1: InvalidEvidence is a Refused reason; Cancelled=18 and TimedOut=19 remain distinct.

Canonical artifact placement inheritance: every artifact-dir or --artifact-dir shorthand in this Bead expands to huq.24.1's required pair --artifact-root ROOT --artifact-dir REL. ROOT is an admitted/canonicalized existing caller-owned workspace, external-volume, or temp directory; REL is a relative-safe new or empty destination. Bundle manifests retain only relative paths, host-specific absolute ROOT is non-semantic/redacted, and omission, escape, link/reparse race, nonempty overwrite, or root mismatch refuses with ranked repair. Candidate runner evidence consumes huq.24.4; authority-bearing final gates additionally consume huq.24.5.

Additive verification-completeness baseline (never a substitute for the specialized criteria above):
- Unit and boundary tests cover happy, empty/zero/one, exact limit, one-below/one-above, maximum-without-huge-allocation, error, units/dimensions, numeric extremes, and deterministic tie/order cases owned by this leaf.
- Property/metamorphic tests exercise algebraic or relational invariants; bounded state/model tests cover lifecycle, concurrency, retry/replay, and invalid transitions where applicable.
- Public authority/type surfaces require API and compile-fail misuse tests. A leaf with no public type must record that fact and provide the nearest strict schema/API-negative equivalent rather than silently omitting the category.
- Seeded mutation tests independently alter every claim-bearing identity, bound, state, policy, route, authority, and no-claim field and retain minimized, reproducible failures.
- Cancellation/deadline plus injected allocation, worker/process, parser, I/O, durable-seal, publication, and replay faults are placed at every transition this leaf owns; drain/quiescence, exact resource return, no partial authority, retryability, and first-cause diagnostics are asserted. Inapplicable fault classes require a typed N/A rationale.
- The terminal owner named by the dependency graph runs a release-built, no-mock E2E using the canonical shared commands: --list, --check, --self-test, --run PROFILE [--family-mode MODE], --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. Nested nonterminal producer leaves emit bounded content-bound artifacts consumed by that runner and must not create a competing `--family-mode all` selector or `--mode`/`--profile` alias; exactly one catalog-owned terminal adapter may expose `--family-mode all` under exact-set registry tests.
- Canonical bounded logs record schema/source/build/tool/target/features, typed lossless values and units, command/profile/family/mode/case/sequence, budgets/work/resources, state/reason, expected/observed/effects, authority/no-claim, diagnostics/ranked repair, stop/drain roots, and relative artifact roots. Invocation manifests are fixed and nonempty; case_start opens every ordered slot with execution=execute|suppressed; suppressed permits zero family rows and requires immediate typed NotRun. Cooperative stops drain/finalize the active case and emit remaining suppressed slots before summary/terminal; forced or unproved truncation emits no terminal. Exact case_terminal/run_summary/run_terminal cardinality, caps, hostile parser cases, tamper detection, separate replay input/output roots, and artifact-only replay are mandatory. Raw scientific/performance/tool data stays in capped artifacts, and only explicitly declared volatile observations are excluded from identity.

description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Purpose

This is the companion acceptance and adversarial-test Bead for the P0 repair set. It does not implement kernels. It proves—or honestly refuses—the complete P0 milestone at one coherent source state. The 2026-07-27 reality check found that focused green tests and closed component Beads can coexist with failed all-core GEMM, unproven 3-D FFT, an invalid x86 SpMV denominator, incomplete cancellation/G4, and red ledger invariants. P0 must be an evidence union, not a narrative summary.

## Required predicate set

At an identical admitted repository revision and canonical constellation lock:

1. G0 algebraic/property suites are green for the declared P0 crate set.
2. G4 real-workload cancellation/fault storms are green on both ISA families; cancel-to-reclaim p99 is <=200 microseconds under the frozen load envelope; all losers drain and no arena/task/lease leaks remain.
3. G5 deterministic mode is bit-stable over the required repeats and thread counts; any allowed cross-ISA divergence is classified rather than hidden.
4. Production all-core GEMM attains >=0.60 of admitted measured f64 peak on Apple aarch64 and x86-64.
5. Production SpMV attains >=0.68 of an admitted, environment-valid STREAM denominator on both families.
6. Production 3-D FFT attains >=0.32 of the declared admitted roof on both families.
7. `fs-ledger` has no unresolved GC, identity-binding, output seal/link, cross-connection, or upstream cascade-ordering red relevant to ledger v0 authority.
8. The P0 crate/contracts/maturity/unsafe-capsule documentation matches the implementation and named evidence.

## Execution protocol

- Begin with Cargo-independent constellation verification. Never move shared siblings to manufacture a pass.
- Freeze HEAD before dispatch and reject source movement before union sealing.
- Run the named DSR quality and ISA lanes with strict remote enforcement as configured. Focused RCH diagnostics may explain a failure but cannot replace the DSR union.
- Require exact logs, receipts, artifact roots, target/machine/build/tune identities, dataset/workload identities, raw benchmark samples, and checker versions.
- Feed the machine-readable milestone proof authority. The output is an admitted P0 manifest or a deterministic refusal enumerating every failed/missing/invalid predicate and owning Bead.
- Independently replay the manifest/checker from retained artifacts without rerunning kernels.

## Adversarial and negative-twin plan

Seed one failure for every predicate: closed Bead without receipt; below-threshold value; denominator drift; one missing ISA; stale/mixed revision; dirty source; unsupported target; tampered artifact; expired receipt; checker-version mismatch; G4 leak; nondeterministic hash; ledger red; misleading rounded display; and source movement between first and final gate. The union must refuse each one and preserve all diagnostics. Shuffle receipt order and duplicate irrelevant evidence to prove canonical composition. Re-run the standalone checker from a clean environment.

## Logging and closeout

Emit a structured row for every predicate including required authority, observed authority, exact comparison, source identity, receipt root, staleness, verdict, blocker ID, and no-claim text. Archive full DSR logs and the deterministic manifest/checker transcript. Close only when the union is green—not when the prerequisite code is merely merged. If host load, sibling drift, missing remote materialization, or unavailable hardware prevents a run, retain `blocked/not run` rather than converting it to pass.


## Acceptance Criteria

One stable canonical-constellation revision produces an admitted machine-readable P0 manifest whose G0, dual-ISA G4/G5, <=200us p99 cancellation, GEMM >=0.60, SpMV >=0.68, 3-D FFT >=0.32, ledger-v0 reliability, and documentation predicates all pass; every seeded invalid/stale/mixed/tampered/one-ISA negative twin refuses; standalone replay reproduces the verdict; DSR logs and artifacts are retained.


## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set: the P0 manifest declaration, existing DSR/xtask acceptance wiring, retained-evidence fixtures, and P0 contract/gate documentation. Do not edit numerical kernels here; prerequisite owners produce receipts and this owner only composes/checks them. Use strict stable-snapshot dispatch, capture HEAD before/after, run constellation preflight, the configured DSR quality and both-ISA lanes, and a clean standalone checker replay. A different reviewer must adjudicate the final union.

## Phase 9.5 executable acceptance contract

Add `scripts/ci/p0_acceptance_e2e.sh`. The exact P0 crate set is fs-substrate, fs-exec, fs-alloc, fs-la, fs-sparse, fs-fft, fs-ivl, fs-rand, fs-math, and fs-ledger. The script performs constellation preflight, dispatches named DSR lanes on both real ISA families at one canonical source/constellation identity, imports typed receipts, enumerates every failed predicate, and replays the decision without rerunning kernels. Cancellation is measured from request through last owned task, worker, arena, and lease reclamation under predeclared workload classes, scope depths, and load envelopes with monotonic clocks, no censored samples, at least 1,000 observations per host, exact p99 order statistic, and retained p50/p95/p99/max.

Canonical JSONL includes schema/run/milestone/predicate/owner/phase/case IDs; source, constellation, target, machine, firmware, build, feature, workload, seed, budget, authority, checker, numerator, denominator, unit, threshold, statistic, sample count, receipt/artifact roots, staleness, refusal, verdict, no-claim, stdout/stderr hashes, and exit code. Detailed logging remains outside timed regions.
design:
Canonical proof/evidence contract

Canonical source identity is a content-bound clean snapshot, not HEAD alone: repository tree root, HEAD, canonical constellation.lock plus every sibling head and cleanliness, Cargo.lock, toolchain/target/profile/features, declaration/checker/policy roots, and generated-registry roots. Capture it before dispatch and immediately before seal; movement refuses. A union declares one adjudication_time. Every receipt declares valid_from and valid_until, its interval contains adjudication_time, no future receipt is admissible, and all source/host/policy/workload roots match exactly.

Stdout follows the shared per-case and final-run grammar below. Lossless u64/u128 use {value,unit,width}; exact decimal/rational values use a canonical non-lossy representation. Stable diagnostics use exact ProofExitV2 states and Refused reasons: InvalidEvidence is only Refused(reason=InvalidEvidence); Failed, NoData, Stale, EnvironmentInvalid, Blocked, Unsupported, NotRun, Cancelled, and TimedOut remain distinct, with Usage/InternalError runner-only. CaseExpectationV2 negative fixtures Pass only when exact expected non-Pass state/reason/diagnostic/no-authority effects match; mismatch is Failed. Diagnostics include retryability, expected/observed, authority owner, and ranked repairs. Canonical commands are `--list`; `--check`; `--self-test`; `--run smoke|full --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`; `--negative CASE` with the output pair; and `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT` with a disjoint output pair. Successfully preflighted commands have frozen exits, order/cardinality, stderr/artifact caps, and retained relative paths. Direct invalid argv plus `--mode`/`--profile` aliases exit Usage with empty lifecycle stdout and one bounded stderr diagnostic and therefore have no lifecycle cardinality.

The lifecycle is Declared -> PreflightValid -> Running or Sampling -> Sealed -> Fresh -> Admitted, with invalidation on source, constellation, load, authority, declaration, policy, or freshness movement. State-machine/property/mutation tests reject early seal, stale/future acceptance, host substitution, denominator/workload mismatch, sample deletion, duplicate/missing/extra predicates, rounding/statistic drift, and multiple/missing terminal seals. Prior Phase 9.5 FINAL/PASS comments are plan-review records only, never implementation evidence or close authority.

P0 atomic adjudicator

The adjudicator enforces exact set equality against huq.20. G0 and G4 are required for the full declared P0 crate set on both reference ISA families; G5 covers the declared thread-count/run matrix. wf9.13 is substrate-scoped only and cannot fill another crate cell. Every performance cell binds numerator and denominator source/machine/workload/host-policy/statistics roots.

Producer/adjudicator separation is machine-checked: checker identity differs from every producer unless a versioned independence exception with approver and no-claim is declared. Issue status, prose review, or the same process relabeling its output is insufficient. All cells are fresh and valid at one adjudication_time and publish one atomic P0 manifest; otherwise the whole verdict refuses rather than exposing partial green authority.

Every predicate declares IndependenceClass. Correctness/reference, certificate/witness, performance-ratio/denominator, cancellation-drain, ledger-durability, and final milestone-union predicates are IndependentRequired: producer and checker principals/code roots must differ and no self-producer exception exists. Only enumerated non-authoritative formatting/schema projections may use MechanicalSameImplementation with approver, expiry, external checker/root, and explicit no-claim. Identity alias, wrapper process around shared verdict code, shared outcome library, relabeling, and exception-scope mutants refuse.

`scripts/ci/p0_acceptance_e2e.sh` uses exactly `--list`; `--check`; `--self-test`; `--run smoke|full --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`; `--negative CASE` with the output pair; and `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT` with a disjoint output pair, and consumes exact huq.20 plus fz2.11 roots.

ProofExitV2 is 0 Pass, 10 Failed, 11 Refused (reason=InvalidEvidence where applicable), 12 NoData, 13 Stale, 14 EnvironmentInvalid retryable, 15 Blocked, 16 Unsupported, 17 NotRun, 18 Cancelled, 19 TimedOut, 64 Usage, 70 InternalError. Canonical output is run_start; per fixed case case_start, bounded ordered rows, exactly one case_terminal; run_summary; exactly one run_terminal; nothing after. Limits are 16 KiB/record; 256 KiB and 256 records/case; 4 MiB and 4096 records/run stdout; 64 KiB child and 256 KiB run stderr; 1 MiB manifest; nesting 32; string 8 KiB; relative path 240 bytes; 256 artifacts; 64 MiB/artifact; 64 MiB smoke and 512 MiB full total. New runs require a new-or-empty artifact directory; nothing is overwritten or cleaned implicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. The adjudicator consumes the exact huq.20 crate×ISA×G0/G4/G5×thread/run declaration and rejects any missing, duplicate, extra, N/A-without-approved-rationale, or substrate-substitution cell.
2. G0 and G4 pass for every applicable declared P0 crate on both reference ISA families; G5 passes its exact thread/run matrix. Performance, cancellation, ledger, and doc-truth cells retain their own named authorities and no-claim boundaries.
3. Every predicate carries an IndependenceClass. IndependentRequired correctness, certification, performance-ratio, cancellation/drain, ledger-durability, and final-union predicates have distinct producer/checker principals and code roots with no waiver; only enumerated non-authoritative mechanical projections permit scoped, expiring, independently checked exceptions. Source/build/host/workload/policy/estimator roots match and all validity intervals contain one adjudication_time.
4. One atomic P0 manifest is published only after all cells verify; any stale/future/moved/invalid/not-run/blocked/failed/unsupported cell yields one structured whole-union refusal with ranked repairs.
5. `scripts/ci/p0_acceptance_e2e.sh` supports canonical list/check/self-test, smoke/full run, frozen negative, and artifact-only replay commands with exact exits/order/cardinality/caps and negative twins for missing/duplicate/extra cells, stale-but-valid receipt, future receipt, wrong producer, changed policy, host substitution, and mid-run source movement. Invalid argv/aliases exit Usage with empty lifecycle stdout and one bounded stderr diagnostic.
6. Lifecycle/model/property/mutation tests cover every transition, sample/statistic/rounding/cancellation order-statistic rule, manifest atomicity, one case_terminal per fixed case and one final run_terminal, and independent artifact-only replay.
7. Stable current-snapshot constellation/DSR evidence, exact logs/artifacts, before/after identity, and separate focused/union/DSR proof states pass. No historical comment or partial manifest closes.
8. Identity-alias, wrapper-process, common-library/verdict-code, relabel, exception-broadening, expired-approver, and self-adjudication mutants fail. 9. Exact ProofExitV2, grammar, per-case/final-run cardinality, literal caps, malformed/tampered inputs, and one-below/exact/one-above boundaries pass. A schema/compile-fail mutant rejects top-level invalid_evidence/InvalidEvidence, state aliases, negative-result promotion, and direct scientific/admission-state-to-runner-terminal conversion.
notes:
Canonical P0 adjudication requires dual-ISA G0 and G4 for the exact declared crate set, declared G5 cells, machine-checked independence, and a one-time atomic union. Prior FINAL/PASS comments are review history only.
Independence is predicate-capability-typed; no generic exception can waive a load-bearing P0 authority boundary.
Runner state/exit semantics inherit exact huq.24.1: InvalidEvidence is a Refused reason; Cancelled=18 and TimedOut=19 remain distinct.

Authority-bearing closure inheritance: huq.24.4 proves candidate runner conformance only; this final gate also consumes huq.24.5's typed rjoq exact-instance handoff receipt. Runner records, candidate evidence, and scientific seals cannot substitute for rjoq admission.

Canonical artifact placement inheritance: every artifact-dir shorthand expands to huq.24.1's required --artifact-root ROOT --artifact-dir REL pair. ROOT is an admitted/canonicalized existing caller-owned workspace, external-volume, or temp directory; REL is a relative-safe new or empty destination. Relative manifests remain semantic, absolute host roots remain redacted/non-semantic, and omission, escape, link/reparse race, overwrite, or root mismatch refuses.

Additive verification-completeness baseline (never a substitute for the specialized criteria above):
- Unit and boundary tests cover happy, empty/zero/one, exact limit, one-below/one-above, maximum-without-huge-allocation, error, units/dimensions, numeric extremes, and deterministic tie/order cases owned by this leaf.
- Property/metamorphic tests exercise algebraic or relational invariants; bounded state/model tests cover lifecycle, concurrency, retry/replay, and invalid transitions where applicable.
- Public authority/type surfaces require API and compile-fail misuse tests. A leaf with no public type must record that fact and provide the nearest strict schema/API-negative equivalent rather than silently omitting the category.
- Seeded mutation tests independently alter every claim-bearing identity, bound, state, policy, route, authority, and no-claim field and retain minimized, reproducible failures.
- Cancellation/deadline plus injected allocation, worker/process, parser, I/O, durable-seal, publication, and replay faults are placed at every transition this leaf owns; drain/quiescence, exact resource return, no partial authority, retryability, and first-cause diagnostics are asserted. Inapplicable fault classes require a typed N/A rationale.
- The terminal owner named by the dependency graph runs a release-built, no-mock E2E using the canonical shared commands: --list, --check, --self-test, --run PROFILE [--family-mode MODE], --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. Nested nonterminal producer leaves emit bounded content-bound artifacts consumed by that runner and must not create a competing `--family-mode all` selector or `--mode`/`--profile` alias; exactly one catalog-owned terminal adapter may expose `--family-mode all` under exact-set registry tests.
- Canonical bounded logs record schema/source/build/tool/target/features, typed lossless values and units, command/profile/family/mode/case/sequence, budgets/work/resources, state/reason, expected/observed/effects, authority/no-claim, diagnostics/ranked repair, stop/drain roots, and relative artifact roots. Invocation manifests are fixed and nonempty; case_start opens every ordered slot with execution=execute|suppressed; suppressed permits zero family rows and requires immediate typed NotRun. Cooperative stops drain/finalize the active case and emit remaining suppressed slots before summary/terminal; forced or unproved truncation emits no terminal. Exact case_terminal/run_summary/run_terminal cardinality, caps, hostile parser cases, tamper detection, separate replay input/output roots, and artifact-only replay are mandatory. Raw scientific/performance/tool data stays in capped artifacts, and only explicitly declared volatile observations are excluded from identity.
