title: P0 ledger-v0 reliability gate: transactional identity, seal/link, GC, cascade, and cross-connection replay
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Why this exists

P0 requires ledger v0, but the current P0 closure Bead directly lists several low-level defects without one owner that composes them into a user-meaningful reliability verdict. Fixing an output seal, foreign-key cascade, or latent unit failure individually does not prove that a real operation can commit, replay, recover, garbage-collect, and preserve identity across connections. This Bead owns that missing acceptance surface; it does not reimplement the prerequisite fixes.

## User-visible outcome

A user, agent, or independent reviewer can create and resume a real run, retrieve its complete lineage and sealed outputs, survive crash/cancellation/fault boundaries, and replay the same committed meaning without orphan artifacts, missing edges, cross-connection anomalies, or silent garbage-collection loss. A refusal is structured and leaves the last committed world intact.

## Required P0 contract

At one stable admitted revision, ledger v0 must prove:

- operation, artifact, edge, evidence, metric, tune, checkpoint, and output seal/link identities bind exact canonical content and source/schema versions;
- commit and publication are atomic across every supported connection pattern; duplicate idempotent submission charges and commits once;
- cancellation, panic, storage errors, process death, and retry cannot expose partial rows, orphan edges, half-sealed outputs, or mixed old/new state;
- foreign-key cascades, explicit GC, retention roots, snapshots, replay, and recovery preserve every live reachable object and remove only proven-unreachable data in the documented order;
- readers never treat uncommitted, tampered, wrong-connection, wrong-revision, or schema-incompatible state as authoritative;
- deterministic replay and explain/lineage projections reproduce their declared semantic roots across repeats and required thread counts;
- bounded work, memory, transaction duration, retry, and finalization budgets are explicit and denial-of-service-shaped inputs refuse before damage.

## Sequencing and ownership boundaries

Consume the exact fixes from `frankensim-0npfh`, `frankensim-fsqlite-fk-cascade-ordering-f2jag`, and `frankensim-fs-ledger-latent-failures-xys1z`. Re-run their regressions, but do not close this Bead from their status or focused tests. Historical `fs-ledger` core completion is lineage only. Any new failure discovered by the acceptance lane gets its own root-cause Bead and remains a red predicate here until proven.

## Unit, property, model, and migration tests

Unit/property tests cover empty and maximum legal transactions, canonical identity, duplicate idempotency keys, same and independent connections, nested/read-write ordering, constraint and cascade order, output seal/link exactness, unknown edges, tampered content, counter/length overflow, schema/version mismatch, and deterministic diagnostic ordering. Model/state-machine tests enumerate begin/write/link/seal/commit/cancel/fault/reopen/replay/GC interleavings and assert atomicity plus reachability invariants. Migration tests open every supported retained schema, prove deterministic forward migration or typed refusal, and prove an unknown future schema is never rewritten. Mutation tests drop or reorder every seal, edge, cascade, commit, and reachability check.

## No-mock end-to-end script

Add repository-owned `scripts/ci/p0_ledger_v0_e2e.sh`. It must drive the real ledger public API and the same Design Ledger path used by a production run, create a multi-stage operation with checkpoint, metrics, evidence, tune decision, artifacts, and sealed outputs, then close/reopen connections, explain lineage, replay, resume, run GC, and independently verify every retained root. It must use real FrankenSQLite transactions and filesystem artifacts, not an in-memory fake, mocked store, hand-authored success receipt, or fixture-only bypass.

Failure drills include cancellation at every transaction/publication boundary; panic and injected storage/write failure; process kill followed by recovery; concurrent duplicate idempotency; writer/reader and two-writer connections; parent deletion/cascade ordering; GC concurrent with readers; stale snapshot; tampered artifact; missing edge; changed source/schema; output-write failure after DB work; retry after ambiguous client outcome; and resource exhaustion. The harness passes only when the subject returns the expected typed outcome and the independent post-state checker confirms no partial authority or leak.

## Detailed logging and replay evidence

Emit deterministic JSONL with schema/checker version, run and scenario ID, sequence, HEAD and constellation root, database/schema/canonical versions, connection/transaction logical IDs, idempotency key hash, operation/artifact/edge/checkpoint/seal roots, stage and injected fault, declared work/memory/time/finalization budgets, expected and observed state transition, row/edge/lease counts before and after, recovery/GC reachability sets, replay root, subject exit/status, verdict, diagnostic code, blocker ID, no-claim text, and ranked repair. Capture the exact command, stdout/stderr hashes, exit code, retained database/artifact manifest, and standalone-checker transcript. Stable semantic rows determine the evidence root; wall time, wall-clock timestamps, OS PIDs, and connection scheduling traces are marked non-identity. Logs are bounded and redact project/user secrets.

## Recovery, rollback, and compatibility

Each failed scenario must leave the prior committed state readable and must be safely retryable with the same idempotency key. Recovery may complete or roll back an acknowledged protocol state only as documented; it cannot invent success. Migration is copy/transaction-safe with a preflight, deterministic receipt, rollback/refusal path, and no destructive rewrite of the only retained evidence. GC defaults fail closed when reachability or authority is uncertain.

## No-claim boundary

Green focused tests for a seal helper, cascade primitive, or single connection are not ledger-v0 reliability. A clean shutdown replay does not prove crash recovery. Row presence does not prove content or lineage authority. An in-memory mock, SQLite foreign-key setting mismatch, dirty/off-pin snapshot, mixed revision, owner-only replay, or acceptance log that cannot reconstruct final state cannot close this Bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

At one stable admitted revision, the real ledger v0 production path passes the full transaction/identity/seal-link/cross-connection/crash-recovery/replay/GC/migration matrix; every injected partial-commit, cascade, tamper, idempotency, reachability, schema, and resource negative twin refuses or recovers with the last committed world intact; deterministic roots, detailed JSONL, retained database/artifact manifests, focused tests, constellation preflight, DSR receipt, and clean independent replay are archived.

## Ownership and verification handoff

Expected touch set is acceptance and minimal integration wiring in `crates/fs-ledger`, its real FrankenSQLite boundary, existing contract/conformance fixtures, and the new script. Root-cause implementation remains with prerequisite owners unless this lane exposes a new scoped defect. A reviewer independent of those owners must run the clean replay and adjudicate the receipt. Hand the admitted ledger-v0 predicate or exact refusal to `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.21`.

Ledger-v0 logical cross-store publication and durability profile

Artifact bytes and manifests become durably staged before one DB-visible transactional seal/link linearization, or an equivalently specified verified protocol. Before linearization, residue is unreachable staging; after it, every referenced artifact is fully readable. Recovery completes only from verified durable intent or rolls back. Row/file presence alone cannot mint success.

Receipts freeze FrankenSQLite journal/WAL and synchronous mode, file fsync, parent-directory fsync, rename protocol, filesystem/storage/platform profile, and failure-injection boundary. GC uses pinned snapshot/epoch/lease roots: a reachable object cannot disappear between reachability scan and reader open. Same idempotency key plus same canonical payload returns the same committed result; same key plus different payload is a structured conflict. Maximum legal values and ±1 refuse overflow before huge allocation. Retained DB/artifacts replay independently from the manifest.

Affine type-state stages are DraftArtifact -> StagedBytes -> FileDurable -> DirectoryDurable -> DBLinked -> SealedManifest; only the owning protocol can advance them. Public callers cannot construct or convert staged/durable/linked/sealed authority. Cancellation/fault injection points are artifact write, short write, file fsync, parent-directory fsync, rename, DB begin/seal/link/commit, recovery intent read/verify/complete/rollback, and GC snapshot/scan/reader-open/delayed-unlink/restart. Each case proves the prior committed world, exact reachable/unreachable residue policy, idempotency, lease return, and no inferred success.

`scripts/ci/p0_ledger_v0_e2e.sh` uses exactly `--list`; `--check`; `--self-test`; `--run smoke|full --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`; `--negative CASE` with the output pair; and `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT` with a disjoint output pair, retaining DB/files.

acceptance_criteria:
Canonical acceptance criteria

1. Seal/link implements the declared logical publication protocol: staging is unreachable before one DB-visible linearization and every reference is readable after; recovery uses verified durable intent or rolls back, never infers success from residue.
2. Receipts bind the exact SQLite journal/WAL/synchronous, file and directory fsync, rename, filesystem/storage/platform durability profile, source snapshot, schema/policy/checker versions, and explicit power-loss/hardware no-claims.
3. Idempotency same-key/same-payload replays the same result; same-key/different-canonical-payload conflicts without reusing authority. Concurrent connections, crashes, reopen, duplicate requests, and cross-connection replay are covered.
4. GC pins snapshot/epoch/lease roots and proves reader safety under concurrent scan/open, delayed unlink, restarted collector, stale/expired leases, cascade ordering, and crash recovery.
5. Unit/property/state-model/mutation tests cover zero/exact/±1/max/overflow without huge allocation, seal/link/GC/cascade transitions, malformed DB/files, source/policy drift, stale/future evidence, partial intent, and atomic manifest publication.
6. A real no-mock ledger E2E supports canonical list/check/self-test, smoke/full run, frozen negative, and artifact-only replay commands with exact logs/exits/caps, retains DB and files, and permits independent manifest-only replay with corruption/tamper twins and one case_terminal per fixed case plus one run terminal. Invalid argv/aliases use diagnostic-only Usage grammar.

title: Populate P1-P6 milestone declarations, schema-migration fixtures, and catalog replay
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Why this exists

The milestone authority must ultimately cover P0 through P6, but populating every later-phase declaration is not a prerequisite for proving P0. This Bead preserves the full P1-P6 feature set while keeping the P0 critical path focused. It consumes the versioned schema/checker and concrete P0 pattern from `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.20`; it does not create a parallel truth system.

## User-visible outcome

Users, planners, and release reviewers can ask for any future milestone and receive one deterministic manifest showing the exact capability, correctness, performance, product-journey, validation, release, and no-claim predicates—plus all current blockers and evidence roots. Schema evolution never silently changes the meaning of historical milestone evidence.

## Scope

- Populate repository-owned P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, and P6 declarations from the authoritative plan and live contracts.
- Give every predicate a stable ID, exact threshold/unit, required evidence/authority class, owner Bead for diagnostic routing, target/ISA/dataset/workload applicability, staleness policy, and composition rule.
- Encode milestone sequencing without using predecessor issue status as proof. A prior milestone is satisfied only by its admitted manifest root.
- Include product-journey and public-claim predicates where the phase claims an end-to-end capability; component presence cannot substitute.
- Preserve ambition tags and the P6 rule that unsupported moonshots remain flagged off rather than blocking the solid spine.
- Define additive and breaking schema transitions, canonical migration receipts, minimum/maximum supported reader versions, and deterministic refusal for unknown future forms.
- Keep generated human/catalog/site projections generated from the same declarations and checker.

## Unit and property tests

Test every declaration for stable IDs, owner existence, exact decimal/rational thresholds, supported authority classes, complete Five Explicits, deterministic composition, no duplicate predicates, and no unknown units. Property tests shuffle declarations/evidence and prove identical semantic roots. Boundary tests cover threshold equality and neighboring representable values. Migration tests replay every retained schema version, verify canonical round trips or typed refusal, and prove migration cannot invent a green predicate. Mutation tests remove or duplicate one predicate, swap milestone/owner/ISA, alter units/thresholds, downgrade authority, reuse stale evidence, drop a no-claim branch, or turn a flagged-off moonshot into a mandatory solid gate.

## No-mock end-to-end script

Add repository-owned `scripts/ci/milestone_catalog_e2e.sh`. It must load the real checked declarations and retained evidence catalog, render P1-P6 human and canonical JSON views, seed at least one missing/red/stale/wrong-revision predicate per milestone, and invoke the standalone checker without mocks or handwritten passing manifests. It must prove that each current incomplete milestone honestly refuses, lists all blockers rather than stopping at the first, and routes repairs to exact owners.

The script also replays one retained older-schema fixture through the supported migration path, rejects an unknown future version, verifies generated catalog/docs match the declaration roots, and demonstrates that an admitted predecessor manifest—not a closed milestone Bead—is required by its successor.

## Detailed logging

Emit deterministic JSONL rows with schema/checker version, run/milestone/predicate/case IDs, owner Bead, source/constellation roots, target/ISA/features, dataset/workload/seed/budgets, exact numerator/denominator/threshold/unit, required and observed authority, staleness/migration state, receipt/artifact roots, verdict/refusal code, no-claim text, and ranked repair. Capture command, binary hash, stdout/stderr hashes, exit code, input/output manifest roots, and mutant identity. Stable semantic rows form the root; timestamps and durations are marked non-identity. Logs are bounded and redacted.

## Recovery and compatibility

A failed generation or migration publishes no replacement catalog. Retained manifests remain readable under their declared versions or refuse with a stable diagnostic and supported upgrade path. An additive declaration change cannot reinterpret an already sealed manifest; a breaking change requires a new schema and explicit migration/re-adjudication. Generated projections are replaced transactionally only after checker success.

## No-claim boundary

A syntactically valid declaration, closed component Beads, or copied historical evidence does not pass a milestone. P1-P6 declarations are future acceptance contracts; creating them does not assert that those phases are implemented, validated, released, or supported.

## Acceptance Criteria

P1-P6 declarations contain every plan exit predicate with stable IDs, exact thresholds/units, evidence authority, diagnostic owner, applicability, staleness, and no-claim semantics; all unit/property/boundary/migration/mutation tests pass; `scripts/ci/milestone_catalog_e2e.sh` deterministically renders each milestone, honestly refuses current incomplete evidence with all blockers, kills every seeded mutant, rejects unknown versions, verifies generated projections, and retains replayable JSONL and artifact roots.

## Ownership and verification handoff

Expected touch set: the declaration registry, migration fixtures, deterministic renderers/catalog projection, related governance/CI documentation, and the new script. No numerical kernels or milestone implementation belong here. Run focused schema/declaration tests, constellation preflight, DSR, and a clean standalone replay; P1 is the first milestone that may depend on this Bead.

title: CanonicalEvidenceRunnerV2 program: portable evidence, atomic publication, independent replay, contained execution, and rjoq handoff
description:
Deliver CanonicalEvidenceRunnerV2 as the P0, agent-usable evidence runner for deterministic lifecycle evaluation, bounded canonical artifacts, capability-safe durable publication, independent byte verification, contained family execution, portable replay/migration, and the exact non-authoritative handoff into rjoq admission.

This program is intentionally decomposed before implementation. Its five phase trees contain exactly 110 implementation tasks and 36 non-root proof, integration, and closeout rollup epics; this root is a 180-minute final exact-set review, yielding 147 in-program Beads without hidden implementation work. No feature from the original plan is removed. The reality check preserves all six commands, every lifecycle and failure state, every publication backend and mode, all seven fixture families, migration, independent verification, native platform containment, and the rjoq journey while repairing schema cycles, storage-accounting ambiguity, dependency drift, identifier bounds, source-location coupling, authority overclaims, route ownership, rollup operability, and hidden integration work.

## Canonical close gate

The dedicated Acceptance Criteria field is the only program close gate. Closure requires every child root, direct dependency edge, exact schema/count/estimate table, comprehensive unit/property/model/race/mutation/fuzz/API/compile-fail/fault/resource/cancellation category, the dedicated release-built no-mock early result-free corpus-generation E2E, all five downstream logical delivery suites through their thin POSIX routes and suite-declared direct native Windows or thin coordinator routes, all source-closed Rust drivers, deterministic detailed logs and redaction, every platform/provider result, recovery path, result partition, and no-claim boundary to agree on one stable source/proof snapshot. Prose, status, a local check, aggregate counts, or one successful backend cannot substitute for missing evidence.

## Success Criteria

All 110 implementation tasks, all 36 non-root proof, integration, and closeout rollups, and this program root close on exact current roots. The result-free corpus generator owned by 24.4.3.9.8 and exact-set reconciled by 24.4.3.9, plus the five downstream logical release-built no-mock delivery suites, jointly retain exact nonzero contribution coverage for every task with deterministic detailed logs and safe reproduction templates. Every exact schema, ownership, budget, estimate, dependency, E2E owner, and source-closure invariant agrees; `br lint`, dependency-cycle analysis, and graph diagnostics are clean; and focused, platform/provider, DSR, family-scientific, publication-durability, rjoq-durability, and handoff-conformance proof states remain separately reported without authority promotion.
design:
## User-facing contract

The exact commands are `--list`; `--check`; `--self-test`; `--run smoke|full --family-mode MODE --seed SEED_SELECTION --publication-protocol PROTOCOL --destination-mode DESTINATION_MODE --artifact-root ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF --bundle-rel BUNDLE_REL`; `--negative CASE` with the same output-publication options; and `--replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF` with the same output-publication options. Independent named options may permute once, then canonicalize to one frozen order. Run has no default mode. Negative and Replay derive immutable family/mode/profile data. Raw paths, credentials, ambient lookup, duplicate/conflicting options, generic `--mode`/`--profile`, retired `--artifact-dir`, and every alias are rejected before acquisition with empty stdout and one bounded actionable diagnostic.

`ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF` is exactly `posix-fd:N`, `windows-handle-slot:N`, or `content-store-capability-slot:N`; canonical unsigned decimal bounds are 2147483647 for Posix and 4294967295 for Windows/ContentStore. Numeric slots are affine acquisition data, always redacted and never semantic identity. StableTokenV2 is lowercase ASCII with an exact 128-byte ceiling. Fully namespaced IDs remain readable and intact; the frozen fixture maximum is 90 bytes, and 127/128/129 plus uppercase, non-ASCII, normalization, confusable, truncation, and alias cases are mandatory.

List freezes one RunnerCatalogV2. Check and SelfTest freeze one exact ten-field LifecycleOnlyCommandResultV2 after clean completion. Run, Negative, and Replay freeze one exact twelve-field DurableCommandResultV2 and nominal root only after bounded lifecycle staging, separate semantic-payload/fixed-header/checked-full-frame/nominal-root/typed-context preflight, publication or exact committed recovery, receipt verification, and byte-identical post-receipt payload plus payload-length/total/root/context reproduction. CommandResultTransportFrameV1 has the exact ordered header api_generation, wire_version, closed frame_kind, payload_encoded_length, frame-kind-selected nominal payload_root, and typed CommandResultTransportContextRootV1, followed immediately by exactly that many canonical payload bytes; it has no serialized completion field or self-root. A consumer accepts only complete exhaustion plus independently matching payload and context roots. Zero bytes, a detectably truncated/uncertain prefix, or one complete frame are physical outcomes; a prefix has zero lifecycle, receipt, or authority and retries use a fresh channel without stitching. Pre-transport failures use empty stdout; delivery faults preserve the frozen semantic result and use the exact outer/native exit distinction. No result serializes its own root, repeats manifest/seal roots, or emits a receipt as lifecycle. Structured repairs are ranked, non-executable, owner-scoped, and reproducible with fresh-capability placeholders.

## Phase and ownership architecture

Phase 1 freezes API generation 2 over first wire version 1: catalogs, typed values and widths, exact limits and eighteen-field RunnerBudgetsV2, the acyclic CaseEvaluationKeyV2/precontext/nested-expectation versus manifest-bound actual-context comparison/effect algebra, family/spec/catalog/executable descriptors, replay/migration schemas, invocation/run/replay identity, three-layer artifact inventory, acyclic manifest/seal model, lifecycle/terminal/stop/drain records, semantic outer results, native argv/signal/deadline/version contracts, TOOL policy, and generated ownership/grammar/coverage evidence. RunnerSpecV2 remains base/family-only. The root-free RunnerPhase1SchemaOwnershipRegistryV2 is separate and later phases add RunnerPhase2SchemaOwnershipManifestV2 through RunnerPhase5SchemaOwnershipManifestV2 without rewriting prior data or feeding later descriptors back into RunnerSpec.

The publish-false TOOL package has one closed direct normal-dependency allowlist with phase owners: fs-blake3 for phase-1 canonical hashing and nominal identity, asupersync for explicit Cx/cancellation/drain/process work added by phase 2, and fsqlite with exactly `async-api` for the production-usable persistent capability-scoped ContentStore provider added by phase 2. Pinned constellation source and feature identity must unify. Product runtime/build dependencies on the TOOL crate, unowned outbound packages/features, promotion/admission imports, and authority constructors are forbidden. The independent verifier and downstream seam remain separate publish-false TOOL/dev crates with one-way dependencies.

Phase 2 owns hostile bounded canonical JSON/JSONL decoding, Identity and full bounded no-dictionary ZstdFrameV1 decoding, deterministic Raw/RLE production, portable BundleLayoutV1, ContentStore envelopes, the public RunnerLaunchContextV1/RunnerBootstrapTableV1 ABI, capability brokers, minimal audited platform effect leaves where a proved safe API is insufficient, the sealed ContentStoreCapabilityV1 interface, the real persistent FrankenSQLite reference provider, the acyclic publication typestate, recovery, exact CommandResultTransportFrameV1 bytes and non-authoritative delivery observations, native release-process E2E, and RunnerPhase2SchemaOwnershipManifestV2. Unsafe code is denied except exact reviewed OS-interface leaves; no generic syscall, ambient path, dynamic symbol, callback, transmute, or external runtime escape exists.

Phase 3 certifies the certifier with an independent decoder/verifier crate, handwritten literal oracles, upstream and downstream mutation registration, differential/model checks, full safe-Rust Zstd decoding, artifact-only verification, original-output recovery verification, minimized seeds, and RunnerPhase3SchemaOwnershipManifestV2. Producer/oracle/verifier agreement is exact root-and-field agreement, not majority voting or exit-code agreement. The verifier imports no producer tables or semantic constructors and mints no scientific, publication, or admission authority.

Phase 4 owns pinned executable resolution, affine verified-executable tokens, explicit platform containment providers, deterministic request-drain-finalize-quiesce process control, replay source discovery, integrity-first current/legacy classification, contained migration adapters, source-independent replay reconstruction, seven release fixtures, RunnerPhase4SchemaOwnershipManifestV2, and the exact 51-field CanonicalEvidenceRunnerV2Receipt. Windows support requires the exact Job/suspended-create/handle-list/overlapped-pipe/flush provider. macOS is Supported only by a registered kernel-containment provider; otherwise it is deterministic pre-spawn Unsupported with ranked repairs to select such a provider or use a declared supported Linux/Windows worker. Process-group simulation never closes support.

Phase 5 owns the concrete Runner-to-rjoq TOOL/dev seam, durable submission/recovery coordinator, independent raw handoff verifier, final no-mock journey, RunnerPhase5SchemaOwnershipManifestV2, and the exact 33-field conformance receipt. External rjoq.7.2.1 remains generic: its seven-field ProducerBindingSchemaRegistrationV1 registry and local six-field fixture know nothing about Runner phases or types. Runner-specific catalog, 26-field CandidateArtifactBindingV1, nominal associations, phase-ownership join, and validation live only downstream. Only rjoq owns CandidateRef, request, durable basis/decision/receipt state, and authority constructors.

## Identity, replay, and resource semantics

Invocation and Run identity bind semantic command/spec/manifests/selections, the complete RunnerBudgetsV2 root, root-capability policies, and optional ReplayLineageRootV2 exactly for Replay. InvocationBasis never directly duplicates MigrationExecutionBasisRootV2; ReplayLineage contains the current basis exactly once. Current-wire replay has typed no-adapter absence. Migration validates stored, encoded, expanded, schema, canonical, and identity layers before adapter lookup; binds exact registry/policy/capability/budget/source/target roots; retains originals; and permits rollback only under a proved bijection.

DestinationResourceBindingV1 is output-publication identity only. Its eight ordered fields bind root class, platform profile, RootCapabilityPolicyRootV2, privacy-preserving stable ResourceIdentityRootV2, identity-provider policy, freshness observation, optional generation observation, and no-claim. Same output resource through a fresh slot is stable; a different output resource moves PublicationKey and every downstream publication/request root. description:
Close the reusable Runner V2 base contract by joining the immutable schema substrate, canonical CLI/lifecycle implementation, and TOOL governance lane on one stable snapshot. This phase rollup owns review and proof-state reporting only; it implements no schema, parser, lifecycle writer, publication backend, process executor, adapter, candidate seam, or authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

All descendant roots, ownership tables, coverage manifests, generated policy facts, comprehensive tests, release-built E2E scripts, and deterministic logs must agree exactly. Missing or stale evidence cannot be replaced by status or prose.

## Success Criteria

The complete phase-1 schema, canonical lifecycle/CLI, fully staged semantic-result and verifiable transport handoff contract, TOOL governance, and no-authority boundary are mutually consistent, independently replayable, and closed on one exact source and proof snapshot.
design:
Implementation is partitioned among 29 tasks and nine nested rollup epics beneath this phase gate. Immutable-schema subtree 24.1.1 contains 20 tasks and five nested rollups beneath its own exact-root gate; CLI/lifecycle/result subtree 24.1.2 exact-sets four implementation tasks; TOOL-governance subtree 24.1.3 contains five tasks and one nested registry/generation rollup. This 180-minute phase gate owns only the exact cross-subtree schema, CLI/lifecycle, TOOL-policy, route, coverage, release-proof, detailed-log, source-closure, and no-authority join.

The joined schema is RunnerSpecV2 API generation 2 over first wire version 1 with no predecessor. It includes closed states/reasons/commands/dispositions/records/diagnostics/repairs/NotRun causes; exact typed values and widths; limits, budgets, structural and complete-result feasibility; publication protocols/profiles/modes/logical targets and root-capability access/right/policy roots; neutral comparison/effect and exact case-conformance algebra; immutable specs/catalogs/executable resolver-policy data; replay/migration contracts; invocation/retry/replay identity; three-layer artifact inventory and logical aggregates; acyclic manifest/seal schemas; and explicit no-scientific/no-admission boundaries.

The six commands are List, Check, SelfTest, Run, Negative, and Replay. Run requires explicit profile and family mode. Durable commands require explicit publication protocol, destination mode, tagged affine root-capability slot, and `--bundle-rel`; the old `--artifact-dir` spelling is rejected. Check and SelfTest use sealed fixed manifests and LifecycleOnlyNoBundle. Negative and Replay derive immutable family/mode/profile selection. Independent option permutations canonicalize to one identity; aliases, defaults, duplicates, conflicts, missing selectors, raw credentials, and ambient paths are Usage or pre-run refusal according to the literal table.

Every lifecycle record has an exact common header and exact ordered payload. Both evaluator lanes execute and are retained. Exact expected mismatch/error conformance may Pass only when both lane frames match; wrong mismatch/detail is Failed; an unexpected EvaluationError uses its operational mapping; ExerciseOnlyNoDomainClaim still produces CaseTerminal but no domain claim. Ordinary operational terminals continue later slots. Only accepted Cancelled, TimedOut, or controlled drained InternalError suppress remaining slots through the three exact NotRun causes.

Aggregation selects state precedence then the lowest manifest ordinal at that state, and that case supplies reason, diagnostic, basis, and root. StopKey is a total logical order independent of physical arrival. Accepted-stop and drain roots bind descendant quiescence, stream drain, finalizers, lease/resource return, window closure, and exact cause. Forced death, leaked descendants/resources, failed staging write/flush, or truncated EOF yields no authoritative LifecycleDocument.

User-visible semantic output is fully staged, and its byte delivery is complete or detectably truncated; this phase makes no physical atomic-write claim. List freezes one bounded RunnerCatalogV2. Check and SelfTest freeze one LifecycleOnlyCommandResultV2 only after clean EOF. A durable command stages bounded lifecycle output and keeps stdout empty until 24.2.2 proves or recovers publication, then freezes one DurableCommandResultV2 containing the lifecycle document and complete PublishedBundleReceiptV2. The receipt is never appended as a lifecycle record. The transport owner separately checks semantic payload length and the fixed six-field-header-plus-payload total against command_result_stdout_bytes, and a consumer accepts only after exact length, nominal payload-root equality, typed context-root equality, complete payload, and clean frame exhaustion. Publication failure starts no stdout frame and uses one exact stderr diagnostic/exit/retry contract. Producer completion depends only on its own complete encode/write/flush/return outcome; downstream acceptance is independently verified. A durable Pass process exit without a matching receipt and complete producer delivery is impossible, while an exit code alone never proves consumer acceptance.

Artifact accounting distinguishes encoded, artifact-stored, expanded, system-publication-stored, and whole-publication-stored work. ContentStore artifact envelopes admit at most 4096 non-payload bytes; artifact-stored ceilings are 65 MiB Smoke and 513 MiB Full; system publication is capped at 8 MiB; whole publication is capped at 73 MiB Smoke and 521 MiB Full. Posix/Windows stored bytes equal encoded bytes. ContentStore stored bytes equal encoded payload plus exact envelope bytes. Actual artifact totals, reserved manifest grants, and final actual system totals remain acyclic and separately owned.

Replay identity binds source manifest, seal, receipt, run, optional nested source support, current migration execution basis, and checked source depth plus one. Migration schemas and integrity-first precedence exist upstream; real adapter execution remains 24.4.2. Artifact manifests retain ReplaySupportBindingRootV2 without retroactively changing invocation identity.

Phase 24.1 defines and implements schema and lifecycle conformance only. It cannot mint filesystem/content-store durability, process-containment proof, scientific Evidence/Certified, promotion, candidate, or admission authority. AdmissionCandidateRefV1 remains singularly owned by rjoq.7.2.1, and the Runner association remains 24.5.1. Governance rejects phase-local mirrors or production/build dependency routes to the publish-false TOOL crate.

The minimal fs-evidence-runner workspace member and lock row belong to 24.1.1.1 for focused proof. TOOL policy, contract/source/claims/docs/count truth, and repo-gate integration belong to 24.1.3.1; the root-free RunnerPhase1SchemaOwnershipRegistryV2, exact grammar/help generation, and coverage joins belong to 24.1.3.2; 24.1.3 owns review only. Focused proof, DSR-wide proof, constellation status, platform support, and later durability/authority proof remain distinct statuses.

## Final phase-1 evaluation provenance gate

Phase 1 joins immutable schema, lifecycle mapping, and governance only when public Presented inputs produce every legal evaluator outcome/error; validated roots, registry, requirements, contexts, raw outcome, verdict, and paired scoped artifacts survive unchanged through the terminal basis; and generated ownership/coverage exact-set matches the final vocabulary/caps. Lifecycle consumes but never constructs evaluator roots, and neither in-process contributions nor static scans claim downstream byte, release, durability, or authority proof.

title: Runner V2 immutable schema and non-authority API exact-root rollup
description:
Close the complete immutable Runner V2 schema substrate by exact-set joining five direct scopes: base-contract rollup 24.1.1.1 over seven implementation tasks; invocation/run/retry/replay identity task 24.1.1.2; evaluator/spec rollup 24.1.1.3 over eight tasks and two nested child rollups; artifact/manifest rollup 24.1.1.4 over three tasks; and immutable replay/migration task 24.1.1.5. The complete subtree contains 20 implementation tasks and five nested rollup epics beneath this 150-minute final schema join.

This parent owns only exact-root review, contradiction detection, ownership conformance, coverage-manifest joining, and honest proof-state reporting. It implements no schema type, evaluator, catalog, lifecycle, codec, process, publication, migration adapter, scientific claim, admission path, test cell, or E2E execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

Closure requires every descendant source/schema/test/log root at the current snapshot, an independently maintained exact-set ownership oracle, comprehensive nonzero test/E2E-or-contribution facets, deterministic redaction, source closure, and proof that every downstream handoff is acyclic and non-authoritative. Status, a direct-child receipt, or aggregate counts cannot replace a grandchild close manifest.

## Success Criteria

All 20 implementation tasks and five nested rollup epics close on exact current schema, source, ownership, codec, test, E2E contribution, deterministic detailed-log/redaction, reproduction, and source-closure roots. Generated exact-set checks report no missing, duplicate, stale, reordered, overlapping, reverse-owned, or mixed-snapshot entry, and every downstream reference remains acyclic and non-authoritative.
design:
Implementation ownership is exact across 20 tasks. Base rollup 24.1.1.1 exact-sets seven tasks owning checked values/catalogs/limits, diagnostics/budgets/capability policy, source-frozen registries/resolvers, runtime evidence/dispositions/resources, route/native ABI/local-close API, deterministic logs/reproduction, and independent proof/E2E projections/source closure. Direct tasks 24.1.1.2 and 24.1.1.5 own invocation/run/retry/replay identity and immutable replay/migration schemas. Evaluator/spec rollup 24.1.1.3 exact-sets its eight tasks and two child rollups. Artifact rollup 24.1.1.4 exact-sets three tasks owning inventory/layout/role membership, acyclic manifest/seal/receipt-link schemas, and cross-module API/proof/source closure. No rollup owns a competing implementation constructor or substitutes aggregate tests for task tests.

Execution order is base; evaluator-schema and admission leaves; deterministic evaluator/conformance; family registries and case sealing; descriptor/catalog sealing; independent child proofs; evaluator and spec subtree rollups; evaluator-spec join; migration/replay and invocation/replay identities; artifact/manifest/seal schemas; then this exact-root join. Independent lanes remain parallel where ownership allows. Every dependency is a compile-order or semantic-consumption edge; no child waits on lifecycle, parser, publication, process execution, adoption, or authority implementation.

The rollup exact-set oracle enumerates every API/wire/predecessor rule; command/profile/disposition; ProofExit/refusal/record/NotRun catalog; diagnostic/retry/repair field and cap; typed value, unit, digest role, width, limit, budget, and feasibility equation; publication protocol/path/profile/mode/target and root-capability access/right/policy; evaluator node, observation, error, mismatch, lane, raw outcome, expected outcome, claim mode, and conformance verdict; case/spec/catalog/executable field; adapter/migration/replay-support field and precedence stage; identity/retry/replay field; artifact codec, three length/root layers, extent/logical aggregate, inventory, manifest, seal, and no-claim boundary. Each item has one constructor owner and one coverage-manifest row.

API generation 2 is distinct from first wire version 1 with explicit no predecessor. Every current schema uses its frozen `.v1` domain. Version-2/no-predecessor, `.v2` first-wire domains, missing or duplicate owners, mixed descriptors, unregistered roots, generic digest conversions, callback-bearing schema data, or post-seal mutation block closure.

RunnerBudgetsV2 distinctly binds lifecycle_encoded_bytes, command_result_stdout_bytes, artifact_encoded_bytes, artifact_stored_bytes, artifact_expanded_bytes, system_publication_stored_bytes, and publication_stored_bytes. Artifact actual totals preserve encoded, protocol-stored, and expanded layers. ContentStore object overhead is at most 4096 non-payload bytes per artifact; artifact-stored ceilings are 65 MiB Smoke and 513 MiB Full. System publication work is separately capped at 8 MiB, making whole-publication ceilings 73 MiB Smoke and 521 MiB Full. The schema join rejects collapsed units, missing protocol equations, checked-overflow gaps, hidden staging copies, or manifest self-length cycles.

PublicationSelectionV2 appears exactly once in every durable InvocationBasisV2 and BundleManifestV2 and is absent for List, Check, and SelfTest. LogicalBundlePathV1 and ContentStoreObjectKeyV1 remain distinct from physical capabilities, prefixes, transactions, generations, and attempts. The portable path set is an antichain. DestinationAdmissionModeV2, PublicationProtocolV2, path profile, and logical target cannot drift between invocation, manifest, later durable identity, seal, receipt, replay, or verifier.

Replay identity is acyclic. ReplayLineageRootV2 derives depth as checked source depth plus one, requires source ReplaySupportBindingRootV2 only for nested Replay sources, and binds the current MigrationExecutionBasisRootV2 before execution. MigrationObservationRootV2 is retained later in ReplaySupportBindingRootV2 and BundleManifestRootV2, never inserted retroactively into InvocationRootV2. Integrity validation precedes unsupported-version/adapter classification. Current wire V1 uses exact no-adapter absence.

Artifact schemas preserve stored-object, encoded-frame, and expanded-content roots and lengths; a canonical logical aggregate map keyed by axis and unit; producer case/ordinal/role/required/extent provenance; actual artifact totals; reserved system/whole publication grants; and exact replay-support linkage. Manifest construction excludes itself, Seal, final receipt, attempts, physical paths, and authority. SealBasis joins manifest and opaque durable pre-seal identity, while production durability and receipt constructors remain exclusively downstream.

Authority remains monotone and absent. Evaluator Match, case conformance, RunnerSpec, InvocationRoot, RunId, inventory, manifest, hypothetical seal root, replay lineage, and migration observation cannot construct ProofExit, publication proof, scientific Evidence/Certified, promotion, candidate, or admission receipts outside their named later owners. Canonical AdmissionCandidateRefV1 and its wrappers remain singularly owned by rjoq.7.2.1; this schema rollup neither mirrors nor imports them.

Retained closeout evidence includes twelve original route-bearing schema-scope coverage manifests, including the two scopes later decomposed into rollups; ten additive decomposition-task manifests; all five nested rollup manifests; independent descriptor and complete-frame oracles; exact test-count tables; compile-fail and mutation-corpus roots; public-API fixture roots; deterministic detailed-log/redaction and reproduction roots; toolchain/source roots; and the final join root. Logs exclude raw bulk bytes, physical paths, capability slots, handles, credentials, PIDs, wall-clock values, scheduler timing, and secrets.

## Final immutable-schema reconciliation gate

This rollup closes only when the base, invocation/run, evaluator/family, replay/migration, and artifact/manifest child roots agree on the 43 base wrappers, ten constructor owners, fourteen final evaluator roots, codes 1-71, normalized registries, Presented/validated provenance, ArtifactCodec/LogicalExtent shared ownership, byte-root handoff, paired contextual inventory/entry identities, scoped ArtifactSet projection, complete manifest order, replay support, and all no-claim boundaries. The dependency graph must remain base to evaluator to family sealing to artifact, with no reverse import or forward constructor authority.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact subtree contains 20 implementation tasks—seven under 24.1.1.1; direct tasks 24.1.1.2 and 24.1.1.5; four under 24.1.1.3.1; four under 24.1.1.3.2; and three under 24.1.1.4—plus five nested rollup epics and this root. Every task and rollup closes on exact current roots. Each applicable literal/unit/boundary, property/metamorphic, state/typestate/model/race, mutation/fuzz, API/compile-fail/trait, fault/resource/cancellation, release-built E2E or immutable contribution, deterministic detailed logging/redaction, reproduction, and source-closure facet is separately nonzero or has an exact registered inapplicability reason.

2. An independent exact-set join covers every catalog, discriminant, ordered field, width, cap, budget, minimum, compatibility cell, precedence rule, root domain/role, unique constructor owner, presence/exclusion rule, and no-claim boundary listed in the design. Missing, duplicate, stale, locally widened, or hand-derived optimistic rows fail.

3. Version tests prove API generation 2 versus wire V1/no-predecessor in every descriptor, contract, root domain, registry handoff, migration rule, and generated expectation. Version 2 plus no predecessor, `.v2` first-wire domains, aliases, mixed descriptors, or missing migration ownership block closure.

4. Ownership conformance proves each base wrapper and schema is declared once; evaluator/spec ownership is split cleanly; migration schemas precede parser/verifier/execution; RunnerSpecRoot feeds invocation; replay support feeds manifest; lifecycle roots remain presented until 24.1.2; durable proof remains 24.2.2; and candidate/receipt authority remains rjoq plus 24.5.

5. Structural feasibility tests join diagnostic nested-size caps, record/case/run equations, expression nodes/edges/depth/visits, artifact counts and three-layer bytes, system/whole publication work, command-result stdout, manifest size, memory staging, and profile ceilings. Independently legal fields that cannot coexist in a declared case/spec/result refuse before allocation.

6. Contradiction and mutation fixtures cover catalog omission/duplication, role swaps, impossible tightening, wrong lifecycle equation, numeric coercion drift, empty Any, masked lane errors, DAG cycles, wrong conformance frames, callable executable descriptors, cyclic/attempt-dependent identities, caller-selected replay depth, source-support mismatch, migration-precedence inversion, stored/encoded/content collapse, scalar cross-unit totals, path-prefix collisions, protocol/mode/target drift, self-length or seal cycles, fabricated durability, candidate mirrors, and authority conversions.

7. The representative no-mock public-API fixture joins all descendant checked constructors, seals a family, evaluates both lanes, checks positive/negative/error conformance, builds normal/retry/replay identity, constructs zero/one/many inventories, manifest, replay support, and a hypothetical seal frame, and independently recomputes every root. It cannot construct lifecycle output, codec bytes, publication proof, process execution, candidate, scientific receipt, or admission receipt.

8. Publication and byte-accounting tests distinguish encoded, artifact-stored, expanded, system-stored, and whole-publication units and roots; enforce exact Posix/Windows equality and ContentStore envelope equations; cover 4096-byte overhead, 8/65/73/513/521 MiB boundaries, overflow, omitted/double-counted objects, staging copy accounting, and actual-versus-reserved manifest fields.

9. Replay/migration tests join source/target schema identity, verifier, registry, selected adapter, policy, capability, limits, budgets, scopes, lineage depth, retained originals, transformed bytes, classification, observation, and support binding. Current V1 no-adapter, fresh/nested replay, integrity-first pairwise defects, wrong source support, and no retroactive invocation mutation are exact.

10. CONTRACT, rustdoc, schema descriptors, registered sources, twelve original route-bearing schema-scope coverage manifests plus ten additive decomposition-task manifests, all five nested rollup manifests, generated catalog inputs, deterministic detailed logs/redaction, and reproduction records agree on all ownership, versions, catalogs, caps, fields, precedence, exclusions, typestates, no-claim language, and downstream handoffs. Any missing manifest, duplicate scope, contradiction, aggregate-for-task substitution, or mixed snapshot blocks closure.

11. Focused format, locked check/test/doc/clippy, compile-fail, schema, mutation, fixture, and scanner proof passes on one stable source snapshot for every implementation leaf. Repo-wide policy, generated-count, and DSR proof remain 24.1.3 and are reported separately; constellation drift is never relabeled as source failure.

12. This rollup has a 150-minute exact-root join/review budget. The 20 implementation tasks total 12,090 minutes; the five nested rollup epics total 570 minutes; therefore the complete 26-node immutable-schema subtree totals 12,810 minutes. Direct subtree totals are 4,860 for 24.1.1.1, 840 for 24.1.1.2, 4,470 for 24.1.1.3, 1,770 for 24.1.1.4, and 720 for 24.1.1.5, followed by this 150-minute join. None of the implementation or integration may be hidden or double-counted.

13. Immutable-schema rollup tests exact-set every child schema/domain/owner/field/cap/root and independently walk the full DAG. They require comprehensive unit/boundary/property/model/mutation/compile-fail/no-mock integration/E2E-contribution/detailed-log/source-closure evidence and reject stale names, partial exact lists, duplicate owners, mixed registries, unbound byte roots, root-only membership, cross-case artifacts, missing negative corpora, or any unexpected mismatch before closure.

14. Immutable-schema DAG closeout exact-set distinguishes fourteen evaluator/conformance nominal roots from four root-free nested member schemas and keeps the 43 presented-wrapper count unchanged. Independent oracles walk view -> CaseEvaluationKey -> expressions/requirements/fixtures/optional validated fixture roots -> EvaluationPrecontext/nested expected frames -> CaseConformanceSpecRoot -> CaseManifestRoot -> actual EvaluationContextRoot -> actual error/detail -> raw outcome -> verdict; verify CaseManifest carries the composite key once and direct read-only accessors preserve ergonomics; and reject invented roots, actual-root expectations, wildcard/generic digests, context collapse, every reverse/self edge, and all one-field key/spec/manifest/context substitutions. All unit/property/model/mutation/compile-fail/no-mock E2E-contribution/detailed-log/coverage/source-closure partitions are nonzero where applicable and exact-joined with zero unexpected mismatches.

15. GLOBAL ROLLUP EXACT-SET AND PROOF-STATE RECONCILIATION (CONTROLLING). This rollup owns review and proof aggregation only and cannot substitute parent prose, dependency presence, inherited status, aggregate counts, or a receipt root for direct-child completion. Its close manifest must bind the frozen exact ordered set of direct child IDs, each child status=closed, each child terminal close-manifest root, source-closure root, build/schema/owner/oracle roots, execution or contribution scope, retained relative artifact references, and focused, release-built E2E or contribution, source-closure, constellation, DSR, scientific, and authority proof statuses on one compatible stable snapshot. Missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, stale, reopened, blocked, mixed-snapshot, wrong-owner, wrong-scope, or root-mismatched children refuse; any intentional child-set change requires an explicit revision of this rollup rather than silent discovery. The join preserves separately the nine leaf categories: literal/unit/boundary; property/metamorphic; state/typestate/model/race; mutation/fuzz; API/compile-fail/trait; fault/resource/cancellation; release-built no-mock E2E or immutable E2E contribution; deterministic detailed logging/redaction; and source closure. It also preserves distinct exact ID sets and checked counters for eligible positives and matched positives; eligible expected refusals and matched expected refusals; eligible expected failures and matched expected failures; and eligible mutations and matched mutations; typed Unsupported and typed inapplicable cells with exact registered reasons; unexpected mismatches; execution failures; and unexplained skips. Aggregate totals are checked sums only and cannot replace a subpartition or make an empty/subset selection green. Every child-owned E2E contribution must resolve to exactly one named downstream execution owner/script and every owner must exact-set consume its contributed rows; the rollup cannot claim execution passed from contribution evidence. Child log roots must prove deterministic ordering, bounded retention, complete forbidden-class redaction and sentinel no-echo across observed values, Display, Debug, canonical bytes, logs, and reproduction text. Child source closures must exact-set implementation, contracts, schemas/owners, independent oracles, fixtures, E2E scripts or contribution rows, log schemas, dependencies/features, and build inputs. Closeout reports all proof statuses separately and never promotes focused proof, a child Pass, a no-authority conformance receipt, or a publication/admission result into scientific or authority evidence.

ROLLUP FIVE-EXPLICITS AND LOG-COMPLETENESS JOIN (CONTROLLING). This rollup exact-set joins every direct child Five-Explicits root and complete-log root on the same source/build snapshot. Missing, extra, duplicate, stale, mixed, unit-ambiguous, seedless-without-typed-reason, over-budget, capability-incomplete, partially logged, silently truncated, or terminal-less child evidence refuses. Aggregate counts or a parent budget cannot replace any child cell exact explicit values or complete terminal log.

SEMANTIC SEED PROPAGATION AND PROOF JOIN (CONTROLLING). This bead does not invent a second seed type or hidden default. Every owned schema, fixture, command, execution, artifact, replay, verifier, receipt, log, source-closure, E2E row, or rollup join that carries an invocation or case preserves the exact upstream `InvocationSeedSelectionRootV2`, `CaseSeedPolicyV2`, and applicable `CaseExecutionSeedRootV2` or registered `NoRandomness` absence through typed parent bindings. Unit/property/model/race/mutation/API/compile-fail/release-E2E-or-contribution/log/source-closure proof covers omission, substitution, wrong case/run, stale/mixed snapshot, override, ambient randomness, and count-only evidence. Test-harness seeds remain separately typed Five-Explicit data and cannot substitute for the semantic workload seed. Seed evidence establishes reproducibility only and never scientific, publication, verification, or admission authority.

MIGRATION-PARALLEL SCHEDULING CLARIFICATION (CONTROLLING). `.24.1.1.5` begins after `.24.1.1.1` and runs in parallel with evaluator/spec implementation. `.24.1.1.2` joins `.24.1.1.5` with exact RunnerSpec owner `.24.1.1.3.2.3`. This supersedes prose implying migration waits for the evaluator/spec rollup; it changes scheduling only and removes no close gate.

ROLLUP E2E ROUTE RESOLUTION JOIN (CONTROLLING). This rollup exact-set joins every direct child execution/contribution classification and proves a one-to-one mapping from each contribution row to one literal downstream owner, driver, script/native route, and immutable manifest. Missing, ambiguous, duplicate, stale, remapped, wrong-owner/script, unexecuted, multiply executed, hidden-skip, contribution-only-Pass, or focused-proof substitution refuses.

BASE AC54 DECLARATION/OBSERVATION EXACT-JOIN (CONTROLLING). This rollup consumes the base leaf AC54 contract without redefining its types, weakening provenance, or collapsing component roots. Every direct-child close row that contains or semantically reconstructs Runner base coverage exact-joins declaration-side five_explicits_declaration_root, numeric_inputs_root, numeric_grants_root, expected_numeric_observations_root, seed_requirement_root, budget_set_root, version_requirements_root, and capability_contract_root on one source/build/schema snapshot. expected_numeric_observations_root is the declared expected-observation contract, not proof of a runtime observation. Only execution-owning evidence may add separately derived actual numeric observations, observed_versions_root, and observed_capability_sets_root; schema-only and contribution-only rows preserve typed nonpresence plus the exact downstream owner and no-claim instead of copying declarations, expectations, owners, budgets, or route facts into observed slots. FixedManifest seed provenance remains bound to the exact case-manifest identity; InvocationDerived provenance remains bound to invocation selection, case identity, registered derivation domain, generator version, and minimizer version; NoRandomness remains a registered inapplicability record. Source ordinal, expected record count, execution scope, category or facet, cell-derived hash, inferred soft budget, and total or parallel child caps cannot substitute for any semantic explicit. Every detailed log, complete LogBudgetExceeded terminal, minimized reproduction, aggregate, and report exact-joins the applicable component roots. Independent literal/unit/boundary, property/metamorphic, state/model, mutation, API/compile-fail, release-E2E-or-contribution, detailed-log/redaction, and source-closure tests reject missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, stale, cross-role, declaration-as-observation, wrong-seed-provenance, mixed-snapshot, and count-only joins. Focused proof, release-route proof, source closure, and DSR remain separate proof states.

AC58 DESCENDANT SCHEMA-IMPACT JOIN (CONTROLLING ROLLUP). This rollup owns no implementation schema and may mint no leaf evidence. It consumes the exact SchemaImpactManifestV1 from every recursively contained implementation leaf on one compatible source snapshot and constructs a deterministic descendant join ordered by stable leaf ID, then stable schema ID. The join records exact descendant and schema-row counts plus exact counts for NewV1NoPredecessor, UnchangedV1, MigratedV1ToV2, DecodeOnlyLegacyV1, RetiredV1, and InapplicableNoCanonicalFrame; every count is checked against the literal descendant inventory rather than inferred from status, labels, estimates, source ordinals, or child aggregate totals. It refuses a missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, stale, owner-remapped, cross-rollup, unknown-disposition, incompatible-snapshot, V1/V2-substituted, partial-migration, or multiply aggregated leaf/schema row, and refuses any authoritative V2 close claim while a required descendant is absent or still names an incompatible authoritative V1 parent.

Comprehensive rollup tests cover exact-empty where structurally legal, one descendant, the exact live maximum, one-over injected input, all six dispositions, nested-rollup associativity without double counting, order/shard/schedule/resume invariance, every missing/extra/duplicate/reorder and mixed-snapshot mutation, first explicit divergence, bounded deterministic step-prefixed logging and redaction, structured reproduction, overflow terminal, coverage counters, and exact source closure. A source-closed release-built E2E join consumes only already produced leaf evidence and proves aggregation fidelity; it does not execute descendants, replace their unit/property/model/mutation/API/fault/E2E/log/source-closure gates, or promote focused, DSR, downstream, durability, scientific, or authority proof. CONTRACT/rustdoc and the final rollup report list every descendant schema-impact manifest and all separate proof states.

LIVE ROLLUP TOPOLOGY, SCHEDULING, AND OPERABILITY 2026-07-29 (FINAL CONTROLLING). This issue is a `runner-v2-rollup` epic. Its exact direct hierarchy children are: `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.1.1.1`, `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.1.1.2`, `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.1.1.3`, `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.1.1.4`, `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.1.1.5`. Its current recursive subtree contains exactly 26 Beads: 20 implementation tasks totaling 12,090 minutes and 6 rollup epics totaling 720 minutes, for 12,810 minutes. The 25 internal `parent-child` relations are closure hierarchy only; no reciprocal parent-depends-on-child `blocks` edge is permitted. This rollup's own 150-minute estimate covers only its explicitly named aggregate, integration, join, driver, rerun, source-closure, or close-review work and is not duplicated in child estimates. While `br epic status` reports `eligible_for_close=false`, this rollup MUST have status `blocked`, never `open` or `in_progress`; when eligibility becomes true, transition it to `open` or `in_progress` only for its scoped closeout, then close it. The canonical executable-work query is `br ready --epic frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24 --type task`. `bv` robot output is diagnostic only; any surfaced rollup is not executable implementation work. Close this rollup only after every exact child-root, integration, test/E2E, detailed-log/redaction, reproduction, source-closure, proof-state, authority, and no-claim gate in this Bead passes. This clause supersedes every earlier numeric node/estimate/subtotal claim and every earlier phrase treating hierarchy children as reciprocal `blocks` dependencies or this epic as an implementation task. It removes no scope, feature, functionality, test, E2E script/contribution, logging, reproduction, source, route, capability, durability, scientific, admission, authority, or no-claim obligation.

title: Runner V2 base-contract implementation and proof rollup: values, evidence, routes, logs, and projections
description:
Decomposed implementation-and-proof rollup for the dedicated publish-false TOOL scaffold and complete Runner V2 base data contract: checked literal catalogs, typed values/units and limits; actionable diagnostics, budgets, and capability policy; source-frozen schemas and migrations; runtime evidence and resource reconciliation; route schemas, native ABI, and local API; deterministic logs and structured reproduction; and independent proof, release-E2E projections, coverage, and source closure. Seven atomic children own those disjoint implementation domains; this epic exact-set joins them and retains the sole integrated base-contract and external-route semantics. It emits no lifecycle, parses no hostile bytes, performs no filesystem or process work, and mints no scientific, admission, or authority evidence.


## Success Criteria

The dedicated Acceptance Criteria field, including its final live rollup topology/accounting reconciliation, is the canonical success gate. Every exact direct child must close on compatible proof and source roots, every assigned aggregate/integration/route obligation must pass, and focused, release-E2E, DSR, durability, scientific, admission, authority, and no-claim statuses must remain separate.
design:
This leaf owns `crates/fs-evidence-runner/Cargo.toml`, the initial crate scaffold and CONTRACT semantics, one root `Cargo.toml` workspace-member row, and the resulting `Cargo.lock` package row so focused locked tests are possible. The package is `publish = false`, layer `TOOL`, inherits workspace package fields and lints, and has no build script or package feature that widens authority. Phase-1-owned schema modules import only `fs-blake3`, exclusively for canonical hashing and nominal identity construction. The closed eventual direct normal-dependency allowlist for the complete package is exactly `fs-blake3`, `asupersync`, and `fsqlite` with its pinned async API feature: later capability, cancellation, process, and persistent ContentStore modules may use only the row assigned to their owning phase. Phase 2 owns the later `asupersync`/`fsqlite` manifest and lock additions; phase-1 tests verify owner-scoped imports rather than asserting a forever-one-row manifest. Build, proc-macro, optional, renamed, ambient registry, and unowned target-specific routes are forbidden. Direct and transitive feature/source identity must unify with the pinned constellation. The crate imports, reexports, and constructs no promotion, verification-admission, scientific-authority, or rjoq type. Dependency policy, contracts, source/claim scans, documentation facts, count gates, and CI wiring are implemented by 24.1.3.1; the root-free Phase-1 schema ownership registry, generated grammar, coverage joins, and exact registry inventory are implemented by 24.1.3.2. Rollup 24.1.3 performs review and exact-root closeout only.

The public product-generation name is RunnerSpecV2 and the API generation constant is 2. The first frozen wire schema version is 1 with explicit no-predecessor policy. Every canonical identity schema introduced by the Runner V2 family therefore uses wire version 1 and a `.v1` domain even when the nominal Rust type ends in V2. API generation and wire version are distinct typed fields and cannot be substituted.

The closed ProofExitV2 catalog is exact: 0 Pass, 10 Failed, 11 Refused, 12 NoData, 13 Stale, 14 EnvironmentInvalid, 15 Blocked, 16 Unsupported, 17 NotRun, 18 Cancelled, 19 TimedOut, 64 Usage, and 70 InternalError. Refused alone carries one RefusedReasonV2: 1 InvalidEvidence, 2 NonCanonicalEvidence, 3 EvidenceIdentityMismatch, 4 EvidenceTampered, 5 LimitExceeded, 6 UnsafeArtifactPlacement, 7 ArtifactCollision, 8 LifecycleViolation, 9 PolicyRefused, 10 AuthorityBoundaryViolation, or 11 MigrationRefused. Unknown codes refuse and domain-specific reasons use separately registered namespaces.

The command catalog is exact: 0 List, 1 Check, 2 SelfTest, 3 Run, 4 Negative, 5 Replay. RunProfileV2 is exact: 1 Smoke and 2 Full; profile presence follows the frozen per-command table rather than a generic run/non-run shortcut. ArtifactDispositionV2 is exact: 1 LifecycleOnlyNoBundle and 2 DurableBundleRequired; List carries typed absence rather than a third disposition. RootClassV2 is exact: 1 InputArtifactRoot, 2 OutputArtifactRoot, or 3 Other with a registered policy ID. PlatformPathProfileV2 is exact: 1 PosixDescriptorRelativeV1, 2 WindowsHandleRelativeV1, or 3 ContentStoreObjectKeyV1. Unavailable profiles are Unsupported.

Lifecycle record kinds are exact: 1 RunStart, 2 CaseStart, 3 FamilyRow, 4 CaseTerminal, 5 RunSummary, 6 RunTerminal. State-bearing record roles are exact: 1 PreRunDiagnostic, 2 ExecutedCaseTerminal, 3 SuppressedCaseTerminal, 4 RunTerminal. PreRunDiagnostic allows Usage, Refused, NoData, Stale, EnvironmentInvalid, Blocked, Unsupported, Cancelled, TimedOut, or controlled InternalError, requires one exact base diagnostic, and has no lifecycle record. ExecutedCaseTerminal allows every non-Usage state except NotRun. SuppressedCaseTerminal allows only NotRun. RunTerminal allows every non-Usage state except NotRun. Pass forbids a diagnostic. Failed requires `case.conformance_mismatch`. NotRun requires `runner.not_run`. Every other allowed state requires its matching base diagnostic. Active Cancelled and TimedOut require a typed proven-drain root; active InternalError requires a typed controlled-drain root. RefusedReason is present exactly when state is Refused.

The base DiagnosticCodeV2 catalog is exact: 1 `case.conformance_mismatch`, 2 `runner.not_run`, 3 `runner.refused`, 4 `runner.no_data`, 5 `runner.stale`, 6 `runner.environment_invalid`, 7 `runner.blocked`, 8 `runner.unsupported`, 9 `runner.cancelled`, 10 `runner.timed_out`, 11 `runner.usage`, 12 `runner.internal_error`. Family diagnostics are separately namespaced and cannot replace or collide with base codes. RetryabilityV2 is exact: 0 Never, 1 SameInvocation, 2 AfterInputChange, 3 AfterEnvironmentChange, 4 AfterPrerequisiteChange. RepairActionKindV2 is exact: 1 ChangeArguments, 2 SupplyEvidence, 3 RegenerateCanonicalEvidence, 4 RefreshEvidence, 5 ReduceResourceDemand, 6 ChooseSafeArtifactDestination, 7 RestoreLifecycle, 8 UpdatePolicyOrCapability, 9 RegisterMigration, 10 RetrySameInvocation, 11 ContactOwner, 12 InspectRetainedArtifact. Actionable diagnostics bind retryability, typed expected and observed values, owner, ordered prerequisites, no-claim scope, and one through sixteen contiguous ranked non-executable repairs.

NotRunCauseV2 is exact: 1 PriorCancelled with a CancelledStopRootV2, 2 PriorTimedOut with a TimedOutStopRootV2, 3 PriorControlledInternalError with a DrainedInternalErrorRootV2. Every value binds the correctly typed causal root and lowest remaining manifest ordinal. There is no generic unattempted or profile-filter cause. This leaf validates that basis only; slot emission and immediate terminal sequencing belong to lifecycle child 24.1.2.3.

TypedValueV2 variants are exact: I8, I16, I32, I64, I128, U8, U16, U32, U64, U128, Rational, Decimal, F32Bits, F64Bits, Digest, Quantity, Token, Text, RelativePath, and OpaqueBytes. Absence is a separate Option-like wire sum and never a value or all-zero sentinel. Rationals have a nonzero positive denominator, sign only in the numerator, and lowest terms. Decimal means coefficient times ten to negative scale; zero uses coefficient 0 and scale 0, and nonzero values remove every removable trailing decimal zero. IEEE values preserve raw bits including signed zero, subnormals, infinity, and NaN payloads and are not silently ordered. Quantity uses one numeric value plus UnitV2. UnitV2 binds a normalized rational scale and seven signed SI base-dimension exponents. Stable tokens are lowercase ASCII, at most 128 bytes, with nonempty alphanumeric segments separated only by `.`, `_`, or `-`. Text is bounded UTF-8. Bundle-relative paths are slash-separated logical paths at most 240 bytes with no empty, dot, dot-dot, absolute, drive, NUL, or backslash component. Raw presented bytes cannot enter validated token, text, unit, or path APIs without a checked constructor.

DigestRoleV2 is exact: Spec, Invocation, Run, Source, Build, Toolchain, CaseManifest, ArtifactEncoded, ArtifactContent, StoredObject, ArtifactInventory, LifecycleLog, RunSummary, RunTerminal, BundleManifest, DurablePublication, Seal, PublishedBundleReceipt, Policy, CandidateBytes, CandidateSchema, SourceClosure, ClaimScope, ProducerManifest, and RegisteredFamilyDomain. A digest value binds role, registered domain, and exactly 32 bytes. Present all-zero bytes are syntactically valid and distinct from absence; no test attempts to find a BLAKE3 preimage whose digest is zero.

LogicalUnitV2 is exact: EncodedBytes, ExpandedBytes, StoredBytes, LogicalBytes, Count, Records, Rows, Elements, Samples, Iterations, Operations, Cycles, Nanoseconds, Seconds, Dimensionless, and RegisteredUnit. Registered family domains, root policies, diagnostics, roles, and units are bounded sealed data, not callbacks or runtime schema implementations.

RunnerLimitsV2 is the sole owner of the base ceilings consumed downstream: 64 argv tokens; 8 KiB per argv token; 64 KiB aggregate argv; 16 KiB per lifecycle record; 256 records and 256 KiB per case; 254 family rows per case; 256 invocation cases; 4096 records and 4 MiB lifecycle document; 5 MiB canonical command-result stdout; 4 MiB per child stdout; 16 MiB smoke or 128 MiB full combined child stdout; 64 KiB per child stderr and 256 KiB combined stderr; 1 MiB per manifest; nesting depth 32; 256 comparison or effect nodes; 8 KiB text; 128-byte stable tokens; 240-byte bundle-relative paths; 32 diagnostics per case and 256 per run; 16 prerequisites and 16 repairs per diagnostic; 256 artifacts; 64 MiB encoded or expanded per artifact; stored per artifact up to 64 MiB for Posix/Windows or 64 MiB plus 4 KiB for ContentStore; 64 MiB Smoke or 512 MiB Full encoded or expanded bundle total; 65 MiB Smoke or 513 MiB Full artifact-stored aggregate; and 73 MiB Smoke or 521 MiB Full whole-publication stored total; 1 MiB discarded overflow drain per child stream; and at most 64 modes, 256 extension diagnostics, 64 artifact roles, 64 root policies, 64 registered units, 64 digest domains, 64 extension schemas, and 64 executable descriptors per family. Every cap carries encoded, stored, expanded, logical, node, item, or byte units. Families may tighten but never widen a base ceiling. Validation checks counts and arithmetic before proportional allocation.

Command semantics are frozen with the catalogs. List has no family, mode, profile, budgets, or disposition. Check uses the sealed fixed preflight manifest and SelfTest uses the sealed fixed bounded internal manifest; neither accepts a caller family, mode, or profile selector, and both use LifecycleOnlyNoBundle. Run requires one explicit registered family mode and one explicit Smoke or Full profile; there is no default mode. Negative identifies one immutable negative case whose sealed manifest supplies family, mode, and profile. Replay identifies one immutable source manifest whose lineage supplies family, mode, and profile. Run, Negative, and Replay require DurableBundleRequired. Omitted, ambiguous, duplicated, or command-inapplicable selectors are Usage.

All closed catalog discriminants, registered namespace/domain/role/policy/unit/schema/descriptor IDs, case ordinals, and registry IDs use unsigned 16-bit wire codes unless a field is explicitly a 32-bit count or ordinal. Counts and ordinals are u32; encoded, stored, expanded, and byte-budget fields are u64; logical extents and logical-work quantities are u128. Rational is exactly an i128 numerator plus nonzero u128 denominator. Decimal is exactly an i128 coefficient plus i32 scale restricted to -6144 through 6144. UnitV2 uses a normalized i128/u128 scale and seven i16 exponents in the exact order length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity. OpaqueBytes is capped at 8192 bytes per value. Integer decimal renderings have at most 39 digits excluding a sign.

RunnerBudgetsV2 is owned here and has one frozen ordered schema: wall_time_ns, max_resident_bytes, max_child_processes, max_parallel_children, logical_work_limit, logical_work_unit, lifecycle_encoded_bytes, command_result_stdout_bytes, combined_child_stdout_bytes, combined_child_stderr_bytes, artifact_encoded_bytes, artifact_stored_bytes, artifact_expanded_bytes, system_publication_stored_bytes, publication_stored_bytes, stop_observation_ns, drain_ns, and finalize_ns. All are semantic invocation inputs. Wall, memory, and the three timeout fields plus command_result_stdout_bytes are nonzero; total children may be zero only for LifecycleOnlyNoBundle; parallel children never exceed total children; the checked sum of stop, drain, and finalize allowances does not exceed wall time; encoded, artifact-stored, expanded, system-publication-stored, and whole-publication-stored byte grants do not exceed RunnerLimitsV2; and logical work is an exact u128 paired with one LogicalUnitV2. Smoke admits at most 900 seconds, 16 GiB resident memory, 32 parallel and 256 total children. Full admits at most 86400 seconds, 128 GiB resident memory, 64 parallel and 256 total children. These are admission ceilings, not performance claims.

Additional literal RunnerLimitsV2 fields are exact: 256 map entries, 4096 generic array items, 32 path segments, 39 integer digits, 16 bytes per rational numerator or denominator, 16 bytes per decimal coefficient, absolute decimal scale 6144, 16 logical extents per artifact, 256 observation keys per case, 64 decision-detail namespaces, 64 output classes, 8192 opaque bytes per value, 65536 retained unknown-extension bytes per document, 512 expression edges, and 4096 memoized evaluation visits. The bundle-wide encoded-byte ceilings equal the expanded-byte ceilings: 64 MiB Smoke and 512 MiB Full. ContentStoreEnvelopeV1 has at most 4096 non-payload bytes per artifact, so the protocol-independent artifact-stored ceilings are exactly 65 MiB Smoke and 513 MiB Full for at most 256 artifacts; Posix/Windows still require stored_length == encoded_length, while ContentStore requires stored_length == encoded_length + the exact canonical envelope non-payload length. Checked sums use complete stored objects and refuse overflow before allocation. No downstream parser may invent or silently derive a different bound.

Family tightening is constrained by structural minima rather than an impossible universal zero rule. A sealed executable family requires at least one mode, one case, one executable descriptor, one comparison root, and one effect root; expression node caps are at least one and edge caps admit the declared roots. Per-case lifecycle capacity is at least two records for CaseStart and CaseTerminal. Run lifecycle capacity must satisfy checked feasibility 3 + sum over cases of 2 + declared maximum family rows for that case, covering RunStart, RunSummary, RunTerminal, and the fixed case records, and must not exceed 4096. Thus 256 cases may coexist with 256 records per case as independent ceilings only when their declared row maxima satisfy the exact run-total inequality; the maxima are not blindly multiplied. Zero remains legal only for genuinely optional extension, artifact, unknown-data, or family-row capacities. Validation rejects a jointly infeasible vector before allocation and reports every violated dimension.

ArtifactRoleV2 is a base catalog owned here: 1 Observation, 2 ComparisonDetail, 3 EffectDetail, 4 DiagnosticLog, 5 FamilyEvidence, 6 PerformanceEvidence, 7 ReplaySupport, and 8 RegisteredFamilyRole carrying a sealed u16 family role ID. LogicalExtentAxisV2 is also base data: 1 Payload, 2 Records, 3 Rows, 4 Elements, 5 Samples, 6 Iterations, 7 Operations, 8 Cycles, 9 Duration, and 10 RegisteredAxis.
