title: Independent Runner-to-rjoq handoff byte verifier
description:
Implement an isolated publish-false raw-byte verifier for the Runner-to-rjoq handoff. It must decode retained frames independently of the seam/coordinator/rjoq verdict implementation; recompute the three-field preinventory producer catalog, its unique ordinary registered inventory carrier, the frozen inventory-only BundleManifest, all three registered digest-preserving nominal associations, exact 26-field postpublication CandidateArtifactBinding, CandidateRef, and complete AdmissionRequest roots; and emit only a descriptive no-authority verification result with exhaustive mutation, import-isolation, replay, and detailed logging evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

The dedicated Acceptance Criteria field is the complete close gate. A production-decoder round trip, shared serializer, or happy-path root comparison is insufficient; raw full-frame independence and every named negative/test/logging requirement must pass.
design:
## Concrete isolated verifier

Create workspace member `crates/fs-evidence-runner-rjoq-verify`, package `fs-evidence-runner-rjoq-verify`, Rust 2024, `publish = false`, safe Rust by default, with `CONTRACT.md`, focused raw-frame decoder/replay modules, fixtures/tests, root workspace member entry, and Cargo.lock resolution. The CONTRACT freezes its descriptive-only authority, import isolation, exact domains/frames, bounded resources, cancellation/drain, determinism, and no-claim scope.

The verifier must not depend on or import `fs-evidence-runner-rjoq-seam`, the 24.5.2 coordinator, rjoq runtime/storage/checker/verdict/basis/decision/receipt code, Runner tracker/terminal/verdict code, or any production serializer/deserializer for the frames under test. It may depend only on admitted lower canonical byte/hash primitives and consume frozen schema descriptor/registry artifacts as data. Dependency, feature, symbol, and source-import scans enforce this boundary. It never calls an authority constructor.

The encoded external prerequisite `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.3.3` supplies the independently verified Runner inventory/manifest/publication input chain. This child depends on both 24.5.1 and 24.3.3; closure exact-set-verifies their current roots and blocks if either edge or root is absent.

## Independent raw-frame work

Starting from retained raw bytes plus schema descriptors, the verifier independently:

1. Parses canonical field tags, lengths, discriminants, bounded sets/maps, and full-frame termination.
2. Recomputes the premanifest RunnerProducerBindingCatalogV1 with exact three top-level fields, LogicalBundlePathV1 key, five-field value, producer derivation, canonical sort, and duplicate rejection.
3. Canonically encodes the catalog bytes, proves exactly one ordinary ArtifactInventoryEntryV2 matches the selected family's frozen fully namespaced role/schema/path registration, recomputes that carrier's stored/encoded/content layers, recomputes the separate candidate entry and ArtifactInventoryRootV2, and proves frozen BundleManifestV2 binds only the inventory root. It rejects any direct catalog field/type in BundleManifest.
4. Recomputes exact DestinationResourceBindingV1, planned pre-intent set, PublicationKey, self-root-free Intent, actual pre-seal durability, DurablePublicationIdentity, Seal/final publication, Presented/real PublishedBundleReceipt, and the registered same-digest BundleManifestRootV2-to-ProducerManifestRootV1 association.
5. Recomputes CandidateArtifactBindingV1's exact 26-field frame/root: field 3 equals the decoded carrier catalog root, field 13 is the whole inventory root, field 14 is the distinct selected candidate entry, and all catalog declaration/candidate byte-layer/receipt/no-claim cross-fields agree. It independently applies the registered ArtifactContentRootV2-to-CandidateBytesRootV1 and CandidateArtifactBindingRootV1-to-generic-ProducerBindingRootV1 same-digest nominal associations; no rehash, generic conversion, or RunnerProducerBindingV1 exists.
6. Recomputes the six-field AdmissionCandidateRefV1 frame/root and eight-field AdmissionRequestV1/Root with CandidateRef exactly once.
7. Cross-checks schema, family/case/role/LogicalBundlePath/source closure/claim scope/case manifest/inventory/BundleManifest/ProducerManifest/receipt/CandidateBytes/producer binding/budgets/no-claim/caller key/resolver/checker/capability across every layer.


It rejects missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, unknown, future, noncanonical, ambiguous, overflowed, trailing, mixed-run/source, and role-confused data. Equal payload bytes under different schema/family/case/role/LogicalBundlePath/source/claim/no-claim/budget/manifest principals move CandidateArtifactBinding and request identity or yield exact refusal.

## Descriptive output

`AdmissionHandoffVerificationV1`, domain `org.frankensim.fs-evidence-runner-rjoq-verify.verification.v1`, has exactly these ordered fields:

1. `verifier_api_generation: u16`
2. `verifier_wire_version: u16`
3. `runner_spec_root: RunnerSpecRootV2`
4. `publication_chain_root: RunnerPublicationChainRootV2`
5. `candidate_artifact_binding_root: CandidateArtifactBindingRootV1`
6. `producer_binding_catalog_root: RunnerProducerBindingCatalogRootV1`
7. `generic_producer_binding_root: ProducerBindingRootV1`
8. `admission_candidate_ref_root: AdmissionCandidateRefRootV1`
9. `admission_request_root: AdmissionRequestRootV1`
10. `verification_transcript_root: AdmissionHandoffVerificationTranscriptRootV1`
11. `input_source_closure_set_root: SourceClosureSetRoot`
12. `verifier_source_closure_root: SourceClosureRoot`
13. `no_claim_scope_root: NoClaimScopeRootV1`
14. `outcome: AdmissionHandoffVerificationOutcomeV1`


Outcome codes are 1 Verified and 2 Refused `{ validation_layer_code_u16, reason_code_u16, diagnostic_root }`. Verified means only byte/schema/association conformance; it cannot imply durability, policy eligibility, Admitted, Evidence, or Certified. Constructors are private to the independent parser after a complete exact-set check. The result has no From/TryFrom or authority conversion.

## Resource and stored-byte contract

All lengths/counts are parsed with checked arithmetic and explicit caps before allocation. The complete RunnerBudgetsRootV2 remains authoritative. Within its full upstream schema, the publication-accounting subsequence contains encoded, stored, and expanded artifact actuals before the two publication grants. The 4096-byte per-ContentStore-object nonpayload envelope cap, 64/512 MiB encoded/expanded bundle ceilings, 65/513 MiB stored ceilings, at most 256 artifacts, Posix/Windows stored==encoded, and ContentStore stored==encoded+exact envelope are independently replayed rather than trusted from logged totals.

ArtifactDispositionV2 code 1 is spelled only `LifecycleOnlyNoBundle`; `OutputlessLifecycle` is an invalid discriminant spelling. Canonical path vocabulary is `bundle_rel`; legacy `artifact_dir` aliases are rejected in any schema/CLI evidence consumed by the verifier.

## Complete publication-budget replay

The independent parser binds the complete RunnerBudgetsRootV2 and treats these as its exact publication-accounting subsequence `artifact_encoded_bytes`, `artifact_stored_bytes`, `artifact_expanded_bytes`, `system_publication_stored_bytes`, `publication_stored_bytes`. It distinguishes three actual artifact measures from two explicit grants, independently recomputes checked whole use as actual artifact-stored plus the system grant, enforces the 8 MiB system cap and 73/521 MiB whole caps in addition to 65/513 MiB artifact caps, and binds the full budget root into AdmissionRequest verification.

## Conformance and replay-source preservation

When verifying Runner lifecycle/source evidence, DiagnosticCodeV2 code 1 is exactly `case.conformance_mismatch`; `comparison.mismatch` is noncanonical. The independent verifier exercises comparison-only, effect-only, and dual-lane divergence. Replay verification preserves the exact source durable command, case manifests, claim modes, and expected comparison/effect frames. Only new Run cases are forced Match/Match; Replay of a source Negative retains its mismatch/error expectations and cannot be normalized into Run semantics.

## Closed lifecycle identity inputs

The handoff verifier independently checks that every CaseTerminal uses the closed `CaseTerminalBasisV2` algebra and that raw outcome presence/absence is controlled only by `CaseExecutionPhaseV2`; ad hoc optional-root combinations or state inference are noncanonical. It also recomputes one `RunOutcomeBasisRootV2` and requires both RunSummary and RunTerminal to bind that identical root. RunSummary contains no self-root, future-summary placeholder, or field later overwritten by RunTerminal.

## Lifecycle document exhaustion contract

The raw verifier decodes LifecycleDocumentV2 as exactly `record_count` plus that many ordered records. It accepts clean completion only from complete outer-frame exhaustion together with retained finalized-writer typestate evidence. No `clean_eof` field, sentinel, footer, or marker is serialized or trusted; a marker cannot bless truncation, trailing bytes, count disagreement, or a writer that never finalized.
## Acyclic producer/publication verification

The raw verifier enforces: preinventory catalog -> canonical catalog bytes as exactly one ordinary registered carrier entry -> ArtifactInventoryRootV2 over carrier plus candidate entries -> frozen BundleManifest inventory-only edge -> registered ProducerManifest association -> DestinationResourceBinding -> planned set excluding Intent/Seal -> PublicationKey including destination -> self-root-free Intent -> actual PreSealObjectSet/ProvenDurablePreSeal -> DurablePublicationIdentity binding destination and both set roots -> Seal/final receipt -> 26-field CandidateArtifactBinding proving unique carrier and separate candidate membership plus registered CandidateBytes association -> registered generic ProducerBinding association -> CandidateRef/request. The catalog has no inventory/destination/later root; BundleManifest has no phase-5 catalog field; same-resource new slots preserve roots; different resources move downstream roots; zero/duplicate carrier, wrong tuple/root/bytes, carrier/candidate confusion, raw locator/slot identity, generic conversion/rehash, feedback, wrong-set membership, and cycles fail.

## Complete budget-root binding

RunnerBudgetsV2 is not a five-field schema. This handoff binds and verifies the complete RunnerBudgetsRootV2, or the rjoq-registered AdmissionBudgetsRootV1 mapping to that complete root. Within the full upstream schema, the publication-accounting subsequence is exactly artifact_encoded_bytes, artifact_stored_bytes, artifact_expanded_bytes, system_publication_stored_bytes, publication_stored_bytes in that relative order. The last two are grants. Tests independently verify the complete root plus this subsequence, units, checked actual/grant equations, caps, identity, receipt, retry/recovery, logs, and replay; no unnamed upstream budget field may be omitted or defaulted.

## Capability-reference evidence and safe reproduction

When canonical argv evidence is present, the verifier accepts only `posix-fd:N`, `windows-handle-slot:N`, and `content-store-capability-slot:N`. `N` must be canonical unsigned decimal: no sign, separator, whitespace, or leading zero except `0`; Posix is capped at 2147483647 and Windows/ContentStore at 4294967295. It verifies that malformed or overflowed references were classified Usage before acquisition with empty stdout.

Numeric descriptor/slot values and payloads are nonsemantic, redacted, and absent from retained identity. The verifier checks a reproduction template containing exact semantic arguments, seed, and roots, fresh-capability placeholders, and backend-specific acquisition instructions; actual values or payloads fail verification.

## Independent outer-result, accounting, and delivery verification

The verifier hand-decodes `LifecycleOnlyCommandResultV2` as exactly ten ordered fields: `api_generation`, `wire_version`, `command`, `invocation_root`, `run_id`, `lifecycle_document`, `lifecycle_log_root`, `run_terminal_record_root`, `authority_scope_root`, and `no_claim_scope`. It hand-decodes `DurableCommandResultV2` as exactly twelve ordered fields: the same first eight, complete `published_bundle_receipt`, `published_bundle_receipt_root`, `authority_scope_root`, and `no_claim_scope`. Result roots are recomputed beside, never inside, their frames. No BundleManifestRoot or SealRoot is duplicated because the receipt binds them.

It independently decodes `PublicationAccountingV1` as exactly: `lifecycle_encoded_bytes: u64`, `artifact_encoded_bytes: u64`, `artifact_stored_bytes: u64`, `artifact_expanded_bytes: u64`, `system_publication_stored_bytes: u64`, `publication_stored_bytes: u64`, `artifact_object_count: u32`, `system_object_count: u16`, and `publication_object_count: u32`. `command_result_stdout_bytes` exists only as a complete RunnerBudgetsV2 grant. The verifier separately recomputes the pure semantic payload length, fixed six-field transport-header length, checked full-frame total, nominal payload root, and typed context root; requires post-receipt byte-for-byte payload plus payload-length/total/root/context equality; applies the grant to the total; and verifies a bounded non-authoritative CommandResultDeliveryObservationV1. It rejects any observed-length/delivery field in PublicationAccounting, PublishedBundleReceipt, either result frame, admission request/receipt, verification result, or an identity root.

## Independent schema-ownership DAG verification

RunnerSpecV2 is decoded as base/family-only with no ownership root. The verifier separately decodes the RunnerPhase1SchemaOwnershipRegistryV2 root from 24.1.3.2 and the append-only RunnerPhase2SchemaOwnershipManifestV2, RunnerPhase3SchemaOwnershipManifestV2, RunnerPhase4SchemaOwnershipManifestV2, and RunnerPhase5SchemaOwnershipManifestV2 roots in exact phase order, then proves unique schema/domain/encoder ownership and no earlier mutation/feedback. Its leaf-close fixtures verify phases 1-4 plus all currently declared phase-5 entries and prove a missing final phase-5 manifest cannot be reported Verified. In 24.5.3.2, the same release verifier is rerun after the final RunnerPhase5SchemaOwnershipManifestV2 is frozen; AdmissionHandoffVerificationTranscriptRootV1 then binds the complete ordered five-root join and the existing handoff-verification result/receipt field carries that proof without changing its 14-field schema.

## Clean-process no-mock E2E script

Implement source-closed Rust companion `verify-runner-rjoq-handoff-v1-driver` as the sole semantic/process driver for this artifact-only verifier, coordinated on POSIX by thin `scripts/ci/verify_runner_rjoq_handoff_v1.sh`; native Windows invokes the same companion directly without a shell wrapper. Its exact forms are `--check`, `--self-test`, and `--run FIXTURE_SET_MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF`. The command token is first; independent options occur once in any order and canonicalize to the shown order. The input root is read-only and uses the exact tagged/decimal capability grammar; the fixture-set path is one canonical logical relative path. Missing, extra, duplicate, conflicting, inapplicable, aliased, absolute, or noncanonical arguments are Usage before acquisition.

`--check` validates release binary/member/CONTRACT/dependency/import/schema-root wiring. `--self-test` runs hand-authored good/bad full frames and proves the forbidden-import tripwires themselves fail. `--run` launches only a clean release-built `fs-evidence-runner-rjoq-verify` process per retained fixture, with no Runner producer, seam, coordinator, rjoq runtime, or production Runner executable in the process or executable lookup path, then independently compares raw output/root/transcript to the fixture manifest. The artifact-only driver executes canonical retained-frame cases, every one-field mutation class, accounting/result/publication-DAG, lifecycle, read-only input capability, Replay/migration-lineage, schema-ownership, verifier cancellation/timeout, allocation/read fault, truncation/trailing, and complete verifier resource-return cases. Native Runner, publication-host, seam, rjoq-submission, signal, delivery, and outer-controller cells are preserved as immutable E2E contributions to `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.5.3.2`, which executes them through canonical owner `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.4.1.4`, driver `canonical-evidence-runner-v2-e2e-driver`, and `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh`; this leaf cannot report those contributed cells executed or passed.

Detailed deterministic logs record script/verifier source/build/CONTRACT/schema/fixture roots; canonical redacted argv; case ordinal/name; each decode/DAG/validation stage start/end; expected/observed/effects; byte/count/cap equations; allocation and resource high-water/return; first failure, cancellation/drain, repairs, result/transcript roots; exact category/pass/fail/skip counts; relative retained artifacts; and safe reproduction templates with fresh-capability acquisition instructions. They exclude live descriptors/slots, credentials, absolute locators, PIDs, wall clocks, scheduler noise, and raw bulk payloads. A case crash, missing terminal log, count mismatch, hidden skip, truncated log, or nonzero unclassified result fails the script.

## Independent destination-resource verification

The verifier hand-decodes `DestinationResourceBindingV1` under domain `org.frankensim.fs-evidence-runner.destination-resource-binding.v1` with exact ordered fields: root class; platform path profile; RootCapabilityPolicyRootV2; privacy-preserving stable ResourceIdentityRootV2; identity-provider policy root; freshness observation root; optional generation observation root; no-claim scope. It recomputes DestinationResourceBindingRootV1 beside the frame and follows it independently through PublicationKey, PublicationIntent, DurablePublicationIdentity, FinalCommit, PublishedBundleReceipt/recovery, CandidateArtifactBinding, generic producer binding, and request.

Same resource presented through a fresh descriptor/handle/slot must yield identical roots; different resources must differ from DestinationResourceBinding onward. Raw path, inode/file ID, slot/handle, credential, capability payload, provider secret, physical locator, and wall-clock freshness substitutes are rejected/redacted. Missing stable identity is Unsupported. Verification is durability-target conformance only, never scientific or admission authority.
## Generic-registration boundary, stable-token limit, and u128 refusals

The verifier consumes rjoq's generic ProducerBindingSchemaRegistrationV1 descriptor as data but all Runner-specific catalog/26-field/full-frame/nominal-association validation remains here and in the seam. rjoq.7.2.1 has no CandidateArtifactBinding, catalog, Runner fixture, or Phase1-5 dependency. title: Final no-mock Runner-to-rjoq admission journey, migration, recovery, and dual-chain replay
description:
Run the final release-built, no-mock Runner-to-rjoq admission-handoff journey across every command/profile/case/decision/resolver/publication/fault/recovery/migration cell; independently replay both durability chains; and invoke the sealed private AdmissionHandoffConformanceReceipt joiner over the frozen exact evidence without rerunning family mathematics or promoting candidate evidence.

This leaf integrates Runner migration only after the dedicated Runner migration/adoption prerequisites. It is the sole phase-5 leaf that consumes Runner migration observations. It preserves every negative and authority boundary and requires comprehensive unit, model, mutation, process-fault, CLI E2E, independent replay, receipt-oracle, and deterministic logging proof.

## Acceptance Criteria

The dedicated Acceptance Criteria field is the complete close gate. Happy-path admission, a Runner Pass, a production round trip, or a receipt root alone cannot close this leaf.
design:
## Concrete final harness and closure prerequisites

Implement the final harness in publish-false TOOL/dev surface `crates/fs-evidence-runner-rjoq-e2e` plus registered source-closed contributions to the `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh` integration solely owned by 24.4.1.4. The package is Rust 2024, safe Rust by default, has CONTRACT and focused fixtures/tests, and is a workspace member with explicit Cargo.lock/dependency evidence. Production crates cannot depend on it. It consumes the 24.5.1 seam, 24.5.2 coordinator, and 24.5.3.1 independent verification result; it cannot implement a second decoder, candidate schema, admission state machine, or receipt authority.

In-scope graph dependencies are 24.5.2 and 24.5.3.1. The graph now encodes exact external blockers on `frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.24.3.3`, `.24.4.2`, `.24.4.3`, `frankensim-ext-epic-gov-rjoq.7.2`, and `.7.2.1`; design and closeout exact-set-verify that every edge and current root is present before work. Runner migration is integrated here only after 24.4.2; coordinator 24.5.2 remains migration-free.

## Frozen complete CLI grammar

The six semantic command forms are presentation-independent. The POSIX shell route spells them as:

- `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh --list`
- `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh --check`
- `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh --self-test`
- `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh --run smoke|full --family-mode MODE --seed SEED_SELECTION --publication-protocol PROTOCOL --destination-mode DESTINATION_MODE --artifact-root ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF --bundle-rel BUNDLE_REL`
- `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh --negative CASE --publication-protocol PROTOCOL --destination-mode DESTINATION_MODE --artifact-root ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF --bundle-rel BUNDLE_REL`
- `scripts/ci/canonical_evidence_runner_v2.sh --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF --publication-protocol PROTOCOL --destination-mode DESTINATION_MODE --artifact-root ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF --bundle-rel BUNDLE_REL`

The command token is first. Independent options may appear once in any order, then canonicalize to the frozen order above before identity. Run has no default family mode; Negative/Replay derive immutable family/mode/profile data. `ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF` and `INPUT_ROOT_CAPABILITY_REF` accept only `posix-fd:N`, `windows-handle-slot:N`, or `content-store-capability-slot:N`. `N` is canonical unsigned decimal: no sign, separator, whitespace, or leading zero except `0`; Posix is capped at 2147483647 and Windows/ContentStore at 4294967295. Overflow, empty suffix, nondecimal text, and every noncanonical spelling are Usage before capability lookup with empty stdout. `--input-artifact-root` is exclusively a read-only source-bundle capability: it must satisfy the backend-specific read/enumerate/stable-snapshot policy and grants no create, replace, rename, delete, publication, or destination-commit role. `--artifact-root` is exclusively the output destination capability: it must satisfy the destination admission/identity/freshness and no-replace create/sync/commit policy and grants no source-bundle decode/read role. The same underlying capability cannot fill both roles in one invocation. Swapped references, wrong-kind slots, insufficient or excessive rights, same-resource dual-role aliasing, revoked/stale handles, or role-policy mismatch refuse before source payload read, output mutation, or stdout. Logs retain only the semantic role and rights-policy root; diagnostics redact numeric refs/payloads and rank acquisition of a fresh read-only source capability or a distinct fresh destination capability as appropriate. Backend-neutral role separation otherwise follows the Runner owner contract. Missing/extra/duplicate/conflicting/inapplicable options, omitted mode/protocol/destination, generic `--mode`/`--profile`, `--artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL`, and every alias are Usage with empty stdout. `--bundle-rel BUNDLE_REL` is the only durable logical-bundle option. Numeric capability refs and slot payloads are nonsemantic, redacted acquisition data and never enter identity.

ArtifactDispositionV2 code 1 is exactly `LifecycleOnlyNoBundle`; `OutputlessLifecycle` is rejected rather than accepted as an alias. Code 2 remains `DurableBundleRequired`.

## Verifiable durable command-result delivery

Durable Run/Negative/Replay freeze the complete bounded lifecycle, verify or recover the exact published bundle, and freeze one canonical twelve-field DurableCommandResultV2 plus its nominal root before starting result transport. The semantic result is complete before delivery, but no physical atomic-write claim is made for a frame larger than an operating-system atomic-write bound.

The PublishedBundleReceipt is a complete field of DurableCommandResultV2 but is not, and cannot be encoded as, a lifecycle record. DurableCommandResultRoot is computed beside the canonical frame and never serialized inside it. BundleManifestRoot and SealRoot are not duplicated because the receipt already binds them. Lost-return recovery first recovers and revalidates the exact receipt and semantic result/root; an authorized retry may re-emit the same complete semantic result but may never stitch prefixes.

24.2.1.3's bounded non-authoritative CommandResultTransportFrameV1 has the exact ordered header api_generation, wire_version, closed frame_kind, payload_encoded_length, frame-kind-selected nominal payload_root, and typed CommandResultTransportContextRootV1, followed immediately by exactly that many canonical payload bytes. It has no serialized completion field or frame self-root. A consumer accepts no lifecycle, receipt, or authority until it receives one complete frame, exact payload length, checked full-frame total, clean exhaustion, a matching independently recomputed nominal payload root, and a matching independently recomputed typed CommandResultTransportContextRootV1. Short write, broken pipe, process death, missing/trailing bytes, concatenation, root mismatch, or a valid prefix is detectably invalid transport with zero result authority. Failures before transport starts leave stdout empty; delivery faults may leave a detectable prefix that remains non-authoritative and use the frozen outer InternalError exit without rewriting lifecycle state. Stderr contains the one bounded redacted diagnostic allowed by the owning failure stage. A semantic durable Pass is impossible without both the matching published receipt and complete accepted transport.

## Final real authority journey

For downstream Runner fixture `rjoq.runner-handoff.exact-bytes-root.v1`, the journey constructs the three-field catalog before inventory; encodes it as exactly one ordinary catalog-carrier entry under the vertical-product family's frozen fully namespaced role/schema/path registration; computes ArtifactInventoryRootV2 over carrier plus separate candidate entries; proves frozen BundleManifestV2 binds only that inventory root; and verifies the registered same-digest manifest association plus DestinationResourceBinding/planned/key/Intent/pre-seal/DurablePublicationIdentity/Seal/final-receipt chain. It requires the independent 24.5.3.1 result to confirm all 26 CandidateArtifactBinding fields, unique carrier, separate candidate membership, registered content association, and registered generic binding association; the harness does not implement a second decoder. It then constructs CandidateRef/request, validates the live resolver, and submits to real rjoq. One opaque AdmissionReceipt is accepted only after independent equality of request, basis/transcript, producer/resource binding, budgets, no-claim, caller key, scope, durable commit, and final Admitted decision.

Every Refused code 1-15 plus NoData, Stale, EnvironmentInvalid, Blocked, Unsupported, cancellation, timeout, publication-preflight refusal, expected/observed mismatch, and fault path mints no admission receipt. Runner Pass on a Negative case means conformance only. Postcommit lost-return recovery queries solely by AdmissionRequestRoot and succeeds even after resolver expiry/revocation/removal; precommit recovery still requires a current resolver.

Runner publication durability and rjoq admission durability are independently replayed and never conflated. The final journey covers every supported Posix, Windows, and ContentStore protocol/path/destination-mode cell and explicit unsupported cells; Smoke/Full; all family modes/adopted family source closures; separate-root Replay; deterministic races; controlled stops/drains; coordinator/rjoq process crashes; stale/mixed/substituted inputs; and current plus registered migration cases.

Migration begins only after the exact 24.4.2 Runner MigrationObservationV2/registry roots are present. InvocationBasisV2 binds optional ReplayLineageRootV2 exactly for Replay and contains no direct MigrationExecutionBasisRootV2; ReplayLineageV2 contains the current MigrationExecutionBasisRootV2 exactly once. The journey verifies integrity-first classification, current wire V1 no-adapter absence, retained originals, transformed bytes, selected adapter and policy/capability/budget/scope joins, monotone authority, idempotent reapplication, rollback, and independent replay. It never migrates inside 24.5.2, duplicates a migration basis, or widens a receipt.

## Consumed private handoff conformance receipt

24.5.3.3 solely owns the AdmissionHandoffConformanceReceiptV1 declaration, private encoder/joiner, descriptor/root, SeamConformanceOnly scope, independent full-frame oracle, and receipt-focused source closure. This journey owns none of those constructors. After freezing the journey outputs, final RunnerPhase5SchemaOwnershipManifestV2, and rerun 24.5.3.1 verification result, it invokes the sealed verify_exact_join operation with complete typed frames/tokens, obtains the one final descriptive receipt instance, and compares it with the independent oracle result retained beside—not inside—the receipt. The exact consumed `AdmissionHandoffConformanceReceiptV1` has literal domain `org.frankensim.fs-evidence-runner.admission-handoff-conformance-receipt.v1`, API generation 1, wire version 1, private fields, no Default/public literal, and exactly these ordered fields:

description:
Revalidate the historical Foundations P0-P6 milestone evidence against one current compatible source and constellation snapshot without rewriting or reopening coherent closed history. Own tests/foundations/manifests/p0-p6-revalidation.toml and scripts/e2e/foundations/revalidate_p0_p6.sh. Enumerate every historical milestone and its exact source, contract, test, artifact, machine, theorem, and authority roots; replay what remains reproducible; classify each exact row as Current, Stale, Refuted, Blocked, Unsupported, NoData, or HistoricalOnly; and create explicit successor ownership for any live gap. Never infer current proof from closure date or aggregate pass counts.

The driver supports --list, --check, --self-test, --run smoke|full, --negative CASE, and artifact-only --replay. It uses release-built real paths, deterministic fixtures, positive and hostile negative twins, evidence severing, input perturbation, cancellation/fault/drain, tamper, missing-source, stale-schema, and mixed-snapshot tests. Bounded JSONL follows the V.3 contract, including exact milestone and receipt IDs, first divergence, authority/no-claim, relative artifacts, ranked repairs, and reproduction. Admission declares maximum milestones/cases, subprocesses, work, memory, deadline, retained bytes, and log output; limits may only tighten per run. Cancellation, signals, allocation/process faults, output truncation, and interrupted publication must drain all children, leave no temporary-state or lock leak, preserve a restartable attempt receipt, and never publish a partially Current milestone. Repeated execution from clean state is deterministic within the declared same-ISA and cross-ISA policy.

title: fs-qty: const-generic dimensional analysis (Qty) + runtime QtyAny + unit parsing
description:
## What
Compile-time dimensional analysis: the const-generic quantity type `Qty<const M:i8, const KG:i8, const S:i8, const K:i8, const A:i8>(f64)` and its ecosystem (plan §11.5, Appendix B). This is the Five Explicits' "units" pillar — a pressure cannot be added to a stress IN THE TYPE SYSTEM.

## Scope
- Core `Qty` type with add/sub (same dims or compile error), mul/div (dimension arithmetic via const generics), powers/roots where representable, comparisons.
- Type aliases for the working set: Length, Area, Volume, Time, Velocity, Acceleration, Mass, Force, Stress/Pressure (Pa = kg·m⁻¹·s⁻²), Energy, Power, Density, Viscosity (dynamic + kinematic), SurfaceTension, Temperature, ThermalConductivity, angular quantities.
- Vectors/fields of quantities: `QtyVec3`, dimensioned array views compatible with FrankenNumpy interop (dimension carried in the type, storage stays raw f64/f32).
- Runtime-checked `QtyAny` (dimension vector as data) for IR values, data files, and FFI-free serialization — compile-time Qty can't cover runtime-loaded data (plan G3 notes unit-rescaling must ALSO be tested through runtime paths).
- Parsing/formatting for SI + engineering units ("0.12Pa*s", "546GB/s", "65deg", "0.5L/s") — the exact literal syntax FrankenScript uses.
- Angle handling (rad/deg), affine temperature (K vs °C offset) handled explicitly to avoid classic footguns.

## Why
Unit errors die at admission, not at hour six. The IR checker (fs-ir-admission) extends this into every study; fs-scenario, fs-material, fs-regime all build on it. Keep it dependency-light: L0-adjacent utility crate usable by everything.

## Acceptance criteria
- Dimension mismatches fail to compile (compile-fail test suite, trybuild-style, in-house).
- QtyAny round-trips through JSON preserving dimension + value; parser accepts the plan's Appendix C literals.

## Testing
Property tests: dimension arithmetic laws (mul commutes, div inverts), parse/format round-trips, runtime/compile-time agreement. Compile-fail battery for illegal ops. Detailed log of every parsed unit expression in test output.
close_reason: Implemented and verified. Qty<M,KG,S,K,A> const-generic type with full dimension algebra (Mul/Div via generic_const_exprs — compiles clean on pinned nightly; fallback documented), 23 SI aliases, units:: constructors (incl. affine celsius, degrees->rad); Dims with SATURATING arithmetic; QtyAny with checked try_add/try_sub + teaching DimensionMismatch errors + to_typed downcasts; parse_qty covering the full Appendix C literal grammar (Pa*s, L/s, deg, m2/s3, ^-1 exponents, prefixes, %, degC-affine-lone-only, GiB refusal w/ fs-ir pointer); in-house bit-exact JSON round-trip (P1: no serde). Tests: 29 unit (incl. 20k-case garbage battery WHICH FOUND AND FIXED a real i8-overflow panic on adversarial 200-deep unit chains — now saturating + ±60 semantic cap), 5-case conformance suite w/ JSON-lines verdicts, compile-fail doctests. Full CONTRACT.md (all 10 sections, honest no-claims: mol/cd, information units, dimensioned roots, unit reconstruction). Workspace: 63 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, policy checks green. Verified on aarch64-apple; x86-64 verification lands with CI bead.

title: CI/CD: both-ISA matrix, Gauntlet tiers, merge gates (gradient/order/determinism/perf)
description:
## What
CI/CD infrastructure that makes the Gauntlet and performance program enforceable: both-ISA runners, tiered nightly jobs, and the merge gates the plan treats as law.

## Scope
- Runner matrix: macOS/aarch64 (Apple Silicon) + Linux/x86-64 (AVX-512-capable). Every Gauntlet tier and conformance suite runs on BOTH — "done" is defined as conformance green on both ISAs, nothing else (plan §13.3).
- PR gates: build/clippy/fmt, unit + G0 property suites, layer-dependency check, constellation policy gate, unsafe-capsule registry check.
- Merge-blocking specialty gates (wired as the relevant crates land): gradient verification (a solver without a passing adjoint-vs-dual/FD check CANNOT merge, §8.7); G1 convergence-order slope gate (fail if deviation >0.2 from theory); determinism audit (bit-identical re-run of a seeded suite).
- Nightly: full Gauntlet tiers G0–G5, roofline perf runs (see perf-regression-ci bead) with results written to the ledger, cross-ISA divergence report regeneration.
- Golden-ledger convention: every merged feature lands with a replayable ledger of its acceptance run (§16.2); CI stores and can replay them.
- Artifact retention for failure forensics: structured logs, event streams, flame-graph reconstructions.

## Why
The Gauntlet is the definition of done; phase gates are Gauntlet states, not dates (§16.1). CI is where that stops being aspiration. Performance regressions are test failures exactly like wrong answers (§14.4).

## Acceptance criteria
Matrix runs green on skeleton workspace; a seeded failing property test, a seeded slope violation, and a seeded perf regression each demonstrably block (test the gates themselves); nightly writes to a ledger file retained as an artifact.

## Testing
Meta-tests for each gate (inject failure, assert red). Log format: per-gate verdicts as structured JSON lines so agents can parse CI outcomes without scraping.

## Addendum: the Decalogue as machine-checkable policy (patch Rev 25)
Each principle maps to a mechanical gate where possible, and this bead owns the mapping doc + wiring: P1 (pure Rust, Franken-only) = dependency-policy gate + unsafe-capsule registry lint; P2 (determinism) = G5 audit gate; P3 (differentiable-or-certifiable) = gradient-check merge gate + certificate-availability lint on operator registration; P4 (budgets) = Five-Explicits lint on ledger ops; P6 (roofline-honest) = perf-regression bands + intensity-metadata requirement; P7 (cancellation) = G4 storm gate; P9 (provenance) = golden-ledger replay gate; P10 (agent-first) = catalog no-drift gate + structured-error schema validation. Principles that resist full mechanization (P5 structure preservation, P8 one data model) get review-checklist status with their G0 law suites (exact-sequence, conservation) as partial gates.

Delivered: .github/workflows/ci.yml (both-ISA matrix macos-14/aarch64 + ubuntu-24.04/x86-64: fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests with retained JSONL verdicts, xtask policy gates, constellation drift gate; per-ref serialized concurrency tuned for a main that moves every few minutes), nightly.yml (dev+release full suites + run recorded into a retained fs-ledger database via new conformance-tested nightly_ledger bin — golden-ledger convention), ci-self-test.yml (gate meta-tests), scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh (materializes all 7 constellation siblings at exact constellation.lock pins, shallow by SHA; verified all pins publicly fetchable), docs/CI_GATES.md (Decalogue->gate mapping with honest live/partial/deferred status per principle). PROVEN: full Linux lane green end-to-end (run 28816513544); macOS lane green through clippy on same run; ci-self-test run 28819512675 GREEN = injected failing test, injected fmt violation, and seeded policy violations each demonstrably block. The matrix immediately caught 2 real cross-ISA bugs invisible to local aarch64 dev (fs-simd unused x86 intrinsic imports; chunks_exact lint on CI's newer nightly) — both fixed. Deferred per the bead's own 'wired as crates land' scoping, documented in CI_GATES.md: gradient-check merge gate (needs fs-ad adjoint infra + first solver), G1 slope gate, perf-regression bands + AVX-512-guaranteed lane (need reference-machine self-hosted runners), G5 determinism audit, golden-ledger replay gate. Known conditions: floating nightly channel causes CI/local clippy drift (tracked frankensim-go7a); main goes fmt-red transiently when agents' unformatted intermediate snapshots are swept — the gate is correct, owners see red and land formatted. title: Contract & conformance infrastructure: CONTRACT.md lint + shared conformance harness
description:
## What
The per-crate contract + conformance discipline, as executable infrastructure (plan §13.3): CONTRACT.md as the inter-agent integration language, plus the shared conformance-test harness crates use.

## Scope
- CONTRACT.md required sections (machine-lintable): purpose & layer; public types & semantics; invariants; error model; determinism class (Deterministic / DeterministicPerIsa / Fast); cancellation behavior; unsafe boundary; feature flags; conformance tests; no-claim boundaries.
- A lint tool (`fs-contract-lint` or xtask) verifying every published crate has a complete CONTRACT.md and that its declared conformance suite exists and runs; wired into CI.
- Conformance harness v0: a shared test framework where each crate registers named conformance cases with structured JSON output (case id, inputs digest, tolerances, verdict, evidence pointers). Any reimplementation of a crate must pass its predecessor's suite.
- Upgrade path note: once fs-ir-core lands, conformance suites gain an IR-speaking front end so they double as the integration language between agents building the system — an agent implementing fs-fft never negotiates with the agent implementing fs-lbm; both negotiate with the contract (§13.3). Design the v0 case format so IR wrapping is additive, not a rewrite.

title: Unsafe-capsule safety cases: SAFETY.md, registry, Miri/fuzz/model-check gates, panic policy
description:
## What
Formal safety cases for every `unsafe` capsule (patch Rev P). "Audited unsafe leaf modules" (Decalogue P1) needs a mechanical shape, or it degrades into informal trust blobs.

## Scope
- Policy: unsafe permitted ONLY in registered leaf modules, each <300 lines, each with a safe façade, each in the registry. Candidate zones: SIMD microkernels, arena internals, memory mapping, arch dispatch, exact low-level layout.
- Per-capsule `SAFETY.md` covering: invariants; aliasing assumptions; alignment assumptions; lifetime assumptions; panic behavior; cancellation behavior; concurrency behavior; Miri coverage; model-checking coverage; fuzz/property coverage; proof obligations discharged by callers.
- Capsule registry: source-of-truth manifest (later mirrored to the ledger `unsafe_capsules` table — see fs-ledger-core) with crate, module, LOC, invariants, last-audit timestamp + hash. CI fails if unsafe exists outside the registry, if LOC exceeds cap, or if SAFETY.md is stale relative to code hash.
- Panic-and-cancellation policy DECISION (the patch demands we choose explicitly): adopt "panic captured inside tile scope, converted to a structured diagnostic before crossing layers" (plan §5.2 failure containment: a panicking tile poisons its scope, siblings cancelled, structured error propagates with tile provenance, never a process abort mid-campaign). Document why over panic=abort: campaign survivability.
- CI lanes: Miri on capsule tests; fuzz targets for each capsule's safe façade; model-checking hooks for concurrency capsules (integrates with gauntlet-g4-harness).

## Acceptance criteria
Registry + lint live in CI; a seeded unregistered `unsafe` block fails the build; one exemplar capsule (e.g., an aligned-arena primitive) ships the full SAFETY.md + Miri + fuzz evidence as the template.

## Testing
Meta-tests for the registry lint. Exemplar capsule: Miri-clean, fuzz corpus checked in, property tests on the safe façade with logs recording invariant checks.

title: PV vertical skeleton: 2D SDF -> PDE -> objective -> adjoint check -> optimize -> replay
description:
## What
Phase PV — the vertical skeleton (patch Rev R): a deliberately tiny end-to-end slice proving the typed-value semantics BEFORE building the full substrate. One study: 2D SDF region → scalar PDE solve (Poisson/plane-stress elasticity) → objective → gradient check → a few optimization iterations → ledger replay → deterministic rerun → text report.

## Why this exists (and why FIRST)
The original P0 was overloaded (executor + allocators + dense/sparse/FFT/intervals/RNG/ledger + perf targets in six weeks). The first thing FrankenSim must prove is NOT GEMM speed — it is that its values really carry geometry, physics, gradients, budgets, provenance, and cancellation end-to-end. Performance then compounds on a working semantic skeleton. This slice de-risks the central bet (the typed continuum) at minimum cost, and its seed components become the real crates' embryos.

## Scope (all "toy but true" — real semantics, minimal performance)
- Mini fs-ir: an s-expression study format with seeds/budgets/units (using qty-units) — hand-rolled parser acceptable.
- Mini fs-ledger: ops + artifacts + edges tables in FrankenSQLite; content-hash artifacts; replay = re-execute ops and compare hashes.
- Mini fs-exec: asupersync scopes + a simple deterministic parallel-for with fixed-shape reduction; cancellation poll points.
- Mini geometry: 2D SDF grid chart for a parametric shape (e.g., plate with parametric hole).
- Mini physics: scalar Poisson or plane-stress on a regular grid (finite differences or P1 elements), CG solver.
- Mini fs-opdsl seed: define the residual ONCE, generate/derive both primal apply and adjoint apply from it (even if by simple symmetry) — establishing the "one source of truth for primal/adjoint" pattern early (patch Rev C).
- Objective (e.g., compliance), hand adjoint gradient, verified against central differences to tolerance.
- Tiny optimizer: 5–10 gradient-descent steps on 1–4 shape parameters.
- Text report: objective trace, gradient-check table, budget accounting, replay verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria (this IS milestone-pv)
One command runs the study twice: identical artifact hashes both times (determinism), replay from ledger matches, gradient check passes, report generated. Total code small enough for one agent to hold in context.

## Testing
The slice IS a test. Additionally: cancellation mid-solve leaves a consistent ledger; corrupting a ledger row makes replay fail loudly; gradient-check failure path produces a structured, actionable error. Verbose structured logging throughout — this doubles as the logging-style exemplar for the whole project.
close_reason: Implemented and verified — ALL PV exit criteria pass as executable tests (pv-001..pv-005): (1) deterministic rerun -> identical artifact hashes + byte-identical reports; (2) ledger replay reproduces bit-for-bit (fsqlite ops/artifacts/edges, FNV content addressing as documented BLAKE3 placeholder); (3) corrupted artifact -> LedgerCorruption refusal, loud; (4) adjoint gradient (derived from ONE EdgeLaw with the primal — the opdsl one-source-of-truth seed) matches central differences at 1e-8..1e-7 rel err, gated <1e-4 every optimizer step; (5) missing budget -> 'budgets are mandatory (P4)', exhausted budget -> BudgetExhausted with fixes. Demo study: 33x33 plate-with-hole, J 9.97e-2 -> 8.51e-2 over 3 projected-GD steps, 1096 CG iters of 2M budget, replay OK. Also: total s-expr parser (garbage-battery), fs-qty literal path rejects dimensioned radius with teaching error, smooth-Heaviside SDF density (R-function doctrine in 1-param form), fixed-chunk deterministic parallel map with row-granularity cancellation polls (drains cleanly, tested), Poisson series-reference check (peak 0.0736713), fs-obs events throughout. CLI: fs-vskeleton run/replay. 12 tests, clippy clean, CONTRACT.md complete with honest substitution notes (asupersync scopes -> fs-exec bead; BLAKE3 -> fs-ledger bead).

title: The Gauntlet: tiered correctness program (G0-G5 + certifier trials)
description:
## Mission
The Gauntlet: FrankenSim's permanent, tiered correctness program (plan §13). A system that sells CERTIFIED error had better be paranoid about its own. Nothing tagged [F] or [M] ships to the default path without passing every tier below it, on both target ISAs, nightly.

## The six tiers
- G0 — Properties and laws: in-house property-based testing (proptest-class shrinking) of algebraic laws — chart-conversion functor round-trips within certified bounds, adjoint consistency ⟨Av,w⟩=⟨v,Aᵀw⟩ to roundoff, GA identities, exact-sequence identities (δδ=0 BITWISE), conservation checks, interval containment under rewrites.
- G1 — Manufactured solutions: every PDE frontend × element family × BC type carries an MMS battery; CI fits observed convergence order and FAILS THE BUILD if slope deviates from theory by >0.2. The tier that catches the quiet death of accuracy.
- G2 — Canonical benchmarks: Cook's membrane, lid-driven cavity Re1000 (Ghia), Taylor–Green, cylinder Cd/Strouhal Re100, NAFEMS shells/locking, plate buckling, NACA 0012 polars, El Centro fiber-frame — acceptance envelopes in repo, results in ledger.
- G3 — Metamorphic: frame invariance, unit-rescaling invariance through runtime paths, estimator monotonicity under refinement, adjoint-vs-FD along random directions, Rep-Router path independence.
- G4 — Chaos and cancellation storms: kill random scopes during real solves; assert zero leaks, no deadlocks, ledger consistency, pause-resume reproduces uninterrupted trajectories in deterministic mode; model-check the executor's core protocols. P7 is a claim; G4 is the proof engine.
- G5 — Determinism audits: bit-identical across runs/thread-counts per ISA; cross-ISA divergence report classifying every difference (FMA contraction, libm ULP, reduction shape) with documented envelopes.

## Certifying the certifiers (§13.2)
Interval/Taylor enclosures vs high-precision oracle; e-process validity under ADVERSARIAL stopping; conformal coverage under distribution shift; sheaf watertightness vs brute-force ray parity. A fooled certificate is a Sev-0 bug — a wrong answer wearing a badge.

## Members
gauntlet-g0-harness, gauntlet-g1-harness, gauntlet-g2-harness, gauntlet-g3-harness, gauntlet-g4-harness, gauntlet-g5-harness, certify-certifiers.

## Success Criteria
All harnesses run nightly on both ISAs; every phase gate (milestone beads) is defined as a Gauntlet state, not a date.

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The Gauntlet gains the addendum's epistemic + flywheel gates:
- **Laundering tests** (Proposal 3, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.1): adversarial pipelines that try to upgrade estimated→verified MUST fail the type check.
- **No-falsifier-no-ship gate** (Proposal 6, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.4): a certificate class without a registered falsifier fails review the way untested code fails CI; falsifier-yield per class is tracked (every falsifier must pay rent).
- **Contract-composition soundness** (Proposal E, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.14): a composed system claim must never be tighter than its weakest member's certificate permits.
- **Degraded-gap refusal suite** (Proposal 5, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.3): deliberately ill-conditioned assemblies where the harmonic/coboundary triage must REFUSE confidence rather than misclassify — the refusal IS the pass condition.
- **Proposer accept-rate benchmark** (Proposal 9, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.3): standing benchmark of accept-rate + end-to-end speedup per physics kernel per regime (also risk R1's early warning).
- **Determinism as a certified contract** (Proposal 2, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.6): bitwise reproducibility across runs AND worker counts as Gauntlet tests (risk R2).
- **Certifying the certifiers extended**: the equilibrated a-posteriori bound (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.1) and the incremental-skip soundness check (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.7) are Sev-0 targets — a fooled bound or an unsound skip is a wrong answer wearing a badge.

title: G0 harness: in-house property-based testing + algebraic law suites
description:
## What
G0 harness: the in-house property-based testing framework (proptest-class generators + shrinking, pure Rust, no external dep) plus the algebraic-law suite conventions every crate uses (plan §13.1).

## Scope
- Generator combinators for the domain's types: floats with controlled distributions (subnormals, signed zeros, near-overflow), dimensioned quantities, small matrices/tensors, meshes/complexes (delegated builders), intervals, RNG streams.
- Shrinking that preserves invariants (e.g., shrink a mesh while staying manifold).
- Law-suite registry: named laws with structured JSON results (law id, seed, shrunk counterexample, evidence). Canonical laws the plan demands: chart-conversion functor round-trips within certified bounds; adjoint consistency ⟨Av,w⟩=⟨v,Aᵀw⟩ to roundoff for every operator with an adjoint; GA identities; exact-sequence identities (δδ=0, div∘curl=0 BITWISE on discrete cochains); conservation checks (mass in free-surface LBM, energy-drift bounds for symplectic integrators); interval containment under random expression rewrites.
- Deterministic replay: every failure records the Philox seed + case index; `--replay <seed>` reproduces exactly.
- CI integration: per-crate law suites discovered and run in the PR gate; nightly widens case counts.

## Why in-house
P1 (Franken-only deps) forbids proptest/quickcheck at runtime paths; and our generators must speak our types (Qty, charts, cochains) natively. The harness is also reused by G3 (metamorphic) and fuzz-adjacent capsule tests.

## Acceptance criteria
Framework crate green on both ISAs; demo law suite (float algebra + a seeded failing law) shows shrinking + replay; docs show an agent how to register laws in a new crate.

## Testing
Self-tests: shrinking terminates and minimizes known counterexamples; replay determinism (same seed → same cases, both ISAs); logging includes per-law case counts, durations, seeds.

title: G1 harness: manufactured solutions + convergence-order slope gate (0.2 tolerance)
description:
## What
G1 harness: manufactured solutions (MMS) and convergence-order verification framework — the tier that catches the quiet death of accuracy (plan §13.1).

## Scope
- MMS machinery: given a symbolic/closed-form exact solution u*, generate forcing terms and BC data so the PDE's exact solution is u*; run the discretization across a refinement ladder (h- and p-refinement); compute error norms (L2, H1, energy, and goal functionals).
- Order fitting: least-squares slope of log(error) vs log(h); THE GATE: build fails if observed order deviates from theoretical order by more than 0.2. Same treatment for ADJOINT convergence order (dual consistency is verified, not assumed).
- Battery matrix: every PDE frontend × element family × BC type carries an MMS battery (body-fitted FEEC, CutFEM-on-SDF with cut configurations deliberately including sliver cuts, IGA patches incl. multi-patch mortar seams). The matrix is declared in data so coverage gaps are visible and lintable.
- Integration with fs-opdsl (once it lands): operator definitions expose MMS hooks automatically — manufactured solutions generated from the same source of truth as the residual, eliminating hand-derived forcing-term bugs.
- Results ledgered: order fits, envelopes, and refinement tables stored with machine fingerprint for trend analysis.

## Why
Accuracy regressions rarely announce themselves; they show up as a 1.7 slope where theory says 2.0. Making the slope a merge gate is the plan's chosen defense (§13.1, CI bead wires the gate).

## Acceptance criteria
Framework runs a reference battery (e.g., Poisson P1/P2 on simplices once fs-feec lands; before that, the PV skeleton's scalar solver) and demonstrably fails on a seeded under-integration bug.

## Testing
Self-test with an intentionally wrong quadrature order → slope gate must trip. Structured logs: per-case h, error norms, fitted slope, theoretical order, verdict.

title: G2 harness: canonical benchmark registry (Ghia cavity, TGV, cylinder, NAFEMS, NACA0012, El Centro)
description:
## What
G2 harness: the canonical-benchmark registry with acceptance envelopes in the repo and results in the ledger (plan §13.1).

## Scope
- Benchmark registry format: each benchmark = declarative spec (geometry/scenario/discretization ladder/quantities of interest) + acceptance envelope (reference values with tolerances + provenance of the reference: paper citation, dataset) + honesty labels (e.g., LES resolution class for aero cases).
- The canonical set (each becomes a registered case as its physics lands): Cook's membrane (elasticity); lid-driven cavity Re 1000 vs Ghia et al. centerline profiles; Taylor–Green vortex decay (energy dissipation curve); circular cylinder Cd/Strouhal at Re 100; NAFEMS shell and locking tests; plate buckling loads; NACA 0012 polars vs experiment (with LES honesty labels); El Centro-class RC frame time-history vs published fiber-model results.
- Runner: executes benchmarks nightly, writes QoIs + envelope verdicts to the ledger, produces trend dashboards (FrankenPandas) and diffs vs previous runs.
- Envelope discipline: envelopes are versioned in-repo; changing one requires a semantic justification note (golden-evidence policy from AGENTS.md).

## Why
MMS proves order; canonical benchmarks prove PHYSICS — they catch modeling and coupling errors that manufactured solutions structurally cannot (wrong convection sign still converges beautifully to the wrong answer).

## Acceptance criteria
Registry + runner operational with at least the PV-era scalar case wired; envelope-violation demonstrably fails CI; ledger rows carry benchmark id, QoIs, envelope verdicts, machine fingerprint, versions.

## Testing
Meta-test: seeded QoI perturbation trips the envelope. Logs: per-benchmark QoI table with reference, computed, tolerance, margin.

title: G3 harness: metamorphic testing (frame/unit invariance, monotonicity, path independence)
description:
## What
G3 harness: metamorphic testing framework — verifying input-output RELATIONS when exact oracles don't exist (plan §13.1).

## Scope — the canonical metamorphic relations
- Frame invariance: rigidly transform every input (geometry, BCs, loads via fs-scenario frames); outputs must be invariant/equivariant to tolerance.
- Unit-rescaling invariance THROUGH RUNTIME PATHS: rescale all runtime data (compile-time Qty can't cover data files); dimensionless outputs must be identical, dimensioned outputs must scale exactly.
- Estimator monotonicity under refinement: error estimators must not increase under uniform refinement (statistically, with declared exceptions).
- Adjoint-vs-finite-difference agreement along random directions at randomized points (complements the per-solver gradient gate).
- Rep-Router path independence: ANY admissible conversion path between charts must land within the composed certificate of the direct path.
- Regime-scaling coherence (added, patch Rev A): solutions of nondimensionalized and dimensional formulations must map onto each other through the declared scaling.
- Framework: relation registry over the G0 generator infrastructure; each relation declares its transform generator, tolerance model (tied to certificates where available), and applicability predicates.

## Why
Most of FrankenSim's deepest bugs (sign errors in adjoints, silent unit assumptions, router edges with optimistic error models) are exactly the class metamorphic testing catches. Certificates give us principled tolerances instead of hand-waved epsilons — a rare luxury.

## Acceptance criteria
Framework + at least frame-invariance and unit-rescaling relations wired against PV-skeleton physics; seeded violation (e.g., a hardcoded meter assumption) demonstrably caught.

## Testing
Self-tests per relation with known violators. Logs: relation id, transform parameters, both outputs, tolerance, margin, verdict.

title: G4 harness: chaos/cancellation storms, fault injection, model checking, ≤200µs cancel latency
description:
## What
G4 harness: chaos and cancellation storms + concurrency model checking — the proof engine for P7 (cancellation-correct compute) (plan §13.1).

## Scope
- Storm driver: kill random asupersync scopes at random times during REAL solves (not toy tasks); configurable kill rates, depths, and timing distributions (including adversarial: at tile boundaries, mid-reduction, during ledger writes).
- Assertions after every storm: zero arena leaks (via fs-alloc accounting), zero task leaks, no deadlocks (watchdog + timeout forensics), ledger consistency (WAL recovery invariants), and — the crown jewel — pause-serialize-resume reproduces the uninterrupted trajectory BIT-EXACTLY in deterministic mode.
- Fault injection: poison allocators (fail at the Nth allocation), fault-inject tiles (panic at tile k), torture the two-lane executor with adversarial preemption patterns; verify panic containment (scope poisoned, siblings cancelled, structured error with tile provenance, campaign continues per policy).
- Latency-to-cancel measurement: distribution of cancel-request→core-reclaimed times; assert the ≤200 µs bound at p99 on reference hardware (the bound e-racing depends on).
- Model checking: run asupersync's model checker over the executor's core protocols (steal/join/cancel state machines); in-house interleaving enumeration for our own primitives (per unsafe-capsule requirements).

## Why
Bet 8 (e-raced optimization) and speculative races are only safe if cancellation NEVER tears state. "Cancellation-correctness is a claim; G4 is the proof engine."

## Acceptance criteria
Storm suite green nightly on both ISAs against fs-exec + PV physics; latency histogram ledgered; seeded leak (deliberately unfreed arena) and seeded deadlock both demonstrably caught.

## Testing
The harness IS testing infrastructure; its self-tests verify each assertion class fires on seeded violations. Logs: storm seed, kill schedule, per-assertion verdicts, latency histograms — fully replayable from seed.

title: G5 harness: determinism audits + cross-ISA divergence classification report
description:
## What
G5 harness: determinism audits — bit-identical results across runs and thread counts per ISA, plus the cross-ISA divergence report (plan §13.1, §5.4).

## Scope
- Same-ISA audit: run registered suites (kernels, solvers, studies) N times at varying thread counts (1, 2, P, P+E, oversubscribed) in ExecMode::Deterministic; assert bit-identical artifact hashes. Any divergence = build failure with the first-divergence locator (binary-search over the event stream to find the offending reduction/kernel).
- Cross-ISA report: classify every NEON vs AVX-512 difference into documented categories — FMA contraction differences, libm ULP differences (bounded by fs-math contracts), reduction shape (should be NONE in deterministic mode) — with envelopes and switches to force strict orderings where bit-equality across ISAs is required. The report is a generated artifact, refreshed nightly, treated as documentation of record.
- Artifact-hash discipline: every ledgered artifact carries its content hash; G5 compares ledgers across runs so silent drift is impossible.
- ExecMode::Fast delta tracking: measure and record the throughput gain (~5–15% expected) and the reproducibility loss, so the tradeoff stays observed rather than assumed.

## Why
P2 (determinism is a contract) is what makes optimization studies replayable from a seed and a ledger entry — and what makes e-raced tournaments and G4's pause-resume equality even checkable.

## Acceptance criteria
Audit runs against fs-exec reductions + fs-rand streams + PV study; a seeded nondeterminism (arrival-order reduction) is caught with correct localization; cross-ISA report generates with all differences classified (no "unclassified" rows).

## Testing
Self-tests with seeded violations per category. Logs: run/thread-count matrix, hash tables, divergence locators, classification tables.

title: Certifying the certifiers: adversarial trials for interval/e-process/conformal/sheaf/SOS certificates
description:
## What
Certifying the certifiers (plan §13.2): the trials that attack FrankenSim's OWN certificate machinery. A false certificate is worse than a wrong answer — it is a wrong answer wearing a badge (Sev-0 policy).

## Scope
- Interval/Taylor-model enclosures spot-checked against the slow in-house high-precision oracle (double-double/quad-double from fs-ivl): random expressions, adversarial cancellation patterns, near-singular evaluations; enclosure must CONTAIN the oracle value, and tightness regressions are tracked.
- e-process validity verified EMPIRICALLY: under simulated nulls, anytime-valid type-I error at ADVERSARIALLY CHOSEN stopping times must stay ≤ α (the adversary peeks and stops at the worst moment; validity must survive). Also: e-BH FWER/FDR control under thousands of simultaneous candidate comparisons.
- Conformal e-prediction coverage tested under distribution-shift scenarios: geometry-family shift, fidelity shift, scenario-cluster shift (coordinates with conformal-hardening bead's Mondrian buckets and drift e-tests); coverage must degrade DETECTABLY (flagged), never silently.
- Sheaf watertightness certificate cross-examined by brute-force ray-parity queries on adversarial multi-chart seams (near-tangent interfaces, sliver patches, mixed-chart T-junctions).
- SOS certificates: extracted dual certificates re-verified in interval arithmetic (the SDP solver may be approximate; the CERTIFICATE must be rigorous).
- Sev-0 protocol: any fooled certificate auto-files maximal severity with the full reproducer ledgered.

## Acceptance criteria
Each trial class implemented as its certifier lands (deps wired accordingly); nightly rotation on both ISAs; at least one seeded-broken certifier per class demonstrably caught.

## Testing
Adversarial self-tests per class. Logs: trial seeds, adversary strategies, violation counts, tightness/coverage statistics over time.

title: Conformance suites speak IR: contract cases as FrankenScript programs, golden-ledger unification, cross-crate negotiation
description:
## What
Upgrade the conformance harness so suites SPEAK FRANKENSCRIPT IR (plan §13.3): "Because the suites speak FrankenScript IR, they double as the integration language between the AI agents building the system — an agent implementing fs-fft never negotiates with the agent implementing fs-lbm; both negotiate with the contract."

## Background
contract-conformance-infra ships v0 as a Rust-native harness with structured JSON cases, DESIGNED so IR wrapping is additive. This bead executes that upgrade once fs-ir-core exists.

## Scope
- IR front end for conformance cases: each registered case exposes an equivalent IR program (inputs as IR values with the Five Explicits, expected outputs as content-addressed artifacts + tolerance models); running a conformance suite = executing a batch of IR studies through the standard admission/session path (conformance now exercises the REAL entry path, not a test-only side door — admission, budgets, and provenance included in every conformance run).
- Golden-ledger unification: conformance acceptance runs ARE golden ledgers (one replay/compare mechanism for both, via ledger-timetravel) — CI replays conformance the same way it replays features.
- Cross-crate contract negotiation: integration points between crates expressed as IR-level contracts (e.g., "fs-lbm consumes an SDF chart satisfying these certified queries") checkable without either crate knowing the other's internals — the team-of-agents integration mechanism made executable.
- Migration: v0 Rust-native cases remain valid (the IR layer wraps them); new cases authored in IR-first form; migration lint tracks coverage.

## Acceptance criteria
The bedrock + morph conformance suites runnable via IR batch execution with identical verdicts to v0-native runs (dual-run equivalence gate during migration); conformance runs appear in the ledger with full Five-Explicits provenance; one cross-crate contract case demonstrates the negotiation pattern (documented as the template).

## Testing
Dual-run equivalence battery; admission-rejection of a malformed conformance program (the entry path is real); replay determinism of conformance ledgers. Logs: per-case IR program hashes, verdict tables, dual-run diffs (must be empty).

title: Gauntlet failure compounding: minimize every counterexample into a regression family

title: ADDENDUM L5 GO-TO-MARKET: the wedge and the conformance-tested plugin surface
description:
## Mission
ADDENDUM LAYER 5 — GO-TO-MARKET STRUCTURE. A single proposal, run in parallel with everything as the commercial track: it consumes the roadmap and constrains vertical-specific kernel work but gates nothing technical. Its lesson governs where FrankenSim points its kernels.

## Proposal 7 — The wedge and the plugin surface (Mean 640, Ex-A 725, Agent 300)
**Do not sell against peak single-physics fidelity anywhere.** Unification at the solver level loses to specialized codes on every individual physics; nobody buys a beautifully glued assembly of second-rate solvers, and nobody needs FrankenSim where one mature code owns the whole problem. Instead pick a beachhead where the *coupling-and-iteration loop* is the pain — a workflow that is today three tools, lossy handoffs, and week-long iteration cycles — where certified seams, incremental re-solve of variants (2), and autonomous gradient exploration (1) dominate even with merely-decent kernels. The Agent score of 300 is honest: this changes nothing about what the system can DO and everything about whether anyone finds out.

Two deliverables:
- **The wedge**: conjugate heat transfer for electronics cooling (kernels individually mature and modest; the thermal↔mechanical/layout iteration loop is the acknowledged pain; ROI quantifiable per design cycle; low regulatory friction so the evidence-package story (12) matures on friendly ground before facing the FAA). Named second/third verticals: aeroelastic screening, then additive-manufacturing distortion — chosen to progressively exercise Proposals 1, 11, and 4.
- **The plugin surface**: the restriction-map layer is where the hard engineering hides (the sheaf faithfully propagates garbage with certificates attached if trace/conversion operators are bad — risk R6). Specify it as an SDK whose conformance suite is auto-generated from the sheaf axioms: functoriality (composition, identity), adjoint consistency (against 1), tolerance honesty via manufactured solutions with known interface traces. Third parties ship converters; the Gauntlet certifies them into tiers; certified converters carry their tier in every ledger entry they touch. The architecture's most dangerous dependency becomes its network effect.

## Governance note
"Build in composite order, sell in Ex-A order." Engineering priority follows the Mean column; commercial narrative + partnership investment follow Ex-A, where 12 and 7 lead despite mid-table composite ranks (regulatory capture and ecosystem moats are how the *company* wins even though they change nothing about a Tuesday-night design session).

## Members
wedge-selection (7), plugin-surface (7).

## Success criteria
A referenceable wedge-vertical customer with measured cycle-time reduction ≥3× within two quarters of GA (else re-select against the same four criteria — the wedge, not the architecture, is wrong). First-party converters pass the same conformance suite, with the same severity, as third-party ones (R6 mitigation).

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- NOTE: `add-layer:Ln` here is the addendum's THEMATIC layer (economic engine / epistemics / coupling / self-knowledge / GTM), NOT the base L0–L6 architecture stack. Member crates still sit at their true base layer and must respect lower-knows-nothing-of-higher dependency direction.

The epic's governance lesson is recorded in fs-govern doctrine: build in composite order, sell in Ex-A order — do not sell against peak single-physics fidelity anywhere; sell the loop. Downstream consumers verified live: the trace corpus feeds the flywheel flagship; the conformance suite is the certification path for third-party converters; the wedge constrains vertical kernel work (CHT correlation rung registered in the fidelity-ladder registry per qmao.7).

title: Proposal 7 — Plugin surface: restriction-map SDK w/ sheaf-axiom-generated conformance suite (functoriality/adjoint-consistency/MMS) + tiered converter certification
description:
## What
Proposal 7's PLUGIN SURFACE — turn the architecture's WEAKEST POINT into its ECOSYSTEM PLAY. The RESTRICTION-MAP LAYER is where the hard engineering hides: the sheaf organizes bookkeeping GIVEN trace/conversion operators and will FAITHFULLY PROPAGATE GARBAGE WITH CERTIFICATES ATTACHED if those operators are bad (risk R6). So specify it as an SDK whose CONFORMANCE SUITE IS AUTO-GENERATED FROM THE SHEAF AXIOMS.

## Scope
- Specify the restriction-map layer as an SDK: third parties ship CONVERTERS (chart-to-chart trace/conversion operators — the Rep Router edges).
- CONFORMANCE SUITE auto-generated from the sheaf axioms:
  1. FUNCTORIALITY (composition, identity).
  2. ADJOINT CONSISTENCY (against Proposal 1 — the converter's transpose must be the adjoint the ledger uses).
  3. TOLERANCE HONESTY via MANUFACTURED SOLUTIONS with KNOWN interface traces (the converter's declared error model must not lie).
- The Gauntlet CERTIFIES converters into TIERS; certified converters carry their TIER in EVERY ledger entry they touch. The architecture's most dangerous dependency becomes its NETWORK EFFECT.
- R6 mitigation: apply this conformance suite to FIRST-PARTY converters with the SAME SEVERITY as third-party ones.

## Acceptance criteria
The SDK spec + auto-generated conformance suite exist; a converter is certified into a tier only by passing functoriality + adjoint-consistency + manufactured-solution tolerance-honesty tests; the tier is stamped on every ledger entry the converter touches; first-party converters run the identical suite; a deliberately dishonest converter (understated error model) FAILS tolerance honesty.

## Kill criterion
Inherits Proposal 7's commercial gate (wedge-selection). For the plugin surface specifically, R6's early warning is the CONFORMANCE-TIER DISTRIBUTION of converters on the hot path — if hot-path converters cluster in low tiers, restriction-map quality is the bottleneck.

## Testing
Auto-generated conformance suite IS the test: functoriality (composition/identity laws), adjoint consistency vs Proposal 1, MMS tolerance honesty. Adversarial: a garbage converter with a lying error model must fail. Logs: converter tier assignments, conformance-test results, hot-path tier distribution (R6 early warning).

## Dependencies
Bet 11 sheaf axioms (base plan fs-geom) + the Rep Router converter registry (base plan morph); Proposal 1 (adjoint consistency). Owns risk R6. Sibling to wedge-selection. Amends the base plan (restriction-map SDK + tiered converter certification as named components).

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- Tiers: functoriality (composition/identity) -> G0; MMS tolerance-honesty -> G1; dishonest-converter (understated error model) rejection -> G4 adversarial.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Add the adjoint-consistency conformance test named in Scope but missing from Testing: a certified converter's transpose EQUALS the adjoint the ledger uses (against Proposal 1) — a converter that is functorial but adjoint-inconsistent silently corrupts every gradient routed through it. Optimality: encode BOTH accuracy AND cost in the converter tier so the Rep Router can route by tier.

title: L6 HELM: orchestration, ledger, and agent interface
description:
## Mission
L6 HELM: orchestration, sessions, and the agent interface. Everything below is callable; HELM makes it programmable, replayable, and governable — for AI agents first, humans equally. This is where P4 (budgets), P9 (provenance), and P10 (agent-first) become running code.

## Core components (plan §11 + patch Rev B)
- FrankenScript IR: THE canonical interface — a typed, versioned intermediate representation with two isomorphic syntaxes (canonical s-expressions + lossless JSON) parsing to one typed AST. Static admission before execution: dimensional analysis in the type system, chart-compatibility via Rep Router, budget feasibility against learned cost models, capability sufficiency. Ill-typed studies rejected in milliseconds with structured diagnoses, not discovered at hour six.
- The Design Ledger (Bet 10): FrankenSQLite as system of record — content-addressed artifacts, event-sourced ops, lineage edges, metrics, autotune cache, session events. Time travel, forkable worlds, and explain() are nearly free because sessions are event-sourced over content-addressed state. A six-month campaign is a database you query, not a directory you fear.
- Evidence/Model Ledger (patch Rev B): Evidence<T> carries numerical + statistical + MODEL-FORM certificates, sensitivity, validity domain, and decision status; model cards for every solver/closure/material law. The system must be able to say "mesh error 0.7%, turbulence-model discrepancy 8–15%, ranking not decision-grade."
- Sessions & capability tokens: budgets ENFORCED not advisory; idempotency keys; estimate() dry runs; errors-as-guidance with ranked fixes ("a refusal that teaches is worth ten silent successes").
- The self-optimizing pipeline (Bet 12): Error Ledger + Time Ledger compose per-operator error/cost models end-to-end; the planner allocates error budget across mesh/order/tolerance/surrogate/samples to maximize accuracy-per-second.
- Five Explicits everywhere: units, seeds, budgets, versions, capabilities — an agent literally cannot express an ambiguous request.

## Members
fs-ledger-core, evidence-model-ledger, ledger-timetravel, fs-ir-core, fs-ir-admission, fs-ir-catalog, fs-session-caps, fs-plan-models, fs-plan-allocator, fs-report, helm-e2e.

## Success Criteria
IR round-trips; admission rejects with teaching errors; ledger survives kill -9 mid-sweep; time-travel replay is bit-exact in deterministic mode; conversational latency ≤100 ms while campaigns saturate the throughput lane.

This rollup does not duplicate leaf unit tests. Its acceptance matrix must name every direct child, owned capability, required local unit/property/metamorphic/integration proof, terminal E2E or adjudication consumer, and no-claim boundary.

## Delegated terminal ownership clarification

This layer epic is a hierarchy rollup and owns no aggregate terminal script. Its acceptance matrix names downstream terminal consumers; it does not execute them. HELM conformance remains owned by `frankensim-epic-helm-gp3.11` through `scripts/ci/helm_conformance_profile.sh` and `tests/e2e/conformance/helm.toml`.
