title: Autotuner: per-machine calibration (bandwidth/GEMM/stencil/steal/reduction), tune table, TilePlan service
description:
## What
The autotuner (plan §5.5): first-run and periodically refreshed calibration that makes NOTHING performance-critical hardcoded to either microarchitecture.

## Scope
- Calibration pass measuring per machine: sustained bandwidth per core class (P vs E; per-CCD), GEMM microkernel throughput across tile shapes, stencil throughput vs tile size and software-prefetch distance, steal latencies, reduction costs, and per-core-class kernel throughput (feeds P/E stealing weights in fs-exec).
- Persistence: results in the Ledger `tune` table keyed by kernel × shape-class × MACHINE FINGERPRINT (hardware topology hash from fs-substrate). Until fs-ledger lands, a local file store with the same schema (migration is a rename).
- TilePlan service: every TileKernel's tile geometry (8³ vs 4³ vs 16³, halo depths, prefetch distances) resolved from tune data with sane cold-start defaults + background refinement.
- Schedule polymorphism support: kernels register bandwidth-rich and bandwidth-starved schedules (fewer/fatter streaming tiles vs aggressive cache blocking + recomputation-over-reload); the autotuner selects per machine (the §5.1 consequence-2 doctrine).
- Refresh policy: staleness detection (fingerprint drift, thermal/frequency anomalies), periodic re-benchmark hooks, and a `--recalibrate` entry point.
- Feeds forward: cost models in fs-plan-models (Bet 12) and Rep Router edge costs read this table; tropical-analytics tells it WHICH kernel to tune next.

## Acceptance criteria
Cold-start → calibrated transition demonstrably improves reference kernel throughput; tune table rows carry fingerprint + confidence; TilePlan decisions reproducible in deterministic mode (calibration randomness seeded); recalibration idempotent.

## Testing
Unit: shape-sweep bookkeeping, fingerprint keying, staleness logic. Integration: end-to-end calibrate→persist→consume on both ISAs. Determinism: tuning decisions themselves ledgered so a study can pin its TilePlans (replay uses RECORDED plans, not re-tuned ones — critical for replay fidelity). Logs: full calibration report per machine as structured JSON.
close_reason: Implemented the autotuner in fs-exec::tune. Calibration pass: tile-edge sweep (4/8/16) running a REAL 7-point stencil through the real TilePool (argmin, lowest-index tie law, best-of-2 repeats), det-sum reduction cost, steal-cost probe (imbalanced 2-worker run, steal count + wall recorded), schedule selection from measured per-core bandwidth (bandwidth-rich vs -starved, §5.1 consequence 2; zero-measurement -> rich default, recorded). Tune table: rows keyed kernel x shape-class x MACHINE FINGERPRINT with repeat-agreement confidence + refresh counter; JSONL file store mirroring the ledger tune schema (migration = rename); foreign-fingerprint rows stale on load; missing store = cold start; corrupt store = teaching TuneError. TilePlan service: tile_edge_for/schedule with pins > tuned > cold-start (E8, bandwidth-rich) precedence; every decision RECORDED (TuningDecision) so studies pin plans and replay uses recorded plans, never re-tuned ones (exec-013 proves pinned replay reproduces on an uncalibrated machine). Recalibration idempotent (same keys replaced, refresh increments — exec-013). Conformance exec-013: calibrate->persist->consume round trip, fingerprint keying, ledgered calibration report validated through fs-obs. No-claims: no calibrated-is-faster CI assertion (report documents measurements; perf harness owns verdicts); GEMM/prefetch rows arrive when fs-la registers benches; P/E per-class bandwidth inherits fs-substrate pinning no-claim. ALSO fixed a broken-on-main fs-math dd test (e892403): the add/sub round-trip and distributivity error models measured relative to a potentially near-zero operand instead of the dominant intermediate magnitude — deterministic failure blocking every agent's workspace lane; fixed the test's error model, dd library untouched. Lanes green: clippy -D warnings, fmt, fs-exec 32 lib + 13 conformance, workspace 52 suites, xtask 0 violations.

title: Substrate G4/G5 battery: storms, cancel-latency certification, pause/resume equality, determinism audit
description:
## What
The substrate-specific G4/G5 test suite: the exhaustive, heavily-logged unit + integration battery proving L0's claims before anything is built on them.

## Scope
- Cancellation storms against fs-exec + fs-alloc with REAL workloads (PV-skeleton physics once available, synthetic tile kernels before): random scope kills at adversarial times; assertions: zero arena/task leaks (accounting-verified), no deadlocks, panic containment produces structured errors with tile provenance, siblings cancelled, campaign-level continuation policy honored.
- Latency-to-cancel certification: p50/p99/max histograms of cancel→reclaim across load levels, tile sizes, and scope depths; ≤200 µs p99 gate on reference hardware; results ledgered per fingerprint.
- Pause-serialize-resume equality: checkpoint mid-solve at random points; resumed trajectory bit-identical to uninterrupted (deterministic mode).
- Speculative-race torture: races where losers are killed at every pipeline stage; winner determinism across thread counts.
- Determinism battery: reduction library + RNG streams + reference kernels across {1,2,P,2P} threads × N runs; artifact-hash equality; Fast-mode divergence measured and bounded.
- Memory discipline: hugepage acquisition/fallback paths, first-touch verification (page-to-node mapping probes on Linux), false-sharing detection microbench (128 B alignment efficacy).
- Model-checking lane: interleaving enumeration on the deque steal/join/cancel protocol (in-house harness per P1) + asupersync's model checker on scope trees.

## Why
Every layer above assumes these invariants silently. The plan's P0 exit criterion is literally "G0+G4 green; deterministic mode bit-stable" — this bead is that criterion made executable.

## Acceptance criteria
Full suite green nightly on both ISAs; every assertion class has a seeded-violation self-test proving the detector works; latency + determinism artifacts ledgered.

## Testing
This IS the testing bead. Logging requirements: every storm/audit emits structured JSON events (seeds, kill schedules, histograms, hash tables, verdicts) sufficient to replay any failure from the log alone — the exemplar for detailed-logging standards project-wide.
acceptance_criteria:
SCOPE PRESERVATION AND EXACT OWNERSHIP. Every clause in the existing description remains normative; this acceptance contract adds executable closure detail and removes no feature, platform, fixture, certificate, benchmark, performance target, or no-claim boundary. Own the L0 G4/G5 closure for cancellation storms on real work, cancel-to-reclaim latency, pause/serialize/resume equality, speculative-race draining, deterministic reductions/RNG/reference kernels, allocation/NUMA/alignment discipline, and executor/scope model checking. Exact planned ownership is script scripts/ci/substrate_conformance_profile.sh, immutable manifest tests/e2e/conformance/substrate.toml, and exactly these top-level case IDs: substrate.cancel_storm, substrate.cancel_latency, substrate.pause_resume, substrate.speculative_race, substrate.determinism, substrate.memory_discipline, substrate.model_check. This bead owns this dedicated runner surface. The manifest contains each ID exactly once with fixed nonempty invocation data, input/root identity, expected disposition and stable exit class, budgets, capabilities, claimed/no-claim predicates, independent checker, positive-or-hostile role, and repository-relative artifacts; duplicate, missing, reordered, unknown, stale-root, or cross-family cases fail --check.

UNIT AND BOUNDARY BATTERY. Focused unit/API/schema tests cover happy; empty/zero/one and minimum admitted input; n-1/n/n+1 around every cardinality, tolerance, iteration, sample, mesh, time-step, queue, depth, and budget boundary this suite owns; exact declared maximum; maximum+1 refusal without huge allocation; malformed, truncated, duplicate, inconsistent, non-finite/extreme, unsupported-version, wrong-unit/frame/clock/ISA/fingerprint input; deterministic enumeration and tie/error ordering; stable typed diagnostics; and every domain refusal. Exercise scope depths, worker counts {1,2,P,2P}, tile sizes, kill schedules, checkpoint locations, allocation classes, huge-page fallback, NUMA-node availability, stream counters, and supported deterministic/Fast modes at their exact limits. Compile-fail misuse tests are required for public authority types; if no public type exists, the nearest strict schema/API-negative test records that fact. Property and metamorphic tests cover thread-count and legal schedule invariance in deterministic mode, logical-tile relabeling, pause/resume equivalence, seed/log replay, equivalent scope-tree association, workload scaling, and declared Fast-mode divergence bounds. Seeded mutation tests independently remove or alter every identity, bound, tolerance, route, invariant, conservation term, reference/envelope, evidence edge, checker, publication guard, and no-claim field; every detector has a known-broken self-test proving nonvacuity.

RELEASE-BUILT NO-MOCK JOURNEYS. scripts/ci/substrate_conformance_profile.sh must document and deterministically implement --list, --check, --self-test, --run pr, --run nightly-full, --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. The happy journey uses release-built production code, real admitted fixtures/workloads, and real persistence/package paths—never a mock, hard-coded verdict, precomputed production result, schema-only shell, validator reused as producer, or silent named-skip. The hostile journey covers seeded arena/task leak, deadlock/livelock, double lease return, loser publication, lost cancellation, panic propagation, corrupted checkpoint, nondeterministic reduction/RNG stream, false-sharing/alignment regression, invalid topology fingerprint, and cancel-latency overrun. Cancellation before/during/after every decisive transition, injected parser/allocator/worker/process/I/O/durable-seal/publication/checker faults, work/memory/deadline/output-cap exhaustion, panic containment, retry, and replay must prove bounded polling, request-drain-finalize, exact resource return, no leaked tasks or leases, no partial authority, and one terminal disposition. An inapplicable fault class needs a typed rationale in the manifest, not silent omission.

INDEPENDENT CHECKING, REPLAY, LOGGING, AND AUTHORITY. Independent accounting reconstructs all task/arena/lease balances and checkpoint roots; a separately clocked latency adjudicator validates histograms only on an admitted idle reference host and a schedule-independent replay checker compares deterministic artifacts across declared thread counts/ISAs. The checker consumes immutable artifacts from a separate input root, does not trust producer verdict fields, and writes replay output to a distinct root; tamper, truncation, stale checker, source/build drift, disagreement, revocation, and repeated clean-store replay are mandatory. Freeze a documented stable exit-class enum and numeric mapping for Pass, UsageRefused, InputRefused, NoData, EvidenceFailed, CancelledDrained, InfrastructureFailed, and InternalFault, with parser and propagation self-tests. Bounded deterministic JSONL is redacted before buffering and hashing and records schema/source/build/tool/target/features, script/profile/family/case/sequence, fixture/reference identities, typed lossless values and units, seeds, capabilities, admitted and consumed budgets/work/resources, expected/observed/margins, state/reason, first divergence, detector/checker, authority/no-claim transition, cancel/drain/finalize roots, relative artifacts, ranked repairs, and one repository-relative reproduction command. It excludes secrets, absolute paths, host identity, PIDs, unbounded payloads, and undeclared volatile noise. DSR may prove repository integration but cannot mint the ≤200 microsecond p99 or cross-ISA performance claim: those require admitted host fingerprints, load/clock quality, raw capped distributions, and the named dual-ISA campaign; otherwise report NO-DATA or no-claim. The terminal repository gate is exactly dsr quality --tool frankensim. Focused Cargo/RCH proof, DSR dry-run, dual-ISA evidence, scientific validation, and performance qualification are distinct evidence and must be reported separately; none substitutes for another.

title: fs-math extensions: tan/atan2/pow/erf family, Payne-Hanek reduction, fast mode, ULP-ledger lint
description:
## What
fs-math extension set: the remaining strict-mode functions and hardening the
v1 core (fs-math-deterministic bead) deliberately deferred. Same doctrine:
pure-IEEE-arithmetic implementations, declared ULP budgets with measured
maxima, cross-ISA golden-hash extension, bitwise symmetry by construction.

## Scope
- Functions: tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, pow (integer + general), cbrt,
  log1p, log2, log10, erf/erfc, sinh, cosh — each with per-function ULP
  budget, edge-table battery, and golden-hash coverage.
- Payne–Hanek big-argument reduction for trig: lift the |x| ≤ 2²⁰ domain
  restriction (v1 no-claim) with the full 2/π bit table.
- Fast mode: platform-libm-backed variants behind the ExecMode::Fast gate,
  emitting the mode into provenance (never silently substituted).
- ULP-ledger lint: mechanical check that deterministic-mode kernels call
  fs_math::det (not f64::sin etc.) — greppable/lintable rule from the
  policy doc, wired into xtask or clippy config.
- dd-oracle battery integration once fs-ivl lands (nightly, large-N).
- Budget tightening pass: v1 budgets are ceilings; re-measure and tighten.

## Why split from the core bead
The v1 set (exp/expm1/ln/sin/cos/tanh/sqrt + policy + nudging) satisfies
every CURRENT consumer (determinism-contract's strict-transcendental needs,
fs-ivl enclosures, FFT twiddles, EdgeLaw tanh) and is cross-ISA-proven;
holding those consumers hostage to erf/pow would serialize the P0 spine for
no benefit. This bead carries the remainder with full context.

## Acceptance criteria
Each new function: budget-gated ULP battery green on both ISAs; golden hash
extended + verified cross-ISA; Payne–Hanek: trig batteries at |x| up to
1e300 within budget; fast-mode provenance test; ULP-ledger lint catches a
seeded f64::sin call in a deterministic-mode kernel.

## Testing
Same harness as v1 (max_ulp batteries, symmetry sweeps, special-value
tables, golden hash, core regressions); Payne–Hanek gets dedicated
worst-case-argument tests (the classic 2^52-adjacent adversaries).
close_reason: fs-math extension family landed (ADDITIVE to det.rs - original golden hash untouched by construction): tan (sin_core/cos_core ratio on the SHARED 4-part Cody-Waite reduction; tan==sin/cos BITWISE on even quadrants - an identity, tested 50k points; odd bitwise), atan (pi/2 + pi/6 two-stage reduction to |t|<=tan(pi/12), 16-term exact-rational odd Taylor, hi/lo constant pairs; 4 ULP declared/measured), atan2 (IEEE special-value table tested bitwise vs libm conventions; y-sign symmetry bitwise), erf/erfc (dd-powered: Taylor sum IN double-double for |x|<=3, Laplace continued fraction in dd for x>3, EXACT-dd x^2 before exp in the tail - plain f64 would cost ~x^2/2 ULP at x=25; 6/10 ULP declared/measured incl deep tail), pow (IEEE specials, integer repeated-squaring + sqrt fast paths, exp(y ln x) with the product in dd via two_prod; budget = the HONEST formula 3(|y ln x|+1)+5 - the magnification is intrinsic, dd-ln refinement recorded). TESTING INSIGHT worth keeping: the plain-f64 test oracle proved WEAKER than the dd implementation in the erf cancellation band (oracle error up to ~1600 ULP at x~3) - resolved by DISJOINT-PATH cross-validation (Taylor-dd vs CF-dd agree <=3 ULP at shared x, both exposed via doc-hidden probe) + oracle-limited sanity tolerance documented in-test. Battery 6/6 green BOTH ISAs (trj /data/tmp/ext_verify.uWVlaT/run.log; golden hash 0x5bbb025667a90b70 IDENTICAL; post-verification lint edits provably bit-neutral - exact-integer arithmetic only). clippy -D warnings, fmt, CONTRACT budgets section extended. Payne-Hanek (with full integer-Machin bignum design) + fast mode + ULP-ledger lint split to frankensim-r6r5.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CLAIMED (numerics-spine agent; post 6ys.13). v1 scope = the ELEMENTARY FAMILY in det.rs style (pure IEEE arithmetic, exact bit-pattern constants where trailing-zero mantissas matter, budgets DECLARED and measured vs 200k-sample libm oracle + edges): (1) TAN via sin_core/cos_core ratio on the existing 4-part Cody-Waite reduced argument (shares reduce_pio2 - same TRIG_DOMAIN limit; consistent reduction means the ratio's relative error stays bounded ~8 ulp declared, poles handled by quadrant logic). (2) ATAN: reduce |x|>1 via atan(x)=pi/2-atan(1/x) (pi/2 as exact hi/lo pair), then the pi/6 rotation identity to |t|<=tan(pi/12)~0.268, then a 16-term odd Taylor polynomial (exact rational coefficients 1/(2k+1), Horner, fused) - budget ~4 ulp declared/measured. ATAN2: quadrant logic + IEEE special cases (+-0, +-inf table, tested exhaustively against libm edge behavior). (3) ERF/ERFC from scratch with the Dd trick: Taylor series for erf SUMMED IN DOUBLE-DOUBLE for |x|<=3 (cancellation eats <=4 digits at x=3; dd's 32 digits keep the result full-precision - this is why dd went to L0), erfc via Laplace continued fraction in dd for x>3 (fast convergence there), erfc(x)=1-erf(x) for small x, negative x by symmetry; budgets measured (~few ulp expected). (4) POW: fast paths (y integer -> powi chain, y=0.5 -> sqrt exact, x=2^k exact), general via exp(y*ln x) with the y*ln(x) PRODUCT in Dd (two_prod) to suppress the classic magnification; budget declared HONESTLY as ~(3*|y*ln x|+5) ulp worst case with the common-range measurement reported - the dd-ln refinement recorded as follow-up. SPLIT (recorded with design): PAYNE-HANEK reduction beyond 2^20 (full plan: 2/pi to ~1200 bits via integer-Machin bignum (16 atan(1/5) - 4 atan(1/239) in u64-limb fixed point, ~550 series terms, verified by a deterministic runtime regeneration test), x*(2/pi) mod 4 in exact u64 multiplies from mantissa/exponent decomposition, quadrant + dd reduced argument) - a full arc of its own; FAST MODE feature flag (needs consumers to define tolerable budgets); ULP-LEDGER LINT (CI lane, huq.4 coordination). Tests: budgets measured + asserted per function, symmetry laws (tan odd, atan odd, erf odd, atan2 quadrant symmetries), identity cross-checks (tan = sin/cos bitwise BY CONSTRUCTION on shared reduction, erf(x)+erfc(x)=1 to budget, pow(x,2)=x*x-ish), special-value tables, golden hash + trj cross-ISA, det golden hash UNTOUCHED (additive only).

title: GEMM: make root orchestration allocations fallible and memory-budgeted
description: gemm_f64_parallel_with_pool allocates transactional C staging, shared B pack, and per-panel band metadata as ordinary Vec values outside TilePool Cx/ArenaPool budgeting. Capacity failures can abort rather than return GemmRunError, and TilePool currently supplies Budget::INFINITE to tiles. Acceptance: add an explicit operation memory envelope bound into execution/tune provenance; preflight checked byte requirements for C staging+B pack+metadata+per-worker arena; use fallible reservation/allocation throughout root orchestration; add a structured allocation/budget refusal variant that leaves C unchanged and drains any started work; ensure Cx receives the effective non-infinite caller budget; ledger requested/used/refused bytes; add huge-shape, tiny-budget, cancellation-during-init, allocator-refusal/fault-injection, and success equivalence tests. Do not weaken transactional C semantics or use unsafe allocation shortcuts.
close_reason: Completed explicit GEMM memory-envelope enforcement end to end. Root plans use checked u128 arithmetic; no-product calls charge only transactional staging; all root allocations reserve fallibly; finite per-worker arena quotas reach TilePool Cx through run_declared_budgeted and allocator refusal returns typed drained reports; C commits only after final cancellation poll; session tuning/provenance keys bind the memory ceiling; requested/peak/refused accounting and full failure reports survive conversion. Error reports are boxed off the success path with a size regression. Verified via RCH local fallback: fs-la gemm_budget 5/5, fs-session lib 10/10, gemm_tune 16 pass + 1 declared ignored oracle, session conformance 17/17, and fs-session all-target no-deps clippy green with only established complexity allowances. Forced only because Beads prevents closing a completed parent with the separately scoped open wf9.15.1 child; that metadata follow-up remains open and is not claimed here.

comments.text:

2. Acceptance requires effective non-infinite budget to reach Cx, but TilePool::run_declared still creates Budget::INFINITE; A-pack arena failure still panics and surfaces as Executor rather than MemoryRefused.
3. MemoryRefused.report claims zero progress, but per-panel band-metadata allocation can fail after earlier panels completed.
4. Report records requested/limit only, not used/refused bytes required by acceptance.
5. Current source has duplicate derive placement, incomplete memory propagation through report/cancelled calls, and fs-session GemmRunReport literals/error matches are not migrated.
Preserve transactional C, but distinguish preflight refusal from post-dispatch allocation failure and ledger actual progress/usage.

comments.text:

title: GEMM tuner: put orchestration metadata under the session memory lease

comments.text:
DESIGN CHECKPOINT (inventory complete, implementation next). Metadata allocation inventory in gemm_tune.rs, all bounded: (1) effective_sweep_candidates: candidates Vec (cap = SWEEP_MC.len x SWEEP_NC_CAP.len = 8) + BTreeSet dedup nodes; (2) measure_candidates: observations Vec (<=8), ranked Vec of (u64,usize,GemmBlockPlan) (<=8), per-candidate samples_ns Vec (SWEEP_SAMPLES=3) ALLOCATED PER CANDIDATE in the loop; (3) TuneObservation::wall_time label Strings (canonical plan spelling, short/schema-bounded) + TuneEvidence::ranked_wall_times internals (fs-exec types, bounded by 8 observations); (4) sealed-row strings via ValidatedGemmTuneRow::from_prepared (params_json/row_json, schema-bounded, built in fs-exec but OWNED by the session row); (5) ledger/cache transients.

Planned implementation: (a) SessionTuneMetadataPlan in fs-session with checked u128 component bounds from the const grid; charged in run_sweep's preflight alongside probe_buffer_bytes -> MemoryRefused{what:tune-metadata-plan} before any probe allocation; (b) REPLACE the BTreeSet dedup with a linear scan over the <=8-entry Vec (BTree node overhead is not honestly accountable in safe Rust; at n<=8 the scan is also faster) and HOIST samples_ns to one reused Vec (8 allocations -> 1); all Vecs via try_reserve_exact helpers mirroring try_filled_buffer; (c) receipt {schema fs-session-tune-metadata-plan-v1, requested_bytes, refused} threaded through SweepResult and bound into ValidatedGemmTuneRow::receipt_json (session-owned provenance; receipt_identity hashes it, so this ROTATES sealed-row identities once - previously persisted cache rows will cold-retune, same class of rotation as a build-fingerprint change, will be documented in fs-session CONTRACT); (d) tests: envelope-just-below-metadata refusal (no validated report lost - refusal precedes probes), cancellation unchanged, cold/warm cache, exact receipt field, success-equivalence (same winner, bitwise outputs) vs pre-plan behavior. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: DESIGN REFINEMENT (adoption invariant): ValidatedGemmTuneRow::receipt_identity must stay 'stable for a freshly measured row and the same row adopted later', and adopt_cached_row REBUILDS the row from the stored measured JSON via prepare_adopt_gemm_row_json. So the metadata-plan receipt cannot live only in fs-session's sealed-row receipt_json - it must ride IN the persisted evidence JSON that fs-exec serializes and re-parses, i.e. TuneEvidence gains an OPTIONAL session_metadata_plan field (canonical JSON: schema fs-session-tune-metadata-plan-v1, requested_bytes, component breakdown, refused=null on success), written by write_json and round-tripped by the adoption parser; validate() checks it is either absent or canonical. Consequences: (a) fs-exec's evidence schema grows one optional field (session provenance transported by the evidence container - NOT wf9.16's executor metadata, scope-checked); (b) previously persisted rows lack the field, parse fine, and re-tune once when a fresh measurement produces the field-bearing identity (same rotation class as a build-fingerprint change; document in fs-session CONTRACT); (c) TuneEvidence::VERSION stays 1 with an optional field rather than bumping - the parser must accept both spellings only if version stays; alternatively bump to 2 and refuse mixed - DECIDE AT IMPLEMENTATION: bump-to-2-and-refuse is the cleaner fail-closed reading of this workspace's schema doctrine and matches the row-rotation consequence anyway. Implementation order: fs-exec evidence field + parser + validate, then SessionTuneMetadataPlan + preflight charge + BTreeSet-to-linear-scan + hoisted samples Vec + try_reserve helpers in fs-session, receipt threading through SweepResult/install_sweep_row, CONTRACT notes, then the five-part test battery from the previous comment.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: DONE, landed bd98fc1. Acceptance mapping: (1) checked session tune-memory plan - tune_metadata_plan module, a pure constant of the const sweep lattice (CANDIDATE_CAP=8) and documented schema caps (LABEL 64B, PARAMS 256B, MEASURED 16KiB), all caps ENFORCED at observation/seal time via asserts rather than assumed; (2) infallible growth replaced - try_reserved_vec (try_reserve_exact, typed MemoryRefused) for candidates/ranked/observations/sample copies; BTreeSet dedup replaced by a bounded linear scan (tree-node overhead is not honestly accountable in safe Rust; n<=8 so it is also faster); the per-candidate samples Vec hoisted to one reused scratch + exact-length per-observation copies; (3) requested/refused accounting without losing a validated report - the plan is charged in run_sweep AFTER probes clear the envelope alone, so 'tune-probe-envelope' keeps its meaning, 'tune-metadata-plan' refusals carry probes+plan exact accounting and fire BEFORE any allocation (report:None is structural - nothing has run); title: fs-simd: scalar baseline + NEON/AVX-512 capsules behind safe facades + experimental portable tier
description:
## What
`fs-simd`: the SIMD tier system — stable-Rust-first, per the patch Rev Q correction (std::simd/portable_simd is nightly-experimental, so it CANNOT be the committed baseline).

## Scope
- Tier 0 (committed baseline): scalar stable Rust, written so the autovectorizer has a fair chance (no aliasing hazards, explicit chunking) — correctness reference for every other tier.
- Tier 1: `std::arch` target-specific leaf kernels behind SAFE FAÇADES — NEON (aarch64) and AVX-512 (x86-64) intrinsics inside registered unsafe capsules (<300 lines each, SAFETY.md per unsafe-safety-cases bead).
- Tier 2 (experimental, feature-flagged): nightly portable-SIMD path for ergonomic exploration; never load-bearing.
- Uniform kernel-facing API: lane-width-agnostic primitives (fma, gather-ish patterns where supported, masked ops, horizontal reductions with FIXED tree shape for determinism), alignment helpers keyed to the 128-byte unconditional alignment policy (superset of both targets).
- Dispatch integration: fs-substrate resolves tables at startup; fs-simd provides the per-ISA implementations. Every intrinsic capsule has a scalar twin, and G0 property tests assert tier equivalence (exact for integer/logic ops; ULP-bounded for float, coordinated with fs-math contracts).

## Why
Plan §5.1 tier list adjusted by patch Rev Q: pretending portable-SIMD is stable would bake nightly into the foundation. The scalar twin + capsule discipline keeps P1 (memory safety) honest while still hitting roofline targets.

## Acceptance criteria
NEON + AVX-512 + scalar tiers for the core primitive set; tier-equivalence property suite green on both ISAs; all capsules registered with SAFETY.md; Miri-clean on capsule tests (via façade where Miri can't see intrinsics, plus interpreter-level checks on the scalar twin).

## Testing
G0 tier-equivalence laws (random inputs incl. subnormals, NaN, ±0); alignment-violation negative tests; per-primitive microbenches feeding the roofline harness. Logs: tier chosen, capability flags, equivalence-test ULP histograms.
close_reason: Implemented and verified ON BOTH ISAs. Scalar twin module (the semantic definition, fused mul_add per the FMA policy); NEON capsule = THE EXEMPLAR (SAFETY.md all 11 sections, registered, as_chunks-derived pointers, tails via scalar twin, <300 lines); x86 capsule (AVX2+FMA and AVX-512F variants of axpy/dot/sum, runtime-ladder safe facades that re-verify CPU features and fall back to scalar — dispatch tier is optimization, never soundness precondition); one-shot Ops function table keyed by fs-substrate tier; fixed per-tier reduction shapes documented (two-accumulator NEON/AVX shapes). EVIDENCE: (1) aarch64 NEON: tier battery green locally (M4 Pro), lens 0..67 x seeds, subnormal/NaN/pm-0/1e18, elementwise BITWISE vs twin, reductions enveloped, same-tier bit-stable; (2) x86-64 AVX2: EXECUTED on trj (Threadripper PRO 5995WX) — tier=avx2 battery pass, all suites EXIT:0 debug+release; (3) Miri lane green (scalar dispatch, compensating checks documented in SAFETY.md); (4) cross-compile checks green for x86_64-apple-darwin + x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; (5) check-unsafe green with both capsules registered. title: fs-simd SME2 exploratory tier: runtime-gated streaming-mode GEMM prototype [F]
description:
## What
Exploratory SME2/streaming-mode matrix path for GEMM-shaped work on Apple Silicon — strictly [F], strictly feature-flagged, strictly runtime-capability-gated (plan §5.1 tier 5, §17 risk "SME2 intrinsics immaturity"; patch Rev Q demotion).

## Scope
- Runtime probe: detect streaming-mode/matrix-unit availability via capability probe; NEVER compile-time assumed. If absent or intrinsics unstable, the flag is inert and NEON remains the committed path.
- Streaming-mode GEMM microkernel prototype behind `frontier-sme2`: outer-product accumulation shapes, ZA-tile-style register management, integration with fs-la-gemm's packing/blocking so only the microkernel swaps.
- Honest benchmark protocol: measured vs NEON baseline on identical problems, ledgered with fingerprints; promotion to default requires beating NEON by a stated margin across the autotuner's shape sweep AND passing the full G0/G5 kernel suites.
- Explicit non-goals: no GPU/Metal work here (separate capability class per Rev Q); no determinism-mode support claims until FMA/accumulation-order semantics are characterized in the cross-ISA report.

## Why
The M-class matrix unit is potential upside for FEM batched-small-dense and GEMM, but intrinsics maturity is a named risk. The mitigation is exactly this bead's shape: committed NEON baseline, exploratory flag, autotuner as judge.

## Acceptance criteria

title: fs-alloc: scope arenas (O(1) cancel reclaim), 128B alignment, hugepages, pools, site tracking
description:
## What
`fs-alloc`: scope arenas, pools, and hugepage-backed memory — the memory discipline of plan §5.3.

## Scope
- Scope arenas: bump allocators tied 1:1 to asupersync scopes; cancellation or completion reclaims in O(1); cross-scope escapes are COMPILE ERRORS (lifetimes do the enforcement — the arena's allocations borrow the scope). This is what makes speculative-race loser reclamation and e-racing kills instantaneous and leak-free.
- Long-lived artifacts "graduate" explicitly to the content-addressed store (ledger) — no silent promotion.
- 128-byte alignment UNCONDITIONALLY (superset of both targets' cache lines): padding + false-sharing avoidance helpers.
- Hugepage-backed arenas for field storage: 2 MB via madvise/THP on Linux; document Apple 16 KB base-page behavior; graceful fallback with the choice recorded.
- Pools for recurring same-shape allocations (tiles, small matrices) with per-CCD sharding hooks (first-touch by owning worker — the NUMA story from §5.1 consequence 3).
- Allocation-site tracking: lightweight tagging so memory usage feeds the Ledger and regressions are DIFFABLE between runs (§5.3).
- Unsafe capsules: the bump-pointer core and mmap wrappers, registered per unsafe-safety-cases with full SAFETY.md, Miri + fuzz coverage.

## Why
P7 (cancellation) and Bet 8 (e-racing) are only real if reclamation is O(1) and leak-proof; G4 storms assert exactly that via this crate's accounting. Arena scoping is also the anti-fragmentation strategy for 10⁸-cell field campaigns.

## Acceptance criteria
Arena lifecycle correct under G4 storms (zero leaks across 10⁶ random cancellations); escape attempts fail to compile (compile-fail battery); hugepage acquisition verified where supported; accounting reports match actual usage.

## Testing
Unit: alignment, growth, reset, OOM behavior (structured error, not abort). Property: interleaved alloc/cancel sequences preserve accounting invariants. Concurrency: arenas under parallel tile writers (Miri + storm). Logs: per-scope byte counts, hugepage status, allocation-site tables.

title: fs-exec: two-lane executor — latency lane + CCD/P-E-aware work-stealing tile lane, Cx contract
description:
## What
`fs-exec`: the two-lane executor on asupersync — the beating heart of L0 (plan §5.2).

## Scope
- Latency lane: asupersync's native async scheduling for orchestration — ledger I/O, IR interpretation, progress streaming, watchdogs, inter-study coordination. Milliseconds matter, throughput doesn't. Serves HELM's ≤100 ms conversational guarantee even while campaigns saturate compute.
- Throughput lane: work-stealing fork-join pool — per-core Chase–Lev-style deques; CCD-AWARE STEAL ORDER (steal within CCD first, then socket) so working sets stay in their 32 MiB L3 islands; P/E asymmetry handled by per-core-class throughput weights (E-cores take proportionally smaller tile quanta rather than being ignored or stalling joins — weights measured by the autotuner).
- The TileKernel contract (Appendix B): `tiles() -> TilePlan` (geometry decided by autotuner), `run(TileId, &Cx) -> ControlFlow<Cancelled, Out>` with `Out: Reduce` on a FIXED-SHAPE reduction tree. Tiles are the unit of scheduling, cancellation, determinism, and NUMA placement.
- `Cx` carries: cancellation token (poll at tile boundaries; bounded latency-to-cancel ≤200 µs target), tile-scoped bump arena, counter-based RNG stream keyed by (seed, kernel_id, tile_id, iteration) — LOGICAL identity, not thread identity — budget accountant slice, and ledger handle.
- Failure containment: a panicking tile poisons its scope; siblings are cancelled; a structured error with full tile provenance propagates; the study continues or halts per policy — NEVER a process abort mid-campaign (policy per unsafe-safety-cases decision).
- Every unit of work spawns inside an asupersync cancellation scope (P7).

## Why
This is where asupersync's cancel-correctness stops being plumbing and becomes algorithmic leverage: statistical preemption (Bet 8) needs the ≤200 µs reclaim; determinism (P2) needs logical-identity RNG and fixed reductions; NUMA reality (§5.1) needs CCD-aware stealing.

## Acceptance criteria
G4 storm suite green (leaks, deadlocks, containment); cancel-latency p99 ≤200 µs on reference hardware, histogram ledgered; steal-order verified CCD-local-first on fixture topologies; RNG stream independence from worker assignment proven by shuffling worker counts (G5).

## Testing
Deterministic lab-runtime tests for steal/join/cancel protocols + asupersync model checker (via G4 harness). Unit: TilePlan execution completeness, reduction-tree shape stability. Property: arbitrary DAGs of scopes complete or cancel cleanly. Logs: per-scope lifecycle events, steal statistics, latency histograms — all as structured events consumable by the future ledger.

title: fs-exec/fs-rand: bind RNG streams to explicit logical run identity
description:
TilePool derives Cx.iteration from a pool-global AtomicU64 fetch_add. Reusing a pool means a kernel stream key depends on unrelated prior runs; concurrent invocation order changes keys. Tests use fresh pools and miss this. Separately fs-exec StreamKey uses four u64 fields and a lossy mixed key128, while fs-rand exposes seed u64 plus kernel/tile u32 and treats iteration as draw index; there is no typed conversion proving collision or replay semantics.

Root cause: execution order is being used as logical identity, and two crates independently define incompatible stream-key contracts.

Repair: require an explicit caller-ledgered RunId or generation in run APIs; derive per-tile keys solely from study, operation/run, kernel, tile, and declared iteration. Provide one canonical collision-analyzed key type or an explicit checked bridge to fs-rand, with versioned field widths and overflow/refusal rules. Pool scheduling and unrelated work must never perturb streams.

Acceptance: same logical run after arbitrary unrelated/concurrent pool activity is bit-identical; distinct declared runs diverge; worker count and arrival order do not affect keys; conversion collision tests cover truncation boundaries; replay reconstructs keys from ledger fields without hidden mutable state.
close_reason: RNG streams bound to explicit logical run identity - LANDED. (1) TilePool's pool-global AtomicU64 iteration REMOVED: stream keys no longer depend on unrelated prior runs or concurrent invocation order (execution order was being used as logical identity). run/run_with_gate now use the fixed implicit RunId(0); the new run_declared(kernel, gate, RunId) takes the caller-ledgered generation/trial/restart id - keys derive solely from (study seed, kernel id, tile, declared run). tune.rs trials now measure IDENTICAL work per trial (the old per-trial stream drift was unintended). (2) Checked fs-exec->fs-rand bridge (in fs-rand, since layering forbids the reverse dep): StreamKey::from_exec_parts(seed, kernel_id, tile, iteration), bridge v1 (EXEC_KEY_BRIDGE_VERSION), REFUSES rather than truncates - KernelOverflow/TileOverflow past u32 slots, IterationUnrepresentable for iteration!=0 (fs-rand's draw index is a within-stream counter, not identity; teaching Display points at ledgering the generation upstream). ACCEPTANCE MET: conformance test proves same logical run bit-identical after pool reuse + 3 unrelated runs + two CONCURRENT probes + arrival-order swap + worker-count change (4 vs 9); distinct declared runs diverge, same declared run replays; keys reconstruct from ledger fields alone (seed, fnv1a64(kernel), tile, run) with no hidden state; bridge collision tests cover every truncation boundary (2^32 refused, 2^32-1 accepted; the (1<<32)|5 vs 5 alias demonstrated refused). fs-exec 38+14 green, fs-rand suites green, clippy clean. CONTRACTs record the declared-identity invariant + versioned bridge. title: fs-exec: speculative races, resumable/forkable SolverState protocol, statistical-preemption kill handles
description:
## What
The three executor behaviors most HPC runtimes lack and FrankenSim treats as core (plan §5.2): speculative races, resumable solvers, and statistical preemption.

## Scope
- Speculative races with loser-cancellation: spawn N strategies as sibling scopes ("try Delaunay refinement AND octree CutFEM concurrently; first to meet the error budget wins"); the loser's scope is cancelled and its arenas reclaimed in O(1). API: race combinator with budget-aware victory predicates and deterministic tie-breaking (P2 — ties broken by logical index, not arrival).
- Resumable solvers: the `SolverState: Serialize` protocol — Krylov, multigrid, and time-stepping loops as EXPLICIT state machines. A paused solve checkpoints to the Ledger, migrates, resumes, or FORKS (two optimizer branches continuing one warm-started solve — the forkable-worlds enabler). Deterministic-mode invariant: pause-serialize-resume reproduces the uninterrupted trajectory bit-exactly (G4 asserts this).
- Statistical preemption: kill-handle registry — the e-process layer (fs-eproc/e-racing) holds handles to candidate evaluation scope-trees; crossing an elimination threshold cancels the candidate's ENTIRE tree mid-flight; cancel-correctness guarantees no torn state, arena scoping guarantees no leaks, cores reclaim within the ≤200 µs bound. This is Bet 8's machinery.
- Graceful-degradation hooks for the resource governor (fs-session-caps): pause-serialize-resume as a first-class operation ("pause the LES, run the urgent trim study, resume" must be routine, not heroic).

## Acceptance criteria
Race combinator: losers always fully drained (G4-verified), winner's result deterministic across thread counts; a reference iterative solver (from PV skeleton) checkpoints/resumes/forks with bit-exact continuation; kill-handles reclaim a deep scope tree within latency budget under load.

## Testing
G4 storms targeting races mid-flight; property tests on serialize/deserialize round-trips of SolverState; fork-divergence test (two forks with different subsequent inputs stay independent); latency measurements ledgered. Structured logs: race outcomes with per-branch progress at kill time, checkpoint sizes, resume verdicts.

## Strategic note: distribution-readiness (plan §17)
The risk register rates "single-machine bias blocks future scale-out" LOW precisely because of this bead: serializable solver states + content-addressed artifacts + event-sourced sessions are EXACTLY the primitives distribution needs later. Design the SolverState protocol and kill-handle registry so that "migrate" can someday mean "to another machine" without API change (no shared-memory assumptions in the serialized representation; artifact references by content hash, never by pointer).

(1) Speculative races: Racer/RaceBranch with per-branch gates+arenas+stream keys; deterministic victory = lowest-index ACCEPTED result recomputed from outcomes (timing moves when kills land, never who wins — proven identical winner index+bits across 10 jittered repeats, exec-010); early kills (j dies once i<j accepted); Fast mode = first-arrival, recorded; parent-gate watcher folds kill-handles into the whole tree mid-flight; losers fully drained (scope join) with arena quiescence oracle; panics contained per branch; NoWinner is a teaching error with per-branch JSON reports. Deterministic liveness caveat documented (below-leader branches must terminate on own budgets). (2) Resumable solvers: SolverState protocol on an in-house little-endian codec (floats as raw bits; self-contained bytes, no pointers — distribution-ready per §17), ResumableSolver::step bounded pause granularity, drive() where pause IS the cancellation path (governor hook), fork() round-trips through bytes proving serializability; pause-serialize-resume reproduces an uninterrupted CHAOTIC trajectory bit-exactly at depths 1/137/9999 (exec-011) plus Jacobi reference in unit tests; codec rejects truncation+trailing garbage with teaching CodecError. (3) Statistical preemption: KillRegistry (candidate id -> Arc<CancelGate>), idempotent kill, kill_where batch elimination (ascending, deterministic), release; deep candidate tree (1M-tile pool run) killed mid-flight drains quiescent with latency histogram ledgered (exec-012). title: fs-exec: make races panic-total and cancellation trees mandatory
description:
Racer::race_with_gate starts a parent watcher whose completion flag is set only by the last branch. With an empty branch vector the watcher never terminates. The branch body is caught, but the accept predicate runs outside catch_unwind; an accept panic unwinds the worker before filling its slot, so the watcher can again run forever. Direct fs-race consumers also construct empty KillRegistry values and ignore kill(false), allowing claimed cancellation storms to exercise no live evaluation tree.

Root cause: drain completion depends on normal branch epilogues and cancellation wiring is optional convention rather than an owned scope invariant.

Repair: reject empty races before spawning; wrap the full branch plus acceptance and finalization path in an unwind-safe guard that always records a terminal slot and releases the watcher; use structured errors, not hangs. Require candidate registration or return a structured missing-handle error from elimination; wire flagship consumers to gates owned by their actual evaluation scopes.

Acceptance: bounded tests for empty races, accept panic, branch panic, parent cancellation, missing candidate handles, and simultaneous completion; all return without leaks; losing evaluation trees observe cancellation and drain; G4 storm proves nonzero registered kills and quiescent arenas.
close_reason: Races panic-total, cancellation trees mandatory - LANDED. (1) Empty races refused with structured NoWinner (empty reports + teaching Display) BEFORE any spawn - the former path hung the parent watcher forever. (2) The branch body AND the acceptance predicate now run inside one unwind guard (an accept panic used to unwind the worker before its slot write, hanging the watcher); the terminal-slot epilogue (slot write + watcher release) is panic-free by construction. (3) Panic-totality: every Mutex use in race.rs and kill.rs is poison-tolerant (PoisonError::into_inner) - a predicate panic in kill_where can no longer cascade panics through the registry. (4) KillRegistry::kill_registered returns structured UnregisteredKill instead of an ignorable false; exported. title: fs-exec: add a versioned self-authenticating solver snapshot envelope
description:
SolverState::to_bytes writes only implementation-defined payload bytes and from_bytes calls the selected type decoder. There is no magic, solver type id, schema version, payload length, checksum, or semantic provenance. A same-length snapshot from another solver or version can decode successfully into plausible but wrong state, and corruption can evade trailing-byte checks.

Root cause: payload serialization is treated as a distribution-ready artifact without an envelope that identifies and authenticates its schema.

Repair: wrap snapshots in canonical bytes containing magic, envelope version, stable solver/state type id, schema version, payload length, payload checksum/content hash, and required provenance. Validate the envelope before invoking the state decoder; provide explicit migrations or structured incompatible-version refusal.

Acceptance: cross-type same-layout bytes, bit flips, truncation, appended bytes, unknown version, wrong type id, and stale schema all refuse; valid pause-migrate-resume remains bit-exact; fork and ledger paths use the envelope rather than raw payloads.
close_reason: Versioned self-authenticating snapshot envelope LANDED (v1). Canonical layout: magic FSEXSNAP + envelope version u32 + stable state TYPE_ID u64 + payload SCHEMA_VERSION u32 + caller-ledgered provenance u64 + payload length u64 + FNV payload checksum u64, then payload — every header field validated BEFORE the payload decoder runs (envelope::open). SolverState now REQUIRES const TYPE_ID (never reused/changed) and const SCHEMA_VERSION (bumped on any layout change) — the compiler forces every state to declare identity; all three existing impls migrated (JacobiState, ChaoticState, fs-session ToySolver). New seal(provenance)/unseal -> (state, provenance) carry run/ledger identity (pairs with wf9.7.1 RunId); to_bytes/from_bytes are the unattributed convenience over the SAME envelope; fork round-trips enveloped bytes; content_hash covers the envelope. Incompatible schema = structured IncompatibleSchema refusal (the explicit no-migration-yet path). ACCEPTANCE MET (envelope_refuses_every_misbinding_class): cross-type same-layout bytes (TwinState with identical payload layout) refused WrongTypeId; payload bit flip -> ChecksumMismatch; magic flip -> BadMagic; header truncation -> Truncated; payload truncation AND appended bytes -> LengthMismatch; unknown envelope version 9 -> refused; stale schema 7 -> IncompatibleSchema{1,7}; valid seal round-trips bit-exactly WITH provenance (0xABCD preserved); existing pause-serialize-resume bit-exact conformance still green. fs-exec 39+14 green, fs-session 10 green, clippy clean. CONTRACT records the envelope contract.

title: fs-math: deterministic elementary functions, ULP budgets, FMA/subnormal/NaN policy, enclosures
description:
## What
`fs-math`: deterministic elementary functions and the floating-point policy contract (patch Rev O). Deterministic reductions and RNG are NOT enough — full determinism requires a math-function contract.

## Scope
- Deterministic scalar + vector implementations of sin/cos/tan/exp/log/log1p/expm1/sqrt/cbrt/atan2/pow/erf with DECLARED ULP contracts per function, identical results across ISAs in strict mode (no platform libm in deterministic paths).
- Strict vs fast modes mirroring ExecMode: strict = cross-ISA reproducible with documented ULP bounds; fast = platform-optimal, permitted only when the mode is ledgered provenance.
- FMA contraction policy: explicit contract for where FMA is allowed (per-kernel declaration), because contraction differences are a top cross-ISA divergence class (G5 report category).
- Subnormal policy (never flush-to-zero silently; document per-ISA behavior), NaN/infinity propagation policy (payloads not relied upon; canonical NaN on production paths), signed-zero handling.
- Interval-safe helpers: directed next_up/next_down nudging utilities and DECLARED ENCLOSURES for every elementary function so fs-ivl's Taylor models and interval evaluation get rigorous elementary-function bounds (this is what makes interval certificates clean — Rev O).
- ULP Ledger: every kernel declares a ULP budget for its sensitive operations; deterministic mode FORBIDS implementation-defined math paths unless wrapped by fs-math (lintable).

## Why
Cross-platform mismatches from libm/FMA/subnormals are a named risk; and fs-ivl's certificates are only as rigorous as their elementary-function enclosures.

## Acceptance criteria
Each function: ULP bound verified empirically against the double-double oracle across systematic + random + adversarial inputs (billions of samples nightly); bit-identical strict-mode results across NEON/AVX-512 for the committed function set; enclosure property (result ∈ declared enclosure) proven by G0 laws.

## Testing
Exhaustive f32 sweeps where feasible; oracle-sampled f64; special-value tables (±0, subnormals, ±inf, NaN); cross-ISA hash comparison in CI (G5). Logs: per-function max-ULP-observed tables, enclosure violation counts (must be 0).
close_reason: v1 CLOSED with cross-ISA proof; remainder split to fs-math-extensions (created, linked). Delivered: det::{exp,expm1,ln,sin,cos,tanh,sqrt} built from pure IEEE arithmetic; policy doc (FMA contraction forbidden-implicit/encouraged-explicit, subnormals never flushed, canonical NaN, strict-vs-fast); nudge_out/next_up/next_down for fs-ivl; ulp_distance. HEADLINE EVIDENCE: golden hash 0xeb79cab7a01643e5 IDENTICAL on aarch64-apple (M4 Pro) and x86-64 (TR PRO 5995WX) across 175k evaluations — cross-ISA bit-determinism proven empirically, not argued. Measured ULP maxima (budgets): exp 1 (3), expm1 2 (3), ln 1 (3), sin 2 (3), cos 2 (3), tanh 3 (5), both ISAs. THREE REAL BUGS found+killed by the test discipline en route, each now a regression test: decimal-rendered Cody-Waite constants losing exact trailing zeros (184 ULP); Taylor cores two terms short (166 ULP at |r|=pi/4); tanh oddness by-luck-not-construction (now sign-applied-to-magnitude). 4-part pi/2 reduction (fdlibm bit patterns) fixed the x=pi near-zero 7-10 ULP cases. NO-CLAIMS: |x|>2^20 trig (Payne-Hanek in extension bead), 0.5-ULP correct rounding, remaining function families. 13 tests green locally + on trj, clippy clean.

title: Constellation drift is live on ALL SEVEN siblings while its owning bead f85xj.13.4 sits CLOSED
description:
BACKGROUND. On 2026-07-28 scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --verify-only REFUSED on ALL SEVEN constellation siblings. Every one is off its constellation.lock pin:

  asupersync        expected 5973b0ff31f4  actual f13fd9f58558
  franken_networkx  expected 4e72da0f0c98  actual b1cc48fe9fcc
  franken_numpy     expected 7fca9f6006c9  actual e5d6405b6ab8
  frankenpandas     expected 803efc1c6dae  actual fd7099458678
  frankenscipy      expected 9e271fd73446  actual 85ffd81bd51e
  frankensqlite     expected 987cfb97f86d  actual 951d9381c5d1
  frankentorch      expected f00c3ce79737  actual 5fdca1bfabae

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS NOT THE DRIFT. It is that frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.13.4 ("Cross-repo compatibility suite + release-train policy: sibling bumps become tested events") is CLOSED, marked done 2026-07-25, while the condition it exists to prevent is live and total. A closed governance bead with a violated condition is strictly worse than an open one, because closure removes it from every triage view. Nobody is watching.

This is a recurrence, not a first occurrence: the identical all-seven-off-pin state was observed in an earlier session, where the finding was that the aggregate lock hash hides WHICH sibling drifted. So a one-time sweep demonstrably does not hold. Whatever 13.4 delivered, it did not survive contact with normal multi-agent operation.

WHY IT MATTERS OPERATIONALLY. AGENTS.md makes this preflight authoritative precisely because sibling drift "breaks this workspace in ways that surface as unrelated compile errors" -- an agent burns hours blaming its own crate. There is a recorded prior incident of exactly this failure mode (a repo-wide cargo death that blamed frankensqlite when the real cause was asupersync off its pin). The drift is also currently INVISIBLE to anyone who does not run the preflight by hand, because local builds may succeed against drifted siblings while remote RCH workers build against their own checkouts entirely.

WHAT.
(a) Determine whether the seven current heads are a legitimate advance (the constellation moved and the lock is stale) or genuine drift (the lock is right and checkouts wandered). These need OPPOSITE remedies and the distinction is the whole job. Do NOT move a shared sibling checkout back to its pin to make the preflight green -- AGENTS.md forbids it; pin movement must follow constellation governance and the compatibility train.
(b) Make the condition STANDING rather than swept: the preflight result must be a checked artifact that goes red on drift, in the same idiom as the other check-all gates, so this cannot silently re-rot.
(c) Record why 13.4's release-train policy did not hold, and either reopen it or supersede it explicitly. Closing this bead while leaving 13.4 closed-and-violated repeats the original error.

DONE WHEN: the seven heads are reconciled with a recorded decision (advance vs drift, per sibling); a standing gate makes future drift visible without a hand-run script; and 13.4's status honestly reflects whether its policy is in force.

TESTS: a falsifier that moves one sibling off-pin and proves the gate goes red naming THAT sibling (not just an aggregate hash mismatch -- the prior finding was specifically that an aggregate hash hides which one drifted).
close_reason: Standing drift-classification gate landed in check-all (xtask constellation_drift.rs, 10/10 falsifiers via RCH), per-sibling advance decision recorded and rendered continuously, f85xj.13.4 superseded explicitly into frankensim-i4hh6, sibling debris findings filed as frankensim-osxyv. Full clause-by-clause evidence in bead comments.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CLAUSE (a) DISCHARGED WITH EVIDENCE, 2026-07-29 (NobleLion). The bead asked whether the seven off-pin heads are a legitimate ADVANCE (the constellation moved, the lock is stale) or genuine DRIFT (the lock is right, checkouts wandered), and noted these need opposite remedies. Measured, per sibling, by asking git whether the pinned commit is an ancestor of the live HEAD:

  sibling            relation                    ahead  behind  dirty
  asupersync         ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)     611       0     no
  franken_networkx   ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)     599       0     no
  franken_numpy      ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)     456       0     no
  frankenpandas      ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)     500       0     no
  frankenscipy       ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)     568       0     no
  frankensqlite      ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)     525       0     no
  frankentorch       ADVANCE (pin is ancestor)      25       0     no

ANSWER: all seven are STRICT FAST-FORWARDS. The pin is an ancestor of HEAD in every case, every sibling is zero commits behind, and none has a dirty worktree. This is not drift at all.

WHY THAT INVERTS THE REMEDY. The refusal text from checkout_constellation.sh reads 'existing checkout is incomplete, drifted, dirty, or unreadable', which invites the conclusion that the checkouts are wrong and should be moved back. They are not wrong: they are clean and strictly newer. constellation.lock is STALE. The correct remedy is to ADVANCE THE LOCK through the compatibility train and constellation governance, not to move any checkout -- which AGENTS.md forbids anyway, and which would in this case be actively destructive, discarding between 25 and 611 commits of legitimate sibling progress per repository.

A SECOND FINDING WORTH ACTING ON. The preflight can tell you WHICH sibling mismatches (it prints expected and actual per sibling), but nothing in the toolchain tells you WHETHER a mismatch is a fast-forward or a divergence. That is the single fact that selects the remedy, and it is exactly the fact no gate reports. A future standing gate for clause (b) should classify, not merely compare: 'off-pin, fast-forward, N ahead' and 'off-pin, DIVERGED' must be visibly different verdicts, because only the second is an incident.

WHAT THIS EXPLAINS. Local cargo builds and remote RCH builds have both been succeeding against these advanced siblings all week, which is consistent with a compatible fast-forward and would be surprising under real drift. It also means the recorded historical incident (a repo-wide cargo death that blamed frankensqlite when asupersync was off its pin) was a DIFFERENT condition from today's, and today's should not be diagnosed by analogy to it.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD: clause (b), a standing gate that classifies rather than compares; and clause (c), the disposition of f85xj.13.4, which remains CLOSED. Note that (c) now reads differently too: 13.4's release-train policy did not fail to prevent drift -- there was no drift. What is missing is a mechanism to advance the lock as siblings legitimately move, which is a release-train GAP rather than a release-train VIOLATION.

DECISION NEEDED FROM THE OWNER: advancing the lock to seven new heads is a constellation-governance event with a compatibility-train obligation, not a mechanical edit. It is deliberately not being done here. This comment supplies the evidence that the decision is now unblocked and that the safe direction is forward, not backward.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CLAUSE (b) LANDED (HazyFortress, 2026-07-29): standing gate xtask check-constellation-drift, wired into check-all (module xtask/src/constellation_drift.rs). Per-sibling classification: on-pin (ok) / fast-forward (stale-lock, VISIBLE but NOT red — remedy is the train, not a checkout move) / retreated / diverged / dirty (all red, drift) / missing-or-shallow-or-pin-absent (NO-DATA, never silently counted). Red verdicts name the sibling and print expected+actual heads, fixing the aggregate-hash defect this bead cites. Falsifier suite 10/10 green via RCH (cargo test -p xtask constellation_drift): retreated, diverged, and dirty fixtures each go red naming asupersync with both heads; the fast-forward fixture stays NOT-red; corrupt/empty/partial lock input refuses closed rather than reporting zero drift. Live classification re-measured with the gate's exact probe sequence: all seven siblings remain pin-present, non-shallow, clean strict fast-forwards (asupersync +643, franken_networkx +606, franken_numpy +463, frankenpandas +519, frankenscipy +586, frankensqlite +549, frankentorch +28; all advanced since the morning measurement). Expected live verdict: 0 violations, 7 stale-lock notes; end-to-end binary proof running.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CLOSING EVIDENCE (HazyFortress, 2026-07-29). DONE-WHEN clause by clause:
(1) 'seven heads reconciled with a recorded decision, per sibling' — MET. NobleLion's clause-(a) measurement (all seven strict fast-forwards) is canonized in the gate itself: check-constellation-drift now renders the advance-vs-drift decision per sibling on every check-all run. Live re-measurement with the gate's exact probes: all seven pins present, non-shallow, fast-forward (+28..+643), so per-sibling decision = ADVANCE for all seven; the lock, not the checkouts, must move (owner: successor frankensim-i4hh6). The same run surfaced four deep-cleanliness findings invisible to git status — filed as frankensim-osxyv (franken_numpy tracked-file raw mismatch; untracked-.gitignore debris in frankentorch/frankenpandas/franken_networkx), explicitly outside frankensim-side remediation authority.
(2) 'standing gate makes future drift visible without a hand-run script' — MET. check-constellation-drift is a check-all member: per-sibling ok / stale-lock (visible, NOT red) / drift (red: dirty, retreated, diverged, observation-refused, head-moved-mid-observation) / NO-DATA (missing, shallow, pin-absent). Red verdicts name the sibling and print expected AND actual heads — the aggregate-hash defect is gone. Documented in docs/CI_GATES.md gate table and AGENTS.md preflight section. Lane-isolated via check-all --only constellation-drift.
(3) '13.4 status honestly reflects whether its policy is in force' — MET without reopening: supersession recorded on f85xj.13.4 (suite/gate artifacts exist and pass; the missing half was TRIGGER+VISIBILITY, now owned by i4hh6 and this gate respectively); successor frankensim-i4hh6 created (run the train now; cadence trigger/owner/runbook).
TESTS — the bead's named falsifier and more: cargo test -p xtask constellation_drift, 10/10 green via RCH. retreated/diverged/dirty fixtures each go red NAMING asupersync with expected+actual heads; fast-forward stays NOT-red (the false-red that invited the destructive remedy); missing siblings are NO-DATA (not pass, not drift); corrupt/empty/partial lock refuses closed.

title: Euler-disc emergent-prediction flagship: blinded geometry, contact, base, air, and V&V
description:
## Background and purpose

Create a compact but scientifically demanding FrankenSim flagship around an Euler-style spinning disc: an axisymmetric squat metal body with a parameterized true fillet/chamfer, optional cone or annular mass distribution, rolling and slipping contact on a shallow supported base, structural compliance, surface losses, and surrounding air. The challenge is to predict held-out trajectory regimes and counterintuitive trends reported in spinning-disc experiments without encoding those outcomes into special-case rules.

This is not a toy animation and not a request to fit one stopping time. It is a staged verification, validation, and model-discrimination program that exercises FrankenSim's core mission: typed geometry and units, constrained dynamics, contact and tribology, flexible structures, moving-boundary flow, uncertainty, deterministic replay, provenance, cancellation, and evidence-qualified claims.

## Binding definition of emergent prediction

General conservation laws, constitutive equations, geometry, independently measured material/interface/environment properties, and parameters calibrated on disjoint coupon or apparatus-characterization data are permitted. Target spin trajectories, claimed rankings, the alleged approximately 1 mm edge optimum, and target-specific per-specimen loss coefficients are forbidden during model construction and calibration. Any use of target outcomes for tuning changes the result class to calibrated reproduction and must invalidate the emergent-prediction claim.

The Steve Mould transcript and related literature are hypothesis sources only. They are not validation data for this apparatus. The campaign must treat air drag, finite-patch rolling/contour loss, sliding or microslip, adhesion, plasticity, viscoelastic hysteresis, base vibration, runout-driven impacts, and contact loss as rival or interacting mechanisms whose applicability is tested. Matching a power-law exponent or final time alone does not identify a mechanism.

## User outcomes

The flagship must let a user define or ingest:
- disc outer radius, thickness, true fillet and/or chamfer geometry, face profile, annulus/insert layout, density field, runout, coating, and roughness;
- base material, thickness, shallow curvature, finish, housing, feet/support geometry, leveling, stiffness, damping, and modal data;
- atmosphere, pressure, gas identity, temperature, humidity, and optional venting;
- complete initial pose and twist with uncertainty, not only a nominal hand-spin speed;
- explicit model ladder, budgets, validity predicates, seeds, capabilities, and requested QoIs.

It must produce full trajectory distributions and refusal states for inclination, precession, body spin, nutation, centre/contact orbit, contact mode, base motion, energy channels, terminal event, stopping time, crossover, rankings, effect directions, and any optimum interval. Every result must retain numerical, parameter, model-form, experimental, and extrapolation boundaries.

## Architecture and ownership

This epic orchestrates existing generic infrastructure instead of duplicating it. Generic rigid multibody dynamics remain owned by fs-mbd work; reusable detection and response by fs-contact; friction/contact-patch/film laws by fs-tribo and fs-material; geometry and certified queries by fs-geom/fs-rep-*/fs-query; flexible base mechanics by fs-solid/fs-mbd adapters; flow by fs-flux/fs-lbm; typed coupling and energy accounting by fs-couple; experiment/DAQ/V&V schemas by their existing campaign, evidence, and registry work. A future fs-euler-disc-e2e crate may own only domain composition, fixtures, reports, and user-facing campaign semantics.

Do not add Euler cases to the exact-membership E2 phase manifest. This flagship owns a separate versioned campaign manifest and consumes the shared runner.

## Workstreams

1. Scientific contract, Context of Use, hypotheses, preregistration, blindness, and model escalation.
2. Axisymmetric geometry, certified support/mass properties, material and interface identities.
3. Rigid constrained dynamics, contact, tribology, impacts, energy closure, and deterministic state.
4. Flexible base/support mechanics and wobble/escape behavior.
5. Reduced and resolved air models with moving-boundary coupling and ablations.
6. Specimen/rig/launcher/DAQ design, raw evidence, trajectory extraction, and physical execution.
7. Prediction freezing, uncertainty, scoring, identifiability, model discrepancy, and adjudication.
8. Unit/property/metamorphic/mutation tests, no-mock E2E, artifact-only replay, reports, DSR, and honest maturity gates.

## Scientific and product no-claims

- Geometric similarity does not imply dynamic similarity when contact, roughness, adhesion, viscosity, yield, or base modes matter.
- A fitted contour-resistance law is not microscopic emergence.
- A deterministic replay, conservation check, software E2E, or DSR pass is not physical validation.
- A successful blind case validates only the exact declared apparatus, population, environment, QoIs, and validity domain.
- A failed, refused, or inconclusive blind prediction is a valid terminal campaign outcome and must remain visible.
- Promotion is optional. The campaign is complete when its immutable result and authority state are honestly adjudicated, including a typed no-promotion result.

## Evidence, tests, and logging doctrine

Every implementation leaf must include proportionate unit tests plus boundary/error/refusal cases. Physics leaves add analytic, manufactured, limiting, metamorphic, refinement, and independent-oracle tests. Stateful/concurrent leaves add cancellation, fault, drain/finalize, checkpoint, resume, and deterministic replay tests. Authority-bearing leaves add hostile twins, mutation tests, tamper/leakage tests, and artifact-only independent checking.

Logs and retained receipts must be schema-versioned, deterministic, bounded, redacted, and content-addressed. They include case/specimen/model/schema/source identities; units, frames, seeds and budgets; admitted regimes and capabilities; step/event/contact/iteration counts; energy/work/impulse and numerical-defect ledgers; expected and observed QoIs or disposition; first divergence and stable reason code; cancellation/drain/finalization; relative artifact paths; evidence/no-claim state; and exact reproduction command. They exclude secrets, absolute paths, PIDs, memory addresses, unbounded dumps, and wall-clock noise from canonical identity.

The exact required phase-rollup set is frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.1, .2, .3, .4, .5, .6, .7, and .8; the root hard-depends on every one. Each rollup separately enumerates its exact direct children and has an executable terminal leaf, so parent prose, partial child closure, or aggregate percentage cannot substitute for evidence.

The reusable generic prerequisites are tracked in frankensim-b8bxd and frankensim-jmh21 and are related here because their individual Euler leaves carry exact hard dependencies. Optional physical maturity promotion is isolated under frankensim-16dip and is not a root child or root closure requirement.

The root closes only after all eight required rollups close, all their blocking dependencies are satisfied, and an independent graph/evidence audit confirms that no required leaf, failed prediction, refusal, censored run, no-data state, or no-claim boundary was omitted. A rollup may close after its explicitly permitted adverse scientific disposition; it may not waive missing execution or evidence.

Campaign success is not defined as reproducing the video's rankings. A blind failure, inconclusive result, or principled refusal can complete the scientific objective if protocol, custody, execution, scoring, independent replay, adverse-result retention, and next-evidence plan are complete. L3 software maturity and L4 physical promotion are distinct; the root may close with an explicit no-promotion outcome. No transcript value, static fixture, local hygiene check, producer status, or attractive visualization may mint physical or mechanism authority.

title: ED-1 Scientific contract, preregistration, blindness, and model-escalation policy
description:
## Purpose

Freeze the scientific question before implementation or target-outcome inspection. This workstream defines the Context of Use, user decisions, claim taxonomy, rival mechanisms, observables, terminal events, scores, calibration permissions, blind partitions, model freeze, and fidelity-escalation rules for the Euler-disc campaign.

## Required content

The contract separates numerical verification, calibrated reproduction, blind physical prediction, mechanism attribution, ranking, optimum localization, and maturity promotion. It defines target QoIs over complete trajectories rather than treating total spin time as sufficient. It distinguishes ordinary stop, contact loss, slip, micro-impact, wandering/escape, boundary collision, saturation, cancellation, refusal, and censored/incomplete runs.

The protocol treats contact/contour loss, finite-patch microslip, elastic or viscoelastic hysteresis, adhesion, localized plasticity, base vibration, runout-driven impacts, and air-gap/boundary-layer loss as competing or interacting model families. It records literature versions and assumptions without inheriting authority from publication. Air dominance, a universal edge-radius optimum, glass superiority, cone/ring rankings, and scale crossover are hypotheses, not encoded facts.

## Parallelism and ownership

This workstream may proceed immediately and should unblock geometry, solver, rig, and analysis work. It consumes existing generic ContextOfUse, ExperimentCampaignIr, V&V, blindness, and evidence schemas rather than creating parallel ones. Authority-bearing sealing depends on the existing access/custody infrastructure; descriptive protocol work must not wait on that broad implementation.

## Done means

A versioned, immutable protocol and adversarial review define permitted inputs, forbidden leakage, factors and aliases, QoIs and scores, applicability/refusal rules, model hierarchy, promotion boundaries, and one-way unlock semantics. Revisions after seal mint a new protocol identity and preserve the old one.

title: Register Euler-disc hypotheses, rival mechanisms, primary sources, and theorem-status boundaries
description:
## Background

Euler-disc dissipation remains regime- and apparatus-dependent. Published models variously emphasize whole-gap viscosity, oscillatory air boundary layers, rolling/contour resistance, slip, contact deformation, vibration, or impacts. Literature informs hypotheses but cannot validate this campaign by citation.

## Scope

Add exact-version registry entries for the principal analytic and experimental sources used by the campaign, including Moffatt's asymptotic air model, rolling/slipping/contact studies, finite-time/contact-loss or imperfection studies, and the March 2026 air-drag preprint. Retain source type, version/date/hash/locator/license, model equations, assumptions, measured configurations, QoIs, reported uncertainty/repeats, and explicit transfer limitations.

Define rival mechanism cards for ideal conservative rolling; phenomenological dry and viscous contour moments; finite-patch elastic/viscoelastic/plastic/adhesive loss; tangential microslip/creep and gross slip; base modal loss; runout/contact-loss impacts; bulk drag; wedge/thin-gap flow; and oscillatory boundary layer. Each card states observables and orthogonal interventions that could falsify or distinguish it.

## No-claims

Do not encode video rankings or an approximately 1 mm optimum as expected truth. Do not treat a preprint as consensus, a fitted power law as mechanism identity, or a paper's material/surface result as transferable to different finish, support, gas, load, or scale.

Closure requires version-pinned registry rows and mechanism cards that fail closed when source, equation revision, assumption, validity domain, or evidence class is missing. Tests must prove citation names alone cannot authorize a model; source-version or assumption changes move identity; and an exponent-only observation cannot select a unique mechanism.

## Required verification and evidence

The implementation must include focused unit tests for happy, empty, malformed, boundary, maximum, maximum-plus-one, unit/frame, canonicalization, deterministic-order, and refusal cases that apply. Add property/metamorphic and mutation tests for every semantic identity, validity, leakage, scoring, budget, evidence, and no-claim guard. Any admitted long-running work is cancellation-correct and publishes no partial authority.

Retained logs are schema-versioned, deterministic, bounded, redacted, and content-addressed. They identify protocol/case/source/schema, units, seeds, budgets, expected and observed disposition, first divergence, authority/no-claim state, relative artifacts, and reproduction command. Focused software proof, DSR, blind physical evidence, and maturity promotion are separate gates.
