title: Freeze Euler-disc QoIs, state and terminal events, analysis windows, scores, and multiplicity
description:
## Background

Total spin time is severely non-identifying and can silently merge different terminal events. Predeclare what is measured and scored before inspecting target outcomes.

## Scope

Define primary and secondary time-series QoIs: inclination, precession phase/rate, body spin, nutation, COM/contact orbit, contact creep/slip estimate, base displacement/velocity/mode energy, environmental state, and channel-wise mechanical/thermal loss. Define event types and uncertainty for ordinary rest, contact loss, micro-impact, gross slip, mode transition, wandering/escape, boundary collision, saturation, aborted run, incomplete/censored run, and extrapolated mathematical collapse.

Specify operational start/stop definitions, transient and asymptotic windows, filters and phase-delay treatment, missingness/censoring, practical-effect thresholds, proper trajectory/interval scores, event-time metrics, empirical coverage, ranking/optimum metrics, multiplicity, preregistered group-sequential or anytime-valid stopping rules with matching inference, prohibition of unplanned outcome-driven stopping, exclusion rules, and sensitivity analyses. Define how physically distinct runs remain distinct in the scorecard.

## Deliverables

Versioned QoI/event/metric specifications bound to the Context of Use; machine-checkable dimensional and frame semantics; canonical ordering and identities; and an intentionally adverse fixture where favorable window selection or outcome merging is refused.

## QoI authority classes

Classify every QoI as RawObserved, MeasurementDerived { measurement_equation_id, covariance }, ProxyBacked { proxy_id, validity }, LatentModelDiagnostic, or Unavailable { reason }. Inclination, phase/rate, body spin, nutation, COM/contact orbit, and instrumented base/environment channels may be scored only under declared measurement authority. Contact creep/slip, mode energy, and channel-wise mechanical/thermal loss are latent by default and cannot receive observation scores without a preregistered measurement equation or validated proxy.

Optional discriminating observations include contact load/patch, support reaction/base mobility, and gap pressure/air traction. Absent instrumentation yields typed Unavailable, never an inferred observation. Prediction-stage artifacts cannot contain target outcomes or decoded blind labels; observation artifacts cannot contain prediction-derived latent values; authorized post-unlock adjudication performs the only join.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires dimensional checks and independent reconstruction for every derived QoI/metric, positive and censored event fixtures, simultaneous/grazing/Unknown cases, filter/window mutations, missing-attempt detection, multiplicity and stopping-policy tests, and proof that no single spin-time field can erase terminal-event class.

## Required verification and evidence

The implementation must include focused unit tests for happy, empty, malformed, boundary, maximum, maximum-plus-one, unit/frame, canonicalization, deterministic-order, and refusal cases that apply. Add property/metamorphic and mutation tests for every semantic identity, validity, leakage, scoring, budget, evidence, and no-claim guard. Any admitted long-running work is cancellation-correct and publishes no partial authority.

Retained logs are schema-versioned, deterministic, bounded, redacted, and content-addressed. They identify protocol/case/source/schema, units, seeds, budgets, expected and observed disposition, first divergence, authority/no-claim state, relative artifacts, and reproduction command. Focused software proof, DSR, blind physical evidence, and maturity promotion are separate gates.

Adversarial fixtures must distinguish valid preregistered anytime/group-sequential monitoring from outcome-driven optional stopping with ordinary fixed-sample inference.

Mutation tests reject latent-to-observed promotion, missing measurement equation/covariance, proxy-domain escape, score over Unavailable, target content in prediction-stage logs, and prediction-derived latent values presented as observations. Independent reconstruction covers every measurement-derived QoI.

title: ED-2 Digital specimen: axisymmetric geometry, mass properties, materials, and interface identity
description:
## Purpose

Create the evidence-bearing digital specimen used by mechanics, flow, optimization, fabrication, and experiment. The current generic F-rep blend is a useful design lever but is not a certified machining fillet, and rounded Boolean composites lose exact-distance authority. This workstream supplies a physically meaningful axisymmetric solid and the queries needed without laundering those limitations.

## Scope

Represent a finite squat disc through a meridional profile with outer radius, thickness, true circular fillet, optional straight chamfer, face cone/profile, annulus or inserts, coatings, runout, and roughness descriptors. External shape and internal density distribution are independent so matched counterfactuals can vary mass, inertia, aerodynamics, and contact shape deliberately.

Provide typed-SI parameter binding, canonical semantic identity, frame and transform rules, exact or certified support/normal/curvature information, analytic or interval mass/COM/inertia, contact-accurate conversion with retained error, scenario/DesignChart integration, and material/interface cards with uncertainty, validity, source, lot, finish, medium, environment, and history.

## No-claims

An R-function blend radius is not a physical fillet radius. A faceted mesh is not contact-accurate merely because it is manifold. Unit-density geometric moments are not material mass properties. Catalog material names do not determine surface loss. Static topology certificates do not validate dynamic contact.

## Done means

Every solver and experimental specimen can bind to one canonical digital-specimen identity; closed-form primitives and independent reconstructions verify its geometry and inertia; all approximation errors and unsupported cases refuse or remain explicitly Estimated; downstream contact and flow consumers never infer stronger geometry authority than supplied.

## Exact implementation ownership

Euler-specific schema and adapters live only in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/geometry.rs and crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/specimen.rs, with positive/negative integration coverage in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/tests/geometry_contract.rs and specimen_binding.rs. Reusable chart/query/moment/conversion behavior belongs to frankensim-b8bxd.1 through .4 in fs-rep-frep, fs-query, and MORPH. Material cards remain fs-matdb; actual spatial inertia remains fs-mbd. No lower-layer crate may depend on fs-euler-disc-e2e.
acceptance_criteria: The exact direct-child set is frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.2.1 through frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.2.11. The rollup has one hard terminal dependency on .2.10, whose integrated conformance battery consumes the admitted line/arc profile grammar, independent upper/lower edge semantics, certified nominal and registered-as-built queries/conversion errors, fixed-topology finite crown chart, unit-density moments, material/interface cards, separated SpecimenControl and LaunchProtocol identities, full spatial inertia assembly, and refusals. title: Freeze the axisymmetric disc/base profile semantics and admissible design families
description:
## Background

The campaign needs one explicit geometric vocabulary for squat discs, rings, center-thick cones or crowns, rounded and chamfered edges, bores, and shallowly curved bases. A loose "smooth chamfer" parameter is insufficient: it hides topology changes, non-smooth joins, unit errors, and contact-feature ambiguity.

## Deliverable

Specify a body-fixed axis and frame, SI units, orientation, material side, signed-distance convention, topology and feature identities, and a piecewise meridian made from admitted line and circular-arc segments. Cover a solid disc, annulus, optional bore, flat or center-thick profile, true circular fillet, explicit straight chamfer, base thickness, and shallow axisymmetric dish. Define exactly which parameters are independent, how face/edge/bore features are named, and deterministic tie rules at equal-distance features.

Declare admissibility inequalities for positive dimensions, non-self-intersection, fillet fit, C0/C1 joins, minimum reach, convexity when requested, and fixed-topology derivative domains. Distinguish nominal design geometry, as-built metrology, and derived collision geometry. Generic splines and unbounded or self-intersecting meridians are refused rather than inheriting exact-distance authority.

## Integration and no-claims

Extend the existing MORPH parameterization and quantity contracts; do not create a second geometry algebra. A nominal profile is not a manufacturing certificate, and geometric similarity alone is not dynamic similarity.

## Opposite-edge semantics

The body has independently identified upper_outer_edge and lower_outer_edge features. Each carries its own fillet or chamfer family and dimensions; an explicit symmetry constraint may equate them but is never assumed. Geometry preserves body-face orientation, while scenario binding records which edge is initially presented to the base.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires a versioned schema and independent validator with fixtures for every admitted family and every inequality boundary. Unit tests cover zero/negative/NaN/infinite and maximum values, fillet-versus-chamfer distinction, bore closure, C0/C1 joins, feature naming, canonical ordering, and deterministic equal-feature ties. Property tests cover rigid-frame and unit rescaling invariance; mutation tests prove every topology, parameter, unit, frame, and feature field changes identity. Malformed, self-intersecting, topology-changing, and unsupported spline inputs return structured refusal without partial geometry. Logs are bounded, deterministic, content-addressed, and include schema/profile identity, units, budgets, disposition, first failing invariant, and reproduction command.

Fixtures cover equal and unequal upper/lower radii, admitted fillet/chamfer mixtures, body inversion, contacted-edge identity, optional symmetry enforcement, and mutation of either edge without aliasing. Identical dimensions with opposite contacted-edge orientation remain distinguishable.

Property, metamorphic, and mutation tests exercise every semantic identity and authority guard. Long work is budgeted and cancellation-correct with request-drain-finalize and no partial publication. title: Bind Euler line/arc profiles to the generic certified ExactDistance chart
description:
## Background and ownership

Contact needs global exact-distance authority, but that reusable theorem belongs to frankensim-b8bxd.1 in fs-rep-frep. This Euler leaf owns only the binding in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/geometry.rs and tests in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/tests/geometry_contract.rs.

## Deliverable

Map every admitted Euler disc/base meridian and feature identity into the generic validated axisymmetric chart. Preserve frame, axis, orientation, topology, source-profile identity, units, tolerance/error budget, and construction-certificate reference. Expose distance, closest-point, normal/gradient availability, active feature, deterministic equal-minimum set, trace-value enclosure, and evaluation receipt without reimplementing minimization.

Exercise solid discs, annuli/bores, cones/frusta/crowns, circular fillets, straight chamfers, shallow base dishes, axis points, seams, grazing equal minima, medial sets, and machine-scale limits. At nonunique or nonsmooth locations, propagate gradient None or typed set-valued information; never choose a favorable normal. Unsupported profiles refuse before ExactDistance is exposed.

## No-claims

The adapter certifies neither as-built dimensions, arbitrary converted geometry, CCD, nor dynamics. Conversion never strengthens its source.

## Contacted-edge preservation

The binding preserves upper/lower edge feature identity, body-face orientation, optional symmetry receipt, and contacted-edge orientation through construction, queries, ties, and reflection/inversion. A chart that aliases opposite unequal edges is incompatible.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires independent high-precision meridian-distance comparisons for discs, annuli, cones/frusta, fillets, chamfers, bores, axis and seam cases; analytic witnesses for simple cylinders and tori-like fillet segments; and adversarial near-tie, near-axis, near-tangent, scale-extreme, malformed, and self-intersecting cases. Tests verify inside/outside signs, closest-point reconstruction, unit normals away from declared singularities, deterministic minima, C1 fillet tangency, cancellation latency, budget exhaustion, and no partial certificate on refusal. Metamorphic tests cover rigid transforms, reflection where allowed, and unit scaling. Logs identify profile/query identity, authority, residual/bounds, active feature, tie rule, budgets, and first divergence.

The binding must reject a generic chart whose certificate/profile/frame/feature set does not exactly match the Euler profile. Tests must prove no per-query authority upgrade and no arbitrary normal at nonunique minima.

Add same-body opposite-edge query/contact twins, unequal upper/lower radii, mixed admitted edge families, inversion, reflection with orientation update, and hostile swapped-edge certificates. Bounds and active-feature identity must follow the physically presented edge.

Canonical adapter output and retained query receipts must replay byte-for-byte under identical logical inputs and thread counts. The geometry E2E uses the production chart/query route, records bounded per-feature diagnostics, and rejects a replay whose active-edge, tie set, enclosure, authority, or first-divergence field changes.

title: Bind generic certified support, curvature, reach, and gap queries to Euler features
description:
## Background and ownership

Finite-patch contact needs more than scalar distance, while global query proofs belong to frankensim-b8bxd.2 in fs-query. This leaf binds those receipts to Euler feature and uncertainty semantics in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/geometry.rs.

## Deliverable

Route convex support, support_slack, interior point, contained-ball radius, normal/curvature/reach sets, singular neighborhoods, exact-distance pointwise gap, motion/conversion inflation, and active feature attribution through the generic capability. Convexity is an admitted profile property; annuli and other nonconvex cases refuse convex/GJK authority rather than returning a hull. Curvature at axes and joins remains interval/set-valued/unavailable. Dense sampled inequalities never certify a global bound.

ImplicitGapOracle is pointwise only and cannot be reported as moving-pair separation, no-tunneling, contact evolution, or CCD evidence. Preserve source and checker identities through every adapter.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires support-inequality witnesses over dense and adversarial directions, independent normal/curvature checks on analytic line/arc segments, gap-oracle checks against high-precision minimization, and explicit nonconvex-annulus refusal twins. Tests cover fillet joins, flat and zero-curvature limits, bore/outer-edge ambiguity, feature transitions, conversion-error inflation, rigid transforms, positive scaling, deterministic ties, cancellation, and budget exhaustion. Mutation tests show removing an error bound, convexity proof, feature identity, or validity domain prevents authoritative routing. Structured logs retain query/capability identity, bounds, active feature, authority, budgets, and reproduction information.

Tests include extrema between samples, false-convexity, zero direction, unsupported contained-ball radius, axis/join nonuniqueness, and an attempted pointwise-gap-to-CCD promotion.

title: Implement the fixed-topology axisymmetric DesignChart and derivative actions
description:
## Background

Systematic studies require typed design variables rather than hand-edited geometry. Derivatives are meaningful only within a fixed admitted topology and away from contact-feature switches.

## Deliverable

Implement the existing DesignChart contract for outer radius, body thickness, center-thick cone/crown coefficients, fillet radius, straight-chamfer dimensions, bore radius, base curvature, and base thickness. Define bounds, units, canonical order, projection/refusal semantics, parameter-to-profile construction, and Jacobian/Jacobian-transpose actions for geometry outputs whose derivatives are valid.

Record non-differentiable branch sets: topology/family changes, vanishing features, active closest-feature changes, impact, stick/slip, and contact loss. These return typed nonsmooth or unavailable derivative status; no smoothing is silently introduced.

## No-claims

This leaf supplies geometric parameter derivatives, not end-to-end adjoints through nonsmooth mechanics or evidence that an optimized design is physically superior.

## Exact API and derivative boundary

Own a campaign-specific ProfileDesignChart in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/geometry.rs, distinct from fs_xform::Parameterization spatial warps. Separate disc and base charts map bounded design coordinates to admitted profile values and provide Jv/J-transpose actions for declared observables. Derivatives are valid only on fixed-topology smooth branches; fillet/chamfer changes, active-set ties, projection, and constraint boundaries return nonsmooth or changed-authority receipts. Projection is explicit and changes identity rather than silently clipping.

## Finite crown basis and separate edges

Use a versioned finite crown-coordinate basis with an explicit constructor into frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.2.1's admitted fixed line/circular-arc topology. Reject coefficients that cannot prove the same topology and required C0/C1 joins; no free spline is admitted. Expose separate upper/lower fillet or chamfer coordinates plus an optional symmetry-constrained subchart.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires round-trip parameter/profile tests, boundary and maximum-plus-one refusal cases, unit correctness, deterministic parameter ordering, and independent centered finite-difference or complex-step comparisons away from declared branch sets. Adjoint dot-product tests cover every derivative action. Property tests cover scale/frame transformations and projection idempotence. Hostile twins cross a topology or active-feature boundary and must demote/refuse derivative authority. Cancellation and budget tests prove no partially authoritative chart. Logs include chart/profile identity, parameter units, active bounds/branches, residuals, budgets, and reproduction command.

Compile and runtime tests distinguish the new parameter-to-profile API from fs_xform spatial warps and verify disc/base non-confusability, Jv/J-transpose duality on smooth branches, projection identity change, and nonsmooth refusal.

Jv/J-transpose and independent derivative checks cover both edge coordinates and the symmetry-constrained chart. Changing crown family, line/arc segment count, edge finish family, or active feature returns changed-topology/nonsmooth status rather than derivative authority.

title: Bind Euler profile families to generic method-aware geometric-moment enclosures
description:
## Background and ownership

Mass-distribution comparisons require unit-density geometry moments, but the reusable analytic/interval implementation belongs to frankensim-b8bxd.3 in fs-query. This leaf owns Euler-family bindings in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/geometry.rs.

## Deliverable

Request method-aware outward enclosures for volume, first raw moments, second raw moments, and the explicitly derived unit-density inertia tensor for admitted solid/holed disc, ring, cone/frustum/crown, fillet/chamfer, and shallow-base profiles. Preserve frame, units, source profile, void orientation, method identity, integration budget, and bound/checker receipts. Positive volume is required before COM is returned.

Never populate the existing grid-specific h/sure_cells/band_cells metadata for an analytic method. Material density, heterogeneous regions, actual mass/COM, and 6x6 spatial inertia are composed later by fs-matdb/fs-mbd and the as-built binding.

## No-claims

A contained numerical witness is not an independent enclosure proof, and geometry moments do not establish physical density or inertia.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires closed-form comparisons for cylinders, annuli, cones and frusta; independent high-precision quadrature for rounded segments; shrinking-tolerance containment; symmetry/off-diagonal checks; parallel-axis metamorphics; positive scale laws for volume and moments; and fixtures for voids, vanishing bores, thin sections, near-degenerate fillets, invalid orientation, cancellation, and budget limits. Every claimed enclosure must contain the independent witness. Mutation tests remove or perturb method, frame, bound, or void identity and force a different receipt or refusal. Logs include geometry/method identity, intervals, subdivision/budget statistics, authority, and replay command.

Cross-check against closed forms and an independent interval evaluator; tests distinguish raw second moments from inertia tensor and reject fake grid metadata, nonpositive volume, and ambiguous void orientation.

title: Bind Euler profiles to existing certified tessellation and conversion ownership
description:
## Background and ownership

Conversion is reusable MORPH behavior owned by frankensim-b8bxd.4 and the existing Router/converter/sheaf/mesh/conformance beads. This leaf contributes Euler axisymmetric fixtures and adapter rules in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/geometry.rs; it does not create a second converter.

## Deliverable

Route an admitted profile to rendering, collision, and resolved-flow representations with explicit downstream capability and QoI budget. Preserve source chart, feature/corner identities, orientation/topology, conversion route, Hausdorff and within-feature normal-angle enclosures, watertightness evidence, and uncertainty/motion inflation. Circular fillets and shallow curvature refine by analytic sagitta or interval bounds over every patch, never sampled visual agreement.

Rendering and collision artifacts remain distinct even when bytes match. Unsupported targets, unresolved features, unaffordable tolerances, or missing certification return structured refusal or Estimate-only output and cannot strengthen the source.

## No-claims

Nominal or tessellated geometry is not an as-built certificate; sample comparisons cannot certify Hausdorff distance.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires Hausdorff and normal-error comparisons against independent analytic samples, watertight/orientation checks, feature-ID preservation, refinement monotonicity, deterministic byte replay, scale/unit metamorphics, and hostile under-resolution fixtures at fillets, bores, and shallow dishes. Tests cover empty/degenerate profiles, maximum facet and budget boundaries, cancellation, and downstream inflation propagation. Mutation tests stripping source identity or any conversion bound must block authoritative contact routing. Logs include source/destination identities, tolerances, achieved bounds, facets, budgets, authority, and reproduction command.

The exact reused owners are frankensim-epic-morph-wqd.8, .10, .13, .16, and .26 plus frankensim-b8bxd.4. Tests prove analytic sagitta bounds, corner preservation, and stripped-receipt refusal.

title: Compile sourced bulk-material packs for discs, bases, housing, and supports
description:
## Background

Names such as tungsten, stainless steel, glass, and PA12 are families, not material identities. Density, stiffness, damping, yield behavior, temperature and process state can all change predicted inertia and dissipation.

## Deliverable

Through the existing MatDB card/compiler protocols, create source-closed candidate cards for explicitly named grades and process states covering tungsten-alloy and stainless disc candidates, glass and comparison-metal bases, housing metal, and PA12 supports when modeled. Record density and every required elastic, plastic, damping/loss, thermal, and rate-dependent property; uncertainty/covariance where supported; temperature, frequency, stress, and process validity; source citations and version; and missing values.

Separate literature candidate cards, supplier certificates, coupon-updated cards, and as-built specimen identity. Define deterministic merge/adjudication rules without averaging incompatible sources.

## No-claims

These cards do not establish the composition of the video product or any physical specimen. Missing contour-loss, restitution, damping, or plastic data stays missing rather than being inferred from hardness or bulk modulus.

## Required-property discipline

Material packs declare required properties per consuming constitutive law and applicability rung, with typed missingness and provenance for each value. Do not require elastic, plastic, damping, thermal, and rate data universally; irrelevant missing data must not block a law that does not consume it, while a required missing field must never be guessed or filled by a favorable default.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires schema/compiler round trips, dimensional validation, source/version closure, deterministic canonical bytes, validity-boundary tests, covariance checks, incompatible-source refusal, and fixtures with every required property individually absent. Mutation tests prove grade, process, environment, uncertainty, citation, claim pin, or validity changes identity and admission. Independent spot checks verify representative conversions and density-to-mass assembly. Logs are bounded and identify card/source/compiler identities, units, missing properties, validity, authority, and reproduction command; no proprietary raw source is leaked.

A law-to-required-property matrix and hostile missing/irrelevant-property fixtures must prove exact admission behavior and prevent invented values.

title: Define disc/base InterfaceSystemCards and bind only admitted generic contact laws
description:
## Background

The dissipative interface is not determined by bulk material alone. Surface finish, roughness, waviness, texture direction, cleaning, humidity, temperature, wear/run-in, third bodies, and measurement history can change friction, compliance, restitution, and rolling/contour loss.

## Deliverable

Create ordered InterfaceSystemCards for each admitted disc-edge/base pair, binding the two surface states, medium, third body, environment, preparation/history, load/speed/frequency domain, parameter uncertainty, provenance, and claim pins. Resolve each card through the generic tribology/constitutive-law registry only when its complete parameter set and validity domain are available.

If the generic stack lacks a rolling/contact-deformation loss moment, the missing capability must remain an explicit dependency on a reusable tribology child. This Euler leaf may provide an adapter and independent coupon-derived parameters; it may not implement or calibrate a target-outcome-tuned law.

## No-claims

Coulomb friction, hardness, restitution, or modulus cannot be silently transformed into contour friction. Card resolution is not validation of the law or the actual surface.

## Exact responsibility

This leaf verifies InterfaceSystemCard identity, ordered-surface semantics, required-property resolution, applicability and claim pins, immutable history, and structured refusal. It does not own constitutive state replay, work-sign proofs, solver residuals, or physical-law validation.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires ordered-pair, surface-reversal, texture-frame, environment, history/run-in, load/speed/frequency-validity, missing-parameter, dimensional, and claim-pin tests. Each admitted generic law has deterministic state replay and nonnegative dissipated-work checks over its valid domain; out-of-domain or incomplete inputs refuse with ranked fixes. Mutation tests cover every surface, medium, preparation, history, uncertainty, source, and model field. Logs identify card/law/state identities, applicability, work and residual summaries, authority, budgets, and reproduction command without embedding expected Euler outcomes.

Resolution tests prove deterministic selected-law identity, parameter completeness, units, ordered-surface behavior, applicability domain, claim pins, and refusal. Constitutive state replay and nonnegative-work proofs remain with frankensim-b8bxd.5 through .7; Euler consumer power/work checks remain with phase 3.

title: Bind canonical digital specimens, scenarios, protocols, and provenance identities
description:
## Background

A replayable study must bind geometry, mass method, material and interface identities, initial-state protocol, environment, solver versions, and evidence role. Otherwise apparently identical runs can hide different physics.

## Deliverable

Using existing project/scenario and semantic-identity types, bind persistent disc, base, housing, and three-support entities to nominal/as-built geometry, tolerance distributions, GeometricMoments receipts, density/material cards, ordered interfaces, units, frames, and model capabilities. Encode separate controlled protocols for fixed initial angular velocity, fixed initial kinetic energy, fixed mass, fixed outer envelope, and geometric scale changes.

Canonical identity must include profile topology/parameters, units and frames, moment method/bounds, material/interface claim pins, surface/history state, atmosphere, initial-condition distribution, seed, budgets, model versions, calibration/validation/blind role, and admissible transformations. Inputs and requested QoIs are stored; expected rankings or signs are forbidden.

## No-claims

Schema validity is not a successful dynamics run, actual manufacture, or physical validation. Three decorative support points do not supply base compliance.

## Optional sealed as-built authority

The semantic binding may reference an optional immutable as-built artifact produced under fs-asbuilt/vvreg authority and bound through frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.2.11. It cannot mint that artifact, infer it from nominal CAD, or make the nominal-only path unavailable. Nominal, sealed-as-built, and derived collision/flow bindings have non-aliasing identities and explicit approximation/uncertainty state.

## Separate control axes

Bind two non-interchangeable typed axes. SpecimenControl covers fixed mass, fixed outer envelope, geometric scale, and associated constructibility constraints. LaunchProtocol covers fixed body spin, fixed total angular speed, fixed angular momentum, fixed kinetic energy, and matched measured launch distributions. Each case binds one specimen-control receipt and one launch protocol; neither enum can masquerade as the other.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires canonical round trips and mutation sensitivity for every identity-bearing field, verified unit/frame aliases, deterministic ordering, distinct identities for each control protocol, and rejection of expected-outcome fields. Fixtures cover nominal versus as-built geometry, uncertain tolerances, missing material/interface claims, incompatible frames, unavailable capabilities, and changed evidence role. Replay under semantic aliases must either crosswalk with proof or mint a new identity. Logs identify scenario/specimen/protocol identities, capabilities, units, seeds, budgets, authority, and reproduction command.

Tests prove nominal/as-built non-aliasing, optional nominal execution, exact sealed-artifact binding, stale/tampered registration refusal, and no authority promotion by the Euler adapter.

Test the canonical cross-product of specimen controls and launch protocols, physical constructibility/refusal, and distinct identities when the same launch is applied to specimens with different inertia or the same specimen uses different launch constraints. As-built authority tests remain in .2.11 and the integrated .2.10 gate.

title: ED-3 Rigid dynamics, finite-patch contact, tribology, impacts, and energy closure
description:
## Purpose

Close the central mechanics loop: digital specimen plus pose/twist and gravity produce contact kinematics; normal/tangential/rolling/spin laws produce forces, impulses, torques, stored energy, dissipation, and heat; the constrained rigid-body step advances state and exposes every balance defect.

## Scope and reuse

Consume the existing fs-mbd rigid-core, fs-contact detection/CCD and smooth/nonsmooth response, fs-tribo dry baseline, fs-time event, fs-solver, and InterfaceSystemCard work. Euler-specific leaves supply the axisymmetric contact adapter, conservative rolling baseline, finite-patch state, law selection and calibration binding, runout/contact-loss events, assembled energy/work ledger, checkpoint identity, and domain battery. Do not clone generic integrators, contact solvers, or friction registries into the flagship.

Required modes include ideal no-slip as a falsifier; finite traction with creep/microslip; gross slip; rolling/contour and spin moments; compliant normal contact; contact loss; re-impact; and typed Unknown/refusal for inconsistent or under-resolved regimes. Model switching is ledgered and applicability-driven, never an unannounced numerical substitution.

## No-claims

A fitted resistance torque may be a useful Estimated reduced model but is not microscopic contact emergence. Ideal no-slip cannot dissipate energy by itself. Pairwise restitution does not establish globally passive multicontact. A force residual does not bound state error without regularity. Agreement with one stop time cannot identify the loss mechanism.

## Done means

Conservative fixtures retain energy/momentum within declared numerical defects, passive interfaces close stored plus dissipated energy globally, contact modes and transitions replay deterministically, cancellation drains without partial authority, and independent analytic/limiting/hostile tests can falsify every claimed lane.

## Exact integration ownership

Reusable finite-patch normal, rolling/spin, and partial-slip laws are owned by frankensim-b8bxd.5 through .7. Euler composition lives in crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/ports.rs and mechanics.rs; lower-layer fs-contact/fs-tribo/fs-mbd crates never depend on the flagship. frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.3.11 freezes the port/ledger skeleton early, while frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.3.8 closes full-channel composition only after all implemented channel laws exist.
acceptance_criteria:
The exact direct-child set is frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.3.1 through frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.3.13. The rollup has one hard terminal dependency on .3.10, whose mechanics battery consumes the nominal/as-built full-spatial-inertia path, conservative reference, pre-constitutive kinematics, generic normal/rolling/partial-slip/impact adapters, contribution-compatibility gate, bounded thermal applicability, mechanics-only composition, and checkpoint/cancellation evidence.

Closure requires bounded finite-patch mechanics, declared applicability, deterministic event and mode ownership, exactly-once physical work, mechanics energy closure, independent reconstruction, refinement/replay, and no target-tuned law. Base and gas ports are explicitly inactive here and full body-base-gas composition belongs to .8.3. Software closure cannot establish physical mechanism dominance.

title: Bind Euler-disc multibody state, frames, initial ensembles, and event surface
description:
## Background

A hand-spun Euler disc does not start from one scalar spin rate. Orientation, precession, body spin, nutation, COM velocity, contact location, base state, and their correlations all influence the trajectory. An under-specified initial state can manufacture apparent material or geometry effects.

## Deliverable

Instantiate the generic multibody scenario for one axisymmetric rigid body above a base, using declared world/body/contact frames and quaternion or equivalent orientation conventions. Define the full state, algebraic constraints, initial-contact construction, finite uncertainty ensemble, launcher-conditioned correlations, admissibility projection, and event surfaces for contact, loss, impact, gross slip, grazing, escape, and terminal rest.

Provide protocols for fixed body-spin, fixed total angular speed, fixed angular momentum, fixed kinetic energy, fixed mass, and matched measured launch distributions. Store the protocol, not an expected outcome. Define which initial states are physically constructible and when projection changes evidence authority.

## No-claims

An initialized state is not a faithful hand launch or a solved dynamics trajectory. Unmeasured launch state remains an uncertainty/discrepancy source.

## General spatial inertia and protocol realization

The nominal chart may be axisymmetric, but the admitted rigid body supports source-bound off-axis COM, unequal transverse moments, off-diagonal inertia products, covariance, and optional sealed nonaxisymmetric geometry perturbations. Symmetry never erases phase origin or general spatial inertia.

This leaf realizes LaunchProtocol identities from .2.9; it does not redefine them. Fixed mass, outer envelope, and geometric scale remain SpecimenControl constraints rather than initial-state protocols. Event meanings and terminal classes are consumed from the frozen .1.3 specification.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires analytic pose/frame fixtures, constraint residual checks, positive and impossible initial-contact cases, quaternion sign/canonicalization tests, correlated ensemble replay, unit/frame metamorphics, and event-surface fixtures for contact, grazing, loss, impact, slip, rest, and escape. Mutation tests cover every initial-state component, distribution/correlation, protocol, frame, seed, and projection receipt. Refused or projected states cannot retain unmodified authority. Cancellation and budget behavior are bounded. Logs include scenario/state/protocol identity, units, frames, seed, residuals, projection/disposition, budgets, and reproduction command.

Add off-axis COM, unequal transverse inertia, nonzero products, phase-origin mutation, body-frame transforms, arbitrary source-bound spatial inertia, and exact zero-perturbation reduction. A specimen control presented as a launch protocol must refuse.

title: Run the mechanics verification, convergence, lane-parity, and energy-closure battery
description:
## Background

The integrated mechanics stack combines smooth and nonsmooth contact, mode switching, dissipative internal state, and adaptive integration. Component tests alone cannot distinguish a physical loss channel from numerical damping or event error.

## Deliverable

Build a no-mock battery spanning ideal conservative references, compliant normal contact, microslip, rolling/spin loss, gross sliding, contact loss/reimpact, coupled wrench assembly, checkpoints, and energy receipts. Run smooth and nonsmooth lanes over an explicitly shared applicability subset and compare agreed QoIs within registered bands; outside it, report no-parity rather than force agreement.

Include manufactured energy-channel cases, timestep/order and contact-regularization studies, geometry/contact tolerance refinement, long late-time trajectories, hostile mode twins, cancellation storms, deterministic worker-count replay, and independent artifact-only checks.

## No-claims

Passing the battery provides G0/G1/G3/G4/G5 software evidence and declared numerical convergence. It does not validate a real disc, identify a dominant mechanism, or authorize blind-prediction claims.

## As-built and edge-orientation integration gate

The terminal battery, rather than early nominal mechanics leaves, binds the sealed registered-as-built geometry/spatial-inertia path from .2.10. It exercises off-axis COM, unequal inertia, runout/topography bounds, both contacted edges, and exact zero-perturbation reduction without making nominal execution wait for physical metrology.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires all listed cases with machine-checkable convergence bands, invariant/residual thresholds, event timing uncertainty, channel-wise energy closure, smooth/nonsmooth applicability and discrepancy receipts, and a zero-loss reference that exhibits no unexplained secular damping. Hostile twins include target-tuned law data, missing/duplicate energy channels, unresolved contact, false convex support, numerical chatter, stale checkpoint, cancellation leak, and insufficient refinement; each must refuse or demote deterministically. Retained logs and content-addressed artifacts identify case/scenario/schema/model/card identity, units, seeds, budgets, timestep/tolerances, expected and observed disposition, first divergence, authority/no-claim state, and exact reproduction command. DSR and physical validation remain separate gates.

Require nominal and registered-as-built mechanics twins, opposite-edge orientation, full spatial inertia, coverage-bound query inflation, and hostile nominal/as-built aliasing. Missing physical as-built evidence remains an explicit nominal-only software path, not fabricated authority.

title: Define the Euler composition port and energy-ledger skeleton before physical channels land
description:
## Why this split exists

## Deliverable

Bind canonical rigid-body state to typed gravity, normal-contact, tangential-contact, rolling/spin, impact, base, and gas port declarations. Freeze frames, signs, effort/flow orientation, timestamps, interpolation/rollback policy, exactly-once work ownership, missing-channel treatment, and cumulative kinetic/potential/recoverable/dissipated/heat/numerical-defect/unresolved ledgers. Ports can be inactive or unavailable with explicit model identity and no-claim state.

Enforce architecture: composition lives in the Euler L6/integration crate; fs-mbd must not depend on fs-solid/fs-flux, and fs-contact must not depend on fs-mbd. This skeleton performs no channel physics and cannot claim energy closure for absent implementations.

## Contribution ownership key

Every force/moment port declares surface pair, patch/region, temporal interval, generalized-velocity coordinate, law/model/card/source identity, and ownership mode Exclusive or AdditiveWithProof { decomposition_receipt }. Duplicate or overlapping ownership is representationally invalid before integration, not merely a late energy residual.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires manifest-direction checks, dimensional/frame/sign tests, action/reaction and exactly-once accounting fixtures, duplicate/missing-owner refusal, inactive/unavailable channel behavior, deterministic ordering, rollback/checkpoint identity, and hostile double-count tests. Focused unit tests cover happy, empty, malformed, n-1/n/n+1, maximum/maximum-plus-one, unit/frame, deterministic ordering, and structured refusal cases. title: Compute bounded finite-patch kinematics and pre-constitutive contact state
description:
## Background

The late Euler-disc motion is not well represented by a single geometric point with one Coulomb slip speed. A finite contact patch has normal approach, rolling speed, spin about the normal, creepage, patch orientation, and changing edge curvature. The active contact may also disappear or change feature.

## Deliverable

Adapt the generic detection/CCD outputs and contact-frame contract into dynamic patch kinematics: closest features, gap and uncertainty, normal/tangent basis, relative normal velocity, rolling velocity, spin, longitudinal/lateral creepage, patch orientation, curvature inputs, and an explicit Unknown/Separated/Approaching/Sticking/Microslip/GrossSlip/Grazing/Impact mode state.

Propagate geometry and motion bounds, surface ordering, feature transitions, and time-of-impact intervals. Deterministic mode tie-breaking and hysteresis are declared and ledgered; no mode is inferred from an unbounded scalar tolerance.

## No-claims

Kinematics do not supply a force law, nonpenetration proof, or dissipation model. Curvature and speed alone do not identify contour friction.

## Pre-constitutive state and tangent gauge

The only kinematic status values are Unknown, Separated, Approaching, Touching, Grazing, and ImpactCandidate. Emit dimensional relative normal/tangent velocity, rolling velocity, spin, and creepage only where its reference-speed definition is valid. Sticking, PartialSlip/Microslip, and GrossSlide are constitutive states owned by .3.6; impact/separation disposition is owned by .3.7.

A tangent basis is a gauge choice. Outputs are covariant under SO(2) tangent-frame rotation while physical vectors and reconstructed power remain invariant. At zero reference rolling speed, normalized creepage is Unavailable unless an explicitly identified regularization applies.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires independent rigid-body velocity reconstruction, analytic rolling/spinning fixtures, pure roll/pure spin/mixed creepage, separated/approaching/grazing/impact cases, feature-transition and equal-contact twins, uncertainty-bound propagation, swapped-surface orientation checks, and deterministic mode replay. Unit/frame, rigid-transform, and speed-scaling metamorphics apply. Mutation tests removing bounds, surface order, curvature, or mode thresholds prevent law admission. Cancellation and bounded-search tests retain no partial contact authority. Logs include body/feature/contact identities, kinematics and units, bounds, mode/reason, budgets, and reproduction command.

Add arbitrary tangent-basis rotation, invariant reconstructed velocity/power, deterministic degenerate-basis fallback, zero-speed creepage refusal, and proof that kinematics alone cannot emit a sticking/sliding constitutive state.

## No-claims

An impact event is not evidence of localized plasticity unless the constitutive/applicability evidence supports it. Runout cannot be invented to improve agreement.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires manufactured separation/grazing/single-impact/repeated-impact/recontact/feature-switch cases, analytic impulse checks where applicable, event-time bracketing convergence, nonpenetration/complementarity residuals, energy accounting, deterministic simultaneous-event ordering, and hostile chatter/runout/budget twins. Zero-runout and decreasing-timestep metamorphics are required. Mutating restitution/compliance, runout identity, event tolerance, or ordering changes replay/authority. Cancellation at event search and impact solve drains safely. Logs include event sequence and intervals, contact/geometry/model identities, impulses/work/residuals, chatter/refusal state, budgets, and reproduction command.

Focused unit tests separately exercise event predicates, root bracketing, simultaneous-event tie-breaking, impulse/residual calculation, checkpoint boundaries, zero-event and maximum-event cases, malformed runout fields, and structured Unknown/refusal. The mechanics E2E uses the production event lane with retained detailed diagnostics and proves deterministic artifact-only replay of the complete event sequence and first divergence.

title: Complete Euler mechanics-channel composition and mechanics energy closure
description:
## Purpose and split

The early port/ledger skeleton is frozen by .3.11, and .3.12 admits non-overlapping contact-law combinations. This terminal composition leaf closes Euler mechanics only: gravity, compliant normal contact, tangential/partial slip, rolling/contour/material hysteresis, and impact. Base and gas ports remain explicit Inactive or Unavailable placeholders here; their actual work and recoverable energy are composed by .8.3.

## Deliverable

In crates/fs-euler-disc-e2e/src/mechanics.rs, connect every admitted mechanics wrench/state to generic MBD equations. Enforce frames, signs, action/reaction, timestamps, interpolation/rollback, contribution ownership, and exactly-once work. Emit per-step/cumulative kinetic and gravitational potential energy, recoverable contact storage, contact/impact dissipation and heat, numerical defect, unresolved mechanics channels, and bounded isothermal-applicability receipt from .3.13.

Inactive/refused/missing models remain explicit; duplicate/missing work ownership is a structured pre-integration failure. Ablations change semantic identity. Manifest checks enforce that the L6 integration crate composes lower layers while no reverse dependency is introduced.

## No-claims

Mechanics energy closure verifies bookkeeping and numerical integration. It does not validate a contact law, supply base/gas results, or establish mechanism dominance.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires force/torque frame and sign tests, action/reaction, work-power, exactly-once ownership, conservative mechanics references, single-channel manufactured loss cases, admitted contact-law combinations, impact/continuous handoff, ablations, timestep/event refinement, thermal-applicability bounds, and hostile missing/duplicate/stale/future samples. Kinetic + potential + recoverable-contact + dissipated-contact/impact + heat + numerical/unresolved mechanics terms close within declared bounds or return Estimate/Unknown. Inactive/unavailable base and gas ports contribute no hidden work; full body-base-gas closure belongs exclusively to .8.3.

Focused unit tests include happy, empty, malformed, n-1/n/n+1, maximum/maximum-plus-one, unit/frame, deterministic ties, and refusal. Property/metamorphic/mutation/checkpoint/cancellation/fault/budget tests cover every port/model/ablation/interpolation/ownership/thermal identity. Logs are schema-versioned, bounded, deterministic, redacted, content-addressed, and include Five Explicits, channel work/storage/heat, residuals, disposition, first divergence, relative artifacts, and exact reproduction command. DSR, physical validation, and maturity remain separate.

title: Make Euler-disc integration checkpointable, deterministic, cancellation-correct, and budgeted
description:
## Background

Long, stiff, event-rich mechanics trajectories need pause/resume and failure recovery. Coupled base/air checkpoint composition is tested later in the integrated campaign; this leaf owns mechanics state only.

## Deliverable

Define the complete mechanics checkpoint state: rigid state, contact patches/modes/internal variables, event queue, integrator/adaptivity state, RNG counters, mechanics energy ledger, budgets, applicability, source/model/card/scenario versions, and provenance. Implement deterministic logical-tile reductions and tie breaking, bounded cancellation polling, request-drain-finalize, and idempotent resume/fork.

Base solver state, gas fields, and coupling histories are not serialized here. They cross the typed port boundary and are composed/tested by frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.8.3. Incomplete or incompatible mechanics checkpoints refuse with ranked diagnostics; fast/nondeterministic mode is distinct provenance and cannot satisfy deterministic evidence.

## No-claims

Byte-stable same-ISA replay verifies deterministic mechanics execution, not physical correctness or cross-ISA identity.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires uninterrupted versus checkpoint/resume/fork equivalence, worker-count determinism on the declared ISA, cancellation at every tile/event/coupling boundary, fault injection during gravity, contact, impact, integration, and mechanics-port publication/rollback work, no task or arena leak, no double-finalization, and exact rejection of stale/truncated/mutated checkpoints. Mutation tests cover every state and identity field. Budget boundaries and maximum-plus-one cases return typed partial/no-authority artifacts. Logs are bounded and identify checkpoint/scenario/model identity, logical step/event, seed, budgets, cancellation/fault disposition, energy/replay hashes, and reproduction command.

Tests must prove mechanics-only scope, exact contact/internal-state restart, and refusal when a caller tries to smuggle unbound base/gas history into a mechanics checkpoint. Coupled checkpoint recovery belongs to frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.8.3.

Any base/gas state in a mechanics checkpoint is rejected as an unbound foreign channel; coupled checkpoint equivalence and recovery remain .8.3.

title: ED-4 Flexible base, housing, supports, leveling, wobble, and escape mechanics
description:
## Purpose

Represent the base as part of the physical system rather than an immovable boundary. This workstream tests whether plate/housing/support motion explains material, radius, and scale trends and separates static leveling from dynamic compliance.

## Scope

Define base plate geometry, shallow curvature, thickness, material/process state, finish, housing mass/stiffness, support/foot count and positions, adjustment state, contact compliance, damping, and measured modal data. Implement a reduced modal plate/support rung first, with a declared truncation and escalation monitor; add a full flexible fs-solid/fs-mbd coupling path only where the target QoIs demand it.

Couple disc contact work into plate/support storage and dissipation with equal-and-opposite force, impulse, torque, and power receipts. Model leveling, gravitational drift, wandering, boundary approach, escape, and base tilt as explicit states/events. Three supports avoid rigid static overconstraint but do not receive a blanket no-wobble claim once compliance and dynamics exist.

## Experimental connection

The model accepts independently measured base modes and damping, and predicts base motion channels that can be compared with vibrometry/accelerometry. Glass-versus-steel comparisons must separate material from thickness, finish, mass, mounting, and modal differences.

## Done means

Analytic plate/mode and rigid-base limits, support permutation/frame/unit tests, energy/passivity accounting, modal refinement, full-model discrepancy checks, event coverage, and retained structured logs establish exactly which base effects are simulated and when escalation or refusal occurs.
acceptance_criteria:
The exact direct-child set is frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.4.1 through frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.4.8. The rollup has one hard terminal dependency on .4.7, whose battery consumes assembly/interface identity, local/global compliance and damping de-embedding, reduced and resolved flexible models, bidirectional moving-contact coupling, support seating/lift/slip, leveling/wandering/escape/impact, and terminal mechanics.

Closure requires independently checked modal/full-field evidence, exact compliance/dissipation ownership, action/reaction and energy closure, convergence, cancellation/checkpoint replay, and retained event/censoring classes. Three-leg stability, glass superiority, shallow-curvature benefit, or rigid-disc adequacy are never encoded; they are outcomes or applicability decisions.

title: Define the base, housing, tripod, leveling, and support assembly contract
description:
## Background

The base is part of the dynamical system, not an immovable boundary. Plate thickness and curvature, housing inertia/rigidity, foot locations, screw adjustment, support compliance, floor coupling, and center-of-mass placement can all affect energy transfer and escape.

## Deliverable

Define persistent entities and frames for the contact plate, housing, three outriggers/feet, adjusters, optional comparison supports, and external foundation. Bind nominal/as-built geometry, material cards, joints, preload/gravity seating, contact interfaces, tolerances, temperature, and leveling state. Specify legal support topologies and deterministic assembly/constraint resolution.

Represent plate curvature independently of edge fillet, and distinguish a three-point geometrical plane from dynamic compliance. Four-or-more support variants are allowed as controlled comparisons with measured preload/contact state, not caricatures.

## Epistemic boundary

Three ideal points define a plane, but a real three-legged assembly can still flex, rock, slip, or lift. The schema alone proves neither stability nor low wobble.

## Interface and seating ownership

Mint distinct ordered interface identities for disc-plate, foot-housing, and foot-foundation contacts; a disc/base card cannot stand in for support interfaces. This schema owns topology, frames, nominal/as-built state, declared preload, and legal constraints only. Static unilateral seating, actual reaction distribution, lift/slip, and state resolution are owned by .4.5.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires assembly round trips, frame/unit checks, three- and four-support variants, nominal/as-built tolerances, adjuster limits, preload/contact-state fixtures, under/over-constrained and disconnected assemblies, deterministic constraint ordering, and mutation sensitivity for every geometry/material/joint/support/foundation field. Impossible or ambiguous seating returns structured refusal. Logs identify assembly/entity/card identities, units, frames, constraint/preload state, tolerances, authority, budgets, and reproduction command.

Tests reject interface-card reuse across physical pairs, nominal/as-built state aliasing, and schema-level claims of seating or stability. Declared preload is input authority, not a solved support reaction.

title: Implement a reduced modal plate-housing-support dynamics model
description:
## Background

A full solid model is expensive and may obscure early identifiability. A reduced model can expose whether base modes and support compliance plausibly receive appreciable energy, provided its modes, damping, and validity are independently established.

## Deliverable

Construct a reduced flexible model for plate bending, housing motion, support compression/shear/rocking, and foundation coupling. Obtain mass, stiffness, damping, mode shapes/frequencies, truncation bounds, and interface participation from analytic/manufactured references, independent modal analysis, or measured calibration data. Preserve rigid modes and energy normalization.

Support material and thickness changes without silently reusing invalid modes. Define frequency/amplitude/contact-location validity and an escalation trigger when omitted-mode or nonlinear-support error can affect registered QoIs.

## No-claims

A fitted modal damping ratio is not proof of glass spring-back or any microscopic mechanism, and modes calibrated on blind target trajectories are forbidden.

## Structural and damping semantics

For a free-free component require positive-definite mass, positive-semidefinite stiffness, and the correct six rigid modes; for a constrained assembly require correctly constraint-reduced positive stiffness. Passive damping is positive-semidefinite. Call truncation results indicators or estimates unless independently enclosed.

Every analytic or measured basis binds evidence role, free-free/assembled measurement state, excitation/response locations, support/foundation/contact condition, included loss channels, and the .4.8 partition/de-embedding receipt. A measured assembled damping fit cannot be combined with explicit support/foundation loss unless residualized with uncertainty.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires analytic beam/plate/oscillator witnesses, positive mass/stiffness and stable damping checks, modal orthogonality/normalization, rigid-mode preservation, free-decay and forced-response comparisons, truncation convergence, contact-location interpolation tests, scale/unit metamorphics, and hostile out-of-band/nonlinear/lift-off cases. Material/thickness/support mutations must invalidate incompatible bases. Cancellation and budget tests retain no partial authoritative basis. Logs include assembly/model/mode/card identities, frequencies/damping/participation/bounds, validity/escalation, budgets, and reproduction command.

Add free-free and constrained operator fixtures, six-rigid-mode checks, passive damping, measurement-basis mutation, component-versus-assembled FRFs, de-embedding conditioning, included-loss metadata, and hostile assembled-fit plus explicit support-loss cases.

title: Couple finite-patch contact to base motion with exactly-once energy transfer
description:
## Background

The disc applies a moving force and moment to the plate; the resulting plate velocity changes relative contact kinematics. One-way forcing can overstate or hide base loss, and duplicate work accounting can make an apparently closed ledger meaningless.

## Deliverable

Implement bidirectional contact-to-base coupling through the existing coupling-port contract. Transfer distributed patch force/moment and location to reduced coordinates; reconstruct plate displacement/velocity/normal at the patch; feed them back to contact kinematics; and account for recoverable base energy, structural/support dissipation, foundation work, and coupling defect exactly once.

Declare partitioned iteration/interpolation and, where available, monolithic reference behavior. Enforce action/reaction, timestamp/order, convergence, and rollback at event/contact-mode changes. Produce an applicability/discrepancy receipt.

## No-claims

Energy transfer into a base mode does not prove that mode dominates physical spin-down; small coupling residual does not validate damping data.

## Coupling-engine dependency

The claimed iterated partitioned convergence, rollback, and reference-mode semantics require the generic co-simulation lane frankensim-ext-couple-cosim-lanes-pelj in addition to the port schema. This leaf consumes frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.3.11 rather than waiting for all terminal contact-loss implementations in frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.3.8.

## Local/global compliance split

Real finite-patch production coupling consumes .3.4 and .4.8. Local normal approach/indentation and global plate/housing/support motion remain separate coordinates with separate storage/work owners. If a resolved structural model already owns local indentation, the analytic patch contribution is disabled or demonstrably de-embedded before coupling.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires manufactured moving-load/modal-response cases, action/reaction and work-power identities, rigid-base and zero-damping limits, single-mode resonance and off-resonance fixtures, partition/refinement convergence, exactly-once energy ownership, and hostile stale/future/duplicate/missing port samples. Contact motion and mode changes must rollback deterministically. Cancellation drains both sides without partial authority. Logs include coupling/port/model identities, timestamps/iterations, patch load and reconstructed motion, storage/work/dissipation/defect bounds, applicability, budgets, and reproduction command.

Conformance must execute through the generic co-simulation lane, not a flagship-local iteration loop, and must preserve port/ledger identity across rollback.

Add analytic series-compliance and manufactured prescribed-load cases, duplicate-local-compliance refusal, local/global coordinate and work reconstruction, de-embedded versus resolved alternatives, and mutation of compliance-partition identity.

title: Add a higher-fidelity flexible-base escalation and cross-fidelity discrepancy receipt
description:
## Background

Reduced modes may fail near localized contact, support lift-off, material nonlinearity, or frequency ranges close to truncation. A higher-fidelity lane is needed as a falsifier and escalation target, not as an automatic source of truth.

## Deliverable

Adapt the generic flexible-body/solid capability to the same plate, housing, support, and contact-port semantics. Preserve geometry/material/interface identities and compare full-field displacement, contact-point mobility, modal participation, support reactions, and channel-wise energy against the reduced model over a registered overlap domain.

Define refinement, spatial/temporal error estimates, model-form discrepancy, cost budgets, and a deterministic certify-or-escalate decision. Outside the overlap or with unavailable capabilities, return a typed no-comparison/refusal.

## No-claims

Agreement between two models sharing cards and assumptions is corroboration, not physical validation. The high-fidelity lane cannot inherit authority merely from cost.

## High-fidelity solver prerequisite

The higher-fidelity lane hard-depends on frankensim-b8bxd.9, the generic transient plate/shell dynamics implementation. The closed fs-iga bead provides useful foundations but is not accepted as proof of the required transient localized-load solver.

## Local-indentation and basis ownership

The higher-fidelity lane declares whether it resolves only global plate/housing deformation or also the local contact indentation region. In the latter case the analytic contact contribution over that region is inactive; in the former it consumes a de-embedded structural basis. Cross-fidelity comparison binds identical compliance/damping partitions.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires manufactured plate/solid responses, mesh/time refinement, energy and reaction balance, reduced/full overlap comparisons with predeclared bands, and hostile localized-load, high-frequency, support-lift, plastic, and missing-capability cases. Identity/crosswalk mutations must prevent comparison. Cancellation, checkpoint, and budget exhaustion are tested. Logs identify reduced/full geometry/card/model/mesh identities, QoI discrepancies and bounds, cost/budgets, escalation decision, authority/no-claim state, and reproduction command.

A real transient plate/shell producer and its independent refinement evidence are mandatory; a reduced adapter or one-dimensional spline fixture cannot satisfy this leaf.

Hostile tests activate resolved and analytic ownership for the same indentation, reuse a basis with different included losses, or compare mismatched partitions; each refuses before energy comparison.

title: Model support seating, lift-off, slip, nonlinear compliance, and foundation loss
description:
## Background

Support topology influences dynamics through real contacts, not only point count. Adjuster tips may seat, lift, microslip, or rock; PA12 and floor materials may store and dissipate energy; preload and surface flatness determine which feet carry load.

## Deliverable

Bind generic contact/joint laws for foot-housing and foot-foundation interfaces, including normal compliance, tangential state, lift-off/recontact, preload, geometric tolerances, and measured or sourced material loss. Resolve static seating before dynamics and propagate uncertainty in reaction distribution. Support three-leg and controlled four-leg variants with identical evidence rules.

Expose support reactions, slip/lift events, stored energy, dissipation, and applicability. Do not encode 'three never wobble' or 'four wobble' as expected behavior.

## No-claims

Elastic PA12 can return some stored energy but does not guarantee it returns to the disc; energy may remain in other modes or dissipate.

## Nonsmooth support-event ownership

Support lift-off, slip, recontact, and mode transitions consume the generic nonsmooth contact-response lane frankensim-ext-contact-nonsmooth-lane-oh0i. Static seating and dynamic events must retain separate residuals and state; neither is inferred from support count.

## Support-specific kinematics and cards

Support-contact kinematics originate from the assembly/support state and generic contact/nonsmooth lanes, not the Euler disc-edge kinematics in .3.3. Foot-housing and foot-foundation InterfaceSystemCards are distinct from the disc-base card. Static seating owns the solved reaction distribution; .4.1 supplies only declared geometry/preload/topology.

Support damping/loss is admitted only under .4.8. If already included in an assembled modal fit, the explicit law is inactive or de-embedded.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires static seating and reaction checks, one-foot-short/long tolerance fixtures, three/four-support load paths, zero/infinite stiffness limits, lift/recontact and tangential slip cases, nonnegative dissipation, foundation-isolation comparisons, deterministic simultaneous seating, and uncertainty containment. Missing support/foundation cards or out-of-domain load/rate must refuse. Mutation, cancellation, checkpoint, and budget tests are required. Logs include assembly/support/interface/model identities, preload/reactions/events, storage/work/heat, applicability, budgets, and reproduction command.

Tests cover complementarity/residual behavior at seating, lift, slip, recontact, and simultaneous support events through the generic nonsmooth lane.

Add wrong-pair card, disc-kinematics reuse, predeclared-versus-solved reaction, assembled-damping overlap, static/dynamic state alias, and support-specific unit/frame/objectivity fixtures.

title: Predict leveling sensitivity, radial wandering, rim escape, and boundary events
description:
## Background

A shallow base reduces curvature but makes a disc more sensitive to leveling and escape. Runs that wander off, strike a rim, or trigger base tilt are physically different terminal events and cannot be merged into ordinary stop time.

## Deliverable

Model gravitational tilt, adjuster settings, dish curvature, contact-orbit drift, manufacturing slope/warp uncertainty, usable aperture, rim/housing geometry, and plate-tilt feedback. Detect and bracket centered orbit, radial drift, rim approach, escape, rim impact, and base-tilt events. Compute sensitivity to level and curvature under matched initial ensembles.

Define a leveling-estimation procedure from independent metrology or pilot runs without using blind outcomes. Record censored/escaped runs rather than excluding them.

## No-claims

A more curved base is not assumed worse; curvature may alter confinement, contact geometry, and base modes simultaneously. Centering does not validate dissipation physics.

## Coupled feedback and event ownership

Because this leaf predicts plate-tilt feedback, support dynamics, rim impact, and escape rather than prescribed rigid-base drift, it consumes bidirectional base coupling .4.3, support events .4.5, impact/event handling .3.7, and compliance/damping partition .4.8. Any leveling estimator learned from pilots is versioned and frozen before blind acquisition; target outcomes cannot retune it.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires analytic tilted-plane/drift limits, axisymmetric zero-tilt symmetry, controlled curvature/level sweeps, event-time bracketing, rim/escape and base-tilt fixtures, uncertainty propagation, reflection/rotation and unit metamorphics, and hostile favorable-exclusion twins. Changing dish, usable aperture, tilt, adjuster, or censoring policy must change identity. Cancellation and budget tests preserve incomplete/censored disposition. Logs include assembly/level identity, orbit/tilt/event series and uncertainty, censoring, budgets, authority, and reproduction command.

Add prescribed-rigid versus fully coupled comparisons, support-lift-induced tilt, rim-impact ownership, level-estimator freeze/leakage, and hostile omission of coupling/support/impact state. Event and censoring identity changes with every policy revision.

title: Run the flexible-base, support, leveling, and escape verification battery
description:
## Background

Base motion spans static seating, structural vibration, moving-contact coupling, support events, and geometric escape. A battery must distinguish physical damping from coupling/integration error and keep terminal-event classes intact.

## Deliverable

Build no-mock tests for the assembly contract, reduced and higher-fidelity models, support contacts, bidirectional coupling, leveling/wandering, and energy receipts. Include rigid-base, massless/infinitely massive limiting references where mathematically meaningful, single-mode manufactured cases, three/four-support controlled comparisons, material/thickness/curvature changes, and full/reduced overlap checks.

Run refinement, checkpoint, cancellation-storm, fault-injection, worker-count determinism, and artifact-only independent checks. Emit a capability/applicability/no-claim matrix for campaign admission.

## No-claims

Passing is numerical/software evidence. It neither proves glass is superior nor confirms base wobble as the cause of any observed ranking.

## Double-count and rigid-disc hostile coverage

The battery consumes terminal mechanics .3.8 and the .4.8 partition. It includes duplicated local indentation, assembled modal damping plus explicit support/foundation loss, duplicated structural mode/basis, undeclared residual damping, ill-conditioned de-embedding, and rigid-disc global-mode applicability attacks.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires stable thresholds for seating/reactions, modal frequency/response, coupling residual, action/reaction, channel energy closure, event timing, cross-fidelity discrepancy, and deterministic replay. Hostile twins cover a hidden fourth contact, stale mode basis, missing damping card, duplicated work, support chatter, favorable escape censorship, unresolved high-frequency content, and canceled partial output; each must refuse or demote. Retained bounded logs and content-addressed artifacts identify case/assembly/model/card/schema identity, units, seeds, budgets, refinement, expected/observed disposition, first divergence, authority/no-claim state, and exact reproduction command. DSR and physical validation remain separate gates.

Each overlap attack refuses with the exact physical domain and owner pair. A rigid-disc case whose global modes approach the forcing/contact bandwidth must escalate or demote rather than rely on local Hertz compliance.

title: Freeze local-contact/global-base compliance and damping ownership and de-embedding
description:
## Purpose

Local patch indentation, global disc/plate deformation, housing/support compliance, and foundation motion can overlap. Likewise, an assembled modal damping fit may already contain support/foundation losses later modeled explicitly. Freeze ownership and de-embedding before activating base models.

## Required artifact

Emit CompliancePartition and DampingPartition entries with physical domain and strain/DOF support; storage/dissipation owner; included/excluded model IDs; load/amplitude/frequency/contact-location validity; evidence/calibration source; and whether each loss is already contained in a measured FRF/modal fit. Record free-free versus assembled measurement basis, excitation/response locations, support/foundation/contact state, de-embedding method, transfer paths, conditioning bound, residual covariance/uncertainty, checker, forbidden overlap pairs, unresolved residual, and authority/no-claim state.

Reject local Hertz compliance plus a resolved model owning the same indentation; an assembled modal-damping fit plus explicit foot/joint/foundation loss without residualization; duplicated modes/bases; undeclared residual damping; or ill-conditioned subtraction. Monitor global disc flexibility versus contact/forcing bandwidth and escalate/refuse the rigid-disc assumption when needed.

## No-claims

A de-embedded model is an explicit decomposition with uncertainty, not proof of a microscopic damping mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
Closure requires safe-Rust production behavior at the named owner, a versioned contract, canonical identities for every semantic input, units/frames/seeds/budgets/versions/capabilities, structured refusal and no-claim state, bounded cancellation and request-drain-finalize with no partial authority. Focused unit tests cover happy, empty, malformed, n-1/n/n+1, maximum/maximum-plus-one, boundary, unit/frame, deterministic-order, error, and refusal cases. Property, metamorphic, mutation, checkpoint/replay, fault, work/memory/deadline/output-cap, and independent-checker tests exercise every mathematical and authority-bearing field. Logs follow the frozen Euler schema: bounded, deterministic, redacted before buffering or hashing, content-addressed, with case/stage/attempt, source/schema/model/checker identities, Five Explicits, stable reason, expected/observed disposition, first divergence, cancellation/drain/finalization, relative artifacts, and a repository-relative reproduction command; secrets, absolute paths, host identity, PIDs, wall-clock noise, and unbounded payloads are forbidden. Focused proof, DSR, blind physical evidence, and maturity promotion remain distinct.

Analytic series-spring and two-oscillator witnesses, free-free versus assembled FRF reconstruction, rigid-contact/base and zero-damping limits, modal support changes, conditioning/uncertainty propagation, exact energy ownership, coordinate/unit metamorphics, and hostile duplicate local compliance, duplicated mode, assembled-damping-plus-support-loss, hidden residual, and ill-conditioned subtraction cases are required.
