`cargo build -p fs-ledger` is CLEAN; `cargo test -p fs-ledger` still fails. The
fsqlite-btree break is CONDITIONAL on the `async-api` feature, which FrankenSim
enables only through fs-ledger's DEV-dependency
(async-api = ["dep:asupersync", "fsqlite-types/native"]).
So the PRODUCTION graph is fine and only test lanes pulling async-api are
blocked. My earlier "fs-ledger and fs-vskeleton are still blocked" was too
broad — they build, they just cannot test. The distinction decides whether a
bead can honestly close, which is why I am correcting it explicitly.

CORRECTION 2026-07-25 (NobleLion). Landed ceddc97b.

I got the coverage inventory WRONG for four of seven siblings and have fixed it.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. The registry recorded franken_numpy, franken_networkx,
frankenscipy and frankentorch as having no boundary-isolating tests. I had
grepped crates/*/tests/ and concluded absence. Three of those boundaries are
covered by #[cfg(test)] UNIT tests inside src/, behind non-default features, so
the grep could not see them; frankenscipy's casebooks are in tests/ and I
mis-stated them as "not consolidated into a selectable target" when they are
per-crate targets already.

  franken_numpy     fs-sparse/src/interop_fnp.rs   2 tests  --features fnp-interop
  franken_networkx  fs-sparse/src/interop.rs       4 tests  --features fnx-interop
  frankentorch      fs-ad/src/bridge.rs            4 tests  --features torch-bridge
  frankenscipy      7 oracle casebooks under tests/, incl. a seeded-corruption drill

WHY IT MATTERED. The recorded release train refused franken_numpy as an
uncovered surface. That was a FALSE reason attached to a TRUE verdict. I
reported to the fleet that a P2 sibling had moved a minor version with no way
to validate it; in fact it had two dedicated round-trip/refusal tests, and they
pass on the new pin.

MEASURED, not asserted. All four surfaces executed green against the live pins:
franken_numpy 2/2, franken_networkx 8/8, frankentorch 4/4, frankenscipy 2/2.
Only frankenpandas is uncovered, correctly — pinned-unused, no consumer, no
claim.

RE-ADJUDICATED. The train is still REFUSED, now on the single true reason: the
frankensqlite P1 durability surface could not execute. The transcript test
carries the correction in its own doc comment rather than quietly changing.

MODEL CHANGES the real data forced:
- SurfaceTest gains `kind` (Unit vs Integration) and `required_features`;
  selector() -> selectors(), one invocation per (crate, feature set). A
  selector that omits a required feature compiles the boundary out and reports
  a VACUOUS PASS, which is the same class of error as the one I just made, so
  a test now asserts every feature-gated test has a selector enabling its
  features and that no selector runs a whole crate.
- coverage_required now scopes the every-train rule to the runtime graph. The
  rule exists because one sibling's move can break another's surface, and that
  propagates only through runtime consumption; a dev-only oracle is required
  when it MOVES, not on every unrelated train. The gate found this itself —
  three fixtures began failing the moment frankenscipy became covered, which
  was the model telling me the rule was too broad.

LESSON worth keeping: absence of a test file is not absence of a test. Unit
tests in src/ and feature-gated boundaries are both invisible to a tests/
directory scan, and a registry that records "no coverage" without checking both
manufactures gaps — which is the mirror image of the vacuous-pass failure this
suite exists to prevent.

DONE-WHEN unchanged at 3 of 4. Item 1 still NOT met: frankensqlite cannot
execute. It is now the ONLY thing between this bead and completion.

title: Independent review of load-bearing sibling components (frankensqlite durability, asupersync cancellation first)
description:
WHY: Common authorship across the constellation means an assumption shared between FrankenSim and a sibling is invisible to every internal test. For the components UNDER the certificates — frankensqlite (ledger durability, crash recovery, the WAL/locking semantics all receipts depend on) and asupersync (cancellation request->drain->finalize, structured-concurrency guarantees under panics) — independent scrutiny is the only cure for that blindness. "Independent" is honestly graded: a genuinely external reviewer is ideal; minimum credible = review by an agent/person with no authorship history on the target, against the target's own claimed contracts, with adversarial tests written from the CONTRACT ALONE before reading the implementation.

WHAT: per target (frankensqlite first, asupersync second, others per e13_1 priority): (a) a review charter: the claims under review (from the sibling's docs + FrankenSim's usage assumptions per the e13_1 map), explicitly including the known sharp edges (e.g. the fsqlite IS-NULL/prepare-time-folding incident class — regressions of fixed bugs are prime review targets); (b) contract-first adversarial testing: reviewer writes crash/interruption/concurrency drills from the contract before reading code (ledger torn-write recovery, mid-transaction kill -9, lock-contention storms; cancellation during drain, panic-during-finalize, nested-scope leak hunts); (c) findings filed as beads in the SIBLING repo where fixable there, with FrankenSim-side mitigations tracked here; (d) the review outcome (scope, method, findings, residual concerns) recorded in the trust-cone assessment — a review that found nothing must still record what it TRIED.

DONE WHEN: both priority reviews completed with recorded charters + adversarial suites + dispositioned findings; the assessment's review-status column updates; residual risks named.

TESTS: the adversarial suites join the e13_4 compatibility suite where they are FrankenSim-runnable; drill-quality bar: each suite must include at least one drill that FAILS on a seeded regression of a historically fixed sibling bug.
notes:
GoldSnow 2026-07-24: asupersync HALF COMPLETE at b0fa4f4a; frankensqlite half BLOCKED. Bead stays in_progress because DONE-WHEN requires BOTH priority reviews.

DONE (asupersync, review SREV-2026-07-A): (a) charter recorded in docs/SIBLING_REVIEW_ASUPERSYNC.md -- claims enumerated from the sibling's OWN asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md (obligations 3/4/5/7, rule index #1-#10) plus fs-exec CONTRACT usage assumptions, with the caller-owned-gate and first-timestamp sharp edges named; (b) contract-first adversarial suite at crates/fs-exec/tests/sibling_review_cancellation.rs, 7/7 green -- claims were enumerated BEFORE reading either implementation (only public CancelGate/Cx signatures were read, to make drills runnable); (c) NO DEFECT FOUND, so nothing filed in the sibling repo; one non-defect hardening observation recorded (clock-free sentinel-vs-measurement distinction is documentary, not typed); (d) trust-cone assessment review_status regenerated from the xtask source of truth, recording what was drilled AND what remains unreviewed rather than a bare 'reviewed'.

DRILL-QUALITY BAR MET: D5 targets the historically fixed caller-owned-gate defect (private cancellation state the owner cannot observe), and D5b is its NEGATIVE CONTROL -- a suite where everything passes proves nothing, so D5b seeds the regression's observable and demonstrates the boundary behaves measurably differently. If D5b ever reports cancellation, D5 has stopped discriminating.

INDEPENDENCE GRADED HONESTLY: meets the bead's MINIMUM credible bar (no authorship history on the target, drills from the contract alone) but NOT the ideal (genuinely external reviewer) -- I am another agent in the same fleet, and a reviewer sharing the fleet's habits can share its blind spots.

RESIDUAL / UNREVIEWED (named per DONE-WHEN): only the fs-exec adapter surface was drilled -- nothing exercises asupersync's scheduler or region state machine internally. Obligation leaks (ob.3), loser drain (ob.4), cleanup-budget bounding, bounded cancel fairness (ob.7), and fs-exec's strongest claim ('a successful receipt cannot cross an observed absolute deadline') are all UNTESTED here because they need a driven runtime with concurrent tasks and a timing race. No crash/kill-9/panic-during-finalize drills.

BLOCKED (frankensqlite, the bead's FIRST priority): frankensqlite does not build -- cargo build -p fs-ledger fails E0053 trait-signature mismatches on get_page/write_page/write_page_data/restore_staged_page_data in fsqlite-pager, an in-flight async migration against the moving asupersync sibling. Torn-write/kill-9/lock-storm drills all need a working build. Charter fixed IN ADVANCE anyway (WAL durability, transaction boundaries, migration refusal, blob/checkpoint per 13.1's P1 list; targeted sharp edge = the prepare-time subquery folding / IS NULL incident class, params=None, fixed upstream 2bd64d114) so the claims are chosen before the implementation can influence them.
close_reason:
BOTH priority reviews complete. asupersync SREV-2026-07-A at b0fa4f4a (7/7 drills); frankensqlite SREV-2026-07-B at 3f200317 (5/5 drills). DONE-WHEN met: charters recorded (docs/SIBLING_REVIEW_ASUPERSYNC.md, docs/SIBLING_REVIEW_FRANKENSQLITE.md), adversarial suites landed and green (crates/fs-exec/tests/sibling_review_cancellation.rs, crates/fs-ledger/tests/sibling_review_durability.rs), findings dispositioned (NO DEFECT at either reviewed boundary; one non-defect hardening observation on the clock-free sentinel), both trust-cone review_status rows regenerated from the xtask source of truth, and residual risks named explicitly in both charters.

METHOD: contract-first throughout -- claims enumerated from each sibling's OWN docs (asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md obligations 3/4/5/7 and the cancellation rule index; fs-ledger CONTRACT's FutureSchema/seal/NotFound/transaction claims) BEFORE reading either implementation. Only public API signatures were read, to make drills runnable.

DRILL-QUALITY BAR MET TWICE, both with negative controls: (asupersync) D5 targets the historically fixed caller-owned-gate defect with D5b proving it discriminates; (frankensqlite) D2 targets commit 904cdef1 / beads cgt07+lnbzs, where a FROM-less-subquery parameter drop made seal_artifact_output silently insert zero rows while returning Ok. The second is the more instructive shape: a drill checking only 'invalid input refuses' would have PASSED during that bug, so the discriminating assertion is that the VALID case leaves an OBSERVABLE seal. When a historical defect was a silent no-op, its regression drill must assert a positive observable.

REVIEW METHOD DEFECT RECORDED (nearly a false defect report against a sibling): D1's first version stamped a future schema by patching byte 60 of the main DB file and observed the ledger opening it happily -- one step from filing 'FutureSchema refusal is not enforced'. Cause: WAL mode; a 519 KB -wal sidecar held a newer page 1, so the engine never read the patched header. Corrected to stamp through the engine, and the same discovery hardened the 'never clobbered' assertion to snapshot the WHOLE database (main + all sidecars) rather than just the main file.

INDEPENDENCE GRADED HONESTLY in both charters: meets the bead's MINIMUM credible bar (no authorship history on either target, drills from the contract alone) but NOT the ideal -- I am another agent in the same fleet and can share its blind spots.

RESIDUAL (named, not hidden): both reviews drilled only the ADAPTER surfaces FrankenSim consumes, never the siblings' internals. UNREVIEWED: asupersync obligation leaks, loser drain, cleanup-budget bounding, bounded cancel fairness, and the no-receipt-past-deadline assumption (all need a driven runtime); frankensqlite torn-write recovery, mid-transaction kill, lock-contention storms, Busy/write-conflict retry, and checkpoint/WAL-truncation (all need process-level orchestration). Those are the drills most likely to find a real defect and they remain undone -- green drills certify the boundary, not the engine.

title: Constellation maintainership, incident-response, and archival policy (the governance half of trust)
description:
WHY: Technical verification cannot answer governance questions an adopting organization will ask: who fixes a critical frankensqlite bug and how fast; what happens if a sibling repo becomes unavailable; what is the support horizon for a pinned constellation state. These have honest answers today (single maintainer, best effort) — the failure mode is not the answers but leaving them UNSTATED, letting evaluators assume either better or worse than reality.

WHAT: A policy document (docs/, referenced by the trust-cone assessment and the release bundle) stating: (a) maintainership reality: who maintains each constellation member, the bus factor, and the explicit single-maintainer risk statement (honesty over theater — inventing a committee would be its own trust defect); (b) incident response: how a correctness/security issue in a sibling is reported, triaged, and released (the e13_4 emergency-bump path), with the claim-integrity framing applied (a sibling bug that breaks a certificate claim is a P0 here, not just there); (c) archival/escrow: the vendored bundles (e13_3) ARE the archival mechanism — every release bundle is a self-contained restorable state independent of any repo's continued existence; state retention policy for bundles; (d) support horizon: what a pinned release can expect (reproducibility forever via bundle; fixes only via new trains); (e) review cadence for this policy itself.

DONE WHEN: policy merged; assessment + release docs reference it; the incident path has been REHEARSED once (tabletop: a hypothetical fsqlite corruption bug walked through report->triage->emergency train->bundle).

TESTS: doc-presence + cross-reference lint; the tabletop rehearsal transcript retained as an artifact; consistency check between this policy, the e13_4 protocol, and the e02 claim-integrity severity rules.
notes: 2026-07-22 f85xj.13.1 input: governance work must address availability in addition to content hashes. Begin with the critical/high-availability-risk asupersync and FrankenSQLite rows, then cover release cadence, incident response, archival, maintainer continuity, and first-consumer admission for the pinned-unused frankenpandas surface. The rendered assessment cites this bead as the authority for those unresolved governance gaps.
close_reason: Completed governance policy, retained tabletop, cross-reference gate, and remote focused proof

title: E14 Surrogates and learned components: proposers, never authorities (metrics + evidence contract)
description:
WHY: FrankenSim can get substantially smarter through learned components — solver/preconditioner selection, mesh and refinement proposals, reduced-order models, warm starts, closure-model selection, design proposal generation, anomaly detection, fidelity-sufficiency prediction, retrieval of similar historical studies from the ledger — but ONLY if the authority boundary stays strict: a surrogate may PROPOSE ("this low-fidelity answer is probably adequate"); only a verifier may permit the workflow to ACT on it. The substrate exists (fs-surrogate certify_or_escalate, ConformalBand, empirical_coverage; ladder feature is Estimated-only), but the governance contract and the DECISIVE metrics are not systematized.

DECISIVE METRICS (not just RMSE/R^2): false-safe-decision rate; uncertainty coverage; out-of-domain detection rate; rate of incorrect non-escalation; cost saved per accepted decision; fraction of cases requiring fallback; performance after geometry-family or operating-regime shift.

CHILDREN: learned-component evidence contract (every learned result carries training-data identity + partition policy, geometry/regime domain, calibration + held-out performance, uncertainty calibration, drift statistics, physics residuals, independent discrepancy checks, escalation + fallback policy); decisive-metrics instrumentation wired into campaign/ledger records; proposer/authority boundary enforcement (type-level: learned outputs cannot mint Verified/Validated colors; lint + adversarial tests); ledger retrieval of similar historical studies [backlog/frontier].

DONE WHEN: any surrogate participating in the cooling workflow publishes the full metric set; an adversarial test demonstrates that a deliberately overconfident surrogate is caught by escalation rather than contaminating a decision; no code path exists in which a learned component's output reaches a user-facing claim without passing a verifier.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .14.1 through .14.4 to preserve the learned-component card, decisive metrics, proposer-only authority boundary, and auditable historical-study retrieval as distinct but interoperable artifacts. The joined record must bind training and evaluation corpus identities, partitions, features, target and loss, calibration, OOD and false-safe metrics, escalation behavior, reproducibility seed and budget, known failure modes, model version, and exact downstream consumers; missing card fields or ambiguous provenance are admission failures. The terminal governance owner is .14.3 for scripts/ci/e2e_surrogate_governance.sh, with .14.4 supplying only ranked retrieval proposals and never evidence-color input. E14 closes after unit, boundary, property, metamorphic, mutation, adversarial-OOD, fault, cancellation, resource, deterministic-replay, and configured DSR checks pass with bounded logs; neither benchmark accuracy nor operator choice may let a learned artifact certify, demote, or promote scientific authority.

title: Learned-component evidence contract: mandatory card for every surrogate/learned artifact
description:
WHY: fs-surrogate's certify-or-escalate and conformal bands govern USE of a surrogate, but nothing standardizes what a learned component must DISCLOSE about itself. Without a mandatory contract, learned components will accrete with undocumented training data, unstated domains, and uncalibrated confidence — the classic ML-in-engineering failure — and the authority boundary becomes unauditable.

WHAT: (a) A LearnedComponentCard (extending the ModelCard pattern) mandatory for every learned artifact (surrogates, ROMs, warm-start predictors, selector policies, anomaly detectors): training-data identity (content-addressed dataset refs + the partition policy under which it was trained — e07_1 taint machinery applies to learned components too: training data is calibration data); geometry/regime domain (typed ValidityDomain); calibration + held-out performance (the decisive split, with metrics); uncertainty-calibration status (conformal/coverage evidence refs); drift statistics refs (e12_8 channels); physics-residual checks where applicable (does the surrogate's output violate conservation? measured, not assumed); escalation + fallback policy (what happens on OOD/band-too-wide — must name the fallback path); (b) registration refuses cardless learned components (the fs-evidence ModelRegistry refusal pattern extended); (c) card completeness is typed: a card with Unstated calibration can exist but caps every downstream use at the weakest evidence — visible, not forbidden; (d) existing surrogates (POD, RB ladder, conformal-gated users in campaign crates) migrated to carry cards.

DONE WHEN: card type shipped; registration gate refuses cardless components; existing surrogate users migrated; taint integration proven (a surrogate trained on validation data is caught).

TESTS: unit (card validation per field; refusal paths; taint intersection); integration (migrated campaign crates still green with cards attached); e2e: registry audit script listing every learned component + card completeness table with per-field logging.

## Acceptance Criteria

Require an admitted learned-component card for every surrogate, operator, classifier, ranker, or learned retrieval artifact, binding purpose, forbidden uses, architecture and version, training and evaluation corpus identities and partitions, features and targets, preprocessing, units, loss, calibration, metrics with uncertainty, OOD policy, escalation path, resource envelope, seed, reproducibility, license, known failures, and exact consumers. Unit tests cover schema, required-field and compatibility validation, canonical serialization, migrations, and artifact binding; boundary tests cover empty or tiny datasets, unknown provenance, changed preprocessing, missing metrics, and expired evidence. Property and metamorphic tests require card round-trip and stable identity under ordering; mutants that omit a failure mode, blur train and test, change a corpus root, default OOD behavior, or detach the model must fail. Corrupt cards, cancellation, deadline, size and nesting caps, missing artifacts, and log overflow must refuse admission with bounded diagnostics. This Bead contributes valid and adversarial card fixtures to .14.3 and scripts/ci/e2e_surrogate_governance.sh. Replay and the configured DSR gate must pass; a complete card documents evidence and never makes the learned component an authority.

title: Decisive-metrics instrumentation for learned components (false-safe rate, OOD detection, escalation correctness)
description:
WHY: RMSE and R^2 flatter surrogates on the cases that do not matter. The metrics that decide whether a learned component belongs in an engineering workflow are: false-safe-decision rate (surrogate said fine, truth said not — the catastrophic direction); uncertainty coverage (its bands vs reality); out-of-domain detection rate (did it KNOW it was extrapolating); rate of incorrect non-escalation; cost saved per accepted decision; fallback fraction; and performance after geometry-family/regime shift. These must be INSTRUMENTED — computed continuously from ledgered decisions, not estimated once at training time.

WHAT: (a) Decision-event records: every certify-or-escalate decision (and every learned proposal acceptance) logs: component identity + card version, input-domain position (in/out/near-boundary), the decision, the band width, the fallback taken if any, and — when ground truth later exists (escalated solve completed, corpus case matched, rig data arrived) — the truth outcome joined back to the decision; (b) metric computation: rolling per-component metrics from the joined records (the false-safe join is the critical one: decision said use-surrogate AND truth was outside band = false-safe event, alarmed immediately, not just aggregated); shift-segmented (per geometry family/regime bucket, Mondrian-style) so aggregate health cannot hide segment failure; (c) thresholds + consequences: per-card declared metric floors; breaching them auto-demotes the component (registration gate consults live metrics, not just the card's training-time numbers); (d) metrics feed the e16 dashboard's surrogate row.

DONE WHEN: decision events flow to the ledger from at least the existing campaign users; metrics compute per segment; a synthetic false-safe injection alarms and demotes; dashboard row renders.

TESTS: unit (event schema; join logic incl. late-arriving truth; metric arithmetic; demotion triggers); statistical (synthetic decision streams with known rates recovered); e2e: a campaign run + truth-arrival simulation logging events, joins, metric updates, and the demotion path.

## Acceptance Criteria

Instrument and retain decision-relevant learned-component metrics including false-safe and false-unsafe rates, subgroup and regime error, calibration, OOD detection, escalation correctness and latency, abstention, cost, and downstream decision flips, with locked partitions and uncertainty rather than a single aggregate accuracy. Unit tests cover metric definitions, weighting, censoring, confidence intervals, thresholds, and serialization; boundary tests cover zero positives or negatives, all abstentions, rare regimes, ties, tiny samples, and unavailable truth. Property tests use controlled predictions with analytic metrics; metamorphic tests cover row permutation, batching, and equivalent label encoding; mutants that remove hard cases, count escalations as correct predictions, tune on held-out data, suppress NO-DATA, or hide uncertainty must fail. Corrupt predictions, cancellation, deadline, memory and row caps, missing strata, and log pressure must produce bounded incomplete evidence. This Bead contributes immutable metric tables and adversarial OOD streams to .14.3 and scripts/ci/e2e_surrogate_governance.sh. Deterministic replay and the configured DSR gate must pass; benchmark accuracy or mean error alone cannot justify safe use or evidence promotion.

title: Proposer/authority boundary enforcement: learned outputs cannot mint or influence evidence colors
description:
WHY: The rule "a surrogate may propose; only a verifier permits action" must be structural, not cultural. The dangerous channels are subtle: a learned mesh proposer whose mesh biases the DWR estimate; a warm start that steers which local optimum the certified solve finds; a fidelity-sufficiency predictor whose skipped escalation never gets checked. None of these mint colors directly — they shape what the verifier sees. The boundary must therefore cover both direct minting AND the audit of influence channels.

WHAT: (a) Direct enforcement: type-level — learned-component outputs are wrapped in Proposal<T> (a marker the evidence layer refuses as an authority input: no Evidence color can cite a Proposal as its support); acting on a proposal requires a verifier receipt (the certify-or-escalate decision record, an admission check, a completed certified solve) that references the proposal but derives authority ONLY from the verification; (b) influence-channel audit: for each learned integration point (mesh proposals, warm starts, selector policies, sufficiency predictions) document the influence channel and its guard: warm starts -> certified solve's convergence criteria are start-independent (and a periodic cold-start cross-check drill validates that claim empirically); mesh proposals -> estimator runs on the proposed mesh but its error claim is start-agnostic + ladder-checked (E06_6); sufficiency predictions -> ALWAYS a sampled audit fraction where escalation runs anyway and disagreement feeds e14_2's non-escalation metric (never 100% trust in the skip); (c) adversarial demonstration: a deliberately overconfident/biased surrogate inserted in tests must be caught by the guards, with the catch logged.

DONE WHEN: Proposal<T> wrapper adopted at all learned integration points; the influence-audit doc merged with each channel's guard named + tested; the adversarial demonstration green; lint for new unguarded learned integration points.

TESTS: unit (Proposal refusal in evidence constructors; receipt-requirement enforcement); the cold-start and audit-fraction drills as standing tests; e2e: adversarial-surrogate scenario logging every guard activation and the final uncontaminated decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

Enforce at type, admission, planner, ledger, and output boundaries that learned artifacts can propose candidates, priorities, initial guesses, or retrievals but cannot create, recolor, suppress, or directly determine certificate, validation, human-lock, compliance, or decision authority. Unit tests cover every allowed proposer path and forbidden authority conversion, provenance propagation, escalation, and deterministic fallback; boundary tests cover missing classical verifier, low confidence, OOD, conflicting proposers, empty candidates, and stale models. Property tests require authority state to be invariant under learned score changes until an independent verifier acts; metamorphic tests cover candidate and model ordering; compile-time, runtime, and policy mutants that add a conversion, bypass verification, hide abstention, or let a score break an authority tie must fail. Model crash, corrupt output, cancellation, deadline, GPU absence, memory and candidate caps, and logging faults must drain and fall back or refuse with bounded diagnostics. This Bead is the terminal owner of scripts/ci/e2e_surrogate_governance.sh, joining .14.1, .14.2, and proposer fixtures from .14.4. The configured DSR gate and clean replay must pass; no learned metric or operator delegation can substitute for independent scientific or human authority.

title: Ledger retrieval of similar historical studies (learned retrieval as a proposer) [backlog]
description:
WHY: The design ledger accumulates exactly the experience a new study should exploit — similar geometries, regimes, model choices, what escalated, what the budgets looked like — but nothing retrieves it. Retrieval-as-proposer is the safest possible learned component (it proposes starting points and expectations; verifiers still govern everything), making it a good proving ground for the e14 contract at low risk. Backlog priority: valuable, not on the vertical's critical path.

WHAT: (a) Study fingerprints: deterministic feature vectors over ledgered runs (geometry summary stats from charts/regions, regime/pi-group coordinates, scenario-class tags, model-graph choices, budget outcomes) — engineered features first (interpretable, deterministic), learned embeddings only later under a full LearnedComponentCard; (b) retrieval: given a new project's fingerprint, return ranked similar studies with the SIMILARITY EVIDENCE shown (which features matched — explainable retrieval, in keeping with the explain-everything culture) and the useful payloads: prior model choices + their escalation outcomes, budget actuals (planning priors for fs-plan), settings that failed; (c) integration as PROPOSER only: retrieved suggestions enter as Proposal<T> (e14_3 machinery) — e.g. proposed fidelity-graph starting node, proposed budget allocation — always verifier-gated; (d) privacy/scope note: retrieval operates within the local ledger.

DONE WHEN: fingerprints computed for existing ledgered campaigns; retrieval returns explainable rankings on a held-out study; one proposer integration (budget prior into fs-plan) works end-to-end through the Proposal gate.

TESTS: unit (fingerprint determinism; ranking stability; explanation completeness); retrieval-quality eval (leave-one-out over ledgered studies: does the true sibling rank top-k); e2e: new-project retrieval session logging fingerprint, candidates, explanations, and the gated proposal handoff.

## Acceptance Criteria

Implement historical-study retrieval strictly as a proposer that returns ranked immutable study references with query, filters, similarity features, score explanation, corpus snapshot, access decision, and explicit warning that relevance is not validity or applicability. Unit tests cover indexing, filtering, deterministic ranking and tie breaks, provenance, permissions, and result serialization; boundary tests cover empty corpus, one result, identical scores, stale or deleted studies, incompatible schemas, and unauthorized artifacts. Property tests compare exact small-corpus ranking; metamorphic tests cover corpus insertion order, query-unit normalization, and duplicate elimination; mutants that leak restricted data, fabricate citations, omit the corpus root, treat similarity as applicability, or alter authority must fail. Index corruption, cancellation, deadline, memory and result-count caps, embedding or learned-model absence, and log overflow must fall back or refuse with bounded diagnostics. This Bead contributes immutable retrieval cases to .14.3 and scripts/ci/e2e_surrogate_governance.sh; replay must reproduce ranked identifiers and explanations on the bound corpus. The configured DSR gate must pass; retrieved studies are suggestions for review and cannot validate the current scenario or influence evidence color directly.

title: E15 GPU/accelerator policy: evidence-driven pilot, never calendar-driven
description:
WHY: There is NO GPU execution path in the workspace (verified: fs-substrate gpu field is a descriptive probe string never consumed; zero CUDA/Metal/wgpu/WebGPU/OpenCL/Vulkan hits; fs-govern lists GPU reductions as a determinism RISK). That absence is a real gap — but GPU must not outrank external V&V, product workflow, CAD admission, or constellation trust merely because it is 2026. Many relevant workloads are bandwidth-bound, irregular, latency-sensitive, or dominated by geometry preprocessing, BC setup, solver convergence, model discrepancy, and human/agent workflow latency; peak FLOPs are the wrong denominator. Also "few percent of machine FLOPs" arguments cut both ways — the decision must be MEASURED.

POLICY (encode, then follow): (1) complete one representative vertical; (2) profile END-TO-END wall time and energy (not kernel microbenchmarks); (3) identify the top three kernels; (4) build ONE accelerator pilot only if GPU-suitable kernels dominate; (5) any GPU path requires: a CPU reference path, a backend-specific evidence class binding device + driver + compiler + kernel identity + reduction policy + numerical equivalence envelope, deterministic-or-bounded-equivalence semantics, cancellation semantics, and machine-scoped performance data. The GPU path does NOT automatically get "lower certainty" — it gets its own evidence class. Plausible pilot candidates if profiling justifies: LBM streaming/collision, SpMV, FFT, batched constitutive updates, volume rendering.

CHILDREN: doctrine + backend evidence-class specification; end-to-end vertical profiling harness (depends on the working Level-3 workflow); conditional pilot [moonshot, gated on profiling evidence, subject to the e16 moonshot displacement rule].

DONE WHEN: the doctrine is in fs-govern with a named falsifier; profiling artifacts exist for the reference cooling project; the pilot decision (go/no-go) is recorded WITH the measured evidence it rests on.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .15.1 through .15.3 to connect accelerator policy, end-to-end workflow profiling, and a conditional one-kernel pilot without assuming that device speed implies product benefit. The joined go or no-go record must bind workload and dataset, machine and driver fingerprint, compiler flags, energy measurement method, wall-time attribution, transfer and orchestration overheads, numerical and determinism class, CPU differential evidence, cancellation latency, resource ceilings, and Amdahl projection with uncertainty. The terminal profiling owner is .15.2 for scripts/ci/e2e_extreal_vertical_profile.sh; if and only if its gate admits a pilot, .15.3.4 owns scripts/ci/e2e_extreal_accelerator_pilot.sh and independent performance adjudication. E15 may close with an evidence-backed refusal, but it cannot promote a GPU path until functional equivalence, full workflow benefit, bounded logs, replay, and the configured DSR gate pass; kernel-only speedups and unrepresentative synthetic cases carry no production authority.

title: GPU/accelerator doctrine + backend evidence-class specification (policy before silicon)
description:
WHY: GPU work approached calendar-first would burn the program's scarcest resource (focused effort) on an unmeasured bet, and approached naively would break the determinism story (fs-govern already lists GPU reductions as a reproducibility risk). Writing the doctrine BEFORE any pilot means the eventual pilot (if profiling justifies one) starts with its evidence obligations defined instead of retrofitted.

WHAT: (a) The doctrine (fs-govern registration + docs): pilot admission requires the e15_2 profiling evidence showing GPU-suitable kernels dominate end-to-end wall time/energy for the ratified vertical; any pilot is [M]-classed and subject to the e16 moonshot displacement rule; a named falsifier (e.g. profiling shows top-3 kernels are bandwidth/latency-bound in ways accelerators do not help at our sizes -> the pilot does not run); (b) the backend evidence class, specified now: any accelerator result must bind device identity, driver/runtime version, compiler + kernel source identity, reduction policy (fixed-order or documented tolerance), and a numerical-equivalence envelope vs the CPU reference path (bitwise where promised, bounded-delta elsewhere — the GPU path gets its OWN evidence class, not an automatic lower-certainty stamp); a CPU reference path remains mandatory forever (fallback + differential testing substrate); cancellation semantics required at kernel-batch boundaries; (c) candidate list recorded with honest suitability notes (LBM streaming/collision, SpMV, FFT, batched constitutive updates, rendering).

DONE WHEN: doctrine registered with falsifier; evidence-class spec reviewed against the fs-evidence/fs-roofline machinery it will plug into; e15_2/e15_3 cite it.

TESTS: governance-record completeness; spec-consistency check (every evidence-class field maps to an existing or explicitly-new record type — no hand-waving fields); doctrine-presence lint.

title: End-to-end vertical profiling: wall-time + energy attribution, top-3 kernels (the GPU go/no-go evidence)
description:
WHY: The GPU decision needs the one artifact nobody has: an END-TO-END profile of the real product workflow (not kernel microbenchmarks) showing where wall-clock and energy actually go — including the unglamorous phases (import, census, assembly, BC setup, report, ledger I/O) that accelerators never help. fs-roofline + fs-substrate provide machine axes and measurement discipline; this extends attribution to the whole pipeline.

WHAT: (a) Pipeline-phase attribution: instrument the e06_5 orchestration stages (already ledgered ops) with wall-time and, where the platform exposes it, energy estimates; within solve stages, kernel-level attribution (assembly, SpMV, factorizations, coupling iterations, radiation exchange, UQ sampling loop) via the existing tune/roofline machinery; (b) runs across the representative workload set (the e06_12 examples + a scaled-up stress case) on BOTH reference ISA families with machine fingerprints (quiet-host discipline for anything feeding decisions — the shared-M4 lesson); (c) the decision artifact: phase/kernel attribution tables, the top-3 kernel identification with their roofline positions (compute-bound? bandwidth-bound? latency/irregular?), and the honest GPU-suitability read per the e15_1 doctrine (a bandwidth-bound SpMV at our sizes is a known-marginal case — say so); (d) the go/no-go recommendation recorded with the evidence, either outcome legitimate.

DONE WHEN: profiles captured on both ISAs; decision artifact rendered deterministically from ledgered measurements; the doctrine's falsifier evaluated against real numbers; e15_3 proceeds or closes-as-refused accordingly.

TESTS: instrumentation-overhead check (profiling changes wall time by a bounded, measured fraction); attribution completeness (phases sum to total within tolerance, gaps named); determinism of the artifact from fixed measurement inputs; e2e: full profiling campaign logged per phase/kernel with fingerprints.

## Acceptance Criteria

Profile the complete admitted cooling workflow on frozen representative scenarios and machine states, attributing wall time, CPU and device time, energy, memory traffic where measurable, transfers, synchronization, orchestration, I/O, and cancellation overhead to stable stages and naming the top three kernels with uncertainty. Unit tests cover trace aggregation, clock and energy-unit conversion, overlap accounting, warmup policy, outlier handling, confidence intervals, and artifact serialization; boundary tests cover sub-resolution stages, zero device work, one sample, thermal throttling, loaded-host refusal, and counters unavailable. Property and metamorphic tests use synthetic traces and stage reorderings with preserved totals; mutants that omit overhead, double-count overlap, cherry-pick runs, ignore host load, or rank by kernel-only time must fail. Counter failure, cancellation, deadline, sample and log caps, disk pressure, interrupted runs, and unstable host conditions must return bounded NO-DATA or noncertifying evidence. This Bead owns scripts/ci/e2e_extreal_vertical_profile.sh and immutable workload, host fingerprint, raw trace, summarized attribution, and replay metadata. The configured DSR gate and accepted measurement window must pass; profiling identifies candidates only and cannot authorize the accelerator pilot or assert speedup.

title: Conditional GPU pilot [M]: one kernel, full evidence class, CPU-differential harness (gated on profiling)
description:
WHY: IF (and only if) e15_2's evidence shows accelerator-suitable kernels dominating, a single-kernel pilot answers the real questions: can the backend evidence class be implemented honestly; what does deterministic-or-bounded equivalence cost; does the end-to-end speedup survive contact with the whole pipeline (Amdahl accounting mandatory). This bead is DELIBERATELY conditional — if profiling says no, it closes as refused-with-evidence, which is a success of the policy, not a failure of the program.

WHAT (contingent scope): (a) backend selection recorded (wgpu-class portable vs Metal-first given the primary dev platform — the choice must address the Franken-only policy explicitly via the e11_1-style ruling: an accelerator runtime is a production dependency and needs its own admission decision); (b) ONE kernel from the profiling top-3 implemented with: CPU reference path unchanged, fixed-order reductions or a declared equivalence envelope, the full e15_1 evidence class emitted per run (device/driver/compiler/kernel identity, envelope verification), cancellation at batch boundaries, and fs-roofline measurement on the accelerator's own axes; (c) the differential harness: continuous CPU-vs-GPU comparison over the kernel's test corpus with envelope enforcement (a divergence outside envelope is a determinism incident); (d) end-to-end honesty: the pilot's report states the WORKFLOW-level speedup (Amdahl), not the kernel-level flatter number; (e) [M] discipline: feature-flagged, off the product path, displacement-rule compliant.

title: E16 Governance and metrics: maturity registry, critical path, moonshot WIP cap, dashboards, doc truth
description:
WHY: 130+ crates, per-crate contracts, and a very large fine-grained issue graph can reward LOCAL completeness while delaying integrated usefulness. A crate passing its local suite must not move the product score unless it advances an end-to-end supported capability. Governance must make the vertical capability graph the authoritative critical path and make integration ownership real. Also: the README's stale 127-crate count (actual: 135 native workspace fs-* members + xtask + standalone fs-wasm = 136 fs-* dirs) is small but symptomatic — the project evolves faster than its global narrative synchronizes, which is itself a trust defect for a project whose product IS trustworthy claims.

CHILDREN: machine-readable capability maturity registry (levels L1 experimental component / L2 numerically verified / L3 integrated workflow / L4 experimentally validated / L5 supported product capability) + xtask check; vertical capability graph as authoritative critical path (bv label/track conventions + integration-owner annotations); moonshot WIP cap policy in fs-govern (every new [M] workstream must DISPLACE an existing one, name a falsifier, carry a capped budget, and stay off the product critical path — research is not banned, it is budgeted); program metrics dashboard as a deterministic artifact (time-from-CAD-to-decision, blind-experiment error, empirical coverage, false-safe rate, % outputs with complete error budgets, import success/repair/refusal rates, time-to-explain, cross-machine reproducibility, surrogate escalation correctness, independent reproduction success); frozen public schema set with migration policy (project schema, package FORMAT, scenario IR, matdb packs, ledger schema); documentation drift repair + capability matrix distinguishing experimental/verified/validated/supported; e2e-acceptance-weighted DSR gate wiring.

DONE WHEN: maturity states are queryable and enforced (promotion blocked by e02 claim-integrity gate); the critical path is visible in bv; at least one moonshot has been displaced/deferred BY THE RULE rather than by argument; the dashboard regenerates deterministically from ledger + corpus artifacts; README counts are generated or checked, not hand-maintained.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .16.1 through .16.12 to join maturity definitions, authoritative registry state, critical-path metrics, moonshot WIP limits, risk and decision records, documentation truth, semantic audits, portfolio disposition, and primary-spine proof without replacing source evidence with dashboard assertions. The joined governance snapshot must bind issue and artifact identities, maturity and authority states, owner, budget, dependency rationale, evidence freshness, falsifier, promotion gate, exceptions, and machine-readable disposition for every portfolio item; stale or contradictory inputs must be displayed and block promotion. The terminal semantic-truth owner is .16.9 via scripts/e2e/semantic_doc_truth.sh and the portfolio activation owner is .16.12 via scripts/ci/portfolio_primary_spine_e2e.sh, with .16.11 providing the complete disposition contract. E16 closes only after schema, graph, cycle, stale-data, mutation, fault, cancellation, resource, deterministic-replay, bounded-log, and configured DSR checks pass; dashboards, status labels, or planner recommendations never mint scientific, human-review, or release authority.

title: Machine-readable capability maturity registry (L1-L5) + xtask check (promotion is a recorded event)
description:
WHY: "Is this capability experimental, verified, integrated, validated, or supported?" currently has no queryable answer — status lives in README prose, CONTRACT no-claims, and folklore. The maturity registry is the spine of program governance: the e02 promotion gate needs promotions to be EVENTS; the capability matrix (e06_10) needs a source of truth; the dashboard needs states to count.

WHAT: (a) A versioned registry file (repo root, identity-hashed like identity-authorities.json) mapping capabilities (product-meaningful units: "steady conduction solve", "correlation convection rung", "evidence packaging", "VTU export" — not crates; one crate can host several capabilities, one capability can span crates) to: maturity level (L1 experimental component / L2 numerically verified / L3 integrated workflow / L4 experimentally validated / L5 supported product), the evidence refs justifying the level (tests/corpus/scorecard entries per level-specific criteria: L2 requires named Gauntlet tiers green; L3 requires e2e-lane coverage; L4 requires corpus validation + coverage; L5 requires support policy + migration promises), owner, and last-review date; (b) xtask check-maturity: registry schema valid; level criteria's evidence refs exist and are green-checkable; promotions since the last committed state flagged for the e02 claim-integrity gate; DEMOTIONS always allowed and logged; (c) level-criteria doc merged (what each level requires, per capability class); (d) initial population for the cooling vertical's capabilities honestly (most start L1/L2 — that is the point).

DONE WHEN: registry populated for the vertical + the load-bearing substrate capabilities; check-maturity in check-all; a rehearsed promotion (with evidence) and a rehearsed blocked-promotion (e02 gate) both demonstrated.

TESTS: unit (schema; criteria-evidence resolution; promotion/demotion event detection); e2e: registry audit run logging per-capability level, evidence status, and staleness (last-review age), plus the two rehearsal transcripts.
close_reason:
Landed at the capability-maturity commit (docs/MATURITY_LEVELS.md + capability-maturity.json + xtask/src/maturity.rs + check-all wiring).

(a) REGISTRY: capability-maturity.json, schema frankensim-capability-maturity-v1, 14 capabilities keyed by product-meaningful id (not crate), each with level, owner, last_review, crates scope (what the e02 gate matches on), and typed evidence refs. Honest population: L1=4, L2=10, L3=0, L4=0, L5=0. Nothing is L4 because the external V&V corpus (e04) does not exist; nothing is L5 because no written support policy does. Entries carry their own gaps: solvers.krylov names open bead f85xj.2.24 as a do-not-promote condition; ledger.design-ledger cites NO test evidence because none currently passes (bead frankensim-fs-ledger-latent-failures-xys1z); wasm.browser-flagships cannot be exercised in place at all (bead f85xj.2.39).

(b) CHECK: xtask check-maturity, wired into check-all. Validates schema/entry structure; RESOLVES every evidence ref against the tree (test refs must name a real , so a renamed or deleted test silently voiding a level is a violation); enforces the mechanically-checkable level bars (L2+ needs a test, L3+ a lane, L4+ a corpus, L5 a support-policy doc); detects promotions and demotions against the last committed registry. Demotions are ALWAYS allowed and merely logged — the asymmetry is deliberate, since a registry where lowering a claim is procedurally harder than raising one accumulates false claims by construction. Deterministic: no wall-clock arithmetic, so check-all output does not change with the date.

(c) LEVEL CRITERIA DOC: docs/MATURITY_LEVELS.md — what each level requires, why a capability is not a crate, the promotion-as-event rule, and the explicit statement that a golden hash alone keeps a capability at L1 (a golden freezes behavior, it does not verify meaning).

(d) INITIAL POPULATION: cooling vertical + load-bearing substrate, deliberately unflattering. thermal.conduction-solve is L1 because bead f85xj.5.1 is not built — the registry credits the substrate to the substrate, not to the unbuilt capability.

VERIFICATION: 5 unit tests green (structural defects each caught; level bars per level; unresolvable refs — missing file, missing fn, and corpus-not-resolved; plus a test asserting the LIVE registry is clean, so the shipped file cannot rot). check-maturity reports 0 violations on the live tree. title: Semantic doc-truth Gauntlet: contradiction mutants, authority drift, and independent public-claim replay
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Purpose

Independently prove that the semantic documentation-truth repair works across the live repository and fails when the narrative drifts. This is not a spelling/style review. It is the acceptance lane for public project-state claims whose wrong value can misdirect users, agents, maturity promotion, and release decisions.

## Test corpus

Maintain reviewed before/after fixtures for every 2026-07-27 contradiction: partial CLI solve versus unavailable/full wording; 4 Level-B and 4 Level-C corpus records versus stale one/one prose; transient+duty conduction versus `STEADY ONLY`; live `Catalog::builtin` versus no catalog; project schema frozen versus pre-freeze; fs-wasm lock/build state variants; four-versus-five ledger reds; capability maturity 4 L1/11 L2/0 L3+; and no released/supported product.

## Adversarial plan

- Independently mutate each authority without its projection and each projection without its authority.
- Add simultaneous true statements at different scopes, such as a real two-stage solve prefix plus an unavailable full solve, and require unambiguous scoped wording rather than a false contradiction or false pass.
- Duplicate positive and negative claims in separate sections/contracts and require both locations in diagnostics.
- Rename/move symbols, change generated counts, close/reopen Beads, alter historical sections, and change feature gates to verify the checker follows declared authority rather than brittle line numbers or issue status.
- Remove a required fact marker, introduce an unknown state, corrupt a registry, and make the authority itself inconsistent; all must fail closed.
- Test deterministic ordering and exact JSON/text diagnostics under shuffled files and parallel extraction.

## Independent replay and user outcome

A second agent/process runs the checker from a clean artifact set and reconstructs every public high-risk fact from its declared source without reading implementation notes. Generate a concise current-capability projection suitable for README/report/site reuse, but preserve narrative no-claim context. Confirm that a new user can distinguish component code, partial CLI prefix, L2 evidence, L3 workflow, L4 validation, and L5 support without consulting source.

## Logging and evidence

For every fact, retain fact/schema version, authority kind/path/root, projection path/location, declared scope, expected/observed state/value, extraction/checker version, verdict, and suggested repair. Archive mutant identities and prove every seeded mutant is killed. Run the named doc-truth/check-all/DSR lane at a stable snapshot and retain its receipt. A generic symbol-exists check, regex-only pass, or manual prose audit cannot close this Bead.


## Acceptance Criteria

Every reviewed contradiction fixture and every authority/projection/scope/duplication/unknown/corruption mutant is detected or correctly scoped; a clean independent replay reconstructs all high-risk public facts and current capability levels deterministically; real README/CONTRACT checks, detailed JSON/text logs, mutant-kill inventory, and stable-snapshot check-all/DSR receipt are retained.

## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set is primarily test/acceptance infrastructure: semantic-fact fixtures, contradiction mutants, real-tree doc integration, deterministic JSON/text snapshots, and DSR wiring. Do not manually repair prose from this Bead; `16.9` owns implementation. A second agent/process must run the clean replay, preserve every killed/surviving mutant, and execute constellation preflight plus `dsr quality --tool frankensim`.

## Phase 9.5 real supported-command E2E

The acceptance lane executes the actual binary for `frankensim --help`, valid and invalid validate, admitted import, solve at whatever prefix the typed authority currently declares, and report/package in unavailable and implemented states as the project evolves. Expectations come from authority, not a frozen 2026 snapshot. Mutants cover omitted/false-advertised commands, partial solve stated as absent or complete, report/package on incomplete solve, feature/default mismatch, historical-as-current, unknown/duplicate/missing axes, stale/source movement, overlapping positive/negative scopes, and exit/diagnostic drift. The archive binds command, binary hash, HEAD, constellation, schema/checker, stdout/stderr hashes, exit, event sequence, and mutant and reconstructs the verdict without source inspection or rerun.
design:
The acceptance boundary is an independent bounded transformation: UnverifiedTruthArchive -> verify_bounded -> AdjudicatedPublicTruthReceipt. The input archive contains authority snapshots, projections, CLI transcripts, schema and checker versions, source closure, mutant manifest, budgets, and artifact roots, but confers no public authority. The verifier does not import implementation extractors or trust producer verdict fields.

Verification checks exact required-fact and command-case set equality, authority uniqueness, scope overlap, freshness, feature and history partitioning, projection consistency, deterministic ordering, log cardinality, exit and diagnostic semantics, artifact integrity, and every mutant outcome. Missing, duplicate, malformed, unknown-version, over-budget, stale, source-moved, or owner-only evidence yields a typed non-Pass state.

A new user comprehension matrix is reconstructed from receipts alone: component code, refusal-only or partial prefix, measured evidence, verified component, validated workflow, released artifact, and supported product remain visibly distinct. The checker produces stable codes and ranked repairs and retains one bounded family decision row per fact, command case, and mutant. Those rows are not runner terminals; the outer RunnerSpecV2 family stream alone owns case_terminal, run_summary, and final run_terminal.
acceptance_criteria:
1. UnverifiedTruthArchive and AdjudicatedPublicTruthReceipt are distinct typed schemas and only verify_bounded can create the latter. 2. The independent checker rebuilds every high-risk public fact and CLI expectation without production extractor code, implementation notes, or producer verdicts. 3. Exact set equality is checked separately within the typed fact, projection, command-case, feature-partition, history-interval, and mutant domains; declared foreign-key and coverage joins connect those domains. Heterogeneous rows are never compared as one set. 4. Reviewed contradiction fixtures and authority, projection, scope, duplicate, unknown, corrupt, stale, source-movement, exit, diagnostic, and partial-capability mutants are detected or correctly partitioned. 5. Unit, property, metamorphic, state-model, strict-parser, schema-version, compile-fail, resource-cap, tamper, and replay tests pass. 6. The actual built CLI help, validate, import, solve prefix, report, package, refusal, and migration cases are run with authority-derived expectations. 7. Canonical bounded JSONL binds binary, source closure, constellation, schema, checker, commands, outputs, exits, events, facts, mutants, roots, verdicts, no-claims, and repairs with exactly one case_terminal per fixed case, followed after all cases by one run_summary and one final run_terminal; nothing follows it. 8. A clean independent replay reconstructs all decisions and user capability distinctions without source inspection or rerun. 9. Snapshot and verify-only constellation checks plus DSR registry, dry-run, and terminal quality evidence are retained.

## Terminal E2E ownership

Name exactly one retained, no-mock terminal harness and its owning Bead.

If this Bead owns the harness, freeze its repository-relative script path, CLI modes and case IDs, fixtures, exit classes, source closure, artifact roots, and DSR gate.

If another Bead owns it, name that exact Bead and dependency. This leaf emits a typed contribution only and cannot self-promote.

Do not create one script per scientific leaf when a shared runner is authoritative.

## Exact VisionPromise terminal contribution

The sole terminal owner is frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.7.1.7, which already hard-depends on this leaf. This Bead contributes immutable case_id vision.semantic_doc_truth to tests/e2e/leapfrog/vision-promise-coverage.toml and scripts/e2e/leapfrog/vision-promise-coverage.sh. Required modes are --list, --check, --self-test, --run --case vision.semantic_doc_truth, --negative CASE, and artifact-only --replay.

The owner must consume the full fact/projection/command/feature/history/mutant partitions and independently rebuild their declared foreign-key joins, not collapse them into one heterogeneous set. Unit/schema/property/metamorphic/state-model/strict-parser/mutation/resource/tamper/cancellation tests cover every authority/projection/scope/duplication/unknown/corrupt/stale/source-movement/partial-capability/exit/diagnostic mutant and clean actual CLI cases. Bounded deterministic redacted JSONL, exact case/run terminal cardinality, immutable archive, source closure, independent replay, and DSR are mandatory. This contribution can expose doc truth but cannot itself classify every VisionPromise or mint product maturity.
notes:
Reality-check revision makes independent public-truth adjudication a typed authority transition, not a second invocation of the implementation checker. This removes common-mode and producer-verdict risk while retaining all command and mutant coverage.

Authority-bearing closure inheritance: huq.24.4 proves candidate runner conformance only; this final gate also consumes huq.24.5's typed rjoq exact-instance handoff receipt. Runner records, candidate evidence, and scientific seals cannot substitute for rjoq admission.

Additive verification-completeness baseline (never a substitute for the specialized criteria above):
- Unit and boundary tests cover happy, empty/zero/one, exact limit, one-below/one-above, maximum-without-huge-allocation, error, units/dimensions, numeric extremes, and deterministic tie/order cases owned by this leaf.
- Property/metamorphic tests exercise algebraic or relational invariants; bounded state/model tests cover lifecycle, concurrency, retry/replay, and invalid transitions where applicable.
- Public authority/type surfaces require API and compile-fail misuse tests. A leaf with no public type must record that fact and provide the nearest strict schema/API-negative equivalent rather than silently omitting the category.
- Seeded mutation tests independently alter every claim-bearing identity, bound, state, policy, route, authority, and no-claim field and retain minimized, reproducible failures.
- Cancellation/deadline plus injected allocation, worker/process, parser, I/O, durable-seal, publication, and replay faults are placed at every transition this leaf owns; drain/quiescence, exact resource return, no partial authority, retryability, and first-cause diagnostics are asserted. Inapplicable fault classes require a typed N/A rationale.
- The terminal owner named by the dependency graph runs a release-built, no-mock E2E using the canonical shared commands: --list, --check, --self-test, --run PROFILE [--family-mode MODE], --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. Nested nonterminal producer leaves emit bounded content-bound artifacts consumed by that runner and must not create a competing `--family-mode all` selector or `--mode`/`--profile` alias; exactly one catalog-owned terminal adapter may expose `--family-mode all` under exact-set registry tests.
- Canonical bounded logs record schema/source/build/tool/target/features, typed lossless values and units, command/profile/family/mode/case/sequence, budgets/work/resources, state/reason, expected/observed/effects, authority/no-claim, diagnostics/ranked repair, stop/drain roots, and relative artifact roots. Invocation manifests are fixed and nonempty; case_start opens every ordered slot with execution=execute|suppressed; suppressed permits zero family rows and requires immediate typed NotRun. Cooperative stops drain/finalize the active case and emit remaining suppressed slots before summary/terminal; forced or unproved truncation emits no terminal. Exact case_terminal/run_summary/run_terminal cardinality, caps, hostile parser cases, tamper detection, separate replay input/output roots, and artifact-only replay are mandatory. Raw scientific/performance/tool data stays in capped artifacts, and only explicitly declared volatile observations are excluded from identity.

title: Primary-product portfolio defect: the ratified Cooling/TDA spine is not uniquely projected or triaged
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Defect

Closed `frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.16.2` declared the EXTREAL vertical graph authoritative, yet the live Beads graph still presents multiple overlapping product spines without a machine-enforced disposition: Cooling L3 (`f85xj.6`), the older 3-D SDF/elasticity vertical (`v6dn`), the shipping marquee CLI (`226w`/`ty23`), the general HELM study-scale suite (`epic-helm-gp3.11`), and the closed original flagship epic (`epic-flagships-mye`) whose contract reality is smoke/component rather than full-fidelity product authority. The creation-time prose recorded roughly 1,236 dependency-blocked and 257 actionable issues, but it retained no exact Beads data root, command/version tuple, or stable snapshot identity. Those figures are therefore an explicitly unrooted historical observation, not current evidence or an acceptance input. Every current blocked, ready, selected, on-path, and off-path count must be recomputed from the exact live `br` snapshot and bound to its database/source/version identity; no copied literal may drive authority.

## End state

Propose Cooling 0.1 as the unique first L3 product spine; L4 and L5 remain separately gated successor scope in an inert candidate snapshot; independent 16.12 must accept and activate it before it changes operational truth. Every other end-to-end/flagship/CLI spine must carry a machine-readable disposition relative to Cooling:

- prerequisite consumed by Cooling, with an explicit edge and seam owner;
- shared infrastructure, with one owner and multiple thin consumers;
- capped research/second-vertical work, with budget, falsifier, and non-blocking status;
- deferred until the applicable separately gated Cooling L3, L4, or L5 successor gate; or
- superseded/absorbed, with preserved historical context and no duplicate acceptance authority.

The disposition affects robot triage and capability critical-path projections; a title/label alone is insufficient.

## Technical approach

- Inventory every open/in-progress Bead that claims vertical, flagship, product, shipping CLI, end-to-end, release, or L3+ scope and map it to capabilities/seams.
- Extend the existing capability-to-Bead/critical-path authority with a versioned `spine_role`, primary-spine ID, disposition, integration owner, budget/WIP class, prerequisites, shared acceptance owner, and promotion gate.
- Repair dependency edges so the Cooling path is executable: stage producers -> solve -> convergence/UQ/report/package -> acceptance -> examples/validation/promotion. Keep research dependencies off this path unless the reference project actually requires them.
- Link or classify `v6dn`, `226w`, `ty23`, `gp3.11`, and `mye`; do not delete history or silently merge distinct theorem/domain work.
- Consolidate repeated shared verification/replay infrastructure once while preserving thin domain-specific proof obligations.
- Make `bv`/robot recipes expose the primary path, its actionable roots, its blockers, and off-path WIP separately.

## Policy and no-claim

This does not cancel ambitious MORPH/FLUX/ASCENT/LUMEN research. It makes the 70/20/10 vertical/substrate/frontier allocation measurable and prevents a research branch from masquerading as product-critical. A closed smoke epic is not a shipped product, and Cooling L3 does not imply L4 validation or L5 support.

## Tests and evidence

Seed duplicate primary spines, a missing disposition, a circular prerequisite, an off-path moonshot blocking Cooling, an unowned seam, duplicate acceptance owners, a closed smoke epic projected as supported, and an absorbed Bead with lost history. Each must fail with exact IDs and ranked repair. `bv --robot-plan --label extreal` and the primary-spine projection must return one acyclic Cooling critical path with actionable roots and explicit off-path classes. Retain before/after graph metrics, edge/disposition inventory, WIP allocation, robot outputs, and stable-snapshot check-all/DSR receipts.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `bv --robot-plan` and inspect all open/in-progress issues that claim vertical, flagship, product, shipping CLI, end-to-end, release, or L3+ scope. 2. Observe Cooling `f85xj.6`, `v6dn`, `226w`/`ty23`, `epic-helm-gp3.11`, and the historical `epic-flagships-mye` without one enforced machine-readable disposition/acceptance owner relative to the first L3 goal. 3. Run the documented EXTREAL label recipe and compare it with the global actionable roots; labels/capability cross-references do not mechanically prevent competing spines from consuming integration WIP or projecting smoke completion as product progress. 4. Confirm there is no versioned rule that rejects duplicate primaries, unowned seams, off-path blockers, or duplicate acceptance authorities.

## Acceptance Criteria

A versioned spine-role/disposition authority classifies every product/vertical/flagship/CLI e2e Bead; Cooling f85xj.6 is the unique primary L3 spine until its gate closes; v6dn, 226w, ty23, gp3.11, and mye have explicit non-lossy dispositions and seam/acceptance ownership; robot plan exposes one acyclic Cooling path plus off-path WIP; all duplicate/cycle/moonshot/unowned/smoke-as-supported mutants fail; graph and DSR evidence are retained.

## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set: the existing capability/critical-path authority and `xtask` enforcement, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, affected Bead metadata/dependency edges through `br` only, and robot-triage recipes. Preserve every historical issue; do not delete, merge, or defer without the exact governed disposition. Run schema/graph/unit fixtures, active and all-edge cycle checks, EXTREAL robot plan, constellation preflight, and DSR. `16.12` owns operational acceptance.

## Phase 9.5 portfolio authority and non-loss rules

`f85xj.6` is the Cooling 0.1 realization of the ratified thermal-design-assurance wedge and the unique active primary L3 integration/promotion spine; `f85xj.6.11` is the sole primary acceptance authority. Closing acceptance does not choose a successor or confer L4/L5. A versioned transition must retain, validate, or replace the primary.

Roles are primary_product, primary_acceptance, primary_enhancement, shared_infrastructure, secondary_candidate, capped_frontier, deferred, historical_evidence, and absorbed_with_successor. Each declaration binds spine, phase, owner, blocking eligibility, budget basis, rationale, acceptance owner, transition gate, and history/successor. Reclassification may not lose features, children, proofs, history, or no-claim boundaries; absorbed requires complete successor mapping; false dependencies may not suppress actionability. Measure 70/20/10 by effort/compute, with missing estimates unaccounted. A governed Cooling label/recipe returns executable leaves; broad extreal remains a portfolio view.
design:
CandidatePortfolioAuthoritySnapshot is the versioned source of primary-spine identity, spine roles, dispositions, owners, phase gates, WIP budgets, falsifiers, exceptions, feature inventory, and historical preservation. Roles include primary product spine, prerequisite consumed, shared infrastructure, capped research or second vertical, deferred by gate, superseded or absorbed, and historical evidence. Every applicable Bead has one role for the snapshot interval.

Cooling f85xj.6 is the unique active primary L3 spine and f85xj.6.11 is the sole acceptance authority until a governed transition. Primary transition is two-phase: propose a successor snapshot with complete feature, proof, child, owner, and history inventory; independently validate uniqueness, non-loss, dependencies, acceptance ownership, budgets, and user projection; then atomically activate it. Acceptance close alone cannot select a successor or confer L4 or L5.

The 70, 20, and 10 allocation is tracked separately for human attention and compute budget, with exact denominators, interval, owner, and exceptions. Exceptions require reason, evidence, owner, expiry, return condition, and effect on both budgets. Shared infrastructure has one acceptance owner and thin consumers; off-path work cannot become a transitive primary blocker without an explicit reviewed exception.

No disposition deletes or collapses ambitions. Absorbed and historical records retain features, children, proofs, no-claims, and lineage. Robot projections distinguish executable leaves from containers, shortest hard blockers from related links, preserved off-path work, and sole acceptance authority.

A CandidatePortfolioAuthoritySnapshot is inert candidate data: it cannot change robot selection, public capability projection, active budgets, or promotion authority. 16.11 validates producer-side completeness and emits the candidate only. Independent 16.12 reconstructs the decision from bounded inputs, adjudicates non-loss/uniqueness/dependencies/budgets/user projection, and alone may atomically install `ActivePortfolioAuthoritySnapshot`. Every non-Pass preserves the exact prior active snapshot.

description:

## Purpose

This is the independent acceptance, atomic activation, and operational drill for the critical-path enforcement repair. It consumes an inert 16.11 candidate; it does not validate an already-active producer decision. It proves that the new disposition data changes actual robot planning and human execution choices rather than adding decorative metadata.

## Drill setup

At a stable Beads snapshot, project every open/in-progress end-to-end, flagship, CLI, release, and L3+ issue into its declared spine role. Reconstruct the Cooling 0.1 route from dirty project input through validate/import/assignment, material/flow/conduction/QoI producers, solve/resume, convergence/UQ/export, report/package, acceptance, examples, external validation, and capability promotion. Identify the actual actionable roots and seam owners.

## Scenarios

1. Normal: Cooling is primary; shared infrastructure appears once; second-vertical/frontier work remains visible but non-blocking.
2. Primary blocker closes: the next Cooling root becomes actionable without manual graph surgery.
3. Shared dependency changes: every consumer sees the same owner/receipt without duplicate implementation Beads.
4. Research urgency: a P0 claim-integrity defect may preempt via an explicit trust-risk exception; a generic moonshot cannot.
5. Primary gate closes: the policy can deliberately promote a second vertical through a versioned decision rather than silently allowing two primaries.
6. Failure mutants: duplicate primary, absent seam owner, off-path dependency inserted into Cooling, absorbed history lost, shared owner duplicated, acceptance task bypassed, closed smoke epic promoted to L5, and WIP allocation above policy.

## User and agent verification

Run the documented `bv` robot recipes and a clean agent handoff. An agent given only the projected graph must select the same top Cooling roots, explain every blocker, distinguish product-critical from trust-risk/frontier work, and find the sole acceptance authority. A reviewer must be able to trace each disposition back to its rationale and preserved issue history.

## Evidence

Retain the exact Beads data root, source/version tuple, issue/edge/disposition sets, primary path, ready/actionable roots, blocker cascade, seam owners, WIP allocation, exception decisions, mutant verdicts, robot outputs, and replay command. The earlier roughly-257-actionable/1,236-blocked prose observation had no retained exact snapshot identity and is classified `HistoricalUnrootedNoData`; it cannot be compared numerically, drive selection, or satisfy evidence. Current and future comparisons require two separately sealed exact snapshots and set-derived counts. Run check-all/DSR and archive receipts without claiming metadata alone completes product work.


## Acceptance Criteria

Every normal/promotion/exception/failure scenario produces the declared deterministic primary-spine verdict; a clean agent selects and explains the same Cooling roots and sole acceptance authority; duplicate/cycle/off-path/unowned/bypass/smoke-as-L5/WIP mutants fail; before/after graph metrics, dispositions, robot outputs, check-all/DSR receipts, and replay commands are retained.

## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set is acceptance-only: portfolio fixtures, robot-plan/replay scripts or existing e2e harness integration, deterministic graph receipts, and governance docs. Do not implement Cooling stages or reclassify issues ad hoc from this task. The drill changes prioritization truth, not code reality: it cannot create L3, L4, or L5 authority and must report that no supported product exists until the corresponding evidence passes. Run cycle/orphan/primary-spine checks, all documented `bv --robot-*` recipes, constellation preflight, and DSR; retain input data hash and exact outputs.

## Phase 9.5 execution modes and user output

Mode 1 is read-only replay against the live tracker. Mode 2 creates isolated mutant fixture repositories exclusively through br create/update/dep commands, never handwritten JSONL or direct SQLite. All analysis invokes robot-only bv. Output sections are Now actionable Cooling leaves, Next after each blocker, Why blocked shortest paths, Off path preserved role/budget/falsifier, Exceptions with owner/evidence/expiry/return, and Acceptance with sole authority/promotion prerequisite.

Mutants cover container selection, secondary transitive blocker, related-as-prerequisite, duplicated shared work, exception without expiry/evidence, acceptance close without transition, successor feature/history loss, stale bv hash or graph movement, primary priority inversion, unknown role, and unaccounted WIP. JSONL binds HEAD, Beads hash, br/bv/schema versions, sequence, issue/role/phase/owner, blocking eligibility/path, budget, selection, verdict, and repairs; timings are non-identity.
design:

Fixture mode creates an ephemeral isolated Beads repository through br create, br update, and br dep commands only; it never writes JSONL or SQLite directly and never creates a Git clone, branch, or worktree. Replay mode consumes retained bounded inputs and outputs without tracker access. Every graph analysis call uses a documented bv robot flag only.

The selection algorithm distinguishes executable leaves from epics and containers, blocking from related edges, transitive shortest blockers from descriptive parents, shared owners from duplicate work, and active exceptions from expired ones. Inputs bind the PortfolioAuthoritySnapshot, Beads data root, br and bv versions, source closure, schema, and algorithm version. Graph movement during a run yields Stale.

A clean independent implementation must select the same roots and explanations. No nondeterministic agent judgment may enter canonical selection. Mutant repositories are bounded and cover container choice, secondary blockers, related-edge misuse, shared-work duplication, missing exception data, illegal acceptance transition, successor loss, stale data, priority inversion, unknown role, and unaccounted WIP.

Every component has an exact integer/byte encoding and ascending/descending direction; canonical issue ID is the final tie-break. Equal priority/impact, shuffled discovery, and graph serialization cannot change roots.

title: Program metrics dashboard: outcome metrics as a deterministic artifact (not vibes, not test counts)
description:
WHY: The program optimizes what it measures, so it must measure OUTCOMES: time from CAD to defensible decision; error vs blind experiments; empirical coverage; false-safe rate; % of outputs with complete error budgets; import success/repair/refusal on the supplier corpus; time-to-explain a surprising result; cross-machine reproducibility; surrogate escalation correctness; independent reproduction status.
