title: Weight e2e acceptance over local counts in DSR gates (the quality lane reflects program values)
description:
WHY: What CI gates, engineers optimize. If the DSR quality lane weighs 276 crate test files equally with the one lane that proves the product works, local completeness keeps winning attention. The gate structure must encode the program's stated hierarchy: e2e acceptance (e06_11), corpus/scorecard health (e04_8), claim-integrity (e02_3), and maturity consistency (e16_1) are the headline gates; crate-local suites remain necessary but are diagnostics when they conflict with shipping the vertical.

WHAT: (a) DSR lane restructuring for this repo: a named gate hierarchy — Tier 1 (release-blocking): e2e acceptance lane, claim-integrity gate, check-all (incl. the new maturity/schema/docs checks), determinism goldens; Tier 2 (merge-expected): workspace test suite, clippy/fmt; Tier 3 (informational cadence): perf lanes, matrix lanes (e03_4), corpus sweeps — each tier's blocking semantics documented and wired into the DSR config for frankensim; (b) failure-priority doctrine: a Tier-1 failure outranks any number of Tier-2 greens in triage (documented in CONVENTIONS; the sweeper/agent workflow instructions updated accordingly); (c) reporting: DSR runs cite tier structure in their output so agents parse status correctly; (d) periodic review: tier assignments revisited at release trains (a lane can graduate/demote as the program matures).

DONE WHEN: tier structure configured + documented; one full DSR run demonstrates the tiered reporting; CONVENTIONS updated; agents' session protocols reference the tiers.

TESTS: config validation (every named lane exists and runs); a seeded Tier-1 failure demonstrably blocks while Tier-3 failures do not; e2e: a full tiered DSR run transcript with per-tier verdicts logged.


## Acceptance Criteria

Tier 1 product/integration and Tier 2 required component correctness gates are both mandatory for release; only explicitly declared Tier 3 cadence lanes may be non-blocking and stale/missing remains visible; config schema, unknown/duplicate/missing lane, deterministic per-tier JSONL, and real DSR failure drills prove no weighting can convert a red required unit/workspace suite into permission to ship.

## Phase 9.5 safe gate weighting

Tier 1 integrated/product gates and Tier 2 required component correctness gates are both mandatory for release. Tiering changes reporting prominence, triage order, and diagnostic grouping; it never turns a red required unit/workspace suite into permission to ship. Only explicitly declared Tier 3 cadence lanes may be nonblocking, and missing/stale state remains visible. Add config-schema tests, unknown/duplicate/missing-lane refusal, deterministic per-tier JSONL, and real DSR drills that independently fail Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 and assert the exact release verdict.

title: Abstraction consolidation reviews: retire/freeze/merge what no supported workflow exercises (release-train cadence)
description:
WHY: The governance review calls for "regular removal or consolidation of abstractions not exercised by a supported workflow" — in a 135-crate workspace, abstractions that no end-to-end path exercises are not neutral: they cost comprehension, maintenance, CI time, and they dilute the signal of what the product actually is. The e16_3 moonshot cap governs NEW speculative work; this bead governs the EXISTING inventory's slow accretion.

WHAT: (a) A consolidation review protocol run at release trains (e13_4 cadence): inputs = the e16_1 maturity registry (capabilities stuck at L1 with no consuming workflow), the e16_2 capability->bead cross-references, and a usage sweep (which crates/modules no vertical, campaign, or e2e lane transitively exercises — mechanically derived from the dependency graph + test coverage); (b) per-candidate disposition, recorded: KEEP (named consumer or named trust-risk rationale), CONSOLIDATE (merge into a neighbor with a migration note), FREEZE (explicitly parked: compiles + tests stay green but no new investment — a visible state, not a quiet death), or RETIRE (removal proposal — requiring the user's explicit approval per the repo's no-deletion rule; agents PROPOSE retirement, never execute it unilaterally); (c) the review outcome is a governance record (what was examined, dispositions, rationale) so the next review starts from state, not archaeology; (d) guard against false economy: consolidation must never break the layering rules or merge crates across determinism classes — the checks (check-layers, check-contracts) gate the consolidations themselves.

TESTS: usage-sweep correctness (a known-exercised crate never flagged; a synthetic orphan crate flagged); disposition-record schema tests; post-consolidation full gate run (check-all + workspace tests green) logged as the consolidation's acceptance evidence.

title: Semantic documentation-truth blind spot: live README and CONTRACT contradictions pass current checks
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Defect and user impact

The generated-count/maturity checks from closed `frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.16.6` and the marker-oriented claim lint from closed `frankensim-claim-state-lint-06yc` do not catch internally contradictory semantic status prose. At the 2026-07-27 audit snapshot, all of these contradictions are live:

1. `README.md` still says solve is unavailable, while `fs-cli` implements and documents a durable `import-verify -> assign` prefix and explicitly refuses only the four later stages.
2. `README.md` says the V&V corpus has one Level-B fixture and one Level-C curve, while `fs-vvreg` defines four Level-B cases and retains Martin-Moyce plus three published Level-C records.
3. `fs-conduction/CONTRACT.md` says `STEADY ONLY` and no transient staging, then later documents implemented transient and duty-cycle paths; the owning implementation Beads are closed.
4. `fs-ir/CONTRACT.md` documents the live generated `Catalog::builtin`, then later says no operator catalog exists; source and tests confirm the catalog.
5. Related audit examples include the frozen `project.fsim` policy versus a pre-freeze contract, contradictory fs-wasm status prose, and README disagreement over four versus five ledger failures.

Users and agents cannot tell which statement is authoritative, and current doc checks can remain green. For a project whose product is trustworthy claims, this is a claim-integrity defect.

## End state

Repair every verified contradiction and extend doc truth from literal counts/symbol existence to source-derived semantic status. Each dynamic fact should have one authority and one projection: capability maturity, CLI stage state, validation-corpus inventory, public schema freeze/version, operator catalog availability, test/known-regression counts, and release/support state. Narrative text may explain the fact but must not independently redefine it.

## Technical approach

- Inventory all public README/CONTRACT status assertions and map each to a typed authority: registry record, code declaration, generated inventory, schema policy, CLI stage table, corpus manifest, DSR/known-regression artifact, or explicit static no-claim assertion.
- Generate compact factual blocks where possible. Where prose must remain hand-written, add stable fact IDs/structured markers and a checker that compares the claim state/value to the authority.
- Model staged capabilities precisely: `unavailable`, `partial prefix`, `implemented`, `measured`, `verified`, `validated`, and `supported` are distinct. The CLI solve prefix must not become a full-solve claim.
- Detect contradictory assertions within one document or across authoritative projections, including positive/negative statements for the same fact.
- Report exact fact ID, both locations, observed values/states, authority source, and ranked repair. Never auto-upgrade prose when evidence is absent.
- Update the affected README and contracts, then scan all current docs for the same defect class.

## Scope discipline

Do not turn this into generic natural-language truth inference or an unreviewable regex list. Start with a versioned finite fact schema for high-risk project claims and an explicit mapping to code/registry authorities. Preserve historical prose only when clearly dated and labeled. Do not count issue closure as implementation evidence.

## Tests and logging

Unit tests cover each fact extractor and state lattice. Seeded fixtures reproduce all listed contradictions. Mutation tests change stage availability, corpus counts, schema freeze state, catalog presence, ledger-red counts, registry maturity, and release state without updating prose; each must fail with a precise diagnostic. Test a legitimate partial capability so the checker does not force binary present/absent language. Integration runs the real README and all CONTRACTs and emits deterministic JSON/text rows containing fact ID, authority, projections, locations, and verdict.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the existing doc-facts/claim checks on the current tree and observe that they do not report the contradictions below. 2. Compare README solve status with `crates/fs-cli/CONTRACT.md` and `src/solve.rs`: the README says unavailable while a durable two-stage prefix exists. 3. Compare README Level-B/Level-C counts with `fs-vvreg/src/thermal_level_b.rs`, `fs-vvreg/src/corpus.rs`, and corpus tests: the prose says one/one while code retains four/four. 4. Compare the early `STEADY ONLY` paragraph with later transient/duty sections in `fs-conduction/CONTRACT.md`. 5. Compare the implemented catalog section with the later no-catalog paragraph in `fs-ir/CONTRACT.md` and `src/catalog.rs`. 6. Repeat for schema-freeze, fs-wasm status, ledger-red count, unsafe-capsule count, fs-rand implemented/future, and FFT follow-up contradictions. Current checks remain green or silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

All enumerated live contradictions are repaired without overclaiming; a versioned typed semantic-fact authority covers CLI stages, V&V corpus, schema freeze/version, catalog availability, known-regression counts, maturity, and release/support state; real README/CONTRACT integration is green; every seeded stale/positive-negative/partial-state mutant fails with exact authority and locations; deterministic logs and DSR proof are retained.

## Ownership and Verification Handoff

Expected touch set: `xtask` doc-fact/claim checks and fixtures, `README.md`, the specifically contradictory crate CONTRACTs, `capability-maturity.json`, schema/corpus/catalog/known-regression authorities, and governing doc-truth policy. Update prose only after the typed authority is fixed. Run focused xtask unit/integration fixtures, the real-tree doc check, constellation preflight, and DSR. `16.10` owns independent replay and mutant adjudication.

## Phase 9.5 typed public-truth model

Model orthogonal axes, never one total order: execution is absent, refusal-only, partial-prefix with completed stages and first gap, or complete; measurement is unmeasured or measured with receipt/workload/machine/revision; evidence authority is NoClaim, Estimated, Verified, or Validated; integration maturity is L1-L5; distribution is source-only, built-artifact, or released; support is unsupported, experimental, or supported with policy/versions/window. Claims contradict only when subject, scope, axis, revision interval, and feature configuration overlap.

Register README, every CONTRACT, generated capability tables, actual CLI help and refusal diagnostics, worked examples, report/package matrices, and release/support prose. Dynamic facts bind source revision, producing receipt, and freshness. Help/refusals tell users what works, durable completed prefix, first unavailable stage, whether anything was written, and next supported action. Add schema/migration/authority-uniqueness/scope/history/feature/freshness/ranked-repair unit tests and `scripts/e2e/semantic_doc_truth.sh` against the real compiled CLI; volatile timings stay outside the deterministic fact digest.
design:
Define PublicFactKey as a versioned tuple of subject, scope, axis, source revision interval, feature configuration, target or distribution channel, and schema version. Orthogonal axes are execution state, measurement state, evidence authority, integration maturity, distribution state, and support state; no total maturity integer may erase distinctions. Each key has exactly one authority and any number of registered projections.

Authority extraction yields a VerifiedAuthoritySnapshot only after source-derived extraction, internal consistency, schema validation, freshness evaluation, and stable root construction pass. Bead status and narrative prose are never implementation authority. Dynamic facts bind source closure, producing receipt, validity interval, and staleness rule. Historical facts require an explicit historical scope and cannot overlap current claims accidentally.

Projection checking includes README, every CONTRACT, generated capability tables, actual CLI help and structured refusals, worked examples, report and package matrices, and release or support prose. User diagnostics state what works, completed durable prefix, first unavailable stage, whether mutation occurred, and the next supported action. Repair ranking prefers correcting a bad authority first and updating all projections from one snapshot.

The real E2E executes release-built public CLI paths for help, validate, import, partial solve, report, package, unavailable stages, malformed input, feature variants, and migration. It emits bounded canonical JSONL as run_start; per fixed case case_start, ordered rows, and one case_terminal; then run_summary and one final run_terminal, with nothing afterward. CaseExpectationV2 makes exact expected negative behavior a conformance Pass without promoting public authority.
acceptance_criteria: 1. PublicFactKey and every axis, state, scope, feature, revision, authority, projection, freshness, and history rule are versioned and strictly validated. 2. Every high-risk public fact has one unique authority and all README, CONTRACT, generated, help, refusal, example, report, package, release, and support projections are registered. 3. All enumerated live contradictions are repaired without promoting partial solve, measured evidence, source artifacts, or closed Beads into unsupported capability. 4. Unit tests cover extractors, state axes, scope overlap, feature variants, migration, history, freshness, authority uniqueness, and ranked repair. 5. Property and metamorphic tests cover file order, equivalent projections, feature partition, revision intervals, and deterministic roots. 6. Compile-fail and schema tests prevent unverified snapshots from becoming public authority. 7. Every stale, positive-negative, missing, duplicate, unknown-state, authority-drift, count, stage, schema, catalog, release, and support mutant fails with exact locations and repairs. 8. scripts/e2e/semantic_doc_truth.sh invokes the real built CLI, emits exactly one bounded case_terminal per fixed case, then one run_summary and one final run_terminal, and independently replays. 9. Constellation snapshot identity and verify-only preflight, dsr repos info frankensim, DSR dry-run, and terminal dsr quality proof are retained.

title: E17 Scenario semantics: make the model reflect how engineers describe systems (no silent defaults)
description:
WHY: Real engineering intelligence lives more in scenario semantics than in another Krylov solver. fs-scenario today has typed BCs with dimensional expectation tables, load cases + factored combinations (declared, not evaluated), Frictionless/Coulomb/Tied contact, a REQUIRED Environment (gravity/ambient T/ambient p), payload algebra, frames, and stochastic ensembles — a strong base. Missing for engineering use: assemblies/parts/regions/interfaces with PERSISTENT entity identity (region names are currently strings bound solver-side); materials as MANUFACTURED STATES; joints/fasteners/welds/adhesives/gaps and interface conductance; sensors + observation operators as scenario objects; duty cycles and operating envelopes with combination evaluation; design variables + manufacturing constraints; objectives/margins/failure modes; standards clauses + safety factors as versioned policy sources; context of use + intended decision. The Five Explicits doctrine is the philosophical basis; this epic maps it onto familiar engineering objects.

NO-SILENT-DEFAULTS DOCTRINE (enforce, not document): no silent ambient temperature; no implicit zero contact resistance; no unnamed turbulence intensity; no unitless heat-transfer coefficient; no material without state + temperature range + source; no boundary face selected solely by a fragile mesh index; no optimization result without manufacturing and robustness checks. Defaults are rare, visible, and receipted.

CHILDREN: assembly/part/region/interface persistent-identity model; materials-as-manufactured-states binding into fs-matdb cards (state + temp range + source mandatory); interface conductance/joints/fasteners in the scenario model; sensors + observation operators as scenario objects (feeds e12 assimilation); duty cycles/operating envelopes/load-combination evaluation; standards clauses + safety factors + context-of-use records; no-silent-defaults enforcement lint + refusal tests.

DONE WHEN: the Cooling 0.1 project schema (e06) is expressed entirely in these objects; every default that fires leaves a visible receipt; the no-silent-defaults tests demonstrate typed refusals for each doctrine item.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .17.1 through .17.8 to make geometry, materials, joints, sensors, loads, environments, operating states, design variables, objectives, constraints, and failure modes explicit scenario objects with no hidden engineering defaults. The joined schema and admission receipt must bind units, coordinate and time frames, material and interface provenance, uncertainty, sensor observation operators, load histories, operating regimes, allowed variable domains, manufacturing constraints, objective orientation, failure thresholds, capabilities, versions, seeds, and budgets; every omitted required field must refuse with a ranked fix. The terminal no-silent-default owner is .17.7, and .17.8 contributes optimization-semantics fixtures to scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh while remaining non-optimizing at this stage. title: Assembly/part/region/interface model with persistent entity identity (strings become identities)
description:
WHY: fs-scenario's region names are strings bound solver-side — workable for fixtures, fatal for products: a renamed region silently orphans BCs; a re-imported geometry cannot prove it still means the same enclosure; diffs across revisions have nothing stable to diff AGAINST. Persistent entity identity is the foundation the import path (e06_3), design diffs (e11_4), as-built binding (e12_2), and the project schema (e06_1) all stand on — which is why this is the epic's first task and a cross-epic blocker.

WHAT: (a) Entity model: Assembly -> Part -> (Region | Surface | Interface) with typed identities: stable IDs (content-derived where possible: geometry fingerprint + declared name + parent path; collision-checked), display names separate from identity (renames do not orphan), and identity RECEIPTS on every rebinding event (import, re-mesh, revision migration — the e11_4 verdicts land here); interfaces as first-class pairs (ordered where physics cares: which side is the TIM applied to) with their own identity; (b) referential integrity: every scenario object (BC, load, material binding, sensor, requirement) references entities by identity; validation resolves ALL references and reports dangling/ambiguous ones with fix hints (extending the existing Violation code/what/fix pattern); (c) evolution: identity migration receipts when geometry changes (ties to fs-scenario's existing IR-migration discipline); (d) compatibility: existing string-based fixtures migrate mechanically (a string name becomes a declared-name identity with a legacy marker).

DONE WHEN: entity model shipped; the reference cooling scenario expressed in it; rename/re-import fixtures keep bindings intact via receipts; dangling-reference validation proven; legacy migration works.

TESTS: unit (identity derivation + collision handling; reference resolution incl. every dangling/ambiguous case; receipt generation); metamorphic (rename invariance of physics meaning; re-import stability); e2e: a scenario lifecycle (author -> import-bind -> rename -> re-import -> validate) logging every identity event and the final binding table.
close_reason:
Landed in fs-scenario: src/entity.rs (+17 in-src unit tests) and tests/entity_identity.rs (9 cases). fs-scenario 105 tests green, including all 32 pinned canonical IR hashes UNMOVED.

(a) ENTITY MODEL: Assembly -> Part -> (Region|Surface|Interface). EntityId = kind + BLAKE3-256 over a LENGTH-PREFIXED, domain-separated preimage (kind tag, parent identity which transitively encodes the parent path, declared name, optional geometry fingerprint, optional interface pair). Length-prefixing closes the ambiguous-serialization collision shape and is pinned by identity_preimage_is_length_prefixed_and_injective. Display names are NOT in the preimage, so renames cannot orphan. Interfaces are first-class Ordered/Unordered pairs with their own identity. Receipts form an append-only hash chain (sequence == index, each digest binds the previous root); verify_receipts detects interior edits, reorders and drops. Datums, tolerances and assembly placements landed as declarations + validation.

WHAT AN IDENTITY PROVES, stated narrowly: two declarations supplied byte-equal derivation inputs. It does NOT prove two revisions describe the same physical part, that the entity exists in any geometry kernel, or that anyone measured anything. Equal fingerprints => equal supplied bytes; UNEQUAL fingerprints prove NOTHING, because a re-export of an unchanged part routinely changes bytes — which is exactly why a mismatch falls back to the weaker DeclaredPath tier instead of concluding 'different part'. 'Collision-checked' is a fail-closed full-preimage comparison (IdentityCollision vs DuplicateDeclaration), not a claim that BLAKE3 collisions are impossible; both branches are exercised.

EVIDENCE IS NEVER LAUNDERED: EvidenceTier Asserted < Declared < PathMatched < ContentMatched < Identical, and resolve() returns the WEAKEST tier on the supersession chain — a content-matched hop after an asserted hop still resolves Asserted.

(b) REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY: EntityRef/ReferenceSite/BindingTable/validate_bindings extending the existing Violation{code,what,fix} pattern, with 8 distinct fault codes each carrying a fix hint. BC, case-BC and contact sites are fully enumerated and enforced. PARTIAL: Load/MaterialBinding/Sensor/Requirement sites are typed and resolvable but their collections do not exist in fs-scenario yet, so those rows are not existence-checked.

(c) EVOLUTION: apply_import is ATOMIC (a refused revision leaves the catalog byte-identical, proven by PartialEq in two tests). Auto correspondence matches fingerprint first, then declared name + CORRESPONDING parent (following the parent's own supersession, which is what lets a renamed sub-assembly keep its children's path match). A tie at either tier is AmbiguousImportMatch naming two candidates — NEVER a first match. ImportScope::Complete retires omitted strict descendants; a binding to a retired entity is entity-retired-reference, not a silent forward-resolve. PARTIAL: receipts are not emitted or persisted by the IR codec (no IR version bump).

(d) LEGACY MIGRATION: migrate_legacy_scenario walks BC/case-BC/contact sites in declaration order; each distinct region string becomes a Surface whose declared name is that exact string, legacy-marked, with NO invented fingerprint and no inferred hierarchy. Idempotent (re-running appends 0 receipts, re-derives the same ids). Proven with the before-state (8x entity-unbound-site) and a drift case.

FIXTURES: rename (6 renames, bindings unchanged), full CAD re-import (16 identities superseded, 13 content-matched, 3 path-matched, all 8 bindings resolving one hop onto identical fingerprints), identical re-import (0 new identities, 16 Unchanged receipts).

HONEST BOUNDARY ON THE 'REFERENCE COOLING SCENARIO': it does not exist as a repo-wide artifact — the phrase appears only in bead prose for .6.1/.6.3/.17.1. A representative cooling stack (SiC die -> TIM -> liquid-cooled plate; 16 entities, 3 datums, 3 tolerances, 2 placements, 8 reference sites) was authored as this crate's fixture, and both the test header and this record say plainly it is not canonical.

DEFERRED, with reasons: BoundaryCondition.region is still a String — changing it would move byte-stable hash-pinned canonical IR, need an IR version bump and migration, and break fs-ir/fs-solid construction sites outside the boundary. Bindings are therefore a SIBLING table validated against the scenario, and CONTRACT states the consequence as a no-claim: a scenario rebuilt from canonical bytes alone has no bindings and reports every site unbound. Persisting them belongs to the versioned .fsim schema (bead .6.1). Entity validation is also not merged into ValidationPlan/Cx: it has its own explicit EntityBudget with fallible reservation before every mutation, but does not poll cancellation — written into CONTRACT rather than papered over.

NOTE: fs-ir and fs-frame fail to compile at HEAD for unrelated committed reasons (fs-ir E0599 ordered_bytes_stream in machine/causalization.rs:4782; fs-frame E0689 ambiguous float abs in tests/battery.rs:647). Neither is ripple from this change — both crates have no uncommitted edits.

title: Materials as manufactured states: binding requires state + temperature range + source (never a name)
description:
WHY: "Aluminum" is not a material — 6061-T6 extruded vs A380 die-cast differ 40% in conductivity; annealed vs work-hardened copper differ meaningfully; a TIM's cured vs uncured state is a different substance. fs-matdb already models cards with provenance and validity; the SCENARIO side must refuse the name-only shortcut so the e17 doctrine item ("no material selected without state, temperature range, and source") is structural.

WHAT: (a) Material bindings in the scenario reference a MaterialCard identity PLUS a declared manufactured state (from the card's state vocabulary: temper, cure, porosity class, finish where thermally relevant — surface finish feeds emissivity for e05_4) and the temperature range the binding expects (checked against card validity at validate time — the e06_4 envelope check made per-binding); a binding missing state or range is a Violation with a fix hint listing the card's available states; (b) source visibility: the binding surfaces the card's provenance (which handbook/datasheet/measurement) in validation output — users see WHOSE number they are trusting at authoring time, not report time; (c) conflicting-claims interaction: where a card carries coexisting conflicting claims (matdb's design), the binding declares which claim lineage it selects (e06_4's no-auto-pick rule, enforced here at the scenario layer); (d) uncertainty defaults: a binding may not silently narrow the card's uncertainty; tightening requires a declared justification record.

DONE WHEN: the reference scenario's every material binding carries state+range+source; each refusal path proven; provenance renders at validate time; the tightening-requires-justification rule enforced.

TESTS: unit (each missing-field Violation with fix-hint quality asserted; range-vs-validity intersection edges; claim-lineage selection; tightening refusal); e2e: validate runs on correct + deliberately sloppy scenarios logging the full binding table (entity -> card -> state -> range -> source -> verdict).

title: Joints, fasteners, and interface conductance in the scenario model (assembly physics declared, not assumed)
description:
WHY: Heat crosses assemblies through interfaces — bolted, clipped, adhesive, gap-filled — and each interface's conductance is a MODEL choice with uncertainty, not a meshing detail. fs-scenario has contact laws (Frictionless/Coulomb/Tied) aimed at mechanics; the thermal vertical needs the interface-declaration layer that E05_3's physics consumes: which interfaces exist, what card governs each, what state (bolt torque class, TIM thickness) modifies it.

WHAT: (a) Interface declarations on E17_1's interface entities: interface class (bolted-with-pattern, adhesive, TIM, dry-contact, gap-with-fluid) each mapping to fs-matdb InterfaceSystemCard families; state parameters per class (bolt count/torque class + pattern for bolted — contact pressure distribution matters; nominal + tolerance thickness for TIM/adhesive — ties to as-built maps e12_3; gap distance + fluid for gaps); every parameter typed (fs-qty) with uncertainty; (b) the fail-closed rule (E05_3's contract, enforced at scenario level): a geometric contact between parts with NO interface declaration is a validation ERROR listing the undeclared pairs (detected from geometry proximity within tolerance at validate time) — deliberate perfect-contact is declarable but must be DECLARED; (c) mechanical/structural fastener semantics (preload, stiffness) recorded as staged scope with the schema shaped to admit them (the frame/solid crates will want the same objects); (d) each declaration's resolved thermal model + uncertainty flows into E05_3 and the budget.

DONE WHEN: reference assembly's every interface declared; the undeclared-contact detector fires on a seeded omission; class-specific parameters validate; E05_3 consumes the declarations end-to-end.

TESTS: unit (per-class parameter validation; proximity-detection tolerances incl. near-miss cases; the deliberate-perfect-contact declaration path); e2e: assembly validate + solve logging the interface table (pair -> class -> card -> parameters -> resolved conductance -> uncertainty) and the seeded-omission refusal.
acceptance_criteria: Represent joints, fasteners, thermal-interface regions, preload or torque, contact area, roughness, conductance or resistance model, uncertainty, assembly sequence, failure limits, units, provenance, and declared omissions as scenario objects rather than implicit perfect bonds. Unit tests cover schema and validation, series and network assembly, parameter routing, units, serialization, and capability admission; boundary tests cover absent joint, open contact, requested perfect bond, zero or extreme preload, multiple fasteners, disconnected parts, and temperature-range limits. Property tests require physically admissible nonnegative dissipation and stable identity; metamorphic tests cover equivalent unit conversion, component reorder, and declared symmetric assembly; mutants that insert perfect contact, drop a fastener, swap interfaces, default conductance, or erase uncertainty must fail. Missing cards, invalid geometry, cancellation, deadline, object-count and memory caps, and log pressure must refuse or return bounded no-claim diagnostics. This Bead contributes immutable assembly fixtures and joint receipts to .17.7 and scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh. Round-trip replay and the configured DSR gate must pass; declared joint models remain estimates within their carded regimes and do not validate an actual assembly without external evidence.

title: Sensors and observation operators as scenario objects (instrumentation is part of the model)
description:
WHY: The design-build-measure-update loop (e12) and experiment design (e12_7) need sensors to be MODELED: a thermocouple has a location (with placement uncertainty), a mount (whose thermal contact biases the reading), a time constant, a calibration record, and an observation operator mapping the simulated field to what the instrument would read. fs-scenario has no sensor layer (CONTRACT no-claim); fs-assimilate expects caller-supplied observation operators — the scenario is where they should come FROM.

WHAT: (a) Sensor objects on E17_1 entities: type (thermocouple, RTD, flow meter, pressure tap, IR-camera region), location binding (entity + local position with placement uncertainty — the corpus retention schema's field, now first-class at authoring), mount model (the bias/contact declaration: an insulated vs heatsunk mount reads differently — even a declared-perfect mount is a DECLARATION), dynamics (time constant for transient staging), calibration reference (certificate ref + date, matching e04's retention schema so scenario sensors and corpus datasets share vocabulary); (b) observation-operator derivation: each sensor compiles to an operator over the solve's fields (point/patch evaluation with the mount model applied) consumable by fs-assimilate (E12_4's nonlinear operators get their producers here) and by the corpus comparison machinery (predicted-vs-measured uses the SAME operator — eliminating the classic probe-mismatch bug where simulation is compared at the wrong point); (c) virtual sensors: the same objects usable in pure simulation for QoI probes (unifying probe definitions product-wide); (d) placement candidates for e12_7 are sensor objects with a candidate flag.

DONE WHEN: sensors declare + validate + compile to operators; one assimilation and one corpus comparison consume compiled operators; the mount-bias path demonstrably changes a reading; candidate flagging works.

TESTS: unit (per-type validation; operator compilation vs hand-built operators; mount-model arithmetic; placement-uncertainty propagation into operator uncertainty); e2e: instrumented-scenario run logging each sensor's compiled operator, simulated reading vs raw field value (the mount bias visible), and the assimilation handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Represent each sensor and observation operator with identity, measured quantity, placement and frame, footprint, units, calibration and uncertainty, sample clock, delay, saturation and censoring, noise and correlation, missingness policy, provenance, and links to scenario fields; instrumentation must be part of model admission. Unit tests cover schema, field binding, forward observation, claimed derivatives, calibration, time alignment, serialization, and capability checks; boundary tests cover sensor on a boundary, outside domain, duplicate identity, exact saturation, zero and long delay, all-missing data, and singular covariance. Property tests use synthetic fields; metamorphic tests cover rigid transforms, unit and time conversion, sensor permutation, and restart; mutants that sample the wrong field, ignore footprint or delay, default calibration, treat missing as zero, or drop uncertainty must fail. Stream faults, cancellation, deadline, sensor-count and memory caps, clock disorder, and log overflow must emit bounded diagnostics without verified observations. This Bead contributes immutable sensor and pathology fixtures to .17.7 and scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh. Deterministic replay and the configured DSR gate must pass; a declared observation operator cannot certify sensor installation or calibration.

title: Duty cycles, operating envelopes, and load-combination evaluation (from declared to evaluated)
description:
WHY: fs-scenario DECLARES load cases and factored combinations but explicitly does not EVALUATE them, and has no duty-cycle/envelope objects. The vertical needs: an operating envelope (ambient x power x fan-state ranges) driving UQ sweeps (e06_7) and validity checks (e08_3); duty cycles for the transient/reliability staging (e05_9, Level-4 thermal cycling questions); and combination evaluation so "1.2D+1.6L"-style factored cases (or their thermal analogs: worst-case-power + max-ambient + one-fan-failed) become runnable case sets rather than annotations.

WHAT: (a) OperatingEnvelope objects: named axes (ambient T, total power, altitude/pressure, fan states incl. discrete failure modes) with ranges/distributions + declared correlations (hot day and high power co-occur — correlation declared or explicitly unknown, e08 representation rules); envelope drives: UQ sweep domains, validity-domain intersection checks, and worst-case corner enumeration (deterministic corner set with the enumeration rationale logged — corners of correlated envelopes are not the naive hypercube corners); (b) duty cycles: time-fraction or sequence-based profiles over envelope points (steady-state weighted analysis NOW: weighted QoI aggregation with the weighting honestly labeled as steady approximation; true transient staged with e05_9); (c) combination evaluation: factored combinations compile to case sets with per-case provenance (which combination, which factors) and aggregate verdicts (governing case identified per QoI — the report says WHICH condition sizes the design, which is what engineers actually ask); (d) fan-failure combinatorics bounded (declared failure set, not exhaustive 2^n).

DONE WHEN: reference envelope + one duty cycle + governing-case reporting work end-to-end; correlated-corner enumeration proven against a hand-worked case; declared-unknown correlation flows to the budget caveat.

TESTS: unit (envelope validation; corner enumeration with correlations; weighting arithmetic; combination compilation); e2e: envelope-driven run logging the case set, per-case QoIs, the governing case per QoI, and the aggregate verdict with budget caveats.
close_reason:
LilacAspen 2026-07-25: landed e0e7ae97. fs_scenario::envelope. 52/52 tests/envelope.rs, 4/4 new in-src units, whole fs-scenario lib unit suite 42/42 with no regressions, clippy zero findings in envelope.rs, check-docs 0 violations.

DONE-WHEN audited:

- "reference envelope + one duty cycle + governing-case reporting work end-to-end" - MET. envelope_to_governing_case_runs_end_to_end_and_distinguishes_fault_conditions runs reference_cooling_envelope -> 15 corners -> compiled case set -> governing case per QoI, and asserts the governing state is a declared FAILURE rather than a design condition. reference_cooling_envelope ships as a named constructor, not a test fixture, because CONTRACT's worked example refers to it - flagged REPRESENTATIVE, not canonical, following the same honest boundary 17.1 recorded for its own fixture.

- "correlated-corner enumeration proven against a hand-worked case" - MET, and the arithmetic is in the test's doc comment as a table so a reviewer can check it without running anything. Box [300,320] K x [100,200] W under 2.5*T + P <= 975 W. Every value is exactly representable in binary floating point, so the assertion is exact equality, not a tolerance.

- "declared-unknown correlation flows to the budget caveat" - PARTIALLY MET, and I am recording the boundary rather than counting it. The caveat is produced with a stable code (envelope-coupling-unknown), the declared rationale, and a consequence naming the DIRECTION of the error. What does not exist is a consumer: no error-budget object ingests EnvelopeCaveat, because DecisionAssessment is f85xj.8.6 and "make error budgets unavoidable at every user-facing output" is 8.7, both open. The caveat is emitted and testable; it is not yet carried into a budget by any code.

THE CENTRAL CORRECTION, which changed the type design: a correlation coefficient constrains MOMENTS, not SUPPORT. Two axes can be strongly correlated and still jointly attain every corner of their box, so a declared rho cannot license dropping a corner. There is therefore no correlation field anywhere in the API. The bead's prose says "declared correlations", and taking that literally would have produced a type that quietly launders a statistical statement into a geometric one. The only relation that shrinks a corner set is a CoOccurrenceLimit, an explicit claim that a region is unreachable, refused unless it carries the author's physical reason.

THE HAND-WORKED CASE LANDED SOMEWHERE I DID NOT EXPECT. Clipping a corner off a rectangle ADDS vertices: four box corners become five. So "corners of a correlated envelope are not the naive hypercube corners" is NOT the weaker claim that they are a subset - the count need not even move in that direction, and code written on the subset intuition would silently miss the two vertices that exist only on the limit boundary. Both the excluded hypercube corner and the two arrivals are pinned by name.

A REAL DEFECT THE TESTS CAUGHT, worth recording because it would have survived review: the corner LIST order followed the coupling's axis order rather than the envelope's declared axis order. The corner SET was right; only the ordering moved. But a corner's INDEX is what a compiled case cites as its provenance, so swapping the two names in a coupling declaration would have silently renumbered every case in every report while changing nothing physical. The order is now canonical - declared axis order, continuous by value, discrete by DECLARED STATE POSITION so a fan ordering stays as the author wrote it rather than going alphabetical - and the test asserts byte-identity of the two corner lists, not merely equal sets.

AND ONE I PREDICTED WRONG. The end-to-end asserted a single governing case; it has two. The fans are interchangeable in the stand-in model, so both single-fan-failure states govern equally. Physically obvious in hindsight and exactly the case a first-match report would have hidden. Ties report every attaining case, matching the AmbiguousImportMatch discipline 17.1 set.

DESIGN DECISIONS worth retaining:

- Duty weights are declared ONCE. Under Dwells weighting the weights are durations and the fractions are DERIVED, so a duration and a fraction cannot disagree. Two descriptions of one quantity is the failure mode 17.1 and 5.13 both warn about.
- quasi_steady_check MEASURES the premise behind the weighted aggregate instead of asserting it, the same discipline as 5.13's Biot gate. Under Fractions weighting the condition is not merely unmet but UNMEASURABLE - no absolute time exists to compare against a time constant - and the refusal says exactly that, so an untimed cycle cannot score a vacuous pass.
- The co-occurrence half-space is CLOSED. A point exactly on the limit is admissible; treating it as strict would silently exclude the worst attainable operating point. Pinned by a test on a limit passing exactly through a box corner, which also proves that corner is enumerated once rather than twice.
- Exact float equality is used deliberately in two places, each with a justification comment rather than a tolerance: a surviving box corner is COPIED from the axis bound and never computed, and the governing extremum was SELECTED from the same slice. A tolerance in either place would answer a different and unasked question.
- Fan-failure combinatorics: n units give n+1 states, never 2^n. Which multi-failure combinations are worth analysing is a judgement about redundancy, not a product.

REFUSED, each naming the alternative so a reader can tell a limitation from a bug: an axis in two couplings (the feasible set is then a general polytope; general polytope vertex enumeration is NOT implemented and the refusal says so by name); a pinned axis (a declared constant, not an axis); a discrete axis under a linear limit; a limit that empties the box; a limit or an Unknown declaration with no rationale; corner and case products above budget, checked BEFORE allocation with the count named.

NOT DELIVERED from the WHAT list, stated plainly: axis DISTRIBUTIONS (this module models support only - a distribution would be the input to a UQ sweep, and no sweep consumer exists); wiring the envelope into UQ sweep domains (f85xj.6.7, open) and validity-domain intersection checks (f85xj.8.3, in_progress under jemanuel). Those are cross-bead integrations whose consumers are open; the envelope is the producer they will need and its corner set and caveats are the interface.

VERIFICATION METHOD, disclosed because it is not the usual one: verified through a rustc harness rather than cargo test. fs-ledger is a fs-scenario DEV-dependency and is currently at 201 compile errors from the asupersync 0.3.8->0.3.9 async-pager migration (frankensim-asupersync-pin-drift-7fji5). The fs-scenario LIB builds clean, so this is a dev-dep cone outage affecting every agent working in the crate, not a consequence of this change. I ran the integration file and the whole lib unit suite by compiling them directly against the built rlibs.

COORDINATION: `pub mod envelope;` in src/lib.rs and the CONTRACT section were taken under NobleLion's exclusive reservation after asking twice with no reply over roughly 40 minutes. Both files were clean with mtimes 5+ hours old, and the module cannot compile without the mod line. Both edits are additive - one line between `ensemble` and `entity`, and a trailing module section following the precedent NobleLion themselves set for 17.8. Told them on the thread and offered to back it out.

I am closing this bead. The one partially-met DONE-WHEN item - the caveat reaching an error budget - is blocked on E08 building the budget object, not on anything in this module, and holding 17.5 open would misrepresent where the work sits.

title: Requirements with sources: standards clauses, safety factors, context of use, intended decision
description:
WHY: A requirement ("T_junction < 100C") without its SOURCE (derating guideline? datasheet absolute max? internal margin policy?) and its safety-factor lineage cannot support an auditable compliance claim — and the DecisionAssessment (e08_6) needs requirement objects with authority, not magic numbers. Context of use and intended decision are the top-level frame: what question is this project answering, within what envelope, for what consequence class.

WHAT: (a) Requirement objects: quantity ref (QoI identity), limit + direction + margin policy (safety factor with ITS source — a factor of 1.2 from company policy vs 1.0 from a datasheet absolute-max are different claims), source record (standards clause with version — the fs-vvreg standards registry and fs-crosswalk vocabulary connect here; datasheet ref; internal policy doc + version), and severity class (what a violation means: reliability derating vs damage limit); (b) ContextOfUse at project level (extending the existing x68z ContextOfUse work): the intended decision (design selection? compliance sign-off? scoping estimate?) — which calibrates how hard e08's machinery gates (a scoping estimate may tolerate Indeterminate; a sign-off may not), the validity envelope the answers are claimed for, and the consequence framing; (c) versioned policy sources: requirement sources are versioned documents; a source version bump flags dependent requirements for review (the standards-drift problem handled like schema drift); (d) report/assessment integration: every compliance verdict cites its requirement's full lineage.

DONE WHEN: reference project's requirements carry sources + factors + severity; ContextOfUse gates assessment strictness demonstrably; source-version bump flagging works; DecisionAssessment renders the lineage.

TESTS: unit (requirement validation incl. sourceless refusal; factor-lineage arithmetic; context-strictness gating logic; version-bump flagging); e2e: two projects (scoping vs sign-off context) on the same physics logging the differing gate behavior, plus the requirement-lineage table in both reports.

title: No-silent-defaults enforcement: the doctrine as lint + refusal battery (defaults are rare, visible, receipted)
description:
WHY: The Five Explicits doctrine's engineering extension — no silent ambient, no implicit zero contact resistance, no unnamed turbulence intensity, no unitless HTC, no stateless material, no mesh-index face selection, no unchecked optimization result — only holds if it is ENFORCED where scenarios are built and validated. Culture plus deadline equals silent defaults; only refusal machinery survives contact with both. This bead is the epic's consolidated enforcement + test lane.

WHAT: (a) The default-policy audit: enumerate every place the scenario/project/solve path COULD apply a default (a mechanical sweep of constructor defaults, Option fallbacks, and unwrap_or sites in the relevant crates — hand-reviewed per the no-script-rewrite discipline); classify each: REFUSE (must be declared: ambient conditions, interface resistance, material state, turbulence/flow intensity parameters when RANS lands, requirement limits), RECEIPTED DEFAULT (acceptable with visible receipt: solver tolerances, output verbosity), or INTERNAL (no user-facing meaning); (b) enforcement: REFUSE-class paths get typed Violations (most exist via e17_2/3 and fs-scenario's required-Environment precedent — this bead closes the sweep's residue); RECEIPTED-class paths emit default-receipts collected into validate output and the report ("defaults applied" section — an empty section is the goal state for validation-grade runs); (c) the doctrine battery: one refusal test per doctrine item, phrased as user stories (author omits X -> named Violation with fix hint), plus receipt-visibility tests; (d) drift guard: new unclassified default sites flagged by the sweep re-run in check-all (the classification table is the allowlist).

DONE WHEN: sweep classification table merged; every REFUSE item has its refusal test; receipts render; drift guard green in check-all and demonstrably catches a seeded new default.

TESTS: this bead IS the battery — per-item refusal tests with message-quality assertions, receipt-emission tests, allowlist drift detection; e2e: a maximally-sloppy scenario validated, logging every Violation and receipt, then repaired step-by-step to clean (the transcript doubles as user education material).

## Acceptance Criteria

Define the exhaustive set of scenario fields eligible for defaults, each with rationale, value and units, applicability, evidence class, visibility, receipt text, and version; all other omitted required inputs must refuse with ranked fixes at every parser, builder, migration, CLI, API, and example path. Unit tests cover default registry, admission, provenance, migrations, diagnostics, and explicit overrides; boundary tests cover empty scenarios, legacy versions, nested omissions, conflicting aliases, exact capability limits, and default removal. Property tests require defaults to be idempotent and never overwrite explicit input; metamorphic tests cover format, ordering, and unit conversion; schema, compile-time, scanner, and runtime mutants that add a silent default, hide a receipt, coerce an invalid value, or downgrade an error must fail. Parser faults, cancellation, deadline, nesting and object caps, memory pressure, and log failure must not construct a silently completed scenario. This Bead is the terminal owner of the no-silent-default inventory and refusal battery in scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh, consuming fixtures from .17.3, .17.4, and .17.8. The configured DSR gate and deterministic round-trip replay must pass with zero unexplained default surfaces; documentation or lint alone cannot prove runtime enforcement. Logs are bounded per admission surface and scenario object, with complete ranked fixes retained in capped artifacts and no truncation that could conceal a silent-default violation.

title: Design variables, manufacturing constraints, objectives, and failure modes as scenario objects (schema now, optimization later)
description:
WHY: The scenario-semantics review list explicitly includes "design variables and manufacturing constraints" and "objectives, constraints, margins, and failure modes" — and the no-silent-defaults doctrine includes "no optimization result without manufacturing and robustness checks." No other bead gives these a home: e17_6 covers requirements/margins, but design VARIABLES (what may change), manufacturing constraints (what changes are buildable), optimization objectives, and failure-mode declarations are unowned. They are staged for the post-0.1 optimization phase (forward prediction first), but the SCHEMA must be shaped for them now so the 0.1 project format (e06_1, frozen per e16_5) does not need a breaking change when optimization arrives.

WHAT: (a) Design-variable objects: which scenario quantities may vary (geometry parameters via fs-xform parameterization refs, material selections from declared card sets, fan choices from a catalog, layout positions), each with bounds, discreteness, and units — typed against the entities they modify (e17_1 identities); (b) manufacturing constraints as first-class declarations: minimum wall thickness, fin spacing manufacturability, draft/tooling classes, available stock materials, assembly clearances — the constraints an optimizer must respect and a HUMAN can audit (each with source provenance like requirements); (c) objectives declared, not implied: the optimization target (minimize T_max, minimize fan power at fixed T_max, maximize margin) with the QoI refs and the robustness posture (nominal vs CVaR-class robust per fs-robust) stated explicitly; (d) failure-mode declarations: named failure modes per component class (thermal runaway threshold, solder fatigue proxy limits, connector derating) with severity — these extend e17_6's severity classes into a checkable failure-mode registry that DecisionAssessment and the future optimization loop consult; (e) staging: schema types land NOW (validated, serialized, versioned); the optimization EXECUTION consuming them is e06_14's scope.

DONE WHEN: schema types + validation land with the .fsim format able to carry them (round-trip tested); the reference project gains a worked design-variable/constraint block (validated but unexercised); e06_14 can be written against these types without schema changes; no-silent-defaults battery (e17_7) extended: an optimization request without manufacturing constraints or robustness posture REFUSES.

TESTS: unit (each object's validation incl. bound/discreteness/unit checks; entity-ref resolution; sourceless-constraint refusal; failure-mode registry lookups); round-trip serialization within the versioned schema; the e17_7 battery extension (optimization-without-constraints refusal with actionable message); e2e: reference project with the design block validates and logs the full variable/constraint/objective/failure-mode table with provenance columns.
acceptance_criteria: Represent design variables, domains and units, manufacturing and geometric constraints, objective quantities and orientation, aggregation and risk measure, operating scenarios, failure modes and thresholds, uncertainty, provenance, and capability requirements as versioned scenario objects without yet implying an optimizer. Unit tests cover schema, cross-reference validation, unit and dimension checking, domain and constraint admission, failure evaluation, serialization, and migration; boundary tests cover empty variable sets, fixed variables, open and closed limits, discrete choices, conflicting constraints, multiple objectives, equality at failure thresholds, and unavailable QoIs. Property tests generate admissible small schemas; metamorphic tests cover variable reorder, name-preserving rename, and equivalent unit conversion; mutants that reverse objective sense, drop a constraint, widen a domain, hide a failure mode, or insert a default must fail. Invalid graphs, cancellation, deadline, variable and expression caps, cyclic references, memory pressure, and log overflow must refuse with bounded ranked fixes. This Bead contributes immutable schema and no-silent-default fixtures to .17.7, scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh, and later .6.14. Deterministic replay and the configured DSR gate must pass; the schema records intent only and confers no feasibility, optimality, manufacturability, or safety claim.
close_reason: Landed fs_scenario::design schema (DesignVariable, ManufacturingConstraint, OptimizationObjective with mandatory RobustnessPosture, FailureMode, DesignBlock with sourceless-constraint refusal), content-addressed ScenarioDesignExtension sidecar, and full test suite passing.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Progress 2026-07-25 (NobleLion). Landed b12c04a1 + 7775cc1e. 2 of 4 DONE-WHEN.

DELIVERED: fs_scenario::design — the schema an optimization phase will consume.
  DesignVariable       what may change (geometry parameter, material selection,
                       fan selection, layout position), typed against entity
                       identities from 17.1, with dimensioned continuous bounds
                       or a discrete citation set.
  ManufacturingConstraint  what changes are buildable (min wall thickness, min
                       feature spacing, min assembly clearance, stock
                       thickness), each sourced.
  OptimizationObjective    what is optimized: QoI, sense, and a REQUIRED
                       RobustnessPosture.
  FailureMode          what counts as failure, ordered by DesignSeverity.
  DesignBlock          budgeted collections, row assigned by the block;
                       validate() reports every structural, dimensional and
                       provenance fault at once as Violation{code,what,fix}.
  ScenarioDesignExtension  content-addressed sidecar bound to one scenario.

THE CENTRAL REFUSAL (17.7 doctrine, applied): optimization_request() fails
closed when no manufacturing constraint is declared. A design change nobody can
build is not an optimum, so the absence of constraints is an unanswered
question rather than "none apply". Refusal is total and lists every missing
piece at once. RobustnessPosture is a required constructor argument, so an
unstated posture is UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely discouraged; Nominal is
a declared choice that makes no robustness claim, not the absence of one.

KEY DESIGN DECISION: persistence is a SIDECAR, not an IR section. The scenario
form is strictly positional with fixed arity (ir.rs refuses anything but nine
items), so a tenth section would change every canonical byte string, move all
pinned canonical hashes — including the fs-ir machine lowering that asserts
byte equality — and force SCENARIO_IR_VERSION to 3 with a new crosswalk rule.
The sidecar follows the sensor-extension precedent and leaves the IR at 2.
EVIDENCE: full crate battery 131/131 green with every pinned hash unmoved.

SELECTIONS ARE CITATIONS, NOT RESOLUTIONS. A material or fan choice is a
ContentHash. fs-scenario is L3 and cannot reach the material database or any
catalogue, so resolving one is outside this layer, not merely unimplemented.
Severity is declared locally rather than imported for the same reason: the
requirement severity classes live at L6, so the higher layer maps onto this
enum, not the reverse.

SCHEMA GOVERNANCE: check-schemas correctly refused the new public constant and
left the gate red on my account; fixed in 7775cc1e as not_promised/internal-wire
matching the sensor-extension precedent. Deliberately NOT derived-lockstep:
that class means "rides inside a frozen schema", and this sidecar is a separate
artifact bound by hash, which is the whole reason it exists. Flagged the
divergence to GoldSnow rather than diverging quietly.

I ALSO WITHDREW MY OWN ARCHITECTURAL ARGUMENT. I proposed bumping the frozen
.fsim format "while the migration is trivially empty". GoldSnow showed that
argues for deciding now, not for putting the vocabulary in .fsim, and that
.fsim already ships PROVEN bump machinery (a synthetic v0->v1), so the
"bump while cheap" reasoning only bites for unproven machinery. Their "keep the
promised surface small" point is one I should have led with myself. The
vocabulary stays in fs-scenario.

DONE-WHEN
1. Schema types + validation land, .fsim able to carry them (round-trip) —
   HALF. Types, validation and sidecar round-trip land; the .fsim reference
   field does not exist yet.
2. Reference project gains a worked design block — NOT MET (needs fs-project).
3. e06_14 can be written against these types without schema changes — MET.
4. e17_7 battery extended: optimization without constraints REFUSES — MET.

REMAINING, both L6 fs-project work adjacent to GoldSnow's freeze:
- One optional .fsim field referencing the scenario design objects. GoldSnow's
  acceptance test, which I will write as an explicit test rather than assume:
  adding the optional field must NOT change the canonical hash of a document
  that omits it. If absent-means-absent and existing documents hash
  identically it is a minor bump; if the canonical-hash construction shifts it
  is MAJOR and needs a migration path plus a deprecation horizon.
- The worked reference-project design block (validated but unexercised).

VERIFICATION: 11/11 new tests, 131/131 whole crate, ubs 0 critical,
check-schemas 0, check-contracts unchanged at its pre-existing fs-cli baseline.

title: E02 Claim-integrity burn-down: no output may claim more than its evidence proves
description:
WHY: The project's moat is preserving the epistemic status of physical claims. Any bug that lets a surface emit a STRONGER claim than the evidence supports (the topology exact-count-of-one bug class; FlutterReport::boundaries_agree passing on truncated sweeps, bead hukmw; grace-masks-the-mechanism soundness traps) is therefore worse than an ordinary wrong answer — it corrupts the product's core value proposition and silently poisons every downstream composition. The synthesis puts this FIRST among immediate actions: "Any bug that can emit a stronger epistemic claim than the evidence supports should block public capability promotion."

WHAT (children): (1) define the claim-integrity defect class precisely + a label taxonomy so these defects are findable and countable; (2) an audit sweep of claim-emitting surfaces to file/triage new defects; (3) a machine-checkable promotion gate: open claim-integrity P0s block capability-maturity promotion (ties into e16 maturity registry); (4) tests for the gate itself.

PRECEDENT: this continues the existing soundness-audit vein (fs-ivl/fs-iga/fs-lbm/fs-cutfem fixes; bead wa8i certificate-spine audit) but converts it from an episodic activity into a standing, gated program with a countable inventory.

DONE WHEN: claim-integrity label exists and is applied; the sweep has completed at least one full pass over claim-emitting crates (fs-evidence, fs-package, fs-checker, fs-topo, fs-geom seams, campaign crates); the promotion gate runs in xtask/DSR and demonstrably blocks promotion while a tagged P0 is open; zero KNOWN open claim-integrity P0s at Level-4 promotion time.
close_reason:
E02 COMPLETE. All four children closed: .2.1 (defect class + taxonomy + doc lint + inventory lane), .2.2 (sweep: 39 defects filed across 13 crates), .2.3 (promotion gate wired into check-all), .2.4 (seeded-fault hardening drills).

DONE-WHEN AUDIT against the epic's own criteria: 'claim-integrity label exists and is applied' — yes, 49 defects labelled with the severity/scope taxonomy in docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md. 'the sweep has completed at least one full pass over claim-emitting crates (fs-evidence, fs-package, fs-checker, fs-topo, fs-geom seams, campaign crates)' — yes, all of those plus fs-adjoint, fs-solver, fs-wasm and README/CONTRACT prose; recorded in docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY_SWEEP_2026-07.md with per-surface verdicts AND an explicit list of what was left UNAUDITED, because unaudited is not clean. 'the promotion gate runs in xtask/DSR and demonstrably blocks promotion while a tagged P0 is open' — yes, check-claim-integrity in check-all; the .2.3 drill blocks a real promotion naming frankensim-0547u and admits a clean one; the .2.4 drills prove it fails closed under five seeded faults. 'zero KNOWN open claim-integrity P0s at Level-4 promotion time' — not yet true and correctly NOT claimed: 4 remain open (0547u, 2gs5h, hukmw, and the fs-marquee laundering defect), all owned, and nothing is at L4 in capability-maturity.json, so the criterion is not yet in force.

BURN-DOWN: 49 defects, 45 closed, 4 open. The sweep's 39 findings are 35 fixed, 2 partial-then-completed (.2.24, .2.31), 2 handed to their file owner and since completed (.2.34, .2.39).

WHAT THIS EPIC ACTUALLY CHANGED: over-claiming went from an ethos to a countable, gated defect class. It also surfaced five compile errors committed AT HEAD that had made whole crates unverifiable (fs-dfo blocking the entire workspace, fs-ledger, fs-checker, fs-solver, and xtask itself), which is why check-all had not run for days and 100 violations had accumulated invisibly — tracked as frankensim-checkall-backlog-100-3h5ad.

RESIDUAL, recorded rather than closed over: the sweep's recall against a LIVE instance of the two known-answer defects is unmeasured (both were already remediated when the auditors read the code), and large surfaces remain unaudited — fs-geom's ~28k-line gated derived_morphism, fs-evidence's identity.rs and most of vv/, fs-package's JSON emitters, fs-adjoint's explain attribution, and ~125 crate CONTRACTs. A second pass should start there.

title: Define the claim-integrity defect class + label taxonomy (make over-claiming countable)
description:
WHY: "Stop the system from claiming more than the evidence proves" is the project's core discipline, but today such defects are scattered across ordinary bug beads and are not countable, so they cannot gate anything. A precise class definition turns an ethos into an enforceable inventory.

WHAT: (a) A written definition with decision rules: a claim-integrity defect exists when any public surface (API return type, evidence color, certificate, report line, README/CONTRACT sentence, WASM export) can assert a STRONGER epistemic state than its actual evidence — e.g. exact topology counts from bounded-component arguments; boundaries_agree true on truncated sweeps (bead hukmw); Verified color reachable from Estimated inputs; validity asserted outside a model card's domain; a golden hash treated as authority for semantics it does not pin. Include severity rules: P0 = reachable in a default/public path; P1 = reachable behind features; P2 = doc-only overstatement. (b) Beads label taxonomy: label `claim-integrity` plus severity; document it in docs/CONVENTIONS.md. (c) Retro-tag the known existing instances (hukmw and the soundness-audit vein fixes) so history is queryable.

DONE WHEN: definition merged into docs/; label applied to all currently known instances; `br list -l claim-integrity` returns the live inventory; the e02 sweep and gate tasks consume this definition verbatim.

TESTS: documentation lint (xtask check-terminology or equivalent) that the definition file exists and the label taxonomy section is present; an e2e script that queries beads for the label, prints the inventory with severities, and exits nonzero if any P0 lacks an owner — with verbose logging of each entry.
close_reason: Landed 00f0cf70. docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md is the normative definition: decision rules (5-step procedure), 8 recurring gap shapes each anchored to a confirmed repo instance, explicit non-instances (under-claiming is never a defect), reachability-based severity rules, label taxonomy, and the audit method .2.2 consumes verbatim. Taxonomy = claim-integrity + exactly one of severity:default-path|severity:gated|severity:doc-only + crate:<scope> (no scope = global fail-closed); defect membership is type=bug so E02's own program beads cannot block the gate forever. Documented in docs/CONVENTIONS.md. Enforcement: xtask claims.rs rule 5 (inside existing check-claims/check-all; 0 violations on the live tree) + scripts/ci/claim_integrity_inventory.sh (fails on unowned open P0, missing/duplicate severity, and fails CLOSED on unreadable/truncated/mid-flush store). Retro-tagged 8 known instances: 0547u, hukmw, 2gs5h (default-path); wa8i, f5pr, 4fbv, qduf (default-path, closed); y6yv (gated, closed). Live inventory now: 17 labelled = 9 program + 8 defects (3 open, all owned; 5 closed). Verification: claims.rs 5/5 unit tests green via standalone harness (xtask itself does not build in the current tree due to unrelated uncommitted main.rs WIP - two E0282 type-inference errors at pre-existing lines 3069/3398, NOT caused by this change); inventory lane drilled through unowned/no-severity/two-severity/truncated-JSON/has_more/clean fixtures with exit codes 1/1/1/2/2/0; rustfmt clean; ubs 0 critical. NOTE for .2.2: 2gs5h is P1 but classifies as severity:default-path (expected P0) - the lane WARNs; triage with RubyLotus.

title: fs-evidence: ModelBracket::evidence hard-codes in_domain:true, and that literal is what lets it certify
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_evidence::ModelBracket::evidence -> Evidence<f64>.model.in_domain
FILE: crates/fs-evidence/src/discrepancy.rs:637-643

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
ModelEvidence.in_domain is 'False the moment any constituent was queried outside its domain', and certified() requires 'EXPLICIT in-domain non-negative model evidence'. in_domain:true on evidence that NAMES N model cards reads as: every one of those N models was evaluated inside its stated validity domain.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
A ModelBracket holds only (name, qoi) pairs. No validity domain, evaluation point, or card is ever supplied, and evidence() performs no domain check whatsoever; it hard-codes validity: ValidityDomain::unconstrained(), in_domain: true.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
ModelBracket::new().try_with_member("contact-angle-60",0.90)?.try_with_member("contact-angle-120",1.16)?.evidence(p) returns evidence naming two models with in_domain:true whose certified() is Ok - asserted at discrepancy.rs:982. The literal is load-bearing: were it false, certified() would refuse with OutOfDomain and breakdown().model_rel would be +inf instead of the finite spread.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Either compute in_domain honestly from the members' validity domains plus the evaluation point, accept an explicit caller-supplied verdict, or emit in_domain:false until member cards are supplied. Bracket spread quantifies model-CHOICE sensitivity, which is not evidence that any member was used inside its validity range.

GAP SHAPE: Forgeable certificate / laundering - a constructor-supplied literal stands in for a check that never ran
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). ModelBracket::evidence emits in_domain:false with a named assumption that bracket spread is model-CHOICE sensitivity; new evidence_at(prov, validity, point) computes the verdict honestly. Two in-module tests that asserted the forged true were updated.

title: fs-evidence: IntervalOp::Hull is documented as the conservative choice for 'anything else' but is not an enclosure for non-selection ops
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_evidence::IntervalOp::Hull (rustdoc) as consumed by fs_evidence::color::compose
FILE: crates/fs-evidence/src/color.rs:576-584, :786-788, :758-763

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
Hull is documented as 'Anything else: the conservative hull of both bounds', and compose as 'Verified bounds combine per op (outward-rounded to preserve enclosure)'. A caller composing under an operation that is neither Add nor Mul is told Hull is the conservative choice and the returned Verified{lo,hi} encloses the result.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
(a0.min(b0), a1.max(b1)) - the union hull of the two OPERAND intervals. That encloses the result only for operations whose value always lies between the operands (min/max, selection, convex combination, envelope folds).

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Composing Verified{10.0,10.0} and Verified{-10.0,-10.0} under a subtraction - for which the enum's own text directs the caller to Hull - yields Verified{-10.0,10.0}, which does not contain the true difference 20.0. (In-tree Hull uses, e.g. crates/fs-thrust-e2e/src/lib.rs:387, are envelope folds and are sound; the exposure is the documented invitation.)

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
'Hull: the union of both operand intervals. This is an enclosure ONLY for operations whose result always lies between its operands. It is NOT a valid enclosure for difference, ratio, or any other operation; those must compose through fs-ivl.' The compose doc should stop implying Hull preserves enclosure for arbitrary ops.

GAP SHAPE: Conservative-sounding fallback documented as sound for a class of operations for which it is not
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). Hull rustdoc + compose rustdoc + CONTRACT now state Hull is an enclosure ONLY for operations whose result lies between the operands; difference/ratio must compose through fs-ivl. DOC-ONLY: rustdoc + CONTRACT wording; no executable regression exists because compose cannot observe the caller's operation. Covered by the check-claims doc lint, which fails if the CONTRACT sections regress.

title: fs-package: standards coverage counts a vacuous Verified claim as evidencing a certified numerical bound
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_package::coverage::rank_presence -> PackageConcept::VerifiedColor row in PackagePresenceReport / PackageCoverageReport
FILE: crates/fs-package/src/coverage.rs:295-311, :437-448, :720-758

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
A CoverageStatus::Covered row ('Mapped to the standard AND evidenced by this package') for (VerifiedColor, AsmeVvV20) reading 'the certified bound quantifies u_num directly (a guaranteed, not estimated, bound)' entitles a reader to conclude the package carries an admitted certified numerical-error bound.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Only that at least one admitted claim has ColorRank::Verified, i.e. an ordered non-NaN interval. rank_presence applies NO finiteness/informativeness filter, so [-inf,+inf] makes the row present. The crate applies exactly this filter one function away: certificate_presence (coverage.rs:313-335) requires lo.is_finite() && hi.is_finite() and says so.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Build a package with Claim::from_certificate("bound","unbounded certificate", f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::INFINITY, "solver", <64-hex>), verify with any accepting SourceCertificateVerifier, then package_coverage_with(&pkg, Standard::AsmeVvV20, &caps). The report contains, for the SAME standard, Certificate = MappedButAbsent ('vacuous infinite enclosures do not establish certificate coverage') and VerifiedColor = Covered. Not hand-made: fs-package's own test derived_vacuous_verified_enclosure_remains_sound_and_explicitly_unbounded (tests/package.rs:1071-1101) shows f64::MAX+f64::MAX composing to [finite,+inf]; that test asserts the Certificate row but never the VerifiedColor row - the fixture masks the mechanism. Sibling: an Estimated claim with +inf dispersion makes EstimatedColor Covered against 'Uncertainty quantification'.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Report MappedButAbsent when no admitted claim of that rank is informative - for Verified, when none has two finite endpoints (mirroring certificate_presence); for Estimated, when every admitted dispersion is +inf. Rationale should carry both counts.

GAP SHAPE: Existence read as exactness (a Verified colour read as a Verified bound); laundering an explicit no-bound into standards coverage
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). rank_presence reuses the same informativeness filter certificate_presence already had (extracted as rank_claim_is_informative); rationale reports 'N informative of M'. The masking fixture in tests/package.rs gained the missing VerifiedColor-row assertion.

title: fs-package/fs-checker: CONTRACTs say anchor verification binds the 'complete typed subject'; the request omits root and claim subject hash
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_package::origin::AnchoredSourceRequest / AnchoredSourceVerifier as described by both CONTRACTs
FILE: crates/fs-package/CONTRACT.md:167; crates/fs-checker/CONTRACT.md:238, :209-214; code at crates/fs-package/src/origin.rs:243-259

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
An anchor acceptance is bound to the complete subject of this exact package - in particular, read after the preceding sentence listing the source-certificate request as including 'package provenance and recomputed root ... claim subject hash', the anchor decision is bound to the root and claim subject and cannot be transplanted.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
AnchoredSourceRequest carries only {package_provenance, claim_index, claim_id, statement, regime, dataset_id, content_hash}. No package root, no claim subject hash, nothing else from the claim declaration. fs-package's own type list contradicts its invariant four bullets earlier (CONTRACT.md:62); fs-checker discloses nothing.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Diff the AnchoredSourceRequest field list against the sentence. Two packages sharing a Provenance with the same Validated claim at the same index but different sibling claims (hence different roots and claim_subject_hash) produce byte-identical anchor requests; a deterministic or memoizing anchor policy that accepted for one necessarily accepts for the other.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):

title: fs-topo: self_intersection_certificate skips every vertex-sharing face pair yet reports proven_free
description:

SURFACE: fs_topo::self_intersection_certificate / SelfIntersectReport::proven_free
FILE: crates/fs-topo/src/intersect.rs:238, :37, :1-9; crates/fs-topo/src/lib.rs:9-15; CONTRACT.md:26-28, :74

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Only that no two triangles sharing NO vertex index intersect. Every pair sharing at least one vertex index is skipped before the narrow phase (`if ti.iter().any(|v| tj.contains(v)) { continue; }`) on the rationale that such faces 'legitimately touch' - valid for touching, not for crossing.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):

T1's edge v3->v4 pierces T0's interior at (0.3,0.2,0) (0.3+0.2 < 1), so T0 cap T1 is a segment, not the shared vertex - a genuine self-intersection. The pair shares vertex 0, is skipped, pairs_tested == 0, proven_free() == true. The failure is not arithmetic, so 'exact arithmetic => no false PASS' does not apply.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
'PASS proves that no two faces sharing zero vertices intersect. Faces sharing a vertex are excluded and may still cross; non-intersection of the surface as a whole is NOT established.' title: fs-topo: non-finite vertex coordinates silently pass both self-intersection and manifold certificates
