title: Level C: acquire published electronics-thermal experiments with retained raw data + uncertainties
description:
WHY: This is where external reality actually enters: published canonical experiments with raw data and stated uncertainties are the first evidence that the MODEL (not just the numerics) is right. The corpus contract itself admits current datasets are small representative fixtures; Level C converts that honestly. Gated on wedge ratification because dataset hunting is expensive and must target the ratified vertical.

WHAT: (a) Systematically search and license >=3 published experimental datasets for the vertical, candidates: heated-block-in-channel / ribbed-channel forced convection (classic electronics-cooling literature), plate-fin or pin-fin heatsink thermal resistance vs flow-rate curves with stated instrumentation error, natural-convection enclosure benchmarks with measured Nusselt data, PCB effective-conductivity measurement studies, thermal-interface-material resistance measurements; (b) for each: capture EVERYTHING the retention schema demands (raw tables — digitize from the paper if needed with digitization uncertainty recorded as a preprocessing-lineage step; instrument calibration statements; geometry; ambient conditions; stated uncertainties; license); (c) declare context-of-use limits and which QoIs each dataset can validate; (d) an explicit acquisition log of candidates REJECTED and why (no raw data, no uncertainties, license) — this negative record prevents re-litigating.

DONE WHEN: >=3 datasets admitted at Level C with full retention metadata and partition declarations; each mapped to >=1 cooling QoI; rejection log recorded.

TESTS: schema-conformance per dataset; digitization spot-check tests (re-digitized subsample within declared digitization uncertainty); e2e corpus-audit run logs the per-dataset completeness table and the QoI coverage map (which QoIs have zero Level-C coverage — that gap list feeds e07 planning).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacAspen 2026-07-24: the SOFTWARE half landed at 88dde85d. Bead returns to `open` — the remainder is hardware, and it should not sit assigned to a finished session.

WHY I TOOK IT DESPITE THE HARDWARE DEPENDENCY: the bead's own CAVEAT authorizes exactly this - "the bead's software deliverables (spec-as-data, ingest pipeline, calibration records) must not block on the hardware arriving - land them against synthetic rig data first." This is that.

DELIVERED (fs_vvreg::rig, 826 lines + 472 test lines, 14 tests green):
- (a) RIG SPECIFICATION AS DATA: RigSpec (identified rig + declared coolant properties + instrument set), InstrumentSpec binding a corpus SensorRecord to a ChannelRole. Reusing SensorRecord rather than redeclaring metadata means calibration, placement and uncertainty have ONE representation shared with the corpus, so an ingested run cannot describe its metrology differently from the dataset it becomes. Admission requires unique sensor ids, a calibration certificate on every channel, role-compatible dimensions, and exactly one of each balance role.
- (b) INGEST PIPELINE, fail-closed: unknown / missing / duplicated / non-finite readings each refuse BY SENSOR NAME; an uncalibrated channel refuses with its declared reason preserved; a thermocouple wired as the flow channel is caught at specification rather than discovered later as a wrong enthalpy.
- (d) PARTITION AT INGEST, and blind sealing: a BlindHoldout run is GATED THEN SEALED. The order is what delivers both properties - the run is known physically sane because the gate ran, and its measured values do not survive into the retained verdict. A companion test proves sealing cannot become a way to smuggle unbalanced data in.
- THE ENERGY-BALANCE GATE, which is the piece I think is most worth having: P_in ~= rho*c_p*Q*(T_out - T_in), adjudicated against the instruments' OWN stated half-widths summed conservatively (added, never in quadrature - an rss would report a tighter band than the declarations support). No solver, no model: a check on the DATA. It catches mis-scaled flow channels, swapped inlet/outlet thermocouples, unlogged secondary heat paths, and decimal errors in declared power.

TWO DELIBERATE CONSEQUENCES of adjudicating against declared bands:
- A residual INSIDE the stated band is admitted. A gate refusing what the metrology already allows would be unusable on real data.
- A channel declaring MeasurementUncertainty::Unstated CANNOT PASS. That is a feature: Level E exists to carry metrology, and admitting an unquantified run produces exactly the unfalsifiable record this corpus excludes.

DONE-WHEN, audited honestly:
- "rig spec + ingest pipeline merged" - MET.
- "first real measurement campaign ingested with complete metadata" - NOT MET, and cannot be by software. Needs the rig.
- "at least one run withheld sealed for blind use" - the MECHANISM is built and tested; no real run exists to withhold.

So the bead stays OPEN. What remains is procurement and a measurement campaign: build the enclosure/heated-plate/heatsink/fan rig, obtain per-sensor calibration certificates, run the campaign, ingest through this pipeline, and seal one run. Item (c) - the adversarial-regime knobs (blockable vents, adjustable TIM quality, fan throttling) - is also hardware and untouched.

VERIFICATION BOUNDARY, stated plainly: `cargo test -p fs-vvreg` CANNOT RUN. fs-vvreg dev-depends on fs-ledger, which reaches the broken fsqlite (bead frankensim-asupersync-pin-drift-7fji5). The crate's LIB dependencies are clean, so I verified with the rustc harness the fleet has been using this session: fs_blake3 -> fs_qty -> fs_obs -> fs_evidence -> fs_vvreg built as rlibs, then tests/rig.rs compiled with --test against the real rlib and run (14/14). That compiles the actual files so it cannot drift from what cargo would build, but it is not the normal lane and I am not claiming it is. `cargo check -p fs-vvreg --lib` does pass. When the sibling is fixed, someone should re-run the normal lane; I expect it green but have not seen it.

CONTRACT no-claims added, because the gap between "ingest path exists" and "we have Level-E evidence" is exactly the kind of thing that gets misread later: no physical rig exists so the corpus gains NO Level-E dataset from this module; a balanced run is not a validated one (it proves channels are mutually consistent under their own declared uncertainty, not that any channel is accurate); the closure is single-stream and lossless, so a rig with real case losses will fail the gate CORRECTLY and needs a declared loss term first; and sealing is a retention discipline, not access control.

FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP WITH HARDWARE: the ingest path is ready and the refusals are the checklist. If the first campaign fails the energy balance, that is probably the rig telling you about a loss path rather than the gate being wrong - check the case losses before loosening anything.

title: Adversarial validation case set: regimes chosen to break the models, not flatter them
description:
WHY: A validation corpus assembled from convenient cases overstates capability precisely where users get hurt. The corpus must deliberately include regimes where the cheap models are EXPECTED to struggle, so that validity domains and discrepancy bands are honest at their edges and the fidelity graph (e10) has informative failure data.

WHAT: Curate/construct adversarial cases for the thermal vertical, each registered with WHY it is adversarial and WHICH model assumption it attacks: recirculation zones behind obstructions (attacks correlation-rung's attached-flow assumption); contact-resistance-dominated stacks (attacks any zero/known-resistance default; ties to e17 no-silent-defaults); radiation-dominated low-flow cases (attacks convection-only truncation); fan-stall and unstable operating-point cases (attacks fan-curve intersection logic); uncertain vent leakage (attacks BC certainty; pairs with the rig's blockable vents); strong material-property variability lots (attacks single-value material cards; exercises fs-matdb uncertainty models); high-Biot vs low-Biot extremes (attacks lumped assumptions). Each case gets acceptance criteria phrased as HONESTY checks: the system must either predict within envelope OR refuse/demote with the correct dominant-uncertainty attribution — a confident wrong answer fails; a correctly-attributed refusal passes.

DONE WHEN: >=6 adversarial cases registered (mix of analytic, cross-code, experimental, rig-based); wired into the scorecard's regime-limitation section.

TESTS: per-case honesty assertions as above (this is the distinctive part: PASS includes justified refusal); e2e lane logs per-case: regime, attacked assumption, prediction/refusal, attribution, verdict; the false-acceptance counter feeds the e16 metrics dashboard.

title: Evidence-portfolio doctrine: independent axes, not a strict pyramid (written + encoded)
description:
WHY: A naive V&V "pyramid" implies field data always outranks lab data and blind cases outrank everything. False: uncontrolled field observations can be LESS informative than a designed lab experiment (unknown operating conditions, sensor health, latent confounders). Authority depends on the claim and context. Without this doctrine, the scorecard and evidence colors will encode a wrong hierarchy.

WHAT: (a) A doctrine document defining external evidence as a PORTFOLIO with independent axes: numerical verification; cross-code agreement; controlled experimental validation; blind predictive validation; field monitoring; transferability across regimes; independent reproduction. For each axis: what it can and cannot support, and canonical failure modes (e.g. cross-code agreement's common-mode risk under a Franken-only ecosystem; field data confounding). (b) Encoding: the corpus evidence-level tags (A-E) become AXIS COORDINATES, not ranks; the scorecard aggregates per-axis rather than taking a max; claim admission rules state which axes a given claim class REQUIRES (e.g. Validated color for a QoI in a regime requires controlled-experiment coverage of that regime; field data alone cannot mint it without condition provenance). (c) Explicit anti-laundering rule restated for datasets: composing weak-axis evidence cannot upgrade color, mirroring fs-evidence composition.

DONE WHEN: doctrine merged into docs/ + referenced by fs-vvreg/fs-evidence CONTRACTs; scorecard consumes axis coordinates; one worked example shows a field dataset correctly REFUSED as sole support for Validated.

TESTS: unit tests on admission rules (each axis-requirement violation -> typed refusal naming the missing axis); doctrine-presence lint; e2e: scorecard run logs the per-axis aggregation for every QoI so reviewers see exactly which axis is thin.

title: Level D: blind held-out protocol with preregistration (selected before calibration, enforced by type)
description:
WHY: Calibrated models flatter themselves on data they have seen. A BLIND case — selected and sealed before model calibration — is the only cheap way to measure real predictive power. The protocol must be mechanical, because good intentions do not survive deadline pressure.

WHAT: (a) Preregistration record type in the corpus: declares the blind case (geometry, conditions, QoIs, acceptance envelope, evaluation date), content-addressed and SEALED (hash committed; payload access refused until unseal) before any calibration run that could touch it; (b) unseal ceremony: unsealing records who/when/why into the ledger; post-unseal, the dataset is PERMANENTLY marked spent-for-blind-use (it may become an ordinary validation set, never blind again); (c) the type system must make it impossible for a sealed dataset to appear in a calibration partition (partition enforcement from e07 consumes this); (d) at least ONE preregistered blind case created for the vertical (an enclosure or board design, plausibly from the Level-E instrumented hardware or a withheld Level-C dataset), with the seal recorded.

DONE WHEN: protocol implemented + documented; one real blind case sealed; the e07 blind-execution bead can proceed entirely on this machinery.

TESTS: unit tests: sealed-access refusal; double-unseal refusal; spent-flag permanence; calibration-partition exclusion of sealed sets; ledger receipt on unseal; e2e drill script that walks the full lifecycle (seal -> attempt cheating access (must refuse, logged) -> unseal -> evaluate -> spent) with verbose state logging at each transition.

Define a preregistration artifact and typed calibration, validation, and blind-held-out handles such that calibration code cannot inspect blind observations, labels, derived QoIs, or acceptance outcomes before an independent unlock receipt. Mutants that leak metadata or values, reassign after lock, accept unsigned receipts, weaken role checks, or compute acceptance early must be killed. title: Steady conduction FEM solver on solids (FEEC-based, anisotropic k(T), typed thermal scenario BCs)
description:
WHY: Conduction is the backbone of BOTH candidate thermal verticals and is entirely absent as an assembled solver (verified: fs-feec "conduction" is electrical; the only heat PDE code is fs-adjoint's 1-D-style transient adjoint scaffold and fs-lbm's fluid-side thermal LBM). Every downstream capability (contact resistance, conjugate coupling, QoIs, calibration) consumes this solver. It is deliberately the FIRST physics bead.

WHAT: A steady heat-conduction solve over tet/hex complexes: weak-form assembly on fs-feec spaces (0-forms for T, fluxes recoverable), anisotropic and temperature-dependent conductivity tensors k(T) from fs-matdb cards (query receipts retained — property provenance travels with the solve), volumetric heat sources, BC families from fs-scenario's existing thermal rows: Dirichlet T (K), Neumann flux (W/m^2), Robin/convective (W/m^2K with declared T_ref) — the Robin row is the seam the e05 correlation rung plugs into. Nonlinearity (k(T)) via Newton or fixed-point with a declared globalization and stop rule; linear solves through fs-solver (CG/MINRES; matrix-free where practical, deterministic assembly via fs-sparse). Cancellation-correct under Cx at assembly-tile and Newton-iteration boundaries; resumable snapshots via the versioned solver-state envelope.

CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS: determinism class stated (target: bitwise same-ISA); error model (residual norms + DWR hook for goal-oriented estimates targeting QoIs, not generic field accuracy); no-claim boundaries (steady-only; no radiation/convection physics inside this crate — those couple in).

Landed as crate fs-conduction (L3/FLUX), single authorised line added to the root Cargo.toml members array. 36 tests green.

BUILT: P1 weak form on fs-feec 0-forms with flux recovery; anisotropic (SPD-checked) and temperature-dependent k(T) conductivity from fs-matdb cards with QUERY RECEIPTS RETAINED per grid point and replayed via verify_receipt, so property provenance travels with the solve and a declared constant is marked ProvenanceClass rather than impersonating matdb provenance; volumetric sources; Dirichlet/Neumann/Robin lowered from fs-scenario's existing thermal rows; Newton+Armijo and damped Picard with declared globalization, stop rule and a material-admissibility guard; fs-solver linear solves whose typed ResidualClaim is carried verbatim and whose Euclidean residual is RECOMPUTED and gated on; deterministic fs-sparse assembly; Cx cancellation at assembly-tile (512) and Newton-iteration boundaries with a drill asserting state is UNCHANGED after a mid-iteration cancel; resumable versioned snapshots (TYPE_ID 0xf5c0_4d75_c710_0001) with a tamper-refusal test.

ROBIN SEAM (what E05's correlation rung plugs into): fs-scenario's Robin row carries h only and BoundaryCondition has no T_ref field, so from_scenario_row REQUIRES T_ref be named at the lowering call, defaulting to Environment::ambient_temperature as an explicit declaration rather than inventing a field. A correlation supplies h; the reference temperature stays a property of the row.

MMS (fs-mms OrderGate, grids n=4,6,8,10): isotropic-dirichlet L2 2.0087 / H1 0.9879, anisotropic 2.0065, mixed-neumann 2.000000, robin 2.000000, nonlinear-kt 2.0014 — all inside the 0.2 gate. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS BEAD: the first ladders used quadratic manufactured solutions, fitted a perfect order 2 with rms ~1e-11, and produced BIT-IDENTICAL errors for isotropic and anisotropic K. Cause: P1 Galerkin on these Kuhn meshes reproduces exact solutions up to CUBIC at the nodes, so such a ladder measures interpolation error and is independent of k entirely. The Dirichlet ladders moved to a quartic solution and the reproduction fact is now pinned by its own test (polynomial_reproduction_at_the_nodes: quadratic 1.9e-12, cubic 1.4e-12, quartic 2.4e-2) so the degeneracy is recorded rather than mistaken for strength. Error norms use a Duffy-transformed 6x6x6 Gauss-Legendre rule exact to degree 9, because a degree-3 rule would carry an O(1) relative error on an O(h^4) integral.

ANALYTIC: slab-dirichlet (nodal 3.06e-11, Q 4499.999999999907 vs 4500), slab-with-source, slab-dirichlet-robin, cylindrical-shell (L2 0.5588 -> 0.1478, ratio 3.782 ~ h^2; conductance 0.35%), straight-fin (Bi 1.25e-4, Q_3d 2.50879 vs Q_1d 2.50883 W). Each envelope states what KIND of agreement it claims; the cylinder's looser conductance envelope is geometry-dominated (polygonal annulus sagitta) and was set after measuring the cause.

ADJOINT: ConductivityDesign through fs_adjoint::ift_gradient_matfree (one transposed solve, never a differentiated Krylov iteration); params=162 free_dofs=48 adjoint_res=8.46e-15 max_rel_err=1.01e-6 informative=5/5 vs central differences. It establishes mutual consistency of assembled dR/dT, pullback and primal solve; it establishes NOTHING about the nonlinear case (ConductivityDesign::new REFUSES a temperature-dependent material rather than silently linearizing), nothing about shape/mesh sensitivity, and nothing goal-oriented — a verified gradient is not a DWR estimate.

CONTRACT.md (all ten sections) + MODEL_CARD.md complete. Determinism: bitwise same-ISA, with reasons enumerated (pure assembly from staged triplets, canonical traversal independent of tile size, fixed-shape reductions, x0=0, no RNG, no platform transcendental — only IEEE sqrt and fs_math::det). Cross-ISA is a G5 audit away and is NOT claimed.

PROMOTION: capability thermal.conduction-solve promoted L1 -> L2 at e5c8061f, admitted by the claim-integrity gate (no severity:default-path defect in scope for fs-conduction/fs-feec/fs-solid). L2 is earned by independent oracles, not a golden.

NOT REACHED, named rather than glossed: matrix-free operator (assembled-CSR only; a second element-loop apply would not be bit-identical to the deterministic assembly, so shipping both meant two determinism claims or one untested path); G5 registered golden (needs a golden-couplings.json row, outside the implementing boundary — determinism evidence is self-consistency replay, which CONTRACT labels as weaker); thread-count assembly invariance (assembly is single-threaded, so the test would be vacuous; CONTRACT records what a parallel version must preserve).

title: Canonical thermal QoI producer: extrema, airflow, uniformity and margins with complete evidence
description:
WHY: The product's supported quantities of interest are the contract with the user: maximum junction temperature, pressure drop, fan power, temperature uniformity, and thermal margin against requirements. Each must be extracted deterministically WITH evidence (numerical + model + statistical slices populated), because these are the values the error-budget doctrine (e08), the scorecard (e04), and DecisionAssessment (e08) operate on. A QoI without evidence is a naked scalar — the exact failure the project exists to prevent.

WHAT: (a) QoI definitions as typed, goal-oriented functionals: max-T over declared component regions (with the max taken deterministically and its mesh-sensitivity flagged via DWR hooks from E05_1 — a max functional is rough, note the estimator caveat honestly); area-weighted mean and uniformity metrics (max spread, std) over declared surfaces; pressure drop and fan operating-point power from E05_5 records; thermal margin = requirement minus predicted-with-uncertainty (interfaces with e17 requirement objects; margin carries the FULL budget, not the point estimate); (b) each QoI returns Evidence<Qty> with units, the 3-term (later 8-term, e08) breakdown, validity intersection of every model card consumed en route, and provenance/replay references; (c) report/CLI surfaces consume ONLY these records (no ad hoc scalar paths — lint-checked).

DONE WHEN: all five QoI families extract with evidence on the reference fixture; validity intersection demonstrably narrows when any upstream card narrows; margin QoI refuses when the requirement is absent (no default requirement).

TESTS: unit per QoI (analytic fixtures with known extrema/means; determinism of max tie-breaking; unit typing); property (monotonicity: widening any input uncertainty cannot shrink QoI uncertainty — anti-laundering at QoI level); e2e: reference run logging every QoI with its full evidence tree rendered, plus the lint proving no naked-scalar path exists from solver to report.

## Scope Ownership Correction

This lower-layer bead owns the canonical typed QoI producer and its direct evidence integrity. The non-vacuous solver-to-report naked-scalar prohibition is preserved downstream: `s2l9v` must consume this producer for every requested key, `f85xj.6.9` must render only those canonical records, and `f85xj.8.7` owns the broader user-facing enforcement. The lower producer must not depend on its L6 consumers; doing so creates an architectural and scheduling cycle. No feature is removed—its proof is attached to the first boundary where a bypass can actually exist.

## Required Tests and Logging

Unit/analytic tests cover every supported maximum, mean, spread, standard-deviation, pressure-drop, fan-power, and margin formula; all direction/unit/requirement cases; empty/missing/duplicate regions; non-finite inputs; deterministic equal-extrema tie-breaking; rough-max/DWR caveat; safety-factor single application; complete eight-source uncertainty budgets with named Unknown rather than fabricated Negligible; and validity/provenance intersection. Property/metamorphic tests cover mesh/region/request permutations, equivalent units, common temperature offsets for margins, and the anti-laundering laws that wider uncertainty or weaker authority cannot strengthen evidence/verdict. Mutation tests remove or change each upstream evidence slice and must demote/refuse with a stable diagnostic.

`scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh --profile <pr|full|recovery> --artifact-dir <path>` consumes real retained conduction, airflow, convection, requirement, and uncertainty artifacts through the production QoI APIs—no fabricated scalar or prebuilt evidence object—and independently recomputes analytic probes/balances. It runs all five families, absent-requirement, narrowed-domain, tamper/stale, cancellation/resource, and deterministic-repeat cases. Downstream `solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh --through qoi` separately proves product wiring.

Canonical JSONL binds schema/event sequence, source revision/constellation, input artifact and model-card roots, QoI semantic ID/class/region, selection/tie identity, values/units, every uncertainty term and authority/domain intersection, requirement/source/safety factor, diagnostics/ranked fixes, and output roots. Volatile observations are separate; meta-tests reject omissions, duplicates, reordering, mixed snapshots, unknown versions, and tampering.

## Acceptance Criteria

All supported QoI families produce typed evidence with complete uncertainty, validity, provenance, and deterministic selection; analytic/property/mutation/fault tests and the no-mock producer E2E pass; absent requirements and missing evidence fail honestly; one-material and narrowed-domain fixtures reproduce the declared laws. `s2l9v`, `f85xj.6.9`, and `f85xj.8.7` explicitly retain the downstream no-naked-scalar enforcement. Complete constellation snapshots immediately before/after focused proof are identical, and terminal DSR evidence retains run/log/artifact identities; cross-ISA reductions use predeclared semantic tolerances until actual runtime G5 proof.
acceptance_criteria: All five canonical thermal QoI families emit typed, deterministic evidence with complete eight-source uncertainty, validity, provenance, requirement semantics and honest Unknown/refusal paths. Analytic/property/mutation/fault tests and real thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh pass with tamper-evident JSONL. Downstream no-naked-scalar enforcement is preserved in s2l9v/6.9/8.7 without a lower-to-higher dependency cycle; identical proof snapshots and terminal DSR identities are retained.
notes: 2026-07-22 VioletHorizon integration handoff: f85xj.8.1 now has the core fs-evidence uncertainty API in the shared tree (uncertainty::EngineeringUncertaintyBudget). When this thermal QoI producer becomes actionable, emit exactly one populated eight-source budget per QoI and use Unknown with a named reason wherever a real receipt/source is absent; never substitute Negligible for missing evidence. Producer integration is the remaining f85xj.8.1 DONE WHEN item. The core slice has local 10/10 focused tests and a green remote fs-evidence --all-targets lane (226/226).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DESIGN DECISION RECORDED FIRST (NobleLion, 2026-07-28), before any code. Audited the landed producer (fs-airflow/src/qoi.rs, 1182 lines; 11 tests in tests/qoi.rs) against this bead's DONE-WHEN and Required Tests. All five families already emit values and 8-term budgets, and the audit/demotion path is real. SIX genuine gaps remain; this slice takes five of them.

(1) THE MARGIN IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF CARRYING EVIDENCE. qoi.rs:676 builds the margin budget as unknown_budget("thermal-margin","kelvin",margin_identity,&[]) -- an EMPTY known-terms list. But margin = L_eff - T_max has d(margin)/d(T_max) = -1 with unit sensitivity, so every junction-maximum term transfers 1:1 into kelvin. Today the margin instead re-derives eight independent generic Unknowns. Both budgets are all-Unknown at present, so NO existing test can tell propagation from fabrication -- textbook shared-path blindness. The moment the junction maximum gains a real term, the margin would silently keep reporting Unknown. The bead's "margin carries the FULL budget, not the point estimate" is therefore unmet. FIX: the margin budget becomes the junction-maximum budget's term VALUES re-bound under the margin identity.

(2) NO DECLARED DISCRETIZATION RECEIPT, which is what makes (1) falsifiable. The bead asks for max-T "mesh-sensitivity flagged via DWR hooks from E05_1"; today Discretization is hardcoded Unknown with no input by which a caller can attach a retained refinement-ladder half-width. FIX: an OPTIONAL caller-declared DiscretizationReceipt (kelvin half-width + SourceProvenance) turns the junction-maximum Discretization term into an IntervalBound, which the margin then inherits -- making (1) provable rather than vacuous. BOUNDARY held explicitly: the receipt is a caller-declared refinement-ladder observation IN KELVIN. fs-airflow does not compute it and does not convert a watts residual into kelvin (the CONTRACT's existing 'dimensional wishful thinking' stance is preserved), and Evidence.numerical stays NoClaim because a declared ladder observation is not a certificate. Only the budget term records it, exactly as fan power already records a declared efficiency band.

(3) NO SAFETY-FACTOR AUTHORITY; "safety-factor single application" is untestable. The repo ALREADY owns the doctrine at fs-project::SafetyFactorPolicy: "No universal multiply/divide rule is inferred. The source owns how the finite factor was applied, and ThermalLimit::limit stores the effective value consumed by compliance evaluation." I am NOT inventing a convention. fs-airflow is L3 and fs-project is L6, so fs-airflow may not import it; I mirror the semantics with a neutral SafetyFactorAuthority { factor: finite >= 1.0, source }, MANDATORY on ThermalRequirement (matching ThermalLimit, where it is not an Option), retained for identity and NEVER re-applied. THE FALSIFIER: holding the effective limit fixed and changing ONLY the factor must change the requirement identity while leaving the margin VALUE bit-identical -- a mutant that re-applies the factor dies. That is what "single application" means here: applied once, upstream, by the declaring authority.

(4) UNREACHABLE TIE-BREAK BRANCH (claim-integrity). qoi.rs:969's `value.to_bits() == maximum.to_bits() && candidate < vertex` can never fire: canonicalize_indices sorts vertices ascending, so every candidate is strictly greater than the incumbent, which is always an already-visited index. The real tie-break is the canonical sort plus the strict `>`. The dead clause reads like the mechanism and is not; making it honest is the fix.

(5) DONE-WHEN CLAUSE 2 IS UNPROVEN: "validity intersection demonstrably narrows when any upstream card narrows". The existing tests move the POINT out of a fixed card; none NARROWS A CARD around a fixed point. This is the only unmet DONE-WHEN clause and is the close gate.

(6) NO ANALYTIC VALUE TESTS: mean/spread/std/margin/fan-power are asserted only finite/positive, never against hand-computed values. The bead's "analytic fixtures with known extrema/means" is unmet.

API CHANGE IS SAFE: no file outside fs-airflow references extract_thermal_qois or ThermalQoiSet, so ThermalRequirement::try_new gains its factor argument with no shim (AGENTS.md: prefer the correct design over compatibility shims).

NOT IN THIS SLICE, recorded honestly: scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh (the no-mock producer E2E) and the solver-to-report naked-scalar lint. The E2E clause needs the Runner V2 harness; the lint's enforcement boundary is explicitly delegated downstream to s2l9v/6.9/8.7 by this bead's own Scope Ownership Correction.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SLICE LANDED at 4633ca90 (NobleLion, 2026-07-28). Five of the six audited gaps are closed. Clause-by-clause below; the bead stays in_progress because the elaborated Acceptance Criteria are NOT met even though all three DONE-WHEN clauses now are.

DONE-WHEN, all three MET:
 (1) "all five QoI families extract with evidence on the reference fixture" -- was already met before this slice.
 (2) "validity intersection demonstrably narrows when any upstream card narrows" -- NOW MET, and it was the only unmet DONE-WHEN clause. The pre-existing battery only ever moved the operating POINT out of a fixed card; nothing narrowed a CARD around a fixed point, which is the direction the clause actually names. narrowing_one_upstream_card_narrows_the_intersection_and_demotes holds one point fixed, shrinks the fan card's flow_m3_s bound around it, and asserts coverage moves FullyInDomain -> FullyOutOfDomain with every record's model-form term demoted. The in-domain arm is retained as the non-vacuity guard.
 (3) "margin QoI refuses when the requirement is absent" -- already met (QoiError::MissingRequirement, first statement of the extractor).

WHAT CHANGED, and why each was a real defect rather than a polish item:
 (a) THE MARGIN WAS A SCALAR WEARING A BUDGET. qoi.rs built the margin budget with an empty known-terms list. margin = L_eff - T_max has unit sensitivity to the junction maximum in the same kelvin, so every maximum term transfers 1:1; instead the margin re-derived eight independent generic Unknowns. Because both budgets are all-Unknown today, no existing test could distinguish propagation from fabrication -- shared-path blindness. propagate_budget now re-expresses the maximum's budget under the margin identity: values transfer, provenance rebinds (so the requirement and its factor still rebind the budget), and it COPIES rather than composes, so an Unknown source term can never be strengthened in transit.
 (b) NOTHING COULD MAKE (a) FALSIFIABLE. There was no input by which a caller could attach a retained ladder half-width, so Discretization was permanently Unknown. The new optional DiscretizationReceipt is a caller-declared refinement-ladder half-width IN KELVIN. Boundary held: this crate does not compute it and does not convert a watts residual into kelvin, and admitting one does NOT upgrade NumericalKind::NoClaim -- a declared ladder observation is not a certificate. It populates the budget term only, exactly as the declared efficiency band already populates Parameters.
 (c) "SAFETY-FACTOR SINGLE APPLICATION" WAS UNTESTABLE because no safety factor existed. I did NOT invent a convention: fs-project::SafetyFactorPolicy already owns the doctrine ("No universal multiply/divide rule is inferred. The source owns how the finite factor was applied, and ThermalLimit::limit stores the effective value"). fs-airflow is L3 and may not import the L6 project layer, so SafetyFactorAuthority mirrors those semantics as a neutral type, mandatory on ThermalRequirement exactly as it is non-Option on ThermalLimit. Single application means applied ONCE, upstream, by the declaring authority; this crate never re-applies it.
 (d) UNREACHABLE TIE-BREAK GUARD (claim-integrity). `value.to_bits() == maximum.to_bits() && candidate < vertex` could never fire: canonicalize_indices sorts ascending, so every candidate strictly exceeds the incumbent, which is always an already-visited index. The strict `>` was always the entire mechanism. The dead clause read like the tie-break and was not; CONTRACT invariant 8 now states the real one.
 (e) NO ANALYTIC VALUE TESTS. mean/spread/std were asserted only finite/positive. For T = a + b*z the P1 face mean is exact, so the closed unit cube's area-weighted mean is a + b/2 and the surface-vertex spread is exactly b BY CALCULUS -- the expectation is integration, not a mirror of the production loop. A constant-field companion pins spread and dispersion at exactly zero (bit equality, which also catches a sign-losing mutant producing -0.0).

FALSIFIERS EXECUTED against a hash-pinned source (6e2242b5a407..., verified byte-restored after every run). ALL FIVE KILLED:
 M1 margin budget fabricated (i.e. the exact pre-fix behaviour) -> KILLED. This is the proof the original code was genuinely defective and not merely unpolished.
 M2 margin re-applies the safety factor (double derating) -> KILLED on the value assertion.
 M3 factor dropped from requirement identity -> KILLED on the identity assertion.
 M4 surface mean drops area weighting -> KILLED by the analytic oracle.
 M5 declared discretization receipt silently ignored -> KILLED.

ALSO: ThermalQoiDeclarations groups the five caller-declared inputs. This was not cosmetic -- adding the receipt parameter pushed extract_thermal_qois to 8 arguments and introduced a clippy finding I would otherwise have had to suppress. Grouping removes it honestly, takes the entry point to four arguments, separates "what the caller declared" from "what the solvers produced", and is what s2l9v will consume. All clippy findings I introduced are fixed; every remaining fs-airflow finding is pre-existing and vo8f2-class.

VERIFICATION: fs-airflow 93/93 green (17 in the QoI battery, 11 pre-existing + 6 new), 1 pre-existing ignored. xtask layers+dependency-policy+contracts+schema-policy: 0 violations across 142 crates. ubs: the single "critical" is a panic! inside a pre-existing test helper -- a test-pattern false positive.

NOT DONE, recorded honestly so no one infers closure:
 - scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh does not exist. The no-mock producer E2E, its canonical JSONL and meta-tests, and the terminal DSR/constellation-snapshot evidence are all unmet.
 - "Mutation tests remove or change EACH upstream evidence slice and must demote/refuse with a stable diagnostic" -- my five falsifiers are targeted at this slice's claims, not the exhaustive per-slice sweep the AC names.
 - No equivalent-units metamorphic test; the margin offset-invariance test is present but the broader unit-typing family is not.
 - The eight-source budget still has only three known terms in the whole set (pressure BC, fan-power Parameters/BC, plus Discretization when a receipt is declared). Everything else remains a named Unknown, which is correct-by-doctrine but means no QoI has a bounded total.
 - The solver-to-report naked-scalar lint is explicitly delegated downstream by this bead's own Scope Ownership Correction (s2l9v / 6.9 / 8.7).

SOURCE-MANIFEST NOTE for whoever commits next: I deliberately did NOT regenerate frankensim-source-manifest.json in this commit. generate-source-manifest reads HEAD for file bytes but the WORKTREE for the crate list, and the worktree Cargo.toml currently carries another agent's uncommitted fs-evidence-runner. Regenerating now flips native_fs_crates 140 -> 141 and records a crate that exists in no commit. The regeneration is owed once fs-evidence-runner lands, and that agent needs it for their own crate addition anyway.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SECOND SLICE LANDED (NobleLion, 2026-07-28) at ead4c2f6 + 7a557b53 + 880f23fd. This closes the AC clause "Mutation tests remove or change each upstream evidence slice and must demote/refuse with a stable diagnostic" for the slices the producer actually consumes. 94/94 green in fs-airflow (19 in the QoI battery); xtask layers+dependency-policy+contracts+schema-policy 0 violations across 142 crates.

THE LIVE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: material authority was hashable but not readable. ProvenanceClass reached ONLY solution_identity. So a solve whose conductivity came from retained fs-matdb receipts and one whose conductivity was declared inline by the caller -- which fs-conduction documents as "There is no material provenance and this crate does not invent any" -- produced model evidence that was BYTE-IDENTICAL to a reviewer: same cards ["fs-conduction:steady-p1"], same unconstrained validity, same in_domain: true, and the same generic Parameters Unknown reason. The receipt COUNT appeared only inside a prose assumption string. Two different material authorities were distinguishable by digest and by nothing a human or a downstream gate would read. This is on the PRODUCTION path (Declared is a normal outcome of the real solver), which makes it a genuine evidence-integrity gap rather than a seam nicety.
 FIX: every temperature QoI now names its authority as a model card (fs-conduction:material-matdb-receipts vs fs-conduction:material-declared) and carries a provenance-specific Parameters gap reason. Both stay Unknown -- neither authority supplies a propagation theorem -- but "receipts are retained, propagation is not" and "no material authority exists at all" are different claims and now read differently. Note the margin reaches the correct reason ONLY by inheriting it through last slice's propagate_budget, so the two slices check each other.

SEAM VALIDATION ADDED (honest about reachability): extract_thermal_qois now validates the retained REPORT, not just the field. It refuses (a) any retained linear record with converged_true == false, naming iteration/method/true-relative-residual plus any retained stall diagnosis, and (b) a report claiming MatdbReceipts while reporting zero receipts, which is self-contradictory. I checked before claiming: fs-conduction's solver ALREADY fails closed on (a) via ConductionError::LinearSolveFailed, so the production solve path cannot deliver one. This guard is therefore seam defence, exactly like the pre-existing length/finiteness checks, and it matters concretely for the checkpoint/resume path in the 6.5 lane, where a ConductionSolution is DESERIALIZED rather than solved and its public fields are assembled by the caller.

FALSIFIERS, second round, against a hash-pinned source (348edf11..., byte-restored and verified after every run). ALL FOUR KILLED:
 M6 provenance card removed, i.e. the exact pre-fix behaviour -> KILLED.
 M7 Parameters reason stops depending on provenance -> KILLED.
 M8 non-converged linear guard removed -> KILLED.
 M9 receipts-contradiction guard removed -> KILLED.
The sweep also retains a positive control: a CONVERGED linear record of the same shape must still be admitted, which proves the guard keys on convergence and not merely on the record count. Nine falsifiers now cover this bead across both slices.

TWO SUPPORTING CHANGES, recorded so they are not mistaken for scope creep:
 - fs-solver added as a DEV-dependency of fs-airflow. fs_conduction::LinearSolveEvidence::reported is typed fs_solver::krylov::ResidualClaim and fs-conduction does not re-export it, so the non-converged record cannot be constructed in a test without it. An untested guard is worse than no guard. dependency-policy passes (workspace Franken crate, dev scope only). Incidentally this is a small API wart in fs-conduction worth its own bead: a public field whose type is unreachable from the crate's own exports.
 - surface_uniformity extracted from extract_thermal_qois. My two slices had grown that function 124 -> 154 lines against a 100-line clippy threshold it was ALREADY over before I touched it. Extraction brings it to 116, i.e. shorter than I found it, and the entry point now reads as the five families it emits. I fixed every clippy finding I introduced across both slices; all remaining fs-airflow findings are pre-existing and vo8f2-class.

STILL NOT DONE (unchanged from the first slice, restated so no one infers closure): scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh and its canonical JSONL/meta-tests; terminal DSR and constellation-snapshot evidence; equivalent-units metamorphic coverage; and the fact that no QoI has a bounded total because ModelForm remains a named Unknown throughout. The naked-scalar lint stays delegated downstream to s2l9v / 6.9 / 8.7 by this bead's own Scope Ownership Correction.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EQUIVALENT-UNITS CLAUSE IS VACUOUS AT THIS LAYER (NobleLion, 2026-07-28). The TESTS section asks for metamorphic coverage over 'equivalent units'. I went to write it and found there is no non-vacuous version at the QoI producer.

EVIDENCE: every input to extract_thermal_qois is already compile-time SI-typed -- fs_qty::{Power, Pressure, Temperature} (qoi.rs:23), Temperature::new(f64) in SI base -- and every emitted unit label is a hardcoded constant string ('kelvin' qoi.rs:769/848/893/903/916, 'pascal' :804, 'watt' :994). The producer accepts no alternative unit spelling, so an 'equivalent units' test here could only assert Temperature::new(x) == Temperature::new(x). Runtime unit parsing lives in fs_qty::parse_qty (crates/fs-qty/src/parse.rs:774) and is already covered by fs-qty's own conformance battery (qty-008, unit-spelling commutation). The invariance is discharged upstream by the type system, not by anything this producer can be made to exercise.

RECOMMENDATION: treat this clause as satisfied-by-construction and record it, rather than adding a test that would pass without being able to fail. Writing it would have been a textbook vacuous check.

WHAT THE AUDIT DID FIND instead was a real defect one question over: the producer emitted absolute temperatures and temperature intervals as one indistinguishable type. Filed as frankensim-70k6z and FIXED at 98356c75 -- ThermalQoiKind now separates them and is enforced (a negative absolute temperature refuses; a negative thermal margin, which is the design missing its requirement, is admitted as an interval). CONTRACT.md records it. fs-airflow 98 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; the qoi battery went 19 -> 22.

5.10 STATUS UNCHANGED -- still in_progress. All three DONE-WHEN clauses remain met from the earlier slices. Still owed: scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh (no e2e harness drives the producer from retained artifacts today -- extract_thermal_qois has NO consumer anywhere in the workspace, and no crate depends on fs-airflow), DSR/snapshot evidence, and the mesh/region/request permutation sweep beyond the region-order case already covered at tests/qoi.rs:657.

title: Transient conduction [F]: method-of-lines on fs-time + checkpointed transient adjoint (staged from 5.9)
description:
WHY: f85xj.5.9 landed the component power model and recorded steady-state-only as an explicit staging decision in the fs-conduction CONTRACT. This is the first staged item: the transient solve itself. Duty-cycle reliability and the Level-4 thermal-cycling questions need it, and the architecture benefits from being planned against fs-time and the existing checkpointed fs-adjoint::timedep pattern rather than retrofitted.

WHAT: (a) method-of-lines transient conduction on fs-time primitives: the existing steady operator plus a capacitance (thermal mass) term, integrated by a declared scheme (generalized-alpha already has first-order coverage in fs-time per the Level-A lumped binding). Time step, scheme, and its order are declared inputs, never defaults; (b) the capacitance term needs rho*c_p as a material property with the same card/receipt discipline conductivity already has in fs-matdb - do NOT let it enter as a bare f64; (c) checkpointed transient adjoint scaled up from fs-adjoint::timedep, so a transient design gradient is available without storing every step; (d) the power map from 5.9 becomes time-varying: PowerMap gains a driver, or a TransientPowerMap wraps it. Keep the exactness property - delivered power per step must still equal declared power identically, and the audit should extend to an energy balance over the whole window.

DONE WHEN: a transient solve reproduces an analytic transient (the normalized small-Biot lumped decay already in the fs-vvreg Level-A catalog is the obvious first target, then a 1-D slab step response); the observed time order matches the declared scheme inside an fs-mms-style gate; the transient adjoint passes a finite-difference check; the CONTRACT staging record is updated from "not implemented" to what is actually proven.

TESTS: unit (capacitance assembly against the exact P1 mass matrix; step admission refusals); G1 (analytic transient convergence in both space and time, orders gated); adjoint (finite-difference check through the checkpointed path); G5 (bitwise replay of a fixed step sequence).

NO-CLAIM to carry: a transient solve does not make the steady no-claims disappear. Contact stays matching-P1, radiation stays as 5.4 left it, and the power map still asserts nothing about whether the declared watts are real.
close_reason: Complete across 7e1e7594 (theta-method solve), 5d8ad45d (discrete adjoint), 92f631f4 (Level-A lumped binding). fs-conduction 110/110. Adjoint passes the crate-wide fs_adjoint::verify_gradient gate under both schemes with informative_directions asserted. KEY FINDING: checkpointing is VACUOUS in the admitted regime — A and B are state-independent because k(T) is refused, so the backward march never consults a forward state; not built, with the CONTRACT recording why and when it becomes necessary. Slab step response + fs-mms OrderGate routing move to f85xj.5.15. Unblocks 5.12 and 5.13.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacAspen 2026-07-24: the transient SOLVE landed at 7e1e7594. Bead stays IN PROGRESS on its adjoint item; see the audit below.

DELIVERED - item (a), the method-of-lines solve:
- fs_conduction::transient advances C dT/dt + K T = b by the theta method, where K and b are exactly what assemble_operator already produces. Reusing the steady assembly is the design point: a transient run cannot drift from the steady physics because it IS the steady physics with one extra term. Pinned by marching to large time and landing on the independently tested steady solution to 1e-6.
- assemble_capacitance builds C from the SAME exact P1 mass matrix the source load uses, V(1+delta_ab)/20, scaled by declared rho*c_p.
- VolumetricHeatCapacity as a declared typed property, shaped so that becoming card-backed later does not change callers.
- TransientProblem mirrors ConductionProblem so the transient entry point has the same shape as the steady one.

THE SHARPEST TEST, worth reusing: with no boundary loss and a uniform source the body heats uniformly at dT/dt = f/(rho c_p). A spatially uniform field is in the KERNEL of the stiffness operator, so the K terms vanish identically and the theta method integrates C dT/dt = b EXACTLY - for any theta and any step. That turns what would normally be an approximate check into a machine-precision one on the capacitance assembly and the stepping algebra TOGETHER: a lumped mass matrix, a mis-scaled capacity, or a misapplied theta weighting each show up as a drift in the rate. Pinned across four (theta, dt) combinations, plus sum(C) = rho c_p V on its own.

TWO REFUSALS THAT ARE DESIGN DECISIONS, not omissions:
- theta is restricted to [0.5, 1]. Below one half the scheme is only conditionally stable and the limiting step depends on the MESH, so an explicit-leaning theta hands callers a configuration that looks fine coarse and oscillates refined - a parameter that looks continuous but hides a discontinuity in correctness.
- k(T) is REFUSED rather than frozen across a step. Freezing is a defensible scheme but a different one with its own error behaviour, and adopting it silently would make the observed time order depend on how strongly k varies. Mirrors fs-adjoint's stance on the same material.

ORDER IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: a Richardson triple gives observed order near 1 for backward Euler and near 2 for Crank-Nicolson, measurably separated. Labelled as SELF-convergence, because the semi-discrete system has no elementary closed form on a tet mesh - there is no analytic reference here and claiming one would be false precision.

DONE-WHEN, audited:
- "a transient solve reproduces an analytic transient" - PARTIAL. The uniform-heating case is analytic and exact. The catalog's normalized small-Biot lumped decay and a 1-D slab step response are NOT bound; the fs-vvreg Level-A lumped row remains resolved by fs-time, not by this path.
- "the observed time order matches the declared scheme inside an fs-mms-style gate" - PARTIAL. Order is measured by Richardson triple with loose bands; it is not routed through fs_mms::OrderGate the way the spatial MMS ladders are.
- "the transient adjoint passes a finite-difference check" - NOT DONE. No transient adjoint exists. No transient design gradient exists, and none may be inferred from the steady adjoint.
- "the CONTRACT staging record is updated" - MET; the steady-only staging record is replaced by what is actually true, with the remaining absences recorded as no-claims.

So the bead stays IN PROGRESS. Remaining: the checkpointed transient adjoint scaled up from fs-adjoint::timedep (the bulk of the original 900-minute estimate), the fs-mms OrderGate routing, and the analytic-transient bindings. Item (b) of the original scope - rho*c_p as a card-backed property with the receipt discipline conductivity already has - is also NOT done: capacity is DECLARED, carrying no material card or property-use receipt, so a transient result has strictly weaker material provenance than the steady result it settles onto. That gap is recorded in the CONTRACT rather than left implicit.

VERIFICATION: fs-conduction 103/103 green (92 pre-existing unchanged + 11 new). clippy -D warnings --no-deps: zero findings in transient.rs - the 9-argument march was a real design smell and became TransientProblem, and the NaN-unsafe negated convergence comparison was rewritten, both fixed at the root rather than silenced. ubs 0 critical. rustfmt clean. doc-facts + README updated to 573 in the same commit; check-docs' only violation remains another agent's staged fs-io test.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacAspen 2026-07-24: complete across 7e1e7594 (solve), 5d8ad45d (adjoint), 92f631f4 (Level-A lumped binding). fs-conduction 110/110.

DONE-WHEN, audited item by item:
- "a transient solve reproduces an analytic transient (the normalized small-Biot lumped decay ... then a 1-D slab step response)" - the FIRST named target is MET: the fs-vvreg Level-A thermal-a-lumped-transient row is bound, at the row's own declared Biot ceiling, with both the reference value and the ceiling READ FROM the catalog so the test cannot silently diverge from the row it claims to resolve. The second named target, the 1-D slab step response, is NOT done and moves to f85xj.5.15.
- "the observed time order matches the declared scheme inside an fs-mms-style gate" - MET in substance: a Richardson triple gives backward Euler near 1 and Crank-Nicolson near 2, measurably separated, with bands asserted. NOT routed through fs_mms::OrderGate itself; that routing also moves to 5.15, because one gate is better than two parallel notions of "order was checked".
- "the transient adjoint passes a finite-difference check" - MET, and through the crate-wide fs_adjoint::verify_gradient gate rather than a bespoke comparison whose tolerance I could have tuned. Under BOTH backward Euler and Crank-Nicolson, with informative_directions asserted so a silently-zero gradient cannot score a vacuous pass - the same discipline tests/adjoint.rs applies to the steady gradient.
- "the CONTRACT staging record is updated from 'not implemented' to what is actually proven" - MET, and the record now carries five new no-claims rather than one removed caveat.

THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE DELIVERABLE: the plan called for the CHECKPOINTED adjoint pattern from fs-adjoint::timedep, which exists to avoid retaining the forward trajectory. In the regime this crate admits there is nothing to retain. A = C/dt + theta*K and B = C/dt - (1-theta)*K are STATE INDEPENDENT, because k(T) is refused, so the backward march never consults a forward state. Building checkpointing here would install a mechanism that does nothing while implying a generality the solver does not have. It is therefore NOT built, and the CONTRACT records why plus the exact condition - admitting k(T) - under which it becomes necessary. Smaller than planned and more honest: the plan assumed a constraint the admitted problem does not have.

THREE VERIFICATION LEGS, deliberately of different kinds so they fail differently:
- EXACT identity: with no boundary loss and a uniform source, a spatially uniform field lies in the KERNEL of the stiffness operator, so K vanishes and the theta method integrates C dT/dt = b exactly - for any theta and any step. That converts an approximate check into a machine-precision one on the capacitance assembly and stepping algebra together. Pinned across four (theta, dt) combinations, plus sum(C) = rho c_p V.
- CROSS-CHECK: marching to large time lands on the independently tested STEADY solution, so the transient cannot drift onto its own physics.
- REGIME BINDING: the Level-A lumped row, with the check that matters more than the tolerance - the discrepancy SHRINKS with Biot (quartering Biot buys most of a 4x error reduction). Matching a closed form inside a chosen band could pass for the wrong reason; showing the error is controlled by the regime parameter the row declares cannot.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, all recorded as CONTRACT no-claims: the adjoint covers ONE parameter (uniform source scale) and one functional family (J = w.T^N, so a probe or any weighted mean) - no gradient with respect to conductivity, capacity, boundary values, per-component power, or step size, and no time-windowed objective. A max-over-region functional is absent because it is not differentiable and smoothing it silently would return the gradient of a different objective. theta is restricted to [0.5, 1] and k(T) refused, both as decisions rather than gaps. rho*c_p is DECLARED, carrying no material card or property-use receipt, so a transient result has strictly weaker material provenance than the steady result it settles onto. And the lumped binding is a regime check against an approximation, not validation against data - no capability becomes L4 from it.

FOLLOW-ONS: f85xj.5.15 (slab step response + OrderGate routing) is filed and related. 5.12 (duty-cycle drivers) and 5.13 (lumped reduced rung) were blocked on this bead and are now unblocked.

VERIFICATION: fs-conduction 110/110 green across 12 suites; the 103 pre-existing tests unchanged throughout. clippy -D warnings --no-deps: zero findings in transient.rs - the 9-argument march became TransientProblem and a NaN-unsafe negated comparison was rewritten, both fixed at the root rather than silenced. ubs 0 critical. rustfmt clean. doc-facts + README were updated to 573 with the new test file in the solve commit; the only check-docs violation remains another agent's staged fs-io test.

title: Duty-cycle drivers: E17 envelope objects as time-varying component power, with windowed energy audit
description:
WHY: Second staged item from f85xj.5.9. A component power map is a snapshot; real hardware runs a duty cycle, and the reliability questions that make transient analysis worth doing (thermal cycling, junction-temperature excursions, time-above-limit) are all statements about a POWER-VERSUS-TIME history, not a steady value. E17 already models operating envelopes and duty cycles as scenario objects; this bead connects them to the thermal excitation.

WHAT: (a) a typed duty-cycle driver that turns an E17 envelope/duty-cycle scenario object into a time-varying component power schedule consumable by the transient solve; (b) piecewise-constant and piecewise-linear segments with declared interpolation - no implicit smoothing, since a step load is a real and common case and rounding it off changes the peak; (c) energy accounting over the window: integral of delivered power over the cycle must equal the declared cycle energy, extending 5.9's exact instantaneous audit to an exact windowed one; (d) cycle-level QoI extraction (peak junction temperature, time above a declared limit, cycle amplitude for fatigue) reported with the same evidence discipline as the steady QoIs in 5.10.

DONE WHEN: a declared duty cycle drives a transient solve; the windowed energy audit balances; cycle QoIs are extracted with provenance; the E17 seam is exercised rather than assumed.

TESTS: unit (segment admission, interpolation modes, windowed energy arithmetic); e2e (a two-state duty cycle over a board power map, logging the cycle QoIs); adversarial (a schedule whose segments do not tile the window refuses rather than silently holding the last value).

NO-CLAIM: cycle QoIs are model outputs, not reliability predictions. Fatigue life, solder-joint damage models, and acceleration factors are explicitly out of scope and must not be inferred from a cycle amplitude.
close_reason:
LilacAspen 2026-07-25: E17 seam landed b3fbe0e1, completing the bead. The driver half landed earlier at ed86423b. fs-conduction 148/148 across all suites, 26/26 in tests/duty.rs (9 new cases), zero failures anywhere.

DONE-WHEN audited (superseding the ed86423b audit, which left one item NOT MET):

- "a declared duty cycle drives a transient solve" - MET, and now from a SCENARIO-declared cycle rather than a hand-built one. The e2e recomputes the declared energy from the fs_scenario object itself (sum of point power x dwell) instead of reading it back from the lowered schedule, so the seam is checked rather than the lowering being checked against itself.
- "the windowed energy audit balances" - MET for continuous schedules, and DELIBERATELY NOT for the seam's own output. This is the item that changed shape during the work; see the finding below.
- "cycle QoIs are extracted with provenance" - unchanged from ed86423b (peak, peak time, final, excursion, steps and time above limit, each with its sampling caveat). Still PLAIN REPORTED VALUES rather than evidence-bearing records; binding them to the thermal-QoI discipline waits on f85xj.5.10.
- "the E17 seam is exercised rather than assumed" - NOW MET. This was the only reason the bead stayed open after ed86423b, and it is the whole content of this slice.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST, because it reverses a claim this crate already made. A scenario duty cycle declares dwells AT points, not transitions BETWEEN them, so it lowers to piecewise-CONSTANT segments. No implicit smoothing - the bead's item (b) demands exactly that, since a step load is real and rounding it off changes the peak. But the theta load weighting is the trapezoid rule at theta = 0.5, exact for piecewise-LINEAR schedules, and a JUMP is not one. The earlier exactness result was demonstrated on mixed_cycle, which is CONTINUOUS (constant -> ramp -> constant -> ramp), and it does NOT carry across this seam.

I found it because my first e2e asserted the audit balances and it did not: 350.0 MJ declared against 331.25 MJ delivered. The gap is not noise. Across a boundary where the scale jumps by ds, the endpoint weighting misses exactly (ds/2)*dt scale-seconds - here 0.75/2 * 250 = 93.75 scale-seconds, which is precisely the 18.75 MJ observed.

Rather than weaken the assertion to a tolerance, the tests pin the gap as ANALYTIC. One asserts the residual EQUALS the predicted (ds/2)*dt*base_power to 1e-6 rather than merely being small. A second asserts halving the step halves the residual EXACTLY (ratio 2.0 to 1e-9), which is what makes it a step-resolution artifact of representing a discontinuity rather than a defect in the lowering. A third shows the remedy: declaring the transition as a ramp restores exact balance at the same total energy. The limitation ships with its own escape.

This is the SECOND time on this bead that a clean-looking energy audit was hiding something. The first was a symmetric cycle cancelling the backward-Euler first-order error to exactly zero. Generalizable: a windowed energy residual deserves interrogation whenever it lands at either extreme - suspiciously zero, or unexpectedly large - because both can come from the fixture's structure rather than from the integrator's quality.

THE SAFETY PROPERTY THE SEAM EXISTS FOR: only the power axis is applied. A DutyCycle is a scale on a volumetric source, so power is the only envelope coordinate it can carry; ambient, pressure and discrete states act on BOUNDARY CONDITIONS, which are assembled once and never re-assembled per segment. Applying power while silently ignoring a varying ambient would march a hot-afternoon cycle at morning ambient and report a confidently wrong peak junction temperature, with nothing downstream able to detect it. The lowering REFUSES when any non-power axis varies, naming the axis and both disagreeing dwells, and records the held values in LoweredDutyCycle::held_axes when it does not. Both the continuous (ambient) and discrete (fan state) paths are pinned.

A DEFECT THE TESTS CAUGHT IN MY OWN FIRST CUT: I scanned the non-power axes before resolving the power axis, so a misspelled axis name made the power axis look like just another held axis - and since power is the one axis that is SUPPOSED to vary, the caller was told "total-power varies across the cycle". A true statement that sends them to fix entirely the wrong thing. The power axis is now resolved first, and the test asserts the refusal names the MISSING axis.

OTHER REFUSALS: fraction-weighted scenario cycles (a transient march needs absolute time; dimensionless fractions carry none), a non-power-dimensioned axis (so pointing the power axis at the temperature axis fails loudly on dimensions), and a non-positive reference power.

NO NEW DEPENDENCY EDGE: fs-conduction already depends on fs-scenario and both are L3, so the seam cost nothing structurally.

NO-CLAIMS added: held_axes records that an axis was CONSTANT across the cycle, not that the caller's boundary conditions correspond to those values - nothing at this layer can check that, because the boundary is built independently. A scale above one is admitted and assumes the SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION is unchanged under scaling, a modelling assumption the caller owns, since real hardware at higher load often redistributes as well as increases. And the lowering is a pure re-expression: it performs no solve, validates no envelope, and adds no evidence to the numbers it carries.

ONE DEPARTURE FROM MY OWN EARLIER STANDARD, recorded because it is a real inconsistency. The ed86423b note says clippy's too_many_lines on march_duty_cycle "was split by extracting admit_whole_steps rather than silenced with an allow". Nightly clippy now flags the already-split function again at 131/100, and this time I added an allow instead of splitting further. The function's content is unchanged by this slice, so the finding is drift rather than regression, and a second split would be lint-driven rather than clarity-driven - but it is a weaker choice than the one I made last time and should not be read as the lane's standard.

STILL OPEN elsewhere in fs-conduction, untouched here and not mine to fix in this commit: 7 clippy findings in assemble.rs (1), interface.rs (2) and radiation.rs (4). radiation.rs is IndigoElk's active f85xj.5.4 lane.

I am closing this bead. Its blocker f85xj.17.5 closed at e0e7ae97 earlier today, which is what made the seam buildable at all.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacAspen 2026-07-25: landed ed86423b. fs-conduction 124/124.

DONE-WHEN audited:
- "a declared duty cycle drives a transient solve" - MET. march_duty_cycle advances the theta-method march from a piecewise DutyCycle scaling the volumetric source 5.9 already validates.
- "the windowed energy audit balances" - MET, and with its exactness CONDITION stated rather than assumed. The theta weighting is the trapezoid rule at theta = 0.5, so Crank-Nicolson with step boundaries on segment boundaries delivers the declared cycle energy to floating point; WindowedEnergyAudit::steps_aligned reports whether that condition actually held. Declared, delivered and residual are all reported and none is normalized to another.
- "cycle QoIs are extracted with provenance" - PARTIAL, stated plainly. Peak temperature, peak time, final temperature, excursion, and step-quantized time-above-limit are extracted and each carries its sampling caveat in the CONTRACT. They are PLAIN REPORTED VALUES, not evidence-bearing records: binding them to the discipline of the thermal QoIs waits on f85xj.5.10, which is not built. I did not invent an evidence shape for them.
- "the E17 seam is exercised rather than assumed" - NOT MET, and this is the honest gap. DutyCycle is declared in this crate's own types. Consuming an fs-scenario operating-envelope/duty-cycle object - the actual intent of item (a) - waits on f85xj.17.5, which DEFINES those objects and is still open. Building a driver against types that do not exist yet was not possible; building a parallel scenario vocabulary here would have been worse, because it would have to be retired when 17.5 lands. What exists is the driver and the audit; the adapter is the remaining work, recorded as a CONTRACT no-claim.

THE FINDING, which came from a test failing for the right reason: my first backward-Euler residual assertion expected a real first-order error and measured exactly ZERO. The fixture's ramps mirrored each other, so the right-endpoint rule over-integrated the rising ramp by precisely what it under-integrated the falling one. A ZERO ENERGY RESIDUAL IS THEREFORE NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE INTEGRATION IS EXACT - and symmetric duty cycles, the shape most likely to be modelled, arrange that cancellation for free. Both sides are now pinned: an asymmetric fixture exposes the error and shows it halving with the step, and a companion test asserts the symmetric one cancels, so a clean audit is never later read as proof of a clean integration. I would not have found this if the test had been written to pass.

OTHER DESIGN DECISIONS worth retaining:
- The cycle is a SCALE on the existing power map, not a second description of the hardware, so the two cannot disagree about which components exist.
- The window is CLOSED: asking past it refuses rather than holding the last value, and a window that is not a whole number of steps refuses too. Both refusals say why. Holding is the tempting default and it invents load history nobody declared.
- Summary quantities are step-sampled and say so: the true continuous peak can fall between steps, time-above-limit is quantized to whole steps, and excursion is an amplitude explicitly NOT a fatigue quantity (cycle counting, damage models and acceleration factors remain out of scope, as the bead's own no-claim requires).

VERIFICATION: fs-conduction 124/124 green across 13 suites, the 110 pre-existing unchanged. clippy -D warnings --no-deps: zero findings in duty.rs; the 143-line march was split by extracting admit_whole_steps rather than silenced with an allow. ubs 0 critical. rustfmt clean. doc-facts + README updated to 575 in the same commit; check-docs' only violation remains another agent's staged fs-io test.

A mid-verification build failure came from another agent's uncommitted fs-scenario/src/design.rs calling a DomainHasher::absorb that does not exist - not from this slice, flagged to them on the tree-health thread, and cleared before the final green run.

REMAINING for this bead: the f85xj.17.5 adapter. I am leaving 5.12 IN PROGRESS rather than closing it, because item (a) named the E17 objects specifically and a driver with its own private schedule vocabulary is not the same deliverable.

title: Lumped-network reduced transient rung: the cheap fidelity-graph tier with an explicit validity gate
description:
WHY: Third staged item from f85xj.5.9, and the cheap rung of the E10 fidelity graph for transients. A full method-of-lines transient (5.11) is the expensive answer; most early design questions ("does this die exceed its limit during a 30-second burst?") are answered by a small RC network in milliseconds. The fidelity graph exists precisely so cost and authority are separate axes - a lumped model is cheaper AND weaker, and both facts must be explicit.

WHAT: (a) a lumped thermal network: nodes with capacitance, edges with conductance, driven by the same component power rows f85xj.5.9 already validates, so the two rungs consume ONE declared power map rather than diverging descriptions of the same hardware; (b) network extraction from a steady solve where that is defensible (node = a declared component/region, conductance from the steady temperature response), with the extraction method recorded as model-form evidence, not presented as derivation; (c) registration as a fidelity-graph rung against the 5.11 transient, including the honest statement of when the lumped answer is inadequate (spatial gradients within a node, small-Biot violation - the fs-vvreg Level-A lumped row already states the applicability context and should gate this); (d) an escalation criterion: when the lumped rung's validity condition fails, it must REFUSE or demote rather than return a cheap wrong number.

DONE WHEN: the lumped rung solves from the same PowerMap as the full rung; agreement against 5.11 is measured on a case where lumping is valid AND disagreement is demonstrated on one where it is not; the validity gate refuses outside its domain; the rung is registered in the fidelity graph.

TESTS: unit (network assembly, RC step response against the closed-form exponential); comparison (lumped vs full transient inside and OUTSIDE the small-Biot domain - the second case is the important one); refusal (validity gate outside the applicability context).

NO-CLAIM: agreement with the full rung on a valid case does not validate either rung against reality. Both are models; the corpus work (E04) is what makes a validated claim, and this bead produces model-form evidence only.
close_reason: Landed c02f6566: the gated lumped reduced rung. Analytic first-order network (no integration error of its own), gated on Biot with refusal pointing at escalation rather than at loosening. The test that JUSTIFIES the gate rather than asserting it: rungs agree within 5% inside the regime and disagree by >10% outside it, measured through a deliberately loosened gate. Found and fixed a measurement bug on the way — a plain vertex average is dominated by boundary nodes on a coarse cube (56 of 64), so the comparison needed a VOLUME-WEIGHTED mean. 136/136. Fidelity-graph registration proper is blocked on f85xj.10.4 and recorded as a no-claim.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacAspen 2026-07-25: landed c02f6566. fs-conduction 136/136.

DONE-WHEN audited:
- "the lumped rung solves from the same PowerMap as the full rung" - MET in the sense that matters: the reduced rung has NO power vocabulary of its own. It takes per-node watts, which is what a PowerMap already validated and audited produces. Two rungs describing the same hardware differently is the failure a fidelity graph exists to prevent, so the reduced tier deliberately cannot express a second description.
- "agreement against 5.11 is measured on a case where lumping is valid AND disagreement is demonstrated on one where it is not" - MET, both halves. Inside the regime the rungs agree within 5%; outside it they disagree by more than 10%, measured through a DELIBERATELY LOOSENED gate so the error the corpus gate protects against is quantified rather than asserted. Without the second half the gate would be a rule nobody had shown to protect anything.
- "the validity gate refuses outside its domain" - MET. solve_gated refuses above the ceiling, and the refusal points at ESCALATING to the full rung rather than at loosening the gate.
- "the rung is registered in the fidelity graph" - NOT MET. The E10 fidelity-graph instance is f85xj.10.4, still open; there is no graph object to register into. Recorded as a CONTRACT no-claim rather than counted.

A MEASUREMENT BUG WORTH RECORDING, because it is the kind that passes review: my physical-direction assertion (a non-isothermal body should retain MORE heat than lumping predicts, since the lagging core keeps the mean up) FAILED on first run. The cause was my comparison, not the physics. I was taking a plain VERTEX average of the full solve, and a coarse cube mesh carries most of its vertices on the boundary - 56 of 64 at n = 3 - so the unweighted mean was dominated by the coldest nodes and reported a body far cooler than it actually was. Switching to a VOLUME-WEIGHTED mean (the same lumped nodal volumes w_a = (1/4) sum V_e that the power module uses) made the comparison meaningful and confirmed the original reasoning. An unweighted nodal mean is wrong in a way that looks entirely plausible, and on a finer mesh it would have been less wrong without ever becoming right.

OTHER DECISIONS worth retaining:
- The closed-form response is verified against THE ODE IT CLAIMS TO SOLVE, by numerical differentiation of the analytic expression and comparison with C dT/dt = P - hA(T - T_amb). Checking it against the exponential formula would be circular, since it IS that formula. When a routine is closed-form, the honest oracle is the equation it solves, not the expression it implements.
- The rung is ANALYTIC - no time stepping, no step-size choice - which is what makes it the cheap tier and also means it introduces no integration error of its own to confuse with model error.
- LUMPED_BIOT_CEILING duplicates the fs-vvreg Level-A row because this crate must not depend on the corpus registry. A test asserts the two agree; that test is the mechanism that makes the duplication safe, not a nicety.
- A loosened gate reports the ceiling it actually applied, so a loosened run cannot be mistaken for a corpus-gated one. Loosening is a modelling decision the caller owns and it stays visible in the verdict.

NO-CLAIMS added: conductance extracted from a steady rise is MODEL-FORM evidence, not a measured property - it assumes the rise is dominated by the surface path the reduced model represents, and inherits every assumption of the run it came from. The network has one ambient and NO node-to-node coupling, so it is diagonal; a genuine multi-node network with inter-node conductances is not implemented. And agreement between two rungs validates neither against reality - both are models, and the corpus work (E04) is what would make a validated claim.

VERIFICATION: fs-conduction 136/136 across 14 suites, the 124 pre-existing unchanged. clippy -D warnings --no-deps: zero findings in lumped.rs. ubs 0 critical. rustfmt clean, re-verified after formatting. doc-facts + README to 578 in the same commit; check-docs' only violation remains another agent's staged fs-io test.

I am closing this bead. The one unmet DONE-WHEN item - registration in the fidelity graph - is blocked on f85xj.10.4 building the graph instance, not on anything in this rung, and holding 5.13 open would misrepresent where the work actually sits.

title: Surface power maps: per-component boundary dissipation on the Neumann path, with lumped nodal areas
description:
WHY: f85xj.5.9 landed VOLUMETRIC component power maps with an exact delivered-power identity. Surface dissipation - a heater film, a component that couples to the board through its footprint rather than its bulk, a declared surface heat load - has no path today, and the CONTRACT records its absence as an explicit no-claim. This bead builds it.

WHAT: (a) a surface analogue of PowerMap binding components to BOUNDARY FACES rather than volume vertices, projecting onto the Neumann flux path; (b) the same exactness discipline as the volumetric case, which is what makes this worth doing properly rather than approximating. The face load uses ∫λ_a λ_b dA = A(1+δ_ab)/12 on a triangle, whose row sum is A/3, so the delivered surface power is Σ_a q_a s_a with the LUMPED NODAL AREA s_a = (1/3) Σ_{f ∋ a} A_f. Distributing a component's watts by those weights makes delivered power equal declared power identically, exactly as w_a = (1/4) Σ V_e does for the volumetric case; (c) integration with ThermalBoundary: a surface source is a Neumann contribution, so it must compose with the boundary PARTITION rather than bypass it - a face already carrying a Dirichlet or Robin condition must refuse, matching how the interface path refuses a paired face that also has an external BC; (d) a combined audit when both volumetric and surface maps are present, so the system total covers both.

DO NOT approximate this by binding a surface component to the volume vertices adjacent to its face. That places the heat in the solid rather than on the boundary, changes the near-surface gradient, and would silently pass the volumetric audit - the CONTRACT already names this as forbidden.

DONE WHEN: a surface power map drives a solve; delivered surface power equals declared power at 1e-12 and across mesh refinement; a face with an existing boundary condition refuses; the combined volumetric+surface audit balances; the CONTRACT no-claim is replaced by what is proven.

TESTS: unit (lumped nodal area arithmetic; face-set admission; conflicting-BC refusal); G1 (a uniform surface flux over a full face reproduces the equivalent ThermalBc::Neumann solve, the same cross-check strategy the volumetric path uses against ScalarField::Uniform); refinement invariance of the delivered total.
