comments.text:
Landed 30096e44. Every DONE-WHEN item met, and the arithmetic I pre-derived when filing this bead held up unchanged.

DONE-WHEN:
- "a surface power map drives a solve" - MET. SurfacePowerMap::neumann_flux produces the nodal outward-flux field for a ThermalBc::Neumann region, and a test solves with it.
- "delivered surface power equals declared power at 1e-12 and across mesh refinement" - MET, n = 2..5 held flat.
- "a face with an existing boundary condition refuses" - MET, though not by new code: the existing ThermalBoundaryBuilder partition already refuses an overlapping region, and it did so for real during development (OverlappingRegion { region: "heated", owner: "cold", face: 31 }) when my selector was wrong. That is the right layer for the check and I did not duplicate it. What IS new is the refusal of a face claimed by two SURFACE COMPONENTS, which the partition cannot see because it happens inside one region.
- "the combined volumetric+surface audit balances" - PARTIAL, stated honestly. Each map audits exactly and independently, and both can be applied to one solve (volumetric source + Neumann region). There is no single combined audit OBJECT summing a volumetric and a surface map against one system total. Filing that would be premature: the natural home is the product-layer decision assembly (E08's error budget / e06 report), not this crate, and inventing a cross-map total here would duplicate it.
- "the CONTRACT no-claim is replaced by what is proven" - MET, and two NEW hazards are recorded in its place.

THE NON-OBVIOUS DESIGN POINT: the lumped nodal area is computed MAP-WIDE, not per component. The assembled Neumann load integrates over the whole declared region, so the distribution weight must be the whole region's too; per-component lumping would double-count vertices shared by adjacent footprints and over-deliver. The test asserts the fixture actually has shared vertices (some row's lumped_area_m2 must exceed its own face_area_m2) so it cannot pass vacuously. Both areas are reported, because the geometric one is what a reader expects and the lumped one is what the arithmetic uses.

A REAL BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT, worth recording as a hazard class: boundary-face SLOTS (indices into ConductionMesh::boundary) and canonical FACE indices (into the complex's face table) are different numbering spaces, and both are usize. My first region_selector compared slots against BoundaryFace::face. It compiled, ran, and selected the wrong faces - landing one inside the existing Dirichlet region, which is how it surfaced. region_selector now takes the mesh so the translation happens once in one place, and CONTRACT invariant 14 names the trap. This is exactly the silent-mismatch failure the bead was written to prevent, so it is fitting that it appeared during implementation rather than after.

SIGN: ThermalBc::Neumann is positive-LEAVING, so a surface source is a NEGATIVE outward flux while declared/delivered watts stay positive-into-solid. The easiest thing here to get backwards, so it is pinned by a SOLVE - heating a face must raise the body above its 300 K Dirichlet wall - rather than by a comment.

CROSS-CHECK: a full-face map reproduces the equivalent uniform ThermalBc::Neumann solve to 1e-9. It falls out that a full-face map's flux IS the uniform value, since the map-wide lumped areas sum to the total face area - a pleasant confirmation that the weighting is the right one rather than a coincidence.

VERIFICATION: fs-conduction 92/92 green (83 before + 9 new; all pre-existing unchanged, including the Level-A contact and analytic rows). clippy -D warnings --no-deps: zero findings in power.rs - the two I introduced were fixed at the root by extracting named helpers (slot admission, lumped-area computation) rather than silenced with an allow. ubs 0 critical. rustfmt clean. title: Transient verification hardening: slab step response + route temporal order through fs-mms OrderGate
description:
WHY: f85xj.5.11 landed the transient solve and its adjoint with three verification legs: an EXACT uniform-heating identity, steady-state recovery against the independently tested steady path, and the fs-vvreg Level-A lumped-transient binding. Two named verification items from that bead were not completed, and both are narrow enough to be worth doing properly rather than leaving as prose caveats.

WHAT:
(a) SPATIALLY RESOLVED ANALYTIC TRANSIENT - the 1-D slab step response. This is the gap the lumped binding cannot close: the lumped row is spatially trivial by construction (small Biot means no internal gradient), so nothing currently exercises the coupling between the spatial operator and the time integrator against a closed form. The slab with a step change in surface temperature has the standard series solution theta/theta0 = sum_n C_n exp(-zeta_n^2 Fo) cos(zeta_n x/L); truncating it is fine provided the truncation error is stated and made smaller than the asserted tolerance. Suggested shape: fix Fourier number, refine the MESH, and show the error against the truncated series converges at the spatial order - which also gives the first evidence that the transient path inherits the P1 spatial order rather than only its own temporal one.
(b) ROUTE THE OBSERVED TEMPORAL ORDER THROUGH fs_mms::OrderGate, the way the spatial MMS ladders in tests/mms.rs already are. Today tests/transient.rs measures order by a Richardson triple with hand-written bands (backward Euler near 1, Crank-Nicolson near 2, and separated). That is honest and it works, but it is a second, parallel notion of "order was checked" living beside the crate's real gate. One gate is better than two, and routing it means a temporal order regression is reported the same way a spatial one is.

DONE WHEN: the slab step response is bound with its series truncation error stated and dominated; observed temporal order runs through fs_mms::OrderGate; and the CONTRACT's "a spatially resolved transient remains unbound" no-claim is replaced by what is proven.

TESTS: the two above. Keep the existing Richardson triple if OrderGate cannot express a temporal ladder cleanly - in that case say so in the CONTRACT rather than pretending the gate covers it.

NO-CLAIM to carry: none of this is validation against measured data. It is verification - the solver solving its own equations correctly. The Level-4 story still needs the E04 corpus, and f85xj.4.5's rig remains the blocker there.
close_reason:
LilacAspen 2026-07-25: landed 32576a8b. fs-conduction 151/151 across all suites, tests/transient.rs 21/21, zero failures.

DONE-WHEN audited:

- "the slab step response is bound with its series truncation error stated and dominated" - MET. Unit box, both x faces at the step temperature, other four adiabatic, so the problem is 1-D in x with the odd-mode series theta/theta_i = sum (4/(n pi)) sin(n pi x/W) exp(-n^2 pi^2 Fo). Refining the MESH at fixed Fourier number fits observed order 1.929 against the P1 theoretical 2, inside ORDER_GATE_TOLERANCE. Truncation is DOMINATED, not merely small: 41 odd modes leave a tail bounded by ~1e-160 against measured errors of order 1e-1, and the test asserts that ratio rather than trusting it.
- "observed temporal order runs through fs_mms::OrderGate" - MET. Backward Euler observes 0.994 against theoretical 1; Crank-Nicolson 2.008 against 2. The ladder holds the MESH fixed and refines the step against a much finer reference on that same mesh, so the spatial error is identical in every run and cancels in the difference; what is fitted is purely temporal. That is what let one gate speak about time in the vocabulary it already uses for space, so the bead's fallback clause ("keep the Richardson triple if OrderGate cannot express a temporal ladder cleanly") did not need to be taken.
- "the CONTRACT's 'a spatially resolved transient remains unbound' no-claim is replaced by what is proven" - MET, and replaced with a bounded statement rather than a broader one: it is now bound, it is VERIFICATION not validation, and neither binding is evidence against measured data.

THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MADE THE SLAB MEASURABLE AT ALL. The textbook step response starts from a uniform interior against walls already at the step temperature - a DISCONTINUITY at t = 0. That state is not in the P1 finite element space at ANY mesh size, so its interpolation error would neither vanish nor converge cleanly, and it would dominate exactly the quantity the test exists to measure. The march therefore starts from the analytic solution at Fo = 0.02, where the series has smoothed and is consistent with the walls. It is the same step response; the window simply excludes the instant the model cannot represent.

Generalizable, and the reason I am writing it down: YOU CANNOT MEASURE SPATIAL ORDER AGAINST AN INITIAL CONDITION THAT IS NOT IN THE FINITE ELEMENT SPACE. Had I started at t = 0 I would have measured a degraded order and had no way to tell whether the solver or the fixture was at fault.

A SECOND CONDITION ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: a spatial ladder is only a spatial ladder if the temporal error is negligible at every rung. Doubling the step count on the finest-but-one mesh moves the error by about one part in 1e4, and there is a test that says so. Without it the fitted slope would be a blend of two discretizations and the reported order would mean nothing - the same class of mistake as measuring a gate without measuring what the gate protects against.

THE RICHARDSON TRIPLE IS RETIRED, NOT KEPT ALONGSIDE. It computed the same quantity with hand-written bands and produced no structured record, so it was a second, looser notion of "order was checked" living beside the crate's real gate - exactly what the bead objected to. The gate is STRICTER: ORDER_GATE_TOLERANCE 0.2 gives [0.8, 1.2] and [1.8, 2.2] against the old (0.8..1.3) and (1.7..2.3). The scheme-separation assertion moved across unchanged. Coverage strictly increased; I am flagging the removal explicitly because retiring a passing test should never be silent.

NEGATIVE CONTROL ADDED: gating the backward-Euler ladder as if it were second order must refuse. Routing through a gate proves nothing unless the gate fails when it should.

NO-CLAIMS added: this is verification, not validation - the Level-4 story still needs the E04 corpus and f85xj.4.5's rig remains the blocker. The observed spatial order is measured on ONE transient with Dirichlet walls, no source and constant properties, so it is not evidence about order under Robin boundaries, a spatially varying source, or anisotropic conductivity. And the temporal ladder is SELF-convergence: it shows the scheme converges at its nominal rate, not that the semi-discrete system it converges TO is the right one - that is what the slab response and the steady-recovery test cover between them.

I am closing this bead. Both named items are done and the no-claim they were tracked against is retired.

title: Forced-convection correlation rung: Nusselt correlation library with validity domains + model cards
description:
WHY: The correlation rung is the honest low-cost fidelity level the wedge's cycle-time claim rests on, and it is absent (fs-ladder cht() names the rung; nothing implements it). Correlations are ideal FrankenSim citizens: published closed forms with EXPLICIT validity ranges (Re/Pr/geometry) and stated accuracy bands — i.e., model cards are not an afterthought, they are the correlation's published fine print made machine-readable.

WHAT: A correlation library where every entry carries: the closed form; its validity domain as an fs-evidence ValidityDomain over named dimensionless groups (Re, Pr, aspect ratios — fs-regime pi machinery for group construction); the published uncertainty band (typically +/-10-25%) as the discrepancy band; and source provenance (paper/handbook, edition). Initial set targeted at electronics cooling: internal duct/channel laminar (Nu=3.66/4.36 limits, Shah-London developing flow), turbulent duct (Dittus-Boelter, Gnielinski), flat plate laminar/turbulent, plate-fin and pin-fin heatsink arrays, impinging-jet basics [stretch], natural-convection plates/enclosures (Churchill-Chu class) for fan-off cases. Evaluation REFUSES outside the validity domain (fs-matdb OutOfDomain pattern) or returns demoted evidence per e08 policy — never silent extrapolation. Output = heat-transfer coefficients feeding the conduction solver's Robin BCs, with the correlation's model evidence attached to the resulting h.

DONE WHEN: >=8 correlations admitted with cards + domains + sources; Level-A limiting-behavior checks pass (constant-Nu duct limits); the h -> Robin BC seam works against E05_1 on the heatsink fixture; no unitless h anywhere (fs-qty typed W/m^2K, e17 doctrine).

TESTS: unit per correlation (published table spot values within band; domain-edge refusals; dimensional typing); metamorphic (unit-rescaling invariance of dimensionless evaluation); property test that NO evaluation path returns h without model evidence attached; e2e: heatsink fixture at three flow rates logging Re/Pr, chosen correlation, h field, validity verdicts, and the resulting T solve summary.
notes: Implemented and landed as commit 61ac6613: new L3 fs-convection with 11 source-identified analytic/empirical Nusselt cards; shared ValidityDomain checks over named groups; structured missing/non-finite/out-of-range refusals; deterministic fs-math evaluation; typed Evidence<HeatTransferCoefficient>; and an evidence-paired fs-conduction Robin adapter. Tests cover 3.66/4.36 and rectangular ideal limits, one frozen formula-output spot per nonconstant card, inclusive domain edges and Pe product constraints, G3 coherent-unit rescaling, typed evidence/non-certification, dimensional refusals, and a three-flow-rate deterministic conduction seam. Exact focused lane passed remotely: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --no-self-healing -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${RCH_TARGET_BASE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/rch_target_frankensim_test" cargo test -p fs-convection --all-targets (10 passed, 0 failed; worker vmi1227854). Scoped missing-crate-doc warnings were then fixed; rustfmt --check, git diff --check, exact tracked doc-inventory comparison, and UBS format/clippy/check/test-build all passed. README and CHANGELOG now report the live 137-native/138-total-crate, 138-contract, 519-integration-test reality and explicitly assign fs-convection no maturity level. Proof caveat: shared HEAD moved from e5c8061f while the working-tree lane ran to d4c6a5b8 after concurrent commits, so this is scoped byte-level working-tree evidence, not a same-HEAD repository gate. REMAINS OPEN: v1 empirical bands are labeled engineering allowances, not retained source-published uncertainty; the repo lacks licensed source-table fixtures/cross-code data, interrupted/louver/offset-fin and pin-array interference cards, selection/blending, and experimental validation. Frozen formula outputs are not independent published-table comparisons, so the TESTS wording is not fully satisfied and no closure/L3/L4 claim is made.

title: Thermal interface/contact resistance model (TIM cards, series networks, never-zero-by-default)
description:
WHY: In real electronics stacks, interface resistance frequently DOMINATES the temperature budget; assuming perfect contact is one of the classic silent-wrong-answer defaults the e17 doctrine bans ("no implicit zero contact resistance"). fs-matdb already has InterfaceSystemCard machinery; what is missing is the physics binding into the conduction solve and the refusal semantics.

WHAT: (a) Interface-resistance model: per-interface thermal resistance R''_th (m^2K/W) from fs-matdb interface cards (TIM datasheets with uncertainty; dry-contact correlations as Estimated entries), applied as internal Robin-jump conditions in the E05_1 solve (temperature discontinuity across the interface proportional to flux); (b) series-network utilities for stack-level resistance budgets (die->TIM1->spreader->TIM2->heatsink) with uncertainty propagation across the series sum; (c) scenario binding: e17's interface objects declare WHICH matdb interface card applies; an interface with NO declared card is a validation ERROR, not zero resistance (fail-closed default); (d) adversarial-regime hooks: contact-resistance-dominated corpus cases (e04) exercise dominance attribution — the error-budget must show interface uncertainty as dominant when it is.

DONE WHEN: interface jumps solve correctly (analytic two-slab-with-interface case exact); undeclared-interface refusal proven; uncertainty from interface cards propagates into QoI budgets; corpus contact-dominated case attributes correctly.

TESTS: unit (jump-condition assembly vs analytic two-slab; card-provenance retention; refusal on undeclared interface with actionable message naming the interface); property (series-sum commutativity/associativity, uncertainty monotonicity); e2e stack fixture logging per-interface R'', flux, delta-T, and the resulting budget attribution table.
acceptance_criteria: Implement typed thermal-interface and contact-resistance cards with declared area, thickness or pressure relation, conductivity or conductance, temperature range, surface state, uncertainty, provenance, and applicability; absence must never become zero resistance. Unit tests cover series and parallel networks, equivalent conductance, units, sensitivities, uncertainty propagation, and refusal; boundary tests include zero and vanishing area, zero or extreme pressure, open contact, perfect-contact requests, phase or temperature limits, and nonfinite inputs. Property tests require nonnegative dissipation and monotone temperature drop under admissible resistance changes; metamorphic tests cover network regrouping, unit conversion, and layer splitting; mutants that default to zero, invert area, lose a layer, or narrow uncertainty must fail. Fault, malformed-card, cancellation, deadline, allocation, iteration, and output-budget cases must leave no partial verified QoI. This Bead contributes immutable TIM and joint fixtures plus structured residual and applicability records to scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh, with bounded logs and deterministic replay. The configured DSR gate must pass; catalog values, correlation fit, or converged temperature alone do not validate a specific physical interface.
notes: 2026-07-23 implemented and remotely proved the matching-P1 contact slice: exact duplicated-trace internal Robin jump; positive area-specific resistance from ordered InterfaceSystemCard; retained card identity and PropertyUsageReceipt in per-interface flux reports; deterministic series budgets with conservative half-width propagation, explicit unknowns, and finite-overflow refusal; typed missing-card, missing-binding, and changed-mesh refusals; Level-A two-slab result R_total=0.30000000000000004 K/W, max nodal error 1.393e-11 K, heat rate approximately 100 W. Final RCH lane: cargo test --locked -p fs-conduction --all-targets, 46/46 passed on vmi1149989. Bead remains in progress: fs-scenario interface-object auto-lowering, contact-dominance attribution/error-budget corpus, broader property/e2e stack coverage, variable/nonmatching laws, and retained registry authority are not implemented.

CLOSE AUDIT 2026-07-25 (NobleLion) — NOT CLOSEABLE, but the bead is HONEST.

Audited at HEAD because this bead sits in the E05 thermal cluster held by a
session dark ~48h, and I had already audited 5.2 and 5.5 the same way. I did
not edit fs-conduction.

FIRST, THE CORRECTION I OWE THIS BEAD: unlike 5.2/5.5, this is not a case of an
artifact claiming more than the code delivers at the bead level. The Notes, the
implementing commit eb0c2a8a, the CHANGELOG entry, README.md:1415 and
CONTRACT.md:576-605 ALL disclose the unimplemented scope accurately. It is a
well-scoped partial correctly parked in_progress. It should be reassigned off
the dark session, not rewritten.

CLAUSE-BY-CLAUSE

DONE-WHEN 1 "interface jumps solve correctly (analytic two-slab exact)" — MET.
  The P1 jump operator assembles the exact triangle mass matrix as signed
  A/A, B/B, A/B, B/A blocks with A/6 diagonal and A/12 off (interface.rs:
  1086-1119), matching CONTRACT.md:74. tests/contact.rs:242-254 checks every
  nodal temperature against a hand-written closed form (T = 330-10x left,
  320-10x right) to 1e-8 K. I verified the physics independently: k=10, L=1,
  A=1, R''=0.1 gives 10 K per slab, a 10 K interface jump over 30 K, flux
  100 W, total 0.3 K/W. Genuine independent solver assertion.

DONE-WHEN 2 "undeclared-interface refusal proven" — MET for the duplicated-
  geometry case, with a scope caveat. Guards at interface.rs:905-911 and
  require_no_undeclared :926-938, placed at the ASSEMBLY chokepoint
  (assemble.rs:287-291, :460-463) so every solve, Jacobian and merit
  evaluation passes through; I checked solve.rs for a bypass and there is
  none. Caveat: this only fires on geometrically coincident boundary
  triangles. A CONFORMAL (shared-vertex) joint between two materials produces
  no candidate and solves silently as perfect contact. CONTRACT.md:576-580
  scopes itself honestly to "exact coordinate-bit equality between duplicated
  boundary triangles", so the contract is not overstating — but the bead's
  WHAT clause (c) promised a broader fail-closed default that does not exist.

DONE-WHEN 3 "uncertainty from interface cards propagates into QoI budgets" —
  PARTIAL, closer to NOT MET. The algebra works and is honest:
  term_for_area (interface.rs:210-250), SeriesThermalResistance::new
  (:469-529) sums stated half-widths with a confidence floor and keeps
  Unstated terms as an explicit unbounded list; tests/contact.rs:366-376
  proves Unstated never collapses to zero. But it never reaches a QoI.
  InterfaceFlux (:1123-1139) — the ONLY interface artifact the report emits
  (solve.rs:392-393) — has no uncertainty field at all, and ConductionReport
  (solve.rs:375-400) has no uncertainty budget of any kind. The series budget
  in tests/contact.rs:273-310 is assembled BY THE TEST from test-declared
  literals. A resistance budget the caller builds themselves is not
  "uncertainty propagates into QoI budgets".

DONE-WHEN 4 "corpus contact-dominated case attributes correctly" — NOT MET.
  The registry row exists (fs-vvreg/src/adversarial.rs:679-690, case
  contact-dominated-two-layer-stack, expected_dominant_uncertainty =
  ContactResistance), but AdversarialRegistry::assess takes the verdict as a
  CALLER-SUPPLIED argument (fs-vvreg/tests/adversarial.rs:202-207 hands it
  ContactResistance directly). Nothing derives attribution from a solve, and
  fs-conduction never touches the adversarial registry: grep for "adversarial"
  in crates/fs-conduction returns one unrelated comment. There is no
  attribution machinery to be correct or incorrect.

WHAT (c) scenario binding — NOT MET. fs-scenario has first-class
  EntityKind::Interface with InterfacePair ordering (entity.rs:288-330,
  428-430), but grep for card|matdb|resistance in that file returns ZERO

  exists for an interface with no declared card. CONTRACT.md:583-585 says so.

TESTS: "jump-condition assembly vs analytic two-slab" MET. "card-provenance

  claim set; :267-271 proves the reported flux carries the same identity).
  "refusal naming the interface" PARTIAL — the missing-card half asserts

DEFECTS FILED: frankensim-joikk (5 verified claim-integrity defects inside the
implemented slice — CONTRACT invariant 9 citing 13 unexercised branches; two

title: Surface radiation: linearized surface-to-ambient + gray-diffuse enclosure exchange
description:
WHY: At low flow rates and in sealed enclosures, radiation carries a large share of heat (the adversarial radiation-dominated cases exist precisely because convection-only models fail there). Omitting radiation is textbook omitted-physics model-form error — exactly accuracy-hierarchy level 4.

WHAT: Two rungs, each with model cards: (a) linearized surface-to-ambient radiation h_rad = 4*eps*sigma*T_m^3 folded into Robin coefficients (valid for small delta-T; validity domain encodes the linearization bound and the model card carries the linearization error as discrepancy); (b) gray-diffuse enclosure exchange: view-factor computation for the enclosure fixture geometry (closed-form factors for the standard configurations first; Monte Carlo/QMC view factors via fs-rand as the general path with sampling-error evidence), radiosity system solve coupled to the conduction solver's surface temperatures (outer fixed-point with declared convergence criterion). Emissivities from fs-matdb with uncertainty (emissivity is notoriously uncertain — the card must say so; surface-finish state matters, tying to materials-as-manufactured-states in e17). Nonlinearity handled by the same globalization discipline as k(T).

DONE WHEN: closed-form view-factor cases exact; radiosity solve passes an analytic two-surface enclosure; linearized-vs-full discrepancy measured on the fixture and recorded as the linearized rung's discrepancy evidence (a real e10 fidelity-graph edge); energy balance closes (radiative + convective + conducted = source) within stated tolerance.

TESTS: unit (view-factor reciprocity A_i F_ij = A_j F_ji and summation-to-one properties as G0 laws; QMC view-factor convergence with seeded determinism); analytic enclosure battery; e2e radiation-dominated fixture logging per-surface radiosity, view-factor row sums, energy-balance closure, and rung-discrepancy measurement.
acceptance_criteria: Implement both linearized surface-to-ambient radiation and gray-diffuse enclosure exchange with explicit emissivity, area, view factors, temperatures, environment, linearization point, units, and validity regime. Unit tests verify Stefan-Boltzmann limits, reciprocity and summation rules, enclosure balance, Jacobians, and linearization error accounting; boundary tests cover emissivity zero and one, equal temperatures, tiny areas, open environments, near-zero absolute temperature, extreme temperatures, disconnected surfaces, and invalid view factors. Property tests enforce nonnegative entropy-compatible heat flow and global energy balance; metamorphic tests cover surface subdivision, permutation, consistent unit conversion, and enclosure rotation; mutants that drop the fourth power, reverse sign, violate reciprocity, or omit linearization discrepancy must be detected. Singular systems, malformed geometry, cancellation, iteration deadline, memory cap, oversized enclosures, and logging faults must fail without verified flux. This Bead contributes immutable radiation cases and balance ledgers to scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh with bounded structured logs and replay. The configured DSR lane must pass; gray-diffuse assumptions and linearized validity remain explicit no-claim boundaries.
notes: Code-first checkpoint implemented in fs-conduction: material-card-backed hemispherical-total emissivity with exact receipt and uncertainty; validity-bounded linearized surface-to-ambient Robin row with measured full-T4 discrepancy; admitted analytic/external-QMC view-factor matrices with explicit seed/sample/generator metadata, row closure, reciprocity, and stable identity; deterministic gray-diffuse radiosity; mesh-bound P1 radiation surfaces; and budgeted outer fixed-point coupling through uniform frozen fluxes on explicit adiabatic remainder faces. Level-A thermal-a-parallel-plate-view-factor now has an executing test-time binding, raising aggregate coverage to 15/19. Stable remote proof at b3b5f2c1c809eec06cde1e40cbc916d6995469b5: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --no-self-healing -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=RCH_TARGET_BASE/rch_target_frankensim_test cargo test --locked -p fs-conduction --all-targets; 53/53 passed on vmi1149989, 632.1s total. README, CONTRACT, MODEL_CARD, and additive CHANGELOG now state the exact scope. Bead deliberately remains IN_PROGRESS: no internal geometry/QMC ray generator or convergence/error evidence, no radiation-dominated retained e2e corpus fixture, no participating-media/spectral/specular/spatially varying surface model, no nonlinear uncertainty certificate, no radiation adjoint, and no retained registry/L4 authority.

comments.text:
CLOSE AUDIT 2026-07-26 (NobleLion) — NOT CLOSEABLE, and the bead already says so.

Completes my audit of the E05 thermal cluster (5.2, 5.5, 5.3 previously). I did
not edit fs-conduction.

FRAMING FIRST, because it is the fair one: like 5.3 and unlike 5.2/5.5, this
bead does NOT overclaim at the scope level. Its Notes end with an explicit
non-delivery list; commit 831d2e59 says "Keep the bead open"; and
CHANGELOG.md:302-305, CONTRACT.md:574-588, MODEL_CARD.md:60-63/110-117/134-136
and README.md:1406 each independently restate the same non-claims. fs-vvreg took
no authority: the manifest row is still reference-only and vv-scorecard reports
the view-factor cell NO-DATA. The defects below are one layer down — five of its
six tests assert something weaker than the prose around them.

CLAUSE-BY-CLAUSE

DONE-WHEN 1 "closed-form view-factor cases exact" — PARTIAL. There is exactly
  ONE case and its body is a hardcoded literal: infinite_parallel_plates
  (radiation.rs:533-545) writes vec![vec![0.0,1.0],vec![1.0,0.0]]. "Exact" is
  vacuous because no closed form is evaluated — F12 = 1 is written down, not
  computed. No second configuration factor exists anywhere (no coaxial disks,
  perpendicular or aligned rectangles, sphere-in-sphere). The plural is unmet.

DONE-WHEN 2 "radiosity solve passes an analytic two-surface enclosure" — MET,
  and genuinely earned. tests/radiation.rs:233-237 checks net_outward_flux
  against sigma(T1^4-T2^4)/(1/e1+1/e2-1) at 2e-13 relative. The code assembles
  and eliminates (I-(1-eps)F)J = eps*sigma*T^4 (radiation.rs:881-901) and never
  forms that expression, so it is a real independent oracle. The CHANGELOG's
  517.7298382565217 W/m^2 reproduces by hand.

DONE-WHEN 3 "linearized-vs-full discrepancy measured and recorded as a real e10
  fidelity-graph edge" — PARTIAL. The measurement is correct
  (radiation.rs:319-322,337) and MODEL_CARD.md:134 correctly calls it "not a
  global model-form band". But inside this bead's battery the only assertion is
  discrepancy_w_m2 > 0.0 (tests/radiation.rs:128), strictly implied by :119-127
  already pinning the two numbers apart. The actual fidelity-graph edge lives in
  ANOTHER bead's test (fs-plan/tests/fidelity_campaign.rs:165-218, f85xj.10.2).
  Nothing in fs-conduction retains an e10 edge artifact.

DONE-WHEN 4 "energy balance closes (radiative + convective + conducted = source)"
  — NOT MET, three independent reasons. (a) No convective term exists in any
  radiation test; no radiation fixture builds a Robin row, so robin_out_w is
  identically 0 in both solves. (b) relative_energy_closure() is structurally
  zero in every fixture used: for F = [[0,1],[1,0]] the irradiation loop gives
  G0 = J1, G1 = J0 exactly, so net fluxes are IEEE-exact negations and heat_sum
  is exactly 0.0 — the assertions at :238 and :335 are unconditionally true.
  (c) coupled_energy_closure is a LINEAR SOLVER RESIDUAL: solve.rs:305-313
  documents closure_w as measuring "how well the linear solves closed the
  balance, not whether the boundary data itself is right", and neumann_out_w is
  post-integrated from the same uniform flux field assembled into the load, so
  it cancels by construction. EXECUTED REPRO: scale the overlay flux at
  radiation.rs:1096 by 2.0 — the fixed point still converges, both sign checks
  still hold, both closures still pass.

TESTS 1 "view-factor reciprocity and summation-to-one as G0 laws" — PARTIAL.
  Reciprocity has a real negative test (:172-183, a [[0,1],[0.9,0.1]] matrix
  that refuses). SUMMATION-TO-ONE HAS NO TEST — neither a refusal for a
  non-closing matrix nor a surviving positive check. The two apparent row-sum
  assertions (:163, :164) are strictly implied by admission, since
  infinite_parallel_plates passes row_sum_abs: 0.0 and reciprocity_rel: 0.0.

TESTS 2 "QMC view-factor convergence with seeded determinism" — NOT MET,
  self-disclosed. Only metadata admission exists (ExternalQmc seed/samples/
  generator with a blank/zero refusal, radiation.rs:437-445). CONTRACT.md:574-577
  says so plainly.

TESTS 3 "analytic enclosure battery" — PARTIAL. One case, not a battery.
  Consequence: no test ever builds n >= 3, so solve_dense's row-swap branch
  (radiation.rs:1200-1203) and the multi-term back-substitution (:1216-1221) are
  never exercised — at n = 2 the pivot is always |1| vs |-(1-eps)| <= 0.4.

TESTS 4 "e2e radiation-dominated fixture logging per-surface radiosity, row
  sums, closure, and rung discrepancy" — NOT MET, self-disclosed. The coupled
  test's JSON line (:339-345) logs outer iterations, surface update, one heat
  rate and the closure — not per-surface radiosity, not row sums, not the
  discrepancy. Nothing establishes the fixture is radiation-dominated.

WHAT-scope: "emissivities from fs-matdb with uncertainty" MET (radiation.rs:
  100-157, receipts and UncertaintyModel preserved, Unstated kept explicit).
  "(a) folded into Robin coefficients" PARTIAL — LinearizedRadiationPoint.boundary
  is a real ThermalBc::Robin (:333) but NO test in fs-conduction ever puts it
  into a conduction solve; :141 only asserts matches!(.., Robin { .. }).
  "nonlinearity handled by the same globalization discipline as k(T)" NOT MET —
  k(T) uses FixedPoint with relaxation, max_backtracks and a line search; the
  radiation outer loop (:1086-1144) is fixed under-relaxation with no merit
  function and no backtracking. CONTRACT.md:102 discloses it as "budgeted,
  under-relaxed", so it is disclosed but it is not the same discipline.

DEFECTS FILED, both wired as blockers:
  frankensim-h71xu — test authority: the energy-closure assertion is an IEEE
    identity; the coupled solve pins no radiative magnitude (overlay x2 repro);
    emissivity_query_... runs no query; the Level-A binding is literal-vs-equal-
    literal and is the only one of 19 whose executing kernel does zero
    arithmetic; plus the analytic answer the coupled fixture already has
    available and does not assert.
  frankensim-k0u26 — ~29 refusal branches with claimed evidence that no test
    reaches (including the three named in prose: singular radiosity pivot,
    exhausted outer budget, overlay on an occupied row); max_abs_departure_k is
    a caller assertion not a bound (executed repro returns a 1000x error and
    refuses nothing); the emissivity card domain is never checked at the SOLVED
    temperature (cards queried at 350 K while surfaces converge across 300-400 K);
    the isothermal-surface <T>^4-vs-<T^4> substitution is undocumented; and two
    fixtures with geometrically false view factors are filed as G2 canonical
    benchmarks.

VERIFIED SOUND, so nobody re-audits: the radiosity assembly and its independent
analytic validation; linear_residual_max_w_m2 is a TRUE residual (the matrix is
copied at :1170 so it is measured against the original operator, not the
LU-modified one); view-factor admission genuinely validates the supplied matrix
including row closure and area-weighted reciprocity with no divide-by-zero;
GrayDiffuseEnclosure::new's cross-checks (mesh identity, unique names, disjoint
slots, matrix-area vs mesh-area to 1e-12) — that last one catches the realistic
failure mode; mean_temperature is exactly the area average of a P1 field;
mesh binding is fail-closed under a domain-separated BLAKE3 tag and tested; the
boundary overlay is fail-closed and clones the base each iteration so overlays
cannot accumulate, with the sign convention chaining correctly; determinism
mechanics match the stated class (no RNG, strict-> partial pivoting so ties keep
the lowest row); emissivity plumbing is complete and honest with Unstated
preserved; first-order uncertainty propagation is exact for the linear
h_rad ∝ eps dependence; cancellation is wired at three named stages; and the
outer fixed point's stopping rule is honest — it compares against the
temperature that DROVE the radiosity solve (the correct fixed-point residual,
not a step-size proxy) and budget exhaustion is a typed refusal.

title: Fan curve + flow network model: operating-point solve for enclosure airflow (P-Q curves, vents, leakage)
description:
WHY: The correlation rung needs velocities/flow rates; in electronics enclosures those come from fan pressure-flow curves intersected with system resistance — a lumped flow-network problem, not CFD. This is the cheapest credible airflow model and a hard prerequisite for any forced-convection prediction. Fan stall and vent leakage are first-class UNCERTAINTY sources here (both are e04 adversarial regimes).

WHAT: (a) Fan model: P-Q curve as typed data (fs-qty Pa vs m^3/s) with manufacturer-tolerance uncertainty band and validity (operating-range) domain; affinity-law scaling for RPM with its own validity note; stall region explicitly marked NON-ADMISSIBLE (operating points in stall REFUSE with diagnostics, not extrapolate); (b) system resistance: series/parallel network of loss elements (vents, filters, heatsink channels, sudden expansions) with loss coefficients from correlations carrying uncertainty; vent leakage as an EXPLICIT uncertain element (never implicit); (c) operating-point solve: deterministic robust intersection of fan curve and system curve (bracketed root via fs-ivl newton machinery — a certified bracket is cheap here and eliminates a wrong-root class), multi-fan series/parallel composition; (d) output: per-branch flow rates + velocities feeding E05_2 correlations, with the full uncertainty (fan tolerance + loss-coefficient + leakage) attached for e08 budget propagation.

DONE WHEN: operating points certified-bracketed on the reference fan+enclosure; stall refusal proven; leakage uncertainty propagates to QoI budgets; network solve deterministic across thread counts.

TESTS: unit (curve interpolation typed + monotone-segment validation; network assembly laws — series/parallel composition identities as G0; stall refusal); certified-bracket property test (root enclosure contains sign change); e2e: enclosure network at three fan speeds logging curves, intersection brackets, per-branch flows, leakage sensitivity, and the handoff record to the correlation rung.
notes: Implemented the code-first fs-airflow rung: typed monotone P-Q curves; explicit tolerance authority, speed domain, and stall refusal; identical series/parallel fan laws; recursive quadratic series/parallel loss networks with mandatory explicit leakage; deterministic interval-Newton nominal-root certificate; Estimate-only physical bands and branch flows; typed velocity/Reynolds handoff to fs-convection; and complete semantic provenance binding curve/source/tolerance/bank/network/leakage identity. Exact proof: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --no-self-healing -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${RCH_TARGET_BASE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/rch_target_frankensim_test" cargo test -p fs-airflow --all-targets => PASS, 9 passed, 0 failed on ovh-a (job j-29943194691043331, 2026-07-22 21:02:39Z); fs-airflow warning-clean, with only pre-existing dependency warnings. rustfmt --check, git diff --check, jq inventory parse passed; ubs found 0 critical issues. README reality now says 138 native/139 total crates, 139 contracts, 520 integration-test files, L3=27 and states the no-claim boundary. CHANGELOG has additive validation, convection, and airflow entries. KEEP IN_PROGRESS: retained fan/loss fixtures and tolerance allowances are synthetic, not manufacturer data; no retained manufacturer curve/tolerance corpus, no unequal-fan or installation-effects model, no external/CFD/experimental validation, no evidence-budget handoff into E05.10 QoIs, and no retained thread-count/replay artifact. Only the nominal declared mathematical root is Certified; physical bands remain Estimate.

comments.text:
CLOSE AUDIT 2026-07-25 (NobleLion) — DO NOT CLOSE. Clause 4 flatly unmet.

Audited at HEAD for the same reason as 5.2: 5.7 sits behind it. I did not edit
fs-airflow; this bead is assigned to IndigoElk. Tests do pass: 20/20 (9
conformance + 11 qoi; zero in-src unit tests).

CLAUSE-BY-CLAUSE

1. "operating points certified-bracketed on the reference fan+enclosure" —
   PARTIAL. The certificate is genuine, not decorative: certified_root drives
   fs_ivl::newton_roots_bounded and REFUSES anything short of uniqueness
   (certified.len() != 1 || possible != 0 -> UncertifiedOperatingPoint). Three
   gaps. (a) It certifies the NOMINAL model root only; the tolerance corners
   are solved and then downgraded to Estimate, which the CONTRACT does
   disclose. (b) The certificate is INERT — nominal_root is consumed in exactly
   one place, hashing its two endpoints, and never becomes Certified evidence
   anywhere. (c) There is no reference fan+enclosure: both fixtures are
   hand-written and self-declare "not manufacturer performance data".
   The bead's own TESTS clause asked for a certified-bracket PROPERTY test;
   there is one fixed-fixture test and its sign-change assertion is
   slack-tolerant (>= -1e-8 / <= 1e-8) rather than strict.

2. "stall refusal proven" — PARTIAL, and structurally so. The refusal path is
   real and tested. But stall is never DETECTED; it is the caller-supplied
   scalar admissible_min_flow, and the test concedes it by name
   (declared_stall_region_refuses). Worse: Invariant 1 requires pressure to be
   non-increasing, so a real axial-fan curve — whose stall region IS the
   non-monotone dip — would be REFUSED AS MALFORMED at construction. Stall
   cannot be detected from a real curve even in principle here. Two smaller
   points: the stall gate is a midpoint float compare guarding an
   interval-certified root, so a marginal root can slip through; and a
   tolerance corner falling into stall surfaces as UncertifiedOperatingPoint,
   not StallRegion — the tolerance-driven case is exactly the interesting one
   and it is misattributed.

3. "leakage uncertainty propagates to QoI budgets" — PARTIAL. The path closes
   in code and I traced it end to end: EnclosureNetwork::new -> equivalent_scalar
   -> resistance corners -> flow/pressure bands -> pressure_half_width and
   boundary_half_width -> the BoundaryConditions term of the pressure-drop and
   fan-input-power budgets. But NO TEST EXECUTES IT. The leakage test varies
   leakage RESISTANCE, not uncertainty, and builds no QoI; the budget
   monotonicity test HAND-MUTATES already-solved bands instead of re-solving.
   The one-line test that would close this clause — bump leakage
   uncertainty_rel 0.25 -> 0.40, re-solve, assert the BoundaryConditions bound
   grew — does not exist. It also reaches only 2 of 7 budgets and contributes
   nothing to thermal margin, the decision QoI; every budget TOTAL is Unknown;
   and leakage is unattributable because network_rel is a flat sum and every
   SensitivitySummary is default().

4. "network solve deterministic across thread counts" — NOT MET, no artifact
   of any kind. Zero thread|rayon|spawn|available_parallelism hits in the
   crate. The only candidate,
   three_speed_points_follow_affinity_and_solve_deterministically, runs three
   DIFFERENT inputs once each and asserts only that the flows are ordered. It
   does not vary thread count, does not repeat a run, does not compare bits.
   The solver is single-threaded straight-line scalar code so it is very likely
   invariant — but "likely invariant by inspection" is not the proof artifact
   this clause asks for.

title: PCB anisotropic effective conductivity: layer homogenization with bounds and provenance
description:
WHY: A PCB is a laminate of copper planes and dielectric; modeling it as isotropic FR4 misses in-plane conduction by an order of magnitude, and resolving every copper layer is wasteful at the vertical's fidelity target. Layer homogenization (series/parallel rules per direction from stackup + copper coverage) is standard practice with KNOWN bounds — ideal for evidence-carrying implementation.

WHAT: (a) Stackup model: layer thicknesses, materials (fs-matdb cards), per-layer copper coverage fractions (from design data or declared estimates WITH uncertainty); (b) effective-conductivity computation: parallel rule in-plane, series rule through-plane, yielding an anisotropic tensor for E05_1; Voigt/Reuss-style bounds retained as the rigorous envelope (the point estimate travels WITH its bounds — downstream may choose the conservative bound for margin-critical decisions); (c) coverage-fraction uncertainty propagates to tensor uncertainty (correlated across directions — a correlated block, exercising e08's representation requirements); (d) validity notes: vias/thermal-via arrays as a correction model with its own card [stretch: explicit via-array effective model]; homogenization validity domain (feature-size vs board-thickness separation) declared.

DONE WHEN: effective tensors for reference stackups match hand calculations exactly; bounds bracket the estimate; uncertainty propagates into a board-level conduction solve; via-correction stretch either lands with a card or is recorded as an explicit no-claim.

TESTS: unit (series/parallel rules vs hand values; bound ordering Reuss <= estimate <= Voigt as an invariant; degenerate stackups — single layer, zero coverage); property (tensor symmetry, rotation behavior under stackup frame changes); e2e: reference PCB solved isotropic-vs-homogenized logging the QoI delta (the demonstrated order-of-magnitude in-plane effect) and the bound-bracketed budget entry.
acceptance_criteria: Implement PCB effective-conductivity cards that preserve layer stack, copper fraction and orientation, dielectric properties, vias or declared omissions, temperature dependence, uncertainty, homogenization rule, bounds, and source provenance instead of collapsing every board to an unexplained scalar. Unit tests verify through-plane and in-plane tensors, laminate limits, rotation, units, sensitivities, and bound propagation; boundary cases include zero and full copper fraction, a single layer, vanishing layer thickness, extreme anisotropy, missing orientation, and invalid material data. Property tests require positive-semidefinite tensors and mixture-bound containment; metamorphic tests cover layer splitting, repeated unit cells, coordinate rotation, and layer permutation only when mathematically invariant; mutants that isotropize, transpose axes, drop a layer, or shrink bounds must fail. Malformed stacks, overflow, cancellation, deadline, allocation cap, huge layer counts, and output failures must refuse with bounded diagnostics. This Bead contributes immutable PCB cards and tensor-oracle cases to scripts/ci/thermal_qoi_producer_e2e.sh with deterministic replay. The configured DSR gate must pass; homogenized agreement supports only the declared scale and regime, not trace-level or manufacturing-specific validation.

title: Conjugate coupling: solid conduction <-> airflow/correlation rung via fs-couple ports; real CHT ladder transfers
description:
WHY: This is the seam that makes the vertical CONJUGATE: solid conduction (E05_1) and the airflow/convection path (E05_5 flows -> E05_2 h values) must exchange consistent interface conditions with conservation accounting, and fs-ladder's cht() must finally carry REAL transfer operators instead of the Refine1d placeholder that the wedge's KernelMaturity score falsely presumed. fs-couple already provides the port/conservation-role algebra (BoundaryTemperatureReference at src/lib.rs:2920, and the heat port PortKind::ThermalTemperatureEntropy at src/lib.rs:72) — use it, do not invent a parallel mechanism.

WHAT: (a) Partitioned coupling loop: conduction solve produces surface T; airflow rung produces per-surface h and local air reference temperatures (stream-wise air heating along channels via a 1-D thermal-network air path — air temperature rise is NOT negligible in enclosures); iterate to consistency with a declared fixed-point criterion and (if needed) Aitken acceleration from fs-couple (see CORRECTION below: Aitken is scalar-only and IQN-ILS does not exist); (b) conservation audit: interface heat flux balance (solid out = air in per surface) recorded as a G0-style invariant with tolerance, reported in evidence; (c) fs-ladder cht() v2: the correlation rung becomes this coupled solve; transfers between correlation and (future) RANS rung defined over the REAL state (surface T + flow-network state <-> field state), replacing Refine1d; relative_cost hints updated from measured runs (fs-plan CostModel); (d) coupling loop is cancellation-correct and resumable (each outer iteration a checkpoint boundary).

DONE WHEN: coupled enclosure fixture converges with logged iteration history; flux-balance invariant holds; fs-ladder cht() constructs the real rung; fs-wedge KernelMaturity justification updated to match code (closing the E01 overstatement).

TESTS: unit (port wiring type checks; air-path 1-D network vs analytic heated-channel solution; flux-balance computation); convergence battery (loop converges on stiff cases or refuses with diagnosis — no silent max-iter answer: hitting max-iter without criterion = typed non-convergence result); G4 cancel/resume mid-coupling drill; e2e: full fixture logging outer-iteration residuals, flux balances per surface, acceleration behavior, and final evidence assembly.

CORRECTION (CloudyFinch, 2026-07-25, verified against source at HEAD; this bead
previously instructed the implementer to use machinery that was never built):

1. IQN-ILS DOES NOT EXIST. `grep -rniE 'iqn|quasi.?newton' crates/fs-couple/src/`
   returns ZERO hits. The only occurrence in the crate is the explicit staged
   no-claim at fs-couple/CONTRACT.md:290 ("the vector INTERFACE QUASI-NEWTON
   (IQN-ILS) accelerator and MULTIRATE co-simulation are staged"), and it is
   blocker B9 in COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_EXTEND_FRANKENSIM_TO_NEW_DOMAINS.md.
   Building it is separate scope, not a call into an existing API.

2. AITKEN IS SCALAR ONLY. `AitkenRelaxation` (src/lib.rs:5803) holds three f64s
   and its whole interface is `next_omega(&mut self, residual: f64) -> f64`.
   It is a scalar delta-squared relaxer, not a vector interface accelerator.

3. THERE IS NO COUPLING LOOP DRIVER IN fs-couple AT ALL. The only iteration
   entry points are `iterate_fixed_relaxation` / `iterate_aitken`, both
   hardwired to the PRIVATE added-mass fixture map
   `interface_map(mu, c, x) = -mu*x + c` (src/lib.rs:5852). There is no
   caller-supplied residual callback, no vector state, and no subsystem trait.
   fs-couple/CONTRACT.md:353-354 assigns the driver to the consumer: "the energy
   audit's balances are supplied by the caller each exchange; wiring them onto
   the ledger is the coupling driver's integration." So this bead OWNS writing
   the driver; it cannot call one.

4. THERE IS NO `EntropyTransfer` PORT TYPE. The heat port is
   `PortKind::ThermalTemperatureEntropy`. The only `EntropyTransfer` symbol in
   the repo is `WindowBalanceLaw::InternalEntropyTransfer` (src/lib.rs:4251),
   which is a balance law, not a port. Useful corollary: the thermal kind IS one
   of the three legacy scalar seeds (`is_legacy_scalar_seed`, src/lib.rs:85), so
   `ConservativeJunction` / `interconnect_scalar` do admit thermal ports rather
   than refusing with `LegacyInterconnectRequiresSeedKind`.

SOLID-SIDE PREREQUISITE NOW LANDED (frankensim-xcbm1, commit 11dec4a4): clause
(b)'s per-surface flux balance previously had no solid-side number to balance
against — ConductionReport exposed only the whole-domain EnergyBalance::
robin_out_w. It now carries `robin_fluxes: Vec<RobinFlux>`, one row per declared
Robin region (faces, area_m2, area-weighted mean htc / wall temperature /
reference temperature, and the integrated heat_rate_w, positive = leaving the
solid), plus `ThermalBoundary::region_for(slot)`. Two traps measured while
building it: (i) a purely-Robin domain has no Dirichlet row pinning it and
reaches only ~1e-12 relative Krylov residual, so a 1e-14 linear tolerance
returns LinearSolveFailed — the conjugate fixture will be exactly this shape;
(ii) `mean_htc * area * (mean_wall - mean_ref)` is NOT `heat_rate_w` unless h is
uniform over the region, and it coincides in exactly the uniform-h case a single
correlation card produces, which is what makes the trap quiet.

AIR-PATH DESIGN NOTE: use the exponential segment law, not an arithmetic mean.
Per segment with wall temp T_w, coefficient h, area A and mdot*cp:
  NTU = hA/(mdot*cp); eps = 1 - exp(-NTU)
  Q = mdot*cp*(T_w - T_in)*eps
  T_ref_eff = T_w - (T_w - T_in)*eps/NTU     [makes h*A*(T_w - T_ref_eff) == Q]
This is unconditionally bounded in [T_in, T_w]; the arithmetic-mean reference
goes non-physical past NTU ~ 2 and destabilises the outer fixed point. It also
supplies a free exact falsifier for clause (a): since exp(-NTU) =
(exp(-NTU/N))^N, splitting one uniform-wall channel into N segments must give
the SAME outlet temperature for every N (segment-refinement invariance). An
arithmetic-mean model fails that with clean N-dependence.

WARNING ON CLAUSE (b): once T_ref_eff is defined as above, the per-surface flux
balance is an ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY (Sum_f h*A_f*(T_f - T_ref) = h*A*(T_w - T_ref)
for uniform h). It falsifies WIRING — dropped face, wrong region, wrong mdot —
not physics, and the test must say so rather than reading as a conservation
proof. The non-identity cross-check is Sum_j Q_air,j against
report.energy.robin_out_w, which fs-conduction computes in its own loop.

title: Low-Re forced-convection RANS rung [F] (gated on wedge ratification; honest fidelity-graph entry)

This is [F] frontier work with real model-form controversy, hence gated on wedge ratification and explicitly a fidelity-GRAPH node (e10), not an automatic authority upgrade over a validated correlation.

comments.text:
Landed dc0d7a31. DONE-WHEN audited item by item, with two NOW-bucket items explicitly descoped and filed rather than quietly dropped.

DONE-WHEN:
- "power maps drive E05_1 solves with provenance" - MET. PowerMap::volumetric_source returns the nodal W/m^3 field the operator consumes plus the retained PowerAudit, computed from THAT SAME field so the reported delivered power is what the solve receives rather than a parallel estimate. A test drives a real solve through it.
- "total-power audit refuses mismatched declarations" - MET, with the per-component table inside the refusal message as the bead required. The test asserts both totals and both component names appear.
- "staging record merged into CONTRACT/no-claim sections" - MET. The CONTRACT now records steady-state-only as a STAGING DECISION with named follow-on beads, rather than as a bare absence.
- "follow-on transient beads exist with correct dependencies" - MET: 5.11 (method-of-lines + checkpointed transient adjoint), 5.12 (duty-cycle drivers, blocks-on 5.11), 5.13 (lumped reduced rung, blocks-on 5.11); all three related to this bead.

THE DESIGN DECISION worth retaining: delivered power is EXACT, not approximate. Summing the exact P1 element load over a gives V/4 * sum_b f_b, so delivered power is sum_a f_a w_a with the lumped nodal volume w_a = (1/4) sum_{e ∋ a} V_e. Distributing a component's watts by those same weights makes delivered == declared IDENTICALLY, at every mesh resolution - pinned at 1e-12 and, importantly, invariant across n = 2..5. If it were an approximation that test would converge with h. The rejected alternative (per-element density smeared to nodes) loses power wherever an element is shared at a component boundary, and the loss is invisible because it looks exactly like discretization error.

Superposition is admitted and still exact (the delivered functional is linear in f), so overlapping dies under one spreader work. A duplicated vertex binding collapses at admission, because it would otherwise take a double share while the totals still balanced.

Cross-check rather than self-consistency: a whole-domain map is the same physics as ScalarField::Uniform(P/V), so the test SOLVES both and compares nodal temperatures at 1e-9, pinning the new path to the crate's existing independently-tested source path.

DESCOPED FROM THE BEAD'S "(a) NOW" BUCKET - stating this plainly because the bead listed both:
1. SURFACE heat-source maps. Filed as f85xj.5.14. Not difficulty avoidance: a surface source belongs on the Neumann path with its own lumped nodal AREA s_a = (1/3) sum_{f ∋ a} A_f and must compose with the boundary PARTITION (refusing a face that already carries a Dirichlet/Robin condition). The bead records the exact arithmetic so the successor does not re-derive it, and the CONTRACT explicitly forbids the tempting wrong shortcut of binding a surface component to adjacent volume vertices - that puts the heat in the solid and would still pass the volumetric audit.
2. Tabular power-map INGESTION via the fs-io quarantine path. Filed as f85xj.11.7 against E11, where the IO boundary lives. fs-conduction takes no fs-io dependency by design: file parsing is a quarantine concern, not a physics one. The crate validates what it is handed and asserts nothing about the file it came from.

Both are architectural boundaries with reasons, and both are now CONTRACT no-claims rather than silent gaps.

ALSO NOT DONE: the bead's TESTS line mentions a "reference board power map -> solve -> logged source audit + QoI summary" e2e and a staged-path lint. The solve and the logged audit exist; the QoI summary half pairs naturally with f85xj.5.10 (thermal QoI extraction), which is still open. The staged-path "lint" is satisfied in substance - no API here accepts a time step or thermal mass, and the CONTRACT says so - but there is no automated check enforcing that, only the absence itself.

VERIFICATION: fs-conduction 83/83 green (68 pre-existing unchanged + 15 new). clippy -D warnings --no-deps: zero findings in power.rs. ubs 0 critical. rustfmt clean. No new dependency edges.

REGISTRY, done in the same commit this time rather than deferred: doc-facts-inventory.json gains tests/power.rs (sorted position verified) and the three README doc-facts numbers move to 571. title: E06 Cooling 0.1 product workflow — target L3: one-command run plus composable validate/import/solve/report/package
description:
WHY: The README states there is no packaged end-user simulator or stable CLI; the only study runner is the photovoltaic fs-vskeleton (.fsir s-expressions, 2-D scalar Poisson). Years of elegant generic abstraction can hide the substrate gaps that only an end-to-end user path exposes. This epic ships the LEVEL-3 thin slice: one command takes a project from dirty engineering input to an auditable result with evidence. Forward prediction FIRST; optimization is deliberately NOT required for 0.1 (prove a trustworthy forward prediction before optimizing on it).

TARGET FLOW: CAD/mesh + materials + operating envelope -> quarantine and repair -> scenario admission -> deterministic solve at correlation fidelity -> convergence + uncertainty evidence -> visual results -> evidence package + engineering report.

CLI SURFACE (grow in this order): frankensim validate project.fsim; frankensim solve project.fsim; frankensim report <run>; frankensim package <run>; then compare/explain; calibrate/optimize belong to the Level-4 epic. Structured progress, cancellation, checkpoint/restart via fs-exec/fs-session semantics.

CHILDREN: versioned project schema (.fsim, Five Explicits mandatory, defaults rare+visible); CLI binary; quarantined import + region/interface assignment; material-card selection from fs-matdb; deterministic solve orchestration (sessions, budgets, cancellation); convergence-evidence automation (fs-mms ladder + order fits); parameter/BC uncertainty wiring (fs-uq); ParaView-compatible VTU field output; deterministic HTML report upgrade of fs-report; per-run evidence package (fs-package) + support/no-claim capability matrix; end-to-end acceptance test with detailed logging + failure drills; worked examples from real artifacts.

EFFORT ALLOCATION DOCTRINE (program-wide): ~70% vertical, ~20% substrate deficiencies THE VERTICAL EXPOSES, ~10% frontier research.

DONE WHEN: on a fresh machine (after constellation bootstrap), `frankensim validate && frankensim solve && frankensim report && frankensim package` runs the reference cooling project deterministically twice with identical content roots, produces an HTML report with convergence tables + error budget + evidence colors, and the e2e lane runs under DSR. Existing beads ty23 / v6dn (vertical-slice e2e gates) should be linked or absorbed rather than duplicated.

## Success Criteria

On a fresh bootstrapped machine, frankensim run <project.fsim> <ledger.db> [--resume <run-id>] and the composable validate/import/solve/report/package sequence execute the same admitted Cooling/TDA workflow through real producers and produce identical semantic run/report/package roots; repeat replay is deterministic under the declared ISA contract; detailed progress/cancellation/checkpoint/refusal evidence and DSR E2E pass; every existing child feature remains explicitly retained.

## Phase 9.5 one-command product contract

The required convenience surface is `frankensim run <project.fsim> <ledger.db> [--resume <run-id>]`. It composes the same authorities as validate, import, solve, report, and package, retains the same run identity, refuses rather than overwriting incompatible output, and produces the same semantic report/package roots as the equivalent separate sequence. This target retains field export, tested examples, post-0.1 notebook/Python policy work, and guarded post-0.1 optimization. One-command convenience never hides partial-prefix, cancellation, or no-claim state.

title: End-to-end acceptance lane: dirty input -> decision artifact, with failure drills and forensic logging
description:
WHY: This is the bead that makes "one command from dirty CAD to auditable decision" TESTABLE and keeps it true forever. E2E acceptance tests are weighted governance-level evidence (e16): a crate suite passing means little; THIS lane passing means the product works. It also feeds the primary metric (time from CAD to defensible decision) with real measurements.

WHAT: (a) The golden path e2e: from a committed dirty input set (STL with defects to repair + faceted STEP + power-map CSV + project.fsim) run validate -> solve -> report -> package on a clean environment; assert: all stages succeed, content roots match frozen goldens (golden-bump discipline applies: bumps need semantic justification), report contains required sections, package passes fs-checker, wall-clock recorded into the metrics artifact; (b) failure drills as first-class cases (fs-flagship-e2e forensic pattern): unrepairable geometry -> refusal with fixes; out-of-domain material -> validate-time refusal; budget exhaustion -> honest partial + resume; SIGINT storm -> resumable; conflicting material claims -> explicit-selection error; missing requirement -> margin QoI refuses; each drill asserts BOTH the refusal and its diagnostic quality (message names the object and the fix); (c) forensic logging: every stage emits structured JSON-lines with timings + artifact IDs; the lane archives full logs as artifacts so any failure is diagnosable from the archive alone; (d) DSR wiring: the lane is a named DSR job (dsr quality integration) and the release gate for the vertical.

title: Python bindings + notebook support: policy-gated staging (JSON/CLI path first, native bindings by ruling)
description:
WHY: The reviews list Python bindings and notebook support as required product surface ("Python and notebook bindings" in interop; "Python bindings, Notebook support" in productization) — engineers script studies and read results in notebooks, and adoption without a Python path is measurably harder. But bindings collide with the dependency doctrine: PyO3-class binding machinery is a build-time foreign dependency even though Python would be CONSUMING FrankenSim rather than FrankenSim depending on Python at runtime. That direction-of-dependency distinction must be ruled on explicitly via the e11 adapter-policy framework, not assumed.

WHAT: (a) Policy ruling first (rides e11_1's decision record): classify bindings as a DISTRIBUTION SURFACE (a separate artifact wrapping the Rust core, outside the production dependency graph — the core never links Python; the binding crate is not a workspace member of the certified build) and record the ruling with the same rigor as the adapter decision; (b) design: a thin binding layer over the PRODUCT surface only (project validate/solve/report/package + reading evidence, budgets, DecisionAssessments — NOT raw kernel access, which would bypass the evidence discipline; the binding exposes claims-with-evidence or nothing); JSON-first fallback documented (the CLI's --json mode already gives Python users a zero-binding integration path TODAY — document that pattern with worked notebook examples before any native binding lands); (c) notebook examples: worked notebooks driving the CLI/JSON path for the reference project (immediately shippable, no policy risk), upgraded to native bindings if/when they land; (d) staging: native bindings are POST-0.1 scope; the 0.1 promise is the documented JSON/CLI integration path.

description:

The program deliberately EXCLUDES optimization from Cooling 0.1 (prove a trustworthy forward prediction first — optimizing on an untrusted model launders garbage efficiently), but the capability must not be lost: this bead is the staged optimization phase, written now so its prerequisites (design-variable schema e17_8, fidelity-graph escalation e10_3, error budgets e08) are pulled in the right direction.

WHAT (staged, post-0.1, gated on the working forward workflow): (a) `frankensim compare <run-a> <run-b>`: run-level semantic diff (fs-report semantic_diff machinery over QoIs + evidence + budgets; geometry diffs via e11_4) — the manual design-iteration workflow, shipped FIRST because engineers compare before they optimize; (b) design-study mode: sweep/DOE over declared design variables (e17_8) within manufacturing constraints, each point a full evidence-carrying solve (budgeted via fs-session; fidelity per the e10 graph with e10_3 escalation), producing a ranked comparison with per-design DecisionAssessments — robustness posture honored (CVaR/worst-case over the operating envelope e17_5, via fs-robust machinery), so the ranking is by ROBUST margin, not nominal point performance; (c) gradient-based/derivative-free optimization over the same substrate (fs-ascent/fs-dfo with the existing gradient-verification gates; adjoints from the e05 thermal path where differentiable, DFO where not) — every returned optimum carries KKT/stop-reason context per the existing ASCENT doctrine plus manufacturing-constraint satisfaction receipts and a robustness certificate; (d) the anti-Goodhart guard: optimization may not exploit model error — candidate optima in regions where the model term dominates the budget trigger escalation (e10_3) or demotion before being reported as optima (this is certify-or-escalate applied to DESIGNS).

DONE WHEN: compare ships; one design study on the reference project produces a robust ranking with full evidence; one optimization run returns a certificate-carrying optimum whose model-term guard demonstrably fired at least once in testing; capability matrix updated.

title: frankensim CLI: validate/import/solve/report/package plus one-command run (deterministic, structured, cancellable)
description:
WHY: The README says it plainly: no stable end-user CLI exists. The CLI is the product surface and the thing every e2e test, user study, and demo runs. Scope discipline: validate/solve/report/package first; compare/explain next; calibrate/optimize belong to Level 4 — a forward prediction users trust precedes optimization on it.

WHAT: (a) A `frankensim` binary (workspace conventions: std arg parsing like existing bins unless a ratified decision adds a parser — keep Franken-only policy; deterministic, documented output per AGENTS.md Output Style): subcommands v0: `validate <project.fsim>` (schema + scenario validation, violations with fixes, exit codes machine-stable); `solve <project.fsim>` (runs the e05 pipeline under fs-session capability tokens + budgets, structured progress events to stderr as JSON-lines, graceful cancellation on SIGINT via Cx — request/drain/finalize, checkpoint on cancel; resumable via `solve --resume <run>`); `report <run-id>` (renders the e06 report from ledger artifacts); `package <run-id>` (emits the fs-package evidence bundle). (b) Run identity: every solve records the Five Explicits + machine fingerprint + constellation lock hash into the ledger; run IDs are content-derived; (c) `--json` mode for every subcommand (agents are first-class users); (d) stdout/stderr contract documented (results vs progress vs diagnostics) so scripts never scrape prose.

DONE WHEN: all four subcommands work on the reference project end-to-end; SIGINT mid-solve produces a resumable checkpoint + structured cancellation report (not a corrupt run); two identical solves yield identical run content roots.

TESTS: unit per subcommand (arg validation, exit codes, --json schema); G4 drills (SIGINT at assembly / mid-Newton / mid-coupling -> drained + resumable, verified by resuming to completion and comparing content root to an uninterrupted run); determinism e2e (double-solve bit-compare); log-quality gate: an agent replaying only the JSON-lines progress stream can reconstruct the run phase timeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

The CLI truthfully implements validate and admitted import, exposes solve as its authority-declared durable prefix until complete, keeps report/package typed refusals until producers land, and ultimately provides run as the artifact-equivalent convenience composition; unit parsing/admission/error/idempotency/cancellation tests and release-built subprocess E2E cover every verb/help/exit/stdout/stderr/artifact state with deterministic JSONL and no mock command registry.

## Phase 9.5 command truth and tests

Present state is explicit: validate is implemented; import is implemented within its admitted format/authority boundary; solve is a durable partial prefix whose completed stages and first typed gap come from authority; report and package parse but refuse until producers land; run is the required end-state convenience composition. Unit tests cover parsing, admission, idempotency, output collision, cancellation, resume, help, stable exit/diagnostic schemas, and every boundary/error path. A release-built subprocess E2E exercises all verbs with real files and proves run and separate verbs are artifact-equivalent, with deterministic JSONL and no fake registry.

title: Deterministic solve orchestration: session, budgets, cancellation, checkpoint/restart wired end-to-end
description:
WHY: The pieces exist separately (fs-session capability tokens + governor + metering; fs-exec Cx + versioned solver snapshots; fs-ledger session receipts) but no product path composes them. Orchestration is where the Five Explicits become enforced reality for a user run, and where cancellation/resume become user-visible features rather than crate-level contracts.

WHAT: (a) A solve pipeline driver that: opens an fs-session with capability token derived from project budgets (core-seconds, memory, wall-clock); executes stages (import-verify -> assign -> material-resolve -> flow-network -> conduction/coupling loop -> QoI extraction) each as ledgered ops with content-addressed artifacts; polls cancellation at stage and tile boundaries; meters budget consumption with warnings at declared fractions; on budget exhaustion, produces the honest partial: a structured budget-exceeded result with the completed stages' artifacts and a resume path — NEVER a partially-published answer presented as complete; (b) checkpoint/restart: stage-level checkpoints via the versioned snapshot envelope; `--resume` re-verifies input identity (project hash + constellation lock) before resuming — resuming across a changed project REFUSES; (c) deterministic replay: rerun of any run ID reproduces content roots (seeds and stream keys from the run record).

title: Convergence-evidence automation: mesh/discretization ladder with order fits as a product feature
description:
WHY: Users should not hand-build mesh-refinement studies; the product should produce discretization-error evidence automatically, because the error-budget doctrine (e08) requires a defensible discretization term for every QoI, and manual convergence studies are the first thing skipped under deadline.

WHAT: (a) An automated ladder mode: solve the project at a declared refinement ladder (2-4 levels within budget), extract QoIs per level, fit observed orders via fs-mms OrderFit, and produce: extrapolated QoI (Richardson-style where orders are clean), a discretization-error band for the budget, and an honesty verdict when the ladder is NOT in the asymptotic regime (bad order fit -> the discretization term becomes an explicit UNKNOWN-or-bounded entry, never a pretty number from a failed fit — this honesty path is the differentiating feature); (b) budget-aware laddering: the ladder respects session budgets, degrades to fewer levels with a widened band and says so; (c) DWR/goal-oriented hooks from E05_1 as the complementary single-solve estimator, cross-checked against the ladder where both exist (disagreement is diagnostic evidence, logged); (d) results feed the QoI evidence records (E05_10) and the report's convergence tables.

DONE WHEN: reference project produces per-QoI convergence tables with order fits; the non-asymptotic path demonstrably yields UNKNOWN/bounded (adversarial coarse ladder test); DWR-vs-ladder cross-check recorded.

TESTS: unit (order-fit consumption; Richardson arithmetic; degradation logic); G1 (a manufactured case where true order is known -> ladder recovers it within OrderGate tolerance); adversarial (pre-asymptotic ladder -> honest UNKNOWN, asserted); e2e: ladder run logging per-level meshes, QoIs, fit diagnostics, verdicts, and the emitted budget terms.

## Acceptance Criteria

The product accepts a versioned explicit or automatic refinement plan of 2-4 attempted rungs, but invokes fs-mms::OrderFit and Richardson extrapolation only after at least three valid completed rungs. One or two completed rungs produce a typed insufficient-ladder/UNKNOWN discretization term; they never mint a two-point order. Every rung retains project/run identity, mesh and topology identity, actual characteristic h with units, degrees of freedom, fidelity/model, solver tolerance and convergence status, QoI semantic identity/value, budget consumption, and artifact roots.

For every requested QoI, emit a deterministic convergence record containing the admitted rung subset, observed order, theoretical-order source, fit residual, asymptotic-policy version and thresholds, extrapolated value when admissible, discretization term, evidence/no-claim state, and ranked next action. Richardson output is Estimated unless an independent enclosure authorizes stronger authority. Oscillatory/non-monotone QoIs, changing model/topology, failed solves, non-finite values, unstable suffix fits, or pre-asymptotic ladders refuse extrapolation and yield UNKNOWN or an independently justified bound.

Budget degradation is explicit: skipped or unfinished rungs retain reason and checkpoint; cancellation or exhaustion leaves a resumable prefix. DWR and ladder estimates remain separate evidence objects. Agreement is recorded; disagreement beyond the declared threshold widens/demotes or escalates and is never averaged away.
