title: Parameter/BC uncertainty propagation wired into the product (sampling plans under budget, honest truncation)
description:
WHY: Accuracy-hierarchy level 3 (geometry/parameter/BC uncertainty) has good pieces (fs-uq MLMC/PCE/anytime probability; fs-rand QMC; matdb uncertainty models; fan/leakage uncertainty from e05) but no product wiring: a user declaring uncertain inputs must get QoI distributions/intervals without writing UQ code.

WHAT: (a) Uncertain inputs come from the project file: material properties (matdb uncertainty models), interface resistance, fan-curve tolerance, vent leakage, power-map tolerance, ambient range — each already typed at its source; the propagation plan is DERIVED: small input counts -> tensor/QMC sampling or PCE (fs-uq fit_pce constraints respected); expensive-with-cheap-pairs -> MLMC where a coarse rung exists (correlation vs RANS later fits MLMC's coupling contract); anytime probability estimates for threshold QoIs (P(T_j > limit)) via the confidence-sequence machinery so sampling stops when the DECISION is stable (fs-voi posture); (b) correlated inputs honored where declared (matdb JointStatistics once e07 wires them — until then, correlation-unknown is an explicit budget caveat, not an independence assumption silently applied: independence-by-default is BANNED for same-card properties); (c) outputs land in the QoI evidence statistical slice + e08 budget terms with sampling-error accounting; (d) all sampling Philox-keyed for replay.

DONE WHEN: reference project with declared uncertainties yields QoI intervals + P(compliance) deterministically; sampling-plan derivation logged and justified; the correlation-unknown caveat path proven.

TESTS: unit (plan derivation rules; refusals on invalid tolerances — fs-uq admission patterns; replay determinism); statistical validation (synthetic cases with known answers: propagated intervals match analytic propagation within tolerance; anytime stopping validity respected); e2e: full UQ run logging plan choice, sample counts, convergence of estimates, stop reason, and final budget-term emission.

## Acceptance Criteria

The product deterministically derives and records a sampling/propagation plan from typed uncertainty authorities, requested QoIs, the available fidelity graph, and budget. It distinguishes aleatory distributions, epistemic intervals/bands, statistical confidence statements, and unstated uncertainty. A half-width or confidence annotation does not silently become a probability distribution. P(compliance) is emitted only when a complete admitted probability measure and dependence model exist; otherwise the result is an explicit interval/UNKNOWN/NoClaim with a ranked data or declaration requirement.

Declared dependence is preserved in canonical variable order. Same-card properties are never assumed independent. Missing correlation refuses joint probabilistic propagation or selects only an honestly valid non-probabilistic route. Correlation matrices, marginals, units, source receipts, and applicability domains are validated; non-PSD or inconsistent declarations refuse.

Plan admission enforces method contracts: PCE requires an admitted germ family, adequate oversampling, and conditioning; QMC respects the currently supported dimension and direction-table authority; MLMC requires same-germ coarse/fine coupling and a valid telescoping hierarchy; anytime confidence sequences consume bounded indicators and a predeclared error budget. Unsupported high dimension chooses an admitted fallback or refuses; it never wraps or reuses Sobol dimensions. High-dimensional Sobol completion remains related research, not a hidden blocker.

Every result retains input semantic IDs, uncertainty/dependence authority, plan rationale and rejected alternatives, logical sample/stream identities, model/fidelity, stop reason, estimator diagnostics, sampling-error term, evidence/no-claim state, and replay roots. Budget exhaustion or cancellation returns an honest resumable partial and never a final compliance probability.

Unit tests exhaust plan selection; aleatory/epistemic/unstated classification; explicit independence versus unknown correlation; variable ordering; unit/domain validation; non-PSD and dimension mismatch refusal; zero variance; invalid/non-finite tolerances, confidence, and sample counts; PCE basis/conditioning; QMC dimension caps; MLMC coupling/telescoping/allocation; anytime-CS admission/stopping; deterministic Philox streams; error-budget emission; authority composition; resume identity; serialization; and ranked fixes. Analytic/statistical fixtures cover linear Gaussian, correlated bivariate, bounded Bernoulli, PCE, coupled MLMC, and preregistered adversarial optional stopping. Property/metamorphic tests cover variable-plus-covariance permutation, unit rescaling, zero-uncertainty collapse, worker scheduling, repeated seeds, MLMC regrouping, and cancel/resume equivalence. Fault tests cover every batch/level boundary, stale receipts, unknown correlation, out-of-domain or nonconverged samples, invalid coupling, duplicate invocation, and ledger/output failures.

scripts/e2e/cooling_uq.sh invokes the actual release-built frankensim binary, reference Cooling physics, project-declared uncertainty sources, real solver/QoIs, FrankenSQLite ledger, report/package consumers, and standalone checker. It exercises explicit correlation, zero uncertainty, correlation-unknown refusal, absent probability measure, budget truncation, out-of-domain sampling, cancel/resume, and deterministic repeat with no mocked QoIs or prebuilt success receipts.

Canonical JSONL records include schema/version, event sequence, source revision and constellation identity, run/project/QoI IDs, uncertainty kind and authority roots, canonical variable order, marginal/correlation roots, chosen plan and rejected alternatives, method parameters, logical sample/batch/level and StreamKey IDs, fidelity, solver verdict, estimator state, interval/probability/confidence bounds, counts, budget, stop reason, error-budget term, evidence/no-claim state, diagnostic code, ranked fixes, and artifact roots. Per-sample evidence is retained in bounded content-addressed artifacts; timings and host observations are separate non-authoritative rows. Focused tests, statistical acceptance bands, no-mock E2E, constellation preflight, and the named DSR lane must pass with retained artifacts before closure.

### Panic-Free Admission and Proof-State Binding

Product admission preflights every panic/assert surface before calling the current numerical APIs: empty/undersampled/ill-conditioned PCE designs, invalid Hermite basis sizes, zero or over-cap Sobol dimensions, sample counts that do not fit the current u32 point/tile identities, and malformed KL germ lengths return bounded typed refusals. The live Sobol table authorizes dimensions 1..=10 only. For KL dimensions above 10, only the documented hybrid is admitted: scrambled Sobol on the leading variance-dominant 10 modes and Philox-normal tail streams keyed by seed, kernel 0x0517, and logical sample tile; no dimension wrap/reuse or undisclosed fallback is allowed.

Seed/stream/plan identities can be byte-exact, while solver QoIs and final intervals use predeclared semantic tolerances across ISAs until actual dual-runtime G5 evidence. Immediately before and after authoritative proof, `scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --snapshot` reports identical complete root-plus-sibling content identities and unchanged `constellation.lock` identity. Evidence binds source/snapshot/toolchain/target/profile/features and DSR run/log/artifact roots and rejects cross-snapshot splicing. Focused Cargo/RCH is focused proof only.

title: ParaView-compatible field output: deterministic VTU/XDMF export of solution fields
description:
WHY: Engineers will not abandon their post-processors, and they should not have to (the interop doctrine: let users keep their tools while FrankenSim earns authority). fs-io currently WRITES legacy ASCII VTK; modern ParaView workflows want VTU (XML unstructured) and XDMF/HDF5-class layouts for larger fields. Visualization is also the fastest trust-builder: engineers believe fields they can see.

WHAT: (a) Deterministic VTU writer in fs-io's export family (write-only, like 3MF/GLB precedent): unstructured grids from the solve mesh, point/cell data for T fields, flux vectors, material/region IDs, h values on surfaces; binary-appended encoding with fixed byte order for determinism (byte-identical across runs — export is part of the replay surface); (b) XDMF-style index over heavy data as the staged second tier for large/time-series fields (transient future-proofing; keep the heavy format within Franken-only constraints — document the container decision explicitly); (c) CLI integration: `solve` emits requested fields per the project's output requests; artifacts content-addressed in the ledger like everything else; (d) round-trip verification tooling: a reader-side checksum/summary utility so tests can verify without ParaView (external ParaView validation is a documented manual step in the e2e checklist).

DONE WHEN: reference run produces VTU files that load in ParaView (manually verified once, checklist-recorded) and are byte-deterministic across replays; field values spot-match ledger QoIs at probe points.

TESTS: unit (writer against tiny hand-checked meshes — vertex order, connectivity, data alignment; encoding determinism); property (probe-point values in the file equal solver values exactly); e2e: export run logging per-field sizes, checksums, and probe comparisons; corrupted-write drill (disk-full simulation -> typed failure, no partial file presented as complete).

## Acceptance Criteria

Cooling 0.1 requires deterministic VTU output for every requested solution field. The staged XDMF/heavy-data tier is preserved and must either land here with the same proof battery or have a named linked successor plus truthful typed unavailability before closure; no requested field may be silently omitted.

The VTU writer defines a versioned canonical layout for cell types, connectivity and offsets, point/cell association, scalar/vector components, semantic names and units, byte order, header/offset widths, appended-data encoding, escaping, and array order. It validates finite coordinates and fields, indices, lengths, associations, duplicate names, component counts, and checked size/offset arithmetic before publication. Any XDMF heavy container remains inside the Franken-only production dependency policy and records exact version, byte order, offsets, dataset identities, and replay contract; no undeclared HDF5 or foreign runtime dependency is permitted.

Export is transactional. Bytes, independent summary, and ledger artifact become visible only after complete write, content addressing, and independent readback. Cancellation, short write, capacity exhaustion, or ledger failure produces a typed refusal and no complete artifact. Given identical mesh/field input bits, writer bytes are identical across runs and ISAs; this does not overclaim that all upstream solver fields are cross-ISA bit-identical.

An independently implemented reader/checker reconstructs topology, arrays, units, checksums, extrema, and probes. Field summaries/probes agree with source ledger artifacts and QoIs. A version-pinned ParaView/pvpython lane opens retained VTU/XDMF artifacts and records topology and array results; if unavailable, the verdict is explicitly not-run, never inferred from XML shape.

title: Deterministic HTML engineering report: convergence, error budget, evidence colors, sensitivities, provenance
description:
WHY: fs-report v0 renders deterministic Markdown with scalar metrics; its own contract stages HTML with embedded tables, convergence tables, error attributions, and renders. The report is what a reviewing engineer actually reads — it must carry the FULL epistemic story (colors, budgets, validity, provenance) or the architecture's honesty never reaches the human.

WHAT: (a) Extend fs-report to a deterministic HTML render (self-contained single file, embedded CSS, no external assets — reproducibility and archivability; content hash covers the bytes): sections = summary + DecisionAssessment block (e08; requirement, margin, P(compliance), flip conditions, recommended next action); QoI table with evidence colors and full error budgets (8-term when e08 lands; 3-term until then, labeled); convergence tables with order fits and honesty verdicts (from E06_6); uncertainty section (inputs, plan, distributions/intervals, stop reasons from E06_7); material/interface provenance tables (from receipts); model cards consumed + validity intersections; import/quarantine receipts; run identity (Five Explicits, machine fingerprint, constellation lock, content roots) and replay instructions; known-gaps/no-claim section AUTO-GENERATED (whatever is Estimated or UNKNOWN says so here — the report must be as loud about ignorance as about results); (b) embedded field imagery via fs-img deterministic renders [staged if needed; text-first is acceptable for 0.1]; (c) machine-readable JSON twin of every table (agents read reports too).

DONE WHEN: reference run renders byte-deterministically; every number in the report traces to a ledger artifact (spot-check tooling); the no-claim section is non-empty and honest for the 0.1 feature set.

TESTS: unit (section renderers on synthetic inputs; HTML validity; determinism); traceability test (sampled report numbers == ledger values); e2e: full render with log of every artifact consumed; adversarial: a run with failed convergence must render the failure prominently (assert the honesty path renders, not just the happy path).

## Required Tests and Logging

Unit tests cover every section and table; canonical sorting; locale/timezone independence; finite/non-finite/Unknown/NoClaim rendering; units; escaping of project/material/source text; markup/script injection; URL/path handling; resource and row-count bounds; missing/duplicate/tampered artifacts; field-image availability; deterministic CSS/HTML/JSON bytes; and stable actionable diagnostics. Schema tests guarantee the HTML and machine-readable JSON twins contain the same semantic cells and source roots. Property/metamorphic tests permute ledger insertion/request order, rescale equivalent units, weaken authority, widen uncertainty, and change feature configuration: ordering remains canonical and the report can only preserve or weaken claims. Mutation tests delete/change each provenance, budget, validity, convergence, UQ, DecisionAssessment, no-claim, and replay field and must fail traceability or render an explicit gap.

The non-vacuous naked-scalar gate scans the actual `s2l9v -> fs-report -> CLI/package` consumer path and refuses any displayed engineering value that lacks the canonical QoI/evidence root. This preserves the original `f85xj.5.10` obligation at the first boundary where a bypass can exist; `f85xj.8.7` extends it to every user-facing output.

`scripts/e2e/cooling_report.sh --profile <pr|full|recovery> --artifact-dir <path>` invokes the release-built CLI against a real completed Cooling ledger and canonical QoI/verdict, convergence, UQ, material/interface, import, field-image, and package artifacts. It renders/checks HTML and JSON twins in a clean process; independently traces sampled and boundary cells back to ledger bytes; executes failed-convergence, UNKNOWN, noncompliance, incomplete/tampered/mixed-run/stale, cancellation/write-failure, large-table, injection, deterministic-repeat, and reconstruction-without-solver cases. No synthetic success report or renderer-only self-check counts. If embedded imagery is unavailable, closure requires a named linked successor plus explicit typed unavailability; it may not disappear silently.

Canonical JSONL records schema/event sequence, source/constellation/toolchain/target/profile, run/report/section/table/cell IDs, every consumed artifact/content root, semantic QoI/evidence/requirement IDs, displayed value/units/color/no-claim state, trace verdict, render/checker versions, output roots, diagnostics/ranked fixes, and DSR run/log/artifact IDs. Volatile timing/host observations are separate and excluded from report identity; meta-tests reject missing, duplicate, reordered, cross-run/snapshot, unknown-version, and tampered rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

The real Cooling run renders byte-deterministic self-contained HTML and semantically identical JSON; every displayed engineering number traces to a canonical ledger/QoI/evidence root; DecisionAssessment, convergence honesty, uncertainty, provenance, validity, replay, known gaps, and no-claim sections are complete and cannot be silently omitted. The non-vacuous naked-scalar gate and unit/property/mutation/fault/recovery batteries pass, as does `cooling_report.sh` with its negative corpus and independent clean-process checker. Complete constellation snapshots immediately before/after proof are identical; terminal DSR run/log/artifact identities are retained. Cross-ISA report bytes are exact only for identical input artifact bytes.

title: E07 Level-4 validation program: calibration partitions, model discrepancy, blind case, external reproduction
description:
WHY: Level 3 (integrated workflow) is not Level 4 (experimentally validated workflow). The reviews' original 90-day plan conflated them; this epic owns the honest 3-9 month program whose clock STARTS ONLY when datasets and a validation partner exist (epic e04 supplies them). The schema for model-form evidence already exists (fs-evidence ModelEvidence: cards, assumptions, validity, discrepancy_rel, in_domain; DecisionStatus; EscalationAdvice) — the REAL gap is empirical population and enforcement: are discrepancy bands based on meaningful data, are validation regimes defined from retained experiments, are flagship outputs forced through the model-evidence path, are intervals empirically calibrated, do discrepancy estimates change actual decisions.

CHILDREN: typed calibration/validation partition enforcement (no leakage, laundering-proof); model-discrepancy estimation (several auditable discrepancy models — Kennedy-O'Hagan-style as ONE method, not the universal ontology, since calibration parameters and discrepancy functions can substitute for each other; require identifiability + held-out predictive checks); correlation-aware propagation of material/BC uncertainty (wire fs-matdb JointStatistics into query receipts); empirical coverage checks at product level (nominal 95% interval must contain ~95% of held-out observations, using fs-eproc Mondrian conformal + fs-surrogate empirical_coverage machinery); preregistered blind validation case execution; independent external reproduction of the full workflow.

DONE WHEN: the Cooling workflow has been calibrated on a declared partition, validated on held-out data with published coverage, survived one preregistered blind case, and been reproduced end-to-end by someone outside the authoring environment from the release bundle (epic e13). Failure of the blind case is a REPORTABLE RESULT with a scorecard entry, not something to bury.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .7.1 through .7.6 to form an auditable Level-4 chain: leakage-proof partition types, discrepancy alternatives, identifiability analysis, empirical coverage, preregistered blind execution, and independent external reproduction. The join must identify immutable calibration and validation populations, preregistration receipt, frozen metrics and tolerances, all attempted models, discrepancy-selection rationale, coverage intervals, deviations, and the external reproducer identity without disclosing the blind target before lock. The terminal owner is .7.6 for scripts/e2e/cooling_validation_l4.sh, which must replay the bundle from a clean environment with bounded structured logs and include unit, boundary, property, metamorphic, mutation, fault, cancellation, resource, and deliberate-leakage cases. E07 reaches Level 4 only after .7.5 and .7.6 independently pass the configured DSR gate; calibration fit, retrospectively selected partitions, missing negative results, or machine-generated human approval cannot promote validation status.

title: Typed calibration/validation partition enforcement (leakage-proof by construction)
description:
WHY: Calibrating and validating on the same data is the most common way simulation tools lie to themselves, and under deadline pressure it happens by accident: a dataset used to tune a discrepancy model quietly reappears in the coverage statistics. The corpus schema (e04) DECLARES partitions; this bead makes crossing them impossible rather than discouraged.

WHAT: (a) Partition-typed access: corpus queries are parameterized by purpose (Calibration | Validation | BlindEvaluation); a dataset's declared partition is checked at query time and a mismatched purpose REFUSES with a typed error naming dataset + declared partition + attempted use; (b) taint propagation: any model artifact (discrepancy model, calibrated parameter set, tuned closure constant) records the content IDs of every calibration dataset it consumed; validation/coverage computations REFUSE inputs whose taint set intersects the validation set (transitive laundering — calibrate A on X, fit B to A, validate B on X — is caught by the transitive taint closure); (c) repartitioning is a versioned corpus event with a receipt (a dataset may move calibration->validation only with justification; validation->calibration moves mark all downstream coverage claims stale); (d) the sealed blind sets (e04 Level D) are a third, stricter tier on the same machinery.

DONE WHEN: refusal + taint paths proven; a deliberate transitive-laundering attempt in tests is caught; repartition receipts recorded in the ledger; e07 coverage and blind beads build on this without exceptions.

TESTS: unit (purpose mismatch refusal per partition pair; taint-set recording; transitive closure correctness on synthetic DAGs); adversarial e2e: scripted laundering attempts (direct, transitive, repartition-then-use) each refused with full audit logging of the taint chains; determinism of taint IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce non-interchangeable calibration, validation, and blind-partition types whose constructors require immutable dataset identity, stratification rule, assignment seed or preregistered mapping, and authorization receipt; APIs that fit models must not accept validation or blind handles. Unit tests cover constructors, role-specific access, serialization, migrations, and forbidden conversions; boundary tests cover empty and singleton strata, duplicate identities, late arrivals, missing labels, and exact split thresholds. Property tests prove disjointness, completeness, and stable assignment; metamorphic tests cover row permutation and lossless file repackaging; compile-fail and runtime mutation tests attempt role erasure, handle cloning across studies, seed changes, and metadata leakage. Corruption, concurrent access, cancellation, deadline, memory cap, and oversized partition faults must preserve roles and bounded logs. This Bead contributes immutable partition manifests and deliberate-leakage fixtures to .7.6 and scripts/e2e/cooling_validation_l4.sh. The configured DSR gate and deterministic replay must pass; convention, filenames, or reviewer intent are insufficient to claim leakage prevention.

title: Model-discrepancy estimation: multiple auditable models, identifiability-checked, held-out-validated
description:
WHY: fs-evidence has the SCHEMA (DiscrepancyBand, DiscrepancyModel.fit on FidelityPairs, OutOfDomain refusal) but discrepancy bands populated from meaningful DATA are what separate a real validation program from decoration. Crucially: Kennedy-O'Hagan-style discrepancy is ONE method, not the universal ontology — calibration parameters and discrepancy functions can substitute for one another (identifiability), so the machinery must support several auditable discrepancy models and force identifiability + held-out checks rather than blessing whichever fit converged.

WHAT: (a) Discrepancy-model families over the corpus: constant/regime-binned relative band (the current DiscrepancyBand, fit honestly per regime); parametric trend models over pi-groups (fs-regime) with uncertainty on coefficients; adjacent-fidelity probes (correlation-vs-RANS, model-vs-experiment) as FidelityPairs feeding e10 graph edges; [F] GP-style discrepancy reserved as a flagged extension; (b) identifiability discipline: when calibration parameters and discrepancy are fit together, require either separable experiments (parameters pinned by dedicated datasets — e.g. contact resistance measured directly, not co-fit with convection) or an explicit confounding declaration that DEMOTES the resulting claims; (c) held-out predictive checks mandatory: every fitted discrepancy model reports held-out error vs its claimed band (a band that fails held-out is rejected, logged, and the rejection retained); (d) all fits partition-enforced (predecessor bead) and ledgered with replay.

DONE WHEN: at least two discrepancy-model families fit on real Level-C data with held-out validation; an identifiability-confounded fit is demonstrably demoted; bands flow into QoI budgets (e08 model term) and fidelity-graph edges (e10).

TESTS: unit (fit refusals on insufficient data — MIN_OBS discipline like fs-plan; band arithmetic; regime binning); statistical (synthetic truth recovery: known injected discrepancy recovered within tolerance; confounded synthetic case correctly flagged unidentifiable); e2e: full fit->held-out->admit/reject cycle on corpus data with logged diagnostics per model family.

## Acceptance Criteria

Implement multiple explicit model-discrepancy alternatives with priors or bounds, units, covariance or structural assumptions, identifiability diagnostics, selection criteria frozen before held-out evaluation, and a typed outcome of identified, weakly identified, confounded, or refused. Unit tests cover each discrepancy model, likelihood or residual calculation, gradients where claimed, posterior summaries, and serialization; boundary tests cover zero discrepancy, sparse observations, singular covariance, collinearity, extrapolation, and nonfinite data. Property tests use synthetic truth for coverage and recovery only in identifiable regimes; metamorphic tests cover unit conversion, observation permutation, and equivalent parameterization; mutants that force zero discrepancy, reuse held-out data, suppress confounding, or understate uncertainty must fail. Optimizer failure, cancellation, deadline, ensemble depletion, memory and iteration caps, malformed data, and excessive diagnostics must yield bounded fail-closed receipts. This Bead contributes frozen candidate-model and identifiability artifacts to .7.6 and scripts/e2e/cooling_validation_l4.sh. Clean replay and the configured DSR lane must pass; good fit or narrow posterior cannot promote validity when discrepancy and parameters are not separately identifiable.

title: Wire fs-matdb JointStatistics into query receipts: correlation-aware material uncertainty
description:
WHY: fs-matdb already stores JointStatistics (covariance/correlation across properties, PSD-gated) but query-time propagation is NOT wired (a documented no-claim). Treating correlated properties as independent typically UNDERSTATES output uncertainty (e.g. thermal conductivity and density of an alloy co-vary with composition) — a silent optimism bias in exactly the numbers users trust most. This closes a known, honest gap in the substrate the product depends on.

WHAT: (a) Extend the matdb query path so multi-property samples from one card can return the joint uncertainty block (correlated covariance) in the PropertyUsageReceipt when JointStatistics exist and are valid for the requested condition; (b) downstream: e06_7's propagation consumes joint blocks (correlated sampling via the existing PSD-gated machinery + Philox streams) instead of independent per-property draws; when joints are absent, the receipt says CORRELATION-UNKNOWN and the e08 budget carries that caveat explicitly (the banned path is assuming independence silently); (c) uncertainty-model interactions defined: Unstated + joint cannot combine into a certified anything (no-laundering); (d) validity: joint blocks have their own domain checks (a correlation measured at room temperature does not automatically hold at 120C — domain intersection applies).

DONE WHEN: joint-aware receipts flow end-to-end into a QoI budget on the reference project; correlation-unknown caveat renders in the report; independence-silent path is unreachable (lint/test).

TESTS: unit (joint retrieval + PSD gate; domain intersection; refusal/caveat paths); statistical (correlated propagation vs analytic bivariate cases — variance of a sum with known covariance); e2e: reference run twice (with/without joints on a synthetic card) logging the budget difference, demonstrating the optimism-bias magnitude.

The matdb authority surface this bead owns is complete: (a) joint blocks selected and bound at query time — one admitted block covering every SELECTED claim through Scalar members yields the principal covariance submatrix packed in REQUEST order (member-disjointness admission invariant makes it unambiguous; exact-ClaimId matching against the .6.4 selection machinery settles block applicability AND domain validity, since every selected claim already contains the query point); (c) no-laundering proven — an Unstated marginal yields CorrelationUnknown(unstated-marginal), never a joint band; (d) domain checks inherited exactly (member refusals incl. NoClaimInDomain propagate unchanged; no joint machinery weakens the validity gate). The silent-independence path is unrepresentable at this API: absence of correlation is always a named reason (no-block / partial-membership / non-scalar-member / unstated-marginal) in a content-addressed, pack-bound, replay-verified receipt (golden-couplings row org.frankensim.fs-matdb.joint-usage-receipt.v1). Battery tests/joint_query.rs: 5 tests incl. both request orders against one block, analytic bivariate variance-of-sum sanity, every unknown reason, degenerate refusals, receipt determinism + field-level tampering refusals. fs-matdb 62 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean as primary. ROUTED PER THE BEAD'S OWN TEXT: (b) downstream consumption — correlated sampling via PSD machinery + Philox, QoI budget on the reference project, and report-level caveat rendering — is e06.7/e08 scope ('e06_7's propagation consumes joint blocks'); the CONTRACT names it explicitly as their authority. Also not claimed (CONTRACT): portable joint-receipt bytes (ledger transport follow-up), pinned joint queries, curve-knot covariance, card-level blocks.

title: Empirical coverage verification at product level: nominal intervals vs held-out reality
description:
WHY: An uncertainty interval that claims 95% and covers 70% is worse than no interval — it is a confident lie. The machinery exists in pieces (fs-eproc MondrianConformal with per-bucket refusal, DriftMonitor, CoverageClaim/miss_rate, FCR budgets; fs-surrogate empirical_coverage) but nothing verifies the PRODUCT's emitted QoI intervals against held-out observations. This is the "a nominal 95% interval should contain approximately 95% of held-out observations" requirement made operational.

WHAT: (a) A coverage-verification lane: for every (QoI, regime) with validation-partition observations, compare the product's predicted intervals (from e06_7 + e07_2 budgets) against observations; compute empirical coverage with proper small-sample treatment (report coverage WITH its own confidence interval — 3-of-3 covered is not proof of 95%); Mondrian bucketing per regime so pooled flattery cannot hide per-regime failure (a bucket lacking mass REFUSES, mirroring fs-eproc's design); (b) miscalibration response is TYPED: under-coverage triggers a calibration-defect record that demotes affected claims (colors fall; report/no-claim sections update) until recalibration — coverage failure must have consequences, not a dashboard shrug; (c) drift monitoring hooks (fs-eproc DriftVerdict) for ongoing Level-E data so coverage claims age honestly; (d) results feed the scorecard's coverage column and the e16 dashboard.

DONE WHEN: coverage computed per bucket on real validation data; an induced miscalibration (synthetic) demonstrably demotes claims; scorecard consumes the results; small-sample honesty proven in rendering.

TESTS: unit (coverage arithmetic incl. small-sample CIs; bucket refusal on thin mass; demotion triggering); statistical (synthetic generator with known true coverage -> estimator calibrated); e2e: full lane over corpus with per-bucket logs (n, covered, empirical rate, CI, verdict) and the demotion audit trail.

## Acceptance Criteria

Measure product-level empirical coverage on the locked held-out population for every advertised interval or decision band, preserving nominal level, finite-sample uncertainty, stratification, multiplicity policy, censoring, exclusions, and all failed subgroups. Unit tests verify inclusion, weighted and stratified estimators, exact or declared interval methods, and report serialization; boundary tests cover no samples, one sample, all hits or misses, ties at endpoints, rare regimes, and missing outcomes. Property tests use controlled generators with known coverage; metamorphic tests cover row permutation, consistent unit conversion, and duplicate rejection; mutants that count calibration rows, drop misses, select favorable strata, change nominal levels, or hide wide uncertainty must fail. Corrupt data, cancellation, deadline, memory cap, large strata, and logging faults must retain partial status without a passing claim. This Bead contributes immutable coverage tables and falsification fixtures to .7.6 and scripts/e2e/cooling_validation_l4.sh with bounded per-stratum logs and deterministic replay. The configured DSR gate must pass; nominal-looking aggregate coverage does not validate unmeasured strata or justify retrospective interval tuning.

title: Execute the preregistered blind validation case (the program's honesty exam)
description:
WHY: This is the single highest-information event in the program: a prediction made with the full product workflow against a case the models have never seen, with acceptance criteria fixed in advance. Pass or fail, the result is publishable evidence of what the system actually does. The synthesis is explicit that the Level-4 clock runs through exactly this gate.

WHAT: (a) Preconditions verified mechanically: the blind case is still sealed (e04 Level-D machinery); calibration is frozen (a declared model-state content root — predictions must come from THIS state; any recalibration after unseal invalidates the exercise); acceptance envelopes were declared at seal time; (b) execution: unseal ceremony (ledgered); run the FULL product path (validate->solve->report->package) on the blind case within its declared budget; compare per-QoI predictions + intervals against the blind observations; (c) scoring: per-QoI within-envelope verdicts, interval-coverage outcomes, and the honesty checks (did the system's own uncertainty admit the miss where it missed? a miss WITH honest wide bars scores differently than a confident miss); (d) publication: the outcome (either way) enters the scorecard with full workflow provenance; a failed QoI spawns attribution analysis (which budget term was wrong) and corrective beads — failure is data, burying it is the only unacceptable outcome.

DONE WHEN: the exercise completes with ledgered unseal; scorecard updated; attribution analysis for any misses filed as beads; the model-state freeze is verifiable by a third party from the package.

TESTS: precondition gate tests (unsealed-early refusal; post-unseal recalibration detection via content roots); the run itself uses the e06_11 lane; e2e: the whole ceremony scripted with forensic logging (seal check, freeze root, unseal receipt, per-QoI comparison table, verdicts).
acceptance_criteria: Execute exactly the preregistered blind case after authorized unlock, using the frozen source revision, model, parameters, metrics, tolerances, hardware or corpus identity, and run budget; retain every attempt and deviation rather than rerunning to a preferred answer. Unit tests validate receipt binding, one-time unlock, frozen configuration, metric evaluation, and deviation recording; boundary tests cover equality at thresholds, missing sensors, late observations, partial runs, and authorized abort. Property and metamorphic tests verify deterministic evaluation under harmless ordering and packaging changes; mutants that reveal targets early, alter tolerances, replace inputs, discard a failed attempt, reuse calibration data, or mint an unlock must be detected. Cancellation, crash, worker loss, timeout, power or data interruption, memory and disk caps, corrupt observations, and log failure must produce a bounded incomplete or failed receipt, never pass. This Bead supplies the immutable preregistration-to-result chain consumed by .7.6 and scripts/e2e/cooling_validation_l4.sh. Independent review, deterministic result replay, and the configured DSR gate must pass; a failed blind case remains valuable evidence but cannot be relabeled validation success.

title: Independent external reproduction of the validated workflow (someone who does not trust us, from the bundle)
description:
WHY: Every result so far was produced inside the authoring environment. Level 4's final requirement is reproduction by an external party from the release artifacts alone — the strongest test of the reproducibility story (constellation bundle, deterministic replay, self-contained docs) and the first contact with "users who do not already trust the system."

WHAT: (a) Reproduction kit: the vendored source bundle (e13), the reference + blind-case projects, the corpus subset needed, the quickstart, and a reproduction protocol (exact commands, expected content roots, expected report values with tolerance semantics — bitwise where determinism class promises it, banded where cross-ISA policy applies per docs/CROSS_ISA_VERIFICATION.md); (b) recruit an external reproducer (different person, machine, and ideally institution; a clean-room agent on an unconfigured host is the minimum bar) and RECORD their friction log verbatim — every confusion is a docs/UX defect bead; (c) success criteria: reproduction of solve content roots within declared determinism class + independent fs-checker verification of the shipped packages; (d) discrepancies become determinism-incident investigations (playbook exists) or docs fixes; the reproduction outcome joins the scorecard.

DONE WHEN: an external party reproduces the workflow from the kit with zero author intervention beyond the kit itself; friction log triaged into beads; scorecard's independent-reproduction row is TRUE with a citable record. Gated on the claim-integrity promotion gate: reproduction of over-claiming would be reproducing a lie.

TESTS: dry-run the kit internally on a blank VM/host first (the 1t8i blank-box precedent) with full logging; kit-completeness lint (every referenced file present, every command executes); the external run's verification transcript archived as an artifact.

## Acceptance Criteria

An independent reproducer with no reliance on ambient developer state must obtain the retained bundle, verify its identity, build or install from documented inputs, execute the locked workflow, and compare all declared outputs, intervals, decisions, logs, and no-claim states against frozen tolerances. Unit tests verify bundle and receipt validation, environment capture, comparator semantics, and attribution; boundary tests cover missing optional capabilities, alternate supported ISA, paths and locales, clock skew, and tolerance endpoints; property and metamorphic tests exercise archive reordering and equivalent environment relocation. Mutants that omit a dependency, use an unretained input, relax a tolerance, read a hidden cache, alter a seed, or accept a missing result must fail. Offline mode, dependency failure, cancellation, timeout, memory and disk caps, corrupt bundles, and bounded-log truncation must give actionable nonpassing receipts. This Bead is the terminal owner of scripts/e2e/cooling_validation_l4.sh and must publish independent identity, source and artifact roots, exact commands, environment, deviations, and replay outcome. The configured DSR gate and external rerun must both pass; internal reruns, documentation review, or identical aggregate metrics alone do not constitute independent reproduction.

title: E08 Error-budget doctrine + DecisionAssessment: mandatory 8-term uncertainty decomposition at user-facing outputs
description:
WHY: Today fs-evidence::UncertaintyBreakdown has three sources (numerical_rel, statistical_rel, model_rel). An engineering decision needs the full budget: DeltaQ = roundoff + solver + discretization + geometry + parameters + BC + model-form + measurement — where terms need not be additive or Gaussian (representation must allow intervals, distributions, ensembles, correlated blocks, and EXPLICITLY UNKNOWN terms). The three-color model is excellent but currently a compositional substrate; it must become UNAVOIDABLE at every user-facing output of the vertical.

KEY POLICY (the no-promotion rule): no numerical certificate may promote model-form or experimental authority. A well-converged solve is only as trustworthy as its closure model, wall treatment, material state, fan curve, contact resistance, leakage assumptions, and validation regime.

CHILDREN: extend UncertaintyBreakdown to the 8-term budget with rich term representations; enforce the no-promotion policy at type level + lint; automatic evidence demotion outside validated parameter/geometry domains (fs-regime admission at product outputs); typed REFUSAL when an unbounded unknown could change requirement compliance; sensitivity attribution (which uncertainty dominates the decision); DecisionAssessment<Q> as an L6/HELM PROJECTION (explicitly NOT a god type threaded through numerical layers — solvers keep producing evidence-bearing quantities; HELM assembles them with requirement, margin, P(compliance), context of use, validation domain, flip conditions, weakest evidence link, recommended next action, replay package); make budgets unavoidable in report/CLI outputs.

USER QUESTIONS this must answer: will max junction temperature stay under 100C across manufacturing and ambient variation; which assumption contributes most to failure probability; is another mesh refinement valuable or is contact resistance now the dominant unknown; would a thermocouple at A or B reduce decision uncertainty more (ties to fs-voi); which design is robust rather than nominally optimal; what is the cheapest next evidence that could change the decision.

DONE WHEN: every Cooling 0.1 QoI ships with a complete 8-term budget (unknown terms shown as UNKNOWN, never silently dropped), the no-promotion lint gates CI, and DecisionAssessment renders in the report with flip conditions and a recommended next action.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .8.1 through .8.7 to define, compute, serialize, and enforce the complete eight-term error budget and DecisionAssessment projection at every user-facing output. The joined contract must preserve each term separately, covariance or dependence assumptions, units, confidence or enclosure semantics, evidence-regime provenance, requirement and compliance state, flip conditions, next action, and replay key; unavailable terms remain typed unknowns and may not be folded into zero. The terminal enforcement owner is .8.7, contributing naked-scalar refusal and end-to-end cases to scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh, while .8.6 owns the canonical decision-assessment replay cases. E08 closes only when unit, boundary, property, metamorphic, mutation, fault, cancellation, and resource tests plus the configured DSR lane prove schema round-trip, monotone demotion, bounded logs, and identical replay; no output may promote evidence color or compliance above the weakest admitted component.

title: Extend UncertaintyBreakdown to the 8-term engineering error budget with rich term representations
description:
WHY: The current 3-term breakdown (numerical/statistical/model) cannot answer an engineer's actual question: WHERE does my temperature uncertainty come from — mesh, material data, fan tolerance, contact resistance, or the model itself? The 8-term budget (roundoff, solver/algebraic, discretization, geometry, parameters, boundary-conditions, model-form, measurement) is the decomposition decisions get made against, and its terms must NOT be forced additive-Gaussian: representation must allow intervals, distributions, ensembles, correlated blocks, and EXPLICITLY UNKNOWN.

WHAT: (a) New budget types in fs-evidence (versioned alongside the existing 3-term, with a lossless projection 8->3 so existing consumers keep working during migration): each term = a TermValue enum {IntervalBound, Distribution(summary+replayable ref), Ensemble(ref), CorrelatedBlock(covariance ref spanning terms), Unknown{reason}, Negligible{justification}} — Unknown and Negligible are DIFFERENT states and both require content (an empty-string justification refuses); (b) composition rules: conservative aggregation honoring correlation blocks; Unknown terms poison totals into bounded-below/unknown-total states rather than vanishing; dominant-term extraction generalizing the current dominant(); (c) sources: roundoff (fs-ivl/det evidence), solver (residual certificates), discretization (E06_6 ladders/DWR), geometry (import receipts + as-built when e12 lands), parameters (matdb + e07_3 joints), BC (fan/leakage/ambient from e05/e06), model (e07_2 discrepancy), measurement (corpus sensor uncertainty when comparing); (d) identity/serialization for ledger + package embedding.

DONE WHEN: 8-term budgets constructible + composable with tests; projection compatibility proven; at least the E05_10 QoIs emit them populated from real sources (Unknown where sources do not yet exist — honestly).

TESTS: unit (each TermValue variant round-trips; refusals on empty justifications; composition laws incl. correlated-block math vs analytic cases; Unknown poisoning semantics); property (anti-laundering: no composition can strengthen a term's class; monotonicity of totals under widening); e2e: reference-run budget rendered with per-term provenance links, logged term-by-term.

title: Enforce the no-promotion policy: numerical certificates cannot upgrade model-form or experimental authority
description:
WHY: The single most dangerous laundering channel in a certificate-rich system: a beautifully converged, tightly bounded SOLVE gets read as evidence the ANSWER is right. A well-converged solution is still only as trustworthy as its closure model, material state, fan curve, contact resistance, and validation regime. The composition rules mostly prevent color laundering already; this bead closes the specific numerical->model-form channel everywhere, by type and by lint.

WHAT: (a) Type-level: in the 8-term budget and in Evidence composition, improvements to numerical terms (roundoff/solver/discretization) must be INCAPABLE of tightening model-form or measurement terms or of upgrading Validated-requiring colors — audit every composition path in fs-evidence for accidental cross-term influence and add sealed constructors where needed; (b) authority-source rule: Validated color requires an anchoring path to corpus evidence (e04 axes doctrine); no combination of Verified numerical inputs may mint Validated — verify fs-package/fs-checker admission agrees (their color-admission bridge must enforce the same rule at package level); (c) lint: an xtask/conformance check over claim-producing crates that flags APIs returning model-class conclusions from purely numerical inputs (heuristic, reviewed — the goal is catching new seams, not proving absence); (d) documentation: the policy stated in fs-evidence CONTRACT and the e09 doctrine, with the RANS example spelled out.

DONE WHEN: adversarial laundering tests (constructed attempts to strengthen model terms via numerical evidence) all refuse across fs-evidence AND fs-package admission; lint runs in check-all; CONTRACT language merged.

TESTS: unit (each constructed laundering attempt -> typed refusal, incl. the subtle ones: intersection of validity domains must not IMPLY in-domain validation; discrepancy-band tightening requires new FidelityPairs, not smaller residuals); integration (package-level admission mirrors evidence-level rules); e2e: a demonstration script logging each attempted upgrade and its refusal reason — doubles as reviewer education material.

title: Automatic evidence demotion outside validated domains at product outputs (fs-regime admission everywhere user-facing)
description:
WHY: Validity domains exist (model cards, matdb, correlations) and fs-regime can rank distance-to-validity — but demotion outside domains must be AUTOMATIC at every user-facing output, not a convention kernel authors remember. The moment a project's operating envelope drifts outside a card's domain, every affected downstream claim must weaken without anyone noticing in code review.

WHAT: (a) Product-output admission: E05_10 QoI extraction and the e06 report/package paths run a final domain-intersection audit — the operating point(s) of the run checked against EVERY model card consumed (correlations, discrepancy models, closures, matdb cards, fan curves); any out-of-domain consumption demotes the affected QoI's color and adds a named regime violation to the budget's model term (with distance-to-validity from fs-regime as severity context); (b) partial-envelope handling: when an UQ sweep (e06_7) spans in- and out-of-domain regions, results split honestly (in-domain fraction with full evidence, out-of-domain fraction demoted; never averaged into one flattering number); (c) demotions are receipts (what card, what axis, how far out, what color change) rendered in the report's no-claim section; (d) override path: an explicit, ledgered user acknowledgment can proceed-despite-demotion but can never restore the color (informed use of estimates is legitimate; silent extrapolation is not).

DONE WHEN: an envelope nudged outside any single card's domain demonstrably demotes the affected QoIs end-to-end (test per card class); the split-sweep path proven; receipts render.

TESTS: unit (intersection audit per card class; severity computation; color-transition rules; override non-restoration); property (demotion monotonicity: shrinking any domain never strengthens output evidence); e2e: reference project + perturbed-envelope variants, logging the full demotion audit trail per variant.
acceptance_criteria: At every admitted user-facing output, evaluate the requested context and QoI against validation domains, capability evidence, fidelity edges, and freshness, then monotonically demote evidence to the weakest applicable regime with an explicit reason and escalation path. Unit tests cover each regime transition, overlapping domains, unknown context, stale evidence, partial support, and serialization; boundary tests hit domain surfaces and exact expiry or tolerance limits. Property tests require demotion idempotence and forbid authority increase under added uncertainty or removed evidence; metamorphic tests cover equivalent units, reordered evidence, and narrower domains; mutants that skip a check, choose the strongest row, treat unknown as valid, or drop the demotion receipt must fail. title: Typed refusal when an unbounded unknown can flip requirement compliance (no verdict built on sand)
description:
WHY: The budget's Unknown terms are honest — but honesty must have teeth: if a term is Unknown AND unbounded, and the compliance verdict (T_junction < limit) could flip within any plausible magnitude of that term, then issuing ANY verdict is malpractice. The system must refuse the verdict and name the unknown, converting a hidden gamble into an explicit evidence-acquisition demand (which fs-voi can then price).

WHAT: (a) Flip analysis: for every requirement-bearing QoI, compute the margin against the aggregate of BOUNDED terms; then for each Unknown term, determine whether ANY value (for truly unbounded) or any value within a declared plausibility bound (for Unknown-but-bounded) could flip the verdict; (b) outcomes typed: Compliant{margin, budget} | NonCompliant{shortfall, budget} | Indeterminate{flipping_unknowns: named list with the magnitude each needs to flip, recommended_evidence: the cheapest resolution action per unknown, wired to fs-voi action-value where cost models exist} — Indeterminate is a RESULT, rendered as prominently as pass/fail (tri-state discipline like fs-asbuilt's DecisionState precedent); (c) plausibility bounds for Unknowns are declared data with provenance, never invented at check time; (d) the report's DecisionAssessment block consumes this verdict directly.

DONE WHEN: verdict machinery handles all three outcomes on constructed cases; an Unknown contact-resistance case yields Indeterminate naming the interface and the resistance magnitude that flips it; fs-voi recommendation wiring demonstrated for at least one unknown class.

TESTS: unit (flip arithmetic per TermValue variant; boundary cases where margin exactly equals the flip magnitude — deterministic tie-break DOCUMENTED and tested; refusal of undeclared plausibility bounds); property (adding information never moves Compliant->Indeterminate unless a new unknown appeared); e2e: three fixture projects (clearly compliant / clearly not / indeterminate) logging full flip analyses.

title: E09 Certificate-regime doctrine: match the evidence object to the claim (incl. honest NoUsefulBound)
description:
WHY: "Certified" must not mean "we propagated a pointwise interval as long as possible." For chaotic, strongly nonlinear, or event-rich systems a long-horizon trajectory enclosure becomes rigorous AND useless; a large honest interval is a valid RESULT but not an engineering certificate. The certified OBJECT must change with the claim: from trajectory to observable, event, invariant, or distribution — rigorous numerics still matter, applied to the right object.

DOCTRINE TABLE (to be encoded, not just written): root/event time -> interval root isolation or Taylor enclosure (fs-ivl newton/taylor); short-horizon collision avoidance -> validated reachability tube; conserved quantity -> discrete conservation/balance certificate; local stability -> spectral/Lyapunov evidence within a stated domain (fs-spectral, fs-sos); long-term mean load -> statistical observable with sampling + model evidence (fs-uq, fs-eproc); turbulent spectrum -> distributional/spectral validation; reliability over duty cycle -> sequential/rare-event statistical evidence; exact long chaotic trajectory -> explicit NoUsefulBound, never a cosmetic certificate. Intervals retain valid roles in chaotic systems: short-time event detection, local exclusions, parameter bounds, conservation audits, finite-horizon reachability.

CHILDREN: doctrine document (docs/ + fs-govern doctrine entry with risk linkage); NoUsefulBound as a first-class typed result with honest rendering in reports; a claim-type router mapping claim kinds to evidence machinery with refusal for mismatches; a chaotic-system demonstrator test showing trajectory-enclosure blowup while the observable-level claim stays decision-grade.

DONE WHEN: the router exists and is used by at least one campaign crate; requesting a long-horizon pointwise enclosure of a chaotic fixture yields NoUsefulBound plus a suggested observable-level reformulation; doctrine is cited by CONTRACT.md no-claim sections in affected crates.

## Success Criteria

Rollup acceptance requires .9.1 through .9.4 to map claim classes to admissible evidence objects, implement honest NoUsefulBound, prevent false certificate elevation, and demonstrate doctrine behavior on a chaotic system. title: NoUsefulBound as a first-class typed result with honest rendering
description:
WHY: Today an uninformative enclosure ([-1e30, 1e30]) is structurally identical to a tight one — the honesty lives in the width, which prose can ignore. NoUsefulBound makes uselessness UNIGNORABLE: a typed outcome that cannot be formatted as a certificate, cannot silently satisfy a requirement check, and carries the reformulation hint (what observable-level claim COULD be supported instead).

WHAT: (a) The type: a bound-producing computation may return Bound{interval, decision_context} or NoUsefulBound{width_achieved, usefulness_criterion_failed, cause: (horizon too long | Lipschitz blowup | domain exit | budget exhausted), suggested_reformulation: claim-class from the e09 table}; usefulness is DECLARED by the caller (a width threshold relative to the decision need — the same enclosure can be useful for one requirement and useless for another, so usefulness is contextual, never absolute); (b) integration: fs-ivl/Taylor/newton drivers and downstream certificate assemblers get bounded variants accepting a usefulness criterion; requirement checks (E08_4) treat NoUsefulBound as Indeterminate-with-cause, never as pass or fail; (c) rendering: report/package show NoUsefulBound as its own visual class with the cause and suggestion (education by interface); (d) no-laundering: NoUsefulBound composes as absorbing (any composition containing it is at best NoUsefulBound for that term).

DONE WHEN: type shipped with driver integration; a chaotic/stiff fixture produces NoUsefulBound with correct cause; report renders it; requirement checks consume it correctly.

TESTS: unit (constructor validation; absorbing composition; contextual usefulness — same bound, two criteria, two outcomes); integration (drivers return it at the right thresholds, not before — a still-useful bound must not be discarded); e2e: fixture run logging the width trajectory to failure, the emitted cause, and the rendered suggestion.

title: ArtifactWriter must poison after failed chunk flush
description: ArtifactWriter::write removes a full chunk from its buffer before INSERT succeeds. If that INSERT fails, the writer remains finishable with hasher/len covering bytes that are no longer staged, so finish can publish a receipt and malformed artifact. Make every flush/write failure poison the writer, retain failed bytes until insertion succeeds, and make finish roll back and refuse. Add a trigger-induced regression proving a failed full-chunk insert followed by finish yields no receipt, artifacts, chunks, or open transaction.
acceptance_criteria: A trigger forces the first full-chunk INSERT to fail; write returns the injected SQL error; finish refuses, rolls back, and leaves zero artifacts/chunks and no transaction. Focused fs-ledger test passes under strict RCH.
close_reason: Fixed and strict-remote regression passed: failed chunk flush now poisons writer and finish rolls back with zero residue.

title: [P0] Fail closed on non-finite evidence regimes and emit valid color JSON
description:
## Defect
The three-color evidence path violates fail-closed and canonical-JSON invariants in three related ways:

1. check_regime compares state values with less-than/greater-than only, so NaN satisfies neither comparison and a Validated claim remains Validated. Non-finite regime bounds have the same problem.
2. Composition of two Validated claims with disjoint regimes demotes to Estimated but records dispersion 0.0, falsely encoding perfect agreement when there is no jointly supported state. The existing regime-exit convention correctly uses infinite/no-claim dispersion.
3. Color::payload_json interpolates unescaped identifiers and bare non-finite floats. Regime demotion intentionally produces infinite dispersion, so ordinary demotion rows can contain invalid JSON (inf/NaN); quotes/control characters in dataset, estimator, or axis names can also corrupt structured ledger payloads.

## Scope
- Harden fs-evidence regime/color functions only.
- Non-finite state or non-finite/empty regime bounds must demote/refuse conservatively.
- Disjoint validated regimes must produce Estimated with infinite/no-claim dispersion.
- Color payload JSON must escape strings and encode non-finite values as valid JSON without pretending they are finite numbers.
- Update fs-evidence contract language and focused tests. Touch fs-ledger colors/tests only if required to validate emitted rows end to end.
- Do not redesign Certified<T>, package serialization, signatures, or budget pies in this bead.

## Acceptance
- NaN, +Inf, and -Inf state values cannot preserve Validated color.
- Non-finite regime bounds cannot preserve Validated color.
- Disjoint regime composition demotes with infinite/no-claim dispersion.
- Payloads for infinite dispersion and hostile quote/newline/control-character strings parse as syntactically valid JSON and preserve deterministic output.
- Existing color/ledger conformance remains green.

## Verification
Focused fs-evidence and, if touched, fs-ledger tests/clippy through RCH; rustfmt; ubs on changed files; git diff --check.

description: RE.Q1 validates that control and disturbance variables are present but does not require existential control and universal disturbance. title: Retained workspace-suite green receipt with an explicit known-red set (L3 cannot be claimed without it)
description:
BACKGROUND. Nothing in this repository establishes that the workspace test suite passes. The README says so itself (README.md:63): the 590-file count "is an inventory count, not a claim that every test is green on the current tree." There is no CI log, no committed test-run artifact, and no scorecard-style "N passed" record anywhere in the tree.

Meanwhile the repo's own tracked evidence says it CANNOT currently be green: four fs-ledger GC tests are red on a documented upstream FrankenSQLite root cause (bead frankensim-fsqlite-fk-cascade-ordering-f2jag, which names all four by file and function), and none of them is #[ignore]d, so they run in an ordinary cargo test -p fs-ledger. Separately, as of 2026-07-28 a workspace check --all-targets exits 101 on crates/fs-alloc/tests/lease_delegation.rs, though that one is a concurrent agent's in-flight refactor and is expected to clear.

WHY THIS BLOCKS L3. The capability-maturity ladder's L3 tier is an ADMITTED end-to-end integration claim. An integration claim over a workspace whose green/red state is unknown is not admissible: you cannot claim composition works when you cannot state that the components pass. This is the same "composition cannot outrank its weakest operand" rule the evidence algebra enforces on values, applied to the test suite itself. Today the weakest operand is unmeasured, so the composition is unbounded.

Note the honest asymmetry: #[ignore] is used well in this repo. All 39 instances are cost/host/perf lanes, not hidden failures. The known-red tests are tracked in prose and beads, not suppressed. So this bead is about producing a RECEIPT, not about uncovering concealment.

WHAT.
(a) Produce a retained, dated, reproducible workspace-suite receipt: the exact command, toolchain, host fingerprint, constellation pin state, per-crate pass/fail/ignored counts, and the total. It must record the KNOWN-RED set explicitly with its owning bead rather than hiding it, so "green except these four, which are tracked upstream" is a statable, checkable position.
(b) Decide and record the disposition of each known-red test: blocked-upstream (with the bead), or repaired. A receipt that silently omits them is worse than no receipt.
(c) Retain it as a checked artifact in the same idiom as program-metrics.json and vv-scorecard.json so staleness is visible.

DONE WHEN: a tracked receipt exists that states the workspace suite result with per-crate granularity and an explicit known-red set; regenerating it is one documented command; and its staleness is detectable.

TESTS: the receipt generator is deterministic given the same run inputs; a negative control proves the receipt refuses to claim green when any non-known-red test fails.

PRACTICAL NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the shared /Volumes/USB_NVME/cargo-target lock is frequently held for 20+ minutes by concurrent agents, and the fs-cli solve suite alone takes ~807s. Use rch exec with a dedicated CARGO_TARGET_DIR under RCH_TARGET_BASE to run on a Linux worker without local lock contention; that is the only way this has been made to complete reliably. Measure a baseline on the SAME worker before attributing any failure to your own change.

Unit/property/mutation tests cover ordering, duplicate/missing crates, stale known-red entries, a new unowned failure, hidden omission, malformed output, interrupted shard, retry/resume, and deterministic regeneration. A negative control must prevent any green claim when a non-known-red test fails; known-red does not become ignored or passing. The execution uses DSR first and records constellation preflight separately from focused/RCH fallback. Bounded V.3 JSONL contains run/shard/crate/test identities, disposition, first unexpected failure, cancellation/drain, known-red owner, relative artifacts, redaction, and exact reproduction. Static review, inventory counts, or a partial suite cannot close.

title: Flywheel compounding authority: identify interactions with a factorial held-out E2E experiment
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The historical whole-loop E2E measured the composed configuration and isolated configurations and correctly showed a large user-visible combination benefit. That contrast cannot identify pairwise or higher-order interactions and therefore cannot support a superadditivity or causal-compounding claim. Users need both the combined performance result and an honest account of which mechanisms interact, in which workload regimes, with what uncertainty and stopping policy.

EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: Implement a complete 2^4 factorial design for the Phase-1 mechanisms (certified speculation, incremental recompute, sheaf-adjudicated merge, and tombstone pre-exploration), or a preregistered fractional/sequential design whose alias matrix demonstrably identifies every claimed main and interaction effect. Treat the declarative query stage as a separately declared Phase-2 factor or held-constant integration layer; do not silently count it as a fifth manipulated factor. Randomize or deterministically counterbalance configuration order within immutable workload/seed blocks. Separate calibration/tuning traces from a locked held-out evaluation corpus. Bind hardware fingerprint, source and workload identities, factor versions/policies, cache warm/cold state, agent schedule, seed, budgets, and measurement protocol before looking at held-out outcomes.

ANALYSIS AND AUTHORITY: Report raw per-block observations, main effects, all identifiable pairwise and higher-order interactions, uncertainty intervals, multiplicity handling, practical effect thresholds, model diagnostics, and a Shapley or other explicitly defined contribution decomposition as descriptive attribution. Predeclare whether effects are expressed on cost, latency, throughput, or log-speedup scale; superadditivity is evaluated on the declared scale against a precisely stated null. Use an e-process/confidence-sequence or fixed-horizon plan valid for the actual optional-stopping policy. A large combined speedup may still be reported if interaction authority is Unknown, but it must not be relabeled superadditive. Failed randomization, insufficient power, unstable workload, hardware drift, unmodeled cache state, or violated diagnostics yields typed Inconclusive rather than a positive interaction claim.

HARNESS: Extend scripts/ci/flywheel_authority_e2e.sh with selector --case factorial-compounding. The real no-mock journey executes every declared factor configuration through admission, solve/speculation, cache, branch/merge, tombstone, query/report, ledger packaging, and independent analysis replay. No synthetic replacement may stand in for a claimed production factor. Retained evidence includes the immutable design manifest, calibration/evaluation split, configuration schedule, raw measurements, phase telemetry, analysis inputs/outputs, and checker receipt.

TESTS AND LOGGING: Unit tests cover factor encoding, alias-rank detection, block randomization/counterbalancing, estimand scale, interaction and Shapley calculations, missing/duplicate observations, warm/cold state, uncertainty math, optional-stopping boundaries, multiplicity, seed determinism, units, and authority transitions. Property/metamorphic tests cover factor relabeling, run-order permutations, cost-unit rescaling, zero-interaction synthetic controls, known positive/negative interactions, and equivalent blocked designs. E2E cases cover full factorial happy path, main-effects-only control, positive and antagonistic interactions, calibration leakage, insufficient power, drift, cancellation, budget/deadline exhaustion, tampering, checker disagreement, and clean replay. G4 injects cancellation/faults at each configuration and analysis/publication boundary with bounded draining and no partial positive claim; G5 replays the immutable schedule and semantic results. Bounded schema-versioned logs include factor vector, block/workload/seed, calibration versus held-out role, hardware/mode, budgets and consumption, raw outcomes, phase telemetry, estimator/uncertainty state, stopping decision, main/interaction effects, attribution, diagnostics, authority transition, checker identity, and artifact roots.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) every claimed interaction is identifiable under the retained design matrix; (2) held-out confirmation is isolated from tuning; (3) the stopping and uncertainty procedure matches execution; (4) combination benefit, interaction, and superadditivity are separate typed claims; (5) independent replay reproduces estimands and rejects any missing, changed, or reordered evidence that affects semantics; (6) the harness returns explicit nonzero exit classes for invalid design, inconclusive evidence, tamper, cancellation, and checker failure; (7) retained DSR or narrowly qualified RCH proof names exact source state, command, machine, log, and receipt paths.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the historical whole-loop experiment with each Phase-1 mechanism isolated and with all mechanisms composed on the same modeled workload.
2. Confirm that the composed speedup exceeds the best isolated speedup by the stated margin.
3. Attempt to recover pairwise or higher-order interaction effects from only those isolated-versus-composed observations.
4. Observe that multiple additive, multiplicative, fixed-cost, and interaction models fit that contrast, so the evidence identifies combination benefit but not superadditivity or causal interactions.
5. Run the successor factorial case; invalid or rank-deficient designs must be refused before any interaction claim.


## Acceptance Criteria

Execute scripts/ci/flywheel_authority_e2e.sh --case factorial-compounding with a retained full 2^4 or demonstrably identifying design, locked calibration/held-out split, declared estimand scale, valid stopping/uncertainty and multiplicity handling, main and interaction estimates, diagnostics, descriptive attribution, and independent replay. Unit/property/metamorphic/mutation and E2E controls must detect aliasing, leakage, drift, insufficient power, warm/cold confounding, tamper, cancellation, and checker disagreement. Report combination benefit, interaction, and superadditivity as separate typed claims with bounded detailed logs and qualified proof.

Unit/property/metamorphic/mutation and E2E controls must detect aliasing, leakage, drift, insufficient power, warm/cold confounding, tamper, cancellation, and checker disagreement.
