title: solve stage producer: project Cooling -> fs-airflow network lowering and flow-network stage
description:
Child of f85xj.6.5 (solve orchestration). The flow-network stage must lower the project cooling section (fs-project spec.rs: Fan { name, flow m^3/s, static_pressure Pa }, Vent { region, area m^2 }, Cooling { fans, vents, leakage W }) into fs_airflow::solve_operating_point(&FanBank, &EnclosureNetwork).

DESIGN PROBLEM stated honestly: the project declares ONE (flow, static_pressure) point per fan, but fs-airflow validates MONOTONE TYPED FAN CURVES with a pressure_tolerance_rel and a domain; a single point is not a curve. Options to decide: (a) extend the .fsim cooling schema (schema v1 is NOT frozen yet, fs-project/CONTRACT.md:410-412) to carry a declared curve (list of points + tolerance); (b) a declared-operating-point mode in fs-airflow that skips the curve intersection and takes the point as authority-Estimate; (c) synthesize a quadratic through the point (REJECT: invents physics). Vent area -> quadratic loss coefficient needs a sourced discharge-coefficient model with validity domain, not a magic constant. Leakage is already a declared W sink.

DONE WHEN: reference project cooling section produces an OperatingPoint (or typed refusal) through the solve pipeline with retained evidence incl. the interval-certified nominal root fs-airflow already provides; the stage-gap refusal for flow-network in fs-cli/src/solve.rs is deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria

Flow-network lowering consumes only declared project physics. Every solve fan has a valid declared curve, pressure tolerance, minimum-flow policy, basis/source identity, and admitted domain; a single point remains insufficient and refuses. No curve or loss law is synthesized. Every vent and mandatory airflow-leakage branch lowers through the sourced sharp-edged-orifice model; thermal leakage watts can never populate airflow leakage.

Envelope pressure and temperature lower deterministically to typed density under the recorded ideal-gas policy and R_air = 287.05 J/(kg K), retaining provenance and units; missing/non-finite/out-of-domain data refuses. Fan, vent, leakage, density, tolerance, source, and regime identities bind into the receipt. The production solve_operating_point route returns a retained OperatingPoint with interval-certified nominal-root evidence, branch flows, loss accounting, and regime audit, or a typed refusal. Nominal-root evidence is never presented as certification of undeclared manufacturing tolerance or real-world discrepancy. Flow cannot publish before a valid material checkpoint.

Unit/independent tests cover missing, one-point, non-monotone, duplicate-flow, non-finite, wrong-unit, negative-flow, and invalid-tolerance curves; absent/zero/negative vents; absent leakage; thermal-W versus airflow-area confusion; invalid ambient state; one/multiple fans; series/parallel paths; asymmetric leakage; root outside domain; no root; multiple-root refusal; analytic fan/system intersections; conservation; and stable argument order. Properties/metamorphic tests cover resistance versus vent area, admitted flow versus fan pressure, branch conservation, equivalent parallel-area split/merge, declaration permutations, and equivalent units. Cancellation/fault tests inject at lowering, bracketing, interval iterations, reconstruction, regime audit, serialization, publication, density derivation, card lookup, non-finite aggregation, ledger writes/links, and resume re-attestation. No refusal or fault publishes a flow checkpoint.

scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh --through flow-network --profile <pr|full|recovery> --artifact-dir <path> invokes the real release-built frankensim CLI, canonical .fsim project, real promoted geometry/card packs, material predecessor, production flow driver, and real FrankenSQLite ledger. It runs clean success twice, missing/invalid-physics refusals, cancellation at every work boundary, predecessor-checkpoint resume, budget exhaustion, corrupt/stale/tampered inputs, write/link failure, duplicate invocation, and retry. The E2E proves the material receipt is consumed lineage, not merely present elsewhere. Uninterrupted and cancel/resume runs must have identical semantic roots.

Canonical JSONL uses deterministic record/field order and includes schema/version, case/event sequence, source revision/constellation/workspace, run/project/stage/ordinal/operation IDs, material predecessor, capability verb, declared model/source identities, fan curves, vent/leakage parameters, ambient/density policy, interval bracket/iterations/residuals, branch flows, regime results, input/output/receipt roots, budget grant/use, cancellation boundary, resume source, authority/no-claim state, diagnostic code, ranked fix, and verdict. Timing/load observations are separate non-authoritative rows. Meta-tests reject missing, duplicate, reordered, mixed-run/revision, truncated, unknown-version, and tampered records. Focused tests, no-mock E2E, constellation preflight, and named DSR lane must pass with retained artifacts before closure.

### Operating-State Authority

`Envelope` currently declares ambient low/high, not a nominal temperature. The Project schema must therefore add versioned explicit operating state(s), or the solve must evaluate every declared state required by the claim. Lowering may not silently choose low, high, midpoint, or ambient-as-nominal. Each density receipt binds the exact pressure/temperature state, gas model/constants, units, applicability domain, and whether the result is a point-state output or envelope-wide aggregation. Envelope-wide claims require all declared states or an admitted UQ/coverage policy; missing selection refuses with a ranked migration fix.

### Implementability and Proof-State Binding

`frankensim-frn2i.1` is a hard prerequisite: the flow stage may not select the first fan, infer count/arrangement/speed/domain, collapse heterogeneous declarations, or bypass explicit topology. Rated-point versus curve semantics follow that child's contract. Full operating-point outputs use same-ISA deterministic replay and predeclared semantic tolerances across ISAs until actual dual-runtime G5 evidence; a cross-compile is not runtime proof.

Immediately before and after authoritative proof, `scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --snapshot` reports identical complete root-plus-sibling content identities and unchanged `constellation.lock` identity. Evidence binds source/snapshot/toolchain/target/profile/features plus DSR run/log/artifact roots and rejects cross-snapshot splicing; focused Cargo/RCH is focused proof only, and shared siblings are never repinned to manufacture a pass.
design: Hierarchy-only rollup: contract/lowering=frankensim-frn2i.1; production flow stage=frankensim-frn2i.2. Runner publication is owned by frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.6.5.3.
acceptance_criteria: Close only when the exact contract and production-stage children close. Core lowering and flow execution require comprehensive focused tests and real solve-stage cases; only frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.6.5.3 waits for Runner phase 4. Preserve every original Project, Cooling, fs-airflow, evidence, cancellation, replay, and no-claim clause.
close_reason: Rollup closes on its two exact children: frn2i.1 (fan-system contract, closed 2026-08-09) and frn2i.2 (production flow stage, closed today with full evidence). Parent DONE-WHEN met clause by clause: the tracked reference project's cooling section produces an OperatingPoint through the real solve pipeline with the interval-certified nominal root retained in the stage receipt (fs-airflow solve_operating_point; receipt schema frankensim.cli.solve-flow-network-receipt.v1), and the flow-network stage-gap refusal in fs-cli/src/solve.rs is deleted (gap_dependency None, pinned by test). Design decisions held: option (a) declared curve + typed refusal for curveless fans; option (b) rejected; no synthesized physics; vents/leakage through the sourced sharp-edged-orifice model (Cd 0.61 Idelchik/ASHRAE, slice 1 at 67841498); thermal leakage watts can never populate airflow leakage (separate declared area, refusal when absent). A fan WITHOUT a declared curve triggers a TYPED REFUSAL at the flow-network stage naming exactly what is missing; option (b) declared-operating-point mode is REJECTED for the solve path because it bypasses the crate's certified root and the DONE-WHEN explicitly retains that evidence; option (c) synthesized quadratic stays rejected (invents physics). (2) Schema-freeze analysis: schema-policy.json row project.fsim minor_bump explicitly allows adding optional fields with receipted defaults while keeping prior docs loadable and hash-stable; the existing duty field is the in-tree precedent for optional accretion inside v1 (its omission is 'the schema's ONE receipted power default'). title: Cooling fan-system contract: lossless Project declarations and fail-closed fs-airflow lowering
description:
> Canonical closure notice (2026-07-28 reality-check): the Design, Acceptance Criteria, and Notes fields are authoritative. Any embedded Acceptance Criteria, Success Criteria, Ownership and Verification Handoff, or Phase 9.5 sections below are retained as scope and history; they cannot weaken, override, or independently close the canonical fields.

## Outcome

Make every Cooling fan declaration losslessly constructible as production `fs_airflow::FanCurve`/`FanBank` evidence. Replace the ambiguous `Vec<Fan>` lowering contract with a versioned fan-system declaration carrying every parameter the solver consumes; never infer bank topology, speed law, or nominal point.

## Scope

Project wire/canonical identity spells stable bank/group identity, count, `Series|Parallel` arrangement, speed ratio, admitted speed-ratio domain, monotone curve, min-flow/stall boundary, pressure tolerance/basis, source citation/ID, and explicit series/parallel topology when more than one heterogeneous bank is declared. The current rated point is either checked against the declared curve within a predeclared tolerance or typed as correlation-only and excluded from the network solve. Lowering consumes every fan exactly once, preserves source/domain/units, and constructs the production composite fan system; zero/duplicate/orphan banks, ambiguous topology, and unsupported composition refuse. No first-fan choice, implicit count=1/speed=1, midpoint, or identical-fan collapse is allowed. Early-stage schema migration uses a ranked explicit rewrite/refusal, never a semantic compatibility default.

## Required Tests and Logging

Unit/wire tests cover strict/canonical roundtrip, migration/refusal, unknown/missing fields, stable identity, zero/overflow count, every arrangement/topology, speed values at/beyond domain edges, two-point and larger curves, min-flow, curve monotonicity, tolerance/source, rated-point agreement/disagreement, and all unit/non-finite cases. Analytic tests independently derive series pressure addition, parallel flow addition, heterogeneous composition, and representative fan/system intersections. G0/property/metamorphic tests cover allowed declaration/curve permutations, equivalent units, identical-bank expansion/collapse only when explicitly equivalent, topology associativity where physically valid, provenance mutation, and deterministic replay. G4/fault tests inject cancellation, budget, allocation, serialization, and ledger failures at parsing, composition, bracketing, and publication; no partial fan/flow receipt survives.

`scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh --through flow-network --case fan-system-contract --profile <pr|full|recovery>` runs the release-built CLI on real Project declarations, production fan/network paths, and a real FrankenSQLite ledger. It includes single, identical multi-fan, heterogeneous explicit-topology, rated-point mismatch, absent/ambiguous topology, domain-edge, cancel/resume, tamper, and deterministic-repeat cases. No direct `FanBank` construction outside production lowering or fabricated receipt counts.

Canonical JSONL binds schema, event sequence, source revision/constellation identity, project/run/stage IDs, every declaration/curve/source/domain root, topology, composite result, bracket/residual, budget/cancel/resume, authority/no-claim state, diagnostics/ranked fixes, and artifact roots. Volatile observations are separate and excluded from semantic roots; meta-tests reject missing, duplicate, reordered, mixed-run/revision, truncated, unknown-version, and tampered records.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every admitted Project fan declaration is consumed exactly once and losslessly reconstructs the production fan-system input; independent analytic fixtures agree; ambiguous/incomplete declarations fail before solve with stable diagnostics; uninterrupted and resumed semantic roots match; the no-mock E2E and negative corpus pass. `scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --snapshot` must pass against the unchanged pinned source snapshot, and `dsr quality --tool frankensim` must terminate PASS with retained run/log/artifact identities. Same-ISA bit replay is required; cross-ISA numerical equality is not claimed without actual dual-runtime evidence.

### Snapshot Evidence Binding

Capture the complete root-plus-sibling constellation snapshot immediately before and after authoritative proof. The two snapshot identities and constellation.lock identity must be exact matches; evidence rows bind source HEAD, snapshot schema/identity, toolchain, target ISA, profile/features, and DSR run/log/artifact roots, and reject cross-snapshot splicing. A dirty/off-pin refusal is reported, never repaired by repinning a shared sibling.
design:
Dependency direction is explicit: L6 project and CLI code owns wire-schema parsing and calls a lower-layer fs-airflow construction API; fs-airflow never imports fs-project or HELM types. A versioned neutral FanSystemDeclaration crosses the seam with checked units and content-bound provenance. Lowering is one-way, total over admitted declarations, and consumes each declared bank exactly once.

Every curve declares flow unit, pressure unit and basis, reference density if required, reference speed, admissible speed-ratio interval, monotone domain, stall or minimum-flow boundary, interpolation rule, source, and tolerance. The fan affinity law is exact for admitted scaling: Q at speed s maps from Q_ref by Q = s times Q_ref, and pressure at Q maps as delta-p_s(Q) = s squared times delta-p_ref(Q divided by s), subject to declared density and validity assumptions. Outside the domain refuses or returns an explicit no-claim according to frozen policy.

Topology is an explicit ordered typed tree. Series banks share flow and add pressure; parallel banks share pressure and add flow. Heterogeneous composition solves the declared topology rather than collapsing counts or selecting the first curve. Rated points are checked against the curve under declared tolerance or classified correlation-only and excluded from solver authority. Identity, ordering, migration, diagnostics, work limits, cancellation, publication, and ledger roots are canonical.

The leaf E2E stops at the real flow-network consumer. Higher Cooling solve and acceptance are parent integration responsibilities, avoiding hidden coupling while retaining the complete product journey.

Speed is a checked `FanSpeedState`, never an unqualified scalar. `Positive { ratio }` requires finite ratio in a declared [s_min,s_max] with s_min strictly > 0 and alone uses Q/s and s^2 affinity scaling. `Stopped { policy }` at +0 or -0 never evaluates Q/s; it requires an explicit versioned check-valve/blocking, sourced passive-resistance, or sourced freewheeling curve policy and defines pressure/backflow/topology behavior. If no stopped policy is declared, zero refuses. Ratios below s_min refuse before division/overflow. Negative/reverse ratios are UnsupportedReverseOperation in this version and require a separately sourced/versioned reverse curve before future admission. Density/basis rules and series/parallel behavior remain explicit for stopped banks.

1. Speed-domain semantics now make stopped/near-zero/reverse operation physically and numerically explicit rather than relying on undefined division.

- Public authority/type surfaces require API and compile-fail misuse tests. A leaf with no public type must record that fact and provide the nearest strict schema/API-negative equivalent rather than silently omitting the category.
- Seeded mutation tests independently alter every claim-bearing identity, bound, state, policy, route, authority, and no-claim field and retain minimized, reproducible failures.
- Cancellation/deadline plus injected allocation, worker/process, parser, I/O, durable-seal, publication, and replay faults are placed at every transition this leaf owns; drain/quiescence, exact resource return, no partial authority, retryability, and first-cause diagnostics are asserted. Inapplicable fault classes require a typed N/A rationale.
- The terminal owner named by the dependency graph runs a release-built, no-mock E2E using the canonical shared commands: --list, --check, --self-test, --run PROFILE [--family-mode MODE], --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on write modes. Nested nonterminal producer leaves emit bounded content-bound artifacts consumed by that runner and must not create a competing `--family-mode all` selector or `--mode`/`--profile` alias; exactly one catalog-owned terminal adapter may expose `--family-mode all` under exact-set registry tests.
- Canonical bounded logs record schema/source/build/tool/target/features, typed lossless values and units, command/profile/family/mode/case/sequence, budgets/work/resources, state/reason, expected/observed/effects, authority/no-claim, diagnostics/ranked repair, stop/drain roots, and relative artifact roots. Invocation manifests are fixed and nonempty; case_start opens every ordered slot with execution=execute|suppressed; suppressed permits zero family rows and requires immediate typed NotRun. Cooperative stops drain/finalize the active case and emit remaining suppressed slots before summary/terminal; forced or unproved truncation emits no terminal. Exact case_terminal/run_summary/run_terminal cardinality, caps, hostile parser cases, tamper detection, separate replay input/output roots, and artifact-only replay are mandatory. Raw scientific/performance/tool data stays in capped artifacts, and only explicitly declared volatile observations are excluded from identity.

title: fs-ledger: 5 latent test failures revealed once the crate compiles again
description:
REVEALED BY: the E02 repair wave fixed crates/fs-ledger/src/identity_migration.rs:3528 (E0308 - upstream frankensqlite Connection::execute now returns Result<usize,_>; fixed with the file's own .map(|_| ()) idiom). The crate had not compiled, so its whole test suite was silently unrunnable. With it building again, 5 tests fail. NONE are caused by the compile fix or by the fs-evidence changes in the same wave - verified by inspecting each failure.

FAILURES:
1. identity_migration::tests::source_generation_refuses_updates_deletes_and_rowid_reuse - 'no such column: rowid in table ops'. Upstream FrankenSQLite gap (no implicit rowid on that table), same sibling-drift class as the execute() signature change.
2. travel::tests::gc_reclaims_only_unreferenced
3. conformance: qty_crosswalk_artifacts_are_gc_roots
4. conformance: runtime_state_artifacts_are_gc_roots
   (2-4 are GC/reachability-root related and likely one root cause.)
5. identity_migration: exact_evidence_binding_freezes_bytes_and_preserves_receipt_ambiguity - panics at tests/identity_migration.rs:688 'a bound evidence body must not be silently reinterpreted': put_extension with a DIFFERENT body for an already-bound evidence name is expected to be refused and is not.

NOTE ON (5): if confirmed, that is itself a claim-integrity defect (a bound evidence body silently reinterpreted = a durable record asserting provenance it no longer has). It is deliberately NOT labelled claim-integrity yet - the class requires a verified reachable repro and a stated honest claim per docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md, and this is currently only a red test. Triage it against the decision rules and, if it holds, re-file/label with severity + repro + honest claim.

WHY P1: fs-ledger is a load-bearing HELM crate and these are real reds, but the crate was already effectively untested, so this is not a new regression - it is newly VISIBLE debt.

DONE WHEN: each of the 5 is either fixed or has a named, justified exemption; sibling-drift items (1) should be routed to the frankensqlite pin rather than worked around locally.
close_reason: Closed ALL-FIVE-DISPOSED on fresh receipts (BeigeGlacier, 2026-08-26, cargo test -p fs-ledger via rch: 309 passed / 0 failed / 16 suites). Item 1 identity_migration::tests::source_generation_refuses_updates_deletes_and_rowid_reuse now passes (log line: ok; sibling-drift 'no such column: rowid' resolved upstream). Item 5 exact_evidence_binding_freezes_bytes_and_preserves_receipt_ambiguity passes => the hypothesized claim-integrity defect (silent bound-body reinterpretation) does NOT materialize at current HEAD.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED. The baseline was actually 7 failures, not 5 — the bead mis-attributed two to tests/conformance (they are tests/crosswalk.rs and tests/state_checkpoint.rs) and missed vc_005_gc_never_collects_live_branch_artifacts plus ledger_008_event_throughput_ledgered.

FIXED (2): (5) exact_evidence_binding — a genuine claim-integrity defect, confirmed and filed as frankensim-ledger-bound-evidence-reinterpret-vs6u7 (severity:default-path), fixed at b4ece64b. (1) source_generation rowid probe — FrankenSQLite's UPDATE assignment-target resolver never resolves the implicit rowid/_rowid_/oid alias (upstream site: fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs collect_update_assignment_columns -> TableSchema::column_index, declared columns only). The test was ADAPTED not weakened at 60b3041b: the alias probe is now a tripwire asserting the engine refuses the statement and that the refusal does not advance the generation, and the substantive invariant is still asserted through the executable spelling. Sound because the V20 guard is a value-aware AFTER UPDATE trigger keyed on the value, not the spelling.

STILL RED (4), deliberately not weakened: gc_reclaims_only_unreferenced, qty_crosswalk_artifacts_are_gc_roots, runtime_state_artifacts_are_gc_roots, vc_005_gc_never_collects_live_branch_artifacts. ONE upstream root cause — FrankenSQLite runs ON DELETE CASCADE actions BEFORE deleting the parent row while real SQLite runs them after, so fs-ledger's conditional sidecar guards fire during the legitimate cascade. title: Low-Mach aeroacoustic source models: Curle analogy over fs-lbm jet flows
description:
GAP: fs-lbm is honest incompressible low-Mach — no acoustic radiation from flow. Full compressible LES of a flute jet is neither feasible nor needed; but the program needs jet/edge-tone SOURCE models (flute embouchure, recorder labium, air noise) grounded in real flow physics rather than hand-tuned noise.

Smartest implementation (honest hybrid, standard aeroacoustics practice):
1. Acoustic-analogy post-processing on fs-lbm: compute incompressible unsteady base flow (2D jet-labium at instrument-relevant Re), extract Lighthill/Curle source terms (surface pressure on the labium = dipole sources dominate at low Mach), and radiate via the free-space Green's function — this SPLITTING (incompressible CFD + analogy) is exactly what low-Mach aeroacoustics does professionally, and it stays inside fs-lbm's honest contract because the acoustics never enters the flow solve.
2. Deliverables tuned to synthesis, not CFD glory: (a) dipole source spectra vs jet velocity/geometry (the fitted noise-source tables the synths consume); (b) jet receptivity/amplification curves (gain and phase of jet displacement vs frequency — the Rayleigh instability data behind the jet-drive delay line's nonlinearity); (c) edge-tone Strouhal staging vs distance/velocity to validate the base flow against classic experiments.
3. Verification chain: fs-lbm jet vs analytic Bickley-jet instability growth rates (linear regime); edge-tone stages vs published Brown/Coltman data; grid-convergence of source spectra with certified Mach<0.3 diagnostics recorded per run.
4. Explicit refusals: no claim of absolute SPL prediction; spectra are relative/shape authorities plus scaling laws (U^6 dipole power) — state it in every output.

Acceptance: Bickley-jet growth-rate fixture within authored tolerance; edge-tone Strouhal numbers reproduce published staging within scatter; source-spectra convergence under grid refinement recorded; a fitted flute-noise table (spectrum shape vs blowing pressure) exported with provenance and consumed by a demo synth; Mach/incompressibility diagnostics green on every run; scope-refusal text present in outputs (marketing-claim mutation caught by validator).

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). CORRECTION (real 2D trap): Curle's analogy in 2D uses the 2D Green's function — line sources with cylindrical spreading and a non-compact time tail — NOT the 3D 1/r form; naive 3D formulas over 2D LBM data give wrong spectra slopes. Smartest handling: stay in the FREQUENCY domain where the 2D Green's function is the Hankel function H0(kr) (clean to implement, no tail convolution), and state that absolute levels need the 2D-to-3D span correction (Oberai-style) — which is another reason outputs are shape/scaling authorities, never absolute SPL. Add this to the refusal text.
Pilot intel: the fs-lbm slot pilot (2026-08-06) ran 640x128 D2Q9 at Re 50-202, Mach <= 0.122, flux imbalance 0.7-6% — the imbalance at Re 200 (6%) shows outlet BC reflection sensitivity; the source-extraction runs need the sponge/absorbing-layer treatment BEFORE trusting spectra (add: absorbing-layer implementation with reflection-coefficient measurement as an explicit sub-task and unit test).
Testing and logging: unit tests (Bickley growth rates; H0 Green's function vs reference values; absorbing-layer reflection coefficient < authored ceiling across frequencies); e2e casebook: jet-labium sweep -> surface-pressure dipole spectra -> JSON-lines per run (Re, Mach max, imbalance, grid, spectra hashes, convergence deltas between grid levels); edge-tone staging table vs Brown/Coltman with logged stage boundaries. Every output artifact embeds the honest-scope statement; a validator test asserts its presence (the marketing-mutation guard). Mutations: 3D-Green's-function swap (spectral slope test catches), disabled sponge (reflection test catches), Mach-cap bypass refused.

title: Distributed unilateral contact with energy-consistent collision potentials
description:
GAP: fs-contact covers certified CCD and analytic point-contact laws (Hertz, Hunt-Crossley); fs-tribo covers partial-slip point patches. Missing: DISTRIBUTED unilateral contact along lines/surfaces with friction — string-fretboard rattle, sitar/tanpura bridge (jawari), snare wires, reed-lay beating along a curved facing, fingerboard buzz. These distributed collisions are signature timbres.

Smartest implementation:
1. Penalty-potential collisions with energy-consistent discretization (Bilbao-Chatziioannou): contact force from a one-sided power-law potential phi(eta) = K*[eta]_+^alpha, integrated with a discrete-gradient scheme so contact adds/removes exactly the ledgered energy — no LCP machinery needed, provably stable, and the published standard for musical collisions. Fits the pHS bead as a switching resistive-capacitive port.
2. Distributed discretization: contact potential evaluated per collocation point along the obstacle (fret line, bridge curve, lay profile) against the string/reed displacement field; obstacle geometry as polyline/spline with per-point gap.
3. Friction where it matters: tangential Coulomb regularized (or Cattaneo-Mindlin from fs-tribo at patch level) for bow-string later — but SEPARATE bead-of-its-own if bowing becomes a target; keep this bead normal-contact-first, state it.
4. Implicit solve per step: local Newton on the contact nonlinearity (structure linear part prefactored), iteration/convergence bounds frozen in the API contract (the jazz program's solver laws apply).

Acceptance: single-point bouncing-ball-on-spring analytic energy/restitution fixture; string-against-flat-fret rattle conserves energy to epsilon with the discrete-gradient form (explicit-integration mutation visibly grows energy, caught); jawari-style graded bridge produces the documented spectral enrichment vs a hard point bridge (qualitative literature fixture with quantified band energies); iteration caps never exceeded across a velocity sweep; determinism bitwise.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) the contact stiffness/exponent (K, alpha) per obstacle material pair comes from the instrument-matdb bead where available (felt, ebony, bone) — wire the lookup, log the provenance id used; (b) penetration diagnostics: max penetration depth per block logged, with an authored ceiling that flags (not refuses) stiff-parameter inadequacy; (c) the Newton solve shares the frozen-iteration-budget law: budget, per-step iteration histogram, and fallback behavior all logged and capped (no wall-clock cutoffs).
Testing and logging: unit tests (single-point potential force vs closed form; discrete-gradient contact energy exactness on the bouncing fixture; polyline gap computation vs analytic geometry); property tests (energy monotonicity with loss > 0 across random obstacle profiles, seeded; grid-refinement convergence of contact force distribution); e2e casebook: string-over-24-fret rattle at three excitation levels -> JSON-lines (per-block contact events, energy ledger, max penetration, iteration histogram) + jawari fixture band-energy table vs the hard-bridge control. Mutations: explicit integration (energy growth caught), dropped [.]_+ one-sidedness (attraction detected), budget exceeded path.

title: 1D viscothermal duct/horn acoustics: TMM, tone-hole junctions, radiation loads
description:
GAP: no 1D duct/horn acoustics with viscothermal losses — the workhorse of wind-instrument physics (bores, tone holes, flares) is absent. This is the highest value-per-effort acoustic facility for the music program and broadly useful (mufflers, HVAC, waveguides).

Smartest implementation:
1. Transfer-matrix method (TMM) over cylinder/cone segments with EXACT Zwikker-Kosten viscothermal wave numbers (complex Bessel-function-based wide-tube approximations with certified validity ranges; fs-math supplies the special functions or add Kelvin functions) — this reproduces measured input impedances of real instruments to a few cents and is the mature-literature standard (openwind, Chaigne-Kergomard).
2. Tone holes as T-junction transfer matrices with shunt/series lumped elements; the compact-limit inertance end corrections come from the Laplace BEM recipe already validated in the jazz-studio program (flanged 0.8216a reproduced) — wire that in as the geometry-to-inertance front end.
3. Radiation load: unflanged/flanged pipe analytic impedances (Levine-Schwinger fits with stated validity), later replaceable by the Helmholtz BEM bead's computed loads.
4. Horn flares: conical TMM is exact; add the multimodal (mode-matching) expansion ONLY if a validation gap at strong flares demands it — defer honestly, record the trigger condition (bell mismatch > authored tolerance).
5. Outputs: input impedance Z_in(f), reflection functions (for waveguide runtime lowering via the vector-fitting bead), pressure transfer to the bell.

Acceptance: cylinder closed-form impedance matches Zwikker-Kosten analytics to 1e-10 (self-consistency); cone vs published analytic cone impedance; a full clarinet-like fingering lattice reproduces published measured impedance-peak frequencies within authored cents tolerances (provenance-pinned dataset); loss-model mutation (dropped thermal term) shifts peaks/widths detectably and is caught; every fixture states its validity envelope.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Pilot intel: the compact-limit end-correction front end is now VALIDATED numerics (jazz-program pilot: closed-body added-mass route reproduced the PISTON/uniform-profile disc aperture inertance, delta = 0.86416a vs the analytic 8/(3pi)a = 0.84883a, +1.8% with clean h-convergence). REVIEW ROUND 2 precision: that validated value is the uniform-velocity-profile disc limit, NOT the flanged-pipe 0.8216a constant — the pipe-mouth case (non-uniform profile from duct mode matching) hit fs-bem near-field work caps before converging, so pipe-mode-matched end corrections need either mode-matched boundary conditions in the driver or the crate's work-cap envelope raised; treat 0.8216a as a still-open pilot target, and calibrate TMM tone-hole inertances against the disc-limit validation plus literature until it lands. Also confirmed by local-mirror grep: fs-math has NO Bessel/Kelvin functions, so the special-function sub-task in (c) is definitely live, not conditional. Additions: (a) state the T-junction sign/impedance convention (series vs shunt element placement) once in the crate docs with a diagram, because half of all TMM bugs are convention bugs; (b) bore geometry input as a simple typed segment list (cylinder/cone radius-length records) — no CAD; (c) Kelvin/Bessel special functions: verify fs-math coverage first; if missing, implement with ULP-budgeted tests per fs-math conventions (that sub-task belongs to this bead, state it); (d) temperature/humidity as explicit parameters (c, rho, viscosity from published formulas) since tuning claims depend on them.
Testing and logging: unit tests (Zwikker-Kosten wavenumber vs high-precision reference across tube radii/frequencies; single-segment transfer matrices vs closed forms; junction continuity laws); metamorphic tests (segment splitting invariance: one cylinder = two half-cylinders chained, to 1e-12; reciprocity of transfer matrices); e2e casebook: full clarinet-like lattice -> Z_in(f) sweep -> peak table vs provenance-pinned published measurement, JSON-lines per fingering (peak freqs/cents deviations, Q's, magnitudes, work counters). Log the validity-envelope check per segment (wide-tube approximation bounds) and refuse outside with named codes. Mutations: dropped thermal loss term, flipped junction sign, missing end correction — each caught by named fixtures with logged deltas.

title: Helmholtz BEM with Burton-Miller: radiation impedance and directivity
description:
GAP: no acoustic wave solver of any kind. fs-bem is Laplace-only; fs-fmm's kernel trait is structurally real-valued (excludes Helmholtz). Radiation impedance, radiativity/directivity, and diffraction are unreachable — yet they are the difference between a simulated soundboard and a heard one.

Smartest implementation:
1. Complex-kernel Helmholtz BEM as an fs-bem extension: collocation panels (reuse geometry/quadrature machinery), CBIE+HBIE Burton-Miller combination to kill fictitious-frequency breakdown (mandatory — instrument bodies are analyzed across wide bands where fictitious frequencies WILL land), with the standard alpha = i/k coupling. REVIEW ROUND 2: the sign of alpha depends on the chosen time convention (i/k under e^{-i omega t}; conjugate under e^{+i omega t}) and a wrong sign silently DEGRADES conditioning below plain CBIE instead of fixing it — pin the convention once in the crate docs and add a unit test asserting the BM system's condition number beats CBIE's at a fictitious frequency (the sign-flip mutation then fails loudly).
2. Complex dense solve first (fs-la complex LU exists) — instrument-scale surface meshes (few thousand panels) are fine dense; wideband directional FMM is explicitly deferred (record it), do not block on it.
3. Outputs that the music program actually consumes: (a) radiation impedance matrices at the structural interface (feeds the vibroacoustic-coupling bead); (b) far-field directivity extracted to spherical-harmonic coefficient tables per frequency (feeds runtime stereo/space rendering); (c) radiated-power ratios (radiation efficiency per mode).
4. Validation: pulsating/oscillating sphere analytic solutions (monopole/dipole radiation impedance), circular piston in baffle (Rayleigh), fictitious-frequency stress test on a sphere at its interior resonance wavenumbers — Burton-Miller must hold where plain CBIE visibly fails (that contrast IS the near-miss fixture).
5. Reciprocity + passivity checks: Re(Z_rad) >= 0 at all frequencies; symmetric impedance matrices to discretization tolerance.

Acceptance: sphere/piston fixtures within authored tolerance over ka in [0.05, 5]; CBIE-alone fails at fictitious frequencies while Burton-Miller passes (mutation-style contrast); directivity tables reproduce known dipole patterns; passivity/reciprocity checks green; work/memory bounds recorded.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Pilot intel folded in (2026-08-06 jazz-program pilots): (a) fs-bem's Laplace side validated the closed-body added-mass route to +1.8% on aperture end corrections, but the mixed flanged-pipe geometry hit the crate's M2L/near-field work-cap refusals at >=3456 panels — the Helmholtz extension MUST budget for near-field pair work explicitly and prefer closed-body formulations where possible; document the work-cap envelope in the public API and emit the cap diagnostics in evidence rather than refusing opaquely. (b) Out-of-workspace scratch drivers need FRANKENSIM_DEPGRAPH_SALT exported (fs-la build.rs gate) — document in the crate README's driver-authoring section.
Additions: (c) singular/near-singular quadrature is the correctness heart — polar-coordinate singularity cancellation for self-panels, adaptive subdivision for near-singular pairs (thin bodies!), each with its own convergence unit test; (d) condition-number and discretization-density (panels-per-wavelength) diagnostics logged per solve; refuse below 6 panels/wavelength with a named code rather than silently degrading.
Testing and logging: unit tests (kernel values vs closed forms, quadrature convergence on singular integrals, Burton-Miller assembly symmetries); analytic suite (pulsating/oscillating sphere, baffled piston) across ka in [0.05,5] with per-ka JSON evidence rows (panels, panels-per-wavelength, condition estimate, relative error); the fictitious-frequency contrast test (CBIE fails, BM passes at sphere interior resonances) as a named near-miss pair; reciprocity/passivity property tests on random scatterer meshes (seeded). E2e casebook: mesh -> impedance matrix -> directivity SH table -> JSON-lines with hashes, timings, memory, and the work-cap headroom. Mutations: dropped hypersingular term (fictitious-frequency test must fail), conjugated kernel, wrong alpha sign.

title: Populate fs-matdb with provenance-pinned instrument materials incl. loss factors
description:
GAP: fs-matdb's schema is excellent (dims-checked, license-gated, provenance-complete) but its seed data is aerospace/tribology/magnetics — no woods, no loss factors, no Q, no sound speeds, `young_modulus` appears once. Instrument simulation dies without material truth.

Smartest implementation:
1. Populate with provenance-pinned instrument materials, each with uncertainty ranges (min/typ/max) and moisture/frequency qualifiers where the source gives them: TONEWOODS orthotropic sets (Sitka/Engelmann spruce, maple, Indian rosewood, mahogany, ebony, cedar): E_L/E_R/E_T, G_LR/G_LT/G_RT, nu's, rho, and loss factors eta_L/eta_R vs frequency where published. Primary sources: Wegst "Wood for sound" (2006), Brémaud's tonewood database publications, Haines, Hearmon, USDA Wood Handbook (public domain) — pin DOI/URL, retrieval date, license class per row.
2. Strings: steel (music wire), phosphor bronze, nylon, PVF (fluorocarbon), wound-string effective density/stiffness models; gut. Felt (piano hammer): Stulov/Giordano published force-compression parameters. Cane (Arundo donax) for reeds: E across/along, density, moisture sensitivity. Membranes: calfskin, Mylar. Metals for bars/bells: aluminum, bronze (bell bronze 80/20), brass, silver — with thermoelastic parameters (the visco-damping bead's Zener formula consumes them).
3. Schema extensions ONLY where forced: frequency-dependent loss factor field (table or fractional-Zener params — coordinate with the visco-damping bead's model IDs), moisture content qualifier, grain-angle convention documented once and enforced by validators.
4. Every value crosses the existing license gate; no scraped proprietary datasheets; uncertainty honesty (wood scatters +-20% — the ranges ARE the data).

Acceptance: >=25 materials with complete orthotropic/isotropic sets and provenance rows passing the existing validators; loss-factor data for at least spruce/maple/aluminum/bronze; cross-checks (E_L/rho sound speed vs published c values within stated scatter); a consuming demo (plate bead computes a spruce top's modes from db values alone); license-gate green; per-row mutation (unit swap) caught by dims checks.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) machine-readable UNITS AND AXIS CONVENTION file (L/R/T grain axes mapping to the plate bead's material frame) shipped beside the data — the cross-bead consumer contract; (b) each wood row carries moisture content and the reference condition (12% MC standard) explicitly; density-specific values (E/rho) included where sources give them since they transfer better across specimens; (c) a small "derived quantities" validator: sound speeds c_L = sqrt(E_L/rho), characteristic impedances, and the radiation ratio R = c_L/rho — computed and compared against published ranges as a sanity gate on every row (catches unit slips better than dims checks alone); (d) source tiering logged per row (measured-primary / handbook-secondary / estimated) so fits can weight by data quality.
Testing and logging: unit tests (schema round-trip; dims checks per field; derived-quantity gates with per-row JSON verdicts); the consuming e2e (spruce top plate modes from db values alone through the plates bead) logs which rows/tiers were consumed and the resulting mode table; license-gate run recorded. Mutations: unit swap (GPa->MPa caught by derived-speed gate), axis swap (E_L<E_R flags), missing provenance row (validator refuses).

title: Experimental modal identification: Loewner + RFP with stabilization and MAC gates
description:
GAP: no experimental modal identification — nothing fits measured FRFs (impact-hammer/laser data of real instruments) into modes (f_k, eta_k, phi_k) or state-space models. Without it the foundry cannot CALIBRATE simulated bodies against real ones, and the whole simulate-vs-measure loop (the jazz program's "measure, never assume" law) has no measurement-side tooling.

Smartest implementation:
1. Loewner-framework identification as the core (matrix pencil from frequency-response data — modern, deterministic, handles MIMO, no iterative starts) plus rational-fraction-polynomial (orthogonal Forsythe polynomials) as the classical cross-check; two independent identifiers catching each other, same pattern as the vector-fitting bead (share the pole/residue post-processing with it — one codebase, two front doors).
2. Mode-quality gates: stabilization diagram automation (pole stability across model orders), MAC (modal assurance criterion) matrix for shape independence, complex-mode-indicator function for close modes — with machine-readable accept/reject per pole, no analyst hand-waving.
3. Uncertainty: residual-based confidence intervals per (f_k, eta_k), noise-floor estimation from off-resonance bands; fits refuse when SNR is insufficient (named refusal, per FrankenSim law).
4. Bridge to the rest: identified modes flow into the same modal data structures the eig/plate beads emit, so calibration is literally diffing two instances of one type (simulated vs measured mode tables with MAC pairing).

Acceptance: synthetic known-answer FRFs (10 modes, added noise sweeps) recovered within certified intervals down to authored SNR; close-mode pair (0.5% separation) resolved where single-identifier runs fail (the cross-check near-miss); stabilization automation matches hand-picked poles on a published benchmark dataset; MAC pairing of a simulated-vs-perturbed-simulated plate flags the perturbed modes; refusal fires below the SNR floor.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) input formats: plain CSV/JSON FRF tables only in v1 (freq, complex H, coherence per channel) — no UFF/proprietary formats, state it; coherence, when present, feeds the per-band SNR estimate; (b) exponential-window bias correction for impact-hammer data (added damping from windowing is a classic systematic error — correct eta_k analytically and log both raw and corrected); (c) share the pole/residue core with the vector-fitting bead as one module with two front ends (explicitly the same code, tested once).
Testing and logging: unit tests (Loewner pencil on exact rational data recovers poles to 1e-10; RFP orthogonal-polynomial conditioning vs naive powers demonstrated; MAC of identical/orthogonal shapes = 1/0); property tests (noise-robustness curves: recovered-parameter error vs SNR across seeds, monotone); e2e casebook: synthetic 10-mode MIMO FRF + noise -> stabilization diagram -> auto-accepted poles -> JSON-lines (per-order pole tables, stability flags, MAC matrix, confidence intervals, SNR map, window-correction deltas); published-benchmark comparison logged. Mutations: disabled window correction (eta bias detected vs known-answer), close-mode pair with single identifier (cross-check divergence flagged), sub-SNR refusal path.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: DOCTRINE SHARPENED (owner, 2026-08-08): NO instrument modules in FrankenSim, ever — no clarinet crate, no guitar code path. An instrument is a DESCRIPTION: a typed data artifact (fs-scenario / fs-project / fs-matdb layer) declaring geometry, composition, mechanical and material attributes, which COMPOSES the generic physics crates. Example target: 'pluck this guitar string while fretting at this pressure with a human finger' = generic prestressed-string dynamics + fs-contact Hertz/Hunt-Crossley with an indenter material card (human fingertip hardness from a matdb pack) + fs-tribo stick-slip + the plate/cavity/radiation chain — then simulate the actual emitted sound waves. title: Orthotropic plate/shell/stiffener elements with prestress and Leissa validation
description:
GAP: fs-solid is 2D, fixture-scale, statics-only; shell.rs self-declares "estimate-only, not a Kirchhoff-Love discretisation"; no orthotropy in bending, no stiffened panels, no curved shells. Instrument bodies ARE thin orthotropic stiffened plates/shells (guitar tops with bracing, violin arched plates, piano soundboards with ribs and downbearing, vibraphone bar undercuts).

Smartest implementation:
1. Plate bending: DKT (discrete Kirchhoff triangle) + MITC4 quad elements — both classical, locking-free, compact to implement, and well-documented; orthotropic bending stiffness D-matrix from ply/grain constants (fs-material supplies constants; the instrument-matdb bead supplies wood data).
2. Stiffeners/bracing: offset Timoshenko beam elements rigidly coupled to plate nodes (eccentricity matters — braces raise stiffness asymmetrically); variable cross-section beams for vibraphone-bar undercuts and tapered braces (fs-feec 1D high-order machinery reusable here).
3. Curved/arched: flat-facet shell assembly first (DKT membrane+bending superposition, drilling-DOF stabilized) — honest about facet error; true curved shell elements only if a validation gap demands them.
4. Prestress: geometric stiffness from membrane pre-tension (piano soundboard downbearing, drumheads) — reuses the buckling K_G machinery; a drumhead is then just K_G-dominated with near-zero D, giving membranes for free.
5. Validation ladder: Leissa analytic plate tables (isotropic + orthotropic, multiple BCs), Timoshenko beam closed forms, stiffened-panel literature cases, THEN a real guitar-top mode-shape comparison from published holography data (provenance-pinned).

Acceptance: Leissa fixtures within authored tolerances at two mesh densities with h^2 (or better) trend; orthotropy mutation (swapped E_L/E_R) caught; bracing raises the right modes (literature case); prestressed membrane limit matches ideal-membrane analytics; all eigen runs through the vibration-eig facility with certified intervals.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) all material inputs through fs-qty dimensioned types; orthotropic D-matrix construction validated against hand-computed spruce values from the instrument-matdb bead (cross-bead fixture); (b) patch tests are mandatory gates (constant-curvature and rigid-body-motion patch tests per element type — the standard FEM correctness certificates); (c) element quality diagnostics (Jacobian bounds, aspect warnings) logged, refusing degenerate meshes with named codes; (d) mesh I/O minimal: structured quad/tri generators in-crate; no external mesh formats in v1 (state it).
Testing and logging: unit tests per element (stiffness/mass symmetry, patch tests, single-element eigenvalues vs closed form); convergence suite (Leissa cases at 3 mesh densities with observed-order assertion h^p, p>=2, logged as a convergence table in JSON evidence); prestress path vs analytic membrane limit; stiffened-panel literature case with mode-pairing MAC table logged. E2e casebook: geometry+material -> assembled pencil -> vibration-eig facility -> mode table + certified intervals, JSON-lines (element counts, assembly time, per-mode freq/interval/MAC-vs-reference). Mutations: swapped E_L/E_R, dropped drilling stabilization (spurious modes must be detected by the zero-energy-mode check), eccentricity zeroed on braces (mode shift assertion).

title: Port-Hamiltonian core: structural passivity, discrete gradients, preserving reduction
description:
STRATEGIC GAP: passivity in FrankenSim today is checked (audits, monotonicity evidence), not STRUCTURAL. Port-Hamiltonian systems (pHS) make passivity a property of the formulation itself: dx/dt = (J - R)*grad H(x) + G*u, y = G'*grad H(x), with J skew, R >= 0 — then ANY interconnection through power-conjugate ports is passive by construction, discrete gradients give energy-exact time stepping, and model reduction can preserve the structure. This is the deepest single upgrade for a "simulate everything" system and the natural completion of fs-couple's port taxonomy (fs-couple defines the vocabulary; pHS supplies the algebra).

Smartest implementation:
1. A pHS core type: storage (H, grad H with AD), structure matrices (J, R, G) — dense first; explicit constructors for the standard zoo (mass-spring-damper, LC/transmission-line, modal banks, nonlinear springs via non-quadratic H).
2. Discrete-gradient integrators (midpoint discrete gradient / average vector field) that conserve/dissipate H EXACTLY in discrete time — this subsumes and strengthens the symplectic story for damped-driven systems (symplectic methods do not handle R; discrete gradients do). Wire as an fs-time strategy.
3. Power-preserving interconnection: compose two pHS through a Dirac-structure port map and get a pHS back — fs-couple's ConservativeJunction becomes an instance, with the watt-dimension checks retained as admission gates.
4. Structure-preserving model reduction: effort-constraint or spectral-factor balanced truncation variants that keep (J,R) form, so reduced instrument models remain passive with certified H-error bounds — feeding real-time synthesis with provably-safe reduced bodies.
5. Nonlinear exciters (reed, lip, bow, hammer) recast as pHS components with contact/friction as resistive/switching ports — aligns with published pHS musical-acoustics literature (Falaize-Helie piano/brass work) and makes whole-instrument energy audits trivial.

Acceptance: discrete-gradient integrator conserves quadratic H to machine epsilon undriven and matches ledgered dissipation exactly with R > 0; interconnection of two known pHS reproduces the monolithic system's trajectories; reduced modal bank keeps passivity (Hamiltonian test from the vector-fitting bead) and meets its H-error bound; a reed-as-pHS demo reproduces the existing reed solver's steady states; mutation (symmetrized J / sign-flipped R) caught by energy audit.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) constrained/DAE pHS (Dirac structures with algebraic constraints — e.g. rigid interconnection, Kirchhoff laws) explicitly DEFERRED to a follow-up with the trigger stated (first consumer needing constraints), so v1 stays ODE-form and shippable; (b) non-quadratic H requires the discrete-gradient formula choice to be pinned (Gonzalez midpoint discrete gradient) with its known order (2) documented; (c) the R >= 0 admission check runs at construction (symmetric eigen check with tolerance) and every interconnection re-verifies the composed structure matrices' properties — matching fs-couple's no-false-passivity discipline; (d) provide the modal-bank constructor as the first-class bridge from the eig/plate beads (mass-normalized modes -> canonical pHS).
Testing and logging: unit tests (J skewness/R semidefiniteness admission incl. rejection cases; discrete-gradient exactness on quadratic H to machine eps; Gonzalez gradient consistency on non-quadratic H at order 2 via Richardson); property tests (interconnection associativity on random pHS triples, seeded; power balance u'y = dH/dt + dissipation per step to eps); e2e casebook: reed-as-pHS driving a 24-mode bore bank -> steady-state amplitudes vs the existing solver -> JSON-lines (per-step H, dissipation ledger, port powers, iteration counts). Reduction path logs H-error bound vs realized error on a validation input. Mutations: symmetrized J, sign-flipped R, broken interconnection map — each caught by the energy audit with named codes.

title: Standards-anchored psychoacoustic metrics: loudness, sharpness, roughness
description:
GAP: fitting objectives are purely physical (spectra, decay); nothing measures what a listener HEARS. The jazz program's Pareto-fitting methodology needs perceptual axes, and a simulate-everything system should score sounds like standards do.

Smartest implementation (small, standards-anchored, no ML):
1. Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1) — stationary first, time-varying second: third-octave/critical-band decomposition, specific loudness, total sones. Deterministic table-driven implementation with published test signals as fixtures.
2. Sharpness (DIN 45692 weighting over specific loudness), roughness and fluctuation strength (Daniel-Weber style modulation analysis) — the axes that separate "warm" from "harsh" and capture beating/tremolo salience.
3. Tonality/harmonicity (spectral-peak vs noise separation reusing the alias/HNR extractor patterns from the jazz program) and attack sharpness (log-attack-time per timbre-toolbox definitions).
4. All metrics ship as pure functions over PCM + rate with certified fixture answers from the standards' published test cases; every metric declares its validity envelope (mono, free-field assumption, level calibration required — refuse when uncalibrated absolute claims are requested, per the honest-scope law).
5. Consumption: these become objective axes in the NSGA-II Pareto fits and columns in listening-evidence tables — never a substitute for human listening (state it in the module docs; the jazz program's law).

Acceptance: ISO 532-1 published test signals reproduce reference sones within the standard's tolerance; DIN sharpness test values match; roughness of 100% AM tones peaks at ~70 Hz modulation as published; determinism bitwise; uncalibrated-absolute-SPL request refuses with named code; docs carry the not-a-substitute-for-listening statement (mutation: removed statement caught by doc validator if present, else test asserts the docstring).

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) calibration contract made explicit in types: metrics that need absolute level (loudness in sones) take a calibration struct (dB SPL at digital full scale) and REFUSE without it; level-relative metrics (sharpness ratio changes, roughness) work uncalibrated and say so in their signatures; (b) sample-rate handling pinned: internal resample to the standard's reference rate with a tested resampler rather than per-rate filter redesign (determinism preserved, one code path); (c) batch API over PCM sets for the Pareto-fitting consumer with stable ordering.
Testing and logging: unit tests (ISO 532-1 published test cases within standard tolerance; DIN sharpness references; roughness AM peak at ~70 Hz; resampler passband/stopband specs); property tests (loudness monotone in level; scale invariance of level-relative metrics; bitwise determinism across repeats); e2e casebook: a rendered instrument-note set -> full metric battery -> JSON-lines per clip (all metrics, calibration used, validity flags, timings) suitable for direct use as Pareto objective columns. Mutations: dropped critical-band term (test-case deltas exceed tolerance), uncalibrated-absolute misuse refused, resampler bypass caught by rate-mismatch test.

title: Supernodal sparse LDLT with AMD ordering and inertia (audit fs-solver first)
description:
GAP (verify first): fs-sparse is iterative-only (COO/CSR/BSR/SELL, PCG, ILU0 smoother, SA-AMG); the survey noted sparse direct factorization "lives in fs-solver" — AUDIT fs-solver's actual coverage before building. Shift-invert modal analysis, plate/shell statics, and Newton loops on stiff assemblies all want a robust sparse symmetric factorization.

Smartest implementation (if the audit finds it missing or weak):
1. Supernodal sparse LDLT (symmetric indefinite with Bunch-Kaufman-ish 2x2 pivoting restricted to supernodes) — indefinite support matters because shift-invert (K - sigma*M) is indefinite for interior shifts, and inertia (from D) is exactly what the eigenproblem bead's slicing certification needs. Cholesky alone is not enough.
2. AMD (approximate minimum degree) ordering, dependency-free port (~600 lines from the classic algorithm), plus optional nested dissection later.
3. Deterministic by construction (no thread-dependent pivot order in v1). Factor and solve are separate API stages: each shift sigma requires its own factorization of (K - sigma*M), and each factorization then serves many right-hand-side solves; make that cost model explicit in the API docs so callers batch RHS per shift.
4. Out-of-scope honestly: unsymmetric multifrontal, GPU. State it.

title: Passive rational approximation: vector fitting + Loewner with passivity enforcement
description:
GAP: nothing turns a computed/measured frequency response (impedance, mobility, reflection function) into a RUNTIME-REALIZABLE passive filter. This is the single most valuable missing bridge between foundry and real-time synthesis — every offline result (BEM radiation load, TMM bore impedance, coupled-body mobility) must become a compact stable state-space/biquad chain to be heard.

Smartest implementation:
1. Vector fitting (Gustavsen-Semlyen) with relaxed non-triviality constraint: iterative pole relocation fitting sum_k r_k/(s - p_k) + d + s*e to tabulated H(j*omega); complex-conjugate pole enforcement, stable-pole flipping. ~400 lines over fs-la least squares. Add the Loewner-framework alternative (matrix-pencil from data) as a cross-check second front end — two independent identifications catching each other's artifacts.
2. PASSIVITY ENFORCEMENT as a separate certified pass: check Re(H) >= 0 (or |S| <= 1 in scattering form) on a dense grid PLUS Hamiltonian-matrix eigenvalue test for exact crossing detection; repair via convex residue perturbation (QP over residues minimizing L2 deviation subject to passivity at violation bands, iterated with the Hamiltonian test). Without this, fitted radiation loads WILL create energy in a feedback loop — the jazz program's passivity laws make this non-negotiable.
3. Discretization: s-to-z via bilinear transform with frequency pre-warping at the band of interest, or direct z-domain vector fitting; emit both state-space (A,B,C,D) and factored biquad-cascade forms with coefficient quantization sensitivity reported.
4. Scattering-form option (fit the reflection function directly with |S|<=1 enforcement) — the natural form for digital-waveguide termination filters.

Acceptance: known-answer fits (synthetic 6-pole passive impedance recovered to 1e-9; measured-style noisy data fit within noise floor); passivity repair demonstrably fixes a deliberately active fit (near-miss fixture) with Hamiltonian test green after repair; bilinear-discretized filter matches continuous response within authored band tolerance; a TMM clarinet input impedance (duct bead) lowers to a <=24-pole passive filter whose impedance peaks sit within authored cents tolerances; determinism (seeded starts, bitwise repeat).

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) weighting options are not optional polish — inverse-magnitude weighting is what makes impedance fits musically honest at antiresonances (which set waveguide reflection nulls); expose per-sample weights with three presets (uniform, 1/|H|, log-band) and log which was used; (b) DC and asymptotic constraints (fix d >= 0, e >= 0 for impedance-form passivity of the direct terms) enforced in the LS solve, not post-hoc; (c) model-order selection automated: fit at ascending order until the weighted error plateaus, log the order-vs-error curve, refuse overfit (error below data noise floor estimate); (d) the Hamiltonian passivity test needs the descriptor-form variant for improper systems (e != 0) — state and test it.
Testing and logging: unit tests (pole relocation convergence on synthetic data; conjugacy/stability enforcement; QP repair KKT residuals); property tests (fit-of-a-fit idempotence; scaling covariance H -> a*H); the two-front-end cross-check (vector fitting vs Loewner agree within authored tolerance on clean data, disagree diagnostically on aliased data — logged comparison table). E2e casebook: TMM clarinet impedance -> 24-pole passive fit -> bilinear discretization -> impedance re-measured from the digital filter -> JSON-lines (order curve, band errors in cents at peaks, passivity margins before/after repair, coefficient quantization sensitivity at f32/f64). Mutations: disabled repair on an active fit (Hamiltonian test must fail), dropped prewarp (peak cents error must exceed gate), weight preset swap detection.

title: First-class vibration eigenproblem facility with certified intervals and inertia slicing
description:
GAP: no vibration eigenproblem entry point exists — K*phi = omega^2*M*phi has no first-class facility (the buckling code in fs-solid is a pattern, not an API). Everything modal (bars, plates, soundboards, bells, resonators) needs this; it is also the most-requested generic structural facility.

Smartest implementation:
1. A `fs-modal` facility (new crate or fs-la module): generalized symmetric-definite eigensolver with three strategies auto-selected by size: dense (QZ-free: Cholesky reduction + symmetric QR, already mostly present), Lanczos with shift-invert for sparse K,M (needs sparse direct — see the sparse-factorization bead), and LOBPCG with AMG preconditioning for the largest problems (fs-sparse SA-AMG exists).
2. Shift-invert with SPECTRUM SLICING for wide mode ranges: factor (K - sigma*M) at a ladder of shifts, harvest each window, verify counts with Sylvester inertia from the LDLT — gives certified "no missed modes", which matters because a missed body mode is an audible hole.
3. Every eigenpair ships with the residual-derived certified interval (the fs-spectral CertifiedEigenvalue idea, generalized to the pencil): ||K*phi - lambda*M*phi|| / (phi' * M * phi) bounds.
4. Damped/complex extension: quadratic eigenproblem (M, C, K) via state-space linearization with structure-preserving scaling, for the viscoelastic bead's complex modes.

Acceptance: analytic fixtures (free-free beam, simply-supported plate via 5-point-squared identity, spring-mass chains with closed-form spectra); inertia-count certification catches a deliberately-skipped window (mutation); intervals contain the analytic values; quadratic path matches perturbation theory for light damping; scales to >=100k DoF with recorded work/memory bounds.

Additions: (a) matrix-free operator variant (user closure for K*x, M*x) so FD/spectral discretizations avoid assembly; (b) oracle cross-check per workspace convention: dense-path results verified against the frankenscipy sibling eigensolver in the oracle casebook (dev-dependency only, like fs-time's casebook); (c) mode-shape mass-normalization convention documented once (phi' M phi = 1) and enforced; (d) expose Sylvester inertia counts in the public result so downstream (spectrum slicing certification, sparse-direct bead) consumers get certified no-missed-modes evidence, not a boolean.
Testing and logging: unit tests per strategy (dense/Lanczos/LOBPCG) on analytic fixtures; metamorphic tests (spectral shift invariance: eig(K + c*M, M) = eig(K,M) + c; scaling covariance); e2e casebook: assemble a 100k-DoF FD plate pencil, slice three windows, verify counts vs inertia, emit JSON-lines per window (shift, factor time, iterations, residual norms, certified intervals, inertia counts, memory high-water). title: Modal vibroacoustic coupling: structure-cavity-radiation as fs-couple engine
description:
GAP: no fluid-structure/acoustic-structure coupling — a soundboard in vacuo is not an instrument. Needed: structure <-> interior cavity (Helmholtz + higher air modes) <-> exterior radiation, i.e. the guitar-box problem, the violin f-hole problem, the piano rim/soundboard-room problem.

Smartest implementation:
1. MODAL coupling (not monolithic FEM-BEM): project the coupled problem onto (structure modes from the plates-shells+eig beads) x (rigid-wall cavity modes from the same eig facility on the Laplacian) with the standard area-integral coupling matrix over the interface; Helmholtz resonator (f-hole/soundhole) enters as the cavity's lowest mode with a neck end-correction from the Laplace BEM recipe. This is cheap, certified (mode-truncation error observable by convergence-in-N), and exactly the fs-couple port-thermodynamic pattern — build it as fs-couple's first real numerical engine rather than a new silo.
2. Exterior radiation: attach the Helmholtz-BEM bead's radiation impedance at the wet surface, reduced onto the structural modes (Z_rad projected). Frequency-domain first (FRFs, radiated power, driving-point mobilities); time-domain runtime realization goes through the vector-fitting bead.

Validation ladder: (a) analytic two-DOF limit — plate mode + Helmholtz resonance = the classic coupled-oscillator split (guitar T(1,1)_1/T(1,1)_2 pair) with closed-form frequency split vs coupling strength; (b) rectangular box with flexible top vs literature; (c) measured guitar-body driving-point mobility from a provenance-pinned publication.

title: Viscoelastic damping constitutive models: complex modulus, Prony, fractional Zener
description:
GAP (musical-acoustics program, requested by owner 2026-08-06 from the jazz-studio audit): FrankenSim has NO damping or viscoelastic constitutive model anywhere — zero Prony/Maxwell/Kelvin/loss-factor/complex-modulus content in fs-material. For instrument simulation, damping IS the decisive physics: it sets decay times, brightness-vs-time, and the difference between spruce and plywood. It is also the top gap for any structural-dynamics claim generally.

Smartest implementation (in order):
1. fs-material gains a viscoelasticity module with THREE tiers: (a) frequency-domain complex modulus E*(omega) = E'(1 + i*eta(omega)) — the workhorse for modal synthesis: solvers consume eta(omega_k) per mode; (b) generalized Maxwell / Prony series with N certified terms for time-domain FEM (sum-of-exponentials internal variables, unconditionally stable convolution-free recursive update); (c) FRACTIONAL Zener (4-5 params) as the fitting-side canonical model — wood, polymers, and felt exhibit nearly-constant loss factor over decades of frequency, which integer-order Prony needs many terms to mimic but fractional models capture with 4 parameters. Implement the fractional kernel via provably-convergent sum-of-exponentials approximation (e.g. Jiang-Zhang-Zhang or de Hoop style quadrature of the spectral representation) with a certified truncation error bound, so tier (c) LOWERS to tier (b) for time stepping — one runtime path, two fitting front-ends.
2. AD tangents (fs-ad duals) through all three tiers so complex-modulus fits use exact gradients; verify_gradient gate mandatory.
3. Thermoelastic damping (Zener's classic formula for beams/plates) as an analytic closed-form contributor — it dominates in metal bars (vibraphone!) at low modes and is nearly free to add.
4. Energy accounting: each internal variable carries a dissipation ledger term so fs-couple window audits close; integrators (fs-time) must dissipate exactly the ledgered energy (test: single-mode Prony vs analytic complex eigenvalue).

Acceptance: analytic single-Maxwell and fractional-Zener known-answer fixtures (complex modulus vs closed form over 6 decades); Prony recursive update matches convolution reference to 1e-12; loss-factor plateau reproduced within authored tolerance by <=8 exponential terms with certified bound; modal-damping injection path produces complex eigenvalues matching perturbation theory for small eta; dissipation ledger closes per block; mutation controls (sign of internal-variable update, dropped term) each caught.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) tier 0 for completeness — classical Rayleigh (alpha*M + beta*K) and constant modal damping, trivial but must exist so users are not forced into Prony for quick studies; (b) the fractional->Prony lowering must state its certified validity band [f_lo, f_hi] in the emitted model and refuse evaluation outside it; (c) integrate with fs-time: galpha consumes C matrices, discrete-gradient (port-Hamiltonian bead) consumes R blocks — one damping definition, both consumers; (d) use fs-qty dimension checks on all moduli/viscosities.
Testing and logging requirements (workspace conventions: zero external deps, forbid(unsafe), deterministic, oracle casebooks): unit tests colocated per module (complex-modulus closed forms, Prony recursion vs direct convolution at 1e-12, fractional kernel vs high-precision quadrature reference); property tests (eta >= 0 over the stated band for all fitted models; monotone relaxation); an e2e casebook binary that fits a synthetic fractional-Zener dataset end-to-end (fit -> lower -> time-step -> re-measure eta(omega) from decay) and emits JSON-line evidence: input hash, seed, per-iteration fit residuals, term count, certified truncation bound, per-block dissipation ledger, wall/work counters. Every failure path logs the named refusal code and offending parameter. Mutation controls (sign flip in internal-variable update, dropped Prony term, out-of-band evaluation) each caught by a named test.

title: Von Karman modal plates and Kirchhoff-Carrier strings: geometric nonlinearity
description:
GAP: no geometric nonlinearity for thin structures — yet gongs, cymbals, steelpans, and hard-struck plates live on von Karman nonlinearity (mode coupling, pitch glide, the crash's spectral cascade), and even guitar tops at forte show tension modulation. fs-material has NeoHookean/MooneyRivlin 3D hyperelasticity but nothing for the thin-structure modal regime the music program needs.

Smartest implementation:
1. Von Karman plates by MODAL PROJECTION: precompute the cubic coupling tensor Gamma[p,q,r,s] (or the H[p,q,k] quadratic Airy-stress form) offline from the linear modes (plates-shells bead supplies them); runtime is then N coupled oscillators with quadratic/cubic terms — the Ducceschi-Touze/Bilbao formulation, proven for cymbals/gongs at N ~ 30-200.
2. Energy-conserving time stepping: invariant-preserving (Bilbao) or discrete-gradient (port-Hamiltonian bead — von Karman fits pHS with non-quadratic H) schemes; explicit schemes WILL blow up at crash dynamics, say so and refuse.
3. Coupling-tensor symmetries exploited for storage (Gamma fully symmetric pairs) and certified by discrete integration cross-checks (two independent quadratures agree).
4. String tension modulation (Kirchhoff-Carrier) as the 1D sibling: same machinery, one scalar coupling integral per string — gives electric-guitar/piano pitch glide nearly free.
5. Honest scope: no damage/plasticity/wrinkling; moderate-rotation regime stated.

Acceptance: single-mode Duffing limit matches analytic backbone curve (frequency vs amplitude) to authored tolerance; two-mode 1:2 internal resonance energy exchange matches literature; energy conserved to machine epsilon undamped (mutation: unsymmetrized tensor breaks it, caught); Kirchhoff-Carrier pitch glide matches perturbation formula; work/memory bounds vs N recorded.

POLISH ROUND (2026-08-06). Additions: (a) coupling-tensor computation is the expensive offline step — cache it keyed by (mesh hash, mode count, thickness) with a manifest, and log tensor symmetry residuals as the correctness certificate; (b) modal truncation for the Airy stress function is a SEPARATE count from the displacement modes (literature uses more stress modes); expose both and log the convergence-in-both-counts table; (c) damping enters per mode from the visco-damping bead (eta_k) — wire the type, do not invent a second damping representation.
Testing and logging: unit tests (tensor symmetries; single-mode Duffing backbone vs analytic; energy conservation undamped to eps over 1e6 steps); property tests (tensor recomputed by two independent quadrature orders agrees; amplitude-scaling covariance in the weakly nonlinear limit); e2e casebook: struck cymbal-like plate at three strike levels -> spectrograms' cascade onset level -> JSON-lines (modal energies over time, conservation residual, step rejections). Kirchhoff-Carrier string path: pitch-glide curve vs perturbation formula logged. Mutations: unsymmetrized tensor (conservation breaks, caught), swapped stress/displacement counts, explicit-integrator swap (must refuse at crash amplitudes per the stability guard).

title: FrankenSQLite runs ON DELETE CASCADE actions BEFORE deleting the parent row (blocks fs-ledger GC)
description:
UPSTREAM ENGINE DIVERGENCE, diagnosed while repairing frankensim-fs-ledger-latent-failures-xys1z. Four fs-ledger tests are red because of it and were deliberately left red rather than weakened.

DIVERGENCE: real SQLite runs sqlite3FkActions() AFTER OP_Delete removes the parent row. FrankenSQLite runs execute_fk_delete_action BEFORE the table-delete program (/Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs, Statement::Delete arm, ~25306-25318 vs ~25370).

CONSEQUENCE: fs-ledger's conditional sidecar guards are BEFORE DELETE triggers with WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM artifacts WHERE hash = OLD.artifact_hash) — they deliberately rely on the parent already being gone when the cascade fires (the design intent is stated verbatim in crates/fs-ledger/CONTRACT.md). Under FrankenSQLite's ordering the guard fires DURING the legitimate cascade and aborts every artifact deletion, so gc_unreferenced_artifacts is a hard outage.

PROOF: same DDL reduced to two tables. Real sqlite3 3.51.0 -> DELETE succeeds, artifacts_after=0, sidecar_after=0. FrankenSQLite -> FunctionError('artifact content identity is retained with its artifact'). Control: with PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF, deleting artifact-then-sidecar succeeds, confirming the guard WHEN is false once the parent is gone.

RED TESTS: travel::tests::gc_reclaims_only_unreferenced; qty_crosswalk_artifacts_are_gc_roots (tests/crosswalk.rs); runtime_state_artifacts_are_gc_roots (tests/state_checkpoint.rs); vc_005_gc_never_collects_live_branch_artifacts (tests/vcs.rs).

WHY NOT WORKED AROUND LOCALLY: under FrankenSQLite's ordering, 'cascade delete of the sidecar' and 'bare delete of the sidecar while the artifact lives' present IDENTICAL database state to the trigger, so no WHEN clause can separate them. PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF is a global connection setting and a documented no-op inside a transaction. Every legal delete order is blocked by either the FK or the guard.

TWO CORRECT FIXES:
(a) UPSTREAM (preferred): move check_fk_on_delete/execute_fk_delete_action to after the table-delete program and before the AFTER DELETE triggers, matching sqlite3FkActions() placement, preserving the multi-level propagation fix from abef2e0f7.
(b) fs-ledger schema v21 if upstream will not move: drop ON DELETE CASCADE and the FK from artifact_content_identities.artifact_hash; add AFTER DELETE ON artifacts to delete the sidecar (AFTER DELETE runs post-parent on BOTH engines, so the existing guard stays verbatim and still refuses a bare child delete); restore insert-side integrity with a BEFORE INSERT existence RAISE. That is a table rebuild (edge_content_identities and artifact_semantic_bindings hold FKs into it), a SCHEMA_VERSION bump, and a CONTRACT change — a durable-schema decision for the crate owner.

LATENT SCOPE: the same guard+cascade pattern exists at schema.rs:1117 (edge_content_identities v15), :1284 (op_content_identities v18) and :1330 (tune_content_identities v19). They are green today only by accident — nothing deletes edges, and ops/tune sidecars come from reconciliation rather than a dual-write trigger. Any path that deletes an op or tune row AFTER reconciliation hits the same wall.

NOT A REGRESSION: the ordering dates to d314d32bc (Feb 28) / abef2e0f7 (Mar 11). What is new is fs-ledger 9aa38f7e (Jul 18, 'code-first, batch-test pending') adding the guard, which turned a latent divergence into an outage.

title: fsqlite: parameters inside subqueries under a FROM-ful WHERE never bind (EXISTS and scalar forms)
description: Sibling of frankensim-lnbzs, discovered while pinning its fix at fsqlite HEAD b532362d4 (which adds the armed #[ignore] test fromful_where_subquery_params_bind in tests/fromless_where_subquery_params_contract.rs). PROBE MATRIX: seeded edges(op=1, artifact=32xAA). LITERAL subquery predicates return 1 row; ?N-int, ?N-blob, aliased and unaliased EXISTS, and scalar (SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE op=?1)>0 ALL return 0 rows. Controls: top-level WHERE op=?1 binds (C1); param outside + literal EXISTS inside works (C2); PREPARED-STATEMENT route fails identically (PR). EXPLAIN emits a CORRECT inline program (OpenRead 128 / Column / Variable(1) / Eq) — bindings are DROPPED AT EXECUTION, not miscompiled. Suspect the canonical-SQL program-cache compile wrapper (connection.rs ~51100): canonicalization inlines top-level placeholders but subquery Variables reach the VM with no bindings attached (engine.rs Variable handler: unbound reads NULL -> EXISTS false). sqlite3 returns 1 row everywhere. Same silent-data-loss family as lnbzs/lar1/i3m4i. FIX FLIPS THE ARMED TEST GREEN (cargo test -p fsqlite-core --test fromless_where_subquery_params_contract -- --ignored).
close_reason: Fixed upstream at frankensqlite 2bd64d114: prepare-time eager subquery rewrite no longer folds parameter-dependent subqueries without bindings; placeholder-bearing subqueries route through dispatch paths that bind at execution. (4) EVIDENCE THAT CANNOT ARRIVE. xtask/src/vv_scorecard.rs:25 calls build_scorecard(corpus(), adversarial_registry(), &[], &[]). The function signature (crates/fs-vvreg/src/scorecard.rs:577) accepts run_records and assessments, but NOTHING in the workspace produces them.
