THE SPINE. The one claim worth buying: a tracked .fsim project goes in, a junction temperature with a composed evidence colour AND its binding-constraint witness comes out, an evidence package is produced, and a standing gate fails the build if that ever stops being true.

GOVERNING IDEA. A task list is exactly what already failed: the beads existed and the swarm still aimed elsewhere. Steering must become a CHECKED ARTIFACT, not a judgment call, or the next reality check finds the same drift. Three mechanisms, all built from machinery this repo already has at L2: the spine is MEASURED (program-metrics), GATED (check-all), and FALSIFIABLE (executed falsifiers per acceptance case -- an end-to-end run that merely completes proves nothing, and this project's identity is 'no CLI-shaped mock').

1. A tracked .fsim -> package run completes with zero stage gaps.
2. The QoI carries a composed colour AND its binding-constraint witness.
3. An executed falsifier per acceptance case: perturb an input, the answer moves; sever an evidence slice, the claim demotes or refuses.

6. The capability-maturity promotion gate admits the L1->L3 move AND a blocked promotion is rehearsed (which also clears governance.capability-maturity's own stated L1 bar).

title: Bound TaylorModel1 order and non-finite admission
description:
TaylorModel1 admits arbitrary polynomial orders and non-finite scalar inputs through infallible constructors/operations. factorial overflows at order 171; reciprocal factorial then becomes zero, so exp/sin Lagrange terms can collapse instead of conservatively enclosing truncation. Arbitrary orders also permit unbounded allocation and polynomial work. Separately, CONTRACT.md still says no Taylor models while the type is public, and README calls the arbitrary-order implementation first-order.

Root fix: define and enforce a resource- and numerics-justified maximum order through fallible constructors/operations, reject non-finite domains/scalars before mutation/allocation, keep every admitted factorial/reciprocal finite and enclosure-valid, and make contract/README claims match the public surface. Do not weaken pure-Rust or evidence semantics.

Acceptance: exact max/max+1, order 0/1/170/171, NaN/infinity/domain edge, hostile allocation, exp/sin containment, deterministic replay, and no-partial-mutation tests; arbitrary-order requests fail structurally before allocation/work; contract states supported order, error model, and no-claim boundary.
close_reason: Bounded fallible Taylor admission, sound overflow handling, rigorous reciprocal-factorial/exp enclosures, downstream migration, and exact remote Taylor battery are complete.

title: WS2: CutFEM vector elasticity — Nitsche + ghost penalty on SDF cuts
description: WHY (reality check NO_BEAD gap 1 — the single dependency gating the MARQUEE demo): fs-topopt::marquee is heat-conduction-only because its own docs say elasticity rides CutFEM elasticity when it lands, and NOTHING was landing it. title: Pin a dated nightly toolchain to stop CI/local clippy drift
description:
## What
rust-toolchain.toml pins the floating 'nightly' channel. CI runners resolve today's nightly while local rch build workers hold older cached ones, so clippy lint sets diverge: the first CI runs failed on lints (chunks_exact->as_chunks) that no local lane could reproduce, and lint drift will recur every time upstream adds a lint.

## Proposal
Pin a dated nightly (e.g. channel = "nightly-2026-07-01") and bump it deliberately on a cadence, treating a toolchain bump like a dependency bump (own commit, full both-ISA gate run). CONVENTIONS.md already calls each nightly feature a liability with a documented fallback; a floating channel is the same liability without the paper trail.

## Coordination
Changing rust-toolchain.toml invalidates every agent's and rch worker's cache simultaneously — land it at a quiet moment, announce in the tracker, and re-run bv/CI after. Verify fs-qty (generic_const_exprs) and fs-simd portable tier still compile on the chosen date.

## Context
Found while landing frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.4: run 28815907293 failed macOS clippy on lints absent from local toolchains; see docs/CI_GATES.md.
close_reason: Pinned rust-toolchain.toml to nightly-2026-07-06, which is BIT-IDENTICAL to the floating nightly every local agent had active at pin time (rustc 1.99.0-nightly 3659db0d3 2026-07-05, verified by installing the dated toolchain and comparing) - so the pin stops CI lint drift without changing anyone's compiler. ANNOUNCEMENT TO ALL AGENTS: the toolchain IDENTITY changed even though the binary did not, so cargo will re-fingerprint and rebuild the workspace once on your next command - expected, one-time. Bump policy documented in the file per the bead: deliberate bumps only, own commit, tracker announcement, full gate run after. Verified under the pin: fs-qty (const-generic dimension arithmetic, the flagged canary) builds + clippy -D warnings clean + 30 tests green.

title: fs-ivl TaylorModel1 remainder under-covers on domains with half-width > 1
description:
SOUNDNESS BUG (false certificate) in crates/fs-ivl/src/taylor.rs. Confirmed and fix prototyped; blocked ONLY on a cross-ISA golden-hash re-pin that must be done on an x86-64 host (trj/ts1/ts2).

## The bug
`split_mid(iv, rem)` (taylor.rs) stores a coefficient's midpoint `p_k` and absorbs the deviation `δ_k = c_k − p_k` into the remainder FLAT (as `δ_k·h^0`). But that stored error reaches f(x) as `δ_k·(x−c)^k = δ_k·h^k`, and `eval_interval` adds `rem` once at the end. So for a domain whose centered half-width |h| = max|x−c| exceeds 1, the flat absorption under-covers the true `δ_k·h^k` by a factor |h|^k, silently violating the module's central containment law `f(x) ∈ P(x−c) + rem`. For |h| ≤ 1 the flat form over-covers (safe), which is why it went unnoticed.

## Why tests miss it
Every taylor_battery.rs fixture uses domain [-0.8, 1.2] → center 0.2 → h = [-1, 1], i.e. |h| = 1 EXACTLY (the boundary where |h|^k = 1 and flat absorption is exactly rigorous). The containment test also grants ±1 ulp grace. CONTRACT.md:169 still says "No Taylor models yet (future bead 6ys.13)", so the module is experimental and not part of the certified surface — but TaylorModel1 IS publicly exported (lib.rs:39).

## Reproducer (deterministic, ~26 ulp violation)
f(x) = (x + 0.38371695125150285)·(−1.1202845397051888·x) + (x + 0.15914017704475958)·(2.114360809331372 + x), order-5 TM on domain [−18.72527873358944, 16.653298481159304] (c ≈ −1.036). At x = 16.653298481159304: eval_interval = [−2.31981334891575752, −2.31981334891563540], true = −2.31981334891576907 — truth is 1.15e-14 (~26 ulp) BELOW the enclosure lower bound. Gap is 0 for half-width ≤ 12, nonzero at 17.7 (the |h|^k signature).

## The fix (prototyped; passes containment + convergence locally)
Thread the coefficient power `deg` and the centered-domain enclosure `h = domain − point(c)` into split_mid, and absorb `dev * h.powi(deg)` instead of `dev`:
```
fn split_mid(iv: Interval, deg: usize, h: Interval, rem: &mut Interval) -> f64 {
    let m = iv.midpoint();
    let dev = iv - Interval::point(m);
    *rem = *rem + dev * h.powi(deg);
    m
}
```
Update all 6 call sites to pass (deg, h): scale, exp (final scaling loop), sin (term loop), Add, Sub, Mul. In each, deg is the coefficient/loop index and h = self.domain − Interval::point(self.c). Full working patch saved at /Volumes/USB_NVME/taylor_fix.patch during the diagnosing session (regenerate with git if lost). Since |h|^deg ≤ 1 for |h| ≤ 1, the fix is no looser than the old flat form on the narrow domains it got right.

## Verification status
With the fix applied, `functional_containment` and `subdivision_convergence_beats_intervals` still PASS. ONLY `taylor_golden_hash` fails because the remainder bits change (some coefficient devs are ~1-ulp asymmetric at h=[-1,1], and dev*[-1,1] symmetrizes them). New aarch64 hash observed: 0x3a612d034133f478 (old GOLDEN_HASH = 0xa16d9759a35295d8 at taylor_battery.rs:279).

## What remains (why this is a bead, not a landed fix)
Landing requires bumping GOLDEN_HASH, which is a CROSS-ISA golden ("Recorded on aarch64-apple (M4 Pro); must match on x86-64 (trj)"). Per the golden-bump protocol (and the rand_nla mis-pin lesson), the new hash MUST be verified bit-identical on an x86-64 Threadripper before pinning. The fix only adds standard Interval ops (already cross-ISA stable), so it SHOULD match, but this must be confirmed empirically. Steps: (1) apply the patch, (2) build+run `cargo test -p fs-ivl --test taylor_battery` on trj/ts1, (3) confirm the printed taylor-golden hash == 0x3a612d034133f478, (4) update GOLDEN_HASH, (5) add a wide-domain (|h|>1) containment regression test using the reproducer above, (6) ubs + clippy + commit. Optionally update CONTRACT.md:169 once TMs are certified.

title: Evidence composition must retain its binding-constraint WITNESS, not just the weakest colour
description:
BACKGROUND. fs_evidence::color::compose (crates/fs-evidence/src/color.rs:818) implements the project's central rule: composition cannot outrank its weakest operand. It is correct and it is tested at L2 (capability evidence.colour-algebra).

But a meet returns a VALUE and discards its WITNESS. Across a six-stage spine (import-verify, assign, material-resolve, flow-network, conduction, qoi) the composed result tells a user the answer is Estimated. It does not tell them WHICH stage made it Estimated. That is the difference between a label and an explanation, and the explanation is the product.

WHY THIS IS THE PRODUCT AND NOT A NICETY. FrankenSim's entire pitch is that "what did we compute?" and "why should anyone believe it?" are not separate artifacts. A number stamped Estimated is what every other solver already gives you, implicitly. The sentence worth paying for is:

  "Junction temperature 84.2 C, Estimated -- BECAUSE the Dittus-Boelter
   correlation is outside its validated Reynolds domain at this operating
   point; every other stage on this path is Verified."

Nothing in the tree can produce that sentence today. The information exists at every stage and is destroyed at each composition.

RELATED PRECEDENT IN THIS REPO. Two defects of exactly this shape have already been found and fixed: ProvenanceClass reached only the identity hash so receipt-backed and caller-declared solves were byte-identical in evidence (fixed ead4c2f6); and thermal QoIs emitted absolute temperatures and temperature intervals as one indistinguishable type (fixed 98356c75). The pattern is: the distinction is respected by the computation and unreadable at the boundary. This is the same vein at the composition layer, and it is the highest-value instance because it is user-facing.

WHAT.
(a) Carry the argmin through spine composition: the composed claim retains which stage (and which model card within it) bound the result. This is why-provenance over the evidence lattice -- the meet's witness, not merely its value. Where several operands tie at the weakest colour, retain ALL of them in a canonical order; "the binding constraint" is a set, not necessarily a singleton, and silently picking one would be a fresh laundering.
(b) The witness must be machine-readable (a stable discriminant plus the stage/card identity), not prose, so a downstream gate can branch on it and a report can render it. Prose in a message string is what the ProvenanceClass defect already taught this project not to do.
(c) f85xj.6.9 (the HTML engineering report) renders the witness as the HEADLINE finding, not a footnote.

DONE WHEN: a composed spine claim exposes its binding-constraint witness; a test proves that changing WHICH stage is weakest changes the witness (not merely the colour); and the report surfaces it.

TESTS. Discrimination: two runs with identical composed colour but different binding stages must produce different witnesses -- this is the test that would have caught the ProvenanceClass defect and is the one that matters. Tie handling: an engineered tie retains every tied operand in canonical order. Anti-laundering: the witness can never report a stage STRONGER than the composed colour. Non-vacuity: prove the witness actually varies across the fixture set rather than being pinned to one stage by construction.

DEPENDS ON: the spine executing far enough that more than one stage contributes a colour. Until flow-network/conduction/qoi land there is only one composition path and the test above cannot be non-vacuous.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a typed nonempty canonical set of binding witnesses for evidence meet/composition. Focused unit/property/mutation tests cover every colour pair, singleton and multiway ties, permutation and grouping invariance, stable canonical ordering, duplicate elimination, stage/card identity changes at constant colour, anti-laundering, serialization/migration, unknown/stale evidence, and max-cardinality refusal. A solve-stage positive/negative case runs through scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh and proves that changing the weakest stage changes the witness while severing a slice demotes or refuses. f85xj.6.9 renders all tied witnesses as the headline explanation. Bounded V.3 JSONL records operand roots, witness set, ordering rule, composed colour, first divergence, no-claim, relative report artifact, and replay. A colour without a reconstructible witness cannot promote.
close_reason: done

title: fs-conduction radiation test authority: the enclosure energy-closure assertion is an IEEE identity, and the coupled solve pins no radiative magnitude
description:
Found auditing f85xj.5.4 against HEAD (full verdict is a comment on that bead).

FRAMING, because it matters: 5.4 does NOT overclaim at the scope level. Its
Notes, commit 831d2e59, CHANGELOG.md:302-305, CONTRACT.md:574-588,
MODEL_CARD.md:60-63/110-117/134-136 and README.md:1406 all independently
disclose what is unimplemented, and fs-vvreg took no registry authority (the
manifest row is still reference-only and vv-scorecard reports the view-factor
cell NO-DATA). Same standard as 5.3: an honest partial. These defects are one
layer down -- five of its six tests assert something WEAKER than the prose
around them.

The radiosity algebra itself is sound and independently validated; do not
re-audit it. radiation.rs:881-901 assembles (I-(1-eps)F)J = eps*sigma*T^4
correctly, and tests/radiation.rs:233-237 checks the net flux against the
genuinely independent textbook closed form sigma*(T1^4-T2^4)/(1/e1+1/e2-1) at
2e-13 relative -- an expression the code never forms. That clause is earned.

(1) THE ENERGY-CLOSURE ASSERTIONS ARE UNCONDITIONALLY TRUE.
tests/radiation.rs:238 asserts relative_energy_closure() <= 2.0e-15 and :335
asserts < 1.0e-12. Both fixtures are 2-surface with F = [[0,1],[1,0]] and
bit-identical areas (pinned by to_bits() at :223 for the first; the second uses
two copies of the same box_grid([2,2,2],[0.5,1.0,1.0])). For that matrix the
irradiation loop (radiation.rs:911-915) yields G0 = J1 and G1 = J0 EXACTLY, so
net_outward_flux = [J0-J1, J1-J0] are IEEE-exact negations and heat_sum
(radiation.rs:919) is exactly 0.0. The assertion cannot fail for any enclosure
this crate has ever been run on. CONTRACT.md:212 says "Enclosure exchange
closes globally"; the evidence is a tautology. CHANGELOG.md:284 reports "zero
measured enclosure-energy residual" without disclosing that the zero is forced.

(2) THE COUPLED SOLVE ASSERTS NOTHING THAT PINS THE RADIATIVE MAGNITUDE.
tests/radiation.rs:327-338 has exactly four assertions: convergence
(update <= final_threshold_k), two sign checks, relative_energy_closure (see
(1), identically zero), and coupled_energy_closure -- which is a LINEAR SOLVER
RESIDUAL, not a cross-physics balance. solve.rs:305-313 documents closure_w as
"-sum_{free} r_i exactly: this number measures how well the linear solves
closed the balance, not whether the boundary data itself is right", and
neumann_out_w is post-integrated from the same uniform flux field that was
assembled into the load, so it cancels by construction.
EXECUTED REPRO: multiply the overlay flux at radiation.rs:1096 by 2.0. The
fixed point still converges, net_outward_heat_w[0] > 0 > net_outward_heat_w[1]
still holds, and BOTH closures still pass. The radiative flux magnitude is
unconstrained by the test.
The fixture HAS an exact answer available and does not use it: slab thickness
0.5, k = 10, so q = 20(400 - T_s1) = 20(T_s2 - 300) = sigma(T_s1^4 - T_s2^4)/1.5,
and P1 reproduces this linear solution exactly on that mesh.

(3) emissivity_query_uses_absolute_temperature_dimensions RUNS NO QUERY.
tests/radiation.rs:400-404. It asserts TEMPERATURE_DIMS == Dims([0,0,0,1,0,0]),
restating src/lib.rs:114 token-for-token, and EMISSIVITY_DIMS == Dims::NONE,
restating radiation.rs:41. It never calls from_card. The name promises an
emissivity query. This is one of the 6 radiation tests counted in the
CHANGELOG's 53/53 proof.

(4) THE LEVEL-A RADIATION BINDING IS A LITERAL AGAINST AN EQUAL LITERAL.
tests/radiation.rs:160-164 asserts factors()[0][1] == reference_value_si, where
the left side is the literal 1.0 written at radiation.rs:536
(infinite_parallel_plates hardcodes vec![vec![0.0,1.0],vec![1.0,0.0]]) and the
right side is the literal 1.0 at fs-vvreg/src/thermal_level_a.rs:325. Same vein
as frankensim-z87uy. This is the sole evidence behind CHANGELOG's "raised
aggregate Level-A execution coverage from 14/19 to 15/19" and README.md:1415's
"all 19 Level-A rows now have executing-kernel bindings". Of the 19, this is
the only row whose "executing kernel" performs ZERO arithmetic -- compare
thermal-a-contact-series, which actually solves a two-slab network.
Related: the row-sum and reciprocity assertions beside it (:163, :164) are
strictly implied by admission, since infinite_parallel_plates passes
row_sum_abs: 0.0 and reciprocity_rel: 0.0 (radiation.rs:540-543), so admit()
already refuses anything but exactly 1.0 and 0.0.
Related: the crosswalk at tests/analytic.rs:88-91 stores the binding string and
the completeness test at :905-937 only checks starts_with("tests/radiation.rs::"),
so deleting or renaming the radiation test leaves the coverage claim passing.

(5) MINOR, same file. tests/radiation.rs:128 asserts discrepancy_w_m2 > 0.0,
strictly implied by :119-127 already pinning linearized and nonlinear to two
different numbers. tests/radiation.rs:119 builds expected_h as
4.0*0.8*sigma*320^3 -- token-for-token the implementation expression at
radiation.rs:313-318 with the same operand order, so the difference is exactly
0.0 and the f64::EPSILON envelope is decorative. Pinning the formula is
legitimate; presenting it as a tolerance check is not.
tests/radiation.rs:226-232 calls the same pure function twice and asserts
equality -- it cannot distinguish determinism from purity, yet
MODEL_CARD.md:154 cites "radiosity replay" as G5 evidence.

DONE WHEN
  1. The coupled two-slab test asserts the analytic answer. Solve
     q = 20(400-T_s1) = 20(T_s2-300) = sigma(T_s1^4-T_s2^4)/1.5 for
     (T_s1, T_s2, q) by Newton on one scalar, then assert the converged
     surface_temperatures and net_outward_heat_w[0] against it. This is the
     highest-value item: without it the coupling has no magnitude evidence at
     all, and it is what DONE-WHEN 4 actually asks for.
  2. relative_energy_closure is measured on an enclosure where cancellation is
     NOT exact -- a 3-surface case with unequal areas (e.g. [1, 1, 0.5] with
     factors satisfying closure and reciprocity). This simultaneously covers
     the pivot-swap branch at radiation.rs:1200-1203 and the multi-term
     back-substitution at :1216-1221, which n=2 can never reach because the
     pivot is always |1| vs |-(1-eps)| <= 0.4.
  3. emissivity_query_uses_absolute_temperature_dimensions actually queries a
     card whose emissivity claim carries wrong dims and asserts
     ConductionError::Dimensions -- which also covers radiation.rs:130-138,
     currently untested -- or is renamed to say it checks constants.
  4. Either a second, non-degenerate closed-form configuration factor is added
     (aligned parallel rectangles or coaxial disks; both are short closed forms
     and would give DONE-WHEN 1 its plural), or CONTRACT.md:529-545 gains a note
     distinguishing this Level-A row from the eight that perform arithmetic.
     Also resolve the tests/analytic.rs:88-91 binding against something real
     rather than prefix-matching it.
  5. Every repair is falsifiable by DEMONSTRATION: perturb the guarded quantity
     and show which assertions fail, the way frankensim-z87uy did. In
     particular show that the new coupled assertion fails under the
     overlay-flux x2 perturbation that currently passes.

NON-GOALS: the self-disclosed 5.4 scope stays with 5.4 -- no QMC generator, no
radiation-dominated retained corpus fixture, no participating media, no
spectral/specular model, no radiation adjoint, no registry authority.

title: Euler Disc Cinematic 4K: simulation-driven Maxwell-style animation and sound
description:
## Mission

Deliver a visually exceptional, simulation-driven Euler-disc cinematic at UHD 4K resolution with synchronized physically informed sound, using FrankenSim's own LUMEN spectral renderer and Euler-disc mechanics. The target is not a diagnostic plot or a pile of disconnected frames: it is a polished, reproducible short film that makes the geometry, wobble, precession, spin, contact evolution, base response, and terminal acceleration legible and emotionally compelling.

## Why this program exists

FrankenSim already has the hard foundations: resolved axisymmetric disc geometry, a coupled reduced Euler trajectory, certified chart tracing, a deterministic hero-wavelength path tracer with NEE+MIS, GGX and Lambertian surfaces, EXR/PNG writers, and progressive sample accumulation. It does not yet have a movie pipeline. Current Euler samples omit the complete time-indexed rigid pose; the renderer has static primitives, a pinhole camera, one rectangular light, opaque materials, serial pixel traversal, and no frame orchestration. There is no waveform synthesizer, WAV writer, A/V clock contract, or video mux boundary.

This epic closes that product gap without pretending that cinematic plausibility is experimental validation. The reduced Euler campaign remains uncalibrated and does not resolve the final structural-contact-air-film acoustic regime. The first film may therefore claim deterministic simulation-driven imagery and physically informed sound synthesis, but not measured acoustic prediction, validated Steve Mould correspondence, or physical stopping-time accuracy.

## Product target

The reference deliverable is an 8-12 second 3840x2160, 24 fps product-style animation with float EXR masters, high-quality display previews, stereo 48 kHz WAV, thin-lens camera, motion blur, studio/environment lighting, refractive glass, credible tungsten/stainless materials, readable spin cues, temporally stable denoising, deterministic manifests, cancellation/resume, and an optional quarantined out-of-process mux step. A 1080p low-sample daily must provide fast creative iteration before the expensive 4K render. Final acceptance also covers frame pacing, temporal aliasing or false spin reversal, native-4K and downscaled display behavior, color metadata, A/V synchronization, programme loudness/headroom, and intelligibility with audio muted; these are user-experience checks, not new physics claims.

## Governing principles

- Simulation state is the source of motion. Camera, lighting, materials, exposure, and optional surface markings are visualization choices and must be labeled separately.
- Physics authority, render convergence, denoiser bias, artistic sound synthesis, and experimentally calibrated acoustics are distinct evidence classes.
- The default path remains pure Rust and Franken-only. Foreign media tools may appear only as optional quarantined out-of-process adapters; they cannot enter the runtime dependency graph or mint authority.
- Deterministic seeds, frame times, shutter intervals, budgets, versions, capabilities, source trajectory identity, and output hashes are recorded.
- Product implementation dominates. Tests and logs must diagnose real failures without becoming a second product.

## Success criteria

This epic closes only when the capstone bead produces the reference 4K film and its replay bundle from a committed Euler trajectory, every required child bead has a terminal result, focused unit/property/integration tests pass, cancellation/resume is demonstrated, the exact DSR gate is reported, and remaining physical/acoustic no-claims are visible in both human and machine-readable deliverables. Optional escalation beads may remain open only with an explicit not-required disposition, capability/evidence rationale, and proof that their absence does not invalidate the accepted canonical EXR+WAV bundle.
notes:
EXECUTION MAP (polished 2026-08-04)

1. Start at h7xu5.1.1 authority contract, then .1.2 shot/timeline, .1.3 budgets, and .1.4 canonical configuration/identity. This short serial prefix prevents incompatible clocks and hidden defaults.
2. After .1.4, run parallel product lanes: full-pose trajectory (.2); rigid instances/camera/motion (.3); conductor/dielectric/multi-light look foundations (.4); tile/adaptive/checkpoint scaling (.5); AOV/color/sequence (.6); modal/resampled/WAV sound (.7); and CLI admission (.8.1).
3. Converge early at .9.2, the tiny production-backed render-plus-sound fixture. It intentionally uses a supported nonterminal trajectory interval and does not wait on final look approval, temporal denoising, spatial room processing, or the artistic terminal chirp.
4. Use .9.8 as the stable E2E runner, then prove cancellation/resume/invalidation in .9.4.
5. Converge creatively at .4.6 reference still and .8.3/.9.3 complete 1080p daily. Do not spend the full 4K budget until daily approval.
6. Qualify throughput in .5.5 and one representative final-quality 4K frame in .9.5.
7. Finalize through .9.7 only after unit/property coverage, E2E hostile twins, daily approval, exact resume, 4K frame qualification, independent verification, and user docs.

OPTIONAL/OFF-MINIMUM-PATH: .2.6 higher-fidelity backend adapter, .4.5 conditional caustic specialization, .6.5 scientific overlays, .7.8 calibrated fs-acoustics bridge, and .8.5 external mux adapter. They remain valuable but cannot hold the first verified canonical EXR+WAV cinematic hostage unless measured evidence makes one necessary.

title: Cinematic contract, creative brief, authority boundaries, and resource envelope
description:
## Objective

Freeze the user-facing movie target and the technical/epistemic contract before implementation fans out. This workstream owns creative intent, shot grammar, delivery formats, frame/audio clocks, quality tiers, resource budgets, and the distinction among visualization choices, simulated mechanics, physically informed synthesis, and calibrated predictions.

## Required decisions

Specify UHD dimensions, frame rate, duration range, shutter convention, working/output color spaces, EXR/PNG channel policy, audio sample rate/layout, reference camera language, studio lighting intent, disc/base material variants, readable-spin treatment, preview and final quality tiers, storage limits, deterministic seed policy, and cancellation/resume expectations. Define one canonical timeline shared by physics, camera, shutter samples, base response, sound synthesis, and muxing.

The reference shot plan must tell a coherent story: establishing product shot, readable transition into stable precession, controlled macro view of contact/wobble, and a terminal close-up whose speed and sound remain legible rather than aliased. Alternative cuts are allowed, but one reference sequence is frozen for acceptance.

## Authority rules

A beautiful render does not validate mechanics. Denoised pixels remain biased derivatives of raw Monte Carlo estimates. A contact-driven modal soundtrack is physically informed unless material/modal/radiation parameters are calibrated. The current reduced trajectory does not predict the last acoustic singularity. Any artistic chirp, procedural brushed texture, engraved marker, exposure adjustment, time remapping, or camera stabilization must be recorded as a visualization transform.

## Success criteria

This workstream closes when downstream teams can implement without consulting a separate plan: schemas, units, clocks, quality targets, resource envelopes, no-claims, shot list, and acceptance metrics are all present in child beads and exercised by a machine-readable configuration fixture.

## Workstream test strategy

Children must include schema/unit boundary tests, known timeline vectors, configuration-identity mutation tests, and one admission E2E fixture. Contract prose alone cannot close this epic; downstream consumption and prohibited authority promotion must execute.
close_reason: All four child deliverables are implemented and closed: authority/deliverable contract, exact creative brief and A/V timeline, checked quality/resource admission, and versioned partitioned composition configuration. Machine-readable fixtures and focused/full tests execute the workstream's clocks, no-claim boundaries, admission, and identity mutation requirements.

title: Freeze cinematic deliverable and evidence-authority contract
description:
## Background and user outcome

The movie combines mechanics, Monte Carlo rendering, denoising, artistic direction, sound synthesis, and optional external encoding. Without an explicit authority contract, a visually persuasive result could accidentally be presented as experimental validation or a physically predictive acoustic waveform. This bead freezes what the first deliverable is and is not.

## Technical approach

Define the canonical deliverable as a deterministic simulation-driven visualization: 3840x2160, 24 fps, 8-12 seconds, float EXR masters, display previews, stereo 48 kHz WAV, sequence manifest, and optional muxed derivative. Define four non-interchangeable authority classes: raw simulated state; raw Monte Carlo render; biased visualization derivative; and sound class (artistic, physically informed, or calibrated). Require every artifact and log record to carry its class, source identity, units/clocks, configuration version, and applicable no-claims.

Freeze terminology for render convergence, deterministic replay, visual approval, model calibration, experimental validation, and media encoding. State that neither image realism nor audio resemblance validates stopping time, ring/cone ranking, contact law, terminal singularity, or Mould-video correspondence.

## Success criteria

A typed contract is consumable by trajectory, renderer, image, sound, CLI, and report layers; illegal authority promotion is refused; every final artifact can answer which source and transform produced it. Human-facing end credits/metadata and machine manifest expose the same limitations.

## Tests

Unit/schema tests cover each authority class, required metadata, version refusal, unknown class, and prohibited promotion. Mutation tests remove source/no-claim/bias fields and must fail. E2E negative twin attempts to label denoised imagery or modal audio as calibrated evidence and is refused with a stable reason code.

## Considerations

The contract must be small enough to use at runtime. It governs scientific honesty, not aesthetic choices. Future physical calibration may promote specific acoustic or mechanical claims only through new evidence; it never retroactively changes old artifact labels.
close_reason: Implemented typed Euler cinematic v1 deliverable and authority contract in fs-evidence: 4K/24 fps/8-12 s master envelope, exact A/V clocks, four non-interchangeable authority classes plus sound tiers, content/source/transform/config identities, canonical codec and manifests, stable terminology/no-claims, illegal-promotion refusal, calibration declaration boundary, and G0/G3 mutation/negative-twin coverage. Focused cinematic tests 10/10 pass; full fs-evidence tests 251/251 pass; focused lib+cinematic Clippy -D warnings passes. Repo DSR is non-green only at unrelated standing constellation/fs-tribo/fs-substrate/fs-alloc gates (log 20260804T095938-54112).

title: Freeze the reference shot list, visual language, and A/V master timeline
description:
## Background and purpose

Expensive 4K rendering should not begin before the film's story, camera intent, and timing are testable at preview quality. This bead converts “make it look amazing” into a concrete yet editable reference sequence that downstream implementation can target.

## Technical approach

Define an 8-12 second 24 fps master timeline with named shots and frame ranges: an establishing studio product view; a transition that makes disc inclination and contact orbit readable; a macro precession/wobble view; and a terminal close-up with controlled shutter and sound. For each shot specify camera pose/keyframes, focal length or FOV, focus distance, aperture, shutter interval, exposure intent, lighting preset, disc material, glass/base visibility, background, and audio perspective.

Define safe action/title areas, cut/transition rules, whether time remains physically linear, and how censored or prematurely terminated simulations are depicted. Choose a visualization-only spin cue—prefer subtle anisotropic brushing and optionally a tiny engraved radial mark—and require it to remain absent from contact/mass geometry. Define the intended apparent-rotation behavior at every shot: temporal sampling, shutter, and marking frequency must be checked for false reversal, frozen spokes, objectionable flicker, and loss of wobble/contact readability. Any deliberate stylization is labeled; accidental aliasing is a defect. The visual story must remain understandable with audio muted, while sound adds timing and material cues rather than carrying essential scientific context alone.

Freeze a rational time base shared by frames and 48 kHz samples. Define interpolation domain, first/last frame conventions, shutter centering, cut boundaries, and audio lead/lag policy.

## Success criteria

A low-cost storyboard/proxy can be generated entirely from this brief. Every frame and audio sample maps to a declared simulation time or an explicitly labeled visualization-only hold/taper. No shot depends on an unspecified feature. Proxy review can identify false apparent rotation, flicker, unreadable contact motion, or audio-only meaning before expensive rendering begins.

## Tests

Schema/unit tests cover valid/invalid shot ranges, overlap/gaps, camera singularities, out-of-trajectory time, shutter crossing a cut/event, missing focus target, and non-integral A/V mapping. A golden timeline reconstructs exact frame and sample timestamps. Apparent-rotation fixtures sweep angular velocity, marking frequency, shutter, and frame rate across alias boundaries. E2E preview uses the whole shot list and includes a muted-audio review artifact.

## Considerations

Creative controls must not be hard-coded in the renderer. The reference brief is acceptance input, not the only supported movie. Camera stabilization or time remapping, if later desired, must be explicit transforms rather than silent modifications of simulated motion.
close_reason: Implemented the validated renderer-independent 240-frame four-shot reference brief with exact 24 fps/48 kHz/simulation clocks, per-shot camera/optics/material/light/audio intent, safe areas, muted storyboard proxy, sample-exact A/V mapping, clipped shutter windows, bounded terminal-only labeled censored holds, and alias/flicker diagnostics. Proof: focused cinematic_brief 10/10; full fs-evidence 261/261; strict focused Clippy -D warnings passed; UBS found 0 critical issues (remaining warnings are test assertions/indexing heuristics). DSR repo gate remains independently blocked by pre-existing constellation/format/clippy findings logged at /Users/jemanuel/.local/state/dsr/quality-logs/frankensim/20260804T095938-54112.

title: Define preview/final quality tiers and admitted 4K compute, memory, time, and storage budgets
description:
## Background

At UHD 4K, one f64 XYZ film is about 190 MiB; the current transactional copy roughly doubles live film memory. A 256-spp frame launches about 2.12 billion camera paths, and uncompressed float RGB EXR is roughly 100 MB per frame. Quality and feasibility therefore require explicit budgets rather than an unbounded “maximum quality” setting.

## Technical approach

Freeze at least three profiles: storyboard/smoke, 1080p daily, and 4K final. Each declares resolution, fps/timeline subset, spp floor/ceiling, path depth, adaptive error target, denoise policy, AOV set, shutter samples, tile size, worker limits, checkpoint cadence, memory ceiling, per-frame and whole-sequence wall-time envelope, output-byte ceiling, and minimum free-space reserve. Include a representative 4K-frame qualification profile separate from the entire film.

Define admission formulas using checked arithmetic before allocation or work begins. Estimate film, AOV, staging, checkpoint, EXR/PNG, WAV, and temporary mux storage. Specify behavior when budgets conflict: ranked repairs such as lower preview SPP, smaller AOV set, shorter range, or additional resources; never silent quality reduction in final mode.

## Success criteria

All profiles are explicit, reproducible, and suitable for static admission. Exact maximum values succeed in bounded fixtures; maximum+1 refuses before large allocation. Final mode cannot accidentally inherit preview quality.

## Tests

Boundary tests cover zero/one/max dimensions, frame counts, spp, depth, tiles, bytes, workers, and audio duration; arithmetic overflow; insufficient disk/memory/time; unsupported profile combinations; and deterministic repair ranking. E2E dry admission prints a bounded resource summary.

## Considerations

Performance envelopes are host-specific measurements, not universal promises. The final visual acceptance may choose more spp than the initial budget, but that is a versioned configuration change with a new estimate and artifact identity.
close_reason: Implemented four validated cinematic quality tiers (storyboard smoke, 1080p daily, representative 4K qualification frame, full 4K final) and checked pre-allocation admission for camera paths, film/staging/AOV memory, EXR/PNG/checkpoint/WAV/mux storage, disk reserve, workers, and host-measured wall time. Final-tier anti-downgrade rules and deterministic explicit repair advice prevent silent preview inheritance. Proof: cinematic_budget 8/8; full fs-evidence 269/269; strict focused Clippy -D warnings passed; UBS found 0 critical issues. DSR repo-level blockers remain unrelated/pre-existing at /Users/jemanuel/.local/state/dsr/quality-logs/frankensim/20260804T095938-54112.

title: Define the versioned cinematic configuration and content-addressed composition identity
description:
## Background

Trajectory, scene, camera, materials, lights, renderer, image finishing, sound, and media assembly must compose without hidden defaults. A stable configuration and identity allow safe checkpoint reuse and precise invalidation when a user changes only one part of the film.

## Technical approach

Define a versioned pure-data cinematic configuration containing source trajectory reference; output/timeline profile; shot list; scene geometry and instance mapping; material/light/environment assets; renderer sampler/depth/adaptive/shutter settings; image/AOV/denoise/color settings; sound model/microphone/room settings; artifact roots; and optional mux adapter request. Every numeric value carries units or an unambiguous semantic type. Seeds, versions, capabilities, and budgets are mandatory.

Define canonical encoding and a domain-separated composition fingerprint. Partition sub-identities so camera changes invalidate beauty frames but not trajectory/audio excitation, while sound-room changes invalidate audio but not images. External assets bind bytes and declared color/spectral interpretation, not path strings. Unknown fields/versions fail closed unless an explicit forward-compatible rule exists.

## Success criteria

Equivalent configurations encode identically; semantically different values alter the appropriate identity; invalidation is minimal but never under-invalidates. The CLI and all workstreams consume this schema rather than introducing private configuration files.

## Tests

Known-answer identity vectors, field-order permutation, unit rescaling to equivalent canonical values, unknown-version refusal, missing Five Explicits, non-finite inputs, stale asset hash, path relocation, and one-field invalidation matrix. E2E changes camera, material, sound room, and trajectory separately and verifies exactly which artifacts are reusable.

## Considerations

This is product configuration, not a second planning language. Keep it specific to cinematic composition and reuse existing quantity, budget, and content-addressing primitives.
close_reason: Implemented the versioned pure-data cinematic composition schema with mandatory units, seed, capabilities, versions, and separately partitioned render/audio budgets; typed trajectory/timeline/camera/scene/render/image/sound references; byte-bound interpreted assets with relocatable locator hints and stale-byte verification; quarantined mux requests; canonical compact encoding; and domain-separated trajectory/image/audio/mux/composition identities. Fresh-eyes fixes prevented budget/capability over-invalidation and arbitrary unverifiable asset hashes. Proof: cinematic_config 9/9; full fs-evidence 278/278; strict focused Clippy -D warnings passed; UBS over all cinematic modules reported 0 critical findings. title: Euler render trajectory: full pose, contact, base, event, and replay artifacts
description:
## Objective

Turn the existing reduced Euler campaign into an animation-grade trajectory source. The renderer and sound engine require complete time-indexed state, not only inclination, spin, precession, and final checkpoint state.

## Scope

Retain full disc center-of-mass position, normalized body-to-world quaternion, linear and angular velocities or momenta with declared frames, contact location/normal/feature identity, contact-active state and localized transitions, normal/rolling/gas/base channel values, base modal coordinate and velocity, energy bookkeeping, terminal brackets, and applicability/no-claim metadata. Define deterministic interpolation and resampling onto frame, shutter, and audio-control timelines without crossing discontinuities or inventing events.

The artifact must bind geometry/profile identity, mass properties, solver/model versions, timestep rung, initial state, configuration fingerprint, seed, units, frame conventions, terminal disposition, and source campaign identity. Restart/continuation concatenation must not duplicate or omit samples.

## Boundaries

This workstream exposes what the simulation computed; it does not upgrade the reduced model, fabricate missing high-frequency physics, or claim measured truth. A separate adapter may later consume the higher-fidelity transactional contact stack, but it must implement the same trajectory contract rather than fork the movie pipeline.

## Success criteria

A deterministic encoded trajectory round-trips bitwise, reconstructs the full accepted state sequence, resamples safely at reference frame and shutter times, survives cancellation without partial publication, and drives a minimal moving-disc render fixture.

## Workstream test strategy

Children own focused state/schema/interpolation/codec tests plus an E2E campaign-to-artifact journey. Required falsifiers include q/-q handling, continuation seams, event-straddling queries, corrupt artifacts, cancellation, and a renderer/sound consumer proving the artifact is sufficient.

title: Define animation-grade Euler trajectory sample and artifact semantics
description:
## Background

The existing CoupledSample retains scalar QoIs, contacts, channel work, and energies, while the complete RigidBodyState appears only in the restart checkpoint. Animation and sound need the accepted state at every retained time. Reconstructing orientation from inclination/spin/precession scalars would lose phase, frame conventions, translational motion, and event behavior.

## Technical approach

Define RenderTrajectorySample with exact time; center-of-mass world position; normalized body-to-world quaternion; world linear velocity or momentum; body angular velocity or momentum with mass-property identity; disc symmetry-axis direction; contact point/normal and support feature; contact branch and localized transitions; base modal displacement/velocity; channel wrenches/work; mechanical energy/defect; and terminal/censor flags. Prefer authoritative state fields over redundant derived angles, but retain derived QoIs as auditable conveniences.

Define frames, handedness, quaternion sign canonicalization, SI units, monotone-time rules, finite-value requirements, discontinuity markers, and optional-field authority. Define top-level metadata binding resolved specimen chart/profile, mass properties, initial state, timestep/model/configuration fingerprints, applicability, and no-claims.

## Success criteria

A sample contains everything required to place and orient the disc, evaluate camera-relative motion, locate contact, and derive sound controls without querying hidden runner state. Schema evolution is versioned and unknown versions refuse.

## Tests

Construction tests cover valid state, canonical q/-q identity, non-unit/non-finite quaternion, nonmonotone/duplicate time, frame/unit mismatch, contact flag/geometry inconsistency, missing base fields, terminal placement, and redundant QoI disagreement. Property tests rigidly transform the whole trajectory and preserve intrinsic QoIs.

## Considerations

Do not copy every internal integrator field. Retain accepted public state and diagnostics needed for visualization/replay. The artifact is simulation evidence, not calibrated truth.

Focused RCH test 10/10; UBS 0 critical; changed-file format/Clippy/build clean.

title: Capture complete accepted rigid-body and base state in the reduced coupled Euler runner
description:
## Background

The animation schema is useful only if the production reduced campaign records it at accepted integration points. Capturing provisional midpoint or rejected event-localization states would create visible jumps and break energy/contact interpretation.

## Technical approach

Extend the reduced coupled runner to publish animation samples only after a macro-step or localized terminal/contact substep is accepted. Populate pose and momenta directly from RigidBodyState; derive velocity with the bound mass properties; retain base state from the same accepted stage; evaluate contact geometry at the retained pose; and attach channel ownership/energy values for the interval with explicit start/end semantics.

Preserve restart and continuation: resuming a checkpoint must append a strictly later sample, avoid duplicating the boundary, and produce the same trajectory as an uninterrupted run. Cancellation/refusal must return no falsely complete artifact; an optional incomplete internal buffer may be used for resume but is not a published trajectory.

## Success criteria

All campaign profiles emit full-state samples, existing scalar QoIs remain numerically consistent, continuation equals uninterrupted output, and the final sample matches checkpoint state and terminal disposition.

## Tests

Focused unit tests cover first sample, one step, contact opening/reimpact, bracketed terminal, horizon censoring, continuation seam, zero/near-zero spin, quaternion canonicalization, base state, energy/channel alignment, cancellation at each publication boundary, and corrupted checkpoint refusal. E2E runs a short resolved filleted disc and verifies sample/state consistency.

## Considerations

Avoid materially increasing the campaign's memory footprint by retaining unnecessary private stages. If sampling cadence is configurable, its decimation must preserve all event endpoints and be recorded.
close_reason: Implemented complete accepted rigid-body/base trajectory publication with exact runner-configuration binding, deterministic restart seam behavior, atomic cancellation, and accepted terminal/reimpact root samples. Focused proof: cargo test -p fs-euler-disc-e2e --test coupled_runner --test render_trajectory (7 + 13 passed); rustfmt --check and git diff --check passed; UBS reported 0 critical findings. Strict crate Clippy remains blocked by pre-existing unrelated lint debt, disclosed separately.

title: Implement event-aware SE(3) interpolation and deterministic timeline resampling
description:
## Background

Video frames, shutter sub-samples, and audio controls rarely coincide with integrator sample times. Naive linear quaternion interpolation, angle interpolation across wraps, or interpolation through contact/terminal discontinuities can invent motion and smear events.

## Technical approach

Implement deterministic translation interpolation and shortest-arc normalized quaternion interpolation with explicit handling of q/-q equivalence, small-angle limits, and antipodal ambiguity. Prefer a velocity-aware interpolation when authoritative endpoint velocities support it; otherwise record the lower-order method. Interpolate base continuous state consistently.

Build a resampler for arbitrary sorted query times. Partition the trajectory at contact transitions, impacts, terminal events, continuation seams, and declared discontinuities. Never interpolate a discontinuous field across an event: use frozen left/right semantics and return event metadata. Shutter queries spanning an event either subdivide the exposure or follow the configured explicit policy.

## Success criteria

Frame, shutter, and audio-control timelines are deterministic; endpoints reproduce exact samples; constant twist and simple analytic motions meet tolerances; no query silently extrapolates beyond the trajectory. Event timing remains within its original bracket uncertainty.

## Tests

G0/property tests cover constant translation, constant-axis rotation, q/-q, tiny/near-pi angles, frame-rate changes, rigid-transform equivariance, time translation/scaling with units, exact endpoints, duplicated/out-of-order query refusal, out-of-range requests, event-straddling shutter, censored terminal, and continuation seams. Compare against an independent analytic SE(3) fixture.

## Considerations

Interpolation smoothness is a visualization/reconstruction assumption, not added mechanical resolution. The method/version becomes part of composition identity.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic event-aware timeline resampling: velocity-aware Hermite translation/base state, shortest-arc canonical quaternion SLERP, exact endpoint reproduction, strict sorted/in-range queries, explicit left/right contact and terminal semantics, accepted-sample-aligned declared seams, and shutter subdivision/refusal. Tightened terminal and reimpact-refusal root/sample equality. Proof: 7 coupled-runner + 13 render-trajectory + 9 timeline-resampling tests passed; rustfmt and diff checks passed; changed timeline module has no strict Clippy findings; UBS found 0 critical issues; bounded peer reread found no remaining correctness issue.

title: Derive synchronized render and sound control channels from trajectory state
description:
## Background

The renderer needs contact indicators, motion vectors, and optional overlays; the sound engine needs band-limited excitations derived from contact, rolling, gas, and base motion. These controls should be derived once with explicit semantics rather than independently and inconsistently in each consumer.

## Technical approach

Produce a control stream containing contact location in world/body/base frames; normal force; tangential/rolling power proxies; reimpact impulses or bounded event measures; gas/base work rates; disc and base velocities; spin/precession/inclination QoIs; and uncertainty/event flags. Define interval-centered versus point-sampled quantities, signs, units, filters, and missing-data behavior.

Provide separate visualization channels (contact glow/overlay, debug vectors, object transforms) and audio excitation channels. Visualization-only scaling is stored outside raw physical controls. Apply anti-alias filtering before downsampling any high-rate control; never infer high-frequency energy absent from the source.

## Success criteria

Consumers receive synchronized, unit-correct channels sharing the trajectory clock and source identity. Energy-integral checks reconcile power-like controls with retained work within declared numerical tolerance.

## Tests

Unit tests cover signs/frames, zero contact, continuous contact, opening/reimpact, negative/positive work, missing base/gas channels, interval endpoints, resampling conservation, alias fixture, saturation, and non-finite refusal. Metamorphic tests cover rigid transforms and equivalent unit presentations.

## No-claims

A control-stream frequency is not automatically a physical acoustic source frequency. Contact-force and base-energy controls remain model outputs/proxies under the trajectory's original authority.
notes: Implemented a source-bound synchronized control stream with exact point-sampled visualization state and positive-duration interval-sampled audio/control excitations. The stream retains world/body/base contact coordinates, disc/base/relative point velocities, explicit per-channel availability, force and torque time measures, signed work and mean work rate, contact activity, and timing-only opening/reimpact events without inventing impulse amplitude. Whole-interval boxcar coarsening is duration-weighted, partitions at event barriers, isolates endpoint-only preroll, preserves explicit audiovisual coverage and horizon semantics, reconciles per-channel work integrals, refuses non-finite or over-capacity results transactionally, and observes cancellation inside inner scans and accumulation loops. Admission now rejects contradictory contact activity, branch history, transition origin, negative base-normal force, and unrepresentable large-clock intervals. G0/G3/G4 evidence: 49 library, 9 control-stream, 7 coupled-runner, 14 render-trajectory, and 9 timeline-resampling tests pass; rustdoc and non-fatal clippy complete; ubs reports zero critical findings. No claim: boxcar coarsening is not a band-limited acoustic source model, timing-only reimpact has no inferred amplitude, controls retain source authority, and physical sound calibration/rendering remain downstream.
close_reason: Completed synchronized trajectory-derived render/audio controls with event-preserving coarsening, work reconciliation, cancellation, admission hardening, and focused G0/G3/G4 regressions; calibrated modal audio remains explicitly downstream.

title: Implement deterministic Euler render-trajectory encoding, decoding, fingerprinting, and replay
description:
## Background

A long render must not rerun mechanics for every frame or depend on in-memory Rust structs. The accepted trajectory needs a durable, content-addressed artifact suitable for independent consumers, cancellation, and exact replay.

## Technical approach

Define a bounded versioned binary or canonical structured encoding for metadata, samples, event lists, and controls. Use checked sizes and explicit little-endian float bits where bit preservation is claimed. Bind schema, source campaign/configuration, resolved geometry/mass, sample count, time range, interpolation policy, units/frames, terminal status, and payload bytes into a domain-separated fingerprint.

Decoder admission validates lengths before allocation, finiteness, monotone time, quaternion norms/canonical signs, event ordering/brackets, index references, terminal consistency, and fingerprint. Support streaming or chunking if required by measured trajectory size, with whole-artifact completeness and per-chunk integrity.

## Success criteria

Encode-decode-encode is byte-identical; corrupted/truncated/reordered data refuses; two uninterrupted/restarted equivalent runs produce identical artifacts. Renderer and sound engine consume the decoded public artifact only.

## Tests

Known-answer golden, every-prefix truncation, bit flips in metadata/sample/event, duplicate/missing chunks, max/max+1 resource budgets, allocation refusal, unsupported version, stale fingerprint, cancellation, deterministic replay, and fuzzed junk rejection. E2E decodes a campaign artifact and renders one transform plus synthesizes a control sample.

## Considerations

Do not treat file paths as identities. Logs reference relative artifacts and hashes. Partial checkpoints remain separate from published complete trajectories.

title: Define and implement the higher-fidelity Euler backend adapter to the common render trajectory contract
description:
## Background

The current cinematic critical path uses the reduced closed runner. FrankenSim also has a separately composed transactional finite-patch/partial-slip/rolling/gas/base stack that is not yet the campaign event-loop backend. The movie pipeline must not hard-code reduced-runner assumptions or claim that higher fidelity is already integrated.

## Technical approach

Define a producer trait or adapter boundary that maps any accepted Euler mechanics backend into the same render trajectory schema. Implement the reduced runner as the reference producer and add a bounded higher-fidelity prefix adapter using its actual accepted disc/base states, contact patch summaries, and channel ownership. Preserve each backend's applicability, authority, refusal, restart, timestep, and missing-channel semantics.

Do not invent terminal continuation for a backend that only supports smooth-contact prefixes. Mixed-backend splicing is forbidden unless a separate handoff contract proves state/energy/frame continuity and labels model change.

## Success criteria

The renderer and sound engine are backend-agnostic. A higher-fidelity prefix can drive the same minimal visualization without schema forks, and unsupported terminal requests produce an honest typed refusal.

## Tests

Producer conformance suite covers reduced and higher-fidelity fixtures, field completeness, frame/unit parity, restart, contact patch reduction, energy ownership, cancellation, refusal propagation, and deliberately incompatible handoff. Compare identical simple regimes where both backends apply without requiring equality outside their model scopes.

## Priority note

This is a valuable escalation lane but must not block the first cinematic unless the reduced model lacks a required state. It cannot be used to imply experimental calibration.

title: Animated scene core: transforms, motion blur, camera, and acceleration structures
description:
## Objective

Extend fs-render from a static spectral tracer into a deterministic animated-scene renderer suitable for the Euler disc. Preserve existing certified chart, NURBS, and mesh semantics while adding rigid instancing, frame/shutter time, moving cameras, and practical acceleration structures.

## Scope

Introduce validated rigid transforms and instances, ray time, transform interpolation, shutter distributions, thin-lens depth of field, camera keyframes, autofocus/focus pulls, motion bounds, and animated scene traversal. The resolved axisymmetric Euler chart must render directly in its moving body frame or through a certified transform wrapper; it must not be remeshed per frame unless an explicitly labeled preview path chooses that tradeoff.

Separate immutable geometry/material data from per-frame transforms so the disc, glass base, housing, and lights can be reused. Add top-level instance acceleration and bounded refit/rebuild policy. All time and transform inputs must reject non-finite values, invalid quaternions, singular scales, inverted shutter intervals, and out-of-domain trajectory queries.

## Quality requirement

Fast spin must produce physically meaningful shutter blur rather than frame aliasing. Camera animation must remain deterministic and avoid roll/up-vector singularities. The same frame rendered as one sample range or multiple progressive ranges must be identical.

## Success criteria

A moving certified chart and a moving triangle instance render correctly under an animated thin-lens camera; motion-blurred and zero-shutter limit fixtures pass; deterministic hashes are invariant to legal tile/sample scheduling; cancellation leaves resumable state.

## Workstream test strategy

Children own analytic ray/camera/motion fixtures, transformed-chart and BVH-oracle comparisons, zero-shutter limits, deterministic sample-partition tests, cancellation/resume, and a real moving Euler chart E2E render. Static golden images alone are insufficient.
close_reason: Epic rollup: all 6 children closed with executed evidence — 3.1 rigid instances + transformed intersection, 3.2 ray time/shutter/motion-blurred evaluation (zero-shutter limits, progressive-range equality), 3.3 thin-lens cinematic camera + keyframes + stable orientation, 3.4 deterministic TLAS with bounded refit/rebuild + budget refusal + adversarial oracle battery (closed 2026-08-16 with clause-by-clause audit), 3.5 exact motion vectors + stable hit identities, 3.6 animated scene bridge. The epic-level criteria (moving chart + triangle under an animated thin-lens camera, blur/zero-shutter fixtures, schedule-invariant hashes, cancellation) live in the children's executed batteries; the smoke/replay E2E (9.8, closed) renders the moving disc through this stack end to end. Certified-perf promotion of the acceleration remains with 5.5 by design.

title: Add validated rigid instances and transformed chart/mesh intersection
description:
## Background

fs-render currently stores geometry directly in each static primitive. Euler animation needs one immutable disc chart reused under hundreds of body poses, plus static or moving base/housing meshes. Rebuilding or transforming geometry per frame wastes work and risks losing certified chart semantics.

## Technical approach

Add an Instance abstraction separating geometry, material, emission, object identity, and a finite proper rigid transform. Transform world rays into local space, intersect through the existing certified chart/mesh backend, and transform hit points, geometric/shading normals, tangents, and derivatives back to world space. Preserve t ordering under rigid transforms and retain backend audit/authority.

Support shared immutable geometry and deterministic instance ordering/tie breaks. Reject non-unit quaternions, reflections/scales in the rigid path, non-finite translations, missing normals, and object-ID collisions. If general affine transforms are later desired, keep them separate with correct inverse-transpose and distance/error semantics.

## Success criteria

The resolved axisymmetric Euler chart can render at arbitrary poses without tessellation or certificate laundering; shared mesh instances work; translated/rotated scenes match equivalently transformed camera fixtures.

## Tests

G0/property tests cover identity, translation, rotations, composition/inverse, rigid scene-camera equivariance, normal orientation, closest-hit ordering, tangency, chart refusal propagation, mesh BVH equivalence, shared geometry, invalid transforms, deterministic ties, cancellation, and object IDs. E2E renders one moving-pose sample.

## Considerations

A visualization transform places geometry; it never changes mass/contact geometry. Instance transforms become part of frame identity but not underlying geometry identity.
close_reason: Implemented validated proper-rigid shared chart/mesh instances and production tracer integration. Proof: instances 14/14; charts 24/24; differentiable battery 9/9; tracer battery 11 passed/1 intentional ignored; local fs-render Clippy clean with only enumerated pre-existing lint classes allowed; UBS 0 critical; git diff --check clean. title: Add ray time, shutter distributions, and motion-blurred instance evaluation
description:
## Background

Euler spin and precession accelerate strongly. Sampling only one pose per frame produces wagon-wheel aliasing and unnaturally frozen edges. Cinematic motion blur requires every camera ray to carry an exposure time and evaluate moving geometry consistently.

## Technical approach

Extend Ray and sampling dimensions with normalized and absolute shutter time. Define global/frame/shot shutter-open/close semantics and deterministic distributions. Evaluate instance transforms from the event-aware trajectory interpolator at ray time; compute conservative motion bounds for acceleration traversal. Subdivide or apply the frozen policy when a shutter crosses a contact/terminal discontinuity.

Ensure additional random dimensions use stable counter domains so adding motion blur does not accidentally correlate wavelength, lens, light, or BSDF samples. Zero-width shutter must reduce exactly to static rendering.

## Success criteria

Constant-velocity/constant-spin fixtures produce analytic blur envelopes; zero shutter matches the prior static image; fast Euler motion is legible without temporal strobing; progressive sample partitioning remains replay-identical.

## Tests

Unit/property tests cover shutter endpoints, centered/front/back conventions, zero/max exposure, out-of-trajectory time, event crossing, moving-camera plus moving-object relative motion, deterministic RNG domains, motion bounds containing sampled geometry, cancellation, and malformed intervals. E2E compares high-rate reference temporal accumulation.

## No-claims

Motion blur reconstructs the supplied continuous interpolation model. It does not add mechanical bandwidth or validate unresolved terminal motion.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic backward-compatible ray-time sampling, exact shutter/progressive provenance, animated proper-rigid evaluation, conservative Hermite/rotation bounds, transactional temporal accumulation, spectral-tracer motion blur, and the event-aware Euler render bridge. Focused proof: fs-render 36 lib + 12 motion + 18 active tracer tests passed (1 unrelated opt-in test ignored); Euler bridge 9/9 passed; rustdoc and diff check passed. Strict clippy is clean for changed code and remains blocked only by five pre-existing charts.rs lints.

title: Implement thin-lens cinematic camera, keyframes, focus pulls, and stable orientation
description:
## Background

The current pinhole camera is useful for correctness fixtures but cannot produce the depth cues and controlled product-shot language expected from a Maxwell-style film.

## Technical approach

Add physically interpretable camera parameters: pose, focal length/sensor or FOV, focus distance, aperture radius/f-number, optional aperture blades, shutter interval, exposure metadata, and lens sample dimensions. Generate thin-lens rays that converge on the focus plane. Add validated camera keyframes and deterministic interpolation with stable look-at/up handling; allow explicit focus pulls and optional focus target tracking.

Keep lens distortion, chromatic aberration, rolling shutter, and autofocus heuristics out of the default unless separately enabled and labeled. Camera animation must use the same master timeline and avoid hidden smoothing.

## Success criteria

Pinhole limit reproduces the legacy camera; focused-plane fixtures are sharp; foreground/background blur follows geometry; keyframed motion is continuous and deterministic; invalid or singular cameras refuse with ranked fixes.

## Tests

Known-answer ray geometry, aperture distribution statistics, pinhole limit, focus plane, aperture rotation/blades, camera rigid-transform equivariance, nearly collinear up vector, keyframe endpoints, cuts, out-of-range times, moving focus target, RNG stream independence, cancellation, and replay hashes.

## Considerations

Depth of field and exposure are visualization choices. Extreme shallow focus must not hide the contact behavior required by the creative brief; preview mode should expose focus-distance diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented validated thin-lens cinematic camera, circular/polygon apertures, physical projection/f-number admission, robust look-at and quaternion keyframes, focus pulls/world targets, hard-cut exposure binding, deterministic lens streams, cinematic tracer integration, and progressive camera-path/shot checkpointing. title: Build deterministic animated instance acceleration with bounded refit/rebuild
description:
## Background

Hundreds of frames should reuse immutable chart/mesh acceleration rather than rebuild all geometry. Motion blur also needs conservative spatiotemporal bounds. The current scalar per-mesh BVH has no top-level instance structure.

## Technical approach

Implement a deterministic TLAS over instance motion bounds while retaining geometry-local BLAS/chart backends. Define construction ordering, tie breaks, outward-rounded slabs, finite bounds, shutter interval, and refit-versus-rebuild criteria. For analytic charts, obtain or conservatively derive local bounds. Include static lights/environment proxies where useful, but do not conflate light selection with geometry traversal.

Expose fingerprints and traversal counters. Poll cancellation at bounded node/primitive intervals; construction is transactional. Preserve a brute-force instance oracle for tests.

## Success criteria

TLAS closest hits match brute force for static and moving scenes, motion bounds never cull a sampled hit, repeated builds fingerprint identically, and per-frame refit materially reduces measured setup cost for the reference scene without changing images.

## Tests

Randomized BVH-vs-brute-force, grazing/sliver/large-coordinate cases, overlapping/tied instances, empty/one/max objects, max+1 budget refusal, invalid bounds, high angular velocity, full shutter, refit threshold, cancellation/fault cleanup, and thread-order determinism. Performance is measured separately from correctness.

## Considerations

Wide/SIMD traversal is owned by the scale workstream after profiling. This bead first establishes correct animation-aware structure.

title: Generate exact object/camera motion vectors and stable per-hit identities
description:
## Background

Temporal denoising, diagnostics, and compositing require mapping a visible surface point between frames. Screen-space velocity inferred only from depth fails on rotating discs and at disocclusions.

## Technical approach

Assign stable object, primitive/chart feature, and material identities. At each hit, retain sufficient local coordinates or a stable surface parameter to evaluate the same material point at previous/current/next reference times. Combine object and camera transforms to project motion vectors, mark disocclusions and invalid correspondences, and distinguish geometric from shading normals.

For charts without stable parameterization, define a conservative unavailable status rather than fabricate correspondence. The Euler axisymmetric chart should expose a usable local point mapping.

## Success criteria

Motion vectors match analytic translating/rotating fixtures, remain zero under common scene-camera motion, flag occlusion/topology ambiguity, and align exactly with beauty/depth/normal AOV pixels.

## Tests

Translation, rotation, camera pan, combined motion, q/-q, edge/disocclusion, off-screen projection, behind-camera, cuts, chart/mesh identities, invalid correspondence, deterministic replay, and AOV shape checks.

## Considerations

Motion vectors are rendering derivatives and cannot be fed back as measured mechanical velocity without an explicit measurement model.
close_reason: Implemented exact stable primary-hit correspondence and rigid object/camera motion-vector evaluation with focused and full fs-render verification.

title: Compose Euler disc, glass base, housing, lights, and camera into an animated scene bridge
description:
## Background

General renderer features do not by themselves create a movie. A focused bridge must map the resolved Euler specimen and trajectory into render instances, preserve scale/frames, and build the reference product scene.

## Technical approach

Consume only the public render-trajectory artifact and cinematic configuration. Create the disc from its resolved AxisymmetricChart, place it using per-time RigidBodyState, construct the glass plate/base/housing geometry from declared dimensions, attach stable materials/object IDs, instantiate lights/environment and camera, and provide frame/shutter scene evaluation. Include optional visualization-only engraving/brushing without altering the simulation chart.

Validate world units, base plane, center-of-mass offset, chart local axis, support/contact overlays, camera near/far requirements, and scene bounds. Debug mode may render axes/contact point/base mode, but those layers remain separate from beauty output.

## Success criteria

One command/library call builds every reference frame from trajectory+configuration; first/last/sample poses agree with independent coordinate checks; no hand-entered duplicate disc geometry or inertia appears.

## Tests

Known pose snapshots, unit-scale mismatch, chart identity, COM offset, base/contact alignment, material assignment, optional marker isolation, static and moving frame renders, censored trajectory, missing asset, cancellation, and deterministic scene fingerprint. E2E emits a minimal EXR of the real filleted disc.

## No-claims

Scene composition conveys simulation outputs; it does not validate them. Base/housing visual geometry may be representative unless bound to measured configuration.

## Parallelization boundary

This bridge consumes generic admitted material/light handles and must land before final look development. Its production fixture may use the simplest existing material/light needed to prove coordinate and motion composition. The reference conductor, glass, layered spin cue, and studio rig converge later in the look-development scene bead; they do not block the geometry/trajectory bridge.

title: Spectral materials, lighting, product scene, and cinematic look development
description:
## Objective

Provide the rendering features that determine whether the result looks like a scientific demo or a high-end Maxwell-style product film: physically plausible metal and glass, controlled studio/environment illumination, fine surface detail, and a deliberately composed Euler-disc scene.

## Scope

Add spectral conductor Fresnel with complex index of refraction, dielectric reflection/transmission with absorption and nested-medium rules, roughness and anisotropy, layered clearcoat where justified, procedural brushed-metal and micro-scratch normals, texture-coordinate support, multiple lights, environment maps, emissive geometry, importance sampling, and product-scene presets. Material data must name source, wavelength domain, interpolation, units, and whether it is measured, fitted, representative, or artistic.

The glass base must refract and absorb rather than masquerade as opaque GGX. Tungsten and stainless presets must be distinguishable under neutral illumination. A visualization-only engraving or subtle radial marker may make axial spin readable; it must not alter collision geometry or physical mass properties.

## Success criteria

Canonical material balls and the Euler product scene pass energy/furnace tests, dielectric critical-angle and total-internal-reflection checks, conductor comparisons against independent Fresnel evaluation, light-sampling/MIS tests, and artist-facing look controls. A reviewed 1080p still establishes the target look before final animation spending.

## Workstream test strategy

Use analytic and independent known answers for conductor/dielectric optics; furnace, reciprocity, sampling/PDF, and radiance-scaling properties for energy behavior; deterministic Monte Carlo confidence tests for light/MIS estimators; and hostile fixtures for invalid spectra, medium orientation, missing assets, and grazing paths. Material-ball and product-scene goldens are diagnostic composition evidence only, never the sole correctness oracle. Bounded logs record case/scene identity, wavelength or path class, sample budget, expected/observed value and tolerance or confidence interval, first non-finite event, and reproduction command without per-ray floods.

title: Implement spectral conductor Fresnel and tungsten/stainless material presets
description:
## Background

The current GGX material treats a lifted RGB reflectance as Schlick F0. Convincing tungsten and stainless steel require wavelength-dependent conductor Fresnel using complex refractive index and declared roughness.

## Technical approach

Add spectral conductor evaluation from eta(lambda) and k(lambda), integrated with microfacet reflection and existing hero wavelengths. Define tabulated spectral-data assets with source/provenance, wavelength range, interpolation, endpoint behavior, units, and representative-versus-measured status. Provide tungsten and one or more stainless presets plus artist-controlled roughness that does not alter optical constants.

Enforce energy bounds, finite positive data, consistent reference medium, and stable sampling/PDF. Preserve the simpler GGX path for legacy fixtures.

## Success criteria

Normal and grazing incidence match an independent Fresnel evaluator; furnace/white tests show no energy gain; tungsten and stainless render distinguishably under a neutral reference light; unsupported wavelength/data gaps refuse or use an explicit documented extension.

## Tests

Known-answer wavelengths/angles, eta/k boundaries, interpolation knots, roughness limits, reciprocity where applicable, sampling/PDF consistency, furnace, spectral packet permutation, invalid tables, deterministic replay, and material preset fingerprints. Golden material-ball images are diagnostic, not the sole oracle.

## Considerations

If exact product optical data are unavailable, label presets representative. A visual match cannot calibrate composition or surface finish.
