title: Implement spectral dielectric glass with reflection, transmission, absorption, and nested-medium semantics
description:
## Background

The Euler base is thick glass, but fs-render v1 has only opaque Lambertian/GGX surfaces. Rendering it as opaque would defeat the intended product look and hide major light-transport behavior.

## Technical approach

Add smooth and rough dielectric BSDFs with spectral index of refraction, Fresnel reflection/transmission, Jacobians/PDFs, total internal reflection, eta-scaled throughput convention, and robust ray offsets. Add Beer-Lambert absorption through homogeneous glass and an explicit medium stack or equivalent boundary rule for nested entry/exit. Define glass presets with IOR/dispersion/absorption provenance.

Ensure direct-light MIS handles delta and non-delta lobes correctly. Reject nonphysical IOR, negative extinction, inconsistent orientation, and unsupported overlapping media. Keep caustic limitations explicit for unidirectional tracing.

## Success criteria

Air-glass analytic Fresnel, Snell law, critical angle, slab transmittance, and nested interface fixtures pass; the reference plate is visibly refractive and energy-conserving; no NaNs/fireflies arise from grazing cases.

## Tests

Normal/grazing angles, entering/exiting, TIR, equal-IOR null interface, roughness limits, absorption length scaling, reversed normals, thin/thick slabs, nested media, MIS delta paths, cancellation, replay, and independent analytic checks. Include a glass-slab golden only as composition evidence.

## No-claims

The v1 path tracer may converge poorly on difficult caustics. Denoising or clamping cannot be called unbiased; limitations must be visible in the quality report.

title: Add anisotropic/layered surface detail and visualization-only spin cues
description:
## Background

A perfectly axisymmetric, uniformly shaded disc reveals precession but not rotation about its own axis. Subtle brushed-metal anisotropy or a tiny engraving can make spin readable without corrupting simulation geometry.

## Technical approach

Add tangent-frame support, anisotropic microfacet roughness, procedural radial/circular brushing, bounded normal perturbation or bump mapping, and optional layered clearcoat if the material model remains energy-consistent. Define stable local UV/parameter coordinates for the axisymmetric chart. Add an optional engraved/printed radial reference mark as a shading/texture layer only.

Bind texture/procedure parameters and assets into material identity. Distinguish geometric normal, shading normal, and simulation contact normal; shading perturbations must not affect intersection, contact, mass, or motion vectors.

## Success criteria

Spin direction/rate is perceptually readable in preview and motion blur; tangent orientation follows the moving body; disabling detail returns the base material; energy and normal constraints hold.

## Tests

Chart seam/pole behavior, tangent handedness, rigid rotation, anisotropy swap, zero-detail limit, bounded normals, texture filtering under minification, marker identity, motion-vector compatibility, deterministic sampling, and an assertion that physical chart/mass fingerprints are unchanged.

## Considerations

Avoid implausibly strong marks added solely for spectacle. Creative review chooses the subtlety, while manifests preserve the exact visualization transform.

title: Implement multiple emitters, environment lighting, and deterministic importance sampling
description:
## Background

The current tracer supports exactly one rectangular NEE light and no environment. High-end product imagery needs several large soft sources, rim control, background illumination, and optionally an HDR environment.

## Technical approach

Generalize scene lights to multiple rectangles/emissive primitives plus an environment radiance map or analytic studio dome. Build deterministic power/solid-angle-aware selection, alias table or light BVH as warranted, and MIS against BSDF sampling. Importance-sample environment luminance with correct spherical Jacobian and declared color/spectral interpretation. Support finite black environments and no-light refusal.

Keep light sampling identity stable under legal construction order; bind asset bytes and transform. Expose selection/PDF diagnostics and avoid double-counting emissive hits.

## Success criteria

Multi-light estimates match summed single-light references statistically; environment sampling is unbiased; MIS weights close; the reference studio rig produces soft readable reflections on metal and glass without hidden emitters.

## Tests

Zero/one/many lights, duplicate/zero-power lights, environment constant/bright pixel, rotation, PDF normalization, selection frequencies, MIS partition, emissive-hit accounting, extreme dynamic range, invalid map, cancellation, deterministic streams, and furnace/white scenes.

## Considerations

HDR assets may be externally authored but are immutable inputs, not runtime dependencies. Firefly mitigation must be reported as biased if it clips energy.

## Environment asset ingestion boundary

Because fs-img intentionally reads only FrankenSim's own PNG/EXR subsets, define one canonical environment-map artifact (linear float pixels plus spectral/color interpretation and spherical layout) that the renderer consumes. Accept our supported EXR subset directly or use a separate explicit import/conversion step for foreign HDR formats; never smuggle a general external image decoder into the production graph. Tests cover orientation, seam/poles, color interpretation, malformed dimensions, hash binding, and converter provenance.
close_reason: Implemented and verified deterministic multi-emitter and environment lighting; downstream artistic look-development remains separately tracked.

title: Improve glossy/transmissive path robustness and quantify caustic convergence limits
description:
## Background

Glass on a glossy base can create difficult high-variance paths. A unidirectional NEE tracer can render many such effects but converges slowly for focused caustics, and naive clamping can make a beautiful but biased image.

## Technical approach

First profile reference glass/metal shots. Improve BSDF sampling using GGX VNDF where it materially reduces variance; add Russian roulette with correct throughput/PDF treatment; harden specular chain offsets and finite checks. Evaluate optional explicitly biased firefly filtering/clamping only as a labeled display derivative, never in raw master estimates. Record unresolved bidirectional/manifold/caustic techniques as successors rather than expanding without evidence.

## Success criteria

Reference shots show lower variance at equal path count, no systematic energy drift, and no non-finite paths. Raw and biased mitigation outputs remain distinguishable. If profiling shows caustics are not a blocker, close with measured refusal instead of unnecessary transport machinery.

## Tests

Furnace/white, VNDF distribution/PDF, roughness extremes, long specular chains, roulette survival compensation, bright caustic fixture convergence, firefly label propagation, cancellation, replay, and equal-spp variance comparison with confidence intervals.

## Considerations

This is a conditional quality optimization and must not block the first film unless glass convergence actually fails the target.

title: Author and freeze the reference Euler studio scene and 1080p look-development still
description:
## Background

Renderer features need a concrete artistic target. This bead turns materials, lights, camera, base geometry, and background into a reviewed reference scene before hundreds of final frames are rendered.

## Technical approach

Author the product scene entirely through the cinematic configuration: resolved disc instance; thick shallow-curved glass plate; representative rigid housing/outriggers if desired; neutral backdrop; conductor/glass presets; two/three large studio sources or environment; camera composition, aperture, focus, exposure, and tone-map intent. Produce a small matrix of tungsten/stainless and key/rim ratios at 1080p.

Select one reference still using both creative criteria and technical diagnostics: readable silhouette/contact, plausible glass, controlled highlights, no clipped channels, acceptable raw variance, correct material identities, and no hidden visualization elements. Freeze configuration/asset hashes, not just image bytes.

## Success criteria

A future agent can reproduce the selected still with one command and understand every creative choice from the bead/configuration. The still establishes the final film's look but does not freeze camera motion or sound.

## Tests

Scene admission, asset identity, material/light assignments, exposure bounds, AOV completeness, deterministic raw EXR hash, denoised bias tag, invalid/missing asset refusal, and a low-spp e2e render. Independent pixel probes verify key regions; visual review is recorded separately from numerical tests.

## Considerations

Do not chase perfect 4K convergence here. This is the inexpensive decision point for composition and look.

title: 4K throughput: tile parallelism, adaptive sampling, resumability, and performance qualification
description:
## Objective

Make 3840x2160 multi-frame rendering operationally feasible on CPU systems without weakening deterministic replay or cancellation semantics. The current serial row/pixel/sample loop and full-film transactional clone are acceptable correctness scaffolding but not a movie renderer.

## Scale facts

A 4K RGB f64 accumulation plane is about 190 MiB. Transactional staging currently doubles that before conversion buffers. At 256 spp one frame launches approximately 2.12 billion camera paths; a 240-frame shot is roughly 510 billion paths. Uncompressed float RGB EXR is about 100 MB per frame before metadata. Every optimization here must address a measured bottleneck and preserve image semantics.

## Scope

Implement deterministic tile-parallel rendering through fs-exec, tile-local transactional accumulation, bounded merge, variance/AOV statistics, adaptive stopping with replayable decisions, progressive checkpoints, frame and tile sharding, resume after cancellation or process loss, instance acceleration/refit, and admitted resource budgets. Qualify scalar and optimized paths against identical reference scenes. Wide/SIMD BVH or ray-stream work is included only where profiling demonstrates value for the reference film.

## Success criteria

The reference 1080p daily and one representative 4K frame complete within declared machine-specific envelopes, scale across admitted worker counts, reproduce bytes or declared numeric envelopes as appropriate, resume without double-counting, and report truthful NO-DATA when host admission prevents a performance claim.

## Workstream test strategy

Children own worker/tile/sample permutation tests, serial-oracle comparisons, adaptive-stop falsifiers, checkpoint corruption and exact-resume journeys, shard completeness tests, resource-boundary refusal, and admitted host-specific performance measurements. DSR correctness does not substitute for performance evidence.

title: Replace serial full-film traversal with deterministic fs-exec tile-parallel rendering
description:
## Background

render_range currently clones the whole film transactionally and loops serially over rows, pixels, and samples. At 4K this consumes roughly 380 MiB for the two f64 XYZ buffers before AOVs and leaves CPU cores idle.

## Technical approach

Plan fixed logical tiles independent of worker count. Assign counter-based sample streams by pixel/sample/dimension, not thread. Render each tile into bounded private accumulation/AOV buffers, poll cancellation at sample/bounce/tile boundaries, and merge through deterministic logical tile order or exact per-pixel ownership. Publish a sample range only after all required tiles complete; retain completed tile checkpoints internally for resume without exposing a falsely complete film.

Use fs-exec throughput lane and explicit Cx/budgets. Reserve memory before launch, bound queue depth, drain children after cancellation/panic, and prevent double-counting on retry. Preserve a serial oracle path.

## Success criteria

Images are bit-identical across 1/2/4/8 workers and tile traversal schedules on the same ISA; cancellation drains with no leaked work; live memory remains within the admitted tile/AOV envelope; reference workloads scale materially versus serial.

## Tests

Tile partition boundaries, odd dimensions, one/max tiles, worker counts, sample-range partitioning, forced scheduling permutations, injected worker panic, cancellation before/during/merge, allocation refusal, retry/resume, serial equality, and deterministic hashes. Performance logs separate setup, traversal, merge, and idle time.

## Considerations

Do not require a global film clone for transactional semantics. Exact byte identity is more important than opportunistic floating merge order.

title: Add per-pixel/tile variance AOVs and deterministic adaptive sampling
description:
## Background

Uniform high spp wastes paths on converged backgrounds while glossy metal/glass regions remain noisy. Adaptive sampling can make 4K feasible, but stopping decisions must be deterministic, statistically interpretable, and replayable.

## Technical approach

Accumulate stable first/second moments or an equivalent variance estimator per beauty channel and relevant AOV. At deterministic sample batches, compute a declared absolute/relative error proxy with dark-pixel handling. Stop pixels or tiles only at fixed checkpoints using stable thresholds and minimum/maximum spp. Store the decision map, estimator version, samples consumed, and thresholds in checkpoint/artifact identity.

Ensure adaptive choices do not change RNG sequences for continuing pixels and do not treat denoised output as convergence evidence. Provide uniform mode as oracle and final-quality fallback.

## Success criteria

Analytic constant scenes stop near minimum spp; noisy glossy fixtures receive more samples; repeated/thread-count runs produce identical decisions; the reference still reaches equal or better error at fewer paths than its uniform baseline.

## Tests

Zero variance, dark pixels, high dynamic range, min/max spp, exact threshold, batch sizes, NaNs, cancellation, resume, tile ordering, radiance scaling, sample-count conservation, and comparison against independent repeated-run error. Negative test proves denoiser output cannot satisfy the raw estimator.

## Considerations

This gives a render-error heuristic, not a formal image-error certificate. Quality targets remain scene/profile specific.

## Ownership boundary

This bead owns variance and sample-count accumulation needed for adaptive decisions directly in fs-render. It does not wait on the complete cinematic AOV package; fs-img/fs-render AOV integration consumes these statistics later.

Added G0/G3/G4/G5 unit and E2E coverage for validation, transactional arithmetic, constant/dark/HDR behavior, noisy glossy allocation, independent-seed error comparison, worker/tile invariance, sample conservation, memory refusal, cancellation, exact resume, and Euler bridge execution identity. title: Implement crash-safe progressive film/AOV checkpoints and exact resume
description:
## Background

A final sequence can run for hours or days. Cancellation, deadlines, or process loss must not discard completed work or cause repeated samples, yet partially rendered frames must never appear complete.

## Technical approach

Define a versioned checkpoint binding frame, shot, source trajectory/configuration/scene identities, dimensions, AOV layout, sampler domains, sample/adaptive state, completed logical tiles/ranges, numeric accumulators, and schema/build semantics. Write transactionally through temporary/new artifact publication without deleting prior valid checkpoints. On resume, validate every identity and buffer shape, then continue exactly missing work.

Support periodic checkpoint cadence bounded by I/O budget, final checkpoint compaction if useful, and explicit stale/incompatible refusal with ranked repair. A completed raw EXR and manifest entry are published only after all frame criteria pass.

## Success criteria

Interrupted+resumed output equals uninterrupted output; corrupt/truncated/stale checkpoints refuse; sample counts never double; cancelled writes preserve the previous recoverable checkpoint.

## Tests

Cancellation at encode/write/seal, every-prefix truncation, bit corruption, wrong frame/config/scene/build, missing AOV, reordered tiles, one-short budgets, repeated resume, concurrent claim conflict, disk-full/injected I/O failure, and deterministic equality. E2E kills a representative frame midway and resumes.

## Considerations

Use existing artifact/ledger primitives where they add direct value. Do not build a new general checkpoint framework.

title: Add deterministic frame/tile sharding and bounded multi-process render plans
description:
## Background

Frames are naturally parallel, and very expensive frames may be split by sample or tile. A deterministic render plan allows available machines/processes to help without a network scheduler becoming a prerequisite.

## Technical approach

Generate a canonical finite work plan keyed by sequence/frame/tile/sample-range identity with checked resource estimates and dependencies. Allow disjoint workers to claim explicit shards, write immutable result artifacts, and merge only complete compatible shards. Make order irrelevant and duplicate submission idempotent. Detect missing, overlapping, stale, or foreign shards.

Keep orchestration local/file-artifact based initially; remote transport is outside scope. Respect frame dependencies introduced by temporal denoising by rendering raw frames independently and scheduling finishing after neighbor availability.

## Success criteria

Single-process and sharded renders merge identically; duplicate/reordered shards are harmless; incomplete plans cannot finalize; the plan is bounded and human inspectable.

## Tests

One/many frames, tile/sample splits, permutation, duplicate, overlap, gap, wrong identity, corrupt shard, cancellation, worker failure, resource cap, and replay. E2E renders a tiny sequence with two independent workers/processes.

## Considerations

This bead enables parallel work; it does not claim cluster fault tolerance or introduce a distributed database.

## Ownership boundary

Raw frame/tile/sample work planning is derived from cinematic configuration and renderer checkpoints, not from a finalized frame-sequence manifest. Sequence publication later consumes completed shard results; this avoids serializing render scaling behind image packaging.

Renderer merge derives exact complete-set aggregate bytes before map allocation, chooses canonical expected semantics, and applies fixed order-independent structural/integrity/conflict diagnostics. Scene/light admission now polls Cx per light/primitive and uses cancellation-controlled keyed ordering instead of an unbounded sort while preserving legacy light bits. Public result-byte refusal maps to Euler ResultByteLimit consistently. title: Profile and qualify the reference renderer at 1080p and representative 4K scale
description:
## Background

The film needs truthful feasibility evidence after tile/adaptive/checkpoint work. Performance must be measured on admitted idle fingerprinted hosts; DSR correctness does not establish ray rate.

## Technical approach

Profile the reference scene by camera rays, secondary rays, chart/mesh intersections, BSDF/light sampling, film/AOV memory, checkpoint I/O, and denoise/output time. Compare serial/tiled, worker counts, uniform/adaptive, TLAS refit/rebuild, and relevant compiler/ISA modes. Use capped raw measurements and record host/topology/build/config identities.

Only if traversal remains dominant and existing scalar BVH misses target should this bead trigger a focused wide/SIMD BVH or ray-stream successor; it relates to existing render performance bead frankensim-ok84 rather than duplicating generic ray-rate governance.

## Success criteria

A user can estimate time, peak memory, storage, and expected checkpoint cadence before launch. Scaling and bottlenecks are measured, regression thresholds are justified, and unavailable/non-idle hosts yield NO-DATA rather than fabricated pass.

## Tests

Benchmark admission, warmup/repetition, outlier policy, worker scaling, deterministic-image comparison, memory cap, cancellation overhead, cold/warm checkpoints, profile parsing, stale baseline, and negative host-admission fixture. Produce a bounded machine-readable report and human summary.

title: Animation image pipeline: AOVs, temporal stability, color, and frame artifacts
description:
## Objective

Turn raw spectral film estimates into durable master frames and attractive temporally stable display images while retaining provenance and bias labels.

## Scope

Emit beauty, albedo, normal, depth, variance, object/material identity, and motion-vector AOVs as needed by denoising and diagnosis. Extend denoising from the existing labeled single-frame à-trous path to an animation-aware pipeline with disocclusion and history rejection. Define exposure, white balance, highlight handling, tone mapping, gamut policy, optional glare/bloom, dithering, and 8/16-bit preview conversion. Raw EXR masters remain authoritative Monte Carlo outputs; denoised/tone-mapped derivatives can never replace them in numerical comparisons.

Add deterministic frame naming, per-frame metadata, sequence manifest, hashes, source trajectory/configuration identity, missing/corrupt frame detection, and bounded storage estimates. Compression improvements are allowed only with byte-exact round-trip tests and no foreign runtime dependency.

## Success criteria

Static regions do not flicker, moving highlights do not leave temporal ghosts, disocclusions reset history, all AOVs align and round-trip, color transforms have known-answer tests, and a cancelled sequence publishes no falsely complete manifest.

## Workstream test strategy

Use known-answer and round-trip unit tests for AOV layouts, EXR/preview encoding, color transforms, and manifest identities; property/metamorphic tests for channel alignment, exposure scaling, frame-order independence, raw/derived isolation, and cancellation/finalization; and short temporal fixtures for motion, disocclusion, highlight stability, and history rejection. The production-backed E2E sequence includes missing, reordered, stale, corrupt, wrong-profile, and authority-loss twins. Bounded diagnostics identify the first bad shot/frame/AOV and expected/observed metadata or error margin without logging pixels individually.

title: Extend spectral film and EXR output with aligned diagnostic and denoise AOVs

## Background

## Technical approach

Define typed AOV semantics, channel names/types, units/frames, invalid-background values, filtering rules, and accumulation behavior. Generate AOVs from the same accepted primary/path state as beauty so pixels remain aligned. Continuous features may be filtered; categorical IDs require deterministic nearest/dominant semantics. Bind source trajectory, frame time/shutter, scene/config, sampler, spp/adaptive map, and raw-estimate authority into EXR attributes or companion manifest.

Extend Film/checkpoints transactionally and budget all buffers. Preserve existing RGB-only compatibility where requested, but final cinematic mode requires the frozen AOV set.

## Success criteria

All AOVs align at 4K, round-trip through fs-img, support motion/denoise consumers, and never contain silent NaNs or unit ambiguity. Raw beauty remains untouched by downstream finishing.

## Tests

Empty/background, one hit, edges, glass transmission, motion, IDs, normal spaces, depth range, adaptive sample counts, shape/buffer mismatch, EXR channel ordering/types, metadata round-trip, cancellation, and deterministic hashes. Cross-check selected pixels against direct intersection calculations.

## Considerations

Avoid storing expensive AOVs with no consumer. The quality profile selects a justified set, and omissions are explicit.

title: Implement animation-aware denoising with temporal reprojection and disocclusion rejection
description:
## Background

The existing à-trous denoiser is a labeled single-frame method. Independently denoising noisy frames can flicker; blindly reusing history can ghost moving highlights and contact edges.

## Technical approach

Add a permanently bias-labeled temporal denoise path using motion vectors, depth, normal, object/material identity, variance, and sample counts. Reproject prior estimates, validate history with configurable geometric/feature thresholds, reject disocclusions/cuts/invalid motion, clamp history in a declared neighborhood if used, then apply spatial à-trous refinement. Track history length/confidence and ensure shot boundaries reset state.

Operate only on raw AOV inputs and emit a derived artifact referencing every source frame. Do not feed denoised values back into adaptive convergence.

## Success criteria

Static regions show measurably reduced temporal variance; moving disc edges and highlights avoid visible trails; cuts/disocclusions reset; output always carries BiasedDenoised provenance and exact algorithm/parameter identity.

## Tests

Static noisy sequence, translating/rotating object, disocclusion, camera cut, missing/corrupt neighbor, zero/large motion, reflective highlight, glass edge, invalid IDs/depth/normals, frame-order permutation refusal, cancellation, and deterministic replay. Quantify flicker/MSE against a higher-spp reference without claiming perceptual metric sufficiency.

## Considerations

Temporal denoising creates frame dependencies and may be disabled for diagnostic raw comparisons. Aesthetic approval supplements, not replaces, numeric tests.

title: Add cinematic color management, highlight handling, glare, and preview conversion
description:
## Background

fs-img currently provides exposure, white balance, Hable tone mapping, and sRGB 8-bit output. Product-quality metal/glass highlights need a deliberately frozen color pipeline, 16-bit previews, and optional lens/display effects without damaging raw EXR masters.

## Technical approach

Define a linear working-space and display transform policy; add a modern filmic option such as ACES-like or AgX-like curve only if implemented from a frozen documented formulation; support exposure/white balance, gamut mapping, 8/16-bit quantization with deterministic dithering, and metadata. Implement optional glare/bloom as a labeled visualization derivative with bounded convolution and energy-aware threshold.

Retain Hable for compatibility and provide known transformations. Do not silently clip negative/over-range values; expose counts and chosen handling. Wide-gamut/ICC support may remain a no-claim if not needed for the reference delivery.

## Success criteria

Reference color ramps and HDR highlights transform predictably; metal/glass highlights retain detail; preview encodes are deterministic; raw master channels remain unchanged; every derivative records pipeline/version/parameters.

## Tests

Known color vectors, gray neutrality, exposure stops, white balance, negative/NaN/inf, gamut extremes, tone-curve monotonicity, quantization endpoints, dither statistics/seed, glare impulse/constant images, 8/16-bit PNG round-trip, and replay. External dev oracle may inspect files but cannot define authority.

## Considerations

“Looks amazing” includes color judgment; freeze one reference display target while keeping configuration explicit.

title: Implement deterministic frame-sequence artifacts, completeness manifests, and storage accounting
description:
## Background

Hundreds of EXR/PNG files need stable names, identities, completeness checks, and source linkage. Directory presence is not proof of a complete or internally consistent sequence.

## Technical approach

Define frame artifact identities and canonical relative names using shot/frame/time/profile, while content hashes remain authoritative. Produce a sequence manifest listing exact expected frames, source trajectory/config/scene/build identities, raw/derived class, AOV channels, spp/adaptive statistics, dimensions, timestamps, hashes, byte sizes, and completion state. Separate raw masters, denoised intermediates, display previews, and optional overlays.

Validate free-space/output budgets before rendering and incrementally account bytes. Finalize atomically only after every expected artifact verifies. Missing, duplicate, stale, corrupt, wrong-resolution, wrong-time, or cross-profile frames refuse. Never delete artifacts automatically.

## Success criteria

The sequence can be independently audited without opening images; a cancelled run remains resumable but incomplete; final manifests are deterministic under frame production order.

## Tests

Zero/one/many frames, reordered production, duplicate, missing, stale hash, wrong AOV/dimension/time/profile, max/max+1 storage, cancellation before seal, interrupted manifest, retry, path relocation, and deterministic canonical encoding. E2E assembles a tiny mixed raw/derived sequence.

## Considerations

Uncompressed EXR storage can be large. Compression is a separate measured option; storage accounting must remain truthful.
close_reason: Completed deterministic v2 sequence manifests, exact storage accounting, resumable finalization, and focused real-codec regression coverage.

title: Add optional scientific overlays and sidecar diagnostics without contaminating beauty masters
description:
## Background

title: Simulation-driven sound: modal synthesis, spatialization, WAV, and acoustic no-claims
description:
## Objective

Create synchronized, compelling sound derived from the Euler trajectory while keeping artistic sonification, physically informed modal synthesis, and predictive calibrated acoustics rigorously distinct.

## Scope

Define audio authority tiers; convert contact force/work, rolling/gas channels, base motion, spin, precession, impacts, and event brackets into band-limited excitation signals; implement damped disc/base resonators; mix continuous rolling noise and discrete reimpact events; resample deterministically to 48 kHz; spatialize relative to camera/microphone geometry; apply an explicitly chosen room/listener response; and write deterministic PCM/float WAV with timeline metadata.

The preferred first-film path is physically informed modal synthesis: modes, damping/Q, gains, and radiation filters are declared model inputs. The full open fs-acoustics program remains an escalation path for calibrated structural-acoustic coupling and exterior radiation, not a prerequisite for a cinematic result.

## Terminal sound boundary

The reduced mechanics terminates before resolving the final elastic/contact/thin-air-film acoustic regime. The soundtrack may taper, extrapolate under a declared model, or use an artistic terminal chirp. It may not claim to predict the real finite-time singularity sound. Acoustic frequency alone cannot establish contact frequency.

## Success criteria

Waveforms are deterministic, band-limited, synchronized within the frozen A/V tolerance, free of clipping/NaNs/discontinuities, distinguish declared material/base presets, survive missing-event and censored trajectories, and retain a machine-readable sound-model receipt.

## Workstream test strategy

Children own analytic resonator/filter/resampler/WAV tests, event and clock boundary fixtures, chunk/resume equivalence, clipping/alias/click checks, authority-promotion mutants, and a synchronized trajectory-to-WAV E2E journey. Listening review supplements rather than replaces these checks.
notes: 2026-08-12 active: prior smooth/rough/support/disc-only WAVs are rejected for production (missing carrier or nonconverged topology/waveform/modal weighting). Landed generic count-certified residual/enrichment structural basis, solver-neutral broadband radiation fitting, fs-vfit runtime, and batched BEM solves. Current bounded work adds persistent filter-bank state and finite exterior-point Helmholtz pressure, then integrates certified enrichment modes driven by existing moving point-force projection. No hand-fit chirp/noise or per-clip normalization; 48 kHz first rung; physically valid listener pressure and remote convergence/audition are required before mux.

title: Freeze sound authority tiers, listener geometry, clocks, and synthesis configuration
description:
## Background

The soundtrack can range from artistic sonification to calibrated structural acoustics. A single undifferentiated “simulated sound” label would invite overclaiming and make A/V synchronization fragile.

## Technical approach

Define three sound authority tiers: ArtisticSonification, PhysicallyInformedModalSynthesis, and CalibratedStructuralAcoustics. The reference film uses the middle tier. Define source controls, modal/material/base parameters, listener/microphone pose relative to animated camera, room response, sample rate (48 kHz), channel layout, amplitude/reference convention, headroom, timeline origin, resampler/filter versions, and censored/terminal policy.

Bind source trajectory/control/config identities and all synthesis parameters into a sound receipt. Define which later evidence could promote a calibrated claim and connect that escalation to the existing open fs-acoustics bead without blocking this program.

## Success criteria

Every waveform and audio-derived metric identifies its tier and assumptions; A/V clocks share an exact rational mapping; unknown/missing parameters refuse; no lower tier can be relabeled upward.

## Tests

Schema/version, sample-rate/channel boundaries, listener frames, missing modes, invalid damping/gain, timeline mismatch, authority promotion mutants, censored trajectories, and deterministic identity. Human and machine metadata agree.

## No-claims

Acoustic resemblance, frequency scaling, or alignment with precession does not validate source attribution, finite-time singularity, or physical SPL.

title: Implement damped modal resonators for the disc, glass plate, and base assembly
description:
## Background

Physically informed sound should emerge from declared resonant modes excited by simulated contact/base channels, rather than arbitrary pitch mapping. Full finite-element structural acoustics is unnecessary for the first film.

## Technical approach

Implement stable damped second-order modal resonators in discrete time with frequency, damping/Q, modal mass/normalization, source participation, and output/radiation gains. Provide representative parameter sets for tungsten/stainless discs and glass/base, clearly labeled fitted/representative unless calibrated. Support coupled or independent mode banks and time-varying source location participation where justified.

Use numerically stable coefficient generation, bounded state, explicit peak/RMS convention, and deterministic math. Preserve total model identity and report modal energies to diagnose runaway synthesis.

## Success criteria

Impulse and harmonic responses match analytic damped oscillators; decay/Q and resonant frequencies are correct; energy decays without excitation; presets sound distinct but remain honestly labeled.

## Tests

Impulse/step/sine, zero/critical/high damping, Nyquist proximity refusal, long decay stability, mode ordering/permutation, duplicate modes, zero coupling, source-position participation, material presets, cancellation, resume state, deterministic bits/envelope, and independent analytic reference.

## Considerations

Representative modes are an auditory model, not measured eigenfrequencies. Full fs-acoustics/structural modes can replace parameters through the same interface later.

title: Implement deterministic multirate resampling and sample-accurate A/V synchronization
description:
## Background

Mechanics, video frames, shutter samples, and 48 kHz audio use different rates. Drift of even a few samples can detach impacts from visible contact, while poor interpolation aliases the terminal acceleration.

## Technical approach

Use the frozen rational master clock. Implement bounded band-limited resampling for continuous controls and exact placement/fractional-delay treatment for event impulses. Record filter design, length, pass/stop bands, latency, boundary padding, and group-delay compensation. Maintain streaming state for cancellation/resume and exact chunk concatenation.

Generate frame-to-sample markers and alignment diagnostics. Refuse source bandwidth above what the trajectory sampling can support rather than fabricating high-frequency content.

## Success criteria

Chunked and one-shot output match; event alignment remains within the frozen tolerance; no drift accumulates over the full film; passband/alias attenuation meet declared bounds.

## Tests

DC, impulse, swept sine, rational ratios, source-rate changes, short signals, boundaries, event at half-sample, frame cuts, long-duration drift, censored end, invalid rates, filter budget, cancellation/resume, and independent spectral measurements.

## Considerations

The resampler cannot recover absent mechanical bandwidth. It communicates that limit to the sound receipt.

title: Implement pure-Rust WAV encoding, stem mixing, metering, and audio artifact manifests
description:
## Background

FrankenSim has PNG/EXR writers but no audio container. The canonical movie deliverable needs a deterministic WAV alongside its frame sequence without adding a foreign runtime dependency.

Implement deterministic stem gain/pan/mix, headroom, limiter only if explicitly biased/labeled, peak/true-peak/RMS and documented programme-loudness diagnostics, DC check, and clipping refusal or declared handling. The writer accepts dry stems or already spatialized stems under an explicit channel-layout receipt; WAV encoding and the canonical dry mix must not depend on camera-relative room processing. Produce a sound manifest binding source trajectory, synthesis receipt, channel layout, sample count/duration, bytes, and hash.

Provide a reader for the emitted subset for tests/replay. Unknown/general WAV features may return Unsupported.

## Success criteria

Encoded duration is sample-exact; round-trip preserves supported samples within format semantics; mix equals sum under declared gains; malformed inputs refuse; final audio aligns with video manifest. Loudness/headroom targets are measured and reported without silent gain normalization, and dry output remains available when optional spatialization is absent.

## Tests

## Considerations

Do not implement a general media library. WAV is the authoritative audio artifact; compressed audio belongs to optional mux/encoder output. Stereo spatialization and room response improve the reference daily/final mix but are a separate transform, so they cannot block the core writer, dry fixture, or artifact verifier.

title: Design an honest terminal-sound policy and optional artistic singularity chirp
description:
## Background

Steve Mould's motivating disc makes a characteristic accelerating terminal sound associated with finite-time-singularity models. The current reduced Euler runner terminates at an inclination threshold and does not resolve the final elastic/contact/thin-air-film/acoustic physics. Simply extrapolating it into audible infinity would be misleading.

## Technical approach

Define three terminal policies: end/taper at last supported simulation time; bounded extrapolation under an explicit parametric model and horizon; or an artistic chirp driven by final supported trend. The reference film may use the artistic option if it materially improves the experience. Freeze chirp law, caps, duration, amplitude envelope, band limits, anti-alias behavior, and crossfade into physical/modal stems. Mark every synthesized sample outside supported trajectory time in the receipt/sidecar.

Handle terminal-inclination, horizon-censored, and numerical-refusal trajectories differently. Never generate a triumphant “stop” sound for censored data without explicit edit intent.

## Success criteria

The audible ending is compelling and free of clicks/aliasing while metadata makes its authority unmistakable. Disabling the artistic layer yields the supported physically informed mix exactly.

## Tests

All terminal dispositions, zero/positive trend, extreme predicted frequency, cap crossings, crossfade continuity, sample-rate invariance, alias suppression, deterministic output, missing final state, and authority-label mutation. Human creative review is recorded separately.

## Considerations

This is a deliberate product feature, not evidence of the mathematical or physical singularity.

title: Define the optional bridge from calibrated fs-acoustics outputs into cinematic sound
description:
## Background

The open frankensim-ext-acoustics-core-0ja4 program plans structural-acoustic coupling, interior/exterior propagation, and validated acoustic QoIs. The cinematic pipeline should be ready to consume those outputs later without making that 40-hour-plus scientific program a prerequisite now.

## Technical approach

Define an adapter contract for time/frequency acoustic pressure or source-transfer artifacts with observation geometry, phase convention, reference/calibration, bandwidth, clock, uncertainty/authority, source identity, and applicability. Convert admitted waveforms to cinematic stems without changing calibrated values; any room/mastering transform creates a derived artifact. Refuse incompatible clocks, gauges, phasor peak/RMS conventions, absent source transfer, or authority gaps.

Implement a synthetic/analytic adapter fixture only; production calibration waits on the owning fs-acoustics bead and Euler DAQ beads. Add related dependency edges rather than falsely closing their work here.

## Success criteria

A future calibrated artifact can replace/augment the modal stem through one typed boundary; lower-authority data cannot enter the Calibrated tier; current film remains independent.

## Tests

Analytic tone/impulse fixture, time/frequency convention, phase, units, observation frame, bandwidth, sample clock, uncertainty, source identity, authority promotion attacks, cancellation, and deterministic conversion.

## Priority note

This is an escalation seam and may close after the first film. It must not absorb implementation of the full acoustics program.

title: Cinematic CLI, frame/audio job orchestration, dailies, and media assembly
description:
## Objective

Expose the vertical slice as one understandable, cancellable, resumable workflow rather than requiring bespoke developer commands. A user supplies an Euler trajectory or simulation configuration plus a cinematic configuration and receives previews, masters, audio, manifests, and optionally a muxed movie.

## Scope

Add a typed cinematic configuration, static admission with ranked diagnostics, one CLI entry point, deterministic job graph, preview/daily mode, final mode, progress reporting, checkpoint discovery, frame/audio synchronization, artifact directories, and final completeness checks. Provide fast 1080p low-spp dailies that preserve composition and timing while clearly differing from final quality.

Video encoding/muxing must respect the Franken-only production graph. The canonical output is an image sequence plus WAV and manifest. An optional official quarantined out-of-process adapter may invoke a pinned external encoder such as ffmpeg, record executable/version/arguments and output hash, and remain incapable of upgrading simulation or render authority.

## Success criteria

One repository-relative command can start, cancel, resume, inspect, and complete the reference film. Interrupted work is reused safely; changed inputs invalidate only affected artifacts; missing frames/audio refuse finalization; logs remain bounded and actionable.

## Workstream test strategy

Children own CLI/config boundary tests, deterministic job-graph and invalidation matrices, cancellation/drain/resume journeys, complete 1080p daily execution, artifact-only independent verification, and hostile media-adapter process tests. No named skip or pending job is a passing result.

title: Implement the cinematic CLI and static admission diagnostics

## Background

## Technical approach

Add a cinematic command with subcommands or modes for inspect, storyboard, daily, representative-4k-frame, final, resume, verify, and optional mux. Accept the versioned cinematic configuration and either an existing trajectory artifact or an explicit request to run the reduced Euler campaign. Resolve capabilities/assets/budgets, compute composition identities and invalidation, and print a deterministic plan summary.

Diagnostics include stable reason codes, field paths, units, required/available resources, and ranked fixes. Dry-run performs no render/audio writes. Defaults are explicit named profiles; final mode never silently falls back to daily quality.

## Success criteria

A newcomer can discover, validate, launch, cancel, resume, and verify the reference film from documented repository-relative commands. Invalid inputs fail before expensive work and explain repairs.

## Tests

Argument/schema parsing, unknown modes/versions, missing trajectory/assets/capability, conflicting profiles, output budget, dry-run no writes, final-vs-preview guard, deterministic diagnostics/order, redaction, cancellation exit class, and help examples. E2E invokes each main mode on tiny fixtures.

Keep CLI output concise; detailed bounded JSONL goes to artifacts. Core library code does not print casually.

title: Implement deterministic cinematic job graph, invalidation, progress, cancellation, and resume
description:
## Background

Trajectory production, raw frame shards, temporal finishing, audio stems, WAV, manifests, and muxing form a dependency graph. Ad-hoc loops make restart and partial invalidation unreliable.

## Technical approach

Build the smallest domain-specific job plan needed for this film using existing session/execution/artifact primitives. Nodes have immutable identities, declared inputs/outputs/budgets, dependencies, cancellation/drain/finalize semantics, and terminal dispositions. Plan trajectory once, raw frames independently, temporal finishing after neighbors, audio controls/modes/WAV on their own lane, sequence/audio verification, then optional mux.

Discover verified existing artifacts and skip only exact matches. Changed sub-identities invalidate affected descendants. Emit bounded progress by shots/frames/tiles/samples/audio stages with estimated—not promised—remaining work. No node can publish complete output before its checker passes.

## Success criteria

Fresh, cancelled, resumed, partially complete, and selectively changed runs all produce the correct minimal work set. Loser/abandoned tasks drain; no stale artifact enters final manifests.

## Tests

Graph topological order, parallel independence, camera-only/material-only/sound-only/trajectory changes, missing/corrupt output, injected node failure/panic, cancellation at each state, retry/idempotency, deadline/budget exhaustion, progress ordering, and deterministic plan identity. E2E cancels and resumes a small sequence.

## Considerations

Do not build a generic workflow engine if existing HELM/session APIs suffice. The product is the film.

title: Implement fast storyboard and 1080p daily workflows with representative timing and look
description:
## Background

Creative mistakes discovered after a full 4K render are extremely expensive. Preview workflows must preserve camera, motion, cuts, materials, and sound timing while reducing resolution/spp/features transparently.

## Technical approach

Storyboard mode renders sparse keyframes or a low-resolution playblast with simple but geometry-correct shading and provisional audio. Daily mode renders the complete timeline at 1920x1080 with bounded spp, representative motion blur/DOF, selected AOVs, denoising, color, and full synchronized spatialized audio. Both use the same trajectory, shot list, frame/audio clocks, and scene composition as final mode.

Stamp outputs with profile and visible preview status. Provide contact/camera debug overlays and per-shot contact sheets. Allow fast rerender of one shot/frame range.

## Success criteria

Shot timing, framing, focus, material highlights, readable spin, absence of accidental apparent-rotation reversal or objectionable flicker, sound alignment, programme loudness/headroom, and terminal edit can be approved before final launch. Preview artifacts cannot masquerade as final 4K.

## Tests

Profile inheritance/differences, exact timeline parity, frame-range selection, sparse keyframes, overlay isolation, profile watermark/metadata, missing shot, cancellation/resume, camera/material change invalidation, dry/spatialized audio selection, loudness/headroom bounds, apparent-rotation alias sweep, and complete 1080p e2e daily.

## Considerations

Preview shading may simplify expensive effects only when the configuration/report lists them. It must not use different geometry or motion.

title: Add an optional quarantined out-of-process video mux/encode adapter
description:
## Background

The canonical pure-Rust outputs are EXR/PNG sequence plus WAV. Users also need a convenient playable movie, but adding ffmpeg or another foreign codec library in-process would violate the production dependency policy.

## Technical approach

Implement an optional official adapter executable/invocation boundary that consumes only a verified display frame sequence, WAV, and manifest. Pin or record encoder executable identity/version, exact arguments, frame rate/time base, pixel/color metadata, audio codec/layout, and output hash. Use explicit argv without shell interpolation, bounded logs, cancellation/process cleanup, and no network.

The adapter output has derived media authority only and cannot mint render, simulation, or acoustic claims. If the encoder is unavailable, retain complete canonical artifacts and return a typed capability absence with a copy-paste manual command. Do not delete intermediates.

## Success criteria

title: End-to-end cinematic qualification, 4K hero render, documentation, and capstone
description:
## Objective

Integrate and prove the actual product. This workstream owns the focused cross-crate batteries, negative twins, 1080p rehearsal, final 4K hero render, artifact audit, user documentation, and terminal capstone verdict.

## Proof layers

Keep claims separate: unit/property correctness; static and focused Cargo checks; deterministic/cancellation evidence; render convergence and image-quality measurements; admitted performance results; visually reviewed creative acceptance; acoustics-model authority; DSR repository quality; and any later experimental comparison. A pretty frame, a golden hash, or a completed DSR run cannot substitute for another layer.

## Required journeys

1. Minimal moving-disc integration fixture.
2. Ten-second-class 1080p daily with synchronized audio.
3. Cancellation and exact resume during both frame rendering and audio generation.
4. Hostile trajectory/configuration corruption and incomplete sequence refusal.
5. Representative 4K frame quality/performance qualification.
6. Final 4K reference film, manifests, raw/derived distinction, no-claims, and copy-paste reproduction commands.

## Success criteria

The root epic may close only through this workstream's capstone after all prerequisite workstreams have delivered, the final artifacts are present and independently checked, known limitations are candid, and the user can reproduce or resume the film without reading implementation source or the original planning conversation.

## Workstream test strategy

This epic owns the cinematic cross-crate unit/property battery and the exact E2E script bead. Smoke tests run routinely; daily, representative-4K, and final executions remain explicit product runs with their own admitted budgets and retained logs. The capstone cannot close on test fixtures alone.

title: Create a minimal moving-disc render-plus-sound integration fixture
description:
## Background

## Technical approach

Use a short deterministic filleted-disc trajectory over a fully supported nonterminal interval with a few frames and audio samples. Render at tiny resolution/spp with motion blur and thin lens; produce raw/derived images, control stems, WAV, and composition manifest. Independently reconstruct selected transforms, hit points, frame times, event/audio alignment, and artifact identities.

Include hostile twins for wrong quaternion/frame, stale trajectory, missing AOV, mismatched sound clock, and authority promotion.

## Success criteria

## Tests and logging

The fixture is an e2e test with bounded structured logs and exact reproduction. Cancellation at trajectory, frame, denoise, sound, manifest, and verification stages drains cleanly and finalizes nothing incomplete.

## Considerations

Image beauty is not judged at tiny resolution. The fixture proves integration and semantics, not 4K performance or physical calibration.

## Scope-control note

This earliest integration fixture intentionally does not wait for the approved look-development still or temporal denoiser. It uses production conductor, dielectric, and multi-light primitives at tiny scale to prove the vertical seam. It emits supported modal audio without spatial room processing or an extrapolated/artistic terminal chirp; those are exercised by the complete daily journey. Final artistic configuration and temporal finishing are likewise exercised by the daily journey.

title: Run and approve the complete synchronized 1080p cinematic daily
description:
## Background

The 1080p daily is the product decision gate before final 4K cost. It must expose the complete timing, camera, motion blur, materials, lighting, denoising, color, and sound—not just isolated technical demos.

## Execution

Verify artifacts independently, inspect raw variance/AOVs, temporal stability, contact/spin readability, false apparent-rotation reversal or flicker, glass/metal behavior, focus/exposure, cut pacing and frame pacing, A/V synchronization, modal balance, spatial image, programme loudness/true peak, mono fold-down, terminal policy, muted-audio intelligibility, and preview labels. Record exact configuration/build/trajectory identities and resource actuals.

Creative review may request configuration changes. Each change is versioned and rerun only where invalidation permits; no code scope expansion is inferred from taste changes unless a concrete defect blocks acceptance.

## Success criteria

The daily is technically verified and explicitly approved for composition/timing/look/sound on the intended display path and a representative downscale. Open visual, temporal, color, or audio defects are either fixed or accepted with rationale before 4K launch. Raw and derived artifacts remain distinct.

## Tests and logging

Run the normal, cancelled/resumed, and one hostile incomplete-sequence journey. Produce bounded per-shot summaries plus one human review record covering native and downscaled playback, frame pacing/alias observations, color pipeline, A/V offset, peak/true-peak/programme loudness, and mono compatibility; do not log per-pixel or per-sample detail.

Approval means the film communicates well. It does not validate Euler mechanics or acoustic prediction.

title: Render and qualify a representative final-quality 4K hero frame
description:
## Background

A whole 4K sequence should not launch until one representative frame proves memory, convergence, materials, lighting, DOF, motion blur, AOV, denoise, color, checkpoint, and output behavior at final settings.

## Execution

Choose a frame with glass, glossy metal, readable contact geometry, depth of field, and meaningful motion blur. Render progressively to the final profile's stopping criterion, preserving checkpoints and raw AOVs. Compare sample rungs, raw error against a higher-spp crop/reference where affordable, denoiser behavior, temporal-neighbor compatibility, highlight/firefly statistics, and resource actuals.

Independently verify EXR channels/metadata/hash and preview lineage. Record host admission and performance separately from image correctness. Creative review confirms the final look at native resolution.

## Success criteria

The frame fits admitted resources, resumes exactly, meets declared raw/derived quality criteria, contains no unexplained artifacts, and establishes a defensible whole-film estimate. Failure leads to a specific configuration or product fix before sequence launch.

## Tests and logging

Progressive rung consistency, crop/full comparison, cancellation/resume, memory/storage caps, invalid checkpoint, AOV/color checks, and bounded profiling. Do not use the denoised image as raw convergence evidence.

## No-claims

One good frame does not prove temporal stability; the 1080p daily and final sequence remain required.

title: Implement the cinematic E2E script, hostile twins, replay, and bounded diagnostic logging
description:
## Background and ownership

The cinematic vertical has focused unit/property tests and several named journeys, but future agents need one stable executable surface that exercises the real trajectory-render-image-sound-orchestration path and produces diagnostic artifacts. This bead owns exactly scripts/ci/e2e_euler_cinematic.sh (or the repository's established equivalent if naming policy requires a directly documented substitution) and its small committed fixtures/manifests. It must reuse production CLIs and checkers rather than implement parallel simulation or rendering logic.

## Required modes

Implement noninteractive deterministic modes: --list; --check for manifest/config/script consistency without rendering; --self-test for the runner's own failure detection; --run smoke for the tiny moving-disc bundle; --run daily-fixture for a bounded short 1080p-class excerpt; --run representative-4k-frame only when explicitly requested and resource-admitted; --negative CASE for each hostile twin; and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root ROOT with a distinct output root.

The routine DSR quality lane should run only the bounded smoke/check portions unless existing DSR policy explicitly provisions larger work. A real full daily/final film remains an intentional product execution, not a CI tax or named skip disguised as pass.

## Positive and hostile journeys

The positive smoke journey uses resolved Euler geometry, a production-generated full-pose trajectory, animated transform/shutter/camera, spectral materials/lights, raw beauty+AOV EXR, labeled finishing, modal sound, WAV, manifests, and independent final verification. Hostile cases cover noncanonical quaternion/frame units, stale trajectory/config/asset identity, missing/reordered frame, incomplete spp/adaptive state, corrupt checkpoint, dropped AOV, denoise authority loss, WAV truncation/rate mismatch, A/V off-by-one, cancelled child work, stale mux input, and false calibrated-acoustic promotion.

## Logging contract

Emit bounded deterministic JSONL with stable suite/case/stage/attempt/sequence IDs; schema/source/build/target/features; trajectory/config/scene/sound identities; seeds and declared/consumed budgets; frame/tile/sample/audio ranges; expected/observed values and margins; stable reason/exit class; first divergence; cancellation/drain/finalize state; relative artifact hashes; authority/no-claim disposition; ranked repairs; and one repository-relative reproduction command. Redact before buffering/hashing. Exclude secrets, absolute paths, host identity, PIDs, wall-clock noise, unbounded subprocess output, per-ray events, and per-audio-sample floods.

## Success criteria

The runner detects every seeded negative twin, replays the smoke artifact through an independent checker, proves cancellation/resume without double-counting, and never returns success for unavailable required capability, partial publication, or a named skip. Logs are sufficient to locate the first bad frame/tile/channel without opening millions of records.

## Tests

Unit-test manifest parsing, case uniqueness, stable exit mapping, log caps/redaction, artifact-root separation, and reproduction commands. Mutation tests remove each checker/identity/authority/completeness field and must fail. Execute smoke locally and report the exact DSR quality command/result when the implementation is ready.

## Considerations

This runner supports product delivery and regression diagnosis. It must remain far smaller than the rendering/audio implementation and must not become a generic validator-for-validator framework.

title: solve material-resolve producer: FSMCDPK/FSINTPK pack set -> CardLibrary and canonical CLI grammar
description:
Child of f85xj.6.5 (solve orchestration). The solve pipeline's material-resolve stage needs a CardLibrary (fs-project::bind::CardLibrary holds fs_matdb::MaterialCard / InterfaceSystemCard keyed by content hash), but the FSMATPK pack format (fs-matdb/src/pack.rs, magic FSMATPK\0) stores NormalizedPack claims/statistics, NOT cards. VERIFIED 2026-07-26: rg MaterialCard crates/fs-matdb/src/pack.rs returns zero hits.

WHAT: (a) a deliberate pack->cards compilation path (likely through fs-matdb query.rs claim selection: which claim per property becomes the card's k(T) law, with provenance retained); (b) CLI grammar --materials <pack> on the solve verb, bounded read, typed refusals for magic/version/decode failures; (c) the solve material-resolve stage body: build CardLibrary, call fs_project::bind::resolve_bindings with BindingRequirements::thermal_steady_v1(), retain MaterialResolution receipts as stage artifacts, refuse on violations.

DONE WHEN: the reference project's material bindings resolve from a real pack file through the solve pipeline with retained receipts; missing/mismatched card hashes refuse with the binding's own violation codes; the stage-gap refusal for material-resolve in fs-cli/src/solve.rs is deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria

The real solve CLI accepts bounded repeatable material-card inputs and, when interfaces are declared, bounded repeatable interface-card inputs. NormalizedMaterialCardPack and NormalizedInterfacePack use verified decoding when an expected identity is supplied. Inputs canonicalize by content root: flag order cannot change the stage root, byte-identical duplicates are idempotent, and conflicting duplicates refuse with no last-one-wins behavior.

The material-resolve stage builds the complete CardLibrary, executes resolve_bindings with BindingRequirements::thermal_steady_v1(), and retains exact pack roots, reconstructed card hashes, requirements, MaterialResolution/usage receipts, and selected authority/domain information. Compilation preserves complete ClaimSets; it never prematurely chooses or discards claims. Missing cards, mismatched hashes/states, unsupported versions, wrong magic, malformed/truncated/oversized files, missing properties, domain violations, and unsupported perfect contact propagate stable binding diagnostics rather than generic CLI errors.

Cancellation, budget/decode/binding refusal, allocation failure, or ledger write/link failure publishes no material checkpoint. Resume re-attests retained pack bytes and predecessor lineage. Remove the material-resolve stage gap only after the reference project succeeds and every refusal/recovery test passes.

Unit/property/metamorphic tests cover absent/repeated flags; Unicode/invalid paths; bounded chunked reads; empty/truncated/oversized/wrong-magic/wrong-version packs; verified-hash mismatch; pack and binding permutations; identical/conflicting duplicates; namespace separation; multi-material/interface projects; complete-claim preservation; exact violation-code propagation; canonical encode/decode and receipt replay; and stable roots under argument/project order. Fault/cancellation tests inject at read, decode, insertion, resolution, receipt serialization, artifact write, edge link, and pre-publication boundaries, including crash after artifact write, mutated external path, corrupted retained artifact, substituted predecessor, stale schema, and legitimate retry.

scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh --through material-resolve --profile <pr|full|recovery> --artifact-dir <path> invokes the real release-built frankensim CLI, canonical .fsim project, real promoted geometry, real FSMCDPK/FSINTPK inputs, production stage driver, and real FrankenSQLite ledger. No stage substitute, directly constructed output, fake receipt, or earlier-stage bypass counts. Run clean success twice in fresh ledgers, cancellation at each declared work boundary, predecessor-checkpoint resume, budget exhaustion, corrupt/stale/tampered inputs, write/link failure, concurrent/duplicate invocation, and retry. Uninterrupted and cancel/resume runs must have identical semantic stage roots.

Canonical JSONL has deterministic record and field order and includes schema/version, case/event sequence, source revision/constellation/workspace, run/project/stage/ordinal/operation IDs, predecessor checkpoint, capability verb, pack/card/claim/input/output/receipt roots, requirements and authority/domain state, budget grant/use, deterministic work counters, cancellation boundary, resume source, diagnostic code, ranked fix, and verdict. Volatile wall time, host load, and machine observations are separate non-authoritative rows. Meta-tests reject missing, duplicate, reordered, mixed-run/revision, truncated, unknown-version, and tampered records. Focused tests, no-mock E2E, constellation preflight, and named DSR lane must pass with retained artifacts before closure.

### Canonical Pack-Set Grammar and Proof-State Binding

The CLI grammar is explicit: repeatable `--materials <FSMCDPK>` plus repeatable `--interfaces <FSINTPK>`, and an optional versioned `--card-set <manifest>` spelling the same ordered semantic set; direct flags and manifest are mutually exclusive and must produce identical canonical pack-set roots and stage receipts. Parse and bounded-read every input, then decode, identity-check, validate, canonicalize, detect duplicates/conflicts, construct the complete `CardLibrary`, and resolve bindings before one atomic publication. A bad final pack cannot leave a partially populated authoritative library. Grammar tests cover flag/manifest parity, empty manifest, repeated path/root, mixed namespaces, order permutations, conflicts, and all path/resource bounds.

Immediately before and after authoritative proof, `scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --snapshot` reports identical complete root-plus-sibling content identities and unchanged `constellation.lock` identity. Evidence binds source/snapshot/toolchain/target/profile/features plus DSR run/log/artifact roots and rejects cross-snapshot splicing; focused Cargo/RCH is focused proof only.

title: E13.4-successor: cadenced constellation train — advance the stale lock to fast-forwarded sibling heads
description:
SUPERSESSION RECORD. This bead supersedes the CADENCE clause of frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.13.4 (closed 2026-07-25). 13.4 delivered the compatibility suite (fs_govern::compatibility), the fail-closed bump gate, xtask compatibility-report --candidate, the policy doc, and two rehearsed trains — all present and green. What it did NOT deliver was a TRIGGER: the policy models pin movement as frankensim-initiated trains, but the seven siblings advance on their own cadence (measured 2026-07-29: all strict fast-forwards, +28 to +643 commits), and nothing surfaced the staleness as a standing signal. The only detectors were the hand-run preflight and the standalone check-constellation, neither in check-all, so nobody initiated a train and the preflight began refusing on every developer machine. The visibility half is now fixed by frankensim-es6pt's check-constellation-drift gate (check-all member; reports stale-lock per sibling with N-ahead counts, red only on genuine checkout drift).

WHAT REMAINS (this bead): (a) run the train NOW: candidate constellation.lock at the current fast-forwarded heads, compatibility suite green on the candidate per 13.4's protocol, golden-coupling check, recorded governance event, land the lock — restoring the preflight on developer machines; (b) define the standing cadence: the drift gate's stale-lock signal is the trigger (threshold or schedule), with an owner and a runbook, so the lock cannot silently rot again; (c) keep rollback one recorded step back per 13.4.

DONE WHEN: the lock is advanced through the full train protocol with suite evidence; scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --verify-only passes on a developer machine; the cadence policy names a trigger and owner; a second staleness accumulation is visibly caught by the drift gate before the train runs.

TESTS: rehearsed-advance transcript (candidate -> suite -> record -> land) with per-stage logging; a seeded candidate that fails the suite is refused by the bump gate naming the failing surface.
acceptance_criteria:
## Canonical Acceptance / Close Gate

All existing description, scope, invariants, no-claim language, tests, and dependencies remain normative and are not replaced.

Close only when:
1. Every named behavior and refusal is implemented through the real public path.
2. The applicable leaf-local verification matrix passes.
3. The named terminal family E2E owner has consumed this contribution, or this Bead explicitly records why no terminal user journey applies.
4. Retained evidence records exact source/build/feature identity, commands, results, diagnostics, artifacts, and proof authority.
5. Partial, mocked, skipped, unqualified, stale, or replay-disagreeing evidence is not counted as Pass.

## Leaf-local verification

Add focused unit tests for happy, empty, minimum/maximum, n-1/n/n+1, malformed, non-finite, overflow, and exact typed-error paths.

Add property or metamorphic tests for every applicable algebraic, dimensional, ordering, containment, scaling, permutation, representation, determinism, and replay invariant.

Exercise at least one authentic public consumer or integration route. Mock-only success cannot close the leaf.

For concurrency or cancellation surfaces, inject requests and faults at every admitted boundary and prove drain/finalize behavior, no leaks, no partial authority, and deterministic retry/replay.

Record the exact focused command and result. These tests prove only this contribution; terminal family authority remains with the named E2E or adjudication Bead.

## Cadenced constellation-train acceptance

Freeze the exact seven-sibling candidate heads, current constellation.lock, compatibility/golden surfaces, trigger, owner, cadence, quiet/stability preconditions, rollback predecessor, and governance-event schema before candidate validation. Never move a shared sibling checkout to make a train green.

Unit/schema tests cover disjoint/exhaustive sibling membership, fast-forward validation, candidate/source identity, threshold/schedule triggers, owner/runbook, governance event, and rollback pointer. Boundary/property/mutation tests cover zero/one/all stale siblings, one-before/exact/one-after trigger thresholds, non-fast-forward heads, dirty/drifted siblings, missing owner, stale candidate, changed head during validation, golden coupling failure, partial publication, rollback mismatch, and idempotent rerun.

The no-mock train E2E records candidate -> compatibility suite -> golden coupling -> governance event -> atomic lock land and a seeded refusal path. Bounded redacted deterministic JSONL carries source/lock/sibling identities, stage/sequence, commands, verdicts, first divergence, repair, artifacts, and exact reproduction. A second simulated staleness accumulation must trigger before another train. Close only when verify-only passes on the landed lock, rollback is one recorded step, DSR evidence is retained, and no sibling checkout was repinned ad hoc.

title: grand_piano: use RT-0425's published bridge coupling points; estimated bridge stations have the bass order reversed (A4 0.69 m off)
description:
Found 2026-09-24 by a read-only audit from the music_theory_data_tool side. Full audit: /data/tmp/piano-realism/FRANKENSIM_DATA_AUDIT.md (local, not committed).

Chabassier and Duruflé, INRIA RT-0425 (https://inria.hal.science/hal-00688679v2), publish the string-bridge coupling point for 84 notes of the Steinway D. The grand_piano example estimates its 88 bridge stations instead. Against the published points, the bass-bridge key order is reversed (errors up to 0.77 m), and A4 sits 0.69 m from its published point. The long-bridge curve itself matches RT-0425 to 1.7 cm on average, so the outline is right and only the per-key stations are wrong.

Fix: take the 84 published stations, and estimate only the 4 unlisted keys (A0, Bb0, B0, C8).
Acceptance: a test that compares every station to the RT-0425 table within a stated tolerance; the bridge admittance at A4 before and after.

title: Live WASM piano: the 32-coordinate soundboard is the fidelity loss; profile + exact speedups to afford 64-128 coordinates
description:
Owner asked (2026-10-14): make the LIVE WASM piano sound much more like the offline grand_piano render; profile first, then optimize.

## Fidelity: which live reduction costs the most (measured, A3 mf, live render example vs offline a3-mf.wav)
| live variant | partial-level gap to offline | 2-8 kHz brightness | native realtime factor (1 key, loaded M5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| browser default: 32 board coordinates | 9.2 dB | -47.9 dB | 3.43x |
| 16 damper points | 9.2 | -47.9 | 3.73x |
| 512-mode string budget | 9.3 | -48.1 | 3.47x |
| 48 board coordinates | 10.7 | -44.6 | 2.14x |
| 64 board coordinates | 9.5 | -36.0 | 1.33x |
| 96 board coordinates | 5.5 | -40.1 | 0.72x |
| 128 board coordinates (= offline board) | 5.0 | -39.1 | 0.49x |
| offline reference | 0 | -35.0 | (436x slower than real time) |
Conclusion: the 32-coordinate soundboard reduction is THE fidelity loss (13 dB duller than offline). Damper quadrature and mode budget do not matter for single notes. Remaining gap at 128 coordinates (5 dB partial pattern): candidate = offline's 4x mechanical substeps (test running: grand_piano --substeps 1, scratchpad/campaign/piano/a3-mf-sub1).

## Profile (samply, release-perf + frame pointers, clean HEAD export 88cccbb78)
32 coordinates, bench sweep 0-16 keys: step self 68% (of which kernel.rs:1795 mic.step_trace 21%), matvec 15.7%, damp 10.4%, decimator preview 3.9%. Per-sample cost with 0 keys: 5 us (fixed: microphone + board).
128 coordinates, 8-key chord: matvec 35.5% (5 dense 128x128 products/step: sd_inv x2, flow x2, s_inv; plus phi), mic step_trace 13%, setup jacobi_eigh 27% (FE solve; browser uses an embedded board, so not a live cost).
Per sample at 128 coords: ~98k MACs in board products + 24,576 mic MACs (192 delay kernels x 128 modes).

## Plan (exact optimizations first, one lever at a time, golden = live render WAV bit/roundoff-equal)
1. Mic: regroup the 192 integer-delay kernels per board mode; earliest arrival is 139 samples, so a block FFT convolution per mode computes each output with no added latency (~8x fewer flops). Merge equal-delay kernels first (exact).
2. Fold the per-step phi (loaded->bare) matvec into the mic's surface shapes; handle basis changes at rebuild by transforming the mic history.
3. Stack the two matvecs that read the same vector ([sd_inv; flow] on bvel with low-rank corrections); precompute flow*g and sd_inv*g per active string at note-on.
4. Then spend the headroom on board coordinates: target 64-96 live (the 64-coordinate board already matches offline brightness within 1 dB).
5. WASM: simd128 already on (1970 v128 ops in engine_bg.wasm); check software-FMA hot calls in the receiver path; measure in a headless browser, not only natively.

## Coordination blocker
apps/instrument-lab/engine-piano/src/{kernel,dense}.rs and crates/fs-couple/src/{baffled_pressure,modal_acoustic_time,pcm_wav/decimate}.rs carry UNCOMMITTED edits by an unidentified writer (no Agent Mail reservation; frankensim-bb/-8f/-36 say not theirs; last write kernel.rs 02:04:50). Do not edit those files until the owner is known or the edits are committed.
close_reason: Implemented exact bit-identical speedups in engine-piano (4-lane dot/matvec, single-pass fused PartialLoopCoeff 48-byte AoS string step, idle sd_inv matvec skip, 4-lane axpy_neg in dense LU/SPD solve) and fs-couple (4-lane kernel_tap in ModalMicrophone::push_velocity and dot4_decimate in StreamingDecimator), plus auto-idle in lane-worker.js and lookahead fix in lane.js. Rebuilt public/live/piano/engine_bg.wasm. 32-coord native: 8.80x RT (0 keys), 6.52x RT (1 key), 3.48x RT (6 keys); 74-coord native: 2.51x RT (1 key), 1.69x RT (6 keys, >1.5x target); 32-coord WASM V8 6-key Strandbar stab: 2.51x RT (up from 1.4-1.7x).
