title: Make fs-conform arbitrary-f64 certificates exact or outward-enclosed
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND AMBITION
The hardened fs-conform path now rejects malformed dimensions, non-finite evidence, exact-product residual underflow, complete DD accumulator erasure, and several norm-collapse cases. It honestly labels its current double-double rung as bounded numerical evidence rather than a theorem-strength enclosure. However DD add/mul/div/sqrt are approximate: collapse predicates catch total loss, not every partial rounding error. A converter adversarially placed within the DD error neighborhood of a tolerance boundary could therefore require refusal or stronger arithmetic before FrankenSim may claim arbitrary-f64 certification. False certificates are Sev-0.

MISSION
Ratchet restriction-map certification beyond ordinary commercial plugin harnesses: make every adjoint, identity, functoriality, and manufactured-error comparison either mathematically exact over finite IEEE-754 inputs or proven by outward enclosures. Preserve accepted functionality; do not solve this by broadly refusing scale disparity. Use an adaptive ladder: cheap f64/EFT filter, shared DD with a rigorously propagated error interval, exact floating expansion or deterministic binned/Kulisch superaccumulator near the boundary, and interval-enclosed square-root/norm comparison. A powerful new theorem about sufficient exactness or compositional sheaf-restriction error bounds is explicitly welcome, but it must ship with executable hypotheses and a no-claim boundary.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
- Exact signed dot evidence: represent each f64 product and sum without residual-underflow loss, cancellation ambiguity, or order dependence. Support arbitrary finite vector length within an explicit admitted dimension/workspace budget. A fixed exponent-bin superaccumulator spanning the full binary64 product range, a fallible exact expansion, or a proven equivalent is acceptable.
- Exact/enclosed Euclidean distance: retain exact coordinate differences and squared sums; compare norm <= bound without an inward-rounded sqrt. Prefer squared-domain comparison with overflow-free exact scaling and handle zero, subnormal, f64::MAX, opposite-sign extrema, and declared+tolerance addition exactly or outwardly.
- Typed arithmetic evidence: report which rung decided, exact/enclosed lower and upper bounds, operation/dimension budget, refusal reason, and deterministic first inconclusive site. Do not encode arithmetic uncertainty as an ordinary measured failure.
- Resource and cancellation closure: preflight/fallibly reserve all adaptive-expansion or bin work; bound dimension, components/bins, and diagnostic size; add Cx/tile polling if work can exceed the synchronous cold-path envelope. No panic/OOM/partial certified report.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and bit-stable receipts. Bind algorithm/schema version, bounds, budgets, and rung transitions into the certification evidence identity. Keep L2 dependency direction valid and Franken-only.

GAUNTLET
G0 exhaustive boundary fixtures for zero/signed zero, all subnormal transition classes, min-normal neighbors, max finite/opposite-sign extrema, exact and inexact products, cancellation, three-plus exponent scales, exact equality, one-ULP and sub-ULP-beyond-bound cases, bound-sum absorption, and every exact/plus-one resource limit. All existing description, scope, invariants, no-claim language, tests, and dependencies remain normative and are not replaced.

Close only when:
1. Every named behavior and refusal is implemented through the real public path.
2. The applicable leaf-local verification matrix passes.
3. The named terminal family E2E owner has consumed this contribution, or this Bead explicitly records why no terminal user journey applies.
4. Retained evidence records exact source/build/feature identity, commands, results, diagnostics, artifacts, and proof authority.

## Leaf-local verification

Add focused unit tests for happy, empty, minimum/maximum, n-1/n/n+1, malformed, non-finite, overflow, and exact typed-error paths.

Add property or metamorphic tests for every applicable algebraic, dimensional, ordering, containment, scaling, permutation, representation, determinism, and replay invariant.

Exercise at least one authentic public consumer or integration route. Mock-only success cannot close the leaf.

For concurrency or cancellation surfaces, inject requests and faults at every admitted boundary and prove drain/finalize behavior, no leaks, no partial authority, and deterministic retry/replay.

Record the exact focused command and result. These tests prove only this contribution; terminal family authority remains with the named E2E or adjudication Bead.

## Retained staged-producer receipt acceptance

Freeze the tracked receipt path, frankensim.ci.solve-e2e-summary.v1 schema/version, exact full-profile source/build/feature/run/host-class identity, stages_executing semantics, SolveStage authority, freshness/expiry rule, and program-metrics projection. Unit/schema tests cover every receipt field, stage-set equality, green-state rules, count projection, source/freshness, paths, stable errors, and empty/min/max/n-1/n/n+1 stage sets. Property/metamorphic/mutation tests cover stage enumeration/order, duplicate/missing/unknown/gapped stages, zero pass, claimed-but-unadmitted stage, stale source, wrong profile, mixed runs, truncation, tamper, unknown schema, non-finite/overflow metrics, and NO-DATA versus measured transitions.

The real full-profile scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh run emits bounded redacted deterministic JSONL and an immutable summary with exact reproduction. xtask check-spine-metrics independently validates the retained bytes against the live SolveStage table and refuses before publishing a measured dashboard row on any divergence. Artifact-only replay uses read-only input and disjoint fresh output, recomputes the semantic projection, retains first divergence, and never reruns the producer lane as replay. Close only after focused tests, no-mock full E2E, replay, source closure, and DSR pass.

## Structured logging and failure evidence

The terminal harness emits bounded, redacted, schema-versioned JSONL containing:
- run, case, attempt, stage, and monotonic sequence identities;
- exact source, build, feature, and machine identity;
- units, seed, capabilities, and admitted budgets;

- typed failure and exit class;

Missing, duplicated, reordered, truncated, post-terminal, over-cap, unredacted, stale, or mixed-run records refuse replay and cannot Pass.

## Artifact-only replay

Retain an immutable receipt plus an exact repository-relative reproduction command.

Replay input is read-only and replay output is fresh and disjoint. Refuse overlap, traversal, symlink escape, missing inputs, wrong source/schema/identity, tampering, and unknown versions before publication.

Replay independently recomputes the declared semantic projection, preserves the first divergence, and never reruns timing to verify a retained performance observation. Any fresh timing run is a separate measurement with separate authority.

title: ArtifactWriter single-call streaming has quadratic copying and unbounded buffering
description: ArtifactWriter::write currently appends the entire caller slice to buf, then repeatedly split_off(STORAGE_CHUNK_LEN). For a large single write, peak buffering scales with the full input and each split copies the remaining suffix, making work quadratic and violating the documented streaming intent. Rework write to fill one partial chunk, stage complete chunks directly from the input slice in linear time, and retain at most one tail chunk; use checked length/sequence arithmetic and fail-closed allocation handling. Add a multi-chunk single-write regression/instrumented invariant proving exact bytes, bounded tail, and linear chunk staging.
design: Process each write in one pass: checked-add the logical length before mutating state; fill and flush an existing partial buffer; stage every remaining full chunk directly from the caller slice without copying through buf; then retain only the final sub-chunk tail. Advance sequence with checked arithmetic only after a successful INSERT. Any length, sequence, allocation, or SQL failure poisons the writer with a sticky error; finish rolls back and returns that original failure.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A single arbitrarily multi-chunk write performs direct full-chunk staging with at most one sub-chunk tail retained. 2. Total length and sequence arithmetic are checked; buffer growth is fallible. 3. Every error is sticky/fail-closed and finish rolls back with zero residue. 4. Regression proves exact bytes, expected chunk count, bounded tail, and direct multi-chunk staging. 5. rustfmt, UBS review, git diff --check, and strict targeted RCH proof complete.
close_reason: Bounded linear ArtifactWriter streaming implemented, contract documented, and strict remote proof passed on frozen source hash

title: fs-convection claim-integrity: mis-cited turbulent plate correlation, overstated CONTRACT test coverage, and Invariant 1 contradicted by a public accessor
description:
Three claim-integrity defects found while auditing f85xj.5.2 against HEAD. Each
is a case of the artifact claiming more than the code delivers, which is the
E02 defect class.

(1) MIS-ATTRIBUTED SOURCE. CorrelationId::FlatPlateTurbulentAverage computes
Nu_L = (0.037 Re^0.8 - 871) Pr^(1/3) (src/lib.rs:111) — the mixed
laminar+turbulent average carrying the Re_x,c = 5e5 leading-edge constant
(Incropera/Whitaker lineage). It is cited to Pohlhausen, ZAMM 1 (1921) 115-121
(src/lib.rs:687), which is the LAMINAR flat-plate solution and cannot contain
that relation. The FLAT_PLATE source constant is shared by the laminar and
turbulent cards, which is how the wrong one was inherited. A reader checking the
citation finds a paper that does not contain the formula.

(2) CONTRACT OVERSTATES TEST COVERAGE. CONTRACT.md:98 claims "rectangular
square/parallel-plate endpoint checks". Only the SQUARE endpoint (aspect ratio
1.0) is exercised; grep for 7.541|8.235 in tests returns nothing, and only
aspect ratios 1.0 and 0.5 appear. The parallel-plate endpoint check does not
exist.

(3) INVARIANT 1 CONTRADICTED BY A PUBLIC ACCESSOR. CONTRACT Invariant 1: "No
unitless heat-transfer coefficient leaves the crate. The only public conversion
returns Evidence<HeatTransferCoefficient>." But
CorrelationRobinBoundary::boundary_condition() (src/lib.rs:403) publicly returns
&fs_conduction::ThermalBc, whose Robin variant holds htc as a bare f64 inside
ScalarField (fs-conduction/src/bc.rs:51, field.rs:16). The crate's own test
reads it that way: htc.at(0).to_bits() (tests/robin_seam.rs:96). The typed
conversion at src/lib.rs:432 is correct; the invariant as WRITTEN is false
because a second public path exists.

RELATED, lower severity and possibly wontfix-with-a-note: the
"three_flow_rate_heatsink_slab..." test (tests/robin_seam.rs:57) has no heatsink
— it is a box_grid([4,2,2],[0.010,0.020,0.020]) slab — and its "three flow
rates" are three hard-coded Reynolds numbers with no flow, velocity or geometry
behind them. The seam it proves is real (it runs the actual fs_conduction::solve
and matches analytic series resistance to 1.5e-14); only the naming overclaims.

DONE WHEN: (1) the turbulent card cites a source that contains its formula, with
the laminar and turbulent cards no longer sharing one constant; (2) either the
parallel-plate endpoint test exists or the CONTRACT sentence is narrowed to what
is tested; (3) Invariant 1 is either enforced (the accessor stops handing out an
untyped BC) or restated to describe the two paths honestly.

PREFER NARROWING THE CLAIM OVER WIDENING THE CODE where the two are equally
honest — (2) and (3) may well be contract edits, not code edits. (3) in
particular may be unfixable in code until fs-conduction's ThermalBc::robin takes
a typed h, which is a separate cross-crate decision.

Found by audit during f85xj.5.2 close review (NobleLion, 2026-07-25). Not fixed
in that pass because fs-convection was assigned to another agent.

title: rch path_topology drift: ~/projects + ~/dp outside canonical root — all offload refuses (RCH-E413)
description:
# rch offload refuses all builds from ~/projects and ~/dp (path_topology drift)

# Evidence (2026-08-29, RoseBasin session)

Attempting `cargo test -p fs-g1-train` from `~/projects/frankensim` via rch:

1. Default config: `[RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback (remote
   execution failed ...)` — hook log: `Project path normalization failed for
   /Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensim: input resolves outside canonical root
   (input: ... detail: resolved=/Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensim
   root=/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data/projects)`. The canonical root points at
   `/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data/projects`, which does not exist as the repos'
   parent (repos live at `/Users/jemanuel/projects/*`; `/Users/jemanuel/projects`
   is NOT a symlink — realpath resolves to itself).
2. With `RCH_CANONICAL_PROJECT_ROOT=/Users/jemanuel/projects`: dependency
   closure planner fail-open `[RCH-E413]` — frankensim's workspace has a path
   dependency `/Users/jemanuel/dp/asupersync` which lies OUTSIDE that root.
   So BOTH roots (`~/projects`, `~/dp`) must be inside the canonical root for
   offload to be admissible; no single configured value covers them.
3. `RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1` runs the real local cargo (workaround only;
   defeats offload and burns local CPU while sibling agents also build).

Impact: every rch-routed cargo invocation from `~/projects/*` and `~/dp/*`
workspaces on this machine either refuses (fail-closed) or fail-opens to
local. Fleet-wide build contention consequence, not a one-off.

# Remediation options (operator/fleet-owner decision required — affects all agents)

- Preferred: set `[path_topology]` canonical_root to a directory that
  contains both `projects/` and `dp/` (e.g. `/Users/jemanuel`), or add alias
  mappings per PATH_DEPENDENCIES.md, then `rch daemon reload`.
- Alternative: symlink `/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data/projects` ->
  `/Users/jemanuel/projects` and `.../data/dp` -> `/Users/jemanuel/dp` so the
  existing canonical root resolves (verifies with `rch workers probe --all`
  + a canary `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo metadata --offline`).
- Do NOT hand-edit workers.toml priorities as part of this; benchmark first

title: Reusable blind-prediction, scoring, identifiability, and OED enablers exposed by the Euler-disc flagship
description:
## Why this exists

The Euler-disc campaign needs prediction sealing, target-inaccessible execution, one-way blind unlock, trajectory/event scoring, factorial inference, identifiability, and next-experiment design. Those algorithms are reusable V&V/HELM/UQ capabilities and must not be implemented inside a flagship integration crate.

## Ownership rule

This epic owns generic schemas, transactions, analyzers, and conformance only. Euler-specific QoIs, factor names, mechanism signatures, specimens, prediction values, physical outcomes, rankings, and claim dispositions remain in frankensim-euler-disc-emergent-flagship-t6314.7. Generic children build on existing fs-evidence, fs-uq, fs-eproc, fs-opt, ledger, and shared-runner authorities instead of forking them.

## Program shape

The direct children separately own canonical prediction bundles and atomic sealing; target-inaccessible ensemble execution; single-use unlock/spent-partition transactions; trajectory/event/censoring scoring; factorial effects/rankings/crossovers/optimum sets; practical identifiability/discrepancy; evidence-aware OED; and a terminal compatibility/no-leakage/release gate.

## No-claims

Reusable software can verify process and numerical semantics. It cannot provide Euler physical evidence, identify a mechanism, validate a model, or convert a synthetic fixture into a blind result.
acceptance_criteria:
The exact direct-child set is frankensim-jmh21.1 through frankensim-jmh21.8. The epic has one hard terminal dependency on .8; that release gate consumes prediction bundle/sealing, target-inaccessible execution, single-use unlock/spend, trajectory/event/censoring scoring, factorial effects/rankings/optima, practical identifiability/discrepancy, and evidence-aware OED on one compatible snapshot.

Every child names a generic production owner and independent tests; no child contains Euler factors, target values, mechanism signatures, or physical outcomes. Closure requires release-backed no-mock positive and hostile journeys, independent artifact reconstruction, cancellation/fault/budget/replay proof, canonical authority transitions, no target leakage, bounded deterministic redacted logs, and exact DSR evidence. Software proof cannot mint campaign or physical authority.

title: Generic canonical prediction-input/output bundles and atomic sealers
description:
## Owner and purpose

Extend fs-evidence at crates/fs-evidence/src/prediction_bundle.rs with tests in crates/fs-evidence/tests/prediction_bundle.rs. Define generic canonical PredictionExecutionInput and PredictionOutputBundle schemas that build on ContextOfUse, ValidationPlan, split, solution-verification, and PredictionAssessment rather than duplicating them.

## Required behavior

The input binds source/build/runtime identity, typed scenarios and cards, parameter distributions/covariance, random-stream design, allowed model rungs and applicability/refusal policy, numerical tolerances and budgets, QoI/event/metric identities, evidence role, blind partition, and access policy. It contains no target labels, outcomes, or computed predictions.

The output binds exactly one input root and complete success/refusal/failure sample accounting, trajectory/event/energy artifacts, registered aggregate distributions/effects, applicability/cost/discrepancy, numerical evidence, and checker instructions. Publication is atomic: interrupted, partial, stale, incompatible, or target-contaminated outputs are unscoreable. Every semantic edit mints a new identity.

## No-claims

Canonical identity and a seal establish bytes, ordering, and schema semantics only; they do not prove execution correctness, coverage, or physical validity.

Closure requires safe-Rust production behavior at the named owner, versioned contracts, canonical semantic identities, typed units/frames, explicit seeds/budgets/versions/capabilities, structured refusals, cancellation request-drain-finalize, and no partial authority. title: Generic target-inaccessible ensemble executor with complete sample accounting

description:

title: fs-conduction contact claim-integrity: CONTRACT cites tests for 13 refusal branches nobody exercises, and two 'solve' tests run no solve at a jump-free uniform field
description:
Found auditing f85xj.5.3 against HEAD (full verdict is a comment on that bead).
5.3 itself is an HONESTLY-SCOPED partial -- its Notes, its commit eb0c2a8a, its
CHANGELOG entry and CONTRACT.md:576-605 all disclose what is unimplemented. It
is NOT a false-closure case. These are defects inside the slice that IS
implemented, where the artifact claims more than the code delivers (E02 class).

The underlying physics is sound and I verified it independently: the P1 jump
operator's mass matrix, sign structure and per-face conductance are correct
(interface.rs:1086-1119), the two-slab nodal profile is checked against a real
closed form to 1e-8 K (tests/contact.rs:242-254), and the fail-closed guard is
correctly placed at the assembly chokepoint with no bypass. The defects below
are about test and contract AUTHORITY, not about wrong answers.

(1) CONTRACT INVARIANT 9 CITES TESTS THAT DO NOT EXIST.
CONTRACT.md:196-202 claims "Every pair requires one named surface ... Reusing a
bound object with a different face set, vertex mapping, area, or boundary
condition refuses. Evidence: tests/contact.rs". Grepping the test directory for
each refusal's message text returns NOTHING for ten branches in interface.rs:
face pair bound more than once (:864-870), non-coincident pair (:854-863), face
paired with itself (:846-852), out-of-range slot (:834-845), non-opposing
normals (:1172-1180), three-or-more coincident faces (:1186-1195), duplicate
surface name (:750-761), blank surface name (:734-744), empty face-pair list
(:763-772), and an interface face also carrying an external BC (:871-881 bind,
:962-974 validate). Of validate_for's three "changed mesh" branches (:981-993 --
vertex mapping, side-B mapping, area bits) only the face-set-mismatch branch
(:955-961) is reached, by interface_binding_cannot_be_reused_on_a_different_mesh
(tests/contact.rs:399-431). The contract names FOUR failure modes as tested;
ONE is.

(2) TWO TESTS CLAIM A SOLVE, RUN NONE, AND COMPARE A JUMP-FREE QUANTITY.
  (a) an_all_equal_map_reproduces_the_uniform_surface_exactly
      (tests/contact.rs:586-629). Its doc comment (:588-591) claims "the
      assembled solve must agree bitwise ... pins the mapped path to the
      existing Level-A contact result". It never calls solve or
      solve_with_interfaces. It calls fluxes(&temperature) with
      temperature = vec![T_HOT; vertex_count] (:614) -- a UNIFORM field, so
      every vertex jump temperature[a]-temperature[b] in interface.rs:1061-1067
      is identically 0.0 and both heat_rate and mean_jump_k are zero. The only
      bitwise comparison (:618-622) is on conductance_w_per_k = sum(area/R''),
      which is pure input arithmetic over geometry and the card value. THE TEST
      PASSES IF THE JUMP OPERATOR IS ENTIRELY BROKEN.
  (b) a_thicker_bond_line_conducts_less (tests/contact.rs:631-680). Same
      uniform T_HOT field, same conductance-only comparison. Since
      conductance = sum(A_f/R''_f), doubling every R'' halving the conductance
      is the identity sum(A/2R) = 0.5*sum(A/R). The name promises a directional
      conduction behavior; the body checks that f64 division works.

(3) NO TEST EVER BUILDS MORE THAN ONE INTERFACE SURFACE, while CONTRACT.md
:307-309 and :379 claim surface-level determinism coverage: "Contact surfaces,
face pairs, and series-resistance terms are sorted by stable names/slot keys
before assembly or summation. Input permutation cannot change their
floating-point accumulation order." Every test in tests/contact.rs builds
exactly one surface, always named "bondline". The surface-level sort
(interface.rs:825) and refuse_duplicate_names (:750-761) are never executed.
What DOES exist is a single hard-coded 3-term series permutation
(tests/contact.rs:312-314) -- real, but one case, and the TESTS clause also
asks for associativity (not expressible: there is no API to nest a sub-network)
and uncertainty monotonicity (no test adds a term or widens a half-width and
checks the budget cannot shrink). No property-testing framework is present:
grep for proptest|quickcheck in crates/fs-conduction returns nothing.

(4) contact_level_a_row_exposes_a_tolerance_gate GATES NOTHING
(tests/contact.rs:433-442). Line 436 is
assert_eq!(reference.to_bits(), 0.3f64.to_bits()) where reference is
case.reference_value_si, which fs-vvreg/src/thermal_level_a.rs:334 literally
sets to 0.3 -- a literal against an equal literal, same vein as
frankensim-z87uy. Lines 437-441 accept ANY Tolerance { atol, rtol } that is
finite and >= 0.0, so it passes for atol=rtol=0 (no gate at all) and equally
for atol=1e9. The registry's real values are atol=rtol=1e-12
(thermal_level_a.rs:171-173) and contact.rs:438 is the ONLY place acceptance is
touched -- it is pattern-matched for shape and never applied as a comparison
bound, unlike mms.rs:152-155 and adjoint.rs:272-275 which destructure and apply
their OrderGate.

(5) THE CHANGELOG REPORTS AN ALGEBRAIC SUM AS A SOLVE RESULT. commit eb0c2a8a:
"Bound thermal-a-contact-series to a G1 two-slab solve. The focused remote
fixture REPRODUCED the 0.3 K/W Level-A network as 0.30000000000000004 K/W".
That number is series.budget().value_k_per_w (tests/contact.rs:300-307), the
sum of two test-declared slab terms and one card term = 0.1+0.1+0.1 from
literals; the only solve-derived input is flux.area_m2, which is exactly 1.0.
The solve IS independently validated elsewhere (the nodal profile at :242-254,
the 100 W heat rate at :266) -- but this specific number is not a solve result.
Minor, same site: the assertion message at :306 says "within one ULP" while the
gate is f64::EPSILON = 2.22e-16, about 4 ULP at 0.3 (1 ULP there is 5.55e-17).

DONE WHEN
  1. Either the ten unexercised refusal branches and two unexercised
     validate_for branches get tests, or CONTRACT invariant 9's evidence claim
     is narrowed to what actually executes. Prefer tests -- these are
     fail-closed guards and an untested guard is the failure mode the crate
     exists to prevent.
  2. The two uniform-field tests either run a real solve and compare a
     jump-BEARING quantity, or are renamed and their comments corrected to say
     they check input-derived conductance arithmetic. Do not leave a test whose
     name promises physics and whose body is an identity.
  3. At least one test builds TWO named interface surfaces so the surface sort
     and the duplicate-name refusal execute, or CONTRACT.md:307-309/:379 is
     narrowed to face-pair and series-term determinism only.
  4. The Level-A contact row applies the registry tolerance as an actual
     comparison bound (follow mms.rs:152-155), or the test is renamed to say it
     checks row SHAPE.
  5. Every repair is falsifiable: perturb the guarded thing and show the test
     fails. Do not assert it -- demonstrate it, the way frankensim-z87uy did.

NON-GOALS: the unimplemented 5.3 scope (scenario interface-object lowering,
dominance attribution corpus, nonmatching/mortar, variable contact law,
registry authority) stays with 5.3. This bead is authority repair only.

SEPARATELY WORTH FILING (different owner, f85xj.12.9 code): InterfaceFlux drops
ResistanceValueOrigin. InterfaceSurface::expand (interface.rs:669-689) forwards
only card_identity and receipt, and fluxes() (:1073-1081) emits those two and
nothing else, so a surface whose every value came from with_measured_value
reports a flux stamped with the CARD's identity and a replayable receipt with
no CallerSupplied signal anywhere in the report. No public accessor exposes
per-face origin after binding (surface_face_resistances, :1025-1036, returns
bare f64). This directly contradicts CONTRACT.md:595-599, which says
ResistanceValueOrigin "SEPARATES CITING A CARD FROM LAUNDERING A MEASUREMENT
THROUGH ONE". The origin type is tested at the InterfaceResistance level
(tests/contact.rs:731-785) but does not survive into the reported artifact,
which is exactly where laundering would occur.

title: fs-constraint unsat core is not verified jointly infeasible (deletion filter can return a feasible set)
description:
CONTRACT-INVARIANT GAP in crates/fs-constraint/src/diagnose.rs:296-319 (the deletion-filter minimal-unsat-core). Found in the deep-review hunt; beaded (not landed) because the fix changes the unsat-core algorithm and needs careful testing against the existing fscon-005 fixtures.

## The bug
`minimal_unsat_core` (deletion filter) guarantees only that EACH single deletion `core \ {member}` is feasible; it never checks that the seeded/filtered `core` is itself JOINTLY infeasible. It assumes the seed (the elastic support = constraints violated at the sum-minimizing elastic optimum) is infeasible "by construction," which is false in general.

## Why the assumption fails
The support is the set of constraints violated at the SUM-optimum x*. A constraint can be violated at the sum-optimum yet be jointly SATISFIABLE with the other support members, because x* is a trade-off pulled by a THIRD constraint that is satisfied there. The loop keeps every member for which `core \ {member}` is feasible, but nothing tests `core` as a whole — so a `core` whose members are jointly feasible can be returned as an "unsat core," violating CONTRACT invariant 5 ("the core is jointly infeasible … dropping any member restores feasibility").

## Trigger (constructible)
Three linear constraints where A and B are jointly feasible over the domain, but a third constraint C forces the elastic optimum x* into a region where A and B are both violated while C is satisfied. Support = {A, B}. Deletion filter: test {B} (feasible) -> keep A; test {A} (feasible) -> keep B. Reported core = {A, B} with feasible=false, but {A, B} is jointly feasible. The conformance fixtures (fscon-005) happen to land on interior-ridge supports and don't exercise this.

## Fix
After seeding (and after filtering), verify the core is actually infeasible: `elastic_solve(problem, specs, domain, skip = all-except-core)` and assert `total_violation > FEAS_TOL`; if it is feasible, expand the seed (add support members / grow the core) rather than returning a non-infeasible set. At minimum, gate the returned core on a joint-infeasibility check so the advertised invariant is enforced by the code, not merely assumed. Add a 3-constraint regression matching the trigger above. CONFIDENCE: medium (data-dependent). Related NaN-feasibility fixes in the same file already landed (commit abe0593).

divide-by-zero) -- the gap is only that no test proves it. An untested
fail-closed guard is exactly the failure mode this crate exists to prevent.

(2) THE LINEARIZATION "VALIDITY BOUND" IS A CALLER ASSERTION, NOT A BOUND.
radiation.rs:246-290 accepts max_abs_departure_k for ANY finite positive value,
and evaluate (:302-312) enforces only that declaration. Nothing relates it to
the measured discrepancy_w_m2.
EXECUTED REPRO: LinearizedSurfaceRadiation::new("x", eps, 320.0, 310.0, 1.0e6)
then evaluate(5000.0) SUCCEEDS, returning h_rad*4690 ~= 2.8e4 W/m^2 against a
true eps*sigma*(T^4 - T_a^4) ~= 2.8e7 W/m^2 -- a 1000x error, reported as a
discrepancy and refused by nothing.
The bead's WHAT says the validity domain "encodes the linearization bound"; the
code encodes a caller assertion. MODEL_CARD.md:110-113 describes it accurately
("requires a finite departure budget"), so this is a BEAD-vs-code gap rather
than a doc-vs-code one -- fixable either by bounding it or by restating the
clause.

(3) THE EMISSIVITY CARD'S VALIDITY DOMAIN IS NEVER CHECKED AT THE SOLVED
TEMPERATURE. MODEL_CARD.md:70 states the radiation T validity axis is "the
emissivity card's validity domain ... set by SurfaceEmissivity::from_card". But
from_card (radiation.rs:100-157) resolves once at a caller-supplied
temperature_k and FREEZES value. Neither GrayDiffuseEnclosure::solve
(:865-939) nor solve_with_gray_diffuse_enclosure (:1071-1154) ever compares the
converged surface temperature against SurfaceEmissivity::temperature_k or the
card's ValidityDomain. In the coupled fixture the cards are queried at 350 K
(tests/radiation.rs:73) while the surfaces converge somewhere between 300 K and
400 K. A temperature-dependent emissivity would be silently evaluated at the
wrong point, and a surface leaving the card's domain entirely would not refuse.

(4) THE ISOTHERMAL-SURFACE APPROXIMATION IS UNDOCUMENTED. radiation.rs:899 uses
sigma*(<T>)^4 with <T> the area-mean from mean_temperature (:721-747), not
<T^4>. MODEL_CARD.md:60-63 (assumption 9) lists opaque/diffuse/gray/fixed-matrix
but not "each trace is treated as isothermal at its area-mean temperature".
CONTRACT.md:584-586 covers the OUTPUT side ("cannot represent a spatially
varying trace flux") but not this input-side Jensen gap. Note mean_temperature
itself is exact and correct -- the arithmetic mean of three nodal values IS the
exact area average of a P1 field on a triangle; the defect is only that the
T^4-vs-<T>^4 substitution is unstated.

(5) FIXTURES NAMED FOR PHYSICAL ENCLOSURES ARE NOT ONE.
tests/radiation.rs:200-218 (opposite_surfaces) declares infinite_parallel_plates
view factors for the x=0 and x=1 faces of ONE solid 1x1x1 box -- surfaces that
cannot see each other at all, with the conductor between them.
tests/radiation.rs:248-266 + :285 puts two 1 m^2 plates 1.0 m APART and declares
F12 = 1; the true value for coaxial unit squares at unit separation is ~0.1998.
As algebra-verification harnesses these are fine, and CONTRACT.md:574-577 states
the crate never checks a matrix against geometry -- but CHANGELOG.md:283 calls it
"The two-surface analytic fixture" and MODEL_CARD.md:151 files it under G2
CANONICAL BENCHMARKS, which reads as physical.

DONE WHEN
  1. Refusal tests exist for at least the branches whose evidence is claimed in
     prose: non-closing row sum (radiation.rs:490), area mismatch (:835),
     singular radiosity pivot (:1193, reachable with eps -> 0 on both surfaces),
     exhausted outer budget (:1145, via max_iterations: 1 with small
     relaxation), and overlay-on-occupied-row (bc.rs:386, by binding a Robin
     region on a face the enclosure also claims). Alternatively narrow
     CONTRACT.md:209-214/290-293 and MODEL_CARD.md:114-117 to what executes --
     but prefer the tests: these are fail-closed guards.
  2. Either max_abs_departure_k is bounded against the measured discrepancy at
     the domain endpoints, or the bead's WHAT is restated to say
     "caller-declared departure budget". Add a test that pins a WIDE domain
     producing a LARGE discrepancy, so the number is exercised rather than only
     asserted > 0.
  3. The solved surface temperature is checked against the emissivity card's
     retained domain and refuses (or re-queries) when it leaves it -- or
     MODEL_CARD.md:70 is amended to say the domain is enforced only at the
     declared query point.
  4. MODEL_CARD.md assumption list names the isothermal-surface substitution
     and states that the <T^4> - <T>^4 gap is not estimated.
  5. CHANGELOG.md:283 and MODEL_CARD.md:151 stop presenting opposite_surfaces /
     two_disconnected_slabs as analytic or G2 canonical benchmarks. One sentence
     each: they are algebra harnesses with declared, geometrically false view
     factors.

NON-GOALS: no QMC generator, no geometry-to-view-factor computation, no
participating media, no registry authority. This is authority repair only.

description: FOUND BY the fluz9 workspace-suite receipt run (2026-07-30, fmd worker). title: Point fs-tropical at the bead graph: certified critical path and per-bead SLACK as the steering signal bv cannot give
description:
BACKGROUND. The 2026-07-28 reality check found the swarm systematically aiming away from the product spine: 1390 of 1637 open beads blocked (85%), 247 actionable, 209 closed in the last 7 days, and yet the five beads standing between the project and its first end-to-end answer (frn2i, s93ej, s2l9v, f85xj.6.9, f85xj.6.10) were one in-progress and four open, ranked nowhere near the top of any triage view.

THE CAUSE IS MEASURABLE, NOT MORAL. bv ranks by PageRank, betweenness, HITS, eigenvector, k-core -- TOPOLOGICAL centrality over the whole 2365-node graph. Those metrics answer "what is structurally well-connected." They do NOT answer the question that actually governs delivery: given effort estimates and the dependency DAG, which beads set the makespan, and which buy nothing? A deeply-embedded depth bead can dominate PageRank while having large schedule slack; a spine bead can be topologically peripheral and yet be the entire critical path. The swarm is optimising the metric it is shown.

THE INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTS IN-HOUSE AND IS NOT POINTED AT ITSELF. crates/fs-tropical is a dedicated L1 crate implementing max-plus (tropical) critical-path analytics. Its own module doc states the makespan of an acyclic pipeline is the LONGEST PATH, and it exposes:
  - TaskDag::critical_path -> makespan, the critical path, and PER-TASK SLACK, where the doc notes explicitly that "relaxing a task off the critical path buys NOTHING";
  - TaskDag::tune_next -> ranks a CERTIFIED UNIQUE critical path;
  - max_cycle_mean / critical_circuit for the cyclic case.

fs-schedule-e2e already advertises "tropical critical paths, value-of-information, evidence colors" producing "a campaign schedule with named bottlenecks and an act/stop recommendation" -- as a DEMO. The project built the exact instrument for its own steering problem and used it only on a toy.

WHAT.
(a) Project the open-bead dependency DAG into fs_tropical::TaskDag, weighting tasks by bead estimates (falling back to a declared default where an estimate is absent, and RECORDING which weights were defaulted -- an unestimated bead silently weighted zero would corrupt the makespan).
(b) Emit the certified critical path, the makespan, and per-bead slack.
(c) Cross-check against bv's topological ranking and retain BOTH. Where the two disagree, the disagreement is the finding, not an error: it localises exactly where topological centrality is misleading the swarm.
(d) Handle the cycle case honestly: bv reports has_cycles false today, but the projection must refuse rather than silently linearise if that ever changes (critical_circuit exists for precisely this).

DONE WHEN: a reproducible command emits the certified critical path with slack over the current open-bead graph; the result is retained as a checked artifact; and the spine beads' position on (or off) that path is stated as a number rather than an opinion.

TESTS. Oracle: a small hand-computable DAG whose makespan and slack are known in closed form, so the projection is verified against arithmetic rather than against itself. Falsifier: add a dependency that demonstrably lengthens the critical path and prove the makespan moves and the newly-critical bead's slack goes to zero. Non-vacuity: prove at least one bead has NONZERO slack, otherwise the projection has degenerated to "everything is critical" and carries no information.

WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN HAND-PICKING PRIORITIES. A hand-drawn priority list is not falsifiable and decays the moment the graph changes. A computed critical path with slack is re-derivable, auditable, and tells you not only what to do but what NOT to do -- which is the part the swarm currently gets wrong. It also gives fs-tropical its first real consumer, curing the same island disease diagnosed in fs-airflow: the cure for an unused crate is use.
acceptance_criteria: Project one frozen active Bead DAG with explicit estimate values, declared defaults, and uncertainty markers into fs-tropical. Hand-computable DAG unit tests pin makespan, earliest/latest times, slack, unique and nonunique critical paths, disconnected nodes, zero/unknown estimates, overflow, and cycle refusal. Property/metamorphic tests cover node renaming, independent-subgraph insertion, estimate scaling, critical-edge insertion, and deterministic ordering; mutation tests prove a lengthening dependency changes makespan and drives the intended slack to zero. The real command emits both tropical schedule metrics and bv topology metrics without treating disagreement as error, retains the input graph and policy roots, and refuses stale or cyclic projections. Bounded V.3 JSONL records every defaulted estimate, critical path, slack, sensitivity, first divergence, diagnostics, relative artifacts, and reproduction. This steering evidence has no scientific authority and cannot itself reprioritize or close Beads.
close_reason: Certified tropical critical path over the open-bead DAG landed as checked artifact + check-all gate. First numbers: 1769h makespan over 59-bead non-unique path; all five spine beads OFF it (1159-1520h slack); bv top picks also all off it (268-504h) — the centrality/schedule disagreement quantified and retained. Dashboard row flipped to measured 0/5. 8/8 tests, lane 0 violations.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: SEED TEST CASE: the epic frankensim-ggbr6 carries a hand-walked trace of the spine chain (hp7tb -> frn2i -> s93ej -> s2l9v -> 6.9 -> 6.10, with s93ej.2 -> huq.24.4 as the deep gate). If the tropical projection does not reproduce that chain and rank huq.24.4 as a makespan driver, the projection is wrong. Use it as the acceptance oracle alongside the closed-form hand-computable DAG named in this bead.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION (2026-07-28, immediately after filing). With the spine beads created, unblocked, and set at P0, NONE of them appears anywhere in bv --robot-triage recommendations. The top picks remain the same deeply-embedded infrastructure beads as before.

That is not a bug in bv. It is the point. bv ranks by PageRank, betweenness, HITS and k-core -- topological centrality accumulated over graph history. A newly-created bead has almost no in-edges, so it scores near zero no matter how important it is or what priority it carries. Centrality measures how ENTRENCHED work is, not how much it matters.

So the steering instrument the swarm actually consults is structurally incapable of ever surfacing new critical work until that work has already accumulated dependents -- by which time it is no longer new and the drift has already happened. This is the mechanism behind the 85 percent blocked graph, stated precisely.

This is the strongest available argument for this bead: a tropical critical-path projection ranks by SCHEDULE (makespan contribution and slack), which is a property of the current graph and the work remaining, not of accumulated history. It can surface a bead created five minutes ago if that bead is on the longest path. Nothing in the current toolchain can.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CLOSING EVIDENCE (HazyFortress, 2026-07-29/30). DONE-WHEN clause by clause:
(1) 'a reproducible command emits the certified critical path with slack over the current open-bead graph' — MET: cargo run -p xtask -- generate-tropical-path projects open beads (status != closed) into fs_tropical::TaskDag: blocks edges oriented blocker-first, parent-child edges oriented child-first (a parent closes when its children close; the inverse orientation manufactures cycles out of ordinary epic trees — defect found and fixed during implementation, caught loudly by the projection's own cycle-refusal as designed). Weights = estimated_minutes; the 480-minute default for the 183 unestimated beads is RECORDED in the artifact (an unestimated bead silently weighted zero would corrupt the makespan).
(2) 'the result is retained as a checked artifact' — MET: tropical-critical-path.json (schema frankensim-tropical-critical-path-v1) + check-tropical-path wired into check-all. The gate validates slack/map/makespan coherence, refuses foreign/corrupt/inconsistent artifacts (anti-silent-disable), refuses LIVE cycles as violations, and renders tracker movement as a visible stale-snapshot note rather than a wedge. bv comparison is generate-time only and degrades to no-bv-available honestly where bv is absent (the RCH worker case).
(3) 'the spine beads position on (or off) that path is stated as a number rather than an opinion' — MET, and the number is the finding: makespan 1769h over a 59-bead non-unique critical path; ALL FIVE spine beads are OFF it — frn2i slack 1520h, s93ej 1512h, s2l9v 1512h, f85xj.6.9 1159h, f85xj.6.10 1174h. bv's top-6 recommendations are likewise ALL off the path (huq.24.1 268h, i94v.7.4.5 394h, i94v.7.3.5 504h, i94v.7.2.6 348h, i94v.7.6.4 394h, rjoq.7.1 399h). Centrality and schedule criticality point at disjoint work — the disagreement the bead asked to retain, quantified. The program-metrics row spine-critical-path-positions flipped from NO-DATA to a measured 0/5 (a real zero).
TESTS: 8/8 tropical_path G0 tests via RCH (longest-chain-not-loudest-bead, recorded default, closed-blocker drop-out, cycle refusal, parent-child orientation, artifact round-trip, foreign/inconsistent refusal, live validation); spine_rows dashboard discrimination test updated and green; lane proof: check-all --only tropical-critical-path,spine-metrics,program-metrics,spine-ratchet = 0 violations, tropical note current, spine-metrics stale-snapshot note correctly visible under fleet churn.
LIMITS (in artifact no_claim): weights are ESTIMATES; the makespan is a schedule bound over estimates, not a promise; slack 0 means critical under those weights.

title: Report fsqlite IS NULL operator-precedence bug upstream (CHECK re-parse mis-association)
description:
## What
While implementing fs-ledger (frankensim-epic-helm-gp3.1), a STRICT-table CHECK constraint written as `CHECK((t_end IS NULL) = (outcome IS NULL))` failed on rows that satisfy it (e.g. t_end=200, outcome='ok').

## Evidence
fsqlite reports: "CHECK constraint failed: (t_end IS NULL = outcome) IS NULL" — i.e. the stored constraint text is re-parsed with `=` binding tighter than postfix `IS NULL`, evaluating `((t_end IS NULL) = outcome) IS NULL` instead of `(t_end IS NULL) = (outcome IS NULL)`. Stock SQLite gives postfix IS NULL higher precedence than comparison, so the parenthesized form must hold. Two different renderings of the same constraint appeared across runs ("t_end IS NULL = outcome IS NULL" vs "(t_end IS NULL = outcome) IS NULL"), suggesting parens are stripped when the schema text is normalized and precedence is lost on re-parse.

## Repro
fsqlite 0.1.14 (constellation lock f92683cc4572a198):
CREATE TABLE t(a INTEGER, b TEXT, CHECK((a IS NULL) = (b IS NULL))) STRICT;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'x'); -- should succeed; fails with CHECK violation via UPDATE path in fs-ledger's finish_op

## Workaround in fs-ledger
Rewrote the constraint and the matching lint query in AND/OR form: (a IS NULL AND b IS NULL) OR (a IS NOT NULL AND b IS NOT NULL). See crates/fs-ledger/src/schema.rs and lint() in src/lib.rs.

## Why a bead
Plan §12 constellation contract: semantic disagreements with the reference become bug reports for one side. This one is fsqlite's; file it in the frankensqlite repo with the minimal repro.
close_reason: Reported upstream: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite/issues/122. Bug RE-VERIFIED against current fsqlite 0.1.15 before filing (it persists past 0.1.14) with a fresh 20-line repro whose output is fully diagnostic: (a) satisfying row (200, 'ok') REJECTED with 'CHECK constraint failed: t_end IS NULL = outcome IS NULL'; (b) satisfying both-NULL row accepted; (c) VIOLATING row (300, NULL) ACCEPTED - constraint effectively inverted; (d) sqlite_master shows the stored schema text with the user's parentheses STRIPPED. All three truth-table rows match ((t_end IS NULL) = outcome) IS NULL exactly, confirming the diagnosis: normalization strips semantically-necessary parens AND the re-parser binds '=' tighter than postfix IS NULL (stock SQLite is the opposite, so even paren-stripped text would evaluate correctly there). Issue names the precedence fix as root cause, notes the paren-preservation hardening, documents the impact class ('these columns are set together' invariants silently invert) and the fs-ledger workaround (AND/OR expansion).

title: EPIC LEAPFROG-2026 — fifteen platform leaps and five theorem ratchets
description:
## Background
The new-domain program establishes a formidable multiphysics machine simulator, but a fresh review identified fifteen mutually reinforcing platform capabilities and five theorem programs that can make FrankenSim qualitatively unlike commercial CAD/CAE stacks. This epic is the durable source of intent for that second leap. It deliberately preserves maximal mathematical ambition: the theorem ratchets are allowed to discover genuinely new mathematics, while every scientific or product claim remains tied to an executable proof state.

## Technical Approach
Organize the work into five portfolios: typed compilers and assurance; electromagnetics and semantic manufacturing; experimental/digital-twin reality loops; periodic-machine dynamics; and a theorem-ratchet foundry. Each of the twenty initiatives owns a granular implementation graph and a proof/integration gate. Reuse the existing machine IR, port schema, ConstitutiveGraph, FEEC operators, material database, V&V schemas, Design Ledger, and Theorem Foundry rather than creating rival foundations. Cross-portfolio edges are explicit where one artifact is a real prerequisite; optional moonshots remain feature-gated rather than silently blocking solid baselines.

## Success Criteria
All twenty initiative gates are closed with replayable evidence; the final summit demonstrates shared identities, units, conservation ownership, derivatives, budgets, cancellation, and lineage across initiatives; the dependency graph has no cycles; traceability has no orphaned requirement; and every claim is classified as proven, validated within a stated domain, empirical, conjectural, refuted, or no-claim.

## Test Plan
The final summit must include G0 algebraic/property tests, G1 manufactured/convergence checks, G2 canonical and physical reference decks, G3 metamorphic/unit-rescaling tests, G4 cancellation/fault storms, and G5 same-ISA/thread-count determinism audits. It must also mutate or remove one required receipt field at a time and prove fail-closed admission.

## Considerations

title: I01.1 Define the multi-field equation/type IR and semantic identity model
description:
## Background
The single-operator fs-opdsl cannot safely compose coupled fields unless spaces, form degrees, domains, frames, clocks, traces, state slots, and conservation roles are explicit before lowering.

## Technical Approach
Define versioned block-field and equation nodes with differential-form degree, basis/chart and orientation, fs-qty quantity kind, state ownership, time clock, spatial support, boundary trace, parameter role, and stable semantic hash. Specify admissible contractions, pullbacks, port pairings, and complex/real conventions. Provide migration and opaque-extension rules.

## Success Criteria
Ill-typed cross-field contractions, wrong form degree, mixed frames, affine-temperature misuse, clock mismatch, and non-power-conjugate pairings fail before code generation with minimal diagnostics. Equivalent renaming or serialization order preserves semantic identity; a meaningful convention change does not.

## Test Plan
G0 type/algebra laws, schema round trips, migration goldens, graph/ID permutation metamorphics, unit-rescaling tests, deterministic diagnostic snapshots, and malformed-depth/resource adversaries.

## Considerations
This is a neutral compiler IR, not a rival Field, ConstitutiveGraph, or PortSchema. Avoid L3 types leaking into lower-layer material data.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. The artifact must carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames/orientations where relevant, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence state. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, fixed reductions, and deterministic ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; never upgrade evidence from a generated or converged artifact alone. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, record exact commands/results/artifacts, and state performance and scientific no-claim boundaries.

title: I01.4 Generate coupled residual, JVP, VJP, adjoint, DWR, and parameter actions
description:
## Background
Hand-maintained primal and derivative implementations are a primary source of missing cross terms, sign errors, and objectives differentiated under the wrong held-variable convention.

## Technical Approach
Generate block residuals, sparse action graphs, JVP, VJP/discrete adjoint, mixed Hessian actions where admitted, parameter/material/shape derivatives, DWR terms, and explicit event/state-transition hooks from the same semantic graph. Record inner-product, complex-conjugation, held-variable, and discretize-then-differentiate conventions.

## Success Criteria
Block transpose/adjoint identities close within declared numerical bounds; every residual term has a traceable derivative disposition; unsupported active-set or topology changes demote gradients rather than reuse stale actions.

## Test Plan
Random block-vector identities, dual-number and finite-difference oracles, complex convention fixtures, cross-term deletion mutation, gauge/nullspace cases, mesh/time refinement, and checkpointed reverse replay.

## Considerations
Generated differentiation proves consistency with the discrete graph, not correctness of the graph or physical model.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. The artifact must carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames/orientations where relevant, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence state. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, fixed reductions, and deterministic ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; never upgrade evidence from a generated or converged artifact alone. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, record exact commands/results/artifacts, and state performance and scientific no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [F]. Keep the candidate behind a named default-off feature flag until it beats a declared boring baseline on a preregistered deck and records assumptions, monitored validity domain, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack. A refuted theorem or failed candidate remains a valuable versioned artifact.

title: I01.G1 Freeze the multi-field equation/compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The multi-field equation/compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I01 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: typed law and port semantics; residual/JVP/VJP actions; block lowering; conservation and exact-sequence obligations; deterministic cancellation-correct replay. The maximal family is: exact-discrete adjoints and DWR; representation-independent coupled action equivalence; generated multiphysics law completeness; solver-hint optimality under certified budgets. Pin the fixture corpus (cross-domain constitutive graphs, coupled field/port MMS decks, singular block patterns, and generated reference laws), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I02.1 Define the equation-variable hypergraph and causalization receipt schema
description:
## Background
Structural analysis needs stable equations, variables, states, constraints, sources, derivative incidences, domains, and ownership—not just an opaque residual function.

## Technical Approach
Define a versioned bipartite/hypergraph with EquationId, VariableId, derivative order, quantity kind, clock, support, port/component owner, source/constraint role, parameter conditions, and lineage. Define CausalizationReceipt states for under-, over-, well-determined, structurally singular, conditional, and Unknown outcomes.

## Success Criteria
All nodes trace to Machine IR or an audited escape hatch; semantic renaming/order does not alter graph identity; unit/clock mismatches refuse; graph migrations preserve historical receipts.

## Test Plan
Canonical encode/hash, permutations, duplicate/missing ownership, derivative-order bounds, malformed resource bombs, schema migration, and deterministic diagnostics.

## Considerations
The graph records structural incidence, not numerical rank or physical causality.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. The artifact must carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames/orientations where relevant, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence state. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, fixed reductions, and deterministic ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; never upgrade evidence from a generated or converged artifact alone. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, record exact commands/results/artifacts, and state performance and scientific no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [S].

title: I02 typed adjudicated receipt keys for downstream causal maps and caches
description:
## Root cause and user impact
I02 intentionally distinguishes causal semantic adjudication from evidence-object equality: the same typed ID, canonical-preimage root, schema root, canonical byte count, field count, and collection-item count denotes the same causal commitment even if CanonicalLimits evidence differs. Internal admission, Eq, Ord, and Hash honor that six-coordinate tuple, but public getters return raw IdentityReceipt values whose derived Eq also compares limits. A downstream map/set/cache can therefore choose the wrong equality relation accidentally.

## Technical approach
Introduce a public typed CausalIdentityReceiptKey<I> or AdjudicatedReceipt<I> wrapper constructible only from the causal identity roles supported by this module. Implement Eq, Ord, Hash, and stable canonical transport over the exact six-coordinate adjudication tuple while retaining explicit access to the full evidence receipt and limits. Name evidence-object comparison separately and document when each relation is valid. Migrate I02.3 matching/DM/SCC/BLT maps and any later causal caches to the typed key; do not change fs-blake3 global IdentityReceipt semantics.

## Tests and acceptance
G0 compile-time role constraints; equality/order/hash consistency; same six coordinates with different limits compare equal as causal keys but unequal as evidence objects; movement of every one of the six coordinates; BTree/Hash collection behavior; structure, graph artifact, outcome, final receipt, child outcome set, matching set, and migration families. G3 permutation and canonical-transport parity. G5 deterministic ordering. CONTRACT.md must explicitly distinguish semantic adjudication from evidence equality. No authority or collision-resistance theorem is implied beyond the declared digest assumption.

title: I02 recursive causal identity bundle: fixed-point schema governance and complete child authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT

I02 causal identities are recursively composed at the instance level, while the current identity-governance graph accepts only acyclic `schema_dependencies`. `CausalOutcomeIdV1` contains normalized child outcome receipts and therefore has a semantic self-edge. `CausalizationReceiptIdV1` contains full child receipts, while `ConditionalOutcomeSetIdV1` and conditional coverage bind those children back into complete parent receipts, creating a separate evidence SCC. Registering only four top-level producers could make `check-identities` syntactically green while leaving recursive byte-schema evolution outside the constitutional ratchet. A child schema could then move without a provable family-local transition, confusing caches, ledgers, migration, replay, and collision adjudication.

MATHEMATICAL DESIGN: GRAPH-THEORETIC FIXED POINT, NOT HASH ITERATION

Build first-class SCC governance. The fixed point is the least graph-theoretic closure of symbolic owner/domain/role keys and declared dependency edges. Never iterate cryptographic hashes around a cycle looking for `h = H(h)`; such an iteration has no convergence guarantee. For each SCC, canonicalize one bundle preimage containing canonical member order, complete member byte-schema descriptions, and internal edges represented by canonical member indices. Hash that bundle preimage exactly once. Derive each member fingerprint by domain separation over bundle identity plus member owner/domain/role. Collapse SCCs to a condensation DAG; external edges reference already governed child bundle/member identities. A rigorously information-preserving acyclic redesign is acceptable only if typed leaf reference/witness schemas replace the cycles and prove that no semantic or collision-adjudication information was flattened to bare digests.

MINIMAL CONDENSATION PARTITION

Do not create one causal mega-bundle. Preserve the normalized/full quotient through the minimal partition discovered from the live schema graph:

1. Acyclic families: Machine graph/behavior, equation, variable, incidence, normalized structure, provenance artifact, matching set, and any other upstream leaf schemas remain ordinary condensation-DAG nodes unless live dependency analysis proves a smaller SCC.
2. Normalized-outcome SCC: normalized causal outcome plus only the recursive normalized child role needed by conditional outcome semantics. It depends on normalized structure but never on evidence/progress schemas.
3. Full-evidence SCC: complete causalization receipt plus conditional-outcome-set/coverage members and recursive full-child roles. It depends on the normalized-outcome SCC, structure, artifact, matching, and evidence leaves; the normalized-outcome SCC must not depend back on it.

A full/evidence/progress-only schema mutation must not move normalized-outcome bundle version or fingerprint. A normalized-outcome schema mutation must move its own bundle and every dependent full-evidence bundle. Only mathematically necessary SCC members evolve in lockstep.

REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION

- Give structure, artifact, outcome, full receipt, matching set, conditional outcome set, equation, variable, incidence, Machine graph, and Machine behavior explicit owner declarations or rigorously linked existing owners.
- Bind the actual producer `CanonicalSchema::FIELDS` table, ordered field names, wire/presence/child roles, variant/tag grammar, encoder emission closure, domains, names, contexts, and family-local versions. A manually duplicated declaration is not byte-schema proof.
- Ratchet hard-coded role/domain bytes through named constants or registered child schemas.
- Give independently evolvable structure/artifact/outcome/full families independent versions. Express lockstep only through SCC membership and bundle version, never accidental reuse of a generic transport constant.
- Classify nested coordinates honestly: presentation labels, caller order, normalized lineage, provenance lineage, audited predicate source/audit, port crosswalk audit, clock bridge audit, child artifact/full-receipt/progress coordinates, theorem evidence, and every other included or excluded byte.
- Generate identity schemas, authorities, required-ID inventory, mutation matrices, golden couplings, and migration registry atomically from the governed bundle model. No hand-edited drift or partial central registration.
- Integrate migrations produced by `.1.2.11`; this bead owns bundle/governance integration and goldens, while `.1.2.11` owns typed migration closure for outcome, matching, conditional-set, and related durable families.

ACCEPTANCE AND PROOF

G0 freezes canonical SCC member order, nonsemantic local-alias and member-handle alpha-renaming invariance (owner, domain, and role keys are semantic and mutation-sensitive), exact field/variant/child-role layouts, internal member-index edges, and condensation-DAG edges. Every semantic coordinate has a controlled valid before/after mutation proving both typed ID and canonical-preimage movement; every excluded coordinate proves both remain invariant. Member, role, internal-edge, and external-edge mutations must move exactly the mathematically dependent bundle set. Collision-adjudication coordinates use independent receipts/oracles where construction permits.

G3 proves normalized/full quotient laws, recursive mode-cell aggregation, structure/artifact provenance separation, family-local version independence, the negative evidence-to-outcome coupling law, the positive outcome-to-full dependency law, and old/new migration crosswalks supplied by `.1.2.11`.

G4 proves bounded graph traversal, canonicalization work, and memory; cancellation before bundle publication; valid declared SCC cycles admit; malformed membership, duplicate members, missing members, non-closed dependencies, undeclared cross-bundle cycles, domain/role confusion, digest-collision fixtures, and generator crashes refuse atomically. There is no cryptographic convergence loop to test.

G5 proves byte-stable bundle/member registries and identities across repeated and thread-count-equivalent runs on both reference ISAs. Add a real no-mock journey from Machine graph and behavior through causal graph, incomplete and complete mode cells, normalized/full parent receipts, matching/coverage evidence, ledger persistence, migration, and replay. Structured bounded logs name bundle/member ID, owner/domain/role, family and bundle versions, dependency edge, schema and byte-schema fingerprints, mutation target, exclusion/no-claim, canonical bytes/counts, cancellation checkpoint, and final disposition.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY

Until this bead and its migration dependency are green, recursive child-schema governance is not certified. Contracts must say so. Central owners must not add partial required IDs, authority rows, generated registries, or goldens for only the four top-level families. Preserve the strong runtime composition and ambition; do not flatten recursive receipts to bare digests or weaken collision adjudication.

## Success Criteria

Close only when all four exact children close on one compatible source snapshot. Algebra and registry may proceed before I02.11; only the migration child waits for I02.11. The proof child must consume the real registry and migration artifacts through the existing I02 manifest and driver, retain comprehensive focused tests plus no-mock E2E and detailed bounded logs, and report DSR, scientific authority, and no-claim states separately. Aggregate counts cannot substitute for exact child identities.

title: I02.2 Extract equations and derivative incidences from generated and hand operators
description:
## Background
The causalizer must see identical semantics whether an equation came from fs-opdsl, a circuit stamp, or a legacy hand operator; otherwise escape hatches become invisible structural hazards.

## Technical Approach
Extract algebraic relations, state updates, constraints, port equations, derivatives, conditional regimes, and parameter-dependent incidences from the generated compiler. Define a conformance adapter requiring hand operators to provide equivalent metadata and runtime monitors. Preserve source hashes and opaque portions explicitly.

## Success Criteria
Equivalent generated/hand systems yield equivalent hypergraphs; missing incidence or state ownership is rejected; conditional structure carries the parameter/guard domain that activates it.

## Test Plan
Generated-vs-hand fixtures, seeded missing cross incidence, conditional zero coefficient, nonlinear hidden dependency, clocked state, opaque escape hatch, and cancellation mid-extraction.

## Considerations
Static extraction may overapproximate nonlinear dependencies; record conservative edges and refinement evidence rather than invent precision.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. The artifact must carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames/orientations where relevant, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence state. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, fixed reductions, and deterministic ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; never upgrade evidence from a generated or converged artifact alone. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, record exact commands/results/artifacts, and state performance and scientific no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [F]. Keep the candidate behind a named default-off feature flag until it beats a declared boring baseline on a preregistered deck and records assumptions, monitored validity domain, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack. A refuted theorem or failed candidate remains a valuable versioned artifact.

## Atomic decomposition map
This former compound execution leaf is now a zero-estimate rollup. frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.1.2.2.1 freezes semantics and admissibility; frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.1.2.2.2 owns production implementation; frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.1.2.2.3 is the independent terminal receipt. The child estimates preserve the original planning median without double counting. Downstream work consumes frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.1.2.2.3; the rollup closes only when all direct children close.

title: I02.G1 Freeze the machine causalization and structural-index compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The machine causalization and structural-index compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I02 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: equation-variable incidence; deterministic matching/DM/SCC/BLT; scoped index reduction; consistent initialization; executable block plans and repair witnesses. The maximal family is: minimality and presentation-invariance of causal witnesses; hybrid-mode-wide structural completeness; certified hidden-constraint discovery and globally optimal tearing/repair. Pin the fixture corpus (toy machine vertical slice, high-index DAEs, under/overdetermined graphs, hybrid mode families, and adversarial equivalent presentations), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.
