title: I02 resource closure: streamed identities and lease-admitted causal workspaces
description:
## Root cause and user impact
I02.1 advertises bounded resource-bomb-safe admission up to 1,048,576 incidences, but its current graph/receipt path materializes Vec<Vec<u8>> identity rows, uses infallible BTreeMap/BTreeSet and stable-sort workspaces, and does not charge temporary memory to the active operation lease. A syntactically legal graph can exceed available memory and abort instead of returning a typed ResourceLimit refusal. Weakening the published envelope would reduce capability and is not acceptable.

## Technical approach
After the fs-blake3 streaming leaf lands, migrate causal structure, artifact, outcome, conditional-outcome, matching, and receipt encoders to direct ordered-row streaming. Convert row encoders to exact-length checked sinks so no million-row payload is retained. Preflight every index/sort/adjacency workspace with checked arithmetic and fallible reservation. When Cx carries an OperationMemoryLease, admit all peak-live temporary storage before allocation and hold RAII charges through the true live interval; lease-less compatibility Cx is explicitly unbounded and cannot support a bounded-memory evidence claim. Replace large tree maps/sets with deterministic lease-admitted flat indexes, sorted vectors, CSR-style adjacency, or another fallible representation whose tie/order semantics are identical. Preserve fixed logical ordering, cancellation polling, exact identity bytes, and no-partial-publication.

## Typed refusal and observability
Resource refusals must identify phase/site, requested bytes/items, admitted/used/limit bytes, arithmetic/layout/allocator/lease cause, and whether any prior phase drained. Do not collapse memory exhaustion into generic identity failure. Request -> drain -> finalize applies synchronously to all temporary state and lease charges.

## Tests and evidence
G0 exact-limit and one-byte-below/above lease cases, injected try_reserve failure, empty and max-cardinality reduced-limit fixtures, duplicate/adversarial keys, and byte/receipt parity with the pre-streaming implementation. G3 permutation, representation, chunking, and streamed-vs-materialized equivalence. G4 deterministic cancel-on-N checkpoints through index build, sort, structure hash, artifact hash, outcome hash, receipt hash, and final publication; assert typed refusal, zero leaked lease charge, and no admitted identity. G5 fixed identities and diagnostics across thread counts and row chunk schedules. Add a reduced-cap instrumented allocator harness rather than allocating a real half-gigabyte in routine tests; retain an opt-in hostile-scale E2E script with detailed phase/peak logs. Update fs-ir CONTRACT.md with exact peak-memory accounting and the lease-less no-claim boundary. Central DSR/RCH batch proof is required before closure.

## Dependencies and acceptance
Depends on the fs-blake3 fallible streaming leaf and the landed Cx/LeasedVec operation-lease substrate. I02.1 remains blocked until this leaf is green because its current success criteria explicitly include malformed resource bombs and exact public envelope caps.

title: I02 exact row plans: admit causal identity payloads before allocation
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The first I02 streaming slice retained only one row, but it computes a row length by constructing the full Vec payload inside the row_lengths iterator. This violates the fs-blake3 ordered stream contract: row length must be independently available so field and row limits are admitted before payload construction. An oversized row can allocate or abort before the encoder rejects it.

MISSION
Introduce an exact causal-row plan or equivalent two-phase producer for every ordered-row identity family. The declaration phase must compute exact checked length without allocating the payload. Only after fs-blake3 admits that length may the producer fallibly reserve bounded storage or stream canonical chunks. Preserve byte-for-byte identity parity and all logical ordering.

- Cover causal structure, graph artifact, normalized outcome, complete receipt, matching set, conditional outcome set, migration/test adapters, and every future call through one API that makes premature materialization difficult.
- Replace saturating length arithmetic with checked typed refusal. Validate usize/u64 conversions. Refuse exact one-over row and collection caps before producer allocation or mutation.
- Use fallible reservation or direct sink writes; no infallible Vec growth on hostile input. Allocation refusal is distinct from canonical limit, producer, and cancellation failure.
- Poll cancellation during length derivation and payload production with real prior progress. No partial identity publication.
- G0 tests for empty, fixed, variable, maximum reduced limit, one-over, injected reserve failure, length/payload disagreement, and every row family. G3 parity against the eager historical frames and chunking or representation variants. Include detailed deterministic phase/row/byte logging.
- Update CONTRACT with exact peak-live row claim and remaining workspace or allocator-overhead no-claims.

title: I04 EPIC — conservation-defect microscope and causal balance attribution
description:
## Background
A global energy mismatch says a simulation is wrong but not where or why. Multiphysics machines need a microscope that attributes defects to cells, interfaces, time windows, remaps, constitutive updates, controls, and numerical tolerances.

## Technical Approach
Define a common balance-event algebra over chain/cochain regions and ports; compute local residual measures, interface jump/commutator defects, integrator and remap contributions, loss ownership, and QoI-weighted adjoint attribution. Produce minimal witnesses and uncertainty-aware explanations rather than a single scalar.

## Success Criteria
Injected sign, orientation, dropped-loss, nonconservative-remap, loose-solve, and bad-event faults are localized to the responsible artifact and time interval, while exact transfers cancel without double counting.

## Test Plan
Telescoping partition laws, refinement and repartition invariance, fault mutation campaigns, window recomposition, unit scaling, cancellation storms, and whole-machine conservation decks.

## Considerations
A decomposition may be nonunique; report attribution policy and ambiguity. Never force defects to sum by hiding unowned remainder terms.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [F]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

Energy, exergy, entropy, charge, mass, elements, momentum, and information have different admissible accounting rules; do not force one generic equation beyond its semantics.

Use safe Rust by default with layer-correct dependencies. title: I04.G1 Freeze the conservation-defect microscope claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The conservation-defect microscope gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I04 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: local and machine-scale balance attribution; reset/impulse accounting; spatial/temporal/interface localization; counterfactual replay and actionable witnesses. The maximal family is: minimal causal explanations across coupled representations; first-divergence guarantees under hybrid topology changes; certified blame stability and counterfactual completeness. Pin the fixture corpus (manufactured balance defects, missed events, nonconforming interfaces, scale transfers, hidden source terms, and equivalent chart representations), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

description:

title: I08.5 Replan online with scoped cost authority, cancellation, and idempotency

title: I08.G1 Freeze the evidence-budget co-design planner claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The evidence-budget co-design planner gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I08 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: typed evidence actions; calibrated response/cost models; constrained portfolio planning; online idempotent replanning; anti-Goodhart and falsification budgets. The maximal family is: anytime-valid globally adaptive evidence allocation with theorem-aware value of information; robust multi-horizon optimality and self-improving cost/error models. Pin the fixture corpus (cold-plate and motor evidence portfolios, censored costs, dependent tests, optional stopping, adversarial Goodhart loops, and budget shocks), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I12 EPIC — hybrid mode-automaton compiler from machine equations
description:
## Background
Contacts, backlash, valve opening, circuit commutation, saturation, stick-slip, phase change, controller sampling, and protection trips create hybrid systems. Ad hoc event callbacks cannot support validated timing, adjoints, Zeno handling, or reproducible mode lineage.

## Technical Approach
Define a typed hybrid automaton IR with modes, invariants, guards, resets, complementarity branches, state transfer maps, superdense time, priorities, and conservation obligations. Extract candidate modes from causalized equations and constitutive regimes, validate events, generate saltation/adjoint artifacts, and compile deterministic schedules with explicit Zeno/grazing policies.

## Success Criteria
Representative gear impact, diode commutation, valve/choking, stick-slip, and controller-trip systems lower from machine definitions into replayable automata whose event times, state maps, balances, and derivatives satisfy stated enclosures.

## Test Plan
Guard perturbation, simultaneous-event permutation, grazing/tangency, chattering/Zeno, reset unit/frame checks, event-time gradients, and pause/resume equivalence.

## Considerations
Mode enumeration can explode; use symbolic constraints and lazy reachability without dropping reachable safety modes. A chosen priority policy must be ledgered, not implicit.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [F]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. title: I12.G1 Freeze the hybrid mode-automaton compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The hybrid mode-automaton compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I12 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: typed modes/guards/resets/invariants; structural consistency per mode; bounded coverage; deterministic superdense runtime; event-time and generalized derivative protocols. The maximal family is: complete bounded-horizon mode coverage; certified Zeno/accumulation handling; topology-changing reset semantics; global hybrid derivative correctness. Pin the fixture corpus (gear contact and backlash, 0-D gas valves, chatter, simultaneous events, rank-changing DAEs, and topology-changing resets), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I15 EPIC — executable standards compiler with versioned conformance witnesses
description:
## Background
Engineering standards are currently read by humans and reimplemented as fragile spreadsheets, scripts, or tribal knowledge. FrankenSim can compile a licensed, version-pinned normative subset into typed obligations, calculations, tests, evidence requirements, and explicit nonautomatable judgments.

## Technical Approach
Create a standards source/edition registry and formal requirement DSL; encode applicability, definitions, equations, tolerances, exceptions, sampling, evidence, and human-judgment nodes. Bind obligations to machine/evidence identities, generate conformance tests and minimal failure witnesses, and compute change impact across editions without redistributing protected source text.

## Success Criteria
At least three dissimilar standards families—mechanical rating, EMC test method, and V&V/assurance—compile into replayable obligation graphs whose results trace to licensed source locators and distinguish pass, fail, not-applicable, insufficient-evidence, and human-review-required.

## Test Plan
Golden hand calculations, edition diffs, boundary/tolerance cases, ambiguity/refusal fixtures, license redaction tests, adversarial omitted exception, and generated-test mutation campaigns.

## Considerations
This does not make FrankenSim an accredited laboratory or legal certifier. Preserve exact source/version jurisdiction and do not hallucinate normative text.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [F]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

title: I15.G1 Freeze the executable standards compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The executable standards compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I15 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: edition-aware clause identity; typed normative rules and human judgments; applicability; obligation execution; scoped conformance receipts and semantic edition diffs. The maximal family is: proof-carrying cross-standard composition; automated transitive impact completeness; jurisdiction/edition-aware theorem obligations; machine-checkable assurance without erasing human authority. Pin the fixture corpus (gear-rating, motor-method, EMC/V&V packs, edition changes, conflicting clauses, licensed-source boundaries, and declared human judgments), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

description:

## Success Criteria

## Test Plan
Run applicable G0 algebraic/schema properties, G1 manufactured convergence, G2 canonical/held-out benchmarks, G3 unit/basis/scale/refinement metamorphics, G4 cancellation/fault/leak campaigns, and G5 deterministic replay. title: I03.2a Freeze typed semantics, admissible domains, and artifact contracts — Add conductors, floating potentials, terminals, and capacitance extraction
description:
## Background
Capacitive devices need equipotential conductors with prescribed voltage or charge, floating potentials, terminal identities, and extracted Maxwell capacitance matrices rather than arbitrary point constraints.

## Technical Approach
Define conductor components and terminal charts; assemble equipotential and total-charge constraints in a saddle system; handle floating conductors and reference choice; extract terminal charges, Maxwell capacitance, reduced capacitance, energy, and ElectrostaticTerminalReceipt. Preserve Machine IR terminal identity and port pairing.

## Success Criteria
Terminal permutation and potential reference leave physical results invariant; total charge closes; reduced matrices are symmetric/positive semidefinite only under reciprocal SPD assumptions; missing floating constraints refuse with a minimal witness.

## Test Plan
Multi-conductor analytic cases, isolated/floating conductor, multiply connected geometry, reference changes, terminal permutations, charge versus voltage control, and singular constraint mutation.

## Considerations
Matrix symmetry is conditional on reciprocity and consistent terminal conventions, not universal.

## Repository-wide implementation contract

Carry explicit units, seeds, versions, validity domains, error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, cancellation, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts and machine fingerprints, and state scientific/performance/conformance no-claim boundaries.

title: I03.3 Implement steady-current conduction and resistance/conductance extraction
description:
## Background
Electrical conductivity, leakage, Joule heating, and terminal resistance are separate from static displacement fields but share scalar weighted operators and terminal semantics.

## Technical Approach
Solve steady charge continuity with scalar/tensor conductivity, insulating/current/voltage boundaries, terminals, and temperature-dependent material sampling. Extract conductance/resistance matrices and local Joule-loss ownership, then couple losses through typed ports to thermal storage.

## Success Criteria
KCL and electrical-input/Joule-output power close; analytic slab/coaxial resistance and anisotropic cases converge; reciprocal symmetry is claimed only for reciprocal cards; Hall/nonreciprocal media refuse or route elsewhere.

## Test Plan
Slab/coaxial oracles, parallel/series networks, anisotropic rotation, temperature coefficient, insulating boundaries, terminal permutation, zero conductivity, and loss double-count mutation.

## Considerations
Steady current is not an EQS transient and cannot represent displacement-current-dominated behavior.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default, preserve architectural layer direction, and reuse canonical quantities, frames, material claims, evidence, ports, and semantic identities. Carry explicit units, seeds, versions, validity domains, error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, cancellation, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. title: I03.4 Add nonlinear, dispersive, and memory dielectric constitutive laws
description:
## Background
Real dielectrics may be field-dependent, lossy, dispersive, hysteretic, and history-dependent. Treating them as one constant epsilon invents accuracy and misses dissipation.

## Technical Approach
Start with potential-based nonlinear polarization and consistent tangents; add Debye and admitted distributed-relaxation state nodes; pursue ferroelectric/hysteretic laws only with explicit free-energy/dissipation charts, internal state, passivity or stability obligations, material validity, and generated derivatives. Retain constant linear dielectric as baseline.

## Success Criteria
Pure linear and zero-loss limits recover the baseline; tangents/VJPs agree independently; relaxation matches analytic response; lossy fits pass declared passivity/dissipation checks or refuse; state checkpoints replay.

## Test Plan
Nonlinear capacitor, Debye relaxation, frequency/time agreement, passivity adversary, hysteresis loop energy, state migration, extrapolation, and cancellation during state batches.

## Considerations
A good frequency fit does not validate breakdown, aging, or microscopic polarization mechanism.

## Repository-wide implementation contract

title: I07 EPIC — AP242 semantic manufacturing round trip
description:
## Background
Geometry-only STEP exchange loses assembly intent, PMI/GD&T, material/process state, kinematics, and traceability. A supplier round trip must reveal semantic loss rather than return a visually similar but engineering-different model.

## Technical Approach

Emit canonical AP242, re-import it, and produce a semantic diff with certified geometry bounds and refusal for unsupported constructs.

## Success Criteria
Pinned public/licensed corpora and FrankenSim-generated assemblies survive import-export-import with stable semantic identities, bounded geometry error, preserved tolerance/material/kinematic meaning, and exhaustive loss reports.

## Test Plan
Parser fuzzing, entity-reference cycles, unit/frame adversaries, PMI tolerance boundary cases, assembly identity, canonical serialization, B-rep/SDF cross-checks, and unsupported-schema refusal.

## Considerations
Claim conformance only to the implemented application protocol/conformance class and corpus. Do not promise arbitrary vendor-dialect round trips.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. ## Ambition discipline

title: I07.4 Map semantic PMI, GD&T, datums, dimensions, and surface texture
description:
## Background
Graphical annotations can look correct while carrying no machine-readable tolerance meaning. Manufacturing and UQ need semantic PMI bound to exact datums and shape aspects.

## Technical Approach
Map supported semantic dimensions/tolerances, datum systems and precedence, geometric tolerances, target shape aspects, modifiers, units, surface texture, and presentation links into typed manufacturing constraints. Keep semantic PMI distinct from graphical presentation and retain unsupported constructs.

## Success Criteria
Pinned semantic-PMI corpora round trip with datum, tolerance, unit, target, and modifier identity; a picture-only annotation never becomes semantic PMI; tolerance changes propagate to as-built/UQ constraints.

## Test Plan
Datum precedence, composite tolerances, unit scaling, target mismatch, graphical-only annotation, boundary modifiers, missing referenced geometry, and corpus mutation.

## Considerations
Do not claim drawing approval or complete AP242 PMI coverage from a selected corpus.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default, preserve architectural layer direction, and reuse canonical quantities, frames, material claims, evidence, ports, and semantic identities. Carry explicit units, seeds, versions, validity domains, error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, cancellation, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts and machine fingerprints, and state scientific/performance/conformance no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [F]. Keep the lane behind a named default-off flag until its established baseline, current reference status, monitored assumptions, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack are recorded. Refutation is preserved rather than obscured.

title: I07.6 Map electrical harness and EWIS semantics into the native HarnessGraph
description:
## Background
AP242 can carry harness assemblies, wires, connectors, terminals, placement, and bundle membership. EMC needs declared connectivity, not proximity-derived nets.

## Technical Approach
Map supported harness products, wires/cables, connectors/pins, terminals, splices, nets, bundles, routes, placements, and occurrence identities into a neutral native HarnessGraph. Leave electrical/material parameter models as referenced cards; preserve unsupported entities and loss reports.

Connector-pin continuity, assembly transforms, route length, bundle membership, and wire lists round trip; proximity never creates connectivity; ambiguous pins/nets refuse with minimal witnesses.

Simple/branched harnesses, repeated connectors, swapped pins, open/shield drain, route frames, bundle changes, missing net, and native-versus-AP242 semantic diff.

The native HarnessGraph must remain usable without AP242 or licensed schemas.

title: I07.K Map AP242 kinematic pairs, joints, freedoms, limits, and coupled motion semantics
description:
## Background
AP242 placements and assembly occurrences describe where parts are, not how they are permitted to move. The program promises a semantic manufacturing round trip that preserves kinematics, yet the existing AP242 work packages do not explicitly map kinematic pairs, joint frames, degrees of freedom, limits, screw pitch, or coupled motion. Inferring joints from proximity or placement would silently change machine physics.

## Technical Approach
Define a versioned supported AP242 kinematics profile and map each admitted kinematic pair/mechanism into Machine IR with stable occurrence identity, two named joint frames, pair type, allowed and constrained degrees of freedom, coordinate/sign convention, reference state, lower/upper limits, screw pitch, gear or coupled-pair ratio, units, configuration/effectivity, and source provenance. Support a deliberately bounded initial set such as revolute, prismatic, cylindrical, spherical, planar, screw, gear, rack-and-pinion, and explicitly admitted coupled pairs. Preserve unsupported entities as safe opaque extensions when possible and emit an exhaustive semantic-loss receipt otherwise. Export must reconstruct the supported pair without guessing; import must never infer a joint solely from placement, geometry, or contact.

## Success Criteria
Supported kinematic assemblies survive import-export-import with stable pair identity, frames, freedoms, limits, pitch/ratio, units, signs, and occurrence lineage. Machine IR constructed from the round trip produces equivalent configuration-space constraints under the admitted kinematics contract. Unsupported or ambiguous pairs are refused or preserved opaquely with a precise receipt; placement-only assemblies remain unjointed.

## Test Plan
Round-trip revolute, prismatic, cylindrical, spherical, planar, screw, gear, rack-and-pinion, and coupled-pair fixtures; zero and asymmetric limits; negative pitch/ratio; swapped-frame and reversed-axis mutations; nested occurrences and effectivity; mixed units; missing references; unsupported pair subtypes; placement without a joint; canonical serialization; configuration-graph equivalence; parser fuzzing; deterministic replay; and independent semantic-diff checks.

## Considerations
Claim only the pinned AP242 edition/profile and enumerated pair subset. Frame orientation and sign conventions are physics-bearing. A visually correct pose is not kinematic equivalence. Contact, compliance, friction, backlash, actuator, and control semantics remain separate unless explicitly represented by admitted AP242 entities and mapped receipts.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain pure-Rust and Franken-only in production, layer-correct, safe by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync scopes, deterministic in parsing and canonical serialization, explicit about units/versions/capabilities/budgets, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names relevant Gauntlet tiers, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its exact fallback, retains the supported schema profile and corpus hashes, and includes independently replayable round-trip and semantic-diff artifacts.

## Frontier promotion discipline
Ambition class: [F]. Use feature flag `frontier-ap242-kinematics`. The boring baseline imports placements and occurrences with no joint claim. Activation requires the pinned conformance corpus, negative/refusal corpus, stable Machine IR mapping, deterministic round-trip evidence, quantitative geometry/configuration equivalence bounds, and independent reproduction. title: I07.Ka Freeze typed semantics, admissible domains, and artifact contracts — Map AP242 kinematic pairs, joints, freedoms, limits, and coupled motion semantics

Define a versioned supported AP242 kinematics profile and map each admitted kinematic pair/mechanism into Machine IR with stable occurrence identity, two named joint frames, pair type, allowed and constrained degrees of freedom, coordinate/sign convention, reference state, lower/upper limits, screw pitch, gear or coupled-pair ratio, units, configuration/effectivity, and source provenance. Support a deliberately bounded initial set such as revolute, prismatic, cylindrical, spherical, planar, screw, gear, rack-and-pinion, and explicitly admitted coupled pairs. Preserve unsupported entities as safe opaque extensions when possible and emit an exhaustive semantic-loss receipt otherwise. title: I13 EPIC — EM topology optimization with winding cohomology
description:
## Background
Conventional EM topology optimization treats material density but struggles with manufacturable windings, integer turns, terminal connectivity, insulation, moving interfaces, losses, thermal limits, demagnetization, and topology-changing derivative consistency.

## Technical Approach
Create a mixed discrete/continuous design algebra: material/shape fields plus relative-cohomology winding classes and terminal periods. Couple gauged EM, circuits, thermal, structural/NVH, loss ownership, manufacturing constraints, robust UQ, and topology-aware adjoints. Explore differential-cohomology formulations behind a moonshot flag while retaining a solid winding-graph baseline.

## Success Criteria
The optimizer discovers nontrivial rotor/stator/winding designs that satisfy connectivity and insulation constraints, close power/loss balances, reproduce gradients across topology-stable steps, and use explicit surgery/restart receipts when topology changes.

## Test Plan
Known magnetic circuits, winding-number invariance, mesh/chart conversion, finite-difference gradients, robust manufacturing perturbations, demagnetization/hotspot constraints, and held-out flagship comparisons.

## Considerations
Do not relax integer/topological constraints into meaningless gray windings. A better objective without manufacturability and validation evidence is not a promoted design.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [M]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

title: I13.1 Define admissible EM design fields and energy-consistent material interpolation
description:
## Background
Gray interpolation of permeability, magnets, conductors, dielectrics, and void can violate energy positivity and create numerically optimal but physically meaningless material.

## Technical Approach
Define multi-material density, level-set, shape, magnetization-direction, lamination, and conductor design fields with filters/projections and mesh-scale receipts. Interpolate convex energy potentials or bounded homogenized material cards rather than arbitrary coefficients; retain pure-material limits and uncertainty.

## Success Criteria
Pure limits recover certified material operators; incremental energy/monotonicity and objectivity conditions hold or refuse; design identity includes filter, projection, mesh, material cards, and validity domain.

## Test Plan
Pure/mixture limits, negative-energy falsifier, filter-refinement, rotated anisotropy, material extrapolation, mesh dependence, and deterministic field serialization.

## Considerations
A relaxed design is not manufacturable material. Promotion requires a realization or an explicit homogenized manufacturing route.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Reuse canonical geometry, fields, materials, ports, quantities, evidence, and semantic identities. Carry units, frames/orientations, seeds, versions, validity/error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, cancellation with bounded drain, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts and machine fingerprints, and state scientific, manufacturing, standards, and performance no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion

Keep the frontier or moonshot off by default until a declared boring baseline, primary-reference status, monitored assumptions, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack exist. description:
## Background
Real harmonic cochains and Betti numbers do not determine integer winding constraints. Integral relative homology can contain torsion; valid basis changes are unimodular; period lattices, Smith normal form, and exact chain identities are needed to prevent mesh or basis choices from changing turn counts.

## Technical Approach
Implement exact integral boundary matrices, Smith and optionally Hermite normal forms with certified transformations, free and torsion decomposition, relative long-exact-sequence checks, integer cycle/cocycle bases, period lattices, and deterministic canonicalization. Track coefficient growth, modular/reconstruction acceleration with exact verification, orientation, and basis/cut transforms. Produce unimodular witnesses and distinguish torsion linking information from free winding periods. Provide bounded resource/cancellation behavior and structured Unknown for coefficient explosion or unsupported complexes rather than falling back to floating rank.

## Success Criteria
Canonical fixtures reproduce integral free/torsion groups; every basis transformation has an exact unimodular witness; integer periods are invariant under tree/cut and mesh labeling; modular acceleration verifies against exact multiplication; floating-rank agreement never substitutes for integral proof. ## Considerations

## Execution and evidence

## Fresh-eyes scientific correction — abstract torsion versus physical 3-D topology
Lens-space and other torsion-rich finite complexes are retained as valuable abstract algebra-kernel fixtures only. They are not physical conductor/insulator regions embedded in ordinary three-dimensional Euclidean space and may not be used to infer a material winding-torsion claim. title: I13.2c Certify chain maps and winding-period naturality across mesh and representation changes
description:
## Background
Optimization, remeshing, chart conversion, refinement, and different trees/cuts change the computational complex. Winding and flux-linkage meaning survives only when there is a checked chain/cochain map that commutes with boundaries and transports the integral period lattice and terminal work correctly.

## Technical Approach
Construct or admit chain maps for refinement, coarsening, remeshing, chart conversion, terminal-preserving geometry updates, and tree/cut changes. Verify boundary/coboundary commutation, terminal-relative incidence, induced integral maps, unimodularity or stated index, free/torsion action, and compatibility with distributed/filament winding and circuit duality. Emit WindingClassReceipt with canonical class identity, period vector, map composition/naturality defects, error budgets for geometric/field quantities, and exact lineage. Refuse maps that merge terminals, cross insulation, lose integral periods, or cannot establish their induced action.

## Success Criteria
Equivalent meshes/charts/bases preserve classes and terminal observables; map composition agrees with direct transport; refinement/coarsening round trips preserve integral periods where claimed; filament/distributed realizations agree in declared norms; invalid maps fail closed and invalidate dependent caches.

## Test Plan
Use repeated refinement, remesh and chart round trips, tree/cut changes, conductor and phase permutations, nonunimodular maps, lost terminal cells, insulation crossings, map-composition mutations, winding/circuit duality fixtures, restart replay, and G5 determinism.

## Considerations
Naturality is conditional on a declared admissible map. It does not claim that arbitrary topology-changing geometry has a canonical transport.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [M]. Emit content-addressed WindingClassReceipt and ChainMapNaturalityReceipt artifacts with exact integral actions, terminal work/flux-linkage conventions, defects, provenance, and refusal reasons.

title: I13.2d Classify topology events and emit induced-map, redesign, and invalidation obligations
description:

Detect and classify Betti/torsion changes, conductor births/deaths/splits/merges, insulation bridges/breaks, terminal contacts/separations, and near-simultaneous ambiguous events. Emit one of: certified induced transport; a finite set of admissible class relations; discrete redesign request; or deterministic invalidation obligations for topology, gauge, state, adjoint, preconditioner, surrogate, and gradient caches. Ledger pre/post identities, event ordering/partial order, ambiguity, and restart boundary.

## Success Criteria
No event invents or destroys terminal/winding data silently; ambiguous events preserve alternatives or Unknown; cache and gradient invalidation is complete; split/merge and insulation mutations replay; every continuation or redesign decision cites the exact induced-map witness or absence.

## Test Plan
Create births/deaths, tunnel events, conductor splits/merges, insulation bridges, terminal contact/swap, torsion changes, near-simultaneous events, missing maps, stale-cache mutations, cancellation during event transaction, and restart replay.

This task classifies topology and emits transfer obligations only. I13.4b exclusively owns physical field, circuit, thermal, stress, state, adjoint, and restart transfer; ordinary differentiability stops unless a separate generalized theorem applies.

Publish separate WindingTopologyReceipt, WindingClassReceipt, and topology-event evidence states.

## Success Criteria
Independent results agree exactly for integral data and within directed bounds for declared physical observables; basis/cut/mesh/chart changes preserve the same class; nonintegral rounding, lost torsion, wrong orientation, missing terminal, stale map, and silent topology-event mutations are killed. Any mismatch blocks optimization, routing, and initiative promotion.

Run linked/relative/torsion fixtures, random unimodular bases, refinements/remeshes, terminal swaps, conductor split/merge, insulation bridge, missing induced maps, corrupted receipts, feature-off baseline, cancellation/fault finalization, and deterministic replay.

The receipt certifies the declared relative-topology capability. It does not prove differential-character, cobordism, or global topology-optimization theorems; those remain ambitious Ratchet A targets.

title: I13.4 Implement topology optimization and certified topology-event restart
description:
## Background
SIMP, level-set, and topological-derivative steps can create or destroy tunnels, components, and winding classes. Continuing stale state or adjoints across the event is unsound.

## Technical Approach
Adapt existing L4 optimizers to EM design fields; detect topology events; update geometry/mesh lineage, project state conservatively, recompute relative classes and gauges, invalidate derivative/preconditioner caches, and restart trust regions with explicit surgery receipts. Retain a fixed-topology shape baseline.

## Success Criteria
Fixed-topology cases converge reproducibly; seeded tunnel/split events are detected and replay-identical; no pre-event gradient survives without a proved transport; failure falls back to fixed-topology or discrete redesign.

## Test Plan
Known topology problems, continuation/reversal, split/merge, stale-gradient falsifier, remap balance, cancellation during event transaction, and thread determinism.

## Considerations
Topological derivatives are local asymptotics, not global optimum certificates.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Reuse canonical geometry, fields, materials, ports, quantities, evidence, and semantic identities. Carry units, frames/orientations, seeds, versions, validity/error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, cancellation with bounded drain, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts and machine fingerprints, and state scientific, manufacturing, standards, and performance no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [M]. Keep the frontier or moonshot off by default until a declared boring baseline, primary-reference status, monitored assumptions, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack exist. Preserve refutations and negative results.

title: I13.4d Independently adjudicate fixed-topology cohomology-aware optimizer progress and no-event equivalence
description:
## Background
I13's core is intentionally moonshot-level: it seeks cohomology-preserving electromagnetic topology optimization with exact-discrete gradients and auditable design progress. That core, however, must not silently require the still stronger topology-event remesh/restart/generalized-adjoint branch. A separate fixed-topology receipt is needed so future agents can distinguish optimization within one declared topology stratum from optimization that crosses a topology event.

## Technical Approach
Consume the fixed-topology optimizer artifact from I13.4a and the independently adjudicated fixed-topology EM/circuit/motion/loss adjoint receipt from I13.3c. Preregister the admissible design stratum, cell-complex identity, relative/absolute boundary split, harmonic-basis convention, Betti/cohomology invariants, feature-size and persistence margins, objective and constraint graph, optimizer settings, seeds, and error/resource budgets. Recompute objective, constraints, gradients, line-search or trust-region acceptance, and progress using an independently owned checker. At every accepted iterate, evaluate explicit no-topology-event guards and retain chain/cochain, persistence, connectivity, energy, conservation, KKT/residual, and lineage witnesses. If a guard is crossed or cannot be certified, emit Unknown and route to the maximal I13.4b/I13.4c topology-event lane rather than borrowing its conclusion.

## Success Criteria
A content-addressed core receipt identifies the exact admitted topology stratum and independently reproduces claimed objective/constraint values, fixed-topology gradients, conservation balances, and optimizer progress within declared tolerances. The receipt proves that no admitted iterate changed the declared cohomology/topology invariants and that the core dependency closure contains I13.3c but not I13.3d or I13.3e. Near-event, ambiguous, or checker-disagreeing cases deterministically escalate to the maximal lane with a minimal witness. The result is consumable by I13.G2 and I13.G3 without weakening the maximal topology-event theorem program.

## Test Plan
Use pinned fixed-topology motor and winding fixtures; analytic and independent finite-difference/complex-step gradient checks where admissible; KKT and trust-region/line-search replay; unit, frame, basis, mesh, refinement, and representation metamorphics; cohomology and persistence invariance checks; deliberately near-event level-set/density sequences; missed-event and false-event mutations; remesh or harmonic-basis corruption; deterministic checkpoint/resume; cancellation and resource exhaustion; and independent G2/G3 reproduction with raw artifacts. Require the no-event guard to fail closed on every injected topology crossing.

## Considerations
This receipt does not claim a global optimum, topology-changing differentiability, generalized derivatives across events, conservative remesh/restart equivalence, winding manufacturability, or real-machine improvement. Those stronger claims remain first-class maximal work in I13.3d/I13.3e and I13.4b/I13.4c. Keeping the boundary explicit increases ambition by allowing both theorem programs to advance without letting the maximal hypothesis contaminate the independently useful core.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Carry typed units and quantity kinds, frames and orientations, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence polarity. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, reductions, and ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; failed or refuted candidates remain retained evidence. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run applicable DSR/Gauntlet lanes, record exact commands, artifacts, machine fingerprints, costs, assumptions, and no-claim boundaries, and require independent checker ownership.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [M]. Keep this default-off until the fixed-topology receipt beats the declared boring baseline on a preregistered deck, its no-event guard survives adversarial mutation, and an independent reproduction pack is adjudicated. Promotion of this core does not promote the topology-event branch; a refutation or Unknown result remains valuable versioned knowledge.

title: I13.7b Route manufacturable connected coils that realize an integer winding class
description:
## Background
An admissible integer winding class still may lack a fabricable conductor realization. Real machines may intentionally contain multiple galvanically isolated phase coils, declared series/parallel branches, splices, taps, and terminal groups; demanding one globally connected network could short phases. End turns, slot fill, clearance, insulation, layer changes, current density, and assembly order constrain each declared electrical component.

## Technical Approach
Take an explicit winding/netlist specification containing phase, branch, parallel-path, splice/tap, terminal-incidence, and galvanic-isolation identities. Route oriented conductor centerlines, finite cross-section sweeps, bundles, layers, vias/crossovers, end turns, and terminal leads inside declared manufacturing regions. Enforce that connected components and semantic joins exactly realize the netlist; geometry contact alone never creates a splice. Enforce bend radius, conductor/insulation thickness, creepage/clearance, slot fill/packing, forbidden inter-phase contact, current-density/thermal proxy, assembly access, and process constraints. Allow topology-preserving repair with an explicit chain map to the integer winding class. Compare filament and finite-cross-section/distributed fields using declared integral/energy/QoI norms on stated domains, excluding or analytically regularizing filament self-singularities.

## Success Criteria
Return a conductor graph whose connected components and terminal-incidence matrix exactly match the declared phases, branches, parallel paths, splices, taps, and isolation specification. Each swept conductor/insulation geometry passes declared predicates; its integral periods equal the input class; and filament versus distributed linkage/field QoIs agree in named norms and comparison domains. A disconnected required branch, unintended short, geometric touch without a joint, missing splice, colliding insulation, or pointwise centerline self-field comparison fails.

## Test Plan
Single coil, three isolated phases, series/parallel paths, center tap, declared weld/splice, insulated crossover, geometric touch without electrical joint, multilayer crossover, tight bend/fill, terminal swap, end-turn congestion, insulation growth, conductor-size change, route homotopy, filament/distributed norm comparison away from self singularity, mesh refinement, cancellation, and deterministic rerouting.

## Considerations
Manufacturability is process-specific. Name winding/insertion method, joint technology, tolerances, materials, and inspection predicates. Thermal life and dielectric breakdown are downstream evidence. No global routing optimum is promised, and electrical connectivity comes from semantic joint artifacts validated against geometry—not intersections alone.

## Execution and evidence
Carry units, frames, conductor/net/phase/terminal/joint identities, topology-class hash, material/process versions, tolerances, comparison norm/domain, budgets, provenance, deterministic seeds/ties, checkpoint/resume, and bounded cancellation. title: I14 EPIC — EMC cable/harness, PEEC, transmission-line, and full-wave escalation ladder
description:
## Background
Motors, converters, sensors, and controllers fail through conducted and radiated coupling that magnetostatic machine models cannot see. Engineers need a fidelity ladder from harness networks through PEEC to shield/aperture/full-wave analysis with shared sources and evidence.

## Technical Approach
Model cable/harness topology, bundles, shields, connectors, grounds, common/differential modes, transmission lines, and frequency-dependent materials; add PEEC extraction with passivity/causality checks; escalate selected regions to FEM/BEM/FMM full wave. Couple converter switching and moving-machine sources to EMC metrics and the assurance program.

## Success Criteria
Canonical crosstalk, loop inductance, shielding, aperture, cable-bundle, and motor-drive emission/immunity decks meet stated envelopes; the router chooses or refuses fidelity based on wavelength, geometry, material dispersion, and QoI.

## Test Plan
Analytic line/circuit cases, passivity and positive-realness, reciprocity where valid, mesh/frequency convergence, shielding-effectiveness corpora, source decomposition, uncertainty sweeps, and cross-rung agreement.

## Considerations
A PEEC or transmission-line result outside its electrical-size/material assumptions must escalate or refuse. Passing simulation is not regulatory compliance.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [F]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

title: I14.2a Assemble typed frequency- and temperature-dependent RLGC operators
description:
## Background
A multiconductor transmission-line model is meaningful only relative to ordered conductors, an explicit reference/return topology, port orientation, and a quasi-TEM validity region. I14.2 must not duplicate electrostatic, conduction, PEEC, or MQS field extractors; it assembles their admitted receipts and measured RLGC data into one typed operator.

## Technical Approach
Define MtlOperator with dimensioned per-unit-length RLGC matrices, conductor/reference identities, terminal orientation, geometry/material lineage, frequency/temperature domains, evidence class, reciprocity class, covariance or certified bounds, and QuasiTemValidityReceipt. Accept versioned samples from I03 capacitance/conductance extraction, I14.3a PEEC extraction, moving-conductor/MQS internal-impedance adapters, or admitted measurements. Validate and crosswalk those sources without recomputing their fields. Preserve potential-coefficient versus capacitance quotient semantics, skin/proximity provenance, phasor/sign convention, charge/current continuity, and the map to HarnessGraph/PortSchema. Refuse missing references, inconsistent gauges/quotients, incompatible terminals, invalid material states, ambiguous units, or an extraction claim lacking its own receipt.

## Success Criteria
Coax/two-wire admitted datasets meet analytic envelopes; matrix dimensions, realness/conjugate symmetry, reciprocity obligations, and positive-semidefinite loss preconditions are checked for their declared class; temperature/frequency interpolation preserves evidence and bounds; conductor permutations and reference changes have explicit transforms. The artifact distinguishes computed, measured, and fitted evidence and never upgrades one class to another.

## Test Plan
Use analytic and admitted coax/pair/bundle receipts, conductor/reference changes, potential-coefficient/capacitance quotient cases, lossy/anisotropic materials, temperature sweeps, measurement covariance, stale extraction versions, non-PSD R/G, unit and gauge mismatches, cancellation, and replay.

## Considerations
RLGC are matrix-valued causal operators. Geometry-derived entries exist only when the relevant field-extraction receipt is present; otherwise the lane may use admitted measurements or return Unknown. Full-wave and connector validity are separate.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit content-addressed MtlOperator and QuasiTemValidityReceipt artifacts with source evidence class, units, conventions, validity/error budgets, versions, and no-claim boundaries.

## Deterministic execution floor
Assign semantic logical work identities to every frequency, mode, parameter point, branch, profile slice, matrix block, target artifact, and reduction tile rather than deriving identity from worker order. Deterministic mode uses stable traversal, fixed-shape reductions, deterministic pivot/tie/cluster/branch rules, counter-based RNG where relevant, and versioned serialization. Test thread, shard, schedule, resume and same-ISA replay matrices; any permitted fast-mode or cross-ISA divergence is classified, bounded and ledgered rather than silently accepted.

title: I14.2b Fit passive causal RLGC models and construct modal/common-differential decompositions
description:
## Background
Raw frequency samples are not a safe transient model. Naive interpolation or eigenvector tracking can create noncausal gain, negative dissipation, broken real-valued time response, incorrect DC/high-frequency behavior, mode swaps, and arbitrary phase flips near degeneracy.

## Technical Approach
Fit admitted MtlOperator samples with stable positive-real rational/state-space models when that family can honestly represent the band. Enforce realness and conjugate symmetry, DC and high-frequency asymptotics, passivity, causality, residual/error bounds, and reciprocity only for reciprocal classes. Admit diffusive, fractional, convolutional, or tabulated causal operators when rational approximation would require an unjustified order or distort skin-effect asymptotics. Build power-normalized modal and application-declared common/differential coordinates with deterministic subspace tracking at clustered modes; do not pretend a general bundle has a universal canonical common/differential basis. Carry conditioning, truncation, interpolation, repair perturbation, and inverse maps as receipts.

## Success Criteria
Admitted models are stable, causal, passive, real-valued in time, and asymptotically consistent over the declared region; repeated-mode invariant subspaces remain continuous even when individual modes are not identifiable; transform/recompose preserves terminal voltage/current/charge/power within directed bounds. Noncausal, nonpassive, or unrepresentable data refuses or uses a stronger admitted operator class.

## Test Plan
Exercise exact rational, diffusive skin-effect, delayed/lossy, sparse/noisy, DC-singular, and high-frequency fixtures; repeated/crossing modes; noncanonical bundle groupings; passivity/causality/realness mutations; unstable poles; temperature interpolation; and independent positive-real checks.

## Considerations
Modal labels are coordinate choices. A small fit residual is not a causality or asymptotic proof, and rational order must not hide unsupported physics.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Produce PassiveMtlFitReceipt with raw identity, operator family/order, asymptotic and realness witnesses, residual/perturbation bounds, passivity/causality evidence, subspace identities, and refusals.

## Cancellation, drain, and resumability floor
Long loops poll the explicit asupersync Cx at bounded semantic chunks and record the achieved latency bound. Cancellation is request → drain owned/speculative work → finalize a non-Pass receipt; it cannot drop tasks, arenas, temporary artifacts, optimizer state, partial uncertainty samples, or checker branches. Save versioned resumable state where recomputation is material, verify checkpoint compatibility before resume/fork, and test cancellation before, during and after each expensive phase plus fault/cancel races. Partial results remain useful only with explicit incompleteness and no-claim effect.

title: I14.2c Propagate time/frequency waves through terminations, connectors, and circuits
description:
## Background
The MTL lane must predict propagation, reflection, attenuation, crosstalk, and terminal interaction with sources, loads, connectors, and descriptor circuits without inventing energy or silently adopting a switching-device dependency.

## Technical Approach
Implement deterministic frequency-domain and transient telegrapher solvers over the admitted passive causal operator. Support piecewise-uniform sections, oriented terminations, connector/discontinuity models within their validity, application-declared modal coordinates, admitted source waveforms, and descriptor-MNA coupling. Use power-consistent variables and explicit reference conductors; account exactly once for conductor and dielectric loss. Provide stable convolution/state-space realization, multirate boundaries, timestep/error controls, checkpoint/resume, and bounded cancellation drain. Keep switching-device model integration an optional I14.7/source adapter rather than a baseline blocker. Route algebraic-loop, bandwidth, discontinuity, higher-mode, or validity failures to PEEC/full wave or Unknown.

## Success Criteria
Matched/open/short/mismatched analytic lines reproduce delays and reflection coefficients; bundles meet crosstalk envelopes; time/frequency paths agree within stated bounds; terminal power equals stored, transmitted, and dissipated power. Circuit coupling preserves orientation and DAE semantics, and unsupported source/connector spectra escalate.

## Test Plan
Run matched/reflected pulses, dispersive lines, coupled bundles, mode conversion, connector steps, admitted sources, circuit loads, reference mistakes, double-counted loss, partial cancellation, restart, and replay. Test optional switching adapters separately.

## Considerations
A compact connector or source adapter is not a full three-dimensional field/device solution. Radiation, unsupported modes, and out-of-band material behavior require a higher rung.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit traces, balance ledgers, solver/error receipts, route decisions, and exact links to operator, circuit, source, harness, and material versions.
