title: I14.2d Independently verify MTL validity, passivity, propagation, and upward routing
description:
## Background
The production extractor, fitter, and propagator share enough conventions that a common sign, reference, passivity, or loss-ownership defect can survive ordinary end-to-end tests. Promotion therefore requires an independently implemented terminal receipt that also proves the router refuses invalid MTL regimes.

## Technical Approach
Build a checker that reconstructs conductor/reference topology, dimensions, positive-real/passivity conditions, modal-subspace invariants, analytic propagation cases, and port-power balances without calling production fit or propagation code. Re-run retained raw frequency samples and transient fixtures, compare time/frequency predictions, perturb conventions and material domains, and evaluate the quasi-TEM and discontinuity escalation predicates. Bind every result to exact artifacts, thresholds, seeds, code versions, and machine fingerprints. Produce an MtlCapabilityReceipt with separate Proven, EmpiricallySupported, Unknown, Refuted, and Invalid states.

## Success Criteria
The checker reproduces admitted coax, pair, and bundle results; kills non-PSD, noncausal, mode-swap, wrong-reference, sign, loss-double-count, and unsafe-extrapolation mutations; verifies deterministic replay and cancellation finalization; and demonstrates that higher-mode or strongly 3-D cases route upward. Any checker disagreement blocks promotion and localizes the smallest artifact or convention boundary.

## Test Plan
Use analytic fixtures and blind held-outs; repeated-mode and conductor-permutation metamorphics; nonpassive and unstable fit mutations; connector and source-spectrum regime violations; power-balance sign flips; corrupted or stale receipts; feature-off fallback; G4 fault/cancellation storms; and G5 replay across thread counts.

## Considerations
This receipt certifies the declared MTL capability region, not universal cable accuracy or regulatory EMC compliance. Independent code and data ownership are required.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. This is the terminal I14.2 scientific artifact consumed by grounding, source/victim, multirung-routing, and I14 gate campaigns. Preserve all counterexamples and no-claim boundaries.

title: I14.3 Build PEEC extraction, circuit stamping, passivity, and MOR receipts
description:
## Background
PEEC can bridge conductors and circuits through partial inductance and coefficients of potential, but truncation, gauge/reference choices, skin/proximity approximations, and model reduction can create active or noncausal models.

## Technical Approach
Implement quasi-static then admitted retarded PEEC extraction, partial inductance and potential coefficients, skin/proximity submodels, circuit stamping, public solve interfaces, and structure-preserving reduction. Emit gauge/reference, discretization, retardation, power, passivity, and MOR receipts.

## Success Criteria
Loop/plate/coax inductance-capacitance oracles converge; gauge/reference changes preserve ports; field/circuit power closes; reduced models remain passive/causal or refuse; electrically large cases escalate.

## Test Plan
Analytic geometries, mesh refinement, skin/proximity limits, gauge/reference, truncation active-model falsifier, MOR passivity, retarded crossover, and cancellation.

## Considerations
PEEC accuracy and cost depend on discretization and retardation; never use a passive stamp as proof of geometric accuracy.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Reuse canonical geometry, fields, materials, ports, quantities, evidence, and semantic identities. Carry units, frames/orientations, seeds, versions, validity/error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, cancellation with bounded drain, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts and machine fingerprints, and state scientific, manufacturing, standards, and performance no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion

Keep the frontier or moonshot off by default until a declared boring baseline, primary-reference status, monitored assumptions, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack exist. Preserve refutations and negative results.

title: I14.3a Extract gauge-explicit quasi-static and admitted retarded PEEC operators
description:
## Background
PEEC connects conductor/dielectric geometry to circuit variables through partial inductance, coefficients of potential, resistance, and—when admitted—retardation. The potential-coefficient matrix P and Maxwell capacitance matrix C are not interchangeable: inversion or pseudoinversion is defined only on a declared reference/gauge quotient. Symmetry and positive-semidefinite energy properties require reciprocal quasistatic media. Retarded PEEC must preserve charge continuity and Lorenz-gauge coupling across scalar and vector delayed terms.

## Technical Approach
Define canonical volume/surface/filament unknowns, incidence/continuity maps, conductor components, terminal/reference quotient, and gauge. Extract partial inductance, potential coefficient P, quotient capacitance C where invertible/pseudoinvertible under explicit nullspace constraints, resistance, and admitted skin/proximity operators. State reciprocity, symmetry, PSD/energy, dispersion, and anisotropy hypotheses separately. Start electro-/magneto-quasistatic. For retarded paths, co-discretize scalar and vector potentials/delays with discrete continuity-equation and Lorenz-gauge consistency, causal kernels, delay/quadrature error, and wavelength admission. Carry singular self terms, geometry/discretization error, nullspaces, and escalation to full wave.

## Success Criteria
Loop, plate, coax, and busbar oracles converge; P-to-C conversion is performed only on the declared quotient and preserves terminal observables; reciprocal quasistatic fixtures meet stated symmetry/PSD laws while nonreciprocal/dispersive cases use their correct weaker contract; delayed scalar/vector terms satisfy continuity/gauge residuals; electrically large or rank-uncertain cases escalate/refuse; and no passivity claim for assembled/reduced circuits is inferred from extraction alone.

## Test Plan
Analytic inductance/capacitance; floating/disconnected conductors; reference and quotient changes; P inversion/pseudoinversion nullspace; reciprocal and nonreciprocal media; mesh/self-term refinement; skin/proximity limits; retarded continuity and Lorenz-gauge mutations; scalar-only/vector-only delay corruption; wavelength crossover; reciprocity/sign corruption; cancellation and replay.

## Considerations
Compression/FMM must preserve operator and continuity/gauge error. Retarded PEEC has stricter causality semantics than static partial elements. Energy symmetry claims do not apply universally to nonreciprocal or active media. Radiation is an exterior flux phenomenon handled in the power ledger, not a local material loss coefficient.

## Execution and evidence
Use safe Rust, typed SI quantities, stable geometry/terminal IDs, explicit quotient/gauge/material/media class, deterministic quadrature/reductions, bounded cancellation, and content-addressed receipts. Retain analytic oracles, G0 laws, G1 convergence, G2 benchmarks, retarded continuity/gauge falsifiers, and DSR artifacts. Ambition class [F].

title: I14.3b Stamp PEEC models with discrete power, positive-real, and causal semantics
description:
## Background
Extracted partial elements become useful only when stamped into MNA without losing charge/current conservation, reference invariance, field-to-circuit power, passivity, or causal delay semantics. Numerical identity can be exact algebraically while quadrature, solve, extraction, and model discrepancy remain bounded rather than zero. Radiation is boundary/Poynting outflow, not interchangeable with local dissipative loss. Sampled j-omega positivity is not a positive-real theorem in the analytic half-plane.

## Technical Approach
Map PEEC incidence, charge, flux, resistance, controlled sources, and delays into the canonical circuit descriptor with explicit reference quotient and initial/algebraic state. Define port effort/flow orientation and an exact algebraic discrete power identity, then attach bounded quadrature, extraction, solve, retardation, and model-discrepancy terms. Separate conductor/dielectric dissipation, stored energy, source work, and radiation/exterior Poynting flux to avoid double counting. For admitted rational or delay systems, implement fail-closed passivity as a positive-real/analytic right-half-plane or supply-rate claim with poles, residues/delay class, and descriptor well-posedness; sampled frequency checks are diagnostics only. Structure-preserving repair must report perturbation.

## Success Criteria
Algebraic charge/power identities close exactly in their discrete arithmetic while total physical closure respects named error bounds; port observables are reference/coordinate invariant; passive fixtures receive the exact positive-real/supply theorem they satisfy; active, unstable, noncausal, or truncated fixtures are detected; radiation appears as boundary flux; delayed descriptors have explicit history/initial consistency; and sampled positivity alone never verifies passivity.

## Test Plan
RLC/transformer limits, coax/loop/plate stamps, floating conductors, reference quotient, skin/dielectric loss ownership, radiation-flux fixture, external circuits, rational and delayed elements, unstable/active pocket between samples, non-passive truncation, descriptor inconsistency, missing/double-counted loss, power-error accounting, cancellation/resume, and sign mutations.

## Considerations
Positive-realness requires an analytic-domain theorem for the admitted model class. Active devices use supply-rate/dissipativity semantics. A passive stamp does not validate extraction fidelity. Exact algebraic identity does not erase numerical/model uncertainty.

## Execution and evidence
Bind stamp to extraction hash, quotient/gauge, port orientation, media/model class, units, validity domain, solver budget, algebraic identity, bounded discrepancy ledger, analytic passivity witness, and exterior flux. Provide G0/G2/G3/G4 evidence, independent dense checks, and DSR artifacts. Ambition class [F].

## Deterministic execution floor
Assign semantic logical work identities to every frequency, mode, parameter point, branch, profile slice, matrix block, target artifact, and reduction tile rather than deriving identity from worker order. title: I14.3c Reduce and independently adjudicate PEEC models without losing structure
description:
## Background
PEEC systems are dense and often too large for repeated coupled solves. Model-order reduction can erase nullspaces, destabilize descriptor modes, break reciprocity/passivity, or fit sampled ports while failing outside the training band. An independent terminal checker must own promotion.

## Technical Approach
Implement structure-preserving projection/interpolation for admitted descriptor systems, with port/tangent subspaces, delay treatment, reciprocity and passivity constraints, error indicators, and frequency/time validity domains. Independently recompute selected full-order responses and energy/power identities using a dense small-case path or separate oracle. Run passivity/causality adjudication over adaptive frequency regions, retain counterexample frequencies/states, and escalate rather than repair beyond declared perturbation budgets.

## Success Criteria
Reduced models preserve declared algebraic constraints, ports, reciprocity, passivity/causality status, and power semantics; meet predeclared transfer/time-domain error bands on training and held-out probes; expose p50/p95/p99 cost and compression; and return Refuted/Unknown when an active pocket or descriptor mismatch is found. Canonical models reproduce full-order baselines.

## Test Plan
RLC/transformer and PEEC fixtures; clustered poles; wideband skin effect; floating/gauge modes; delayed kernels; out-of-band adversary; near-passive perturbation; port/reference changes; reduction-rank sweep; proof-artifact corruption; cancellation, resume, and independent replay.

## Considerations
Finite frequency sampling cannot by itself certify global passivity or causality. Report the exact theorem or sampled domain. Reduction error and extraction error remain separate ledger terms, and good port fits do not prove internal-field accuracy.

## Execution and evidence
Retain full/reduced hashes, projection maps, validity region, power/passivity witnesses, held-out corpus, independent implementation path, deterministic budgets, machine fingerprint, DSR logs, and minimal falsifiers. Meet G1/G2/G3/G4/G5 where applicable. This terminal artifact is consumed by I14.G and downstream coupling/optimization.

title: I14.8a Generate exact-discrete adjoints within admitted EMC model regimes
description:
## Background
EMC design variables affect MTL, PEEC, circuit, and full-wave solves through coupled geometry, materials, ports, solvers, and fidelity routing. Complex electromagnetic states usually feed real QoIs containing conjugation, norms, absolute values, power, and nonholomorphic material laws, so naive complex-step checks can be invalid. Reverse differentiation of the exact recorded iteration trace and an implicit adjoint of a converged discrete residual are also distinct when stopping, preconditioning, or active branches depend on tolerances.

## Technical Approach
Define independently admissible per-rung computational graphs for MTL, PEEC, circuit, and full-wave operators; lower rungs do not wait for every higher rung. For complex fields, freeze real-variable or Wirtinger derivatives, conjugate-transpose/inner-product convention, and real scalar objective semantics. Implement two typed adjoint lanes where valid: TraceAdjoint for the exact recorded discrete iteration/control-flow trace, and ImplicitResidualAdjoint for an admitted converged residual with differentiability/invertibility and inexact-solve terms. Generate route, shield, bond, termination, filter, ground, aperture, material, and smooth-geometry derivatives. Record primal/adjoint residuals, tolerances, active/router branches, units/scales, loss convention, and event identity. Emit NoGradient/SetValued/Unknown at topology, remesh, active-set, rung, or nonsmooth switches absent a proved generalized derivative.

## Success Criteria
Tangent-adjoint duality and Taylor remainder tests pass at multiple scales by default; finite-difference/dual independent checks agree within conditioning/error budgets. Complex-step is used only when the entire declared path and QoI are proved holomorphic; otherwise it is forbidden. Trace and implicit adjoints agree only under their stated convergence/branch hypotheses and remain separately identified. Discontinuities are localized with one-sided/set-valued evidence. Any cost claim independent of parameter count is scoped to a fixed number of scalar objectives and fixed state/operator regime.

## Test Plan
MTL route spacing, PEEC placement, shield impedance, bond/filter values, aperture geometry, grounding, multiport real power/norm QoIs, holomorphic synthetic complex path, conjugated/nonholomorphic QoI where complex-step must refuse, trace-vs-implicit tolerance sweep, inexact solves, preconditioner/state-dependent stopping, remesh/router/topology switches, corrupt checkpoints, cancellation, and unit-rescaling.

## Considerations
An exact discrete adjoint is exact only for its typed recorded algorithm or residual theorem. Shape derivatives require chart/material-transport conventions. Model discrepancy is separate. Fixed-objective adjoint cost does not imply parameter-independent end-to-end optimization cost.

## Execution and evidence
Carry complex derivative convention, objective count, rung/regime, operator/state hashes, tolerances, branch identities, units, budgets, deterministic reductions, cancellation, checkpoints, provenance, tangent/Taylor/independent checks, G0/G2/G3/G4 evidence, costs, and DSR artifacts. title: I14.8b Model EMC uncertainty, discrepancy, and anytime-valid reliability objectives
description:
## Background
Nominally effective mitigation can fail under source spectra, harness placement, contact/bond state, material dispersion, manufacturing tolerances, measurement error, and fidelity-model discrepancy. These uncertainties have different semantics and dependence; collapsing them into independent Gaussian noise creates unearned reliability claims. Adaptive optimization also invalidates fixed-sample confidence unless optional stopping is handled.

## Technical Approach
Define a provenance-complete uncertainty model separating aleatory variability, epistemic intervals/sets, calibration uncertainty, spatial/process correlation, model-form discrepancy, and fidelity-router uncertainty. Propagate through admitted rungs using deterministic ensembles, QMC, interval/affine bounds, multifidelity control variates, or rare-event methods selected by declared assumptions. Form robust, distributionally robust, chance, and worst-case objectives with anytime-valid e-process/confidence semantics under adaptive sampling. Escalate when discrepancy or tail effective sample size exceeds budget.

## Success Criteria
Coverage/reliability claims meet preregistered calibration and adversarial optional-stopping tests; correlation and tail assumptions are explicit; held-out source/material/layout cases are not leaked into tuning; model-rung disagreement is a ledgered uncertainty term; and insufficient tail information yields Unknown or a conservative bound rather than a nominal percentile.

## Test Plan
Analytic linear-Gaussian and bounded cases; correlated harness/material variables; heavy tails and multimodality; rare emissions; source-spectrum shift; calibration drift; adaptive stopping; fidelity disagreement; interval-vs-Monte-Carlo containment; seed/thread-count determinism; and deliberately misspecified discrepancy.

## Considerations
No distribution-free finite-sample guarantee exists for every dependent/nonstationary process. State exchangeability, martingale, mixing, support, or ambiguity-set assumptions precisely. Compliance limits and measurement uncertainty must use the actual standard/test context.

## Execution and evidence
Carry units, distribution and dependence version, seeds, sample identities, fidelity route, budgets, provenance, and deterministic reduction. Retain null simulations, coverage curves, e-process stopping traces, discrepancy diagnostics, baseline comparisons, independent reproduction, and DSR evidence. Ambition class [M].

## Cancellation, drain, and resumability floor
Long loops poll the explicit asupersync Cx at bounded semantic chunks and record the achieved latency bound. Cancellation is request → drain owned/speculative work → finalize a non-Pass receipt; it cannot drop tasks, arenas, temporary artifacts, optimizer state, partial uncertainty samples, or checker branches. Save versioned resumable state where recomputation is material, verify checkpoint compatibility before resume/fork, and test cancellation before, during and after each expensive phase plus fault/cancel races. Partial results remain useful only with explicit incompleteness and no-claim effect.

title: PORTFOLIO — material reality, experimental campaigns, and hard-real-time twins
description:
## Background
Simulation becomes engineering only when actual lots, specimens, sensors, calibration chains, uncertainty, and deployment targets can update or falsify the model.

## Technical Approach
Coordinate initiatives 05, 06, 10, and 11. Trace material-lot evidence into constitutive identifiability and coupon design; compile defensible DAQ campaigns; then lower qualified reduced twins to fixed-point, budget-bounded SIL/PIL/HIL targets.

## Success Criteria
A material substitution or new specimen campaign propagates through posterior model parameters and prediction risk to a deterministic real-time twin, with every transformation replayable and every extrapolation visible.

## Test Plan
Synthetic truth recovery, blind splits, tamper and calibration faults, fixed-point equivalence, WCET/latency campaigns, and evidence-monotonicity tests.

## Considerations
HIL timing evidence is target-specific. Calibration is not validation. Lot posteriors must not erase raw observations or hide population-vs-lot uncertainty.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

title: I05.2a Define exact fixed-point operation, cast, rounding, overflow, and evaluator semantics
description:
## Background

Specify panic/refusal behavior and serialization independent of host integer overflow. Build a canonical arbitrary-precision evaluator and compact exhaustive truth tables that generated targets and all abstract transfer functions must reference. Treat wrap as modular dynamics and saturation as a nonlinear state update, never as interchangeable overflow policies.

## Success Criteria
Every operation has one unambiguous, host-independent result or structured fault; the canonical evaluator matches exhaustive hand oracles; equivalent encodings preserve semantics; missing policy cannot fall back favorably; toolchain or schema drift changes semantic identity. Downstream range and code generators cannot instantiate an operation without its semantics witness.

## Test Plan
Enumerate small widths, signed extrema, every rounding tie, shifts beyond width, rescale chains, multiply-accumulate intermediates, saturation/trap/wrap, casts, corrupted schemas, and deterministic serialization. Bit-exact local semantics do not establish reachable ranges or closed-loop stability. They are the foundation those later claims quantify over.

title: I05.4a Prove target-qualified static WCET for admitted binaries and memory regimes
description:
## Background
Worst-case execution time is a property of a particular binary, target microarchitecture, memory map/state model, clock regime, and environmental assumptions—not source code in the abstract. General out-of-order processors with uncontrolled caches and DMA may defeat tight static proof, but exact/simple targets and sharply admitted regions can support bold certified bounds.

## Technical Approach
Define StaticWcetBound with binary hash, target and stepping fingerprint, instruction/timing model, memory map, cache/scratchpad policy, alignment, branch/path model, initial-state set, clock bounds, and proof TCB. Implement exact exhaustive analysis for reduced/simple targets, then abstract interpretation, IPET/path constraints, cache/pipeline analysis, and compositional microkernel lemmas for admitted complex targets. Independently validate decoder, control-flow recovery, infeasible-path claims, and timing tables. Demote automatically when firmware, linker layout, microcode, clock, cache policy, or hardware assumptions drift.

## Success Criteria
For admitted finite/exhaustive fixtures, the bound equals or safely dominates every legal execution; for larger fixtures it carries a checkable derivation and explicit slack. Unknown instructions, indirect control flow, uncertain timing, self-modification, uncontrolled DMA/cache state, or assumption drift yield Unknown/NotApplicable. Every seeded legal bound violation refutes the certificate.

## Test Plan
Hand-solvable basic blocks and loops; exhaustive reduced processors; alignment and cache conflicts; branch predictors; indirect calls; compiler/linker mutations; instruction-table errors; scratchpad versus cache; clock tolerance; DMA interference; binary hash changes; proof corruption; deterministic/cancellation replay.

## Considerations
No universal tight WCET claim is made. Hardware vendor timing claims are inputs, not automatically trusted theorems. Sound loose bounds remain useful if resource and deadline decisions record their pessimism.

## Execution and evidence
Use safe Rust checkers, target-qualified schemas, exact units/clocks, deterministic paths/ties, bounded cancellation, content-addressed binaries/models/proofs, and explicit TCB. Retain G0 checker laws, G2 known targets, G3 layout/clock metamorphics, independent exhaustive or FPGA/trace spot checks, and DSR evidence. Ambition class [M].

title: I05.4b Compose task WCET with scheduler, interrupt, DMA, I/O, and clock deadlines
description:
## Background
Even a sound task WCET does not bound closed-loop response when release jitter, preemption, blocking, interrupts, DMA/bus contention, sensor/actuator conversion, queues, communication, clocks, fault handling, and emergency-stop paths contribute. End-to-end timing needs a compositional theorem over the deployed schedule and hardware envelope.

## Technical Approach
Define CompositionalWcetBound and response-time/jitter receipts over tasks, priorities or time partitions, precedence, locks/resources, interrupt service, DMA/bus arbitration, I/O and network stages, clock drift/synchronization, mode changes, and overload/fault policies. Implement exact/simple schedule analysis first, then fixed-priority/EDF/time-triggered and network-calculus-style modules with explicit assumptions. Compose task bounds and blocking/interference lemmas into end-to-end sensor-to-actuator and fault-to-safe-state deadlines; produce minimal critical chains and admission diagnostics.

## Success Criteria
Canonical schedules reproduce analytic response times; every admitted execution trace lies within release/completion/jitter envelopes; emergency and degraded modes are included; incompatible scheduler/resource assumptions refuse; and a mutated interrupt, DMA, blocking, queue, or clock term causes proof failure. Output separates static proof, configured margin, and observed timing.

## Test Plan
Fixed-priority and EDF task sets, time-triggered schedules, priority inversion, nested interrupts, DMA/bus bursts, sensor/actuator latency, network queues, clock drift, deadline miss, overload/fault modes, multicore interference envelope, compositional associativity, cancellation, and proof corruption.

## Considerations
Multicore shared-resource interference may require conservative envelopes or target-specific isolation. A scheduler theorem says nothing about unmodeled firmware or vendor driver behavior; those paths must be in the admitted boundary or out of the proof.

## Execution and evidence
Bind exact deployment configuration, task/binary hashes, timing-model versions, clocks, budgets, critical-chain witnesses, provenance, and deterministic replay. Retain analytic oracle cases, adversarial schedules, independent checker results, G2/G3/G4 evidence, and DSR artifacts. Ambition class [M].

title: I05.4c Run pinned-target measured-tail and adversarial latency campaigns
description:
## Background
Measurement cannot prove a worst case, but pinned-target tail campaigns are essential for finding missing paths, invalid hardware assumptions, pathological interference, and regressions. This bead independently produces empirical evidence; it does not wait for or reconcile static/compositional proofs, and it never calls an observed percentile or maximum WCET.

## Technical Approach
Run preregistered campaigns on exact binary/target/configuration identities with synchronized hardware timestamps, trace/path coverage, warm/cold initial states, cache/alignment variants, interrupt/DMA/bus/I/O/network storms, clock/environment monitoring, thermal/frequency regimes, and fault/overload modes. Report p50/p95/p99/p99.9/p99.999 with dependence-aware uncertainty, censoring/loss, effective sample size, instrumentation error, and optional-stopping policy. Use bounded adversarial search to maximize latency and discover rare legal paths while preserving raw immutable traces. Export MeasuredTailReceipt only; I05.4d owns proof reconciliation.

## Success Criteria
Every measurement binds binary, target stepping, linker layout, clock, scheduler, interference, instrumentation, environment, and campaign identity. Percentiles carry uncertainty/effective support and are never upper bounds. Preregistered modes are covered or explicitly missing; rare injected paths are found within the declared campaign; timestamp/trace loss is quantified; and independent replay reproduces summaries. Insufficient support yields Unknown.

## Test Plan
Known synthetic timing distributions, hand-timed kernels, alignment/cache/branch sweeps, interrupts/DMA/bus/network/I/O bursts, clock perturbation, thermal throttling, rare path injection, binary/config drift, optional stopping, dependent samples, censoring/trace loss, instrumentation overhead, cancellation, and deterministic analysis replay.

## Considerations
Absence of a violation is not proof. Extreme percentile estimation requires dependence-aware intervals and no extrapolation beyond evidence. Instrumentation and clock synchronization are explicit errors. ScaleQualification is related benchmark evidence, not a prerequisite for the campaign.

## Execution and evidence
Retain raw traces, clock calibration, target/config fingerprints, preregistration, seeds, path coverage, statistical code/version, uncertainties, adversarial search trace, costs, DSR logs, and reproduction pack. Meet G2/G3/G4/G5. Ambition class [F].

title: I05.4d Independently reconcile static, compositional, and measured timing evidence
description:
## Background
Static task bounds, schedule-level response-time proofs, and empirical tail campaigns have different semantics and failure modes. None should wait for the others to exist, and none may silently upgrade another: measurement cannot prove WCET, while a proof whose target assumptions do not match a trace is irrelevant. A separate terminal adjudicator must align exact identities and attack contradictions.

## Technical Approach
Build an independent safe-Rust reconciler over StaticWcetBound, abstract/concrete TaskWcetBound, CompositionalWcetBound, and MeasuredTailReceipt. Match binary, target stepping, linker layout, clock, cache/scratchpad, scheduler, interrupts, DMA/bus, I/O/network, instrumentation, thermal/frequency, and fault-mode identities. Map traces to static paths and compositional critical chains; verify each legal observation lies below every applicable bound; decompose slack; localize unmatched assumptions; demote stale certificates; and generate adversarial campaign suggestions. Verdict each evidence lane separately and emit a joint Consistent/Refuted/Inapplicable/Unknown assessment.

## Success Criteria
A legal observation above an applicable bound produces a retained high-severity refutation; an observation from a mismatched target/configuration is Inapplicable rather than contradictory; tails retain uncertainty and never become bounds; proof slack and unexplained latency are explicit; seeded identity, clock, path, interference, and instrumentation errors are localized; and independent replay reconstructs the verdict from content-addressed inputs.

## Test Plan
Hand-solvable bound/trace fixtures, exact and loose bounds, rare path above a false bound, target/binary/layout drift, scheduler and interrupt mismatch, DMA and I/O omission, clock/instrumentation uncertainty, thermal throttling, censored/optional-stopped tails, proof corruption, missing path attribution, cancellation storms, and deterministic replay.

## Considerations
Consistency does not establish completeness of either proof or campaign. Observed maxima and percentiles are lower evidence about the worst case, never upper bounds. Reconciliation must preserve contradictory artifacts and cannot repair them by silently widening tolerances.

## Execution and evidence
Retain all input hashes, identity crosswalk, path/critical-chain links, mismatch and slack witnesses, statistical uncertainty, target fingerprint, TCB, deterministic budgets, provenance, DSR logs, falsifiers, and reproduction pack. Meet G0/G2/G3/G4/G5 as applicable. This is the terminal I05.4 artifact.

Maximal: end-to-end floating-to-target closed-loop refinement with compositional deadlines, measurement reconciliation, hardware-specific WCET arguments, robust fault injection, and theorem-qualified deployment equivalence. Represent Solid/Frontier/Moonshot and Failed/Refuted/Unknown/no-claim states explicitly.

## Success Criteria
An unfamiliar agent can run all later campaigns from this artifact without the plan. Freeze is immutable; amendments fork lineage and invalidate affected descendants. Scope, metrics, fixtures, versions, and oracles cannot change silently.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/unit/identity/lattice laws; G3 assumption deletion, holdout swap, tolerance relaxation, and correlated-oracle mutations; G4 resumable freeze; G5 canonical replay.

Preregistration is not proof and never blocks stronger theorem discovery through versioned amendments.

title: I06.4d Build nontransitive contextual substitution hypergraphs and evidence-request frontiers
description:
## Background

This graph ends at query-level compatibility and evidence acquisition. I06.5a owns artifact/claim invalidation; I06.5b owns QoI impact propagation.

Identifiability and optimal design need derivatives of the actual time/space/constitutive discretization, including state updates, geometry, load path, sensors, and nuisance parameters.

## Technical Approach
Compose consistent constitutive tangents, checkpoints, state/geometry/load/environment/sensor derivatives, and discrete adjoints for admitted coupon simulations. Monitor return-map failure, active-set/path bifurcation, event/nonsmooth boundaries, and refinement error; route unsupported cases to derivative-free methods.

## Success Criteria
Tangent/adjoint identities close; finite-difference/dual checks converge across mesh/time refinement; every observation/parameter derivative has provenance; failed regularity demotes rather than produces a gradient.

## Test Plan
Elastic, viscoelastic, plastic, dielectric/magnetic and frictional microcases; path reversal; active-set changes; mesh/time refinement; and omitted-state derivative mutation.

## Considerations
An adjoint consistent with a wrong constitutive law is still wrong physics.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Carry typed units, frames, clocks, specimen/sensor/machine identities, seeds, versions, validity/error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, evidence state, asupersync cancellation/drain, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts, and state scientific, laboratory, privacy, safety, and performance no-claim boundaries.

Keep the candidate default-off until a named baseline, primary-reference status, monitored assumptions, activation and kill criteria, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack exist. description:
## Background
I10.3 Discover structural identifiability, symmetries, gauges, and identifiable combinations contains multiple theorem, algorithm, and evidence objects that deserve separate ownership. This child owns: Formulate exact/rational/polynomial or scoped analytic law-observation systems, eliminate states/nuisance variables, compute structural rank and identifiable ideals/combinations under declared genericity, experiment inputs, initial conditions, and observation windows.

## Technical Approach
Formulate exact/rational/polynomial or scoped analytic law-observation systems, eliminate states/nuisance variables, compute structural rank and identifiable ideals/combinations under declared genericity, experiment inputs, initial conditions, and observation windows. Freeze exact objects, hypotheses, quantifiers, units, coefficient/metric/frame/gauge conventions, admissible domains, errors and uncertainty, deterministic/cancellation semantics, versions, capabilities, and provenance. Emit theorem cards or executable intermediate witnesses with explicit Refuted/Unknown/no-claim states.

## Success Criteria
The scoped output is independently reviewable and consumable. All claimed identities, derivatives, bounds, invariances, or statistical guarantees name their norm/domain and have an orthogonal falsifier/checker path. It composes through typed contracts and cannot silently inherit sibling claims.

## Test Plan
Use textbook identifiable/nonidentifiable models, exact symbolic/numeric rank, singular parameter cells, input changes, hidden states, and generic-versus-specific counterexamples. Include G0 algebra/schema/unit laws, G1/G2 analytic/manufactured/canonical cases, G3 invariance and assumption-deletion metamorphics, G4 cancellation/fault/resource tests where executable, and G5 deterministic replay with retained counterexamples.

## Considerations
Generic structural identifiability does not guarantee practical identifiability or apply at singular parameter values. Numerical or empirical regularity is not theorem proof, and a theorem does not validate an incorrect physical adapter.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [M]. Content-address statements and evidence, ledger TCB/checker versions, use safe Rust and explicit scopes, and require independent adjudication.

## Scientific verification obligations — structural identifiability quantifiers
Every result states whether it is local or global, generic or pointwise, over a real-positive physical domain or an algebraic closure, and which inputs, initial conditions, observation schedule and nuisance parameters are quantified. Unit/property tests include complex-generic versus real-constrained counterexamples, gauge/symmetry actions, singular/boundary parameter points, hidden initial-state symmetries, reparameterizations and exhaustive small polynomial/rational fixtures. A symbolic success over an algebraic closure may not be reported as physical global identifiability without the missing domain proof; failures return the actual indistinguishable family/witness.

title: I10.4 Quantify practical identifiability, confounding, sloppiness, and discrepancy
description:
## Background
A structurally identifiable model may still be practically uninformative under noise, sampling, nuisance variables, prior choice, model discrepancy, and limited excitation.

## Technical Approach
Compute design-conditioned sensitivity/Fisher spectra, profile likelihoods, posterior geometry/multimodality, sloppiness, observability, nuisance/discrepancy confounding, prior sensitivity, posterior-predictive checks, and decision-relevant identifiable combinations. Preserve rival noise/discrepancy models.

## Success Criteria

title: I11.3a Define campaign hazards, authority, residual energy, envelopes, and minimum-risk states
description:
## Background
Safe experimental control begins before code generation: the campaign must name hazards, stored/residual energy, operating envelopes, detection and actuation paths, operator authority, independent emergency authority, and minimum-risk states. Waiting on a flagship-level assurance program would invert the architecture.

## Technical Approach
Compile ContextOfUse and campaign intent into a narrow SafetyProtocolContract covering electrical capacitor/inductor energy, rotating inertia, elastic energy, pressure/vacuum, thermal and chemical hazards, moving hardware, environmental exposure, and data-integrity hazards. Define typed limits, warning/trip margins, detection-to-compute-to-communication-to-actuator latency budgets, sensor/actuator fault assumptions, latching/reset permissives, operator roles, hardware-enforced interlocks, common-cause independence assumptions, residual-energy verification, and minimum-risk/de-energized states. Link broader hazard/assurance artifacts when available without making them a circular prerequisite.

## Success Criteria
Every excitation and failure mode maps to named hazards and bounded authority; safe/minimum-risk states include residual energy and verification criteria; software cannot override independent emergency authority; missing containment or independence is explicit Uncontained/Unknown; reset and restart require positive permissives.

## Test Plan
Model capacitor discharge, spinning rotor, pressure/thermal cooldown, stuck sensors/actuators, common-cause loss, delayed detection, emergency stop, operator conflict, brownout, unsafe reset, and missing hardware enforcement.

## Considerations
This contract does not certify a stand or replace trained operators, hardware review, or the wider safety program. It supplies the prerequisite that those programs and runtimes refine.

title: I11.3b Lower campaigns into timed/superdense protocol automata without inventing event order
description:
## Background
Excitation, settling, triggers, acquisition, holds, and completion occur on multiple clocks with bounded uncertainty and simultaneous events. Forcing a deterministic total order can hide unsafe interleavings even if one replay is repeatable.

## Technical Approach
Lower ExperimentCampaignIR into a timed or superdense SafetyProtocolIR with excitation, settling, arming, trigger, acquisition, hold, completion, and synchronization modes. Preserve physical/logical clocks, timestamp uncertainty, simultaneity, partial-order constraints, deadlines, nondeterministic environment choices, and deterministic tie rules only where the contract truly orders events. Enumerate or symbolically cover all admissible interleavings; if that set exceeds capability or contains an unsafe ambiguity, fail safe. Bind signals, channels, control-runtime interfaces, and replay identity.

## Success Criteria
All admitted schedules preserve required settling/trigger/acquisition relations; clock uncertainty expands behavior rather than being erased; no unsafe interleaving is hidden by arbitrary serialization; restart identities are stable; unsupported concurrency returns structured refusal. Replays reproduce the same set/receipt, not merely one chosen trace.

## Test Plan
Use simultaneous triggers, skewed clocks, out-of-order packets, skipped settling, deadline ties, nondeterministic device latency, partial orders, reordered independent events, state explosion, cancellation, and deterministic set-level replay.

## Considerations
Determinism means reproducible semantics and exploration, not inventing a physical order where none is justified.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit TimedCampaignProtocolReceipt with automaton, clocks, admissible partial orders/interleavings, deadlines, capability bounds, and refusal states.

title: I11.3c Implement interlock, abort, drain, de-energization, recovery, and restart transactions
description:
## Background

## Technical Approach

Account for detection, compute, communication, and actuator latency; stuck/missing sensors or actuators; brownout and torn persistent state; independent emergency paths; latching and reset permissives; operator handoff; and cancellation/fault finalization. Specify idempotency and checkpoint/commit semantics. Emit hardware-unenforced obligations rather than treating software behavior as containment.

## Success Criteria
Every declared reachable fault reaches a verified minimum-risk state within its bound or an explicit Uncontained result; abort drains and records all owned resources; loss of power or partial writes cannot authorize unsafe restart; independent emergency authority remains available; repeated commands are idempotent.

title: I11.5b Compile measurement equations and transfer/filter/clock/processing graphs
description:
## Background
Raw samples become a QoI through dynamic sensors, clocks, filtering, synchronization, deconvolution, quantization, corrections, censoring, and analysis code. If that graph is implicit, correlations and processing uncertainty disappear.

## Technical Approach
Compile a typed MeasurementEquationGraph from raw channels to intermediate values and QoIs. Represent static and complex dynamic transfer functions, phase/group delay, clock offset/drift/time warp, synchronization, sampling and aliasing, filtering/deconvolution conditioning, quantization, saturation/dropout/censoring metadata, environmental/drift corrections, and analysis transforms. Label measurement, timing, calibration, processing, model-form, and numerical uncertainty ownership separately. Bind every node to code/config/version, units, frames, clocks, and calibration identities.

## Success Criteria
Every processed value has an explicit path to declared raw channels and measurands; shared clocks/references and cross-channel covariance survive; ill-conditioned deconvolution, aliasing, saturation, missing clock models, or ownership ambiguity returns refusal/Unknown; equivalent graph rewrites preserve QoIs and covariance semantics.

## Test Plan
Use static/dynamic sensors, common clocks/references, time warp, asynchronous channels, filters, deconvolution, aliasing, quantization, saturation, dropout/censoring, drift corrections, graph rewrites, ownership double-count mutations, and deterministic replay.

## Considerations
This is a pre-data semantic graph. It does not claim a particular raw stream is authentic or that a propagation approximation is adequate.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit MeasurementEquationGraphReceipt with transforms, transfer/clock models, uncertainty ownership, conditioning, versions, and admission boundaries.

## Scientific verification obligations — measurement chain and clock uncertainty
The raw-byte-to-QoI battery propagates clock/synchronization uncertainty into phase and all affected QoIs; tests aliasing and anti-alias filters, transfer-function inversion/deconvolution regularization and model-form error, calibration expiry, channel/cross-axis/crosstalk covariance, saturation/dropout and unit/frame conventions. Logs bind device/firmware/calibration hashes, clocks, uncertainty terms, filter/regularization choices, raw hashes and abort/drain/finalize events.

Long loops poll the explicit asupersync Cx at bounded semantic chunks and record the achieved latency bound. Cancellation is request → drain owned/speculative work → finalize a non-Pass receipt; it cannot drop tasks, arenas, temporary artifacts, optimizer state, partial uncertainty samples, or checker branches. Save versioned resumable state where recomputation is material, verify checkpoint compatibility before resume/fork, and test cancellation before, during and after each expensive phase plus fault/cancel races. title: I09.2 Implement matrix-free multiple shooting, collocation, and harmonic-balance baselines
description:
## Background
Long transient settling is slow and cannot find unstable cycles. Single shooting may be ill-conditioned, while different periodic representations excel in different regimes.

## Technical Approach
Implement matrix-free single/multiple shooting and orthogonal collocation with phase conditions, block Newton-Krylov, continuation warm starts, deterministic checkpoints, and interior segment defect accounting. Add harmonic balance for smooth admitted periodic systems with aliasing/truncation receipts. Retain long transient as baseline where stable.

## Success Criteria

## Test Plan
Harmonic oscillator, Van der Pol, forced Duffing, constrained rotor, manufactured periodic DAE, unstable orbit, near recurrence, and harmonic aliasing.

## Considerations
Convergence proves a discrete nonlinear solution, not continuous orbit existence.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Unknown orbit or spectrum states are valid outcomes.

## Fresh-eyes scientific correction — isolated periodic-orbit fixtures

Algebraic constraints and infinite descriptor eigenstructure are not Floquet multipliers: they are separate admission and consistency evidence. Treating a raw eigensolver list as the spectrum can duplicate neutral directions, mix algebraic and dynamic structure, or force identities through defective clusters.

## Technical Approach
Import RB.1 fail-closed problem admission, RB.K regular/singular descriptor structure, and RB.7 verified spectral primitives. Construct matrix-free monodromy and transpose actions from variational checkpoints. For admitted regular DAEs, first certify the consistent finite-dimensional tangent bundle/projector and propagate only dynamic perturbations; retain infinite/algebraic/impulse structure in a separate descriptor receipt. For relative cycles use group-reduced return maps; for finite-event hybrid cycles compose validated saltation/reset actions under explicit transversality and event-sequence assumptions. Deflate only declared phase/symmetry neutral subspaces. Compute invariant-subspace/cluster enclosures with residual, separation, conditioning, multiplicity, coverage, and Unknown semantics, transporting cluster rather than eigenvalue identity through collisions.

## Success Criteria
Every spectral artifact binds the validated orbit, section, gauge, consistent tangent projector, separate descriptor-structure receipt, event sequence, monodromy construction, solver residual, verified cluster/count evidence, and enclosure state. Analytic dynamic multipliers lie within bounds; algebraic/infinite modes are never reported as Floquet multipliers; neutral modes are neither lost nor double counted; defective/clustered cases remain set-valued; and missing saltation, inconsistent tangent, wrong reset, or incomplete spectral-region mutations fail.

## Test Plan

## Considerations
This bead certifies the dynamic spectrum of an admitted finite return map, not global attraction. Infinite descriptor structure belongs to RB.K and consistent-initial-data semantics; it must not be folded into a multiplier list. Cluster completeness depends on verified contour/count or equivalent evidence and may be Unknown. Grazing and event-sequence changes require separate local treatment.

## Execution and evidence

title: I09.4b Quantify nonnormal transient and structured Floquet sensitivity
description:
## Background
Asymptotic multiplier modulus can conceal enormous finite-time amplification. For periodic systems, transient behavior depends on starting phase: within-period propagator U(t,s), stroboscopic powers M(s)^n, discrete-time Kreiss behavior, and lifted/harmonic resolvent response are different observables. A monodromy matrix at one section cannot by itself capture all intra-period growth. Energy metrics may be time-periodic or semidefinite after constraints and require a positive-definite quotient.

## Technical Approach
Build separate typed services for: phase-resolved within-period propagator singular growth, maximized or reported over starting phase s; stroboscopic growth of phase-indexed monodromy powers; discrete-time Kreiss/resolvent bounds outside the unit disk; and lifted/harmonic forced response. Work on the certified consistent tangent quotient, with declared phase transport between sections. Accept positive-definite possibly time-periodic energy metrics on that quotient; for semidefinite metrics require an explicit nullspace quotient/coercivity witness or return Unknown. Add spectral projector conditioning, structured perturbation pseudospectra, and robust margins, separating metric, perturbation structure/units, coefficient uncertainty, discretization, and solver error.

## Success Criteria
Normal fixtures reduce to modal predictions; canonical nonnormal cases reveal transient growth; phase shifts transform rather than change physical maxima; within-period and stroboscopic results are not conflated; Kreiss and lifted-response claims use their correct domains; direct propagator/forced probes lie within bounds; and semidefinite/ill-conditioned quotient metrics refuse without a witness. Structured margins respect physical perturbation sets.

## Test Plan
Normal periodic rotations, Jordan/near-Jordan monodromy, time-periodic nonnormal system with phase-dependent intra-period growth, lift-up model, rotor whirl, neutral phase quotient, time-periodic metric, semidefinite constraint metric, section change, stroboscopic powers, discrete Kreiss contour, harmonic resolvent, structured/unstructured perturbations, direct propagation, hidden peak, cancellation, and replay.

## Considerations
Transient bounds are norm/phase/horizon dependent and may be conservative. Linear growth is not nonlinear basin size. Arbitrary matrix-norm perturbations are diagnostics unless mapped to physical units. Keep the four transient/response objects separately typed.

## Execution and evidence
Bind orbit/operator, phase/section transport, tangent quotient, metric/coercivity witness, horizon, perturbation set, contour/frequency domain, budgets, seeds, provenance, direct comparisons, falsifiers, G2/G3/G4/G5 evidence, costs, and DSR logs. Ambition class [M].

title: I09.4d Converge Floquet robustness and bifurcation evidence in an independent terminal receipt
description:
## Background
I09.4 deliberately has two scientifically distinct terminal branches. I09.4b studies phase-resolved within-period amplification, stroboscopic powers, Kreiss-type bounds, lifted/harmonic response, nonnormal sensitivity, and quotient energy metrics. I09.4c classifies local periodic bifurcations with consistent-flow and descriptor-aware spectral semantics. Neither branch should block the other, yet the initiative needs one immutable receipt proving that their conventions, clusters, phase gauges, quotient spaces, and Unknown boundaries agree before promotion. This bead is that convergence layer; it is not a new solver and must not conceal disagreement by choosing the more favorable analysis.

## Technical Approach
Define a versioned `FloquetBifurcationConvergenceReceipt` that consumes the terminal artifacts of I09.4b and I09.4c plus their referenced `ConsistentFlowMonodromy` and `DescriptorInfinityStructure` receipts. Canonicalize orbit identity, section phase, symmetry quotient, tangent-space dimension, cluster identity, metric, units, precision, tolerances, and regime assumptions. Recompute a small independent set of multiplier clusters and phase-resolved propagator QoIs through a checker implementation that does not reuse the production reduction path. Crosswalk multiplier collisions and unit-circle crossings to candidate fold, flip, Neimark-Sacker, symmetry-breaking, grazing, border-collision, or descriptor events only when each theorem card’s transversality, smoothness, isolation, and rank hypotheses are satisfied. Preserve branch-local results when a crosswalk is inapplicable. Emit `Converged`, `Disagrees`, `InsufficientHypotheses`, `RankChange`, `MetricUnavailable`, or `Unknown` per claim; never collapse them to one boolean.

## Success Criteria
The receipt proves identity and convention compatibility across both branches, reports every compared quantity with directed tolerances and provenance, and contains minimal witnesses for each disagreement. It distinguishes finite consistent-tangent Floquet multipliers from descriptor infinity structure; within-period growth from stroboscopic growth; and candidate crossings from theorem-qualified bifurcations. A phase shift, symmetry-equivalent orbit, admissible basis change, or deterministic refinement preserves the canonical verdict. Incompatible tangent dimensions, rank/index changes, semidefinite metrics without an admitted quotient, unresolved clusters, or failed transversality produce localized Unknown/no-claim states. The I09 promotion gate consumes this receipt instead of manually trusting either container or branch.

## Test Plan
G0 property tests cover canonical identity, cluster matching, quotient metrics, dimensional/unit checks, verdict lattice monotonicity, and refusal on malformed receipts. G1/G2 fixtures include smooth fold/flip/Neimark-Sacker manufactured families, a nonnormal but spectrally stable periodic system with large intra-period growth, a constrained DAE with separate finite and infinite structure, and declared hybrid grazing/border-collision cases. G3 metamorphic tests vary section phase, basis, orbit representative, symmetry gauge, time scaling, refinement, and equivalent receipt serialization. G4 cancellation/fault tests prove partial comparisons finalize deterministically without losing completed evidence. G5 replay is bit-stable across thread counts on the same ISA. An independent red-team pack injects swapped pre/post reset states, hidden rank change, cluster aliasing, favorable metric substitution, and false bifurcation labels.

## Considerations
This receipt can validate compatibility and theorem preconditions; it cannot manufacture hyperbolicity, smoothness, transversality, diagonalizability, or a positive-definite energy metric. Local bifurcation evidence does not prove a global branch, basin, or attractor. Nonnormal amplification does not itself imply asymptotic instability. Hybrid and descriptor events require their own typed semantics. Any surviving novel equivalence between phase-resolved robustness and bifurcation invariants may be promoted to a separate theorem card only after the counterexample registry and independent checker agree.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [M]. Implement behind the periodic/Floquet moonshot capability gate in safe Rust with explicit budgets, cancellation polling, deterministic reductions, content-addressed inputs, and a ledgered checker version. Store the complete claim matrix, hypotheses, counterexamples, minimal disagreement witnesses, and reproduction commands. Completion requires independent ownership of the checker path, Gauntlet evidence through G5, and an adjudication note stating exactly which claims are promoted, remain candidate, or stay Unknown.

title: I09.4e Independently reproduce baseline numerical Floquet residuals or Unknown
description:
## Background
Multiple shooting, collocation, and harmonic balance fail in different ways, but producer metadata and shared residual code can make them agree for the wrong reason. A separate terminal bead must reconstruct candidate trajectories and compare representations without trusting any producer's convergence flag. Agreement strengthens candidate evidence; it still does not prove continuous orbit existence.

## Technical Approach
Build an independent safe-Rust candidate checker that reconstructs each orbit on a common physical clock, frame, phase/symmetry gauge, variable/constraint schema, and event identity. Recompute endpoint, interior, DAE, phase, event, Fourier-tail, and time-domain defects using independently selected refined meshes/quadrature/integration. Convert among segment, collocation, coefficient, and sampled representations with explicit conversion error. Compare shooting/collocation/harmonic results on overlapping admitted classes, preserve method-specific failures, and emit Consensus/Disagreement/Refuted/Unknown plus minimal mismatch intervals/modes.

## Success Criteria
All three representations agree within combined producer, conversion, and independent-check budgets where jointly applicable; stable and unstable canonical candidates survive; near recurrence, collocation underresolution, and harmonic aliasing are each caught; phase/time/segment/mesh transformations preserve observables; disagreement is localized rather than averaged away; and resource exhaustion never yields Consensus. No existence, uniqueness, stability, or basin claim is emitted.

## Test Plan
Harmonic oscillator, Van der Pol, forced Duffing, relative rotor, constrained periodic DAE, unstable orbit, subharmonic cycle, near recurrence, stiff layer, aliasing/truncation, phase/time shift, mesh/segment refinement, blind producer outputs, shared-sign mutation, artifact corruption, cancellation storms, and deterministic replay.

## Considerations
Method diversity is meaningful only when derivative/residual implementations and discretizations are sufficiently independent. Nonsmooth hybrid cases may support only shooting/collocation; the applicability matrix must say so. I09.3 owns validated existence and uniqueness.

## Execution and evidence
Retain independent source/dependency path, producer and reconstructed artifacts, conversion maps, mismatch witnesses, applicability matrix, budgets, provenance, machine fingerprint, DSR logs, and reproduction pack. Meet G0/G1/G2/G3/G4/G5 as applicable. This is the terminal I09.2 artifact.

## Core-receipt role
Construct monodromy-vector actions for admitted smooth or explicitly discretized event maps, compute clustered multipliers with residual and conditioning evidence, and independently reproduce the numerical result. It refuses theorem-grade bifurcation, nonnormal transient, or validated-existence claims.

This F/core receipt is deliberately narrower than the sibling M/maximal path. It must return Verified, Refuted, Partial, or Unknown with typed validity domains, budgets, deterministic identity, bounded cancellation, content-addressed lineage, and explicit escalation. Core gates consume this artifact; maximal adjudication remains a separate additive obligation.

## Fresh-eyes scientific correction — isolated periodic-orbit fixtures
A free autonomous harmonic oscillator is an amplitude/energy family. A phase condition removes time translation but does not remove amplitude degeneracy. Therefore it is never a positive unique-orbit fixture by itself. Positive isolation tests must use either (a) a fixed-energy or fixed-amplitude constraint with its quotient and multiplier exposed, or (b) a forced oscillator with a genuinely isolated periodic response in the admitted regime. The unconstrained autonomous case is a mandatory negative control and must return `RankDeficient`, `NonIsolatedFamily`, or typed `Unknown`; its monodromy/Floquet receipt exposes the extra unit multiplier or the exact constraint/quotient that removes it. Shooting, collocation, harmonic balance, validation, Floquet, and continuation artifacts must agree on this classification.

title: I09.6d Independently reproduce deterministic local branch continuation or Unknown
description:
## Background
Multiple shooting, collocation, and harmonic balance fail in different ways, but producer metadata and shared residual code can make them agree for the wrong reason. A separate terminal bead must reconstruct candidate trajectories and compare representations without trusting any producer's convergence flag. Agreement strengthens candidate evidence; it still does not prove continuous orbit existence.

## Technical Approach
Build an independent safe-Rust candidate checker that reconstructs each orbit on a common physical clock, frame, phase/symmetry gauge, variable/constraint schema, and event identity. Recompute endpoint, interior, DAE, phase, event, Fourier-tail, and time-domain defects using independently selected refined meshes/quadrature/integration. Convert among segment, collocation, coefficient, and sampled representations with explicit conversion error. Compare shooting/collocation/harmonic results on overlapping admitted classes, preserve method-specific failures, and emit Consensus/Disagreement/Refuted/Unknown plus minimal mismatch intervals/modes.

## Success Criteria
All three representations agree within combined producer, conversion, and independent-check budgets where jointly applicable; stable and unstable canonical candidates survive; near recurrence, collocation underresolution, and harmonic aliasing are each caught; phase/time/segment/mesh transformations preserve observables; disagreement is localized rather than averaged away; and resource exhaustion never yields Consensus. No existence, uniqueness, stability, or basin claim is emitted.

## Test Plan
Harmonic oscillator, Van der Pol, forced Duffing, relative rotor, constrained periodic DAE, unstable orbit, subharmonic cycle, near recurrence, stiff layer, aliasing/truncation, phase/time shift, mesh/segment refinement, blind producer outputs, shared-sign mutation, artifact corruption, cancellation storms, and deterministic replay.

## Considerations
Method diversity is meaningful only when derivative/residual implementations and discretizations are sufficiently independent. Nonsmooth hybrid cases may support only shooting/collocation; the applicability matrix must say so. I09.3 owns validated existence and uniqueness.

## Execution and evidence
Retain independent source/dependency path, producer and reconstructed artifacts, conversion maps, mismatch witnesses, applicability matrix, budgets, provenance, machine fingerprint, DSR logs, and reproduction pack. Meet G0/G1/G2/G3/G4/G5 as applicable. This is the terminal I09.2 artifact.

## Core-receipt role
Reproduce deterministic pseudo-arclength stepping over a declared local parameter interval using admitted orbit and baseline Floquet receipts, retain tangent/residual/step-control evidence, and return Unknown at singular, event, or missed-branch boundaries. It does not claim a complete global atlas.

This F/core receipt is deliberately narrower than the sibling M/maximal path. It must return Verified, Refuted, Partial, or Unknown with typed validity domains, budgets, deterministic identity, bounded cancellation, content-addressed lineage, and explicit escalation. Core gates consume this artifact; maximal adjudication remains a separate additive obligation.

## Fresh-eyes scientific correction — isolated periodic-orbit fixtures
A free autonomous harmonic oscillator is an amplitude/energy family. A phase condition removes time translation but does not remove amplitude degeneracy. Therefore it is never a positive unique-orbit fixture by itself. Positive isolation tests must use either (a) a fixed-energy or fixed-amplitude constraint with its quotient and multiplier exposed, or (b) a forced oscillator with a genuinely isolated periodic response in the admitted regime. The unconstrained autonomous case is a mandatory negative control and must return `RankDeficient`, `NonIsolatedFamily`, or typed `Unknown`; its monodromy/Floquet receipt exposes the extra unit multiplier or the exact constraint/quotient that removes it. Shooting, collocation, harmonic balance, validation, Floquet, and continuation artifacts must agree on this classification.

title: RA.F Derive the spacetime differential-character action and on-shell force/torque theorem
description:
## Background
A spatial differential character can encode magnetic curvature and global holonomy, but terminal voltage, Faraday induction, motional EMF, and force arise from spacetime transport and variation. Topology and gauge invariance alone do not determine constitutive stress or force: a material action or free energy, controlled electrical variables, boundary and corner terms, and a deformation law are indispensable. The Hodge star generally does not preserve an integral lattice, so constitutive metric data cannot silently be treated as an endomorphism of integral differential cohomology.

## Technical Approach
Formulate the conservative core on an oriented and time-oriented spacetime worldtube with terminals, interfaces, and corners as relative pairs. State the degree convention explicitly: a U(1) connection or differential character with curvature F versus its spatial reductions. Bind coefficient lattice or real variant, singular-current policy, gauge group, and twisted excitation/current objects. Couple the character to a real constitutive operator and circuit ports without claiming that the material Hodge map preserves characteristic classes. Pull back along material motion and derive Faraday-Reynolds transgression and motional EMF on material loops and worldsheets. Vary the on-shell discrete and continuum action under admissible spacetime/material diffeomorphisms to derive stress-energy, net force and torque, terminal work, interface/corner traction, and the exact power identity. Bind the appropriate Legendre transform for fixed voltage, charge, current, flux linkage, or coupled-circuit control. Treat hysteretic and dissipative media only through a separately stated Lagrange-dAlembert, GENERIC, or internal-state extension, or return no theorem.

## Success Criteria
The theorem card distinguishes four-dimensional spacetime objects from three-dimensional quasi-static reductions; every pullback, pushforward, pairing, orientation, coefficient, terminal trivialization, material metric, and held variable is typed. Gauge, representative, basis, tree, cut, and frame changes preserve net observables. Direct FEEC-circuit assembly, Maxwell or declared material stress, virtual work, and the theorem path produce intersecting guaranteed force/torque enclosures on admitted conservative fixtures. Boundary and corner terms close power. A seeded Hodge-lattice claim, omitted terminal Legendre term, wrong motional-EMF sign, or hidden dissipative state is rejected. Local stress nonuniqueness is allowed while net force remains invariant under the stated hypotheses.

## Test Plan
G0 exact-sequence, gauge, and pairing identities; static capacitor and magnetic-gap fixed-control sign oracles; linked moving loop and Faraday disk; rigid and deforming ALE worldtubes; air/material interface and corner traction; coefficient-lattice counterexamples; Hodge-star lattice nonpreservation; topology-stable motion; direct force-bound cross-check; gauge/tree/cut/frame changes; and formal assumption deletion.

## Considerations
This is intentionally a strong theorem target. If a universal material-force statement fails, preserve the counterexample and prove the maximal conservative, linear, reciprocal, or topology-stable theorem that survives. Do not infer force from topology alone, confuse circle-valued holonomy with an unwrapped engineering linkage, or promote method agreement to physical validation.

## Theorem-lane execution contract
Separate theorem truth, formal kernel checking, discrete conformance, numerical enclosure, and physical validation. Record exact hypotheses, trusted computing base, feature flags, boring direct-assembly baseline, activation and kill criteria, fallback, costs, deterministic and cancellable checker behavior, retained falsifiers, content-addressed artifacts, DSR evidence, and independent reproduction.

Ambition class: [M]. Runtime consequences remain default-off until all checked assumptions hold. Refutation closes the strongest false statement only after retaining the counterexample and obstruction; it does not authorize a vague weaker claim.

title: RB.K Certify regular pencils and expose singular Kronecker/minimal-index structure
description:
## Background
Generalized and polynomial eigenproblems split fundamentally into regular problems, whose finite and infinite elementary divisors define a projective spectrum at a fixed declared grade, and singular problems, whose left/right minimal indices and Kronecker structure carry constraints and hidden freedoms. A singular leading coefficient alone does not decide which case applies. Changing grade, reversing a polynomial, or applying a Möbius transform changes the finite/infinite labeling through explicit laws; it is not naive invariance. Treating a determinant-identically-zero matrix polynomial as an ordinary eigenvalue list can invent completeness, stability, and mode counts.

## Technical Approach
Define exact RegularPencil and RegularMatrixPolynomial witnesses with fail-closed admission before numerical solver routing. Build rank-revealing staircase or Kronecker-like reductions with exact/interval small-case witnesses, finite and infinite elementary-divisor semantics at fixed grade, explicit grade-shift, reversal, scaling, and projective/Möbius transformation laws, left/right minimal indices, descriptor consistency and impulse/strangeness structure for named LTI classes, and structure-preserving linearization maps. Distinguish pencil strict equivalence, matrix-polynomial constant/unimodular/strong equivalence, and strong-linearization minimal-index shifts. Keep approximate sparse diagnostics distinct from verified certificates. Route regular problems to RB.3 and singular problems to constraint/descriptor diagnostics rather than an eigenvalue-only API.

## Success Criteria
At fixed declared grade, admitted equivalences preserve exactly the invariants their theorem states. Grade changes and projective transformations produce checked shift/transport receipts rather than invariance claims. Singular determinant-identically-zero fixtures return minimal-index and constraint evidence or Unknown, never a complete spectrum. Descriptor fixtures distinguish dynamic modes, algebraic constraints, impulses, and inconsistent initial data. Naive companion linearizations that erase/shift structure without accounting or invent roots fail.

## Test Plan
Regular and singular 2x2/3x3 pencils; zero rows/columns; singular-mass QEPs in regular and singular cases; known Kronecker blocks; fixed-grade equivalence; grade increase/decrease; reversal and Möbius maps; scaling; descriptor impulse fixtures; strong and weak linearizations; rank-uncertain intervals; and exact/high-precision oracle comparison.

## Considerations
Full verified Kronecker structure at scale is a moonshot. Partial or Unknown with exact regularity witnesses is successful. Grade is semantic input; numerical rank folklore is not a theorem. Algebraic structure, discretization interpretation, control-system structure, and physical stability are separate evidence states.

## Theorem-lane execution contract
Separate algebraic theorem, finite-arithmetic checker, sparse numerical diagnostic, discretization interpretation, and physical stability. Carry TCB, coefficient uncertainty, tolerances, budgets, cancellation/resume, deterministic pivots/ties, baselines, retained falsifiers, DSR evidence, and independent reproduction.

## Moonshot promotion discipline
Ambition class [M]. Keep large-scale certified structure default-off until exact admission, quantified cost, compatible fallback, and independent reproduction close. Fail-closed Regular/Singular/Unknown semantics are mandatory even when stronger structure certification is unavailable.

## Background
A square pencil or matrix polynomial is regular when its determinant is not identically zero, even if its leading coefficient is singular. Finite and infinite elementary divisors are defined projectively at an explicit polynomial grade. Increasing grade generally adds or shifts infinity structure; reversal and Möbius maps transport rather than preserve finite/infinite labels. ## Technical Approach

Distinguish constant nonsingular strict equivalence for pencils; constant, unimodular, and strong equivalence for matrix polynomials; reversal/scaling/Möbius transformations; determinant/minor regularity witnesses; finite/infinite algebraic and partial multiplicities; and strong-linearization structure maps. Implement fail-closed Regular/Singular/Unknown admission with coefficient uncertainty and deterministic rank decisions. For each admitted transformation prove and encode its exact spectral law, including grade-induced infinity shifts and residual/backward-error transfer. Algebraic admission precedes and routes numerical Arnoldi/Jacobi-Davidson work; it does not depend on those solvers.

title: RB.K2 Expose singular Kronecker chains, minimal indices, and descriptor constraints

title: RC EPIC — Spin/Pin path-lift, chart cocycle, and holonomy engine
description:
## Background
Rotations and rigid motions are represented by double covers. A global continuous canonical sign does not exist, so sign normalization heuristics create discontinuities, broken adjoints, and false 2pi behavior in long machine paths and reflection-capable assemblies.

## Technical Approach
Represent Spin/Pin structures and obstruction classes on motion/configuration graphs; perform path lifting with chart cocycles and quotient-aware identity; compute holonomy/monodromy; support orientation-reversing Pin cases; and develop differentiable transition protocols around pi cuts without claiming an impossible global section.

## Success Criteria
Closed and open motion paths lift reproducibly, distinguish 2pi from 4pi monodromy where appropriate, preserve quotient-level physical identity, expose holonomy, and provide stable derivatives through chart transitions or explicit nondifferentiability receipts.

## Test Plan
2pi/4pi loops, random chart refinements, sign-flip metamorphics, reflections and parity, near-pi trajectories, concatenation/reversal laws, pause/resume, and PGA/quaternion/matrix cross-representation.

## Considerations
The goal is not a global canonical sign. Any theorem must state base-space regularity, chosen structure, path homotopy assumptions, and behavior at singular/ambiguous configurations.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack.
