title: RC.6a Formalize admitted cover, lift, holonomy, obstruction, and convention kernels
description:
## Background
Several distinct lifting and holonomy problems coexist and must not share an undifferentiated obstruction claim. A path in a covering space lifts uniquely once its starting sheet is fixed. A global lift of a map f:X->SO(n) through Spin(n)->SO(n) has a pullback-cover obstruction in H^1(X;Z2). A Spin structure on an oriented SO(n)-bundle is governed by w2, while Pin+/Pin- structures on O(n)-bundles use convention-qualified w2 and w2+w1^2 conditions. Deck monodromy, connection holonomy, and nonholonomic/constraint holonomy are also different objects with different invariance.

## Technical Approach
Freeze separate theorem cards and typed artifacts for: local/path lifting and uniqueness by starting sheet; global map lifting and its H1 pullback-cover obstruction; Spin structure on oriented bundles via w2; Pin+/Pin- bundle structures via the declared Clifford-sign convention; Cech transition cocycles and relative/boundary variants; deck monodromy as homotopy-class/groupoid data; connection holonomy as curvature-dependent parallel transport; and nonholonomic holonomy from a declared connection/distribution. State component/basepoint behavior, including conjugation rather than literal equality where appropriate. Specify the actual configuration/parameter-space complex carrying every class—never infer H2 from a graph incidence complex. Formalize PGA/dual-quaternion cover and exceptional-locus statements as a separate algebraic theorem family. Orbifold/action-groupoid and braid-monodromy generalization belongs downstream in RC.O.

## Success Criteria
Every theorem names exact quantifiers, carrier space, coefficient system, bundle/map/path object, convention, regularity, component, basepoint, and gauge action. Path lifting is not confused with global section existence. H1 map-lift, w2 Spin, and Pin obstruction fixtures yield their distinct results. Deck monodromy is homotopy invariant where admitted; connection/nonholonomic holonomy varies according to curvature/distribution. Basepoint/gauge changes produce the proved conjugacy/covariance law. False global-section, graph-H2, literal-holonomy-invariance, or convention-swapped claims are rejected.

## Test Plan
Circle and SO(2)/Spin(2); SO(3)/Spin(3) map lifts; oriented bundles with w2 obstruction; reflection bundles for both Pin conventions; disconnected spaces; nonorientable loops; Mobius/projective examples; flat versus curved connections on homotopic loops; nonholonomic rolling loop; periodic quotient paths; corrupt cocycles; basepoint/gauge conjugation; degenerate PGA elements; false graph carrier; and proof corruption.

## Considerations
Formal cover theory does not validate numerical path sampling. Connection holonomy is generally not homotopy-only, and representatives may change by conjugation. Pin conventions vary in the literature. Higher obstruction claims require the real cell/cover/bundle complex. RC.O is a stronger downstream extension, never a prerequisite for this core.

## Execution and evidence
Retain separate theorem manifests, definitions, TCB, carrier/coefficient/convention tables, exact fixtures, counterexamples, deterministic proof builds, budgets, provenance, DSR evidence, and independent reproduction. External proof assistants are development oracles unless admitted. Ambition class [M]; preserve maximal conjectures and exact refutations.

title: RD.V Prove dynamics-aware viability of stratified hybrid transitions
description:
## Background
Geometric incidence gives candidate neighboring strata, but it does not prove a physical trajectory can take a transition. Availability depends on vector fields or differential inclusions, tangent and normal cones, guard transversality, complementarity and friction, constitutive reset laws, and possible event accumulation.

## Technical Approach
Augment each stratum and exit morphism with validated tangent-cone viability and transversality evidence for the admitted smooth, complementarity, or measure-differential dynamics. State one-sided soundness and completeness theorems for generated modes and guards; require constitutive reset and energy or impulse closure; represent simultaneous and grazing transitions set-valuedly; hand Zeno accumulation to an explicit limit receipt rather than fabricating a next mode.

## Success Criteria
No compiled transition is labeled dynamically realizable from incidence alone. Canonical contact, Geneva, grazing, cusp, and multicontact cases distinguish geometrically adjacent, dynamically viable, blocked, set-valued, and Unknown exits. Seeded wrong vector-field direction, missing impact law, and false anti-Zeno assumption fail.

Inward and outward vector fields on the same stratification; unilateral contact and friction; simultaneous impact; Geneva entry and exit; grazing; cusp branches; Zeno adversary; reset-energy mutation; and direct hybrid comparison.

## Theorem-lane execution contract

title: RD.V1 Prove scoped tangent-cone viability and transition soundness on stratified dynamics
description:
## Background
Geometric incidence identifies candidate neighboring strata, but dynamics determines whether a trajectory can remain in, leave, or reach them. For a differential inclusion xdot in F(x) on K, weak/existential viability and strong/all-solutions invariance have different tangent conditions: under appropriate hypotheses, F(x) intersects T_K(x) can support existence, while a stronger inclusion such as F(x) subset T_K(x) is needed for strong invariance. Contingent, Clarke, proximal, and model-specific cones are not interchangeable. Local outward crossing is not eventual reachability from an interior set.

## Technical Approach
Define separate theorem cards and verdict types for existential viability, strong invariance, local outward/guard crossing, blocked transition, and bounded-horizon/eventual reachability. For each admitted smooth ODE/DAE, complementarity, sweeping/measure-differential, or set-valued class, name solution concept, tangent/normal cone, regularity, constraint qualification, selection semantics, and quantifier over solutions. Construct validated cone and vector-field/inclusion evidence; state Nagumo-style conditions with exact one-sided necessity/sufficiency strength; handle transversality and set-valued grazing/simultaneous exits; and pursue global reachability only with an explicit flow/reachability argument. State finite-event/non-Zeno hypotheses separately. Runtime lowering is downstream in RD.V2 and is not a prerequisite for the theorem.

## Success Criteria
The same stratum with inward, outward, and mixed set-valued dynamics yields distinct existential-viable, strongly invariant, locally exiting, blocked, and Unknown verdicts. Canonical contact, Geneva, cusp, and multicontact cases match direct/exact analysis. No local cone test is labeled eventual reachability. Completeness is claimed only for its exact solution/dynamic class. Wrong quantifier, cone, vector direction, regularity, selection, or anti-Zeno assumption is refuted with a witness.

## Test Plan
Inward/outward/mixed inclusions on identical strata; examples where F intersects T but is not a subset; smooth boundary crossing; unilateral contact; stick/slip candidate cones; Geneva dwell/engagement; cusp branches; simultaneous constraints; grazing; non-Lipschitz inclusion; inconsistent DAE; reachable versus locally viable but unreachable set; Zeno sequence; contingent-versus-Clarke cone difference; refinement; and false incidence-to-reachability implication.

## Considerations
Existence, strong invariance, uniqueness, selection, local exit, and global reachability are separate. Cone approximations may be conservative. Some nonconvex/set-valued dynamics admit only one-sided statements. Preserve maximal theorem ambition, but attach the exact quantifier and solution concept to every result.

## Execution and evidence
State dynamic class, solution concept, quantifiers, cone, regularity, boundary conventions, TCB, theorem polarity/strength, budgets, and no-claim boundary. Retain formal derivations, exact/interval fixtures, counterexamples, deterministic checker inputs, G0/G2/G3 evidence, DSR artifacts, and independent reproduction. Ambition class [M].

title: RD.V2 Conform contact/reset laws and lower viability-qualified exits into hybrid IR
description:
## Background
A viable approach to a boundary still does not define post-event physics. Impact, friction, adhesion, compliance limits, impulses, energy loss, and state projection require constitutive laws. Simultaneous impact generally requires a joint impulse/complementarity or measure law; it cannot be represented faithfully by an arbitrary ordering unless a sequential-impact model is explicitly chosen. Hybrid lowering can also invent a unique trace for set-valued dynamics or fabricate a next mode after Zeno accumulation.

## Technical Approach
Define the interface from viability-qualified exits to HybridAutomatonIR: guards with sidedness/transversality/set-valued status; reset/projection/impulse maps; contact/friction/adhesion law identity and parameter validity; conservation/dissipation or supply-rate closure; and state-dimension/topology transfer. For simultaneous events, make a joint impulse/complementarity/set-valued law the primary artifact. Permit partial orders/permutations only under a declared sequential-impact semantics and preserve order dependence. Represent nonunique outcomes as reachable sets/branches. Define grazing/chatter and Zeno limit receipts. Prove transactional lowering preservation for admitted classes with stable mode/event identities and deterministic enumeration—not false physical selection. Compare set-valued results by reachable-set containment or an identical declared selection rule.

## Success Criteria
Canonical impacts, stick/slip, Geneva engagement, multicontact, grazing, and Zeno cases lower with guards/resets matching declared laws and conservation/dissipation bounds. Simultaneous impacts use joint laws unless sequential semantics are explicit. Missing law or nonunique selection remains explicit. Direct comparison uses set containment or the same selection rule. Wrong reset energy, impulse sign, event order, lost branch, arbitrary selected-trace equality, or fabricated post-Zeno mode fails.

## Test Plan
Elastic/inelastic impact; Coulomb/static friction; adhesion/release; compliant-to-rigid limit; Geneva entry/exit; joint simultaneous impact versus sequential permutations; order-sensitive sequential model; set-valued reachable outcomes; grazing; chatter; bouncing-ball Zeno; DAE projection; state topology transfer; transactional cancellation; checkpoint/resume; and reset mutation.

## Considerations
Contact laws are scoped models. Set-valued physics must not be collapsed for determinism. Regularization can change bifurcation/dissipation. Sequential impact is one constitutive choice, not a universal resolution of simultaneity.

## Execution and evidence
Bind law/version/material state, solution/selection semantics, units/frames, mode/guard/reset identities, viability witness, conservation ledger, error/time budgets, deterministic enumeration policy, cancellation/drain, provenance, reachable-set/direct comparisons, G2/G3/G4/G5 evidence, and DSR logs. title: RD.H Build higher Kuranishi/L-infinity obstruction models beyond the Jacobian complex
description:
## Background
The two-term tangent complex records infinitesimal mobility and first obstruction or cokernel data, but it does not determine whether an infinitesimal mechanism integrates to a finite branch. Second and higher jets, nonlinear compatibility, syzygies, and formal-moduli operations carry the missing obstruction information. Without them, the derived mobility theorem risks being Jacobian rank analysis with new names.

## Technical Approach
For admitted analytic or semialgebraic constraint germs, construct a presentation-invariant cotangent-complex resolution and a finite Kuranishi model or equivalent L-infinity formal-moduli representation from the tangent complex, relation modules, and higher derivatives. Compute second-order rigidity maps, obstruction classes, brackets and higher operations, branch multiplicity, and convergence or effectivity conditions. Prove invariance under admitted coordinate changes and quasi-isomorphic constraint resolutions; distinguish arbitrary redundant equations from equivalent derived presentations. Provide exact and interval microcase checkers and truncate with an explicit Unknown remainder when effectivity cannot be proved.

## Success Criteria
Regular cases collapse to the implicit-function theorem. Bennett, Bricard, and second-order locked examples distinguish infinitesimal flex, obstructed flex, and genuine finite branch. Adding generated redundant equations or changing an equivalent resolution preserves the formal-moduli receipt. A nonzero tangent vector alone never becomes a motion certificate. At least one theorem links vanishing obstruction data plus precise analytic or effectivity hypotheses to a validated local branch, or records the sharp counterexample.

## Test Plan
Regular linkage; cusp and node; redundant generators and explicit syzygies; infinitesimally flexible but rigid frameworks; Bennett and Bricard cases; higher-order locked germs; coordinate and resolution changes; interval rank uncertainty; truncated-series false positives; and formal-checker mutation.

## Considerations
Vanishing of finitely many obstructions need not imply convergence without Noetherian, analytic, or effectivity hypotheses. Preserve formal versus actual solution states separately.

title: RD.X Certify exit-path infinity-category approximations and constructible descent

## Background
A stratum-incidence poset is not generally the exit-path category: nontrivial fundamental groups inside strata and topology of links can create distinct morphisms and monodromy even when incidence is identical. Collapsing this data would make the hybrid compiler miss path-dependent branches.

## Technical Approach

Build constructible descent, monodromy, refinement-equivalence, and obstruction checkers.

## Success Criteria
Two stratified spaces with the same incidence poset but different link or stratum monodromy cannot receive the same certified exit-path artifact. Cones and regular cells; punctured and circular strata; links with nontrivial fundamental group; same-poset/different-exit-path falsifier; cusp and branch intersections; entrance-versus-exit reversal; local-system monodromy; subdivision; and corrupted composition.

An ordinary one-category may be a deliberate truncation, but its information loss and supported consumers must be explicit. Do not invoke constructible-sheaf equivalence outside admitted stratifications.

title: RE.M Enclose invariant measures, statistical QoIs, escape rates, and Lyapunov spectra
description:
## Background
A deterministic attractor atlas does not by itself answer long-time engineering questions such as fatigue-driving residence fractions, rare escape rates, mean power, acoustic statistics, or Lyapunov spectra. Chaotic and metastable machines need certified statistical statements, while nonunique invariant measures and finite-time sampling bias must remain visible.

## Technical Approach
Construct validated transfer/Perron–Frobenius operators on admitted maps, Poincare sections, and flow suspensions. Combine adaptive Ulam or spectral partitions with Lasota–Yorke-type inequalities, compactness/mixing hypotheses, interval eigen-enclosures, mass and positivity checks, and certified discretization error. Enclose invariant measures, multiple ergodic components, statistical QoIs, escape rates for open systems, and Lyapunov exponents or spectra under explicit regularity and cocycle assumptions. Treat physical/SRB measure claims as stronger and distinct from mere invariant-measure existence. Route nonhyperbolic, intermittent, or unresolved regions to Unknown.

## Success Criteria
Canonical expanding, intermittent, open, and chaotic systems yield independently checked measure, escape-rate, and Lyapunov enclosures at the claimed order. A machine-relevant rotor, impact, or electromechanical case reports certified long-time QoI bands and distinguishes multiple invariant measures or unresolved selection. Results refine monotonically or carry a validated explanation for partition/topology change.

## Test Plan
Doubling and logistic maps in admitted regimes, cat-map/cocycle spectra, open maps with known escape rates, Lorenz-like return maps where hypotheses can be checked, metastable double wells, nonergodic mixtures, intermittent counterexamples to spectral gaps, partition and coordinate mutations, normalization/positivity checks, independent high-precision eigen-enclosures, cancellation, and deterministic replay.

## Considerations
Finite trajectory histograms do not certify invariant measures. Existence, uniqueness, ergodicity, mixing rate, physicality/SRB selection, and statistical stability are separate claims with separate hypotheses. Ulam convergence is not universal; essential spectrum and lack of a spectral gap must produce Unknown rather than optimistic error bars.

## Theorem contract
The theorem artifact records the map/flow and domain, function space, partition, transfer operator, Lasota–Yorke or alternative compactness evidence, invariant-mass/positivity witness, spectral enclosure, discretization error, and exact statistical claim. An independent checker validates operator bounds and QoI integration. Multiple measures are represented explicitly. No SRB, uniqueness, escape, or Lyapunov claim is inferred solely from simulation.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain layer-correct, safe Rust by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync Cx scopes, deterministic under logical partition identities, budgeted in time/memory/error/capability, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names Gauntlet tiers, retains exact seeds and partition hashes, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its fallback, and includes independent checker replay.

## Moonshot promotion discipline
Ambition class: [M]. Use feature flag `moonshot-certified-statistical-dynamics`. The boring baseline is finite-time ensemble evidence labeled empirical. Activation requires canonical convergence cases, retained no-spectral-gap falsifiers, a machine demonstration, quantitative error/cost thresholds, and independent reproduction. Kill on lost mass/positivity, unjustified uniqueness or SRB language, non-enclosing error estimates, or checker disagreement. Fallback returns empirical summaries and Unknown for theorem claims.

title: RE.Q Certify quantified reach-avoid and viability games over machine uncertainty
description:
## Background
Machine safety and reachability claims are quantified statements, not pictures from sampled trajectories. The answer can change completely between “there exists a control for every disturbance,” “for every disturbance there exists a clairvoyant control,” and open-loop existence. FrankenSim needs a theorem-bearing game semantics that can certify robust reach-avoid and viability regions over uncertain machine states, parameters, contacts, and loads without silently changing quantifier order.

## Technical Approach
Define typed finite- and infinite-horizon game contracts with explicit quantifier prefixes over initial sets, admissible feedback or open-loop controls, disturbances, model parameters, event schedules, and strategy information patterns. Implement validated predecessor, reachable-set, and viability-kernel operators using interval/Taylor set propagation, barrier and SOS witnesses where applicable, adaptive inner/outer approximations, and deterministic subdivision. Couple hybrid guards/resets and differential-algebraic consistency through admitted model classes. Every cell carries Proven, Refuted, or Unknown plus a retained witness, counterexample, or obstruction; approximation widening must never be relabeled as safety.

## Success Criteria
For canonical controlled and adversarial hybrid systems, produce independently replayable inner safe-strategy regions and outer impossible regions with explicit horizons, quantifier order, information pattern, model class, and numerical enclosure. Demonstrate a machine case in which sampled simulation appears safe but the quantified solver finds a certified disturbance strategy, and another in which a retained controller/barrier witness proves robust reach-avoid. Unsupported or unresolved cases return Unknown with ranked refinement options.

## Test Plan
Use pursuit/evasion and double-integrator games, controlled impacts, backlash and friction adversaries, parameter-box uncertainty, switched-actuator faults, known viability kernels, swapped-quantifier mutation tests, unit rescaling, subdivision invariance, independent high-precision replay, cancellation storms, and deterministic thread-count replay. Include adversaries where open-loop control fails but feedback succeeds and where existential-after-universal accidentally assumes clairvoyance.

## Considerations
State compactness, regularity, nonanticipativity, disturbance measurability, DAE consistency, hybrid non-Zeno assumptions, and finite-versus-infinite horizon explicitly. A failed search for a controller is not a proof of impossibility; impossibility requires an outer/exclusion certificate. A numerical trajectory is neither a strategy nor a quantified proof.

## Theorem contract
Hypotheses and quantifier prefixes are machine-readable and hashed into the theorem artifact. The checker independently verifies set inclusions, guard/reset images, barrier or dynamic-programming inequalities, strategy admissibility, and enclosure arithmetic. Claimed inner and outer regions must be monotone under certified refinement or explain a validated topology event. Counterexamples are retained. The theorem makes no claim outside the admitted dynamics, information pattern, uncertainty set, or horizon.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain layer-correct, safe Rust by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync Cx scopes, deterministic under fixed logical-tile reductions, budgeted in time/memory/error/capability, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names Gauntlet tiers, retains machine fingerprints and exact seeds, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its exact fallback state, and includes an independently replayable checker pack.

## Moonshot promotion discipline
Ambition class: [M]. Use feature flag `moonshot-quantified-viability-games`. The boring baseline is bounded validated forward reachability with no game claim. Activation requires checker-backed canonical and machine cases, quantitative enclosure and cost thresholds, and independent reproduction. Kill on unsound quantifier lowering, non-monotone certified bounds without explanation, checker disagreement, or unbounded cancellation latency. Fallback returns the baseline reachability evidence and Unknown for the game claim; a falsified conjecture remains a retained result.

title: RE.Z Certify Zeno/chatter accumulation, continuation, and global invariant semantics
description:
## Background
Chatter and Zeno behavior are central to impacts, relays, dry friction, backlash, power electronics, and protective control. Ordinary event stepping can execute an unbounded number of transitions in finite time, miss the accumulation state, or invent a post-event trajectory. A global dynamics atlas cannot claim completeness until accumulation, continuation, and invariant-set semantics are explicit.

## Technical Approach
Define an admitted hybrid-system class with typed modes, guards, resets, time domains, complementarity/contact laws, and event identity. Build validated enclosures for event-time sequences and accumulation states; prove finite-event separation where possible and detect certified Zeno accumulation where separation fails. Represent post-Zeno semantics as one of: uniquely certified continuation, set-valued continuation enclosure, terminal accumulation, or Unknown. Derive finite products or renormalized limits for variational/saltation data only under stated summability and transversality hypotheses; never multiply an unverified infinite saltation sequence. Integrate accumulation objects into Conley/Morse and viability reasoning.

## Success Criteria
Certified examples distinguish non-Zeno chatter, true finite-time Zeno accumulation, grazing ambiguity, and numerical event-loop artifacts. Each Zeno artifact encloses the accumulation time/state, records the active transition word or language, and states exactly what post-Zeno continuation is proven. Demonstrate at least one impact or relay machine model with independently replayed accumulation and one case correctly returning Unknown because continuation is nonunique or the admitted hypotheses fail.

## Test Plan
Bouncing ball with restitution families, relay chatter, complementarity contact, grazing impacts, simultaneous guards, zero-time reset cycles, event-time interval overlap, restitution approaching one, post-Zeno sticking versus rebound, Zeno regularization mutation tests, cancellation during dense event sequences, deterministic replay, and independent high-precision interval checks.

## Considerations
A time-step cutoff, event-count cap, or regularized compliance model is not a Zeno theorem. Distinguish physical model semantics from a chosen numerical regularization. State guard regularity, reset contraction, transversality, uniqueness, accumulation compactness, and any summability assumptions. Never infer post-Zeno dynamics from a finite prefix alone.

## Theorem contract
The artifact records the admitted hybrid automaton, event ordering semantics, interval enclosures for event times and states, accumulation proof or finite-separation proof, and the exact continuation category. An independent checker verifies guard hits, reset images, contraction/separation inequalities, and claimed limits. Counterexamples with reordered simultaneous events and nonunique continuations are retained. No theorem transfers across a regularization or model change without a new refinement receipt.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain layer-correct, safe Rust by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync Cx scopes, deterministic under fixed logical-event identities, budgeted in time/memory/error/capability, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names Gauntlet tiers, retains exact seeds and model hashes, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its fallback, and includes independent replay of the checker and event trace.

## Moonshot promotion discipline
Ambition class: [M]. Use feature flag `moonshot-zeno-continuation`. The boring baseline stops with a structured event-density diagnostic and no continuation claim. Activation requires canonical analytic cases, adversarial simultaneous-event cases, a machine demonstration, bounded cancellation, and independent reproduction. Kill on missed certified accumulation, invented uniqueness, regularization leakage, or checker disagreement. Fallback preserves the finite trace and returns Unknown beyond the certified horizon.

title: TR.G3 Check cross-ratchet theorem composition and pursue new synthesis theorems
description:
## Background
The program seeks novel leverage from composing differential cohomology, spectral flow, Spin/Pin lifts, stratified derived geometry, and global dynamics. Composition can create new theorems but can also smuggle incompatible hypotheses.

## Technical Approach
Construct typed cross-ratchet lemma graphs and evidence sheaves for selected flagship mechanisms. Check naturality, shared domain, units, coefficient and orientation compatibility, model identity, proof polarity, and absence of circular dependence. Pursue explicit new composite conjectures where the interfaces genuinely align, retaining counterexamples and strongest surviving statements.

## Success Criteria
Every composite theorem has machine-readable interface hypotheses and an independent checker plan; incompatible artifacts refuse; at least one high-value cross-ratchet conjecture is formalized or sharply refuted with retained evidence.

## Test Plan
Valid and invalid compositions, model-version mismatch, spatial versus spacetime confusion, topological versus connection holonomy, incidence versus viability, spectral versus nonlinear stability, and proof-color mutation.

## Considerations
This is an ambition ratchet: discovering a new theorem is encouraged, but suggestive analogy is never promoted as proof.

## Execution and evidence
This cross-ratchet campaign uses immutable content-addressed manifests, explicit theorem identities and proof polarity, versions, budgets, deterministic replay, bounded cancellation, independent reviewers, and retained falsifiers. Completion records DSR evidence or exact fallback, every trusted computing base and oracle role, machine fingerprints for cost claims, conflicts and unresolved claims, and a signed program-level promotion, refutation, or Unknown ledger. No vote can override failed mathematics.

title: LEAPFROG-2026 SUMMIT — integrate all fifteen initiatives and five theorem ratchets
description:
## Background
This is the executable definition of completion for the entire leapfrog program. The original planning conversation or markdown is not required: the umbrella, portfolio, initiative, leaf, gate, comment, and dependency records contain the intent, implementation contracts, falsifiers, and proof boundaries.

## Technical Approach
Run five portfolio campaigns and one shared flagship machine thread: semantic machine/material/harness input; generated coupled equations; causal and hybrid execution; electrostatic/EMC and topology-aware design; periodic/global dynamics; blind experiment/material update; target deployment; conservation microscope; executable standards; evidence-budget decisions; AP242 supplier round trip; and theorem-strengthened paths where assumptions hold. Generate one content-addressed Design Ledger/traceability/competitive report with orthogonal numerical, material, validation, prediction-domain, performance, standards, and theorem evidence axes.

## Success Criteria
All five portfolio gates close; all twenty initiative gates are reachable in the dependency DAG; no cycles or orphaned program leaves exist; every normative program claim maps to an owner, falsifier, evidence route, fallback, and no-claim boundary; a separate process reproduces the summit; default-off flags remain off unless their own gates authorize them; deliberate receipt deletion and semantic drift fail closed.

## Test Plan
Full G0-G5 matrix; cross-schema and version migrations; cancellation/fault storms at every layer; deterministic same-ISA/thread-count audits; unit/frame/clock and identity mutations; material/DAQ/AP242 tampering; solver/model/fidelity faults; theorem-assumption deletion; and independent report/checker replay.

## Considerations
Completion does not mean every moonshot theorem is true or every feature is default-on. It means FrankenSim knows exactly what it proved, validated, refuted, measured, inferred, cannot claim, and can replay.

## Program-wide closure contract
This gate consumes proof artifacts; it does not infer completion from issue status or demos. All inputs must preserve typed units/frames/clocks, stable identities, versions, provenance, evidence colors, error/time/memory/capability budgets, cancellation/drain and checkpoint behavior, deterministic mode, structured events, no-claim boundaries, baseline/fallback, feature flags, retained falsifiers, and exact DSR/reproduction evidence. Any missing, stale, incompatible, or inaccessible load-bearing artifact fails closed with a minimal diagnostic.

title: SUMMIT.1 Freeze the integrated artifact, schema, flag, budget, and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
Fifteen initiatives and five theorem ratchets produce many versioned schemas, flags, evidence states, and external prerequisites. A summit cannot integrate a moving or ambiguous target.

## Technical Approach
Freeze a versioned summit manifest enumerating exact terminal artifacts, Machine IR and Operator IR schemas, units and frames, material-card versions, model crosswalks, feature flags, boring baselines, capability and resource budgets, evidence polarity, theorem atlas, licensed/public corpora, benchmark identities, and unresolved exclusions. Detect stale, missing, circular, or semantically incompatible inputs.

## Success Criteria
Every summit campaign resolves all inputs by content hash and semantic version; no hidden default or original-plan backlink remains; unresolved prerequisites and no-claim regions are visible and ranked; regeneration is deterministic.

## Test Plan
Missing artifact, schema and unit mismatch, stale crosswalk, duplicate identity, flag without fallback, circular evidence, incompatible theorem version, and manifest replay.

## Considerations
Freezing an interface does not freeze research ambition; later stronger artifacts enter through a new manifest version and explicit migration.

## Execution and evidence
This summit work uses immutable content-addressed manifests, the Five Explicits, exact model and evidence identity, versions, budgets, deterministic logical identities, bounded asupersync cancellation and drain, transactional checkpoints, and independent reviewers. Completion records configured DSR evidence or exact fallback, machine fingerprints, performance bands, trusted computing bases, retained falsifiers, physical-validation state, and replayable reports. No integration demo may strengthen any component claim.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: LEAPFROG EXPERIENCE & PROOF SPINE — user workbench, executable journeys, observability, and replay
description:
## Background
The fifteen Leapfrog initiatives and five theorem ratchets contain unusually strong local Test Plans, but local prose is not executable proof and does not by itself make a system usable. A feature can look complete while its independent oracle, user workflow, scientific-visualization semantics, long-job control, cancellation finalization, failure diagnosis, evidence closure, or replay path remains implicit.

This cross-cutting portfolio is a direct child of LEAPFROG-2026. It is not a sixteenth scientific initiative and does not reduce, merge, cap, or postpone any feature. It gives every current and future capability a common, falsifiable, agent-native route from declared intent to unit evidence, production execution, durable operation, honest scientific adjudication, retained artifacts, and exact replay.

## User and agent outcomes
A user can inspect installation and host readiness; discover capabilities and no-claim boundaries; inspect inferred defaults; estimate cost; author or import a case through supported CLI, Rust API, FrankenScript, and WASM surfaces; select an explicit Core or Max claim stratum and independent campaign profile; submit a durable job; disconnect and reconnect; watch from a cursor; checkpoint, pause, migrate, cancel, resume, or fork with exact authority and lineage; inspect unit/frame/time/uncertainty-aware results and truthful visualizations; verify, report, redact/share, and replay artifacts; and receive ranked repairs for invalid input or environmental gaps.

An agent receives the same semantics through versioned schemas and stable JSONL, never screen scraping or a hidden test-only path. A status query, cancel request, worker attempt, scientific job, and aggregate campaign remain distinguishable, so operational success cannot overwrite scientific truth.

## Technical Approach
Build one additive verification-and-experience spine around fs-obs, shared conformance, G0-G5 Gauntlet, HELM/session execution, DSR, Design Ledger, benchmark and V&V registries, LUMEN/fs-viz, and phase batteries. Own:

1. a generated VerificationManifest mapping every execution leaf and future descendant to concrete tests or a reviewed, narrow, expiring not-applicable rationale;
2. comprehensive Rust unit, boundary, error, doctest, executable-example, compile-fail/UI, type-invariant, property, metamorphic, manufactured-solution, benchmark, conformance, mutation, fuzz, certifier-of-certifier, deterministic-concurrency, chaos, security, and replay runners;
3. one typed protocol shared by product HELM/CLI/session APIs, the fs-test/DSR engine, and hermetic shell adapters, with conformance evidence that wrappers add zero semantics;
4. a canonical no-mock E2E runner plus exact per-family scripts and manifests;
5. one bounded, schema-versioned observability, diagnostic, evidence-retention, FailureBundle, replay, redaction, and share contract;
6. exact identity and causality for DSR runs, campaigns, shards, journeys, cases, submissions, durable jobs, attempts, control/query operations, execution scopes, tiles, leases, cursors, checkpoints, and artifacts;
7. scoped OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt objects with an orthogonal scientific/evidence outcome algebra;
8. a complete durable asynchronous lifecycle with reconnectable observation and fenced control;
9. progressive-disclosure human/agent workbench, first-run doctor, generated help/completions, accessibility, teaching diagnostics, truthful scientific visualization, temporal presentation integrity, and data/image/timeline/report parity;
10. explicit Core and MAX test receipts plus post-promotion journeys for all fifteen initiatives;
11. executable pre-final and post-final journeys for all five theorem ratchets, admitting stronger independently checked theorems and durable refutations;
12. cross-portfolio semantic-seam campaigns, DSR/scale/cross-ISA/release qualification, forty retained family user journeys, executable Core and MAX tutorial corpora, and final independent adjudication.

Generated catalogs, manifests, help, completions, and tutorials come from Beads, contracts, IR, and code rather than hand-maintained parallel lists. Every inferred default is surfaced and ledgered. Legacy suites are admitted only through versioned semantic-diff adapters.

Consume the canonical schemas from frankensim-ext-vv-artifact-schemas-x68z: ContextOfUse, CalibrationSplit, SolutionVerificationReceipt, PredictionAssessment, and the uncertainty waterfall. Every evidence edge is typed as code verification, solution verification, calibration, model validation, prediction assessment, exploratory discovery, or confirmation. None implies another. Exploratory or adaptively selected results may create bold new ClaimRecords and theorem conjectures, but empirical promotion requires independent confirmatory lineage: preregistered/held-out evidence or anytime-valid optional-stopping control, multiplicity/selective-reporting accounting, and an exact ContextOfUse. Formal theorem promotion remains governed by its proof/checker receipts, never empirical fit.

## Protocol and executable-surface contract
There is one typed VerificationProtocol/JourneyEngine semantic authority. Product CLI and HELM/session APIs expose user operations and durable lifecycle semantics. The fs-test command is the test and DSR execution adapter over the same protocol. 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh' is a hermetic, portability-tested adapter that only selects and invokes typed operations; it does not define selection, lifecycle, verdict, artifact, or exit semantics.

V.4.2 owns command grammar, selectors, plan/estimate/explain/diff, and synchronous convenience behavior. V.4.9 exclusively owns Submission/Job/Attempt lifecycle, status/watch/attach, checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork, reconnect/restart, artifact/report/share/offline verification, and terminal state transitions. Conformance tests compare all surfaces for selection hashes, typed requests, events, artifacts, scoped receipts, and process projections.

## Identity, causality, and receipt scopes
Names are never aliases:

- DsrRunId identifies one DSR invocation; CampaignRunId identifies one canonical manifest expansion/execution; ShardId identifies a deterministic partition.
- JourneyId and CaseId are stable logical definitions, not executions.
- SubmissionId identifies immutable pre-admission client intent within an exact idempotency scope. An AdmissionReceipt records acceptance or rejection; only acceptance creates or links a JobId for the durable logical computation. Repeating the same key and canonical payload returns the same decision, while the same key with a different payload is a typed collision and never aliases. AttemptId identifies one worker incarnation caused by initial execution, retry, resume, or migration.
- OperationId identifies one user/API control or query such as submit, status, watch, cancel, or verify. ExecutionScopeId and TileId identify local work inside an Attempt. ArtifactId and CheckpointId are content-addressed lineage nodes.
- A resume or migration normally creates a new Attempt for the same Job. A fork creates a new Job with an explicit checkpoint/parent edge. Replay creates a new CampaignRun or Submission with a replay-of edge. DSR hosting and scientific causality are separate typed edges.

Within an Attempt, execution containment is a tree. Globally, submissions, jobs, attempts, forks, replays, checkpoints, artifacts, campaigns, and DSR hosting form a typed acyclic causal DAG with explicit multi-parent edges.

Receipts are scoped:

- OperationReceipt describes the current CLI/API operation and alone projects to that process exit code.
- AttemptReceipt describes one execution incarnation, its lifecycle, resources, faults, and produced evidence.
- JobReceipt aggregates the durable computation and carries its exact scientific claim/evidence state.
- CampaignReceipt aggregates deterministic selection, shards, cases, independent reproduction, and promotion effect.

A successful 'status' operation may exit zero while embedding a JobReceipt with ClaimAdjudication=refuted or a failed ExecutionDisposition. An accepted 'cancel' operation may exit zero before a later JobReceipt reaches drained cancellation. No unqualified terminal result is allowed.

## Claim strata and campaign profiles
Scientific scope and campaign intensity are separate axes. Every executable scientific request selects exactly one claim stratum from the grammar {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Profiles control workload, duration, fault model, platforms, and evidence obligations; they never silently upgrade or downgrade the claim surface.

Selection, defaults, filters, profile composition, budgets, capabilities, and shard expansion are canonicalized, diffable, and ledgered. Legacy SMOKE/MID/FULL names are accepted only by V.4.6 semantic adapters. A mapping is valid only if cases, claims, budgets, capabilities, acceptance rules, negative cases, and artifacts reconcile; otherwise it refuses with ranked migration guidance.

## Orthogonal scientific and evidence outcome algebra
Every ClaimRecord has a stable ClaimId plus immutable ClaimRevisionId, kind, statement, quantifiers, units/conventions, hypothesis set, exact domain, version, and typed relations to other claims. Every implication, refinement, restriction, equivalence, incompatibility, or counterexample edge is itself an evidence-bearing ClaimRelationReceipt with explicit direction, source/target domains and quantifiers, checker identity, proof artifact, and TCB overlap. Relation cycles fail closed except independently certified equivalence components; transitive use requires admitted relation composition. The receipt records separate fields:

- ExecutionDisposition: completed, rejected, cancelled-and-drained, timed-out-and-finalized, budget-exhausted-and-finalized, infrastructure-error, or execution-integrity-error.
- RequestedPredicateOutcome: satisfied, unsatisfied, indeterminate, or not-evaluated for the exact operation/campaign predicate.
- ClaimAdjudication: established, refuted, unresolved, or not-claimed for the exact ClaimRecord.
- EvidenceMethodSet: formal-kernel, computer-assisted-certified, interval/certified-numerical, exact-discrete, independently reproduced numerical, validated-empirical, empirical-only, expert-judgment, or other versioned methods, with provenance and TCB overlap.
- EpistemicGrade: proof, certified, validated, corroborated, preliminary, or conjectural, derived by a versioned policy from claim kind and admitted evidence rather than chosen cosmetically.
- DomainApplicability: in-domain, outside-domain, domain-unknown, or not-evaluated.
- OperationalSupport: available, missing-capability, hardware-unavailable, license-unavailable, policy-denied, data-unavailable, temporarily-unavailable, or not-evaluated.
- EvidenceCompleteness: complete, partial, missing, or not-required.
- EvidenceIntegrity: verified, unverified, corrupt, or conflicting.
- PromotionEffect: eligible, restricted, quarantined, demoted, no-change, or ineligible, with the affected claim/capability set.

Human terms are typed projections, not mixed enum values. For example, a theorem ClaimRecord that is established with proof-grade admitted evidence renders Proven; a validation claim with validated evidence renders ValidatedWithinDomain; unresolved renders Unknown; not-claimed renders NoClaim. Unsupported is a projection of DomainApplicability and OperationalSupport, not a truth value.

'Partial' is never a ClaimAdjudication. A weaker, restricted, or local theorem is a separate hashed ClaimRecord with exact implication/refinement edges and its own adjudication. Incomplete evidence remains EvidenceCompleteness=partial and cannot promote the original claim. This preserves ambitious theorem ratcheting without laundering unfinished closure.

Old ClaimState and combined EvidenceCompleteness/Integrity fields migrate through explicit, loss-reporting adapters. Ambiguous old values do not default favorably.

## Process projection
The typed receipt is authoritative. A process code is a deterministic, versioned projection of the current finalized OperationReceipt only: 0 operation predicate satisfied; 10 unsatisfied; 11 invalid manifest/schema/admission; 12 indeterminate or required operation evidence incomplete; 13 operation unsupported by domain/capability/policy; 14 current operation cancelled and drained; 15 current operation finalized timeout; 16 infrastructure error; 17 integrity/security failure; 18 current operation budget exhaustion. If the client, shell, host, or service dies before a finalized OperationReceipt is durably observable, no 0/10-18 scientific projection may be fabricated: the platform signal/transport status is reported separately and recovery proceeds by SubmissionId, idempotency key, or authorized job discovery.

Thus a sound refutation can be exit 0 for an 'adjudicate' operation and exit 10 for a 'prove' operation. A successful status query is exit 0 even when its embedded JobReceipt has ClaimAdjudication=refuted, a finalized timeout, outside-domain applicability, or unavailable support. Successful execution never implies a claim is established, and a missing receipt never defaults favorably.

## Executable test and logging contract
The future hermetic adapter is 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh', with per-family drivers under 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/<family>.sh' and manifests under 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/<family>.toml'. Typed operations cover list, doctor/capabilities, plan/estimate, submit/run, status, watch/attach, checkpoint/pause/migrate, cancel/resume/fork, inspect/artifacts/report/share/verify, explain/diff, and replay. Pretty output renders the same typed events as stable JSONL.

Every run emits stable identity and typed causal edges; manifest/code/contract/schema hashes; units/frames/clocks; seed and logical RNG/work identity; requested and consumed budgets; capabilities/flags; machine/ISA/thread/mode fingerprint; fixture/input/output hashes; oracle/checker and TCB overlap; tolerance derivation; progress/residual/balance/conservation/uncertainty/error summaries; lifecycle and control events; scoped outcome receipts; diagnostic/repair decisions; artifact, FailureBundle, minimized-witness, report, and exact reconnect/replay pointers; timing and memory. Promotion-critical events are never sampled. Large or sensitive data is content-addressed and policy-redacted; logs are bounded and backpressure-safe.

## Success Criteria
Every current and future execution leaf has mechanically checked coverage. Every Core/MAX initiative gate, theorem final disposition, portfolio gate, and Summit consumes the appropriate executable receipt. The twenty capability families each have Core and MAX post-promotion journeys—forty retained journey receipts—plus executable Core and MAX tutorial branches.

Users can install, preflight, recover long jobs, distinguish operation success from job/scientific outcome, interpret temporal and visual evidence, verify closure, and replay without tribal knowledge. Human and agent surfaces agree. Failures replay from immutable closure. The graph remains acyclic, capability-stratified, ambition-preserving, and explicit about unsupported or unsettled frontiers.

## Test Plan
Self-test manifest compilation with missing, duplicate, stale, cyclic, falsely not-applicable, and ambition-downgrade entries. Exhaustively test valid scoped-receipt products, invalid combinations, process projections, old-field migrations, restricted-claim graphs, and operation-versus-job examples. Mutation-test identity aliasing, causal edges, lease fencing, stratum/profile expansion, legacy adapters, oracle independence, tolerance arithmetic, visualization and temporal transforms, redaction, cancellation/draining, pause/migration, retention, and generated help/tutorials.

Run comprehensive Rust unit, boundary, error, doctest, executable-example, compile-fail/UI, property, metamorphic, model-checking, Miri/sanitizer-or-explicit-OperationalSupport-gap, and certifier tests. Run no-mock production-path E2E at declared profiles; inject client, shell, process, worker, service, artifact, clock, storage, network, license, and security faults; audit boundedness and secret/license leakage; install and run packaged artifacts from clean non-repository hosts; replay same-ISA and supported cross-ISA modes; and independently reproduce promotion receipts from clean stores.

Mutate discovery into confirmation, reuse calibration data as validation or prediction holdout, hide model/parameter selection, optional stopping, multiple looks, forked hypotheses, multiplicity, or uncertainty components, and substitute solution verification for model validation or prediction assessment. Require fail-closed relation edges, independent holdout/preregistration or anytime-valid receipts, and retained rejected discoveries; stronger discoveries remain visible without laundering.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

Retain ContextOfUseId, CalibrationSplitId, SolutionVerificationReceiptId, PredictionAssessmentId, uncertainty-waterfall components, evidence-stage and dataset-role lineage, preregistration/holdout commitment, adaptive looks/stopping rule, multiplicity family and adjustment/e-process, model/parameter selection history, and independent confirmation relation. Promotion records the exact stage-qualified evidence and never collapses the waterfall or stage distinctions.

## Considerations
This portfolio reuses rather than forks existing infrastructure. Accessibility applies to visual and interactive surfaces; machine APIs retain equivalent information. Successful bulk telemetry may expire under policy, but promotion evidence, refutations, minimized failures, semantic interchange artifacts, and theorem counterexamples are durable. Hardware-, data-, policy-, or license-dependent tests yield explicit support/applicability receipts, never silent green.

A novel theorem may exceed today's conjecture. The harness records the stronger exact ClaimRecord, proof method, domain, implication lattice, and runtime witness rather than imposing an artificial ceiling.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. title: V.1.1 Specify VerificationManifest v1, authority lattice, ClaimRevision, and stable Case/Journey identities
description:
## Background
Without stable semantic identity and source authority, renamed tests, revised Beads, reorganized scripts, or changed contracts can sever evidence from claims or retroactively reinterpret an old receipt.

## Technical Approach
Specify the versioned VerificationManifest schema, authority lattice, canonical normalized graph, and hashing rules. ClaimId identifies a continuing conceptual lineage; ClaimRevisionId binds one exact statement, kind, quantifiers, units/conventions, hypotheses, domain, code/contract surface, and no-claim boundary. Supersession never mutates an old revision.

A manifest record binds exact source snapshot hashes; Bead obligation ID; ClaimRevision; Core/Max stratum; admitted campaign profiles; ambition tag; public surface; Case/Journey IDs; unit/property/conformance/E2E ownership; fixture/oracle/checker IDs; TCB overlap; tolerance derivation; budgets; capabilities; event kinds; retention; replay command; DSR lane; scoped receipt expectations; and consuming gate.

Define typed ClaimRelationReceipt for implication, refinement, restriction, counterexample, and certified equivalence edges. It records direction, proof/checker/TCB, domain/quantifier variance, and policy version. Promotion/fallback transfers only across admitted relations. Reject cycles unless independently certified equivalence; canonicalize a certified-equivalence strongly connected component to one representative without erasing members.

Define additive versus breaking migration, collision handling, and explicit lossy migration reports. Heterogeneous human, JSON, and ledger renderings share one canonical normalized graph/digest and tested semantic projection; they are not required to be byte-identical.

## Success Criteria
Equivalent semantic manifests normalize to the same digest; distinct ClaimRevisions cannot collide; mutable source changes create new snapshots/revisions; every field has units, cardinality, authority, default visibility, and migration semantics; invalid, incomplete, conflicting, or relation-unsound records produce stable diagnostics and ranked fixes.

## Test Plan
Canonicalization/round-trip unit and property tests; duplicate/collision, Unicode, and ordering cases; missing field/wrong unit; source-authority conflict; post-receipt source mutation; old-reader/new-writer compatibility; ClaimRevision supersession; relation orientation, transitive composition, quantifier variance, domain contradiction, favorable relabeling, cycle, and certified-equivalence SCC tests; semantic parity of human/JSON/ledger projections.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit frozen source snapshot IDs/hashes, normalized graph/digest, Claim/ClaimRevision/Case/Journey identities, relation receipts, schema/compiler/policy versions, ownership, stratum/profiles, Five Explicits, capabilities, oracle/TCB/tolerance, expected scoped outcome fields, retention, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and replay. Log the complete scoped outcome algebra when execution occurs; manifest compilation itself never invents a scientific adjudication.

## Considerations
The manifest is metadata and obligation authority, not proof. unresolved/not-claimed ClaimAdjudication language requires an exact ClaimRevision and owned rationale; EvidenceCompleteness=partial is not a claim state.

title: V.1.2 Compile the complete frozen verification inventory from the source-authority lattice
description:
## Background
Manual parallel inventories drift. A naive generator is also unsafe if mutable Beads can override shipped contracts or if a new code registration can rewrite an old scientific receipt.

## Technical Approach
Build a deterministic inventory compiler over content-addressed snapshots of normalized Beads records, crate CONTRACT.md declarations, typed IR/catalog registries, code and test registrations, V&V artifacts, benchmark registry entries, and ledger receipts. Apply the V.1.1 authority lattice rather than last-writer-wins precedence. Emit explicit conflicts among obligation, declared semantics, executable registration, validation context, and observed evidence.

Reconcile aliases, renames, splits, merges, ClaimRevision supersession, and certified equivalence without losing historical lineage. Produce human, JSON, and ledger views as semantic projections of one canonical normalized graph and digest. Store the exact input snapshot set, compiler version, policy versions, conflict set, and output digest so later source edits cannot alter prior results.

## Success Criteria
Every live or historical ClaimRevision has one canonical identity and explicit verification owner. Additions, removals, conflicts, and semantic changes generate reviewable diffs. An old receipt resolves against its frozen source set. Heterogeneous views normalize to the same graph/digest and pass semantic-projection conformance; no false bit-for-bit promise is made across renderings.

## Test Plan
Golden miniature repositories; orphan, duplicate, rename, split, merge, supersession, certified equivalence, stale-code, and closed/refuted-history fixtures; Bead/contract/code/V&V/evidence conflicts; source mutation after receipt; unavailable historical snapshot; mutation tests for every adapter and authority rule; deterministic output across enumeration/thread variations; human/JSON/ledger semantic parity.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit source type, immutable snapshot/hash, authority role, adapter/compiler/policy versions, canonical identities, conflict and reconciliation decisions, normalized graph/digest, view projection hashes, diagnostics, immutable inventory artifact, and exact replay. Inventory compilation uses scoped Operation/Campaign receipts and never writes a favorable Job scientific result.

## Considerations
Generation is read-only with respect to sources. It must not invent defaults, discard closed/refuted history, infer implementation from a Bead, or let current metadata reinterpret historical evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured `acceptance_criteria` field contains the controlling, complete implementation/contribution, unit, E2E, logging, replay, source-closure, authority, and `NoData` close gate.
acceptance_criteria:
The canonical inventory must cover every Bead in the frozen input snapshot exactly once, including all 2,477 records in the 2026-07-30 baseline and every later added, removed, split, merged, superseded, or reopened diff. Each row classifies the Bead as hierarchy rollup, execution leaf, evidence contributor, independent checker, terminal E2E owner, or historical-only record; names exact source/contract/schema owners; names focused unit, boundary, property, metamorphic, mutation, compile, concurrency, cancellation, determinism, and negative-test owners or a typed not-applicable reason; names one E2E suite and case ID or the exact downstream gate that consumes its immutable contribution; names required log/reproduction fields, authority and no-claim boundary, estimate provenance, and direct dependencies. Generation fails on orphan scope, duplicate ownership, missing terminal owner, unmapped active leaf, contradictory authority, stale supersession, or aggregate-count-only closure. Human, JSON, and ledger views are semantic projections of one content-addressed graph. Closed or refuted history is retained, and a Bead description never proves implementation. Comprehensive test ownership and exact E2E/log mapping are mandatory inventory facts, not optional prose lint.

## Compiler contribution and no-terminal rationale

The phrase “terminal E2E owner” is a required field in each generated inventory row; it does not make this inventory compiler a terminal product-journey owner. This Bead is a compiler/evidence contributor consumed by the V.1 lint chain and `frankensim-leapfrog-2026-program-i94v.7.1.7`, whose exact route is `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/vision-promise-coverage.sh`. This Bead retains exhaustive unit/golden-repository/property/mutation/fault/logging/replay/source-closure integration proof for compilation and semantic projection, but owns no competing terminal script and cannot report downstream execution.

title: V.1.3 Enforce coverage, no-orphan, waiver-expiry, ambition, and no-claim lints
description:
## Background
Coverage percentages can be gamed unless missing tests, broad waivers, hidden skips, and weakened claim language fail closed.

## Technical Approach
Implement lints that require every execution leaf and exposed capability to map to appropriate unit/boundary/error, G0-G5, conformance, E2E, logging, retention, and replay obligations. Validate ambition tags against claim prose, require explicit core/max strata, expire waivers, and reject unresolved/not-claimed ClaimAdjudication entries without reason and effect on promotion.

## Success Criteria
A newly added uncovered leaf fails immediately; deleted or renamed cases cannot leave green ghosts; waivers have owner, narrow scope, expiry, and gate impact; ratchets can strengthen but cannot silently weaken statements.

## Test Plan
Seed one defect per rule: orphan, stale case, fake N/A, unbounded wildcard, expired waiver, unnamed skip, ambition downgrade, missing negative/cancel/replay case, and dangling gate. Require minimized diagnostics.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
Not every schema-only leaf needs every Gauntlet tier, but omission must be semantically justified and reviewable—not inferred from labels.

title: V.1.4 Specify independent fixture, oracle, golden, license, migration, and tamper protocol
description:
## Background
A test can faithfully reproduce the same bug if production and checker share formulas, fixtures, tolerance logic, or serialization assumptions.

## Technical Approach
Define FixtureReceipt, OracleReceipt, GoldenReceipt, TcbOverlapReport, LicensePolicy, MigrationReceipt, and TamperVerdict. Require independent analytic, exhaustive-small, high-precision, alternate-discretization, physical, or formally checked oracles as appropriate. Record generator/checker separation, raw bytes, normalization, tolerance arithmetic, license/export restrictions, schema history, signatures/hashes, and immutable legacy views.

## Success Criteria
Promotion cannot consume an oracle with undeclared circularity; protected or secret data cannot leak; old artifacts remain interpretable without rewriting history; corruption and unauthorized mutation fail closed.

## Test Plan
Same-bug oracle fixture; adversarial tolerance inflation; raw/normalized mismatch; license denial; stale signature; truncated and oversized artifact; migration round trip and non-migratable refusal; bit-flip localization.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
TCB independence is graduated and explicit, never a boolean marketing claim. Dev-only external references remain outside production dependencies.

title: V.1.5 Define deterministic claim-stratum, campaign-profile, filter, budget, capability, and sharding metadata
description:
## Background
Core and Max are claim/capability strata, while smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release describe campaign intensity and evidence obligations. Mixing them into one tier makes a soak run ambiguously change scientific scope, and invisible selection changes across hardware, filters, budgets, or workers can silently omit cases.

## Technical Approach
Define two orthogonal, versioned axes: the stratum enum {core, max} selects the declared claim and capability surface. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Deterministically expand stratum, profiles, filters, capabilities, accuracy/time/memory/sample budgets, expected artifacts, timeout/cancellation policy, named skip predicates, and shard assignments over stable Claim/Case/Journey identities. Emit a canonical selection and semantic-diff receipt before execution; estimates do not run production computation.

Legacy SMOKE/MID/FULL names exist only inside V.4.6 adapters. They cannot silently alias a stratum/profile pair: the adapter must reconcile selected cases, claims, budgets, capabilities, acceptance rules, and artifacts or refuse with a ranked migration.

## Success Criteria
The same manifest and capabilities select the same logical cases independent of enumeration, worker count, or presentation. Stratum/profile/budget/capability/filter changes produce exact diffs. Profile selection cannot upgrade or downgrade scientific scope. No case disappears silently, and an empty or unsupported selection is explicitly non-green.

## Test Plan
Unit/property tests cover stratum and profile schemas, valid/invalid composition, permutation/thread/shard union-disjointness, filter algebra, boundary budgets, capability routing, timeout/cancel semantics, deterministic selection hashes, estimate calibration, and adversarial empty selection. E2E mutation tests swap Core/Max, add/remove profiles, misuse legacy aliases, change a profile's claim set, omit a shard/case, and require fail-closed semantic diff.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit stable Claim/Case/Journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, explicit stratum and one atomic CampaignProfileId plus any frozen composite-input expansion, selection/filter expansion, seed/logical work identity, budgets, capabilities/flags, machine/mode, shard plan, named skip predicates, expected artifacts, legacy mapping receipt where applicable, scoped outcome product and promotion effect. Retain canonical selection, semantic diff, cost estimate, discrepancies, and exact replay. No unnamed skip or proof-critical sampling is allowed.

## Considerations
Wall-clock scheduling may vary in fast mode, but logical identity, selection, and promotion effect remain ledgered. Profiles may grow through versioned manifests; adding a profile never changes old meanings.

title: V.1.6 Independently adjudicate manifest coverage, migration, omission, and drift
description:
## Background
The manifest compiler and its lints are themselves certifiers and require an independent falsification path.

## Technical Approach
Build a separately owned checker that reconstructs the leaf/claim/case graph from immutable inputs, compares it with generated output, mutates each required field, exercises schema migrations, and issues a VerificationManifestReceipt with exact coverage and unresolved exceptions.

## Success Criteria
Zero unowned execution leaves or public claims; every omission is intentional, narrow, and gate-visible; drift and migration defects are minimized and retained; checker TCB overlap is disclosed.

## Test Plan
Independent graph walk; randomized rename/split/merge histories; field-deletion mutations; stale cache and reordered input; waiver expiry; malformed and hostile manifest; deterministic replay from clean artifact store.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/verification-manifest-independent-adjudication.toml`. No-mock independent driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/verification-manifest-independent-adjudication.sh`. Separately retained canonical execution is `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite verification-manifest-independent-adjudication --stratum core --profile standard`. The compiler and separately owned checker start from immutable source snapshots and an empty generated inventory. A missing path, divergent selection, bypass, or incomplete receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
This receipt validates manifest integrity, not the scientific truth of listed claims.

title: Compile and independently adjudicate the immutable README and plan VisionPromise inventory
description:
Purpose: close the gap between implementation-oriented verification inventories and the complete normative product/science vision. Preserve every promise from README.md, COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FRANKENSIM.md, COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md, COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_TO_EXTEND_FRANKENSIM_TO_NEW_DOMAINS.md, the capability-maturity registry, milestone declarations, and public schema/policy sources without silently merging, weakening, or dropping any feature.

Freeze exact content-addressed source revisions. Compile every normative user outcome, invariant, crate/domain promise, flagship, performance target, ambition-tagged capability, roadmap exit criterion, activation trigger, kill trigger, and no-claim boundary into a stable VisionPromiseId and revisioned statement. Classify each atom as current-state fact, aspirational, conditional horizon, explicit no-claim, superseded-with-lineage, or historical-only.

Map every atom to exactly one owning Bead or a ratified deferral with owner, reason, trigger, falsifier, budget, WIP bound, expiry/review point, and user-visible effect. Name the unit/property/metamorphic/integration test owner, terminal E2E owner, structured-log owner, artifact-only replay owner, DSR proof lane, and promotion/admission authority, or a typed reason why a category does not apply. Emit explicit NO_BEAD, PARTIAL, OPEN, CLOSED_HISTORICAL, INVALIDATED, PROVEN_CURRENT, and DEFERRED_RATIFIED states; closed historical work never counts as current proof by status alone.

Own scripts/e2e/leapfrog/vision-promise-coverage.sh with --list, --check, --self-test, --run, --negative, and artifact-only --replay modes. The harness must be deterministic, no-mock for the public source/Beads path, bounded, redacted, schema-versioned, and produce copy-pasteable repository-relative reproduction commands plus retained source closure and first-divergence evidence.

Adversarially test missing, duplicate, merged, split, renamed, weakened, ambition-downgraded, source-moved, stale, contradictory, superseded, and authority-laundered promises. Independent adjudication must compare exact source-set and VisionPromiseId equality and refuse publication on omission, ambiguity, stale source identity, expired waiver, or replay disagreement.

No-claim boundary: this inventory proves traceability and plan completeness. It does not prove that an implementation exists, that science is valid, that performance targets are met, or that a capability may be promoted.

The structured acceptance_criteria field is controlling. It preserves the complete unit, boundary, property, metamorphic, mutation, fault, cancellation, integration, terminal E2E, structured-log, artifact-only replay, source-closure, DSR, authority, and no-claim close gate for this Bead.
