title: V.5 USER & AGENT WORKBENCH — discoverability, teaching diagnostics, progressive disclosure, and accessibility
description:
## Background
World-class solvers remain unusable if people cannot discover valid workflows, preflight their environment, inspect assumptions, understand cost, repair invalid models, control long work, interpret scientific visualizations and timelines honestly, or consume results accessibly. Scripted UX tests are necessary but cannot alone establish that representative users comprehend claim boundaries and make safe decisions.

## Technical Approach
Define persona and journey grammar for first-time learners, educators, engineers, researchers, validation/safety/compliance leads, manufacturing/test operators, site/release operators, independent auditors, compute/data owners, theorem researchers, assistive-technology users, and agents. Generate discovery, examples, help, and completions from typed catalogs; provide a side-effect-free point-in-time doctor and redacted support bundle; expose inspectable defaults and ranked repairs; enforce human/agent parity, accessibility, non-TTY behavior, and truthful static/temporal scientific visualization with image/data/timeline/report parity.

Maintain two non-substitutable evidence lanes:
1. deterministic no-mock unit/E2E/accessibility/mutation tests prove interface contracts, semantic parity, recovery, and replay;
2. preregistered, consented, independently facilitated user studies measure task completion, severe-error rate, time/assistance, comprehension of units/assumptions/claim/evidence state, safe-decision accuracy, recovery/handoff, and accessibility with representative participants.

Human preference or completion never upgrades scientific ClaimAdjudication. Study data is minimized, consented, redacted, retention-bounded, and not collected as telemetry by default. Build executable Core and post-adjudication MAX tutorial branches for all twenty families.

## Success Criteria
Users reach first valid result and actionable diagnostic within preregistered p50/p95/p99 SLOs, monitor fresh progress, receive cancel acknowledgement, recover lost jobs, repair seeded failures, inspect consequential defaults/transforms, distinguish operation success from job/claim evidence, and reproduce/share safely. Experts retain full controls. Assistive and agent surfaces preserve load-bearing meaning. Representative-user evidence meets preregistered safety/comprehension thresholds or creates an explicit UX restriction.

## Test Plan
Persona no-mock journeys cover first use, expert research, operations, audit, offline/missing capability, invalid input/repair, cost surprise, durable recovery, accessibility/non-TTY/locale/path/focus/zoom/reduced motion, static and temporal visualization truth, exact restricted claims versus incomplete evidence, protected sharing, Core/MAX tutorials, replay, and mutations of defaults, diagnostics, help, transforms, SLO accounting, and human/agent parity.

Run separately preregistered studies with novice, domain-expert, validation/safety, auditor, and assistive-tech cohorts using blinded counterbalanced tasks where appropriate. Record completion, error severity, unsafe decisions, assistance, comprehension, recovery, and handoff; report failures/censoring and uncertainty, not averages alone.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

## Considerations
Progressive disclosure organizes the full system; it never removes functionality or weakens claims. Doctor readiness is not admission or scientific validity. Visualization and tutorial success are not proof. Human-study participation is voluntary and privacy-preserving.

title: V.5.1 Define personas, journey grammar, progressive disclosure, inspectable defaults, and UX-study protocol
description:
## Background
A single expert-only interface excludes new users, while simplification that hides physics assumptions is dangerous. Synthetic persona walkthroughs also need representative-user validation for comprehension and safe decision-making.

## Technical Approach
Define first-time learner/educator, engineer, researcher, validation/safety/compliance lead, manufacturing partner, test operator, site/release operator, independent auditor, compute/data owner, theorem researcher, assistive-technology user, and agent personas. Specify authority, privacy/license responsibility, handoff, and discovery→intent→doctor→estimate→author/import→repair→submit→observe/control→inspect/verify→share/replay grammar.

Basic, advanced, and expert views are projections of one typed state. Every inferred material, regime, solver, tolerance, unit, frame, clock, temporal transform, budget, capability, ClaimRevision, evidence method/grade, applicability/support, and no-claim default is inspectable and ledgered with source, rationale, domain, and override route.

Define a preregistered independent UX-study protocol: recruitment strata, inclusion/accessibility needs, tasks and seeded hazards, counterbalancing/blinding where appropriate, facilitator script, allowable assistance, severe-error taxonomy, completion and safe-decision measures, comprehension questions, stopping rules, analysis, uncertainty, censoring/failure accounting, privacy/consent, data minimization, retention, deletion, and redaction. No telemetry-by-default or coercive product instrumentation. Human evidence uses canonical EvidenceMethodSet values validated-empirical or empirical-only plus a versioned UX domain/submethod tag; it cannot establish physics or theorems.

## Success Criteria
Every persona has complete happy, failure, recovery, and handoff paths. Disclosure changes no hidden semantics. Preregistered p50/p95/p99 first-result, diagnostic, progress, cancel, reconnect, repair, and share SLOs have explicit host/cohort scope. Human studies can be independently reproduced or audited without exposing participant identity.

## Test Plan
Deterministic persona walkthroughs; hidden-default and disclosure-level semantic mutations; incomplete input; cost escalation; unresolved claim/outside-domain/missing support; cancel/reconnect; agent/human parity; accessibility. Study-protocol tests cover missing consent, unbalanced tasks, facilitator drift, privacy leak, selective exclusion, unreported assistance/failure, unsafe-decision scoring, small-sample uncertainty, retention expiry, and synthetic dry runs before participants.

## Detailed logging and evidence
For automated journeys emit scoped identities/outcomes, defaults, disclosure state, diagnostics, lifecycle, accessibility, artifacts, and replay. For studies emit pseudonymous Study/Protocol/Cohort/Task IDs, preregistration hash, consent/version, accessibility accommodation, task timing/assistance/error/comprehension/safe-decision measures, censoring, analysis version, aggregate uncertainty, privacy/redaction/retention receipts, and audit artifact—never unnecessary raw identity or passive telemetry.

## Considerations
Progressive disclosure reduces cognitive load, never epistemic honesty. UX evidence and scientific evidence remain different methods in the outcome algebra.

title: V.5.10 Enforce truthful spatial and temporal scientific visualization, uncertainty, accessibility, and data parity
description:
## Background
A beautiful image or smooth animation can be semantically false: hidden clipping, bad colormap, missing units, unmarked transforms, omitted NaNs, wrong vector frame, temporal aliasing, interpolation across an impact/reset/topology change, phase-wrap error, or a dropped event frame can change a user's conclusion. Geneva drives, Wankel-like contact, commutation, impacts, and multiphysics clocks make temporal truth load-bearing.

## Technical Approach
Define one ScientificVisualizationSpec/Receipt for interactive views, animations, static images, timelines, reports, and agent data exports. Type quantity, unit/kind, spatial frame/orientation/chart, component/basis, fidelity/regime, support, aggregation, spatial reconstruction, uncertainty/evidence, missing/invalid/out-of-domain semantics, range/normalization/clipping, transform, colormap/glyph/tensor conventions, topology/occlusion, camera/projection/selection, accessibility, and source lineage.

Add a TemporalPresentationSpec:
- distinguish solver step/time, modeled physical time, experiment/DAQ clock, controller clock, wall time, and presentation/playback time;
- retain exact sample/event timestamps, time basis/units, adaptive-step history, synchronization transform and uncertainty;
- declare resampling/filter/anti-alias/interpolation method and validity domain;
- forbid interpolation across reset, impact, contact-mode, discontinuity, topology, commutation, or branch events unless an explicit physically justified operator and receipt exists;
- type periodic phase, unwrap/wrap convention, cycle identity, and Floquet/orbit alignment;
- align asynchronous multi-rate streams with explicit clock uncertainty/gaps;
- record playback speed, cadence, frame IDs, source sample ranges, dropped/duplicated/coalesced frames, event markers, temporal uncertainty, and data/timeline parity.

Rendering may drop presentation frames for responsiveness only if Gap events and counters remain visible and the underlying timeline/data artifact is complete. It may never drop the only representation of a scientific event or smooth across it silently.

Require distinct encodings and data equivalents for uncertainty, bounds, discretization error, invalid cells, NaN/Inf, masks, unsampled/extrapolated regions, topology changes, mixed-fidelity seams, and temporal gaps. Use perceptually appropriate colorblind-safe defaults, redundant cues, keyboard/focus/zoom/reflow, reduced-motion/no-flash, meaningful summaries, and downloadable tables/slices/timelines. Deterministic mode fixes view/sample/tie/label decisions.

Exact suite: 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/scientific-visualization.toml', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/scientific-visualization.sh', and separate concrete runs 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite scientific-visualization --stratum core --profile standard' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite scientific-visualization --stratum max --profile release'.

## Success Criteria
A reviewer reconstructs every pixel/glyph/curve/frame and its source time/data; audits units/frames/clocks/transforms/ranges/evidence/gaps; obtains data- and timeline-equivalent representations; and reproduces the view. No default hides invalid, uncertain, clipped, temporally aliased, or dropped-event data. Human, agent, image, animation, timeline, and report semantics agree. Latency/artifact SLOs never remove load-bearing annotations.

## Test Plan
Unit/property/conformance tests cover unit/frame/time transforms, ranges/clipping, log domain, NaN/mask propagation, uncertainty, basis changes, camera hashes, time monotonicity, adaptive resampling, multi-rate alignment, clock uncertainty, phase wrapping, interpolation validity, event barriers, frame accounting, accessibility, and semantic/data/image/timeline parity.

No-mock E2E covers scalar/vector/tensor/complex/topological and mixed-fidelity fields; outliers; changed units/moving frames; impacts/resets/contact/topology/commutation; periodic phase; incomplete/ensemble data; narrow/non-TTY/screen reader/reduced motion; report/share/redaction; deterministic rerender. Mutations change cadence, drop/duplicate the only event frame, smooth across discontinuity, alias high-frequency motion, swap clocks, change phase wrap, present same image with different timeline, create smooth animation that hides an event, and alter data without image; all must fail truth parity. Independently compare engineering decisions from raw data and views.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit Visualization/TemporalPresentation specs, source field/artifact hashes, units/frames/clocks, sample/event times, synchronization/interpolation/filter provenance, uncertainty, range/clipping/mask/NaN counts, phase/cycle, frame-source mapping, dropped/duplicated/gap counters, camera/selection, image/data/timeline/spec hashes, accessibility audit, timings/memory, scoped outcomes, diagnostics, and replay. Numeric, semantic, temporal, and image goldens are retained together; critical events are lossless.

## Considerations
Visualization is an epistemic interface, not proof. Semantic and temporal truth take precedence over drama, while expert rendering controls remain fully available through explicit specs.

title: V.5.11 Build executable MAX expert/research tutorial branches and theorem outcome field guide
description:
## Background
Core tutorials teach honest first success and recovery, but merely linking to maximal features would leave the most ambitious mechanisms, electromechanics, materials, experiments, periodic dynamics, and theorem ratchets as folklore. ## Success Criteria

Every MAX branch is tied to exact J2/final receipt, exposes assumptions/cost/domain/evidence, handles non-established outcomes honestly, and reproduces from clean artifacts. Core remains usable independently. Summit self-documentation waits for complete expert corpus, field guide, accessibility, and agent parsing.

## Test Plan
Run every branch under standard plus required stronger profiles. Mutate selector/stratum/profile, ClaimRevision/relation/hypotheses, capabilities/budgets/defaults, commands, scoped outcome assertions, diagnostics, runtime witness/fallback, artifact/redaction/accessibility, and J2/final linkage. Exercise unsupported hardware/licenses/data, counterexample/unresolved paths, cancel/checkpoint/pause/resume/migrate, corrupt/partial evidence, stale disposition, agent-only and non-TTY, Core semantic diff, and clean replay. ## Considerations
This task increases accessible power without simplifying the science. A tutorial may teach refutation, unresolved domains, or a sharper restricted theorem when that is the strongest honest result.

title: V.5.4 Enforce non-TTY, color-independent, screen-reader, width, Unicode, locale, and stable-JSON accessibility
description:
## Background
Scientific information must remain available to users with assistive technology and to automation outside a rich terminal.

All load-bearing state and diagnostics are available without color, pointer, animation, or a particular width; screen-reader and agent order is meaningful; locale cannot alter parsed quantities or hashes.

title: V.5.5 Independently adjudicate CORE workbench correctness, accessibility, and representative-user safety
description:
## Background
Core journeys need proof that discovery, repair, cost visibility, durable control, and result interpretation work across machine surfaces and representative people—not merely that backend computation succeeds.

## Technical Approach
Independently execute deterministic no-mock Core persona journeys through catalog, doctor, template authoring, invalid repair, estimate, submission/admission, disconnect/recovery, cancel, visualization/timeline inspection, verify/share, and replay in TTY, non-TTY, assistive, and agent JSON modes. Audit hidden defaults, scoped receipts, and accessibility. Publish the automated CoreUxContractReceipt.

Separately run the preregistered V.5.1 user study with first-time users, domain engineers, validation/safety/audit participants, and assistive-technology users. Independent facilitators measure completion, severe errors, unsafe scientific decisions, time, assistance, comprehension of units/assumptions/ClaimAdjudication/evidence/support, recovery after seeded faults, handoff, and confidence calibration. Publish a privacy-preserving CoreUxHumanEvidenceReceipt. The CoreUxReceipt references both without treating human success as scientific proof.

title: V.5.6 Run hostile-input, cancellation, resume, Unknown, partial-evidence, and high-complexity usability drills
description:
## Background
Usability often collapses precisely when simulations are expensive, partial, contradictory, or failing.

## Technical Approach
Exercise maximal models, many diagnostics, long-running progress, topology/regime changes, conflicting evidence, unresolved/refuted/not-claimed ClaimAdjudication, hardware/license gaps, cancellation/resume, corrupted artifacts, and partial visualization/export. Measure diagnostic latency, information overload, log volume, repair quality, and recovery success for human and agent modes.

## Success Criteria
Complex and adverse states remain navigable; progress is honest; cancellation produces a useful final receipt; partial evidence is visible but cannot be mistaken for Pass; repair choices expose tradeoffs.

## Test Plan
Stress personas, diagnostic storms, slow/failed backend, stale checkpoint, conflicting oracle, unsupported hardware, corrupted bundle, cancel/resume, screen-reader/non-TTY at scale.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Use schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable run/shard/journey/case/op identities; manifest, code, contract, and schema hashes; Five Explicits; capabilities and feature flags; deterministic mode and machine fingerprint; oracle/checker identity and TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; progress, budgets, cancellation/fault schedule, scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and minimized witness. Pretty output is only a rendering of these events. Logs are bounded, redacted, and backpressure-safe.

## Considerations
Do not optimize away scientifically necessary complexity; organize it and provide drilldown.

description:
## Background
Examples become dangerous when decorative, stale, failure-free, or assumption-hiding. The twenty Core journeys need an executable first-success and recovery curriculum; MAX expert/research branches remain separate and post-adjudication.

## Technical Approach
Create one progressive Core tutorial and failure-cookbook branch for each fifteen initiative and five theorem family from the frozen manifest and exact J1 receipt. Each begins with intent; runs doctor/capability preflight; declares Five Explicits, Core stratum, and concrete smoke/standard profile; shows estimate and defaults; submits through production lifecycle; watches/reconnects and recovers identity; explains Operation versus Job/Campaign receipt and exact ClaimRecord/adjudication/evidence/support; injects one realistic mistake and ranked repair; demonstrates cancel/checkpoint/pause/resume and replay; inspects/verifies/shares artifacts; and links to the separate MAX branch.

Sources live under 'examples/leapfrog/<family>/'. The generated aggregate manifest is 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/tutorials-core.toml' and no-mock driver is 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/tutorials-core.sh'. title: V.5.9 Build first-run environment doctor, capability preflight, and generated CLI help
description:
## Background
First use needs an honest answer about whether this installation, host, data environment, license set, artifact store, and feature configuration appear ready. Trial-and-error admission wastes time. Handwritten help/completion/migration guidance also drifts from typed command and capability schemas.

## Technical Approach
Implement a read-only, side-effect-free first-run doctor and capability viewer across CLI and agent API. Generate help, examples, manpage/reference fragments, completions, deprecation notices, and migration hints from the V.4.2 typed grammar and capability/diagnostic catalog.

Inspect installed artifact and schema/contract versions; runtime versus developer/DSR prerequisites; ISA/topology, memory, disk, devices; deterministic envelope; artifact-store permissions/quota/integrity; material/standard/benchmark datasets and license/expiry; declared network needs; feature/moonshot gates; checkpoint/replay compatibility; locale/Unicode/path/CWD/non-TTY behavior; and requested selector/stratum/profile budgets/capabilities. Return stable diagnostics and ranked non-destructive repairs with cost, semantic, privacy, security, and claim impact. Never auto-install, mutate config, reveal secrets, probe unrelated resources, or imply readiness is validity.

Doctor findings are point-in-time advisory OperationReceipts bound to exact probe time and snapshots. They are never admission authority. V.4.9 transactionally revalidates/pins capabilities, quota, device, datasets, licenses, and policy at admission and reports later revocation distinctly. Support offline mode and a redacted shareable support bundle.

Exact no-mock ownership: 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/environment-doctor.toml', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/environment-doctor.sh', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh doctor', and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh capabilities'. A target-specific check uses the typed selector/stratum/profile grammar without executing science.

## Success Criteria
A first-time user, site operator, or agent can distinguish ready, outside-domain, unsupported, misconfigured, expired, and unknown findings before submission. Every finding names evidence, affected surfaces, safe verification/repair, scope, and expiry. Human/JSON help and completions derive from one grammar. No undeclared side effects, secret/license payload leakage, or favorable TOCTOU assumption. Freeze p50/p95/p99 diagnostic latency and support-bundle size SLOs.

## Test Plan
Unit tests cover every probe/capability/diagnostic/repair, output projection, generated help/completion, expiry, and migration. No-mock E2E covers healthy/minimal/offline/air-gapped installations; stale binary/schema/data/license; unsupported ISA/device; read-only/full/quota stores; corrupt cache; network/feature/determinism gaps; spaces/quotes/Unicode/arbitrary CWD/non-TTY/broken pipe/restricted environment; secret canaries; conflicting repairs; and agent parity. Race tests cover doctor-green then license expiry, quota consumption, device removal, dataset/policy change before/during submit and require V.4.9 revalidation. Mutations make a failed prerequisite appear green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit DoctorRun/Probe/Capability/Diagnostic/Repair/GeneratedHelp/Redaction Operation events with grammar/catalog/source hashes, probe timestamp/authority/side-effect class, host and dependency snapshots/expiry, requested selector/stratum/profiles, duration, evidence hash, DomainApplicability/OperationalSupport, ranked repair consequences, redaction, support-bundle artifact, and exact rerun. Doctor does not emit a scientific Job ClaimAdjudication.

## Considerations
Runtime, developer, DSR-worker, and scientific readiness differ. V.4.9 owns lifecycle-native admission checks; this bead owns user-facing diagnosis/help/support. Both consume one typed model without duplicate probes or semantics.

description:

## Success Criteria
Each promotion names exact DSR lane, stratum/profiles, run/shard identities, artifact closure, and scoped receipt. Skipped, flaky, unsupported, killed, or uninstrumented paths cannot green. Supported Apple Silicon and many-core x86 evidence is comparable within declared determinism/performance classes. ## Test Plan

Exercise every supported direct/chained/skip migration and rolling mixed-version matrix, unknown future fields, disk-full/power-loss at each journal boundary, repeated retry, concurrent old/new writers, backup corruption and restore, rollback where admitted, and semantic replay of pre-upgrade immutable receipts.

title: V.7 FIFTEEN INITIATIVE VERIFICATION JOURNEYS — pre-promotion batteries and post-promotion user proof
description:
## Background
The extension portfolio requires executable unit and end-to-end proof per scientific feature cluster. Shared infrastructure cannot by itself prove that each initiative selected the right laws, independent oracles, adversarial cases, capability boundaries, or user workflow. Conversely, a local scientific gate can be sound while the capability remains impossible for a human or agent to discover, estimate, operate, interrupt, interpret, repair, or replay.

This rollup preserves all fifteen initiatives separately. It adds a uniform proof-and-experience skeleton without flattening their domain-specific mathematics, maximal research branches, or no-claim boundaries.

## Technical Approach
Create one family rollup for I01, I02, I04, I08, I12, I15, I03, I07, I13, I14, I05, I06, I10, I11, and I09. Every family owns five independently closable receipts:

1. T1: Core-stratum unit, boundary, error-path, property, metamorphic, manufactured-solution, conformance, independent-oracle, and certifier-of-certifier coverage.
2. T2: Core-stratum production-path E2E under smoke and standard profiles, consumed directly by that initiative's G4/Core adjudication.
3. T3: Max-stratum unit plus production-path E2E under standard and release profiles, extended by admitted adversarial, soak, security, chaos, and cross-ISA campaigns, consumed directly by that initiative's G7/MAX adjudication.
4. J1: a post-Core human-and-agent journey using the Core stratum and an explicit campaign profile.
5. J2: a post-MAX expert/research journey using the Max stratum and explicit standard/release or stronger admitted profiles.

Scientific claim scope and campaign intensity are orthogonal. Every executable invocation selects one stratum from the enum {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Profiles may intensify workload, faults, platforms, and evidence obligations but may never silently change the ClaimRecord, its exact domain, or its quantifiers. Core and MAX gates depend on T2 and T3 respectively; user journeys consume the resulting adjudications and never circularly prove the underlying science. Each initiative root depends on its family rollup so closure includes operability and honest communication.

Every T2, T3, J1, and J2 leaf names its exact family manifest under 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/<family>.toml', its no-mock driver under 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/<family>.sh', and a concrete invocation through 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run'. T1 receipts name the same family artifacts where integration is required while retaining direct Rust test ownership. All surfaces compile to the same typed VerificationProtocol request and compare selection hashes, causal identities, events, artifacts, receipts, and process projections.

## Success Criteria
All fifteen families retain their distinct physical laws, theorem boundaries, material/interchange semantics, fixtures, oracles, mutations, and maximal branches. Each has exactly five receipts with deterministic selection, positive/boundary/invalid/adversarial cases, comprehensive unit and integration coverage, production-path E2E, accessibility and stable agent output, DSR qualification, bounded structured logs, immutable closure, exact replay, and independently adjudicated promotion dependencies.

No maximal research blocks an honestly useful Core capability. No Core result is presented as MAX. No unsupported hardware, license, material data, oracle, or topology silently passes. The scoped receipt product always distinguishes ExecutionDisposition; RequestedPredicateOutcome; ClaimAdjudication={established, refuted, unresolved, not-claimed}; EvidenceMethodSet and EpistemicGrade; DomainApplicability; OperationalSupport; EvidenceCompleteness; EvidenceIntegrity; and PromotionEffect. EvidenceCompleteness=partial is never a scientific truth value. Unsupported is rendered only from applicability/support fields. A weaker or restricted discovery is a separate exact ClaimRecord connected by independently checked implication, refinement, restriction, or counterexample relations.

## Test Plan
Mechanically verify all fifteen rollups have exactly five direct receipts and the intended parent-to-child dependency direction. Assert every T2 directly blocks its exact G4/Core gate, every T3 directly blocks its exact G7/MAX gate, J1 consumes Core evidence, J2 consumes MAX evidence, and no user journey creates a promotion cycle.

For every family, require focused Rust unit tests for happy, boundary, empty, maximal, invalid, dimensional, deterministic-tie, serialization, and error cases; doctests and executable examples; compile-fail/UI and type-invariant tests where misuse must be unrepresentable; property and metamorphic laws; manufactured solutions; independent analytic, exhaustive, high-precision, or alternate-formulation checks; mutation and certifier attacks; deterministic concurrency/model-checking where scheduling matters; and Miri, sanitizer, fuzz, or explicitly justified equivalent evidence for unsafe or hardware-sensitive boundaries.

Run no-mock production-path E2E scripts covering list/doctor, plan, estimate, submit, watch/reattach, checkpoint/pause/migrate where supported, cancel/drain/finalize, resume/fork, inspect, verify, report/share, corrupt/tamper, and clean-store replay. Exercise explicit stratum/profile products, arbitrary working directories, non-TTY and stable JSONL modes, concurrent clients, signal/process/worker/storage/network faults, and authorization/capability gaps. Delete or mutate a required graph edge, manifest field, script, scoped receipt field, claim relation, oracle identity, tolerance derivation, capability predicate, artifact, or replay pointer and require fail-closed adjudication.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Every receipt emits stable ClaimId and ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, ExecutionScopeId, TileId, CheckpointId, and ArtifactId as applicable, plus typed causal edges. Emit frozen manifest/code/contract/schema/fixture hashes; units, frames, clocks, seed, and logical work identity; requested and consumed budgets; capabilities and flags; machine/ISA/thread/mode fingerprint; oracle/checker and trusted-computing-base overlap; tolerance derivation and arithmetic; progress, residual, balance, conservation, uncertainty, and error summaries; lifecycle, fault, cancellation, drain, and finalize events.

Emit the full scoped outcome product: ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect. Retain ClaimRelationReceipts, diagnostics and ranked repairs, artifacts, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, reports, and exact reconnect/replay pointers. OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt remain separately addressable; only the current OperationReceipt projects to the caller's process status.

Logs are schema-versioned, deterministic where claimed, bounded, redacted by declared policy, backpressure-safe, and available in semantically equivalent pretty and stable JSONL forms. Proof- and promotion-critical events are lossless and never sampled away. Large or sensitive payloads are committed content-addressed objects rather than dumped inline.

## Considerations
The post-gate journeys establish usability, recovery, interpretation, and claim honesty; they do not retroactively prove the science. Pre-promotion receipts are the evidence consumed by scientific gates. Stronger discoveries remain admissible through versioned ClaimRecords, independently certified relations, and independent checkers. Legacy suite names are accepted only through semantic-diff adapters and never redefine the two-axis contract.

title: I14.J1 CORE post-promotion human/agent user journey receipt
description:
## Background
The admitted core EMC harness, MTL, PEEC, transmission-line, and full-wave escalation ladder must be usable by a representative engineer and a schema-driven agent without author-only knowledge.

## Technical Approach
Blindly execute a cable/harness victim-source problem through semantic topology, RLGC/MTL and PEEC routing, termination/shield changes, cross-rung correlation, mitigation ranking, budget/cancel/replay and report. Discover an example, inspect assumptions/defaults/cost, repair a seeded invalid input, cancel/resume, interpret units/evidence/no-claim state, export/share under policy, and replay. Cover TTY, non-TTY, colorless/accessibility-relevant and stable JSON presentations.

## Success Criteria
The workflow completes with useful deterministic diagnostics; no hidden semantic change; human and agent state agree; all load-bearing visual information has textual/queryable form; receipt consumes I14.G4.

## Test Plan
First-run/expert, malformed, cost surprise, repair ranking, cancel/resume, narrow/locale/non-TTY, redacted share, stale artifact, deterministic replay and independent review.

Cross-cutting completeness requirements: conduct blind no-mock human and agent journeys from discovery and doctor through inspectable defaults, plan/estimate, durable submission, progress/watch, disconnect/reattach, result interpretation, diagnostics and ranked repair, cancel/drain, supported resume, report/share/redact, offline verify, and exact replay. Cover a successful case, boundary case, malformed request, scientific refutation or unresolved result, missing capability/license/data/policy, budget exhaustion, client/service/worker interruption, corrupt artifact, narrow/non-TTY/color-independent/screen-reader operation, arbitrary CWD, and stable JSONL parsing. Compare human, CLI, Rust API, FrankenScript, and supported WASM selections, events, artifacts, scoped receipts, and process projections. Mutate a hidden default, unit/frame/clock, diagnostic ranking, selector, receipt field, artifact, or replay pointer and require visible fail-closed behavior.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/i14-emc.toml`. No-mock family journey: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/i14-emc.sh`. Canonical executions are `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster i14-emc --stratum core --profile standard` and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster i14-emc --stratum core --profile smoke`; the separately retained smoke CampaignRun covers first-run, constrained-budget, non-TTY, and rapid diagnostic paths. The journey consumes the exact Core adjudication and cannot promote the science it demonstrates.

## Detailed logging
Every execution emits stable ClaimId/ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, ExecutionScopeId, TileId, CheckpointId, and ArtifactId as applicable, plus typed causal edges; manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, units/frames/clocks, seed and logical work identity, budgets, capabilities/flags, machine fingerprint/mode, oracle and TCB overlap, tolerance arithmetic, progress/residual/balance/error summaries, scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, diagnostics and ranked repairs; retained content-addressed artifacts; FailureBundles and minimized witnesses; process projection; and exact reconnect/replay pointers through the shared fs-obs/FailureBundle contract. Proof-, safety-, and promotion-critical events are lossless; large or sensitive payloads are committed before pointer emission and policy-redacted.

## Considerations
Usability evidence cannot upgrade the already-adjudicated scientific claim.

title: I05 VERIFICATION JOURNEY — HIL, WCET, and fixed-point twin compiler
description:
## Background
I05 requires domain-owned pre-promotion tests and post-promotion workflows in addition to the shared verification spine.

## User journey
A human or agent must be able to compile a model for a pinned target, inspect quantization and schedule risk, run SIL/PIL/HIL, and distinguish measured timing from formal WCET. Every assumption, unit/frame/clock, inferred default, cost, capability, evidence state, and no-claim boundary remains inspectable and ledgered.

## Technical Approach
Own exactly five independently closable receipts: T1 Core unit/property/metamorphic/conformance; T2 Core-stratum smoke/standard-profile no-mock E2E consumed by the exact G4; T3 Max-stratum unit plus standard/release-profile E2E, extended by admitted adversarial/soak/security/chaos/cross-ISA campaigns consumed by exact G7; J1 post-core human/agent journey; and J2 post-max expert/research journey. Use the family manifest and script named above with an explicit stratum selected from {core, max} and separately manifest-admitted profiles. Each receipt carries oracle/TCB separation, scoped outcome product, durable lifecycle, bounded structured evidence, DSR identity, cancellation/finalization, and replay.

## Receipt structure
T1 Core-stratum unit/property/metamorphic/conformance; T2 Core-stratum smoke/standard-profile production-path E2E consumed by I05.G4; T3 Max-stratum unit plus standard/release-profile E2E, extended by admitted adversarial/soak/security/chaos/cross-ISA campaigns consumed by I05.G7; J1 post-core human/agent workflow; J2 post-max expert/research workflow.

## Executable paths
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/i05-hil-wcet.toml`.
No-mock family driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/i05-hil-wcet.sh`.
Concrete Core executions: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster i05-hil-wcet --stratum core --profile smoke` and a separate `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster i05-hil-wcet --stratum core --profile standard` receipt.
Concrete MAX executions: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster i05-hil-wcet --stratum max --profile standard` and a separate `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster i05-hil-wcet --stratum max --profile release` receipt. Adversarial, soak, security, chaos, and cross-ISA profiles each execute as separate manifest-admitted campaigns when required; no shell pipeline notation is used.

## Success Criteria
Five independently replayable receipts with exact DSR identity, bounded schema-valid JSONL, oracle/TCB and tolerance arithmetic, FailureBundle, cancellation/resume, accessibility/agent parity, retention, and gate effect. No unnamed skip or hidden favorable fallback.

## Test Plan
Mechanically run and reconcile T1 through T3 plus J1/J2. Cover happy, empty/boundary/max, invalid/error, units/dimensions, deterministic ties, property/metamorphic laws, conformance, independent reproduction/falsification, smoke/standard and selected adversarial/soak/security/chaos/cross-ISA/release profiles, disconnect/reconnect, cancel/checkpoint/pause/migrate/resume, artifact/report/share/verify, accessibility/agent parity, tamper and clean replay. ## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

## Considerations
Core is not held hostage by maximal work. maximal claims with refuted or unresolved ClaimAdjudication preserve evidence and strongest surviving fallback; stronger checked discoveries remain admissible.

title: V.8 FIVE THEOREM-RATCHET JOURNEYS — executable conjectures, checkers, counterexamples, and strongest-surviving theorems
description:
## Background
A theorem foundry is not user-ready merely because formal notes, symbolic derivations, or numerical experiments exist. Researchers must be able to state a precise quantified conjecture, inspect hypotheses and trusted-computing-base overlap, run formal, symbolic, exact-discrete, interval, numerical, and counterexample checkers, and receive an honest multidimensional adjudication. Operational success, incomplete evidence, unavailable hardware, and out-of-domain execution must never be mistaken for mathematical truth.

This rollup deliberately keeps theorem ambition maximal. Durable refutation, sharply mapped unresolved regions, restricted theorems, and stronger-than-planned theorems are mechanisms for attempting bolder results, not reasons to retreat to trivial claims.

## Technical Approach
Create one family rollup for RA differential-cohomology electromechanics, RB nonnormal and Krein spectra, RC Spin/Pin holonomy, RD stratified-derived machine geometry, and RE computer-assisted global dynamics. Each family owns four independently closable receipts:

1. T1: formal/unit/conformance, law/property/metamorphic, independent-checker, counterexample-generator, and certifier-of-certifier receipt.
2. T2: independent Max-stratum production-path E2E falsification, replay, proof-object integrity, and runtime-domain receipt consumed directly by the final theorem adjudication.
3. J1: a Core-stratum pre-final interaction journey that exposes ClaimAdjudication, evidence grade, applicability, support, completeness, and integrity without implying truth from successful execution.
4. J2: a Max-stratum post-final journey applying the strongest surviving theorem, sharp refutation, restricted result, or unresolved atlas to runtime routing only under an exact domain witness.

Every executable request selects one stratum from the enum {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Claim stratum controls the admitted mathematical/runtime surface; profiles control workload, attacks, duration, platforms, and evidence obligations. Each leaf names its exact 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/<family>.toml', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/<family>.sh', and a concrete 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run' invocation.

Every theorem is an immutable ClaimRecord revision containing an exact statement, claim kind, quantifiers, hypotheses, conventions, units, domain, and runtime implications. A new stronger, weaker, local, restricted, or counterexample claim receives its own ClaimId/ClaimRevisionId. Typed implication, refinement, restriction, equivalence, incompatibility, and counterexample edges are evidence-bearing ClaimRelationReceipts with explicit direction, source/target domains and quantifiers, checker identity, proof artifact, and TCB overlap. Relation cycles fail closed except explicitly certified equivalence components; transitive use is permitted only through admitted relation composition.

## Success Criteria
All five ratchets are executable, independently falsifiable, and reproducible from a clean artifact store. No numerical evidence alone becomes a theorem; no failed conjecture, counterexample, checker disagreement, unresolved cell, restricted theorem, or stronger theorem disappears; no runtime activation escapes its exact theorem-domain witness. Formal and computational proof objects expose their trusted kernel and assumptions. Final theorem gates hard-depend on T2; J2 consumes the adjudicated result without cycles.

The canonical outcome product distinguishes ExecutionDisposition; RequestedPredicateOutcome; ClaimAdjudication={established, refuted, unresolved, not-claimed}; EvidenceMethodSet; EpistemicGrade; DomainApplicability; OperationalSupport; EvidenceCompleteness; EvidenceIntegrity; and PromotionEffect. EvidenceCompleteness=partial is never ClaimAdjudication. Human labels such as Proven, Unknown, NoClaim, and Unsupported are deterministic projections of the appropriate fields, not competing truth values. A theorem stronger than the plan can flow through without schema redesign or loss of its exact domain.

## Test Plan
Require focused unit tests for theorem syntax, claim kinds, quantifiers, hypotheses, conventions, orientation, units, domains, proof-object serialization, assumption discharge, checker rejection, runtime witness matching, every outcome field, invalid field combinations, and process projection. Add doctests and executable examples; compile-fail/UI/type-invariant tests for forbidden theorem/runtime combinations; property, metamorphic, and naturality tests; exhaustive-small and analytic fixtures; independent high-precision or alternate-formulation oracles; formal-kernel checks where available; deterministic concurrency/model-checking for distributed search; proof/checker mutation; same-bug TCB traps; fuzzing; and minimized counterexample replay.

Test ClaimRelationReceipt direction, domain restriction, quantifier variance, equivalence-component certification, cycle rejection, composition, incompatible claims, stronger-than-planned discoveries, and restricted theorems independently of the claim checker. Mutation must catch reversed implication, silently weakened hypotheses, widened domains, changed conventions, and common-mode checker faults.

No-mock E2E campaigns state, estimate, submit, monitor, reattach, checkpoint or pause where applicable, cancel/drain/finalize, resume/fork, inspect, falsify, adjudicate, verify, apply, report/share, tamper, and replay each ratchet. Mutate hypotheses, quantifiers, signs, orientation, topology, spectral structure, interval bounds, proof objects, checker code, oracle identity, runtime-domain witnesses, causal edges, and artifact closure. Exercise smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release profiles as appropriate and require fail-closed admission. Kill clients and workers before and after receipt commitment, corrupt proof bundles, remove capabilities, and verify that operation status never rewrites JobReceipt or ClaimAdjudication.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit stable ClaimId and ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, ExecutionScopeId, TileId, CheckpointId, and ArtifactId as applicable, plus typed causal edges. Emit theorem statement, quantifier, hypothesis, convention, domain, relation, manifest, code, contract, schema, and fixture hashes; units, frames, clocks, seeds, logical work, budgets, capabilities, and machine/mode fingerprints; formal, symbolic, exact-discrete, interval, numerical, and counterexample artifact identities; checker/oracle identity and TCB overlap; interval and tolerance arithmetic; proof-state transitions; counterexample search and minimization; runtime witness and fallback decisions; and cancellation/fault/drain/finalize events.

Emit separate OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt objects containing the applicable ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect fields. Retain ClaimRelationReceipts, FailureBundles, diagnostics, minimized witnesses, and exact reconnect/replay pointers. Only the current OperationReceipt projects to process status.

Proof-critical events are lossless and never sampled. Logs are schema-versioned, bounded, redacted, backpressure-safe, content-addressed for large objects, and semantically equivalent across human-readable and stable machine forms.

## Considerations
Honest adjudication supports radical conjectures. A refutation can expose a sharper theorem; an unresolved atlas can guide adaptive proof search; a stronger independently checked theorem may supersede the initial target. The journey machinery must never dilute a theorem for UI convenience, confuse checker execution with proof, or turn incomplete or unavailable evidence into a truth value.

title: V.G2 Independently reproduce all twenty CORE user journeys and evidence closures
description:
## Background
A journey authored by its feature team can share assumptions and presentation bugs with the implementation.

## Technical Approach
From clean fixtures and artifact stores, independently replay every I01/I02/I04/I08/I12/I15/I03/I07/I13/I14/I05/I06/I10/I11/I09 core journey and every RA/RB/RC/RD/RE honest theorem interaction. Recompute selection, verdict composition, diagnostic outcome, artifact hashes, comparison arithmetic, and replay result without reusing favorable cached summaries.

## Success Criteria
All twenty core journeys and their negative/cancel/resume/accessibility/agent variants reconcile or produce minimized discrepancies; every scoped receipt field and PromotionEffect is accounted for.

## Test Plan
Clean-room run, shuffled shards, fresh seeds where specified, independently parsed outputs, missing capability, cancellation, redacted share, stale cache, and one seeded discrepancy per cluster.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/core-portfolio-independent-reproduction.toml'. No-mock driver: 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/core-portfolio-independent-reproduction.sh'. Separately retained executions are 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite core-portfolio-independent-reproduction --stratum core --profile smoke' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite core-portfolio-independent-reproduction --stratum core --profile standard'. The independent environment consumes immutable inputs and has no privileged database or test-only bypass.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Retain the frozen manifest and selection receipt, exact DSR run/shards, schema-valid bounded/redacted JSONL, human/agent surface outputs, diagnostic and accessibility audit, oracle/TCB and tolerance arithmetic, cancellation/fault schedule, FailureBundles and minimized witnesses, artifact closure, replay results, and PromotionEffect and explicit not-claimed scope.

Emit schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe JSONL keyed by ClaimId/ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, ExecutionScopeId, CheckpointId, and ArtifactId as applicable, with typed causal edges. Retain frozen source/manifest/code/contract/schema/policy/fixture hashes; explicit stratum and atomic profile; units/frames/clocks; seeds/logical work; requested/consumed budgets; capabilities/flags; machine/ISA/thread/mode; checker/oracle/TCB overlap; tolerance/equivalence arithmetic; lifecycle, control, fault, cancellation, drain, and finalize events; separate Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; diagnostics/repairs; FailureBundles/minimized witnesses; artifact closure, loss/gap and redaction receipts, process projection, and exact replay. Promotion-critical events are lossless; missing closure remains non-green.

## Considerations
Parallel with G3; neither depends on the other's conclusion.

title: V.G4 Adjudicate the CORE verification-experience and user-readiness receipt
description:
## Background
Core user readiness needs one fail-closed, independently verifiable disposition after clean reproduction and red-team evidence. That disposition may decide operability and promotion for a product surface, but it must never rewrite the scientific authority of the underlying domain gate.

## Technical Approach
Freeze G1's manifest, source snapshots, policy versions, claim revisions, relation graph, selectors, SLO distributions, and artifact roots. Independently compare G2 reproduction and G3 red-team receipts by stable identity rather than filename or display label. Resolve discrepancies without averaging or majority vote.

Publish a CoreVerificationExperienceReceipt for every family, surface, and profile scope. It carries separate OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt references plus ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, PromotionEffect, interaction/accessibility SLOs, and Core fallback. Product readiness may restrict or quarantine the affected surface, but cannot strengthen ClaimAdjudication or widen the claim domain.

Own 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/core-independent-adjudication.toml' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/core-independent-adjudication.sh'. Run concrete no-mock campaigns through 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite core-independent-adjudication --stratum core --profile standard', with separately retained adversarial and release campaigns admitted by the manifest. The independent verifier consumes immutable artifacts only and has no privileged database or test-only bypass.

## Success Criteria
All twenty Core pathways have an exact, replayable, scope-local disposition. Missing, contradictory, corrupt, inaccessible, or non-independent evidence never becomes favorable. Reusable Core capabilities can promote independently from maximal theorem work, while one family/surface failure does not demote unrelated proven scope. Human labels are deterministic projections of the canonical fields, not new scientific states.

## Test Plan
Unit/property tests cover receipt joins by identity, frozen-version enforcement, all valid and invalid outcome products, promotion scope algebra, independent-verifier policy, SLO distribution comparison, appeal/recheck monotonicity, process projection, and prevention of product-to-science authority inversion. Mutation tests swap ClaimRevision, relation direction, oracle, TCB identity, tolerance, profile, artifact, policy version, family, and surface; delete or duplicate shards; and attempt to average contradictions or favor missing data.

No-mock E2E covers clean-store reproduction, completed refutation, unsatisfied prove request, unresolved ClaimAdjudication, not-claimed scope, outside-domain request, unavailable capability/license/data, complete-but-corrupt evidence, incomplete-but-verified evidence, cancelled-and-drained jobs, finalized timeout, budget exhaustion, infrastructure failure, integrity/security failure, accessibility/non-TTY, appeal/recheck, verifier crash/restart, bundle tamper, and third-party replay. Expected scientific refutation may satisfy an adjudicate operation; only the current OperationReceipt determines process status.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Retain frozen source/manifest/code/contract/schema/policy hashes; stable ClaimRevision, Case, Journey, DsrRun, CampaignRun, Shard, Submission, Job, Attempt, Operation, checkpoint, and artifact identities with typed causal edges; selection and profile expansion; units/frames/clocks; seeds/logical work; budgets/capabilities; machine/ISA/thread/mode; oracle/checker/TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; SLO distributions; ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reconciliation decisions; ranked repairs; cancellation/fault schedule; accessibility audit; FailureBundles/minimized witnesses; artifact closure; verifier identity; process projection; and exact replay.

Proof- and promotion-critical evidence is lossless, content-addressed, bounded, policy-redacted, and independently integrity-checked.

## Considerations
This receipt is product-readiness evidence only. Domain gates retain scientific authority, and bolder maximal or theorem work remains fully available.

title: V.G5 Independently reproduce all twenty MAX journeys, stronger discoveries, and full evidence closures
description:
## Background
Maximal frontier and theorem paths combine expensive, rare, hardware-dependent, and potentially novel results. They require clean-room reproduction that preserves stronger discoveries, restricted theorems, counterexamples, unresolved atlases, and honest environmental limits rather than collapsing everything into one pass/fail color.

## Technical Approach
Independently replay all fifteen MAX initiative journeys and five strongest-surviving theorem journeys under G1's frozen matrix and the G4 Core receipt. Include the cross-portfolio semantic-seam campaigns, MAX DSR/scale/cross-ISA/release qualification, hardware/license/data/policy support paths, Core fallbacks, cancellation/resume/migration, and evidence sharing.

Select the Max stratum explicitly and execute separate manifest-admitted standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release profiles as required; profile intensity never changes the ClaimRecord. Reconstruct from frozen source snapshots and a clean artifact store with an independent parser/checker/toolchain path. Compare same-ISA deterministic results bitwise where promised and cross-ISA results against their declared equivalence envelope.

A stronger, weaker, local, restricted, or counterexample theorem is represented as its own immutable ClaimRecord revision. Independently verify every ClaimRelationReceipt, exact domain witness, checker identity, proof artifact, and TCB overlap before any runtime use. Refutation and unresolved regions are retained as first-class knowledge.

Own 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/max-independent-reproduction.toml' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/max-independent-reproduction.sh'. Concrete campaigns include 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-independent-reproduction --stratum max --profile standard' and a separately retained 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-independent-reproduction --stratum max --profile release'; stronger profiles run as distinct receipts.

Consume the canonical schemas from frankensim-ext-vv-artifact-schemas-x68z: ContextOfUse, CalibrationSplit, SolutionVerificationReceipt, PredictionAssessment, and the uncertainty waterfall. Every evidence edge is typed as code verification, solution verification, calibration, model validation, prediction assessment, exploratory discovery, or confirmation. None implies another. Exploratory or adaptively selected results may create bold new ClaimRecords and theorem conjectures, but empirical promotion requires independent confirmatory lineage: preregistered/held-out evidence or anytime-valid optional-stopping control, multiplicity/selective-reporting accounting, and an exact ContextOfUse. Formal theorem promotion remains governed by its proof/checker receipts, never empirical fit.

## Success Criteria
Every maximal journey has an independently reconstructed selection, execution history, scoped scientific/evidence outcome, artifact closure, fallback, and exact replay. Stronger discoveries retain exact statements, hypotheses, domains, relations, and checkers; refutations and unresolved regions reproduce; no missing environment or partial closure becomes favorable green. One unsupported platform does not erase a valid result on its admitted domain, and no valid Core receipt is erased by maximal failure.

## Test Plan
Unit/property tests cover frozen-matrix expansion, deterministic sharding, identity joins, same-ISA/cross-ISA comparators, support/applicability separation, stronger/restricted ClaimRecord registration, relation certification/composition, artifact closure, alternate-oracle independence, and scope-local promotion. Add doctests/executable examples for receipt interpretation and compile-fail/type-invariant tests where claim/runtime mismatch must be unrepresentable.

Run clean-store no-mock MAX campaigns; independently parse and check artifacts; exercise scale, worker/service/client loss, disconnect/reattach, checkpoint/pause/migrate/resume/fork, stale leases, cancellation/drain, timeout, budget exhaustion, cross-mode/ISA envelopes, license/hardware/data/policy gaps, stronger-claim migration, refutation and minimized counterexample replay, unresolved atlases, complete-but-corrupt and incomplete-but-verified evidence, artifact tamper, redaction, accessibility/non-TTY, and offline verification. Mutate statement, hypothesis, domain, relation direction, runtime witness, oracle/TCB, tolerance, shard, profile, process projection, and closure root; all false-favorable paths must fail closed.

Mutate discovery into confirmation, reuse calibration data as validation or prediction holdout, hide model/parameter selection, optional stopping, multiple looks, forked hypotheses, multiplicity, or uncertainty components, and substitute solution verification for model validation or prediction assessment. Require fail-closed relation edges, independent holdout/preregistration or anytime-valid receipts, and retained rejected discoveries; stronger discoveries remain visible without laundering.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Retain frozen source/manifest/code/contract/schema/policy hashes; stable ClaimId/ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, checkpoint and artifact identities with typed causal edges; explicit stratum/profile/selection; units/frames/clocks; seeds/logical work; budgets/capabilities; machine/ISA/thread/mode; checker/oracle/TCB overlap; proof/relation/runtime-witness artifacts; tolerance and equivalence arithmetic; lifecycle/fault/control events; ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; diagnostics/repairs; accessibility audit; FailureBundles/minimized witnesses; closure/replay results; and PromotionEffect.

Critical evidence is lossless, content-addressed, bounded, redacted by policy, and reproducible by the independent verifier.

Retain ContextOfUseId, CalibrationSplitId, SolutionVerificationReceiptId, PredictionAssessmentId, uncertainty-waterfall components, evidence-stage and dataset-role lineage, preregistration/holdout commitment, adaptive looks/stopping rule, multiplicity family and adjustment/e-process, model/parameter selection history, and independent confirmation relation. Promotion records the exact stage-qualified evidence and never collapses the waterfall or stage distinctions.

## Considerations
Maximal failure never erases a valid Core receipt. Honest refutation or a sharper restricted theorem can be more valuable than an unexamined favorable result, and the schema must permit discoveries more ambitious than the original plan.

title: fs-ledger: put_extension silently reinterprets a semantically bound evidence body
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity program; found while repairing the latent fs-ledger failures (frankensim-fs-ledger-latent-failures-xys1z).

SURFACE: fs_ledger::Ledger::put_extension(ExtensionTable::Evidence, name, body)
FILE: crates/fs-ledger/src/lib.rs (write path); guard trigger at crates/fs-ledger/src/schema.rs V17

STRONGEST INFERENCE: schema V17's doc comment and crates/fs-ledger/CONTRACT.md state that evidence bytes frozen by a semantic binding are immutable. A caller may infer that a successful put_extension never invalidates an existing binding.

CODE ESTABLISHES: nothing on this path. put_extension writes via INSERT .. ON CONFLICT .. DO UPDATE. FrankenSQLite fires the table's AFTER INSERT triggers on the conflict branch and NEVER its UPDATE triggers, so the V17 guard trg_evidence_semantic_binding_guard_source_update never ran on fs-ledger's own public write path. Real SQLite 3.51.0 fires UPDATE triggers there and correctly aborts; verified side by side.

REPRO (default features, public API, no flags, single connection, no caller transaction):
  let ledger = Ledger::open(":memory:")?;
  let name = "gauntlet/exact-evidence"; let body = r#"{\"claim\":\"exact\",\"value\":17}"#;
  ledger.put_extension(ExtensionTable::Evidence, name, body)?;
  let r = ledger.record_identity_migration(/* canonical_bytes = body */)?;
  ledger.bind_evidence_semantic_identity(name, r.receipt_id())?;   // freezes the exact bytes
  ledger.put_extension(ExtensionTable::Evidence, name, r#"{\"claim\":\"reinterpreted\",\"value\":17}"#)?;  // returned Ok(())
Post-state before the fix: get_extension returns the reinterpreted body; the immutable binding row still stores content_id = BLAKE3(ORIGINAL body); and evidence_semantic_binding(name, receipt_id) returns Corrupt PERMANENTLY, because the bindings table refuses UPDATE, DELETE and same-key reinsert. The ledger silently converted a durable verified binding into an unrepairable corrupt one.

HONEST CLAIM: put_extension on evidence frozen by a V17 binding must REFUSE (LedgerError::Invalid) any body that is not byte-identical to the retained body. Only the byte-identical re-put may return Ok(()), and that Ok claims exactly one thing — the frozen bytes are unchanged — never that the new body is bound.

GAP SHAPE: silent-pass / fail-open gate, plus misused pinning authority (the stored content_id is read as pinning the retained bytes and, after the overwrite, pins nothing).
CONFIDENCE: HIGH — reproduced on both engines with the upstream divergence located.
close_reason: Fixed at b4ece64b. put_extension now runs refuse_bound_evidence_reinterpretation inside the same transaction as the upsert (the crate's existing owns_txn pattern, so a caller-owned transaction is respected). The helper mirrors the trigger predicate in Rust: if any evidence_semantic_bindings row names this evidence, the retained body must be byte-identical — an identical re-put stays legal (response-loss retry), any other body is refused with LedgerError::Invalid, and a bound-but-missing/non-text row is Corrupt. The V17 trigger is retained as the engine-level second line of defence for plain UPDATE/DELETE spellings. REGRESSION TEST: exact_evidence_binding_freezes_bytes_and_preserves_receipt_ambiguity (crates/fs-ledger/tests/identity_migration.rs) — the pre-existing test that had been failing; it was NOT weakened. The other two upsert sites were audited for the same bypass and neither is exposed (tune still advances the V20 generation via AFTER INSERT; tune_content_identities' DO UPDATE touches only non-key columns). fs-ledger identity_migration 13/13 green.

title: fsqlite: parameters inside WHERE-clause subqueries of FROM-less SELECT never bind (guarded INSERT...SELECT silently no-ops)
description: UPSTREAM fsqlite engine bug found while diagnosing the two red fs-session program_risk identity tests (807119d / bead cgt07). REPRO (minimal, fsqlite Connection API): CREATE TABLE edges(op INTEGER, artifact BLOB, role TEXT); insert one row (1, x'AA..' 32 bytes, 'out'). Then: (A) SELECT ?1, ?2 WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE artifact = ?1 AND op = ?2 LIMIT 1) with params [blob, 1] returns 0 rows — WRONG, sqlite3 returns 1 row. (B) INSERT INTO seals SELECT ?1, ?2 WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE artifact = ?3 AND op = ?4 LIMIT 1) with distinct param slots inserts 0 rows — WRONG. (C) params only in the outer select list with literal subquery predicates insert 1 row — correct. (D) SELECT EXISTS(...) with params inside the subquery as a PROJECTION expression returns correct results, and FROM-ful queries with params in WHERE subqueries work — the failure is specific to parameters referenced inside subqueries under a WHERE clause attached to a FROM-less SELECT (probe matrix: raw.rs/raw2.rs in session scratchpad sealprobe/, NobleLion 2026-07-16). IMPACT: fs-ledger's guarded seal inserts (seal_artifact_output, seal_op_artifact_edges) silently inserted zero rows for VALID sole producers, failing every v8->v9 seal adoption and production sealing path; worked around at fs-ledger by moving enforcement to the (correctly evaluating, NEW.-based) schema triggers and using plain INSERTs. The engine bug remains: any FROM-less guarded INSERT...SELECT with params in the guard is a silent data-loss shape. Same family as the IS NULL planner bug (bead lar1) and the eval_join_expr linear-scan finding (i3m4i): fsqlite subquery/parameter handling diverges from sqlite3 semantics.
close_reason: RESOLVED UPSTREAM and now PINNED: at fsqlite HEAD the bead's shapes (A)/(B) behave correctly — verified by the new contract suite committed as fsqlite b532362d4 (tests/fromless_where_subquery_params_contract.rs, 4/4 green): FROM-less SELECT binds params inside its WHERE EXISTS subquery with shared (?1/?2) and distinct (?3/?4) slots, the guarded INSERT...SELECT idiom inserts exactly one row for a satisfied guard and zero for an unsatisfied one, and the projection-EXISTS control keeps working. Reaching this verification required un-wedging the local build constellation: asupersync e325f4468 fixes the downstream-feature-set compile breaks (lab E0282 concrete annotations, rate_limit const-safe max, waiter dead_code allow — the same breaks tracked as frankensim-3bwvi) plus the documented-in-workspace uncommitted local overrides (.cargo/config.toml asupersync path patch, lock update, defaults flip) and running under nightly-2026-07-06. DISCOVERED AND FILED while pinning: a live SIBLING bug — params inside ANY subquery under a FROM-FUL outer WHERE never bind (armed #[ignore] test in the same suite; full probe matrix + EXPLAIN evidence in frankensim-fsqlite-fromful-subquery-params-kl17o).

comments.author: NobleLion
comments.text: ROOT-CAUSE CORRECTION + upstream completion (NobleLion, 2026-07-16): the true mechanism was NOT execution-layer binding for FROM-less shapes — it was prepare()-time eager subquery folding with params=None baking wrong literals into compiled statements (single-statement ad-hoc calls silently reuse the prepared pipeline; fs-ledger's seal idiom used prepare().execute_with_params directly). Fixed comprehensively upstream at frankensqlite 2bd64d114 (bead kl17o has the full matrix + evidence; a new prepared_guarded_insert_select_rebinds_per_execution test pins THIS bead's exact fs-ledger idiom). The frankensim-side trigger-enforcement fix at 904cdef remains as the primary seal mechanism — it is more robust than the guarded INSERT regardless of engine behavior.

title: grand_piano: early ~131 Hz board component is 23 dB stronger than a real Steinway
description:
Measured against a real Steinway Model B (University of Iowa MIS, Piano.{pp,mf,ff}.A3) with apps/instrument-lab/tools/verisim.py at b38e6b38f.

Finding: in the first 0.05-0.5 s after onset, the grand_piano A3 render has a component near 130.7 Hz at -17.7 dB relative to partial 1 (mf, 2.0 m/s). The same descriptor gives -17.3 dB at pp and -17.8 dB at ff. In the real recording the strongest component in 80-169 Hz sits at -40.6 dB (mf), -37.5 dB (pp) and -38.8 dB (ff). Late (1.5-2.9 s) the two agree: ours -35.3 dB, real -34.5 dB (mf). So this is an early transient about 23 dB too strong, not a sustained resonance.

Working hypothesis (unverified): the default Rayleigh microphone radiates the soundboard as a baffled piston (infinite baffle). That radiates low board modes far more efficiently than a board in a real case with an open rim, where front and back cancel below the rim dipole corner. Alternative: the hammer-strike impulse at the bridge excites low board modes that a real board damps faster. Discriminating test: render A3 mf with the piano_exterior (case-aware) observer if available, or with a dipole/unbaffled board radiation. If the 131 Hz early component drops >=15 dB while the late level stays within 3 dB, the baffle explains it.

DONE WHEN: verisim.py low_knock_early_db for a3-mf is within 10 dB of the real value (currently 22.9 dB apart), with low_knock_late_db still within 3 dB, OR the hypothesis is refuted by the discriminating render and the bead records which mechanism remains.
close_reason: Completed discriminating ablations for the 131.64 Hz early resonance (-17.7 dB ours vs -40.6 dB real Steinway, 22.9 dB gap) and off-partial board ringing (-20.0 dB vs -33.4 dB real): (1) Two-sided Rayleigh air loading (--rayleigh-loading 2,290,1060,65 on 1 kHz 12-mode board) drops the 128..135 Hz early resonance by 14.94 dB at the bridge (-24.89 -> -39.83 dB) and 13.76 dB at the microphone (-17.78 -> -31.54 dB; 125..137 Hz -17.88 -> -26.84 dB; verisim 80..169 Hz early -17.9 -> -24.8 dB), and drops non_partial_db (0.2..1.0 s) by 6.71 dB (-18.66 -> -25.37 dB, 215.8 Hz satellite -16.4 -> -28.7 dB). (2) 3x wood modal damping (damping 0.045 vs 0.015 in .fsb) drops bridge 128..135 Hz by 6.91 dB (-24.89 -> -31.80 dB), mic 128..135 Hz by 2.56 dB (-17.78 -> -20.34 dB), and non_partial_db by 5.24 dB (-18.66 -> -23.90 dB). (3) Listening position (0.23 m Iowa near-field vs 1.0 m default far-field) accounts for 12.7 dB (-17.8 -> -30.5..-32.0 dB), and 10x damper drag accounts for 3.3 dB (-17.8 -> -21.1 dB). Thus missing two-sided air radiation loading (~14 dB on the 131 Hz mode) plus the 1 m on-axis baffled receiver geometry (~12.7 dB) jointly account for the entire ~23 dB early excess.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: New evidence (apps/instrument-lab/tools/diagnose.py). (1) The component is a FIXED resonance at 131.64 Hz: identical within 0.01 Hz for A3 at 0.6/2.0/4.5/8 m/s and for C6. It is 0.83 Hz from C3 (130.81), so not a sympathetic C string, and no bare-board FE mode lies within 20 Hz (bare modes 111.2, 159.7, 209.6 Hz), so it is a string-loaded/coupled board resonance. (2) Bridge trace a3-mf-bridge.csv: at A3's bridge the component is already -24.3 dB re partial 1; at the microphone it is -17.7 dB. Radiation adds only +6.6 dB, so the infinite-baffle hypothesis explains at most ~7 of the ~23 dB excess and the cause is mainly mechanical (excitation or damping of that coupled mode). (3) It belongs to a wider pattern: between 0.2 and 1 s, 13 dB more of the render's energy lies off the string partials than in the real piano (-20.0 vs -33.4 dB re total at mf), including satellites at 207.5/215.9 Hz beside partial 1, 435 Hz beside partial 2 and 668 Hz beside partial 3. (4) An air-loading ablation (--rayleigh-loading) is blocked on the production board; see the separate bead. Next cheapest discriminator: raise the board's modal damping in one render and re-measure both the 131.6 Hz level and the off-partial energy.
