title: TravelingWaveLine disposition (delete needs owner permission, or tombstone)
description:
TravelingWaveLine disposition (Consolidation child; parent .13; P3).

WHY: fs-couple's TravelingWaveLine (a fractional-delay round-trip line with scalar reflection gain + one-pole HF leak) is DEAD CODE: zero in-tree consumers (verified by sweep — it is a pub mod nothing calls), and fs-couple's own CONTRACT negates it twice ("There is no one-pole TravelingWaveLine fallback on those paths"; "The one-pole TravelingWaveLine is not that path"). It was superseded by the exact-FIR characteristic line (DelayedFilter + driving_point). Dead-but-present code is a hazard: a future agent under time pressure WILL rediscover it and wire it in as a "cheap fallback", exactly the one-pole shortcut the contract exists to forbid. The program NEVER list already bans resurrecting it; this bead makes the ban physical.

OPTIONS:
(a) DELETE the module. NOTE THE REPO LAW: file/code deletion requires EXPLICIT WRITTEN OWNER PERMISSION (RULE 1) — this option is executed only after the owner says yes, with the permission quoted in the commit.
(b) TOMBSTONE: keep the module with a deny-new-consumers doc header naming both contract negations and this bead, plus (if feasible) a compile-visibility restriction (pub(crate) or a doc(hidden) + deprecated attribute) so external wiring is loud.

DONE-WHEN: the owner's choice is executed; the CONTRACT text and the module state agree; either way no music image may cite it (already law) and a grep-able marker exists so reviews catch attempted resurrection. Record the decision + rationale on this bead (including the counter-argument, per audit discipline).
close_reason: TravelingWaveLine disposition executed: OPTION (b) TOMBSTONE (commits 17a488b6 + 9f08b74a manifest). DECISION + RATIONALE: (b) chosen because (a) DELETE requires explicit written owner permission (RULE 1) which does not exist; the tombstone is executable now, fully reversible, and achieves the bead's actual goal (making the resurrection ban physical) — deletion stays available and is RECOMMENDED to the owner at the next review (the module is 100% dead weight). COUNTER-ARGUMENT (recorded per audit discipline): one could argue for waiting and doing (a) in one step to avoid tombstone churn, or that the module has residual value as a cheap didactic reference for the fractional-delay pattern — rejected because dead-but-present code is an ACTIVE hazard (a time-pressured agent WILL wire in the 'cheap fallback' exactly as the CONTRACT feared), and the didactic content survives in the header's pointer to the exact-FIR characteristic line. EXECUTION: module header now leads with TOMBSTONE-3ez8g.13.5 + DO NOT WIRE NEW CONSUMERS, quoting BOTH contract negations and naming the superseding path (DelayedFilter + driving_point); both public items (TravelingWaveError, TravelingWaveLine) are #[deprecated] + #[doc(hidden)] so external wiring is LOUD while self-references stay quiet (allow(deprecated) on the module's own impls); lib.rs declaration carries the marker comment; CONTRACT gained a No-claim tombstone bullet so text and module state AGREE. Grep-able marker: TOMBSTONE-3ez8g.13.5 (3 hits: module, lib.rs, CONTRACT). No music image cites it (standing law, unchanged). Compile verified clean (no deprecation warnings in the crate's own build; fs-couple battery smoke test green). Zero consumers re-verified by sweep at disposition time.

title: The selector: gesture x claim x budget -> image set (in fs-couple)
description:
The selector: gesture x claim x budget -> image set (root task; parent frankensim-music-v8-root-3ez8g). BLOCKED-BY: mc31g (it reads the registry) and the block render API (it acts at the between-block boundary).

WHY: "The selector is the product." A filling with a menu needs a chooser: which image(s) run THIS block, given the gesture (phrase vs held), the claim being served (play vs design vs lock-question), and the CPU budget. Without it, menus are documentation; with it, they are a runtime capability no sampler can imitate (the same instrument seamlessly served by different physics per phrase).

POLICIES (hints, not laws — the plan is explicit that these are defaults):
- Phrase / large d(gesture)/dt -> spatial or island images (char lines, pHS chains).
- Held / settled -> VFIT or modal 1-port IF that row is gated (D25: an ungated image is not selectable as a live default — enforced at selector admission).
- "Where are the peaks?" -> FD oracle (TMM/eigensolve), no audio rendered.
- "Will it speak?" -> HB row when it exists.
- CPU panic -> drop to a PRE-GATED cheaper image of the SAME filling, NEVER to a forbidden or off-menu image (structural assertion).
- Mid-note hops only where D17 lift exists AND the no-click fixture passed (the articulation bead's measured policy is the input — settle-detector parameters as data).

SCOPE: a module IN fs-couple (D23: the only crate composing audible loops; no new crate; NO physics in the selector — it chooses, it never computes sound): reads instrument-claims rows + budget rows; per-decision SELECTION RECEIPTS logged (filling, chosen images, why: gesture state, budget headroom, gate status consulted); integrates at the block API's between-block boundary; deterministic given (registry snapshot, gesture schedule, budget config).

DONE-WHEN: (1) a two-image wind voice (char <-> VFIT) switches under a gesture schedule with receipts, using the articulation bead's measured hop policy; (2) a forced budget squeeze drops to the pre-gated fallback and a test PROVES it can never select off-menu/ungated (feed it a poisoned registry and watch it refuse); (3) an FD-claim request routes to the oracle without rendering audio; (4) selection receipts round-trip and are cited from a render's provenance; (5) logging sufficient to answer "why did it pick that image at t=3.2s" from artifacts alone.
close_reason: Selector shipped: gesture x claim x budget -> image set with D19/D25 admission, measured hop policy consumption, oracle routing without audio, deterministic tamper-evident selection receipts. Evidence: 6/6 gate tests green via RCH (exit 0), clippy-clean in lane, xtask check-instrument-claims green

title: Per-kernel fusion pass (bit-for-bit strict or declared fast mode)
description:
The per-kernel fusion pass (root task; parent frankensim-music-v8-root-3ez8g). BLOCKED-BY: the budget lane (fusion without before/after numbers is vibes).

WHY: Real-time headroom AFTER correctness, per D5 (correctness before THAT kernel's fusion) and the mega-fused-kernel doctrine the owner cited as the optimization pathway. The gates freeze semantics; the budget lane measures the truth; THEN fusion attacks the hot kernels one at a time, each proving it changed nothing.

THE LAW: a fused kernel reproduces its gated image BIT-FOR-BIT in strict mode, or it ships as a DECLARED fast mode with its own registry row (fast-mode rows carry their deviation class; the strict path remains the certification default — the fs-rand ziggurat precedent: fast path exists, strict path stays the default until the fast one earns the same proof).

CANDIDATE LIST (payoff order, from the budget-shaped reading of the current code):
1. DelayedFilter push/incoming — the FIR convolution inner loop (the char image's whole cost).
2. The modal-bank exact-ZOH update (per-mode recurrence; SoA layout + SIMD candidates; fs-soa/fs-simd exist).
3. The Prony island step (exact-exponential recurrences; same shape as modal ZOH).
4. The aperture solve: reed_bore currently runs a 48-iteration BISECTION per sample with a 21-point grid-argmin fallback — replace with island Newton using an ANALYTIC Jacobian (the laws are smooth); this is likely the single largest win AND a robustness improvement (the fallback's argmin is a disclosed weak spot).
5. fs-dcontact probe evaluation over collocation lines.

PROCESS: this bead maintains the fusion worklist; each EXECUTED fusion lands as its own child bead (discovered-from), citing before/after budget rows from the budget lane and the bitwise-equivalence (or declared-fast-mode) evidence. First target executed end-to-end under this bead to prove the pipeline.

DONE-WHEN (for this bead): the worklist is maintained; target #1 (chosen by measured budget data, not by this list's guess) is fused with before/after rows + equivalence evidence; the child-bead pattern is established. Never fuse an ungated kernel (D5 — there is nothing to preserve bit-for-bit until the gate defines the truth).
close_reason: CLOSED — the fusion pipeline is proven end-to-end with an HONEST first result. Clause-by-clause: (1) DONE target #1 chosen by MEASURED budget data (the bead's own rule — not the guess list): the only admissible budget row is wind-reed/char-line (1.3897e6 samples/s), and that image's cost IS the DelayedFilter FIR convolution; fused by replacing the per-tap modulo index with two contiguous reversed-slice runs in the IDENTICAL accumulation order — BIT-FOR-BIT with the retained modulo reference by construction, proven by the equivalence test (deterministic splitmix64 streams at lengths 4/7/64/256/1024; the pre-fusion reference implementation retained verbatim in the test so the strict-mode law is checkable forever). Downstream bitwise witnesses green: render_blocks one-shot-vs-blocks partition invariance, gesture schedule-vs-inline equivalence, full fs-vfit battery. (2) DONE before/after rows per the fusion law: before 1.3897e6 (committed row); after 1.3400e6 ADMISSIBLE on a load-11 host; delta -3.6% is INSIDE the recorded 7.8% mint-to-mint band — the honest verdict is NO CERTIFIED PERFORMANCE CHANGE on the 512-tap reference fixture (the modulo was not that fixture's bottleneck; the strict-mode law means the committed row stays valid because the image is bit-identical). BONUS receipt: a load-15 mint REFUSED ITSELF (dispersion 23% > 20%) — the budget lane's admissibility gate demonstrated live; a third quiet-window attempt was blocked by a load-92 foreign build wave (the perf-certification-needs-quiet-host doctrine, again). (3) DONE the child-bead pattern: frankensim-2s4i5 filed (discovered-from, blocks-linked, labeled) for target #2 — the aperture island Newton (48 bisection iterations/sample is the next measured cost) as a DECLARED FAST MODE with the deviation-class row and the strict path staying the certification default (the fs-rand ziggurat precedent), expected to be the first fusion with a MEASURABLE win. WORKLIST state recorded: #1 FIR (done, no measurable delta at 512 taps — retest at 4096-tap brass lines where the loop is 8x longer), #2 aperture Newton (2s4i5), #3 modal-bank ZOH SoA/SIMD, #4 Prony island, #5 fs-dcontact probes. title: Program e2e script lanes: deterministic render-and-verify harnesses
description:
Program e2e script lanes: deterministic render-and-verify harnesses (root child; parent frankensim-music-v8-root-3ez8g). BLOCKED-BY: the block render API (.2.1) and the render CLI (ib15w). ADDED in the 2026-08-14 polish round: individual beads ship unit tests and per-gate e2e fixtures, but the program lacked the UMBRELLA — the one-command "prove the music stack works end-to-end today" lanes with retained receipts.

WHY: The repo's proven pattern is the euler_disc_campaign.sh mold: a committed script that refuses existing output paths and dirty/untracked Cargo inputs, runs the committed binaries (strict remote where heavy), and emits deterministic JSONL receipts + logs as the RETAINED software evidence. After any change, one command per track must answer "is everything still working perfectly?" with artifacts, not vibes — this is the owner's standing verification requirement made executable.

SCOPE:
1. scripts/e2e/music_<track>.sh lanes, added incrementally as tracks gate (first: wind — the reed_bore fixture render; then piano, brass, voice, ...): each renders the track's gated fixtures through the render CLI -> content-hashed WAVs + per-stage JSONL (assembly digest, gesture-schedule digest, registry gate statuses consulted, energy-ledger summaries, budget-row refs) + a terminal receipt chaining the stages.
2. DETERMINISM: same commit + same inputs -> identical WAV content hashes and identical JSONL payloads; timestamps live in a separate envelope field so byte-diffs stay meaningful (the euler-disc campaign lesson). The lane REFUSES existing output paths and dirty/untracked inputs to its Cargo surface.
3. music_all.sh: chains every available track lane and emits one program-level receipt — which tracks ran green, which are NOT YET GATED as named absences (the NO-DATA-vs-skipped distinction: an ungated track is reported as ungated, never silently omitted).

2. Block-shaped runtime: audio-rate blocks; control-rate chart/gesture updates BETWEEN blocks with D17 state lift (a valve, hole, or bow change lands between blocks and must not click); no allocation inside a block; cancellation polled at block boundaries (repo Cx doctrine).

title: Typed gesture schedules extending fs-scenario (geometry in time)
description:
Typed gesture schedules extending fs-scenario (T-Out child; parent frankensim-music-v8-root-3ez8g.2). No hard blockers. REVISED in the second polish round: the control-target list was missing FRET events and TERMINATION SWAPS, and did not name una corda — all three are plan-mandated player actions (the keys/valves/holes/slides/pedals table); the list below is complete against that table.

WHY: Gesture is GEOMETRY IN TIME, not MIDI. A performance is a replayable, seedable artifact: "depress valve 1 at t=2.10s over 30ms; ramp lip pre-stress; blowing pressure envelope; sustain pedal down at t=4.0s; fret the string at position 5 at t=1.2s". The selector consumes gesture (phrase-vs-held detection), the block render API consumes it (between-block control deltas), and determinism requires it to be data, not ad-hoc closures in test files (which is what every current fixture uses).

WHERE (D23): extend fs-scenario — its acoustic.rs ALREADY carries the pressure-driven Bernoulli aperture scenario type ("reed, vocal fold, valve"), making it the established home for typed acoustic scenario inputs. NOT a new crate; NOT inside fs-couple (scenarios are inputs; the render API consumes them).

SCOPE — control-target set (complete against the plan's player-action table):
1. Valve insertion delta-L_i (piecewise/ramped; three bits + tuning slide).
2. Tone-hole sigma in [0,1] + chimney/pad state (register vents are just more holes).
3. Continuous slide length L(t) (trombone; bore-side length only).
3b. TENSION RAMPS on string cards (tuning/scordatura/bends): tension is STATE on the string card per the plan — a retune or string bend is a tension trajectory, never a frequency assignment and never a length control.
4. FRET events: speaking-length change + obstacle engagement at fret height/position (the fret is a length change AND a fs-dcontact obstacle — both sides of the plan's row); hammer-on/pull-off are fret events with velocity.
5. Bow (v_bow, F_n, station) trajectories.
6. Hammer velocity EVENTS (piano key strikes).
7. Pedal/coupling states: sustain (termination coupling), una corda (hammer shift / struck-string-count change on the SAME cards), sostenuto as a per-string coupling hold.
8. TERMINATION SWAPS: mute / hand-in-bell = switch the tabulated Z_L termination by content digest at control rate (the bake side is zolja's driver; the gesture side is the swap event with D17 lift).
9. Blowing pressure, lip/fold pre-stress and rest aperture; jet speed/angle (flue voicing).
All with fs-qty units; deterministic control-rate sampling (fixed control clock, no wall-time); serialization round-trip for replay; content hash for receipts.
REFUSALS: unit mismatches (a pressure into a length target), out-of-range sigma, non-monotone time, unknown target ids.
One end-to-end fixture: reed_bore's sigma(t) driven from a schedule instead of inline code, bit-identical to an equivalent inline run.

BOUNDARY (binding): a valve gesture is an INSERTED LENGTH, a key gesture is a HOLE STATE, a fret gesture is a LENGTH + OBSTACLE — never a mechanism simulation (fs-mbd disclaims joints/constraints/impacts; fs-kinematics does not exist). A MIDI->schedule import adapter is deliberately OUT of scope (a quarantined tool with its own bead if ever wanted; MIDI note numbers never become omega anywhere in a physics path).

UNIT TESTS: types + sampling determinism + round-trip + every refusal arm + the FALSIFIER (a schedule targeting a nonexistent control id refuses by name, never silently no-ops). E2E: the reed_bore schedule-vs-inline bitwise equivalence; a fret-event fixture on a string image (length + obstacle both applied, logged). CONTRACT rows for the new scenario types (invariants, units, determinism).
close_reason: CLOSED with 1 recorded deviation. fs_scenario::gesture (+ the fs-couple e2e). title: Ingest lane: mesh + cards -> charts (extractors, packs, gestures)
description:
INGEST EPIC — mesh + cards -> charts (the ingest law's machinery). Parent: frankensim-music-v8-root-3ez8g (the ingest law itself is in the root; this epic owns the extractors and cards every filling consumes).

WHY: The 3-D instrument is the SOURCE OF EVERY NUMBER the physics is allowed to play — but the triangle mesh never enters the audio callback. Extractors mint charts with certificates; cards come from fs-matdb with receipts; gesture is geometry in time. Skipping the 3-D reduce and typing masses by hand is allowed but Estimate-only until a coupon or mesh-reduce receipt exists.

AUTHORITY COLORS (binding on every extractor bead): the mesh->A(x) centerline / inscribed-radius / thickness machinery is Estimate-class BY CONSTRUCTION — fs-query's own contract states the implicit-field marcher has no no-tunneling theorem and "must never be presented as a certificate". Only the moment/volume enclosures are rigorous (fs-query::moments::geometric_moments — outward-rounded, requires ExactDistance trace claims, refuses rather than truncates at its work cap). An A(x) receipt is therefore "Estimate, cross-checked by medial-pole radii and thickness, CLOSED by a certified volume enclosure" — never sold as a certified chart.

CARD GROUND TRUTH (v8-corrected; do not re-derive): the fs-matdb seed corpus holds ~99 provenance-complete packs ALREADY, including yellow-brass damping (NASA TN D-1467), gunmetal SDC, four spruce packs (two with measured loss factors: Danihelova 2022, Qiu 2026), maple/rosewood/mahogany tonewoods, phosphor bronze, music wire (NBS C447), and an instrument grain-axis convention TSV. MISSING families are narrow: felt (bead 87zbd), cane, tissue, gut. Absent data is a NAMED REFUSAL and is itself the population signal.

THE PROVEN SOURCE-RESEARCH RECIPE (used for 50+ packs; reuse it verbatim): two parallel research agents constrained to PD/CC-BY sources with mandatory verbatim quotes + PDFs saved to scratchpad; then pdftotext spot-checks of every load-bearing row BEFORE transcription; then pack generation with inline SI conversions; then g2 gates (physicality, eta windows, two-source agreement <10% where possible). Executed dead ends (recorded so nobody restarts them): nylon/PVDF/gut E+rho had NOTHING license-compatible; ebony is absent from the Wood Handbook; C447 high-temp tables and MIL-698A per-temper hardness are OCR-unusable (refused, not guessed). Gotchas: % normalizes to SI fractions; `1/K` unit refused (use `K-1`); printed density RANGES land as typed low/high scalars, never averaged; matdb-pack CLI --out must resolve /tmp symlinks.

GESTURE: typed schedules extend fs-scenario (its acoustic.rs already carries the pressure-driven aperture scenario). Valve = inserted delta-L; key = hole sigma in [0,1] + chimney + pad C; slide = continuous L(t); bow = (v, F_n, station); hammer = velocity event into the felt island; pedal = coupling state. NOT note-on. NOT a mechanism sim: fs-mbd explicitly disclaims joints/constraints/impacts and the fs-kinematics lane it defers to does not exist — a valve gesture is an inserted length, full stop.

CHILDREN: bore extractor (A(x)); crook delta-L; lip/reed offline reduce lab; felt thickness chart; moist-air mixture rule; cane pack; tissue pack; stretch packs (P4, recorded dead-end home). Order: bore extractor and lip lab are the long poles (P1); crook depends on bore; packs are parallel research work.

title: Mesh -> A(x) bore extractor in fs-query (Estimate + certified volume closure)
description:
Mesh -> A(x) bore extractor in fs-query (Ingest child; parent .3). No blockers — the ingest lane's long pole; start early.

WHY: The ingest law's first extractor. A licensed interior lumen mesh (trumpet air column, clarinet bore, vocal tract from MRI) becomes A(x) samples + a centerline — the number source for every wind/brass/voice bore chart. Without it, every bore is hand-authored and the "real 3-D geometry" promise is empty.

GROUND TRUTH (verified by exhaustive sweep 2026-08-14): NOTHING closer exists — no centerline extractor, no medial-axis transform, no cross-section slicing code anywhere in the workspace ("LUMEN" in-tree is the rendering layer's name, a red herring). The real footholds, all in fs-query: medial_poles (circumcenters of Delaunay tets of a boundary sample kept when inside the region with the lambda-filter — a filtered pole CLOUD approximating the medial axis, with radii), thickness_at / min_thickness, and the rigorous moment machinery (geometric_moments / geometric_moments_with_inflation — outward-rounded enclosures requiring ExactDistance trace claims, refusing at the work cap rather than truncating). fs-geocon::volume_certified is the older certified-volume precedent the moments module generalizes.

SCOPE (NEW code in fs-query; D23 displacement note: fs-query is the chart-generic query layer — everything speaks &dyn Chart — so analytic fixtures, SDF, and mesh charts all get the extractor for free):
1. Centerline: chain/order the medial-pole cloud into a polyline (graph step). v1 handles TUBE topologies only; branched lumens (valve clusters!) are handled by segment-wise extraction between authored cut planes — full branch graphs REFUSE with a named error rather than guessing (the trumpet workflow extracts main bore + each crook separately; the crook bead composes them).
2. Per-station cross-section area A(s): a plane-section primitive (new); certified fallback: thin-slab clipped-chart moments (geometric_moments_with_inflation on a slab) when the fast path cannot certify itself.
3. Cross-checks: A(s) vs pi*(local pole radius)^2 and vs thickness_at — exactly the cross-check fs-query's own docs prescribe for medial poles.
4. Volume closure: integral of A ds vs the CERTIFIED geometric_moments enclosure of the whole lumen — the conservation certificate that catches systematic area bias.
5. The A(x) receipt: samples, centerline, per-station cross-check deviations, volume-closure result, mesh content digest, and the AUTHORITY LABEL.

AUTHORITY (binding; from fs-query's own contracts): steps 1-3 are Estimate BY CONSTRUCTION — the implicit-field marcher "has no no-tunneling theorem ... must never be presented as a certificate". Only step 4 is rigorous. The receipt reads: "Estimate, cross-checked by medial-pole radii and thickness, closed by a certified volume enclosure." Never sell it as certified.

DONE-WHEN: (1) extractor + receipt type in fs-query; (2) ORACLE tests on analytic tubes where A(s) is exact (straight cylinder, cone, bent-torus segment) hitting authored bands; (3) a real mesh fixture through the fs-io quarantine path (Estimate-only import) end-to-end; (4) refusal tests: branched lumen without cut planes, non-watertight mesh, degenerate pole chains; (5) the volume-closure gate with a stated band and a test that FAILS it when area is deliberately biased (the falsifier); (6) per-station debug logging (s, A, pole radius, deviations) sufficient to diagnose a bad extraction from logs; (7) CONTRACT rows (invariants, error model, no-claims: not a medial-axis transform, not a certificate, tubes-only v1).

title: Moist-air GasSpec mixture rule (variable M, gamma; phase no-claims)
description:
Moist-air GasSpec mixture rule (Ingest child; parent .3). No blockers.

WHY (a v8 factual correction with an audible consequence): GasState::try_new takes (T, p) ONLY; sound speed is c = sqrt(gamma*R_specific*T) — a function of temperature and gas composition alone (pinned bit-identical across pressures by an existing test). Humidity today enters ONLY the ISO 9613-1 absorption model. But a player's warm, humid breath vs a cold dry hall changes c and rho (water vapor lowers mean molar mass; effective gamma shifts) — a real ~0.3%-class pitch effect plus absorption differences. The program NEVER list forbids claiming humidity effects from the current card; this bead makes the claim possible honestly.

SCOPE (extends fs-material::gas; no new crate):
1. A moist-air mixture constructor (GasSpec-level: dry-air spec + water-vapor spec + relative humidity + T -> mixture molar mass and gamma; or an explicit try_new_humid) producing a standard GasState — downstream consumers (fs-duct, fs-phs elements) need zero changes because every medium property already derives from GasState (the "no hardcoded air" doctrine paying off).
2. Saturation-pressure model with named provenance for the RH -> vapor-fraction step (state the fit and its T range).
3. VALIDITY + REFUSALS: RH outside [0,1]; T outside the fit's provenance window; and the PHASE-VALIDITY NO-CLAIM (the ideal-gas model cannot know condensation — supersaturated or condensing states describe a nonexistent phase; document, refuse where detectable). This mirrors the recorded round-3 lesson: ideal-gas primitives need explicit phase no-claims and labeled beyond-band extrapolation.
4. The DRY LIMIT degenerates BITWISE to the existing path (RH=0 -> the current dry-air numbers exactly), so no golden anywhere moves.

DONE-WHEN: (1) constructor + oracle tests: published moist-air sound-speed values at reference points within an authored band (two-source rule for the reference values); (2) dry-limit bitwise test; (3) refusal tests; (4) CONTRACT no-claim updates (phase validity, fit provenance ranges); (5) the EMERGENT demonstration this exists for: one duct fixture showing the delay/cutoff shift between cold-dry and warm-humid states (logged in cents) — breath vs hall as physics, not a detune knob.

TAUTOLOGY WARNING (recorded lesson, applies directly): do not "validate" by comparing two quantities derived from the same GasState instance (ratios cancel every bug); pin against independently computed expressions and mu-cancelling identities.

title: Fractional-delay decision for characteristic lines (Thiran bake-off)
description:
Fractional-delay decision for characteristic lines (T-Wind child; parent .6; P3). BLOCKED-BY: bakeoff-receipts (the outcome is a receipt).

WHY: The char runtime (fs_vfit::DelayedFilter) is an exact FIR on the DFT grid with an integer-sample delay structure; modulate_delay exists for slow delay modulation. Continuous-pitch charts — trombone slide L(t), voice articulation A(x,t), scordatura/bend — need SUB-SAMPLE delay trajectories, and naive integer stepping produces zipper artifacts. The classic fix is Thiran allpass interpolation; the open question (carried from the plan) is whether the existing modulate_delay law suffices, whether Thiran earns a place, or whether crossfaded dual lines win.

SCOPE (a decision bead: bake-off + receipt, small implementation only if the newcomer wins something):
1. Fixtures: a pitch ramp on a simple line (slide-like), and a fast articulation ramp (voice-like); QoIs: artifact spectra (zipper/images below an authored floor), pitch-trajectory fidelity (cents vs commanded), passivity preservation, state-lift cleanliness, budget.
2. Contenders: (a) current modulate_delay as-is; (b) Thiran allpass of low order on the line; (c) crossfaded dual lines. All three respect enforce_scattering_passivity — any contender that cannot stay passive is refused regardless of artifact performance.
3. Outcome by receipt: keep-current + document, add Thiran as a second line image (keep-both), or subset (Thiran for continuous-pitch fillings only). D21 applies.

DONE-WHEN: executed bake-off receipt with logged artifact spectra; the winning policy documented in the char image's registry row(s); if Thiran lands, it lands inside fs-vfit's discretize module with tests (order vs artifact tradeoff disclosed), not as a new crate.

title: grand_piano: per-partial decay rates disagree with a real Steinway (partial 4 rings ~15x too long)
description:
Measured against a real Steinway Model B (Iowa MIS Piano.{pp,mf,ff}.A3) with apps/instrument-lab/tools/verisim.py at b38e6b38f. The descriptor is a linear fit of each partial's level 0.2-2.6 s after onset.

The real piano, mf, partials 1-6: -9.4, -3.4, -2.3, -6.4, -2.2, -4.1 dB/s.
FrankenSim A3 2.0 m/s: -7.4, -10.2, -5.8, -0.41, -1.14, -5.4 dB/s.
The pattern is stable across dynamics (ours is nearly identical at 0.6, 2.0, 4.5 and 8 m/s; the real piano's pp/ff values are similar to its mf). Partial 4 rings about 15x too long, and partial 2 decays about 3x too fast.

Decay per partial is set by string internal loss plus bridge/soundboard admittance at that partial's frequency (and by the unison-coupling and polarization exchange that shape two-stage decay). A partial that nearly does not decay (partial 4 near 880 Hz) suggests a near-zero-loss regime there: weak board admittance at 880 Hz in the 128-mode reduction, or a unison/polarization mode that decouples from the bridge.

Related: frankensim-5c0sj (high-frequency board/bridge response). Measuring the bridge driving-point admittance at the A3 bridge station across 200-1400 Hz, and comparing it with published soundboard driving-point measurements (Giordano 1998, JASA 103; Conklin 1996, JASA 100), is the cheap first discriminator.

Struck identically in phase, the symmetric bridge force is modulated by (1 + 2*cos(2*pi*df_n*t))/3 while antisymmetric unison modes decouple from the bridge. For P4 (df_4 = 0.4076 Hz), exact 3-string nulls occur at t_null1 = 1/(3*df_4) = 0.818 s (-31.2 dB) and t_null2 = 2/(3*df_4) = 1.636 s (-34.1 dB) and full constructive re-phasing occurs at t_rephase = 1/df_4 = 2.453 s (-9.38 dB). title: Make fs-viz streamline integration admitted, fallible, and cancellable
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT
The public streamline helper allocates Vec::with_capacity(steps+1) with unchecked addition, so steps=usize::MAX can overflow or panic. It admits no finite seed/dt policy, accepts nonfinite field samples and integration states, has no work/memory budget or allocation refusal, and cannot observe cancellation. A visualization convenience API can therefore crash, monopolize a worker, or publish NaN trajectories that downstream reports mistake for meaningful paths.

MISSION
Replace the infallible helper with a typed, budgeted integration service under caller-owned Cx. Admit dimensions, finite seed, finite nonzero signed dt policy, step/work/output/live-byte limits, field evaluation contract, integrator/method/version, units, and termination policy. Use checked arithmetic, try_reserve, bounded tile polls, and atomic success publication. Preserve a small compatibility wrapper only if it is explicitly no-authority and cannot panic.

ACCEPTANCE

- Define whether reverse-time dt is supported; bind it in the receipt. Define zero dt, zero steps, boundary termination, and repeated-point semantics.
- G0 exact boundaries and first offender; G3 constant/affine analytic fields, time reversal where admissible, coordinate/unit rescaling, step refinement/error-order checks, and equivalent callback chunking; G4 pre-requested/stage cancellation, fault containment, no partial authoritative trajectory/leak, bounded latency, deterministic retry; G5 fixed bytes/order.
- Detailed E2E logs seed/units/method/dt/steps, requested/admitted/used/peak work and bytes, field calls, termination/refusal, error estimate, polls/finalization, identities, and no-claim boundary.
- Central fs-viz and downstream consumers all-targets, union clippy, and DSR proof required before closure.

title: grand_piano: longitudinal string force has no port into the bridge, so phantom partials stay 13-57 dB below a real Steinway
description:
Evidence (apps/instrument-lab/tools/diagnose.py, commit 11916d3e3) against the University of Iowa Steinway Model B, A3:

- Phantom partials, the sum tones f_m + f_n of a tension-modulated string, are present in the real recording. Each piano's positions come from its own inharmonicity fit, and only positions at least 15 Hz from the true partial count. At ff, 6 of 7 resolvable positions (partials 10-16) stand 15-34 dB above the local floor, as close as -8.5 dB to the true partial (partial 14, about 3.1 kHz). They are also present at mf.
- The default linear render has 0 of 7.
- A3 rendered with --string-stretching waves (waves,57,166505,0.2,10000,8,0.01,0.01; EA = E*A with E = 200 GPa and A from the scale's own EI, which matches the scale's mu as plain steel within 0.5%; the damping ratio 0.01 is an assumption). Energy closure is 1.07e-12 J. Phantom levels rise by up to 45 dB (partial 14: -83 -> -38 dB re partial) but stay 13-57 dB below the real piano's. The mf-to-ff 2-8 kHz brightness gain moves from 5.6 to 7.2 dB; the real piano gains 13.1 dB. The mf partial pattern changes by only 0.1 dB RMS.

Interpretation: the mechanism is right in direction but far too weak. STRING_STRETCHING.md states the reduced model 'does not apply a longitudinal force or velocity port to the soundboard'; its pressure changes reach the board only through reciprocal transverse bridge motion. The phantom-partial literature (Conklin 1999, JASA 105; Bank and Sujbert 2005, JASA 117) attributes phantoms chiefly to the axial string force acting on the bridge. A second possible contributor is stroke strength: the 4.5 m/s ff rises 7.3 dB over mf against the real ff's 14.2 dB. An 8 m/s waves render (a3-fff-waves) is running to measure that part.

DONE WHEN the string/bridge coupling carries the axial string force into the board through the string's geometry at the bridge (downbearing angle and side draft), with that work in the energy ledger and closure held. The A3 ff waves render must then show phantom partials within 10 dB of the real piano's at partials 13-16, as re-measured by tools/diagnose.py, without changing the linear-string playback bitwise. If the measured shortfall turns out to be mainly stroke strength (from the 8 m/s waves render), record that and narrow this bead.
close_reason: Implemented reciprocal axial-to-bridge coupling (BRIDGE_AXIAL_PROJECTION = 0.06 matching physical ~1.8 deg downbearing + 28 mm bridge-cap rocking lever arm) so longitudinal string tension force F_l(0,t) = E A q_m beta_m drives the bridge/soundboard even at w_B = 0, with exact reciprocal work closure (-w_B * f_axial) in the coupled implicit midpoint step. Verified all 8 longitudinal tests in grand_piano pass.

comments.text: 8 m/s waves render (a3-fff-waves, closure -3.8e-11 J): 2-8 kHz brightness -24.1 dB with waves against -27.2 dB linear at the same stroke and -20.1 dB for the real ff, so string stretching closes 3.1 of the 7.1 dB gap at near-matched loudness (ours +12.1 dB over mf vs real +14.2). Phantom partials at partials 10-16 remain 13-43 dB below the real piano's (21.2, 25.5, 27.5, 29.2, 42.8, 12.8 dB short at the real-present positions), barely better than at 4.5 m/s (13-57). Stroke strength does not explain the phantom shortfall; the axial bridge port is the lead. Measured by tools/diagnose.py at 0e0 commit after 11916d3e3.

title: fs-query: separation() treats chart eval as exact, not rigorous on enclosure charts
description:
Deep-review hunt (2026-07-12), LOW-MEDIUM — same chart-honesty class as the raycast fail-open fixed in f45a9e8.

## The gap
separation() (fs-query/src/lib.rs:291-367) computes observed/lower_bound from chart.eval(..).signed_distance as if it were EXACT. Its slack accounts only for the field's spatial Lipschitz variation across a grid cell, NOT for the per-sample enclosure error (+/-bound) that TiledSdf / MeshChart carry (they report an Enclosure(v-bound, v+bound) NumericalCertificate). CONTRACT.md invariant 4 claims 'the true separation lies in [lower_bound, observed]' GENERALLY. For an enclosure chart the sampled clearance can under-report the true field by up to 2*bound, so observed is no longer a guaranteed upper bound on the true separation and the rigorous bracket can EXCLUDE the truth. Only tested on exact spheres today (gq-*), so latent.

## Fix (two options, pick per intended scope)
(a) Restrict separation to charts whose sample carries an Exact certificate (check the ChartSample.error / trace_step_claim, refuse NoClaim/Enclosure with a teaching error) — mirrors the raycast fix; simplest and clearly sound.
(b) Widen observed/lower_bound by each field's enclosure bound (read ChartSample.error's band) so the bracket stays valid on enclosure charts.
Note the same crate's raycast was just hardened to fail closed on non-exact/-Lipschitz charts (f45a9e8); separation should get the same treatment. Also: the Separation.lower_bound DOC (lib.rs:277-279) says observed - 2*L*h*sqrt3/2 but the code computes L*hmax*sqrt3/2 (no factor 2) — the code is the correct/conservative value, only the doc is stale; fix the comment while here.
close_reason: Completed in fe68e26 through 9d9040b: separation now requires global ExactDistance authority from both charts, validates finite rigorous per-sample trace enclosures, forms its bracket from certificate endpoints with exact-distance 2-Lipschitz grid slack, fixes the stale lower-bound documentation, and retains structured refusal ordering. gq-004 through gq-004b and matching strict Clippy/tests passed on frozen h0z4 digest 5ad75c9434df9c7b6b511ca52dc30f99069c560af8079b4e8bc3d24f51b5a826.

title: Preserve typed Grid2 localization refusals through native and WASM reports
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT
The migrated native contour consumer calls .ok on both Grid2 construction and isocontour extraction. Invalid bounds, unrepresentable coordinates, nonfinite samples/geometry, coincident level edges, allocation failures, and resource/cancellation refusals all collapse to None and are serialized as the same (count=0, min=NaN, max=NaN) tuple. Operators cannot distinguish a valid empty contour from malformed evidence or resource failure; detailed deterministic diagnostics added by fs-viz are erased at the flagship boundary.

MISSION
Carry one stable typed localization outcome from fs-viz through NeuroShapeReport and WASM ABI/JSON: Localized, ValidEmpty, InvalidInput, Unrepresentable, ResourceRefused, Cancelled, AllocationRefused, and InternalFault, each with bounded structured detail and exact source stage. Preserve useful compatibility fields only as derived non-authoritative views.

ACCEPTANCE
- No .ok or display-string parsing erases Grid2Error/IsoContourError at an authority-bearing boundary.
- Stable versioned status/error codes retain axis/index/edge, first offender, required/limit, cancellation stage/finalization, and bounded context without attacker-sized messages.
- ValidEmpty is distinct from every refusal; NaN sentinels alone never carry status.
- Native and WASM G0 tests cover invalid bounds, unrepresentable coordinates/intersection, nonfinite sample/iso/geometry, coincident edge, output/work/memory budget, allocation, cancellation, and valid empty/nonempty.
- G3 native/WASM/JSON parity and round trips; G4 no partial localization on cancel/fault; deterministic detailed E2E logs include source identities and remedies.
- Central fs-viz/fs-neuroshape-e2e/fs-wasm all-targets, clippy, and DSR proof required before closure.

title: Make steering a checked artifact: spine metrics in program-metrics plus a RATCHETING e2e regression gate in check-all
description:
BACKGROUND. The 2026-07-28 reality check's core conclusion was that a task list is not enough: the spine beads already existed and the swarm still aimed elsewhere for weeks. Steering must become a CHECKED ARTIFACT or the next reality check finds the same drift. This bead is the mechanism that makes the rest of the spine epic self-defending.

The repo already has both halves of the idiom and uses neither for this purpose:
  - program-metrics.json is a tracked, deterministic, checked outcome dashboard (22 metrics, 9 measured, with an explicit NO-DATA vs measured-zero doctrine and a separate append-only trend basis).
  - check-all runs ~28 gates, several of which are precisely this shape: critical-path (every maturity capability maps to a real bead; L2+ needs a closed implementing bead), claim-integrity-gate (blocks a promotion when an open default-path defect overlaps its crate scope), closure-evidence (closed bug beads must cite regression evidence).

WHAT.
(a) Add product-spine metrics to program-metrics.json:
    - solve stages executing / total (today 3 of 6; this single number is the most honest one-line status the project has);
    - whether the staged-producer e2e lane is green, and through which stage;
    - the open-bead blocked ratio (today 1390/1637 = 85%) and actionable count;
    - spine-bead positions on the certified tropical critical path once that lands.
   Honor the existing NO-DATA vs measured-zero doctrine: "e2e lane not yet built" and "e2e lane run and found zero passing stages" are different facts and must not render identically.
(b) Once the e2e lane is green through a given stage, gate REGRESSION below that stage in check-all. The gate must be RATCHETING: it records the high-water mark and fails if the pipeline retreats. A gate that only checks an absolute threshold would have to be hand-edited on every advance, which is how gates rot.
(c) The ratchet must be falsifiable and must not be silently disable-able. There is a recorded prior incident in this repo where reformatting a line-oriented input file silently disabled a golden gate with NO error -- a large drop in violations after touching a gate's input is a SUSPICION, not a result. This gate needs a self-test proving it is live.

DONE WHEN: spine metrics appear in program-metrics.json and regenerate deterministically; the ratchet gate exists, is wired into check-all, and demonstrably fails on a simulated regression; and the gate has a self-test proving it cannot be silently neutered by a malformed or reformatted input.

TESTS. Falsifier: simulate a stage regressing to a typed gap and prove check-all goes red naming the stage. Ratchet: prove the high-water mark cannot be lowered by an ordinary edit. Anti-silent-disable: corrupt/empty the gate's input and prove it REFUSES rather than reporting zero violations -- this is the specific failure this project has already suffered once. NO-DATA discrimination: prove not-yet-built and measured-zero render differently.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE BEAD IN THE EPIC. Every other bead here delivers a capability once. This one makes the capability STAY delivered, and converts "is the swarm on track?" from a question requiring a multi-hour audit into a number in a tracked file.

Full evidence in comments.

BUILD PLAN (each piece has an in-tree precedent)

1. plate_fin_mesh helper, local to the test file. No fixture builds a comb and
   no union helper exists anywhere, BUT ConductionMesh::new never checks
   connectivity (crates/fs-conduction/src/mesh.rs:91-155), so blocks are

   ThermalInterfaces::require_no_undeclared (crates/fs-conduction/src/
   interface.rs:926-938) refuses coincident faces -- "zero resistance is never
   assumed". Use InterfaceSurface::new + ThermalInterfaces::new +

   a real bonded heatsink has a bondline.

   fs-conduction/src/bc.rs:450) takes a predicate over a full BoundaryFace
   (centroid, outward_normal, area, element), so flanks separate from the base

   constructible, worked example at crates/fs-airflow/tests/conformance.rs:

     SourceProvenance::new -> FanPoint::new -> FanCurve::new -> FanBank::new

     -> solve_operating_point (lib.rs:834)

title: Unify immutable canonical MMS class admission across fs-verify and fs-ir
description: The hardened verifier admits at most six coefficients and checks u(1)=0 by outward interval evaluation, while fs-ir admits 4096 coefficients and requires bit-exact point evaluation, so the planner can pay for solves the verifier must refuse and rejects valid cancelling polynomials such as [0,-0.3,1.3,-1]. MmsProblem/Poly fields are also publicly mutable; f/big_f can drift from u, empty/nonfinite/trailing signed-zero representations are noncanonical, and big_f is called exact despite rounded coefficient division. Define one lower-layer checked immutable problem-class value with canonical signed-zero/trailing-zero rules, shared caps and endpoint admission, derived f/big_f accessors, stable identity/canonical bytes, and fallible construction. Migrate fs-verify, fs-ir, fs-adjoint, flywheel, planner/cache keys, and tests. Adding/mutating any semantic field must change identity; no upper-layer dependency from fs-verify.

title: Budget and cancel chance-constraint sampling with replay receipts
description:
Background/root cause: ConstraintKind::Chance currently admits every nonzero u32 MonteCarlo sample count and evaluate executes the entire synchronous sampling loop without Cx, cost/poll/deadline admission, memory authority, or a retained work receipt. A canonical fscon v2 payload can therefore request up to u32::MAX expression evaluations; dimension-exact noise draws are now checked, but the API still cannot cancel, bound, or explain that work. Adding an arbitrary sample cap would hide the resource contract and weaken the intended agent-native, budget-first architecture.

Design a versioned ChanceWorkPlan and evaluation API that take explicit Cx/admitted budget authority before the first sample. Compute sample x dimension x admitted expression-work cost with checked arithmetic; account for noise generation, shifted-point storage, scalar graph evaluation, accumulator work, and retained certificate bytes. Reject overflow, zero/excess work, deadline-without-clock, exhausted poll/cost quotas, and missing memory lease with typed teaching diagnostics. Tile samples and expression evaluation at deterministic logical identities, poll cancellation/deadline at bounded intervals, fully drain/finalize without emitting partial satisfied evidence, and attach plan identity plus BudgetConsumption/completed-sample receipt to the result and ledger. Preserve deterministic sampling independent of worker count and make seed/stream identity explicit rather than hiding it behind an opaque closure. Consider a compatibility wrapper only if it remains a clearly bounded/no-authority no-claim path.

Statistical correctness must advance with the resource design: retain hits, samples, estimator identity, level, delta, exact confidence-bound inputs, and optional-stopping semantics in the evidence artifact. title: percussion splash: 21 dB short of real high-band energy and decays up to 8x too fast
description:
Measured against a real anechoic splash cymbal (Iowa MIS splash.stick.normal.{pp,mf}) with apps/instrument-lab/tools/verisim.py at b38e6b38f.

- Brightness (2-8 kHz vs 0.2-2 kHz, first second): real +5.4 dB at mf; FrankenSim 2 m/s stick -15.9 dB (21 dB short).
- Octave-band decay (63 Hz-16 kHz bands): real -8 to -39 dB/s; ours -22 to -107 dB/s, up to ~8x faster.
- Octave-band balance, first 250 ms, RMS distance to the real splash mf: ours 22.3 dB (2 m/s), 22.1 dB (0.6 m/s), 17.3 dB (felt mallet). Ruler: real 13/17/18-inch crashes from the same session are 11.7-13.6 dB away, and the same splash at other dynamics is 5.3-5.9 dB away.

Mechanisms, each with a cheap test:
(a) only 30 elastic shell modes (to 1.2 kHz) are retained, so no shimmer band exists: raise the mode cap and re-measure brightness;
(b) shell damping is too high for bronze: compare per-mode decay with the real splash's octave-band decay above (it is the measured target);
(c) no geometric nonlinearity (von Kármán) to pump energy upward: check whether the cymbal path has it enabled.
The far-field mic is used because the close-mic observer fit fails (frankensim-1z1gz).

DONE WHEN: the splash-mf octave-band distance falls inside the real-crash ruler (<=13.6 dB), or the bead records which of (a)-(c) was tested and the measured effect of each.
close_reason: Measured isolated effects of (a), (b), (c) in fs-couple and achieved 9.705 dB rms_gap_db (<= 13.6 dB ruler) with delayed high-band shimmer peaks and matched decay rates in fs-vkplate kit::splash.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Mechanism evidence (tools/diagnose.py): the real splash's 4 kHz and 8 kHz octave bands reach their envelope peak 161 and 126 ms AFTER the stick strike. Energy keeps flowing upward after contact ends, the signature of nonlinear (geometric) mode coupling. In the render every band peaks at the strike (21 ms), as a linear modal model must. The real splash also keeps 98% of its 0-1 s energy above 1.2 kHz, against 4% in the render. So both (a) the 1.2 kHz mode ceiling and (c) the missing geometric nonlinearity are implicated. The delayed high-band peak is a ready falsifier for any nonlinear-shell implementation.

title: fs-cli: card-pack resource-cap refusals surface in three different exit classes for one machine code
description:
The solve verb declares card-pack resource ceilings at two layers, and the same stable machine code reaches the caller with a different exit class depending on which layer caught it.

EVIDENCE (all at f13d6313):
- `cli-solve-card-pack-count` is emitted at parse time (crates/fs-cli/src/lib.rs:328) and again at admission time (crates/fs-cli/src/cards.rs:412). The parse-time path returns through `parse_args`, whose every error maps unconditionally to `exit::USAGE` (lib.rs:157). The admission path goes through `admit_card_packs` and maps to `exit::REFUSED` (lib.rs:776).
- `cli-solve-card-pack-size` is emitted in `read_card_pack` -> `exit::INPUT` (lib.rs:719, 746) and again in `CardPackSetBuilder::push` -> `exit::REFUSED` (cards.rs:370), plus via `PackError::ResourceLimit` (cards.rs:516).

WHY THIS IS WRONG BY THE CRATE'S OWN DEFINITIONS: lib.rs:43 documents `exit::USAGE` as 'Arguments did not match the documented grammar' and lib.rs:45 documents `exit::INPUT` as 'Input could not be read, decoded, or admitted by the CLI resource cap'. The USAGE string (lib.rs:60) spells the flags as unbounded repetition -- `[--materials <pack>]...` -- with no declared bound, so an invocation of 129 pairs DOES match the documented grammar. It is refused by a resource cap, which is the case `exit::INPUT` names explicitly. Reporting it as USAGE tells an agent its syntax is wrong when the syntax is correct; the accompanying fix text already says 'reduce the pack set', so only the exit class misleads.

FALSIFIER (executes today): crates/fs-cli/tests/cli.rs::g0_the_invocation_card_pack_ceiling_refuses_before_any_file_is_touched pins the current behaviour -- 128 pairs reaches project I/O (exit::INPUT + cli-input-read), 129 pairs refuses with cli-solve-card-pack-count at exit::USAGE. That assertion is deliberately labelled 'pinned, not endorsed' so the class cannot drift silently while this is decided.

DONE WHEN: an agent can key on (machine code, exit class) without ambiguity -- either each card-pack resource-cap code maps to exactly one documented class across every layer that can emit it, or lib.rs's exit-class doc comments are amended to state that one code may span classes and say how a caller should disambiguate. Changing the class requires `parse_args` to carry an exit class rather than assuming USAGE (lib.rs:233-304, 157), which is why this is filed rather than folded into hp7tb: it is a product-surface decision about a documented stable exit contract, not a test gap.

NOT IN SCOPE: the ceilings themselves are correct and now proven at both boundaries (bead frankensim-hp7tb slice, 2026-07-28).
close_reason: Landed: code at 2f9079e5 (sweeper committed my staged work mid-flight with an accurate message), CONTRACT at 0acd7080. Decision: each card-pack resource-cap code maps to exactly ONE class — exit::INPUT — from every layer (parse/read/admission), centralized in resource_cap_exit_class(); the grammar spells unbounded repetition so USAGE misreported correct syntax, and INPUT's doc names the resource-cap case explicitly. The 'pinned, not endorsed' ceiling-test assertion is now endorsed and asserts INPUT. CONTRACT error-model section states the one-code-one-class rule. Verified by executing the built test binaries directly (cargo's runner wedged): tests/cli.rs 15/15 incl. g0_the_invocation_card_pack_ceiling..., lib unit tests 20/20.

title: Variable-exponent f64::powi is build-mode-dependent: purge from deterministic paths, add fs-math powi_det + lint
description:
CONFIRMED with a minimized counterexample: 0.7f64.powi(k) differs by 1 ulp between debug and release builds from k=4 upward (0.7^4 = 0x3fcebb98c7e2823e debug vs ...3f release, cargo-built, pinned nightly 2026-07-05, aarch64). Root cause: std powi precision is documented as unspecified and its lowering (runtime exponentiation-by-squaring vs LLVM const-folding) depends on optimization level. Exponents <=3 are safe (squaring and sequential rounding orders coincide); divergence starts at 4.

This broke the fs-la rand_nla golden (debug observed 0x3e928bac8cf9fd48, release 0xf3dcb63be63f8ab9) and provoked an unjustified re-pin. The fixture is now fixed with a sequential product chain, but the same hazard is LATENT IN PRODUCTION PATHS:
- fs-feec/src/highorder/vecfam.rs (~10 sites): high-order basis monomials xi.powi(order) — G5 bit-stability hazard for r>=4 FEEC spaces across build modes/const-folding contexts.
- fs-ad/src/dual.rs:263-264: powi(n), powi(n-1) in dual-number pow rule.
- fs-dfo/src/cma.rs:245: powi(2*generations) — exponents in the thousands; maximal exposure.
- fs-la/tests/factor_battery.rs:50 fixture (test-only).

Fix: (1) fs-math gains a deterministic integer power (fixed evaluation order, conformance-tested, with a cross-build-mode golden); (2) migrate the sites above, bumping any affected goldens with justification; (3) a lint/xtask check forbids std powi with non-literal exponent or literal >3 outside fast-mode/no-claim paths (fits the existing ULP-ledger lint direction in wf9.14/r6r5).

Acceptance: powi_det golden identical across debug/release and both reference ISAs; migrated sites' batteries green; seeded violation caught by the lint. Found while executing the failure-compounding protocol (frankensim-epic-gauntlet-6nb.9) on the rand_nla golden break.

title: fs-conduction leaks fs_solver::krylov::ResidualClaim in a public field without re-exporting it
description:
FOUND while building the f85xj.5.10 upstream-evidence mutation sweep (NobleLion, 2026-07-28).

`fs_conduction::LinearSolveEvidence` is re-exported from the crate root (lib.rs:104-108) and its
`reported` field is public with type `fs_solver::krylov::ResidualClaim` (solve.rs:295). But
`ResidualClaim` itself is NOT re-exported by fs-conduction — `solve.rs:45` imports it privately
(`use fs_solver::krylov::{CgState, ResidualClaim, StallDiagnosis};`) and no `pub use` names it.
The same applies to `StallDiagnosis`, used by the public `stall: Option<StallDiagnosis>` field.

CONSEQUENCE: a downstream crate cannot construct or exhaustively match a `LinearSolveEvidence`
without taking its own direct dependency on fs-solver, purely to name a type fs-conduction already
exposes. I hit this exactly: fs-airflow's QoI seam needed to build a non-converged record to prove
its refusal guard is live, and had to add `fs-solver` as a dev-dependency (see the note in
crates/fs-airflow/Cargo.toml) for no reason other than naming `ResidualClaim`.

This is an API-surface bug, not a correctness bug: nothing computes a wrong answer. It is filed P3
accordingly.

DONE WHEN: `ResidualClaim` and `StallDiagnosis` are re-exported from fs-conduction's root alongside
`LinearSolveEvidence`, so every type reachable through a public field of a publicly re-exported
struct is nameable from the same crate; fs-conduction's CONTRACT public-types section names them;
and fs-airflow's dev-dependency on fs-solver plus its explanatory comment are removed, with the
crate's tests still green (the `a_contradictory_or_unconverged_conduction_report_refuses` test in
crates/fs-airflow/tests/qoi.rs is the exact consumer to re-point).

NOTE the DONE-WHEN deliberately does NOT ask for a general audit of every leaked type in the
workspace. If a broader sweep is wanted, file it separately: this bead is scoped to the two types
reachable from `LinearSolveEvidence`, which are the ones with a demonstrated downstream cost.
close_reason: Landed 53cb3579 (+lock). ResidualClaim + StallDiagnosis re-exported from fs-conduction root next to LinearSolveEvidence; CONTRACT public-types table names them with the reachability rationale; fs-airflow's naming-only fs-solver dev-dep and its explanatory comment removed; qoi.rs re-pointed to fs_conduction::ResidualClaim. title: frankentorch kernel-cpu at 74df606b does not compile under the pinned nightly-2026-07-06 (portable-SIMD Mask::select); torch surface unrunnable, pin held at 9627f39c by train 3
description:
Found during constellation train 3 (bead frankensim-rc-root-q61wp.39, 2026-09-02). At the frankentorch head the Mac checkout sits on (74df606bd5f1440d109deea115a0ab1bdf4cfd1b), `frankentorch-kernel-cpu 0.1.1` does not compile under FrankenSim's pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml channel nightly-2026-07-06, rustc 1.99.0-nightly 3659db0d3): `crates/ft-kernel-cpu/src/lib.rs:4546` and :4547 (and 17 more sites) call `.select(..)` on a portable-SIMD mask (`a.simd_le(neg3).select(zero, mid)`), which that nightly's `Mask` does not provide — E0599 "no method named `select` found for struct `f64x4`/`f32x8`". The frankentorch compatibility selector (`cargo test --locked -p fs-ad --features torch-bridge --lib bridge -- --exact ...`) therefore exits 101 with zero tests executed on yto (x86-64) — an ABSENCE of evidence, which the bump protocol refuses for that mover. Train 3 advanced the other six pins and held frankentorch at 9627f39c; the Mac's frankentorch checkout stays off-pin (drift gate: stale-lock, visible not red) until this closes.

DONE-WHEN: either (a) frankentorch's kernel-cpu builds under nightly-2026-07-06 (the sibling repo's call; likely `Mask::select` vs `simd_select`/`select` API drift — pin-compatible code, or a frankentorch toolchain bump the compatibility train then re-evaluates), or (b) FrankenSim's toolchain pin advances via bead go7a's protocol AND a new train moves frankentorch with the surface executed green (exactly 4 registered tests, not a module filter — see the selector fix landed with train 3). Repro on yto: cd /data/projects/sj-20260901/frankensim; git -C ../frankentorch checkout 74df606b; cargo test --locked -p fs-ad --features torch-bridge --lib -- --list.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CORRECTION (NobleLion, 2026-09-02 ~15:50Z): the defect is NOT specific to the candidate head. `.select(` on portable-SIMD masks entered ft-kernel-cpu at 014b3f44 (2026-08-04, "retire obsolete SIMD APIs"), which is BEFORE the recorded pin 9627f39c (2026-08-21); `git show 9627f39c:crates/ft-kernel-cpu/src/lib.rs` has 29 call sites. So under FrankenSim's pinned nightly-2026-07-06 the frankentorch compatibility surface has been unbuildable at the recorded pin as well — it was simply never executed exactly there (the selector was also vacuous, see q61wp.39). Consequence for train 3: frankentorch is held at 9627f39c and Cargo.lock is relocked to kernel-cpu 0.1.0 for consistency with the declared pin; the surface is honestly NotRun at both heads. Consequence for THIS bead: the fix is either (a) frankentorch making ft-kernel-cpu build on nightly-2026-07-06 (a `Mask::select` shim or `simd_select`), or (b) FrankenSim advancing its toolchain pin under bead go7a's protocol and then a train moving frankentorch with the surface executed green. Until then, any Mac build without --locked will rewrite Cargo.lock's kernel-cpu line back to 0.1.1 (the Mac checkout is at 0.1.1): that churn is the visible cost of an off-pin sibling and must not be "fixed" by re-pinning the lock to a version the declared head does not have.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
RECURRENCE COST (NobleLion, 2026-09-03): Cargo.lock's frankentorch-kernel-cpu line has now been rewritten from the declared pin 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 three times in two days, and restored three times (3106f497, c176af4a, f558ef34). Mechanism: the constellation lock pins frankentorch at 9627f39c whose kernel-cpu is 0.1.0, but the Mac's sibling checkout sits at a newer head whose kernel-cpu is 0.1.1, so any local build without --locked rewrites the line, and the rewritten line then refuses --locked builds at the declared pins on the Linux verification host. Every agent who touches either side pays for it.

Two ways to end it, both owner calls:
1. ADVANCE the pin — blocked by this bead: ft-kernel-cpu has used portable-SIMD Mask::select since 014b3f44 (2026-08-04) and does not build under the pinned nightly-2026-07-06 at EITHER head. Advancing needs the toolchain pin moved or the kernel changed.
2. MOVE the Mac's frankentorch checkout onto 9627f39c so both sides agree with the declared TCB. Cheap, but it is a shared sibling checkout and other lanes may be building against the newer head deliberately — which is exactly why I have not done it unilaterally.

Until one of those, expect the line to keep flipping; anyone who sees a --locked refusal naming kernel-cpu should check this line first rather than debugging the sibling.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
OSCILLATION ENDED (NobleLion, 2026-09-04, owner-authorized, commit 906c73b7). Diagnosis first, because the earlier framing was incomplete: the flapping was not carelessness by any lane, it was structural. Cargo.lock records a PATH dependency's version as found ON DISK. The workstation's frankentorch sits at main (kernel-cpu 0.1.1) and the Linux verification clone sat at the declared pin 9627f39c (0.1.0). One shared Cargo.lock cannot satisfy --locked on both machines at once, so whichever machine ran cargo last rewrote the line and broke the other. Four rewrites in two days.

FIXED by making the two checkouts agree, in the direction that costs nothing: /data/projects/sj-20260901/frankentorch moved forward from 9627f39c to 74df606b, the same head the workstation already had, and Cargo.lock now records 0.1.1. The other direction was rejected on inspection: the pin is 619 commits behind main, so moving the workstation onto it would have rolled a shared repository back a month.

WHY THIS IS SAFE. frankentorch is an OPTIONAL dependency of fs-ad (ft-autograd / ft-core, `optional = true`) and is off in the default feature set, so nothing on either machine compiles ft-kernel-cpu. Aligning the checkouts changes no build, no test, and no retained evidence. It also means this bead's blocker — ft-kernel-cpu not building under nightly-2026-07-06 since 014b3f44 — never affected frankensim's builds at all; it only ever blocked frankentorch's own surface test during train 3.

VERIFIED: `cargo metadata --locked` resolves on the Linux host with the aligned checkout and the new lock.

CONSEQUENCE, recorded rather than hidden: constellation.lock still declares frankentorch at 9627f39c, so the drift gate will now report this one sibling off-pin on the verification host. That is the honest state — the pin is a month stale — and a visible drift row is strictly better than a lock line that silently flapped. The remaining decision for a train 4 is whether to advance the frankentorch pin to 74df606b (its surface still cannot execute under the pinned nightly, so it would be admitted the way train 3 admitted it: declared, with the surface recorded as unrunnable) or to drop frankentorch from the declared TCB entirely on the grounds that an optional, never-compiled dependency is not part of the trusted computing base. I have not made that call; it is governance, not bookkeeping.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DONE-WHEN MET, ALL FOUR CLAUSES MEASURED (NobleLion, 2026-09-04, tree at b92b00ec, Linux verification host at the declared pins).

1. "check-constellation-drift reports all seven on-pin" — YES. Measured after train 4: 183 crates, 0 violations, and the frankentorch row now reads "on-pin and clean at 74df606bd5f1440d109deea115a0ab1bdf4cfd1b". check-constellation additionally reports lock OK with all sibling trees clean (exit 0).
2. "check-source-manifest 0" — YES, exit 0, "policy OK: 183 crates".
3. "yto spine tests pass at the pins" — YES, and this is the clause that was PARTIAL since 09-02. Measured tonight at the declared pins: fs-mesh green across every target, fs-project 71 tests / 0 failed, fs-cli 156 tests / 0 failed.
4. "the train log row exists" — YES. Train 4 is recorded in docs/CONSTELLATION_GOVERNANCE.md with the cost that forced it and the evidence that backs it.

WHAT CLAUSE 3 COST, because "the spine tests now pass" understates it — the host had never run them since 09-02 and four defects were hiding behind the full disk:
- fs-mesh's LIBRARY did not compile at HEAD (13 errors from a half-landed bounding-box index refactor), so fs-project, fs-cli and everything downstream could not build at all. Repaired fbf60467.
- fs-project's exact-containment test asserted a rounding coincidence that holds on aarch64 and not x86-64. Repaired 796d61e5.
- fs-project's g3 interface test matched a substring the diagnostic never emits — red on every platform, not the x86 divergence I first guessed. Repaired cc18fc9e.
- fs-cli's step_heatsink target did not compile and its STEP fixture was non-canonical by one byte. Repaired f99e4bf6 / 75e80838; that battery went from zero executions to 5 of 5, which also closed q61wp.51.

TRAIN 4, the substance of this bead's remaining decision: frankentorch advanced 9627f39c -> 74df606b, the other six heads untouched, lock hash 4a7ffa243c0cf006 -> 0730b0a5295eeab7 (361b931a). Train 3 held that sibling because its surface cannot compile under the pinned nightly; holding it turned out to carry a cost nobody had priced, because Cargo records a path dependency's version as found on disk and one shared Cargo.lock cannot satisfy --locked on two machines whose checkouts disagree. The line flipped four times in two days. Retreating the workstation was refused by this bead's own guardrail (619 commits behind; pins never move backwards), so both checkouts were aligned forward and the pin followed. The advance is recorded as the bookkeeping change it is: nothing in frankensim compiles that sibling (optional dependency of fs-ad, off by default), so what was verified is what it touches — metadata --locked resolves at the new head and both constellation gates are green on the host.

ONE THING LEFT STANDING DELIBERATELY: the workstation still reports constellation drift, and did before this change too — its own sibling checkouts have moved past the declared pins independently (asupersync among them). That is a separate, true signal about a dev machine, and locking to a dev machine's heads to silence it would defeat the point of a declared TCB.

Closing: the declared TCB and the built TCB agree, the gates that prove it are green on the verification host, and the spine runs at those pins.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: STATUS AFTER TRAIN 4 (NobleLion, 2026-09-04): this bead's defect is UNCHANGED and still true — ft-kernel-cpu does not compile under nightly-2026-07-06 at either head. What changed is that it no longer costs anything: the pin was advanced to 74df606b so the declared and built trees agree, and the Cargo.lock oscillation it was causing is over. It matters again only if someone enables fs-ad's optional frankentorch feature, at which point the pinned toolchain must move or the kernel must stop using portable-SIMD Mask::select. title: Prevent delimiter injection in RANS model-card manifest bindings
description: RansModelCard::manifest_hash concatenates statement keys and values with raw NUL delimiters, but RansCardDraft admits caller-controlled NUL bytes in manifest text. A one-entry boundary-condition map can therefore encode the same hash preimage as a different two-entry map, defeating the exact-card binding promised by the API.
acceptance_criteria: Freeze rejects any draft whose rendered statement manifest contains an embedded NUL before minting an immutable card, preserving existing valid-card hashes. A focused regression demonstrates the previously colliding one-entry/two-entry construction and passes after the refusal; fs-scenario RANS-card tests remain green.
notes: Fresh-eyes root cause: commit d1e70141 made the legacy authority exclusion an unconditional item-level exception. That admitted both the semicolon-containing exclusion and its two-item split, whose exclusion rows and manifest hash preimages are identical; it also bypassed comma validation if copied into a comma-delimited field. Current patch scopes the legacy atom to exclusions, rejects its adjacent split spelling, preserves canonical rendered bytes, and adds focused collision and field-scope regressions in rans_card_gates.rs. rustfmt and git diff --check pass. UBS scanned exactly the two changed files; it reported only test panic/assert inventory and bounded windows(2) indexing as non-actionable heuristics, with no true positive in the patch. The strict RCH test command was refused before execution with exit 103 because no worker was admissible. Required host preflight sbh check --need 20G returned exit 2: Data volume about 111.8 GB free, 5.61 percent, status critical. Per AGENTS.md, no heavy Cargo or RCH workload may run until pressure is reclaimed. Runtime proof is pending and this bead remains in progress.
close_reason: Fixed-and-verified by GoldOrchid. Root cause: RansModelCard::manifest_hash binds k-0-v concatenations while RansCardDraft admitted NUL bytes in manifest text, letting one boundary-condition entry encode the same hash preimage as two. Guard landed 2026-08-24 in 1089b779 (EmbeddedManifestDelimiter refusal over the rendered manifest at freeze; with NULs excluded the encoding parses back uniquely so it is injective), but its regression test never passed - the fixture cleared boundary_conditions and inserted arbitrary keys, tripping regime-completeness refusal [inlet/walls/thermal-wall/outlet] before the delimiter gate could speak. Repair (this commit): crates/fs-scenario/tests/rans_card_gates.rs embedded_nul_cannot_alias_manifest_pair_boundaries now overwrites inlet with a NUL-smuggled value on the canonical draft while the split variant carries the same content as separate rows, preserving every required row so both sides reach the delimiter gate; smuggled variant refuses EmbeddedManifestDelimiter as asserted. Independent verification by GoldOrchid via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE on worker vmi1227854: cargo test -p fs-scenario --features rans-rung --test rans_card_gates => 14 passed 0 failed; then cargo test -p fs-scenario --all-targets --features rans-rung => all 14 test binaries green (216 tests total, 0 failures). Note: default-feature builds do not compile this gated test binary; the feature flag is required.

comments.text: Progress handoff 2026-08-26 by GoldOrchid [claimant]: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED and guard verified present at HEAD (1089b779 added EmbeddedManifestDelimiter refusal in RansCardDraft::freeze over the rendered manifest; with NULs excluded the k\0v\0 concatenation parses back uniquely, so distinct manifests cannot share a preimage). However its regression test embedded_nul_cannot_alias_manifest_pair_boundaries NEVER PASSED: the fixture cleared boundary_conditions and inserted arbitrary keys, tripping the regime-completeness refusal [inlet/walls/thermal-wall/outlet] before the delimiter gate. title: REALITY CHECK 2026-09-01 — two journeys, one rule, five owner decisions
description:
## Why this epic exists

A full reality check of FrankenSim was run on 2026-09-01 at HEAD b46da547 (twelve read-only investigation lanes plus an executed compile/test run on the yto verification host). The finding: the workspace is a large, mostly honest library substrate (1.33 M source lines, 171 crate directories, 171/171 contracts, layer direction enforced) whose central thesis — a design study running from typed intent through certified physics and adjoints to an optimized geometry — has never executed once on a production PDE. The only production-grade 3-D physics is steady conduction, reachable through a CLI that stops before any user-visible answer (QoI, report, package, run, compare all refuse). Meanwhile the tracker holds 3,289 beads, 83 % blocked, 2 ready, with ~1,250 live beads (leapfrog-2026, ext theorem lanes, ext machine flagships, Euler physical-lab beads) that describe studies on physics that is 2-D, toy-scale, or absent.

Two mechanisms produced the gap and both are still live: (1) claims are self-certified prose — the QoI bead s2l9v was closed "done" while fs-cli still hits `unreachable!` at the QoI stage; `thermal.conduction-solve` was promoted to L3 on a lane (scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh) that never runs conduction; two orphaned fs-cli files contain hard-coded "Verified 342.15 K" report output; (2) nothing gates scope expansion on a delivered journey.

## What this epic delivers

Two journeys, one rule, five owner decisions:

- **Journey A** — Cooling 0.1 completes all six stages and earns a legitimate L3 (children rc-j1 … rc-j6).
- **Journey B** — the plan's P2 marquee (topology optimization on a raw SDF, no mesh, composed certificate) un-gated and shipped as `frankensim study` (children rc-m1 … rc-m4).
- **One rule** — capability levels and README facts read retained, digest-pinned receipts from executed lanes, never prose (rc-t2).
- **Five decisions** only the owner can make (rc-o1 … rc-o5), each with a stated default.
- **Truth repairs** for every defect the audit found (rc-t1 … rc-t7), **portfolio/graph moves** (rc-p1, rc-p3, rc-p4, finish-out lanes) and a **wedge-first frontier** (rc-w1 … rc-w5).

## How to use it

Every child carries: the vision goal it serves (plan section pointer), the falsifier that distinguishes done from claimed, the existing seam to reuse, the receipt it must retain, and the logging it must emit. All children are labelled `reality-check-2026-09`. The full audit report (vision checklist with per-goal status, program table, truth defects, bridge plan) is the published artifact from the 2026-09-01 session; this epic is self-contained without it.

## Success criteria

- `capability-maturity.json` records exactly the L3 entries whose cited receipts list the capability's stage as executed (check-maturity enforces it).
- `frankensim run examples/heatsink-fan/heatsink-fan.fsim …` completes six stages; the Python client reads a QoI verdict with an evidence colour and an 8-term budget; the solver-free checker accepts the package.
- `frankensim study` runs the 2-D marquee loop to a certificate with a retained golden.
- `br ready` returns ≥ 10 items and every one of them is on a journey path.
- The five owner decisions are recorded (comment on each rc-o bead) and executed.

## Non-goals

No re-beadification of the plan documents. No new harness, analyzer, or dashboard beyond the receipt rule and one DSR gate line. No deletions: fabricated files are rewritten in place, parked work is deferred, not removed.

title: Fix four committed-red test targets; add a no-run workspace test build to the DSR quality gate
description:
## Background

`cargo test --workspace` cannot build at HEAD b46da547. Four test targets were committed red between 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-27 and never compiled since (verified on yto, pinned constellation, three `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` runs):

1. `crates/fs-scenario/tests/rans_card_gates.rs` (commit 501220ba0): imports `fs_scenario::rans_card`, which is behind `#[cfg(feature = "rans-rung")]`; the test target has no `[[test]] required-features` entry, so the default test build breaks.
2. `crates/fs-feec/tests/differential_characters.rs` (b3dc1dc2): uses `TypedMap` and `ObjectSpace` (both exist in `fs_feec::differential_characters`) without importing them.
3. `crates/fs-session/tests/snapshot_freeze_gate.rs` (8c53e7e0): E0308 expected `SnapshotFreezeReceipt`, found `CommittedFreeze<FixtureState>`; `PressureReceipt` is not an iterator. fs-exec's freeze API moved in c991e5f9; b93af059 repaired the library but not this test target.
4. `crates/fs-evidence-runner/src/value.rs` unit tests at :4158 and :4165 (6c066636): E0425 `domain` is never defined in the test fn.

None of these breaks was announced in any commit subject. The last suite receipt (suite-receipt.json) is from 2026-08-01, ~2,200 commits ago. A red test target that sits unannounced for nine days means no agent is building the workspace test set.

## Deliverable

- All four targets compile; each fix is the smallest correct one (feature gate the test, add the imports, adapt to the moved freeze API, define `domain` from the fixture).
- The DSR quality gate for frankensim gains one step: a no-run build of every workspace test target, so a committed-red test target fails the repo gate the day it lands. This is the one process addition this audit permits; it is tied to this exact defect.

## DONE-WHEN

- On the yto verification clone at the fix commit: `cargo test --workspace --no-run` exits 0 with the pinned constellation.
- `dsr quality --tool frankensim --dry-run` shows the no-run test-build step; the gate's log names the step and its wall time.
- Commit subject names all four targets.

## Tests and logging

The four targets themselves are the tests. The DSR step logs the target count and the first compiler error verbatim on failure.

## Reuse / seams

fs-exec `freeze.rs` (moved API), fs-scenario `Cargo.toml` `[features] rans-rung`, docs/CI_GATES.md (record the new step in its table).

## Vision pointer

AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" / "DSR — Required CI"; plan §13.3 "done is conformance green on both ISAs".
