title: A13 export of a run retained under an older receipt schema refuses as unknown-run: name the real reason and define the export compatibility rule
description:
REPRODUCTION (2026-09-02, SlateOwl). A heatsink run retained at 22:45 by the frankensim binary built 22:38 (SOLVE_DRIVER_VERSION 11, conduction receipt v3) in a 640 KiB ledger with 9 ops. The binary rebuilt at 00:40 (same driver 11, conduction receipt v4 from bridge plan B3) answers "frankensim report RUN LEDGER" with exit 4 cli-solve-unknown-run: "no solve run ... exists in this ledger". A fresh import + solve + report with the 00:40 binary works. So the run exists; the loader (crates/fs-cli/src/solve.rs, load_latest_state / validate_resume_candidate around the "no solve run" refusal) finds no candidate it accepts and reports non-existence.

WHY IT MATTERS. Users who upgrade lose access to yesterday's runs with a message that blames them; the L3 lane receipts refer to ledgers that a later binary cannot export; compare (B8) across an upgrade becomes impossible.

WORK.
1. In the candidate scan, distinguish "no op for this run id" from "candidates found, none accepted"; the latter refuses with a new code cli-solve-run-incompatible naming the stage, the retained schema string, the expected one, and both driver versions.
2. Decide and document the export compatibility rule: a receipt MINOR bump (additive keys, as B3's v4) keeps old runs exportable — export reads retained receipts as retained and does not re-validate keys it does not need; a MAJOR bump refuses by name. Write it in crates/fs-cli/CONTRACT.md next to the receipt schema list.
3. Test: a checked-in v3 conduction-receipt fixture (bytes from the reproduction ledger) drives both branches.
4. Logging: the refusal lists the candidate op ids seen and why each was rejected.

FALSIFIER. The reproduction ledger (scratch j1-trial6-run/trial.db, or the checked-in fixture) exports after the fix, or refuses with the new code and the named schemas — never as unknown.

SIZE. M. DEPENDS. none. RELATED. q61wp.47 (compare) and q61wp.62 (export speed) touch the same loader.

--- Standard (bridge plan §15) ---
Falsifier named above is the exact command or test that fails if this item is faked.
Receipt: path, schema, digest; names the commit and host fingerprint.
Logging: the lane JSONL alone must locate a failure.
Source: COMPREHENSIVE_BRIDGE_PLAN_FOR_FRANKENSIM.md (item A13, added 2026-09-02).
acceptance_criteria: report/package (and resume) on a ledger whose completed run carries an older stage-receipt schema refuse with a code saying the run EXISTS but its rows do not validate under this driver (schema and driver versions named), never cli-solve-unknown-run; a checked-in v3 receipt fixture pins it; the CONTRACT states which schema bumps keep old runs exportable.
notes:
2026-09-02 (SlateOwl) MECHANISM, part 1 (confirmed by reading): crates/fs-cli/src/solve.rs
is_supported_stage_discovery_row -> parse_stage_discovery_ir returns Err when the op's recorded
driver_version != SOLVE_DRIVER_VERSION, and the row is silently dropped as a non-candidate, so ANY
run retained under an older driver version is reported as unknown-run. Part 2 (the reproduction is
same-driver 11, receipt v3 vs v4): not yet located — validate_resume_candidate errors would surface
as a different code, so some other discovery predicate (row.session, outcome, t_start/t_end, ir
length <= 512, STAGE_STATE_KIND filter) is dropping the candidate; instrument the scan (count rows
seen / rejected per predicate) as the first step. Both parts get the same fix shape: count
candidates seen vs accepted and refuse with cli-solve-run-incompatible naming the predicate that
rejected them.

Dependencies:
2026-09-02 03:20 (SlateOwl) IN PROGRESS: stage_discovery_rejection(row, run) -> Result<SolveStage, String> names every predicate (op id, other run, outcome, diagnostic, IR size, IR parse incl. driver version, no producer, timing slots); load_latest_state counts ops of this run and their rejection reasons (plus branch / exec-mode / no driver-state artifact) and, when ops exist but none is admissible, refuses with cli-solve-run-incompatible listing '<count> x <reason>' — unknown-run only when no op carries the run id. CONTRACT updated. Suites running; the reproduction ledger (scratch j1-trial6-run/trial.db, v3 receipts) is the falsifier and will also tell us which predicate rejects the same-driver v3 run.

Mechanism confirmed by the falsifier: the reproduction ledger was retained under driver version 10 (7 of its 8 ops rejected by 'solve-stage discovery driver version is unsupported', 1 by 'names an unknown stage'), and the loader silently dropped every candidate and said the run did not exist. Now stage_discovery_rejection names every predicate; load_latest_state counts ops per run and refuses with cli-solve-run-incompatible (exit 4) listing '<count> x <reason>' when ops exist but none is admissible; cli-solve-unknown-run only when no op carries the id (verified: all-zero id still unknown). title: Restore compilation of the 15 non-compiling targets at 6c33d6a18 and execute the suites they were hiding
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-24)

Since ~2026-09-13 most commits on main come from a committer whose own messages say "Native execution remains requested, not claimed passing: local Cargo/rustc are absent" (86 such commits 09-19..09-23). The result, measured on 2026-09-24:

- At `018246530` the `frankensim` binary itself did not compile: `fs-session` referenced a non-existent `fs_la::GemmRunReport` (fixed later by `b8d4e25c1`).
- At `6c33d6a18`, `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going` exited 101 with **15 targets that do not compile**. A test target that does not compile emits no red test, so every proof inside it is silently absent:
  - `fs-conduction` (lib test): `src/adjoint/robin/nonlinear/tests.rs:154-158` assigns through a `&RobinLinearization` deref (E0594). The WHOLE fs-conduction unit-test suite is hidden by this.
  - `fs-couple` (lib test): `src/render/plate/impact/cavity/neck/exterior_tests.rs:117,120` calls a missing `samples_rendered`. The WHOLE fs-couple unit-test suite is hidden.
  - `fs-couple` tests `iqn_ils` (ambiguous `{float}.abs()`, line 23) and `plate_aperture` (`radiation.rs:143,146` u64 vs usize).
  - `fs-cli` tests `cooling_contact_controls`, `cooling_materials`, `cooling_transient_radiation`, `cooling_transient_uq`, `cooling_uq_radiation`: invalid format strings (`}}}}` unmatched, e.g. `cooling_contact_controls.rs:62`). These are the regressions cited as evidence for the 09-17..09-23 cooling features.
  - `fs-cli` bin `equilibrium_uq` test: `src/bin/equilibrium_uq/joint.rs:120` `mod tests` file not found.
  - `fs-marquee` bin `fs-marquee-elasticity-robust` (a PRODUCT binary, not only its tests): `src/bin/elasticity_robust/projected.rs:15-18` cannot resolve `stress`, `checkpoint`, `refinement`, `design_regions` modules (files exist under `projected/`; module path resolution is wrong).
  - `fs-dwr` test `motion_goal3` (missing `fs_solver` dev-dep, missing `AdaptiveElasticity3::{n,apply}`).
  - `fs-ascent` test `frankenscipy_optimizer_oracle_casebook` (non-exhaustive enums, missing lifetime, removed field `has_general_constraints`).
  - `fs-vfit` test `reactive_network` (ambiguous float literals).

## What

Make every target compile, with the smallest correct fix per site (do not delete tests to get green). Where an API changed underneath a test, fix the test to the new API only if the test's claim is still meaningful; otherwise restore the API.

## Done when

1. `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets` exits 0 on a HEAD that contains the fixes (cite the HEAD and the log path).
2. Because cargo stops scheduling dependents after a failure, re-run the check after each fix batch (see memory "compile debt hides proofs").
3. The now-compiling suites are EXECUTED once and the result recorded here verbatim (pass/fail counts): `cargo test -p fs-conduction --lib`, `cargo test -p fs-couple --lib`, `cargo test -p fs-cli --test cooling_contact_controls --test cooling_materials --test cooling_transient_radiation --test cooling_transient_uq --test cooling_uq_radiation`, `cargo test -p fs-marquee --bins`. Failures that are real defects get their own bug beads; do not `#[ignore]` a true-defect test.

## Notes

This is the P0 of the 2026-09-24 check: until it is done, no feature landed since ~09-13 has test evidence, and the tracker/README cannot honestly describe them.

title: Radiative cooling transient: a cold radiative sink RAISES the sampled peak (301.4269 vs 301.4242 K without radiation)
description:
## Defect (found 2026-09-24 by the first native run of tests/cooling_transient_radiation.rs)

`nonlinear_contact_trajectory_keeps_radiation_out_of_the_air_ledger` asserts that adding surface radiation to COLD black reservoirs lowers the transient peak. It does not.

Reproduction (release build of the 2026-09-24 working tree): examples/cooling-network/radiative-contact-pulse.json with transient.intervals = [{duration_s 4, power_scale 1, fan 1}, {duration_s 6, power_scale 0, fan 1.5}] (the test's short()):
- with radiation (first-face eps 0.85 to 280 K, last-face eps 0.6 to 290 K): sampled peak 301.42690016868977 K, radiative loss 12.916 J (about 1.29 W per sample);
- the same input with the radiation section removed: sampled peak 301.4242295696386 K.

A pure heat sink cannot raise the maximum of this parabolic problem (comparison principle), so either the radiating trajectory is wrong or the two runs differ in something besides the sink (time grid, nonlinear-contact iteration, coupling iterations). The energy ledger closes (the test's energy checks pass), so the defect is in where the heat goes, not how much.

## Done when
Root cause identified; the radiating peak is below the plain peak on this input; the regression passes natively. Do not relax the inequality.
close_reason: Root cause: the consistent P1 capacitance is non-monotone (its inverse has negative entries). The difference converged to +0.0036 K as dt->0; it was not a coupling defect, and steady was correct. Decisive: with the capacitance lumped, the radiating peak falls below the plain peak. Fixed at 05db922bf with row-sum lumping (rho c_p V/4 per vertex; uniform heat content exact). The test's strict inequality is unchanged and passes natively. 1035 tests across conduction/vvreg/vmanifest/plan/phs/cli(lib, solve, all cooling*) are green. The one-tet BE oracle was re-derived for the lumped mass. Self-verified by native re-execution only.

comments.author: SlateOwl
comments.text:
Diagnosis 2026-09-25 (native, release build of 5254181bf):
- NOT the nonlinear conductivity: with both k(T) curves made constant at their 300 K values the peak still rises by +0.00270 K.
- NOT a structural replacement of convection by radiation: the rise scales smoothly with emissivity (eps 0.85: +0.00269 K; 0.1: +0.00032 K; 0.001: +0.000003 K).
- STEADY is correct: without the transient section, radiation lowers every one of the 16 solid vertices by 2.23-3.62 K (max 332.4355 -> 329.4194 K), energy closes.
- TRANSIENT only: +0.00267 K at t=4 s, +0.00089 K at t=10 s; stored energy is lower by almost exactly the radiated heat; the air heat gain turns NEGATIVE with radiation (-0.0087 W vs +0.0062 W at t=2 s).
Leading hypotheses: (a) the consistent-mass P1 backward-Euler step is not monotone (no discrete maximum principle), so a localized sink produces a small wrong-signed response at the far hot spot - test by switching to a lumped mass or halving dt and watching the sign; (b) the transient conjugate air coupling redistributes heat once the radiating faces fall below the air temperature. If (a), the test's physical premise is wrong for this discretization and should compare against a lumped-mass run or a looser, justified tolerance; if (b), it is a coupling defect.

comments.author: SlateOwl
comments.text: Time-step study (radiating minus plain, peak objective): max_step 2 s: +0.00267 K (t=4), +0.00089 K (t=10); 0.5 s: +0.00336 / +0.00192; 0.125 s: +0.00355 / +0.00221. The difference CONVERGES to about +0.0036 K as dt -> 0, so it is not a backward-Euler time artefact; it is consistent with hypothesis (a) in its semi-discrete form: a consistent P1 mass matrix has an inverse with negative entries, so M T' = -K T + f is non-monotone at every dt, and on this 12-tet fixture a localized sink can raise a distant nodal maximum by millikelvin. Decisive next check: rerun with a lumped mass (if the lab exposes one) or on a refined mesh; if the anomaly vanishes, the TEST premise (strict inequality) is wrong for consistent-mass P1 and should compare against a tolerance derived from the mass-matrix non-monotonicity, not assert a strict physical ordering.

comments.author: SlateOwl
comments.text: CORRECTION (SlateOwl, 2026-09-25): my close reason and 05db922bf claimed 'every fs-cli cooling* binary green'. That was false. The run's --test list came from 'ls | rg ^cooling' under an aliased ls (lsd, inode columns) and selected almost nothing. The lumping actually broke 21 tests (bin unit tests plus 7 integration binaries). Fixed at 45af6da3d: oracles re-derived for the lumped mass, design limits re-tuned with the real binary, measurement pins re-pinned. The full 'cargo ltest -p fs-cli -p fs-conduction' is now green (72 binaries, 1112 passed, 0 failed). A refinement probe justifies keeping lumping: lumped and consistent peaks agree within 0.6% of the rise at n=4..32, and both converge to 57.28 K; the rules are not systematically ordered in conservatism.

title: Enclosure-radiation design search: conjugate balance unclosed after one iteration (4.63e-8 W vs 3.33e-8 W gate)
description:
## Defect (found 2026-09-24 by the first native run of tests/cooling_radiative_design.rs)

`enclosure_target_search_keeps_reflection_and_internal_heat_accounting` refuses with: airflow heat transport: Airflow(ConjugateBalanceUnclosed { iterations: 1, max_region_imbalance 4.6300e-8 W, tolerance 3.3333e-8 W }). The exchange met its temperature criterion after ONE iteration while the solid/air heat rates disagree by 1.39x the gate.

Questions to answer (not a tolerance to loosen): is the 3.33e-8 W gate absolute and below what the enclosure-radiation fixed point resolves after its own tolerance; does the design search's candidate evaluation skip an iteration the plain solve performs; does the imbalance shrink with more exchange iterations (stop rule wrong) or stay (balance inconsistent with the enclosure's internal exchange)?

## Done when
Root cause stated with a measurement; the test passes natively with an unchanged or justified gate.
close_reason: Root cause (measured): the coupled-transport driver treated the per-branch probe's ConjugateBalanceUnclosed as terminal, so it stopped on the kelvin criterion and refused instead of iterating. The gate is absolute heat/(n+1) = 3.33e-8 W; at candidate h up to 1000 W/m2K, hA is about 5 W/K, so a 1e-8 K step leaves about 4.6e-8 W. Fixed at the new HEAD commit: iterate while unclosed; the refusal is final at budget exhaustion or at an exact fixed point. Gate unchanged; test green natively; fs-airflow 232/0; all fs-cli cooling binaries green except .68.1. Self-verified by native re-execution only.

title: fs-topopt CutFEM marquee never refines: DWR gate authorizes no split (tm_001, tm_003)
description:
## Defect (found 2026-09-24 by the first native run of fs-topopt tests with --features cutfem-marquee)

`tests/marquee.rs` tm_001_improves_with_zero_rebuilds and tm_003_dwr_splits_concentrate_at_the_boundary fail: the CutFEM-octree topology marquee never refines. tm_001 output: {"first_analysis":0.00956,"final_returned_design":0.00789,"total_splits":0,"total_rebuilds":0}; the assertion "refinement happened as splits" fails, and tm_003's "the DWR gate authorizes refinement" fails.

So the DWR-guided octree refinement the README advertises for fs-topopt's cutfem-marquee lane (and that the P2 marquee exit criterion depends on) does not run: either the DWR gate never authorizes a split or the split path is unreachable. The objective still improves, so the optimizer itself runs.

## Done when
Root cause stated (gate threshold, estimator scale, or wiring); tm_001 and tm_003 pass natively without loosening their assertions; the fs-topopt CONTRACT/README text matches the behaviour.
close_reason: Root cause: the gate DEFINITION was wrong, not the estimator. v1 counted mass only on zero-straddling cells, while the policy refines cut + one-cell ghost halo, and the error sits in that halo. Measured by a scratch probe on the seeded fixture at level 4: cut cells 11% of mass on 10% of cells (no concentration), cut+halo 48% on 26%, and the top-10 indicators were all one cell off the interface. Policy v2 (e7a6e21dc) measures band mass on the shared in_dwr_refinement_band predicate and keeps the 0.15 floor unlowered. It adds a concentration clause (band share > area share), planted-negative tested. tm_001 green (328 splits, 0 rebuilds, compliance 0.00956->0.00823) and tm_003 green (advances at L4/L5, declines at L6). fs-topopt --features cutfem-marquee 171/0. CONTRACT updated. Self-verified by native re-execution; no independent verifier. Side find: golden-couplings.json had been pretty-printed (c5f447e1c), which blinded check-goldens. Restored at 0b883575f; the hidden matdb compiler drift was re-pinned at 911c97328.

comments.author: SlateOwl
comments.text: Diagnosis 2026-09-24 (native, rch): tm_003 per-iteration decisions are all GateNotMet: cut-band indicator mass / total = 0.1100, 0.0932, 0.0841 (cut 4.19e-5, 3.56e-5, 3.18e-5 of total ~3.8e-4) against DWR_CUT_BAND_MASS_GATE = 0.15, band level 4 of max 6. So the estimator runs and the wiring works; the indicator mass now sits mostly OFF the cut band. Marquee code is unchanged since 6557969ec (08-25, CutFEM stabilization represented via the physical-coefficient API) - the likely point where ghost/stabilization contributions moved mass. Do NOT lower the gate to 0.08 to go green: find where the off-band mass comes from (per-cell eta map of iteration 1, split cut vs ghost-band vs interior) and decide whether the estimator or the gate definition is wrong.

title: OWNER DECISION: a verification lane for the no-Cargo remote committer (uncompiled commits reach main)
description:
## Decision requested from the owner (2026-09-24 reality check)

Most of main's recent volume (698 commits from the GitHub-noreply identity since 09-13; 608 commits in the week to 09-23) is written by a committer that has NO Cargo/rustc. It commits code it could not compile, and says so in the body. Consequences measured 2026-09-24: the product binary failed to compile at 018246530; 15 targets do not compile at 6c33d6a18; four new GitHub lanes have 0 successes in 137 runs; 0 of the last 40 product-crate commits updated the tracker.

AGENTS.md makes DSR/rch the verification path, but that committer cannot reach them. Nothing in the repo's process catches this; the damage accrues silently (compile debt hides proofs).

## Options

title: JOURNEY A — Cooling 0.1 completes six stages and earns a receipt-backed L3
description:
## Why this journey

The repository has never delivered a user-visible answer from its product CLI. Today `frankensim solve` executes import-verify, assign, material-resolve and an interval-bracketed flow-network operating point, plus conduction when the project declares a `cooling.conduction` section; it then hits `unreachable!` at the QoI stage. `report`, `package`, `run`, `compare` return `cli-stage-unavailable`. The two showcase examples (heated-plate, heatsink-fan) declare no conduction, so the documented walkthrough never solves physics. The QoI producer exists (`crates/fs-airflow/src/qoi.rs:777 extract_thermal_qois`) and nothing wires it. The one L3 in the registry was earned on a lane that never runs the capability (rc-t2 demotes it).

Journey A finishes the spine the EXTREAL program already chose (E06 Cooling 0.1) and earns the first L3 that survives its own falsifiers.

## Target (user-visible)

`frankensim run examples/heatsink-fan/heatsink-fan.fsim ledger.db --materials data/reference-project/aa6061.fsmcdpk` completes all six stages. The user reads: a junction-temperature QoI against the project's ThermalLimit requirement with an evidence colour; an 8-term error budget (fs-session `DecisionAssessment`); a deterministic HTML report plus JSON twin rendered from the ledger; and an evidence package the solver-free checker accepts.

## Falsifiers (what makes this L3 real)

1. **Independent consumer.** The Python client runs `run` and reads the verdict; `fs-checker` re-derives the QoI colour from the package receipts without the solver stack.
2. **Hostile twin.** The same project with the AA6061 card swapped for a low-conductivity foam card must flip the requirement verdict; the same project with `--materials` omitted must refuse at material-resolve with the typed code.
3. **Physical anchor.** The predicted junction temperature agrees with the Level-A hand calculation (fin efficiency × the applicable Nusselt card) within the budget the report states; the comparison is logged, not asserted with a loose tolerance.
4. **Receipt-backed promotion.** The lane receipt lists six executed stages with digests; check-maturity (rc-t2 rule) reads it.

## Children and order

rc-j1 (examples declare conduction; fixes rc-t7) → rc-j2 (conjugate coupling: Robin rows from the fan operating point, IQN-ILS fixed point, coupling residual in the budget) → rc-j3 (QoI stage wired, verdict with colour and 8-term budget) → rc-j3b (guaranteed equilibrated-flux error bound → Verified-colour discretization term) → rc-j4 (report/package/run/compare real, ledger-traced) → rc-j5 (honest lane, receipt, L3 promotion) with rc-j6 (falsifier battery) alongside j3–j5. Existing beads reused: s93ej.3 (conduction stage integration, in_progress), f85xj.6.9 (report renderer, in_progress), f85xj.6.10 (package, in_progress), f85xj.6.11 (acceptance lane; depends on rc-j5), f85xj.6.14 (compare, staged), s2l9v (QoI; reopened; depends on rc-j3).

## Success criteria

All four falsifiers executed in `scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh` and retained in its receipt; `thermal.conduction-solve` promoted to L3 through the receipt rule; program-metrics rows "capabilities at L3", "error-budget completeness" and "decision-turnaround" move from NO-DATA/0 to measured values.

## Vision pointer

EXTREAL E06/E08 (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN addendum P7 wedge; docs/MATURITY_LEVELS.md L3); README "What You Can Use Today".

title: OWNER DECISION: one cooling product — .fsim solve pipeline vs cooling-network JSON lab
description:
## Decision requested from the owner (2026-09-24 reality check)

There are now TWO cooling products, and they have diverged:

1. **`.fsim` → `frankensim solve|run|report|package`** (Journey A, the L3 capability): geometry import (STL/faceted STEP) → meshing → material/contact cards → interval-certified fan/duct operating point → 3-D P1 conduction (conjugate Robin) → QoI with an 8-term budget → sealed report/package in the ledger. Executed 2026-09-24 at 6c33d6a18: 66/66 checks, 7/7 stages, `temperature-max = 293.363 K`, limit 353.15 K, nominal margin 59.79 K, **verdict `indeterminate` because all 8 budget terms are NO-DATA** — byte-for-byte the same verdict as 2026-09-03.
2. **`frankensim cooling-network <request.json>`** (+ `-uq`, `cooling-component-design`), self-described as "not a .fsim migration or a ledger-backed solve result" (`crates/fs-cli/src/network_command.rs:1-3`): hand-written tet solids (every tracked example is 12 or 42 tets), no geometry import, no ledger/report/package — but it now has enclosure radiation, transient trajectories, nonmatching contact, total adjoints, fan sizing, component power allocation, QMC UQ with resume, Sobol sensitivity. ~270 of the ~300 cooling commits since 09-05 went here.

None of surface 2's physics reaches surface 1's QoI budget. The work of three weeks did not move the product answer.

## Options

- **A (recommended): `.fsim` pipeline is THE product; cooling-network is the lab.** Freeze new cooling-network features. Port features into `.fsim` one at a time, each as a declared project section consumed by the existing stages (radiation first — fs-conduction already owns it), and each port must fill or tighten a named QoI budget term. The sidecar-not-IR-section rule applies.

- **C: keep both.** Not recommended: two adaptive implementations already exist (`solve.rs:1518` and `network_command/mesh_convergence/mark.rs`) and will keep diverging.

## Done when

Owner comment picks A/B/C. The dependent beads (discretization/parameters/algebraic budget terms, radiation port) assume A and must be revisited if B is chosen.

title: Journey A discretization budget term: goal-error adaptivity on the conjugate/interface heatsink project, written into the QoI budget
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-24)

The Journey A QoI's `discretization` budget term is NO-DATA ("no retained DWR or refinement-ladder bound is attached to this QoI") although both a uniform ladder and a goal-oriented adaptive loop now exist in `crates/fs-cli/src/solve.rs`:

- `adaptive_study` (solve.rs:1518) solves, builds a uniformly enriched copy, computes `ConductivityDesign::discrete_goal_error` (fs-conduction/src/adjoint.rs:284) for the nodal max in the goal region plus a max-relocation term, Dörfler-marks 50%, refines, repeats; stops when both estimated and measured change ≤ `accuracy_rel·|T_max|`, capped at `ADAPTIVE_MAX_SOLVES = 17`.
- BUT adjoint data is built only when there are no interfaces and no conjugate coupling (solve.rs ~5823), so the heatsink-fan project (the real Journey A geometry: airflow-coupled) stops after ONE solve with status `unresolved` (test at tests/solve.rs:4729 confirms `solved_meshes:1`).
- AND the loop's result never reaches `budget_terms[discretization]`.
- The tolerance is relative to absolute Kelvin: `accuracy-rel 0.01` ≈ 3 K at 300 K, so "converged" is loose.

## What

1. Extend the goal-error estimate to the conjugate/Robin-coupled and interface-contact cases. For linear Robin coupling at the frozen airflow operating point this is the same adjoint with the Robin mass added (the transpose is symmetric); for the fixed-point conjugate loop, differentiate at the converged operating point and state the frozen-airflow assumption in the receipt.
2. Measure tolerance on the temperature RISE (T_max − T_inlet), not absolute Kelvin.
3. Write the final estimate into the QoI `discretization` budget term as an Estimated number with its provenance (estimator, rungs, last two measured changes). NOT a guaranteed bound — that is q61wp.11.
4. Adaptive-vs-uniform comparison at equal independently checked accuracy on the heatsink-fan project (the original q61wp.44 acceptance), reported in the receipt.

## Done when

`frankensim run examples/heatsink-fan/heatsink-fan.fsim` (with the documented import step) on a native host produces a report whose discretization term is a number (not NO-DATA), solved_meshes > 1 on the conjugate project, and a falsifier: perturbing the estimator (e.g. dropping the relocation term) changes the reported term, proving it is wired. Evidence: HEAD, command lines, report JSON excerpt.

Relationship: completes the remaining acceptance of frankensim-rc-root-q61wp.44 (whose 09-11 comments describe "driver16" work that is NOT in git — HEAD has SOLVE_DRIVER_VERSION 14).

title: Journey A parameters term: .fsim-declared uncertainty through real solves, adjoint control variates for the mean, anytime-valid CS for P(compliance)
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-24)

`frankensim cooling-network-uq` executes real coupled child solves (verified 2026-09-24: 8 samples in 0.73 s) and reports `empirical_probability_of_compliance: 0.375` from **n = 8** with no interval — a decision number with no decision-grade uncertainty. Its own no_claim: "no confidence sequence, optional-stopping guarantee…". Meanwhile the product QoI's `parameters` and `boundary-conditions` budget terms are NO-DATA because `.fsim` projects cannot declare uncertainty and nothing propagates it through `solve` (remaining acceptance of frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.6.7).

The repo already owns the missing pieces: `fs_eproc::BernoulliMixtureCs` (crates/fs-eproc/src/bernoulli.rs:68 — anytime-valid confidence sequence for a Bernoulli mean), randomized QMC with replicates and resume (fs-uq, b16305a0a/04eedadf0), and exact total adjoints of T_max with respect to power, fan speed, inlet temperature, contact and radiation parameters (cooling commits 09-17..09-18).

## What (the ambitious-but-convergent version)

1. `.fsim` gains a declared uncertainty section (distributions + explicit dependence; independence is never a default — keep the existing refusal) consumed by the QoI stage.
2. Propagate through the REAL solve path (not the JSON lab), reusing the fs-uq QMC engine and its checkpoint/resume.
3. **Adjoint control variates for the MEAN:** use the first-order adjoint Taylor model T̂(θ) = T(θ0) + ∇T·(θ−θ0) (the adjoint already exists) as a control variate for E[T_max]; E[T̂] = T(θ0) + ∇T·(E[θ]−θ0) is exact for any declared distribution with a known mean. Report the measured variance-reduction factor. This tightens the `parameters` term (mean shift and spread), NOT the compliance probability.
4. **Anytime-valid decision for P(compliance):** stream the raw per-sample compliance indicators (no control variate — that would break the Bernoulli CS's assumptions) into `BernoulliMixtureCs`; stop when the CS excludes the decision threshold or the budget runs out; report the CS at stop. Optional stopping is then legitimate (the plan's e-process doctrine, finally on the product path). Note: the CS needs i.i.d. draws — use plain randomized MC for this stream, or treat each randomized-QMC replicate mean as one observation of a bounded mean with a bounded-mean CS; state which.
5. Fill the `parameters` (and, where declared, `boundary-conditions`) budget terms with these Estimated numbers and their provenance.

## Done when

On the heatsink-fan project with a declared 4-parameter uncertainty section: report shows P(compliance) with a CS, the stop reason, sample count, and control-variate variance ratio; replay reproduces bytes; a falsifier (wrong closed-form mean for the control variate) is detected by a test. The fixed-n empirical path remains available but is labelled as such.

Depends on the owner's product decision (one cooling product).

title: Journey A solver-algebraic and roundoff terms from the existing adjoint: exact z^T r_k algebraic QoI error plus interval residual enclosure
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-24)

Two Journey A budget terms are NO-DATA for reasons that are cheap to remove:

- `solver-algebraic`: "the recomputed residual has no admitted inverse-stability map into this QoI unit".
- `roundoff`: "no retained outward-roundoff propagation receipt reaches this QoI".

For a LINEAR discrete problem A u = b with goal J(u) = gᵀu, the algebraic QoI error of an iterate u_k is EXACTLY J(u) − J(u_k) = zᵀ r_k, where z solves Aᵀ z = g and r_k = b − A u_k. The adjoint z is already computed for the adaptive goal loop (fs-conduction adjoint). So the algebraic term needs no inverse-stability constant at all — only the dual solution and a recomputed residual, plus the dual's own algebraic error |(z − z_m)ᵀ r_k| bounded the same way (Meidner–Rannacher–Vihharev / Jiránek–Strakoš–Vohralík style stopping). For the nonlinear k(T) and radiation cases, state that this is the linearization at the converged state (Estimated).

For roundoff: recompute r_k in outward-rounded interval arithmetic (fs-ivl) and bound |zᵀ r_k| by interval evaluation; that is a real enclosure of the residual's contribution given z, cheap relative to the solve.

## What

Wire both computations into the QoI stage for the linear/Robin conduction solve; write them as numbers into the two budget terms with provenance (dual solve tolerance, interval evaluation receipt). Also use zᵀr_k as the solver stopping criterion when a QoI tolerance is declared (stop when the algebraic QoI error is ≤ 10% of the discretization term) instead of a blind relative residual.

## Done when

Report JSON for the reference project shows `solver-algebraic` and `roundoff` as numbers; a test shows zᵀr_k matches the true J(u*) − J(u_k) on a small system solved to machine precision (independent dense solve) within the dual's own error; a falsifier (sign flip in r_k) is detected. Two NO-DATA terms become measured.

comments.text:
REOPENED 2026-09-26 (SlateOwl): my close earlier today was wrong at HEAD for the LADDER heatsink. Native release run at 49313c65a: heatsink-fan-ladder.fsim is back to 7/8, verdict indeterminate, and examples_freshness_e2e.sh fails 3 of 39 checks (8 measured, none-no-data, satisfied).
The solver-algebraic term is NO-DATA with SolidInverseUnavailable. Coupled residual upper 6.87e-11, response iterations 164, solid_inverse_infinity_upper null. The upstream rule 'no frozen-solid or tolerance fallback' (3c6a26889, bf1df5b1c) is sound: the 30 K frozen-reference fixture justifies it. So the fix is a verified inverse on the fine rung, NOT restoring the fallback.
Diagnosis:
- The base heatsink (about 250 free vertices, bound 1.12e-7 K enclosed) gets its solid inverse from prepare_inverse_columns, the dense small-system fallback, which admits n <= 256 only.
- The ladder's finest rung (43,840 tets, about 10k vertices) must pass scaled diagonal dominance of the comparison matrix in fs_solver::goal::enclose_goal_error, and it fails.
- I tested tightening the proposal A w = 1 from rel 0.01 to 0.25/sqrt(n), so every (A w)_i >= 0.75. That did NOT restore the bound (reverted). So the obstacle is sign structure: the volumetricized heatsink has 1.6 deg slivers, obtuse dihedrals give positive P1 off-diagonals, and <A> is not an M-matrix. No positive scaling can succeed.
RECOMMENDED: a verified lower bound on lambda_min of the SPD solid matrix via Rump-style shifted Cholesky (Rump 2006, 'Verification of positive definiteness'). Factor A - s I with fs-sparse's LDLt, with s set by the rounding bound of the factorization, and accept iff it succeeds. Then ||A^-1||_2 <= 1/(lambda_min lower) and ||A^-1||_inf <= sqrt(n) * ||A^-1||_2. The sqrt(n) of about 100 is harmless here: residual 6.9e-11 times 100/lambda_min is still around 1e-6 K. That route is O(fill), has no n <= 256 cap, and covers every obtuse mesh.
Also stale until this lands: the README and CONTRACT '8 measured, verdict satisfied' claims for the ladder, and the freshness lane's three checks.

title: Marquee convergence: feasible terminal design, binding stress limit, per-iteration FD gate, independent body-fitted elasticity oracle
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-24)

The P2 marquee (plan §16.1: "topology optimization on a raw SDF — no mesh in the loop — with a composed error certificate; G1 orders verified; adjoint FD-checks green") now has a real 2-D producer: `frankensim study examples/marquee/bracket-2d.fsim` runs a free-boundary level-set plane-strain elasticity study (CutFEM on the level set, topological-derivative nucleation, WENO5 advection, AL volume multiplier; crates/fs-cli/src/study_elasticity.rs → fs-topols). Executed 2026-09-24 at 6c33d6a18: 8 iterations, 1.6 s, final compliance 16.3267 J.

But:
- **The run ends infeasible and says `completed`:** final material area 0.6745 vs the declared `:volume-fraction 0.45`. An 8-step budget cannot reach the constraint; nothing in the receipt flags infeasibility.
- **The projected-stress example is vacuous:** `bracket-projected-stress-2d.fsim` runs with `stress_limit_pa = 1e12` (1 TPa) — a limit that can never bind, so the "stress-constrained study" demonstrates nothing.
- **No per-iteration gradient check** on the level-set path: only `tls_005` (fs-topols/tests/battery.rs:505-596) with an accepted predicted/measured ratio anywhere in [0.25, 4].
- **No independent elasticity oracle:** every "independent" check re-solves with the same CutFEM operator or compares split vs uninterrupted runs. mq_007's fix covers only the scalar thermal study.
- **No error estimate in the loop** (`rg dwr crates/fs-topols/src` is empty), no adaptivity, 2-D only in the CLI (3-D SIMP-on-SDF exists only as feature-gated fs-topopt examples).
- q61wp.16's ≥30-step tracked fixture, golden and certificate are absent.

## What (in this order; stop adding variants until done)

1. Receipt/status: a study that ends with a violated constraint reports `completed-infeasible` (or equivalent) with the violation, never plain `completed`.
2. Example budgets that reach feasibility: ≥30 accepted steps on bracket-2d with area within tolerance at termination; a stress example whose limit actually binds (choose the limit from the baseline's max von Mises, e.g. 0.8×).
3. Per-iteration shape-derivative FD gate on a sample of iterations (central differences on the level-set velocity direction), with a band derived from measured FD noise, not [0.25, 4].
4. Independent oracle: on the final design, extract the zero level set, body-fit mesh it (fs-mesh 2-D) and solve with fs-solid; compare compliance within a refinement-derived band, with a mutation that must fail.
5. Only then: DWR/goal-error in the loop (fs-dwr has an elasticity estimator; motion_goal3 currently does not compile — see the compile bead).

## Done when

Items 1–4 executed natively with evidence posted; q61wp.16/.17 updated to reflect what remains (5 + 3-D).

(3) Per-iteration shape-derivative FD gate, bca9b357f. (4) Independent body-fitted elasticity oracle, c6d2a4100. .16 and .17 updated with what remains: item 5 (DWR in loop), 3-D, and the remaining falsifiers. Self-verified by native re-execution only.

title: The only L3 fails its own receipt gate: re-retain the Journey A receipt from a real checkout and refuse receipts from rch-synced or dirty trees
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-24)

`thermal.conduction-solve` is the only L3 capability. Its registry note and README L130/L150 claim the retained receipt (`spine-e2e-summary.json`) is "at a HEAD at or after the lane's own commit". False today:
- receipt `head_sha` = 51acb4b0 (09-03);
- the cited lane `scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh` last changed in 9ea4d7b74 (09-04), which is NOT an ancestor of 51acb4b0;
- `xtask/src/maturity.rs:789-811` requires `merge-base --is-ancestor lane_head receipt_head`, so `check-maturity` should refuse the L3 as it stands;
- the L3 re-promotion was never logged in `promotion_events` (only the 09-01 demotion is);
- parent frankensim-rc-root-q61wp.7 (JOURNEY A L3) was closed 09-03 claiming all children incl. .11 closed, but .11 was reopened 09-04 and is open.

The lane itself is healthy: executed 2026-09-24 on source 6c33d6a18 it passed 66/66 checks with 7/7 stages. But that run was on an rch-synced tree whose `.git` HEAD was stale (fae92f51), and the receipt recorded THAT head — so a receipt produced under rch cannot be trusted to name the source it ran.

## What

1. Re-run `scripts/e2e/cooling_01.sh --retain` from a REAL git checkout at a clean HEAD (yto or local), so head_sha is truthful, and commit the refreshed receipt together with a `promotion_events` entry for the L3 promotion.
2. Make the lane refuse to retain when the working tree differs from HEAD (it already hashes sources; compare against `git rev-parse HEAD`'s tree), so an rch-synced or dirty tree cannot mint a receipt.
3. Run `cargo run -p xtask -- check-maturity` and record the verdict before/after.

## Done when

check-maturity passes with the refreshed receipt, or L3 is demoted with a promotion_events record if the lane cannot be run honestly.

title: Journey A geometry and parameter terms: declared geometric tolerance / design-intent in .fsim, card-stated conductivity uncertainty
description:
## Why (2026-09-24)

After the declared-input propagation landed, the heatsink QoI measures 5 of 8 budget terms (discretization via ladder, boundary conditions, model form, solver-algebraic, measurement). The verdict stays `indeterminate` because three remain NO-DATA: roundoff (q61wp.73), parameters (the admitted AA6061 card states no conductivity uncertainty) and GEOMETRY. Nothing in `.fsim` can declare a geometric tolerance, so the geometry term has no input to propagate; declaring it `Negligible` by fiat would be laundering.

## What

1. `.fsim` schema (fs-project v4 -> v5 with a migration receipt, per docs/SCHEMA_POLICY.md): an optional per-artifact geometric tolerance declaration — a uniform outward/inward surface offset band in metres with a cited source (drawing tolerance, process capability) — OR an explicit `design-intent` declaration stating the prediction is for the exact declared geometry (then the term is `Negligible` with that user-owned justification, and the report says so).
2. Propagation: re-solve at the offset bounds. For faceted STL/STEP input the cheapest honest route is a normal offset of the audited surface before volumetrization; if that is not robust for thin fins, refuse the declaration with a typed diagnostic rather than approximating.
3. Material cards: when a card carries a stated conductivity uncertainty, propagate it as the Parameters term through the same vertex machinery (k x (1 -/+ rel)); cards without one keep Parameters NO-DATA with the card named.

## Done when

The heatsink example with a declared tolerance (and a card with stated uncertainty) reports 7/8 or 8/8 measured terms on a native run, and a test shows a declared offset changes T_max in the physically expected direction.

description:

title: cooling-network fixtures declare a 1e-12 linear tolerance at the CG floor; design searches refuse at arbitrary candidates
description:
## Defect
Several cooling-network examples declare `"linear_relative": 1e-12`, which is at the double-precision floor of the recomputed CG residual on these small systems. A run can refuse at an arbitrary design candidate with, for example:

    linear solve at nonlinear iteration 0 reached recomputed Euclidean relative residual 1.0000027883290022e-12 after 4 Krylov iterations, tolerance was 1e-12

Observed on size-transient-fan.json at a 319.6 K limit, adaptive stepping (2026-09-25). Which candidate trips it depends on the search path, so a limit change or an unrelated numerical change can turn a passing design search into a refusal.

## Do
Choose one rule, either:
- (a) the fs-cli solve rule: linear tolerance = max(declared*1e-2, 1e-13) relative to the nonlinear stop; or
- (b) admit the stall as converged when the recomputed residual is within a stated factor of the machine-precision floor.

Either way, document the rule. Do not just loosen the fixtures.

## Done when
size-transient-fan at a 319.6 K limit completes, and a test pins the rule at the floor.
close_reason: Fixed upstream (999a0a728 + 4fc364bd7, from this bead's comment). The transient backward-Euler linear solve now uses checked_cg with up to 2 restart corrections when the recomputed residual misses after the recurrence says converged. The design tolerance is not loosened. Verified NATIVELY by SlateOwl, since upstream stated it did not compile or run: (1) size-transient-fan at a 319.6 K limit now completes, target-bracketed at multiplier 0.98198 (it refused before); (2) fs-conduction backward_euler lib tests 7/0 and fs-cli sizing tests 15/0, including the new regressions.

title: Product QoI stage: expose registered scalar families (pressure drop, fan power, surface uniformity) beside temperature-max
description:
WHY. The heatsink example's declared decision is "compare fan operating points before layout freeze", which needs pressure drop and fan power. The product QoI stage accepts exactly one scalar `temperature-max`. It refuses every other registered family with cli-solve-qoi-unsupported-output (crates/fs-cli/src/solve.rs, QoI stage admission). fs-airflow already implements them: registered_qoi::extract_registered_qois (surface mean/spread/std-dev, pressure drop, fan power, thermal margin), but fs-cli never calls it. Found by the 2026-09-29 audit of closed product-CLI beads; s2l9v and f85xj.5.10 claimed this wiring.

BLOCKERS IN THE LIBRARY API. extract_thermal_qois computes the whole family at once. It requires a SurfaceRegion (boundary-face slots) and a FanPowerSpec (a cited total-efficiency interval) even when neither is requested. The project schema has no fan-efficiency declaration.

PLAN (smallest honest slice).
1. fs-airflow: make surface_region and fan_power optional in ThermalQoiDeclarations. A family whose declaration is absent is not computed, and requesting it refuses by name.
2. Schema v9: an optional fan-system `:efficiency (efficiency :total T :half-width W :source S :source-id I)`. Output `(qoi :name "surface-mean-temperature" :region "<surface>")` names an fsim-v8 `(surface ...)` entity. Its boundary-face slots come from the same selector lowering conduction_boundary uses.
3. QoI stage: temperature-max stays the decision QoI (requirement, 8-term budget, package claim). The other requested scalars are retained as additional Estimated rows in the QoI receipt (`additional_qois`), each with value, unit, colour and its own uncertainty. The report renders them in a table. compare diffs them (qoi_diffs is already plural).
4. Heatsink example: request pressure-drop and fan-power with a declared efficiency.

FALSIFIERS. pressure-drop equals the flow-network receipt's operating-point pressure (same bytes). fan-power = Q * dp / eta, within the declared efficiency interval. surface-mean over the chip footprint surface sits between the conduction T_min and T_max. A surface-mean request with no declared surface refuses by name.

SIZE. L (schema bump, receipt, report, compare, Python client).
close_reason: Landed in three slices: 96ad89d62 (pressure-drop, v35), 2fae24dfa (fsim v9 fan-efficiency + output :region; fan-power, v36), 2e07d2767 (surface mean/spread/std-dev over a declared surface, v37). Each family is a new pub per-family extractor over fs-airflow's existing builders, not the all-at-once API. Rows sit beside the decision QoI in the receipt's qoi array; report and package show them as Estimated; compare diffs them. Falsifiers, all exact and all in cli.rs G1 tests: heatsink fan 0.7->0.9, dp ratio (0.9/0.7)^2 and fan power (0.9/0.7)^3 to 1e-9; fan-power without a cited efficiency refuses; plate-hole skin mean = 293.15+P/(hA) to 1.05e-6 K (gate 5e-6). Refusals by name for no air network, no efficiency, missing or empty surface region; fs-project validates output regions and the efficiency interval. Not exposed: thermal-margin, which duplicates the requirement row's nominal_margin.

title: Conjugate coupling: branch-fed Robin rows, IQN-ILS fixed point, coupling residual in the budget
description:
## Background

The solve pipeline computes an interval-certified fan/loss-network operating point (`fs_airflow::solve_operating_point`, used only in the flow-network stage, `solve.rs:2692-2800`) and, separately, a conduction solve whose Robin rows come from user literals. The operating point is never consumed by conduction; convection is "handed off" in a receipt, not coupled. `fs_airflow::conjugate` already contains a steady partitioned conjugate fixed point for a 1-D air path with an energy-balance gate and an exact NTU refinement falsifier (`conjugate.rs`, `conjugate_e2e.rs`), and `fs_couple` has IQN-ILS (interface quasi-Newton) relaxation. Bead s93ej.3 (in_progress, CreamPelican, updated 2026-09-01) owns "conjugate solve and candidate" inside the conduction stage integration; its 2026-08-25 comment lists coupling and parser gaps. This bead extends s93ej.3 to the product path; do not fork its design — read its notes first and coordinate through Agent Mail.

## Deliverable

- A boundary law `convection-from-branch <branch-id>` (introduced by rc-j1) resolves at solve time: branch velocity and hydraulic diameter from the flow-network operating point → the applicable `fs_convection` Nusselt card (validity-gated; a refusal when outside the card's domain, with the card id and the violated bound) → Robin coefficient h with the card's declared discrepancy band → conduction Robin row.
- Steady partitioned fixed point between conduction (surface temperatures / heat rates) and the air path (branch temperature rise → film temperature → properties → h), relaxed with IQN-ILS from `fs_couple`; iteration stops on a declared tolerance and budget; the coupling residual at exit enters the 8-term budget as its own term (iteration error), never silently absorbed.
- Energy balance gate: heat leaving solids = heat gained by air ± declared tolerance; failure is a typed refusal with the imbalance in watts.
- Receipt: per iteration `k`, the interface residual norm, the relaxation factor, and the branch/film temperatures; final Robin coefficients per boundary with card ids and colours.

## DONE-WHEN

- heatsink-fan solve executes conduction with branch-fed Robin rows; the receipt shows the fixed point converging (monotone residual, ≤ declared iterations) and the balance gate passing.
- Falsifiers, executed: (a) doubling the fan curve's head raises branch velocity, raises h, and lowers the junction temperature (metamorphic direction test); (b) a branch outside every card's Reynolds domain refuses with the card and bound named; (c) a deliberately broken air-side energy term trips the balance gate.
- `fs-airflow` and `fs-cli` CONTRACT no-claim sections updated (conjugate exchange is now steady, 1-D air path, card-bounded; still no CFD).

## Logging

One JSONL row per coupling iteration (`iter`, `residual`, `omega`, `t_film_by_branch`), plus the final `robin_rows` table. Enough to diagnose a stalled fixed point without a debugger.

## Reuse

`fs_airflow::conjugate`, `fs_couple` IQN-ILS, `fs_convection` catalog + Robin seam, `fs-conduction` Robin rows and per-region heat rates. Existing seam recipe for turning a gap stage into an executing one (SOLVE_DRIVER_VERSION bump when invocation inputs change).

## Vision pointer

EXTREAL E05 (conjugate coupling), E08 (budget term); plan §8.4 coupling; feeds rc-j3, rc-j5.

title: Reject bare carriage returns in strict CSV records
description: ROOT CAUSE: Catalog CSV parser v2 advertises a strict RFC-4180 subset with no embedded record separators, but CsvLines recognizes LF/CRLF only and split_csv accepts a bare U+000D as ordinary unquoted or quoted field data. Thus malformed records can retain hidden carriage-return controls, disagree with strict CSV consumers, and produce line-oriented output ambiguity. MISSION: Reject the first bare CR at its absolute input-byte offset in every parser state; retain CR only as the consumed half of a CRLF record delimiter. Preserve LF/CRLF equivalence, quoted escapes, empty/whitespace record semantics, resource caps, cancellation, and no partial CatalogRead publication. ACCEPTANCE: G0 covers bare CR in header, unquoted, quoted, and after-closing-quote positions plus CRCRLF; G3 proves canonical LF/CRLF inputs remain equivalent and every malformed form reports the first absolute offender. Update CONTRACT and leave in_progress pending central fs-io all-targets/clippy/DSR proof. Code-first: rustfmt/diff checks only.

title: Make every session governor mutation retry-idempotent
description:
The plan and closed gp3.7 contract require idempotency keys on every mutating call, but Governor::charge(session, delta) accepts no report identity or monotone sequence. Retrying after an uncertain response double-meters the same usage and can falsely throttle/pause. apply_memory_pressure(session, 1|2) likewise appends duplicate declarations on retry, while a retried level-3 call after acknowledgement/activation starts a new pause generation. submit_once and acknowledge_pause are keyed, but they do not make these public mutators retry-safe.

Root fix: introduce bounded typed MeterReportId and PressureActionId authority. Either accept monotone cumulative meter snapshots or retain same-payload keyed deltas; identical replay must return the original receipt without mutation, conflicting payload reuse must fail closed, and IDs must bind governor/session/scope/generation. Pressure retries must replay the exact declared/requested events rather than append or start a new cycle. Reserve retained row/byte/ordinal capacity before mutation, flush replay receipts to the ledger, and keep state bounded.

Acceptance: response-loss, concurrent duplicate, conflicting reuse, cross-session, stale-generation, exact-cap/limit+1, crash/replay, and ledger-flush tests; duplicate charge changes no meter/counter; duplicate pressure changes no event/gate/reservation; structured receipts bind exact payload and authority; no unkeyed public mutating convenience path can satisfy production orchestration.

comments.text: Additional causal-replay defect found in fresh review: submit_once allocates next_submission_ordinal at Pending admission, then runs arbitrary work and charge outside that lock. Concurrent keys can complete in reverse order across a grant threshold: A admits t=1 and blocks, B admits t=2 and charges 5 => Ok, then A charges 15 => Throttled; persisted t-order A(Throttled), B(Ok) cannot re-earn those outcomes. title: Persist immutable session mutation receipts for crash-safe replay
description:
The ujhp acceptance requires crash/replay, but fs-session currently keeps all retry registries and flush cursors only in one process. A crash after ledger commit and before in-memory cursor commit can append duplicate audit rows, and a new Governor cannot reconstruct private open, meter, pressure, or submission authorities from events. Arbitrary pending FnOnce work cannot be silently rerun after a crash because its side effects are indeterminate.

Root fix: add an immutable, bounded, typed terminal-mutation registry in fs-ledger and integrate it with fs-session flush in the same transaction as audit events. Registry identity must bind physical LedgerInstanceId, durable governor nonce, scope, session/open receipt, mutation kind and authority hash, exact payload identity, terminal receipt, causal meter ordinal and pre/post snapshots where applicable, and schema version. Insert-if-absent must return exact replay for identical bytes and structured conflict for different bytes. A deterministic flush-batch identity or semantic event uniqueness record must make commit-before-cursor retry append-once. Provide bounded lookup by authority hash so fs-session can rebuild terminal replay state and current meter/generation state after reopening. Recovered Pending executions are RecoveryRequired or Indeterminate and never auto-rerun.

Acceptance: kill/reopen after terminal commit for open, meter, pressure L1/L2/L3 lifecycle, successful submission, and failed submission; exact client retry returns the original receipt with no counter, meter, event, gate, reservation, or audit-row change; altered payload and foreign ledger/governor/session/scope conflict; crash after database commit before cursor publication does not duplicate rows; exact-cap and limit+1 storage/read budgets; corrupt, partial, future-schema, duplicate-conflict, and recovered-Pending cases fail closed; one transaction proves event rows and terminal registry cannot diverge; tests use a real on-disk ledger reopened through a fresh process/handle. This is mutation-level durable terminal replay; study-scale kill storms remain in frankensim-epic-helm-gp3.11.

title: Roofline Freshness must bind live authority and return a typed recorded receipt
description:
The sealed production roofline protocol now binds registry, pre/post axes, dependency receipt, build identity, manifest, and ledger rows. Two authority gaps remain: staleness_at accepts only a baseline hash and cannot observe that the signing/promotion authority has since been revoked; ProductionRun::record returns a bare i64 op id, so callers can conflate committed recording with a row that has subsequently passed Fresh revalidation.

Extend freshness with an explicit pinned authority/policy context and revocation state. A revoked or policy-rotated baseline must never remain Fresh merely because its bytes/hash are intact. Replace or supplement the bare op id with an opaque RecordedProductionRun receipt carrying the op, run receipt, baseline/dependency authority fingerprints, record time, and a method that revalidates to a typed FreshProductionEvidence under current policy. Report-only/custom/refused runs cannot construct the positive type.

Acceptance: authority revocation, key rotation, policy change, clock rollback, baseline replacement, dependency receipt revocation, and record-then-tamper all fail closed; re-promotion under the new authority recovers; compile/API tests prevent bare i64 from satisfying citation APIs; existing honest sealed runs stay Fresh; CLI language distinguishes measured, recorded, revalidated Fresh, and citable.
close_reason: Both authority gaps closed at HEAD: typed RecordedProductionRun/FreshProductionEvidence protocol (d7bd5433) with fail-closed revalidation across revocation/rotation/policy/clock/baseline/dependency/tamper axes (ed34eb04 refinements), compile-fail API guards, and v2 CLI evidence language; staleness_at remains diagnostic-only by design with no cross-crate citation path (TRANSFORMED boundary documented in comment). Central gate 194 green via RCH.

A mutable/revoked verifier can therefore produce admission, receipt hash, and persisted baseline receipt from different authority states within one run. The typed RecordedProductionRun work must materialize exactly one immutable admission snapshot/receipt, bind and reuse its exact canonical bytes throughout finalization and recording, then perform at most a named live recheck whose mismatch fails closed. Add a stateful verifier that flips/revokes between calls and prove no mixed-state run can record or become Fresh.

title: Bound roofline staleness history with authenticated snapshots
description:
Roofline staleness currently reconstructs manifested runs by scanning tune history and repeatedly querying sibling rows/artifacts. The integrity checks are strong, but cost grows with retained history and can become quadratic across a large long-lived ledger. An attacker or merely sustained CI can turn verification into an unbounded resource sink.

Define bounded, authenticated history snapshots/checkpoints for production roofline evidence. Index by run receipt/build/baseline/machine, retain the complete ordered manifest root and dependency authority, and verify one snapshot plus bounded deltas rather than rescanning all history. Compaction must preserve tombstones, corrupt-evidence findings, and historical failure knowledge; it must never make a previously corrupt row Fresh.

Acceptance: explicit row/byte/query bounds; adversarial 10^5-row fixture stays within declared time/memory/query budgets; snapshot/delta tamper, missing rows, duplicate manifests, rollback, and compaction interruption fail closed; result matches the exhaustive verifier on bounded randomized histories; cancellation is checked at chunk boundaries; performance evidence and bounds are ledgered.
close_reason: Implemented and landed at 6d39a90: crate::checkpoint module with chained authenticated staleness-history checkpoints. Fast path verified at exactly 2 ledger reads independent of history depth (read_queries asserts, 40-run scale fixture) vs O(H*(K+4)) exhaustive; verdict-lattice equivalence tested across Fresh/Expired/ClockRollback/BuildDrift/NeverMeasured/FingerprintDrift/BaselineUnavailable; tamper, rollback simulation, chain tamper, and ordinal gaps all classify CorruptEvidence or fail closed to exhaustive; tombstone permanence tested through restore+reseal. Battery 8/8 plus scale fixture green, full fs-roofline suite green (91+11+8+1+2+8), CONTRACT.md updated with semantics and no-claim boundary.

Plan: (1) map the current verification cost precisely - per-row validate now walks the op-bound manifest and tune_gets every sibling, so staleness over a kernel with H historical runs is O(H x K) queries and the whole-ledger audit is the quadratic the reviewer named; (2) design the bounded authenticated snapshot: a checkpoint row indexed by (run receipt, build, baseline, machine) retaining the ordered manifest root (the existing domain-separated receipt hash IS the root - snapshots authenticate by rehashing stored roots into a chained checkpoint digest, no new crypto claims, operator-observed per workspace doctrine), so verification = one snapshot check + bounded deltas since it; (3) compaction keeps tombstones and corrupt-evidence findings as first-class retained records - a compacted history can refuse but never un-corrupt (previously-corrupt can never become Fresh); interrupted compaction fails closed to the uncompacted path; (4) battery: explicit row/byte/query budget asserts, 10^5-row adversarial fixture within declared budgets, snapshot/delta tamper + missing rows + duplicate manifests + rollback + interruption all fail closed, and DIFFERENTIAL EQUIVALENCE - bounded randomized histories where the snapshot verifier must agree with the exhaustive gp3.15 verifier verdict-for-verdict. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PROGRESS CHECKPOINT (design finalized against today's code, counter primitive built). Cost map at current HEAD: per-kernel staleness fetch is now CAPPED upstream (fs-ledger MAX_TUNE_ROWS_PER_KERNEL=1024, 16MiB scan guard - the bounds lane's work), but the per-row exhaustive validation is DEEPER than at gp3.15: op fetch + canonical-production-op parse + protocol axes validation + dependency-receipt structural fetch + manifest-membership checks + the K-sibling tune_get walk + artifact fetch per sibling. So one kernel probe over H retained runs of a K-kernel registry costs O(H*(K+4)) ledger queries with H up to 1024 - the quadratic the bead names, now precisely measurable: I added Ledger::read_queries(), a Cell counter on the five typed read APIs (tune_rows/tune_get/get_artifact/op/edge_exists) with an exact-count unit test - this is the basis for the acceptance's explicit query budgets. (Counter currently rides the shared working tree entangled with the in-flight LedgerInstanceId lane's WIP in the same file; single-file self-contained, safe under any sweep.)

Refined checkpoint design incorporating the current validation stack: checkpoint rows live in the tune table under a reserved kernel ('roofline-staleness-checkpoint'), machine-keyed like production rows, shape_class 'roofline-ckpt-v1:<ordinal>', measured = canonical JSON {schema, ordinal, prev_digest, upto_op, runs:[{receipt, op, manifest_root, build, dependency_receipt_hash, recorded_at_ns, verdict: valid|corrupt}]}, params = {schema, chained_digest} where digest_i = blake3_domain(prev || canonical_bytes) - authentication is the chained digest over roots the exhaustive verifier produced (operator-observed, no-crypto no-claim per workspace doctrine). Fast path: 1 bounded checkpoint fetch + chain recompute + per-row cheap identity check against the checkpointed entry + CURRENT-context classification (build/dependency/age compare using the checkpointed per-run build+dependency+recorded_at - no sibling walks); rows newer than upto_op get the exhaustive path (bounded delta). corrupt verdicts are TOMBSTONES: compaction can refuse but never un-corrupt; a broken/partial chain fails closed to the exhaustive path. Battery: budget asserts via read_queries(), 1e5-row fixture (spread across kernels under the 1024/kernel cap), snapshot/delta tamper + missing rows + duplicate manifests + rollback + interrupted-compaction fail-closed, and randomized differential equivalence vs the exhaustive verifier. Implementation next stretch on fresh context - this checkpoint verifier is security-relevant and deserves a full budget.

comments.text: IN-FLIGHT FRESH-EYES BLOCKERS on current checkpoint.rs (do not close/land until resolved): (1) staleness_at_checkpointed calls select_matching_rows before load_chain, so deleting or moving every sealed row returns NeverMeasured/FingerprintDrift/BaselineDrift without authenticating a nonempty chain, contradicting removal=>Corrupt. Load and authenticate the chain before lattice early exits. (2) recheckpoint rebuilds entries only from current matching rows and carries old tombstones only for shapes still present; a missing valid/corrupt row disappears from the newest snapshot, while load_chain/fast path use the newest entries, laundering rollback/removal. New state must be a monotone union with explicit tombstones and transition validation. (3) the fast path seals only one kernel's rows and skips receipt_recomputes_from_stored_rows; deleting/tampering a different-kernel sibling in the same op manifest, the op, dependency artifact/edge, or payload artifact can stay Fresh although exhaustive verification is Corrupt. Checkpoint identity must bind the full finalized manifest/op/artifact dependency set. (4) appended full snapshots make cumulative storage/read work quadratic and eventually hit tune_rows 16MiB/1024 caps, currently propagating error instead of bounded fallback. Use bounded epochs plus authenticated deltas/compaction, with explicit exhaustive fallback semantics. Add removal-all, moved-all, cross-kernel sibling tamper, op/artifact/edge deletion, rollback, and long-history cap regressions.

title: Floating-nightly clippy drift blocks the strict lane workspace-wide: fs-substrate and fs-alloc fail before any dependent crate is linted
description:
SYMPTOM: 'cargo clippy -p <anything> --all-targets -- -D warnings' cannot evaluate the requested crate, because two L0/L1 dependencies fail the strict lane first and the build aborts:

  error: using `chunks_exact_mut` with a constant chunk size
    --> crates/fs-substrate/src/bandwidth.rs:47:10
  error: using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size
    --> crates/fs-substrate/src/bandwidth.rs:48:21
  error: using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size
    --> crates/fs-substrate/src/bandwidth.rs:49:21
  error: could not compile `fs-substrate` (lib) due to 3 previous errors

  error: this function has too many lines (116/100)
    --> crates/fs-alloc/src/arena.rs:432:5   (fn acquire_chunk)
  error: could not compile `fs-alloc` (lib) due to 1 previous error

Reproduced 2026-07-26 at HEAD c91d0cdb on rustc 1.99.0-nightly (3659db0d3 2026-07-05), the toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, via:
  RCH_MIN_LOCAL_TIME_MS=999999999 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Volumes/USB_NVME/cargo-target cargo clippy -p fs-rep-neural -p fs-neuroshape-e2e --all-targets -- -D warnings

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TWO CRATES: 'strict local lint lane green' is a named acceptance criterion on a large number of parked code-first beads (frankensim-1obak names 'clippy' explicitly; the 2026-07-18 wave is full of similar wording). Because clippy aborts in a shared L0/L1 dependency, NO dependent crate can satisfy that criterion, no matter how clean the crate itself is. One two-crate defect is silently holding the lint half of dozens of acceptance criteria hostage, and the failure is easy to misread as a defect in whatever crate you happened to name on the command line — I hit exactly that while verifying the neural lane and had to read the log to see the errors were upstream.

CAUSE: floating-nightly lint drift, not a code regression. `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` is a recent lint that fires on `chunks_exact(N)`/`chunks_exact_mut(N)` with a CONSTANT N and asks for `as_chunks::<N>()`/`as_chunks_mut::<N>()`. `clippy::too_many_lines` has a 100-line default and fs-alloc's acquire_chunk is 116. Neither file was edited recently: nothing in fs-substrate or fs-alloc appears in the last-12-hour modification set.

PRESCRIBED FIX (either direction is defensible; pick one and record it):
(a) Migrate the three fs-substrate sites to `as_chunks`, which is what the lint asks for and is available on the pinned nightly. NOTE THE HAZARD: crates/fs-substrate/src/bandwidth.rs is the STREAM-triad bandwidth probe, and frankensim-4o6dp is an open P1 alleging that this very probe under-reads Zen 3 single-thread streaming. Do not let a lint refactor silently change what that probe measures — re-run the roofline attestation after touching it, and land the lint fix separately from any behavioural change.
(b) Add a targeted, justified allow at each site, or set the thresholds in [workspace.lints.clippy] in the root Cargo.toml. Note that section currently exists but is EMPTY (only [workspace.lints.rust] carries unsafe_code=deny and missing_docs=warn), so a workspace-level threshold is a one-line addition rather than a new mechanism.

Do NOT 'fix' this by dropping -D warnings from the acceptance criteria; that converts a real lane into a decorative one.

DONE WHEN: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings reaches every crate (whatever it then reports), and the chosen direction is recorded so the next nightly bump has a precedent. Consider pinning clippy expectations to the rust-toolchain.toml nightly explicitly so this drift is dated rather than mysterious.

Filed by LilacPanther while supplying central proofs for the parked 2026-07-18 code-first wave. I changed no file in fs-substrate or fs-alloc; both were clean and untouched for 3+ days at filing time.

title: Fail closed when gradient verification encounters non-finite values
description: fs-adjoint::verify_gradient computes worst = worst.max(relative_error). title: solve stage producer: QoI extraction vs ThermalLimit requirements
description:
Child of f85xj.6.5 (solve orchestration). The qoi stage must extract the project's requested outputs (OutputRequest { name, kind }) from the ConjugateSolution/ConductionReport, compare against requirements (ThermalLimit { qoi, region, direction, limit, margin, source, safety_factor }) via fs_airflow::qoi (JunctionRegion/ThermalRequirement/ThermalQoiSet/AuditedThermalQoiSet already exist), and retain verdict artifacts suitable for f85xj.8.6's DecisionAssessment consumption (which needs a fs-package VerifiedPackage with non-zero merkle root — coordinate the artifact shape with VioletHorizon). Indeterminate verdicts must respect fs-project decision gating (ProjectDecisionAuthority refuses Indeterminate outside ScopingEstimate/non-SafetyCritical contexts).

DONE WHEN: reference project yields per-requirement verdicts with margins and evidence colors through the pipeline; the stage-gap refusal for qoi in fs-cli/src/solve.rs is deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria

The QoI stage defines one versioned mapping from every supported scalar OutputRequest.name to its production extractor. Field/report requests remain with downstream producers or receive explicit unsupported-at-QoI diagnostics; they are never reinterpreted as scalar QoIs. Unknown names/kinds, duplicate names, missing regions/outputs, or a requirement naming an unproduced QoI refuse.

Extract all requested supported thermal QoI families, including junction/region extrema, declared means/uniformity, pressure drop, fan power, and thermal margins, with deterministic tie-breaking and typed units. Requirements retain qoi/class/region/direction/effective limit/required margin/source/safety-factor/severity, and safety factor is not applied twice. Each requirement receives exactly one Compliant, NonCompliant, or Indeterminate result under project decision-authority rules.

Evidence color and validity are the conservative intersection of mesh, material, interface, flow, convection, solver, QoI, and requirement authorities. Widening uncertainty, losing evidence, or shrinking a domain cannot strengthen a verdict. An unbounded unknown able to flip compliance yields Indeterminate with the flipping term and required evidence. Emit canonical QoI/verdict artifacts suitable for later packaging and DecisionAssessment, but do not mint a VerifiedPackage, fabricate a Merkle root, or self-upgrade package authority. Cancellation, invalid evidence/lineage, non-finite QoI, serialization failure, or ledger failure publishes no partial verdict set; resume from conduction reproduces the uninterrupted QoI root.

Unit/property/metamorphic tests cover every supported and unknown/duplicate/missing output mapping; AtMost/AtLeast, exact-boundary tie policy, positive margin, safety factor, severities, stale authority; analytic extrema/means/uniformity, equal-max tie-breaking, pressure-drop and fan-power identities; missing regions/flows/reports and corrupt evidence; compliant/noncompliant/bounded-indeterminate/unbounded-flipping cases; weakest-link authority and regime demotion; forged package roots; and cancellation during scans, reductions, evidence intersection, comparisons, serialization, and publication. Properties prove increased required margin or widened uncertainty cannot strengthen a result; output/requirement/mesh order, equivalent temperature units, and common temperature offsets preserve declared semantics. Resume/substitution/stale-project/duplicate-checkpoint and ledger fault cases are mandatory.

scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh --through qoi --profile <pr|full|recovery> --artifact-dir <path> invokes the real release-built frankensim CLI, canonical .fsim project, real promoted geometry and card packs, actual material/flow/conduction predecessors and field artifacts, production QoI/requirement logic, and real FrankenSQLite ledger. It runs clean success twice, all mapping/evidence/verdict/refusal cases, cancellation at each work boundary, checkpoint resume, budget exhaustion, corrupt/stale/tampered evidence, write/link failure, duplicate invocation, and retry without mocked fields/verdicts/receipts or bypasses. Uninterrupted and resumed roots match.

Canonical JSONL has deterministic record/field order and includes schema/version, case/event sequence, revision/constellation/workspace, run/project/stage/operation/predecessor IDs, capability verb, output and requirement semantic IDs, region/tie identity, values/units/limits/margins/safety factors, upstream authority/domain roots, uncertainty/error terms, evidence composition, verdict and flip condition, input/output/receipt roots, budget grant/use, cancellation boundary, resume source, diagnostic code, ranked fix, and final verdict. Timings/load are separate non-authoritative rows. Meta-tests reject missing, duplicate, reordered, mixed-run/revision, truncated, unknown-version, and tampered records. Focused tests, no-mock E2E, constellation preflight, and named DSR lane must pass with retained artifacts before closure.

### Complete Extraction Matrix and Proof-State Binding

Consume the canonical thermal QoI producer from `f85xj.5.10` and deterministically group/extract every requested `(QoI semantic ID, requirement class, region)` and every `ThermalLimit`. The current single-junction/single-surface shape is not an admissible shortcut. No hardcoded region, first-match selection, duplicate overwrite, or silently dropped request is allowed; diagnostics enumerate the complete missing/ambiguous key set. Requirement source/context/safety-factor semantics bind to closed `f85xj.17.6`, and evidence demotion/refusal remains governed by `f85xj.8.3/.8.4`.

Immediately before and after authoritative proof, `scripts/ci/checkout_constellation.sh --snapshot` reports identical complete root-plus-sibling content identities and unchanged `constellation.lock` identity. Evidence binds source/snapshot/toolchain/target/profile/features plus DSR run/log/artifact roots and rejects cross-snapshot splicing. QoI reductions require same-ISA deterministic replay and predeclared cross-ISA semantic tolerances until actual dual-runtime G5 evidence; focused Cargo/RCH is focused proof only.

## Success Criteria

Close only when the exact four-child QoI contract is complete. Focused QoI mathematics, requirement/evidence semantics, lifecycle transaction, and independent no-mock stage E2E remain separate proof states. The E2E uses scripts/ci/solve_stage_producers_e2e.sh with detailed bounded V.3 logs; Runner, DSR, and scientific promotion are non-substitutable later gates. No original QoI, ThermalLimit, evidence, cancellation, checkpoint, logging, or no-claim functionality is removed.

title: grand_piano: air loading cannot be admitted on the production board (ceiling, mesh, passive fit)
description:
The production instrument-lab piano render (grand_piano --preset steinway-d --board-band-hz 2400 --board-reduction 128,64,200,400,800,1600,2300) has no air reaction on the soundboard. Real boards lose much of their low-mode energy to radiation, and the render's extra board ringing (frankensim-loos8: 131.6 Hz resonance and off-partial satellites, 13 dB more off-partial energy than a real Steinway) makes air loading a prime suspect. The ablation cannot currently be run; measured refusals on 2026-10-13:

1. --rayleigh-loading 2,20,2400,129: retains at most 32 complete board modes, so --radiation-ports is required.
2. With --radiation-ports 32: 2.53e11 cell-mode-frequency visits, above the 6.4e10 offline ceiling. At 33 samples it is 6.48e10, still 1.3% over.
3. With --board-reduction 126 (6.38e10, passes): FS-BEM-HELM-TOO-COARSE, 2.75 panels per wavelength at 2400 Hz (floor 6). The mesh supports about 1.1 kHz.
4. A 20-1000 Hz loading band is refused because it must cover all loaded board reference oscillators (299.7-2390.8 Hz).
5. On a 1 kHz board (--board-band-hz 1000, 43 modes; loading 2,20,1060,33, 32 ports), the passive BEM load fit is refused: complex peak/RMS 0.187/0.169 and power peak/RMS 0.177/0.189 against limits .05/.02/.10/.05.

DONE WHEN an A3 mf render with two-sided air loading completes on a board whose band covers the 131.6 Hz resonance and partials 1-3 (at least 0.1-1 kHz), together with a matched no-air baseline on the same board, and the 131.6 Hz level and off-partial energy are re-measured with apps/instrument-lab/tools/diagnose.py. Options include a finer --mesh-divisions for the loading quadrature only, a raised offline ceiling for explicit offline renders, or a better-conditioned port fit. None of these may weaken the existing passivity and accuracy limits.
