Raw caller-constructed SheafComplex values remain available for incidence, mismatch, and fixture diagnostics but watertightness() always returns Unknown with NumericalKind::NoClaim, and provenance binds raw-public-parts versus chart-sampling-builder origin. A compile-fail doctest locks post-admission immutability; raw-part tests lock inability to mint either positive or negative authority. This proves admission-path provenance and immutability only, not truthfulness of an arbitrary Chart producer. The broader property-specific continuum migration, strong identities, coverage, and consumer migration in this bead remain open.

title: Continuum cover engine: adaptive exhaustive overlap and finite-intersection witnesses
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Independent pairwise sample sets and graph cliques do not prove domain coverage or a common triple/higher intersection. Build a certified cover and intersection substrate.

SCOPE: Use adaptive interval, affine, or Taylor subdivision; chart derivative/Lipschitz bounds; verified overlap atlases; oriented traces; exact predicates where available; explicit domain-exhaustion trees; and real common-intersection witnesses. Triple and higher cells are admitted only from a witness shared by all members. Handle empty intersections, slivers, tangencies, trim boundaries, T-junctions, singular parameterizations, overlapping charts, nonmatching resolution, unsupported charts, and budget exhaustion with set-valued truth. Bind source/chart versions, domain, norm, units, arithmetic mode, subdivisions, witnesses, and uncovered regions.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Every positive coverage/intersection result replays to a complete subdivision or analytic witness; every uncovered, ambiguous, non-finite, unsupported, or exhausted branch remains localized Unknown/Refused. Candidate cliques never enter topology-sensitive skeletons. G0 tests cover and restriction laws plus false-clique cases. G1 manufactured analytic surfaces verify convergence and coverage order. G2 exercises seam/sliver/tangent/trim/nonmanifold/mixed-chart zoos. G3 uses reparameterization, chart order, rigid motion, unit scaling, and refinement. G4 attacks interval storms, caps, and cancellation with no partial authority. G5 replays deterministically. Mutation/certifier tests seed missed boxes and false intersections. Logs retain cover trees, bounds, common witnesses, budgets, and exact stopping/no-claim state.

title: Continuum descent authority: good-cover, Leray, hypercover, cellular routes and named property profiles
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Even an exhaustive overlap nerve does not automatically compute continuum topology, and topology properties do not imply geometric embedding or material semantics. Define exact theorem routes and composable profiles.

SCOPE: Support independently witnessed good-cover results when all relevant finite intersections are empty or contractible; Leray or acyclic-cover results for a declared coefficient system; verified hypercover or refinement/descent results for non-good covers; and direct cellular proofs where appropriate. Each records exact theorem, quantifiers, coefficient system, regularity, refinement map, exhaustion, and trusted computing base. Pursue stronger necessary-and-sufficient local-to-global theorems through the Theorem Foundry, with admitted assumptions and proof objects. Define named profiles such as ClosedCover, EmbeddedClosedBoundary, OrientedManifoldBoundary, and MaterialInterface that list required independent evidence for coverage, restriction, closedness, incidence, manifoldness, orientation, embeddedness, material side, and metric seam bounds.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: No route substitutes a graph clique for an intersection witness, a nerve theorem without its hypotheses, or one property for another. A positive profile exposes every component receipt and exact theorem revision; missing or indeterminate components keep unrelated evidence usable. G0 tests profile lattice and theorem admission; G2 includes good and non-good covers, false cliques, nonorientable/manifold/self-intersecting/material-side counterexamples; G3 compares valid refinements and coefficient changes; G4 exhausts hypercover and proof-checker budgets; G5 replays. Counterexample and mutation campaigns attack each assumption and property boundary. Logs retain theorem/assumption/TCB IDs, coefficient system, component states, refinement lineage, budgets, and authority relation.

title: Continuum geometry gate: production consumers, independent checking, and real no-mock replay
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Correct evidence types and theorem machinery still fail users if a production consumer bypasses them or a checker merely repeats the certifier's evidence. Build the integration and adversarial proof gate.

SCOPE: Route every continuum-sensitive operation through explicit named admission profiles. Package complete evidence trees, independently replay source and cover identities, and use a checker whose derivation is auditable. Cross-examine where applicable with separately derived oriented intersection or winding evidence without reusing the seam certifier's samples or conclusion. Preserve useful lower-authority results when one property is Unknown. Define cancellation, rollback, partial diagnostic artifact, and publication semantics for the complete pipeline.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: A real no-mock E2E uses actual mixed NURBS, mesh, SDF, and F-rep charts through adaptive cover construction, common intersections, theorem/profile assembly, ledger persistence, package/checker replay, and a continuum-sensitive downstream consumer. Seed gaps, overlaps, false cliques, non-good covers, exhausted hypercovers, nonmanifold edges, self-intersections, orientation reversals, material-side errors, source drift, corrupted receipts, and cancellation. Each fails or becomes Unknown at the exact missing property while unrelated evidence remains usable. G4 fault-injects every certify/package/check/publish boundary; G5 replays on both reference ISAs/thread counts. Mutation tests remove every profile gate. Bounded logs expose cover/refinement lineage, theorem route, coefficient system, component property states, budgets, cancellation/drain/finalization, identities, and no-claim reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured `acceptance_criteria` field contains the controlling, complete route, test, E2E, logging, replay, source-closure, authority, and `NoData` close gate.
acceptance_criteria:
## Exact continuum-geometry terminal route

This leaf solely owns `scripts/ci/e2e_continuum_geometry_gate.sh` and `tests/e2e/continuum_geometry_gate/manifest.toml`. The exact case set is {continuum.mixed-chart-positive, continuum.exhaustive-cover, continuum.common-intersection, continuum.watertight-profile, continuum.manifold-orientation-profile, continuum.embedded-material-profile, continuum.metric-seam-profile, continuum.false-clique, continuum.uncovered-sliver, continuum.sampled-as-continuum-refusal, continuum.invalid-theorem-assumptions, continuum.seam-mismatch, continuum.nonmanifold-orientation, continuum.self-intersection, continuum.cancel-fault-resource, continuum.checker-disagreement, continuum.tamper-stale, continuum.artifact-replay}. Canonical modes are `--list`, `--check`, `--self-test`, `--profile PROFILE --case CASE`, frozen `--negative CASE`, `--fault CASE`, and artifact-only replay with disjoint roots.

Literal/unit/boundary, property/metamorphic, model/state, mutation, API/refusal, fault/resource/cancellation/drain, release-built mixed NURBS/mesh/SDF/F-rep no-mock E2E, independent checking, deterministic bounded redacted JSONL, replay, both-ISA/thread-count evidence where applicable, and source closure must exact-set all properties and hostile twins. Logs retain chart/cover/refinement/intersection/theorem/profile/coefficient/component/property/case/sequence roots, budgets, expected/observed state, first divergence, drain/finalize, no-claim, safe relative artifacts, and exact reproduction. Planned paths remain `NoData`; sampled evidence never promotes continuum authority.

title: fs-geom: build an authentic oriented-intersection and winding cross-examiner
description:
ROOT CAUSE: The legacy ray_parity_falsifier samples a Boolean inside/outside sequence along segments whose endpoints must both be strictly outside. Such a sequence necessarily has an even number of toggles, so parity cannot independently falsify the sheaf seam result. It is a bounded input/sampling diagnostic, not a topology oracle. Existing plan and Gauntlet wording that treats it as independent cross-examination is unsound.

SCOPE: Keep the legacy routine only under an honestly named diagnostic contract, then add one or more genuinely independent falsifiers: certified oriented surface-ray intersections with multiplicity and tangency handling; interval winding/degree computation; generalized winding for nonmanifold diagnostics; and representation-independent intersection witnesses. Define how open boundaries, coincident sheets, grazing rays, trim curves, singular charts, overlapping surfaces, orientation reversal, and multi-material interfaces alter truth semantics. Use exact predicates/interval subdivision and set-valued results when intersection count or orientation is ambiguous. Explore an ambitious local-to-global theorem connecting oriented intersection data, cover/sheaf compatibility, and continuum boundary validity, without turning a conjecture into default authority before proof.

ACCEPTANCE: A positive cross-examination result states the exact domain and theorem it supports; ambiguous/tangent/budget-exhausted cases are Unknown, never guessed. The oracle is algorithmically and evidentially independent of the seam certifier it audits. Seeded broken seam certificates and orientation errors are detected with localized witnesses. Existing ray diagnostic cannot be mistaken for or converted into this authority.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 exact intersection/orientation laws; G2 analytic sphere/torus/polyhedron/trimmed-patch and adversarial seam zoo; G3 rigid transform, reparameterization, chart conversion, unit scaling, ray permutation/density, and subdivision metamorphics; G4 cancellation, caps, singularity/tangency storms, and no-partial-publication; G5 deterministic replay. Mutation tests flip orientation, drop multiplicity, merge coincident roots, and reintroduce Boolean-toggle parity. Logs retain source/representation identity, ray or integration domain, exact predicates/interval boxes, multiplicities, orientations, ambiguity/refusal reasons, budgets, seeds, and verifier/theorem versions.

REAL NO-MOCK E2E: Exercise the production geometry path from actual NURBS, mesh, and implicit charts through representation routing, certified oriented intersections or winding/degree computation, seam-certificate cross-examination, ledger persistence, package generation, independent checking, and replay. The cross-examiner may consume admitted source geometry and declared domain but must not reuse the seam certifier's samples, candidate cells, residual classification, or conclusion as its oracle. Seed orientation reversal, missing sheet, coincident sheet, even-multiplicity tangency, trim sliver, open boundary, nonmanifold, and material-side defects; require localized witnesses or typed Unknown at ambiguity. Logs make evidential independence auditable by recording separate algorithm, input derivation, subdivision, predicates, budgets, and verifier identities.

title: fs-geom sheaf merge: base-aware assignments, generation-checked CAS, and atomic publication
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: three_way_merge accepts branch assignment edits but no authoritative base assignment map, and its success variants cannot return merged assignments. The former path detected direct type collisions yet silently discarded non-conflicting edits. The current fail-closed refusal prevents data loss but means useful assignment merges are unavailable. Geometry cochain reconciliation, assignment truth, parent labels, and publication identity are not atomically bound; MergeResidualReceipt contains only post_norm/tol and caller labels are unauthenticated.

SCOPE: Define a canonical base/left/right assignment model keyed by stable EntityId plus typed quantity/schema identity. Implement the complete three-way truth table: unchanged, one-sided update/delete/create, equal concurrent update, conflicting update, delete/update, split/merge ancestry, unit-compatible conversion, and type/schema conflict. Preserve tombstones and identity transforms. Return one atomic merged artifact containing geometry/cochain state, assignments, lineage, conflict set, and evidence; never publish one plane without the other. Bind base and parent artifact roots, validated skeleton, union, gauge/decomposition report, merged assignment root, algorithm/schema version, budgets, and outcome into a collision-resistant receipt. Replace caller strings as authority with verified ledger identities.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY: Nominal residual reconciliation is not continuum watertightness or an H1 certificate. Candidate remainders remain operational conflict signals unless separate closed/non-exact witnesses exist. Assignment equality must respect units, semantic quantity kind, uncertainty/error model, and provenance rather than raw bytes alone.

ACCEPTANCE: No non-conflicting edit disappears; every conflicting edit is localized and retained; retry/order changes are deterministic; cancellation or any validation/publication error leaves the authoritative base unchanged; identical/disjoint writes deduplicate or union; identity collisions and same-ID/different-content refuse before partial commit. Resolved and Trivial outcomes return all merged state plus a content-bound replay receipt.

TESTS AND LOGGING: Exhaustive table-driven unit tests and property tests over the three-way assignment lattice, stable-ID ancestry, units/schemas, and empty/max cases. G3 branch swap, edit-order, equivalent-unit, reindex, and serialization round trips. G4 failure injection at every validate/merge/receipt/commit boundary, concurrent retries, cancellation, atomic rollback, and no leaks. G5 replay across thread counts. Mutation tests must catch dropped fields/tombstones, unauthenticated parents, and partial commit. A no-mock E2E must merge a mixed geometry/material/BC scenario and replay it from ledger roots. Logs retain base/parent/output roots, exact outcome histogram, per-plane write/conflict sets, units/schemas, budgets, cancellation/finalization, receipt version, and explicit authority/no-claim state.

CONCURRENCY AND PUBLICATION: Every merge begins from an ExpectedBase containing both a strong base artifact identity and an admitted generation or version token. Before publication, compare-and-swap both values against the authoritative store; pathname equality or a content root without generation is insufficient because replacement and ABA can restore an old root after intervening writes. Bind base, left, and right snapshots before and after computation. A stale generation, changed parent, concurrent writer, repository replacement, or publication-target drift returns a typed retry or refusal and publishes nothing. Retry rereads the authoritative base and recomputes; a stale successful receipt cannot be replayed as commit authority. Identical concurrent commits may deduplicate idempotently only when complete output and authority contexts match. Disjoint concurrent commits must not lose updates.

OUTCOME CONSERVATION: Define a complete per-plane outcome algebra for geometry, cochain, and assignment entities: unchanged, one-sided create/update/delete, equal concurrent edit, merged compatible edit, tombstoned, conflict by kind, refused, and any explicitly deferred state. The receipt carries a full histogram plus localized identity sets. Every admitted base/left/right identity in the merge universe appears in exactly one outcome class per applicable plane; histogram totals equal independently recomputed universe cardinalities, and no entity is omitted or double-counted. Geometry repair and gauge outcomes receive the same accounting. The checker recomputes these conservation laws rather than trusting merger-supplied counters.

title: fs-cheb roots: typed real/complex regions, set-valued multiplicity, and certified completeness
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-cheb currently exposes three distinct root paths whose authority must not be conflated. Cheb1::roots performs a fixed-grid sign scan and is explicitly incomplete; colleague_roots emits policy-filtered, cluster-deduplicated approximate matrix candidates; certified_roots independently invokes fs-ivl adaptive interval Newton over the full normalized domain. The certifier does not consume the grid or colleague candidates. Its live authority defect is that certified_roots projects the underlying RootSearchReport into a plain list, discarding complete, boxes_examined, exhaustion, and domain-coverage metadata, while none of the paths can express certified multiplicity/count clusters or unresolved candidate families. Thus callers cannot distinguish a complete exhaustion receipt from a partial set of boxes, and approximate discovery paths can still miss even-multiplicity, tightly clustered, endpoint, or highly scaled roots if misused as complete.

SCOPE: Preserve distinct discovery, approximation, and certification APIs with non-interchangeable types. Introduce a public RootSearchReport projection that retains disjoint set-valued clusters, multiplicity/count bounds, candidate provenance, domain coverage/exclusion tree, boxes examined, work and memory budgets, stopping reason, and Complete/Partial/Indeterminate/Refused truth state. Combine stable colleague pencils, adaptive interval subdivision, interval Newton/Krawczyk where admissible, derivative/GCD or square-free structure, Bernstein/Chebyshev exclusion bounds, argument-principle or Sturm-like counts for supported real classes, and arbitrary-precision/escalation hooks. Handle zero polynomials, degree drops, endpoint roots, repeated/even roots, extreme affine domains, coefficient dynamic range, underflow/overflow, and complex-conjugate clusters. Keep ambitious new completeness and multiplicity theorems as explicit feature-gated authority that can be promoted only with retained proofs.

ACCEPTANCE: Complete means every root in the admitted domain is covered by exactly one returned cluster and every cluster has certified count/multiplicity bounds; Partial explicitly names uncovered domain/work. The fs-ivl exhaustion metadata is preserved end-to-end rather than inferred from a list. No fixed sample density or colleague-candidate list can silently determine completeness. Domain and physical widths are typed and conservatively mapped. Deterministic ordering/tie-breaking is specified. Existing simple-root callers receive a checked projection only when singleton/simple obligations are proven.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 algebraic and property tests separately exercise the grid, colleague, and interval-certification contracts against analytic polynomials, zero/constant/degree-one, repeated/clustered/endpoint roots, coefficient/domain scaling, and non-finite inputs. G1 convergence of isolation widths. G2 Wilkinson-like and minimax/spectral benchmark families. G3 affine-domain, basis-conversion, coefficient rescaling, factor permutation, differentiation/integration, and equivalent-representation metamorphics. G4 cancellation and budget exhaustion at every subdivision/eigensolve boundary with retained partial state and no false Complete. G5 deterministic replay and two-ISA evidence. Certifier-of-certifier checks use independent high-precision/counting oracles; mutation tests remove exclusion/count/metadata propagation logic and deliberately misuse discovery as certification. Logs bind path kind, coefficients, domain/units, normalization, budgets/consumption, boxes examined, clusters/counts/residuals, uncovered regions, stopping/authority state, algorithm/theorem versions, and verifier artifacts.

POLYNOMIAL AND DOMAIN TRUTH STATES: Classify the admitted polynomial before root search. A proven zero polynomial returns IdenticallyZero or WholeDomainRoots for the declared real interval or complex region; it is never represented as an empty or finite cluster list. A proven nonzero constant returns NoRoots. Coefficients whose uncertainty prevents deciding a degree drop or zero polynomial return IndeterminatePolynomialClass. Preserve the proof basis for classification.

COUNT VERSUS MULTIPLICITY: Distinguish distinct-root count from total algebraic multiplicity. Claim exact multiplicity only when coefficient representation and algorithm support an exact witness, such as exact dyadic or rational algebra, validated square-free/GCD or subresultant structure, or another independently checked theorem. Floating or interval-uncertain coefficients generally return lower/upper count and multiplicity bounds or Unknown, not a guessed integer. A cluster may have exact total root count while individual multiplicities remain unresolved. Repeated, nearly repeated, and unresolved clusters retain set-valued semantics.

REAL VERSUS COMPLEX COMPLETENESS: Parameterize completeness by explicit RootDomain: a real interval with endpoint policy, or a bounded complex region with boundary policy. CompleteReal says nothing about non-real roots; CompleteComplex says nothing outside its admitted region. Complex-conjugate pairing is available only for certified-real coefficients. Boxes or discs touching a domain boundary or each other require explicit overlap and allocation rules and cannot be double-counted or silently discarded. Physical-domain affine mapping conservatively preserves enclosure, count, boundary inclusion, units, and truth state.

REAL NO-MOCK E2E: Build Chebyshev objects through public constructors, serialize/package them, run actual discovery, colleague, and interval-certification paths, persist the full report, and replay it through an independent checker. Include identically zero, nonzero constant, simple real, repeated real, endpoint, tightly clustered, complex-conjugate, real-completeness-only, and exhausted-budget cases. Verify that only an intended typed projection reaches a downstream solver and no list-only adapter launders Partial or Unknown into Complete. Retain detailed logs of coefficient representation, polynomial classification, domain kind, cluster count and multiplicity authority, coverage tree, uncovered region, and checker identity.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-07-14 fresh-eyes note: fixed an immediately compiling regression in a new colleague recurrence-absorption test (Cheb1::from_coeffs argument order). The finite-precision colleague lane now refuses recurrence-row absorption of either a nonzero coefficient contribution or the recurrence half term, while permitting genuine exact cancellation; existing power-of-two normalization and half-ratio guards remain. This does not close the bead: public typed Result APIs, degree/work/memory/Cx admission, complete RootSearchReport propagation, set-valued multiplicity/count semantics, and certifier completeness remain required.

title: fs-opt: seal the typed IR and validate all graph/leaf authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-opt describes a typed, valid-by-construction Problem, while CONTRACT says every constructor validates parameter ranges, but the invariant is neither enforced nor sealed. Problem publicly exposes mutable vars, exprs, objectives, constraints, tags, and budget vectors, so callers can construct or mutate inconsistent IDs/shapes/metadata without ProblemBuilder. Public shape, node_dims, and class index arbitrary public NodeId values; route/reachable transitively trust public objective, constraint, root, and child IDs. The builder itself also admits invalid authority-bearing leaves: Sphere ambient < 2, Stiefel p > n, unchecked u32 point/tangent arithmetic, non-finite constants, non-finite objective weights and objective weights whose sign semantics are undeclared, invalid/NaN chance probabilities, zero-level multi-fidelity tags, and weak legacy u64 bilevel identities. These values can panic, wrap, manufacture shapes, drive allocation, or reach finish(), serialization, hashes, routing, and solvers despite the contract.

SCOPE: Make Problem an opaque sealed IR with private fields and read-only checked iteration/accessors. Define a single versioned ProblemAdmission validator and typed errors for graph topology/references, ManifoldSpec, leaves, objectives, constraints, tags, budgets, and aggregate limits. Validate semantic constraints and checked dimensions before VarId/NodeId assignment, graph mutation, shape derivation, allocation, serialization, route/reachability, or identity. Specify Rn zero-dimensional policy; Sphere ambient minimum; Stiefel 1 <= p <= n; checked point/tangent formulas and u32-to-usize portability; finite constant policy; an explicit objective-weight contract (prefer finite nonnegative weights because Sense already carries direction, unless a separately justified signed policy is adopted); probability domains; nonzero/capped fidelity levels; full-width typed bilevel identity; names/units; acyclicity/reference validity; aligned metadata-vector lengths; and per-item/aggregate graph/dimension/work/memory caps. Make currently infallible mutators/accessors fallible or require opaque validated IDs/tokens. Ensure programmatic builder, parser/deserializer, migration, generated catalogs, routing, evaluation, and all consumers use the same validator. Rejection must leave intern tables, IDs, budget, and ordering unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE: No public safe API can create or mutate an invalid Problem, index an unknown ID, or bypass admission. No invalid manifold, constant, objective, constraint, tag, graph edge, or identity can be hashed as an admitted study, produce a Shape, allocate, route, or reach a solver. Dimension arithmetic is checked and correct for every admitted case. finish authority is either genuinely preserved by construction or becomes fallible with a complete validation report. Repeated rejection/retry is deterministic and ID-stable. Historical invalid bytes remain inspectable only as quarantined legacy artifacts with no execution/certificate authority.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 table/property tests cover arbitrary IDs and graph-reference corruption; metadata-vector misalignment; cycles; Sphere ambient 0/1/2/MAX; Stiefel n/p boundaries, p>n and overflow; Rn policy; checked tangent formulas; non-finite/extreme constants and weights; negative-weight behavior under the chosen explicit policy; probability endpoints/NaN; zero/MAX fidelity levels; typed bilevel identities; aggregate caps; builder rollback; and deterministic error ordering. Compile-fail/API tests prove direct Problem mutation/construction is unavailable. G3 programmatic-vs-wire parity, serialization round trip, equivalent valid graphs, units/names, and route/reachability invariance. G4 adversarial graph/dimension/allocation/metadata storms, budget exhaustion, cancellation at validation boundaries, and no partial builder mutation. G5 exact replay. Mutation tests remove every range/reference/finiteness/checked-arithmetic guard. A no-mock E2E parses, builds, routes, solves, serializes, and replays valid sphere/Stiefel/stochastic/bilevel problems while invalid variants fail before graph authority. Structured logs retain source/problem identity, metadata kind/value class, manifold parameters, graph counts, checked dimensions, caps/consumption, validator/schema version, refusal/ranked repair, and explicit no-claim state.

IDENTITY OUTPUT: Successful common ProblemAdmission produces a ProblemSemanticId over normalized admitted meaning. Programmatic construction does not manufacture a WireContentId; that identity exists only after canonical wire serialization under the v3 schema. APIs, tests, receipts, and logs use the domain-separated types and refuse implicit conversion.

title: fs-opt wire v3: split wire-content and problem-semantic identities, add trust anchors, and bound parsing
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-opt v2 overloads FNV-1a 64 as canonical body hash, study identity, parser source hash, migration anchor, and bilevel reference. FNV is neither collision-resistant nor domain-separated, so distinct studies can alias under current APIs. Parsing is also not total: it lacks aggregate byte, line, directive, variable, node, token, decoded-string, heap, work, depth, deadline, and cancellation budgets, allocates complete line and token vectors, and builds graph state before final canonicality verification. A self-hash establishes content consistency only; it does not authenticate bytes against a writer who can replace both body and digest.

THREE DISTINCT IDENTITIES: Define SourceByteId for exact untrusted bytes received, WireContentId for the canonical schema-versioned v3 wire artifact, and ProblemSemanticId for the admitted typed optimization problem's normalized meaning. These types are domain-separated and non-interchangeable. If v3 accepts only canonical bytes, noncanonical input refuses with a ranked canonicalization remedy. If compatibility parsing accepts alternate presentation, retain SourceByteId, emit a normalization receipt, and compute WireContentId only over canonical re-emission. Programmatic construction produces ProblemSemanticId but no WireContentId until serialization. Parsed and programmatically constructed semantically identical admitted problems yield the same ProblemSemanticId; canonical serialization of either yields the same WireContentId.

REFERENCE SEMANTICS: Packages, caches, exact replay, signatures, and byte-level migration receipts use WireContentId or SourceByteId as appropriate. Bilevel logical references, study deduplication, and semantic graph identity use ProblemSemanticId plus required schema and authority context. A migration receipt binds old SourceByteId or legacy FNV lookup, new canonical WireContentId, new ProblemSemanticId, exact normalization or migration rule, verifier identity, and external trust anchor. Different wire versions may intentionally have different WireContentIds while sharing a proven ProblemSemanticId. No equality or widening conversion between identities is implicit.

TOTAL PARSING: Stream or preflight under explicit byte, line, directive, variable, node, token, decoded-string, aggregate heap/work/depth, deadline, and cancellation budgets. Authenticate schema and enforce caps before graph mutation or large allocation; compute SourceByteId incrementally, validate canonical bytes, and couple parsing to the sealed transactional builder from frankensim-sj31i.48 so error or cancellation rolls back IDs, interning, work accounting, and authority. Preserve v1/v2 FNV only as non-authoritative historical lookup/crosswalk evidence; no silent rewrite, u64 widening, or width truncation.

AUTHORITY: None of SourceByteId, WireContentId, or ProblemSemanticId authenticates its own claims. Expected IDs, signatures, ledger/Merkle roots, attested snapshots, or other independently admitted anchors remain separate AuthorityRef data. Generic parsing returns admitted content with explicitly Unanchored authority. Same-ID/different-preimage adjudication preserves all source, canonical, and semantic encodings and fails closed. Domain/schema confusion, downgrade, and authority-changing ambient context refuse.

ACCEPTANCE: Programmatic and parsed construction yield one ProblemSemanticId only after common ProblemAdmission validation. Canonical serialization yields one WireContentId; exact source-byte replay retains SourceByteId. Whitespace or presentation changes, canonical version changes, semantic normalization, default insertion, and graph-equivalent construction affect exactly the intended identities and no others. Maximum memory/work is derivable from budgets and enforced before breach. Cancellation drains without publishing a Problem, migration authority, or anchored receipt. Current consumers reject bare legacy u64 where a typed identity or AuthorityRef is required.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property/fuzz tests cover every cap at n-1/n/n+1, huge lines/tokens/escapes, integer boundaries, collision/downgrade/confusion attempts, duplicate/unknown directives, byte and UTF-8 policy, CR/LF variants, transactional rollback, identity domain separation, and exact canonical round trips. title: Constellation process supervisor: bounded spawn, cancellation, output caps, and kill-tree drain
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Authoritative paths use process APIs that can wait indefinitely, retain unbounded output, leak descendants, and outlive cancellation. Implement one bounded child-process supervisor for Git and every external bootstrap or verification action.

SCOPE: Spawn only through an admitted AdmissionContext. Stream bounded stdout and stderr, enforce per-stream and combined caps, deadlines, process and descendant counts, retries, cancellation, escalation, kill-and-drain, and deterministic output/event ordering. Define supported-platform descendant containment and explicit degraded or refused semantics where containment cannot be established. Model exit, signal, timeout, output truncation, spawn refusal, cancellation, and drain failure as typed states. No authoritative path retains Command::output, unbounded subprocess execution, or orphanable children.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Real no-mock tests launch hangs, output floods, forked descendants, ignored termination, stalled fetches, malformed output, cancellation races, and caps at n-1/n/n+1. Every child and descendant is reaped or authority is refused with a retained containment failure; logs stay bounded and secrets are redacted. G4 fault-injects spawn/read/kill/wait/drain. G5 proves deterministic event ordering. Mutation tests restore an unbounded wait or drop a descendant/output guard. Receipts bind executable, command class, caps/consumption, exit/timeout/kill/drain state, and verifier identity.

title: Constellation path and repository admission: descriptor-bound roots, ownership, and swap defense
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Canonicalized strings and lexical containment do not survive symlink, hardlink, mount, repository, or pathname replacement races. Admit workspace, repository, sibling, source, destination, and publication locations as descriptor-bound capabilities.

SCOPE: Verify containment, filesystem and repository identity, ownership, mode, symlink/hardlink/mount aliases, nested repository and submodule boundaries, destination overlap, and before/after stability before mutation or authority. Detect repository replacement and path ABA even when a pathname or content spelling returns to an earlier value. Bind descriptor identity and generation into downstream receipts. Define explicit per-platform guarantees and refuse authority when the required descriptor semantics are unavailable.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Relative, Unicode, and control-character paths; symlink/hardlink swaps; mount and repository replacement; hostile ownership/modes; overlapping destinations; nested repos/submodules; archive roots; concurrent replacement; and cancellation all fail before mutation unless explicitly admitted. G3 relocation and equivalent-path metamorphics preserve semantic source identity without conflating capabilities. G4 injects swaps at every check/use boundary. Mutation tests remove each identity, ownership, containment, or stability check. Bounded logs retain descriptor identities and states, not merely path strings.

title: Constellation execution security: pinned executables, scrubbed environment, Git policy, and network authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Ambient PATH, environment, Git configuration, hooks, credentials, proxies, and network access can alter source or verification semantics without appearing in current receipts. Define one executable and ambient-authority policy used by every supervised process.

SCOPE: Bind approved executable path plus descriptor/content identity and version, invocation class, explicit cwd, scrubbed allowlisted environment, Git config and object format, credential/helper and hook policy, offline/fetch/network permission, redirect and proxy behavior, and trust source. Reject executable replacement, PATH aliasing, environment or Git-config injection, hooks, unsafe ownership, unexpected network access, and authority-changing inherited state. Secrets are never logged, placed in public hashes, or included in diagnostic excerpts.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Unit and real-process tests exercise executable swaps, PATH/config/env injection, hooks, credential helpers, proxies, offline violations, redirects, network stalls, and unknown executable versions with bounded ranked refusal. G4 cancels each external phase and verifies drain. G5 replays the admitted policy deterministically. Mutation tests remove pinning, scrubbing, network, or secret-redaction guards. title: Constellation publication transaction: generation-checked CAS, durable fsync, and ABA-safe receipts
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Pathname rename into a mutable parent is not sufficient atomic authority: the parent, destination, or prior generation can change, ABA can restore old-looking state, and success may be reported before durable persistence. Implement a descriptor-bound publication transaction.

SCOPE: Admit parent and target capabilities; create bounded temporary artifacts in the admitted destination domain; bind exact bytes and semantic identity; fsync content and required metadata; compare-and-swap expected parent identity, target absence or expected prior identity, and generation; publish with no-clobber or explicitly versioned replacement semantics; fsync the authoritative directory; then emit a receipt. Recheck source and destination capabilities before and after. Cancellation or any validate/write/fsync/CAS/rename/receipt fault removes no pre-existing artifact and grants no authority. Idempotent deduplication requires identical content plus identical authority context.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Fault injection at every byte write, fsync, metadata update, CAS, rename, directory sync, and receipt step proves no partial authoritative state. Concurrent identical, disjoint, stale, conflicting, ABA, parent-replaced, and target-replaced writers have deterministic outcomes with no lost update. Cross-filesystem or unsupported atomicity refuses or uses a separately proved protocol. Mutation tests kill each generation/durability guard. Logs bind expected/observed generations, descriptor identities, content roots, durability steps, outcome, and verifier.

title: fs-opt eval/descent: validate runtime bindings and make execution total
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-opt public evaluation and descent assume that caller-provided runtime state matches the admitted graph. eval indexes memo by public NodeId before validating bounds; Expr::Var clones a binding without checking the variable manifold point_dim; Component directly indexes runtime vectors; vector add/sub/dot use zip and silently truncate mismatched shapes. descend_fn does not validate x0 length or DescentOptions, and SO3/Stiefel retractions index x/t directly while Sphere/Rn zip may silently shorten. Malformed bindings can therefore panic, compute a different-dimensional objective without refusal, or corrupt optimization semantics. The evaluation budget is also not a hard envelope: when a finite limit is selected, mandatory initial/final evaluations can exceed max_evals. The current max_evals == 0 spelling means Unlimited and must not be reinterpreted as zero work during repair.

SCOPE: Introduce a validated runtime BindingFrame keyed by VarId with exact manifold point shapes, units, finiteness, uniqueness, and aggregate memory/work caps. Validate public NodeId and every node output against the graph's stored Shape/Dims before indexing or arithmetic; vector operators require exact lengths and checked allocation, never zip-truncate. Define typed EvalError/DescentError with node/variable/path attribution. Validate all DescentOptions (finite/positive step, finite learning rate and closure threshold, iteration/evaluation/memory caps, retraction domain) and x0 before the first evaluation. Thread Cx and explicit cancellation through finite-difference coordinate loops, retractions, line/search iterations, and finalization. Replace the overloaded scalar with an explicit EvalLimit::Unlimited or EvalLimit::Limited(NonZeroU64), migrating max_evals == 0 to Unlimited. Turn finite-limit accounting into an exact ledger that includes f0, derivatives/probes, trial points, acceptance checks, and final evaluation; if a finite budget cannot cover the next atomic step, return a resumable partial report without overshoot.

NUMERICAL AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARY: Retractions must return typed set-valued/indeterminate/refused states at singular or invalid points rather than normalize zero, index short storage, or fabricate a manifold point. A finite objective alone is not convergence, feasibility, or stationarity authority. Reports must distinguish completed, budget-exhausted, cancelled/drained, numerical-domain failure, and invalid-input states, and must never publish a final optimum from a partial mandatory step.

ACCEPTANCE: Unknown nodes, missing bindings, unknown or duplicate VarId bindings, short/long/non-finite values, malformed intermediate shapes, invalid x0/options, singular retractions, and insufficient max_evals all fail before unsafe indexing or semantic truncation. title: EPIC: typed strong identities, canonical encoding, and explicit authority migration
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs_evidence::ProvenanceHash is a public u64 FNV-1a accumulator used as evidence provenance across the project. FNV is collision-prone, lacks robust domain/schema separation, and cannot safely bind scientific evidence trees, conversion receipts, merge outcomes, sampled geometry evidence, optimization studies, or migration crosswalks. Local replacements in fs-opt, fs-geom, bootstrap, or packages would create incompatible hash dialects and leave the central Evidence<T> carrier weak. Separately, a self-computed unkeyed digest is content identity/corruption evidence, not authenticity: anyone who may rewrite bytes can recompute it.

SCOPE: Replace ProvenanceHash authority with one shared typed 32-byte identity substrate built on the existing fs-blake3 mode-separated hash_domain implementation and official-vector evidence. Define non-interchangeable types and domains for raw artifact ContentId, schema/domain-specific semantic identities, ordered evidence-composition nodes, source/model/checker identities, and externally anchored AuthorityRef or SignedEnvelope. Use length-delimited canonical preimages, explicit version/domain/context, exact field order, optional/presence tags, and role-specific domains. Preserve legacy FNV only in a quarantined LegacyProvenanceV1 field/crosswalk; never widen u64 and call it strong. Audit all Evidence, Certified, geometry/sheaf, router, merge, fs-opt, bootstrap, ledger, package/checker, generated catalog, cache, serialization, and equality/order consumers. Provide deterministic database/wire schema migration and dual-root receipts anchored to exact old/new bytes plus verifier/schema identity.

AUTHORITY MODEL: Generic construction/parsing computes and returns a ContentId but grants no external trust. Tamper/refusal authority requires a caller-supplied trusted expected ContentId, ledger/Merkle root, signature/MAC, attested source snapshot, or other declared anchor. A changed artifact with a recomputed digest is distinct untrusted content, not generically detectable tampering. Collision resistance is an explicit cryptographic assumption; on any observed same-ID/different-byte event, preserve both byte roots and fail closed for adjudication. Migration receipts authorize a semantic crosswalk only when their verifier/schema and trust anchor are independently admitted.

ACCEPTANCE: No current authoritative API accepts bare ProvenanceHash/u64/FNV where a strong typed identity or trust anchor is required. Every semantic domain and version is non-confusable and mutation-sensitive for every declared field; excluded fields are documented/tested. Parsing/content hashing never claims authenticity. Legacy evidence remains inspectable and crosswalkable without laundering. All migrated consumers derive identical shared identities and cannot accidentally mix artifact, semantic, signature, or authority domains.

TESTS AND LOGGING: Official and independent BLAKE3/derive-key vectors; G0 canonical encoding/composition/field-order/presence/domain/version laws; mutation tests for every semantic and excluded field; same bytes/different domain and raw-vs-domain non-equivalence; legacy crosswalk exact-byte tests; parser width/version/downgrade/truncation cases; recomputed self-hash accepted only as a different untrusted ContentId and refused by expected-ID/signed-root APIs; synthetic collision-adjudication path; schema/database migration, rollback, concurrent readers/writers, and cancellation. G3 equivalent construction/serialization and cross-crate identity parity. G4 bounded hostile input and partial migration faults. G5 two-ISA replay. A no-mock E2E carries evidence from producer through ledger/package/checker/replay with both unanchored and anchored trust states. Logs retain bounded legacy/current content identities, semantic domain/version, anchor/verifier/signature state, migration rule, authority/no-claim state, budgets, and artifacts without presenting hashes as authentication.

title: fs-blake3: fallible allocation-free ordered-row canonical streaming
description:
## Root cause and user impact
CanonicalEncoder can stream already-materialized borrowed rows, but large producers must first build Vec<Vec<u8>>. A legal million-incidence causal graph therefore allocates millions of row buffers and roughly half a gigabyte of retained temporary payload before the encoder sees it. Canonical byte caps do not bound actual peak memory, allocator failure can abort the process, and cancellation cannot interrupt individual row construction. This violates the identity-core hostile-length and no-partial-publication contract.

## Technical approach
Add an allocation-free, fallible ordered-row streaming API to fs-blake3 CanonicalEncoder. The caller declares collection cardinality and each row length before bytes are written. An encoder-owned bounded row sink writes the canonical length frame and absorbs chunks directly into the transactional digest/preimage state. It must fail closed on length underflow/overflow, producer error after partial absorption, field/frame/item limit overflow, arithmetic/layout overflow, and cancellation at row, chunk, and final-publication boundaries. Producer failure consumes or permanently poisons the encoder so a partial identity cannot be finished. Keep ordered_bytes for already-materialized slices. fs-blake3 must remain independent of fs-exec/fs-alloc; expose generic fallible/cancellation closures and typed producer errors.

## Invariants and compatibility
For identical rows, the new API must emit byte-for-byte identical canonical frames, schema IDs, typed IDs, preimage roots, counters, and adjudication metadata as ordered_bytes. Existing public domains and schemas do not move. Declared cardinality, encoded cardinality, and collection_items must agree exactly. No callback may retain a mutable sink beyond its row. Safe Rust only.

## Tests and evidence
G0 parity for empty, singleton, variable-length, nested child, and maximum legal rows; exact underwrite/overwrite and wrong-count refusals; producer error before and after partial absorption; arithmetic and limit boundaries. G3 compare both APIs field-by-field and against an independent canonical-frame parser. G4 cancel at every row/chunk/publication checkpoint and prove no finishable partial identity or leaked state. G5 deterministic receipts across row chunking and callback schedules. Add detailed structured test diagnostics naming schema, field, row, declared/written bytes, counters, limit, cancellation phase, and disposition. Update fs-blake3 CONTRACT.md and owner identity declaration if implementation closure changes; run central batch proof before closure.

## No-claim boundary
This leaf bounds encoder-owned streaming state. Consumer-side graph indexes, sorting workspaces, and operation-memory leases are owned by the dependent I02 resource-closure leaf.

title: Own solver-state identities: collision-proof registry and typed codec/schema charter
description: ROOT CAUSE: SolverStateV2 currently lets any implementation declare arbitrary public 32-byte state-type, state-schema, and state-codec constants plus a codec version. matches_state compares only those bytes. Two unrelated Rust types that copy/reuse all four values can cross-open if their payload layout is plausible; the nominal wrappers prevent role confusion but do not prove owner uniqueness. GOAL: replace unchecked byte declarations with an owner-bound, registry-validated state identity charter. Each state family has a unique typed owner/domain identity; schema and codec receipts bind the actual field grammar, units/endianness/float policy, compatibility/migration policy, code/contract version, and owning solver family. Workspace types are generated or checked against a collision registry; downstream extension uses a signed/admitted owner charter rather than an unscoped from_bytes escape. PreparedResume binds the actual solver instance/config and validates a post-decode state manifest, so nominal identity alone is never activation authority. ACCEPTANCE: duplicate/colliding owner/type/schema/codec declarations fail deterministically at registry/check time; a deliberately malicious same-layout type copying all old constants cannot mint a valid owner-bound charter or activate; legitimate schema/codec revisions rotate exactly the intended IDs and require migration; historical charters remain replayable/quarantined by era; diagnostics identify role, owner, field, expected/found charter IDs. TESTS/LOGGING: compile-time/xtask duplicate fixtures, G0 role/schema laws, G3 same-bytes different-owner and same-owner changed-grammar mutations, downgrade/replay/cross-era tests, no-mock ledger PreparedResume path, and detailed collision/admission logs. NO-CLAIM: until this lands, uniqueness of SolverStateV2 byte constants is an implementer responsibility and expected-root opening is caller-relative, not proof of Rust nominal type ownership.

title: Typed snapshot freeze transaction: bind drained executor run to one immutable solver state
description: ROOT CAUSE: DrainFinalizeReport proves that cancellation was requested and all registered worker guards drained for a caller-selected logical run, but its semantic identity contains only version/run/worker counts. A caller can reproduce that report with another tracker, pair it with arbitrary pause-request and gate-generation labels, and seal an S value at a later time. Snapshot v2 therefore has honest caller-relative consistency today, not proof that the serialized state was atomically frozen by the session owning the paused run. GOAL: introduce a typed, non-copyable snapshot freeze transaction spanning fs-exec and fs-session. The session owner initiates one pause request, binds an owner/session/solver-instance generation, closes mutation admission, drains the exact run, freezes or immutably commits the exact solver state/configuration, and receives a single-use SnapshotFreezePermit<S> (or equivalent linear token) carrying the drain report, pause/gate/session identities, state commitment, remaining/consumed budgets, RNG cursor, and finalization-scope budget. Sealing must consume or irreversibly burn that permit; panic, cancellation, encode refusal, or publication failure poisons/burns it and cannot silently permit a second state. Header declarations remain replayable data and can never reconstruct the permit. The ledger records a predecessor-bound freeze receipt before any resume activation. ACCEPTANCE: no public constructor can pair a report with unrelated pause/generation/state; no TOCTOU mutation exists between freeze commitment and encoding; cross-type/session/run/generation/state substitution fails closed; duplicate, stale, copied, replayed, panic-unwound, and cancelled permits cannot publish; exact retry policy is explicit and idempotency-bound; the resulting artifact/receipt states precisely whether bytes were prepared, committed, or activated. If Rust ownership cannot express a required cross-crate transition directly, use a private owner-held registry nonce/capability with burn-before-call and panic poison rather than a copyable boolean or digest-only token. TESTS/LOGGING: G0 typestate laws and compile-fail misuse fixtures; G3 mutation/substitution/metamorphic tests; G4 real executor cancellation/drain/freeze/seal storms, panic injection at every transaction boundary, concurrent seal races, stale-generation and crash-recovery tests; no-mock fs-exec -> fs-ledger -> fs-session script with deterministic structured logs for request, gate, drain, freeze commitment, permit burn, artifact publication, recovery, and activation. NO-CLAIM: until this task lands, DrainFinalizeReport plus caller labels does not prove atomic checkpoint provenance or association with a particular solver state.

title: New-domain semantic identity: units, frames, experiments, calibration, and context of use
description: ROOT CAUSE: Equal numeric payloads are not interchangeable observations when units, frames, state meaning, experiment role, calibration or correlation differ. SCOPE: Integrate the semantic model owned by sj31i.36 with the typed identity and evidence substrate. Bind units and quantity kind, frame, basis/orientation, state schema, model/operator, spatial and temporal support, experiment/dataset/sample/replicate, instrument/calibration, covariance group, data role, blind split and declared context of use. Legitimate unit/basis/frame aliases require canonical transformation receipts. Duplicate records never become independent evidence; training, calibration and holdout roles are identity-bearing. Content identity is not calibration authority. ACCEPTANCE: Equal bits with incompatible semantics diverge or refuse; valid transformations produce verified crosswalks; duplicate-versus-replicate, train/holdout leakage, stale calibration/model, covariance alias and context mismatch are tested. TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 field and type laws, G3 unit/frame/basis transforms, G4 cancellation and hostile metadata, G5 replay, and no-mock as-built to assimilation to OED ledger/checker replay with bounded semantic and trust logs.

title: HELM identity migration: packages, checker, bootstrap, catalogs, caches, and admission
description: ROOT CAUSE: Package, checker, bootstrap, catalog, cache and admission surfaces use overlapping weak or pathname-only identities and can mistake self-consistency for trust. SCOPE: Give package roots, checker decisions, source snapshots, constellation/bootstrap receipts, generated catalogs, capability sets and cache keys distinct schemas and domains. Expected-root and signed-root APIs expose anchored and unanchored state. Cache keys bind semantic versions, capabilities, determinism mode, machine/ISA only where contractual, and dependency/source receipts. Bootstrap source identity cannot rely on ambient repository metadata. Catalogs derive declarations from code/contracts and refuse unclassified fields. Unknown versions, domain confusion, stale cache, authority mismatch and recomputed self-digests fail closed without generic tamper claims. ACCEPTANCE: In-memory and portable transports agree only under identical gate context; source drift, wrong dependency receipt, stale capability, changed catalog, cache alias and missing/mismatched anchors are typed. TESTS AND LOGGING: Bounded hostile parsing, G4 cancellation, no-mock producer-ledger-package-checker replay and source-distribution bootstrap E2E. Logs retain bounded domain IDs, gate context, source/dependency identity, anchor/verifier and refusal.

title: Global strong-identity gate: eliminate authoritative FNV and prove cross-domain replay
description:
PURPOSE: Own the final cross-project enforcement proof rather than making the identity umbrella a global implementation blocker. SCOPE: Generate an inventory for every persisted, replayed and public identity, classifying content, semantic, legacy, authority and deliberately non-semantic fields. Reject new unclassified fields, authoritative FNV/u64, width truncation, domain reuse, display-hash inputs, stale schema guessing and claims that unkeyed digests authenticate. Legacy readers remain behind explicit types and crosswalks. ACCEPTANCE: Inventory has zero uncovered current surfaces and names all retained legacy surfaces; every semantic field has a mutation target; policy gates catch omitted fields and forbidden conversions; anchored and unanchored replay remain distinct. TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 canonical/type laws, G3 cross-crate parity, G4 migration/cancellation/collision faults, G5 two-ISA replay; real no-mock journey spanning producer, Evidence, geometry or optimization, fs-exec snapshot, ledger, package, checker, migration and replay; documentation lint rejects self-authentication wording for unkeyed digests. Retain bounded logs and replay artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is controlling and preserves the complete close gate.
acceptance_criteria:
## Exact cross-domain strong-identity terminal harness

This Bead owns planned `scripts/ci/strong_identity_e2e.sh` and `tests/e2e/strong_identity.toml` with immutable cases {identity.inventory-exact-set, identity.cross-domain.geometry, identity.cross-domain.optimization, identity.legacy-migration, identity.collision-truncation, identity.cancellation-publication, identity.two-isa-replay}. Both geometry and optimization cases are mandatory, separately named, and independently terminal; neither may substitute for the other or be hidden behind an “or” route. Membership is set-equal and canonicalized by stable case ID.

Canonical modes are `--list`, `--check`, `--self-test`, `--run CASE`, frozen `--negative CASE`, `--fault CASE`, and artifact-only `--replay RECEIPT --input-root PATH --output-root PATH` with disjoint roots. The release-built no-mock journeys each span producer Evidence, the respective real geometry or optimization consumer, fs-exec snapshot-v2 terminal evidence, ledger, package, independent checker, migration, and replay.

Unit/type/schema/API/compile-fail tests cover every identity class and forbidden conversion. Exact-set/property/metamorphic tests cover inventory parity, canonicalization, domain separation, anchored/unanchored distinction, legacy crosswalk, schedule/order invariance, and separate geometry/optimization authority. Mutations target every semantic field, digest width/domain/key, display encoding, schema, authority phrase, and replay link. G4/G5 cover cancellation, crash/retry, collision/truncation, tamper/stale/mixed roots, two-ISA replay, leaks, and partial publication.

Bounded redacted deterministic JSONL records source/build/schema, manifest/case/attempt/sequence, producer/domain/consumer/snapshot/ledger/package/checker/migration roots, expected/observed identity and authority state, first divergence, cancellation/drain/finalize, no-claim, relative artifacts, and exact reproduction. Immutable artifact-only replay independently reconstructs both journeys. An unkeyed digest proves integrity/content identity, not authentication, numerical correctness, or scientific validity. Planned paths remain `NoData` until both journeys execute and replay.

title: fs-blake3 authority: prevent foreign permit-all capabilities from minting promotion trust
description: Current AuthorityVerifier and AuthorityAdmitter are public traits whose only success signal is Result<(), _>. Any downstream PermitAll implementation can therefore drive Presented -> Verified -> Admitted, and fs-spectral converts that admitted value into promotion-capable favorable witnesses. This matches fs-blake3's narrow caller-policy no-claim but contradicts the stronger non-forgeable authority boundary consumed by promotion code. AuthorityRef also retains verifier/key-policy only as parsed digest values, discarding their canonical-preimage observations and preventing same-ID/different-bytes adjudication for authority identities. Acceptance: generic caller checks can produce only an explicitly policy-relative non-promotion result; promotion-capable admission requires an opaque domain-owner decision tied to an independently configured trust root; exact subject receipt/preimage, anchor, verifier receipt/observation, and policy receipt/observation remain bound; foreign PermitAll code cannot mint a promotion witness; verifier/policy namespace and preimage metadata survive bounded audit logging; adversarial and compile-fail tests cover bypass attempts; centralized proof pending.

title: Bind promotion to owner-executed capability decisions
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND EXACT BYPASS
AuthorityRef stores only public verifier and key-policy IDs. Generic verify and admit transitions accept any public AuthorityVerifier or AuthorityAdmitter implementation and return no capability-bound decision receipt. PromotionTrustRoot::admit_for_promotion then re-adjudicates only caller-presented public ByteObservations against its configured observations. A foreign PermitAll can therefore present the OWNER verifier and policy IDs, drive both generic transitions, reuse the OWNER receipts public observations, and receive a PromotionWitness carrying the OWNER charter. Private witness fields do not help because the public root mints the witness. Existing tests use rogue IDs and miss exact-ID capability impersonation.

MISSION
Redesign promotion admission so the root executes or verifies an independently anchored owner capability decision; do not accept a generic policy-relative Admitted value plus caller-supplied observations as sufficient. Bind the actual decision producer, decision transcript, subject, anchor, verifier/policy schemas and observations, context, root charter, capability/code identity, versions, budgets, and final disposition. Identity strings alone are not proof of which code ran.

ACCEPTANCE
- A byte-for-byte regression proves foreign PermitAll with owner IDs and owner observations cannot mint or launder an owner promotion witness.
- The root either owns and invokes immutable verifier/admitter capabilities, consumes a nonforgeable capability-bound receipt, or verifies an externally anchored signature/attestation. Any configuration-relative fallback is nominally typed as non-authoritative and cannot reach promotion consumers.
- Root/witness types and canonical identity distinguish capability implementation/configuration/version, verifier decision, admission decision, and external anchor. Same textual IDs with different code/transcripts refuse.
- No public constructor or caller-selected expected value can convert policy-relative admission into authority. Copy/clone/reconfigure/fork/replay semantics are explicit.
- G0 covers exact-ID spoofing, swapped capabilities, stale/replayed decisions, wrong subject/anchor/context, same-ID different bytes, recomputed unanchored receipts, and downgrade. G3 covers legitimate replay and equivalent owner reconstruction only under an admitted crosswalk. G4 covers panic/cancellation/fault between verify, admit, mint, and publication with no partial witness or leaked capability.
- CONTRACT retracts the current false claim until proven. Central fs-blake3 all-targets/doctests/clippy, identity registry regeneration, fs-spectral consumer tests, and DSR are required before closure.
- Keep code-first slices in progress until consolidated proof; no theorem or security claim may rely on private fields alone.

title: fs-rep-nurbs refit: typed admitted fields, certified geometry error, and budgeted cancellation
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The legacy `refit_radial` accepts an arbitrary scalar closure and previously exposed field-residual and Lipschitz quantities with certificate-like names. The current hardened implementation now keeps sampled retained-sign-bracket-target-to-spline evidence, sampled field residual, and geometric probe-spacing estimates separate, refuses non-finite values, and applies fixed safety caps. That is an honest baseline, not the final authority model: the closure carries no units, zero-set identity, Lipschitz witness, metric error bound, continuity class, provenance, or cancellation context; ordinary f64 arithmetic is not outward rounded; radial sampling can miss features; fixed process caps are not caller budgets. A scalar field can be 1-Lipschitz while `abs(f)` is still a lower rather than upper bound on distance to its zero set, so SDF-like naming alone cannot authorize a Hausdorff claim. SCOPE: Introduce a typed admitted implicit-field capability carrying units, domain, zero-set semantics, continuity/Lipschitz evidence, a metric-regularity witness such as `dist(x,Z) <= kappa*abs(f(x))` where applicable, source identity, uncertainty and evaluation budget. Separate signed distance, approximate distance, generic level set, occupancy, and min/max CSG truth states. Thread `Cx` plus explicit evaluation, work, memory, subdivision, error, deadline, and cancellation budgets through projection, assembly, factorization, probing, coverage, and finalization, with bounded poll latency and resumable partial evidence. Replace static-only caps with admitted caller envelopes while retaining hard defensive ceilings. Build continuum directed-distance and Hausdorff certificates only from exhaustive source and fitted-surface coverage, interval or affine/Taylor evaluation, outward-rounded hodograph and field bounds, topology/visibility witnesses, and independently checked metric assumptions. Generalize beyond star-shaped radial domains through certified segmentation and atlas coverage; preserve the radial estimator as a clearly typed low-authority lane. SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY: Sampled fit residual, sampled `abs(f(S))`, geometric probe spacing, unit-Lipschitz regularity, and Hausdorff distance are non-interchangeable quantities. A positive result names the exact zero set, domain, norm, direction, units, theorem assumptions, coverage witness, and arithmetic authority. Unsupported fields, hidden components, tangencies, trims, topology ambiguity, exhausted budgets, non-finite arithmetic, or cancellation return typed Unknown or Refused and never promote estimates. ACCEPTANCE: No generic closure can manufacture geometric authority. Every allocation and evaluation is admitted before use; cancellation drains and publishes no partial certificate. Certified directed distances enclose independent analytic oracles in both directions and combine into Hausdorff authority only when both coverage obligations close. Historical estimate artifacts remain replayable with explicit no-claim semantics and cannot be silently relabeled. TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property tests cover field-kind and unit mismatches, missing/invalid metric witnesses, center/radius/config boundaries, checked size arithmetic, hidden components, exact SDF versus scaled fields, min/max CSG, extreme and non-finite values, outward-rounding containment, and deterministic ties. G1 manufactured sphere/torus/ellipsoid and multi-patch convergence verifies directed-distance orders. G2 trimmed CAD, thin-feature, non-star-shaped, disconnected, tangent, self-intersecting, and mixed-chart zoos. G3 rigid transforms, parameterization, unit rescaling, chart refinement, equivalent field representation, and route round trips. G4 cancellation and cap exhaustion at every projection/assembly/solve/probe/subdivision/finalization boundary with no leak or partial authority. G5 two-ISA and thread-count replay. Mutation tests remove each assumption, coverage, rounding, budget, and authority guard. A real no-mock E2E runs NURBS to admitted field to refit to continuum checker to ledger/package/checker replay. Bounded schema-versioned logs retain field/source identity, units/domain/norm, assumptions and witnesses, budgets and consumption, sample/subdivision coverage, directed bounds, arithmetic mode, cancellation/drain/finalization, theorem/verifier versions, and explicit authority/no-claim state.

DIRECTED-DISTANCE PRECISION: Treat source-to-spline and spline-to-source obligations as separate exhaustive optimization problems with independently retained coverage trees, witnesses, norms, units, and outward-rounded bounds. Do not infer either direction from field residual or the other direction. A Hausdorff result is the maximum of two admitted directed bounds only when both refer to exactly the same source set, fitted surface, ambient metric, closed-domain policy, and authority context. Include independently checked analytic and adversarial examples where one directed distance is small and the other large.

## Success Criteria

Complete only after all three children close with retained artifacts; generic closures and sampled residuals remain unable to mint geometric authority; both directed coverage obligations close before Hausdorff promotion; historical estimate artifacts stay replayable under explicit no-claim semantics; and the terminal checker/E2E child passes admitted and adversarial cases.
design: ROLLUP ONLY. Preserve the complete typed-field, continuum-certification, cancellation, identity, historical-replay, testing, and no-claim contract in this parent. title: fs-rep-nurbs closest/SDF: restore certified rational-surface distance, sign, and field authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The current NURBS closest-point and NURBS-to-SDF implementation has been correctly downgraded to measured DistanceBracketEstimate and NumericalCertificate::Estimate. Its historical certificate-like result was unsound: HULL_EPS is a fixed heuristic in ordinary f64; rational projection, AABB and norm arithmetic are not outward-rounded; patch-center and dense-grid probes are witnesses rather than exhaustive coverage; trimmed kept regions and trim boundaries are not globally covered; shell orientation does not by itself prove inside/outside sign; finite subdivision caps can leave unsearched boxes. Dense sampling can make the implementation useful, but it cannot authorize an enclosure, Hausdorff claim, exact SDF claim, or global 1-Lipschitz field. Users need the measured lane to remain available while a separate fail-closed certifying lane restores the intended world-class authority.

SCOPE AND MATHEMATICAL DESIGN: Build a typed, per-query rational-surface distance certifier on fs-ivl interval/affine/Taylor arithmetic. Convert each admitted knot span to a canonical homogeneous rational Bezier patch or prove an equivalent partition. Require finite strictly positive weights, bound homogeneous numerators and weight denominator outward, and perform directed interval division; retain all conversion, knot, trim, and arithmetic identities. Use coverage-complete branch-and-bound over compact parameter cells. Lower bounds must enclose distance from the query to every point in each remaining rational patch cell (starting with outward Euclidean control-hull/AABB bounds and admitting sharper convex/Taylor bounds only when checked). Upper bounds must come from an actually evaluated, admitted kept-region point with outward-rounded surface and norm evaluation. Refine with interval Newton/Krawczyk stationary-point tests and boundary/trim solvers without treating their failure as exclusion. Deterministically account for patch interiors, ordinary boundaries, corners, trim curves, trim intersections, degenerate spans, and ties. Termination returns Certified only when the retained global lower and witness upper bounds meet the requested metric error budget; exhaustion, uncertain trim classification, nonpositive weight intervals, nonfinite arithmetic, singular parameterization, or unsupported topology returns typed Unknown/Refused with the best measured evidence kept separate.

SIGN AND FIELD AUTHORITY: Separate unsigned distance enclosure, locally oriented sign estimate, globally certified inside/outside sign, and uniform field-chart authority. A signed result requires an admitted closed-shell topology and orientation receipt plus a coverage-complete, degeneracy-aware winding/ray/parity or equivalent topological predicate whose own interval/exact-predicate assumptions are independently checked. Points on or inseparable from the boundary return a three-valued boundary/Unknown classification. Do not promote pointwise distance queries into a globally certified SDF chart or NumericalCertificate::Enclosure unless a declared spatial domain has exhaustive coverage, a uniform error theorem, continuity and sign obligations, and an independently checked Lipschitz bound. Exact distance is 1-Lipschitz mathematically, but an approximate evaluator does not inherit that claim without a proved uniform evaluator error model. Preserve the current estimated signed/unsigned chart names and Estimate/no-Lipschitz semantics as the low-cost fallback.

EXECUTION, IDENTITY, AND CANCELLATION: Thread explicit Cx and admitted work, evaluation, subdivision, memory, error, deadline, capability, and output budgets through conversion, trim classification, heap/frontier growth, interval evaluation, Newton/Krawczyk, sign classification, checking, and publication. Check all size arithmetic and reserve before allocation; bound queue and transcript growth; poll at deterministic tile/cell boundaries; implement request -> drain -> finalize; never publish partial authority after cancellation or panic. Key deterministic ordering by semantic patch/span/trim-cell identity rather than worker order. Bind source WireContentId, ProblemSemanticId, query/domain/norm/units, orientation/topology/trim receipts, arithmetic mode, tolerances, budgets, algorithm/checker versions, ISA/mode, and all no-claim reasons into content-addressed ledger artifacts. Crosswalk this artifact into the refit directed-distance/Hausdorff successor without conflating the two directions.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) No heuristic epsilon or dense sample can produce Certified authority. (2) Certified point-distance intervals contain independent analytic or high-precision oracles and contract monotonically under admitted refinement. (3) Every kept patch/trim cell contributes a retained coverage/exclusion/witness node so an independent checker can replay the global minimum proof. (4) Signed results are impossible without closed-shell, orientation, and inside/outside receipts; open, self-intersecting, nonmanifold, inconsistently oriented, or uncertain shells remain unsigned/Unknown. (5) The measured legacy lane remains behaviorally available and unmistakably lower-authority. (6) Production and an independently structured checker agree on every retained proof object, while checker disagreement demotes authority rather than averaging results. (7) A real no-mock NURBS -> closest-distance -> signed/unsigned field -> ledger/package -> independent replay pipeline succeeds on admitted fixtures and fails closed on adversaries.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property tests cover homogeneous projection, positive-weight interval division, outward AABB/norm containment, exact point/line/plane/sphere cases, trim polarity, boundary three-valued logic, invalid weights/knots/domains, NaN/infinity/subnormal/extreme scales, deterministic ties, units, and typed authority transitions.
