title: P0 NURBS measured lanes: admit validation, allocations, retained bytes, and validate-once caches
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The hardened KnotVector basis path prices its own live scan, but public NurbsCurve, NurbsSurface, TrimLoop, conversion, closest, SDF, ray, and refit wrappers can still validate mutable structure before operation admission. Caller-mutable knot/control storage permits repeated scans before the advertised cap, and conversion, refit, frontier, and table allocations remain incompletely covered by aggregate retained-byte accounting. This creates denial-of-service, cancellation-latency, stale-validation, and validate-many performance risks.

REPRESENTATION AND TOKEN INVARIANT: Replace publicly mutable representation fields with private sealed storage constructed only through checked constructors and generation-checked mutators, or immutable admitted snapshots. A validation token or admitted view must borrow or otherwise bind the exact immutable generation and cannot outlive or survive mutation. Any mutator performs checked structural admission, advances the generation, and invalidates prior tokens before exposing new state. A content hash may identify bytes for provenance but MUST NOT substitute for structural validation, generation authority, or validate-once safety; there is no recompute-at-every-boundary escape hatch. Safe APIs make stale-token use unrepresentable or return a typed stale-generation refusal.

OWNED PRIMITIVE SUBSTRATE: Introduce a cheap checked structure-work estimator and opaque admitted views for knot vectors, curves, surfaces, trim loops, and Bezier data. Enforce knot/control/degree/table/frontier/output work and aggregate retained bytes before the first full scan or primitive allocation. Reuse one validated generation through basis, evaluation, partials, knot conversion, span boxes, and primitive closest/SDF/refit/ray kernels so nested helpers do not rescan. Replace primitive conversion/refit/frontier/table collect, clone, and capacity growth with checked products and fallible reservation. Expose Cx-aware primitive entry points and typed work, memory, evaluation, subdivision, poll, deadline, capability, and output lease seams while retaining hard defensive ceilings.

ORCHESTRATION OWNERSHIP: This leaf owns sealed representation generations, admitted views, primitive allocation/work estimates, and the cancellation/budget hooks required by consumers. It does not duplicate end-to-end orchestration. ShellSdf query composition, checkpointing, trim/sign traversal, and Chart publication belong to sj31i.59; certified closest/SDF authority belongs to sj31i.57; refit orchestration and field/error authority belong to sj31i.53; render ray isolation, tail exclusion, hit/normal authority, and scene publication belong to sj31i.60. Those leaves must consume this substrate and prove that one caller context and affine budgets traverse their whole workflow.

AUTHORITY BOUNDARY: This leaf proves representation well-formedness and measured-lane primitive execution safety only. It cannot promote heuristic closest, SDF, refit, or ray results to Certified. Keep geometry, topology, distance, sign, convergence, replay identity, and authenticated authority separate.

TESTS AND ACCEPTANCE: No safe public primitive performs an unadmitted full scan, and no primitive allocation occurs before aggregate byte admission. A million-span curve, million-control surface, many tiny loops, huge degree, overflowed products, allocator refusal, stale generation, and mutation during a borrowed admitted view fail deterministically without panic or long preflight. G0 covers empty/min/max forms, checked arithmetic, constructor/mutator invariants, generation invalidation, allocation failure, and deterministic error order. Compile-fail or equivalent API tests prove fields cannot be mutated around validation. G3 covers equivalent knot insertion, degree elevation, reparameterization, and admitted-view versus independent validation. G4 cancels at primitive validation, mutation admission, conversion, allocation, assembly, solve, and probe boundaries with bounded latency and no partial primitive artifact. G5 replays generation and primitive scheduling. A real no-mock curve-to-admitted-Bezier-to-primitive closest/SDF/refit handoff test emits bounded schema-versioned logs for source/generation, structure counts, primitive budgets/consumption, allocation stages, cancellation/drain/finalize, downstream obligation handoffs, and explicit no-claim state.

title: P0 ShellSdfChart: explicit Cx and bounded cancellation through closest, trim, and sign work
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: ShellSdf and its Chart adapter can execute expensive Bezier conversion, closest-point subdivision, trim classification, polishing, regular-witness sign fallback, and tile publication without carrying the caller Cx through every nested operation. Static caps cannot honor request cancellation, deadlines, shared quotas, or request-drain-finalize semantics. A renderer or simulation can continue expensive NURBS work after cancellation and may publish an apparently complete sample from a cancelled request.

SCOPE: Define Cx-aware ShellSdf query and Chart evaluation APIs with explicit work, memory, evaluation, subdivision, trim, sign, poll, deadline, capability, and output budgets. Consume the sealed admitted primitive substrate from sj31i.58 and thread one context through conversion, queue/frontier orchestration, exact trim refinement, Gauss-Newton polish, sign witnesses, certificate/no-claim assembly, tile quantization, logging, and publication. Poll at deterministic structure/cell/tile boundaries with a documented maximum latency. Cancellation performs request, drain, then finalize. Diagnostic partial work may be retained only as a typed non-authoritative cancelled artifact, never a completed ChartSample. Keep the current Estimate and no-Lipschitz scientific boundary.

CHECKPOINT AND RESUME AUTHORITY: Choose and document exactly one public policy. Under restart-only semantics, expose no resumable checkpoint authority and return a typed Unsupported or Refused result for resume attempts. Under resumable semantics, define a sealed schema-versioned ShellSdfCheckpoint binding source identity and admitted generation, query/units, algorithm/work/poll/schema versions, deterministic complete frontier state, best witness and trim/sign state, RNG streams if any, execution manifest, consumed/remaining non-reissuable budgets, and authority/no-claim disposition. Resume rejects stale generations, mismatched policies, noncanonical/truncated state, duplicated leases, and replenished budgets. Checkpoint creation/resume are budgeted, cancellable, content-addressed, independently validated, and cannot strengthen uninterrupted authority.

DEPENDENCY INTENT: Implement after sj31i.58 so orchestration cannot hide unadmitted primitive scans or allocations. This execution leaf precedes the separate rational-distance/sign certifier.

TESTS AND ACCEPTANCE: Pre-cancel and mid-flight cancellation at conversion, per-patch search, queue split, trim validation, exact subdivision, polish, sign witness, tile storage, and final publication returns typed Cancelled within the declared bound. If resumable semantics are selected, also inject cancellation/faults at checkpoint serialization and resume admission and prove interrupted/resumed output and receipts equal uninterrupted execution. If restart-only is selected, API/type tests prove checkpoint authority is absent and resume requests receive the documented typed refusal without hidden retained state. No leaked task, arena, frontier, lease, or authoritative partial sample; poll/work quotas cannot be reissued. G0 verifies budget units, deterministic boundary order, and the selected policy schema. G3 covers valid resume equivalence or restart-only semantic equivalence. G4 runs cancellation storms, allocator/deadline faults, malformed trim/surface state, and checkpoint mutation/replay attacks when applicable. G5 verifies results, frontier order, identities, and logs. A real no-mock E2E drives renderer Chart evaluation through a trimmed shell and logs source/generation, stage, cell/tile, selected checkpoint policy and identity if any, admitted/consumed/remaining budgets, request/drain/finalize, terminal reason, and no-claim authority.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the frozen closest-sdf ShellSdf fixture in tests/e2e/nurbs_authority.toml, request cancellation separately during conversion, closest-point subdivision, trim classification, polish, sign fallback, and tile publication, then attempt the declared restart/resume policy. The pre-repair path does not carry one caller Cx and bounded budgets through every nested operation, so continued work or an authoritative partial sample is the seeded failure. Retain request/poll/drain/finalize and resource-accounting evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is controlling and preserves the complete close gate.

title: P0 fs-render NURBS rays: certified exclusion, caller budgets, and finite typed intersection outcomes
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND CURRENT BASELINE: The legacy ray path now types malformed geometry/settings, resource refusal, cancellation, and bounded Newton exhaustion. Finite scale-safe norms and a dimensionless column-normalized Jacobian prevent parameter-domain or ray-direction scaling from manufacturing convergence or NaN normals, and heuristic exhaustion returns IterationLimit rather than impersonating a miss. The baseline still uses a fixed seed grid, bounded starts and iterations, hard process ceilings, and no coverage-complete exclusion theorem. Result<Option<Hit>> may reserve None only for a proved miss.

SCOPE: Replace fixed legacy admission with caller-owned work, memory, evaluation, iteration, error, poll, deadline, capability, and output budgets plus bounded top-k seed/frontier storage. Reuse the immutable admitted Bezier generation from sj31i.58. Add certified rational-Bezier ray isolation or clipping over every patch/span and trim domain, including boundaries, seams, tangencies, repeated roots, singular parameterizations, and parameter endpoints. Fast Newton remains a witness and refinement accelerator, never exclusion authority.

FINITE AND INFINITE RAY DOMAIN: Every query declares a finite admitted positive-ray interval with units, or separately supplies a checker-recognized tail certificate proving exclusion beyond a finite cutoff. A clean miss requires a coverage-complete exclusion tree over the finite interval plus any required tail certificate. Bounded search over an arbitrarily truncated interval must return a typed interval-local result, never a global miss. If finite extent, compact support, bounding volume, asymptotic behavior, or tail exclusion cannot be certified, return Inconclusive, IterationLimit, or Refused.

HIT AND NORMAL AUTHORITY: A hit retains an independently checkable existence/localization witness for patch/span/trim provenance, world-space point enclosure, positive ray-parameter enclosure, and residual bound. Unique smooth normals are optional stronger evidence, not a universal precondition for geometric intersection. At seams, creases, trim boundaries, singular parameterizations, or other nonsmooth loci, return a typed HitWithNormalCone, HitWithoutUniqueNormal, or equivalent set-valued normal authority. Separate intersection truth from shading/renderability: downstream renderers must explicitly accept a normal policy, choose a conservative set-valued treatment, or refuse the sample, and no arbitrary fallback normal may masquerade as certified geometry.

TESTS AND ACCEPTANCE: Malformed input, invalid configuration, ResourceLimit, WorkLimit, ResourceExhausted, Cancelled, NumericalFailure, Inconclusive, interval-local miss, certified global miss, smooth certified hit, and nonsmooth hit remain distinct. No NaN or infinite hit/normal is constructible. G0 covers finite gates, empty/zero/subnormal/extreme directions, finite interval and tail admission, checked products, allocation failure, singular Jacobians, deterministic ties, exact linear patches, and normal-cone semantics. G1/G2 cover plane, sphere, cylinder, bounded CAD, trimmed/tangent/grazing/multiple-root and seam/crease fixtures. G3 covers knot-domain scaling through at least 1e15, ray-direction scaling through 1e300, rigid transform, unit rescaling, exact knot insertion, patch subdivision, equivalent parameterizations, and finite-cutoff plus tail equivalence. G4 exhausts or cancels every seed, isolation, Newton, checker, tail, and publication boundary with no false miss or hit. G5 replays bit-stably. A no-mock mixed Chart/NURBS/mesh scene proves fail-closed downstream renderability. Logs retain source/generation, patch/span/trim IDs, ray interval and units, tail authority, budgets, isolation cells, residual/conditioning bounds, hit/normal or exclusion disposition, cancellation, checker result, and no-claim state.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the frozen legacy fixture in tests/e2e/conformance/lumen.toml and run the mixed-chart NURBS-ray negative case with a trimmed tangent or repeated-root surface, a finite local ray interval lacking tail proof, and a tight caller budget. The pre-repair route can exhaust its fixed seed/Newton search without coverage-complete exclusion and cannot express the required certified-miss versus interval-local/inconclusive distinction. Retain source, fixture, budgets, result, and first divergence.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is controlling and preserves the complete close gate.

If this Bead owns the harness, freeze its repository-relative script path, CLI modes and case IDs, fixtures, exit classes, source closure, artifact roots, and DSR gate.

Replay input is read-only and replay output is fresh and disjoint. Refuse overlap, traversal, symlink escape, missing inputs, wrong source/schema/identity, tampering, and unknown versions before publication.

Replay independently recomputes the declared semantic projection, preserves the first divergence, and never reruns timing to verify a retained performance observation. Any fresh timing run is a separate measurement with separate authority.

## Exact LUMEN terminal contribution

The sole terminal owner is frankensim-epic-lumen-qfx.7, which already hard-depends on this leaf. title: fs-diffreal-e2e: enforce one non-reissuable invocation budget across nested scientific stages
description:
ROOT CAUSE: stage_as_built_loop passes one Cx through registration, as-built comparison, Belief construction, colored assimilation, and redundant misfit calls, but lower-layer WorkProgress values reconstruct the full ambient poll quota. Outer checkpoints consume no shared allowance. One reported quota can therefore be reissued at each seam, while heterogeneous resource fields are treated as if they shared one counter model.

TYPED BUDGET ALGEBRA: Introduce a sealed invocation admission and ledger whose resource kinds cannot be confused or cloned. Work units, poll opportunities, monetary or energy cost, and evaluation counts are affine consumables. Memory is a reservation lease with current, peak, and retained bytes; child leases may be nested but cannot double-reserve or outlive the parent. Output is bounded capacity charged on retained publication. Deadline is an absolute monotonic horizon checked through a deterministic clock abstraction, not a decrementing copyable counter. Accuracy/error is an obligation or tolerance contract, not spendable work. Capability is authority, not capacity. Child slices are non-cloneable affine leases with unique IDs; unused consumables and released memory may return exactly once to the parent, while spent amounts and elapsed time never replenish. Checked conservation equations and dimensional types prevent cross-kind transfer, duplication, overflow, and negative remaining values.

EXECUTION SCOPE: Preflight the complete cross-crate work, memory, deadline, poll, cost, evaluation, and output shape. Pass capability-scoped child leases to fs-asbuilt and fs-assimilate and use the shared-poll API or typed successor. Remove duplicate misfit traversals because the returned posterior retains before/after values. Charge setup, canonicalization, formatting/log construction, identity hashing, checkpointing if any, and final publication. Retain exact admitted, reserved, consumed, released, returned, peak, remaining, phase, child, and terminal receipts. Raw counters are diagnostics only. Cancellation is request, drain, finalize with no acceptance-capable partial StageLog.

TESTS: G0 exact-boundary and one-below values for every resource kind and child seam; zero and already-expired deadlines under a deterministic clock; memory lease nesting, release, peak and retained bytes; output capacity; cost/work/poll overflow; duplicated, stale, overclaiming, double-return, or post-parent child leases; dimension mismatch; and deterministic error ordering. G3 equivalent legal decompositions conserve the same totals and units. G4 injects cancellation, timeout, allocation failure, and faults at every phase and final publication, proving no task, arena, memory lease, or authority leak. G5 replays numeric results, identities, and ordered receipts across thread counts. Add a production no-mock E2E script with bounded structured logs naming invocation and child IDs, resource kinds/units, admitted/reserved/consumed/released/returned/peak values, deadline observations, cancellation/drain/finalize, and disposition.

ACCEPTANCE: no budget unit can be consumed, reserved, returned, or reissued contrary to its algebra anywhere in the complete stage. Exact-boundary success and one-below refusal are deterministic, nested APIs cannot recreate ambient authority, memory peaks and retained output are honest, and the retained report describes exactly the transaction runtime enforced.

title: fs-oed-e2e: canonicalize once and make EVPI action work and allocation accounting exact

title: fs-assimilate correlated batches: stable whitening or block factor updates with joint receipts
description:
PURPOSE AND DEPENDENCY INTENT: Preserve and complete the correlated-observation scope split out of sj31i.37 so the independent O(n^2) scalar root fix is not unnecessarily blocked. This leaf starts only after sj31i.37 provides a certified deterministic factor-update substrate and sj31i.16 provides explicit calibration and registration covariance groups. The split changes scheduling, not ambition or functionality.

SCOPE: model correlated observation blocks with declared covariance, units, source identity, grouping semantics, and authority. Admit each block with tri-state PSD certification and fail closed on unresolved covariance. Implement stable deterministic whitening, block square-root information filtering, or block QR without forming avoidable normal equations or dense I-KH products. Canonicalize block order, pivot and factor signs, rank decisions, and tie breaks. Propagate joint calibration and registration uncertainty exactly according to the declared model. Produce source-bound receipts for posterior covariance, Loewner contraction, innovation/misfit, rank, factor residual, conditioning, consumed work/memory/poll/deadline budgets, and explicit Certified, Refuted, or Unresolved dispositions. Use checked work algebra, aggregate fallible scratch allocation, bounded cancellation tiles, request-drain-finalize, and non-authoritative partial diagnostics only.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY: Whitening or a successful factorization is not by itself proof that the covariance model is correct. Separate numerical validity, statistical-model assumptions, provenance, and authenticated authority. Do not silently diagonalize, tolerance-clamp negative curvature, invent independence, or promote an unresolved rank decision.

TESTS AND EVIDENCE: G0 covers 1x1 equivalence to the scalar path, exact singular PSD blocks, indefinite and interval-unresolved blocks, unit/dimension mismatch, duplicate group membership, checked arithmetic, allocator refusal, and deterministic error precedence. G1/G2 cover manufactured jointly Gaussian updates and canonical correlated-sensor benchmarks. G3 covers block permutation under the declared policy, equivalent whitening/factor representations, unit rescaling, splitting and recombining independent blocks, and comparison with a high-precision or dense independent oracle. G4 injects cancellation, deadline, quota, and allocation failure at admission, factorization, solve, covariance update, receipt construction, and publication, proving no leak or partial authority. G5 replays identities and numerical outputs across thread counts and supported ISAs. Add a real no-mock multi-sensor assimilation E2E with structured logs for group/source IDs, units, covariance certificate, factor method, rank/conditioning bounds, admitted and consumed budgets, contraction and misfit receipts, cancellation/drain/finalize, and no-claim state.

ACCEPTANCE: correlated and block updates are stable, budgeted, deterministic, jointly source-aware, independently checked, and never reuse scalar independence assumptions. The 1x1 specialization agrees with sj31i.37, and every advertised joint contraction has executable evidence or an honest unresolved/refused result.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is controlling and preserves the complete close gate.
acceptance_criteria:
## Terminal E2E ownership

Name exactly one retained, no-mock terminal harness and its owning Bead.

If this Bead owns the harness, freeze its repository-relative script path, CLI modes and case IDs, fixtures, exit classes, source closure, artifact roots, and DSR gate.

If another Bead owns it, name that exact Bead and dependency. This leaf emits a typed contribution only and cannot self-promote.

Do not create one script per scientific leaf when a shared runner is authoritative.

title: fs-qty: reject exponent narrowing traps and nonfinite literals
description: ROOT CAUSE: fs-qty parses unit exponents into i8 before enforcing the public absolute-exponent cap. The value -128 reaches i8::MIN.abs(), which panics in checked builds and may evade the cap in optimized builds. Quantity parsing and scaling also admit nonfinite values such as 1e999m and overflowed prefix products into authoritative Qty/IR paths. SCOPE: accumulate exponents in a wider checked integer, enforce every intermediate and final cap before narrowing, reject nonfinite raw/scaled/affine/final values, and preserve precise parse offsets. TESTS: m^-128, Pa^127, repeated positive/negative products and divisions, exact cap/cap+1, 1e999, 1e999m, 1e308TW, prefix overflow, debug/release no-panic, and IR defensive refusal. ACCEPTANCE: no textual quantity can panic, wrap, saturate, or produce a nonfinite authoritative value; valid boundary exponents remain deterministic.
close_reason: Fixed and independently re-reviewed; strict remote fs-qty test suite passes

title: Skip SELL padding in chunk-major SpMV

title: grand_piano: hammer stiffness is split across the unison instead of applied per string (3-string hammers 3x too soft); published per-note dissipation ignored
description:
Found 2026-09-24 by a read-only audit from the music_theory_data_tool side. Full audit: /data/tmp/piano-realism/FRANKENSIM_DATA_AUDIT.md (local, not committed).

Chabassier, Chaigne and Joly's grand-piano model (M2AN 2014, eq. 3.8; the same source steinway_scale.rs cites for its string table) applies the hammer felt law to EACH string of a unison. crates/fs-couple/examples/grand_piano/ divides that stiffness across the unison, so a three-string note's hammer is about 3x too soft. That lengthens the contact time and darkens the attack for most of the keyboard. The per-note hammer dissipation values published with the same table are also not used.

Fix: apply K and p per string as in eq. 3.8, and take the dissipation from the published per-note table.
Acceptance: a test that pins contact duration for a 3-string note against the published law; before and after renders of A4 with contact time and a spectral-centroid change reported.

title: fs-airflow conjugate watt gate: absolute tolerance is scale-dependent; relaxation config under-validated
description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified at HEAD 55e00412 by post-landing review of the f85xj.5.7 slice): admit_converged (crates/fs-airflow/src/conjugate.rs:932-950) compares max_region_imbalance_w against the ABSOLUTE balance_tolerance_w (default 1e-6 W, conjugate.rs:467/477) with no scale reference anywhere. The gate's sensitivity therefore scales with problem wattage in both failure directions:

(a) FALSE PASS at small scale: the exact dropped-face fault the gate exists to catch (the HIGH-2 fixture: states[2].heat_rate_w *= 0.5) produces imbalance ~2.5e-7 W when the lumped fixture runs at power_w = 2e-6 W instead of 45 W, and the mis-wired run RETURNS Ok. Existing tests only exercise 1.2-45 W.
(b) FALSE REFUSAL at large scale: at 10 kW-class solves, fp noise in FEM heat-rate integration can exceed 1e-6 W.
(c) INTERACTION with the absent unit guard (f85xj.11.7): a mW-vs-W mistake shrinks the signal and the gate's sensitivity together by 1000x, making the gate vacuous exactly when the input is wrong.

SECONDARY (same review, same seam):
(d) Relaxation::Fixed omega is only finite-checked (conjugate.rs:1002-1004): omega=0.0 is admitted and guarantees a stall that burns max_iterations of solid solves before being misattributed as ConjugateNotConverged; negative/huge omega admitted; Aitken omega_init may be negative. The post-relaxation reference vector is never finiteness-checked before the next solid() call (conjugate.rs:738-740), so an overflow is first refused deep in the callback and misattributed to the solid.
(e) from_robin_flux (conjugate.rs:416-423) drops RobinFlux::mean_reference_temperature_k and mean_htc_w_per_m2_k, forfeiting a free K-denominated wiring cross-check that fs-conduction already returns (solve.rs:354-366); a reference-vector wiring error within hA*tol_W currently passes the watt gate.

PRESCRIBED FIX: hybrid gate imbalance <= max(balance_tolerance_w, balance_rel_tolerance * scale) with scale = max over regions of |heat_rate_w| from the SAME response (keep the absolute floor for the all-zero-power edge); admit omega only in a declared positive range and finiteness-check the relaxed reference with a config-attributed refusal; thread the returned mean reference temperature into the response gate and refuse when it disagrees with the sent reference beyond hA-scaled tolerance.

DONE WHEN: (1) the 2e-6 W dropped-face scenario above is a test and REFUSES; (2) omega=0.0 refuses at admission with a config-attributed diagnostic, not ConjugateNotConverged; (3) the existing conjugate test battery (29 integration + 7 e2e + 3 module at time of filing) still passes; (4) the CONTRACT names the gate's scale semantics and the relaxation admission range. NOTE the DONE-WHEN inputs are the gate's ACTUAL inputs (region heat rates, config omega) - do not gate on axes the formula never reads.

NO-CLAIM: this bead does not add the fs-conduction table-ingest unit guard (f85xj.11.7 owns that); it does not measure convergence rates or add divergence detection (informational-only in the review).

Filed from a five-lane post-landing review; the same review re-verified CoralMeadow's HIGH 1/2/3/5 as genuinely fixed and found no defect in the exponential segment law or the downstream-weighted restriction (independently re-derived).
close_reason: Implemented at c9d98f93. Hybrid gate: admitted imbalance = max(balance_tolerance_w, balance_relative_tolerance * scale), scale = max_j max(|Q_solid,j|,|Q_air,j|) from the judged response; defaults 1e-12 W floor + 1e-6 relative; refusal reports the effective threshold. DONE-WHEN discharge: (1) the 2e-6 W dropped-face scenario is test the_watt_gate_scales_with_the_interface_not_an_absolute_constant and REFUSES, with an in-test assertion that its signal (~2.5e-7 W) sits under the old 1e-6 W absolute gate; (2) omega=0.0 (and -0.5, 2.5, Aitken omega_init 0/over-cap) refuse at admission as InvalidConjugateInput 'conjugate relaxation omega', pinned by inert_and_oversized_relaxation_factors_refuse_at_admission; (3) full battery green - strict remote cargo test -p fs-airflow on vmi1153651 exit 0, 35/35 conjugate (30 pre-existing + 5 new), 6/6 live conjugate_e2e; (4) CONTRACT documents hybrid-gate scale semantics, relaxation admission ranges, the optional reference-wiring claim, and transfer NaN-poisoning. Also landed from the prescribed-fix list: relaxation-overflow attribution (NonFiniteCoupling at 'relaxed reference temperature', test-pinned) and the mean_reference_temperature_k cross-check threaded from RobinFlux (Some held to the sent reference within 1e-9 relative kelvin; None documented no-claim; from_robin_flux always claims so the conduction e2e exercises it live). Relative-term liveness proven by admitting a 45 W fixed point over a deliberate 1e-300 absolute floor. Local pinned-toolchain clippy: zero fs-airflow diagnostics; remaining lane reds are pre-existing go7a-class drift lints in fs-substrate/fs-rand/fs-sparse/fs-alloc, untouched here. UBS on changed files: no patch-specific true positive (test panic arms + entry-arity-checked indexing).

title: fs-airflow claim-integrity: fan-law cited to a test-method standard, a determinism test that asserts no determinism, and a tolerance band no parameter setting produces
description:
Three defects found while auditing f85xj.5.5 against HEAD, separate from the
provenance-hash falsifier filed alongside this.

(1) NORMATIVE CITATION POINTS AT THE WRONG STANDARD.
FAN_LAW_SOURCE_IDENTIFIER = "ANSI/AMCA 210-25; ANSI/ASHRAE 51-25"
(src/lib.rs:27-28) is the retained justification for the s / s^2 affinity
scaling (src/lib.rs:868-871, echoed at CONTRACT.md:174). AMCA 210 / ASHRAE 51 is
the joint LABORATORY TEST-METHOD standard ("Laboratory Methods of Testing Fans
for Certified Aerodynamic Performance Rating") — chambers, nozzles,
instrumentation. It is not the normative source of the fan/affinity laws, which
belong to AMCA Publication 201 / the AMCA Fan Application Manual and the ASHRAE
Handbook. 210/51 applies speed and density conversion only incidentally, to
reduce measured data to a specified speed and standard air. Same shape as the
fs-convection mis-citation filed in the sibling bead.
Secondary: the "-25" suffix implies a 2025 edition that could not be confirmed
(attestable editions are -16, -07, -99) — verify rather than assume fabricated.
Tertiary: the string is a bare designator with no clause, section or table, so a
reviewer cannot check it from the artifact — while every LossElement and
FanCurve is REQUIRED to carry a structured SourceProvenance. The crate's one
normative citation is held to a lower standard than its data.

(2) A TEST NAMED FOR DETERMINISM THAT ASSERTS NO DETERMINISM.
three_speed_points_follow_affinity_and_solve_deterministically
(tests/conformance.rs:152-168) runs three DIFFERENT inputs once each and asserts
only flows[0] < flows[1] < flows[2] (line 167). It does not repeat a solve, does
not compare bits or hashes, does not vary thread count. The name is the only
determinism claim in it. This is how f85xj.5.5's fourth DONE-WHEN ("network
solve deterministic across thread counts") reads as covered when nothing covers
it: grep across the crate for thread|rayon|spawn|available_parallelism returns
zero code hits.

(3) THE REPORTED PRESSURE BAND IS NOT AN OPERATING POINT OF ANY CURVE.
src/lib.rs:905-906 computes pressure_low = resistance_low * low_flow * low_flow,
but low_flow was solved against resistance_HIGH (src/lib.rs:859). Mixing the low
resistance with the high-resistance root yields a band no consistent parameter
setting produces. It errs WIDE, so the ordering assertions still hold and no
test catches it — which is exactly why it needs a test rather than a reading.

DONE WHEN: (1) the fan-law claim cites a source that contains the fan laws, with
a locator; (2) the test is renamed to what it proves AND a real determinism
artifact exists (repeat-run identity at minimum; thread-count invariance if the
DONE-WHEN is to be met at all); (3) each tolerance corner pairs the resistance
it was solved against, with a test that fails on the mixed pairing.

NOTE ON (3): confirm the intended semantics before changing it. A deliberately
conservative outer envelope is a defensible choice — but then it must SAY it is
an envelope, not present itself as the tolerance band.

Found by audit during f85xj.5.5 close review (NobleLion, 2026-07-25). Not fixed
in that pass because fs-airflow was assigned to another agent.

title: Admit fs-io catalog schemas and unify bounded CSV/JSON projection
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The public Schema { columns: Vec<ColumnSpec> } is presently an unchecked authority input. Callers can supply an empty or enormous schema, empty or duplicate names, names whose CSV trim semantics alias, and Number bounds containing NaN/infinity or min > max. Both catalog readers then traverse that unchecked vector per row and build numeric projection maps. CatalogJsonLimits bounds parsed JSON syntax/payload, but it does not admit schema cardinality, schema-name bytes, rows-times-columns validation work, numeric projection entries/key bytes, diagnostics, or all simultaneously live output/scratch storage. The CSV path has no equivalent input/row/header/member/string/decoded/output envelope and performs infallible growth and clone-heavy materialization. Duplicate trimmed CSV headers can collapse when inserted into BTreeMap, making the selected value ambiguous. A syntactically bounded document can therefore trigger unbounded schema-driven work/memory or ambiguous projection.

MISSION
Make schema validity and the complete parse-plus-validate-plus-project resource envelope explicit, typed, deterministic, and shared across CSV and JSON. Preserve the strict JSON work already landed; do not weaken accepted functionality. Fail before authoritative work whenever declared limits cannot cover the schema or worst-case projection, and retain precise row/column/byte diagnostics without allocating attacker-sized messages.

DELIVERABLES
- Introduce a fallible admitted-schema constructor/receipt (or an equivalently sealed admitted Schema) with a versioned deterministic identity. Validate bounded nonempty column/name counts and name bytes, unique names under the exact lookup/trim normalization used by each format, and finite ordered inclusive Number bounds. Define empty-schema, optional-field, unknown-column, column-order, and duplicate-header policies explicitly. Keep raw unchecked construction from serving as authority.
- Introduce a common catalog read/projection budget that composes format syntax limits with schema-driven validation work, rows-times-columns visits, numeric conversions, numeric map entries/key bytes, retained Catalog rows/numbers, scratch, and bounded diagnostic witnesses. Use checked arithmetic and reject overflow. JSON limits must cover the whole operation rather than stop at parser output; CSV gains explicit input/header/row/field/token/decoded/aggregate caps.
- Refuse duplicate CSV headers after the documented normalization before map insertion; never silently overwrite/collapse aliases. Specify and test whether extra document columns are preserved or refused and ensure the policy is identical or intentionally documented across CSV/JSON.
- Replace avoidable cell/key/row cloning with ownership-aware projection; use try_reserve/checked growth wherever containers permit it and document unavoidable allocator no-claim boundaries. No partial authoritative Catalog may escape allocation, syntax, schema, budget, or cancellation failure.
- Return structured deterministic errors distinguishing schema-definition refusal, document syntax, document-to-schema mismatch, resource exhaustion, and allocation failure. Error witnesses must be bounded and identify the first deterministic offender.
- Bind schema identity, format/parser version, exact limits, consumed counters, input identity hook, row/member counts, and result/no-claim status into a receipt suitable for HELM/ledger promotion. Do not treat non-cryptographic local fingerprints as authority.

GAUNTLET
G0 covers empty/max/over-limit schemas; empty/duplicate/normalization-alias names; NaN, infinite, equal, inverted, and extreme finite bounds; duplicate/extra/missing headers and object members; every exact resource boundary; checked-arithmetic overflow; allocation refusal hooks; and deterministic tie/first-error behavior. G3 proves CSV/JSON semantic equivalence for the common subset, column/member permutation invariance where promised, whitespace/escape-preserving JSON rewrites, quoted-CSV rewrites, unit-rescaled numeric range cases, and identity sensitivity to every authoritative policy/limit. G4 injects denial/cancellation at every growth and projection boundary and proves no leaks, no partial Catalog/receipt, bounded diagnostics, and byte-identical retry. G5 freezes admitted-schema and receipt bytes across runs/thread counts on the supported deterministic envelope.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
The current Schema is not admitted; CatalogJsonLimits does not bound total schema-validation/projection work or output storage; parse_csv is not a resource-admitted world boundary; duplicate normalized headers and invalid numeric-bound definitions are not certified safe. The strict JSON grammar fix remains useful but does not close these authority/resource gaps.

title: Admit fenced campaign activation lease and conditional occupancy transaction
description:
Provide an authentic upstream capability for race-safe automated activation of semantic-template work waves. The current program can complete through a reviewed manual single-operator wave handoff, but routine automation must not claim global caps or exactly-once activation without a fenced campaign lease and conditional occupancy transaction.

The capability must be implemented and released in the owning br/tooling project, then independently admitted by FrankenSim conformance evidence. It is a future optimization, related to publisher Bead .1.2, and is deliberately nonblocking for the present manual program.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance field requires a fenced lease/occupancy contract, crash-safe recovery, exhaustive concurrency and fault tests, authentic released-tool E2E, deterministic redacted logs, offline replay, and strict non-authority boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
## Atomic campaign activation capability acceptance

1. Remain deferred and nonblocking for the current manual semantic-template program. Relate to frankensim-semantic-bead-template-hygiene-961yr.1.2; never become an implicit blocker through prose, version detection, or robot ranking.
2. Specify a closed capability schema for atomic campaign lease acquire, renew, fenced mutation, and owner-checked release. Bind released binary identity/version, command grammar, campaign ID/root, holder/session identity, monotonic fencing generation, exact pre/post state, expiry or recovery policy, storage/transaction scope, refusal behavior, and no-claim.
3. A lease token alone is insufficient. Every automated child activation conditionally verifies the current fencing generation, child expected state, campaign/lane/owner occupancy inputs, and activation transition in one admitted transaction or equivalent serializable protocol. Stale holder, stale occupancy, duplicate activation, over-cap selection, and owner mismatch refuse without partial mutation.
4. Crash recovery is observation-first. A successor may supersede an abandoned holder only through the admitted recovery protocol and a strictly newer fencing generation; the old holder can never release, renew, or mutate afterward. Ambiguous responses, clock uncertainty, process death, and partial transport produce typed non-success terminals with exact recovery guidance.
5. Manual wave handoffs remain supported and explicitly non-atomic. Admission of this capability enables AUTOMATED_FENCED_WAVE only after conformance passes; it does not enable automated target repair, external review authority, or any .1.3 mechanical target-apply gate.
6. Unit/schema/boundary/property/metamorphic/state tests cover zero/one/many holders, generation wrap/overflow refusal, exact cap boundaries, stale and forged tokens, wrong campaign/lane/owner, renew/release races, holder death, occupancy drift, duplicate request, ambiguous response, and deterministic retry/replay.
7. Mutation/fault/resource/cancellation/restart tests inject crashes and signals before/inside/after acquire, each conditional activation, renew, export, replay, and release; lock/database/output faults; concurrent holders; delayed stale writers; corrupted journals; and recovery takeover. No stale writer mutates and no inverse overwrites a newer state.
8. Release-built no-mock E2E uses authentic released br/tooling in a disjoint fixture with multiple processes to prove mutual exclusion, fencing after takeover, campaign/lane/owner cap preservation, exact child states, idempotent response-loss recovery, deterministic redacted terminal-last logs, and artifact-only replay with live tracker and network denied. Parser mocks cannot satisfy this gate.
9. Retain bounded schemas, argv-form commands, allowlisted result projections, generations, occupancy before/after, selected IDs, first divergence, recovery, relative artifacts, unique terminal, reproduction argv, and no-claim. Raw stdout/stderr are retained only through content roots, byte counts, redaction verdicts, and safe relative artifact paths. Exclude secrets, environment dumps, absolute paths, PIDs, scheduler timing, bulk Bead bodies, and unbounded command output.
10. Close only after upstream release identity, independent capability probe, all unit/property/concurrency/fault/E2E cases, artifact replay, and named DSR proof pass. A version string or help text alone cannot admit capability. This feature grants scheduling mechanics only, not semantic, human, target, product, or release authority.
11. The 2,880-minute planning floor is explicit: 480 minutes fenced protocol/schema + 600 unit/property/state coverage + 720 multi-holder mutation/fault/cancellation/restart coverage + 480 authentic released-tool no-mock E2E + 360 deterministic logging/offline replay + 240 independent admission review. Additional backends, recovery modes, platforms, or cap dimensions add effort; never weaken fencing or stale-writer evidence to fit the estimate.

title: Admit upstream br atomic conditional-write capability for template repair
description:
Track the optional future capability that can make automated one-target template repair mechanically no-clobber. The current released br 0.2.19 has no conditional update or compare-and-swap primitive over an observed target semantic root or revision. Ordinary br update, repeated show, advisory reservation, workspace write locking, post-hoc comparison, and unconditional inverse do not satisfy this requirement.

This Bead does not block manual br-only remediation or semantic-template program closure. It becomes actionable only when an upstream released br candidate exposes a documented atomic precondition for both forward and compensating writes. Then admit that capability through conformance evidence and wire its exact receipt into .1.3. No FrankenSim code may emulate CAS by directly editing tracker storage.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance field requires upstream capability definition, authentic conformance, race/fault E2E, detailed logging/replay, version admission, and strict no-claim.
acceptance_criteria:
## Conditional-write admission acceptance

1. Start only from an independently released upstream br artifact and immutable source/build/version identity. Help text, version thresholds, unmerged patches, mocks, ordinary workspace locks, or self-declaration cannot establish capability.
2. The admitted operation atomically compares target ID plus exact semantic field root or revision and either performs exactly the named one-field mutation or performs no mutation with a typed mismatch. The compare and write share one transaction/lock scope. Unknown fields, extra targets, partial writes, and fallback ordinary update refuse.
3. Define the same atomic precondition for compensation against the exact intended poststate. Compensation never overwrites an unknown or third-party state. Ambiguous responses have a documented idempotency/audit identity and observation-first reconciliation procedure.
4. Unit/schema/boundary/property/metamorphic/state tests cover all supported fields, zero/one/two targets, exact/mismatched roots, opaque IDs, version/schema negotiation, retry identity, failure atomicity, deterministic errors, and one-before/exact/one-after resource limits.
5. Mutation/fault/resource/cancellation/restart tests inject a third-party edit immediately before forward write, immediately after write, before compensation, during ambiguous response, and at every transaction and observation boundary. They prove no ordinary-update fallback and no inverse over unknown poststate.
6. Release-built no-mock E2E executes the authentic released operation against a disjoint real br fixture under concurrent writers, process interruption, lock failure, response loss, and restart. Current br 0.2.19 is a required negative fixture ending NoData with target identity unchanged.
7. Detailed deterministic redacted logs retain binary/version/source roots, capability probe, exact compare key, argv-form request, observed pre/post roots, an allowlisted transaction-result projection, divergence, recovery, artifacts, and terminal. Raw stdout/stderr are retained only through content roots, byte counts, redaction verdicts, and safe relative artifact paths. Artifact-only replay recomputes the admission verdict with live br and network denied.
8. .1.3 may admit the capability only through a closed versioned registry row and retained conformance receipt. A newly released version, grammar change, semantic change, or failed freshness check invalidates admission until re-proven.
9. Close only when authentic unit/race/fault/no-mock E2E/replay and configured DSR evidence pass on the released capability. This Bead enables optional automated mechanics only; it grants no review authority, target semantic correctness, implementation completion, science, product, promotion, or release authority.
10. The 2,880-minute planning floor is explicit: 480 minutes capability contract/schema + 600 unit/property/state coverage + 720 concurrency/mutation/fault/cancellation/restart coverage + 480 authentic released-tool E2E + 360 deterministic logging/offline replay + 240 independent admission review. New operations, fields, platforms, failures, or provider versions add effort; never reduce race or no-clobber evidence to fit the estimate.

5. Mutation/fault/resource/cancellation/restart tests cover unavailable provider, timeout, partial issuance, stale revocation, compromised or rotated trust material, replay, concurrent conflicting reviews, registry tamper, redaction failure, and cancellation at every verification boundary.
6. Authorized no-mock E2E uses a real isolated provider and released verifier to issue, verify, expire, revoke, rotate, refuse wrong scope, recover from interruption, and replay retained non-secret evidence. A deterministic local fixture provider may prove integration mechanics but cannot substitute for production governance or authority.
7. Detailed deterministic redacted logs retain provider and schema identities, public trust-root identity, subject and scope roots, allowlisted issuance/revocation result projections, first divergence, recovery, safe artifacts, and terminal while excluding credentials, tokens, private keys, personal data, environment values, and raw bulk payloads. 8. .1.3 may enable automated application only when both this exact-scope authority receipt and the separately admitted conditional-write capability verify. Either alone remains at most DECLARED_READY.
9. Close only after governance approval, production operations, unit/fault/authorized E2E/replay, independent review, and the configured DSR or equivalent provider proof pass. This Bead grants only the named review operation; it never proves target implementation, science, performance, product, promotion, or release.
10. The 2,400-minute planning floor is explicit: 480 minutes governance/trust/operations design + 480 receipt schema and unit/property/state coverage + 480 security/fault/cancellation/restart coverage + 480 authorized authentic-provider E2E + 240 redacted logging/offline replay + 240 independent governance/admission review. Provider, jurisdiction, privacy, rotation, or incident-response expansion adds effort; no trust or privacy control may be compressed to fit the estimate.

description: The browser CMA-ES teaching kernel used a linear generation multiplier in the h_sigma normalization, causing the denominator to become NaN and disabling covariance-path updates after a few generations. title: fs-exec parked persistent workers under Cx::scoped_cpu — recover N-D FFT attainment (27d3 follow-up)
description: MOTIVATION (measured, 27d3): per-run worker spawn overhead collapses N-D FFT attainment — every FftNd axis pass calls TilePool run (2D roundtrip = 4 pool runs, 3D = 6), respawning scoped workers each time; ts2 measured 0.011 attainment at 256x256 vs 0.11-0.13 at large sizes, and the m4 numbers show the same small-size collapse. The 27d3 N-D roofline rows ([256,256], [1024,1024], [128,128,64]) are REPORT-ONLY in crates/fs-fft/tests/perf_lane.rs for exactly this reason (floor gates assert settled claims, not aspirations). WHAT: park a persistent worker pool once per TilePool (or per session epoch) UNDER the asupersync scoped lane (TilePool::run_scoped / Cx::scoped_cpu, landed by lx0e at feb6fa8+35aef00, upstream asupersync fa371dcf) so per-run cost drops to wake/sleep instead of spawn/join, WITHOUT breaking P7 scope honesty: the parked workers must live inside a task's scope (e.g. a long-lived session task parks them; runs hand work in and out via the existing deque protocol), never as free 'static threads. The pool CONTRACT defers this alongside the lock-free deques (no-claims) — landing it must update the CONTRACT and keep the G4 storms green (drain, arena quiescence, panic containment, reuse) plus G5 bitwise determinism across lanes and worker counts. ACCEPTANCE: N-D FFT report-only rows flip to floored gates (target 0.40 BindingRoof per 27d3 spec) on both m4-pro-macos and ts2-5995wx-linux baseline stores with pre/post reprobe; small-size attainment recovers by roughly the spawn-overhead factor measured above. Prereqs all landed: 691k (upstream primitive), lx0e (scoped lane).
close_reason: DELIVERED: parked persistent workers under scoped ownership, end to end. (1) fs-exec crew capsule (crates/fs-exec/src/crew.rs, commit 950fda3): N workers park on a condvar INSIDE an owning scope and execute per-run jobs handed over as a lifetime-erased borrow — the ONE unsafe op, justified by the rayon-latch argument (dispatch blocks until the last worker clears the slot, so the borrow provably outlives every dereference); registered in unsafe-capsules.json with full SAFETY.md (invariants, aliasing, lifetimes, panic/cancellation/concurrency behavior); job panics are captured so the latch can never hang; CrewShutdown releases parked workers on unwind so the owning scope's join can never hang. xtask check-unsafe green. (2) TilePool integration (commit 9a6573e): Launch becomes a three-way strategy (own std scope / Cx::scoped_cpu task scope / parked crew) all driving the SAME worker_loop — bitwise-identical across lanes by construction; with_parked_crew parks the crew as scoped-CPU children of the CALLING task (P7: entry/exit checkpoint refusals -> CrewScopeError::Cancelled fail-closed; task cancel/budget bridges at tile boundaries via each worker's park-time CpuCx); with_parked_crew_local is the std twin for untasked callers; excess crew workers no-op on runs with fewer tiles. G4/G5: parked lane bitwise-matches std across reruns on one crew, tile-panic containment with crew survival, gate-drain with crew reuse, task-scoped crew bridges mid-run cancellation and refuses pre-cancelled tasks at entry. 95+ fs-exec tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt all green. CONTRACT no-claims updated (parked deferral delivered opt-in; Mutex deques still deferred). (3) KernelRunner trait (commit 15b2c03): TilePool and ParkedTilePool interchangeable at every call site; FftNd pooled entries generalized source-compatibly. (4) Measurement lane (commit 46a6856): fftnd sweep parks ONE crew for all rows. MEASURED RECOVERY on ts2 (5995WX, quiet): [256,256] 0.011 -> 0.0696 (6.3x — the bead's 'recovers by roughly the spawn-overhead factor' acceptance), [1024,1024] ~0.12 -> 0.4598 (CLEARS the 0.40 floor, within_band, dispersion 0.07), [128,128,64] 0.3098. GATE FLIP NOT INCLUDED, deliberately: floors assert settled claims on BOTH baseline machines, and the m4 was uncertifiable during swarm activity (attainment 0.028-0.039 at dispersion 0.24-0.34 = host-load noise; quiet-host constraint). The one-quiet-run flip is frankensim-o582; the residual small-size gap is granularity (256 pencils / 128 woken workers), tracked with a concrete tuning design as frankensim-3f6c.

(7) Measure fftnd rows m4 + ts2 with the parked path; flip report-only rows to floored 0.40 ONLY where both machines clear it with band margin — floors assert settled claims.

title: Fail closed on non-finite and ambiguous tolerance-allocation inputs
description: The ccmn OED audit found fs-toleralloc allocate admits NaN or positive-infinity feature fields because admission checks only value <= 0, does not reject duplicate names, and does not validate finite outputs. title: CAPSTONE: the vertical-slice e2e gate — one command, ledgered, rendered, replayed, in CI
description:
REFINEMENT ROUND 1 FINDING (the template's own demand: comprehensive e2e test scripts with great detailed logging): the epic's exit criterion had NO executable proof — every workstream tests itself, nothing gates the SLICE. WHAT: scripts/e2e/vertical_slice.sh in the quality-lane house style (JSONL verdict rows, tested-HEAD identity, full retained logs, named-skip/fail-closed semantics per lane doctrine): (1) runs the marquee runner end to end on the committed fixture study (fresh ledger); (2) asserts evidence-color composition in the result (at least one Verified claim, no laundering — parsed from the ledger rows); (3) invokes report --render and asserts the shaded image exists with embedded provenance matching the ledger artifact hash; (4) replays and asserts bit-identity (study hash, artifact hashes, notebook bytes); (5) runs estimate first and asserts the actual run landed within the calibrated band (once WS5-C lands; named-skip before); (6) total wall budget enforced so the gate stays runnable pre-release (~10 min class). Wired as a DSR check after the runtime sweep. Every step emits structured JSONL (step, wall_ms, verdict, evidence) so a red gate localizes in one read. ACCEPTANCE: green run recorded on both the M4 and a Threadripper via the sweep-host path; deliberate-tamper drills (corrupt one artifact; drop one Explicit) fail the exact expected step with teaching output. DEPENDS on marquee runner + same-bytes render + notebooks + estimate.

## Acceptance Criteria

SCOPE PRESERVATION, ESTIMATE, AND EXACT OWNERSHIP. Every existing CAPSTONE and cross-run-drift clause remains normative. This leaf owns planned script scripts/e2e/vertical_slice.sh, planned immutable manifest tests/e2e/vertical_slice/manifest.toml, and exactly these top-level cases: vertical_slice.capstone, vertical_slice.corrupt_artifact, vertical_slice.drop_explicit, vertical_slice.render_provenance_mismatch, vertical_slice.replay_mismatch, vertical_slice.estimate_band, and vertical_slice.cross_run_drift. The manifest lists each once with the committed fixture-study root, fresh-ledger policy, units/seed/budgets/versions/capabilities, expected stable exit class, claimed/no-claim predicates, independent checker, positive/hostile role, output caps, and repository-relative artifacts. The 1,920-minute estimate is reasoned as 360 minutes for manifest/CLI/log/self-test contract, 720 for real runner-ledger-report-render integration, 360 for independent replay/tamper/drift falsifiers, 240 for cancellation/fault/resource hardening, and 240 for dual-ISA/DSR stabilization. Existing hard prerequisites frankensim-226w, frankensim-mh2u, and frankensim-44gd remain intact; the related estimate bead is not silently promoted into a hard prerequisite.

BOUNDARY, PROPERTY, AND MUTATION TESTS. Unit/API/schema tests cover happy; empty/zero/one and minimum study; n-1/n/n+1 operations, evidence rows, artifacts, report sections, render outputs, estimate-history samples and wall/work/memory/output budgets; exact maximum; max+1 refusal before large allocation; malformed/truncated/duplicate/inconsistent/unsupported project, ledger, artifact, notebook, image metadata and replay manifest; missing each Five Explicit; unit/frame/seed/version/capability mismatch; stale source/build; non-finite/extreme metrics; deterministic enumeration/ties/first error; and every refusal. Property/metamorphic tests cover separate-command versus one-command semantic equality, ledger operation reordering only under an explicit equivalence, deterministic clean-store replay, report/notebook pack-unpack identity, artifact and rendered-provenance lineage closure, equivalent relative paths, unit-preserving input transformation, calibrated estimate/run pairing, and bounded-history window recomputation. Seeded mutations remove or alter each Explicit, evidence color/authority edge, study/artifact/image/notebook root, estimate band, drift vector, replay guard, checker, publication gate, and no-claim field; every detector has a known-broken self-test.

RELEASE NO-MOCK HAPPY AND HOSTILE JOURNEYS. scripts/e2e/vertical_slice.sh must implement/document --list, --check, --self-test, --run smoke, --run full, --negative CASE, and --replay MANIFEST_REL --input-artifact-root INPUT_ROOT, with explicit --artifact-root OUTPUT_ROOT --artifact-dir OUTPUT_REL on writes. The release-built happy path executes the real marquee CLI on the committed fixture with a fresh ledger, verifies at least one legitimately Verified claim and no evidence-color laundering, invokes report --render, independently checks image provenance against ledger content, verifies study/artifact/notebook byte identity on replay, validates estimate versus actual only when the named calibration prerequisite exists, appends and adjudicates the bounded cross-run metric history, and publishes the deterministic notebook artifact. No mock, hard-coded verdict, precomputed production result, schema-only shell, validator reused as producer, or silent skip is allowed. Named precondition absence yields typed NotRun/NO-DATA and no promoted claim.

HOSTILE, CANCELLATION, RESOURCE, AND STABLE-EXIT CONTRACT. Hostile cases corrupt one artifact, drop each Explicit, swap render provenance, mutate replay bytes, exceed/refuse an estimate band, inject unexplained drift, tamper/truncate the ledger/manifest/notebook, use stale source/checker roots, and force producer/checker disagreement or post-publication revocation; failure localizes to the exact step with ranked teaching repair. Cancellation before/during/after solve, ledger append, report, render, package, history update and publication plus parser/allocator/worker/process/I/O/durable-seal faults, panic, work/memory/deadline/output-cap exhaustion, retry and replay prove bounded polling, request-drain-finalize, exact resource return, no leaks, no partial authoritative artifact, and one terminal result. Freeze/test one stable enum and numeric mapping for Pass, UsageRefused, InputRefused, NoData, EvidenceFailed, CancelledDrained, InfrastructureFailed, and InternalFault.

INDEPENDENT REPLAY, LOGS, AND AUTHORITY. A separately implemented checker opens the ledger and immutable artifacts through a clean input root, reconstructs evidence-color composition, lineage, render metadata, notebook bytes, estimate/run pairs and drift window without trusting producer verdicts, and writes replay to a distinct root. Bounded deterministic JSONL is redacted before buffering/hashing and records schema/source/build/tool/target/features, step/case/sequence, study/ledger/artifact/image/notebook/checker roots, typed units, seeds/capabilities, admitted/consumed budgets/work/resources, expected/observed/margins, evidence authority/no-claim, first divergence, cancel/drain/finalize roots, relative outputs, ranked repairs, and a repository-relative reproduction command; secrets, absolute paths, host identity, PIDs, unbounded payloads and undeclared volatile noise are forbidden. Full closure requires green release journeys on admitted M4 and Threadripper sweep-host paths under their declared determinism contract plus exactly dsr quality --tool frankensim. Focused Cargo/RCH, dual-ISA replay, estimate calibration, scientific validity, rendering validity, and DSR are non-substitutable evidence; failure or missing preconditions remain explicit no-claim.

EXACT BOUNDARY SPELLING. The maximum+1 case is the required max+1 refusal and must fail before large allocation; it is not covered merely by a nominal maximum test.

title: WS4: cancellation-latency certification at scale — the 200us tile-boundary claim measured
description:
WHY: plan sections 5.2/9.6 promise cancellation observation at admitted tile boundaries within 200 microseconds, but that quantity has never been measured. E-racing and responsive user control depend on distinguishing prompt cooperative observation from the additional time required to drain work, return resources, finalize, and publish a terminal receipt.

WHAT: instrument the real TilePool/KernelRunner cancellation path on both reference ISA families. For deterministic randomized cancel positions during production-scale field, sparse D3Q19, and admitted level-8 elasticity workloads, retain two non-interchangeable latency distributions: request to first cancellation observation at a tile boundary, and request to fully drained/finalized terminal receipt. Also retain the two-lane concurrent-service experiment: while the throughput lane is saturated, measure catalog read, estimate, ledger point-query, and explain-lineage operations on the conversational lane.

DECISION: the advertised 200-microsecond claim applies only to request-to-first-observation p95. Drain/finalize has its own wider engineering envelope and never retroactively changes the observation result. The conversational lane retains its separate 100-millisecond target. Loaded/invalid hosts, missing poll evidence, leaked work, incomplete drain, or unavailable mandatory routes are NoData/Unqualified.

USER VALUE: logs make responsiveness diagnosable by separating queue wait, first observation, draining, resource return, finalization, and service time rather than reporting one ambiguous latency.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `scripts/ci/cancellation_latency_perf_e2e.sh --check` against `tests/perf/cancellation_latency.toml`, then the missing-poll, slow-observation/fast-drain, fast-observation/slow-drain, incomplete-drain, leaked-resource, loaded-host, timer-error, and replay-disagreement negatives. Until the planned harness exists, the claim remains `NoData`.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured `acceptance_criteria` field is the controlling, complete close gate. This navigation section does not weaken, duplicate, or replace its detailed requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
## Leaf-local verification

Unit/boundary tests cover happy, empty, zero/one/min/max, n-1/n/n+1 limits, timestamp order, timer error, non-finite/overflow, missing poll/drain/finalize, and exact typed exits. Property/metamorphic tests cover clock-offset invariance within one provider, workload partitioning, deterministic injection identity, quantile monotonicity, independent observation/drain verdicts, and artifact replay. Authentic public TilePool/KernelRunner and conversational-lane routes are mandatory. Inject cancellation, deadline, allocator, worker, poll, drain, finalize, service, publication, and replay faults at every transition; prove bounded drain, no leaks/partial authority, and stable retry.

## Literal dual-latency and concurrent-service protocol

Freeze `tests/perf/cancellation_latency.toml` before sampling. Mandatory cancellation cases are {cancel.tilepool-field, cancel.sparse-lbm-1m, cancel.elasticity-level8}; each binds exact workload/source/build/host/tile/poll topology and records request, first cancellation observation, drain-complete, resource-return, finalize, and terminal-receipt timestamps. `cancel.elasticity-level8` may be typed Unsupported only under a preregistered capability rule and cannot satisfy or average into the claim. Clock resolution is at most 1 microsecond and calibrated absolute error at most 2 microseconds.

On each qualified M-class arm64 and Threadripper-class x86_64 host, use 1 untimed warmup of exactly 200 injections followed by 5 measured attempts of exactly 2000 deterministic seed-bound injections per workload: 10000 retained injections per workload/host. No outlier deletion, early stop, retry replacement, or post-request exclusion is allowed. Pre/post reference-axis movement above 3 percent, loaded/throttled host, timer failure, missing poll, leaked work, incomplete drain, pin/topology/source drift, or partial logs is Unqualified.

`CancellationObservationVerdict` uses request-to-first-observation: nearest-rank p95 <=200 microseconds and p99 <=500 microseconds for every admitted workload/host. `CancellationDrainVerdict` separately uses request-to-finalized-receipt: engineering p95 <=1000 microseconds and p99 <=5000 microseconds. Meeting the drain envelope cannot satisfy the 200-microsecond observation claim; failing drain cannot be hidden by fast observation. Report full histograms, maxima, Pass, Fail, NoData, and Unqualified on both axes.

Concurrent-service cases are exactly {service.catalog-read, service.estimate, service.ledger-point-query, service.explain-lineage}. While the frozen throughput workload saturates its lane, run one 100-operation-per-kind warmup and 5 measured attempts of exactly 1000 operations per kind/host. Record queue wait, service time, total latency, throughput-lane load, and typed result. The plan target is per-kind p95 total latency <=100 milliseconds; fixed non-collapse ceilings are p95 <=500 milliseconds and p99 <=1000 milliseconds. Candidate observations cannot select these limits. Missing mandatory operation, cross-lane starvation, silent priority inversion, or result error cannot Pass.

## Exact terminal harness, testing, logging, and proof

This Bead owns planned `scripts/ci/cancellation_latency_perf_e2e.sh` and `tests/perf/cancellation_latency.toml` with exact cancellation and service registries above. Canonical modes are `--list`, `--check`, `--self-test`, `--run CASE`, `--negative CASE`, `--fault CASE`, and artifact-only `--replay RECEIPT --input-root PATH --output-root PATH`. Self-test uses bounded synthetic clock/host/receipt fixtures and mints no latency evidence; run uses release-built no-mock production routes.

Unit/schema/boundary/property/metamorphic/statistical/state-model/mutation tests cover registry, timestamp/state ordering, timer/error/sample/quantile arithmetic, dual-verdict separation, service metrics, admission, caps, redaction, and replay. No-mock E2E covers qualified dual Pass/Fail combinations, service target/floor outcomes, NoData, loaded/throttled/unsupported Unqualified, cancellation/drain, every fault, truncation, tamper, stale identity, and clean replay. Mutants specifically collapse first-observation into finalize, omit poll evidence, reorder timestamps, substitute mean for p95, hide a slow drain, average workloads/hosts, or count suppressed cases and must fail.

Bounded redacted deterministic JSONL records source/build/features/host/ISA, manifest/case/attempt/injection/op/sequence, deterministic position, request/poll/drain/resource/finalize timestamps with units, queue/service/load values, warmup/measurement role, budgets, pre/post axes, expected/observed outcomes, first divergence, both authority/no-claim axes, relative artifacts, and exact reproduction. Raw events remain capped artifacts. Artifact-only replay recomputes metrics/policy without timing; a timing rerun is separate evidence. DSR proves harness integrity only. Planned paths remain `NoData` until created and executed on both admitted ISA families.
notes: The <=200 microsecond statement is now precisely request-to-first cancellation observation at a tile boundary. Request-to-drained/finalized receipt and conversational-lane service have separate, explicit envelopes; none can substitute for another.

title: fs-roofline tune-ledger write corrupts on x86-64 (fsqlite 'page freed in concurrent transaction')
close_reason: fsqlite upstream regression (frankensqlite#123, bisected to d1a543e); fs-ledger tune_put rerouted UPDATE-then-INSERT in 0e4534c; rf_004 fail->pass verified on ts1, both-ISA suites green

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DETERMINISTIC x86-64-ONLY CORRUPTION (found via cross-ISA verification on ts1,
Threadripper 5975WX, Zen 3; the ARM-only CI fleet cannot see this). Reproduce:
  cargo test -p fs-roofline --test conformance rf_004 --release
  -> rf_004_staleness_alerts_on_fingerprint_drift PANICS at conformance.rs:373:
     `inject valid-JSON payload corruption: Sql { context: "tune upsert", detail:
      "database disk image is malformed: page 52 was freed earlier in concurrent
       transaction 5" }`
3/3 runs fail with the IDENTICAL page (52) and transaction (5) -> deterministic,
not a flaky race. The failing op is a normal `tune_put` WRITE to the tune ledger
(fs-roofline -> fs-ledger -> fsqlite), during the test's setup that overwrites a
row with "{}" to exercise CorruptEvidence detection; fsqlite's own page manager
reports the DB image malformed BEFORE the write completes.

PASSES on aarch64 (M4) — so it is x86-specific: an fsqlite MVCC/page-management
edge case (a page freed by an internal "concurrent transaction" then referenced),
OR an fs-ledger/fs-roofline transaction pattern (atomic evidence transaction +
rollback + row reuse, crates/fs-roofline/src/kernels.rs:640-838) that fsqlite
tolerates on aarch64 but corrupts on x86.

IMPACT: (1) fs-roofline conformance is RED on x86 (rf_004). (2) The tune ledger is
the SAME fsqlite store the fz2.7 perf-baseline infra (FRANKENSIM_BASELINE_STORE)
writes to — so promoting/writing perf baselines on the Threadrippers likely hits
this too, blocking honest x86 perf rows. Next step: minimal fsqlite repro of the
tune_put write sequence on x86 to localize (fsqlite page-free-in-txn vs fs-ledger
transaction reuse); relates to the existing fsqlite bug bead lar1.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CLAIMED (CloudyFinch — the cross-ISA forensics lane; also the author of the c40j baseline tooling this blocks). Plan: (1) reproduce rf_004 on ts1 at HEAD; (2) extract the exact tune_put SQL sequence from fs-ledger and replay it in a minimal fsqlite-only program on x86 to classify fsqlite-upstream vs fs-ledger-misuse (lar1 precedent: re-verify against current fsqlite before filing); (3) land the fix or a documented workaround, rf_004 green on BOTH ISAs, close with the classification. Reservations: crates/fs-ledger tune paths if the fault is ours; a scratch repro program otherwise; fs-roofline conformance only if the test itself needs a fix.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LOCALIZED (frankensim-side triage; the residual bug is fsqlite-core). Findings:

1. tune_put is a PLAIN UPSERT (fs-ledger/src/lib.rs:1666): `INSERT INTO tune(...)
   ON CONFLICT(kernel,shape_class,machine) DO UPDATE SET params=..., measured=...`.
   No explicit DELETE/VACUUM; but the DO UPDATE reorganizes the tune B-tree page.

2. tune_put is CLEAN IN ISOLATION on x86 — fs-ledger's own suite (incl.
   tune_upserts, many sequential tune_put) is GREEN on x86 (my batch-3 run). So
   tune_put alone does NOT corrupt. The trigger is ACCUMULATED STATE.

3. The distinguishing element in rf_004 vs the passing fs-ledger tests:
   `record_run(...)` (conformance.rs:277) runs fs-roofline's ATOMIC EVIDENCE
   TRANSACTION (crates/fs-roofline/src/kernels.rs:640-838 — explicit begin/commit,
   op + tune rows written together, rollback-with-retry-marker path). That
   transaction frees B-tree pages onto the freelist. The LATER standalone tune_put
   UPSERT then reuses one of those freed pages, and fsqlite reports "page 52 was
   freed earlier in concurrent transaction 5" — transaction 5 == the evidence txn.

HYPOTHESIS: fsqlite freelist/MVCC page-reuse across a transaction boundary is
mis-tracked on x86-64 (a page freed inside the committed evidence transaction is
still seen as owned by that snapshot when a later write reuses it). aarch64 handles
the same sequence correctly (rf_004 GREEN on M4), so it is an x86-specific fsqlite
core bug, NOT fs-ledger/fs-roofline misuse (both ops are normal).

MINIMAL-REPRO DIRECTION for the fsqlite owner: {open ledger; run one explicit
multi-write transaction that frees a tune/B-tree page; commit; then a standalone
UPSERT that reuses the freed page} on x86 — should reproduce without the rest of
the roofline machinery. FRANKENSIM-SIDE MITIGATION if an fsqlite fix is far off:
force a WAL checkpoint (or a fresh Connection) between record_run and the next
tune_put so the freelist is reconciled before reuse — a workaround, not a fix.
Relates to lar1 (other fsqlite reparse bug). Blocks fz2.7 baseline promotion on x86.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
MITIGATION TEST — reconnection does NOT work (refines the diagnosis). Inserted a
fresh `Ledger::open(&db)` (new fsqlite Connection to the same file) immediately
before the corrupting tune_put in rf_004, on ts1/x86. STILL FAILS identically
(conformance.rs:374, "page 52 was freed earlier in concurrent transaction 5").

CONSEQUENCE: the malformation is PERSISTED IN THE DB FILE by record_run's evidence
transaction (transaction 5) — it is NOT a live per-connection snapshot/cache
artifact (a fresh connection reads the same corrupt on-disk freelist state). So the
bug is WRITE-SIDE: record_run's committed transaction writes the freelist/MVCC
page-free bookkeeping for page 52 INCORRECTLY on x86, and fsqlite's integrity check
fires when the later tune_put upsert tries to reuse that page. This is squarely an
fsqlite-core freelist/page-free bug on x86-64; there is NO frankensim-side
reconnection workaround. (A full VACUUM between record_run and tune_put would rebuild
the freelist and likely mask it, but that is heavy and still a workaround, not a
fix.) The proper fix is in fsqlite's freelist page-free bookkeeping on x86 —
recommend an fsqlite-direct repro: one committed transaction that frees a b-tree
page, then a fresh write that reuses it, on x86, checking the on-disk freelist +
per-page "freed-by-txn" bookkeeping for an x86 mis-encode (endianness/width/layout).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LOCALIZED + FIXED (workaround landed 0e4534c). Root cause is an fsqlite UPSTREAM regression, not fs-ledger misuse.

Mechanism: INSERT..ON CONFLICT..DO UPDATE on the tune table corrupts the DB ('page N was freed earlier in concurrent transaction M') when the conflict seek lands after a leaf split. Geometry-gated: needs 3 tune rows with measured ~1265B (600B and 2000B both dodge it); 2 rows fine; plain UPDATE fine; REPLACE INTO fine; DO NOTHING fine; same-size DO UPDATE also corrupts (not about shrinking). Pragmas/journal mode irrelevant.

Bisected frankensqlite 75ba1b7ed..46caaa9 (58 commits) with a raw fsqlite-only repro: first bad commit d1a543e 'fix(btree): rebuild rootless cursor path before INSERT OR REPLACE (bd-kwei8)' - its seek-cache fast path now always leaves a rootless single-entry cursor stack, and the guards it added to delete/table_insert do NOT cover the upsert's DO UPDATE mutation path, so balance treats the leaf as root and double-frees.

Filed upstream with minimal repro + bisect: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite/issues/123 (lar1 precedent).

NOT ISA-specific: reproduces on M4/macOS too at fsqlite HEAD. rf_004 only LOOKED x86-only because macOS receipt JSON lengths dodge the 1265B window. Heads-up: I fast-forwarded the local Mac frankensqlite clone to 46caaa9 (upstream HEAD, matches ts1) - if any fsqlite-backed test suddenly fails with 'page N freed earlier', it is frankensqlite#123, not your change.

Workaround: tune_put now UPDATE-then-INSERT (equivalent under single-writer-per-connection), doc-marked for revert once #123 fixed. Evidence: ts1 rf_004 fail 3/3 before -> conformance 8/8 + fs-ledger 77/0 after; local fs-ledger 87/0, rf_004 green. (Local rf_001 EnvironmentInvalid on the loaded M4 is the known busy-host artifact, pre-exists this change, passes on ts1.)

title: fs-evidence V&V: reject signed-zero aliases in canonical derived state and metric specs
description: The V&V codec preserves exact IEEE-754 bits, but two semantic/canonical gates use ordinary f64 PartialEq inconsistently. Second, QoiValidationPlan sorts metric specs by raw-bit key and then deduplicates via semantic PartialEq; [+0.0, 1.0, -0.0] leaves the equal signed-zero endpoints nonadjacent, admitting logically duplicate NormalizedDiscrepancy specs. Acceptance: derived applicability equality is bit-exact for every numeric field; metric canonical keys normalize semantic zero so signed-zero duplicates are adjacent and refused; codec and model share one ordering rule; canonical decode refuses an opposite-sign derived bound and a duplicate signed-zero metric sequence; honest exact-sign values and a single -0.0 remain representable; static checks pass and centralized Cargo/DSR proof remains pending.
